Commentary of Srimad Bhagavatam Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana, Translated By HH Bhanu Swami

# Vaiṣṇavānandinī. Canto 10 \[BS\]

## Chapter 1 - The Advent of Lord Kṛṣṇa

### Text 1

*śrī-rājovāca—*  
*kathito vaṁśa-vistāro bhavatā soma-sūryayoḥ rājñāṁ cobhaya-vaṁśyānāṁ caritaṁ paramādbhutam*

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: My dear lord, you have elaborately described the dynasties starting with Svāyambhūva Manu and the exalted and wonderful activities of the kings of dynasties of the moon-god and the sun-god.**

**Комментарий:**

May the beautiful Lord Govinda, a festival seen by the group of his own śaktis, Rādhā and others, the nectar of whose lotus feet are the shelter of the bees Rūpa Gosvāmī and others, whose face has the beauty of the full moon, who vows to protect his devotees always, who is described as complete Brahman by the personified Vedas, manifest his excellence.

May dark cloud complexioned, beautiful powerful Śukadeva, endowed with a compassionate heart, who showered thirsty king Parīkṣit with a shower of Govinda’s sweet pastimes, who is the only cause of joy for the creepers of bhāva in the forest of pure devotees connect me with that fragrance at all times.

Because of my meager capacity to immerse myself in the ocean of pastimes of Yaśodā’s son, a particle of mercy from Sanātana, Śrīdhara and Viśvanātha has become at present a heap of śakti.

In the tenth canto Kṛṣṇa, the āśraya, endowed with the nine other qualities, is described, while his destruction of the wicked is described secondarily.

Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda and Vasudeva, is described by Śukadeva, by the Lord’s desire, in a most secret and direct way respectively.

He has three types of pastimes since he has three abodes of Gokula, Mathurā and Dvārakā. These are revealed in an astonishing way by Śukadeva in ninety chapters.

Kṛṣṇa’s birth and related matters are described in the first five chapters when the devatās prayed to him to relieve the earth’s burden.

Then in nine chapters the infant pastimes of the Supreme Lord are described and in six chapters the paugaṇḍa pastimes, suffused with kaiśora rasa.

Then nineteen chapters describe the kaiśora pastimes. Akrūra offers prayers in the Yamunā in one chapter.

The Lord’s pastimes in Mathurā are described in eleven chapters and remainder (thirty-nine) describe pastimes in Dvārakā. Thus ninety chapters are summarized.

*daśamasyādime śrotṛ-vaktor vāṅ mādhurī mithaḥ \|*  
*devājñākāśa-vāk kaṁsāt śaureḥ ṣaṭ-tanayā hatāḥ*

**In the first chapter of the tenth canto, the sweet words of both the listeners and the speaker, the message to the devatās from the sky,and the killing of Vasudeva’s six children by Kaṁsa are described.**

Blissful in the ocean of nectar of topics about Kṛṣṇa avatāra, increasing the enthusiasm of the speaker with topics he should be made to discuss, in three lines, Parīkṣit asks with eagerness something previously mentioned. The numbering system of the verses is that accepted by the wise.

(Though the word sūrya, the sun-god, would usually come before soma,) the moon-god, soma is mentioned first. This is because the moon-god Candra (soma) is the grandson of Brahmā, whereas Sūrya is the great grandson of Brahmā; and he is an aṁśa of Brahmā; the deity of the mind, and most importantly Svayaṁ Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa accepted to appear in his dynasty. The most astonishing stories of conquest, etc., of kings of the moon and sun dynasties were told. Even though the astonishing stories of the Svayambhuva and his dynasty were told in the Third and other cantos, those dynasties’ concluding portions were not so attractive. The concluding portions of dynasties of the sun and moon however was most attractive with the stories of Kṛṣṇa and Rāma. Thus, their superior excellence in noted.

### Text 2

*yadoś ca dharma-śīlasya nitarāṁ muni-sattama tatrāṁśenāvatīrṇasya viṣṇor vīryāṇi śaṁsa naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O best of sages, you have also described the descendants of devotional Yadu. Now, kindly describe the wonderful, glorious activities of Kṛṣṇa, the perfection of all-pervasiveness, who appeared in that Yadu dynasty with Baladeva, his expansion.**

**Комментарий:**

The activities of Yadu was described. Though Yadu disobeyed his father’s order, since he had bhakti, he was fully virtuous. His bhakti is famous in the Ninth and Eleventh Cantos.

Describe to us as praise (śaṁsa) the exploits of Kṛṣṇa, he who is complete and all-pervading (viṣṇoḥ) who appeared along withBalarāma, his aṁśa, in the Yadu dynasty. By using the phrase (along with his aṁśa, Balarāma) Parīkṣit indicates his thirst for hearing about the valor of Balarāma also. Plural is used (naḥ – to us) to give respect to the listener, himself or to indicate himself along with the assembly. How is he who appeared described? The word viṣṇoḥ can also mean complete Svayam Bhagavān of whom Viṣṇu is an aṁśa.

### Text 3

*avatīrya yador vaṁśe bhagavān bhūta-bhāvanaḥ*  
*kṛtavān yāni viśvātmā tāni no vada vistarāt*

**Перевод:**

**Please tell me elaborately about the glorious activities, from the beginning to the end, that the Lord, protector of all beings, benefactor of all beings, performed after appearing in the Yadu dynasty.**

**Комментарий:**

“Already I have described his exploits as in jāto gataḥ pitṛ-gṛhād vrajam edhitārthaḥ (SB [9.24.66](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/24.66)).” Since I was not fully satisfied by that, speak about them in detail now. The Lord acts for the making the living entities soft with prema (bhāvanaḥ) as explained in the following:

*vākyair vikrama-līlayā*  
*nṛ-lokam ramayām āsa*  
*mūrtyā sarvāṅga-ramyayā*

**Kṛṣṇa pleased his devotees by his pleasing, affectionate glances, his satisfying instructions and his heroic actions, using his body which was pleasing in all aspects. (SB** [**9.24.64**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/24.64)**)**

*avitṛpta-dṛśāṁ nṝṇām*

**The Lord was the center of attraction for all eyes. (SB** [**3.2.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.11)**)**

*sva-mūrtyā loka-lāvanya-nirmuktyā locanaṁ nṛṇām*

**The sweetness of Kṛṣṇa’s beauty steals the functions of all the senses. The eyes no longer desire to see any other form. Drowning them in the ocean of his beauty, Śyamasundara gives them prema. (SB** [**11.1.6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/1.6)**)**

He spreads himself to the senses of all people (viśvātmā) by his beauty and other features.

### Text 4

*nivṛtta-tarṣair upagīyamānād*  
*bhavauṣadhāc chrotra-mano-’bhirāmāt*  
*ka uttamaśloka-guṇānuvādāt*  
*pumān virajyeta vinā paśughnāt*

**Перевод:**

**Except for a killer, what person would ever cease hearing glorification of the qualities of the famous Lord, sung profusely by liberated souls, by persons desiring relief from material suffering, and by persons desiring pleasure for the ear and mind?**

**Комментарий:**

“The pastimes of Kṛṣṇa were described once. Why do you ask again?” Who would give up discussing the qualities of Kṛṣṇa (uttama-śloka)? No one would.

The glorification of topics is described. They are profusely sung (upagīyamānāt) by those whose bliss in their ātmā has manifested,who are satisfied in themselves, and are devoid of thirst for sense objects (nivṛtta-tarṣair). The topics are the destroyer of the sicknessof saṁsāra (bhavāuṣadhāt) for persons desiring liberation. By the sweetness of the words and meaning, they are pleasing to the ear and mind of liberated persons. By saying that the topics are served by persons desiring liberation, the jīvan-muktas (i.e. the ātmārāmas), and the liberated, the topics are shown to be puruṣārtha (supreme goal).

Persons who see without distinctions (paśu), who see the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and the others as the same, who are opposed to the Lord, and, becoming like that, consequently fall down (ghnaḥ) are excluded. Or paśu-ghna can refer to persons absorbed in karmas,desiring Svarga.

*trai-vargikās te puruṣa vimukhā hari-medhasaḥ*  
*kathāyāṁ kathanīyoru-vikramasya madhudviṣaḥ*

**These persons are interested in dharma, artha, and kāma, and are averse to topics of the Supreme Lord who knows how to destroy saṁsāra, who is the killer of Madhu, and who is the most heroic lord worthy of praise. (SB** [**3.32.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.18)**)**

Or paśu-ghna means killers of animals. Such a person’s intelligence constantly absorbed in violence is devoid of desire for happiness in this or next life. But I was protected by the Lord from the time I was in the womb. Now, desiring to die, I will live particularly by hearing his topics.

### Text 5-7

*pitāmahā me samare ’marañjayair*  
*devavratādyātirathais timiṅgilaiḥ*  
*duratyayaṁ kaurava-sainya-sāgaraṁ*  
*kṛtvātaran vatsa-padaṁ sma yat-plavāḥ*

*drauṇy-astra-vipluṣṭam idaṁ mad-aṅgaṁ*  
*santāna-bījaṁ kuru-pāṇḍavānām*  
*jugopa kukṣiṁ gata ātta-cakro*  
*mātuś ca me yaḥ śaraṇaṁ gatāyāḥ*

*vīryāṇi tasyākhila-deha-bhājām*  
*antar bahiḥ pūruṣa-kāla-rūpaiḥ*  
*prayacchato mṛtyum utāmṛtaṁ ca*  
*māyā-manuṣyasya vadasva vidvan*

**Перевод:**

**Taking the boat of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, my grandfathers, Arjuna and others easily crossed the difficult ocean of the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra, in which such commanders as Bhīṣma resembled great fish that could very easily have swallowed him, since that ocean became the size of the hoof print of a calf. Because my mother surrendered unto Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, the Lord, with Sudarśana-cakra in hand, entered her womb and saved my body, the body of the last remaining descendant of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, a body which was almost destroyed by the fiery weapon of Aśvatthāmā. O learned Śukadeva! Please reveal the confidential activities of Kṛṣṇa, appearing in a human form by his mercy, appearing within and outside of all materially embodied living beings as time and Paramātmā and giving prema or death to various persons.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking, “I should also hear the topics of Kṛṣṇa because he is the protective deity of our dynasty,” Parīkṣit Mahārāja speaks this verse. My grandfather crossed the ocean of the Kaurava army, though it was difficult to surmount because of Bhīṣma and others (devavratādy), who were like timiṅgala fish (timiṅgilaiḥ) who could easily swallow or defeat Indra and other devatās (amarañjayair). Making that ocean as insignificant as the water in a calf’s hoof- print, my grandfathers were able to cross it because Kṛṣṇa was the boat. Please speak about his valor. Verse 5 is connected with the verb in verse 7.

I should hear his pastimes since he is my sole protector. He saved my body burned (vipluṣṭam) by Aśvatthāmā’s weapon. By idam hetouches his chest with his forefinger. Here it describes that Kṛṣṇa was holding Sudarśana-cakra (ātta-cakraḥ). In the First Canto it is described that he protected (jugopa) Parīkṣit by throwing a club. The word ca indicates that Kṛṣṇa also protected his mother’s body.

I should hear his pastimes because he gives the goal to all. Among all beings, he gives the highest bliss (amṛtaṁ) to the devotees, who are turned to the Lord (antar) by his two-armed and four- armed human forms (puruṣa-rūpaiḥ) and he gives death and later immortality to the enemies of the devotees, who are turned away from the Lord (bahiḥ) by forms of death (kāla). Kālo yam iti vihvalaḥ: Kaṁsa immediately got up from bed, thinking, “Death has come.” (SB [10.4.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/4.3))

Speak (vadasva) the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, even though they may be confidential. Bhāsanopasasmbhāṣā-jñāna-yatna-vimaty- upamantraṇeṣu vadaḥ (Pāṇini 1.3.47) explains why the ātmanepada form of vad is used here.

Or O my dedicated friend (sva), king of sages! Please certainly tell me (vada) for my benefit. Just as sweet drinks taste bitter ontongues spoiled by bile, similarly the form of bliss appears dreadful for the enemies of the devotees.

Kṛṣṇa is described. Māyā means knowledge according to Nighaṇtu. He has a human form of knowledge or vijñāna since the śruti says, tam ekaṁ govindam sac-cid-ānanda-vigraham: Govinda has a form of eternity, knowledge and bliss. (Gopāla Tāpanī Upaniṣad)

It is not a human form. He is like a human in form but made out of gold. Or he has created a human form by his māyā.

### Text 8

*rohiṇyās tanayaḥ prokto rāmaḥ saṅkarṣaṇas tvayā*  
*devakyā garbha-sambandhaḥ kuto dehāntaraṁ vinā*

**Перевод:**

**You have already explained that Saṅkarṣaṇa or Balarāma appeared as the son of Rohiṇī. Without changing bodies, how is it possible that he was also in the womb of Devakī?**

**Комментарий:**

In the next four verses (8-11) Parīkṣit Mahārāja inquires about the details of Kṛṣṇa’s birth.

A general description was given in Śrīmad Bhāgavatam ([9.24.54-55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/24.54)) how Saṅkarṣaṇa, Balarāma was the son of Rohiṇī. He is also counted among the sons of Devakī. Without dying and changing bodies, how did he attain a relationship with Rohiṇī’s womb?

### Text 9

*kasmān mukundo bhagavān pitur gehād vrajaṁ gataḥ*  
*kva vāsaṁ jñātibhiḥ sārdhaṁ kṛtavān sātvatāṁ patiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Why did Kṛṣṇa leave the house of his father, Vasudeva, and transfer himself to Vṛndāvana? Where did the Lord, the protector of the devotees, live with his relatives?**

**Комментарий:**

Why did he leave Vasudeva’s (pitur) house and go to Bṛhad-vana (vrajam)? Though having gone there, from Nanda’s (pitur) house in Bṛhad-vana (gehād) to what special place did he go to live with the cowherds? Later it is said

*nandaḥ sva-putram ādāya*

**Taking his son, Nanda went (SB** [**10.6.43**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/6.43)**)**

Jñāti means cowherds as in the following:

*Jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmaḥ*

**we will come to see you, my relatives. (SB** [**10.45.23**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/45.23)**)**

### Text 10

*vraje vasan kim akaron madhupuryāṁ ca keśavaḥ*  
*bhrātaraṁ cāvadhīt kaṁsaṁ mātur addhātad-arhaṇam*

**Перевод:**

**While Kṛṣṇa lived in Mahāvana, Vṛndāvana, Mathurā and Dvārakā, what did he do? Why did he personally kill Kaṁsa, his mother’s brother? Such killing is not at all sanctioned in the scriptures.**

**Комментарий:**

Madhupuryām (city of the Madhus) refers to Mathurā and Dvārakā. Why did he kill Kaṁsa, the brother of his mother? It was not proper to kill him (addhā atad-arhaṇam) since he was a maternal uncle.

### Text 11

*dehaṁ mānuṣam āśritya kati varṣāṇi vṛṣṇibhiḥ*  
*yadu-puryāṁ sahāvātsīt patnyaḥ katy abhavan prabhoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, has no material body, yet he appears as a human being. For how many years did he live with the descendants of Vṛṣṇi in Dvārakā? How many wives did he marry?**

**Комментарий:**

His form took shelter of a human form, since his actions were very human-like and he lived among humans. This means his form manifested the nature of humans like in the sentence cakṣur āśritya rūpe sthitaḥ: manifesting the eye he is situated in form. How many years did he live in Mathurā and Dvārakā, in his svarūpa, but appearing like a human? Nārada said:

*yūyaṁ nṛ-loke bata bhūri-bhāgā*  
*lokaṁ punānā munayo ’bhiyanti*  
*yeṣāṁ gṛhān āvasatīti sākṣād*  
*gūḍhaṁ paraṁ brahma manuṣya-liṅgam*

**You Pāṇḍavas are most fortunate in this world. Sages who purify the planets come and visit your houses because the Supreme Brahman personally resides in your houses in a human form. (SB** [**7.10.48**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/10.48)**)**

Parāśara said:

*yatrāvatīrṇaṁ kṛṣṇākhyaṁ paraṁ brahma narākṛtiḥ*

**The parabrahman in human form appearing in the Yadu dyasty is called Kṛṣṇa. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa)**

A person is named according to the activities in which he is deeply involved, just as a king, though a human, is called a nṛdevatā(devatā among men), or nṛsiṁha (man-lion) because his actions are like a devatā or lion. That he accepted a human, material body is the claim of only the unintelligent (and denied), since his body is described as the supreme tattva.

*tattvaṁ paraṁ yoginām*

**For the yogīs, Kṛṣṇa was the Absolute Truth. (SB** [**10.43.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/43.17)**)**

### Text 12

*etad anyac ca sarvaṁ me mune kṛṣṇa-viceṣṭitam*  
*vaktum arhasi sarvajña śraddadhānāya vistṛtam*

**Перевод:**

**O great sage, knower of everything! Please describe in detail all the remarkable activities about which I have inquired and also about those which I have not, for I have full faith.**

**Комментарий:**

Since I am ignorant, how many details should I ask? Since you know everything, tell everything.

### Text 13

*naiṣātiduḥsahā kṣun māṁ tyaktodam api bādhate*  
*pibantaṁ tvan-mukhāmbhoja-cyutaṁ hari-kathāmṛtam*

**Перевод:**

**Because I am drinking the nectar of topics about Kṛṣṇa, which is flowing from your lotus mouth, though I have given up even drinking water, my hunger and thirst, which are extremely difficult to bear, cannot hinder me.**

**Комментарий:**

“Parīkṣit, because you are afflicted by hunger and thirst, you should rest a while.”

### Text 14

*sūta uvāca*  
*evaṁ niśamya bhṛgu-nandana sādhu-vādaṁ*  
*vaiyāsakiḥ sa bhagavān atha viṣṇu-rātam*  
*pratyarcya kṛṣṇa-caritaṁ kali-kalmaṣa-ghnaṁ*  
*vyāhartum ārabhata bhāgavata-pradhānaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Sūta Gosvāmī said: O son of Bhṛgu \[Śaunaka Ṛṣi\], after Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the most respectable devotee, the son of Vyāsadeva, heard the pious questions of Mahārāja Parīkṣit, he thanked the king with great respect. Then he began to discourse on topics concerning Kṛṣṇa, which are the remedy for all sufferings in thisage of Kali.**

**Комментарий:**

Sūta Gosvāmī speaks, “O son of Bhṛgu \[Śaunaka Ṛṣi\].” The devotees (bhāgavata) were most important for Śukadeva, in terms of deserving respect.

### Text 15

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*samyag vyavasitā buddhis tava rājarṣi-sattama*  
*vāsudeva-kathāyāṁ te yaj jātā naiṣṭhikī ratiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O best of all saintly kings! Because you are greatly attracted to topics of Vāsudeva, your intelligence is firmly fixed in them.**

**Комментарий:**

Though it was said that Śukadeva Gosvāmī began to discourse (in the previous verse), the phrase śuka uvāca (Śukadeva spoke) is stated again to indicate Śukadeva’s sweet speech. He was like a parrot because of his sweet words, since Kṛṣṇa says in Brahma- vaivarta Purāṇa:

*vyāsaḥ! tvadīya-tanayaḥ śukavan manojñaṁ \|*  
*brūte vaco bhavatu tac chuka eva nāmnā*

**O Vyāsa! Your son speaks attractive words like a parrot. He should be called Śuka.**

O best of saintly kings! Your intelligence is similar to that which is completely fixed. Because of that, you have fixed rati.

### Text 16

*vāsudeva-kathā-praśnaḥ puruṣāṁs trīn punāti hi*  
*vaktāraṁ pracchakaṁ śrotṝṁs tat-pāda-salilaṁ yathā*

**Перевод:**

**The Gaṅgā, emanating from the toe of Viṣṇu, purifies the three worlds, the upper, middle and lower planetary systems. Similarly, when one asks questions about the pastimes and characteristics of Kṛṣṇa, three varieties of men are purified: the speaker or preacher, he who inquires, and the people in general who listen.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva praises questions about Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. Just as Gaṅgā, water from the Lord’s feet, purifies the three worlds, in asking questions about Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, the speaker (you), the inquirer (me) and the listeners (the sages) are purified of contamination which is the cause of not hearing or not speaking about the pastimes. The topics of Hari purify the speaker, the inquirer and the listener in descending order.

### Text 17

*bhūmir dṛpta-nṛpa-vyāja-daityānīka-śatāyutaiḥ*  
*ākrāntā bhūri-bhāreṇa brahmāṇaṁ śaraṇaṁ yayau*

**Перевод:**

**Once when mother earth was overburdened by hundreds of thousands of military phalanxes of various conceited demons dressed like kings, she took shelter of Brahmā.**

**Комментарий:**

The famous reason for Kṛṣṇa’s appearance is described.

Dṛpta-nṛpa-vyāja indicates that though not born in demoniac lineages the kings acted like demons. They were are a heavy burden due to their unlimited army, a heap of sin. Being overrun by them, earth took shelter of Brahmā situated on the pinnacle of Meru.

### Text 18

*gaur bhūtvāśru-mukhī khinnā krandantī karuṇaṁ vibhoḥ*  
*upasthitāntike tasmai vyasanaṁ samavocata*

**Перевод:**

**Mother earth, assuming the form of a cow, very distressed, with tears in her eyes, and crying pitifully, appeared before Brahmā and told him about her misfortune.**

**Комментарий:**

Earth became a cow to invoke compassion. She spoke of her suffering (vyasanam) to Brahmā.

### Text 19

*brahmā tad-upadhāryātha saha devais tayā saha*  
*jagāma sa-tri-nayanas tīraṁ kṣīra-payo-nidheḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, having heard of the distress of mother earth, Brahmā, with mother earth, Śiva and all the other devatās, approached the shore of the ocean of milk.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā heard her suffering. Since the word atha is extra, the following is indicated. Brahmā thought: Creation is my work but protection is Viṣṇu’s and therefore I should go to his abode on the Milk Ocean and request him. Thus, he went to the shore of the milk ocean from the pinnacle of Meru, along with earth (tayā saha).

### Text 20

*tatra gatvā jagannāthaṁ deva-devaṁ vṛṣākapim*  
*puruṣaṁ puruṣa-sūktena upatasthe samāhitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After reaching the shore of the ocean of milk, the devatās with great attention worshiped Viṣṇu, the master of the whole universe, the supreme God of all gods, who provides for everyone and diminishes everyone’s suffering, by reciting the Puruṣa-sūkta.**

**Комментарий:**

It was proper for Brahmā to go to Viṣṇu, since Viṣṇu was lord of the universe (jagannātham). He would listen to their pleas since he is most worshippable (deva-devam). He would fulfill their goal since he showers what is desired (vṛṣa) and removes suffering (akāpi). Brahmā praised him with puruṣa-sūkta with concentrated mind (samāhitaḥ).

### Text 21

*giraṁ samādhau gagane samīritāṁ*  
*niśamya vedhās tridaśān uvāca ha*  
*gāṁ pauruṣīṁ me śṛṇutāmarāḥ punar*  
*vidhīyatām āśu tathaiva mā ciram*

**Перевод:**

**While in trance, Brahmā heard words vibrating in the sky. Thus he told the devatās: O devatās, hear immediately from me the order of Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and execute it without delay.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā related the Lord’s order to the devatās. He heard the unseen speaker in samādhi, in the sky. Hear from me the message (gām)spoken with force (pauruṣīm). It was most difficult for Brahmā and others to see the Lord of the milk ocean, an aṁśa of aṁśa of Kṛṣṇa. By this great power, it is indicated that the powers of Kṛṣṇa, the aṁśī of his aṁśī (and all aṁśīs and aṁśas), are exceedingly superior. Still speaking Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes so that they are visible to the whole world beginning with devatās and humans is due to his great mercy. His pastimes with his powers being secretive are attractive like a mirror covering a picture.

### Text 22

*puraiva puṁsāvadhṛto dharā-jvaro*  
*bhavadbhir aṁśair yaduṣūpajanyatām*  
*sa yāvad urvyā bharam īśvareśvaraḥ*  
*sva-kāla-śaktyā kṣapayaṁś cared bhuvi*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa is already aware of the distress on earth. For as long as the source of all forms of the Lord remains visible on earth to diminish its burden, all of you devatās should appear as sons and grandsons along with his eternal associates in the family of the Yadus at the proper time.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā repeats the words of Lord Viṣṇu in four verses (22-25). The Lord knows the distress of the earth. Previous to your information it was known by Kṛṣṇa (puṁsā). You should appear as Lord’s sons and grandsons among the Yadus, merging with his aṁsas such as Uddhava. How long? You stay there as long as he manifests on earth to destroy the earth’s burden by his śakti of time. Do this quickly. The Lord is described. He is the lord of controllers like us (īśvareśvaraḥ). He is Svayaṁ Bhagavān.

### Text 23

*vasudeva-gṛhe sākṣād bhagavān puruṣaḥ paraḥ*  
*janiṣyate tat-priyārthaṁ sambhavantu sura-striyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who has full potency, will personally appear as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore all the wives of the manvantara-avatāras should also appear in order to satisfy him.**

**Комментарий:**

The puruṣa will appear in the house of Vasudeva, and in the house of King Nanda, both viśuddha-sattva avatāras. Śiva said:

*sattvaṁ viśuddhaṁ vasudeva-śabditaṁ*  
*yad īyate tatra pumān apāvṛtaḥ*

**Viśuddha sattva is called Vasudeva, because there the Supreme Lord appears without coverings. (SB** [**4.3.23**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/3.23)**)**

“Since he does not say, ‘I will appear,’ is this Garbhodaśaya who will appear?” No. He is superior (paraḥ). Then is this Karaṇodaśaya Viṣṇu? No. He is Bhagavān. Then does that mean he is the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha? No. He is directly(sākṣāt) Bhagavān, Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, who is not dependent on any other form. To create friendship with Rādhā, Rukminī and others (priyārtham), their aṁśas, the wives of manvantara-avatāras like Vāmana and Ajita should appear. By the strength of their previous worship they should appear as separate forms.

### Text 24

*vāsudeva-kalānantaḥ sahasra-vadanaḥ svarāṭ*  
*agrato bhavitā devo hareḥ priya-cikīrṣayā*

**Перевод:**

**The foremost manifestation of Kṛṣṇa is Saṅkarṣaṇa, who is known as Ananta. He is the origin of all incarnations within this material world. Previous to the appearance of Kṛṣṇa, this original Saṅkarṣaṇa will appear as Baladeva, just to please the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa in his pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

He who shines (rāṭ) with his brother (sva) Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma will appear previous to him. Just as Bhartṛhari is also called Hari, Deva means Baladeva. Balarāma (devaḥ) is the thousand headed Ananta in his aṁśa because it will be said:

*rāma rāma mahā-bāho na jāne tava vikramam*  
*yasyaikāṁśena vidhṛtā jagatī jagataḥ pate*

**\[Goddess Yamunā said:\] Rāma, Rāma, O mighty-armed one! I cannot know your full prowess. With a single portion of yourself you hold up the earth, O Lord of the universe. (SB** [**10.65.28**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/65.28)**)**

Ananta is a portion (kalā) of Kṛṣṇa (vāsudeva). He is dear to Hari because he thinks, “When I become the elder brother, he (Kṛṣṇa) will be able to perform pastimes without worry .”

### Text 25

*viṣṇor māyā bhagavatī yayā sammohitaṁ jagat*  
*ādiṣṭā prabhuṇāṁśena kāryārthe sambhaviṣyati*

**Перевод:**

**The potency of the Lord, full of power, who bewilders the whole world, will also appear by the request of her master to perform her actions, as a servant of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

As well the Lord Viṣṇu’s māyā will appear, being ordered by him (prabhuṇā). She is called īśvarī, also called parā and yoga(bhagavatī). Māyā means parā.

*svarūpa-bhūtayā nitya-śaktyā māyākhyayā yutaḥ \|*  
*ato māyā-mayaṁ viṣṇuṁ pravadanti sanātanam*

**The Lord is endowed with his eternal energy arising from his svarūpa. It is called māyā. Thus eternal Viṣṇu is māyā- maya or composed of his spiritual energy. (Caturveda- śikhā, quoted in Brahma-sūtra-bhāṣya of Madhvācārya)**

The world is bewildered by her aṁśa (aṁśena), the three guṇas arising as her reflection. This parā will appear with the three guṇas. What is her purpose? She will appear for accomplishing the Lord’s work, for taking Devakī’s seventh embryo and putting Yaśodā to sleep. And to fool Kaṁsa, she will say, “Your enemy is born somewhere.” The first actions were arranged by herself. It was not the three guṇas acting. The action of fooling Kaṁsa was arranged by the three guṇas since that is her influence on the wicked.The three guṇas are an aṁśa of the svarūpa-śakti called parā as described in Nārada Pañcarātra:

*jānāty ekā parā-kāntaṁ saiva durgā tad-ātmikā \|*  
*yā parā paramā śaktir mahā-viṣṇu-svarūpiṇī*  
*yasyā vijñāna-mātreṇa parāṇāṁ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*muhūrtād deva-devasya prāptir bhavati nānyathā*  
*ekeyaṁ prema-sarvasva-svarūpā śrī-kuleśvarī \|*  
*anayā sulabho jñeya ādi devo’khileśvaraḥ*

*asyā āvarikā śaktir mahā-māyākhileśvarī \|*  
*yayā mugdhaṁ jagat sarvaṁ sarva-dehābhimāninaḥ*

**Yogamāyā or Ekanāṁśa, Durgā, is the supreme śakti of Lord Viṣṇu. She is unswerving in devotion to the Lord. By realizing her, one immediately attains the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Soul among all souls. Her nature is prema and she rules over Gokula like a queen. By her one can easily realize the Supreme Lord. Her āvaraṇikā-śakti (covering potency) is mahāmāyā, the controller of the material realm. By the influence of mahāmāyā all jīvas identify with their bodies and become bewildered.**

Ekā in this verse means Ekanāṁśa.

### Text 26

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity ādiśyāmara-gaṇān prajāpati-patir vibhuḥ*  
*āśvāsya ca mahīṁ gīrbhiḥ sva-dhāma paramaṁ yayau*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: After thus advising the devatās and pacifying mother earth by words, the very powerful Brahmā, who is the master of all other Prajāpatis, returned to his own abode.**

**Комментарий:**

Thus relating the order of Viṣnu (iti), Brahmā returned to his abode Satya-loka.

### Text 27

*śūraseno yadupatir mathurām āvasan purīm*  
*māthurāñ chūrasenāṁś ca viṣayān bubhuje purā*

**Перевод:**

**Formerly, Śūrasena, the chief of the Yadu dynasty, had gone to live in the city of Mathurā. There he enjoyed the places known as Māthura and Śūrasena.**

**Комментарий:**

Going to speak of the birth of Kṛṣṇa in Vasudeva’s house, he speaks a topic which is useful for that. Viṣayān means places.

### Text 28

*rājadhānī tataḥ sābhūt sarva-yādava-bhūbhujām*  
*mathurā bhagavān yatra nityaṁ sannihito hariḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Since that time, the city of Mathurā had been the capital of all the kings of the Yadu dynasty. The city and district of Mathurā are very intimately connected with Kṛṣṇa, for Kṛṣṇa lives there eternally.**

**Комментарий:**

This was the residing place of kings (rājadhānī). By saying that the Lord resides there eternally (yatra nityaṁ sannihita), it is indicated that the place is also eternal and since in Padma Purāṇa it is said:

*nityāṁ me mathurāṁ viddhi nityaṁ vṛṇdāvanaṁ tathā*

**Know that Mathurā and Vṛndāvana are eternal.**

Moreover Kṛṣṇa, who will be appearing in the first day of Brahmā, first manifests the place and his associates, and then appears there. Having performed pastimes, he becomes invisible there? Again, at the proper time, as long as there is no prākṛtika-pralaya, hewill appear. But it is not that every time he comes from some Vaikuṇṭha and appears in this world. Moreover when he appears, his aṁśas merge in him from the spiritual world. After his pastimes are completed, they return their respective abodes since the Third Canto states:

*sva-śānta-rūpeṣv itaraiḥ sva-rūpair*  
*abhyardyamāneṣv anukampitātmā*  
*parāvareśo mahad-aṁśa-yukto*  
*hy ajo ’pi jāto bhagavān yathāgniḥ*

**Being compassionate in mind, when his devotees are afflicted by the demons, Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, though not having material birth, appears within this world along with all his Viṣṇu expansions, like fire, since he is the lord of all forms of God and devatās. (SB** [**3.2.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.15)**)**

He manifests pastimes with them in Mathurā. At the time of prākṛtika-pralaya, making the two manifestations one, he remains in his planet above everything else. This is the statement of the knowers of truth.

### Text 29

*tasyāṁ tu karhicic chaurir vasudevaḥ kṛtodvahaḥ*  
*devakyā sūryayā sārdhaṁ prayāṇe ratham āruhat*

**Перевод:**

**Some time ago, Vasudeva, who belonged to the Śūra dynasty, married Devakī. After the marriage, he mounted his chariot to return home with his newly married wife.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva mounted the chariot with his newly married wife (sūryayā) Devakī to go to his house. Details of the marriage are given in Droṇa-parva of Mahābhārata:

*yador abhūd anvavāye devamīḍha iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*yādavas tasya ca sutaḥ śūras trailokya-saṁmataḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa heard that Devamīḍha, was in the succession from Yadu. His son was Śūra, who was approved by the three worlds.**

*śūrasya śaurir nṛ-varo vasudevo mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*dhanuṣy anavaraḥ śūraḥ kārtavīrya-samo yudhi*

**Vasudeva, best of men, most famous was the son of Śūra. Śūra was incomparable using the bow and was equal to Kārtavīrya in battle.**

*tad-vīryaś cāpi tatraiva kule śinir abhūn nṛpa \|*  
*etasminn eva kāle tu devakasya mahātmanaḥ*  
*svayaṁvare rājan sarva-kṣatra-samāgame \|*  
*tatraiva devakīṁ devīṁ vasudevārtham āptavān*

**In that family there was the valiant king Śini. O King! At that time, at the svayaṁvara of Devaka’s daughter, when all kṣatriyas gathered, Śini obtained Devakī for Vasudeva.**

*nirjitya pārthivān sarvān ratham āropayac chiniḥ \|*  
*tāṁ dṛṣṭvā devakīṁ śaure rathasthāṁ puruṣa-rṣabhaḥ*  
*nāmṛṣyata mahātejāḥ somadattaḥ śiner nṛpa*

**Conquering all kings, Śini mounted his chariot. Seeing Devakī on Vasudeva’s chariot, Somadatta, best of men, could not tolerate the great power of Śini.**

### Text 30

*ugrasena-sutaḥ kaṁsaḥ svasuḥ priya-cikīrṣayā*  
*raśmīn hayānāṁ jagrāha raukmai ratha-śatair vṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kaṁsa, the son of King Ugrasena, in order to please his sister (cousin) Devakī on the occasion of her marriage, took charge of the reins of the horses and became the chariot driver. He was surrounded by hundreds of golden chariots.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa’s sister (svasur) was Devakī. Kaṁsa took the reins (raśmīn) of the horses. This means he acted as the driver.

### Text 31-32

*catuḥ-śataṁ pāribarhaṁ gajānāṁ hema-mālinām*  
*aśvānām ayutaṁ sārdhaṁ rathānāṁ ca tri-ṣaṭ-śatam*

*dāsīnāṁ sukumārīṇāṁ dve śate samalaṅkṛte*  
*duhitre devakaḥ prādād yāne duhitṛ-vatsalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**While she and her husband were leaving home, Devaka, out of affectionate for his daughter, gave her with great devotion a dowry of four hundred elephants nicely decorated with golden garlands. He also gave ten thousand horses, eighteen hundred chariots, and two hundred very beautiful young maidservants, fully decorated with ornaments.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Pāribarhaṁ means household articles. The elephants had garlands of gold. There were eighteen hundred chariots (triṣaṭ śatam 3 x 6 x 100) of three separate types. There were young servant girls decorated properly with a variety of excellent garments, ornaments suitable to the festival.

Devaka gave this with great faith (prādāt).

### Text 33

*śaṅkha-tūrya-mṛdaṅgāś ca nedur dundubhayaḥ samam*  
*prayāṇa-prakrame tāta vara-vadhvoḥ sumaṅgalam*

**Перевод:**

**O beloved son, Mahārāja Parīkṣit, when the bride and bridegroom were ready to start, conchshells, bugles, drums and kettledrums all vibrated in concert for their auspicious departure.**

### Text 34

*pathi pragrahiṇaṁ kaṁsam ābhāṣyāhāśarīra-vāk*  
*asyās tvām aṣṭamo garbho hantā yāṁ vahase ’budha*

**Перевод:**

**While Kaṁsa, controlling the reins of the horses, was driving the chariot along the way, an unembodied voice addressed him, “You foolish rascal, the eighth child of the woman you are carrying will kill you!”**

**Комментарий:**

A voice spoke to Kaṁsa who was holding the reins of the houses. O Kaṁsa! Garbha (not specifying boy or girl) is mentioned so that Kaṁsa would have no doubt when he sees the eighth child as a girl. You take this woman to the house of her husband. Her eighth child will kill you. O fool (abudha)! You are fool because you are carrying the mother of your enemy and because you do not know that you will die.

“How will the Lord kill Kaṁsa who has affection for his mother Devakī?” The devatās were worried that the Lord’s appearance would be thwarted. They thus gave this message while being invisible in order that Kaṁsa commit offense to Devakī. They understood that Kaṁsa could not kill the mother of the Lord.

### Text 35

*ity uktaḥ sa khalaḥ pāpo bhojānāṁ kula-pāṁsanaḥ*  
*bhaginīṁ hantum ārabdhaḥ khaḍga-pāṇiḥ kace ’grahīt*

**Перевод:**

**Kaṁsa was a condemned personality in the Bhoja dynasty because he was envious and sinful. Therefore, upon hearing this omen from the sky, he caught hold of his sister’s hair with his left hand and took up his sword with his right hand to sever her head from her body.**

**Комментарий:**

He did not reflect on the meaning of the words. On being addressed/ spoken to (iti uktaḥ), he immediately attempted to kill Devakī(hantum ārabdhaḥ). The formation (of ārabdhaḥ) is according to ādi-karmaṇi kta kartari ca. (Pāṇini 3.4.71) Holding a sword in his hand, he grabbed her hair because he was wicked (khalaḥ). He who became the charioteer for his sister out of affection, giving up the reins, grabbed her hair and was about to kill her with a sword. This is the “affection” of a wicked person. He was sin personified, having no qualms about committing sin. He was a contamination of the dynasty (kula-pāṁsanaḥ), a person who kills (aṁsati) thesuccession of the dynasty (kulapā).

### Text 36

*taṁ jugupsita-karmāṇaṁ nṛśaṁsaṁ nirapatrapam*  
*vasudevo mahā-bhāga uvāca parisāntvayan*

**Перевод:**

**Wanting to pacify Kaṁsa, who was so cruel and envious that he was shamelessly ready to kill his sister, the great soul Vasudeva, who was to be the father of Kṛṣṇa, spoke to him in the following words.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa was cruel (nṛśaṁsaṁ). “Why would such a person listen to Vasudeva’s pacifying words?” Even tigers and other dangers are not inimical to the fortunate (mahābhāgaḥ). Thus Vasudeva enlightened Kaṁsa by conciliation (sāma), by influencing the mind(bheda) through logic and arousing affection successively.

### Text 37

*śrī-vasudeva uvāca*  
*ślāghanīya-guṇaḥ śūrair bhavān bhoja-yaśaskaraḥ*  
*sa kathaṁ bhaginīṁ hanyāt striyam udvāha-parvaṇi*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva said: My dear brother-in-law Kaṁsa, you are the pride of your family, the Bhoja dynasty, and great heroes praise your qualities. How could such a qualified person as you kill a woman, your own sister, especially on the occasion of her marriage?**

**Комментарий:**

Five types of sāma and two types of bheda are described as follows:

*sambandha-lābhāv upakṛty-abhedau guṇa-kīrtanaṁ \|*  
*sāma pañca-vidhaṁ bhedo dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa-bhayaṁ vaca*

Words invoking relationship (sambandha), personal gain (lābha), appealing to benevolence (upakṛti), showing identity (abheda) and glorifying qualities (guṇa-kīrtana) are the five types of sāma. Words inducing fear of perceived danger and unperceived danger are the two types of bheda.

First Vasudeva enlightens Kaṁsa with sāma by praising him. “She is a woman and your sister. Moreover it is her wedding. She should not be killed. Otherwise your fame and bravery will be damaged.” He praises him (guṇa-kīrtana) by saying “you have praiseworthy qualities.”

By mentioning “bhoja,” he invokes relationship (sambandha). By saying “bhaginīm” (sister) he shows identity (abheda). By saying, “How can you kill your sister?” he shows that by refraining from killing a woman, mother of an enemy, one gains fame (lābha). By saying “udvāha” (this is her wedding), he means by obtaining a wife, I would be benefitted (upakṛti).

This is the wedding day of your sister, a woman. By killing her you will become infamous in this life and go to hell in the next life. This shows the two types of bheda: seen and unseen consequences.

Sarasvatī devī explains thus. You are deficient among the praiseworthy. You are famous for increasing the quarrels among the Bhojas who are famous for quarrels. How can you kill only the sister, one person; kill the whole dynasty.

### Text 38

*mṛtyur janmavatāṁ vīra dehena saha jāyate*  
*adya vābda-śatānte vā mṛtyur vai prāṇināṁ dhruvaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O great hero, one who takes birth is sure to die; for death is born with the body. One may die today or after hundreds of years, but death is sure for every living entity.**

**Комментарий:**

“I will kill her because I fear death.” O brave hero! Death is born along with the body for persons who have taken birth, since we see change in the body at every moment. You will not be a hero if you kill her. “I will kill her to delay my death.” You could die today or after a hundred years. Using vā twice indicates that both are equally strong possibilities. If death is unavoidable, it is not proper to earn sin just for the purpose of delaying death. By not acquiring sin, you will enjoy happiness in the next life.

### Text 39

*dehe pañcatvam āpanne dehī karmānugo ’vaśaḥ*  
*dehāntaram anuprāpya prāktanaṁ tyajate vapuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the present body turns to dust and is again reduced to five elements—earth, water, fire, air and ether—the proprietor of the body, the living being, automatically receives another body of material elements according to his karma. When the next body is obtained, he gives up the present body.**

**Комментарий:**

The meaning is clarified. When the body dies (pañcatvaṁ), the jīva (dehī), attaining another body, then (anu) gives up the present body. According to karma (karmānugaḥ), the jīva will attain enjoyment in the next body. One should not commit sin for protecting the present body, by understanding how enjoyment is attained. This procedure takes place unavoidably (avaśaḥ). Thus he is not capable of protecting the body.

### Text 40

*vrajaṁs tiṣṭhan padaikena yathaivaikena gacchati*  
*yathā tṛṇa-jalaukaivaṁ dehī karma-gatiṁ gataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Just as a person traveling on the road rests one foot on the ground and then lifts the other, or as a worm on a vegetable transfers itself to one leaf and then gives up the previous one, the conditioned soul takes shelter of another body and then gives up the previous one.**

**Комментарий:**

An example of giving up the previous body after attaining a new body is given. A person who is walking places one foot firmly in front and then takes the other foot from his previous place and places in front and walks forward. He does not put both feet forward at once, to give up the previous place and go to the next place. Dissatisfied with this example because it involves accepting and giving up of the same earth, he gives another example. A caterpillar situated firmly on one blade of grass gives up the previous place. In the same way, situated on the path of karma, the jīva gives up the previous body.

### Text 41

*svapne yathā paśyati deham īdṛśaṁ*  
*manorathenābhiniviṣṭa-cetanaḥ*  
*dṛṣṭa-śrutābhyāṁ manasānucintayan*  
*prapadyate tat kim api hy apasmṛtiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Just as by mental adjustments one dreams at night of living under different circumstances, in different bodies, and forgets his actual position, in waking state also, having experienced a situation by seeing or hearing about it, one contemplates and speculates about that situation, and thus one thinks of that, forgetting his present body.**

**Комментарий:**

“This body is the ātmā. Like the stain of betel nut, knowledge is its quality. One should not consider anything as the self except the body. Therefore, one should protect the body, the ātmā.”

To refute this idea, three verses explain the difference between body and ātmā. In a dream, just as one sees a body, the object of affection, similar to the body in waking state (īdṛśam), and even while awake one who is wandering by the mind, becomes some king or Indra, i.e. sees those various bodies. And one identifies the self with the body seen (abhiniviṣṭa-cetanaḥ). The method for that is this. Seeing a king or hearing about Indra, one contemplates (anucintayan) by the mind, with those impressions. Forgetting one’s body of the waking state (apasmṛtiḥ), one accepts the dream body or the imaginary body. When considering this body to be the self, its dharma, the consciousness, should not wander elsewhere (but it does). Thus the ātmā is different from the body, which is the experience of the ātmā following various bodies. Knowledge is not the quality of the body since it is not perceived in the dead body.

### Text 42

*yato yato dhāvati daiva-coditaṁ*  
*mano vikārātmakam āpa pañcasu*  
*guṇeṣu māyā-raciteṣu dehy asau*  
*prapadyamānaḥ saha tena jāyate*

**Перевод:**

**The mind, impelled by karma and subject to transformations, leaves a body made of guṇas by māyā and becomes absorbed in another one. The ignorant jīva, thinking in this way, is born with a mind.**

**Комментарий:**

At the time of death, the mind pushed (coditaṁ) by karma, which is about to give results (daiva), pursues bodies of devatā or man,transformation of the thoughts, and attains such bodies. The jīva is born with the mind in bodies made of the five elements (guṇeṣu) made by the Lord’s māyā. The jīva, attaining absorption (prapadyamānaḥ), the quality of the mind such as, “when my son is nourished, I am nourished”, in that body is born with the mind. Thus, it is established that the one ātmā, which follows many bodies, is different from the bodies.

### Text 43

*jyotir yathaivodaka-pārthiveṣv adaḥ*  
*samīra-vegānugataṁ vibhāvyate*  
*evaṁ sva-māyā-raciteṣv asau pumān*  
*guṇeṣu rāgānugato vimuhyati*

**Перевод:**

**When the luminaries in the sky, such as the moon, the sun and the stars, are reflected in water, they appear to be of different shapes because of the movements of the wind. Similarly, when the living entity, the soul, becomes overcome with material attachment, he becomes bewildered in bodies made of the Lord’s māyā.**

**Комментарий:**

Establishing the difference between the ātmā and the body, an example is given, where the ātmā thinks itself in terms of the qualities of the body. The light of the moon’s reflection in vessels full of water is perceived to tremble, following the movements of the wind. The trembling of water caused by wind is perceived there. In the same way, though by nature unchanging, the jīva (pumān) becomes bewildered, following by the qualities of the mind (rāgānugataḥ) the bodies and senses (guṇeṣu) made by theLord’s māyā, who is herself the authority. He obtains an illusion in the ātmā that one is the body.

The ātmā is devoid of birth and other transformations. But the body possesses birth and other transformations. Thus in order to protect such a body you should not kill a woman, since it will put you in hell. If you fear death because of the message from the sky, then because it is a fact, it should happen because of a son born from Devakī in her next life. If you hope to protect the body for a long time, you should perform sat-karmas like Mārkaṇḍeya.

### Text 44

*tasmān na kasyacid droham ācaret sa tathā-vidhaḥ*  
*ātmanaḥ kṣemam anvicchan drogdhur vai parato bhayam*

**Перевод:**

**Giving up violence and performing pious acts, no one should act with hatred. Desiring one’s own welfare in this and next life, one should not harm anyone, for such a person must always fear harm from his enemies.**

**Комментарий:**

After using the method of sāma, Vasudeva uses bheda again. Since a killer must experience unavoidable fear from Yama and others(parataḥ), therefore this temporary body (tathā-vidhaḥ) should not commit violence against anyone else.

### Text 45

*eṣā tavānujā bālā kṛpaṇā putrikopamā*  
*hantuṁ nārhasi kalyāṇīm imāṁ tvaṁ dīna-vatsalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As your younger sister, this poor girl Devakī is like your own daughter and deserves to be affectionately maintained. You are merciful, and therefore you should not kill her.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing that Kaṁsa had not changed his attitude, he invokes compassion and shame in him by sāma. She is worthy of mercy like your daughter (purtikopamā). Or she is devoid of consciousness out of fear, like a doll. She is without fault (kalyāṇīm). Because you are affectionate to the miserable (dīna-vatsalaḥ) you should not kill her. But Sarasvatī devī indicates that the meaning of dīna-vatsalaḥhowever is “one who takes even a calf from a most poor person as a tax.”

### Text 46

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*evaṁ sa sāmabhir bhedair codyamāno ’pi dāruṇaḥ*  
*na nyavartata kauravya puruṣādān anuvrataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: O best of the Kuru dynasty, Kaṁsa was fiercely cruel and was actually a follower of the Rākṣasas. Therefore he did not give up his attempt by pacification or instilling fear.**

**Комментарий:**

Though urged to change his mind (codyamānaḥ), he did not desist. He kept company with daityas (puruṣa-adān, man-eaters)

### Text 47

*nirbandhaṁ tasya taṁ jñātvā vicintyānakadundubhiḥ*  
*prāptaṁ kālaṁ prativyoḍhum idaṁ tatrānvapadyata*

**Перевод:**

**When Vasudeva saw that Kaṁsa was determined to kill his sister Devakī, considering the matter, he immediately thought of a way to cheat imminent death.**

**Комментарий:**

The name ānaka-dundubhiḥ indicates that “At the time of my birth, drums were sounded by devatās, who were extremely happy,announcing that there could be no inauspiciousness.” To cheat (partivyoḍhum) impending death (kālam) he then thought in thefollowing way.

### Text 48

*mṛtyur buddhimatāpohyo yāvad buddhi-balodayam*  
*yady asau na nivarteta nāparādho ’sti dehinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As long as he has strength of intelligence, an intelligent person must try to avoid death. This is the duty of every embodied person. But if death cannot be avoided in spite of one’s endeavors, a person commits no offense in cheating.**

**Комментарий:**

As long as one has strength of intelligence, death should be avoided (apohyaḥ) by the intelligent person. Still if one cannot prevent death, then he may commit an offense which is arises from cheating.

### Text 49-50

*pradāya mṛtyave putrān mocaye kṛpaṇām imām*  
*sutā me yadi jāyeran mṛtyur vā na mriyeta cet*

*viparyayo vā kiṁ na syād gatir dhātur duratyayā*  
*upasthito nivarteta nivṛttaḥ punar āpatet*

**Перевод:**

**By delivering all my sons to Kaṁsa, who is death personified, I shall save the life of Devakī. Perhaps Kaṁsa will die before my sons take birth, or, since he is already destined to die at the hands of my son, one of my sons may kill him. For the time being, let me promise to hand over my sons so that Kaṁsa will give up this immediate threat, and if in due course of time Kaṁsa dies, I shall have nothing to fear.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva silently speaks in two verses: “This is what I will do. I will give my sons to Kaṁsa (mṛtyave).” But then is not proper. “If a son is not born to me, there is no need to worry. If a son is born, and Kaṁsa (mṛtyuḥ) has not already died by then, then it is notproper. But now Devakī should live. If Kaṁsa dies before a son is born, there is no need to worry.”

Or my son offered to him may kill him. “How could your son, a baby, kill that powerful king?” The course of providence who spoke (“the eighth child will kill you”) cannot be counteracted. That being the case, the Devakī’s imminent death at Kaṁsa’s hand should be prevented. In that way, Kaṁsa’s death though avoided by my promise of offering offspring, will happen again.

### Text 51

*agner yathā dāru-viyoga-yogayor*  
*adṛṣṭato ’nyan na nimittam asti*  
*evaṁ hi jantor api durvibhāvyaḥ*  
*śarīra-saṁyoga-viyoga-hetuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When a fire leaps from one piece of wood to the next, the reason is destiny and nothing else. Similarly, when a living being accepts one kind of body and leaves aside another, there is no other reason.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva deliberates further. “what I have considered is not improbable because the fate of living entities is inconceivable.” To illustrate this Vasudeva gives an example. Sometimes fire does not burn a nearby tree but jumps to a far-off tree and burns it. In this way, forest-fire’s skipping one tree and burning another tree (viyoga-yogayoḥ) has no other cause than those trees’ fate. The trees’ karma of happiness and suffering is the cause. Similarly, the cause of leaving and accepting bodies by living beings is a particular karma which is difficult to understand.

### Text 52

*evaṁ vimṛśya taṁ pāpaṁ yāvad-ātmani-darśanam*  
*pūjayāmāsa vai śaurir bahu-māna-puraḥsaram*

**Перевод:**

**After thus considering the matter as far as his knowledge would allow, Vasudeva praised sinful Kaṁsa with great respect.**

**Комментарий:**

Śauriḥ is Vasudeva. Considering in this way, with whatever degree (yāvat) of knowledge (nidarśaṇam) he had by intelligence (ātmani), he praised (pūjayāmāsa) Kaṁsa (pāpaṁ) externally.

### Text 53

*prasanna-vadanāmbhojo nṛśaṁsaṁ nirapatrapam*  
*manasā dūyamānena vihasann idam abravīt*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva’s mind was full of anxiety because his wife was facing danger, but in order to please the merciless, shameless Kaṁsa, with a joyful face, blossoming like a lotus, he externally smiled and spoke to him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva smiled externally in order to cheat him but he was suffering internally.

### Text 54

*śrī-vasudeva uvāca*  
*na hy asyās te bhayaṁ saumya yad vai sāhāśarīra-vāk*  
*putrān samarpayiṣye ’syā yatas te bhayam utthitam*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva said: O best of the sober, you have nothing to fear from your sister Devakī because of what you have heard from the unseen omen. The cause of death will be her sons. Therefore I promise that when she gives birth to the sons from whom your fear has arisen, I shall deliver them all unto your hands.**

**Комментарий:**

O gentle one (saumya)! You have no fear from Devakī (asyāḥ) but from the eighth son. That was according to (yat) the unembodied message from the sky (aśarīra-vak). Thus I will offer you eight sons. From whichever son your fear arises, let him be killed by you. Or kill all the eight since by considering sequentially all are eighth. Thus he shows extreme trust in Kaṁsa.

### Text 55

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*svasur vadhān nivavṛte kaṁsas tad-vākya-sāra-vit*  
*vasudevo ’pi taṁ prītaḥ praśasya prāviśad gṛham*

**Перевод:**

**Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Kaṁsa agreed to the logical arguments of Vasudeva, and, having full faith in Vasudeva’s words, he refrained from killing his sister. Vasudeva, being pleased with Kaṁsa, pacified him further and entered his own house.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa understood the logic in Vasudeva’s words (tad-vākya-sāra- vit). Vasudeva praised Kaṁsa, “You are fixed in dharma.”

### Text 56

*atha kāla upāvṛtte devakī sarva-devatā*  
*putrān prasuṣuve cāṣṭau kanyāṁ caivānuvatsaram*

**Перевод:**

**Each year thereafter, in due course of time, Devakī, the mother of God and all the demigods, gave birth to a child. Thus she bore eight sons, one after another, and a daughter named Subhadrā.**

**Комментарий:**

When the time of the birth of the children arrived, Devakī worshippable (devatā) by Brahmā and others (sarva) since she was the mother of the Lord, gave birth to eight children in eight years (anuvatsaram) and a daughter Subhadrā.

### Text 57

*kīrtimantaṁ prathamajaṁ kaṁsāyānakadundubhiḥ*  
*arpayāmāsa kṛcchreṇa so ’nṛtād ativihvalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva was very much disturbed by fear of becoming a liar by breaking his promise. Thus with great pain he delivered his first-born son, named Kīrtimān, into the hands of Kaṁsa.**

**Комментарий:**

With great difficulty (kṛcchreṇa) he gave the son, fearing breaking his promise (anṛtāt).

### Text 58

*kiṁ duḥsahaṁ nu sādhūnāṁ viduṣāṁ kim apekṣitam*  
*kim akāryaṁ kadaryāṇāṁ dustyajaṁ kiṁ dhṛtātmanām*

**Перевод:**

**What is intolerable for saintly persons? What is desired by the learned? What is not to be done by the wicked? What is hard to renounce for the determined?**

**Комментарий:**

“Granted that Vasudeva feared not keeping his promise, but how could he bear his son’s murder in front of him?” What can personswho are truthful (sādhūnām) not bear? “But how is it a promise to deliver the sons even without Kaṁsa’s ordering it?” For those whoknow the supreme tattva (viduṣām) what is the use of sons?

“But Kaṁsa should not kill the child who has been brought by the truthful Vasudeva, since he will be compassionate.” What will notbe done by the most sinful (kadaryāṇām)?

“Why did Devakī give up her sons?” What is difficult to give up by those who have the Lord in their hearts? With the hope that the Lord, appearing in her womb, would kill Kaṁsa along with his followers and shower bliss, she tolerated all the suffering of offering the previous sons.

### Text 59

*dṛṣṭvā samatvaṁ tac chaureḥ satye caiva vyavasthitim*  
*kaṁsas tuṣṭa-manā rājan prahasann idam abravīt*

**Перевод:**

**When Kaṁsa saw that Vasudeva, being situated in truthfulness, was completely equipoised in giving him the child, he was very happy. O King! Therefore, with a smiling face, he spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva was in all conditions calm (samatvam) because he had no attachment to his sons.

### Text 60

*pratiyātu kumāro ’yaṁ na hy asmād asti me bhayam*  
*aṣṭamād yuvayor garbhān mṛtyur me vihitaḥ kila*

**Перевод:**

**O Vasudeva, you may take back your child and go home. I have no fear of your first child. It is the eighth child of you and Devakī I am concerned with because that is the child by whom I am destined to be killed.**

### Text 61

*tatheti sutam ādāya yayāv ānakadundubhiḥ*  
*nābhyanandata tad-vākyam asato ’vijitātmanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva agreed and took his child back home, but because Kaṁsa had no character and no self-control, Vasudeva knew that he could not rely on Kaṁsa’s word.**

### Text 62-63

*nandādyā ye vraje gopā yāś cāmīṣāṁ ca yoṣitaḥ*  
*vṛṣṇayo vasudevādyā devaky-ādyā yadu-striyaḥ*

*sarve vai devatā-prāyā ubhayor api bhārata*  
*jñātayo bandhu-suhṛdo ye ca kaṁsam anuvratāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana, headed by Nanda Mahārāja and including his associate cowherd men and their wives, are none but associates of the Lord, O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, and so too are the descendants of the Vṛṣṇi dynasty headed by Vasudeva, and Devakī and the other women of the dynasty of Yadu. The friends, relatives and well-wishers of both Nanda Mahārāja and Vasudeva and even those who externally appeared to be followers of Kaṁsa are all associates of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

These verses were spoken by Nārada to Kaṁsa after approaching him (verse 64). Two verses go together. The people of Vraja and their wives such as Yaśodā (amīṣām yoṣitaḥ) and the Vṛṣṇis such as Vasudeva (all the Yadus) and even their servants (ca) were devatās. The second ca is used in the sense of api (also). The members of both families, of Nanda and Vasudeva, were devatās. This was generally true (prāya) since some among the Yadus were demons. They behaved as Kaṁsa’s devotees (anuvratāḥ). Jñātayaḥ means sapiṇḍa  relations. Bandhava are relatives by marriage. Suhṛdaḥ are friends.‘

### Text 64

*etat kaṁsāya bhagavāñ chaśaṁsābhyetya nāradaḥ*  
*bhūmer bhārāyamāṇānāṁ daityānāṁ ca vadhodyamam*

**Перевод:**

**Once the great saint Nārada approached Kaṁsa and informed him of how the demoniac persons who were a great burden on the earth were going to be killed.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhagavān means knowing everything. Nārada thought as follows. By pacification of Kaṁsa, the appearance of the Lord will be delayed. By that the devatās, the devotees and parents, as well as earth will not be happy. Nārada revealed the information, showing false friendship so as to cause the killing of Kaṁsa because of his afflicting the devotees. Nārada repeated what he heard directly in the assembly of devatās on the top of Meru--that the devatās wereendeavoring to kill the demons.

### Text 65-66

*ṛṣer vinirgame kaṁso yadūn matvā surān iti*  
*devakyā garbha-sambhūtaṁ viṣṇuṁ ca sva-vadhaṁ prati*

*devakīṁ vasudevaṁ ca nigṛhya nigaḍair gṛhe*  
*jātaṁ jātam ahan putraṁ tayor ajana-śaṅkayā*

**Перевод:**

**After the departure of the great saint Nārada, Kaṁsa thought that all the members of the Yadu dynasty were devatās and that any of the children born from the womb of Devakī might be Viṣṇu. Fearing his death, Kaṁsa arrested Vasudeva and Devakī and chained them with iron shackles. Out of fear of Viṣṇu, Kaṁsa killed their new-born children one after another.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. When Nārada departed, thinking of Nanda and Vasudeva, etc., (yadūn) were devatās, he thought that Viṣṇu, aiming to kill him would appear in Devakī’s womb. He learnt from Nārada that his previous enemy, Viṣṇu, appearing in Devakī, will kill him. Ajana is Viṣṇu. Due to fear of Viṣṇu (ajana-śaṅkayā) Kaṁsa killed all the new-born children of Devakī and Vasudeva.

### Text 67

*mātaraṁ pitaraṁ bhrātṝn sarvāṁś ca suhṛdas tathā*  
*ghnanti hy asutṛpo lubdhā rājānaḥ prāyaśo bhuvi*

**Перевод:**

**Kings, greedy for kingdoms on this earth to satisfy their own life airs, almost always kill even their mothers, fathers, brothers or friends.**

**Комментарий:**

What Kaṁsa did was not surprising since he was wicked. The seriousness of the killing is from first to last.

### Text 68

*ātmānam iha sañjātaṁ jānan prāg viṣṇunā hatam*  
*mahāsuraṁ kālanemiṁ yadubhiḥ sa vyarudhyata*

**Перевод:**

**In his previous birth, Kaṁsa had been a great demon named Kālanemi and been killed by Viṣṇu. Upon learning this information from Nārada, Kaṁsa became envious of everyone connected with the Yadu dynasty.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa learned from Nārada that in his previous birth as Kālanemi he had been killed by Viṣṇu.

### Text 69

*ugrasenaṁ ca pitaraṁ yadu-bhojāndhakādhipam*  
*svayaṁ nigṛhya bubhuje śūrasenān mahā-balaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kaṁsa, the most powerful son of Ugrasena, even imprisoned his own father, the King of the Yadu, Bhoja and Andhaka dynasties, and personally ruled the states known as Śūrasena.**

**Комментарий:**

Śūrasena indicates Mathurā, which is within Śūrasena.

## Chapter 2 - Prayers by the Demigods

### Texts 1-2

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*pralamba-baka-cāṇūra-tṛṇāvarta-mahāśanaiḥ*  
*muṣṭikāriṣṭa-dvivida-pūtanā-keśī-dhenukaiḥ*

*anyaiś cāsura-bhūpālair bāṇa-bhaumādibhir*  
*yutaḥ yadūnāṁ kadanaṁ cakre balī māgadha-saṁśrayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: With the assistance of Magadharāja, Jarāsandha, the powerful Kaṁsa began persecuting the kings of the Yadu dynasty. In this he had the cooperation of demons like Pralamba, Baka, Cāṇūra, Tṛṇāvarta, Aghāsura, Muṣṭika, Ariṣṭa, Dvivida, Pūtanā, Keśī, Dhenuka, Bāṇāsura, Narakāsura and many other demoniac kings on the surface of the earth.**

**Комментарий:**

*prāpayya garbhaṁ devakyā rohiṇyāṁ yogayā prabhuḥ \|*  
*tasyāḥ kukṣiṁ gataḥ kṛṣṇo dvitīye stūyate suraiḥ*

**In the second chapter, having caused Devakī’s child to be transferred to Rohiṇī by yogamāyā, Kṛṣṇa appears in Devakī’s womb and is praised by the devatās.**

Kaṁsa’s persecution of the Yadus, which was mentioned in the first chapter (SB [10.1.68](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.68)), is now described in two verses. Mahāśanaiḥ means Aghāsura. Ariṣṭa was a dānava who took the form of a bull. Kaṁsa took the assistance of Jarāsandha (māgadha-saṁśarayaḥ).

### Text 3

*te pīḍitā niviviśuḥ kuru-pañcāla-kekayān*  
*śālvān vidarbhān niṣadhān videhān kośalān api*

**Перевод:**

**Persecuted by the demoniac kings, the Yādavas left their own kingdom and entered various others, like those of the Kurus, Pañcālas, Kekayas, Śālvas, Vidarbhas, Niṣadhas, Videhas and Kośalas.**

**Комментарий:**

The Yadus entered the kingdom of the Kurus etc.

### Texts 4-5

*eke tam anurundhānā jñātayaḥ paryupāsate*  
*hateṣu ṣaṭsu bāleṣu devakyā augraseninā*

*saptamo vaiṣṇavaṁ dhāma yam anantaṁ pracakṣate*  
*garbho babhūva devakyā harṣa-śoka-vivardhanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Some of their relatives, however, began to follow Kaṁsa’s principles and act in his service. After Kaṁsa, the son of Ugrasena, killed the six sons of Devakī, the seventh child, known as Saṅkarṣaṇa, filled with Kṛṣṇa, arousing her pleasure and her lamentation, entered her womb.**

**Комментарий:**

Some of the Yadus (eke) such as Akrūra became cooperative with Kaṁsa and carried out his orders out of desire see Kṛṣṇa when he appeared. The seventh child of Devakī appeared in her womb. He is called Ananta. He is an aṁśa of Kṛṣṇa, who pervades (vaiṣṇavam dhāma). He was a cause of joy since the highest bliss had appeared in her womb. He was a cause of lamentation because of thinking that Kaṁsa would kill him. Both joy and sorrow increased.

### Text 6

*bhagavān api viśvātmā viditvā kaṁsajaṁ bhayam*  
*yadūnāṁ nija-nāthānāṁ yogamāyāṁ samādiśat*

**Перевод:**

**Knowing that the Yadus, his personal devotees, were afraid of Kaṁsa, Svayam Bhagavān, the source of all other forms of God, ordered Yogamāyā as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse shows that the Lord’s appearance was hastened as a result of Naradā’s information to Kaṁsa. Understanding the fear of the Yadus, the Lord ordered Yogamāyā, the fifth of his nine superior expansions starting with Vimalā. \[The nine śaktis, potencies, of the Lord are vimalā, utkarṣiṇī, jñānā, kriyā, yogamāyā, prahvī, satyā, īśānā and anugrahā.\]

### Text 7

*gaccha devi vrajaṁ bhadre gopa-gobhir alaṅkṛtam*  
*rohiṇī vasudevasya bhāryāste nanda-gokule*  
*anyāś ca kaṁsa-saṁvignā vivareṣu vasanti hi*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord ordered Yogamāyā: O my potency, who are worshippable for the entire world and whose nature is to bestow good fortune upon all living entities, go to Vraja, naturally wealthy with many cowherds and cows. In that very beautiful land, where many cows reside, Rohiṇī, the wife of Vasudeva, is living at the home of Nanda Mahārāja. Other wives of Vasudeva are also living there incognito because of fear of Kaṁsa.**

**Комментарий:**

Vraja was decorated with a natural wealth of cowherds and cows. After Devakī’s six children were killed, Vasudeva, seeing Rohiṇī pregnant, sent her secretly to Nanda Gokula through a trusted person. Not only she, but even the other wives of Vasudeva (anyāḥ),being sent by him, lived in places (vivareṣu) wherever they could go.

### Text 8

*devakyā jaṭhare garbhaṁ śeṣākhyaṁ dhāma māmakam*  
*tat sannikṛṣya rohiṇyā udare sanniveśaya*

**Перевод:**

**Within the womb of Devakī is my aṁśa known as Saṅkarṣaṇa or Śeṣa. Drawing him out, transfer him into the womb of Rohiṇī.**

**Комментарий:**

There is an embryo in Devakī’s womb, called Śeṣa who is his aṁśa. He is my svarūpa and shelter (dhāma) since he is a form of theādhāra-śakti. Pull him completely (nikṛṣya) unseen with joy (sam) from the womb. Though Rohiṇī is his eternal mother, he first entered Devakī’s womb in order to establish his aṁśa Śeṣa there to act as my residence, bed, etc. It is well known that pregnant Rohiṇī went to Gokula, leaving Vasudeva.

### Text 9

*athāham aṁśa-bhāgena devakyāḥ putratāṁ śubhe*  
*prāpsyāmi tvaṁ yaśodāyāṁ nanda-patnyāṁ bhaviṣyasi*

**Перевод:**

**O all-auspicious Yogamāyā, I shall then appear in different forms as the sons of Devakī and Yaśodā and you will reside in Yaśodā, the wife of Mahārāja Nanda.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why should this be done?” This verse explains. Atha means after that. This indicates that Balarāma was Kṛṣṇa’s elder brother by a short period of time. I will become the son of Vasudeva’s wife, and by the meaning about to be stated, son of Nanda’s wife (devakyāḥ), completely, as the object of service (bhāga) for the aṁśas or as the one who serves his devotees (bhāga) through knowledge, strength, etc. (aṁśa), or by the good fortune (bhāga) of Brahmā and others (aṁśa). Or I will appear as Devakī’s son, as a portion of a portion (aṁśa-bhāgena). For Devakī the sentiment of my being her son is secondary, since she has a prominence of appreciating my great power. But for Yaśodā the sentiment of son will be chief since she has a predominance of sweetness for me. You will appear in Yaśodā but she will not know you. You will stay in Vraja in an unseen form.

### Text 10

*arciṣyanti manuṣyās tvāṁ sarva-kāma-vareśvarīṁ*  
*dhūpopahāra-balibhiḥ sarva-kāma-vara-pradām*

**Перевод:**

**By sacrifices of animals, ordinary human beings will worship you gorgeously, with various paraphernalia, because you are supreme in fulfilling the material desires of everyone.**

**Комментарий:**

Men will worship Māyā, your shadow form, who cheated Kaṁsa, and who is not desired by Vasudeva, and who stays in places like Vidhya mountains, etc. This is explained in three verses. They worship you because you the supreme goddess, the bestower of benedictions to people who desire all material things.

### Texts 11-12

*nāmadheyāni kurvanti sthānāni ca narā bhuvi*  
*durgeti bhadrakālīti vijayā vaiṣṇavīti ca*

*kumudā caṇḍikā kṛṣṇā mādhavī kanyaketi ca*  
*māyā nārāyaṇīśānī śāradety ambiketi ca*

**Перевод:**

**Lord Kṛṣṇa blessed Māyādevī by saying: In different places on the surface of the earth, people will give you different names, such as Durgā, Bhadrakālī, Vijayā, Vaiṣṇavī, Kumudā, Caṇḍikā, Kṛṣṇā, Mādhavī, Kanyakā, Māyā, Nārāyaṇī, Īśānī, Śāradā and Ambikā.**

**Комментарий:**

They will give you many names. Mādhavī means the sister of Mādhava.

### Text 13

*garbha-saṅkarṣaṇāt taṁ vai prāhuḥ saṅkarṣaṇaṁ bhuvi*  
*rāmeti loka-ramaṇād balabhadraṁ balocchrayāt*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Rohiṇī will also be celebrated as Saṅkarṣaṇa because of being sent from the womb of Devakī to the womb of Rohiṇī. He will be called Rāma because of his ability to please all the inhabitants of Gokula, and he will be known as Balabhadra because of his extensive physical strength.**

**Комментарий:**

Rāmeti is a compound formed by saha supā (Pāṇini 2.1.4).

### Text 14

*sandiṣṭaivaṁ bhagavatā tathety om iti tad-vacaḥ*  
*pratigṛhya parikramya gāṁ gatā tat tathākarot*

**Перевод:**

**Thus instructed by the Lord with the Vedic mantra oṁ, she confirmed that she would do what he asked. Thus having accepted his orders, she circumambulated him and went to earth. There she did everything just as she had been told.**

**Комментарий:**

Saying tathā and then oṁ, which is repetitive, is a sign of great respect for the Lord. Having accepted Kṛṣṇa’s words, Yogamāyā circumambulated the Lord and then went to the earth (gām). After that (tat) she did as she was told.

### Text 15

*garbhe praṇīte devakyā rohiṇīṁ yoga-nidrayā*  
*aho visraṁsito garbha iti paurā vicukruśuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the child of Devakī was attracted and transferred into the womb of Rohiṇī by Yogamāyā, Devakī seemed to have a miscarriage. Thus all the citizens lamented, “Alas, Devakī has lost her child!”**

**Комментарий:**

The citizens suspected that Kaṁsa must have done some black magic to cause the “apparent” miscarriage. Thus those people who had affection for Devakī, lamented (vicukruśuḥ) but they did not know the truth.

### Text 16

*bhagavān api viśvātmā bhaktānām abhayaṅkaraḥ*  
*āviveśāṁśa-bhāgena mana ānakadundubheḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus the Supreme Lord, who is the Supersoul of all living entities and who vanquishes all the fear of his devotees, entered the mind of Vasudeva in full splendor.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhagavān entered the mind of Vasudeva along with all his qualities (bhāga) like aiśvarya and with all his aṁśas like the lord ofVaikuṇṭha (aṁśa), who were attracted to his pastimes. For it is said:

*parāvareśo mahad-aṁśa-yukto*  
*hy ajo ’pi jāto bhagavān yathāgnih*

**Although the Lord is unlimited and unborn, he took birth along with his aṁśas. (SB** [**3.2.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.15)**)**

In this way he entered Vasudeva’s mind.

### Text 17

*sa bibhrat pauruṣaṁ dhāma bhrājamāno yathā raviḥ*  
*durāsado ’tidurdharṣo bhūtānāṁ sambabhūva ha*

**Перевод:**

**He manifested the effulgence of the Lord and became as bright as the sun. He became clearly difficult to see or approach through sensory perception and impossible to defeat by any being.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva carried the form (dhāma) of Kṛṣṇa (pauruṣam). Dhāma means body according to Viśva. He could not be approached by the king’s guards (durāsadaḥ). He could not be defeated even by Kaṁsa (durdharṣaḥ).

### Text 18

*tato jagan-maṅgalam acyutāṁśaṁ*  
*samāhitaṁ śūra-sutena devī*  
*dadhāra sarvātmakam ātma-bhūtaṁ*  
*kāṣṭhā yathānanda-karaṁ manastaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, accompanied by his expansions, the root form, who is all-auspicious for the entire universe and gives joy to all jīvas, was transferred from the mind of Vasudeva to the mind of Devakī. Devakī, became beautiful by carrying Kṛṣṇa, joy to all beings, who appeared on his own, just as the east becomes beautiful by carrying the rising moon.**

**Комментарий:**

Then he entered Devakī’s body. From the mind of Vasudeva (tataḥ), Devakī (devī) held in her mind (manastaḥ) that form of the Lord. The Lord is described. He was auspiciousness personified for the world. He was complete with all aṁśas, not devoid of even one aṁśa (acyutāṁśaṁ). He was offered (samāhitam) by Vasudeva (śūra-sutena) through Vedic dīkṣa of the Kāṇva tradition. In this way it is expressed that Kṛṣṇa was his legitimate son. The Lord who produces happiness (kam) in the minds (ātmā) of all devotees andŚiva (sarva), appeared by himself (ātmā-bhūtam).

He was not brought into the mind by meditation with effort like a yogī does. An example is given. She was like the eastern direction carrying the moon (ānanda-karam). Later he was held in her womb, because later in this chapter it is said, diṣṭyāmba te kuksi-gataḥ paraḥ pumān, “Oh fortunate lady, the Supreme Lord has entered your womb.” (SB [10.2.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.41))

The meaning is this. By being related to the bodies of Vasudeva and Devakī the Lord is not subjected to suffering as jīva is due to having a bodily relationship with its mother and father. In the Fourth Canto it is said:

*sattvaṁ viśuddhaṁ vasudeva-śabditam*

**Viśuddha-sattva is called vasudeva. (SB** [**4.3.23**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/3.23)**)**

And Devakī is described by a devotee as follows:

*tvaṁ parā prakṛtiḥ sūkṣma*

**You are supreme prakrti, beyond matter. (Devakī-stotra)**

According to these statements, the two were beyond matter. Standing in a fragrant jeweled palace, a king is not perceived to be in a suffering condition.

### Text 19

*sā devakī sarva-jagan-nivāsa-*  
*nivāsa-bhūtā nitarāṁ na reje*  
*bhojendra-gehe ’gni-śikheva ruddhā*  
*sarasvatī jñāna-khale yathā satī*

**Перевод:**

**Devakī then kept within herself the cause of all causes, the foundation of the entire cosmos, but because she was under arrest in the house of Kaṁsa, she was like the flames of a fire covered by the walls of a pot, or like a person who has knowledge but cannot distribute it to the world for the benefit of human society.**

**Комментарий:**

Devakī, a pure soul (sā), though the dwelling place of Kṛṣṇa, who is the abode for the whole universe, though experiencing extreme bliss by realizing the Lord, did not shine as the cause of bliss of all people (nitarām). Rather she shone as the cause of bliss of herself along with two or three intimate associates present by her side, because she was confined in Kaṁsa’s house. A lamp’s flame covered by a pot does not light up the room. Knowledge restricted in a person who cheats using knowledge (jñāna-khale) does not givebenefit to others. Just as a flame, becoming strong can burn down the house that restricts it, knowledge can destroy its obstruction due to his excessive sin. Thus she could destroy Kaṁsa, her obstructor, due to his offenses to her.

### Text 20

*tāṁ vīkṣya kaṁsaḥ prabhayājitāntarāṁ*  
*virocayantīṁ bhuvanaṁ śuci-smitām*  
*āhaiṣa me prāṇa-haro harir guhāṁ*  
*dhruvaṁ śrito yan na pureyam īdṛśī*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing her jubilant, pure and smiling, because of the Lord in her womb, Kaṁsa thought, “The Lord who will kill me is now within her for she has never before looked like this.”**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Devakī, illuminating the world (bhuvanam) by her effulgence (prabhayā), with Kṛṣṇa in her womb (ajitāntarāṁ), Kaṁsa thought to himself, “The lion (hariḥ) for me--the mad elephant--is certainly in her womb (guhāṁ) because she was not like this before.”

### Text 21

*kim adya tasmin karaṇīyam āśu me*  
*yad artha-tantro na vihanti vikramam*  
*striyāḥ svasur gurumatyā vadho ’yaṁ*  
*yaśaḥ śriyaṁ hanty anukṣaṇaṁ āyuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kaṁsa thought: What should I do? One should think of one’s benefit. Devakī is a woman, she is my sister, and moreover she is now pregnant. If I kill her, my reputation, opulence and duration of life will certainly be vanquished.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks more clearly. What should I do now to Viṣṇu, my enemy previously (tasmin)?

He who is a fetus should not be killed because even those interested in their own welfare (artha tantra) do not destroy their own goodname. If I kill him in the womb, my reputation of prowess will be destroyed.
