Such a deed will not only destroy my fame, but dharmawill also get destroyed: she is my sister and is pregnant (gurumatyā). My reputation will be destroyed immediately (anukṣaṇaṁ).

### Text 22

*sa eṣa jīvan khalu sampareto*  
*varteta yo ’tyanta-nṛśaṁsitena*  
*dehe mṛte taṁ manujāḥ śapanti*  
*gantā tamo ’ndhaṁ tanu-mānino dhruvam*

**Перевод:**

**A person who is very cruel is regarded as dead even while living, for while the sinful person is living and after his death, everyone condemns him and he is undoubtedly transferred to the hell known as Andhatama.**

**Комментарий:**

By killing the embryo my life will be criticized. While his body is living because of his cruelty of killing the child, people will criticize him in their minds out of fear, but after the body is dead, they will loudly shout, “The great sinner should fall to hell.” The person who cares for his own body by killing other living entities will suitably go to the darkest hell. Thus I should not kill the child in the womb. I should kill him when he is born and is a youth. This will maintain my heroic status. He thought with discernment, in this way, suppressing his cruelty because of fear.

### Text 23

*iti ghoratamād bhāvāt sannivṛttaḥ svayaṁ prabhuḥ*  
*āste pratīkṣaṁs taj-janma harer vairānubandha-kṛt*

**Перевод:**

**Deliberating in this way, Kaṁsa, although determined to continue in enmity toward the Lord, refrained from the vicious killing of his sister and decided to wait until the Lord was born.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking he knew what to do (svayam prabhuḥ), he waited till the Lord was born.

### Text 24

*āsīnaḥ saṁviśaṁs tiṣṭhan bhuñjānaḥ paryaṭan mahīm*  
*cintayāno hṛṣīkeśam apaśyat tanmayaṁ jagat*

**Перевод:**

**While sitting on his throne or in his sitting room, while lying on his bed, or while situated anywhere, and while eating or walking, Kaṁsa saw only the Supreme Lord. His world became filled with the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa’s absorption in the Lord caused by his strong hatred is described. While lying on his bed (saṁviśan), he thought of the Lord (hṛṣīkeśam) who had become the object of all his senses. He saw him as the chief object in the world (tan-mayam jagat). Seeing the Lord everywhere because of prema produces bliss and seeing him everywhere because of fear, produces suffering.

### Text 25

*brahmā bhavaś ca tatretya munibhir nāradādibhiḥ*  
*devaiḥ sānucaraiḥ sākaṁ gīrbhir vṛṣaṇam aiḍayan*

**Перевод:**

**Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva, accompanied by great sages like Nārada, Devala and Vyāsa and by other demigods like Indra, Candra and Varuṇa, invisibly approached the room of Devakī, where they all joined in offering their respectful obeisances and prayers to please the Supreme Lord, who can bestow blessings upon everyone.**

**Комментарий:**

They praised (aiḍayan) the Lord, the black cloud who showers sweetness of pastimes (vṛṣaṇam). Brahmā acts as the chief cultivator in the field of the fourteen worlds. Śiva is like the chief peacock with his tail-feathers spread, fondly dancing before the rains. Nārada and others (singers) are like cātaka birds, who maintain their lives on the Lord alone. The devatās are like suffering elephants surrounded by the forest fire of Kaṁsa and other demons.

### Text 26

*satya-vrataṁ satya-paraṁ tri-satyaṁ*  
*satyasya yoniṁ nihitaṁ ca satye*  
*satyasya satyam ṛta-satya-netraṁ*  
*satyātmakaṁ tvāṁ śaraṇaṁ prapannāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The devatās prayed: O Lord, you are true to your promise, truth incarnate, pervading all aspects of time with truth, before the creation, during its existence and after its destruction. You are the revealer of sweet words and truth. We surrender to you, the embodiment of truth.**

**Комментарий:**

You are suitable for surrender because you vow to protect your devotee and are immovable in that.

O Lord! We surrender to you. The Lord is described. Your vow to protect your devotee (vrataṁ) is unbroken (satya) since you have said:

*kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati*

**O Arjuna! I promise that my devotee will not perish. (BG** [**9.31**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.31)**)**

You are superior (param) to jīva, pradhāna and time (satya). You have three states (satya) of jñāna, bala and kriyā (tri-satyam) sinceśruti says svābhāvikī jñāna-bala-kriyā ca: the Lord has natural śaktis of jñāna, bala and kriyā. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad [6.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sveta-bs/6.8)) You are the cause (yoniṁ) of the universe (satyasya) since the śruti says:

*yāthārthyato’rthān vyadadhāt*

**The Lord has established all real objects eternally. (Īśopaniṣad** [**8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/iso/8)**)**

And since the smṛti says:

*brahma satyaṁ tapaḥ satyaṁ satyaṁ caiva prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*satyād bhūtāni jātāni satyaṁ bhūta-mayaṁ jagad*

**Brahman is real, austerity is real, Prajāpati is real. All creatures arise from the real. The universe made of elements is real. (Mahābhārata)**

You are situated (nihitam) in the spiritual sky (satye), and in Goloka above that. You are the real among all the real jīvas (satyasya satyam) since the śruti says, prāṇā vai satyaṁ teṣām eva satyam: the prāṇas are real. The Lord is the real among all reals. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad [2.1.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bau/2.1.20)) The meaning is that jīvas have a semblance of transformation in the form of expansion and contraction of jñāna, whereas the Lord being devoid of that is the supreme real. You establish (netraṁ) pleasing speech (ṛta) and equal vision (satya) in those who have taken shelter of you. You have a real form (ātmā), i.e. you have an eternal form (satyātmakam).

### Text 27

*ekāyano ’sau dvi-phalas tri-mūlaś*  
*catū-rāsaḥ pañca-vidhaḥ ṣaḍ-ātmā*  
*sapta-tvag aṣṭa-viṭapo navākṣo*  
*daśa-cchadī dvi-khago hy ādi-vṛkṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The material world may figuratively be called “the original tree.” From this tree, which fully depends on the ground of material nature, come two kinds of fruit—the enjoyment of happiness and the suffering of distress. The cause of the tree, forming its three roots, is association with the three modes of material nature— goodness, passion and ignorance. The fruits of bodily happiness have four tastes—religiosity, economic development, sense gratification and liberation—which are experienced through five senses for acquiring knowledge in the midst of six circumstances: lamentation, illusion, old age, death, hunger and thirst. The seven layers of bark covering the tree are skin, blood, muscle, fat, bone, marrow and semen, and the eight branches of the tree are the five gross and three subtle elements—earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intelligence and false ego. The tree of the body has nine hollows—the two eyes, the two ears, the two nostrils, the mouth, the rectum and the genitals—and ten leaves, the ten airs passing through the body. In this tree of the body there are two birds: one is the individual soul, and the other is the Supersoul.**

**Комментарий:**

“If it is true that I am endowed with a form, qualities and abode which are material, then the material world is not different from me.”

The material world is different since it can be divided by time. The material world (asau), composed of samaṣṭi and vyaṣṭi, is ādibecause of being actuated from the beginning. It is vṛkṣa meaning that which is cut by time. It takes shelter of one prakṛti. It has two fruits: happiness and suffering. It has three roots: sattva, rajas, and tamas. It has four saps: dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa. It has five senses like ear, etc., as the means of knowing. It has six urges: lamentation, illusion, old age, death, hunger and thirst as its natures (ātmā). It has seven dhātus: skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow and semen as bark. It has eight branches (viṭapa): earth, water, fire, air, ether—the five gross elements, mind, intelligence and ahaṅkāra. It has the nine doors as hollows. It has the ten prāṇas as leaves. On it are two birds: the Lord and the jīva. You are the person whom such a tree takes shelter of.

Though both are real, there is a difference due to the Lord being permanent and the material world being impermanent. Therefore, the Lord should be sought since he is eternal.

### Text 28

*tvam eka evāsya sataḥ prasūtis*  
*tvaṁ sannidhānaṁ tvam anugrahaś ca*  
*tvan-māyayā saṁvṛta-cetasas tvāṁ*  
*paśyanti nānā na vipaścito ye*

**Перевод:**

**You are the one cause of this material existence. You are also its destruction and maintenance. The wise, uncovered by māyā, do not see varieties but only you.**

**Комментарий:**

*brahmā devānāṁ prathamaḥ saṁbabhūva,*  
*viśvasya kartā bhuvanasya goptāḥ*

**Brahmā, creator of the universe and protector of the world, manifested before the devatās. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)**

*eko rudro na dvitīyo’vatasthe*

**Only Śiva existed and no one else. (Śiva Purāṇa)**

“It is said that Brahmā and Śiva are the creators of the universe.Why do you say that I am the creator?”You are the one excellent cause (prasūtiḥ) of the real universe (sataḥ). You are the independent creator. You are the receptacle of destruction (sannidhānam) and the maintainer (anugraha) of the universe. Those whose minds are covered by your māyā see you variously as the forms of Brahmā, etc. Those who know the conclusions of scripture (vipaścitaḥ) see that you are those variousforms. You become Brahmā and Śiva for it is concluded that:

*sattvaṁ rajas tama iti prakṛter guṇās*  
*tair yuktaḥ parama-puruṣa eka ihāsya dhatte*  
*\| sthity-ādaye hari-viriñci-hareti saṁjñāḥ*  
*śreyāṁsi tatra khalu sattva-tanor nṝṇāṁ syuḥ*

**The one supreme puruṣa, accepting the guṇas of prakṛti known as sattva, rajas and tamas, for creation, maintenance and destruction, is called Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva. The best results for the devotees will come from Viṣṇu with śuddha- sattva body. (SB** [**1.2.23**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.23)**)**

The Vedas say:

*yaṁ kāmaye tam ugraṁ kṛṇomi taṁ brāhmaṇa*

**I (Lakṣmī) make whomever I desire into Śiva; I make whomever I desire into Brahmā. (Ṛg Veda 10.125.05.2)**

By determining the meaning of this śruti statement there is no doubt that the you only are situated within Śiva and Brahmā and no one else.

### Text 29

*bibharṣi rūpāṇy avabodha ātmā*  
*kṣemāya lokasya carācarasya*  
*sattvopapannāni sukhāvahāni*  
*satām abhadrāṇi muhuḥ khalānām*

**Перевод:**

**O son of Devakī, source of all other forms! You constantly manifest other forms through śuddha-sattva for the benefit of all beings, for protecting the followers of dharma and punishing the deviants.**

**Комментарий:**

You have protected the world even at other times through various avatāras. You, the all-pervading Lord (ātmā), the single essence of consciousness (avabodhaḥ), manifest (bibharṣi) various forms like Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, etc., in order to protect (kṣemāya) theworld. The forms are endowed with great strength (sattva) and give happiness to the devotees (satām) and give suffering (abhadrāni) to the wicked. Do the same now also!

### Text 30

*tvayy ambujākṣākhila-sattva-dhāmni*  
*samādhināveśita-cetasaike*  
*tvat-pāda-potena mahat-kṛtena*  
*kurvanti govatsa-padaṁ bhavābdhim*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Lord! By concentrating on your pure form of śuddha- sattva in meditation some people cross the ocean of nescience as easily as one steps over the hoof print of a calf, by those lotus feet which act as a boat, obtained by the grace of devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse elaborates on how the Lord gives happiness to the devotees.

The devotees turn the ocean of material existence into the water in a calf’s hoof-print by the boat of your lotus feet, which is obtained because of their consciousness being absorbed by meditation on the attractive pastimes of you, the shelter (dhāmni) of all beingsincluding devatās and humans. They do not know material existence. The Lord’s lotus feet are made into boat by the great souls (mahat-kṛtena).

### Text 31

*svayaṁ samuttīrya sudustaraṁ dyuman*  
*bhavārṇavaṁ bhīmam adabhra-sauhṛdāḥ*  
*bhavat-padāmbhoruha-nāvam atra te*  
*nidhāya yātāḥ sad-anugraho bhavān*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, shining brilliantly! The merciful devotees, easily crossing the insurmountable and terrifying ocean of material life, attain their goal using the boat of your lotus feet. You are merciful to your devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

“If the devotees cross using the boat of his feet, how can the boat be obtained by others?”

O form of concentrated consciousness (dyuman)! Crossing the frightful ocean of material existence, which is difficult to cross, byany other means, while depositing here the boat of your lotus feet in the form of the sampradāya, they went to the other shore, your supreme abode, because they are merciful to all beings (adabhra- sauhrdāḥ).

“How does the boat move without a captain?” You are merciful to the devotees (sad-anugrahaḥ). The sampradāya operates by thesedevotees.

### Text 32

*ye ’nye ’ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas*  
*tvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ*  
*āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ*  
*patanty adho ’nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Lord, although non-devotees who accept severe austerities and penances to achieve the highest position may think themselves liberated, their intelligence is impure. They fall down from their position of imagined superiority because they have no regard for your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Others who are not of this type, though learned, continue in the material world. O lotus-eyed Lord! Others who do not get your mercy, who knowing their ātmā, having eight qualities as stated by Prajapati in ya ātmā’pahata-pāpmā (Chāndogya Upaniṣad [8.7.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/chan-upa/part-8.chapter-7.871)), as the giver of all results due to the śruti statement such as vijñānam brahma cet veda: if one knows the jīva as Brahman (Taittirīya Upaniṣad [2.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/taittiriya/2.5)), realizing (āruhya) the ātmā (paraṁ padaṁ) by difficult samādhi, proudly thinking themselves liberated (vimukta- māninaḥ), not respecting your feet, thinking, “What is the use of the Lord with form since it is temporary?” becoming contaminated with attraction for material objects (aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ) because of the aversion of giving up bhāva (asta-bhāvāt) for you, the master of everyone, fall down from their position that they attained with difficulty.

*jīvan-muktā api punar bandhanaṁ yānti karmabhiḥ \|*  
*yady acintya-mahā-śaktau bhagavaty aparādhinaḥ*

**A jīvan-mukta is again subject to bondage of karma if he offends the Lord endowed with inconceivable great powers. (Bhagavat-pariśiṣṭa, from Vāsanā-bhāṣya).**

In this way, you are the form of Para-brahman. Those who do not know you as such are fools.In this way even realization of thesvarūpa of jīva is because of assistance of bhakti. This is according to your words:

*tāni sarvāṇi saṁyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ \|*

**The person who, after restraining all the senses, becomes devoted to me, will maintain steady realization of ātmā. (BG** [**2.61**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.61)**)**

### Text 33

*tathā na te mādhava tāvakāḥ kvacid*  
*bhraśyanti mārgāt tvayi baddha-sauhṛdāḥ*  
*tvayābhiguptā vicaranti nirbhayā*  
*vināyakānīkapa-mūrdhasu prabho*

**Перевод:**

**O Mādhava, Supreme Lord, Lord of the goddess of fortune, if devotees completely in love with you sometimes fall from the path of devotion, they do not fall like non-devotees, for you still protect them. Thus they fearlessly traverse the heads of their opponents and continue to progress in devotional service.**

**Комментарий:**

“But even some of those who worship me are seen to fall, why are only they (those who disrespect the Lord) described that way?”

That is answered. The devotees never fall like those who disrespect your feet. An opposite example is given. Though they may sometimes fall from seeking you (mārgāt), they still remain having firm friendship with you since you have said, kṣipram bhavati dharmātmā: the devotee who commits sin quickly becomes righteous (BG [9.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.32)). Though Bharata and Citraketu fell, it is seen that they increased their friendship with you. They are protected by you and walk on the head of the leaders of obstacles (vināyakānīkapa). They are fearless because of your favors and, conquering obstacles, respect you.

### Text 34

sattvaṁ viśuddhaṁ śrayate bhavān sthitau  
śarīriṇāṁ śreya-upāyanaṁ vapuḥ  
veda-kriyā-yoga-tapaḥ-samādhibhis  
tavārhaṇaṁ yena janaḥ samīhate

*O Lord, during the time of maintenance you manifest several incarnations, all with transcendental bodies, beyond the material modes of nature. When you appear in this way, you bestow all good fortune upon the living entities by teaching them to perform Vedic activities such as ritualistic ceremonies, mystic yoga, austerities, penances, and ultimately samādhi.*

**Комментарий:**

You manifest your form to spread bhakti. You manifest (śrayate) your form (vapuḥ) which is viśuddha-sattva. Taking shelter of the eye you are situated with form. Śrayati means manifestation. What is the purpose of this? You do this in order to steady the jīvas’(śarīriṇāṁ) hearts in you (sthitau). You preach bhakti to you since Kuntī says bhakti-yoga-vidhānārtham: you appear to spread bhakti. (SB [1.8.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/8.19)) This form is the supreme shelter (upāyanam) of human goals (śreyasām) according to the logic:

*phalam ata upapatteḥ*

**The Lord alone gives all results because that is reasonable. (Brahma-sūtra 3.2.39)**

By accepting that form, people, associating with devotees, worship (arhaṇam samīhate) you with the four dharmas of the four āśramas (study, kriyā-yoga, austerity and meditation).

### Text 35

*sattvaṁ na ced dhātar idaṁ nijaṁ bhaved*  
*vijñānam ajñāna-bhidāpamārjanam*  
*guṇa-prakāśair anumīyate bhavān*  
*prakāśate yasya ca yena vā guṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, possessor of śaktis! If your body were not beyond the modes of material nature, knowledge of your true nature, which destroys ignorance, would be destroyed. You can be inferred by the functions of the intelligence, for one can realize that the intelligence is related to you and that by you alone does it function.**

**Комментарий:**

“But do you say my body is material sattva?” O maintainer (dhātaḥ)! If your body (sattvaṁ) were not a form of self-manifesting saṁvit- śakti (vijñānam), which destroys (apamārjanam) various types of ignorance (ajñāna-bhidā), then you would merely be inferred by the manifestations of sattva-guṇa and not directly perceived.

“How can I be inferred by the manifestations of sattva-guṇa?” Your qualifies manifest or by you those qualities manifest. By a constant relationship of material sattva with you, or by your power to manifest the guṇa, the guṇa manifests. The dawn is an indication that the sun will soon rise. Smoke is an indication of fire. Similarly, your body of sattva arises from saṁvit-śakti (vijñānam), not from material sattva related to rajas and tamas. Material sattva is never called vijñāna. It is mixed with the other guṇas:

*anonya-mithunāḥ sarve sarve sarvatra gāminaḥ*

**The three guṇas are combined with each other and spread everywhere. (A somewhat similar text is found in Mahābhārata 14.36.3)**

Though the Lord’s body is not different from himself, by viśeṣa there is an appearance of difference like “existence existing.”

### Text 36

*na nāma-rūpe guṇa-janma-karmabhir*  
*nirūpitavye tava tasya sākṣiṇaḥ*  
*mano-vacobhyām anumeya-vartmano*  
*deva kriyāyāṁ pratiyanty athāpi hi*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! Your name and form along with your qualities, birth and activities, cannot be realized since you are the witness of all things, and can only be inferred by logic and scripture. The devotees realize you through devotional actions.**

**Комментарий:**

For destroying the wicked and showing mercy to the devotees, your names and forms, which were manifested, will appear. One does not have to endeavor to attain their extent since they are unlimited and inconceivable. With that intention this verse is spoken. Thename and form of you, the witness (sākṣinaḥ) along with your qualities, birth and activities, cannot be determined completely since it will be said:

*janma-karmābhidhānāni santi me ’ṅga sahasraśaḥ*  
*na śakyante ’nusaṅkhyātum anantatvān mayāpi hi*

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear friend, I have taken thousands of births, lived thousands of lives and accepted thousands of names. In fact my births, activities and names are limitless, and thus even I cannot count them. (SB** [**10.51.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/51.36)**)**

Your qualities are omniscience, omnipotence, affection for devotees, etc. Your birth is as son of Vasudeva, and son of Nanda, etc. Your activities are killing Pūtanā, lifting Govardhana, etc. Your names are Govinda, Kṛṣṇa, etc. Your forms are Śyāmasundara, etc. One cannot determine them completely. Still, your devotees realize (pratiyanti) your names and forms along with your qualities, birth and activities when there is pure bhakti of hearing, remembering, etc., (kriyāyām). They attain your names and forms to sufficient amount. You are described. Your path can be inferred through mind and words (anumeya-vartmanaḥ). The logicians infer you, the creator of the universe, but the devotees directly realize you.

### Text 37

*śṛṇvan gṛṇan saṁsmarayaṁś ca cintayan*  
*nāmāni rūpāṇi ca maṅgalāni te*  
*kriyāsu yas tvac-caraṇāravindayor*  
*āviṣṭa-cetā na bhavāya kalpate*

**Перевод:**

**The person who engages in hearing, chanting and remembering your auspicious names and forms and who becomes absorbed in those acts at your lotus feet while performing material duties surpasses saṁsāra.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, chanting and remembering the names and forms repeatedly should be done, but not the effort to attain their extent. A person situated even in material activities (kriyāsu) is not qualified for saṁsāra, rather he becomes liberated.

### Text 38

*diṣṭyā hare ’syā bhavataḥ pado bhuvo*  
*bhāro ’panītas tava janmaneśituḥ*  
*diṣṭyāṅkitāṁ tvat-padakaiḥ suśobhanair*  
*drakṣyāma gāṁ dyāṁ ca tavānukampitām*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, we are fortunate because the heavy burden of the demons upon this earth which arises from your feet is immediately removed by your appearance. We are certainly fortunate, for we shall be able to see upon this earth and in the heavenly planets the marks of your lotus feet and your display of mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

In this verse the devatās hint (by using the word hari – one who steals) that relieving the earth’s burden is necessary.

Pada means coming from the feet as the śruti says, padbhyāṁ bhūmim, “The earth arose from the Lord’s feet.” (Puruṣa-sūkta) What good fortune! The burden of the earth, which arose from your feet, has been removed. Past tense is used. This means “We have understood that Kaṁsa, Jarāsandha and others have now been killed.” “We are fortunate to see the earth (gāṁ) and heaven (dyāṁ) mercifully marked with your tender lotus feet (padakaiḥ) with auspicious marks (suśobhanaiḥ) of the flag, thunderbolt, elephant goad, etc.”

### Text 39

*na te ’bhavasyeśa bhavasya kāraṇaṁ*  
*vinā vinodaṁ bata tarkayāmahe*  
*bhavo nirodhaḥ sthitir apy avidyayā*  
*kṛtā yatas tvayy abhayāśrayātmani*

**Перевод:**

**O fearless without birth Lord! We can only speculate about the cause of your appearance. It has no cause except your desire for pastimes, since creation, maintenance and destruction are eternally carried out by your māyā-śakti, under your shelter.**

**Комментарий:**

It is only our pride that you you have appeared for protecting us due to our prayers, but actually this is a blissful pastime of you, who are independent.

O Lord! We cannot guess the cause of your appearance in Devakī. It can only be your pastimes (vinodam). Your pastime is the cause of creating the universe and none other than that.

*lokavat tu līlā-kaivalyam*

**The Lord’s creation of the world is an act without motive, as we see in an ordinary person’s conduct. (Brahma-sūtra 2.1.33)**

You are unborn (abhavasya). Birth means connection with a new body. Being devoid of that, you, in an eternally perfected body, appear in Devakī, like the moon appears in the east. The birth, maintenance and destruction of the living beings takes place by māyā, which takes shelter of you (ātmani). O destroyer of fear (abhaya)! Thinking of you, fear of time (as death) goes away. In comparsion what is lowly Kaṁsa?

### Text 40

*matsyāśva-kacchapa-nṛsiṁha-varāha-haṁsa-*  
*rājanya-vipra-vibudheṣu kṛtāvatāraḥ*  
*tvaṁ pāsi nas tri-bhuvanaṁ ca yathādhuneśa*  
*bhāraṁ bhuvo hara yadūttama vandanaṁ te*

**Перевод:**

**O supreme controller, you previously accepted incarnations among the fishes, horses, tortoises, man-lions, boars, swans, kings, brāhmaṇas and devatās, to protect the entire world. Now destroy the suffering of the earth. O best of the Yadus, we respectfully offer our obeisances unto you.**

**Комментарий:**

Still, please listen to the request of us, who are unsteady. You have appeared as avatāra among the fishes, etc. Among horses you are Hayagrīva. Among kings you are Rāmacandra. Among brāhmaṇas you are Paraśurāma. Among devatās you are Vāmana. Just as you protect the three worlds and the lords of the three worlds (nas) at all times, similarly now relieve the earth of its burden. We offer respects to you, the complete, with our heads.

*goptā yadūnāṁ bhavitā tavātmajaḥ*

**O mother Devakī, by your good fortune and ours, the Supreme Lord, with all his portions, such as Baladeva, is now within your womb. Therefore you need not fear Kaṁsa, who has decided to be killed by the Lord. Your eternal son, Kṛṣṇa, will be the protector of the entire Yadu dynasty.**

**Комментарий:**

They praise and console the mother of the Lord. Svayam Bhagavān (sākṣat bhagavān) who by his aṁśa is Kāraṇodaśaya (paraḥ pumān) has appeared in your womb for auspiciousness (bhavāya).

*śrī-śuka uvāca*

*brahmeśānau purodhāya devāḥ pratiyayur divam*

**Перевод:**

**After thus offering prayers to the Supreme Lord, who is beyond this world, all the devatās, with Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva in front of them, returned to their homes in the heavenly planets.**

**Комментарий:**

They praised the Lord whose form is non-material (anidam), full of knowledge and bliss. The devatās, thinking that Brahmā and Śiva would see some wonderful pastimes while cheating them, kept Brahmā and Śiva in front.

## Chapter 3 - The Birth of Lord Kṛṣṇa

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*atha sarva-guṇopetaḥ kālaḥ parama-śobhanaḥ*  
*yarhy evājana-janmarkṣaṁ śāntarkṣa-graha-tārakam*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, at the auspicious time for the appearance of the Lord, the entire universe was surcharged with all the qualities of goodness, beauty and peace. The constellation Rohiṇī appeared, as did stars like Aśvinī. The sun, the moon and the other stars and planets were very peaceful.**

**Комментарий:**

*maṅgale kāla-deśādāv ubhayatra janir hareḥ \|*  
*stutiḥ pitṛbhyāṁ prāptiś ca nanda-gehe tṛtīyake*

In this chapter, there is a description of the Lord’s birth when both time and place were auspicious, the prayers by Devakī and Vasudeva and the Lord’s reaching Nanda’s house.

Atha indicates auspiciousness. When the birth constellation (janma-rkṣam) of the Lord who is devoid of birth characterized by connection with a new body, appeared (ajana), then the time was filled with all good qualities. The name of the constellation is indicated indirectly because of the injunction that one should not reveal the birth constellation. Ājana-janma means he who is born from Viṣṇu. Ajana also means Brahmā. Brahmā’s nakṣatra is Rohiṇī. The other constellations such as Aśvini and the planets were peaceful.

### Text 2

*diśaḥ prasedur gaganaṁ nirmaloḍu-gaṇodayam*  
*mahī maṅgala-bhūyiṣṭha-pura-grāma-vrajākarā*

**Перевод:**

**All directions appeared extremely pleasing, and multitude of bright stars twinkled in the sky. Decorated with towns, villages, mines and pasturing grounds, the earth seemed all-auspicious.**

**Комментарий:**

Time assumed all good qualities. In the monsoon period (his birth period), the quality of autumn — clearness of the directions — is mentioned. The five elements were pleased. Gaganaṁ indicates ether situated above. Mahī indicates the earth, situated below.

### Text 3

*nadyaḥ prasanna-salilā hradā jalaruha-śriyaḥ*  
*dvijāli-kula-sannāda-stavakā vana-rājayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The rivers flowed with clear water, and the lakes and vast reservoirs, full of lilies and lotuses, were extraordinarily beautiful. In the trees and green plants, full of flowers and leaves, pleasing to the eyes, birds like cuckoos and swarms of bees began chanting with sweet voices.**

**Комментарий:**

Between the sky and earth are the other three elements described in two verses (3-4). The rivers were clear. Autumn features appeared in the monsoon seasons. Lotuses blossomed in the lakes at night. This is a quality of autumn. The forest resounded with the cries of cuckoos and humming of bees (dvijāli kula sannāda) and was resplendent with leaves and flowers. This is a quality of spring appearing in the monsoon season.

### Text 4

*vavau vāyuḥ sukha-sparśaḥ puṇya-gandhavahaḥ śuciḥ*  
*agnayaś ca dvijātīnāṁ śāntās tatra samindhata*

**Перевод:**

**A pure breeze began to blow, pleasing the sense of touch and bearing the aroma of flowers, and when the dvijas engaging in ritualistic ceremonies ignited their fires according to Vedic principles, the fires burned steadily, undisturbed by the breeze.**

**Комментарий:**

The wind was cool, pleasing to touch. It was attractively (puṇya) fragrant. Amara-kośa says, puṇyaṁ tu cārv api: puṇya also meanspleasing. The wind was clean. Blowing softly, it was pure, not mixed with dust. The fires of the three upper varṇas, though extinguished (śāntās), now blazed (samindhata), undulating clockwise (indicates auspiciousness). The quality of Treta-yuga appeared in Dvāpara- yuga.

Samindhata instead of samaindhata is poetic license.

### Text 5

*manāṁsy āsan prasannāni sādhūnām asura-druhām*  
*jāyamāne ’jane tasmin nedur dundubhayaḥ samam*

**Перевод:**

**Thus when the birthless Lord Viṣṇu, the Supreme Lord, was about to appear, the saints and brāhmaṇas, who had always been disturbed by demons like Kaṁsa and his men, felt peace within the core of their hearts, and kettledrums simultaneously vibrated from the upper planetary system.**

**Комментарий:**

The minds of devotees who were previously afflicted by demons (asura-druhām) became joyful when Kṛṣṇa (ajane) was about to beborn. The mind of the devotees were displeased by their previous disturbance.

### Text 6

*jaguḥ kinnara-gandharvās tuṣṭuvuḥ siddha-cāraṇāḥ*  
*vidyādharyaś ca nanṛtur apsarobhiḥ samaṁ mudā*

**Перевод:**

**The Kinnaras and Gandharvas began to sing auspicious songs, the Siddhas and Cāraṇas offered auspicious prayers, and the Vidyādharīs, along with the Apsarās, began to dance in jubilation.**

### Texts 7-8

*mumucur munayo devāḥ sumanāṁsi mudānvitāḥ*  
*mandaṁ mandaṁ jaladharā jagarjur anusāgaram*

*niśīthe tama-udbhūte jāyamāne janārdane*  
*devakyāṁ deva-rūpiṇyāṁ viṣṇuḥ sarva-guhā-śayaḥ*  
*āvirāsīd yathā prācyāṁ diśīndur iva puṣkalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The devatās and sages showered flowers in a joyous mood, and clouds mildly thundered, making sounds like those of the ocean’s waves. Then the Lord, complete with all his expansions, who is situated in the core of everyone’s heart, responding to the request of his devotees, appeared from Devakī, non-different from the Lord, in the dense darkness of night, like the full moon rising on the eastern horizon.**

**Комментарий:**

The devatās showered flowers (sumanāṁsi). The cloud deeply rumbling imitated the ocean (anusāgaram).

After describing the beauty of the time and place, the appearance of the Lord in both is then described in three lines. It was midnight(niśīthe) and it was spread with darkness due to clouds suddenly covering the sky. At that time, when the Lord, Janārdana, appeared(jāyamāne) in Yaśodā (devakyām), Viṣṇu, who is that Janārdana, appeared in Vasudeva’s wife Devakī through an eternally perfectedbody suitably (yathā). Devakī is described. She had a form of condensed knowledge like the Lord (deva-rūpiṇyām). Thus there was no fault for the Lord appearing in her womb. Two births simultaneously are understood due to the usage of locative absolute and since it is said:

*garbha-kāle tv asaṁprāpte aṣṭame māsi te striyau*  
*devakī ca yaśodā ca saṁṣuvāte samaṁ tadā*

**Before the eighth month in the womb, the two women Devakī and Yaśodā gave birth at the same time. (Hari- vaṁśa)**

After that, Durgā was born to Yaśodā, since it will later be said tataś ca śaurir bhagavat pracodita: when Vasudeva was inspired by Kṛṣṇa to take the child from the prison, Durgā was born to Yaśodā (SB [10.3.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.47)) and since she is described as Kṛṣṇa’s younger sister. Yaśodā gave birth to two children— a son and then a daughter. But this was not known to Vasudeva or Yaśodā. Here the word Devakī also means Yaśodā since it is said:

*dve nāmnī nanda-bhāryāyā, yaśodā devakīti ca,*  
*ataḥ sakhyam abhūt tasyā, devakyā śauri-jāyayā*

**The wife of Nanda had two names, Yasodā and also Devakī. Therefore it was natural that she \[the wife of Nanda\] developed friendship with Devakī, the wife of Śauri \[Vasudeva\]. (Bṛhad-viṣṇu Purāṇa)**

The word devakyāṁ can be syntactically connected with both janārdane and viṣṇuḥ, since being liable to be read in between, it leads to the logic of a lamp placed on the threshold, illuminating two rooms. He, in various forms, sleeps in all inaccessible places (guha) such as the various abodes in the spiritual world, and in the hearts of the jīvas. He is svayam rūpa. An example is given.

He is like the full moon. This indicates that he did not manifest like a material child. The astrologers drew up his birth chart:

*ucca-sthāḥ śaśi-bhauma-cāndri-śanayo lagnaṁ vṛṣo lābha-go jīvaḥ siṁha-tulāliṣu krama-vaśāt pūṣośano-rāhavaḥ \|*  
*naiśīthaḥ samayo’ṣṭamī budha-dinaṁ brahma-rkṣam atra kṣaṇe śrī-kṛṣṇābhidham ambujekṣaṇam abhūd āviḥ paraṁ brahma tad*

**The Moon, Mars, Mercury and Saturn were exalted and Taurus was ascendant. Jupiter was in Pisces. Sun was in Leo, Venus in Libra and Rāhu in Scorpio. At midnight, on Wednesday with the moon in the Rohiṇī nakṣatra, on the eight tithi, the lotus-eyed one known as Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is Surpeme Brahman appeared.**

The following is to be understood here. Just as the Lord entered Vasudeva, according to the statement āviveṣāṁśa-bhāgena: The Lord entered Vasudeva with full powers (SB [10.2.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.16)), in the same way, the Lord appeared in Nanda according to the hints given by the following:

*nandas tv ātmaja utpanne*

**Nanda gave birth to a son. (SB** [**10.5.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/5.1)**)**

*nandaḥ sva-putram ādāya*

**Nanda took his son. (SB** [**10.6.43**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/6.43)**)**

*paśupāṅga-jāya*

**The son of the cowherd. (SB** [**10.14.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.1)**)**

Just as Vasudeva conceived him in Devakī, Nanda conceived him in Yaśodā, just as a guru places the Lord in a disciple. But Durgā by the order of the Lord entered Yaśodā’s womb. This was like Balarāma entering Rohiṇī’s womb. This is according to the following two verses:

*devakyā jaṭhare garbhaṁ śeṣākhyaṁ dhāma māmakam \|*  
*tat sannikṛṣya rohiṇyā udare sanniveśaya*

*aṁśa-bhāgena devakyāḥ putratāṁ śubhe \|*  
*prāpsyāmi tvaṁ yaśodāyāṁ nanda-patnyāṁ bhaviṣyasi*

**Within the womb of Devakī is my aṁśa known as Saṅkarṣaṇa or Śeṣa. Drawing him out, transfer him into the womb of Rohiṇī. O all-auspicious Yogamāyā, I shall then appear in different forms as the sons of Devakī and Yaśodā and you will reside in Yaśodā, the wife of Mahārāja Nanda. (SB** [**10.2.8-9**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.8)**)**

Thus Kṛṣṇa was the child of Yaśodā just as he was the child of Devakī, since this is made clear by statements like yaśodā nanda- patnī ca (SB [10.3.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.53)) and by the uncertain statement in Ādi Purāṇa, nanda-gopa-gṛhe putro yaśodā-garbha-saṁbhavaḥ: A son appeared in Yaśodā’s womb in Nanda’s house.

Thus statements like nandas tv ātmaja (SB [10.5.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/5.1)) should be taken in their primary meaning. Because the meaning is to be kept secret, the sage, dependent on the Lord, has also taught it in a hidden manner. Since the son of Yaśodā and Devakī are one, that one person existed in Mathurā, from time to time came to Vraja and Kurukṣetra. Though this is a secret, it is revealed.

### Texts 9-10

*tam adbhutaṁ bālakam ambujekṣaṇaṁ*  
*catur-bhujaṁ śaṅkha-gadādy-udāyudham*  
*śrīvatsa-lakṣmaṁ gala-śobhi-kaustubhaṁ*  
*pītāmbaraṁ sāndra-payoda-saubhagam*

*mahārha-vaidūrya-kirīṭa-kuṇḍala-*  
*tviṣā pariṣvakta-sahasra-kuntalam*  
*uddāma-kāñcy-aṅgada-kaṅkaṇādibhir*  
*virocamānaṁ vasudeva aikṣata*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva then saw the newborn child, who had very wonderful lotus-like eyes and who bore in his four hands the four weapons śaṅkha, cakra, gadā and padma. On his chest was the mark of Śrīvatsa and on his neck the brilliant Kaustubha gem. Dressed in yellow, his body blackish like a dense cloud, his scattered hair fully grown, and his helmet and earrings sparkling uncommonly with the valuable gem Vaidūrya, the child, decorated with a brilliant belt, armlets, bangles and other ornaments, appeared very wonderful.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Vasudeva saw the amazing child. The adjectives explain how he was amazing. Thus it is parikarālaṅkāra. In this world such descriptions are certainly not heard regarding a child who comes from the womb. He had Kaustubha which was shining because of his neck. He wore a crown and earrings with very valuable vaidūrya gems. Vaidūrya refers to a jewel which shines blue, yellow and red. He had uncountable locks of hair shining with effulgence.

### Text 11

*sa vismayotphulla-vilocano hariṁ*  
*sutaṁ vilokyānakadundubhis tadā*  
*kṛṣṇāvatārotsava-sambhramo ’spṛśan*  
*mudā dvijebhyo ’yutam āpluto gavām*

**Перевод:**

**When Vasudeva saw his extraordinary son, his eyes were struck with wonder. In transcendental jubilation, he mentally collected ten thousand cows and distributed them among the brāhmaṇas as a transcendental festival.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the Lord appear with various weapons, ornaments, etc., Vasudeva became astonished and due to that astonishment, his eyes opened wide. Bewildered by the appearance of the Lord as his son, overcome with joy, he decided to give the brāhmaṇas tenthousand cows.

He was bathed in joy. In his mind he gave (aspṛśat) ten thousand cows since in Kaṁsa’s prison he could not give anything directly.Spṛśa means to distribute as well as to touch.

### Text 12

*athainam astaud avadhārya pūruṣaṁ*  
*paraṁ natāṅgaḥ kṛta-dhīḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ*  
*sva-rociṣā bhārata sūtikā-gṛhaṁ*  
*virocayantaṁ gata-bhīḥ prabhāva-vit*

**Перевод:**

**O descendant of King Bharata! Immediately convinced that this child was the Supreme Lord with all his powers because he had fixed his mind on the Lord, he offered respects and, with folded hands, without fear because he knew the Lord’s powers, began to offer prayers to the Lord, who illuminated the room where he was born.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding that the Supreme Lord was his son, his fear, which arose from seeing the death of his previous sons, was gone because he knew his son’s power (prabhāva-vit). He became absorbed in Lord as his son (kṛta-dhīḥ) with a conception which was predominated by great power.

### Text 13

*śrī-vasudeva uvāca*  
*vidito ’si bhavān sākṣāt puruṣaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ*  
*kevalānubhavānanda-svarūpaḥ sarva-buddhi-dṛk*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva said: I know that you are directly the Supreme Person beyond material existence, known as the impersonal Brahman, as Paramātmā and as Bhagavān.**

**Комментарий:**

By informing the Lord that his fear is gone, he praises the Lord. O Lord! You are known by me. “What is known about me?” You are form who is not dependent on anything (sākṣād). You are the puruṣa beyond prakṛti. You glance upon prakṛti and control it. You are the antaryāmī of all beings (sarva-buddhi-dṛk) as Garbhodaśaya and Kṣīrodaśaya. You are Bhagavān with those aṁśas. “What is my composition?” You are a svarūpa of pure (kevala) knowledge (anubhāva) and bliss (ānanda) which is non-different from it, devoid of difference between body and self.

### Text 14

*sa eva sva-prakṛtyedaṁ sṛṣṭvāgre tri-guṇātmakam*  
*tad anu tvaṁ hy apraviṣṭaḥ praviṣṭa iva bhāvyase*

**Перевод:**

**Just as you created the universe made of three guṇas and entered it, so you seem to have entered Devakī as her son by your inconceivable energy, yet you have not entered.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why do you praise me, who have entered and become restricted by your house?”

You are the one who is described by the stated characteristics. By your māyā, you have created this universe made of three guṇas andthen after the creation, are discerned to be as if you entered it and as if not entered it. Because you are perceived within the universe it seems you have entered it. Because you are perceived outside the universe, it seems you have not entered it.

### Texts 15-16

*yatheme ’vikṛtā bhāvās tathā te vikṛtaiḥ saha*  
*nānā-vīryāḥ pṛthag-bhūtā virājaṁ janayanti hi*

*sannipatya samutpādya dṛśyante ’nugatā iva*  
*prāg eva vidyamānatvān na teṣām iha sambhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The mahat-tattva, the total material energy, is undivided, but because of the material modes of nature, it appears to separate into earth, water, fire, air and ether. Because of the living energy \[jīva-bhūta\], these separated energies combine to make the cosmic manifestation visible, but in fact, before the creation of the cosmos, the total energy is already present. Therefore, the total material energy never actually enters the creation.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses give an analogy. Just as with mahat-tattva and other elements (bhāvāḥ), which are unaltered, so with you. The example is explained. The unaltered elements produce the universe (virājam), after combining (sannipatya) with the sixteen transformations (vikṛtaiḥ). The reason for the combination is described. Separately, they cannot produce the universe (nānā-vīryāḥ). Thus, they combine. Having produced the universe, they seem to enter it(anugatāḥ). But they do not enter it. Why? Since previous to the creation, they existed as causes. Thus after the creation (iha) they do not enter (na sambhavaḥ).

### Text 17

*evaṁ bhavān buddhy-anumeya-lakṣaṇair*  
*grāhyair guṇaiḥ sann api tad-guṇāgrahaḥ*  
*anāvṛtatvād bahir antaraṁ na te*  
*sarvasya sarvātmana ātma-vastunaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, although you are situated with forms, you cannot be perceived by the senses. With our senses we can perceive some things, but not everything. Consequently, you are beyond perception by the senses. Since you are all pervading you are not inside or outside. You are in all beings because your knowledge pervades everywhere.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse connects the source of the analogy to its target. “If I am all-pervading, then why cannot the senses such as eyes, etc., which perceive form, etc., perceive me?”

Though situated (sann api) along with forms, etc., which are perceived by the senses (guṇaiḥ) whose nature is inferable byknowledge of form, etc., (buddhy-anumeya-lakṣaṇair) you are not perceived along with form, etc., by these senses. Just as though ether is situated everywhere, it cannot be perceived by the eyes, etc., since they are unfit for it.

“But since I enter the universe, I should not be situated outside.” You have no inside or outside. Why? You are inside and outside since you are all-pervading (anāvrṭatvāt), by your real śakti. You are everything.

“Then I must be a material body somewhat.” You are spread everywhere (sarvātmanaḥ). You are within everything. “Am I like ether, indifferent in nature?” You spread everywhere by your intelligence, since you are a conscious being (ātma-vastunaḥ).

This is stated later with na cāntar na bahir yasya (SB [10.9.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/9.13)). In this way, the manifestation of the all-pervading in my house byacintya-śakti is itself the entrance. That is my good fortune.

### Text 18

*ya ātmano dṛśya-guṇeṣu sann iti*  
*vyavasyate sva-vyatirekato ’budhaḥ*  
*vinā nu vādaṁ na ca tan manīṣitaṁ*  
*samyag yatas tyaktam upādadat pumān*

**Перевод:**

**The person absorbed in karmas considers material objects to be supreme because of his direct perception, without reference to you. He is a fool, since he does not perceive its connection with you. As a result he accepts as valuable what is rejected by the wise.**

**Комментарий:**

“But some persons absorbed in karmas think that scriptures say that karma alone is the cause of all puruṣārthas, and that the perfection is Svarga with garlands, sandalwood, women, etc., which are achieved through those karmas, and not me as you have explained.” The person absorbed in karmas (yaḥ) concludes (vyavastyate) that among all sense objects (guṇeṣu) seen by himself, object such as sandalwood, garlands, etc., is best and eternal (sann). He performs karmas to attain it. He does not consider you to be the Supreme Lord, the creator of everything and the giver of all results. That person is a fool, devoid of knowledge of the meaning of scripture.

“Why?” Since he is always devoid of connection with that object, and since it is temporary when he gets it (sva-vyatirekataḥ). “But he considers himself wise. Why is he a fool?” His learning (manīṣitam) is certainly (nu) not complete, without argumentation (vādam). His conclusion is refuted by those learned in Vedānta since he considers what is rejected (tyaktam) as useless by the wise as valuable.

### Text 19

*tvatto ’sya janma-sthiti-saṁyamān vibho*  
*vadanty anīhād aguṇād avikriyāt*  
*tvayīśvare brahmaṇi no virudhyate*  
*tvad-āśrayatvād upacaryate guṇaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O my Lord, learned Vedas conclude that the creation, maintenance and annihilation of the entire cosmic manifestation are performed by you, who are free from endeavor, unaffected by the modes of material nature, and changeless in your spiritual situation. There are no contradictions in you, who are the controller of māyā and endowed with all qualities. Your work is assisted by the guṇas, since they act under your inspiration.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse shows that the Lord is the creator of the universe as described. The scriptures say that you are the creator, maintainer and destroyer of the universe (asya).

Yato vā imāni bhūtāni: all beings arise from the Lord. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)

“But the person carrying out actions, like a carpenter, develops joy and sorrow, fatigue and worry.”

You do not act (anīhāt). Since everything happens just by your will, you exert no effort like a carpenter. Thus you experience no transformations such as fatigue, etc. Because you are devoid of the guṇas of māyā (aguṇāt), there is no illusion, joy or sorrow.

“But how is it possible that something without exertion and transformation, does everything?” This is not contrary to you, the controller of māyā and time (īśvara), endowed with great qualities such as every desire coming true (brahmaṇi).

“But the guṇas sometimes said to be the doer?” Your position as the sole agent is assisted by the guṇas since it is said:

kartāram īśam: The lord is the agent. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)

The guṇas are secondary doers.

“Why is this?” By your glance the guṇas are brought to life (tad- āśrayatvāt). A lump of iron becomes capable of burning because of contact with fire. Thus, you who are the creator of the universe and different from it, should be worshipped.

### Text 20

*sa tvaṁ tri-loka-sthitaye sva-māyayā*  
*bibharṣi śuklaṁ khalu varṇam ātmanaḥ*  
*sargāya raktaṁ rajasopabṛṁhitaṁ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ ca varṇaṁ tamasā janātyaye*

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, for the maintenance of the three worlds, you assume the white color of Viṣṇu in goodness; for creation, which is surrounded by the quality of passion, You appear reddish; and at the end, when there is a need for annihilation, which is surrounded by ignorance, You appear blackish.**

**Комментарий:**

Creating this universe in the form of Saṅkarṣaṇa, you perform activities in the universe always, through avatāras such as Viṣṇu, while sleeping in the form of Pradyumna in the Garbhodaka ocean. That is explained in this verse. You, famous (saḥ), are pure (śuklam) by your superior śakti (sva-māyayā) since Viṣṇu, protector of the universe, is blue like the atasī flower, not white (another meaning of śuklam). Red (raktaṁ) and black (kṛṣṇaṁ) are not thecomplexions of Brahmā and Śiva since Brahmā is gold and Śiva is like the moon. Thus, those words (śuklaṁ, raktaṁ, kṛṣṇaṁ) arefigurative with respect to the attributes of the various guṇas. Viṣṇu is not described as sattvenopabṛṁhitam  unlike  rajasopabṛṁhitamsince Viṣṇu instigates sattva from a distance, whereas Brahmā and Śiva become covered by rajas and tamas respectively.

### Text 21

*tvam asya lokasya vibho rirakṣiṣur*  
*gṛhe ’vatīrṇo ’si mamākhileśvara*  
*rājanya-saṁjñāsura-koṭi-yūthapair*  
*nirvyūhyamānā nihaniṣyase camūḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O my Lord, proprietor of all creation, you have now appeared in my house, desiring to protect this world. I am sure that you will kill all the armies that are moving all over the world under the leadership of politicians who are dressed as kṣatriya rulers but who are factually demons.**

**Комментарий:**

“O father! You know the truth. Tell me the goal of my appearing in your house.” You have appeared, desiring to protect the world(asya lokasya). You will kill the troops moving here and there with millions of demonic groups acting like rulers, in order to protect the devotees.

### Text 22

*ayaṁ tv asabhyas tava janma nau gṛhe*  
*śrutvāgrajāṁs te nyavadhīt sureśvara*  
*sa te ’vatāraṁ puruṣaiḥ samarpitaṁ*  
*śrutvādhunaivābhisaraty udāyudhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O my Lord, Lord of the demigods, after hearing the prophecy that you would take birth in our home and kill him, this uncivilized Kaṁsa killed so many of your elder brothers. As soon as he hears from his lieutenants that you have appeared, he will immediately come with weapons to kill you.**

**Комментарий:**

Though knowing the powers of his son, he fears Kaṁsa because of arousal of his affection for his son.

This wicked person (asabhyaḥ), hearing from Nārada of your birth in our house, killed your elder brothers. Hearing of your appearance from information given (samarpitam) by the door- keepers (puruṣaiḥ), he will come (abhisarati). Present tense is used since his future coming is near the present according to vartamāna- sāmipye vartamāna-vat (Pāṇini 3.3.131).

Though I, equal to Kārtavīrya in battle, am capable of killing him, still since his liberation is approaching and since you alone can accomplish that, I did not kill him. As long as that opportunity does not arise, reconciliation should be made.

### Text 23

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*athainam ātmajaṁ vīkṣya mahā-puruṣa-lakṣaṇam*  
*devakī tam upādhāvat kaṁsād bhītā suvismitā*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Thereafter, having seen that her child had all the symptoms of Nārāyaṇa, Devakī, who was very much afraid of Kaṁsa and unusually astonished, began to offer prayers to the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

She praised (upādhāvat) the Lord but was afraid of Kaṁsa out of motherly affection for her son.

### Text 24

*śrī-devaky uvāca*  
*rūpaṁ yat tat prāhur avyaktam ādyaṁ*  
*brahma jyotir nirguṇaṁ nirvikāram*  
*sattā-mātraṁ nirviśeṣaṁ nirīhaṁ*  
*sa tvaṁ sākṣād viṣṇur adhyātma-dīpaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**That form which they say is invisible, the cause of all causes, the greatest, self-manifesting, without qualities, without change, pure existence, without variety and without action, is directly you, the Supreme Lord, who manifests our intelligence.**

**Комментарий:**

Though afraid, seeing you without fear, I offer respects. She describes this in four verses.

What the Vedānta (i.e. Upaniṣads) say is some astonishing (tat) entity (rūpam), you are that (sa tvam). That entity is unmanifest(avyaktam). The reason is that it is the cause (ādyam). Then is this entity a group of atoms as the Nyāya philosophers claim? It is great (brahma). Then is this entity pradhāna as the Saṅkhya philosophers claim? It is conscious (jyotiḥ). Then is it dull matter with knowledge as its quality as claimed by the Vaiśeṣikas? Is without qualities (nirguṇam). It is jñāna-svarūpa, devoid of the material guṇas. It shines with the quality of knowledge as its viśeṣa. Is this entity a transformation of knowledge as propounded by thevijñāna-vādī Buddhists? It has no transformations (nirvikāram). But is it uncertain (relativistic) existence as claimed by the Jainsfollowing syād-vāda? It is accurately defined (miyāte = mātra) existence (sattā).

But the universe also is like that as described by the proponents of Dvaita. You have the additional nature of controlling the universe,as a determined quality (nirviśeṣam). Nir means certainty according to Amara-kośa.

Let that entity be of that nature. What is the use for living beings? He makes people who are turned to him desire completely (nirīham). He is most affectionate, giving all puruṣārthas including himself.

How does he turn people towards him? He is a lamp of knowledge about himself (adhyātma-dīpaḥ). Giving knowledge about himself through the devotees, he turns them towards him. There should be no fear with a person of this nature.

### Text 25

*naṣṭe loke dvi-parārdhāvasāne*  
*mahā-bhūteṣv ādi-bhūtaṁ gateṣu*  
*vyakte ’vyaktaṁ kāla-vegena yāte*  
*bhavān ekaḥ śiṣyate śeṣa-saṁjñaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After the two halves of Brahmā’s life, at the time of cosmic annihilation, when everything manifested is annihilated by the force of time, and the elements merge in prakṛti, you alone remain, with your unlimited devotees who are non-different from you.**

**Комментарий:**

Since you remain after destruction of the universe, what need is there to fear? At the end of Brahmā’s life when all planets are destroyed, when the five elements merge into ahaṅkāra (ādi-bhūtam), the source of ether, ahaṅkāra merges into mahat-tattva (vyakte), and mahat-tattva merges into pradhāna (avyaktam) by the force of time, you alone exist and are thus called Śeṣa, the remainder.

### Text 26

*yo ’yaṁ kālas tasya te ’vyakta-bandho*  
*ceṣṭām āhuś ceṣṭate yena viśvam*  
*nimeṣādir vatsarānto mahīyāṁ*  
*taṁ tveśānaṁ kṣema-dhāma prapadye*

**Перевод:**

**O inaugurator of the material energy! Time which starts with second and ends with years, which rotate to make the life time of Brahmā, and by which the universe moves, is said to be your movement. I surrender to the Supreme Lord, the abode of fearlessness and happiness.**

**Комментарий:**

Since time seems to be independent as in kāla-vegena of the previous verse, sometimes there is fear from time. O master of prakṛti (avyakta-bandho)! Time, which destroys everything at pralaya, is called your nature (ceṣṭā). By time, a form of your nature, this universe acts. What is time? It begins with nimeṣas. Mahīyān means by cycling of years it becomes dvi-parārdha (life of Brahmā). I surrender to you. Who are you? You are the controller of time and pradhāna since the śruti says:

*jñaḥ kāla-kālo guṇī sarva-vid yaḥ \|*

**The Lord is omniscient. He controls time. He has all good qualities. He inspires all knowledge. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad** [**6.25**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sveta-bs/6.25)**)**

You are the shelter of fearlessness or the svarūpa of fearlessness (kṣema-dhāma).

### Text 27

*martyo mṛtyu-vyāla-bhītaḥ palāyan*  
*lokān sarvān nirbhayaṁ nādhyagacchat*  
*tvat-pādābjaṁ prāpya yadṛcchayādya*  
*svasthaḥ śete mṛtyur asmād apaiti*

**Перевод:**

**No one in this material world, fearful of the snake of time, has become free from fear, even by fleeing to various planets. But now that you have appeared, death is fleeing in fear of you, and the living entities, having obtained shelter at your lotus feet by your mercy, are fearless and tranquil.**

**Комментарий:**

Those who take shelter of your lotus feet become fearless, what to speak of you. Beings who are subject to death, running (palāyan)to various planets up to the planet of Brahmā (sarvān) do not attain freedom from fear (nirbhayaṁ). By bhakti attained by chance association with devotees (yadṛcchayā), attaining Dhanvantari, the form of your lotus feet, the person becomes free of fear (svasthaḥ)and rests. Abja can mean Dhanvantari according to Medinī. It is surprising that I, your devotee and mother, fear insignificant Kaṁsa.

### Text 28

*sa tvaṁ ghorād ugrasenātmajān nas*  
*trāhi trastān bhṛtya-vitrāsa-hāsi*  
*rūpaṁ cedaṁ pauruṣaṁ dhyāna-dhiṣṇyaṁ*  
*mā pratyakṣaṁ māṁsa-dṛśāṁ kṛṣīṣṭhāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Lord who delivers the devotee from fear! Please protect us, fearful of the terrifying son of Ugrasena. Make your four-armed form, the object of meditation, invisible to the ignorant people.**

**Комментарий:**

She speaks, desiring fearlessness. Save us, since you are the destroyer of fear in your devotee.

“But appearing in order to kill wicked persons like Kaṁsa, I will kill him now when he comes.” Fearing for her son out of vātsalya, she speaks. Do not show your powerful form (pauruṣaṁ), the object of meditation, to humans (māṁsa-dṛśāṁ). Let there not be the pain of a battle today. We should tolerate another pain also. You will destroy our suffering at another time.

### Text 29

*janma te mayy asau pāpo mā vidyān madhusūdana*  
*samudvije bhavad-dhetoḥ kaṁsād aham adhīra-dhīḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O killer of Madhu! Sinful Kaṁsa should not know that you have been born to me. With mind unsteady because of your mercy I fear what Kaṁsa will do to you.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why do you say that Kaṁsa should not know about me?” Desiring your welfare (bhavad-dhetoḥ), I am fearful of Kaṁsa. Though you, on account of being Madhusūdana (killer of Madhu), should kill Kaṁsa when he comes, still as a mother, my mind is unsteady. Do not show a painful fight in front of my eyes.

### Text 30

*upasaṁhara viśvātmann ado rūpam alaukikam*  
*śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padma-śriyā juṣṭaṁ catur-bhujam*

**Перевод:**

**O soul of the universe! Hide your extraordinary four-armed form, served by the wealth of the conch, disc, club and lotus.**

**Комментарий:**

“When Kaṁsa comes, he will see my form. Then I will fight with him.” Withdraw this form which is unusual. Be like a normal child so that I can hide you somewhere. She shows fear from great vātsalya.

### Text 31

*viśvaṁ yad etat sva-tanau niśānte*  
*yathāvakāśaṁ puruṣaḥ paro bhavān*  
*bibharti so ’yaṁ mama garbhago ’bhūd*  
*aho nṛ-lokasya viḍambanaṁ hi tat*

**Перевод:**

**As Mahāviṣṇu you support the universe which appears in your body after Brahmā’s night. You also have appeared from my womb. Oh! People will ridicule me for this.**

**Комментарий:**

“But O mother! Why should I withdraw this form of the Lord? By this you will become famous: Devakī is the mother of the Lord.”

You, the Supreme Lord, hold this universe in your temple-like (niśānte) body without any restrictions (yathāvakāśam). I will be disrespected (viḍambanaṁ) by the people of this world that the all-pervading Lord came into my limited womb. Anyway, I do not desire fame, but I desire your safety only. Withdraw this form. Kaṁsa will know of the eighth child by other means. The fear in Vasudeva and Devakī is not caused by māyā but by the play of the superior śakti and is full of vātsalya. This was explained in the commentary on viṣṇor māyā bhagavatī (SB [10.1.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.25)).

### Text 32

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*tvam eva pūrva-sarge ’bhūḥ pṛśniḥ svāyambhuve sati*  
*tadāyaṁ sutapā nāma prajāpatir akalmaṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord replied: My dear mother, best of the chaste, in your previous birth, in the Svāyambhuva millennium, you were known as Pṛśni, and Vasudeva, who was the most pious Prajāpati, was named Sutapā.**

**Комментарий:**

O mother! Why do you behave so humbly? You are not a material person, but a spiritual aṁśa. Because of your doing many activities, I have become your son. This is explained in four verses. O chaste woman (sati)! In Svāyambhuva manvantara you were Pṛśniḥ and Vasudeva was Sutapā.

### Text 33

*yuvāṁ vai brahmaṇādiṣṭau prajā-sarge yadā tataḥ*  
*sanniyamyendriya-grāmaṁ tepāthe paramaṁ tapaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When both of you were ordered by Lord Brahmā to create progeny, you first underwent severe austerities by controlling your senses.**

### Texts 34-35

*varṣa-vātātapa-hima-gharma-kāla-guṇān anu*  
*sahamānau śvāsa-rodha-vinirdhūta-mano-malau*

*śīrṇa-parṇānilāhārāv upaśāntena cetasā*  
*mattaḥ kāmān abhīpsantau mad-ārādhanam īhatuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You endured rain, wind, strong sun, scorching heat and severe cold, according to different seasons. By practicing prāṇāyāma you cleansed your minds of all contamination. You ate only air and dry leaves. With your minds concentrated on me, desiring happiness from the Lord being your son, you worshiped me.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Tolerating the qualities of time (kāla- guṇāṇ) such as rain, etc., purifying your minds of attachment using prāṇāyāma (śvāsa-rodhaḥ), with mind pacified, devoid of material attachment (upaśāntena cetasā), you worshipped me.

### Text 36

*evaṁ vāṁ tapyatos tīvraṁ tapaḥ parama-duṣkaram*  
*divya-varṣa-sahasrāṇi dvādaśeyur mad-ātmanoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Twelve thousand celestial years passed while you performed difficult austerities, concentrating only on me.**

**Комментарий:**

Mad-ātmanoḥ means “absorbing your minds in me alone.”

### Texts 37-38

*tadā vāṁ parituṣṭo ’ham amunā vapuṣānaghe*  
*tapasā śraddhayā nityaṁ bhaktyā ca hṛdi bhāvitaḥ*

*prādurāsaṁ varada-rāḍ yuvayoḥ kāma-ditsayā*  
*vriyatāṁ vara ity ukte mādṛśo vāṁ vṛtaḥ sutaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O sinless mother Devakī, after the expiry of twelve thousand celestial years, in which you constantly contemplated me within the core of your heart with great faith, devotion and austerity, I was very much satisfied with you. Since I am the best of all bestowers of benediction, I appeared in this same form as Kṛṣṇa to ask you to take from me the benediction you desired. You then expressed your desire to have a son exactly like me.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhāvitaḥ means “I became the object of your bhāva.”

### Text 39

*ajuṣṭa-grāmya-viṣayāv anapatyau ca dam-patī*  
*na vavrāthe ’pavargaṁ me mohitau deva-māyayā*

**Перевод:**

**You had no desire for material objects and were without children. Though qualified, you did not ask for liberation from me, since you were bewildered by my mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

You did not ask for liberation (apavargam), predominated with happiness and power. You were bewildered by spiritual māyā,endowed with affection for a son. The two became astonishing by the bliss of that taste. It will be said:

*vaiṣṇavīṁ vyatanon māyām, putra-snehamayīṁ vibhuḥ*

**By the influence of his internal potency, yogamāyā, Kṛṣṇa inspired mother Yaśodā to become absorbed in intense maternal affection for her son. (SB** [**10.8.43**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.43)**)**

### Text 40

*gate mayi yuvāṁ labdhvā varaṁ mat-sadṛśaṁ sutam*  
*grāmyān bhogān abhuñjāthāṁ yuvāṁ prāpta-manorathau*

**Перевод:**

**After you received that benediction and I disappeared, you engaged yourselves in sexual union to have a son like me, and I  fulfilled your desire.**

**Комментарий:**

Desiring a son like me, you then engaged in sexual intercourse. According to the Amara-kośa, grāmyān bhogān means sex.

### Text 41

*adṛṣṭvānyatamaṁ loke śīlaudārya-guṇaiḥ samam*  
*ahaṁ suto vām abhavaṁ pṛśnigarbha iti śrutaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Since I found no one else as highly elevated as I in character and great qualities, I became your son and was known as Pṛśnigarbha.**

**Комментарий:**

Pṛśnigarbha gave benedictions to Dhruva. This refers to the Tretā- yuga avatāra mentioned in the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam ([11.5.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.26)):

*viṣṇur yajñaḥ pṛśnigarbhaḥ, sarvadeva urukramaḥ*

**In Tretā-yuga the Lord is glorified by the names Viṣṇu, Yajña, Pṛśnigarbha, Sarvadeva, Urukrama, etc.**

### Text 42

*tayor vāṁ punar evāham adityām āsa kaśyapāt*  
*upendra iti vikhyāto vāmanatvāc ca vāmanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In the next millennium, I again appeared from the two of you, who appeared as my mother, Aditi, and my father, Kaśyapa. I was known as Upendra, and because of being a dwarf, I was also known as Vāmana.**

**Комментарий:**

I appeared as Vāmana in Aditi, from Kaśyapa. I alone became the son of you two in those forms.

### Text 43

*tṛtīye ’smin bhave ’haṁ vai tenaiva vapuṣātha vām*  
*jāto bhūyas tayor eva satyaṁ me vyāhṛtaṁ sati*

**Перевод:**

**O supremely chaste mother, I have now appeared to you in my third birth as Svayam Bhagavān. In this way my promise has been fulfilled.**

**Комментарий:**

In the third birth, now, I have been born to you. By saying, “I am Pṛśnigarbha” (SB [10.3.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.41)) and “I am Vāmana” (SB [10.3.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.42)), it is accepted that these are aṁśas of Kṛṣṇa. By saying, “You were Pṛśni,” (SB [10.3.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.32)) Pṛśni and Aditi are accepted as aṁśas of Devakī. By saying, “He was Sutapā,” (SB [10.3.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.32)) Sutapā and Kaśyapa are accepted as aṁśas of Vasudeva. O learned one (sati)! Sati means learned according to Amara-kośa.

### Text 44

*etad vāṁ darśitaṁ rūpaṁ prāg-janma-smaraṇāya me*  
*nānyathā mad-bhavaṁ jñānaṁ martya-liṅgena jāyate*

**Перевод:**

**I have shown you this form so that you will remember my previous appearances before you. You would not understand my birth if I appeared in my human-like form.**

**Комментарий:**

The reason for showing the four-armed form (etad) to them both (vāṁ) is explained. Starting from giving the benedictions (to Pṛśni and Sutapā), in order that you remember the previous forms that I manifested, I have shown this form, not by considering my principle form since I am principally Parabrahman in human form (two-armed). Otherwise by the human form, though it is complete, knowledge of my true nature would not arise. The knowledge is that the Lord who has now been born is the same Lord whom yousaw in previous forms.

### Text 45

*yuvāṁ māṁ putra-bhāvena brahma-bhāvena cāsakṛt*  
*cintayantau kṛta-snehau yāsyethe mad-gatiṁ parām*

**Перевод:**

**Both of you, husband and wife, constantly think of me with eternal prema as your son, and maybe you once thought of me as Brahman. You will achieve my abode which you already possess.**

**Комментарий:**

Though about to go to Gokula, the Lord makes his parents happy, with faith that they would attain him. By thinking of me as yourson (putra-bhāvena), with secondary thoughts of my powers, and by thinking of me as Brahman (brahma-bhāvena) with secondary thoughts as your son, you will attain the supreme goal (parāṁ gatim). My present goal is Gokula. When I am eleven I will come to Mathurā. That is my supreme goal. You will attain (yāsyethe) that. Now you be separated from me. Do not be despondent. It is not that you will attain liberation by bhakti to me. You did not accept that previously, bewildered by māyā since such liberation is contradicted by the following statement:

*ete hi yādavāḥ sarve mad-gaṇā eva bhāmini*

**All the Yādavas are my associates. (Padma Purāṇa)**

Moreover, Vasudeva is viśuddha-sattva and Devakī is an avatāra of the superior śakti. They are eternally liberated. Still when they act otherwise, as the Lord does, it is for teaching other people.

### Text 46

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity uktvāsīd dharis tūṣṇīṁ bhagavān ātma-māyayā*  
*pitroḥ sampaśyatoḥ sadyo babhūva prākṛtaḥ śiśuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After thus speaking, the Lord remained silent. While they alone watched, by his mercy, he suddenly assumed the form a baby who was svabhāva-siddha.**

**Комментарий:**

Ātma māyayā means “own spiritual energy,” due to the Mahā- saṁhitā statement, ātma-māyā tad-icchā syād guṇa-māyā jaḍātmika: ātma-māyā means the Lord’s own free will and guṇa-māyā means matter. He manifested as a baby with his svarūpa (prākrṭaḥ).Svarūpa and svabhāva are synonyms according to Amara-kośa. Svabhāva and prakṛti are synonyms according to Dhanañjaya-kośa.(Thus svarūpa and prakṛti are synonyms.) The child who went to Gokula was called Parabrahman.

### Text 47

*tataś ca śaurir bhagavat-pracoditaḥ*  
*sutaṁ samādāya sa sūtikā-gṛhāt*  
*yadā bahir gantum iyeṣa tarhy ajā*  
*yā yogamāyājani nanda-jāyayā*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, exactly when Vasudeva, ordered by the Lord, carefully took the child from the maternity room and was about to leave, Yogamāyā took birth as the daughter of the wife of Mahārāja Nanda.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses go together. Vasudeva was instructed by Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, “If you are afraid, then placing me in Yaśodā’s room, and bringing back the child of Yaśodā, Yogamāyā here, give her to Kaṁsa.”

After being instructed, when Vasudeva, looking at his chained feet, taking his son, wanted to leave the prison, then at that timeYogamāyā, called Viṣṇu-māyā, Bhagavatī, who is birth less, took birth through Yaśodā, who was an instrumental cause (i.e. Yaśodā was not the material cause of Yogamāyā).

### Texts 48-49

*tayā hṛta-pratyaya-sarva-vṛttiṣu*  
*dvāḥ-stheṣu paureṣv api śāyiteṣv atha*  
*dvāraś ca sarvāḥ pihitā duratyayā*  
*bṛhat-kapāṭāyasa-kīla-śṛṅkhalaiḥ*

*tāḥ kṛṣṇa-vāhe vasudeva āgate*  
*svayaṁ vyavaryanta yathā tamo raveḥ*  
*vavarṣa parjanya upāṁśu-garjitaḥ*  
*śeṣo ’nvagād vāri nivārayan phaṇaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**By the influence of māyā, all the doorkeepers became unconscious with nonfunctional senses and the citizens were in deep sleep. The doors, locked securely with chains, iron pins and huge bolts, suddenly opened on their own when Vasudeva came carrying Kṛṣṇa, just as darkness dissipates with the coming of the sun. The clouds rumbling gently poured rain. Ananta, giving protection by spreading his hood, followed behind.**

**Комментарий:**

Through her expansion of three guṇas, Yogamāyā covered all the knowledge senses (hṛta-pratyaya-sarva-vṛttiṣu) of the doorkeepersso they fell into deep sleep. The entrances which were locked by doors opened themselves (vyavaryanta) when Vasudeva came out carrying Kṛṣṇa. Vasudeva carried on his head Kṛṣṇa, the supreme bliss, in a small box covered with soft cloth. The entrances which were difficult to surpass by huge doors, iron bolts and chains, opened like darkness dissipated by the sun. Clouds rumbled softy(upāṁśu). Śeṣa, an expansion of Lord Balarāma, spread his hood like an umbrella since Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa says:

*śayyāsana-paridhāna-pādukā-chatra-cāmaraiḥ*  
*kiṁ nābhūs tasya kṛṣṇasya mūrti-bhedaiś ca mūrtiṣu*

**Whenever Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa takes different forms, Lord Balarāma’s expansion Śeṣa serves Kṛṣṇa as his bed, seat, shoes, umbrella and cāmara.**

### Text 50

*maghoni varṣaty asakṛd yamānujā*  
*gambhīra-toyaugha-javormi-phenilā*  
*bhayānakāvarta-śatākulā nadī*  
*mārgaṁ dadau sindhur iva śriyaḥ pateḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because of constant rain sent by Indra, the River Yamunā was filled with deep water, swift foaming currents and hundreds of fierce whirlpools. But as the great Indian Ocean had formerly given way to Rāmacandra the River Yamunā gave way to Vasudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

While Indra showered rain constantly, Yamunā made a path, so that the water became knee-deep. The water was deep. It had waves because of the fast currents of abundant water and was foamy. It was disturbed with hundreds of fearsome whirlpools. The Yamunā made a path for Vasudeva just as the ocean made a path for Rāmacandra who wanted to go to Laṅkā.

### Text 51

*nanda-vrajaṁ śaurir upetya tatra tān*  
*gopān prasuptān upalabhya nidrayā*  
*sutaṁ yaśodā-śayane nidhāya tat-*  
*sutām upādāya punar gṛhān agāt*

**Перевод:**

**When Vasudeva reached the house of Nanda Mahārāja, he saw that all the cowherd men were fast asleep. Thus he placed his own son on the bed of Yaśodā, picked up her daughter, and then returned to his residence.**

**Комментарий:**

The door-keepers of the cowherds of Nanda were also sleeping by the influence of Yoga-nidrā, an aṁśa of the Lord’s superior śakti. The doors had all opened on their own. Yaśodā also was sleeping by the influence of Yoga-nidrā. Vasudeva did not see her son. He placed his own son there and taking the daughter, left. It should be understood that the two sons became one, like merging of clouds. Since Vasudeva knew that Kaṁsa could not kill the daughter, his deceit is not a fault.

### Text 52

*devakyāḥ śayane nyasya vasudevo ’tha dārikām*  
*pratimucya pador loham āste pūrvavad āvṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva placed the female child on the bed of Devakī, bound his legs with the iron shackles, and thus remained locked in the prison as before.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva placed the chains back on his feet and was confined to the prison (āvṛtaḥ).

### Text 53

*yaśodā nanda-patnī ca jātaṁ param abudhyata*  
*na tal-liṅgaṁ pariśrāntā nidrayāpagata-smṛtiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Exhausted by the labor of childbirth, Yaśodā was overwhelmed with sleep and unable to understand the signs that Vasudeva had come.**

**Комментарий:**

It was explained through verse beginning with niśīthe (SB [10.3.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.8)) that Kṛṣṇa was born in Mathurā and in Gokula. In Mathurā he was praised by Vasudeva and Devakī and he spoke. What happened in Gokula? That is explained in the verse.

Like Vasudeva’s wife, Nanda’s wife understood (abudhyata) that Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord (param), was born from her womb. Seeing the signs on his hands and feet she understood that her son was the Lord and appeared to give her bliss. Like Devakī she praised Kṛṣṇa. But by her feeling for him as her son, since her understanding of his powers was suppressed she did not see the daughter that had been born. “But why was she not aware that Vasudeva took the daughter and left?” She was not aware of the signs (liṅgam) that he had come. Liṅgam means a sign according to Viśva. Another version has na tad veda. She did not know that Vasudeva had come. The cause is given. She was overwhelmed with sleep by Yoga-māyā who protected the secret.

## Chapter 4 - The Atrocities of King Kaṁsa

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*bahir-antaḥ-pura-dvāraḥ sarvāḥ pūrvavad āvṛtāḥ*  
*tato bāla-dhvaniṁ śrutvā gṛha-pālāḥ samutthitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: The doors inside and outside the house closed as before. Thereafter, the watchmen, hearing the crying of the newborn child, woke up.**

**Комментарий:**

*devī-vākyenānutāpo bhaginī-bhāmayoḥ kṣamā \|*  
*durmantribhir mantraṇaṁ ca kaṁsasyāsīc caturthake*

**This chapter relates Kaṁsa’s repentance on hearing Māyā’s words, Devakī and Vasudeva’s forgiving Kaṁsa, and the evil ministers’ advice to Kaṁsa.**

All the entrances outside and in the prison were locked as previously with doors. Crying of a newborn means the crying of the infant when he first comes out of the womb. The watchmen were just like dogs protecting a house.

### Text 2

*te tu tūrṇam upavrajya devakyā garbha-janma tat*  
*ācakhyur bhoja-rājāya yad udvignaḥ pratīkṣate*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, all the watchmen very quickly approached King Kaṁsa, the ruler of the Bhoja dynasty, and submitted the news of the birth of Devakī’s child to him. Kaṁsa had awaited this news very anxiously.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa being disturbed because it was the eighth (tad) birth, was waiting for this.

### Text 3

*sa talpāt tūrṇam utthāya kālo ’yam iti vihvalaḥ*  
*sūtī-gṛham agāt tūrṇaṁ praskhalan mukta-mūrdhajaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kaṁsa immediately got up from bed, thinking, “Death has come.” Thus overwhelmed with fear, Kaṁsa, his hair scattered on his head, stumbled as he quickly went to the place where the child had been born.**

**Комментарий:**

Out of fear, Kaṁsa was thinking that the birth of the child was his own death (kāla).

### Text 4

*tam āha bhrātaraṁ devī kṛpaṇā karuṇaṁ satī*  
*snuṣeyaṁ tava kalyāṇa striyaṁ mā hantum arhasi*

**Перевод:**

**Distraught Devakī spoke to her brother in a piteous manner: she will be the bride of your son. You should not kill a woman.**

**Комментарий:**

Devakī was beaming internally because she had been able to hide her son, and because she understood that the daughter of her friend will not be killed by Kaṁsa. Externally she behaved miserably.
