She spoke to invoke compassion. Expert at cheating Kaṁsa (satī), she spoke. O auspicious one! She is your daughter. She will be the bride (snuṣā) of your son. Do not commit the sin of killing a woman.

### Text 5

*bahavo hiṁsitā bhrātaḥ śiśavaḥ pāvakopamāḥ*  
*tvayā daiva-nisṛṣṭena putrikaikā pradīyatām*

**Перевод:**

**My dear brother, by the influence of destiny you have already killed many babies, each of them as bright and beautiful as fire. But kindly spare this daughter.**

**Комментарий:**

She indicates his cruelty by mentioning that he killed many babies. But worried she says, “It is my fate. It is not your fault.”

### Text 6

*nanv ahaṁ te hy avarajā dīnā hata-sutā prabho*  
*dātum arhasi mandāyā aṅgemāṁ caramāṁ prajām*

**Перевод:**

**My lord, my brother, I am suffering, being bereft of all my children, but still I am your younger sister, and therefore it would be worthy of you to give this unfortunate soul the last child, a girl.**

**Комментарий:**

I am your younger sister (avara-jā). You should give to me, most unfortunate (mandāyāḥ) this last child. Oh brother (aṅga)! Do not make my lap empty.

### Text 7

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*upaguhyātmajām evaṁ rudatyā dīna-dīnavat*  
*yācitas tāṁ vinirbhartsya hastād ācicchide khalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: requested by Devakī, crying miserably while hugging her child, cruel Kaṁsa scolded her and pulled the child from her hands.**

**Комментарий:**

Clasping the child who manifested the emotions of being her daughter to fool Kaṁsa, he snatched the child from the hands of Devakī, who was crying like most miserable person as she spoke. She was like a miserable person but in reality she was not like thatsince she had been pacified by the Lord and knew that the daughter was Devī. He scolded Devakī (tāṁ) though he was requested, “Give me this last child.” “You are deceptive, showing false affection for me. You desire to kill me through this eighth child.”

### Text 8

*tāṁ gṛhītvā caraṇayor jāta-mātrāṁ svasuḥ sutām*  
*apothayac chilā-pṛṣṭhe svārthonmūlita-sauhṛdaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Having uprooted all relationships with his sister because of intense selfishness, Kaṁsa grasped the newborn child of his sister by the legs and tried to dash her against the surface of a stone.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa threw the child down with great force (apothayat) so that its limbs would be crushed.

### Text 9

*sā tad-dhastāt samutpatya sadyo devy ambaraṁ gatā*  
*adṛśyatānujā viṣṇoḥ sāyudhāṣṭa-mahābhujā*

**Перевод:**

**The child, the younger sister of Viṣṇu, rose upward from Kaṁsa’s hands into the sky and was seen by Kaṁsa as Devī, the goddess Durgā, with eight arms, completely equipped with weapons.**

**Комментарий:**

The meaning is that though Yogamāyā was thrown to the ground, she forcefully leaped into the sky and kicked him on the head. This is because the Bhaviṣya-uttara Purāṇa says :

*kaṁsāsurasyottamāṅge pādaṁ dattvā gatā divam*

**Yogamāyā (Durgā) put her foot on Kaṁsa’s head as she went up into the sky.**

She is described here as the younger sister (anujā) of Kṛṣṇa, indicating that Kṛṣṇa was born from Yaśodā (and thus Yogamāyā is his sister). She held weapons in her eight arms to frighten Kaṁsa and to instill in him faith in her words.

### Texts 10-11

*divya-srag-ambarālepa-ratnābharaṇa-bhūṣitā*  
*dhanuḥ-śūleṣu-carmāsi-śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-dharā*

*siddha-cāraṇa-gandharvair apsaraḥ-kinnaroragaiḥ*  
*upāhṛtoru-balibhiḥ stūyamānedam abravīt*

**Перевод:**

**The goddess Durgā was decorated with flower garlands, smeared with sandalwood pulp and dressed with excellent garments and ornaments made of valuable jewels. Holding in her hands a bow, a trident, arrows, a shield, a sword, a conchshell, a disc and a club, and being praised by celestial beings like Apsarās, Kinnaras, Uragas, Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Gandharvas, who worshiped her with all kinds of presentations, she spoke as follows.**

### Text 12

*kiṁ mayā hatayā manda jātaḥ khalu tavānta-kṛt*  
*yatra kva vā pūrva-śatrur mā hiṁsīḥ kṛpaṇān vṛthā*

**Перевод:**

**O Kaṁsa, you fool, what will be the use of killing me? He who has been your enemy from a previous birth and who will certainly kill you has already taken his birth somewhere else. Therefore, do not unnecessarily kill other children.**

**Комментарий:**

The goddess Durgā said, “Even if you kill me, you still cannot prevent your own death.”

He who will kill you has already been born somewhere else (yatra kva vā), which cannot be revealed to you. It is a place where you cannot go. Do not kill timid children.

### Text 13

*iti prabhāṣya taṁ devī māyā bhagavatī bhuvi*  
*bahu-nāma-niketeṣu bahu-nāmā babhūva ha*

**Перевод:**

**After speaking to Kaṁsa in this way, the goddess Durgā appeared in different places and became celebrated by different names.**

**Комментарий:**

Māyādevī became famous by many names in different places such as Vārāṇasī (bahu-nāma-nikeṭeṣu).

### Text 14

*tayābhihitam ākarṇya kaṁsaḥ parama-vismitaḥ*  
*devakīṁ vasudevaṁ ca vimucya praśrito ’bravīt*

**Перевод:**

**After hearing the words of the goddess Durgā, Kaṁsa was struck with wonder. Thus he released Devakī and Vasudeva, and very humbly spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

In great astonishment, Kaṁsa thought, “How could a mere mortal like Devakī give birth to Durgā-devī?” Or he thought, “How could the message from the sky be false?”

### Text 15

*aho bhaginy aho bhāma mayā vāṁ bata pāpmanā*  
*puruṣāda ivāpatyaṁ bahavo hiṁsitāḥ sutāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Alas, my sister! Alas, my brother-in-law! I am indeed so sinful that exactly like a man-eater \[Rākṣasa\] who eats his own child, I have killed so many sons born of you.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhāma means husband of sister. Just as a rākṣasa (puruṣādaḥ) kills his own children, I have killed many of your sons.

### Text 16

*sa tv ahaṁ tyakta-kāruṇyas tyakta-jñāti-suhṛt khalaḥ*  
*kān lokān vai gamiṣyāmi brahma-heva mṛtaḥ śvasan*

**Перевод:**

**Being merciless and cruel, giving up my relatives and friends, to which planet will this rascal go? I am like a person who has killed a brāhmaṇa. I am dead while living.**

**Комментарий:**

Though breathing (śvasan) I am dead (mrtaḥ).

### Text 17

*daivam apy anṛtaṁ vakti na martyā eva kevalam*  
*yad-viśrambhād ahaṁ pāpaḥ svasur nihatavāñ chiśūn*

**Перевод:**

**Alas, not only human beings but sometimes even providence lies. And I am so sinful that I believed the omen of providence and killed so many of my sister’s children.**

### Text 18

*mā śocataṁ mahā-bhāgāv ātmajān sva-kṛtaṁ bhujaḥ*  
*jāntavo na sadaikatra daivādhīnās tadāsate*

**Перевод:**

**O fortunate couple! Do not lament for your children who suffered because of their karmas. All jīvas, controlled by fate, never stay in one place forever.**

**Комментарий:**

O fortunate ones! Durgā-devī has come as your daughter, what is the use of those sons who are reaping their karmas. Thinking like this, do not lament. After considering this, he again speaks. Living entities cannot remain together for very long.

### Text 19

*bhuvi bhaumāni bhūtāni yathā yānty apayānti ca*  
*nāyam ātmā tathaiteṣu viparyeti yathaiva bhūḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In this world, we can see that pots, dolls and other products of the earth appear, break and then disappear, mixing with the earth. Similarly, the bodies of all conditioned living entities are annihilated, but the living entities, like the earth itself, are unchanging and never annihilated.**

**Комментарий:**

Lamentation should be removed by distinguishing ātmā from the body. The way in which objects like pots made of earth come fromearth and merge with earth, like that the ātmā, which understands that this is the self, does not undergo transformation (viparyeti) while there is transformation in bodies (eteṣu) in the form of creation and destruction, just as earth does not transform, though objects made of earth do. Similarly, your sons’ bodies are destroyed but not their ātmās. Thus do not lament.

*svapne yathā paśyati deham īdṛśaṁ*  
*manorathenābhiniviṣṭa-cetanaḥ*  
*dṛṣṭa-śrutābhyāṁ manasānucintayan*  
*prapadyate tat kim api hy apasmṛtiḥ*

**Just as by mental adjustments one dreams at night of living under different circumstances, in different bodies, and forgets his actual position, in waking state also, having experienced a situation by seeing or hearing about it, one contemplates and speculates about that situation, and thus one thinks of that, forgetting his present body. (SB** [**10.1.41**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.41)**)**

However, even dehātma-vāda (the idea that body is the self) is accepted by the demons, since the demons have wavering intelligence.

### Text 20

*yathānevaṁ-vido bhedo yata ātma-viparyayaḥ*  
*deha-yoga-viyogau ca saṁsṛtir na nivartate*

**Перевод:**

**The ignorant person who thinks the body is the ātmā sees different ātmās and, separating and joining different bodies, undergoes saṁsāra.**

**Комментарий:**

Those who do not properly (yathā) know the ātmā, which is different from the body (anevaṁ-vidaḥ), think that body and self are non-different. Because of this thinking, saṁsāra consisting of birth and death (deha-yoga-viyogau), wich are contrary to the ātmā,does not cease. But when one understands that the ātmā is different from the body, saṁsāra ceases since birth and death are both absent for the ātmā.

### Text 21

*tasmād bhadre sva-tanayān mayā vyāpāditān api*  
*mānuśoca yataḥ sarvaḥ sva-kṛtaṁ vindate ’vaśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O intelligent Devakī! Do not lament for your sons who were killed by me, since all beings suffer their karmas though they do not desire them.**

**Комментарий:**

Since body is not ātmā, do not lament for the bodies which are accepted with the conception of being sons, killed by me, thinking they are destructible.

“Though it is true that the ātmā is different from the body, they are my sons by connection with my body and give me joy. By destroying their bodies, my joy is destroyed.”

Their karma was like that due which they died at my hands. Thus do not find fault with me.

### Text 22

*yāvad dhato ’smi hantāsmīty ātmānaṁ manyate ’sva-dṛk*  
*tāvat tad-abhimāny ajño bādhya-bādhakatām iyāt*

**Перевод:**

**As long as one does not realize the ātmā and thinks, “I am being killed” or “I have killed my enemies” he ignorantly continues the relationship of oppressor and oppressed.**

**Комментарий:**

Actually, I am not the killer of your sons. As long as one thinks of oneself, who is eternal, with the conception of being non-different from the temporary body, as, “I am the object of killing,” (hato’smi) or thinks “I am independent in killing the body of my enemy,”(hantāsmi) though he subservient to the Lord in the form of time, he continues to suffer. But everything is dependent on time. Balisays:

*kālaḥ sarvaṁ samādatte kālaḥ sarvaṁ prayacchati*  
*kālena vihitaṁ sarvaṁ mākṛthāḥ śatru-pauruṣam*

**Time takes away and gives everything. Time supplies everything. Do not act boldly against your enemy. (Mokṣa- dharma)**

The person who do not know the true nature of ātmā (asva-dṛk), who does not know the independence of time (ajñaḥ), will undergosaṁsāra with the conceptions of killer and being killed (bādya- bādhakatām). Thus, your sons’ bodies were destroyed by time, not by me.

### Text 23

*kṣamadhvaṁ mama daurātmyaṁ sādhavo dīna-vatsalāḥ*  
*ity uktvāśru-mukhaḥ pādau śyālaḥ svasror athāgrahīt*

**Перевод:**

**Kaṁsa begged, “Please be merciful to such a poor-hearted person as me, since both of you are saintly persons with good conduct.” Having said this, Kaṁsa immediately grasped the feet of Vasudeva and Devakī, his eyes full of tears.**

**Комментарий:**

Still if you allege that I am the killer of your sons and excessively lament, then it is true that I am wicked. The atonement for my sin is your mercy. Thus Kaṁsa says to Vasudeva and Devakī, “Please forgive me.” Kaṁsa (śyālaḥ) grasped a foot each of his sister andher husband (svasroḥ). Svasroḥ is a dual form of the word svasṛ (sister) since it is an eka-śeṣa compound where one svasṛ indicates sister (Devakī) and another svasṛ figuratively indicates husband of sister (Vasudeva).

### Text 24

*mocayām āsa nigaḍād viśrabdhaḥ kanyakā-girā*  
*devakīṁ vasudevaṁ ca darśayann ātma-sauhṛdam*

**Перевод:**

**Fully believing in the words of the goddess Durgā, Kaṁsa exhibited his familial affection for Devakī and Vasudeva by immediately releasing them from their iron shackles.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa showed his friendship with affectionate words and released Vasudeva and Devakī from their iron shackles (nigaḍād).

### Text 25

*bhrātuḥ samanutaptasya kṣānta-roṣā ca devakī*  
*vyasṛjad vasudevaś ca prahasya tam uvāca ha*

**Перевод:**

**When Devakī saw her brother repentant she forgave him and was relieved of all anger and lamentation. Vasudeva spoke to Kaṁsa with a smile.**

**Комментарий:**

Devakī forgave Kaṁsa for his offenses and gave up her anger and lamentation.

### Text 26

*evam etan mahā-bhāga yathā vadasi dehinām*  
*ajñāna-prabhavāhaṁ-dhīḥ sva-pareti bhidā yataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O most fortunate Kaṁsa! Just as you have said, by the influence of ignorance does one accept the material body as the self, and because of this one thinks of self and others.**

**Комментарий:**

The conception of ‘I’ arises from the body which is the source of ignorance of the independence of the Lord and ignorance of the difference between ātmā and the body. From this arises the distinctions of “This is my house and money and this is someone else’s.” Thus, saṁsāra arises. Actually, one has no independence and no possessions since house and money are under the control of the Lord.

### Text 27

*śoka-harṣa-bhaya-dveṣa-lobha-moha-madānvitāḥ*  
*mitho ghnantaṁ na paśyanti bhāvair bhāvaṁ pṛthag-dṛśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Persons with material vision, imbued with the material qualities lamentation, jubilation, fear, envy, greed, illusion and madness, do not know the truth about killing, in which one entity is killed by others.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of being independent and possessive is described. Endowed with lamentation, etc., perceiving externals (pṛthag- dṛṣaḥ), low people do not know the independent Lord (bhāvaṁ) who causes entities to be killed (ghnantaṁ) by enemies, weapons, fire and water, etc., which are just instrumental causes (bhāvaiḥ). But they think, “I am independent. I kill him.”

### Text 28

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*kaṁsa evaṁ prasannābhyāṁ viśuddhaṁ pratibhāṣitaḥ*  
*devakī-vasudevābhyām anujñāto ’viśad gṛham*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Thus having been addressed in purity by Devakī and Vasudeva, who were very much appeased, Kaṁsa felt pleased, and with their permission he entered his home.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva and Devakī spoke very sincerely (viśuddhaṁ) to Kaṁsa with pleasing words.

### Text 29

*tasyāṁ rātryāṁ vyatītāyāṁ kaṁsa āhūya mantriṇaḥ*  
*tebhya ācaṣṭa tat sarvaṁ yad uktaṁ yoga-nidrayā*

**Перевод:**

**After that night passed, Kaṁsa summoned his ministers and informed them of all that had been spoken by Durgā.**

### Text 30

*ākarṇya bhartur gaditaṁ tam ūcur deva-śatravaḥ*  
*devān prati kṛtāmarṣā daiteyā nāti-kovidāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After hearing their master’s statement, the envious asuras, who were enemies of the demigods and were not very expert in their dealings, advised Kaṁsa as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

The demons were not skillful in giving advice (nāti-kovidāḥ). Ati (in nāti) indicates that they were not perfect.

### Text 31

*evaṁ cet tarhi bhojendra pura-grāma-vrajādiṣu*  
*anirdaśān nirdaśāṁś ca haniṣyāmo ’dya vai śiśūn*

**Перевод:**

**If this is so, O King of the Bhoja dynasty, beginning from today, we shall kill all the children born within the past ten days or less, in all the villages, towns and pasturing grounds.**

**Комментарий:**

Anirdaśān means children less than ten days old. Nirdaśān refers to children more than ten days old.

### Text 32

*kim udyamaiḥ kariṣyanti devāḥ samara-bhīravaḥ*  
*nityam udvigna-manaso jyā-ghoṣair dhanuṣas tava*

**Перевод:**

**What can the devatās do, since they are always fearful of the sound of your bowstring and are afraid of fighting?**

**Комментарий:**

“But the devatās are eager to kill me. What should be done to counteract them?” This verse answers.

### Text 33

*asyatas te śara-vrātair hanyamānāḥ samantataḥ*  
*jijīviṣava utsṛjya palāyana-parā yayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**While being pierced by your arrows, which you discharged on all sides, some of them, who were injured by the multitude of arrows but who desired to live, fled the battlefield, intent on escaping.**

**Комментарий:**

Being struck by the arrows of you, who were shooting them (asyataḥ), the demigods fled (utsṛjya) the battlefield. Kaṁsa’s heroism and conquest are described in Hari-vaṁśa.

### Text 34

*kecit prāñjalayo dīnā nyasta-śastrā divaukasaḥ*  
*mukta-kaccha-śikhāḥ kecid bhītāḥ sma iti vādinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Bereft of all weapons, some of the suffering devatās folded their hands on their heads. Some, with loosened garments and hair, said, “O lord, we are afraid of you.”**

### Text 35

*na tvaṁ vismṛta-śastrāstrān virathān bhaya-saṁvṛtān*  
*haṁsy anyāsakta-vimukhān bhagna-cāpān ayudhyataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the devatās are bereft of their chariots, when they forget how to use weapons, when they are fearful or when they are fighting with someone else, or when they are fleeing from battle, or when their bows are broken and they have thus lost the ability to fight, Your Majesty does not kill them.**

**Комментарий:**

Your sense of dharma is the cause of the devatās’ increase in strength. You do not kill those who are fighting with someone else (anyāsaktān) and flee the battle (vimukhān). You are a great warrior. Now your sense of dharma has to be rejected. This is not the time for it.

### Text 36

*kiṁ kṣema-śūrair vibudhair asaṁyuga-vikatthanaiḥ*  
*raho-juṣā kiṁ hariṇā śambhunā vā vanaukasā*  
*kim indreṇālpa-vīryeṇa brahmaṇā vā tapasyatā*

**Перевод:**

**The devatās boast uselessly while away from the battlefield. Only when there is no fighting can they show their prowess. As for Viṣṇu, he is in seclusion in the core of the hearts of the yogīs. As for Śiva, he has gone to the forest. And as for Brahmā, he is always engaged in austerities. Indra is devoid of prowess.**

**Комментарий:**

But we are not afraid of the devatās at any time. This is expressed in three lines. What is the use of devatās who show bravery in safeplaces without combat (kṣema) and boast about themselves when at the side of women, away from battle (asaṁyuga)? We have no fear of Viṣṇu or Śiva. Viṣṇu is in the heart (raho-juṣā). We never see him outside. Śiva lives in the Ilāvṛta forest devoid of entrance to men (vanaukasā). If he has strength, he should come out and fight with us.

### Text 37

*tathāpi devāḥ sāpatnyān nopekṣyā iti manmahe*  
*tatas tan-mūla-khanane niyuṅkṣvāsmān anuvratān*

**Перевод:**

**Nonetheless, because of their enmity, our opinion is that the devatās should not be neglected. To uproot their source, engage us, for we are ready to follow you.**

**Комментарий:**

The demons said to Kaṁsa, “Though the devatās are weak, still because they are the enemy they cannot be neglected.” This is according to Nītī-sāstra (civic laws).

### Text 38

*yathāmayo ’ṅge samupekṣito nṛbhir*  
*na śakyate rūḍha-padaś cikitsitum*  
*yathendriya-grāma upekṣitas tathā*  
*ripur mahān baddha-balo na cālyate*

**Перевод:**

**As a disease, if initially neglected, becomes acute and impossible to cure, or as the senses, if not controlled at first, are impossible to control later, an enemy, if neglected in the beginning, later becomes insurmountable.**

**Комментарий:**

Two examples are given to nourish not neglecting the devatās. As a disease in the body becomes acute (rūḍha-padaḥ) when neglected and as senses not brought under control by the yogīs in the beginning become uncontrollable, so the enemy becomes unconquerable.

### Text 39

*mūlaṁ hi viṣṇur devānāṁ yatra dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ*  
*tasya ca brahma-go-viprās tapo yajñāḥ sa-dakṣiṇāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The foundation of all the devatās is Viṣṇu, who lives wherever there is dharma. The foundation of dharma are the Vedas, cows, brāhmaṇas, austerities, and sacrifices with proper remuneration.**

**Комментарий:**

The root of the devatās is Lord Viṣṇu. Viṣṇu resides where there is dharma. The root of dharma is Vedas (brahma), etc.

### Text 40

*tasmāt sarvātmanā rājan brāhmaṇān brahma-vādinaḥ*  
*tapasvino yajña-śīlān gāś ca hanmo havir-dughāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King, we shall therefore make all attempts to kill the Vedic brāhmaṇas, the persons engaged in offering sacrifices and austerities, and the cows that supply milk, from which clarified butter is obtained for the ingredients of sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

Among them, by killing the brāhmaṇas, all of them will perish. Moreover clarified butter is the cause of sacrifices and cows are the cause of clarified butter. The cows should also be killed.

### Text 41

*viprā gāvaś ca vedāś ca tapaḥ satyaṁ damaḥ śamaḥ*  
*śraddhā dayā titikṣā ca kratavaś ca hares tanūḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇas, the cows, Vedic knowledge, austerity, truthfulness, control of the mind and senses, faith, mercy, tolerance and sacrifice are the different parts of the body of Viṣṇu.**

**Комментарий:**

Brāhmaṇas, etc., are the images (tanūḥ) of the Lord for the purpose of worship. With no worship by the brāhmaṇas, the Lord becoming weak will die.

### Text 42

*sa hi sarva-surādhyakṣo hy asura-dviḍ guhā-śayaḥ*  
*tan-mūlā devatāḥ sarvāḥ seśvarāḥ sa-catur-mukhāḥ*  
*ayaṁ vai tad-vadhopāyo yad ṛṣīṇāṁ vihiṁsanam*

**Перевод:**

**Viṣṇu, residing in the heart, is the ultimate enemy of the demons and is the leader of all the devatās because all the devatās, including Śiva and Brahmā, survive under his protection. To persecute the brāhmaṇas is the only way to kill Viṣṇu.**

**Комментарий:**

Though Viṣṇu resides in the hearts of all beings, he is the leader of the devatās. He favors them and kills the demons. He is the root of the devatās. By afflicting the sages, everyone will follow the demons, since there will be no continuation of tradition (of encouraging others to follow him).

### Text 43

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*evaṁ durmantribhiḥ kaṁsaḥ saha sammantrya durmatiḥ*  
*brahma-hiṁsāṁ hitaṁ mene kāla-pāśāvṛto ’suraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Thus, having considered the instructions of his bad ministers, Kaṁsa, who was bound by the laws of Yamarāja and devoid of good intelligence because he was a demon, decided to persecute the saintly persons, the brāhmaṇas, as the only way to achieve his own good fortune.**

**Комментарий:**

He had bad ministers like Pralamba.

### Text 44

*sandiśya sādhu-lokasya kadane kadana-priyān*  
*kāma-rūpa-dharān dikṣu dānavān gṛham āviśat*

**Перевод:**

**These demons, the followers of Kaṁsa, were expert at persecuting others, especially the Vaiṣṇavas, and could assume any form they desired. After giving these demons permission to go everywhere and persecute the saintly persons, Kaṁsa entered his palace.**

### Text 45

*te vai rajaḥ-prakṛtayas tamasā mūḍha-cetasaḥ*  
*satāṁ vidveṣam ācerur ārād āgata-mṛtyavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Surcharged with passion and not knowing what was good or bad for them due to ignorance, the asuras, for whom impending death was waiting, began the persecution of the saintly persons.**

**Комментарий:**

They would soon be approached by death in the form of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 46

*āyuḥ śriyaṁ yaśo dharmaṁ lokān āśiṣa eva ca*  
*hanti śreyāṁsi sarvāṇi puṁso mahad-atikramaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, when a man persecutes great souls, all his benedictions of longevity, beauty, fame, religion, blessings and promotion to higher planets will be destroyed.**

**Комментарий:**

Those who hate saintly persons will have all their good fortune destroyed, including going to Svarga (lokān).

## Chapter 5 - The Meeting of Nanda Mahārāja and Vasudeva

### Texts 1-2

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*nandas tv ātmaja utpanne jātāhlādo mahā-manāḥ*  
*āhūya viprān veda-jñān snātaḥ śucir alaṅkṛtaḥ*

*vācayitvā svastyayanaṁ jāta-karmātmajasya vai*  
*kārayām āsa vidhivat pitṛ-devārcanaṁ tathā*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Nanda Mahārāja was naturally very magnanimous, and when Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa appeared as his son, he was overwhelmed by jubilation. Therefore, after bathing and purifying himself and dressing himself properly, he invited brāhmaṇas who knew how to recite Vedic mantras. After having these qualified brāhmaṇas recite auspicious Vedic hymns, he arranged to have the Vedic birth ceremony celebrated for his newborn child according to the rules and regulations, and he also arranged for worship of the devatās and pitṛs.**

**Комментарий:**

*sūnor janmotsavaṁ kṛtvā vrajeśo mathurām agāt \|*  
*śauriṇā tatra saṁlāpaṁ vyadhād ityāha pañcame*

**This chapter describes that after perfoming the festivities at Kṛṣṇa’s birth, Nanda goes to Mathurā and converses with Vasudeva.**

Śukadeva, king of sages, controlled by the desire of the Lord, having spoken of the birth of Kṛṣṇa at Nanda’s house in a secret way, controlled by the desire of the devotee, describes the Lord’s birth festival in two verses by revealing it. The word tu indicates a different subject. Though Vasudeva was joyful when his son was born, he could not celebrate because he was in prison. But he gave ten thousand cows in his mind. But (tu) Nanda, a great-soul, when he heard from people in the inner chambers that a son was born, became joyful. He called the brāhmaṇas like Bhāguri who knew the Vedas. Bathing with shower of water and joy, by putting on tilaka, doing ācamana, he became especially pure (śuciḥ). He put on valuable ornaments (alaṅkṛtaḥ) and had the jāta-karma of his son performed according to the rules. Thus by this element Vasudeva and Nanda are different. Joy was born (jātāhlādaḥ) along with the birth of the son. This indicates sahokti-alaṅkāra. By that device, utprekṣālaṅkāra is indicated to say he (the son) was born. Rest is clear. Ātmajā is mentioned twice to show clearly that he was the physical son of Nanda. This will be repeated many times after elaborating through statements such as:

*yaśodāyāḥ sutodbhavaṁ*

**The birth as Yaśodā’s son. (SB** [**10.5.9**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/5.9)**)**

*sva-putrasyodayāya*

**For the auspiciousness of his son, (Nanda performed many rituals). (SB** [**10.5.16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/5.16)**)**

*nandaḥ sva-putram ādāya*

**Nanda Mahārāj took his own son onto his lap. (SB** [**10.6.43**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/6.43)**)**

### Text 3

*dhenūnāṁ niyute prādād viprebhyaḥ samalaṅkṛte*  
*tilādrīn sapta ratnaugha-śātakaumbhāmbarāvṛtān*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja gave two million cows, completely decorated with cloth and jewels, in charity to the brāhmaṇas. He also gave them seven hills of grain, covered with jewels and with cloth decorated with golden embroidery.**

**Комментарий:**

Then the charity of Nanda who was blissful is described.

Niyute (dual of niyuta) means twenty times one hundred thousand i.e. two million. Kṣīrasvāmī says:

*ekaṁ daśa-śata-sahasrāṇy ayutaṁ*  
*prayutākhya-lakṣam atha niyutam*

**One, ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, and a hundred thousand, then a niyuta is a million.**

According to Bāskarācārya, a niyuta is prayuta or a hundred thousand. The cows were nicely decorated (samalaṅkṛte) as described in Hemādri’s Dāna-khaṇḍa:

*daśa-sauvarṇike śṛṅge khurāḥ pañca-palānivitāḥ pañcāśat palikaṁ pṛṣṭhaṁ pucche muktā-vibhūṣitāṁ svarṇa-śṛṅgīṁ raupya-khurīṁ tāmra-pṛṣṭha-vibhūsitāṁ sa-vatsām vastra-sahitāṁ sa-ghantāṁ kāṁsya-dohanīm ūdhasvatīm roga-hīnāṁ su-śṛṅgīṁ ca mahoharāṁ*  
*evaṁ gāṁ yo naro dadyāt sa suraiḥ saha modate*

**The cow should have horn weighing ten sauvarṇikas and hooves weighing five palas. The back should fifty palas. The tail should be ornamented with pearls. The horns should be capped with gold and hooves with silver. Copper should ornament its back. The cow should be with calf and decorated with cloth, with bells and a bell-metal milking bucket. The cow should be giving milk and free of disease, should be attractive, with fine horns. If a man gives this type of cow, he enjoys with the devatās. (Hemādri, Dāna- khaṇḍa)**

Other gifts are mentioned. He gave mountains of sesame seed, covered with piles of jewels (ratnaugha) and gold embroidered cloth (śāta-kaumbhambara) in every courtyard.

The Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa describes this as follows:

*uttamo daśabhir drauṇair madhyamaṁ pañcabhir mataḥ tribhiḥ kaniṣṭho rājendra tila-śailaḥ prakīrtitaḥ pūrvavac cāparaṁ sarvaṁ viṣkambha-parvatādikam*

**O King! First-class tilādrī is ten droṇas, second-class tilādrī is five droṇas and third-class tilādrī is three droṇas. The latter ones, like the previous ones, are all like the Viṣkambha mountains. (Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa 4.199.17-18)**

This is described there in the context of mountains of grains:

itthaṁ niveśyāmara-śailam agryam atas tu viṣkambha-girīn krameṇa turīya-bhagena caturdiśaṁ ca saṁsthāpayet puṣpa-vilepanādyān

In this way, placing the foremost divine mountain, one should establish mountain ranges in four parts in the four directions, covered with flowers and sandalwood. (Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa 4.195.20)

The four mountains are Mandara, Merumandara, Supārśva and Kumuda (SB [5.16.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/16.11)). They are described there:

*merur mahān vrīhi-mayaś ca madhye suvarṇa-vṛkṣa-traya-saṁyutaḥ*  
*syāt pūrveṇa muktāphala-vajra-yukto yāmyena gomedaka-puṣpa-rāgaiḥ*  
*ca gārutmata-nīla-ratnaiḥ saumye ca vaidūrya-saroja-rāgaiḥ*  
*brahmātha viṣṇur bhagavān purārir divākaro’py atra hiraṇmayaḥ syāt*

**In the middle a Meru Mountain of rice should be there, decorated with three gold trees. In the east should be pearls and diamonds. In the south should be gomedhas (garnet) and yellow sapphires. In the west should be emeralds and sapphires. In the north should be cat’s eye gems and rubies. There also should a deities of Brahmā, Bhagavān Viṣṇu, Śiva and also the sun, made of gold.**

*śuklāmbarāṇy ambu-dharāvalī syāt pūrveṇa kṛṣṇāni ca dakṣiṇena vāsāṁsi paścād atha karburāṇi raktāni caivottarato ghanāni*

**There should be white cloth in the east, black cloth in the south, multicolor cloth in the west and deep red cloth in the north. (Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa 4.195.15-18)**

The piles were covered with gold cloth to resemble Sumeru. A droṇa is described.

*khārī-droṇāḍhaka-prasthāḥ kuḍavaṁ ca palaṁ picuḥ sāṇako māṣakaś caiva yathā pūrvam caturguṇāḥ*

**The droṇa, āḍhaka, prasthā, kuḍava, pala, picu (karṣa), śāṇaka and māṣaka are from last to first, quadruple in quantity.**

### Text 4

*kālena snāna-śaucābhyāṁ saṁskārais tapasejyayā*  
*śudhyanti dānaiḥ santuṣṭyā dravyāṇy ātmātma-vidyayā*

**Перевод:**

**O King, by the passing of time, land and other material possessions are purified; by bathing, the body is purified; and by being cleansed, unclean things are purified. By purificatory ceremonies, birth is purified; by austerity, the senses are purified; and by worship and charity offered to the brāhmaṇas, material possessions are purified. By satisfaction, the mind is purified; and by self-realization, the soul is purified.**

**Комментарий:**

In the jāta-karma accompanied by various charities, examples are given concerning purification of birth using dīpaka alaṅkāra. Articles are purified by time and other means. Time purifies contaminated earth. Bathing purifies the body; scrubbing purifies limbs smeared with contaminating substances; Vedic saṁskāras purify birth; austerity purifies the senses; yajñas purify the three upper varṇas: charity purifies received grains; satisfaction purifies the mind, and knowledge of ātmā purifies the jīva (ātmā). Sincesaṁskāras are necessary for purifying birth, those saṁkāras must be performed.

### Text 5

*saumaṅgalya-giro viprāḥ sūta-māgadha-vandinaḥ*  
*gāyakāś ca jagur nedur bheryo dundubhayo muhuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇas recited auspicious Vedic hymns, which purified the environment by their vibration. The experts in reciting old histories like the Purāṇas, the experts in reciting the histories of royal families, and general reciters all chanted, while singers sang and many kinds of musical instruments, like bherīs and dundubhis, played in accompaniment.**

**Комментарий:**

Then the brāhmaṇas gave blessings (saumaṅgalya-giraḥ). The sūtas and others sang. Drums constantly sounded at Nanda’s palace-gate and on the roof top because of the occasion of great festival.

### Text 6

*vrajaḥ sammṛṣṭa-saṁsikta-dvārājira-gṛhāntaraḥ*  
*citra-dhvaja-patākā-srak-caila-pallava-toraṇaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Vraja, whose doors, courtyards and interiors were thoroughly cleansed and moistened, was fully decorated with varieties of festoons and flags, and in different places, hung with varieties of flower garlands, flags, pieces of cloth, mango leaves.**

**Комментарий:**

First the doors, courtyards, and interiors of houses, etc., of Vraja were washed and then sprinkled with water of sandalwood, uśīraand rose. Vraja was decorated with colorful flags and banners with arches having colorful garlands, cloth, and branches, and with sandalwood garlands.

### Text 7

*gāvo vṛṣā vatsatarā haridrā-taila-rūṣitāḥ*  
*vicitra-dhātu-barhasrag-vastra-kāñcana-mālinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cows, the bulls and the calves were thoroughly smeared with a mixture of turmeric and oil, mixed with varieties of minerals. Their heads were bedecked with peacock feathers, and they were garlanded and covered with cloth and golden ornaments.**

**Комментарий:**

The beauty of the cows, etc., is described. Their horns were smeared (ruṣitāḥ) with oil mixed with turmeric. They had colorful minerals, peacock feather garlands, colorful cloth and golden garlands as decorations.

### Text 8

*mahārha-vastrābharaṇa-kañcukoṣṇīṣa-bhūṣitāḥ*  
*gopāḥ samāyayū rājan nānopāyana-pāṇayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King Parīkṣit, the cowherd men dressed very opulently with valuable ornaments and garments such as coats and turbans. Decorated in this way and carrying various presentations in their hands, they approached the house of Nanda Mahārāja.**

**Комментарий:**

The cowherds, decorated with very valuable cloth and ornaments and equal to King Nanda, defeated even Indra by their splendor. They held various gifts like valuable jewels in their hands.

### Text 9

*gopyaś cākarṇya muditā yaśodāyāḥ sutodbhavam*  
*ātmānaṁ bhūṣayāṁ cakrur vastrākalpāñjanādibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The wives of the cowherd men overjoyed, on hearing that mother Yaśodā had given birth to a son, began to decorate themselves with proper dresses, ornaments, black ointment for the eyes, and so on.**

**Комментарий:**

Gopyaś refers to the women equal to Yaśodā beginning with her sisters-in-law. They decorated themselves with cloth, etc. They wore fine embroidered silk cloth, jewelled earrings, necklaces, bracelets and anklets. The tips of their noses shone due to the glitter of large pearls. Their eyes were anointed with collyrium. They defeated Śacī, queen of heaven by their beauty.

### Text 10

*nava-kuṅkuma-kiñjalka-mukha-paṅkaja-bhūtayaḥ*  
*balibhis tvaritaṁ jagmuḥ pṛthu-śroṇyaś calat-kucāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Their lotus-like faces were more beautiful than lotus pollen. The wives of the cowherd men hurried to the house of mother Yaśodā with presentations in their hands with wide hips and moving breasts.**

**Комментарий:**

Their lotus faces were more beautiful than the fresh saffron from lotus filaments (kiñjalka). They held in their left hands gifts of gold coins, jewelled necklaces, valuable cloth and coconuts, unbroken dūrva grass, sandalwood and flower garlands on gold plates covered with cloth. They came quickly, and thus their breasts moved.

### Text 11

*gopyaḥ sumṛṣṭa-maṇi-kuṇḍala-niṣka-kaṇṭhyaś*  
*citrāmbarāḥ pathi śikhā-cyuta-mālya-varṣāḥ*  
*nandālayaṁ sa-valayā vrajatīr virejur*  
*vyālola-kuṇḍala-payodhara-hāra-śobhāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In the ears of the gopīs were brilliantly polished jeweled earrings, and from their necks hung metal lockets. Their hands were decorated with bangles, their dresses were of varied colors, and from their hair, flowers fell onto the street like showers. Thus while going to the house of Mahārāja Nanda, the gopīs, their earrings, breasts and garlands moving, were brilliantly beautiful.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the beauty of the gopīs has been described already, because he felt somewhat unsatisfied with that description alone because of their great devotion, Śukadeva elaborates further.

They wore polished jeweled earrings in their ears and niṣkas on their necks. Their chests where decorated with jeweled medallions.Flowers from garlands tied to the tips of their dressed hair showered. Their hair, pleased with their gait, offered garlands to their feet. This is utprekṣā alaṅkāra. Walking, they went to Nanda’s house (nandālayam). Ālaya means the mind of those who see the place, rests there. Its pillars were made of vaidūrya gems. The eaves of the roof were made of gold. The lattice-windows were made of diamonds. The roof pavilions shone with crystal. It was decorated with many huge enclosures. The beautiful walls were glorious with huge decorative tops. The many courtyards touched disk of the moon by their broad expanse. There were colorful flags flying. There were attractive gardens which had jeweled wells. It was filled with attractive people and situated on the bank of the Yamunā. It had this beauty because of chief cowherd’s houses. This is the meaning since it was the king’s house and the residence of the Lord and since Brahmā says:

*cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vṛkṣa- lakṣāvṛteṣu surabhīr abhipālayantam*

**Govinda herds cows in Vraja filled with houses having cintāmaṇi walls, surrounded by thousands of desire trees. (Brahma-saṁhitā** [**5.29**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/5.29)**)**

### Text 12

*tā āśiṣaḥ prayuñjānāś ciraṁ pāhīti bālake*  
*haridrā-cūrṇa-tailādbhiḥ siñcantyo ’janam ujjaguḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Offering blessings to the newborn child, Kṛṣṇa, the wives and daughters of the cowherd men said, “May you long maintain us.” They sprinkled a mixture of turmeric powder, oil and water upon each other.**

**Комментарий:**

Entering the maternity ward, the Vraja-gopīs said, “Becoming the crown prince may you protect us for a long time, since you are the son of a king.”

Then going outside, the elderly gopīs celebrated Kṛṣṇa’s birth by singing auspicious songs loudly and sprinkling each other with a mixture of fragrant oil, water and turmeric. Others interpret that they praised the Lord (ajanam).

### Text 13

*avādyanta vicitrāṇi vāditrāṇi mahotsave*  
*kṛṣṇe viśveśvare ’nante nandasya vrajam āgate*

**Перевод:**

**Now that the unlimited Lord Kṛṣṇa, the master of the cosmic manifestation, had arrived within the estate of Mahārāja Nanda, various types of musical instruments resounded to celebrate the greatest festival.**

**Комментарий:**

The music sounded everywhere because Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the universe came to Nanda’s house. The music was also unlimited because the Lord is unlimited (anante). The music was of various sorts (vicitrāni), with stringed instruments, wind instruments,metallic instruments and drums, rare even for the Indra.

### Text 14

*gopāḥ parasparaṁ hṛṣṭā dadhi-kṣīra-ghṛtāmbubhiḥ*  
*āsiñcanto vilimpanto navanītaiś ca cikṣipuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In joy the cowherd men sprinkled each other with a mixture of yogurt, milk, ghee and water and then smeared each other with butter and threw butter everywhere.**

**Комментарий:**

For fun the gopas energetically threw milk, yogurt, ghee and water on each other, and, being covered with it, slipped (cikṣipuḥ).

### Texts 15-16

*nando mahā-manās tebhyo vāso ’laṅkāra-go-dhanam*  
*sūta-māgadha-vandibhyo ye ’nye vidyopajīvinaḥ*

*tais taiḥ kāmair adīnātmā yathocitam apūjayat*  
*viṣṇor ārādhanārthāya sva-putrasyodayāya ca*

**Перевод:**

**The great-minded Mahārāja Nanda gave clothing, ornaments and cows in charity to the cowherd men in order to please Lord Viṣṇu, and thus he improved the condition of his own son in all respects. He distributed charity to the sūtas, the māgadhas, the vandīs, and men of all other professions, according to their educational qualifications, and satisfied everyone’s desires.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Seated on an attractive throne in meeting hall made of gems, surrounded by paternal and maternal relatives,shining like Indra, generous Nanda gave gifts to the cowherds and sūtas, etc. He gave to those other than them (anye), who made aliving by dancing, singing and playing instruments (vidyopajīvinaḥ), who taught parrots and śārika birds to recite, who taught cuckoos, peacocks, cranes and swans, those who were very skillful with monkeys performing stunts, and comedians. All these gathered from various places at Kṛṣṇa’s birth festival. Whatever was desired or asked (tais taiḥ kāmaiḥ) by them he gave.

Nanda Mahārāja gave suitably according to the level of one’s knowledge and reputation. Or he worshipped those worthy of worship with his own hands and worshipped others through his servants. He was most generous (adhinātmā). The statement is repeated (mahāmanāḥ). This indicates that, opening the locks on the treasury, with his relatives seeing people plundering the treasure, he stood there laughing. The result of giving is described. The result (arthāya) of worship of Viṣṇu was satisfaction of Viṣṇu for the welfare (udayāya) of his son since his abundant affection for his son had manifested.

### Text 17

*rohiṇī ca mahā-bhāgā nanda-gopābhinanditā*  
*vyacarad divya-vāsa-srak-kaṇṭhābharaṇa-bhūṣitā*

**Перевод:**

**The most fortunate Rohiṇī, the mother of Baladeva, honored by Nanda Mahārāja and Yaśodā, and dressed with valuable necklaces, garlands and cloth, was busily moving about.**

**Комментарий:**

Rohiṇī was more fortunate than Vasudeva’s other wives since she could attend the celebrations at the birth of Kṛṣṇa and her son Balarāma. She was honored by King Nanda (nanda-gopa). The word gopa also means king according to the Amara-kośa dictionary. “My son was born because of the auspiciousness of your coming here.” In this way he praised her. She was decorated with cloth, etc., given by Yaśodā.

Absorbed in the bliss of celebrating Kṛṣṇa’s birth, welcoming the women who had gathered, Rohiṇī forgot about her sorrow due to separation from her husband and over her husband’s condition in prison.

### Text 18

*tata ārabhya nandasya vrajaḥ sarva-samṛddhimān*  
*harer nivāsātma-guṇai ramākrīḍam abhūn nṛpa*

**Перевод:**

**O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, the home of Nanda Mahārāja is eternally the abode of the Supreme Lord and his qualities and is therefore always naturally endowed with all wealth. Yet beginning from Kṛṣṇa’s appearance there, it became the place for the pastimes of the goddess of fortune.**

**Комментарий:**

The birth of Lord Kṛṣṇa from Nanda in Vraja was secretly revealed. In a similarly way, Śukadeva states in this verse that Rādhā andother gopīs took birth there from Vṛṣabhānu and others. Nanda’s Vraja was most prosperous with the qualities of the svarūpa (ātmā)of Kṛṣṇa’s abode. It was at all times endowed with all wealth, rare for Kuvera, etc. Starting from Kṛṣṇa’s birth (tataḥ), it became the place of pastimes (ākrīḍaṁ) for Rādhā and other gopīs (ramā). They took birth there after Kṛṣṇa’s birth.

That they are Ramā is stated later by śriya ekānta-vallabham: Lord is the exclusive lover of Śrī (SB [10.33.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/33.14)) because of the following statement in Brahmā-saṁhitā:

*cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vṛkṣa- lakṣāvṛteṣu surabhīr abhipālayantam \|*  
*lakṣmī-sahasra-śata-sambhrama-sevyamānaṁ govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi*

**I worship the Supreme Lord Govinda who affectionately tends the cows in stables whose walls are made of cintāmaṇi, surrounded by desire trees. He is eagerly served by countless gopīs. (Brahma-saṁhitā)**

Among them, Rādhā is Mahā-ramā due to her supremacy. This will be explained in the five chapters on the rāsa dance and is not contrary to the direct meaning of the verse. Vraja became the pastime place of the gopīs because of the qualities of Vraja being the svarūpa of Kṛṣṇa’s abode. Vraja is the abode of Kṛṣna. This is explained by śruti and Śukadeva in many places:

*yo ‘sau gopeṣu tiṣṭhati*

**He stands among the cowherds. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

*prīyān na indro gāvaṁ*

**May Kṛṣṇa, king of the cows, please us. (SB** [**10.26.25**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/26.25)**)**

*bhagavān gokuleśvaraḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa is lord of Gokula. (SB** [**10.10.39**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/10.39)**)**

*jayati jana-nivāsaḥ*

**May the abode of all people remain glorious. (SB** [**10.90.48**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/90.48)**)**

According to Śukadeva (in verse 3) he gave two hundred thousand cows fully decorated and seven mountains of sesame. He gave ornaments and countless cows and bulls. He fulfilled everyone’s desires. By this verse there should be no doubts about Nanda’s capability. How could so many millions of cows fit in the small area? This is answered by saying harer nivasātma-gunāiḥ. Like the form of Bhagavān, his place, Vraja is inconceivable.

### Text 19

*gopān gokula-rakṣāyāṁ nirūpya mathurāṁ gataḥ*  
*nandaḥ kaṁsasya vārṣikyaṁ karaṁ dātuṁ kurūdvaha*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Thereafter, my dear King Parīkṣit, O best protector of the Kuru dynasty, Nanda Mahārāja appointed the local cowherd men to protect Gokula and then went to Mathurā to pay the yearly taxes to King Kaṁsa.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda was extremely joyful with the birth of the most excellent son and with the huge festival celebrating that. Nanda thought, “Though Kaṁsa is not capable of harming us and if he harms us then he can be destroyed by our neighbours, still devotees are not interested in quarrelling. Though he is wicked, he should be somewhat respected since he is in a senior position.” Thus, he went to Mathurā to respect Kaṁsa and to give bliss to Vasudeva by speaking to him. Gopān means those who protect (pā) the land (go). The cowherds were great warriors capable of protecting their land. Because of this, Kaṁsa and his warriors did not attack them in Vraja. Kaṁsa’s wrestlers indicate the cowherds’ absorption in strength and their wrestling by:

*nityaṁ pramuditā gopā vatsa-pālā yathā-sphuṭam*  
*vaneṣu malla-yuddhena krīḍantaś cārayanti gāḥ*

**It is well known that cowherd boys are always joyful as they tend their calves, and that the boys playfully wrestle with each other while grazing their animals in the various forests. (SB** [**10.43.34**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/43.34)**)**

Appointing (nirūpya) those cowherds to protect Gokula, Nanda went to Mathurā to pay the yearly tax (vārṣikyaṁ) of gold coins, etc. (karaṁ).

### Text 20

*vasudeva upaśrutya bhrātaraṁ nandam āgatam*  
*jñātvā datta-karaṁ rājñe yayau tad-avamocanam*

**Перевод:**

**When Vasudeva heard that Nanda Mahārāja, his very dear friend and brother, had come to Mathurā and already paid the taxes to Kaṁsa, he went to Nanda Mahārāja’s residence.**

**Комментарий:**

The word bhrātaram (brother) is explained. King Devamīḍha the chief of Yadu clan (Yadavas) had two wives, one of a kṣatriyafamily, the other of a vaiśya family. Through the kṣatriya wife he bore a son named Śūra and from Śūra, Vasudeva appeared.Through the vaiśya wife he bore a son named Parjanya. Parjanya took up the occupation of his mother’s side. He had great qualities and was enthroned as king of Vraja by Yadus like Ugrasena. This is well known. From Parjanya, Nanda appeared. According to Madhvācārya, the following is a statement by Brahmā:

*tasmai varaḥ sa mayā saṁnisṛṣṭaḥ sa cāsa nandākhya utāsya bhāryā nāmnā yaśodā sa ca śūra-tāta- sutasya vaiśyā-prabhavo ‘tha gopaḥ*

**I had given that boon to him. His name was Nanda. And his wife was Yaśodā by name. He was born of Parjanya (the son of Śūra’s father) and was of vaiśyā-descent and thus a cowherd. (Mahābhārata-tātparya-nirṇaya)**

Śūra-tāta-sutasya means Nanda was the direct son of the son of Śūra’s step-mother, Parjanya. Nanda is described as vaiśyā-prabhava(descending from vaiśyā) is because Nanda’s grandmother was of the vaiśyā-jāti. In this way, Nanda is also counted as a Yādava. In Skanda Purāṇa, the Lord says:

*yādvānāṁ hitārthāya dhṛta-giri-varo mayā*

**To protect the Yādavas I lifted Govardhana.**

In Hari-vaṁśa, Balarāma says the same to Nanda’s brothers:

*yādaveṣv api sarveṣu bhavanto mama vallabhāḥ*

**Among all the Yadavas (those living in Mathurā and Vraja), you are the dearest to me.**

These statements are significant. Vasudeva knew Nanda had given taxes. Otherwise they could not talk together peacefully.

Avamocanam means the place where Nanda’s carts were kept. The phrase means the place where Nanda was residing.

### Text 21

*taṁ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya dehaḥ prāṇam ivāgatam*  
*prītaḥ priyatamaṁ dorbhyāṁ sasvaje prema-vihvalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Nanda Mahārāja heard that Vasudeva had come, he was overwhelmed with love and affection, being as pleased as if his body had regained its life. Seeing Vasudeva suddenly present, he got up and embraced him with both arms.**

**Комментарий:**

When Nanda saw Vasudeva (taṁ), he stood up and embraced him (sasvaje), but did not pay obeisances because he was elder to Vasudeva.

### Text 22

*pūjitaḥ sukham āsīnaḥ pṛṣṭvānāmayam ādṛtaḥ*  
*prāsakta-dhīḥ svātmajayor idam āha viśāmpate*

**Перевод:**

**O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, having thus been received and welcomed by Nanda Mahārāja with honor, Vasudeva sat down very peacefully and inquired about his own two sons because of intense love for them.**

### Text 23

*diṣṭyā bhrātaḥ pravayasa idānīm aprajasya te*  
*prajāśāyā nivṛttasya prajā yat samapadyata*

**Перевод:**

**My dear brother Nanda Mahārāja, at an advanced age you had no son at all and were hopeless of having one. Therefore, that you now have a son is a sign of great fortune.**

**Комментарий:**

Since no offspring was born even after undertaking many sacrifices you had given up hope for it. He speaks this in order to hide hissecret.

### Text 24

*diṣṭyā saṁsāra-cakre ’smin vartamānaḥ punar-bhavaḥ*  
*upalabdho bhavān adya durlabhaṁ priya-darśanam*

**Перевод:**

**It is also by good fortune for seeing you as if reborn since you are in the wheel of dangerous material life. It is rare to see dear friends.**

**Комментарий:**

I have certainly taken birth again (punar bhavaḥ) having suffered from imprisonment, etc., since I have met you. All this while, since I didn’t meet you, it was as if I were dead.

### Text 25

*naikatra priya-saṁvāsaḥ suhṛdāṁ citra-karmaṇām*  
*oghena vyūhyamānānāṁ plavānāṁ srotaso yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Many planks and sticks, unable to stay together, are carried away by the force of a river’s waves. Similarly, although we are intimately related with friends and family members, we are unable to stay together because of our various karmas.**

**Комментарий:**

Anticipating the proposal, “If that is so, then now we can stay together,” Vasudeva speaks this verse: “Dear friend, just as twigs and grass cannot stay together being lead variously by the flow of the river, we also cannot stay together.” Citra-karmaṇāṁ (we who have various karmas) is stated from the commoner’s viewpoint (since being nitya-siddhas Vasudeva and Nanda are beyond karma). This should be understood in SB [10.5.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/5.30) too.

### Text 26

*kaccit paśavyaṁ nirujaṁ bhūry-ambu-tṛṇa-vīrudham*  
*bṛhad vanaṁ tad adhunā yatrāsse tvaṁ suhṛd-vṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear friend Nanda Mahārāja, in the huge forest where you are living with your friends are the cows safe and are the water, grass and plants sufficient?**

**Комментарий:**

Paśavyam means beneficial for the cattle. The affix yat is applied in the sense of “for the benefit of” according to the sūtra: u-gav- ādibhyo yad (Pāṇini 5.1.2). Nirujam means without disease (rujā). Nīrujam becomes nirujam to suit the poetic meter.

### Text 27

*bhrātar mama sutaḥ kaccin mātrā saha bhavad-vraje*  
*tātaṁ bhavantaṁ manvāno bhavadbhyām upalālitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My son Baladeva, being raised by you and your wife, Yaśodādevī, considers you his father. Is he living very peacefully in your home with his real mother, Rohiṇī?**

**Комментарий:**

The phrase sukham asti (is my son happy) should be added to complete the sentence. He thinks of you as his father. This is to increase Nanda’s affection, since such a young child is unaware of such emotions since it is famous that Balarāma was born in on the full-moon day of Śrāvaṇa month and that Kṛṣṇa was born on the dark aṣṭamī of Bhadrā month.

### Text 28

*puṁsas tri-vargo vihitaḥ suhṛdo hy anu bhāvitaḥ*  
*na teṣu kliśyamāneṣu tri-vargo ’rthāya kalpate*

**Перевод:**

**When one’s friends and relatives are properly situated, one’s dharma, artha and kāma, as described in the Vedic literatures, are beneficial. Otherwise, if one’s friends and relatives are in distress, these three cannot offer any happiness.**

**Комментарий:**

To express the fact that his household life was a failure, Vasudeva spoke this verse. For a man (puṁsas) three vargas (duties) areprescribed by the scripture for the purpose of wife and children (suhṛdaḥ), which are to be achieved through one’s karmas (bhāvitaḥ). When those wife and children (teṣu) are in distress then the three vargas cannot produce results (arthāya). In my case, by being separated from wife and child, my household-life has become useless.

### Text 29

*śrī-nanda uvāca*  
*aho te devakī-putrāḥ kaṁsena bahavo hatāḥ*  
*ekāvaśiṣṭāvarajā kanyā sāpi divaṁ gatā*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja said: Alas, King Kaṁsa killed so many of your children, born of Devakī. And your one daughter, the youngest child of all, entered the heavenly planets.**

**Комментарий:**

I cannot say that everything is fine in Vraja, since I suffer because of your suffering. When Nanda says one daughter remained, Vasudeva understood that Nanda still did not know that he had exchanged his son for Nanda’s daughter. Thus, the secret had been kept. He had previously mentioned to Nanda only that an offspring had been born to Nanda (SB [10.5.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/5.23)). Thus Vasudeva became free of worry. Though Vasudeva and Nanda should have known everything since they were full of knowledge, still the superior śakti, which maintain that secret, sometimes covers some knowledge.

### Text 30

*nūnaṁ hy adṛṣṭa-niṣṭho ’yam adṛṣṭa-paramo janaḥ*  
*adṛṣṭam ātmanas tattvaṁ yo veda na sa muhyati*

**Перевод:**

**Every man is certainly controlled by destiny. He cannot escape it. One who knows the truth about fate will not lament.**

**Комментарий:**

“O brother, the river of calamity, should be crossed by the boat of discrimination.” With this intention Nanda speaks this verse. Man is certainly under the control of destiny (adṛṣṭa-niṣṭho). When destiny which gives happiness from children, disappears, then your children also disappear. Destiny is supreme. It is the cause of meeting children who then are separated by their death. He who knows the cause of suffering and happiness (ātmanaḥ tattvam) as destiny, is not bewildered. Destroy bewilderment by discernment.

### Text 31

*śrī-vasudeva uvāca*  
*karo vai vārṣiko datto rājñe dṛṣṭā vayaṁ ca vaḥ*  
*neha stheyaṁ bahu-tithaṁ santy utpātāś ca gokule*

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva said: Since you have paid the annual taxes to Kaṁsa and have also seen me, do not stay in this place for many days. There may be some disturbances in Gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

Desiring the benefit of his brother and himself he speaks. Do not stay here long (bahu-titham).

### Text 32

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*iti nandādayo gopāḥ proktās te śauriṇā yayuḥ*  
*anobhir anaḍud-yuktais tam anujñāpya gokulam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After Vasudeva advised Nanda Mahārāja in this way, Nanda Mahārāja and his associates, the cowherd men, took permission from Vasudeva, yoked their bulls to the bullock carts, and departed for Gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

They went by chariots (anobhiḥ) yoked with their bulls. Anaḥ means cart according to Halāyudha. One cannot say that they did not have a wealth of chariots as vehicles since this would contradict what was previously said: Vraja was full of wealth (SB [10.5.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/5.18)) and since the citizens describe that the gopīs mounted chariots (SB [10.11.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/11.33)). Thus their having chariots is proved by kaimutya.

## Chapter 6 - Killing the Demon Pūtanā

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*nandaḥ pathi vacaḥ śaurer na mṛṣeti vicintayan*  
*hariṁ jagāma śaraṇam utpātāgama-śaṅkitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: While Nanda Mahārāja was on the way home, he considered that what Vasudeva had said could not be false. As Nanda Mahārāja thought about the danger he was afraid, and he took shelter of the destroyer of fear.**

**Комментарий:**

*ṣaṣṭhe śaurer girā nando vrajaṁ gacchan mṛtām pathi \|*  
*vilokya pūtanāṁ tasyā mṛtyuṁ śrutvā ca vismitaḥ*

**In the sixth chapter following Vasudeva’s words, Nanda returned to Vraja and saw Pūtanā dead on the path. Hearing of her death, he was astonished.**

Vasudeva’s words could not be false, since he was a great rāja-rṣi. Nanda took shelter of the Lord, Nārāyaṇa, whom he served.

### Text 2

*kaṁsena prahitā ghorā pūtanā bāla-ghātinī*  
*śiśūṁś cacāra nighnantī pura-grāma-vrajādiṣu*

**Перевод:**

**While Nanda Mahārāja was returning to Gokula, the same fierce Pūtanā whom Kaṁsa had engaged to kill babies was wandering about in the towns, cities and villages, doing her nefarious duty.**

### Text 3

*na yatra śravaṇādīni rakṣo-ghnāni sva-karmasu*  
*kurvanti sātvatāṁ bhartur yātudhānyaś ca tatra hi*

**Перевод:**

**Wherever people in any position do not perform chanting and hearing about the Lord of the devotees while doing their duties, there is danger from bad elements.**

**Комментарий:**

Clarifying that Pūtanā, who was engaged in an improper act, would perish, Śukadeva speaks to Parīkṣit who was worried about Nanda’s child. In cities, etc., where people, engaged in karmas which produce results in this life and the next, do not hear about Kṛṣna, maintainer of the devotees, there demoness are powerful. Hearing about the Lord kills the Rākṣasas (rakṣo-ghnāni). Since in Nanda’s house the Lord was directly present, why worry?

### Text 4

*sā khe-cary ekadotpatya pūtanā nanda-gokulam*  
*yoṣitvā māyayātmānaṁ prāviśat kāma-cāriṇī*

**Перевод:**

**Once upon a time, Pūtanā Rākṣasī, who could move according to her desire and was wandering in outer space, converted herself by mystic power into a very beautiful woman and thus entered Gokula, the abode of Nanda Mahārāja.**

**Комментарий:**

Though she had no influence in Vraja, still for accomplishing the pastime of killing her, inspired by līlā-śakti, Pūtanā attained Vraja to die, as if invited by death. One time, Pūtanā (sā), at night, flying in the sky, arrived in Gokula and, turning herself into a beautiful woman by māyā, entered the house. Without such arrangement she could not enter. “But how could she make this transformation?” She had magical powers (kāma-cārinī).

### Texts 5-6

*tāṁ keśa-bandha-vyatiṣakta-mallikāṁ*  
*bṛhan-nitamba-stana-kṛcchra-madhyamām*  
*suvāsasaṁ kalpita-karṇa-bhūṣaṇa-*  
*tviṣollasat-kuntala-maṇḍitānanām*

*valgu-smitāpāṅga-visarga-vīkṣitair*  
*mano harantīṁ vanitāṁ vrajaukasām*  
*amaṁsatāmbhoja-kareṇa rūpiṇīṁ*  
*gopyaḥ śriyaṁ draṣṭum ivāgatāṁ patim*

**Перевод:**

**Her hips were full, her breasts were large and firm, seeming to oppress her slim waist, and she was dressed very nicely. Her hair, adorned with a garland of jasmine flowers, was scattered about her beautiful face effulgent with her swaying earrings. When she smiled very attractively, glancing upon everyone, her beauty drew the attention of all the inhabitants of Vraja. When the gopīs saw her, they thought that the beautiful goddess of fortune, holding a lotus flower in her hand, had come to see her husband.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. The gopīs thought that she was personified (rūpiṇīm) Śrī, the goddess of wealth. With a lotus in her hand (representing other items) she seemed to have come to see Narāyaṇa (patim) who was worshipped by Nanda. She had jasmines woven (vyktiṣakta) in her braid (keśa-bandha). She had a thin waist as if pressed on both sides by her huge breasts and huge hips. Her face was decorated with locks of hair shining with earrings. She was attractive to the people of Vraja with her glances endowed with attractive smiles. Thus, she entered without being stopped by the cowherd men and women. Pūtanā’s bewildering the people of Vraja by māyā, was by the Lord’s desire to perform the pastime of killing her. Actually, they acted as if (iva) she was attractive, but they were not bewildered.

### Text 7

*bāla-grahas tatra vicinvatī śiśūn*  
*yadṛcchayā nanda-gṛhe ’sad-antakam*  
*bālaṁ praticchanna-nijoru-tejasaṁ*  
*dadarśa talpe ’gnim ivāhitaṁ bhasi*

**Перевод:**

**While searching for small children, Pūtanā, whose business was to kill them, entered the house of Nanda Mahārāja unobstructed, having been sent by the superior potency of the Lord. She entered Nanda Mahārāja’s room, where she saw the child sleeping in bed, his power covered like a fire covered by ashes.**

**Комментарий:**

Pūtanā, searching for babies in Nanda-gokula, by chance saw in Nanda’s house on the bed the child who though was her killer (asad-antakam), was perceived as to be killed by her, since his powers were hidden, like a fire covered by (ahitam) ashes (bhasi).

### Text 8

*vibudhya tāṁ bālaka-mārikā-grahaṁ*  
*carācarātmā sa nimīlitekṣaṇaḥ*  
*anantam āropayad aṅkam antakaṁ*  
*yathoragaṁ suptam abuddhi-rajju-dhīḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord, the antaryāmī of all beings, understanding that Pūtanā was expert in killing small children, closed his eyes. Pūtanā took him on her lap though he was to be her destruction, just as an unintelligent person places a sleeping snake on his lap, thinking the snake to be a rope.**

**Комментарий:**

The antaryāmī of all beings (carācarātmā), the son of Nanda (saḥ), understanding that she was a monster killing children, closed hiseyes, with the nature of a baby, in order to not feel shame on killing her dressed as a nurse, and in order that he not see the sufferingof her death. Then she put her killer (antakam) on her lap. She wanted to show that she would take care of him since his mother was not skillful at caring for a baby. She was ignorant like a person who thinks a sleeping snake is a rope.

### Text 9

*tāṁ tīkṣṇa-cittām ativāma-ceṣṭitāṁ*  
*vīkṣyāntarā kośa-paricchadāsivat*  
*vara-striyaṁ tat-prabhayā ca dharṣite*  
*nirīkṣyamāṇe jananī hy atiṣṭhatām*

**Перевод:**

**Although seeing her within the room, Yaśodā and Rohiṇī, overwhelmed by her affection, thinking her to be the best of women, simply stood and gazed at her, though her heart was most cruel – because she displayed the gentlest behavior, like a knife hidden in a sheath.**

**Комментарий:**

Why did Yaśodā and Rohiṇī, completely devoted to the child, not prevent her? They saw her with attractive (vāmam) actions like a mother, like the best women in the universe (antarā). An example of being cruel internally and gentle externally is given. She was like a sword covered by a soft, colorful sheath. They were defeated (dharṣite) by her power. The mothers were bewildered, thinking, “This women, like the wife of Indra or Śiva, desiring the good fortune of my son, is giving her breast out of affection.” Thus, they remained there watching, not preventing her.

The word jananī (singular) is used for the dual number by poetic license, following rules like supāṁsu luk (Pāṇini 7.1.39).

### Text 10

*tasmin stanaṁ durjara-vīryam ulbaṇaṁ*  
*ghorāṅkam ādāya śiśor dadāv atha*  
*gāḍhaṁ karābhyāṁ bhagavān prapīḍya tat-*  
*prāṇaiḥ samaṁ roṣa-samanvito ’pibat*

**Перевод:**

**On that very spot, the fiercely dangerous Rākṣasī took Kṛṣṇa on her lap and pushed her breast into his mouth though her breast was smeared with a dangerous, immediately effective poison. The Supreme Lord, becoming very angry, squeezed her breast hard with both hands and sucked out her life.**

**Комментарий:**

At that place, ferocious Pūtanā placing Kṛṣṇa on her lap, gave him, i.e. offered to his mouth her breast, filled with poison (durjaramvīryam), which would produce death just by the touch (ulbanam). The child squeezed her breast tightly so that she could not push him away. He was full of anger. He drank the poison with her life. He was angry because the sinful woman wanted to kill even the babies of Vraja, his friends. His śakti of anger, which destroys the wicked, dried up her breast along with her life. It was like cutting down a tree with an axe.

### Text 11

*sā muñca muñcālam iti prabhāṣiṇī*  
*niṣpīḍyamānākhila-jīva-marmaṇi*  
*vivṛtya netre caraṇau bhujau muhuḥ*  
*prasvinna-gātrā kṣipatī ruroda ha*

**Перевод:**

**Unbearably pressed in every vital point, the demon Pūtanā began to cry, “Please leave me, leave me! Suck my breast no longer!” Perspiring, her eyes wide open and her arms and legs flailing, she cried very loudly again and again.**

**Комментарий:**

Afflicted in all life points, her eyes bulging, flailing her arms and legs, with perspiring limbs, she cried out, “Ah!” Ha indicates the astonishment that she could be afflicted just by the child sucking her breast.

### Text 12

*tasyāḥ svanenātigabhīra-raṁhasā*  
*sādrir mahī dyauś ca cacāla sa-grahā*  
*rasā diśaś ca pratinedire janāḥ*  
*petuḥ kṣitau vajra-nipāta-śaṅkayā*

**Перевод:**

**As Pūtanā screamed loudly and forcefully, the earth with its mountains, outer space with its planets, and the lower planets trembled and echoed the sound. All directions vibrated, and people fell on the earth, fearing that thunderbolts were falling upon them.**

**Комментарий:**

The lower planets (rasā) echoed the sound.

### Text 13

*niśā-carītthaṁ vyathita-stanā vyasur*  
*vyādāya keśāṁś caraṇau bhujāv api*  
*prasārya goṣṭhe nija-rūpam āsthitā*  
*vajrāhato vṛtra ivāpatan nṛpa*

**Перевод:**

**In this way the demon Pūtanā, pained in her breast, lost her life. O King Parīkṣit, opening her mouth wide and spreading her arms, legs and hair, she fell down in the pasturing ground in her original form just as Vṛtrāsura had fallen when struck by the thunderbolt of Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

She opened her mouth (vyādāya). She returned to her original form since when demons are in danger, they cannot preserve their forms produced by their māyā.

### Text 14

*patamāno ’pi tad-dehas tri-gavyūty-antara-drumān*  
*cūrṇayām āsa rājendra mahad āsīt tad adbhutam*

**Перевод:**

**O King Parīkṣit, when the gigantic body of Pūtanā fell to the ground, it smashed all the trees within a distance of twelve miles. This was most astonishing.**

**Комментарий:**

Leaping out of the house because of the great pain, she fell outside the town. She crushed the trees, full of attractive, tasty fruit, in the vicinity of six krośas. The gardens were forcibly made by Kaṁsa on Nanda’s land. By this it is indicated that though she set out to benefit Kaṁsa, she produced a loss for him. Even in death, Pūtanā afflicted living beings. This is signified by the word api. That thishappened outside the town and crushed only Kaṁsa’s trees when she fell is the astonishing act of the Lord.

### Texts 15-17

*īṣā-mātrogra-daṁṣṭrāsyaṁ giri-kandara-nāsikam*  
*gaṇḍa-śaila-stanaṁ raudraṁ prakīrṇāruṇa-mūrdhajam*

*andha-kūpa-gabhīrākṣaṁ pulināroha-bhīṣaṇam*  
*baddha-setu-bhujorv-aṅghri śūnya-toya-hradodaram*

*santatrasuḥ sma tad vīkṣya gopā gopyaḥ kalevaram*  
*pūrvaṁ tu tan-niḥsvanita- bhinna-hṛt-karṇa-mastakāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Rākṣasī’s mouth was full of teeth, each resembling the front of a plow, her nostrils were deep like mountain caves, and her breasts resembled big slabs of stone fallen from a hill. Her scattered hair was the color of copper. The sockets of her eyes appeared like deep blind wells, her fearful thighs resembled the banks of a river, her arms, legs and feet seemed like big bridges, and her abdomen appeared like a dried-up lake. The hearts, ears and heads of the cowherd men and women were already shocked by the Rākṣasī’s screaming, and when they saw the fierce wonder of her body, they were even more frightened.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses go together. The cowherd men and women, seeing that body, were frightened. She had mouth (āsyam) with huge teeth which were of the size of plowshare (īṣā-mātrā). Her hair was terrifying (raudram). The body was terrifying with thighs (āroha) like river banks. The arms, legs and feet were like bridges. Her stomach was like a dried-up lake (śūnya-toya-hrada). Previously, the people’s hearts, ears and heads had been pierced by her terrible screaming.

### Text 18

*bālaṁ ca tasyā urasi krīḍantam akutobhayam*  
*gopyas tūrṇaṁ samabhyetya jagṛhur jāta-sambhramāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Without fear, the child Kṛṣṇa was playing on the upper portion of Pūtanā Rākṣasī’s breast, and when the gopīs saw the child’s wonderful activities, they immediately came forward with great jubilation and picked him up.**

**Комментарий:**

The child of Nanda immediately gave joy to the disturbed people of Vraja. He played on her chest, high as mountain. The Lord went outside the city to give joy to those people who wanted to see him but were not allowed into the maternity room. He destroyed Pūtanā, the powerful minister of Kaṁsa and she destroyed his garden. The garden was completely torn apart.

### Text 19

*yaśodā-rohiṇībhyāṁ tāḥ samaṁ bālasya sarvataḥ*  
*rakṣāṁ vidadhire samyag go-puccha-bhramaṇādibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, mother Yaśodā and Rohiṇī, along with the other elderly gopīs, waved about the switch of a cow to give full protection to the child Śrī Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Yaśodā and Rohiṇī did not take a leading role, because they were extremely affected by anxiety for Kṛṣṇa’s safety. Thus, they are mentioned in the instrumental case (yaśodā-rohiṇībhyāṁ). This is according to the sūtra: saha-yukte’pradhāne (Pāṇini 2.3.19). The word ādi indicates that they also offered other items such as mustard seeds, and touched Kṛṣṇa with the edge of the winnowing basket.

### Text 20

*go-mūtreṇa snāpayitvā punar go-rajasārbhakam*  
*rakṣāṁ cakruś ca śakṛtā dvādaśāṅgeṣu nāmabhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The child was thoroughly washed with cow urine and then smeared with the dust raised by the movements of the cows. They protected him while chanting different names of the Lord and applying cow dung on twelve different parts of his body.**

**Комментарий:**

They protected him by touching cow dung (śakṛtā) to twelve parts of his body while chanting twelve names of Viṣṇu. The names arethose mentioned in Padma Purāṇa when putting on tilaka.

*lalāṭe keśavaṁ dhyāyen nārāyaṇam athodare vakṣaḥ-sthale mādhavaṁ tu govindaṁ kaṇṭha-kūpake viṣṇuṁ ca dakṣiṇe kukṣau bāhau ca madhusūdanam trivikramaṁ kandhare tu vāmanaṁ vāma-pārśvake śrīdharaṁ vāma-bāhau tu hṛṣīkeśaṁ tu kandhare pṛṣṭhe ca padmanābhaṁ ca kaṭyāṁ dāmodaraṁ nyaset*

**When one marks the forehead with tilaka, he must remember Keśava. When one marks the lower abdomen, he must remember Nārāyaṇa. For the chest, one should remember Mādhava, and when marking the hollow of the neck one should remember Govinda. Lord Viṣṇu should be remembered while marking the right side of the belly, and Madhusūdana should be remembered when marking the right arm. Trivikrama should be remembered when marking the right shoulder, and Vāmana should be remembered when marking the left side of the belly. Śrīdhara should be remembered while marking the left arm and Hṛṣīkeśa should be remembered when marking the left shoulder. Padmanābha should be remembered when marking the back and Dāmodara should be remembered when marking the hips.**

Protecting him using the Lord’s names shows that they were pure devotees.

### Text 21

*gopyaḥ saṁspṛṣṭa-salilā aṅgeṣu karayoḥ pṛthak*  
*nyasyātmany atha bālasya bīja-nyāsam akurvata*

**Перевод:**

**At first, out of confusion, without performing ācamana, they performed the protection, later understanding the child was healthy, unharmed by the demons, having recovered they performed the protection according to the rules. They performed ācamana (saṁspṛṣta-salilāḥ). After the sādhaka protects one’s own body, one protects the object being protected. Thus first they touched the limbs of their own body (ātmani) and hands separately, using eleven bīja mantras starting with Aja (i.e they performed both kara-nyāsa and aṅga-nyāsa). Of the eleven bīja mantras starting with Aja, they used three bīja mantras for purification of the hands and placed four on the joints of the hands each. Similarly, on each limb starting from the feet, they placed a bīja each. They did the same on the child’s limbs.**

**Комментарий:**

The bīja-nyāsa is formed by the first syllable of the name of the Lord with an ānusvāra, followed by namaḥ (for instance aṁ manaḥ ajas tavāṅghrī avyāt, maṁ namaḥ maṇimāṁs tava jānunī avyāt, etc). The names from aja to īśvara were used to touch eleven parts of Kṛṣṇa’s body.

### Texts 22-23

*avyād ajo ’ṅghri maṇimāṁs tava jānv athorū*  
*yajño ’cyutaḥ kaṭi-taṭaṁ jaṭharaṁ hayāsyaḥ*  
*hṛt keśavas tvad-ura īśa inas tu kaṇṭhaṁ*  
*viṣṇur bhujaṁ mukham urukrama īśvaraḥ kam*

*cakry agrataḥ saha-gado harir astu paścāt*  
*tvat-pārśvayor dhanur-asī madhu-hājanaś ca*  
*koṇeṣu śaṅkha urugāya upary upendras*  
*tārkṣyaḥ kṣitau haladharaḥ puruṣaḥ samantāt*

**Перевод:**

**May Aja protect your legs, may Maṇimān protect your knees, Yajña your thighs, Acyuta the upper part of your waist, and Hayagrīva your abdomen. May Keśava protect your heart, Īśa your chest, the sun-god your neck, Viṣṇu your arms, Urukrama your face, and Īśvara your head. May Hari with carka protect you from the front and with a club protect you from the back; and may the carrier of the bow, who is known as the enemy of Madhu, protect one side and may Ajana, the carrier of the sword, protect your other side. May Urugāya, the carrier of the conch shell, protect you from all corners; may Upendra with Garuḍa protect you from above; may Haladhara protect you on the ground; and may Puruṣottama protect you on all sides.**

**Комментарий:**

They protected the child in this way. Aṅghri and jānu stand for the dual aṅghrī and jānunī, according to supāṁ suluk (Pāṇini 7.1.39).Bhujam is used instead of the dual according to vyatyayo bahulam (Pāṇini 3.1.85). Kam means head.

Then they protected him in the directions.

### Text 24

*indriyāṇi hṛṣīkeśaḥ prāṇān nārāyaṇo ’vatu*  
*śvetadvīpa-patiś cittaṁ mano yogeśvaro ’vatu*

**Перевод:**

**May Hṛṣīkeśa protect your senses, and Nārāyaṇa your life airs. May the master of Śvetadvīpa protect the core of your heart, and may Yogeśvara protect your mind.**

**Комментарий:**

They protect his internal limbs in three lines.

### Texts 25-26

*pṛśnigarbhas tu te buddhim ātmānaṁ bhagavān paraḥ*  
*krīḍantaṁ pātu govindaḥ śayānaṁ pātu mādhavaḥ*

*vrajantam avyād vaikuṇṭha āsīnaṁ tvāṁ śriyaḥ patiḥ*  
*bhuñjānaṁ yajñabhuk pātu sarva-graha-bhayaṅkaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**May Pṛśnigarbha protect your intelligence, and Bhagavān your ahaṅkāra. While you are playing, may Govinda protect you, and while you are sleeping may Mādhava protect you. May Vaikuṇṭha protect you while you are walking, and may Nārāyaṇa, the husband of the goddess of fortune, protect you while you are sitting. Similarly, may Yajñabhuk, protect you while you enjoy life. May all these forms protect you from the bad influence of planets.**

**Комментарий:**

Ātmanam means ahaṅkāra. His actions are then protected in three lines.

### Texts 27-29

*ḍākinyo yātudhānyaś ca kuṣmāṇḍā ye ’rbhaka-grahāḥ*  
*bhūta-preta-piśācāś ca yakṣa-rakṣo-vināyakāḥ*

*koṭarā revatī jyeṣṭhā pūtanā mātṛkādayaḥ*  
*unmādā ye hy apasmārā deha-prāṇendriya-druhaḥ*

*svapna-dṛṣṭā mahotpātā vṛddhā bāla-grahāś ca ye*  
*sarve naśyantu te viṣṇor nāma-grahaṇa-bhīravaḥ*

**Перевод:**
