**Ḍākinīs, Yātudhānīs, Kuṣmāṇḍas, Arbhaka-grahas, Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas and Vināyakas, as well as witches like Koṭarā, Revatī, Jyeṣṭhā, Pūtanā, the Mātṛkās, and Bāla-grahas, who give trouble to the body, the life air and the senses, loss of memory, madness, bad dreams and great disturbances, should be destroyed since they are afraid of the names of Viṣṇu.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses go together.

### Text 30

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*iti praṇaya-baddhābhir gopībhiḥ kṛta-rakṣaṇam*  
*pāyayitvā stanaṁ mātā sannyaveśayad ātmajam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: After the gopīs, bound by maternal affection, protected the child, mother Yaśodā gave the child her breast and got him to lie down.**

**Комментарий:**

The gopīs protected him according to the rules. This shows that they were in knowledge of all scriptures by nature. That was not astonishing since they are eternal associates of the Lord. Though they were always thinking of Kṛṣṇa, having knowledge of him astheir master, they are absorbed in vātsalya for him. The Vraja-vāsīs’ knowledge perceives both Kṛṣṇa’s power and sweetness. Thus they were full of knowledge, feeble in relation to power but abundant in relation to sweetness. Thus protecting him in this way was acceptable. She understood that he was healthy because he drank her milk. Yaśodā then put him to sleep.

### Text 31

*tāvan nandādayo gopā mathurāyā vrajaṁ gatāḥ*  
*vilokya pūtanā-dehaṁ babhūvur ativismitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Meanwhile, all the cowherd men, headed by Nanda Mahārāja, returned from Mathurā, and when they saw on the way the gigantic body of Pūtanā lying dead, they were struck with great wonder.**

**Комментарий:**

They were astonished. Have we been brought to some other place by the power of yoga by some yogī? Or has a great mountain fallen, its wings cut off by Indra? Or is it some magician’s trick? In this way they were full of doubt.

### Text 32

*nūnaṁ batarṣiḥ sañjāto yogeśo vā samāsa saḥ*  
*sa eva dṛṣṭo hy utpāto yad āhānakadundubhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja and the other cowherds exclaimed: You must know that Vasudeva, has become a great saint or a master of mystic power. Otherwise how could he have foreseen this calamity?**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda then drew a conclusion. Vasudeva a sage in our dynasty, fixed in austerity (ṛṣiḥ) or a practitioner of aṣṭāṅga-yoga (yogeśaḥ), shines greatly (samāsa). By the power of his austerity and yoga he knows the future. He saw this disturbance.

### Text 33

*kalevaraṁ paraśubhiś chittvā tat te vrajaukasaḥ*  
*dūre kṣiptvāvayavaśo nyadahan kāṣṭha-veṣṭitam*

**Перевод:**

**Some inhabitants of Vraja cut the gigantic body of Pūtanā into pieces with the help of axes. Then throwing it far away piece by piece, they covered the pieces with wood and burned them to ashes.**

**Комментарий:**

Upananda and others who had stayed to protect Vraja engaged some lower caste inhabitants of Vraja in burning her body. They completely burned the body, fearing it would again come to life. In this way, by the time Nanda and other came closer, those who were low born, taking shelter of Vraja (vrajaukasaḥ), burned the body completely, being engaged by Upananda and others who remained there for protecting Gokula.

### Text 34

*dahyamānasya dehasya dhūmaś cāguru-saurabhaḥ*  
*utthitaḥ kṛṣṇa-nirbhukta- sapady āhata-pāpmanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because Kṛṣṇa had sucked the breast of Pūtanā, when he killed her she was immediately freed of all material contamination. When her gigantic body was being burnt, the smoke emanating from her body was fragrant like aguru incense. Anyone who smelled this smoke had their sinful reactions destroyed.**

**Комментарий:**

Another astonishing event is described. Her sins were destroyed immediately by having Kṛṣṇa drink from her breast. This shows the power of the touch of his mouth.

### Texts 35-36

*pūtanā loka-bāla-ghnī rākṣasī rudhirāśanā*  
*jighāṁsayāpi haraye stanaṁ dattvāpa sad-gatim*

*kiṁ punaḥ śraddhayā bhaktyā kṛṣṇāya paramātmane*  
*yacchan priyatamaṁ kiṁ nu raktās tan-mātaro yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Pūtanā was always hankering for the blood of human children, and with that desire she came to kill Kṛṣṇa; but because she offered her breast to him, she attained him. What then is to be said of those who had faith or devotion for Kṛṣṇa and who offer something very dear, as a mother offers something to a child.**

**Комментарий:**

Incidentally, to narrate the glories of bhakti by kaimutya, Śukadeva speaks of Kṛṣṇa’s quality of giving a great destination to the demons he kills. Pūtanā attained the goal of the wise (sad-gatim), liberation in the form of destruction of the subtle body.

A devotee, having faith, giving to the Lord an object most dear to himself, what to speak of saying that he attains sad-gati, it shouldbe said that he controls the Lord. The example is that of affectionate mothers. The plural is used to hint at the pastime of Brahmā stealing the calves (when many mothers got Kṛṣṇa as their son).

### Texts 37-38

*padbhyāṁ bhakta-hṛdi-sthābhyāṁ vandyābhyāṁ loka-vanditaiḥ*  
*aṅgaṁ yasyāḥ samākramya bhagavān apibat stanam*

*yātudhāny api sā svargam avāpa jananī-gatim*  
*kṛṣṇa-bhukta-stana-kṣīrāḥ kim u gāvo ’nu mātaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, who stepped on Pūtanā’s limbs with his feet which are situated within the heart of the pure devotees and which are worthy of praise by great devotees like Brahmā and Śiva, drank from Pūtanā’s breast. That witch attained his abode as a nurse. What can be said then of the cows and elder gopīs whose breast milk was drunk by Kṛṣṇa?**

**Комментарий:**

The described meaning is repeated because it is astonishing. Two verses go together.

The son of Nanda full of all powers (bhagavān) stepped on the limbs of Pūtanā, devoid of bhakti and moreover acting as an enemy(yasyāḥ), with his feet which are worshipped by Brahmā and others (loka-vanditaiḥ). He was not even touched by her. He drank from her breast. She attained Goloka (svargam), above Vaikuṇṭha. She attained the position of a nurse, with predominance of happinessand grandeur (sukhaiśvarya). The word svar here has the same meaning as in the following:

*brahmā bhavo loka-pālāḥ svar-vāsaṁ me ‘bhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ*

**Thus Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and all other planetary rulers are now praying for me to resume my residence in Vaikuṇṭha. (SB** [**11.7.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/7.1)**)**

She attained the position of Yaśodā and others in a different manifestation (jananī-gatim). Thus it is Kṛṣṇa’s glory that he is extraordinarily satisfied with her just for her wearing the dress of a nurse. If he has such mercy on even such kind of people, then what to say that the mothers whose milk Kṛṣṇa drank and the cows whose milk he drank attained the position of controlling him.

### Texts 39-40

*payāṁsi yāsām apibat putra-sneha-snutāny alam*  
*bhagavān devakī-putraḥ kaivalyādy-akhila-pradaḥ*

*tāsām avirataṁ kṛṣṇe kurvatīnāṁ sutekṣaṇam*  
*na punaḥ kalpate rājan saṁsāro ’jñāna-sambhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī, the bestower of many benedictions, including liberation, drank the milk of those cows and gopīs, which flowed with the highest parental affection. O King! These cows and women who took Kṛṣṇa as their son constantly were not destined for saṁsāra, which produces ignorance.**

**Комментарий:**

“But this mercy should be a characteristic of paramahaṁsas since Kuntī says:

*tathā parama-haṁsānāṁ munīnām amalātmanām -yoga-vidhānārthaṁ kathaṁ paśyema hi striyaḥ*

**How can we women hope to see you, the object of bhakti for the omniscient, liberated sages? (SB** [**1.8.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/8.20)**)**

But since the gopīs are in contact with saṁsāra, that mercy does not occur.” Two verses go together.

The son born to Yāśodā (devakī-putraḥ), who gives all goals including liberation to enemies he kills, Bhagavān, drank the breast milk of those flowing with supreme affection for him as their son (putra-snehena). Drinking that nectar from their breasts, he was extremely pleased with them. Brahmā explains that Kṛṣṇa attained great bliss on drinking that milk (in SB [10.14.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.31)).

Saṁsāra, which causes aversion to the Lord (ajñana-sambhavaḥ), does not occur for them, whose desires are completely fulfilled. Na punaḥ means vai (certainty) according to Amara-kośa. Saṁsāracertainly did not occur for them. It is not that since Viśva-kośa says punaḥ means “not the first time,” the verse should be explained as: saṁsāra would not arise a second time for them (which implies that first time they were in saṁsāra). But this contradicts the śruti and smṛti which say that they are eternal associates of the Lord. They are further explained. They always (avirataṁ) thought of Kṛṣṇa, giver of liberation, Parabrahman, affectionate to the devotees as their son (sutekṣaṇam). Thus they were most favorable to him. Who can say that saṁsāra is possible for them, who always experienced Parabrahman directly? Similarly according to ye yathā mām prapadyante (BG [4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11)), he should always be controlled by them due to their mood of his being their son. Such dealings ofspiritual pastimes appear as devoid of variety in jñāna separated from bhakti, like gold appearing as a mass of form for eyes withoutglasses.

### Text 41

*kaṭa-dhūmasya saurabhyam avaghrāya vrajaukasaḥ*  
*kim idaṁ kuta eveti vadanto vrajam āyayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Upon smelling the fragrance of the smoke emanating from Pūtanā’s burning body, many inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi in distant places were astonished. “Where is this fragrance coming from?” they asked and went to Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the glory of bhakti incidentally, the main topic is described. Kaṭa means a crematorium according to Kṣīrasvāmī. Where is this fragrance coming from? Is it aguru scent which comes down from Indra’s palace to enter Pātāla? Or from Bali’s palace is it ascending to Svarga? These were their words of doubt.

### Text 42

*te tatra varṇitaṁ gopaiḥ pūtanāgamanādikam*  
*śrutvā tan-nidhanaṁ svasti śiśoś cāsan suvismitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Nanda and others heard the whole story of how Pūtanā had come and then been killed by Kṛṣṇa, as well as the safety of the child, they were astonished.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda and others were astonished. “Vasudeva is a siddha. By his meditation on the child’s safety, the child has been protected.” This is what they said.

### Text 43

*nandaḥ sva-putram ādāya proṣyāgata udāra-dhīḥ*  
*mūrdhny upāghrāya paramāṁ mudaṁ lebhe kurūdvaha*

**Перевод:**

**O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, best of the Kurus, Nanda Mahārāja was very liberal and simple. He immediately took his son Kṛṣṇa on his lap, and by formally smelling his son’s head since he had come from a distance, he enjoyed the highest bliss.**

**Комментарий:**

“Since many problems have arisen when I went to Mathurā, why did I go there?” In this way he regretted. Nanda was broad-minded. None of my foolish door-keepers prevented Pūtanā from entering. Thus he began to belittle everyone’s intelligence.

But Nanda, Yaśodā and others, were knowers of all scriptures, and understood Nārāyaṇa as the object of their worship. But they did not know that Kṛṣṇa, who was the aṁśī of Nārāyaṇa, as the object of their worship, rather they thought of him as their son. How could this happen? We will explain this secret in the chapter on Kṛṣṇa’s eating dirt.

### Text 44

*ya etat pūtanā-mokṣaṁ kṛṣṇasyārbhakam adbhutam*  
*śṛṇuyāc chraddhayā martyo govinde labhate ratim*

**Перевод:**

**Any person who hears with faith Kṛṣṇa’s remarkable pastime of liberating Pūtanā attains attachment for Govinda.**

**Комментарий:**

Anyone who faithfully hears the childhood pastimes of Kṛṣṇa (kṛṣṇasya ārbhakam) in which is the liberation of Pūtanā and accepts them as most astonishing, will obtain attraction for Govinda, Nanda’s son.

*avidyāyāḥ kṣayād eva labhyo ’ham iti tan-mayīm ahan pūtanāṁ kṛṣṇo rāghavas tāḍakām iva*

**The Lord, with the thought, “A person can attain me when their ignorance is destroyed,” first killed Pūtanā, who was absorbed in avidyā, just as Rāma previously killed Tāḍakā.**

Moreover,

*ārambhād eva līlāyā bakī-dhātrī-gati-pradaḥ sva-guṇa-mādhurye tṛṣṇayām āsa vaiṣṇavān*

**From the beginning of the pastimes, Kṛṣṇa, who accepted Pūtanā as a nurse, made the devotees thirsty for the sweetness of his qualities. (By hearing this story they develop faith and then rati.)**

## Chapter 7 - The Killing of the Demon Tṛṇāvarta

### Texts 1-2

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*yena yenāvatāreṇa bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ*  
*karoti karṇa-ramyāṇi mano-jñāni ca naḥ prabho*

*yac-chṛṇvato ’paity aratir vitṛṣṇā*  
*sattvaṁ ca śuddhyaty acireṇa puṁsaḥ*  
*bhaktir harau tat-puruṣe ca sakhyaṁ*  
*tad eva hāraṁ vada manyase cet*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! Hearing about the Lord – who is full of all qualities, who is the destroyer of suffering and the attractor of the senses, who through his appearance causes pleasure to the ears and great attraction to the mind – destroys all disinterest in the topics about him and all thirst for material enjoyment, and produces prema for the attractive Lord and friendship with the devotees. Please speak of the Lord’s pastimes if you think I am qualified.**

**Комментарий:**

*autthānikaṁ snānam ano-vibhaṅgaṁ kṛṣṇas tṛṇāvarta-vadhaṁ vyadhatte \|*  
*adarśayan mātaram āsya bimbe viśvaṁ śiśuḥ saptamake pareśaḥ*

**In the seventh chapter, Kṛṣṇa takes a bath after sitting up, and breaks the cart. He kills Tṛṇāvarta and shows the whole universe to mother Yaśodā.**

The king extremely thirsty for pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, inquires. Though all the pastimes of the Lord are attractive for us to hear and are attractive to the mind, still among them which pastimes quickly destroy the listener’s apathy characterized by beginningless aversion (aratiḥ) towards him, quickly produce distaste (vitṛṣṇā) for material objects, and thus quickly purify the heart (sattvam) and thus quickly produce steady bhakti for the Lord and produces friendship for the devotees quickly, please speak of those pastimes of Lord Hari (hāram) or speak of what is to be held on the heart (hāram), if you agree. Though all pastimes of Bhagavān destroy apathy, etc., still the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa immediately do so. Among all the pastimes, they are the sweetest.

### Text 3

*athānyad api kṛṣṇasya tokācaritam adbhutam*  
*mānuṣaṁ lokam āsādya taj-jātim anurundhataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Please describe other astonishing childhood pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, who appeared on this planet earth and identified himself completely with those pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

He clarifies his desire. This is connected with the verb vada (speak) in the previous verse. He manifested pastimes which were likethose of humans (tad-jātim). Disguised in the ways of a human, his pastimes which were pregnant with his supreme power were like a mirror with a picture.

### Text 4

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*kadācid autthānika-kautukāplave*  
*janmarkṣa-yoge samaveta-yoṣitām*  
*vāditra-gīta-dvija-mantra-vācakaiś*  
*cakāra sūnor abhiṣecanaṁ satī*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After three months, on the occasion of a bath for the child when he could raise himself in bed, when the moon was in Rohiṇī constellation, Yaśodā, expert in ceremonies, performed the bathing ceremony for her only son with the assembled women, to the accompaniment of music, singing and brāhmaṇas’ chanting.**

**Комментарий:**

This took place when he was three months old (kadācit). Trai- māsikasya ca padā śakaṭo ’pavṛttaḥ: the cart was overturned by the foot of three-month-old child. (SB [2.7.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.27)) The child turned over on his back (utthānam). In order to see that, the people were joyful,submerged in a festival of pleasure (kautukāplave). On that very day it was Rohiṇī constellation, his birth constellation. Situated among all the women gathered together, Yaśodā performed an auspicious bath of Kṛṣṇa with music.

### Text 5

*nandasya patnī kṛta-majjanādikaṁ*  
*vipraiḥ kṛta-svastyayanaṁ supūjitaiḥ*  
*annādya-vāsaḥ-srag-abhīṣṭa-dhenubhiḥ*  
*sañjāta-nidrākṣam aśīśayac chanaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Yaśodā, after drying her child and having auspicious ceremonies performed by brāhmaṇas, who were honored with food, utensils, cloth, garlands, precious objects and cows, gently put the child to sleep since his eyes had closed.**

**Комментарий:**

Brāhmaṇas who were worshipped with gifts of rice, etc., had uttered auspicious chants for the child. With the child’s eyes getting closed, she put him to sleep in a colorful bed beneath a car in the large yard, very gently, fearing he would wake up.

### Text 6

*autthānikautsukya-manā manasvinī*  
*samāgatān pūjayatī vrajaukasaḥ*  
*naivāśṛṇod vai ruditaṁ sutasya sā*  
*rudan stanārthī caraṇāv udakṣipat*

**Перевод:**

**The liberal mother Yaśodā, absorbed in celebrating the utthāna ceremony, was busy receiving guests, worshiping them with all respect and offering them clothing, cows, garlands and grains. Thus she could not hear the child crying for his mother. At that time, the child Kṛṣṇa, demanding to drink the milk of his mother’s breast, angrily threw his legs upward.**

**Комментарий:**

She was very powerful (manasvinī): she had faith, skill and attention in worshipping the guests who arrived. “You do not hear the sound of my crying, wait, you will hear the breaking of the huge cart situated near the house.” In apparent anger, he moved his foot upwards to break the cart. Later it is said tāṁ stanya-kāma (SB 10.9.4). Thus stanārthī means he desired to drink her milk.

### Text 7

*adhaḥ-śayānasya śiśor ano ’lpaka-*  
*pravāla-mṛdv-aṅghri-hataṁ vyavartata*  
*vidhvasta-nānā-rasa-kupya-bhājanaṁ*  
*vyatyasta-cakrākṣa-vibhinna-kūbaram*

**Перевод:**

**While he was lying beneath the cart sleeping, the cart, filled with utensils made of many metals, when touched by his small, tender foot, was destroyed. Its many metal utensils were scattered here and there, the axel and wheels turned over, and the yoke split.**

**Комментарий:**

The cart kicked by the child’s soft, small but strong feet turned over in such a way that the metal utensils of bell-metal, etc., holding various liquids were scattered and the axel and yoke broke. Kupya indicates metals other than gold and silver. The huge cart was placed in the yard in order to store the vessels. One of Kaṁsa’s servants becoming invisible, and entered the cart. The wheels gradually sunk in the ground because of the weight of the demon. Thus the high cart could be touched by Kṛṣṇa’s feet. By that touch the demon attained death. The cart was possessed by a demon who a servant of Kaṁsa, according to the śakaṭāsura-bhañjana stotra.

### Text 8

*dṛṣṭvā yaśodā-pramukhā vraja-striya*  
*autthānike karmaṇi yāḥ samāgatāḥ*  
*nandādayaś cādbhuta-darśanākulāḥ*  
*kathaṁ svayaṁ vai śakaṭaṁ viparyagāt*

**Перевод:**

**When mother Yaśodā and the other ladies who had assembled for the utthāna festival, and all the men, headed by Nanda Mahārāja, saw the astonishing situation, they became perturbed and said, “How did the cart collapse by itself?”**

**Комментарий:**

They said (verb should be added), “How did the cart turn over by itself?”

### Text 9

*ūcur avyavasita-matīn gopān gopīś ca bālakāḥ*  
*rudatānena pādena kṣiptam etan na saṁśayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The children spoke to the assembled cowherd men and ladies whose minds were unsettled. “There is no doubt that he upset the cart with his foot when he was crying.”**

**Комментарий:**

Their minds were undecided. Is this the work of demons? Or is it the work of the planets? They could not decide (avyavasita-matīn). The children had been placed there by Yaśodā to protect Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 10

*na te śraddadhire gopā bāla-bhāṣitam ity uta*  
*aprameyaṁ balaṁ tasya bālakasya na te viduḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Even the cowherds did not believe the words of the children. They were unaware that Kṛṣṇa had unlimited power.**

**Комментарий:**

They did not believe the children. Though they were qualified to know everything, they did not know Kṛṣṇa’s unlimited strength since their knowledge of his powers was covered by his childhood behavior.

### Text 11

*rudantaṁ sutam ādāya yaśodā graha-śaṅkitā*  
*kṛta-svastyayanaṁ vipraiḥ sūktaiḥ stanam apāyayat*

**Перевод:**

**Fearing some evil spirits, mother Yaśodā picked up the crying child and after brāhmaṇas chanted Vedic hymns and performed an auspicious ritualistic ceremony, she allowed him to suck her breast.**

**Комментарий:**

She had auspicious rites performed with chanting of Vedic verses by brāhmaṇas for destroying Rākṣasas.

### Text 12

*pūrvavat sthāpitaṁ gopair balibhiḥ sa-paricchadam*  
*viprā hutvārcayāṁ cakrur dadhy-akṣata-kuśāmbubhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After the strong, stout cowherd men assembled the pots and paraphernalia on the cart and set it up as before, the brāhmaṇas performed a sacrifice and then, with rice grains, kuśa, water and curd, they worshiped the cart.**

**Комментарий:**

Since strong cowherds set the cart properly, it is understood that cart must have been large and heavy. The brāhmaṇas performed a graha-homa for general protection, worshipping the cart using yogurt etc.

### Texts 13-15

*ye ’sūyānṛta-dambherṣā-hiṁsā-māna-vivarjitāḥ*  
*na teṣāṁ satya-śīlānām āśiṣo viphalāḥ kṛtāḥ*

*iti bālakam ādāya sāmarg-yajur-upākṛtaiḥ*  
*jalaiḥ pavitrauṣadhibhir abhiṣicya dvijottamaiḥ*

*vācayitvā svastyayanaṁ nanda-gopaḥ samāhitaḥ*  
*hutvā cāgniṁ dvijātibhyaḥ prādād annaṁ mahā-guṇam*

**Перевод:**

**The blessings of brāhmaṇas, who are truthful, who are free from envy, untruthfulness, deceit, malice, violence and pride, never go in vain. Considering this, Nanda Mahārāja took Kṛṣṇa on his lap and invited the brāhmaṇas to bathe the child using water mixed with pure herbs, while they chanted mantras of the Sāma Veda, Ṛg Veda and Yajur Veda. After having them chant auspicious verses and perform sacrifice, he gave them tasty, fragrant rice with devotion.**

**Комментарий:**

The blessings of those who are free from ascribing faults in good qualities (asūyā), lying (anṛta), performing dharma for fame (dambha), intolerance (īrṣya), giving suffering to other beings by body, etc., (hiṁsa) and pride (māna), who are of truthful character, are never in vain. The results are seen in my son.

Knowing this (iti), Nanda, lord of Vraja, took Kṛṣṇa and had the best of brāhmaṇas bathe him with water, purified by Sāma mantras and mixed with pure herbs. He had them perform sacrifice and gave them rice which was soft, sweet and fragrant (mahā-guṇam).

### Text 16

*gāvaḥ sarva-guṇopetā vāsaḥ-srag-rukma-mālinīḥ*  
*ātmajābhyudayārthāya prādāt te cānvayuñjata*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja, for the sake of the affluence of his own son Kṛṣṇa, gave the brāhmaṇas cows endowed with all qualities, fully decorated with garments, flower garlands and gold necklaces. The brāhmaṇas bestowed blessings.**

**Комментарий:**

The cows had all qualities such as giving plenty of milk. The brāhmaṇas gave blessings (anvayuñjata).

### Text 17

*viprā mantra-vido yuktās tair yāḥ proktās tathāśiṣaḥ*  
*tā niṣphalā bhaviṣyanti na kadācid api sphuṭam*

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇas, who were expert in chanting the Vedic hymns, were yogīs. Thus whatever blessings they spoke were certainly never fruitless.**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇas were yogīs (yuktāḥ). The blessings were never fruitless since those results are always in Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 18

*ekadāroham ārūḍhaṁ lālayantī sutaṁ satī*  
*garimāṇaṁ śiśor voḍhuṁ na sehe giri-kūṭavat*

**Перевод:**

**A year after Kṛṣṇa’s appearance, mother Yaśodā was pampering her son on her lap. But suddenly she felt the child to be heavier than a mountain peak, and she could no longer bear his weight.**

**Комментарий:**

Another pastime is related. This was after a year since it will later be said eka-hāyana āsīna (SB [10.26.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/26.6)). She was caring for Kṛṣṇa on her lap, raising him in her arms and swinging him. She could not carry him since he was heavy like a stone mountain. When he developed the desire to have pastimes in the sky while swinging in his mother’s arms and desired to see the place of his pastimes from high up, Tṛṇāvarta came to fulfill that desire. My mother will have difficulty if he lifts me up along with her. Thus I will separate myself from her lap. Desiring to do so since he became heavy, he got off her lap. But when he was being lifted, he became light again.

### Text 19

*bhūmau nidhāya taṁ gopī vismitā bhāra-pīḍitā*  
*mahā-puruṣam ādadhyau jagatām āsa karmasu*

**Перевод:**

**Astonished and afflicted by his weight, Yaśodā placed Kṛṣṇa on the earth. She surrendered to the Lord of the universe and engaged in auspicious rites to protect him.**

**Комментарий:**

Yaśodā (gopī), the queen, afflicted by the weight, placed Kṛṣṇa on the ground in confusion and became astonished. “Why has this baby become heavy?” She worried that it was the influence of evil spirits. She meditated on Nārāyaṇa, the great lord of the universe, to pacify the evil spirit and engaged in calling brāhmaṇas for pacifying.

### Text 20

*daityo nāmnā tṛṇāvartaḥ kaṁsa-bhṛtyaḥ pracoditaḥ*  
*cakravāta-svarūpeṇa jahārāsīnam arbhakam*

**Перевод:**

**While the child was sitting on the ground, a demon named Tṛṇāvarta, who was a servant of Kaṁsa, came there as a whirlwind, at Kaṁsa’s instigation, and carried the seated child into the air.**

**Комментарий:**

Tṛṇāvarta was sent by Kaṁsa.

### Text 21

*gokulaṁ sarvam āvṛṇvan muṣṇaṁś cakṣūṁṣi reṇubhiḥ*  
*īrayan sumahā-ghora-śabdena pradiśo diśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Covering the whole land of Gokula with particles of dust, that demon covered everyone’s vision and began vibrating everywhere with a greatly fearful sound.**

**Комментарий:**

He made the ten directions and intermediate directions tremble or resound with terrifying sound. Since he was a demon in the form of wind, he was wicked, very strong and could not be defeated. Since he was Kaṁsa’s servant, he was filled with hatred. Previously Kaṁsa generally sent Pūtanā, who could kill children. Worried by the death of that demon though she had two forms, he sent Śakaṭāsura with apparently no form. When he was killed, Kaṁsa in fear specially sent a great wind, difficult to be caught, simultaneously with form and no form, and the strongest.

### Text 22

*muhūrtam abhavad goṣṭhaṁ rajasā tamasāvṛtam*  
*sutaṁ yaśodā nāpaśyat tasmin nyastavatī yataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Since the whole pasturing ground was overcast with dense darkness from the dust storm in a moment, mother Yaśodā, who had placed her son beside her, was unable to see him.**

**Комментарий:**

Yataḥ means “in that place.”

### Text 23

*nāpaśyat kaścanātmānaṁ paraṁ cāpi vimohitaḥ*  
*tṛṇāvarta-nisṛṣṭābhiḥ śarkarābhir upadrutaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because of the bits of sand thrown about by Tṛṇāvarta, people could not see themselves or anyone else. Thus they could not search and were profoundly disturbed.**

### Text 24

*iti khara-pavana-cakra-pāṁśu-varṣe*  
*suta-padavīm abalāvilakṣya mātā*  
*atikaruṇam anusmaranty aśocad*  
*bhuvi patitā mṛta-vatsakā yathā gauḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because of the dust storm stirred up by the strong whirlwind, mother Yaśodā could find no trace of her son. Thus she fell down on the ground and began to lament very pitifully like a cow which has lost a calf.**

**Комментарий:**

She could not see her son because of the dust thrown up by the strong whirlwind.

### Text 25

*ruditam anu niśamya tatra gopyo*  
*bhṛśam anutapta-dhiyo ’śru-pūrṇa-mukhyaḥ*  
*rurudur anupalabhya nanda-sūnuṁ*  
*pavana upārata-pāṁśu-varṣa-vege*

**Перевод:**

**When the force of the dust storm and the winds subsided, Yaśodā’s friends, the other gopīs, hearing her pitiful crying and not seeing Kṛṣṇa present, became aggrieved and wept, their eyes full of tears.**

**Комментарий:**

When the wind gave up its force of showering dust, hearing Yaśodā crying in Gokula (tatra), the other gopīs having arrived there, notseeing Kṛṣṇa, became greatly pained in their hearts and cried as Yaśodā cried.

### Text 26

*tṛṇāvartaḥ śānta-rayo vātyā-rūpa-dharo haran*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ nabho-gato gantuṁ nāśaknod bhūri-bhāra-bhṛt*

**Перевод:**

**Having assumed the form of a forceful whirlwind, the demon Tṛṇāvarta took Kṛṣṇa high in the sky, but when Kṛṣṇa became heavy, the demon, feeling the heavy weight, could go no further.**

**Комментарий:**

Tṛṇāvarta took Kṛṣṇa, like other children, into the sky. There he became heavy. Aware of the weight, he gave up his endeavor (śānta-rayaḥ). Then he was not able to carry him. Then he could go further.

### Text 27

*tam aśmānaṁ manyamāna ātmano guru-mattayā*  
*gale gṛhīta utsraṣṭuṁ nāśaknod adbhutārbhakam*

**Перевод:**

**Because of Kṛṣṇa’s weight, Tṛṇāvarta considered Kṛṣṇa to be a sapphire mountain. But because Kṛṣṇa had caught the demon’s neck, the demon was unable to throw him off. He therefore considered the child extraordinary.**

**Комментарий:**

Having fulfilled his desire to see his place of pastimes and play in the sky, having made the devatā women blissful, the son of Yaśodā prepared to kill the demon. The demon thought of Kṛṣṇa as a mountain, a body of stone because the child’s weight was much greater than his own weight. Though he desired to give him up, he could not since Kṛṣṇa held his neck. Absorbed in childhood pastimes, Kṛṣṇa acted like a child afraid of falling.

### Text 28

*gala-grahaṇa-niśceṣṭo daityo nirgata-locanaḥ*  
*avyakta-rāvo nyapatat saha-bālo vyasur vraje*

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa grasped him by the throat, Tṛṇāvarta choked, unable to make even a sound or even to move his hands and legs. His eyes popped out, and he died. He fell along with the little boy in Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

By grabbing his throat, he gave up movement. The demon could not scream in pain (avyakta-rāvaḥ). Pūtanā had frightened the people of Vraja by her painful cries. This should not happen now. By squeezing the demon’s throat, the demon was killed in the sky.From that, he gave up his life (vyasuḥ).

### Text 29

*tam antarikṣāt patitaṁ śilāyāṁ*  
*viśīrṇa-sarvāvayavaṁ karālam*  
*puraṁ yathā rudra-śareṇa viddhaṁ*  
*striyo rudatyo dadṛśuḥ sametāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs who had gathered, crying for Kṛṣṇa, saw the demon fall from the sky onto a big slab of stone, his tough limbs dislocated, just as the city pierced by Śiva’s arrows was crushed and fell from the sky.**

**Комментарий:**

He fell on a large stone in the yard.

### Text 30

*prādāya mātre pratihṛtya vismitāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ ca tasyorasi lambamānam*  
*taṁ svastimantaṁ puruṣāda-nītaṁ*  
*vihāyasā mṛtyu-mukhāt pramuktam*  
*gopyaś ca gopāḥ kila nanda-mukhyā*  
*labdhvā punaḥ prāpur atīva modam*

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs immediately picked up Kṛṣṇa, who had been taken by the demon into the sky but was still healthy and now hanging on the demon’s chest, and delivered him, freed from the mouth of death, to mother Yaśodā. The gopīs and cowherd men, headed by Nanda Mahārāja, having attained him again, were extremely happy.**

**Комментарий:**

The astonished women took Kṛṣṇa who was on the demon’s chest, and gave him to his mother. That the child was found on the demon’s chest means the child was unharmed because the demon had fallen on the stone on his back. He was brought by the path ofthe sky (vihāyasā), by the eater of men (puruṣāda). Thus Kṛṣṇa had been freed as if from the mouth of death.

### Text 31

*aho batāty-adbhutam eṣa rakṣasā*  
*bālo nivṛttiṁ gamito ’bhyagāt punaḥ*  
*hiṁsraḥ sva-pāpena vihiṁsitaḥ khalaḥ*  
*sādhuḥ samatvena bhayād vimucyate*

**Перевод:**

**It is most astonishing that although this innocent child was taken away by the Rākṣasa to be eaten, he has returned without having been killed or even injured. Because this demon was envious, cruel and sinful, he has been killed for his own sinful activities. This is the law of nature. An innocent devotee is always protected by the Supreme Lord, and a sinful person is always vanquished for his sinful life.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the thought of Kṛṣṇa as the Lord was rising by seeing the destruction of the great demon, for Nanda and others, by thinking of him as their son this thought disappeared like the river Sarasvatī which became invisible. It is greatly astonishing that this child, though taken to some condition that is unsuitable to describe (nivṛttim), has again attained the presence of his relatives. With disappearance of their appreciation of his powers, words expressing prema out of vātsalya appeared. This is not astonishing for saintly people. Some who were equal to such saintly people spoke. The violent person has been destroyed by his sin of stealing innocent child. Kṛṣṇa by seeing friends and enemies equally, since he is a child, has been freed from fear.

### Text 32

*kiṁ nas tapaś cīrṇam adhokṣajārcanaṁ*  
*pūrteṣṭa-dattam uta bhūta-sauhṛdam*  
*yat samparetaḥ punar eva bālako*  
*diṣṭyā sva-bandhūn praṇayann upasthitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja and the others said: We must previously have performed austerities for a very long time, and worshiped the Supreme Lord by performing pūrtas, iṣṭas, charitable acts, and showing friendship to all beings, for this boy, as if returning from death, has come here, giving life to his relatives.**

**Комментарий:**

Reflecting on the cause of Kṛṣṇa returning unharmed, they speak. We must have performed (cīrṇam) digging of wells (pūrta), pañca- yajña, agni-hotra, etc., (iṣṭam), and charity to qualified persons by giving properly acquired food which is meant for one’s enjoyment(dattam). Because of this (yad) the boy has returned, giving joy (praṇayan) to his relatives.

### Text 33

*dṛṣṭvādbhutāni bahuśo nanda-gopo bṛhadvane*  
*vasudeva-vaco bhūyo mānayām āsa vismitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Having seen all these many remarkable incidents in Bṛhadvana, Nanda Mahārāja remembered the words of Vasudeva and became astonished.**

### Text 34

*ekadārbhakam ādāya svāṅkam āropya bhāminī*  
*prasnutaṁ pāyayām āsa stanaṁ sneha-pariplutā*

**Перевод:**

**One day mother Yaśodā, overflowing with affection, having taken Kṛṣṇa up and placed him on her lap, was feeding him from her breast which flowed with excess milk.**

### Texts 35-36

*pīta-prāyasya jananī sutasya rucira-smitam*  
*mukhaṁ lālayatī rājañ jṛmbhato dadṛśe idam*

*khaṁ rodasī jyotir-anīkam āśāḥ*  
*sūryendu-vahni-śvasanāmbudhīṁś ca*  
*dvīpān nagāṁs tad-duhitṝr vanāni*  
*bhūtāni yāni sthira-jaṅgamāni*

**Перевод:**

**When the child Kṛṣṇa was almost finished drinking, Yaśodā was about to kiss his smiling face, the baby yawned, and mother Yaśodā saw in his mouth the universe. She saw the whole sky, the higher planetary systems and the earth, the luminaries, the directions, the sun, the moon, fire, air, the seas, islands, trees, mountains, rivers, forests, and all kinds of living entities, moving and nonmoving.**

**Комментарий:**

He has almost finished drinking milk. Yaśodā caressing his face (lālayatī), holding his chin. Through his yawning mouth, she saw the whole universe within his belly since it will be said:

*kṛtsnasya cāntar jaṭhare jananyā*

**You showed the whole universe within your abdomen to your mother. (SB** [**10.14.16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.16)**)**

Showing the entire universe right at the time of his yawning was accomplished by his acintya-śakti. My mother is omniscient and knows my form of power at all times. But she has not seen it. Not seeing it, she fears for me. Showing her my powers, I will make her free of worries. Thus, he showed her this form. She saw trees (nagān) such as the Jambu tree, after which islands are named (Jambudvīpa, etc.) and mountains (nagān). Tad-duhitṝḥ(their daughters) means rivers.

### Text 37

*sā vīkṣya viśvaṁ sahasā rājan sañjāta-vepathuḥ*  
*sammīlya mṛgaśāvākṣī netre āsīt suvismitā*

**Перевод:**

**When mother Yaśodā with fawn-like eyes saw the whole universe within the mouth of her child, she trembled, closed her eyes and became struck with wonder.**

**Комментарий:**

At that very moment and simultaneously (sahasā), she trembled. From the astonishing vision she closed her eyes so as to not see it. She was astonished. “How can the universe exist in his belly?” Out of astonishment she became motionless like a picture.

*pūtanām oṣṭhayoḥ sparśāc chakaṭaṁ padayoḥ śiśuḥ \|*  
*bhujayoś ca tṛṇāvartam ahann āsye kṣitākhilaḥ*  
*ahīna-nara-ceṣṭābhir ābhir līlābhir acyutaḥ \|*  
*nijaiśvaryasya pūrṇatvaṁ mādhuryaṁ ca vyajijñapat*

**The baby, destroying them all, killed Pūtanā by the touch of his lips. He killed Śakaṭa by his feet. He killed Tṛṇāvatra by his arms. Acyuta showed the completeness and sweetness of his lordship by acting like a perfectly human cowherd.**

## Chapter 8 - Lord Kṛṣṇa Shows the Universal Form Within His Mouth

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*gargaḥ purohito rājan yadūnāṁ sumahā-tapāḥ*  
*vrajaṁ jagāma nandasya vasudeva-pracoditaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, the priest of the Yadu dynasty, namely Gargamuni, who was highly elevated in austerity and penance, inspired by Vasudeva, went to see Nanda Mahārāja at his home.**

**Комментарий:**

*varṇitaṁ nāma-karaṇaṁ riṅkhaṇaṁ dadhi-moṣaṇam \|*  
*viśva-rūpekṣaṇaṁ mātur aiśya-jñānaṁ tathāṣṭame*

**The eight chapter recounts the child’s name giving ceremony, crawling about, stealing yogurt, displaying the universal form and Yaśodā’s knowledge of Kṛṣṇa’s powers.**

Having described Tṛṇāvarta’s killing related to killing other demons, the previous festivals like the name giving ceremony are described.

### Text 2

*taṁ dṛṣṭvā parama-prītaḥ pratyutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ*  
*ānarcādhokṣaja-dhiyā praṇipāta-puraḥsaram*

**Перевод:**

**When Nanda Mahārāja saw Gargamuni present at his home, he was most pleased. He stood up and received him with folded hands. He worshipped him, seeing him like the Supreme Lord while offering respects in front of him.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda worshipped Garga thinking him to be the body of the Supreme Lord (adhokṣaja-dhiyā).

### Text 3

*sūpaviṣṭaṁ kṛtātithyaṁ girā sūnṛtayā munim*  
*nandayitvābravīd brahman pūrṇasya karavāma kim*

**Перевод:**

**When Gargamuni had been properly received as a guest and was very comfortably seated, Nanda Mahārāja submitted with gentle and submissive words: Dear sir, because you are a devotee, you are complete in everything. Yet my duty is to serve you. Kindly order me. What can I do for you?**

**Комментарий:**

He washed his feet and sat him down comfortably. He received him as a guest by offering madhuparka and other items. He spoke with sweet words of praise. Nanda says that Garga had achieved perfection in all attainments (pūrṇasya) by his devotion to the Lord.

### Text 4

*mahad-vicalanaṁ nṝṇāṁ gṛhiṇāṁ dīna-cetasām*  
*niḥśreyasāya bhagavan kalpate nānyathā kvacit*

**Перевод:**

**O my lord, O great devotee, persons like you move from one place to another not for their own interests but for the sake of poor-hearted householders. Otherwise they have no interest in going from one place to another.**

**Комментарий:**

“But if he is perfected how is it that he came to the house of wealthy people?” Great devotees (mahad) travel from their āśrama to other places, to give benefit to householders and not for their own benefit. “But why do not the householders go to meet them?” The householders are not capable of giving up their house because their minds are withered (dīna-cetasām) due to thinking of the welfare of wife and children. They do not go except to benefit these miserable people.

### Text 5

*jyotiṣām ayanaṁ sākṣād yat taj jñānam atīndriyam*  
*praṇītaṁ bhavatā yena pumān veda parāvaram*

**Перевод:**

**O great saintly person, you have compiled the astrological knowledge by which one gains knowledge which is beyond the normal senses and by which anyone can know the past and future.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to request giving the names to the two children, Nanda describes Garga’s great knowledge. Astrological scripture, which reveals the planets, etc., and from which one attains knowledge beyond the senses has been written by you. By that studying that scripture, any person can know the future (para) and past (avara) events. By that, you can tell us the auspicious future of the two boys.

### Text 6

*tvaṁ hi brahma-vidāṁ śreṣṭhaḥ saṁskārān kartum arhasi*  
*bālayor anayor nṝṇāṁ janmanā brāhmaṇo guruḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because you are the best of the knowers of the Vedas and are a brāhmaṇa by birth, and thus a guru for all human beings, you should perform the saṁskāras for the two boys.**

**Комментарий:**

You are not only the best knower of astrology but the best knower of the Vedas. Knowing astrology and mantras you should perform the name giving ceremony for the two boys. “But this the father’s duty on account of the statement dvādaśe ‘hani pitā nāma kuryād: the father should give the name on the twelfth day.” A brāhmaṇa is the guru for all men just by his birth (janmanā), what to speak of by knowledge. If a person like you is not available, the father should do the ceremony.

### Text 7

*śrī-garga uvāca*  
*yadūnām aham ācāryaḥ khyātaś ca bhuvi sarvadā*  
*sutaṁ mayā saṁskṛtaṁ te manyate devakī-sutam*

**Перевод:**

**Gargamuni said: On this earth I am known at all times as the priest of the Yadu dynasty. Therefore, if I perform the purificatory process for your sons, Kaṁsa will know that they are the sons of Devakī.**

**Комментарий:**

Afraid of Kaṁsa, he speaks to insistent Nanda, that this ceremony must be a secret, as if prohibiting. Though born in the Yadu dynasty, you are not known as a Yadu since you are not a kṣatriya. But I am famous everywhere as the priest of the Yadus. If I do the saṁskāra, Kaṁsa will think that your son is Devakī’s son.

### Texts 8-9

*kaṁsaḥ pāpa-matiḥ sakhyaṁ tava cānakadundubheḥ*  
*devakyā aṣṭamo garbho na strī bhavitum arhati*

*iti sañcintayañ chrutvā devakyā dārikā-vacaḥ*  
*api hantā gatāśaṅkas tarhi tan no ’nayo bhavet*

**Перевод:**

**Kaṁsa, with an evil mind, considering that you are the friend of Vasudeva, and that the eighth child of Devakī could not be a female, and hearing the words of Durgā that the child had been born elsewhere, not in the prison, will be suspicious of you and come here. Therefore it is not safe to do the saṁskāra.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. “How can he ascertain this much?” He looks for clues through spies (papa-matiḥ). There is a clue in the search. You are Vasudeva’s friend. He will use logic. Hearing the words of Devakī’s daughter Durgā, he will think that Devakī’s eighth child cannot be a woman. Since I have not been killed by her, the voice from the sky mentioned the eighth garbha would kill me (SB [10.1.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.34)). The word Garbha though a common word, means a son. My worshipable deity is Durgā. Becoming that female child, she acts for my benefit, though forbidden by Viṣṇu. By generally saying , “Your killer has been born elsewhere” (SB [10.4.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/4.12)) she indicated Viṣṇu’s birth in that statement. By the well-known friendship of both of you and my performing the nāma-karaṇa, if that killer of six children becomes suspicious (gatāśaṅkaḥ), then my performing the ceremony is great calamity (anayaḥ). Api means it is possible. If the meaning is understood then he will suspect that Vasudeva’s son is in Nanda’s house (gatāśaṅkaḥ).

### Text 10

*śrī-nanda uvāca*  
*alakṣito ’smin rahasi māmakair api go-vraje*  
*kuru dvijāti-saṁskāraṁ svasti-vācana-pūrvakam*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja said: Secret even to my associates, perform the saṁskāras of the twice born in the cow shed when no one is present, along with chanting of svasti-vācana**

**Комментарий:**

If you fear Kaṁsa, do as follows. Do the saṁskāra of the twice-born uttering svasti-vācana in secret in the cowshed, unknown ever by my brothers. When will I again meet a great sage like you! Go-vraja (cowshed) indicates that he purity of the place is disregarded. The cowshed is secluded since the cows along with the herdsmen go to the forest during the say. Just the nāma-kāraṇa should be done for the two, kṣatriya and vaiśya (dvijāti), in conformity to them by saying three times the svasti-vācana consists of repeating the three words puṇyāha-svasty-ṛddhi. Since svasti-vācana is necessary in all karmas, svasti-vācana-pūrvakam is used (in the verse). After you go from here, I will arrange the music and dancing, the limbs of the festival.

### Text 11

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*evaṁ samprārthito vipraḥ sva-cikīrṣitam eva tat*  
*cakāra nāma-karaṇaṁ gūḍho rahasi bālayoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Having thus been especially requested by Nanda Mahārāja to do that which he already desired to do, Gargamuni performed the name-giving ceremony for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma in a solitary place.**

### Text 12

*śrī-garga uvāca*  
*ayaṁ hi rohiṇī-putro ramayan suhṛdo guṇaiḥ*  
*ākhyāsyate rāma iti balādhikyād balaṁ viduḥ*  
*yadūnām apṛthag-bhāvāt saṅkarṣaṇam uśanty api*

**Перевод:**

**Gargamuni said: This child, the son of Rohiṇī, will give all happiness to his relatives and friends by his transcendental qualities. Therefore he will be known as Rāma. And because he will manifest extraordinary bodily strength, he will also be known as Bala. Moreover, because he unites two families—Vasudeva’s family and the family of Nanda Mahārāja—he will be known as Saṅkarṣaṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

He explains the name Saṅkarṣaṇa in the last line. He will be called Saṅkarṣaṇa because of attracting to himself the two families of Vasudeva’s and yours by having undiscriminating feelings of father, etc., (apṛthak-bhāvāt), and because of pulling to one place the Yadus who had gone somewhere due to fear of Kaṁsa. That he joined the two families in himself through feelings of father, etc., is on account of Balarāma says to Nanda’s brothers:

*pratyuvāca tato rāmaḥ sarvān tān abhitaḥ sthitān*  
*yādaveṣv api sarveṣu bhavanto mama vallabhāḥ*

**Balarāma then replied to them all standing around him, “Among all the Yādavas, you are the dearest to me.” (Hari- vaṁśa)**

Garga did not reveal that Balarāma had been taken from Devakī’s womb (and therefore called Saṅkarṣaṇa) since that was secret.

### Text 13

*āsan varṇās trayo hy asya gṛhṇato ’nuyugaṁ tanūḥ*  
*śuklo raktas tathā pīta idānīṁ kṛṣṇatāṁ gataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Your son Kṛṣṇa appeared in previous yugas (according to the avatāra he worshipped) with three different colors—white, red and yellow—and now he has appeared in a blackish color.**

**Комментарий:**

Garga explains Nanda’s son’s names.

*sat-puṇḍarīka-nayanaṁ meghābhaṁ vaidyutāmbaram \|*  
*dvi-bhujaṁ mauna-mudrāḍhyaṁ vana-mālinam īśvaram*

**Meditate with concentration on two-armed lotus-eyed, silent Kṛṣṇa, who has the complexion of a cloud, who wears cloth flashing like lightning and a garland. (Gopāla- tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

According to śruti, without beginning, your son who is black like a cloud (asya) has three colors and forms. He manifests (gṛhṇataḥ) forms (tanūḥ) in various yugas (anuyugam) on account of the statement:

*anādeyam aheyaṁ ca rūpaṁ bhagavato hareḥ \|*  
*āvirbhāva-tirobhāvāv asyokte graha-mocane*

**The form of the Lord is not accepted or given up by him. The Lord’s appearance (āvirbhāva) and disappearance (tirobhāva) is called accepting and giving up a body. (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa)**

In Satya-yuga his color is white. In Tretā his color is red and in Kali his color is yellow. But now, at the end of Dvāparā, all the white and other colors have entered this black form (kṛṣṇatām) on account of the statement:

*parāvareśo mahad-aṁśa-yukto*

**Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, though not having material birth, appears within this world along with all his Viṣṇu expansions, since he is the lord of all forms of God and devatās. (SB** [**3.2.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.15)**)**

Thus, he is complete and his name is Kṛṣṇa on account of the following statement in Nārāyaṇiyā:

*kṛṣṇo varṇaś ca me yasmāt tasmāt kṛṣṇo ‘ham arjuna*

**Since I am black in color, I am Kṛṣṇa, O Arjuna. (Mahābhārata)**

“He was yellow in color” means that this was a previous pīta-avatāra (another day of Brahmā), and not an ordinary Kali-yuga since in an ordinary Kali-yuga the color is black according to Hari-vaṁśa. But this refers to Kali following the present Dvāparā.

### Text 14

*prāg ayaṁ vasudevasya kvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ*  
*vāsudeva iti śrīmān abhijñāḥ sampracakṣate*

**Перевод:**

**This beautiful son of yours somewhere appeared previously as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore, those who are learned sometimes call this child Vāsudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

How is your son born to Vasudeva? This happened in a previous life. He was called Vāsudeva then too.

“Previously in some solitary place in Kaṁsa’s prison, your son was born to Vasudeva in Devakī.” But “he was brought here by him and merged in this child.” Since this was a secret, Garga did not reveal this. The learned (abhijñāḥ) call him Vāsudeva, not just I.

### Text 15

*bahūni santi nāmāni rūpāṇi ca sutasya te*  
*guṇa-karmānurūpāṇi tāny ahaṁ veda no janāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**For this son of yours there are many forms and names according to his qualities and activities. These are not known completely to me, so how can people in general know?**

**Комментарий:**

You have said that Kṛṣṇa is the avatārī of the yugāvatāras. Who the avatārī of the puruṣāvatāras, līlāvatāras and manvantarāvatāras? He is only that. Those innumerable avatāras are all his. They are eternally manifest (santi). The names according to his qualities are such as sarva-jña (all-knowing), bhakta-vatsala (affection for devotees). The names according to his activities are such as prakṛti-pravartaka (stimulating prakṛti for creation), viśva-sraṣṭṛ (creator of the material world), and viśvāntaryāmī (antaryāmī of the world). I, an astrologer and knower of the Vedas, do not know them completely. So how can other people know? And your son is the Svayaṁ Prabhu.

### Text 16

*eṣa vaḥ śreya ādhāsyad gopa-gokula-nandanaḥ*  
*anena sarva-durgāṇi yūyam añjas tariṣyatha*

**Перевод:**

**By his nature increasing the bliss of the cowherd men and cows, this child will always act most auspiciously for you. And by his grace only, you will surpass all difficulties**

**Комментарий:**

Though he is of this nature, he will carry out your orders. Giving joy (nandanaḥ) to all the cowherds and cows or as the son (nandanaḥ) of all cowherds and cows in Brahma-vimohana-līlā, he will act for your benefit. Whenever dangers (sarva-durgāṇi) occur he will easily supress them by his aṁśas.

### Text 17

*purānena vraja-pate sādhavo dasyu-pīḍitāḥ*  
*arājake rakṣyamāṇā jigyur dasyūn samedhitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In a previous birth, when Indra was dethroned, and the devatās were afflicted by the demons, they were rescued by Kṛṣṇa, they conquered the demons and they then flourished.**

**Комментарий:**

His nature of protecting devatās is described. Afflicted by the demons (dasyu) when Indra was dethroned (arājake), they increased in strength by the Lord’s favor, as will be described.

### Text 18

*ya etasmin mahā-bhāge prītiṁ kurvanti mānavāḥ*  
*nārayo ’bhibhavanty etān viṣṇu-pakṣān ivāsurāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Enemies cannot harm the devotees who show affection for this greatly fortunate child, just as the demons cannot harm the devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, those who show affection for Kṛṣṇa are alone fortunate souls (mahābhāgaḥ), and enemies cannot defeat them just as the demons cannot defeat the devatās, who are favored by the Lord. Another version has mahābhāge. O Yaśodā! O queen! She was also present there since it said that acts of dharma should be performed with the wife.

### Text 19

*tasmān nandātmajo ’yaṁ te nārāyaṇa-samo guṇaiḥ*  
*śriyā kīrtyānubhāvena gopāyasva samāhitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In conclusion, therefore, O Nanda Mahārāja, this child of yours is as good as Nārāyaṇa by his qualities, opulence, fame and influence. You should protect this child very carefully.**

**Комментарий:**

“But there is someone else like him.” Because of his quantity of great qualities, your son is equal to Nārāyaṇa, lord of the spiritual sky, by qualities which are fixed within him, such as mercy, and external qualities such as beauty (śriyā). Nārāyaṇa is his vilāsaexpansion by these qualities, and thus equal to him. Because Nārāyaṇa is compared to him, Kṛṣṇa excels in some qualities. The qualities of Kṛṣṇa include having companions full of the highest prema, sweetness of his flute which astonishes knowers of tattvalike Brahmā, and enchanting all moving and non-moving beings, the sweetness of form that astonishes everyone including himself,and the rāsa dance that even Lakṣmī could not attain.

But you do not worship him with sixteen upacāras as you worship Nārāyaṇa. Rather with attention protect him, i.e., serve him with articles suitable to the mood of a son. He is extremely pleased by accepting him as a relative, not as a devatā on account of his statement to the cowherds who were doubtful:

*mat-saṁbandhena vo gopā yadi lajjā na jāyate \|*  
*ślāghyo vāhaṁ tataḥ kiṁ vo vicāreṇa prayojanam*  
*yadi vo ‘sti mayi prītiḥ ślāghyo ‘haṁ bhavatāṁ yadi \|*  
*tad-ātma-bandhu-sadṛśī buddhir vaḥ kriyātāṁ mayi*  
*nāhaṁ devo na gāndharvo na yakṣo na ca dānavaḥ \|*  
*ahaṁ vo bāndhavo jāto naitac cintyam ato ‘nyathā*

**If you are not ashamed of having a relationship with me, or if I am praiseworthy, then why think about this at all? If you have affection for me and if I am praised by you, you should think of me as the closest friend. I am not a devatā, Gandharva, Yakṣa or demon. I have been born as your friend. You should not think otherwise. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa** [**5.13.9-12**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/13.9)**)**

*manyante māṁ yathā sarve bhavanto bhīma-vikramāḥ*  
*tathāhaṁ nāvagantavyaḥ sajātīyo ’smi bāndhavaḥ*

**Just as all of you, having great prowess, think of me in that way, I am not understood. I am your relative and friend. (Hari-vaṁśa)**

Though Kṛṣṇa is not different from Nārāyaṇa, they are called different because of some special features which differentiates. Nārāyaṇa is Kṛṣṇa’s vilāsa form on account of the indications in following statements:

*goloka-nāmni nija-dhāmni tale ca tasya*  
*devī-maheśa-hari-dhāmasu teṣu teṣu \|*  
*te te prabhāva-nicayā vihitāś ca yena*  
*govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi*

**I worship the Supreme Lord Govinda by whom respective powers are given to the abodes of Durgā, Śiva and Viṣṇu, which are situated below his own planet of Goloka. (Brahma-saṁhitā)**

*anādy-antaṁ paraṁ brahma na devā na rṣayo viduḥ*  
*eko ’yam veda bhagavān dhātā nārāyaṇo hariḥ*

**The devatās and sages do not know Parabrahma, who is without beginning or end. This one creator Bhagāvan, Nārāyaṇa, Hari, knows Parabrahma. (Bhīṣma-stuti, Mokṣa- dharma)**

### Text 20

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity ātmānaṁ samādiśya garge ca sva-gṛhaṁ gate*  
*nandaḥ pramudito mene ātmānaṁ pūrṇam āśiṣām*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: After Gargamuni, after instructing Nanda Mahārāja, departed for his own home, Nanda Mahārāja was very pleased and considered himself full of all good fortune.**

**Комментарий:**

Instructed that his son was a form full of knowledge and bliss, Nanda was joyful. “Garga has instructed me according to my bhāva.” He considered himself fully blessed in his desires. Then he performed the name ceremony, etc., of his son through his priests like Bhāguri according to his wishes.

### Text 21

*kālena vrajatālpena gokule rāma-keśavau*  
*jānubhyāṁ saha pāṇibhyāṁ riṅgamāṇau vijahratuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After a short time passed, both brothers, Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, began to crawl on the ground of Vraja with the strength of their hands and knees and thus wandered about.**

**Комментарий:**

After speaking of the childhood pastimes which covered Kṛṣṇa’s powers, some pure pastimes (unmixed with power), which are like mirror are described.

### Text 22

*tāv aṅghri-yugmam anukṛṣya sarīsṛpantau*  
*ghoṣa-praghoṣa-ruciraṁ vraja-kardameṣu*  
*tan-nāda-hṛṣṭa-manasāv anusṛtya lokaṁ*  
*mugdha-prabhītavad upeyatur anti mātroḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, with the strength of their legs, crawled about zigzag in the muddy places of Vraja, the sound of their ankle bells was very charming. Pleased by the sound of other people’s ankle bells, they used to follow these people, but when they saw that these were other people, they became afraid and returned to their real mothers.**

**Комментарий:**

The two crawled about crookedly (sarīsṛpantau) in the mud mixed with cow urine and cow dung in the yards of Vraja. This indicates their strength. They crawled on their knees, making attractive jingling sounds with their ornaments (ghoṣa-praghoṣa-ruciram),attractive to the best of yogīs, their minds were pleased by those sounds. Following people who had come, thinking they are familymembers, and later understanding they were strangers, they went to their mothers in fear and bewilderment. It is later said that Yaśodā saw their bewilderment and fear (SB [10.8.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.33)). This bewilderment and fear of the Lord is not false since it is for nourishing the rasa of the pastimes since illusion is not applicable for knowers of truth, Uddhava and Kunti (who have said the following).

Concerning his bewilderment, Uddhava says:

*mantreṣu māṁ vā upahūya yat tvam*  
*akuṇṭhitākhaṇḍa-sadātma-bodhaḥ*  
*pṛccheḥ prabho mugdha ivāpramattas*  
*tan no mano mohayatīva deva*

**O master! O Lord! You who are always full of knowledge, unaffected by time and complete, would call me for consultation and ask me, just as ignorant people would do, attentive to my advice. When you, though full of knowledge, act in this way, it bewilders my mind. (SB** [**3.4.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/4.17)**)**

Concerning his fear, Kuntī says:

*gopy ādade tvayi kṛtāgasi dāma tāvad*  
*yā te daśāśru-kalilāñjana-sambhramākṣam*  
*vaktraṁ ninīya bhaya-bhāvanayā sthitasya*  
*sā māṁ vimohayati bhīr api yad bibheti*

**My dear Kṛṣṇa, Yaśodā took up a rope to bind you when you committed an offense, and your perturbed eyes overflooded with tears, which washed the mascara from your eyes. And you were afraid, though fear personified is afraid of you. This sight is bewildering to me. (SB** [**1.8.31**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/8.31)**)**

Having disheveled locks of hair and nails is not contrary to the svarūpa of the Lord whose form is pure knowledge. Rather they are his intrinsic qualities and nourish his svarūpa.

### Text 23

*tan-mātarau nija-sutau ghṛṇayā snuvantyau*  
*paṅkāṅga-rāga-rucirāv upagūhya dorbhyām*  
*dattvā stanaṁ prapibatoḥ sma mukhaṁ nirīkṣya*  
*mugdha-smitālpa-daśanaṁ yayatuḥ pramodam*

**Перевод:**

**The two mothers took their sons, beautiful with mud and cosmetics, in their arms, and gave them their breasts and fed them milk. Looking carefully at the mouths of their sucking children they became joyful on seeing small teeth when the boys smiled softly.**

**Комментарий:**

Then the two mothers embraced their sons by their arms and felt joy. Their breasts flowed with milk out of compassion aroused by vātsalya. The boys were attractive with mud on their limbs according to the logic “What is not beautiful in the Sundara-khaṇḍa of Rāmāyaṇa?”

Mukham is in the singular since each mother looked at the mouth of her own child. The beautiful smile showed few small teeth (mugdha-smitālpa-daśanaṁ).

### Text 24

*yarhy aṅganā-darśanīya-kumāra-līlāv*  
*antar-vraje tad abalāḥ pragṛhīta-pucchaiḥ*  
*vatsair itas tata ubhāv anukṛṣyamāṇau*  
*prekṣantya ujjhita-gṛhā jahṛṣur hasantyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd ladies, giving up their household chores, would stare intently at the two boys engaged in infant pastimes seen especially by women, as they firmly caught the tails of calves and were pulled from place to place in Vraja. The women laughed and become filled with joy.**

**Комментарий:**

When (yarhi) their childhood manifested a little more, and their kaumāra pastimes became most attractive (darśaṇīyā) to the women (aṅganā), then (tad) those women (abalāḥ) seeing the two in Vraja, gave up their household chores, and while laughing rejoiced (jahṛṣuḥ). The boys they saw are described. They were pulled here and there by the calves whose tails they held. Approaching the sleeping calves by crawling on their knees, they grabbed two or three tails, thinking “What is this?” The calves stood up and ran. Not letting go of the tails, the boys’ stomachs rubbed on the ground and they cried. Seeing this the women laughed thinking, “O! You two exceedingly strong men are dragged by even young animals!” With great effort they made them give up the tails and placing them on their chests rejoiced.

### Text 25

*śṛṅgy-agni-daṁṣṭry-asi-jala-dvija-kaṇṭakebhyaḥ*  
*krīḍā-parāv aticalau sva-sutau niṣeddhum*  
*gṛhyāṇi kartum api yatra na taj-jananyau*  
*śekāta āpatur alaṁ manaso ’navasthām*

**Перевод:**

**When mother Yaśodā and Rohiṇī were unable to protect the babies from calamities threatened by horned cows, by fire, by animals with claws and teeth such as monkeys, dogs and cats, and by thorns, swords and other weapons on the ground, they were always in anxiety, and their household engagements were disturbed.**

**Комментарий:**

When the two mothers were not able to prevent the two boys from holding cows, etc., and could not do their chores they became agitated. How should these two be handled? In the verse śṛṅgin means cows, daṁṣṭriṇ means monkeys and dvija means birds likeherons (which are dangerous).

### Text 26

*kālenālpena rājarṣe rāmaḥ kṛṣṇaś ca gokule*  
*aghṛṣṭa-jānubhiḥ padbhir vicakramatur añjasā*

**Перевод:**

**O sage among kings! Within a very short time both Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa began to walk very easily in Gokula on their legs, without the need to crawl.**

**Комментарий:**

The boys did not have to drag their knees on the ground (aghṛṣṭa- jānubhiḥ).

### Text 27

*tatas tu bhagavān kṛṣṇo vayasyair vraja-bālakaiḥ*  
*saha-rāmo vraja-strīṇāṁ cikrīḍe janayan mudam*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, Kṛṣṇa, along with Balarāma, began to play with the other children of the cowherd men, thus awakening bliss of the cowherd women.**

**Комментарий:**

After giving pleasure to their mothers, Kṛṣṇa gave pleasure to the young cowherd boys and the other women of Vraja.

### Text 28

*kṛṣṇasya gopyo ruciraṁ vīkṣya kaumāra-cāpalam*  
*śṛṇvantyāḥ kila tan-mātur iti hocuḥ samāgatāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Observing the very attractive childhood restlessness of Kṛṣṇa, all the gopīs in the neighborhood, would approach mother Yaśodā and speak to her as follows in order to hear about Kṛṣṇa’s activities again and again.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa’s fickle kaumāra actions such was stealing yogurt, the gopīs became blissful. They went and spoke to his mother, Yaśodā, who even gave up her household-work to hear, on the pretext of scolding him in order to give her that bliss.

### Text 29

*vatsān muñcan kvacid asamaye krośa-sañjāta-hāsaḥ*  
*steyaṁ svādv atty atha dadhi-payaḥ kalpitaiḥ steya-yogaiḥ*  
*markān bhokṣyan vibhajati sa cen nātti bhāṇḍaṁ bhinnatti*  
*dravyālābhe sagṛha-kupito yāty upakrośya tokān*

**Перевод:**

**Your son sometimes comes to our houses before the milking of the cows and releases the calves, and when the master of the house becomes angry, your son merely smiles. Sometimes he devises some process by which he steals palatable curd, butter and milk, which he then eats and drinks. When the monkeys assemble, he divides it with them, and when the monkeys have their bellies so full that they won’t take more, he breaks the pots. Sometimes, if he gets no opportunity to steal butter or milk from a house, he will be angry at the householders, and will make the small children cry and then run away.**

**Комментарий:**

They speak in three verses. He decides, “Making the houses empty, I will steal yogurt.” Sometime, before the cows are milked, he frees the calves. Then he enters the houses with no people and steals the yogurt. When we sometimes shout, “Kṛṣṇa has stolen the yogurt” he laughs. “Look! These foolish women say that I, the master of the house, am a thief.” Saying this, he laughs. When we become bewildered by his smile, he sits on a jeweled seat in the houses, like the master of the house, and eats yogurt and milk.

“But why don’t you all offer it to him?” He finds what he has stolen (steyam), not what is given, to be tasty. Taking what he has stolen, he eats and then divides it among the monkeys saying, “This part is yours, this part is yours.” If the monkeys do not eat because they are full, becoming depressed, he breaks the pot full of yogurt. “How can I eat without you?” When he cannot obtain yogurt etc. he becomes angry at the house, saying “I will burn you” and making the babies sleeping on the bed, cry by pinching, goes away.

### Text 30

*hastāgrāhye racayati vidhiṁ pīṭhakolūkhalādyaiś*  
*chidraṁ hy antar-nihita-vayunaḥ śikya-bhāṇḍeṣu tad-vit*  
*dhvāntāgāre dhṛta-maṇi-gaṇaṁ svāṅgam artha-pradīpaṁ*  
*kāle gopyo yarhi gṛha-kṛtyeṣu suvyagra-cittāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**“When the milk and curd are kept high on a swing hanging from the ceiling and Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma cannot reach it, they arrange to reach it by piling up various planks and turning upside-down the mortar and being quite aware of the contents of a pot, they put holes in the pot. While the elderly gopīs go about their household affairs, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma go into a dark room, brightening the place by their bodies decorated with valuable jewels.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse elaborates on his devised stealing methods. He devises a method for reaching yogurt beyond hand’s reach, climbing by using an upturned mortar or climbing on boys’ shoulders. Knowing the contents, he makes a hole in the pots tied very high up, using the splintered tip of a stick. This shows his extreme cleverness. He knows how to make the hole, how make the yogurt pour out, and how to fill up the mouths of himself and his friends, as they open their mouths wide. Hiding ourselves, we see from far off his fun. It is not that he is incapable in a dark house. He makes his limbs into lamps in the dark house. And there too he is laden with gems. He is capable even in a dark house because his bodily effulgence destroys the darkness.

Though no women, bewildered by his sweet, graceful words, can stop him from his open theft, still he is known to love stealing when no one is looking. Knowing when the gopīs are busy in household affairs through his accomplices, he steals the yogurt from their houses.

### Text 31

*evaṁ dhārṣṭyāny uśati kurute mehanādīni vāstau*  
*steyopāyair viracita-kṛtiḥ supratīko yathāste*  
*itthaṁ strībhiḥ sa-bhaya-nayana-śrī-mukhālokinībhir*  
*vyākhyātārthā prahasita-mukhī na hy upālabdhum aicchat*

**Перевод:**

**Successful at stealing, sometimes he passes urine and stool in a neat, clean place in our houses as well as performing other naughty acts. But now, he is sitting before you like a very good boy. The gopīs would look at Kṛṣṇa sitting there with fearful eyes. His mother, hearing the complaints, smiled softly but did not scold him.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, not only does he steal yogurt, he also causes other disturbances. He does many such (evam) bold acts. Evam meansmanner according to Viśva-kośa. He urinates, while throwing around grass and dust, in a place decorated (uśati) for the Lord’s deity worship. Having accomplished eating (kṛtiḥ) by stealing, he stands in front of you like an innocent boy. Or O attractive queen Yaśodā (uśati)! Within the town (iha), he does bold acts, whichwere mentioned previously, along with (amā) making sounds like cuckoos and peacocks (nādīni) in order to attract his friends. Amāmeans together according to Viśva-kośa. Having revealed (viracita) his skill (kṛtiḥ) at stealing, now he stands in front of you like agentle person with beautiful limbs.

The result of their describing his thievery is then described. His face has fearful eyes, thinking, “My mother will beat me.” Yaśodā was explained about his theft by the women who had the tendency to glance at his face which was endowed with beauty. She, for whom the form of prema for Kṛṣṇa was meant, did not want to scold him, the thief. “They all have prema for the jewel of my womb. He is fickle as a small boy but will be very serious in his youth.” Understanding this, she became joyful and did not even desire to scold him. “How did such a son arise from King Nanda? Who will give their daughter to him?” Saying this, she smiled (prahasita-mukhī). Prahasita is formed according to ādi-karmaṇi ktaḥ (Pāṇini 3.4.71)

“But these stealing actions of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord and the son of a king, are not praiseworthy, since they are insignificant and not astonishing.” Not so. They are most praiseworthy on account of being great by showering sweet mercy on devotees, and being astonishing by the method of theft. This pastime is supreme mercy by arranging various amusements having brought one close to theperson full of bliss, dear as life, desirable to behold at all-times and it is an abode of amazement by the great beauty, by the wearing of many jeweled ornaments, by the fickleness of boyhood, by the association of boys and monkeys equal to himself, which are all unprecedented.

### Text 32

*ekadā krīḍamānās te rāmādyā gopa-dārakāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇo mṛdaṁ bhakṣitavān iti mātre nyavedayan*

**Перевод:**

**One day while Balarāma and other elder cowherd boys were playing with Kṛṣṇa, they informed Yaśodā politely that Kṛṣṇa has eaten some dirt.**

**Комментарий:**

Not satisfied because Yaśodā did not scolded him even after being informed of his yogurt-stealing nature, a pastime in which he is scolded is related.

### Text 33

*sā gṛhītvā kare kṛṣṇam upālabhya hitaiṣiṇī*  
*yaśodā bhaya-sambhrānta- prekṣaṇākṣam abhāṣata*

**Перевод:**

**Mother Yaśodā, who was always full of anxiety over Kṛṣṇa’s welfare, caught him in her hands and then spoke to him, on seeing his eyes agitated with fear.**

**Комментарий:**

Grabbing his hand, suspecting he would flee, she scolded him (upālabhya) because she wanted his benefit. Her scolding was full of prema. His eyes glanced restlessly with fear (bhaya-sambhrānta- prekṣaṇākṣam). He feared that she would beat him.

### Text 34

*kasmān mṛdam adāntātman bhavān bhakṣitavān rahaḥ*  
*vadanti tāvakā hy ete kumārās te ’grajo ’py ayam*

**Перевод:**

**Why are you so restless that you have eaten dirt in a solitary place? This complaint has been lodged against you by all your playmates, including your elder brother, Balarāma. How is this?**

**Комментарий:**

O boy with uncontrolled mind (adāntātman)! Why have you, giving up butter with sugar, eaten dirt in a solitary place? Since you cannot do it in front of me. It is not a lie since your friends say this. “They are against me. They want me beaten.” But your elder brother Balarāma also says this.

### Text 35

*nāhaṁ bhakṣitavān amba sarve mithyābhiśaṁsinaḥ*  
*yadi satya-giras tarhi samakṣaṁ paśya me mukham*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa replied: My dear mother, I have not eaten dirt. All my friends are liars. If you think they are truthful, you can directly look into my mouth.**

**Комментарий:**

Afraid of being beaten he speaks. All my friends including Balarāma want me beaten. If you think their words are true, then look in my mouth. These false words are a part of his svarūpa much like the innocence, etc., which nourish vātsalya-rasa. It is not to be said that “these words are true on account of the earth being inside his stomach” because he deviates from truth in tricking Jarāsandha and in conciliating his beloveds (who feel betrayed).

### Text 36

*yady evaṁ tarhi vyādehī- ty uktaḥ sa bhagavān hariḥ*  
*vyādattāvyāhataiśvaryaḥ krīḍā-manuja-bālakaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Yaśodā challenged Kṛṣṇa, “If you have not eaten earth, then open your mouth wide” Kṛṣṇa, endowed with the highest powers and with the highest sweetness, exhibiting pastimes like a human child, not completely giving up his powers, opened his mouth.**

**Комментарий:**

If they are all telling lies, then open (vyādehi) your mouth. When his mother said this, he opened his mouth. He had a human form, of a child, prone to playing (krīḍa-manuja-bālakaḥ), whose powerswere still present. The meaning is similar to the śāka-pārthiva compound. Though bewildered as a son, his aiśvarya-śakti waswaiting for an opportunity to serve him. This was a second display of the universe. “This is so that my mother does not purify me.”

### Texts 37-39

*sā tatra dadṛśe viśvaṁ jagat sthāsnu ca khaṁ diśaḥ*  
*sādri-dvīpābdhi-bhūgolaṁ sa-vāyv-agnīndu-tārakam*

*jyotiś-cakraṁ jalaṁ tejo nabhasvān viyad eva ca*  
*vaikārikāṇīndriyāṇi mano mātrā guṇās trayaḥ*

*etad vicitraṁ saha-jīva-kāla-svabhāva-karmāśaya-liṅga-bhedam*  
*sūnos tanau vīkṣya vidāritāsye vrajaṁ sahātmānam avāpa śaṅkām*

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa opened his mouth wide by the order of mother Yaśodā, she saw within his stomach all moving and nonmoving entities, bhuva-loka and all directions, along with mountains, islands, oceans, the surface of the earth, the wind, fire, the moon and the stars. She saw the planetary systems, water, light, air, ether, and ahaṅkāra, mahat-tattva and prakṛti. She saw the presiding deities of the senses. She also saw the senses, the mind, the tanmātras, and the three qualities goodness, passion and ignorance. She saw the time, the jīva, the tendency to transform (svabhāva), karma, and desires as well as various bodies. When he opened his mouth and she saw herself and her son along with Vraja, she became doubtful.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses (37-38) go together. When Kṛṣṇa decided, “I will not be beaten by my mother today,” by his aiśvarya-śakti which follows his desire, Yaśodā saw the universe in his stomach through his mouth. She saw moving (jagat) and nonmoving (sthāsnu) beings, and antarikṣa planets (kham). She saw earth with mountains. She saw the zodiac, with wind, lightning (agni), moon and stars. She saw water, fire and air (nabhasvān). She saw the sense devatās (vaikāri) in sattva, the senses in rajas and the tan-mātras like sound in tamas. She saw the three guṇas beginning with sattva. Things which were formless were seen in the form of their presiding devatās since they have forms.

(Verse 39:) Along with the universe she saw in the stomach (tanau) of her son when he opened his mouth the jīva, time – the agitator of the guṇas, svābhava – the cause of transformation, karma – the cause of birth, desire – the impressions of karma, and the differences of moving and nonmoving beings (liṅga) brought about them.

Seeing Vraja along with herself, her husband, and son, she developed doubt (śaṅkām). “How can the universe situated outside and Vraja which is similar, be situated in his stomach as well?” Śaṅkā means fear or doubt according to Viśva-kośa. That the Lord’s body can be eternal and measurable while being situated within the universe and outside is contrary toreality.14 This is accomplished by his acintyaiśvarya-śakti.

### Text 40

*kiṁ svapna etad uta devamāyā*  
*kiṁ vā madīyo bata buddhi-mohaḥ*  
*atho amuṣyaiva mamārbhakasya*  
*yaḥ kaścanautpattika ātma-yogaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Was what I saw a dream, or is it an illusory creation by some devatā? Has this been manifested by bewilderment of my intelligence? It is some natural power of my child.**

**Комментарий:**

Her conjecture is shown. Was what I saw caused by a dream? No. I do not have the tiredness of sleep. Then is it the māyā of somedevatā? No. A devatā has no goal in bewildering me. Then is this some illusion of my intelligence? No. My intelligence is in good condition previously and now. Pondering in this way, she came to a conclusion. The word atho indicates complete according toAmara-kośa. My son, being Svayam Bhagavān, has some natural (autpattika) quality—his inconceivable śakti (ātmā-yogaḥ) bywhich he exists simultaneously outside and inside the universe. The qualities of the Lord related to sweetness are always seen by the people of Vraja. But the qualities related to power, though known to exist in him, are seen only sometimes.

### Text 41

*atho yathāvan na vitarka-gocaraṁ*  
*ceto-manaḥ-karma-vacobhir añjasā*  
*yad-āśrayaṁ yena yataḥ pratīyate*  
*sudurvibhāvyaṁ praṇatāsmi tat-padam*

**Перевод:**

**I offer my respects to the inconceivable lotus feet of Nārāyaṇa who is not to be understood by consciousness, mind, good karma, actions, but is easily realized through surrender.**
