**Комментарий:**

Svayam Bhagavān, my son, shows that quality (of acintya-śakti) by his vilāsa form called Nārāyaṇa. Cetas means citta. This amazing show cannot be properly understood by citta, mind, action or words. I offer respect to that object (tat-padam) which is the basis (yad-āśrayam), the cause of its manifestation (yataḥ) and the cause of its perception (yena). I offer respects to Nārāyaṇa, an expansion of my son, with citta, mind, action and words in order to dispel my doubts regarding the nature of acintya-śakti. What is the nature of that object? He cannot be the object of meditation (durvibhāvyam).

### Text 42

*ahaṁ mamāsau patir eṣa me suto*  
*vrajeśvarasyākhila-vittapā satī*  
*gopyaś ca gopāḥ saha-godhanāś ca me*  
*yan-māyayetthaṁ kumatiḥ sa me gatiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**It is by the influence of the Supreme Lord’s māyā that I wrongly think that Nanda Mahārāja is my husband, that Kṛṣṇa is my son, and that because I am the queen of Nanda Mahārāja, all the wealth of cows and calves are my possessions and all the cowherd men and their wives are my subjects. Therefore I surrender to him.**

**Комментарий:**

She rejects the causes of that astonishing vision as dreams, etc., in three lines. I am the chaste wife of Nanda, skillful in all affairs, protector of all his wealth, known as Yaśodā. The king of Vraja is my husband. This Kṛṣṇa is my son. The cowherds are my subjects. This are confirmed by perception. There is no opportunity for a dream at this time. May intelligence which is produced by dreams not occur again! Thus she surrenders to Nārāyaṇa again in the last line. These doubts about a dream, etc., are not glorious (kumatiḥ).Ku means earth and not glorious according to Hemacandra.

May he, by whose desire (māyayā) the doubts arose, be my shelter in destroying my doubts. Māyā can mean desire according to Śabda- mahodadhi. Kṛṣṇa is my son and should be cared for and instructed. But his vilāsa form, Nārāyaṇa should be worshipped. This is my method of worship, which was also instructed by Garga, who said, “Protect this child.” (SB [10.8.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.19))

### Text 43

*itthaṁ vidita-tattvāyāṁ gopikāyāṁ sa īśvaraḥ*  
*vaiṣṇavīṁ vyatanon māyāṁ putra-sneha-mayīṁ vibhuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Yaśodā understood the truth, the supreme master, by the influence of the internal potency, spread mercy by having her develop the deepest affection for her son.**

**Комментарий:**

“Having eaten dirt with a desire to be scolded, the possibility of being beaten due to that fault was also avoided by that astonishingvision. But becoming immersed in adbhuta-rasa, my mother may become lax in caring for me.” Thinking in this way he made herforget the astonishing vision by the prema of thinking of him purely as her son.

When his mother, the queen, understood the truth about her son’s svarūpa (vidita-tattvāyām), the Lord, her son, spread compassion(māyāṁ), which was filled with affection for him as her son and which was his own māyā (vaiṣṇavīm). It cannot be said that “themāyā was of three guṇas” since that māyā does not possess affection for Kṛṣṇa as a son. It is not that “the māyā is illusory on account of creating an illusion of affection for her son” since if it were so, then it is impossible for that māyā to bring the Lord under control.

### Text 44

*sadyo naṣṭa-smṛtir gopī sāropyāroham ātmajam*  
*pravṛddha-sneha-kalila-hṛdayāsīd yathā purā*

**Перевод:**

**Immediately forgetting that Kṛṣṇa had shown the universal form within is mouth, mother Yaśodā took her son on her lap, feeling full affection in her heart as previously.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of spreading his mercy is described. Forgetting her inquiry about dreaming caused by doubts, Yaśodā, with her heart filled with increased affection, remained as before.

### Text 45

*trayyā copaniṣadbhiś ca sāṅkhya-yogaiś ca sātvataiḥ*  
*upagīyamāna-māhātmyaṁ hariṁ sāmanyatātmajam*

**Перевод:**

**The glories of the Supreme Lord are studied through the three Vedas, the Upaniṣads, the literature of Sāṅkhya and Yoga, and other Pāñcarātras, yet mother Yaśodā considered that Supreme Person an ordinary child.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing and seeing Kṛṣṇa’s powers did not restrict her love for Kṛṣṇa as her son. Rather that increased her love. He is glorified as the Yajña-puruṣa, lord of sacrifice in the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma Vedas (trayyā). He is glorified as Parabrahman by the head of the Vedas, the Upaniṣads. He is glorified as the Parama-puruṣa by followers of Sāṅkhya and Yoga. He is glorified as Bhagavān by Pañcarātra scriptures (sātvataiḥ). Yaśodā considered him to be just her son. Her recognition of him as her son became fixed. On seeing and hearing of her son as the lord of everything, her love for Kṛṣṇa as her son did not decrease, but rather increased. This is related to herintimate bhāvas.

### Text 46

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*nandaḥ kim akarod brahman śreya evaṁ mahodayam*  
*yaśodā ca mahā-bhāgā papau yasyāḥ stanaṁ hariḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Parīkṣit Mahārāja inquired: What pious acts did Nanda perform to cause such affection and what pious acts did most fortunate Yaśodā perform so that the Lord drank from her breast?**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing of Yaśodā who controlled the Lord by accepting him as her son, with no decrease by seeing and hearing of his powers, astonished Parīkṣit inquired. What pious acts did Nanda do, which gave great results (mahodayam)? But Yaśodā attained greater fortune than Nanda. She is described as most fortunate (mahā- bhāgā). “Why are you surprised?” He followed (papau) the orders (ās-stanaṁ) of Nanda (yasya) and he drank (papau) breast milk (stanaṁ) of Yaśodā (yasyāḥ).

### Text 47

*pitarau nānvavindetāṁ kṛṣṇodārārbhakehitam*  
*gāyanty adyāpi kavayo yal loka-śamalāpaham*

**Перевод:**

**Great devotees sing of the activities of Kṛṣṇa in his childhood which Vasudeva and Devakī could not experience and which even today destroy the sins of all people.**

**Комментарий:**

I am surprised by this attainment of the most rare attainment. In our times, the poets sing about Kṛṣṇa’s childhood pastimes, whichgave the highest bliss (udāra) which Vasudeva and Devakī (pitarau), famous as his parents, did not directly experience (nānvavindetāṁ). Rohiṇī who identified herself as Balarāma’s mother and the elder gopīs also identified themselves as Kṛṣṇa’s mothers also experienced those childhood pastimes (i.e. they are excluded from the category of Vasudeva and Devakī). This is indicated by the word udāra (generous).

### Text 48

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*droṇo vasūnāṁ pravaro dharayā bhāryayā saha*  
*kariṣyamāṇa ādeśān brahmaṇas tam uvāca ha*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: To follow the orders of Brahmā, Droṇa, the best of the Vasus, along with his wife, Dharā, spoke to Brahmā in this way.**

**Комментарий:**

Though knowing that Nanda, Yaśodā and their prema were eternally accomplished, Parīkṣit inquired about their excellent sādhana for attaining that fortunate position. Since the aṁśas of Nanda and Yaśodā exist in Droṇa and Dharā, Śukadeva then thought of relating the story of their aṁśas. To follow the order to herd cows, Droṇa spoke to Brahmā (tam).

### Text 49

*jātayor nau mahādeve bhuvi viśveśvare harau*  
*bhaktiḥ syāt paramā loke yayāñjo durgatiṁ taret*

**Перевод:**

**Droṇa and Dharā said: being born on earth, may we two develop prema-bhakti to the attractive Lord, engaged in sweet pastimes, though he is the Lord of the universe. By this bhakti others in this world will easily cross material existence.**

**Комментарий:**

In our next birth (jātayoḥ) may we develop bhakti for the Lord who engages in excellent play (mahādeve), in whom reside all thecontrollers of the universe (viśveśvare) on account of the statement mahad-aṁśa-yukta: the Lord appeared with all his expansions (SB [3.2.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.15)), and who is Svayam Bhagavān. That bhakti should be filled with seeing him as our son (paramā) hearing which other people also can easily cross material existence.

### Text 50

*astv ity uktaḥ sa bhagavān vraje droṇo mahā-yaśāḥ*  
*jajñe nanda iti khyāto yaśodā sā dharābhavat*

**Перевод:**

**When Brahmā said, “Yes, let it be so,” the most fortunate Droṇa appeared in Vraja as famous Nanda Mahārāja, and his wife, Dharā, appeared as mother Yaśodā.**

**Комментарий:**

When Brahmā agreed, Droṇa was born as Nanda and his wife Dharā became Yaśodā. Dharā and Droṇa, sādhana-siddhas entered into Yaśodā and Nanda, nitya-siddhas.

### Text 51

*tato bhaktir bhagavati putrī-bhūte janārdane*  
*dampatyor nitarām āsīd gopa-gopīṣu bhārata*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, O best of the Bhāratas, the bhakti of Nanda, Yaśodā and all the cowherd men and women remained in its highest form, directed towards Kṛṣṇa, who had become their son, who is longed for but not attained by others.**

**Комментарий:**

Janārdana means he who is the object of prayer for desired results. The bhakti for Kṛṣṇa (janārdane) of the husband and wife amongthe cowherd men and women remained continuously. In their previous lives those cowherd men and women were sādhakas following Droṇa and Dharā.

### Text 52

*kṛṣṇo brahmaṇa ādeśaṁ satyaṁ kartuṁ vraje vibhuḥ*  
*saha-rāmo vasaṁś cakre teṣāṁ prītiṁ sva-līlayā*

**Перевод:**

**Thus the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa, along with Balarāma, lived in Vṛndāvana, just to substantiate the benediction of Brahmā and gave pleasure to Nanda, Yaśodā and the cowherd men and women through the pastimes dependent upon their bhakti.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā’s order was, “May you have the highest bhakti for Kṛṣṇa, who is become your son.” To make the order of Brahmā true, Kṛṣṇa produced prema (prītim).

## Chapter 9 - Mother Yaśodā Binds Lord Kṛṣṇa

### Texts 1-2

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ekadā gṛha-dāsīṣu yaśodā nanda-gehinī*  
*karmāntara-niyuktāsu nirmamantha svayaṁ dadhi*

*yāni yānīha gītāni tad-bāla-caritāni ca*  
*dadhi-nirmanthane kale smarantī tāny agāyata*

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: One day when mother Yaśodā saw that all the maidservants were engaged in other household affairs, she personally began to churn the yogurt. While churning, she remembered the childhood activities of Kṛṣṇa which had been sung in the assembly and enjoyed singing those songs.**

**Комментарий:**

*nivārya dadhno mathanaṁ nipīta- stanyo’py atṛpteḥ kupitaḥ pareśaḥ \|*  
*vibhinna-bhāṇḍo navame jananyā druto’parādhād udare nibaddhaḥ*

**In the nineth chapter Kṛṣṇa prevents Yaśodā from churning yogurt, drinks her milk and, unsatisfied, becomes angry and breaks a pot. Pursued by his mother, he is tied around his waist because of his offense.**

Though having given answers according to Parīkṣit’s question, most merciful Śukadeva, though not being asked, shows Parīkṣit, the object of his mercy, that Nanda and Yaśodā’s good fortune was not a result of sādhana, but was accomplished without a beginning.

Hearing this pastime that occurred on a day (ekadā), understand the good fortune of the two. Yaśodā engaged all the servant girls of the house in duties like arranging utensils in the kitchen and churning yogurt. Yāśodā was churning a yogurt. She worshipped Kṛṣṇa, seeing him as a son. This was her daily activity. This butter was Kṛṣṇa’s favorite item. The yogurt came from the best cows, with five udders, smelling of lotuses. Otherwise this work would not be done by the queen. She was the wife of Nanda (nanda-gehinī). She was half his body and thus had his good fortune.

Remembering, she sang of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes in meter for songs, in order pacify her agitation at not seeing her son who was sleeping in another room.

### Text 3

*kṣaumaṁ vāsaḥ pṛthu-kaṭi-taṭe bibhratī sūtra-naddhaṁ*  
*putra-sneha-snuta-kuca-yugaṁ jāta-kampaṁ ca subhrūḥ*  
*rajjv-ākarṣa-śrama-bhuja-calat-kaṅkaṇau kuṇḍale ca*  
*svinnaṁ vaktraṁ kabara-vigalan-mālatī nirmamantha*

**Перевод:**

**Dressed in a yellow cloth with a belt tied about her full hips, mother Yaśodā pulled on the churning rope. Her bangles and earrings swayed and her breasts shook. Because of her intense love for her child, her breasts were wet with milk. Her face, with its very beautiful eyebrows, was wet with perspiration, and jasmine flowers were falling from her hair.**

**Комментарий:**

Yaśodā’s beauty as she churned yogurt is described for meditation. Yaśodā (subhrūḥ) churned the yogurt which was produced. She had a fine, colorful, valuable cloth made of linen (kṣaumam) on her broad hips, bound by a belt (sūtra-naddham). Atasī (flax) andkṣumā are synonyms according to Amara-kośa. Her trembling breasts flowed with milk out of affection for her son. Her jeweled bangles moved on her two arms, tired from pulling the rope. She had earrings studded with gems in her ears, and begemmed bracelets. They indicate that she also had necklace, armbands and ankle bells. Her face was covered with perspiration. These were the five items on her. She had jasmine flowers like stars falling down from her cloud-like hair. The suffix ka is deleted in the compound kabara-vigalan-mālatī by poetic license. This indicates abhūtopamā (a simile implying an impossibility). The words pṛthu-kaṭi-taṭa and subhrūḥ indicate the beauty of all her limbs. Her complexion is described as golden like lightning in some mantras. In some other texts her complexion is seen to be dark like a blue lotus.

### Text 4

*tāṁ stanya-kāma āsādya mathnantīṁ jananīṁ hariḥ*  
*gṛhītvā dadhi-manthānaṁ nyaṣedhat prītim āvahan*

**Перевод:**

**While mother Yaśodā was churning butter, Kṛṣṇa, desiring to drink the milk of her breast, appeared before her, and increased her affection when he caught hold of the churning rod and prevented her from churning.**

**Комментарий:**

Waking up in the room, going outside, he was hungry and crying. In this way he approached his mother. He held the stick. “Though forbidden by me to churn, she does not stop.” Thus he increased the affection of his mother who understood his skillful intelligence.

### Text 5

*tam aṅkam ārūḍham apāyayat stanaṁ*  
*sneha-snutaṁ sa-smitam īkṣatī mukham*  
*atṛptam utsṛjya javena sā yayāv*  
*utsicyamāne payasi tv adhiśrite*

**Перевод:**

**Mother Yaśodā placed him on her lap and, smiling, fed him milk which flowed spontaneously from her breast, while she gazed at his face. Though he was not finished, she put him down and quickly went to the kitchen where milk was boiling over.**

**Комментарий:**

Giving up churning, sitting, she fed him milk, after he climbed on her lap. She gave him up, though he was not satisfied with drinking. Quickly she went to take off the milk since milk, meant for him, placed on the fire, was boiling over. It was overflowing from the pot. Her possessiveness of the milk was not a fault, but an ornament since it was for her son.

### Text 6

*sa jāta-kopaḥ sphuritāruṇādharaṁ*  
*sandaśya dadbhir dadhi-mantha-bhājanam*  
*bhittvā mṛṣāśrur dṛṣad-aśmanā raho*  
*jaghāsa haiyaṅgavam antaraṁ gataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Being intensely angry and biting his reddish lips with his teeth, Kṛṣṇa, with real tears in his eyes, broke the container of yogurt with a piece of stone. Then he entered a room and began to eat the freshly churned butter in a solitary place.**

**Комментарий:**

The unsatisfied son became angry at being ignored by abandoning. Becoming angry, biting his very red lips with his teeth, his eyesfilled with real (amṛṣā) tears out of anger, with the fine tip of a piece of stone he broke the yogurt pot, noiselessly making a small hole in its base. Because of hunger, going into a room (antaram), alone he ate butter, placed there by his mother from the previous days milk to make ghee every day. Babies show their fickleness and sometimes show false tears so that the mother would not become angry. This is the nature of a small child. But now the real tears arose from anger. “ But śruti says vijighatso ’pipāsaḥ: the Lord has no hunger or thirst (Chāndogya Upaniṣad [8.1.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/chan-upa/part-8.chapter-1.815)), and smṛti says nitya-tṛptasyātṛptir: for the Lord who is eternally satisfied there is no dissatisfaction and aroṣaṇo hy asau deva: the Lord has no anger (Mahābhārata). It is contradictory for the Lord who has no anger to become angry.”

Like being bewildered and fearful, being dissatisfied and angry are qualities of his svarūpa which nourish the mother’s vātsalya-rasa,by the previously stated logic. They are not material since he is devoid the eighteen great faults and since he was alone at that time, his anger is not some imitation. This is the opinion of knowers of tattva.

### Text 7

*uttārya gopī suśṛtaṁ payaḥ punaḥ*  
*praviśya saṁdṛśya ca dadhy-amatrakam*  
*bhagnaṁ vilokya sva-sutasya karma taj*  
*jahāsa taṁ cāpi na tatra paśyatī*

**Перевод:**

**Mother Yaśodā, after taking down the hot milk from the oven, returned to the churning spot, and when she saw that the container of yogurt was broken and that Kṛṣṇa was not present, she concluded that the breaking of the pot was the work of Kṛṣṇa and laughed.**

**Комментарий:**

What did his mother do in the mean time? Taking off the well- boiled milk, she came to the churning place and seeing the brokenyogurt pot, seeing it was the work of her son and not seeing him there, she laughed. She laughed because of his skill at breaking the pot out of anger and running away in fear.

### Text 8

*ulūkhalāṅghrer upari vyavasthitaṁ*  
*markāya kāmaṁ dadataṁ śici sthitam*  
*haiyaṅgavaṁ caurya-viśaṅkitekṣaṇaṁ*  
*nirīkṣya paścāt sutam āgamac chanaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, at that time, was sitting on an upside-down wooden mortar and was giving butter which had been hanging by a rope to the monkeys as he liked. Because of having stolen, he was looking all around with great anxiety. Mother Yaśodā, upon seeing him, very cautiously approached him from behind.**

**Комментарий:**

Inferring that he was eating butter in the room by the sounds of his bells and sound of the vessels he moved, after some time his mother came there. What he did till the time she came there is described. Going by a side door, he was situated on top of an upturned mortar, sitting in svāstika āsana. He was taking butter from the pot hanging by cords, and giving it liberally to the monkeys. He was glancing about to see if his mother was coming, worried by fear of being beaten because of his theft. Seeing him from the holes of the lattice, she approached from behind, not making noise with her feet, wanting to catch him.

### Text 9

*tām ātta-yaṣṭiṁ prasamīkṣya satvaras*  
*tato ’varuhyāpasasāra bhītavat*  
*gopy anvadhāvan na yam āpa yogināṁ*  
*kṣamaṁ praveṣṭuṁ tapaseritaṁ manaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa saw his mother, stick in hand, he very quickly got down from the top of the mortar and began to flee as if in fear. Yaśodā chased him, whom the minds of yogīs in samādhi, fit to merge in Brahman and impelled to him with great concentration, cannot attain.**

**Комментарий:**

Then what happened? Seeing her holding a small stick, embedded with small gems, for beating him, understanding that she wouldnow beat him, he quickly came down from the mortar and fled. That fear was like fear (bhītavat) for Queen Kunti said in Śrīmad Bhāgavatam ([1.8.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/8.31)):

*gopy ādade tvayi kṛtāgasi dāma tāvad,*  
*yā te daṣāśru-kalilāñjana-sambhramākṣam*  
*vaktraṁ ninīya bhaya-bhāvanayā sthitasya,*  
*sā māṁ vimohayaii bhīr api yad bibheti*

**O Kṛṣṇa, Yasodā took up a rope to bind you when you committed an offense, and your perturbed eyes overflooded with tears, which washed the mascara from your eyes. You were afraid, though fear personified is afraid of you. This sight is bewildering to me.**

His mother (gopī), the queen, chased him whom the yogīs’ minds, purified (īritaṁ) by austerity extending till samādhi, do not attain though qualified (kṣamaṁ) to attain. By the Lord’s mercy, the mind can attain him, not by one’s own abilities.

### Text 10

*anvañcamānā jananī bṛhac-calac-*  
*chroṇī-bharākrānta-gatiḥ sumadhyamā*  
*javena visraṁsita-keśa-bandhana-*  
*cyuta-prasūnānugatiḥ parāmṛśat*

**Перевод:**

**Following Kṛṣṇa, her thin waist overburdened by her heavy breasts, her hair loosened, with flowers falling after her, mother Yaśodā quickly caught him.**

**Комментарий:**

One should not say that she could not catch him, since he cannot be caught by yogīs’ minds. She chased him with trailing flowers falling from her undone hair. She (parā) caught him (amṛśat) from behind.

### Text 11

*kṛtāgasaṁ taṁ prarudantam akṣiṇī*  
*kaṣantam añjan-maṣiṇī sva-pāṇinā*  
*udvīkṣamāṇaṁ bhaya-vihvalekṣaṇaṁ*  
*haste gṛhītvā bhiṣayanty avāgurat*

**Перевод:**

**She grabbed the hand of Kṛṣṇa who was crying intensely because of his crime, rubbing his eyes which were running with mascara with his hands and looking up at his mother with fearful glances. She made him fearful by scolding him.**

**Комментарий:**

Not only did she catch Kṛṣṇa, whom yogīs’ minds cannot attain. She even scolded him, from whom even Brahmā and Śiva receive scolding. She even frightened him, who gives fear to time, using a stick.

Holding Kṛṣṇa by his right hand, she frightened him with a stick. The short vowel and the syllable ṣ in bhiṣayantī are poetic license.She prepared to beat him (avāgurat) but did not beat him. The verb gur means attempt. He had committed offense (krtāgasam). Thus worried about being beaten, he cried in order to avoid it. He rubbed his eyes, which has mascara smeared all around them, with the back of his left hand since she held his right hand.

Though restricted by his mother’s hand, he used his own hand to wipe away his tears due to his fault.

She is described. She looked at him, whose eyes were agitated with fear.

“O clever one at stealing, overcome with anger! Friend of the monkeys! Maker of the hole in the pot! Plunderer of the house! Stop. I will today punish you so that you cannot go somewhere and play, so that you cannot see your friends and toys.” She looked at him with rough expression. “If you are afraid of being beaten, why did you break the yogurt pot?” “O mother! I will not do so again. Throw the stick from your hands.”

Or, when he trembled because of fear, she took his hand and scolded him for a moment.

The rest is similar (i.e. only the explanation describing her differs).

### Text 12

*tyaktvā yaṣṭiṁ sutaṁ bhītaṁ vijñāyārbhaka-vatsalā*  
*iyeṣa kila taṁ baddhuṁ dāmnātad-vīrya-kovidā*

**Перевод:**

**Understanding her son’s fear, she dropped the stick, and filled with affection for the boy, and though knowing his powers, strongly desired to tie him up with rope.**

**Комментарий:**

Having more love for her son than for her very life, understanding his fear, she gave up the stick. She thought that he should be fixed on the correct path. She desired (iyeṣa) to tie him up with rope since she knew the strength of his intelligence in his bold stealing, etc. (tad-vīrya-kovidā). The phrase dāmnātad-vīrya-kovidā should not be split as dāmnā and atad-vīrya-kovidā (meaning she was notaware of his intelligence) for she was aware of his power since she had seen the universe within him.

### Texts 13-14

*na cāntar na bahir yasya na pūrvaṁ nāpi cāparam*  
*pūrvāparaṁ bahiś cāntar jagato yo jagac ca yaḥ*

*taṁ matvātmajam avyaktaṁ martya-liṅgam adhokṣajam*  
*gopikolūkhale dāmnā babandha prākṛtaṁ yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Thinking of the invisible Lord--who has no inside or outside, has nothing previous or after him, who existed in the past and will exist in the future, inside and outside of the universe, who is the universe--as her son, appearing with a human form though he was beyond material senses-she tied him to the mortar like a normal child with rope.**

**Комментарий:**

Her desire to tie him up was successful. This is explained in two verses. The queen cowherd woman bound him with a yellow silk rope. She knew that he had committed offense (matvā).

He is described. Since he was all-pervading, he had no interior or exterior. Limited objects have an interior and exterior but this is not possible for the all-pervading. Having described his pervasion of space, his pervasion of time is mentioned. He has nothing previous to him, since he is without beginning. He has nothing after him since he is without end. He pervades all time. Because of that, there is nothing previous and later to him in time.

What was stated is now clarified. He existed previous to the universe since he produces it and exists after the universe since he destroys it. He is inside and outside because he is all-pervading. He becomes the universe since by his śakti it transforms in that manner.

He is avyakta, existing within and has a characteristics like that of a human, i.e. he has a human form. He puts down material sensepleasure (adhokṣajam), i.e. he produces eternally perfect happiness. She tied him up the mass of consciousness, just as one ties up some material person. What greatness of accepting the Lord as one’s son by which he could be tied up in this manner though he is of that nature! Being simultaneously all-pervading and human-sized are accomplished by the acintya-śakti.

### Text 15

*tad dāma badhyamānasya svārbhakasya kṛtāgasaḥ*  
*dvy-aṅgulonam abhūt tena sandadhe ’nyac ca gopikā*

**Перевод:**

**When mother Yaśodā was trying to bind the offending child, she saw that the binding rope was short by a distance of two fingers width. Thus she brought another rope to join to it.**

**Комментарий:**

By showing the method of tying him up, his all-pervading nature though he was medium in size is described. The first rope to tie up the child who was just the size of her lap was two fingers short. Then with that rope she tied another rope offered as a joke byneighboring gopīs who came on hearing the mother scolding and the child crying.

### Text 16

*yadāsīt tad api nyūnaṁ tenānyad api sandadhe*  
*tad api dvy-aṅgulaṁ nyūnaṁ yad yad ādatta bandhanam*

**Перевод:**

**This new rope also was also short by a measurement of two fingers, and when she got more rope and joined it, it was still two fingers too short.**

**Комментарий:**

She obtained more rope (bandhanam), that by which he was bound.

### Text 17

*evaṁ sva-geha-dāmāni yaśodā sandadhaty api*  
*gopīnāṁ susmayantīnāṁ smayantī vismitābhavat*

**Перевод:**

**Thus mother Yaśodā joined whatever ropes were available in the household, though her friends were heartily laughing. She also smiled in wonder.**

**Комментарий:**

She tied together all the ropes available since it was a palace. When the gopīs smiled broadly thinking, “The queen cannot tie up even the baby” she also smiled and was astonished. “Oh! His stomach, the size of a fist, cannot be surrounded by a hundred ropes tied together. He is not becoming bigger. His bells do not increase in size. The rope is two fingers short around him.” This astonished her.

On that day Rohiṇī had gone with Balarāma to Upananda’s house on being invited by his wife. If Rohiṇī had been there she would have prevented Yaśodā from tying up Kṛṣṇa. He made up his mind. “When I get tied up, I will be ridiculed by friends. Thus I will not get tied up.” Making his vow, his power ofall-pervasion, following him, manifested and prevented him from being bound up.

### Text 18

*sva-mātuḥ svinna-gātrāyā visrasta-kabara-srajaḥ*  
*dṛṣṭvā pariśramaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛpayāsīt sva-bandhane*

**Перевод:**

**Because of mother Yaśodā’s hard labor, her whole body became covered with perspiration, and the flowers and comb were falling from her hair. When child Kṛṣṇa saw his mother thus fatigued, He became merciful to her and agreed to be bound.**

**Комментарий:**

“O queen Yaśodā! O friend! Kṛṣṇa does not want to get tied up because of shame in front of his friends. He prevents being tied up because his desires are fulfilled, since he is the Supreme Lord. Therefore, give up this attempt.” In this way though Yaśodā wasenlightened by the gopīs, who were awakened to Kṛṣṇa’s supremacy due to the astonishing vision, thinking, “Even if he is the Supreme Lord, since he is my son, binding him with the many ropes brought here, I will remove his fickleness,” she became obstinate. The Lord, to preserve the stubbornness of his devotee, gave up his own stubbornness and, preserving his mother’s stubbornness, accepted being tied up. This is made clear with the words sva-mātuḥ (his mother). She was fatigued. This was like trying to catch and tie up a strong young elephant with ropes.

By the Lord’s strong kṛpā-śakti, his powers as the Lord which arose from his desire now disappeared. When both the labor of bhakti of my devotee and on seeing that my mercy arise, I will be tied up by these two (bhakti effort and mercy). To show this to this mother, the rope was two fingers short.

This conception of Kṛṣṇa as the Lord which arises from seeing astonishing events sometimes does not eclipse the more pervasive conception of him as a son since it it is weaker than that. He is your worshippable deity.

### Text 19

*evaṁ sandarśitā hy aṅga hariṇā bhakta-vaśyatā*  
*sva-vaśenāpi kṛṣṇena yasyedaṁ seśvaraṁ vaśe*

**Перевод:**

**In this way the attractive Lord has shown that he is under the control of the devotee, even though as Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa controls the universe and all the devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

“But accepting to be bound up destroys his position as the supreme controller.”

Being controlled by the devotee in this way was shown by the Lord who is independent (sva-vaśena), under whose control (vaśe) is this universe (idaṁ) including Brahmā and Śiva. Though he is the husband of unlimited Lakṣmīs he steals. Though satisfied, he is hungry. Though complete he is unsatisfied. Though beyond māyā, he becomes angry. Though the destroyer of time, he shows fear and flees. Though not attainable by yogīs’ minds, he is forcibly caught by his mother. Though full of bliss he sheds tears from suffering. Though all-pervading, and the binder of everyone, he is bound by ropes. Thus he is the highest goal for those in knowledge such as Brahmā, etc. In this way he is controlled by the devotee. This is directly shown (sandarśitā). That it is some imitation is refuted. since in the following the phrase tat-vidām (to those who knew him) is spoken.

*darśayaṁs tad-vidāṁ loka ātmano bhakta-vaśyatām*

**To pure devotees throughout the world who could understand his activities, the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa, exhibited how much he can be subdued by his devotees. (SB** [**10.11.9**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/11.9)**)**

Since the phrase tad-vidām (to those who are in knowledge) is used in the above verse it is not that it is a fault that the Lord is controlled by others. This quality of being controlled by the pure devotees is praised due to being a good quality. Mercy is a good quality. If he were rough it would be a bad quality. Since his stealing is intrinsic to his svarūpa, there is no distortion in his svarūpa. This is stated many times.

### Text 20

*nemaṁ viriñco na bhavo na śrīr apy aṅga-saṁśray*  
*ā prasādaṁ lebhire gopī yat tat prāpa vimuktidāt*

**Перевод:**

**Neither Brahmā, nor Śiva, nor even the goddess of fortune, who is always the better half of the Supreme Lord, can obtain from the Supreme Lord, the deliverer from this material world, such mercy as received by mother Yaśodā.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva, astonished at Yaśodā’s good fortune, with hairs standing on end speaks. It is said:

*muktiṁ dadāti karhicit sma na bhakti-yogam*

**The Lord gives liberation sometimes but not bhakti. (SB** [**5.6.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/6.18)**)**

By the above general indication, what pastime of mercy in the form of accepting bondange (prasādaṁ) Yaśodā, the queen (gopī),attained from the giver of liberation that Brahmā and Śiva, though his avatāras, and though leaders by their bhakti, and even his wife (śrī), Lakṣmī, who even resides on his chest (aṅga-saṁśrayā), theleader of devotees, did not attain. The negative “na” is repeated three times to show the complete absence of that attainment.

Similarly in answer to the question nandaḥ kim akarod (SB [10.8.46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.46)), it was related concerning his aṁśa, which was an incidental story. Actually, you should accept that Nanda and Yaśodā from beginngless time are his parents and possess that incomparable good fortune. It was not that this good fortune arose because of Brahmā’s benediction since Brahmā desires to be bathed in the foot dust of their citizens by saying the following:

*tad bhūri-bhāgyam iha janma kim apy aṭavyām*  
*yad gokule ‘pi katamāṅghri-rajo-’bhiṣekam*

**My greatest possible good fortune would be to take any birth whatever in this forest of Gokula and have my head bathed by the dust falling from the lotus feet of any of its residents. (SB** [**10.14.34**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.34)**)**

### Text 21

*nāyaṁ sukhāpo bhagavān dehināṁ gopikā-sutaḥ*  
*jñānināṁ cātma-bhūtānāṁ yathā bhaktimatām iha*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord, son of Yaśodā, is not easily available to materialists or to jñānīs with realization of ātmā, but is easily available to persons with devotion to the son of Yaśodā.**

**Комментарий:**

Describing the good fortune of Nanda and Yaśodā, the good fortune of their followers, the people of Vraja, is now described. Kṛṣṇa, Bhagavān, the son of Yaśodā (ayam), is not easily attained by those who have not given up identity with their bodies (dehinām) and by jñānīs, whose awareness of their own and others’ ātmā has arisen, those who perform austerities, and those situated in ātmā (ātmā-bhūtānām)—who have destroyed identity with their bodies, such as the Kumāras, as he is attained by people living in Vraja, the devotees of Yaśodā’s son. Or ātmā-bhūtānām can refer to Brahmā and others mentioned previously. With regards to all these various people, Kṛṣṇa attains the highest pleasure in the people of Vraja. Their good fortune is nitya-siddha. This is stated even by Vyāsadeva, the author of Brahma-sūtras:

*upapannas tal-lakṣanārthopalabdher lokavat*

**Bhakti is best because by this one attains the Lord who is most attracted to such devotees, just as a king is most attracted to the citizen who serves with most attention. (Brahma-sūtra 3.3.31)**

The idea there is that the excellence of the sādhaka matures to perfection.

### Text 22

*kṛṣṇas tu gṛha-kṛtyeṣu vyagrāyāṁ mātari prabhuḥ*  
*adrākṣīd arjunau pūrvaṁ guhyakau dhanadātmajau*

**Перевод:**

**While mother Yaśodā was very busy with household affairs, the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa, observed two yamala-arjuna trees, which in a former millennium had been the sons of Kuvera.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way, after giving bliss to Yaśodā by protecting her perseverance, Kṛṣṇa thought of giving bliss by fulling the words of his great devotee Nārada.

While Yaśodā, absorbed in Kṛṣṇa, became busy in household duties to make him understand that she was angry with him, he saw two arjuna trees. “Being tied up by my mother, I am her debtor, but am not capable of repaying the debt. But I will liberate these two trees standing at her town’s gate.”

### Text 23

*purā nārada-śāpena vṛkṣatāṁ prāpitau madāt*  
*nalakūvara-maṇigrīvāv iti khyātau śriyānvitau*

**Перевод:**

**In their former birth, these two sons, known as Nalakūvara and Maṇigrīva, extremely wealthy, were cursed by Nārada because of their pride and intoxication.**

**Комментарий:**

The meaning is clear.

*steyakopavato jīvān guṇair badhvaivarodaye \|*  
*tadvan mātrā nibaddhas tair māruhīty āhur arbhakāḥ*

**Having bound by the guṇas the jīvas endowed with thievery and anger, I make them cry. Bound by my mother by ropes, the children say, “Do not cry.”**

## Chapter 10 - Deliverance of the Yamala-arjuna Trees

### Text 1

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*kathyatāṁ bhagavann etat tayoḥ śāpasya kāraṇam*  
*yat tad vigarhitaṁ karma yena vā devarṣes tamaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit inquired from Śukadeva Gosvāmī: O great and powerful saint, what was the cause of Nalakūvara’s and Maṇigrīva’s having been cursed by Nārada Muni? What did they do that was so abominable that even Nārada became angry at them?**

**Комментарий:**

*kuvera-sutayoḥ śāpa-vṛttānto daśame tayoḥ \|*  
*mokṣa-kṛt pariṇūtaś ca tābhyāṁ harir udīryate*

**In the tenth chapter the Lord liberates the two sons of Kuvera, who have been cursed, and praised by them.**

What abominable (vigarhitam) action did they do by which Nārada became angry (tamaḥ).

### Texts 2-3

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*rudrasyānucarau bhūtvā sudṛptau dhanadātmajau*  
*kailāsopavane ramye mandākinyāṁ madotkaṭau*

*vāruṇīṁ madirāṁ pītvā madāghūrṇita-locanau*  
*strī-janair anugāyadbhiś ceratuḥ puṣpite vane*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The proud sons of Kuvera, associates of Śiva, after drinking liquor, wandered in a flowering garden attached to a grove of Kailāsa Mountain on the bank of the Mandākinī River, their eyes rolling in intoxication, while singing women followed them.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together.

### Text 4

*antaḥ praviśya gaṅgāyām ambhoja-vana-rājini*  
*cikrīḍatur yuvatibhir gajāv iva kareṇubhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Entering the waters of the Mandākinī Ganges, which were crowded with groups of lotus flowers, the two sons of Kuvera enjoyed with young girls, just like two male elephants enjoying in the water with female elephants.**

**Комментарий:**

*gaṅgāṁ puṇya-jalaṁ prāpya trayodaśa-vivarjayet*  
*śaucam ācamanaṁ caiva nirmālyaṁ mala-karṣaṇam*  
*taila-samardanaṁ krīḍāṁ pratigraham atho ratim*  
*anya-tīrthābhilāṣaś ca anya-tīrtha-praśaṁsanam*  
*vastra-tyāgaṁ tathā khātaṁ saṁhāraṁ caiva varjayet*

**Going to the pure water of the Gaṅgā one should give up thirteen items: Cleaning oneself, ācamana, garland remnants, removing dirt, rubbing oil on the body, playing, marrying, amorous acts, desiring other tīrthas, praising other tīrthas, taking off all clothing, digging and destroying the place. (Padma Purāṇa)**

Thus it is forbidden to play in the Gaṅgā. The two overlooked this forbiddance. They played in the Gaṅgā. They entered into the water where there were groups of lotuses.

### Text 5

*yadṛcchayā ca devarṣir bhagavāṁs tatra kaurava*  
*apaśyan nārado devau kṣībāṇau samabudhyata*

**Перевод:**

**O descendent of the Kurus! Coming by his own choice, merciful Nārada saw the two intoxicated fellows and understood completely their condition.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing them he understood that they were drunk (kṣībāṇau).

### Text 6

*taṁ dṛṣṭvā vrīḍitā devyo vivastrāḥ śāpa-śaṅkitāḥ*  
*vāsāṁsi paryadhuḥ śīghraṁ vivastrau naiva guhyakau*

**Перевод:**

**Upon seeing Nārada, the naked young girls became ashamed and, afraid of being cursed, they quickly covered their bodies with their garments. But the two sons of Kuvera did not do so.**

**Комментарий:**

The two guhyakas did not put on their clothing.

### Text 7

*tau dṛṣṭvā madirā-mattau śrī-madāndhau surātmajau*  
*tayor anugrahārthāya śāpaṁ dāsyann idaṁ jagau*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the two sons of the devatās intoxicated by opulence and false prestige, Nārada, in order to show them special mercy, while giving a curse, sang as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

He cursed them in order that they see the Lord, the result of the mercy, just like a father who though is most affection, opening thewound of his son, throws alkali into the wound, desiring the health of the son. The idea of saying jagau (sang) is that hearing that song, others too should practice what is beneficial.

### Text 8

*śrī-nārada uvāca*  
*na hy anyo juṣato joṣyān buddhi-bhraṁśo rajo-guṇaḥ*  
*śrī-madād ābhijātyādir yatra strī dyūtam āsavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Nārada Muni said: for the enjoyer of material objects, pride in wealth bewilders one’s intelligence, produces passion and produces enjoyment of wine, women and gambling more than birth in a good family or pride in education.**

**Комментарий:**

For the person serving (juṣataḥ) sense objects (joṣyān), there is no other destroyer of knowledge (buddhi-bhraṁśaḥ) such as pride arising from good family, knowledge, etc., (ābhijātyādiḥ) or other effects of rajoguṇa, such joking, etc., than pride in wealth (śri- madāt). But pride in wealth is such that there is association with women, gambling and intoxication in that pride in wealth. Such a thing is not there in other types of pride.

### Text 9

*hanyante paśavo yatra nirdayair ajitātmabhiḥ*  
*manyamānair imaṁ deham ajarāmṛtyu naśvaram*

**Перевод:**

**In that condition being merciless because they cannot control their senses, thinking that the temporary body is ageless and deathless, such persons kill animals.**

**Комментарий:**

Animals are killed by hunting, etc., by those who think that the temporary body is ageless and deathless.

### Text 10

*deva-saṁjñitam apy ante kṛmi-viḍ-bhasma-saṁjñitam*  
*bhūta-dhruk tat-kṛte svārthaṁ kiṁ veda nirayo yataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The violent person, thinking himself a devatā, but finally ending up as worms, stool and ashes, does not know his own benefit in so acting, since he goes to hell as a result.**

**Комментарий:**

Though one is called king and, in the end, not burned by his sons, is called a pile of worms; eaten by dogs is called stool and burned, is called ashes. Does that person who kills other living entities (bhūta-dhruk) for protecting the body know his own benefit, since by killing other beings he is burned in hell (nirayaḥ)?

### Text 11

*dehaḥ kim anna-dātuḥ svaṁ niṣektur mātur eva ca*  
*mātuḥ pitur vā balinaḥ kretur agneḥ śuno ’pi vā*

**Перевод:**

**While alive, does this body belong to its employer, to the father, to the mother, or to the mother’s father? Does it belong to the person who takes it away by force, to one who purchases it, or to the fire or to the dogs?**

**Комментарий:**

There is no certainty of the possessor of the body since there are many competitors. Is the body the wealth (svaṁ) of the giver offood, or to the father (niṣektuḥ), to the mother, to the mother’s father when he appoints her as a putrikā, or does it belong to aperson who forcibly takes it away (balinaḥ) or to the buyer who buys it (as a slave) by paying (kretuḥ)?

### Text 12

*evaṁ sādhāraṇaṁ deham avyakta-prabhavāpyayam*  
*ko vidvān ātmasāt kṛtvā hanti jantūn ṛte ’sataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**What person, knowing that the body appears from and disappears into invisible pradhāna, would kill other beings, thinking his body is the self? Only a materialistic person would do so.**

**Комментарий:**

Knowing that the body appears from and disappears into prakṛti (avyakta), who except a fool (asataḥ ṛte), thinking that the body isunder one’s control (ātmasāt kṛtvā), would kill others?

### Text 13

*asataḥ śrī-madāndhasya dāridryaṁ param añjanam*  
*ātmaupamyena bhūtāni daridraḥ param īkṣate*

**Перевод:**

**For the materialist blinded by intoxication with wealth, the supreme ointment for his eye is poverty. The destitute person finally sees other beings as equal to himself.**

**Комментарий:**

He determines the remedy for pride in wealth. Only (param) poverty is the ointment because the poor person sees all beings equal to himself. Thus he does not commit violence against them.

### Text 14

*yathā kaṇṭaka-viddhāṅgo jantor necchati tāṁ vyathām*  
*jīva-sāmyaṁ gato liṅgair na tathāviddha-kaṇṭakaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Just as a person whose limbs have been pierced by thorns does not desire that pain for others, having identified with them by seeing the symptoms of pain in them. Those who are not pierced by thorns are not like that.**

**Комментарий:**

He gives an example. He does not desire the pain of a living being different from himself. He develops identity with another jīva by symptoms seen, such as withered face. By his previously experienced pain, he infers a similar pain in the other living entity. A person not pierced by a thorn (aviddha-kaṇṭakaḥ) is not like that. The members of the compound are reversed as in rāja-danta (principal tooth).

### Text 15

*daridro nirahaṁ-stambho muktaḥ sarva-madair iha*  
*kṛcchraṁ yadṛcchayāpnoti tad dhi tasya paraṁ tapaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The poor man is devoid of arrogance arising from wealth, and is free from agitation caused by wealth. He experiences difficulties by the nature of poverty. Poverty is the best austerity for him.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, being poor, the practices for liberation naturally arise. This is expressed in three verses.

The poor man, devoid of arrogance arising from pride in wealth (nirahaṁ-stambhaḥ), is free from all pride arising from good family,etc. Because he is disrespected by everyone, these types of pride also generally disappear. He experiences difficulty by chance. That is the best austerity.

### Text 16

*nityaṁ kṣut-kṣāma-dehasya daridrasyānna-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ*  
*indriyāṇy anuśuṣyanti hiṁsāpi vinivartate*

**Перевод:**

**When the poverty-stricken person is continuously hungry and thirsty and desires food, his senses become completely disinterested in enjoying. He gives up violence.**

**Комментарий:**

Hiṁsā means afflicting other living entities.

### Text 17

*daridrasyaiva yujyante sādhavaḥ sama-darśinaḥ*  
*sadbhiḥ kṣiṇoti taṁ tarṣaṁ tata ārād viśuddhyati*

**Перевод:**

**Saintly persons, seeing all beings equally, freely associate with those who are poverty-stricken, but not with those who are rich. A poverty-stricken man, by association with saintly persons, very soon becomes uninterested in material desires and becomes purified.**

**Комментарий:**

“One should not say that the desire for enjoyment in the poor man will not be destroyed.” That desire is also destroyed. The devotees, because of seeing equally, go to the houses of both the wealthy and the poor, but associate with the poor only since the poor man will respect them because of his lack of pride. But the wealthy man, blinded by wealth, will not respect them. I am a proof for that. By the devotees who teach what is essential and superfluous in life, the poor man destroys his thirst for enjoyment (tarṣam) since the sweetness of tattva-jñāna, obtained from their association destroys that thirst for enjoyment. Thus he becomes purified quickly (ārāt), i.e. at that time he becomes qualified for the path of liberation.

### Text 18

*sādhūnāṁ sama-cittānāṁ mukunda-caraṇaiṣiṇām*  
*upekṣyaiḥ kiṁ dhana-stambhair asadbhir asad-āśrayaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Why should the devotees having proper conduct, having equal vision and being dedicated to the feet of the Lord, show mercy to the materialists who are proud of their wealth, have improper behavior, indulge in sense enjoyment and are indifferent to the devotees?**

**Комментарий:**

It is not that the devotees go to the house of a wealthy man for dharma. For the devotees who though having equal vision, desire the feet of Mukunda, what use are materialists proud of their wealth (dhana-stambhaiḥ), non-Vaiṣṇavas (asadbhiḥ) and those devoted tonon-Vaiṣṇavas (asad-āśrayaiḥ)? They have no use. They do not go to houses of such people. By this it is stated that those wealthy people who serve devotees and are without pride associate with devotees.

### Text 19

*tad ahaṁ mattayor mādhvyā vāruṇyā śrī-madāndhayoḥ*  
*tamo-madaṁ hariṣyāmi straiṇayor ajitātmanoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**I will take away the ignorance of these two intoxicated fellows, blinded by pride of wealth, addicted to women, and unable to control their senses.**

**Комментарий:**

He determines that the remedy is to destroy the sickness of pride. I will take away the intoxication of ignorance (tamaḥ) of these two blinded by wealth, with liquor made from honey (mādhvyā).

### Texts 20-22

*yad imau loka-pālasya putrau bhūtvā tamaḥ-plutau*  
*na vivāsasam ātmānaṁ vijānītaḥ sudurmadau*

*ato ’rhataḥ sthāvaratāṁ syātāṁ naivaṁ yathā punaḥ*  
*smṛtiḥ syān mat-prasādena tatrāpi mad-anugrahāt*

*vāsudevasya sānnidhyaṁ labdhvā divya-śarac-chate*  
*vṛtte svarlokatāṁ bhūyo labdha-bhaktī bhaviṣyataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Since the two were sons of Kuvera but became covered with ignorance, and, out of great pride, did not even recognize their nakedness before me, it is proper that they become trees so that they will not act in this manner again. However, by my mercy they will retain their memory and by Kṛṣṇa’s mercy to me, they will attain association with Kṛṣṇa after a hundred divine years, attain steady bhakti and return to their planet.**

**Комментарий:**

They were naked (vivāsasam). He curses their nakedness. It is proper that they become trees, since they are naked, lacking in humility, and not speaking. Though they will become trees, by my mercy they will have memory. Even in memory, by my mercy after a hundred devatā years, attaining association of Vāsudeva, attaining bhakti, they will attain (bhaviṣyataḥ) the status of devatās in Svarga. The root bhū means to attain.

### Text 23

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*evam uktvā sa devarṣir gato nārāyaṇāśramam*  
*nalakūvara-maṇigrīvāv āsatur yamalārjunau*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Having thus spoken, Nārada returned to Nārāyaṇa-āśrama, and Nalakūvara and Maṇigrīva became twin arjuna trees.**

### Text 24

*ṛṣer bhāgavata-mukhyasya satyaṁ kartuṁ vaco hariḥ*  
*jagāma śanakais tatra yatrāstāṁ yamalārjunau*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, to make true the words of the greatest devotee, Nārada, slowly went to that spot where the twin arjuna trees were standing.**

**Комментарий:**

The narration returns to the subject of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 25

*devarṣir me priyatamo yad imau dhanadātmajau*  
*tat tathā sādhayiṣyāmi yad gītaṁ tan mahātmanā*

**Перевод:**

**Because Nārada is my dear devotee, I will do just as he has predicted concerning the two sons of Kuvera.**

**Комментарий:**

Why should the word by made true? Because Nārada is my dear devotee. Therefore I will make them perfect in the way it was predicted (yad gītam) by him (mahātmanā).

### Text 26

*ity antareṇārjunayoḥ kṛṣṇas tu yamayor yayau*  
*ātma-nirveśa-mātreṇa tiryag-gatam ulūkhalam*

**Перевод:**

**Having thus spoken, Kṛṣṇa went between the two arjuna trees. The mortar turned crosswise as soon as he entered between the trees.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking in this way, Kṛṣṇa came between (antareṇa) the two trees born together (yamayoḥ). Just as he came between the trees, the mortar became horizontal.

### Text 27

*bālena niṣkarṣayatānvag ulūkhalaṁ tad*  
*dāmodareṇa tarasotkalitāṅghri-bandhau*  
*niṣpetatuḥ parama-vikramitātivepa-*  
*skandha-pravāla-viṭapau kṛta-caṇḍa-śabdau*

**Перевод:**

**The two trees were uprooted by the child Dāmodara who steadily pulled the mortar sideways and fell down with force with a fearful sound, while their leaves, branches and trunks trembled violently.**

**Комментарий:**

The two arjuna trees, standing as if their roots were bound, being uprooted by the child (bālena) Dāmodara, tied with a rope by his mother around his waist, who pulled constantly (niṣ) the mortarlengthwise, fell down completely (niṣpetatuḥ). The trunk, branches and leaves trembled violently by Kṛṣṇa’s (parama) strength (vikramita).

### Text 28

*tatra śriyā paramayā kakubhaḥ sphurantau*  
*siddhāv upetya kujayor iva jāta-vedāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ praṇamya śirasākhila-loka-nāthaṁ*  
*baddhāñjalī virajasāv idam ūcatuḥ sma*

**Перевод:**

**Attaining the status of devatās, though situated in the trees, they illuminated the directions with their intense beauty, like fire blazing from two trees, and offered respects with their heads to Kṛṣṇa, the lord of all planets. Purified of their offense, with folded hands, they began to speak.**

**Комментарий:**

The devatās (siddhau) who has been situated as trees (kujayoḥ) shone, spreading their effulgence in all directions (kakubhaḥ), devoid of pride (virajasau), approached Kṛṣṇa and offering respects spoke. They appeared like one fire (jāta-vedāḥ) as their two effulgences merged.

### Text 29

*kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-yogiṁs tvam ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ paraḥ*  
*vyaktāvyaktam idaṁ viśvaṁ rūpaṁ te brāhmaṇā viduḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, endowed with all powers! You are Svayam Bhagavān, superior to Mahā-viṣṇu. The brāhmaṇas know you as the form of universe and as cause and effect.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why do you two devatās offer respects to me, a cowherd boy tied to a mortar?” They offer respects and prayers. Saying Kṛṣṇa twice indicates that the two spoke at the same time. O great yogī! You have inconceivable powers! Though you freed us, we cannot understand the reason for your bondage to the mortar. A cowherd boy, you are the Supreme Lord (puruṣaḥ paraḥ), andthat too Svayam Bhagavān (ādyaḥ). What can bind you who are all forms by your powers? You are cause and effect (vyaktāvyaktam).

### Texts 30-31

*tvam ekaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ dehāsv-ātmendriyeśvaraḥ*  
*tvam eva kālo bhagavān viṣṇur avyaya īśvaraḥ*

*tvaṁ mahān prakṛtiḥ sūkṣmā rajaḥ-sattva-tamomayī*  
*tvam eva puruṣo ’dhyakṣaḥ sarva-kṣetra-vikāra-vit*

**Перевод:**

**You are the Supreme Lord, the controller of everything. The body, life, ego and senses of every living entity are your own self. You are the supreme person, Viṣṇu, the imperishable controller. You are the time factor, the immediate cause, and you are material nature, consisting of the three modes passion, goodness and ignorance. You are the original cause of this material manifestation. You are the Supersoul, and therefore you know everything within the core of the heart of every living entity.**

**Комментарий:**

There is no other controller other than you. This is expressed in two verses. You are the controller (īśvaraḥ) of the body, prāṇas (asu), ahaṅkāra (ātmā) and senses.

“Time is the efficient cause of the universe. Prakṛti is the material cause. From this arises mahat-tattva. In transforming it into theuniverse by ahaṅkāra,etc. the doer and the controller is the puruṣa Kāraṇadaśaya. What relation do I have with this?”

You alone are all these because you are the controller, Bhagavān, spreading everywhere (viṣṇuḥ) on account of the statement:

*sarvaṁ samāpnoṣi tato ‘si sarvaḥ*

**You pervade everywhere, and therefore you are everything. (BG** [**11.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/11.40)**)**

Thus you are the controller of time. But the puruṣa is your svāṁśa. Thus, he too is you. Thus there is oneness because you pervade everything, since pure Advaita with complete oneness of matter and spirit is denied. You know all the transformations such as mindin all bodies (kṣetreṣu): you are omniscient.

### Text 32

*gṛhyamāṇais tvam agrāhyo vikāraiḥ prākṛtair guṇaiḥ*  
*ko nv ihārhati vijñātuṁ prāk siddhaṁ guṇa-saṁvṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You cannot be understood by the material intelligence or the material senses. What person, covered by the guṇas can understand you, who exist eternally in your spiritual body?**

**Комментарий:**

“But why are you overpraising me, standing in front of you, having been bound to the mortar by my mother?” You are not perceived by the senses such as the eye, etc., (gunaiḥ) which are seen by you, the seer, and which are transformations. Where do the transformations come from? They are the effect of māyā (prākṛtaiḥ).

“But the jīva should know me since he is composed of knowledge.”

Though of such nature, which jīva, being covered by the guṇas, losing his knowledge by your māyā, can know you? No one can in mahat-tattva. You are previously accomplished (prāk siddham), since you are the instigator of the senses and body of the jīva. But by saying prākṛtair and guṇa-saṁvṛtaḥ, it is indicated that a devotee who is beyond māyā, perfected in senses by you your superior śakti,can see you.

### Text 33

*tasmai tubhyaṁ bhagavate vāsudevāya vedhase*  
*ātma-dyota-guṇaiś channa-mahimne brahmaṇe namaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you, Svayam Bhagavān, Brahman forms covered by your personal qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

Since you are difficult to understand we just offer respects. We offer respects to you, the creator of the universe (vedhase). Being covered by the guṇas, the reason for the Lord’s being difficult to understand is again stated. You are hard to understand because your glories are covered by the guṇas manifested (dyota) by you, like the sun covered by clouds (which arise due to the sun).

### Texts 34-35

*yasyāvatārā jñāyante śarīriṣv aśarīriṇaḥ*  
*tais tair atulyātiśayair vīryair dehiṣv asaṅgataiḥ*

*sa bhavān sarva-lokasya bhavāya vibhavāya ca*  
*avatīrṇo ’ṁśa-bhāgena sāmprataṁ patir āśiṣām*

**Перевод:**

**Though you have no material body, your avatāras can be inferred in their various forms like Matsya by their indescribable, astonishing powers and activities, which are not found in material bodies. The nourisher of devotees, you have appeared at this time along with portions of your portions like Brahmā and Śiva to give good fortune to all people in this life and the next.**

**Комментарий:**

“By what indications do you describe my position as the Supreme Lord?” They answer in two verses. The avatāras as Matsya, etc., of you who are devoid of a materially distinct body (aśarīriṇaḥ) are inferred (jñāyate) in the species of fish, etc., by feats (vīryaiḥ)that do not occur (asaṅgataiḥ) in jīvas (dehiṣu). You, the avatārī, have now appeared, since you uprooted us two trees, difficult touproot even by a herd of the best elephants, by using little strength through manifesting a childhood pastime and gave similar strength to the rope and mortar. You have manifested for the prosperity (bhavāya) and for destroying the saṁsāra (vibhavāya) of all people, i.e. for giving liberation. You are the fulfiller of desires through your expansions of expansions (aṁśa-bhāgena).

### Text 36

*namaḥ parama-kalyāṇa namaḥ parama-maṅgala*  
*vāsudevāya śāntāya yadūnāṁ pataye namaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O supremely auspicious! O auspicious lord for Śiva and Brahmā! We offer our respectful obeisances unto you, the son of Vasudeva, the lord of the Yadu kṣatriyas and cowherds, the embodiment of joy.**

**Комментарий:**

O most auspicious person from whom comes supreme auspiciousness (parama-kalyāna)!

### Text 37

*anujānīhi nau bhūmaṁs tavānucara-kiṅkarau*  
*darśanaṁ nau bhagavata ṛṣer āsīd anugrahāt*

**Перевод:**

**O Supreme Lord! Please allow us to be servants of your servants, for though that is rare, we have attained your association by the mercy of the most compassionate Nārada Muni.**

**Комментарий:**

Having received devatā bodies, they ask permission to go to their homes. We are servants of Śiva or Nārada (anucara). “But if I am imperceptible, how can I be seen by your eyes?” This is due to the mercy of Nārada, the cause of your mercy.

### Text 38

*vāṇī guṇānukathane śravaṇau kathāyāṁ*  
*hastau ca karmasu manas tava pādayor naḥ*  
*smṛtyāṁ śiras tava nivāsa-jagat praṇāme*  
*dṛṣṭiḥ satāṁ darśane ’stu bhavat-tanūnām*

**Перевод:**

**May all our words describe your qualities, may our ears engage in hearing your glories, may our hands, legs and other senses engage in deity service and may our minds always think of your lotus feet. May our heads offer our obeisances to the Vaiṣṇavas, your dwelling place, and may our eyes see the forms of Vaiṣṇavas and your deity forms.**

**Комментарий:**

Nārada said “Having attained association of the Lord, you will become devotees.” Remembering his words, they pray to Nārada for bhakti to the Lord. The word naḥ (us) is used to indicate not only themselves but their associates. May our minds remember your feet. May our heads offer respects to you, O who dwells in the universe (nivāsa-jagat). May your eyes see devotees, who are yourbodies (bhavat-tanūnām).

### Text 39

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*itthaṁ saṅkīrtitas tābhyāṁ bhagavān gokuleśvaraḥ*  
*dāmnā colūkhale baddhaḥ prahasann āha guhyakau*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Having been glorified by the two sons of Kuvera, the master of Gokula, the cause of good fortune, bound to the wooden mortar by ropes, laughed and spoke to the sons of Kuvera.**

**Комментарий:**

Praised (saṅkīrtitaḥ) by the two, bound by rope and prema (ca), the Lord laughed indicating that “I am not so pleased by the praises of devatās as by the scolding and binding of the gopīs.”

### Text 40

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*jñātaṁ mama puraivaitad ṛṣiṇā karuṇātmanā*  
*yac chrī-madāndhayor vāgbhir vibhraṁśo ’nugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: I have known already that merciful Nārada made you two drunkards, blinded by pride in your wealth, fall into hellish existence by his words.**

**Комментарий:**

The words (vāgbhiḥ) were those starting with na hy anyo juṣato joṣyān (SB 10.10.8). Nārada was merciful in destroying your wealth.

### Text 41

*sādhūnāṁ sama-cittānāṁ sutarāṁ mat-kṛtātmanām*  
*darśanān no bhaved bandhaḥ puṁso ’kṣṇoḥ savitur yathā*

**Перевод:**

**When one is face to face with the sun, there is no longer darkness for one’s eyes. Similarly, when one is face to face with a merciful devotee, who is fully peaceful and surrendered to the Supreme Lord, one will no longer be subject to material bondage.**

**Комментарий:**

“But though we saw Nārada, we did not respect him, how then did we obtain his mercy?” The devotees are equal minded, not disturbed by respect or disrespect of themselves. They have offered their minds to me. By seeing these devotees one is no longer bound, just as from seeing the sun the eye is not bound by darkness.

### Text 42

*tad gacchataṁ mat-paramau nalakūvara sādanam*  
*sañjāto mayi bhāvo vām īpsitaḥ paramo ’bhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Nalakūvara! Fully surrendered to me, now you may both return home. Because you have developed desired prema for me, you are free of saṁsāra.**

**Комментарий:**

Only Nalakūvara is addressed since he was the main brother. Therefore (tat) you two, my great devotees (mat-paramau), go home (sādanaṁ). Having developed bhāva for me by which there is no saṁsāra (abhavaḥ), you are thus qualified for liberation at the end of your term as devatās.

### Text 43

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity uktau tau parikramya praṇamya ca punaḥ punaḥ*  
*baddholūkhalam āmantrya jagmatur diśam uttarām*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: after the Lord spoke, the two brothers circumambulated the Lord, who was bound to the wooden mortar, and offered obeisances to him. After taking permission they went to the north.**

**Комментарий:**

The brothers offered respects to Kṛṣṇa, bound by the mortar (baddholūkhalam). It is similar to the construction āhitāgni: a person who maintains a sacrificial fire, where the order of words is reversed. Taking permission (āmantryā) they went north.

*mama mātrā nibaddhasya mocakasyāpi mocanaṁ \|*  
*nānyas tātaṁ vinā kuryād iti kṛṣṇo vyajijñapat \|*

**Release of me, giver of liberation, tied up by my mother, should be done only by my father. This is what Kṛṣṇa announced.**

## Chapter 11 - The Childhood Pastimes of Kṛṣṇa

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*gopā nandādayaḥ śrutvā drumayoḥ patato ravam*  
*tatrājagmuḥ kuru-śreṣṭha nirghāta-bhaya-śaṅkitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, all the cowherd men in the neighborhood an Nanda, hearing the fierce sound of the falling trees and fearing thunderbolts though the sky was cloudless, went to the spot.**

**Комментарий:**

*ekādaśe nanda-sūnor mokṣo vṛndāvane gamaḥ \|*  
*suprītir vatsa-rakṣā ca tathā vatsa-baka-kṣayaḥ*

**In the eleventh chapter Kṛṣṇa is untied, goes to Vṛndāvana, joyfully protects the calves and kills Vatsāṣura and Baka.**

Nirghāta means lightning strokes.

### Texts 2-3

*bhūmyāṁ nipatitau tatra dadṛśur yamalārjunau*  
*babhramus tad avijñāya lakṣyaṁ patana-kāraṇam*

*ulūkhalaṁ vikarṣantaṁ dāmnā baddhaṁ*  
*ca bālakam kasyedaṁ kuta āścaryam utpāta iti kātarāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**There they saw the fallen pair of arjuna trees on the ground, but they were bewildered so that they could not trace out the cause of their falling, though they saw the cause, Kṛṣṇa, bound by the rope to the mortar, which he was dragging. “Who had done it? This is astonishing. Why? What a disaster.” The cowherd men became frightened.**

**Комментарий:**

The first line goes alone. They saw from far off on the ground the two trees. The next three lines go together. They were bewildered, not understanding the cause of their falling. Though they could see the mortar, etc., the cause of their fall, they were in doubt(babhramuḥ) not having seen due to being situated far away and because the branches of the fallen trees caused obstruction. Then, coming close, not seeing Kṛṣṇa covered by the branches and leaves, they became disturbed. “Who did this? Who did this astonishing act and why?” Hari-vaṁśa says:

*kenemau pātitau vṛkṣau ghoṣasyāyatanopamau vinā vātaṁ vinā varṣaṁ*  
*vidyut-prapatanaṁ vinā vinā hasti-kṛtaṁ doṣam kenemau pātitau drumau*

**How did these two trees, big as a cowherd’s house fall, without wind or rain, without being struck by lightning, without being attacked by elephants?**

### Text 4

*bālā ūcur aneneti tiryag-gatam ulūkhalam*  
*vikarṣatā madhya-gena puruṣāv apy acakṣmahi*

**Перевод:**

**Then all the cowherd boys said: He did it. He pulled the mortar crosswise between the trees. We saw two men.**

**Комментарий:**

The boys just said, “It was done by Kṛṣṇa (anena) pulling the mortar horizontally as he went between the trees.” They failed to say that by Kṛṣṇa the two trees fell because being children they did not speak completely. Moreover, they also said, “We saw two men coming out of the two trees.”

### Text 5

*na te tad-uktaṁ jagṛhur na ghaṭeteti tasya tat*  
*bālasyotpāṭanaṁ tarvoḥ kecit sandigdha-cetasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd men, headed by Nanda, could not believe the children’s words. A child could not uproot the two trees. Others were also doubtful of the children’s words.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda and others (te) could not believe what the children said, since their vātsalya covered knowledge of Kṛṣṇa’s powers. “The child could not uproot the trees.” Others however were doubtful, by inferring the invariable connection due to the death of Pūtanā and others, they thought, “this may be his work.” But even by seeing the softness of his body, their vātsalya just increased by such reasoning.

### Text 6

*ulūkhalaṁ vikarṣantaṁ dāmnā baddhaṁ svam ātmajam*  
*vilokya nandaḥ prahasad- vadano vimumoca ha*

**Перевод:**

**When Nanda Mahārāja saw his own son bound with ropes to the wooden mortar and dragging it, he smiled and released Kṛṣṇa from his bonds.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing his son, his limbs all tied up, Nanda was smiling to give joy to his frightened, bound son. Or your mother, whose lap you prefer compared to even my association, has tied you up for a small offense. Why should I release you? He was smiling to scold him.

### Text 7

*gopībhiḥ stobhito ’nṛtyad bhagavān bālavat kvacit*  
*udgāyati kvacin mugdhas tad-vaśo dāru-yantravat*

**Перевод:**

**Praised by the elderly gopīs, the Lord, like a puppet on strings, sometimes danced. Most charming, sometimes he sang like an ordinary child.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the good fortune of his mother and father, the rulers of Vraja, Śukadeva describes the good fortune of their citizens, the people of Vraja in thirteen and a half verses. He was praised by elderly gopīs. “If you dance, we will give you butter with sugar.” Encouraged by this, the Lord though full of six opulences, and though the controller of Brahmā and Śiva, controlled by them like a puppet on strings, sometimes danced. Sometimes he sang, like any other ordinary child. He was most attractive (mugdhaḥ) indancing etc. Mugdha means beautiful according to Viśva.

### Text 8

*bibharti kvacid ājñaptaḥ pīṭhakonmāna-pādukam*  
*bāhu-kṣepaṁ ca kurute svānāṁ ca prītim āvahan*

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes, being ordered, he would carry shoes pressed against his belly. He would raise his arms bravely, giving pleasure to all the cowherds.**

**Комментарий:**

“How strong is he?” Ordered by those who inquired in this way, first he took shoes, then he took a weight heavier than that, then hetook a stool heavier than that and carried them. He held them to his soft belly. He would repeatedly raise his arms to show his strength. By this the relatives experienced pleasure.

### Text 9

*darśayaṁs tad-vidāṁ loke ātmano bhakta-vaśyatām*  
*vrajasyovāha vai harṣaṁ bhagavān bāla-ceṣṭitaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**By his childhood pastimes the Lord brought joy to the people of Vraja, and showed those who knew about his powers that he was controlled by his devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Not only the relatives but all the people of Vraja had good fortune. It is well known (vai) that he brought joy to Vraja by his childhood pastimes. What did he do? He showed to those who knew of his supreme powers such as Brahmā and Śiva that he was controlled by his devotees. This was not some imitation.

### Text 10

*krīṇīhi bhoḥ phalānīti śrutvā satvaram acyutaḥ*  
*phalārthī dhānyam ādāya yayau sarva-phala-pradaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Once a woman selling fruit was calling, “O inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi, please buy this fruit.” Upon hearing this, Kṛṣṇa, desiring fruit, though he is the bestower of all fruits, immediately took some grains and went to her.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the joy experienced by the townspeople, now the joy of those residing outside the town including even the pulindasis described. Because he never fails in his omniscience (acyutaḥ), the son of Nanda knew that she had brought beautiful tasty fruit forhim. Though he gives all fruits (results), he desired fruit. Quickly he took grains from the courtyard in his hands and came to her.

### Text 11

*phala-vikrayiṇī tasya cyuta-dhānya-kara-dvayam*  
*phalair apūrayad ratnaiḥ phala-bhāṇḍam apūri ca*

**Перевод:**

**While Kṛṣṇa was going to the fruit vendor very hastily, most of the grains he was holding fell. Nonetheless, the fruit vendor filled Kṛṣṇa’s hands with fruits, and her fruit basket was immediately filled with jewels and gold.**

**Комментарий:**

The fruit vendor had her desire to see him fulfilled. She filled with fruit his spread-out hands from which all the grains fell on the path due to coming out quickly from inside the house, and who threw the few grains remaining in his hand into her fruit basket while saying “Please give me fruit.” Her basket was immediately filled with jewels. His powers are astonishing. The young girls, daughters of this woman and other are praised by Uddhava for having supreme anurāga for Kṛṣṇa:

*kvemāḥ striyo vana-carīr vyabhicāra-duṣṭāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇe kva caiṣa paramātmani rūḍha-bhāvaḥ*

**How amazing it is that these simple women who wander about the forest, seemingly spoiled by improper behavior, have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul! (SB** [**10.47.59**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.59)**)**

### Text 12

*sarit-tīra-gataṁ kṛṣṇaṁ bhagnārjunam athāhvayat*  
*rāmaṁ ca rohiṇī devī krīḍantaṁ bālakair bhṛśam*

**Перевод:**

**Once, after the uprooting of the yamala-arjuna trees, Rohiṇī went to call Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, who had both gone to the riverside and were playing with the other boys with deep attention.**

**Комментарий:**

Another story is told in half a verse. Rohiṇī called Kṛṣṇa. Balarāma too is included according what is said later. She was sent by Yaśodā who was attached to giving them meals. Rohiṇī was sent because she thought that they will not come by having her maidservants call them.

### Text 13

*nopeyātāṁ yadāhūtau krīḍā-saṅgena putrakau*  
*yaśodāṁ preṣayām āsa rohiṇī putra-vatsalām*

**Перевод:**

**Because of being attached to playing with the other boys, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma did not return upon being called by Rohiṇī. Therefore Rohiṇī sent mother Yaśodā to call them back, because mother Yaśodā was more affectionate to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

When the two sons, called by Rohiṇi, did not come because of absorption in playing with the boys, Rohiṇī sent Yaśodā. She could control them because she had greater affection than Rohiṇī. “But why did the two queens leave the house and go to the bank of the river?” It was easy to go by the side door since the solitary place was almost like another room within the house. There was a famous playground there, a pleasant bank where they became covered with dust. (Verse 18)

### Text 14

*krīḍantaṁ sā sutaṁ bālair ativelaṁ sahāgrajam*  
*yaśodājohavīt kṛṣṇaṁ putra-sneha-snuta-stanī*

**Перевод:**

**Yaśodā, her breast flowing with milk out of affection, called Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, who were playing with the other boys although it was very late.**

**Комментарий:**

The time was getting late (ativelam). Again and again she called Kṛṣṇa who was playing with other boys. She called them from far away, fearing they would run away if she went close.

### Text 15

*kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇāravindākṣa tāta ehi stanaṁ piba*  
*alaṁ vihāraiḥ kṣut-kṣāntaḥ krīḍā-śrānto ’si putraka*

**Перевод:**

**Mother Yaśodā said: My dear son Kṛṣṇa, lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, come here and drink the milk of my breast. My dear darling, you must be very tired because of hunger and the fatigue of playing so long. There is no need to play any longer.**

**Комментарий:**

She repeatedly called him so he could hear from far away.

### Text 16

*he rāmāgaccha tātāśu sānujaḥ kula-nandana*  
*prātar eva kṛtāhāras tad bhavān bhoktum arhati*

**Перевод:**

**My dear Baladeva, best of our family, please come immediately with your younger brother, Kṛṣṇa. You both ate in the morning, and now you ought to eat something more.**

**Комментарий:**

“Balarāma who obeys my orders will bring Kṛṣṇa by force.” Thinking in this way, Yaśodā called Balarāma. The word tāta indicates worthy of compassion according to Medinī.

### Text 17

*pratīkṣate tvāṁ dāśārha bhokṣyamāṇo vrajādhipaḥ*  
*ehy āvayoḥ priyaṁ dhehi sva-gṛhān yāta bālakāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The King of Vraja, is now waiting to eat. O my dear son Balarāma, he is waiting for you. Therefore, come back to please us. All the boys playing with you and Kṛṣṇa should now go to their homes.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda will not eat without you two. Will you give pain to your father who is hungry? Come back to please us, your two mothers, or to please your parents. O boys! Go to your houses. Your mothers are also suffering like us. Make them happy. She says this to make them stop playing.

### Text 18

*dhūli-dhūsaritāṅgas tvaṁ putra majjanam āvaha*  
*janmarkṣaṁ te ’dya bhavati viprebhyo dehi gāḥ śuciḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Mother Yaśodā further told Kṛṣṇa: because of playing all day, your body has become covered with dust and sand. Therefore, come back and cleanse yourself. Today the moon is conjoined with the auspicious star of your birth. Therefore, be pure and give cows in charity to the brāhmaṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

Invoking his enthusiasm for his giving charity to make him give up enthusiasm for playing she speaks.

### Text 19

*paśya paśya vayasyāṁs te mātṛ-mṛṣṭān svalaṅkṛtān*  
*tvaṁ ca snātaḥ kṛtāhāro viharasva svalaṅkṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Just see how all your playmates have been cleansed and decorated with beautiful ornaments by their mothers. You should take your bath, eat your lunch, wear ornaments, and then play.**

**Комментарий:**

She produces envy by showing the boys who had come there just then. You do not have to give up playing. Play after bathing, etc.

### Text 20

*itthaṁ yaśodā tam aśeṣa-śekharaṁ*  
*matvā sutaṁ sneha-nibaddha-dhīr nṛpa*  
*haste gṛhītvā saha-rāmam acyutaṁ*  
*nītvā sva-vāṭaṁ kṛtavaty athodayam*

**Перевод:**

**O King! Because of intense affection, mother Yaśodā considered Kṛṣṇa, who was at the peak of all crown jewels, to be her son. Thus, she took Kṛṣṇa by the hand, along with Balarāma, so they could not escape and brought them home, where she performed her duties by fully bathing them, dressing them and feeding them.**

**Комментарий:**

Approaching slowly while uttering affectionate words, thinking of him, Svayaṁ Bhagavān (aśeṣa-śekharaṁ) as her son since he was like that, or thinking of her son as the head ornament of the world, she brought him to her house (sva-vāṭam). Vāṭa means place according to Medinī. She performed auspicious acts (udayam) such as bathing him, feeding him and offering him ornaments. Feeding him was the main item. I will explain this later.

### Text 21

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*gopa-vṛddhā mahotpātān anubhūya bṛhadvane*  
*nandādayaḥ samāgamya vraja-kāryam amantrayan*

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: having seen the great disturbances in Mahāvana, all the elderly persons among the cowherd men, headed by Nanda Mahārāja assembled and began to consider what to do for Kṛṣṇa’s safety.**

**Комментарий:**

Having played in Bṛhadvana in this way, they ornamented it. Seeing the beauty of Vṛndāvana when he had killed Tṛnāvarta in the sky, wanting to play there, Kṛṣṇa arranged a cause by having them speak of the dangers in Bṛhadvana. The great dangers refers to wolves which caused suffering to the calves and boys, according to Hari-vaṁśa.

### Text 22

*tatropananda-nāmāha gopo jñāna-vayo-’dhikaḥ*  
*deśa-kālārtha-tattva-jñaḥ priya-kṛd rāma-kṛṣṇayoḥ*

**Перевод:**
