**At this meeting of all the inhabitants of Gokula, a cowherd man named Upananda, who was the most mature in age and knowledge and was very experienced according to time, circumstances and country, made this suggestion for the benefit of Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

He inspired Upananda, so that he gives the intelligence to go to Vṛndāvana. The king of Vraja, Parjanya had five sons named Upananda, Abhinanda, Nanda, Sannanda and Nandana. Among them Upananda gave rulership which was given to himself by his father to Nanda, the middle son who had great qualities, with everyone’s agreement and Upananda acted as his advisor. Upanandahad knowledge of purpose (artha), place and time, taking them individually and all together and had special knowledge of what was best, average and inferior.

### Text 23

*utthātavyam ito ’smābhir gokulasya hitaiṣibhiḥ*  
*āyānty atra mahotpātā bālānāṁ nāśa-hetavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thinking of the welfare of the people of Gokula we should leave this place. Great disturbances, which are dangerous for the children, have occurred here.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking of the welfare of the inhabitants of Gokula we should leave.

### Text 24

*muktaḥ kathañcid rākṣasyā bāla-ghnyā bālako hy asau*  
*harer anugrahān nūnam anaś copari nāpatat*

**Перевод:**

**The child Kṛṣṇa was somehow or other rescued from the hands of the Rākṣasī Pūtanā, who was determined to kill him. Then, again by the mercy of the Supreme Lord, the handcart missed falling upon the child.**

**Комментарий:**

He indicates regret for the great danger to the children. Putting Kṛṣṇa, who had come there out of curiosity, on his lap, he gave examples of his worries in three verses. Somehow, by some unseen cause, Kṛṣṇa was saved from Pūtanā. That is clarified with another example. Anaḥ means a cart.

### Text 25

*cakra-vātena nīto ’yaṁ daityena vipadaṁ viyat*  
*śilāyāṁ patitas tatra paritrātaḥ sureśvaraiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then again, the demon Tṛṇāvarta, in the form of a whirlwind, took the child away into the dangerous sky but the demon fell down onto a slab of stone. In that case also, by the mercy of the Lord’s associates, the child was saved.**

**Комментарий:**

Cakra-vātena means by Tṛṇāvarta. The sky (viyat) is dangerous (vipadaṁ) since it causes falling (vipat). He was saved by the Lord(sureśvaraiḥ). Plural is used out of respect.

### Text 26

*yan na mriyeta drumayor antaraṁ prāpya bālakaḥ*  
*asāv anyatamo vāpi tad apy acyuta-rakṣaṇam*

**Перевод:**

**The child and others did not die on going between the trees. This was also protection by the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks with tears and choked voice. He uses coarse language out of grief in order that they leave quickly. Asau refers to Kṛṣṇa. Though because of being eternal associates they knew internally, like lotus fibers concealed in a stem, that Kṛṣṇa had powers, still they worried about calamities since that intelligence disappeared by their vātsalya-prema. Similarly, Balarāma and others also knew of his powers but worried.

### Text 27

*yāvad autpātiko ’riṣṭo vrajaṁ nābhibhaved itaḥ*  
*tāvad bālān upādāya yāsyāmo ’nyatra sānugāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Taking the children, we should go elsewhere with our followers so that misfortune arising from calamities does not afflict the people of Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

So that inauspicious suffering (ariṣṭa) arising from calamity (autpātika) do not occur we should go elsewhere. Ariṣṭa can mean inauspicious as well as auspicious, according to Amara-kośa.

### Text 28

*vanaṁ vṛndāvanaṁ nāma paśavyaṁ nava-kānanam*  
*gopa-gopī-gavāṁ sevyaṁ puṇyādri-tṛṇa-vīrudham*

**Перевод:**

**The forest called Vṛndāvana has new groves, is suitable for the cows, is suitable of the cowherds and their wives and cows, and is full of pure mountains, grass and shrubs.**

**Комментарий:**

“But where shall we go?” We should go to the forest called Vṛndāvana, where in one place our ancient capitol Nandīśvara existed. We should not go anywhere out of Vraja. It is the forest protected (avanaṁ) by Vṛndā devī. Because of her influence, there can be no disturbances at all and it has all good qualities. It is beneficial for the cows (paśavyaṁ) because there is grass which is healthful. It should be served by the cowherds since it is free of thorns and wicked animals. It has fresh forests within it.

### Text 29

*tat tatrādyaiva yāsyāmaḥ śakaṭān yuṅkta mā ciram*  
*godhanāny agrato yāntu bhavatāṁ yadi rocate*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, we should go today. There is no need to delay. If you agree to my proposal, prepare all the bullock carts and putting the cows in front of us, let us go.**

**Комментарий:**

He hastens them to go there. Do this if it is agreeable to you (bhavatām).

### Text 30

*tac chrutvaika-dhiyo gopāḥ sādhu sādhv iti vādinaḥ*  
*vrajān svān svān samāyujya yayū rūḍha-paricchadāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Upon hearing this advice from Upananda, the cowherd men unanimously agreed. “This is good,” they said. Bringing together all their cows, they placed their possessions on the carts, and departed.**

**Комментарий:**

With minds fixed only on Kṛṣṇa (eka-dhiyaḥ), they agreed in order to avoid the dangers. Gathering (samāyujya) all the cows of Vraja(vrajān), mounted on carts with their possessions (pricchadāḥ), they departed.

### Texts 31-32

*vṛddhān bālān striyo rājan sarvopakaraṇāni ca*  
*anaḥsv āropya gopālā yattā ātta-śarāsanāḥ*

*godhanāni puraskṛtya śṛṅgāṇy āpūrya sarvataḥ*  
*tūrya-ghoṣeṇa mahatā yayuḥ saha-purohitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King Parīkṣit! Keeping all the old men, women, children and household paraphernalia on the bullock carts and keeping all the cows in front, the cowherd men, picking up their bows and arrows with great care and sounding horns, proceeded with the priests, with loud sounding instrumental music.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. They put the women and children on the carts. They were diligent (yattā). They held bows and arrows thinking, “If some wicked servants of Kaṁsa come. We will shoot them.” They blew (āpūrya) horns. They went with the sound ofdrums (tūrya-ghoṣeṇa), which accompany royalty. The sound was loud (mahatā) and entered Kaṁsa’s ears. This indicates they were fearless. They went with priests such as Bhāguri.

### Text 33

*gopyo rūḍha-rathā nūtna- kuca-kuṅkuma-kāntayaḥ*  
*kṛṣṇa-līlā jaguḥ prītyā niṣka-kaṇṭhyaḥ suvāsasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd women, riding on the bullock carts, were dressed very nicely with excellent garments, and their breasts were decorated with fresh kuṅkuma powder. As they rode, they began to chant with great pleasure the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The wives of the principal cowherds rode on the chariots. They were beautiful with fresh kuṅkuma on their breasts. They had locket (niṣka) on their necks as well as other ornaments. They wore fine, colorful cloth.

### Text 34

*tathā yaśodā-rohiṇyāv ekaṁ śakaṭam āsthite*  
*rejatuḥ kṛṣṇa-rāmābhyāṁ tat-kathā-śravaṇotsuke*

**Перевод:**

**Yaśodā and Rohiṇī on one bullock cart with Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, eager to hear Nanda speak, looked splendid.**

**Комментарий:**

The two were situated on one large chariot (cart) with their sons and servant girls since they could not bear separation from their sons. Śakaṭa means chariot according to Halāyudha. They looked splendid with Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. They were eager to hear Nanda’s talks or the boys’ talk.

### Text 35

*vṛndāvanaṁ sampraviśya sarva-kāla-sukhāvaham*  
*tatra cakrur vrajāvāsaṁ śakaṭair ardha-candravat*

**Перевод:**

**Entering Vṛndāvana, where it is always pleasing to live in all seasons, they made a temporary place to inhabit by placing their bullock carts around them in the shape of a half moon.**

**Комментарий:**

They entered Vṛndāvana easily crossing the Yamunā whose water was knee deep, similar to:

*mārgaṁ dadau sindhur iva śriyaḥ pateḥ*

**Yamunā gave way to Vasudeva and allowed him to cross. (SB** [**10.3.50**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.50)**)**

In Vṛndāvana, they made a camp from Govardhana to Kāliya-hrada. They formed a semi-circle with the carts, so that the goods could be kept in the back portion safely and on the front portion there was a wide entrance for the cows to exit comfortably. Viṣṇu Purāṇa also says the same:

*śakaṭī-vāṭa-paryantaś candrārdhākāra-saṁsthitiḥ*

**They lived in a semi-circle made of an enclosure of carts.**

This was their arrangement on the first day. But their arrangements on the next day are known from Hari-vaṁśa:

*kaṇṭakībhiḥ pravṛddhābhis tathā kaṇṭakibhir*  
*drumaiḥ -śākhābhir abhiguptam samantataḥ*

**The area was covered completely with thorny creepers, thorny trees, long branches fixed in the earth.**

They used creepers with thorns. The place of the cowherds was not too far from Mathurā indicating that there was not the slightest fear of Kaṁsa since they are described as follows in Hari-vaṁśa:

*mahābalāḥ khalu te ca bhavanto bhīma-vikramāḥ*

**All of you certainly have great prowess.**

When Keśī had fled out of fear of them, they were living in Nandīśvara.

The order of pastimes of killing Pūtanā, breaking the cart, the name giving ceremony, crawling on their knees, pulling the calves tails, destruction of Tṛṇāvarta, showing the universe in his mouth, dancing to the gopīs’ praise, buying fruit, eating dirt, showing theuniverse a second time, stealing yogurt, being tied up with ropes, being called from playing on the river bank, before coming to Vṛndāvana should be stated as the order of Bṛhadvana pastimes. The pastimes are related because they are suitable and famous.

### Text 36

*vṛndāvanaṁ govardhanaṁ yamunā-pulināni ca*  
*vīkṣyāsīd uttamā prītī rāma-mādhavayor nṛpa*

**Перевод:**

**O King Parīkṣit, when Rāma and Kṛṣṇa saw Vṛndāvana, Govardhana and the banks of the River Yamunā, they both enjoyed great pleasure.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Vṛndāvana, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, forms of complete bliss, since they are Parabrahman, became most blissful (uttamā prītiḥ). This was joy from their svarūpas. Govardhana king of mountains, full of jewels and minerals and the banks of the Yamunā were within Vṛndāvana. That forest is actually the body of the Lord according to Bṛhad-gautamīya-tantra:

*pañca-yojanam evāsti vanaṁ me deha-rūpakam*  
*kālindīyaṁ suṣumnākhyā paramāmṛta-vāhinī*

**This place, measuring five yojanas, is non-different from my body. The Yamunā, flowing with the sweetest nectar, is the suṣumnā(central nerve) of that body.**

### Text 37

*evaṁ vrajaukasāṁ prītiṁ yacchantau bāla-ceṣṭitaiḥ*  
*kala-vākyaiḥ sva-kālena vatsa-pālau babhūvatuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In this way, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, acting like small boys and talking in half-broken language, gave pleasure to all the inhabitants of Vraja. In due course of time, they became old enough to take care of the calves.**

**Комментарий:**

At a suitable time, in the middle of kaumāra period (sva-kālena), they took care of the calves.

### Text 38

*avidūre vraja-bhuvaḥ saha gopāla-dārakaiḥ*  
*cārayām āsatur vatsān nānā-krīḍā-paricchadau*

**Перевод:**

**Not far away from their residential quarters, both Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, equipped with all kinds of playthings, began to tend the calves with other cowherd boys.**

**Комментарий:**

They played neither too far away not too close since good grass was not available too far away and since they could not play freely too close to home. However, they played within calling distance. The two boys carried flutes, canes, horns, vīṇās and balls, and other objects useful for playing.

### Texts 39-40

*kvacid vādayato veṇuṁ kṣepaṇaiḥ kṣipataḥ kvacit*  
*kvacit pādaiḥ kiṅkiṇībhiḥ kvacit kṛtrima-go-vṛṣaiḥ*

*vṛṣāyamāṇau nardantau yuyudhāte parasparam*  
*anukṛtya rutair jantūṁś ceratuḥ prākṛtau yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma would play on their flutes. Sometimes they would throw bilva fruits using slings. Sometimes they danced making their ankle bells tinkle. Sometimes like bulls they roared loudly with the other boys disguised as cows and bulls and would fight with one another, roaring loudly, and sometimes they would imitate the voices of the animals. In this way they wandered about, exactly like two ordinary human children.**

**Комментарий:**

Showing their activities, their playing is described in two verses starting with verse 39. In some suitable place (kvacit) they threwbilva fruits far away using slings. They stomped the earth with their feet bound by ankle bells. They roared like bulls with the dew-laps fashioned out of blankets. They imitated the sounds of animals like the swan, peacock, and cuckoo. They became absorbed in this play since they were Svayam Bhagavān.

### Text 41

*kadācid yamunā-tīre vatsāṁś cārayatoḥ svakaiḥ*  
*vayasyaiḥ kṛṣṇa-balayor jighāṁsur daitya āgamat*

**Перевод:**

**One day while Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, along with their playmates, were tending the calves on the bank of the River Yamunā, another demon arrived there, desiring to kill them.**

**Комментарий:**

The demon, pained by their effulgence, came there taking the form of a calf.

### Text 42

*taṁ vatsa-rūpiṇaṁ vīkṣya vatsa-yūtha-gataṁ hariḥ*  
*darśayan baladevāya śanair mugdha ivāsadat*

**Перевод:**

**When the Lord saw that the demon had assumed the form of a calf and entered among the groups of other calves, he pointed this out to Baladeva and then slowly approached the demon, as if not knowing.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa indicated the demon by a sign. As if ignorant he came close. Otherwise the demon would flee.

### Text 43

*gṛhītvāpara-pādābhyāṁ saha-lāṅgūlam acyutaḥ*  
*bhrāmayitvā kapitthāgre prāhiṇod gata-jīvitam*  
*sa kapitthair mahā-kāyaḥ pātyamānaiḥ papāta ha*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa caught the demon by the hind legs and tail, twirled the demon’s whole body very strongly until the demon was dead, and threw him into the top of a kapittha tree. The huge demon fell down along with fruits from the tree.**

**Комментарий:**

He grabbed his tail along with his hind legs so that the demon could not disturb him. Kṛṣṇa did not deviate from giving himliberation (acyutaḥ). He threw him in the tree in such a way that his life departed (gata-jīvitaṁ) so that the kapittha fruits, which were useful for playing, would fall. The demon in calf form then assumed a huge body because in dying his real form became visible by the disappearance of his illusory power.

### Text 44

*taṁ vīkṣya vismitā bālāḥ śaśaṁsuḥ sādhu sādhv iti*  
*devāś ca parisantuṣṭā babhūvuḥ puṣpa-varṣiṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Upon seeing the dead body of the demon, all the cowherd boys exclaimed, “Very good, very good!” The devatās were pleased and showered flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

The boys were amazed at the huge size of the demon and how easily Kṛṣṇa killed him.

### Text 45

*tau vatsa-pālakau bhūtvā sarva-lokaika-pālakau*  
*saprātar-āśau go-vatsāṁś cārayantau viceratuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The two boys, though the chief protectors of all people, became protectors of the calves. After eating their breakfast they would herd the calves all day.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the two boys were the chief protectors (eka-pālakau) of all people, they became protectors of the calves. They carried theirbreakfast along with them (sa-prātar-āśau).

### Text 46

*svaṁ svaṁ vatsa-kulaṁ sarve pāyayiṣyanta ekadā*  
*gatvā jalāśayābhyāsaṁ pāyayitvā papur jalam*

**Перевод:**

**One day all the boys, including Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, each boy taking his own group of calves, brought the calves to a reservoir of water, desiring to allow them to drink. After the animals drank water, the boys drank water there also.**

**Комментарий:**

The pond was a huge water body east of Nandīśvara. Near that place was the dwelling place of Baka (baka-sthalam). The boys went near (abhyāsam) that body of water.

### Text 47

*te tatra dadṛśur bālā mahā-sattvam avasthitam*  
*tatrasur vajra-nirbhinnaṁ gireḥ śṛṅgam iva cyutam*

**Перевод:**

**Right by the reservoir, the boys saw a gigantic creature resembling the peak of Nandīśvara struck down by a thunderbolt. They became terrified of it.**

**Комментарий:**

The demon appeared like the summit of a Nandīśvara hill (gireḥ) which had toppled over, since it was white in color.

### Text 48

*sa vai bako nāma mahān asuro baka-rūpa-dhṛk*  
*āgatya sahasā kṛṣṇaṁ tīkṣṇa-tuṇḍo ’grasad balī*

**Перевод:**

**That great-bodied demon was named Bakāsura, with the body of a crane possessing a very sharp beak. Approaching, he immediately swallowed Kṛṣṇa.**

### Text 49

*kṛṣṇaṁ mahā-baka-grastaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmādayo ’rbhakāḥ*  
*babhūvur indriyāṇīva vinā prāṇaṁ vicetasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Balarāma and the other boys saw that Kṛṣṇa had been devoured by the gigantic crane, they fainted, becoming lifeless like senses without prāṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Though omniscient and though he could kill the demon, Balarāma fainted because of his affection as a brother by the reasoning of aniṣṭāśaṅkīnīva bandhu-hrḍayāni bhavanti: a relative or intimatefriend is always fearful of some injury to his beloved. (Abhijñāna- śakuntalā-nāṭaka) This will also be explained in relation tokidnapping Rukmiṇī.

### Text 50

*taṁ tālu-mūlaṁ pradahantam agnivad*  
*gopāla-sūnuṁ pitaraṁ jagad-guroḥ*  
*caccharda sadyo ’tiruṣākṣataṁ bakas*  
*tuṇḍena hantuṁ punar abhyapadyata*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, who was the father of Brahmā but who was the son of a cowherd man, became like fire, burning the root of the demon’s palate. The demon immediately disgorged him. When the demon saw that Kṛṣṇa, although having been swallowed, was unharmed, he immediately attacked Kṛṣṇa again with his sharp beak.**

**Комментарий:**

The demon spit Kṛṣṇa out. He was unharmed (akṣatam). The demon tried to kill him with his beak.

Kṛṣṇa burned his palate like fire. Though soft and cool as a blue lotus, Kṛṣṇa felt like fire or a thunderbolt due to the fault of the demon’s palate, just as sugar tastes bitter due to fault of tongue. But actually this was accomplished by his śakti of cruelty. Though Kṛṣṇa was the father of Brahmā (jagad-guroḥ) he was also the son of Nanda (gopāla-sūnuṁ).

### Text 51

*tam āpatantaṁ sa nigṛhya tuṇḍayor*  
*dorbhyāṁ bakaṁ kaṁsa-sakhaṁ satāṁ patiḥ*  
*paśyatsu bāleṣu dadāra līlayā*  
*mudāvaho vīraṇavad divaukasām*

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of the devotees, saw that the demon Bakāsura, the friend of Kaṁsa, was endeavoring to attack him, with his arms he captured the demon by the two halves of the beak, and in the presence of all the cowherd boys he very easily bifurcated the demon, just as a child splits a blade of vīraṇa grass. By thus killing the demon, Kṛṣṇa pleased the devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

Grabbing the two halves of his beak, he split the demon like a piece of vīraṇa grass (whose root is called uśīra). He gave joy to the devatās.

### Text 52

*tadā bakāriṁ sura-loka-vāsinaḥ*  
*samākiran nandana-mallikādibhiḥ*  
*samīḍire cānaka-śaṅkha-saṁstavais*  
*tad vīkṣya gopāla-sutā visismire*

**Перевод:**

**At that time, the devatās profusely showered jasmine flowers grown in Nandana garden upon Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Bakāsura. They praised him by sounding celestial kettledrums and conch- shells and by offering prayers. Seeing this, the cowherd boys were struck with wonder.**

**Комментарий:**

They showered flowers completely (sam-ākiran). They congratulated him through praises along with sounds of drums and conches.

### Text 53

*muktaṁ bakāsyād upalabhya bālakā*  
*rāmādayaḥ prāṇam ivendriyo gaṇaḥ*  
*sthānāgataṁ taṁ parirabhya nirvṛtāḥ*  
*prāṇīya vatsān vrajam etya taj jaguḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Just as the senses become active in the presence of prāṇa, when Kṛṣṇa was freed from this danger, all the boys, including Balarāma, embraced him when he approached them and became blissful. Then they collected their own calves and returned to Vraja, where they declared the incident loudly.**

**Комментарий:**

Just as the senses become calm on contacting the prāṇa, which was afflicted by a swoon and which has again come back to its place, seeing Kṛṣṇa free from the mouth of Baka and present in front of them, they embraced him and became blissful (nirvṛtāḥ). Bringing the calves from here and there, returning to Vraja they loudly sang his pastime of killing Baka.

### Text 54

*śrutvā tad vismitā gopā gopyaś cātipriyādṛtāḥ*  
*pretyāgatam ivotsukyād aikṣanta tṛṣitekṣaṇāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the cowherd men and women heard about the killing of Bakāsura in the forest, they were astonished and showed attention to him with great affection. With eyes ever unsatisfied, with attachment they looked upon Kṛṣṇa as if he had returned from death.**

**Комментарий:**

Respected (ādṛtāḥ) by dear Kṛṣṇa who gave them glance, glancing with thirst to receive his sweet glances (tṛṣitekṣaṇāḥ), the cowherd men and women looked at all his limbs fearing some injury.

### Text 55

*aho batāsya bālasya bahavo mṛtyavo ’bhavan*  
*apy āsīd vipriyaṁ teṣāṁ kṛtaṁ pūrvaṁ yato bhayam*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd men, headed by Nanda Mahārāja, began to contemplate: it is very astonishing that although this boy Kṛṣṇa has many times faced many varied causes of death. Those causes of death were killed, since they had first caused Kṛṣṇa fear.**

**Комментарий:**

The child has had many causes of death (mṛtyavaḥ). Because they at first (pūrvaṁ) committed offense (bhayam), they died (vipriyam).

### Text 56

*athāpy abhibhavanty enaṁ naiva te ghora-darśanāḥ*  
*jighāṁsayainam āsādya naśyanty agnau pataṅgavat*

**Перевод:**

**Although the causes of death were very fierce, they could not even injure this boy Kṛṣṇa. Rather, as soon as they approached to kill him, they themselves were killed, exactly like moths entering a fire.**

### Text 57

*aho brahma-vidāṁ vāco nāsatyāḥ santi karhicit*  
*gargo yad āha bhagavān anvabhāvi tathaiva tat*

**Перевод:**

**The words of persons in full knowledge of Brahman never become untrue. It is very wonderful that whatever Gargamuni predicted we are now actually experiencing in all detail.**

**Комментарий:**

How is this possible? It is because he is the Supreme Lord. This was proved by Garga’s words. Nanda revealed Garga’s words, though spoken privately, a little since he was simple and friendly with the cowherds.

### Text 58

*iti nandādayo gopāḥ kṛṣṇa-rāma-kathāṁ mudā*  
*kurvanto ramamāṇāś ca nāvindan bhava-vedanām*

**Перевод:**

**In this way all the cowherd men, headed by Nanda Mahārāja, enjoyed topics about the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma and played with them. They did not recognize even Śiva.**

**Комментарий:**

Among themselves, they discussed about Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, their childhood fickleness and killing of Pūtanā, etc. They did not recognize (vedanām) even Śiva (bhava) who came to see Kṛṣṇa then. Absorbed in playing with Kṛṣṇa (ramamāṇāḥ), they were noteven aware of Śiva’s arrival. Vedanā means knowledge and pain according to Medinī. Yaśodā and others had the same mentality.One should not think that nāvindan bhava-vedanām means “they did not experience the pains of saṁsāra” since they had no contactwith saṁsāra.

*tāsām avirataṁ kṛṣṇe kurvatīnāṁ sutekṣaṇam*  
*na punaḥ kalpate rājan saṁsāro ‘jñāna-sambhavaḥ*

**O King! Because of their relationship as mother and son, although the gopīs were engaged in various family activities, they certainly never experienced saṁsāra caused by ignorance. (SB** [**10.6.40**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/6.40)**)**

### Text 59

*evaṁ vihāraiḥ kaumāraiḥ kaumāraṁ jahatur vraje*  
*nilāyanaiḥ setu-bandhair markaṭotplavanādibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In this way Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma passed their childhood age in Vraja by engaging in activities of childish play, such as playing hide-and-seek, constructing a make-believe bridge on the ocean, and jumping here and there like monkeys.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way they withdrew their kaumāra pastimes (jahatuḥ).

## Chapter 12 - The Killing of the Demon Aghāsura

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*kvacid vanāśāya mano dadhad vrajāt*  
*prātaḥ samutthāya vayasya-vatsapān*  
*prabodhayañ chṛṅga-raveṇa cāruṇā*  
*vinirgato vatsa-puraḥsaro hariḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: O King, one day Kṛṣṇa decided to take his breakfast as a picnic in the forest. Having risen early in the morning, he blew his horn and woke all the cowherd boys and calves with its beautiful sound. Then Kṛṣṇa and the boys, keeping their respective groups of calves before them, proceeded from Vraja to the forest.**

**Комментарий:**

*dvādaśe śiśubhiḥ kelir aghāsye viśato ‘nu tān \|*  
*praviśyānandayat kṛṣṇo hatvāghaṁ tam amocayat*

**In the twelfth chapter, Kṛṣṇa plays with the young boys, enters Agha’s mouth following the boys and gives pleasure to the boys, and killing Agha, liberates him.**

Though having concluded the kaumāra pastimes in the last verse of the previous chapter, Śukadva begins to speak in three chapterson remembering those extraordinary kaumāra pastimes, desired by Parīkṣit.

One day Kṛṣṇa decided to eat his breakfast in the forest (vanāśāya). But Balarāma did not go that day since his mother kept him home for the sake of ritual bathing and giving charity because it was his birth constellation.

### Text 2

*tenaiva sākaṁ pṛthukāḥ sahasraśaḥ*  
*snigdhāḥ suśig-vetra-viṣāṇa-veṇavaḥ*  
*svān svān sahasropari-saṅkhyayānvitān*  
*vatsān puraskṛtya viniryayur mudā*

**Перевод:**

**At that time, hundreds and thousands of cowherd boys came out of their respective homes in Vraja and joined Kṛṣṇa, keeping before them their hundreds and thousands of groups of calves. The boys were very beautiful, and they were equipped with lunch bags, bugles, flutes, and sticks for controlling the calves.**

**Комментарий:**

Pṛthukāḥ means small boys. Śik is the sack for holding the meal. There were thousands of calves.

### Text 3

*kṛṣṇa-vatsair asaṅkhyātair yūthī-kṛtya sva-vatsakān*  
*cārayanto ’rbha-līlābhir vijahrus tatra tatra ha*

**Перевод:**

**Along with Kṛṣṇa’s asaṅkhya of calves, they each put their calves in groups and, while herding them, sported in the forest in a playful spirit.**

**Комментарий:**

They merged their own calves with Kṛṣṇa’s unlimited calves and herded them. “But how did unlimited number of calves fit in limited Vṛndāvana?” It is possible by the powers of the acintya- śakti of Vṛndāvana like that of the Lord’s form.

### Text 4

*phala-prabāla-stavaka-sumanaḥ-piccha-dhātubhiḥ*  
*kāca-guñjā-maṇi-svarṇa-bhūṣitā apy abhūṣayan*

**Перевод:**

**Although all these boys were already decorated by their mothers with ornaments of crystal, guñja berries, gems and gold, they further decorated themselves with fruits, green leaves, flower clusters, single flowers, peacock feathers and soft minerals.**

**Комментарий:**

Though decorated by their mothers with crystal, etc., the boys decorated themselves with fruits, etc. Ornaments made of crystal and guṇja were used at the insistence of the boys. But by their mothers’ insistence they wore gems and gold.

### Text 5

*muṣṇanto ’nyonya-śikyādīn jñātān ārāc ca cikṣipuḥ*  
*tatratyāś ca punar dūrād dhasantaś ca punar daduḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All the cowherd boys used to steal one another’s ropes, sticks and other items. When a boy came to understand that his bag had been taken away, the other boys would throw it farther away, to a more distant place, and those standing there would throw it still farther. When the proprietor of the bag became disappointed, the other boys would laugh and return the items.**

**Комментарий:**

Their play is described. Understanding that their ropes and bags had been stolen, covered with creepers somewhere, other boys would throw them further away. Running after it to take it, other boys would throw it further away. Seeing the boys were depressed, laughing, they gave bags back to them.

### Text 6

*yadi dūraṁ gataḥ kṛṣṇo vana-śobhekṣaṇāya tam*  
*ahaṁ pūrvam ahaṁ pūrvam iti saṁspṛśya remire*

**Перевод:**

**If Kṛṣṇa went to a somewhat distant place to see the beauty of the forest, all the other boys would run to accompany him, each one saying, “I shall be the first to run and touch Kṛṣṇa! I shall touch Kṛṣṇa first!” In this way they obtained joy.**

**Комментарий:**

When Kṛṣṇa went faw away, then they would shout, “I touched him first, not you,” in this way, touching him, they played.

### Texts 7-10

*kecid veṇūn vādayanto dhmāntaḥ śṛṅgāṇi kecana*  
*kecid bhṛṅgaiḥ pragāyantaḥ kūjantaḥ kokilaiḥ pare*

*vi-cchāyābhiḥ pradhāvanto gacchantaḥ sādhu haṁsakaiḥ*  
*bakair upaviśantaś ca nṛtyantaś ca kalāpibhiḥ*

*vikarṣantaḥ kīśa-bālān ārohantaś ca tair drumān*  
*vikurvantaś ca taiḥ sākaṁ plavantaś ca palāśiṣu*

*sākaṁ bhekair vilaṅghantaḥ saritaḥ srava-samplutāḥ*  
*vihasantaḥ praticchāyāḥ śapantaś ca pratisvanān*

**Перевод:**

**Some boys blew their flutes, and others blew bugles made of horn. Some imitated the buzzing of the bumblebees, and others imitated the voice of the cuckoo. Some boys ran with the shadows of birds, some imitated the beautiful movements of the swans, some sat down with the ducks, and others imitated the dancing of the peacocks. Some boys attracted young monkeys in the trees, some climbed the trees with them, and made faces like the young monkeys, and others jumped from the trees. Some boys jumped over the rivers filled with flowing water from waterfalls with the frogs, and when they saw their own reflections on the water they would laugh. They would also condemn the sounds of their own echoes.**

**Комментарий:**

Four verses describe their fun. Some would blow (dhmāntaḥ) horns. Some would sing along with the bees and cuckoos. Some boys ran with the shadows of birds (vicchāyābhiḥ). Some danced with the peacocks (kalāpibhiḥ). Some pulled the tails of young monkeys hanging in branches of trees. Some climbed trees by holding those tails firmly. Some distorted their faces, moving their brows and yawning, with the young monkeys. Some jumped from branch to branch of the trees. With frogs some jumped over small streams filled by waterfalls from the mountains. Some laughed at their reflections and some cursed their echoes. They shouted, “Who are you? You are imitating us. Thus you should die!”

### Text 11

*itthaṁ satāṁ brahma-sukhānubhūtyā*  
*dāsyaṁ gatānāṁ para-daivatena*  
*māyāśritānāṁ nara-dārakeṇa*  
*sākaṁ vijahruḥ kṛta-puṇya-puñjāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In this way with an abundance of splendor caused by Kṛṣṇa, they played with him, who was pure consciousness known as Brahman for the jñānīs, who was the Supreme Lord for the devotees with dāsya-bhāva and who was an ordinary human child for those covered by material illusion.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described their play, he praises them with hairs standing on end.

These boys played with the Lord in this way (ittham). The Lord is described. He is Brahman as the form of an experience ofhappiness for jñānīs (satām). He is the Supreme Lord, by being full of all powers, for the dāsya-bhaktas such as Brahmā. He appears as a material human child for karmīs, serving material happiness (māyāśritānāṁ).

He appears as a great substance full of knowledge and bliss like the ocean without waves for the jñānīs in samādhi. But persons withdāsya-bhāva worship him by respecting him. Jñāna and bhakti are considered different like an unblinking stare and a brief glance. But karmīs because of lacking both samādhi and dāsya-bhakti, do not have those two experiences. Though the boys were playing withthe Lord who was the rarest, highest puruṣārtha, they were filled with sakhya. Thus who can describe their good fortune? By the instrumental case in the meaning of ‘with’ it is shown that they were the main persons in playing with the Lord, who was controlledby their prema. The boys are described. They were accomplished (kṛtaḥ) by piles of attractive (puṇya) wealth such as being devoted to him. Puṇya means attractive according to Amara-kośa.

### Text 12

*yat-pāda-pāṁsur bahu-janma-kṛcchrato*  
*dhṛtātmabhir yogibhir apy alabhyaḥ*  
*sa eva yad-dṛg-viṣayaḥ svayaṁ sthitaḥ*  
*kiṁ varṇyate diṣṭam ato vrajaukasām*

**Перевод:**

**Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, whose foot dust cannot be seen by yogīs, who have focussed minds, though they have controlled their mind by severe hardship for many births, is eternally situated here, directly visible to the eyes of the people of Vraja. Ah! How can the good fortune of the people of Vraja be described?**

**Комментарий:**

What to speak of the friends’ good fortune, how can one describe the good fortune of all the inhabitants of Vraja? One particle of dust from Kṛṣṇa’s feet or one ray (amśuḥ) from the trees of his abode (pādapa) cannot be attained even by yogīs who have one- pointed minds (dhṛtāmabhiḥ) since it was previously said:

*nāyaṁ sukhāpo bhagavān dehināṁ gopikā-sutaḥ*  
*jñānināṁ cātma-bhūtānāṁ yathā bhaktimatām iha*

**The Lord, son of Yaśodā, is not easily available to materialists or to jñānīs with realization of ātmā, but is easily available to persons with devotion to the son of Yaśodā. (SB** [**10.9.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/9.21)**)**

He is situated directly as the object of vision of the people of Vraja, diregarding the method of seeing him.

O King Parīkṣit (aho)! Can the good fortune of the people of Vraja be described? They are the eternal associates of Kṛṣṇa. In this way he quells the curiosity which arose from the question, “What did Nanda do to attain such good fortune?” (SB [10.8.46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.46))

### Text 13

*athāgha-nāmābhyapatan mahāsuras*  
*teṣāṁ sukha-krīḍana-vīkṣaṇākṣamaḥ*  
*nityaṁ yad-antar nija-jīvitepsubhiḥ*  
*pītāmṛtair apy amaraiḥ pratīkṣyate*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, the great demon named Aghāsura suddenly approached, unable to tolerate seeing the joyful sporting of the boys. The devatās desired his death, though they were deathless from drinking nectar, since they feared him and desired to live long lives to see Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

Another pastime is related. Atha indicates a different subject. The huge demon called Agha arrived in front of them. Having arrived he was intolerant on seeing the boys’ happily playing.

The method of his death (yad antar) was awaited even by the devatās, who thought, “How will he die?” Though they had drunkamṛta they desired to live since were afraid of dying.

Or the happy playing of the boys was meditated on (pratīkṣyate) by the devatās. They had drunk those pastimes (pītāmṛtaiḥ). Drinking the nectar of his pastimes is the giver of life without amṛta or giver of life without death. Thus, they desired to live for seeing the pastimes.

### Text 14

*dṛṣṭvārbhakān kṛṣṇa-mukhān aghāsuraḥ*  
*kaṁsānuśiṣṭaḥ sa bakī-bakānujaḥ*  
*ayaṁ tu me sodara-nāśa-kṛt tayor*  
*dvayor mamainaṁ sa-balaṁ haniṣye*

**Перевод:**

**Aghāsura, who had been sent by Kaṁsa, was the younger brother of Pūtanā and Bakāsura. Therefore when he came and saw Kṛṣṇa at the head of all the cowherd boys, he thought, “This Kṛṣṇa has killed my sister and brother, Pūtanā and Bakāsura. Therefore, in order to please them both, I shall kill this Kṛṣṇa, along with the other cowherd boys.”**

**Комментарий:**

He saw the boys headed by Kṛṣṇa. He had decided to lie on the path to swallow them. This is understood from verse 16. Bakī meansPūtanā. His intention is described. “This Kṛṣṇa killed my brother and sister, Baka and Pūtanā. I will kill him along with his followers in order to offer sesame and water (as funeral rites) to them both.”

### Text 15

*ete yadā mat-suhṛdos tilāpaḥ*  
*kṛtās tadā naṣṭa-samā vrajaukasaḥ*  
*prāṇe gate varṣmasu kā nu cintā*  
*prajāsavaḥ prāṇa-bhṛto hi ye te*

**Перевод:**

**Aghāsura thought: If somehow or other I can make Kṛṣṇa and his associates serve as the last offering of sesame and water for the departed souls of my brother and sister, then the inhabitants of Vraja will be as if dead, for person who take their sons are their life and soul will not care for their bodies when their children die.**

**Комментарий:**

“What is the use of killing them if Nanda and the others of Vraja are living?” When this sesame and water offering is made for my brother and sister the people of Vraja will be as if dead. When thelife-airs have disappeared (gate) even if they are situated in bodies (varṣmasu) what is the worry? Nothing to worry. How is this accomplished? Since (hi) for living beings (prāṇa-bhṛtaḥ) sons are their very life (prajāsavaḥ).

### Text 16

*iti vyavasyājagaraṁ bṛhad vapuḥ*  
*sa yojanāyāma-mahādri-pīvaram*  
*dhṛtvādbhutaṁ vyātta-guhānanaṁ tadā*  
*pathi vyaśeta grasanāśayā khalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After thus deciding, that crooked Aghāsura, assumed the remarkable form of a python, huge like a mountain, eight miles long, with his mouth gaping like a cave, and lay motionless on the path, with the desire to swallow the boys.**

**Комментарий:**

Deciding thus (vyavasya), assuming the huge body of a python, massive like a mountain, measuring a yojana and spread out (vyātta), with a mouth like a cavern, the demon lay on the road.

### Text 17

*dharādharoṣṭho jaladottaroṣṭho*  
*dary-ānanānto giri-śṛṅga-daṁṣṭraḥ*  
*dhvāntāntar-āsyo vitatādhva-jihvaḥ*  
*paruṣānila-śvāsa-davekṣaṇoṣṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**His lower lip rested on the surface of the earth, and his upper lip was touching the clouds in the sky. The corners of his mouth resembled caves and his teeth were like mountain peaks. The depth of his mouth was dark. His tongue resembled a broad road, his breath was a hot, a harsh wind, and his hot eyes blazed like fire.**

**Комментарий:**

His lower lip was on the ground and his upper lip was in the clouds. The sides of his mouth were like caves. The interior of his mouth was dark. His tongue was a wide road. His breath was like harsh fire. The heat of his glance was like a forest fire.

### Text 18

*dṛṣṭvā taṁ tādṛśaṁ sarve matvā vṛndāvana-śriyam*  
*vyāttājagara-tuṇḍena hy utprekṣante sma līlayā*

**Перевод:**

**Upon seeing this demon which resembled a great python, the boys thought that it must be a beautiful feature of Vṛndāvana, comparing it to a gaping python’s mouth as a joke.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Agha with that form, some were agitated, understanding it was a huge snake and others, reassuring them, thinking it to be the beauty of Vṛndāvana, “Such a snake cannot exist. Thus this is some object made by the Supreme Lord for sake of the beauty of the forest,” compared it to an open mouth of a snake plafully. They were without fear (līlayā).

### Text 19

*aho mitrāṇi gadata sattva-kūṭaṁ puraḥ sthitam*  
*asmat-saṅgrasana-vyātta-vyāla-tuṇḍāyate na vā*

**Перевод:**

**The boys said: Dear friends, tell us whether this is some immobile creature in front of us, whose front portion is the gaping mouth of a python ready to swallow us.**

**Комментарий:**

Some boys asked others for proof of their idea. O friends! You please say if this is some immovable creature (sattva-kūṭam) in front of us, which acts like a wide open mouth of snake to swallow us. Kūṭa means immovable according to Medinī. Placing the words in reverse order (in sattva-kūṭam) is poetic license.

### Text 20

*satyam arka-karāraktam uttarā-hanuvad ghanam*  
*adharā-hanuvad rodhas tat-praticchāyayāruṇam*

**Перевод:**

**Others said: You speak the truth. A cloud lit by the morning sun is like a snake’s upper lip. The mountain slope made red by the reflection from the cloud is like its lower lip.**

**Комментарий:**

Others accepted their opinion. This is true. Hanu is used for upper and lower lip since the meaning of uttarā (upper) and adhara(lower) cannot be applied for chin. See! A cloud reddened by the rays of the sun is the upper lip. See! The slope made red by the shadow of the cloud is the lower lip.

### Text 21

*pratispardhete sṛkkabhyāṁ savyāsavye nagodare*  
*tuṅga-śṛṅgālayo ’py etās tad-daṁṣṭrābhiś ca paśyata*

**Перевод:**

**The caves on the left and right side compete with the sides of a snake’s mouth, and the high mountain peaks complete with a snake’s teeth. Look!**

**Комментарий:**

The left and right of the mountain caves compete with (are similar to) the edges of snake’s mouth. High mountain peaks are competing with the teeth of a python. See!

### Text 22

*āstṛtāyāma-mārgo ’yaṁ rasanāṁ pratigarjati*  
*eṣāṁ antar-gataṁ dhvāntam etad apy antar-ānanam*

**Перевод:**

**This long, broad road is like a snake’s tongue and the darkness in the cave is like the blackness inside a snake’s mouth.**

**Комментарий:**

This long wide road, saying (pratigarjati), “I am like you,” is like the tongue of a snake. The darkness between the peaks is like the interior of a snake’s mouth.

### Text 23

*dāvoṣṇa-khara-vāto ’yaṁ śvāsavad bhāti paśyata*  
*tad-dagdha-sattva-durgandho ’py antar-āmiṣa-gandhavat*

**Перевод:**

**This hot, harsh wind, like fire, resembles a snake’s breath. See! The odor of a burned animal is like the odor of flesh in a snake’s stomach.**

**Комментарий:**

The rough fiery wind is like a snake’ breathing. The foul odor of animals by a forest fire are like the odor from meat inside a snake.

### Text 24

*asmān kim atra grasitā niviṣṭān*  
*ayaṁ tathā ced bakavad vinaṅkṣyati*  
*kṣaṇād aneneti bakāry-uśan-mukhaṁ*  
*vīkṣyoddhasantaḥ kara-tāḍanair yayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then the boys said, “Has this living creature come to swallow us if we enter it? If he does so, he will immediately be killed like Bakāsura by Kṛṣṇa, without delay.” Thus they looked at the beautiful face of Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Bakāsura, and, laughing loudly and clapping their hands, they ran towards the snake.**

**Комментарий:**

Together they all spoke, somewhat afraid. Actually, it must be a snake. To that others said, “If that is so it will be destroyed like Baka by Kṛṣṇa in an instant.” Saying this they looked at the beautiful face of Kṛṣṇa (bakāri) situated far away. What is there to worry about, when we are the object of his glance? “What is inside the hole? Should we not see?” they laughed. They clapped their hands, showing fearlessness and bravery, and ran. The calves ran after them with their tails raised.

### Text 25

*itthaṁ mitho ’tathyam ataj-jña-bhāṣitaṁ*  
*śrutvā vicintyety amṛṣā mṛṣāyate*  
*rakṣo viditvākhila-bhūta-hṛt-sthitaḥ*  
*svānāṁ niroddhuṁ bhagavān mano dadhe*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, full of all powers, who is situated as antaryāmi in the core of everyone’s heart, heard the boys talking falsely among themselves like ignorant people. Though it is truly a snake they think it is an object beautifying Vraja. Knowing moreover that it was a Rākṣasa, he wanted to prevent them from entering the demon’s mouth.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing the false (atathyam) words of the ignorant (atad-jñā) boys, the Lord considered, “It is true (amṛṣā) that this is a snake’s body but they think it is not a snake but a beautiful sight of Vṛndāvana.” Considering that it appears to be something else, but not just that he understood that it was a Rākṣasa because he is situated in everyone’s heart as omniscient Lord. By the time he decided to prevent them (svānām) from entering, by that time they entered (next verse).

### Text 26

*tāvat praviṣṭās tv asurodarāntaraṁ*  
*paraṁ na gīrṇāḥ śiśavaḥ sa-vatsāḥ*  
*pratīkṣamāṇena bakāri-veśanaṁ*  
*hata-sva-kānta-smaraṇena rakṣasā*

**Перевод:**

**The moment he desired to stop them, all the cowherd boys along with the calves entered the stomach of the demon. The demon, however, did not swallow them, for he was thinking of his relatives who had been killed by Kṛṣṇa and was just waiting for Kṛṣṇa to enter his mouth.**

**Комментарий:**

They entered but were not swallowed by the Rakṣasa, who was waiting for Kṛṣṇa’s entrance. Why?

The demon remembered his brother and sister killed by him. Even though the boys, were omniscient since they were the Lord’s associates, to accomplish pastimes the līlā-śakti covered their omniscience. The Lord determination to prevent them when the devotees determined, “Nothing will happen if we are swallowed when we enter.” (SB 10.12.24) was checked since their determination was stronger.

### Text 27

*tān vīkṣya kṛṣṇaḥ sakalābhaya-prado*  
*hy ananya-nāthān sva-karād avacyutān*  
*dīnāṁś ca mṛtyor jaṭharāgni-ghāsān*  
*ghṛṇārdito diṣṭa-kṛtena vismitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, giver of fearlessness to all beings, saw that all the cowherd boys, who did not know anyone but him as their shelter, had now escaped from his hand and were helpless. They were now suffering, like straws to be burned by the fire of the abdomen of Aghāsura, who was death personified. Bewildered by his affection, he was astonished by what had been arranged by his appointed śakti.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the boys about to fall like a fistful of grass (ghāsān) in the fire of Agha’s (mṛtyoḥ) stomach, escaping his hand like great gems, pained by compassion (ghṛṇārditaḥ), he was surprised by their actions of entering Agha (diṣṭa-kṛtena). Diṣṭa means time according to Amara-kośa. Time which follows after the pastimes (diṣṭa) had arranged this. How astonishing is the power of my līlā-śakti that knowing me as the form of rasa, makes me experience karuṇa-rasa, and leads even my friends into the snake’s stomach and even acts opposite to my decision. Thus he became astonished. They had no pain when they entered the stomach of Agha since they became blissful by seeing Kṛṣṇa’s beautiful face (according to verse 24). Their suffering (dīnān) was only an appearance, a likeness.

### Text 28

*kṛtyaṁ kim atrāsya khalasya jīvanaṁ*  
*na vā amīṣāṁ ca satāṁ vihiṁsanam*  
*dvayaṁ kathaṁ syād iti saṁvicintya*  
*jñātvāviśat tuṇḍam aśeṣa-dṛg ghariḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Now, what was to be done? The rascal demon should not live and the boys should not die. How to do both simultaneously? Thinking about this and understanding the solution, the attractive Lord who saw the perfect method entered the mouth of Aghāsura.**

**Комментарий:**

What should it do in this difficult situation? The demon should not live. My friends should not be harmed. How should I accomplish both? Thinking in this way, understanding the means, he himself entered the mouth of the snake since he sees everything in thefuture (aśeṣa-dṛk) — when this has happened this should be done. He is Hari since he takes away the dangers of the devotees and the life and ignorance of the wicked. Though he is omniscient, he thought of a method since he acts like a person of this world. This incident ends with the bewilderment of the demon.

### Text 29

*tadā ghana-cchadā devā bhayād dhā-heti cukruśuḥ*  
*jahṛṣur ye ca kaṁsādyāḥ kauṇapās tv agha-bāndhavāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa entered the mouth of Aghāsura, the devatās hiding behind the clouds exclaimed, “Alas! Alas!” But the friends of Aghāsura, like Kaṁsa and Rākṣasas, were jubilant.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the devatās knew of his powers, having attained affection for the Lord, out of worry about dangers to him which arose from their affectionate nature, they shouted, ‘Alas!’ They were hidden by clouds (ghana-cchedāḥ), out of fear of Kaṁsa and Agha. The Rākṣasas (kauṇapāḥ), Kaṁsa and friends of Agha rejoiced, having heard the news through spies.

### Text 30

*tac chrutvā bhagavān kṛṣṇas tv avyayaḥ sārbha-vatsakam*  
*cūrṇī-cikīrṣor ātmānaṁ tarasā vavṛdhe gale*

**Перевод:**

**When the Lord, full of all powers which do not decrease, who is attracted to his devotees, heard the devatās crying, “Alas! Alas!” he immediately expanded himself within the throat of the demon, who wished to crush Kṛṣṇa, the boys and calves.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing the lamentation of the devatās and the rejoicing of Kaṁsa and others, he quickly expanded himself in the throat of Agha who desired to crush him along with the calves and boys, in order to hear the opposite from the devatās and demons. He expanded himself in the snake’s throat because in that place those who witness his sweet pastimes could not see.

### Text 31

*tato ’tikāyasya niruddha-mārgiṇo*  
*hy udgīrṇa-dṛṣṭer bhramatas tv itas tataḥ*  
*pūrṇo ’ntar-aṅge pavano niruddho*  
*mūrdhan vinirbhidya vinirgato bahiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then, because Kṛṣṇa had increased the size of his body, the demon suffocated. The demon became bewildered, his eyes popped out, and with body swelling up because of the life air being blocked, his life air pierced his head at the brahma-randhra and left his body.**

**Комментарий:**

His throat, the path to the mouth, became blocked. His eyes popped out (udgīrṇa). The prāṇa within his body (antaraṅge) became blocked and with no way of leaving, becoming full (pūrṇaḥ), it pierced his head and left.

### Text 32

*tenaiva sarveṣu bahir gateṣu*  
*prāṇeṣu vatsān suhṛdaḥ paretān*  
*dṛṣṭyā svayotthāpya tad-anvitaḥ punar*  
*vaktrān mukundo bhagavān viniryayau*

**Перевод:**

**When all the demon’s life airs had passed away through that hole in the top of his head, Kṛṣṇa glanced over the seemly dead calves and cowherd boys and brought them back to consciousness. Then Mukunda, full of all powers, came out from the demon’s mouth followed by his friends and the calves.**

**Комментарий:**

When his senses left with life airs, he revived by his sweet glance his friends and calves who had entered the snake’s stomach andwho had almost fainted (paretān) by the fire of separation and the fire of his stomach. The rest is clear.

### Text 33

*pīnāhi-bhogotthitam adbhutaṁ mahaj*  
*jyotiḥ sva-dhāmnā jvalayad diśo daśa*  
*pratīkṣya khe ’vasthitam īśa-nirgamaṁ*  
*viveśa tasmin miṣatāṁ divaukasām*

**Перевод:**

**From the body of the gigantic python, a glaring effulgence emerged, illuminating all directions, and remained in the sky, waiting until Kṛṣṇa came out of the corpse’s mouth. Then, as all the devatās looked on, this effulgence entered into Kṛṣṇa’s body.**

**Комментарий:**

Agha was liberated. A great light which arose from the body of the fat snake waited for Kṛṣṇa to come out (īśa-nirgamanam) and was situated in the sky. When the Lord came out, it entered him (tasmin). Having attained sārūpya, he stood near the Lord. Later it is said prāpātma-sāmya: he attained sārūpya (verse 38). The reason he attained sārūpya is that Kṛṣṇa entered his stomach and killed him.

The vision of that form of condensed knowledge of the light, was to announce to people the principle of the Lord giving those he kills an auspicious goal (hatāri-gati-dāyaka) which is nirguṇa. It manifested by the will of the Lord like his beautiful form. Otherwise this light would also not be seen. The devatās looked on. This is in the genitive case to indicate that they were not important.

### Text 34

*tato ’tihṛṣṭāḥ sva-kṛto ’kṛtārhaṇaṁ*  
*puṣpaiḥ sugā apsarasaś ca nartanaiḥ*  
*gītaiḥ surā vādya-dharāś ca vādyakaiḥ*  
*stavaiś ca viprā jaya-niḥsvanair gaṇāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After Kṛṣṇa emerged from the snake, in great jubilation they all worshipped Kṛṣṇa, their creator. The devatās began to shower flowers, the Apsarās began to dance, the Gandharvas offered songs, the Vidyādhāras played instruments, the brāhmaṇas such as sapta-rṣis offered Vedic hymns, and associates of the Lord uttered “Jaya!”**

**Комментарий:**

Then the devatās, overjoyed, worshiped (arhanam akṛta) their creator, the son of Nanda (svakṛtaḥ). Gandharvas (sugā), Vdiyādharas (vādyadharā), the seven sages (viprāḥ) and Garudā, etc., (gaṇā) also worshipped him.

### Text 35

*tad-adbhuta-stotra-suvādya-gītikā-*  
*jayādi-naikotsava-maṅgala-svanān*  
*śrutvā sva-dhāmno ’nty aja āgato ’cirād*  
*dṛṣṭvā mahīśasya jagāma vismayam*

**Перевод:**

**When Lord Brahmā heard the festive, auspicious sounds of amazing verses, music, songs and sounds of “Jaya! Jaya!” he immediately left his abode and approached Kṛṣṇa. Seeing the power of Kṛṣṇa to liberate the demon, he was completely astonished.**

**Комментарий:**

He heard auspicious sounds--the astonishing praises, the fine music, the soft songs, festive shouts of Jaya, near Satyaloka. This indicates that Maharloka and other higher planets were filled with sounds of praises. Then Brahmā (ajaḥ) understood (dṛṣṭvā) the greatness (mahi) of the Lord in giving sārūpya to Agha. Coming to Vṛndāvana quickly, he became astonished.

### Text 36

*rājann ājagaraṁ carma śuṣkaṁ vṛndāvane ’dbhutam*  
*vrajaukasāṁ bahu-tithaṁ babhūvākrīḍa-gahvaram*

**Перевод:**

**O King Parīkṣit, when the python-shaped body of Aghāsura dried up, becoming merely a big skin, it astonished the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana and became a cave for the boys’ sporting for many days.**

**Комментарий:**

For many days (bahu-titham) the body became a cave for extensive (ā) playing (krīḍā). By the touch of the Lord it became a silver mountain.

### Text 37

*etat kaumārajaṁ karma harer ātmāhi-mokṣaṇam*  
*mṛtyoḥ paugaṇḍake bālā dṛṣṭvocur vismitā vraje*

**Перевод:**

**Though the boys saw the liberation of the soul from Agha during Kṛṣṇa’s kaumāra period they spoke about it in Vraja at the beginning of Kṛṣṇa’s paugaṇḍa period with great astonishment.**

**Комментарий:**

Hear about another astonishing fact. The boys naratted this action, which was performed in the fifth year of Kṛṣṇa, in the sixth year in Vraja that “this occurred today”. What was the action? It was our (ātmanām) liberation from the snake (ahi) because of his death(mṛtyoḥ).

*kaumāraṁ pañcamābdāntaṁ paugaṇḍaṁ daśamāvadhi*  
*ā śoḍaśāc ca kaiśoraṁ yauvanaṁ syāt tataḥ param*

**Kaumāra lasts till five years, paugaṇḍa lasts till ten years and kaiśora lasts till sixteen years. Yauvana is after that. (BRS** [**2.1.309**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/2.1.309)**)**

### Text 38

*naitad vicitraṁ manujārbha-māyinaḥ*  
*parāvarāṇāṁ paramasya vedhasaḥ*  
*agho ’pi yat-sparśana-dhauta-pātakaḥ*  
*prāpātma-sāmyaṁ tv asatāṁ sudurlabham*

**Перевод:**

**This was not astonishing for the Lord who was supreme among all lower and higher beings, since he was the creator and mercifully appeared as the son of Nanda. Agha attained similarity to the Lord, generally unobtainable by a sinful person, because he was purified of his sin by the touch of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

This is not astonishing for Kṛṣṇa, who has a human form (manujārbha) and is full of mercy (māyinaḥ), who is Svayam Bhagavān (paramasya) for lower and higher beings, who is the creator by his sweet will (vedhasaḥ). What was this (which was not astonishing)? Agha, by Kṛṣṇa’s touch, became purified of sin and even his subtle body (i.e. even the sinful desire and ignorance) and then attained a form similar to the Lord’s (ātmā-sāmyam) which is rare for the demons, but they do attain liberation in the form ofdestruction of the subtle body.

### Text 39

*sakṛd yad-aṅga-pratimāntar-āhitā*  
*manomayī bhāgavatīṁ dadau gatim*  
*sa eva nityātma-sukhānubhūty-abhi-*  
*vyudasta-māyo ’ntar-gato hi kiṁ punaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**If even only once or even by force one brings the form of the Lord into one’s mind, Kṛṣṇa awards himself as the goal. Residing within, he gives the jīvas the experience of bliss by destroying all māyā completely. What more can be said?**

**Комментарий:**

The reason for attaining sārūpya is explained. The form of the Lord or even his deity such as Śrī Raṅga or Jagannātha, concentratedon with the mind (manomayī), even one time, gives a goal related to the Lord to persons without offense like Khaṭvāṅga. He, Svayam Bhagavān, who has an eternal form (nityātmā), and is the experience of bliss (sukhānubhūti) and who destroys māyā, haspersonally entered within. What more can be given (kiṁ punaḥ)? Just as giving the position of a nurse to Pūtanā because she worethe dress of a nurse, giving sārūpya to Agha just by entering his stomach is the characteristic of Svayam Bhagavān.

### Text 40

*śrī-sūta uvāca*  
*itthaṁ dvijā yādavadeva-dattaḥ*  
*śrutvā sva-rātuś caritaṁ vicitram*  
*papraccha bhūyo ’pi tad eva puṇyaṁ*  
*vaiyāsakiṁ yan nigṛhīta-cetāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Sūta Gosvāmī said: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, after hearing about those remarkable pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, who had saved him in the womb of his mother and delivered to the Pāṇḍavas, with heart controlled by hearing, again inquired from Śukadeva Gosvāmī about the auspicious topics.**

**Комментарий:**

O brāhmaṇas! Parīkṣit, given to Uttara by Kṛṣṇa (yādava-devena), after hearing the amazing story of Kṛṣṇa who gives himself (to his devotees), whose heart was controlled (nigṛhīta-cetaḥ) by hearing, again inquired from Śukadeva.

### Text 41

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*brahman kālāntara-kṛtaṁ tat-kālīnaṁ kathaṁ bhave*  
*yat kaumāre hari-kṛtaṁ jaguḥ paugaṇḍake ’rbhakāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Mahārāja Parīkṣit inquired: O brāhmaṇa! How could activities which occurred in the past be seen in the present time? How could the boys say that what Kṛṣṇa did in his kaumāra period was done in his paugaṇḍa period?**

**Комментарий:**

How can activities done in the past at another time, be seen in the present (tat-kālīnam)?

### Text 42

*tad brūhi me mahā-yogin paraṁ kautūhalaṁ guro*  
*nūnam etad dharer eva māyā bhavati nānyathā*

**Перевод:**

**O greatest devotee, my spiritual master, this is a cause of curiosity. I think that it was the māyā of Kṛṣṇa and no one else.**

**Комментарий:**

Máyá here means the yoga-śakti of the Lord, the form of his superior aṁśa, since only by that māyā can the associates of the Lord be bewildered.

### Text 43

*vayaṁ dhanyatamā loke guro ’pi kṣatra-bandhavaḥ*  
*vayaṁ pibāmo muhus tvattaḥ puṇyaṁ kṛṣṇa-kathāmṛtam*

**Перевод:**

**O guru! Although I am the lowest of kṣatriyas, I am most fortunate in this world because I constantly drink the nectar of topics of Kṛṣṇa made attractive by coming from your mouth.**

**Комментарий:**

O guru! We, though lowest of kṣatriyas, have been most fortunate.

### Text 44

*śrī-sūta uvāca*  
*itthaṁ sma pṛṣṭaḥ sa tu bādarāyaṇis*  
*tat-smāritānanta-hṛtākhilendriyaḥ*  
*kṛcchrāt punar labdha-bahir-dṛśiḥ śanaiḥ*  
*pratyāha taṁ bhāgavatottamottama*

**Перевод:**

**Sūta Gosvāmī said: O Śaunaka, greatest of saints and devotees! When Mahārāja Parīkṣit inquired from Śukadeva Gosvāmī in this way, Śukadeva Gosvāmī, immediately remembering subject matters about Kṛṣṇa within the core of his heart, externally lost contact with the actions of his senses. Thereafter, with great difficulty, he revived his external sensory perception and slowly began to speak to Mahārāja Parīkṣit.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva’s senses were stolen by affection for Kṛṣṇa, on remembering his unlimited powers and sweetness from taking lunch on the grass up to Brahmā’s prayers. All sensory functions disappeared by a manifestation of the pastime through prema. It was bewilderment in prema, a form of knowledge.

With great effort with loud chanting of the Lord’s names, with conch shells blowing and pounding of drums, he revived external sensory perception.

## Chapter 13 - The Stealing of the Boys and Calves by Brahmā

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṁ mahā-bhāga tvayā bhāgavatottama*  
*yan nūtanayasīśasya śṛṇvann api kathāṁ muhuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O best of devotees, most fortunate Parīkṣit, you have inquired very nicely, for although constantly hearing the pastimes of the Lord, you perceive them to be newer and newer.**

**Комментарий:**

*sa jagdhir vatsa-tat-pāla-hṛtir brahma-vimohanam \|*  
*svabhūtādbhuta-vatsādi-prākaṭyaṁ ca trayodaśe*

**In the thirteenth chapter Kṛṣṇa eats, his boys and cows are stolen, Brahmā is bewildered, and he manifests astonishingly the cows and boys from himself.**

Parīkṣit is the best of devotees because he considers the topics ever fresh, though hearing them many times.

### Text 2

*satām ayaṁ sāra-bhṛtāṁ nisargo*  
*yad-artha-vāṇī-śruti-cetasām api*  
*prati-kṣaṇaṁ navya-vad acyutasya yat*  
*striyā viṭānām iva sādhu vārtā*

**Перевод:**

**Rightly topics of the infallible Lord are new at every moment, just as women are ever-fresh for lusty men. This is natural for devotees, who accept the essence of sweetness, and whose minds, ears and words are dedicated to the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

This is the nature (nisargaḥ) of the devotees, who grasp the essence, due to which (yat) the topics of the Lord become as if new at every moment. Because of their extreme thirst for the topics which are the essence of everything they appear amazing. Their words, ears and minds are the recipients of the topics of that Lord. An example is given of lusty men (viṭānām) who are always interested in topics of young women (striyās).

### Text 3

*śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājann api guhyaṁ vadāmi te*  
*brūyuḥ snigdhasya śiṣyasya guravo guhyam apy uta*

**Перевод:**

**O King shining with intelligence! Hear me with great attention since I will speak confidential topics to you. Gurus speak secrets to an affectionate disciple. I will also do this.**

### Text 4

*tathāgha-vadanān mṛtyo rakṣitvā vatsa-pālakān*  
*sarit-pulinam ānīya bhagavān idam abravīt*

**Перевод:**

**In this way, after saving the boys and calves from Agha’s mouth, which was death personified, Kṛṣṇa, brought them all to the bank of the river and spoke the following words.**

### Text 5

*aho ’tiramyaṁ pulinaṁ vayasyāḥ*  
*sva-keli-sampan mṛdulāccha-bālukam*  
*sphuṭat-saro-gandha-hṛtāli-patrika-*  
*dhvani-pratidhvāna-lasad-drumākulam*

**Перевод:**

**O friends! Here is a pleasant river bank endowed with a wealth of items for our play, endowed with soft, clean sand, and groves of shining trees echoing with the sounds of birds and bees which are attracted by the fragrance of blossoming lotuses.**

**Комментарий:**

He praises a suitable place for eating. The place has the requisites for eating in rows and for playing. Thus the area is large. The sand is soft, suitable for sitting. It is filled with trees resplendent with birds and bees whose sounds echo in the water and who are attracted by the fragrance of blossoming lotuses. The wealth of cooling shade, vīṇā music and fragrant incense (suitable place of taking a meal) is shown.

### Text 6

*atra bhoktavyam asmābhir divārūḍhaṁ kṣudhārditāḥ*  
*vatsāḥ samīpe ’paḥ pītvā carantu śanakais tṛṇam*

**Перевод:**

**O hungry boys! Here we should eat, since the day is getting late. Let the calves, after they drink water, graze on the grass slowly.**

**Комментарий:**

Noon had arrived (divārūḍham).

### Text 7

*tatheti pāyayitvārbhā vatsān ārudhya śādvale*  
*muktvā śikyāni bubhujuḥ samaṁ bhagavatā mudā*

**Перевод:**

**Accepting Lord Kṛṣṇa’s proposal, the cowherd boys allowed the calves to drink water from the river and then tied them to trees where there was green, tender grass. Then the boys opened their bundles of food and began eating along with Kṛṣṇa in great pleasure.**

**Комментарий:**

They tied the calves at a place with abundant green grass (śādvale) so that they would not wander to another place out of greed for that grass.

### Text 8

*kṛṣṇasya viṣvak puru-rāji-maṇḍalair*  
*abhyānanāḥ phulla-dṛśo vrajārbhakāḥ*  
*sahopaviṣṭā vipine virejuś*  
*chadā yathāmbhoruha-karṇikāyāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa sat in the center, encircled by lines of his friends, whose eyes were wide with joy. Sitting with him in Vṛndāvana, they shone like the whorl of a lotus flower surrounded by its petals.**

**Комментарий:**

Their arrangement of sitting for eating is described. The boys of Vraja, surrounding (viṣvak) Kṛṣṇa in many great (puru) circles, facing Kṛṣṇa, sat with no space between them (saha). Intrumental is used in maṇḍalair according to vyatyayo balulam (Pāṇini 3.1.85). Controlled by their prema, when Kṛṣṇa wanted to face them all, his face and all limbs manifested in all directions, by his satya- saṇkalpa power, which follows his desire. By that, the meaning of the following śruti became evident:

*sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṁ tat sarvato ’kṣi-śiro-mukham \|*  
*sarvataḥ śrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati*

**Everywhere Paramātmā has his hands and feet. Everywhere Paramātmā has his eyes, heads and mouths. Everywhere are his ears. Paramātmā covers everything in the universe. (BG** [**13.14**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/13.14)**)**

An example is given. They were situated in many circles around Kṛṣṇa, facing him, like petals arranged in many circles around the center of a lotus, facing the centre.

### Text 9

*kecit puṣpair dalaiḥ kecit pallavair aṅkuraiḥ phalaiḥ*  
*śigbhis tvagbhir dṛṣadbhiś ca bubhujuḥ kṛta-bhājanāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Among the cowherd boys, some ate using flower petals for plates. Others used leaves, fruits, sprouts, their packs, bark of trees and stones.**

**Комментарий:**

They ate using flower petals, etc., as plates since each was skillful at making astonishing plates.

### Text 10

*sarve mitho darśayantaḥ sva-sva-bhojya-ruciṁ pṛthak*  
*hasanto hāsayantaś cābhyavajahruḥ saheśvarāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All the cowherd boys showed one another the different items taken from home, which had various fragrances and tastes, and, by laughing and making others laugh, they ate the preparations along with the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of great friendliness they acted with one mood. All of them (sarve), with Kṛṣṇa (saheśvarāḥ), showed the tastiness of their foods. Eating a little they experienced the great tastiness, and giving those foods to Kṛṣṇa and others they made them experience the great tastiness. They laughed and made others laughed. Without others noticing, they would give flower balls which were in the form of round cakes to another instead of the food and made others laugh. After that, playfully they would be beaten by them. The many foods sent by Lord Kṛṣṇa’s mother was brought by followers in slings tied to colorful poles. The food of Kṛṣṇa and the boys was the very form of taste.

*gandha-rūpaṁ svāda-rūpaṁ dravyaṁ puṣpādikaṁ ca yat \|*  
*rasavad bhautikaṁ dravyam atra syād rasa-rūpakam*  
*heyāṁśānām abhāvāc ca rasa-rūpaṁ bhavec ca tat \|*

**The pleasurable nature of material objects like flowers with fragrance and taste exist in the spiritual world as the very essence of pleasure. Because the objects are devoid of any inferior qualities belonging to material objects they are the very form of pleasure. (Hayaśīrṣa-pañcarātra)**

*cid-ānandaṁ jyoti param api tad āsvādyam api ca*

**There all relishable things are also knowledge and bliss. (Brahma-saṁhitā** [**5.56**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/5.56)**)**

The food was like the forms of all objects perfected by the superior śakti. They had no faulty portions.

### Text 11

*bibhrad veṇuṁ jaṭhara-paṭayoḥ śṛṅga-vetre ca kakṣe*  
*vāme pāṇau masṛṇa-kavalaṁ tat-phalāny aṅgulīṣu*  
*tiṣṭhan madhye sva-pari-suhṛdo hāsayan narmabhiḥ svaiḥ*  
*svarge loke miṣati bubhuje yajña-bhug bāla-keliḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Holding a flute in his sash and a horn and stick under his armpit, holding yogurt rice in his left palm and pickles in his fingers, Kṛṣṇa, situated with his close friends, while playing as a child though he was the enjoyer of sacrifice and while making his friends laugh with jokes, ate his food while the devatās watched in astonishment.**

**Комментарий:**

Among them, the extraordinary manner in which Kṛṣṇa ate is described. In the center facing all, like the center of a flower, Kṛṣṇa ate. He wore his flute in a belt around his waist, fearing it would be stolen. This was arranged beautifully on his right side on his abdomen. He had a horn and stick under his left armpit.

He had a morsal of soft, sticky yogurt rice in his left hand, as if teaching his parama-haṁsa friends how to use the hand as a vessel. He held pieces of amalaka and kārira fruit suitable for the rice between the fingers of his left hand. This is tulya-yogitālaṅkāra. Hemade his friends who were eating and situated around him (pari) laugh with his jokes, while the inhabitants of Svarga such as Indra watched in astonishment.

The Lord eats as mere acceptance uncontaminated food purified by mantras, offered only in intention in sacrifices. But playing as a child with other boys he praises and criticizes food already eaten, which is given and received.

### Text 12

*bhārataivaṁ vatsa-peṣu bhuñjāneṣv acyutātmasu*  
*vatsās tv antar-vane dūraṁ viviśus tṛṇa-lobhitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Bhārata! While the boys whose minds were absorbed in the Lord ate their meal as described, the calves, greedy for grass, entered a forest far away.**

### Text 13

*tān dṛṣṭvā bhaya-santrastān ūce kṛṣṇo ’sya bhī-bhayam*  
*mitrāṇy āśān mā viramatehāneṣye vatsakān aham*

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa - the giver of fear to fear itself for the whole universe- -saw that the cowherd boys were frightened he said, “My dear friends, do not stop eating. I shall bring your calves back to this spot.”**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa is fear for the fear of the universe (asya) since the derivation of the word bhayam is bibhety asmāt: one fear this. He is the giver of fear because of the mantra yaḥ kāla-kālaḥ: who is kāla-kālaḥ or death for death itself. He said, “O friends! Do not stop eating in your lines.” He personally jumped up and departed.

### Text 14

*ity uktvādri-darī-kuñja-gahvareṣv ātma-vatsakān*  
*vicinvan bhagavān kṛṣṇaḥ sapāṇi-kavalo yayau*

**Перевод:**

**Saying this, carrying yogurt rice in his hand, Kṛṣṇa, Svayam Bhagavān, searching for all the calves as his own, went into the mountains, caves, and deep recesses in the groves.**

**Комментарий:**

He thought (vicinvan), I should eat a little while searching for the calves. He thus held some yogurt rice in his hand.

### Text 15

*ambhojanma-janis tad-antara-gato māyārbhakasyeśitur*  
*draṣṭuṁ mañju mahitvam anyad api tad-vatsān ito vatsapān*  
*nītvānyatra kurūdvahāntaradadhāt khe ’vasthito yaḥ purā*  
*dṛṣṭvāghāsura-mokṣaṇaṁ prabhavataḥ prāptaḥ paraṁ vismayam*

**Перевод:**

**O Mahārāja Parīkṣit! Brahmā, who was born from Viṣṇu’s lotus navel, who resides in the sky, and who had become astonished on seeing Kṛṣṇa liberate Aghāsura, came to Vṛndāvana. Taking the boys and calves to another place in order to see some other power of the Lord, who was a boy with bewildering power, Brahmā then disappeared.**

**Комментарий:**

When the Lord, leaving the boys who were still eating, went to search for the calves, at that time Brahmā, though was informed by Kṣirodaśayī of Kṛṣṇa’s power, though he had praised the Lord in his mother’s womb, though he had seen the charming glory of the Lord in liberating Agha, again becoming illusioned thought he would investigate Kṛṣṇa’s power, and spread his māyā to his master,the Lord. By that offence of spreading his māyā, the Lord’s māyā bewildered him. Brahmā, who was born from lotus (ambhojanma- janiḥ), because of having a material birth (from a lotus), possessed material intelligence of testing his master.

On the occasion of Agha’s liberation (antare) he went to Vṛndāvana. To see the sweet glory other than the sweet glory of liberatingAgha, of the Lord (īśituḥ), the son of Nanda (arbhakasya), he took the calves and cowherd boys from there to another place like a thief and hid them. When Brahmā’s māyā desired to steal the real calves and the boys, yoga-māyā, covering up the boys and calves where ever they were, created similar forms through the three guṇas, her shadow, and displayed them to Brahmā. He was fooled by yoga- māyā and took those forms elsewhere.

He thought, “What will he do, whose calves and friends I have stolen? Will he manifest power? Will he bring the calves and boys back? Will he pray to me?” Such deliberation is not possible without being bewildered by māyā.

It is not possible to say that the Lord’s friends could be bewildered by Brahmā’s māyā since Brahmā’s māyā can never influence them who were equal to the Lord and since it is later said kṛṣṇa-māyā- hatātmanām: they were covered by Kṛṣṇa’s māyā. (SB [10.14.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.43))

The real boys remained hidden where ever they were since later it is said:

*vatsān pulinam āninye yathā-pūrva-sakhaṁ svakam*

**He took the calves, who were still situated where they had been a year earlier, and brought them to the riverbank, where he had been taking his meal and where his cowherd boyfriends remained just as before. (SB** [**10.14.42**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.42)**)**

Brahmā is described. Previously seeing the liberation of Agha by the powerful son of Nanda (prabhavataḥ), he had become astonished.

### Text 16

*tato vatsān adṛṣṭvetya puline ’pi ca vatsapān*  
*ubhāv api vane kṛṣṇo vicikāya samantataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, when Kṛṣṇa was unable to find the calves, he returned to the bank of the river, but there he was also unable to see the cowherd boys. Thus he began to search for both the calves and the boys everywhere in the forest.**

**Комментарий:**

He did not see the calves situated there. Since it is not said that he did not obtain them, it means that he made a show of not seeingthem. From the grassy area he went to the bank and not seeing the boys, he searched in the forest everywhere for the calves and boys so that Brahmā falsely feels that he was able to bewilder the Lord. He pretended to search like an actor, showing despair. Later it issaid: tatrodvahat paśupa-vaṁśa-śiśutva-nāṭyam: he played the role of a small child in the family of cowherds. SB [10.13.61](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/13.61)

### Text 17

*kvāpy adṛṣṭvāntar-vipine vatsān pālāṁś ca viśva-vit*  
*sarvaṁ vidhi-kṛtaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ sahasāvajagāma ha*

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa was unable to find the calves and the cowherd boys anywhere in the forest, being omniscient as Svayam Bhagavān, he suddenly understood that this was the work of Brahmā.**

**Комментарий:**

Why did he search again? Not seeing the boys on the bank or anywhere else and not seeing the calves in the grass fields or anywhere else, he searched again (verb in previous verse). “Having understood at the time of the theft, why did he search after that?” He was omniscient (viśva-vit). Right at the time of theft (sahasā) he understood, without infering, that Brahmā stole the boys and calves.

### Text 18

*tataḥ kṛṣṇo mudaṁ kartuṁ tan-mātṝṇāṁ ca*  
*kasya ca ubhayāyitam ātmānaṁ cakre viśva-kṛd īśvaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, just to create pleasure both for Brahmā and for the mothers of the calves and cowherd boys, Kṛṣṇa, the lord of Mahā-viṣṇu, made himself appear just like the calves and boys.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa manifested great power to bewilder Brahmā. When Brahmā, thinking he had caused bewilderment, had gone to his planet, the Lord, the son of Nanda, himself became both the calves and the boys (ubhayāyitam), in order to create bliss (mudam) for the mothers of his friends who desired a relationship with him as their son, by being their son, and for Brahmā (kasya), who decided to test his master out of ignorance though he was wise, by giving the experience of great astonishment by showing thousands of forms of Vāsudeva, since Brahmā was the object of his mercy, being the Lord’s son and servant. Because he was viśva-kṛt, Kṛṣṇa was capable of arranging this.

### Text 19

*yāvad vatsapa-vatsakālpaka-vapur yāvat karāṅghry-ādikaṁ*  
*yāvad yaṣṭi-viṣāṇa-veṇu-dala-śig yāvad vibhūṣāmbaram*  
*yāvac chīla-guṇābhidhākṛti-vayo yāvad vihārādikaṁ*  
*sarvaṁ viṣṇumayaṁ giro ’ṅga-vad ajaḥ sarva-svarūpo babhau*

**Перевод:**

**Though unborn, Kṛṣṇa, because he is the embodiment of all forms, different and non-different from them like words being inseparable from their endings, he expanded himself into the exact number of missing cowherd boys and calves, with their exact bodily features, their particular types of hands, legs and other limbs, their sticks, bugles, flutes, ornamental flower petals, their lunch bags, their particular types of dress and ornaments placed in various ways, their names, ages and forms, and their special activities and characteristics, which were all non-different from him.**

**Комментарий:**

This is explained in detail. He expanded himself as the exact size of small boys and calves and no more. Singular is used to indicate a type. They had tender bodies (alpaka-vapuḥ). The ādi in vihārādikam signifies that they had the same actions in relation to their fathers, etc. Kṛṣṇa was devoid having a previous body (ajaḥ). Manifesting himself who is everything as previously described, he became as all those svarūpas like the embodiment of the Vedic statement, ajāyamāno bahudhā vijāyate: Unborn, he appears as many. (Mahā-nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad). That statement personified became as if directly perceivable (to the senses). Some says that this was similar to how oṁkāra, the mahāvākya (giraḥ), manifests in manifold ways as parts of ṛk and other Vedic verses (aṅgavat).

### Text 20

*svayam ātmātma-govatsān prativāryātma-vatsapaiḥ*  
*krīḍann ātma-vihāraiś ca sarvātmā prāviśad vrajam*

**Перевод:**

**Herding back calves who were himself through the boys who were himself, playing with cowherd boys who were himself, Kṛṣṇa entered Vraja.**
