**Комментарий:**

Having played at noon and in the afternoon like before, in the evening Kṛṣṇa entered Vraja. This is described in five verses. How did he, being all the boys and calves, enter Vraja? Being himself the instigator (svayam ātmā), he herded back the calves who were himself as the object of the action, through the boys who were himself as the instigated agent. He played with the boys who were himself with flutes, etc. Thus he personally was all actions and the nouns connected with the actions.

### Text 21

*tat-tad-vatsān pṛthaṅ nītvā tat-tad-goṣṭhe niveśya saḥ*  
*tat-tad-ātmābhavad rājan tat-tat-sadma praviṣṭavān*

**Перевод:**

**O King! Bringing the different sets of calves, he put them in each cow shed and as each boy he entered each house.**

**Комментарий:**

With each particular form such as Śrīdāma, Sudāma and Subala (tat-tad-ātmā), he entered each house.

### Text 22

*tan-mātaro veṇu-rava-tvarotthitā*  
*utthāpya dorbhiḥ parirabhya nirbharam*  
*sneha-snuta-stanya-payaḥ-sudhāsavaṁ*  
*matvā paraṁ brahma sutān apāyayan*

**Перевод:**

**The mothers of the boys, immediately upon hearing the sounds of the flutes being played by their sons, rose up, put the boys on their laps, embraced them with both arms and began to feed them with their breast milk, which flowed forth because of extreme love, thinking of Parabrahman as their son.**

**Комментарий:**

The bewilderment of the mothers is described while describing that Kṛṣṇa fulfilled their desire to have him as their son.

Thinking Parabrahman was their sons, the mothers raised him in their arms and, putting him on their laps, affectionately fed him their breast milk. Nirbharam (excessively) indicates that they had more affection for their sons than previously. What was the nature of that milk? It was like nectar, intoxicating like tasty liquor. Even Parabrahman, knowing this about the milk, drank. Brahmā says:

*aho ‘ti-dhanyā vraja-go-ramaṇyaḥ*  
*stanyāmṛtaṁ pītam atīva te mudā*

**O almighty Lord, how greatly fortunate are the cows and ladies of Vṛndāvana, the nectar of whose breast-milk you have happily drunk to your full satisfaction, taking the form of their calves and children! (SB** [**10.14.31**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.31)**)**

According to the Lord’s statement “As they surrender, I respond,” (BG [4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11)) the Lord developed the desire to be their son in response to their desire of have him as their son. For that purpose, yogamāyā caused bewilderment of the cowherd boys for one year.

### Text 23

*tato nṛponmardana-majja-lepanā-*  
*laṅkāra-rakṣā-tilakāśanādibhiḥ*  
*saṁlālitaḥ svācaritaiḥ praharṣayan*  
*sāyaṁ gato yāma-yamena mādhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, as required according to rules for the last part of the day, Kṛṣṇa returned in the evening, and was cared for by the mothers by massaging him with oil, bathing him, anointing him with sandalwood pulp, decorating him with ornaments, chanting protective mantras, decorating him with tilaka and feeding him. Mādhava gave them joy by his actions.**

**Комментарий:**

With the end (yama) in the last prahara of the day (yāma), Kṛṣṇa, the bodies of those cowherd boys, came back their houses in the evening and were cared for by the mothers by rubbing with fragrant oil (unmardana), bathing (majja), etc. He gave them joy by his splendid actions (svācāritaiḥ).

### Text 24

*gāvas tato goṣṭham upetya satvaraṁ*  
*huṅkāra-ghoṣaiḥ parihūta-saṅgatān*  
*svakān svakān vatsatarān apāyayan*  
*muhur lihantyaḥ sravad audhasaṁ payaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, all the cows hastily entered their different sheds and began mooing loudly, calling for their respective calves. The mothers began licking the calves’ bodies again and again and profusely feeding them with the milk flowing from their milk bags.**

**Комментарий:**

Bewilderment of the cows is described. They approached the calves which were called and which then gathered. Here also satvaram(quickly), muhur lihantyaḥ (they repeatedly licked), and sravat (the milk flowed) indicate that they had more affection for those calves than previously.

### Text 25

*go-gopīnāṁ mātṛtāsminn āsīt snehardhikāṁ vinā*  
*purovad āsv api hares tokatā māyayā vinā*

**Перевод:**

**The cows and mothers’ maternal affection for Kṛṣṇa as their son was similar to the affection they had for their original sons, though their affection for their original sons was actually less. Kṛṣṇa’s acceptance of those women as his mothers, even previously, was almost like his affection for Yaśodā, but now it was direct, as their very son.**

**Комментарий:**

The specialty of Kṛṣṇa’s sentiment as son now and the gopīs’ sentiment as mothers now compared to what were there previously is described. All the cows’ and gopīs’ motherly sentiments filled with caressing, etc., for Kṛṣṇa, Yaśodā’s son, remained as previously(purovat) but without additional affection. Previously they had affection for their sons like Śrīdāmā, Sudāma, etc., but additional affection for the son of Yaśodā. Now however they had an increase of prema for both (their children and Yaśodā’s son), since Kṛṣṇa was one with the boys like Śrīdāmā. Even Kṛṣṇa’s sentiment as a son of all the gopīs existed as previously but was now without intellectual arrangements (māyayā). Māyā means intelligence according to Medinī. Previously he thought, “I am their son too,” but this sentiment was not direct. But now this sentiment was direct, since he was the form of Śrīdāmā and other boys.

### Text 26

*vrajaukasāṁ sva-tokeṣu sneha-vally ābdam anvaham*  
*śanair niḥsīma vavṛdhe yathā kṛṣṇe tv apūrvavat*

**Перевод:**

**Now, for one year, their affection for their own sons gradually increased without limit, for Kṛṣṇa had now become their sons. And their affection for Kṛṣṇa increased more than previously to an astonishing degree.**

**Комментарий:**

Clarifying the equal increase of affection for both the boys and Kṛṣṇa that has been spoken, he describes the uniqueness related to the son of Yaśodā, Kṛṣṇa in undisguised form. For one year, daily, the creeper of affection for Śrīdāmā and others, their sons, who were actually Kṛṣṇa, increased as their affection for Kṛṣṇa, the son of Yaśodā, gradually increased by caring for him. The word kṛṣṇa is repeated due to the word tu. But their affection for Kṛṣṇa increased in a remarkable way, since he is the aṁśī and was undisguised in form and qualities. Others say that the word kṛṣṇa is not to be repeated: Their affection increased rightly (yathā) but their affection for Kṛṣṇa increased remarkably.

### Text 27

*ittham ātmātmanātmānaṁ vatsa-pāla-miṣeṇa saḥ*  
*pālayan vatsapo varṣa cikrīḍe vana-goṣṭhayoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In this way, Kṛṣṇa, disguised as the cowherd boys and the calves, protected himself by himself and played in Vṛndāvana and in the forest for one year.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa, the cowherd (vatsapa), the form of knowledge and bliss (ātmā), on the pretext of herding the calves (vatsa-pāla-miṣeṇa),played while herding himself. This was not perceived by anyone.

### Text 28

*ekadā cārayan vatsān sa-rāmo vanam āviśat*  
*pañca-ṣāsu tri-yāmāsu hāyanāpūraṇīṣv ajaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**One day, five or six nights before the completion of the year, Kṛṣṇa, tending the calves, entered the forest along with Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to speak of the bewilderment even of Balarāma, related the bewilderment of Brahmā, the following is related. With five or six nights (tri-yāmāsu) remaining in the year (hāyana), Kṛṣṇa entered the forest.

### Text 29

*tato ’vidūrāc carato gāvo vatsān upavrajam*  
*govardhanādri-śirasi carantyo dadṛśus tṛṇam*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, while pasturing atop Govardhana Hill, the cows saw their calves pasturing near Vṛndāvana, not very far away.**

**Комментарий:**

While eating grass on the top of Govardhana, the cows saw their calves grazing near Vraja (avidūrāt).

### Text 30

*dṛṣṭvātha tat-sneha-vaśo ’smṛtātmā*  
*sa go-vrajo ’tyātmapa-durga-mārgaḥ*  
*dvi-pāt kakud-grīva udāsya-puccho*  
*’gād dhuṅkṛtair āsru-payā javena*

**Перевод:**

**When the cows saw their own calves they forgot themselves because of increased affection, and although the path was very rough, freeing themselves from the cowherds, they ran toward their calves, the front legs and back legs acting as one leg each, bellowing loudly. Their milk bags full and flowing with milk, their heads and tails raised, and their necks were bent.**

**Комментарий:**

The group of cows, seeing the calves, went to the calves. They are described. They forgot even themselves (asmṛtātmā). They went on a difficult path, escaping the cowherds who were guarding them (atyātma-pa), running with two feet joined and two feet joined, as if they had only two feet, with necks bent at the hump, with heads and tails raised. Milk and tears flowed freely from them.

### Text 31

*sametya gāvo ’dho vatsān vatsavatyo ’py apāyayan*  
*gilantya iva cāṅgāni lihantyaḥ svaudhasaṁ payaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Arriving at the bottom of the hill, the cows, though having given birth to new calves, allowed these older calves to drink milk from their full milk bags while licking their bodies as if wanting to swallow them.**

**Комментарий:**

Arriving from Govardhana the cows made the calves drink the milk flowing from their udders (audhasam). Though the mothers had again given birth to other calves, they still licked them. This shows the cows’ great affection.

### Text 32

*gopās tad-rodhanāyāsa- maughya-lajjoru-manyunā*  
*durgādhva-kṛcchrato ’bhyetya go-vatsair dadṛśuḥ sutān*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd men, having been unable to check the cows from going to their calves, felt simultaneously ashamed and angry. They crossed the rough road with great difficulty, but when they arrived they saw their own sons with the calves.**

**Комментарий:**

The cowherds approached with anger and shame at their useless (maughya) attempts (āyāsa) at stopping the cows and with great difficulty arising from the rough path and saw their sons with the calves.

### Text 33

*tad-īkṣaṇotprema-rasāplutāśayā*  
*jātānurāgā gata-manyavo ’rbhakān*  
*uduhya dorbhiḥ parirabhya mūrdhani*  
*ghrāṇair avāpuḥ paramāṁ mudaṁ te*

**Перевод:**

**At that time, all the thoughts of the cowherd men merged in the mellow of paternal love, which was aroused by the sight of their sons. Experiencing a great attraction, their anger completely disappearing, they lifted their sons, embraced them in their arms, and enjoyed the highest pleasure by smelling their sons’ heads.**

**Комментарий:**

With their hearts filled with the rasa of prema caused by seeing their sons, attaining anurāga, a later stage of prema, they forgot their anger.

### Text 34

*tataḥ pravayaso gopās tokāśleṣa-sunirvṛtāḥ*  
*kṛcchrāc chanair apagatās tad-anusmṛty-udaśravaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter the elderly cowherd men, having obtained great bliss from embracing their sons, gradually and with great difficulty and reluctance ceased embracing them. But by constant remembrance, their eyes flowed with tears.**

**Комментарий:**

The elderly cowherds, though having many sons, became very blissful by embracing them. With difficulty, slowly they gave that up due to obligation to herd the cows and left. Giving up the embraces and going to the cows, they shed tears by remembering the boys.

### Text 35

*vrajasya rāmaḥ premardher vīkṣyautkaṇṭhyam anukṣaṇam*  
*mukta-staneṣv apatyeṣv apy ahetu-vid acintayat*

**Перевод:**

**Because of an increase of affection, the cows had constant attachment to those calves that were grown up and had stopped sucking milk from their mothers. When Baladeva saw this attachment, he was unable to understand the reason for it, and thus he began to consider as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the actions of the cows for their calves and the cowherds for their sons, Balarāma began to reflect. Seeing the intensity due to increase of prema of the gopīs, cows and cowherds for their offspring who were no longer drinking milk, not knowing the cause(ahetu-vit), Balarāma began to think. Even though Balarāma saw the contrary actions starting from the day of the bewilderment of Brahmā, on this day he began to investigate since Kṛṣṇa withdrew his yogamāyā gradually, due to the arousal of the desire to teach this pastime to him at that moment and since Balarāma, who dentifies himself as a devotee, should be submerged suddenly in the ocean of Kṛṣṇa’s powers.

### Text 36

*kim etad adbhutam iva vāsudeve ’khilātmani*  
*vrajasya sātmanas tokeṣv apūrvaṁ prema vardhate*

**Перевод:**

**What is this irrational phenomenon? The affection of all the inhabitants of Vraja, including me, for Kṛṣṇa, the soul and shelter of all of us, increasing as never before, is now increasing for these boys and calves.**

**Комментарий:**

With yogamāyā’s withdrawal of the first part bewilderment, his thoughts arising out of the contrary actions he witnessed are desribed. In the manner Vraja, including I (sātmanaḥ), had prema for Kṛṣṇa, in the same manner that prema for the boys also increases. What is this wonder? It is appropriate that my prema for Kṛṣṇa is in excess to the prema for the boys.

### Text 37

*keyaṁ vā kuta āyātā daivī vā nāry utāsurī*  
*prāyo māyāstu me bhartur nānyā me ’pi vimohinī*

**Перевод:**

**What is this māyā and where as it come from? Is it caused by devatās or by sages? Or it caused by a she-demon? It can only be the māyā of my brother and nothing else. It causes my prema to increase remarkably.**

**Комментарий:**

“Anyway, due to my nature of omniscience I will know the cause.” Reflecting in this way for a moment, when the second portion ofyogamāyā was withdrawn, determining that it was māyā, he again conjectured, “What is the nature of this māyā? Where did it come from? What is it related to?” He thought, “What is this māyā? Why has it come? Is it the work of devatās (daivī)? Did Brahmā andother devatās become the cowherd boys and produce affection in our hearts for them, to test our powers? Is it the work of humans(nārī)? Did sages become the boys to test our knowledge? Is it the work of demons (āsurī)? Unable to defeat us by their strength, did Kaṁsa and others become the boys by disguise to harm us?”

Imagining various alternatives, when the third portion of yogamāyā was withdrawn, again he thought. “This is the māyā called yoga,which belongs to Kṛṣṇa, my master (bhartuḥ). It is not the other māyā made of three guṇas, since she comes only due to aversion to Kṛṣṇa. That māyā cannot bewilder me also. By the māyā of my aṁśa, Kāraṇodaśayī, creator of mahat-tattva, the whole world headed by Brahmā is bewildered. So how can the māyā of the devatās, humans or demons bewilder me? It must be the māyā of my master.” The imperative is used to express probability.

### Text 38

*iti sañcintya dāśārho vatsān sa-vayasān api*  
*sarvān ācaṣṭa vaikuṇṭhaṁ cakṣuṣā vayunena saḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thinking in this way, Balarāma was able to see, with the eye of prema, that all these calves and Kṛṣṇa’s friends were expansions of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

“Anyway, in this way by reconciling again I will see the truth.” Thinking in this way, the fourth part of yoga-māyā dissipated and he saw the calves and boys as the very svarūpa of his master. By the eye of endowed knowledge, he saw all his friends (sa-vayasān) asKṛṣṇa (vaikuṇṭham). The ending on savayasān is poetic license in a compound. Since even Balarāma, the Lord, is a svāṁśa of Kṛṣṇa, and has his knowledge and desire controlled by Kṛṣṇa, the aṁśī, all of this is harmonized. That is the conclusion of the wise.

### Text 39

*naite sureśā ṛṣayo na caite*  
*tvam eva bhāsīśa bhid-āśraye ’pi*  
*sarvaṁ pṛthak tvaṁ nigamāt kathaṁ vadety*  
*uktena vṛttaṁ prabhuṇā balo ’vait*

**Перевод:**

**Baladeva said, “O supreme controller! These boys are not great devatās or sages. Now I can see that you alone are manifesting in all these boys and calves. Although one entity, you are existing in the different forms of the calves and boys. Please briefly explain this to me.” Having thus been requested by Baladeva, Kṛṣṇa explained the whole situation, and Baladeva understood it.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way, though seeing directly the truth, he asked Kṛṣṇa the cause and purpose of taking the forms of the calves and boys. Brahmā and other devatās have not become the calves and boys by māyā. Nor have the sages or the demons (ca). Rather you alone shine in this group of boys and calves, which though performs various activities (bhidāśraye). You alone are engaged in these various activities (pṛthaktvaṁ). Please explain briefly (nigamāt) the cause and the result for all this. Because of the Lord being asked, Balarāma understood (avait) the incident (vṛttam) of Brahmā’s bewilderment.

### Text 40

*tāvad etyātmabhūr ātma-mānena truṭy-anehasā*  
*purovad ābdaṁ krīḍantaṁ dadṛśe sa-kalaṁ harim*

**Перевод:**

**When Brahmā returned after a moment of his time, he saw that, although by human measurement a complete year had passed, Kṛṣṇa was engaged just as before in playing with the boys and calves, who were his expansions.**

**Комментарий:**

Then what happened? After a year passed Brahmā, the son of Viṣṇu (ātmabhūḥ), came after the time of a few second by his calculation (ātmā-mānena). He saw the Lord playing as previously for the whole year with the boys and calves, his expansions (sa-kalam). On the day Balarāma was not been present since he was kept at home by his mother for an auspicious bath on the occasion of his birth constellation.

### Text 41

*yāvanto gokule bālāḥ sa-vatsāḥ sarva eva hi*  
*māyāśaye śayānā me nādyāpi punar utthitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Brahmā thought: Whatever boys and calves there were in Gokula are sleeping on my bed of māyā, and to this very day they have not yet risen.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing this, he then conjectured. This is expressed two verses. They are sleeping on my bed made of māyā (māyāśaye).

### Text 42

*ita ete ’tra kutratyā man-māyā-mohitetare*  
*tāvanta eva tatrābdaṁ krīḍanto viṣṇunā samam*

**Перевод:**

**For this reason, from where did these other boys come? For a whole year they have all been playing with Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking that these forms have been brought there by the Lord, seeing them at a little distance he spoke. The boys bewildered by my māyā are at some place (itaḥ) a little distant from here. Different from those boys are these boys, as many as they, playing with Kṛṣṇa(viṣṇunā samam). Where have they come from?

### Text 43

*evam eteṣu bhedeṣu ciraṁ dhyātvā sa ātma-bhūḥ*  
*satyāḥ ke katare neti jñātuṁ neṣṭe kathañcana*

**Перевод:**

**Thus Brahmā, thinking and thinking for a long time and trying to distinguish between those two sets of boys- which was real and which was false- could not understand at all.**

**Комментарий:**

The special bewilderment of Brahmā is described. Are the forms here real and the forms over there created by Kṛṣṇa? Or are these forms created by Kṛṣṇa and the forms over there real? Or are both forms made by him and then one set was taken by me? He must have taken the real forms somewhere else.

Meditating on these particulars (bhedeṣu) for a long time, being given vision, he thought, “Who are the real forms? Which of the two is not real? Who are produced by his illusion?” He could not understand by any type of questioning. He became bewildered.

### Text 44

*evaṁ sammohayan viṣṇuṁ vimohaṁ viśva-mohanam*  
*svayaiva māyayājo ’pi svayam eva vimohitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus because Brahmā wanted to bewilder the all-pervading Kṛṣṇa, who can never be bewildered, but who, on the contrary, bewilders the entire universe, he himself was put into bewilderment by Kṛṣṇa’s māyā.**

**Комментарий:**

This is clarified. Bewildering the son of Nanda (arbhakam) by stealing the calves and boys, even Brahmā (ajaḥ) was especiallybewildered by the māyā of Viṣṇu because of the offence of using his māyā against the Lord (svayā māyayā). It should not be explained that “he was bewildered by his own māyā,” since māyā cannot bewilder its shelter, and this would contradict the example in the next verse. The Lord is described. He destroys illusion (vimoham). He gives knowledge which destroys māyā. He also appropriately bewilders all other beings other than himself (viśva-mohanam) by the three guṇas.

### Text 45

*tamyāṁ tamovan naihāraṁ khadyotārcir ivāhani*  
*mahatītara-māyaiśyaṁ nihanty ātmani yuñjataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As the darkness of snow on a dark night cannot cover darkness and the light of a glowworm in the light of day cannot reveal the sun, the power of an inferior person who tries to use it against a person of great power destroys his own ability.**

**Комментарий:**

Other māyās cannot affect the Lord who possesses the greatest māyā but they eclipse their source. An example is given. Like thedarkness (tamovat) produced from mist (naihāraṁ) in the night (tamyām). Iva here means vat (like). The darkness produced by frost particles cannot cover the night. The darkness of mist mixing with the darkness of night, becoming thick, makes the mist disappear. Similarly, Brahmā’s māyā, being unable to bewilder the Lord, increases the Lord’s power and eclipses Brahmā.

Since in this example since Brahmā’s māyā is also the cause (of his bewilderment), out of dissatisfaction another example is given. Just as the light from the glowworm does not give out a separate light in the day but merges into the daylight and appears to have lost is light, similarly insignificant māyā of a person used against a great person destroys the powers in that person. Thus the māyā ofBrahmā was destroyed and Brahmā became devoid of power.

### Text 46

*tāvat sarve vatsa-pālāḥ paśyato ’jasya tat-kṣaṇāt*  
*vyadṛśyanta ghana-śyāmāḥ pīta-kauśeya-vāsasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then, while Lord Brahmā looked on, all the calves and the boys tending them immediately appeared to have complexions the color of bluish rainclouds and to be dressed in yellow silken garments.**

**Комментарий:**

Though Brahmā committed offense, because he was the servant of the Lord, Kṛṣṇa showed mercy.

As much as Brahmā reflected, he was only bewildered (tāvat). The calves and boys were seen to be (vyadṛśyanta) dark like clouds. This is a reflexive verb. Since they were self-manifesting, they became visible on their own. Brahmā just looked (paśyataḥ). The genitive case is used to express disrespect.

O Brahmā, living on Satya-loka! By intelligence you create the universe. You spread māya to your master Kṛṣṇa. You cannot know us Vrajavāsīs who are his aṁśas by any means. Look at our great powers which we now show.

### Texts 47-48

*catur-bhujāḥ śaṅkha-cakra- gadā-rājīva-pāṇayaḥ*  
*kirīṭinaḥ kuṇḍalino hāriṇo vana-mālinaḥ*

*śrīvatsāṅgada-do-ratna- kambu-kaṅkaṇa-pāṇayaḥ*  
*nūpuraiḥ kaṭakair bhātāḥ kaṭi-sūtrāṅgulīyakaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All those personalities had four arms, holding conchshell, disc, mace and lotus flower in their hands. They wore helmets on their heads, earrings on their ears and garlands of forest flowers around their necks. On the upper portion of the right side of their chests was the emblem of the goddess of fortune. Furthermore, they wore armlets on their arms, bracelets, anklets, wrist ornaments, ankle bells, foot ornaments, belts around their waists and rings on their fingers. They all appeared very beautiful.**

**Комментарий:**

On their chests (vatsa) they had the line of Lakṣmī (śrī). They had armbands on their arms (do). On their necks resembling conchshells (kambu) they had the Kaustubha (ratna). They had bracelets and threads on their wrists. Kambu can mean either a conch or a bracelet according to Nānārtha-varga. Kaṅkaṇa is a hand ornament according to Nṛ-varga. Kaṭaka are anklets.

### Text 49

*āṅghri-mastakam āpūrṇās tulasī-nava-dāmabhiḥ*  
*komalaiḥ sarva-gātreṣu bhūri-puṇyavad-arpitaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Every part of their bodies, from their feet to the top of their heads, was fully decorated with fresh, tender garlands of tulasī leaves offered by devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

The phrase bhūri-puṇyavad arpitaiḥ means “offered by many devotees who engaged in hearing and chanting, etc, which abundantly purify.”

### Text 50

*candrikā-viśada-smeraiḥ sāruṇāpāṅga-vīkṣitaiḥ*  
*svakārthānām iva rajaḥ-sattvābhyāṁ sraṣṭṛ-pālakāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Those Viṣṇu forms, by their smiling glances, which resembled the pure light of the moon, which were also tinged with red, created and protected the desires of their own devotees, as if by the modes of passion and goodness.**

**Комментарий:**

By their smiles, white like moon light, along with the sidelong glances of their reddish eyes they appreared as if they are creators and maintainers of the desires of their devotees by rajas and sattva. They were creators by the red eyes, as if by rajas, and they were maintainers by their white smiles, as if by sattva.

### Text 51

*ātmādi-stamba-paryantair mūrtimadbhiś carācaraiḥ*  
*nṛtya-gītādy-anekārhaiḥ pṛthak pṛthag upāsitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**These forms were worshipped by the presiding deities of all moving and non-moving beings, including Brahmā, with many items such as singing and dancing, according to their respective capacities and ingredients.**

**Комментарий:**

Ātmā means Brahmā. The forms were worshipped with many items (anekārhaiḥ).

### Text 52

*aṇimādyair mahimabhir ajādyābhir vibhūtibhiḥ*  
*catur-viṁśatibhis tattvaiḥ parītā mahad-ādibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**These forms were surrounded by the powers, headed by the power to become small, by śaktis like Lakṣmī along with expansions like material māyā; and by the twenty-four elements for the creation of the material world, headed by mahat-tattva.**

**Комментарий:**

They were surrounded by many powers (mahimābhiḥ) like aṇimā, by śaktis (vibhūtibhiḥ) like mūla-prakṛti (ajā) and by twenty-fourtattvas. Catur-viṁśatibhir (by twenty-fours) is in plural here since each of the forms was worshipped by two-four tattvas. By separating mahat-tattva and sūtra two-four elements are counted.

### Text 53

*kāla-svabhāva-saṁskāra- kāma-karma-guṇādibhiḥ*  
*sva-mahi-dhvasta-mahibhir mūrtimadbhir upāsitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The personifications of time, the ability to transform, impressions, desire, karma, the guṇas, names and forms, whose powers were dwarfed by Viṣṇu’s powers, worshipped these Viṣṇu forms.**

**Комментарий:**

Time and its assistants, in the form of their presiding deities are described. Their powers were dissipated by the Lord’s powers. This means that they are dependent. Kāla (time) is the agitator. Svabhāva is the cause of transformation. Saṁskāra is the cause of knowledge. Kāma is the desire for sense objects. Karma is the form of results of piety and sin. Guṇas are sattva, rajas and tamas.

### Text 54

*satya-jñānānantānanda-mātraika-rasa-mūrtayaḥ*  
*aspṛṣṭa-bhūri-māhātmyā api hy upaniṣad-dṛśām*

**Перевод:**

**The forms all had eternal, unlimited forms, full of knowledge and bliss, which were one form. Their great glory could not even to be touched by the ātmā-jñānīs.**

**Комментарий:**

The forms were not made by the Lord with māyā made of three guṇas. Satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ brahma: the Lord is existence, infinite and knowledge. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad [2.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/taittiriya/2.1)) vijñānam ānandam brahma: the Lord is knowledge and bliss. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad [3.9.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bau/3.9.28))

They had bodies of the nature of only Brahman, who is existence, knowledge, infinite and bliss, and thus which were unchangeable(ekarasa-mūrtayaḥ). Though the body and the Lord himself are non-different, they are described here as being different (having bodies) because of viśeṣa, like existence existing.

Their glories were not understood (aspṛṣṭam) in full by knowers of Vedānta (upaniṣad). Namo vedānta-vedyāyaupaniṣadaḥ puruṣaḥ: I offer respects to the Lord who is known by Vedānta. (Bṛhad- āraṇyaka Upaniṣad [3.9.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bau/3.9.26)) The Lord is known by the Upaniṣads.

Kārtsnyena nājo ’py abhidhātum īśaḥ: Even Lord Brahmā himself would be incapable of describing the Lord’s qualities entirely. (SB [12.4.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/4.39)) Though he can be known, he cannot be known completely.

### Text 55

*evaṁ sakṛd dadarśājaḥ para-brahmātmano ’khilān*  
*yasya bhāsā sarvam idam vibhāti sa-carācaram*

**Перевод:**

**Thus Brahmā saw all the forms of the Supreme Brahman at once, by whose self-revealing natures the whole universe of moving and non-moving beings gained consciousness.**

**Комментарий:**

Showing once the calves and boys who were of the nature of Brahman, worshipped by the tattvas of prakṛti such as mahat, the most merciful Lord showed them worshipped by those spiritual tattvas. Brahma for once saw all the calves and boys and all the tattvas as Parabrahman. Evam means by numbers and by names they were equal to what was previously displayed. By the śakti (bhāsā) of Parabrahman, the universe of moving and nonmoving beings became capable of action (vibhāti). This is according to the following:

*dravyaṁ karma ca kālaś ca svabhāvo jīva eva ca \|*  
*vāsudevāt paro brahman na cānyo ’rtho ’sti tattvataḥ*

**O brāhmaṇa! The elements, karma, kāla, svabhāva and the jīva are not different from Vāsudeva. Nothing but he exists in truth. (SB** [**2.5.14**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.14)**)**

This is a second display. This will be clear in the next chapter with the following:

*adyaiva tvad ṛte ‘sya kiṁ mama na te māyātvam ādarśitam*

**Have you not shown me today that both you yourself and everything within this creation are manifestations of your inconceivable potency? (SB** [**10.14.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.18)**)**

### Text 56

*tato ’tikutukodvṛtta-stimitaikādaśendriyaḥ*  
*tad-dhāmnābhūd ajas tūṣṇīṁ pūr-devy-antīva putrikā*

**Перевод:**

**Then, by the power of the effulgence of those Viṣṇu forms, Brahmā, his eleven senses stunned in bliss and agitated with eagerness, became silent, just like a child’s clay doll in the presence of the village deity.**

**Комментарий:**

His eleven senses stunned in bliss (stimita), agitated (udvṛtta) by eagerness (atikutuka), he became silent, unable to speak, because of their effulgence (dhāmnā). An example is given. He was an unworthy doll played with by children amidst a powerful goddess worshipped with various articles by all the village people.

### Text 57

*itīreśe ’tarkye nija-mahimani sva-pramitike*  
*paratrājāto ’tan-nirasana-mukha-brahmaka-mitau*  
*anīśe ’pi draṣṭuṁ kim idam iti vā muhyati sati*  
*cacchādājo jñātvā sapadi paramo ’jā-javanikām*

**Перевод:**

**When Brahmā became bewildered about what he saw and was no longer able to look at these forms, which were inconceivable, expansions of Kṛṣṇa’s power, self-revealing, proved by the scriptures through negation of matter, and which were beyond matter, Kṛṣṇa, understanding his bewilderment, immediately covered the vision.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding that Brahmā who drowned in a drop of the sweet glory of the Lord, was not qualified for the ocean which should also be shown, the Lord stopped the display. When Brahmā, who has great intelligence, who is the lord and father (īśe) of Sarasvatī (īrā), was bewildered thinking, “What is this?” and was then not even able to see (anīśe), the son of Nanda (paramaḥ), the lord of all beings, understanding his lack of qualification for seeing and experiencing his sweet glories, immediately removed the screen ofyogamāyā, by which he covered the real boys and calves including himself searching for them and by which he again showed them, his own selves as the many dark forms of Viṣṇu. He made the screen called yogamāyā (ajā-javanikām), disappear. The differencebetween māyā and yogamāyā should be seen in the commentary on the verse viṣṇor māyā bhagavatī. (SB [10.1.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.25))

In which aspect was he bewildered? He was bewildered about the extraordinary greatness seen, the dark forms of great power,inconceivable (atarkye) because they were forms of self-manifesting knowledge and bliss (sva-pramitike). They were inconceivable by having such forms. Thus the Lord is untouched (paratra) by the three guṇas (ajātaḥ). He is known by the Upaniṣads (brahmaka-mitau) through statements such as asthūlam anaṇv ahrasvam: he is not big and he is not small, (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad [3.8.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bau/3.8.8)) which reject negatives.

### Text 58

*tato ’rvāk pratilabdhākṣaḥ kaḥ paretavad utthitaḥ*  
*kṛcchrād unmīlya vai dṛṣṭīr ācaṣṭedaṁ sahātmanā*

**Перевод:**

**Brahmā’s external consciousness then revived, and he stood up, just like a dead man coming back to life. Opening his eyes with great difficulty, he saw the universe, along with himself.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā’s external (arvāk) senses (akṣa) recovered. Somehow, he stood up though as if he were dead since he was crushed by overbearing astonishment. He saw the universe (idam) along with himself.

### Text 59

*sapady evābhitaḥ paśyan diśo ’paśyat puraḥ-sthitam*  
*vṛndāvanaṁ janājīvya-drumākīrṇaṁ samā-priyam*

**Перевод:**

**Then, looking in all directions, Brahmā immediately saw Vṛndāvana before him, filled with trees, which were the means of livelihood for the inhabitants and where everything was dear to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Merciful Kṛṣṇa showed Brahmā, his disciple, Vṛndāvana, the shelter of his sweetness. Looking around in the directions he saw Vṛndāvana filled with trees with various tasty, juicy fruit(janājīvyaiḥ), in which everything was dear (samā-priyam).

### Text 60

*yatra naisarga-durvairāḥ sahāsan nṛ-mṛgādayaḥ*  
*mitrāṇīvājitāvāsa-druta-ruṭ-tarṣakādikam*

**Перевод:**

**In Vṛndāvana there is no anger or greed because of the permanent presence of Kṛṣṇa. There, naturally inimical animals and even human beings and animals live together as friends.**

**Комментарий:**

There, human and animals like tigers which are by nature enemies live together like friends. Anger, greed, etc., have fled (druta) bythe presence of the Lord (ajitāvāsa).

### Text 61

*tatrodvahat paśupa-vaṁśa-śiśutva-nāṭyaṁ*  
*brahmādvayaṁ param anantam agādha-bodham*  
*vatsān sakhīn iva purā parito vicinvad*  
*ekaṁ sa-pāṇi-kavalaṁ parameṣṭhy acaṣṭa*

**Перевод:**

**Then Lord Brahmā saw the Absolute Truth—who is one without a second, who is the supreme controller, who is unlimited, who is incomprehensible—possessing the form of a child in a family of cowherd men with a morsel of food in his hand, searching everywhere just as before for the calves and his cowherd friends.**

**Комментарий:**

Not playing in the forest and village with the manifested calves and boys in a manifested form, Kṛṣṇa was searching the real boys and calves situated here and there in his real form, since he was overwhelmed by his sense of friendship. He showed to Brahmā that real form, into which had entered the calves and boy forms which he had manifested. Brahmā (parameṣṭhī) saw that form in the Vṛndāvana just described (tatra). That form is described. He acted most skillfully (nāṭyam) in his role even as a child in a cowherd family.

Though seeing the calves in the green pastures and the boys on the bank of the river, Kṛṣṇa acted (nāṭyam) as if not seeing them so that Brahmā falsely feels that he was able to bewilder the Lord. He was one, since all the forms he manifested entered into him. Hewas devoid of two forms: jīva and prakṛti (advayam), or completely pure. The negative (a) is used since he is different from jīva andprakṛti. As śaktimān, he possesses jīva and prakṛti as his śaktis. He is supreme (param) since as aṁśī, he manifested all the other forms as his aṁśas. He was unlimited (ānantam) since present in him were unlimited such powers other than those manifested. He was of unfathomable intelligence since he could not be understood even by Balarāma. He searched for the calves even now as previously.

### Text 62

*dṛṣṭvā tvareṇa nija-dhoraṇato ’vatīrya*  
*pṛthvyāṁ vapuḥ kanaka-daṇḍam ivābhipātya*  
*spṛṣṭvā catur-mukuṭa-koṭibhir aṅghri-yugmaṁ*  
*natvā mud-aśru-sujalair akṛtābhiṣekam*

**Перевод:**

**After seeing this, Brahmā hastily got down from his swan carrier, fell down like a golden rod and touched the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa with the tips of the four crowns on his heads. Offering his obeisances, he bathed the feet of Kṛṣṇa with his tears of joy.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding, “this is svayaṁ-rūpa Brahman,” he dismounted his carrier (dhoranataḥ) and fell on the ground, transgressing the rule that devatās do not touch the earth, since this earth was the dhāma of Kṛṣṇa. He touched Kṛṣṇa’s feet with the tips of his four crowns. Thus due to turning his four heads which were in four directions towards Kṛṣṇa by force he bathed Kṛṣṇa’s feet in his tears.

### Text 63

*utthāyotthāya kṛṣṇasya cirasya pādayoḥ patan*  
*āste mahitvaṁ prāg-dṛṣṭaṁ smṛtvā smṛtvā punaḥ punaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Rising and falling again and again at the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa for a long time, Brahmā remembered over and over the Lord’s greatness he had just seen.**

**Комментарий:**

“Brahmā keeps falling” (patan āste) since he became stunned with bliss at the end of offering many obeisances. This verse is in the present tense because Śukadeva was directly experiencing the pastime.

### Text 64

*śanair athotthāya vimṛjya locane*  
*mukundam udvīkṣya vinamra-kandharaḥ*  
*kṛtāñjaliḥ praśrayavān samāhitaḥ*  
*sa-vepathur gadgadayailatelayā*

**Перевод:**

**Then, rising very gradually and wiping his two eyes, Brahmā looked up at Mukunda. Brahmā, his head bent low, his mind concentrated and his body trembling, very humbly began, with faltering words, to offer praises to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

He wiped his two eyes with two hands simultaneously. He praised (ailata) Kṛṣṇa with choked words (ilayā).

## Chapter 14 - Brahmā’s Prayers to Lord Kṛṣṇa

### Text 1

*śrī-brahmovāca*  
*naumīḍya te ’bhra-vapuṣe taḍid-ambarāya*  
*guñjāvataṁsa-paripiccha-lasan-mukhāya*  
*vanya-sraje kavala-vetra-viṣāṇa-veṇu-*  
*lakṣma-śriye mṛdu-pade paśupāṅgajāya*

**Перевод:**

**Brahmā said: O worshipable Lord! I offer my obeisances to you to attain you, Nanda’s son, having a body the complexion of a rain cloud, wearing cloth flashing like lightning, with face shining among peacock feathers and guñja berry decorations, with colorful forest garland, and possessing soft feet, his beauty enhanced by yogurt rice, stick, horn and flute.**

**Комментарий:**

*caturdaśe stutaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sarveśaḥ parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*śuddha-prīti-vidhau praśnottare ca paridarśinī*

**In the fourteenth chapter Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of all beings, is praised by Brahmā and shows through questions and answers the method of pure prema.**

Brahmā praises the dress of Kṛṣṇa, who is the guru by teaching the eighteen-syllable king of mantras, who is the Lord by givingopulence of the universe and who is seen with cowherd dress after the show of sweet greatness on the occasion for instructions.

O object of worship (īḍya)! I offer respects to you, worthy of praise by me since you possess sweet greatness. I praise you in order to attain you. The usage is like “I go for flowers” where the verb obtain (to obtain flowers) is understood. He is described. You have a body like a cloud and cloth like lightning. This suggests destroying all heat (suffering), and giving relief to the cātaka bird devotee of his. Your face shines with a guñja decoration and flowers on the head and ears and peacock feathers on his head. You have a garland made from Vṛndāvana leaves and flowers. You are beautiful with the signs (lakṣma) of a cowherd, with yogurt rice, stick, horn and flute. You have soft feet. You have been born to Nanda.

Similarly, śruti praises Kṛṣṇa as a cowherd, and Svayam Bhagavān Parabrahman.

*tad u hovāca hairaṇyaḥ \|*  
*gopa-veśam abhrābhaṁ taruṇaṁ kalpa-drumāśritam \|*

**Brahmā spoke to them. The form of Kṛṣṇa wears the dress of a cowherd. He has the complexion of a cloud. He is youthful and sits under a desire tree.**

*tad iha ślokā bhavanti—*  
*sat-puṇḍarīka-nayanaṁ meghābhaṁ vaidyutāmbaram \|*  
*dvi-bhujaṁ jñāna-mudrāḍhyaṁ vana-mālinam īśvaram*  
*gopa-gopī-gavāvītaṁ sura-druma-talāśrayam \|*

**Meditating with concentration on two-armed lotus-eyed, silent Kṛṣṇa, who has the complexion of a cloud, who wears cloth flashing like lightning and a garland, who is surrounded by cowherds, gopīs and cows, who is bedecked with shining ornaments, while sitting under a desire tree. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

### Text 2

*asyāpi deva vapuṣo mad-anugrahasya*  
*svecchā-mayasya tanu-bhūta-mayasya ko ’pi*  
*neśe mahi tv avasituṁ manasāntareṇa*  
*sākṣāt tavaiva kim utātma-sukhānubhūteḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Even by controlling the mind, no one can understand the greatness of this form of the Lord of the universe, which manifested in many four-armed forms, but which is actually you, the one form of Svayam Bhagavān, who gave me mercy by you own will, who spread through the universe in many spiritual forms and possess bliss which can be understood only by yourself.**

**Комментарий:**

“What are the powers in me, a young cowherd, that I am praised even by Brahmā, master of the universe and omniscient?” This isshown using kaimutya. O Lord, worshippable by all (deva)! Even, I, Brahmā (kaḥ), cannot understand (avasitum) the greatness of thebody of Vāsudeva, dark-like a cloud (asya vapuṣaḥ), manifested now by you. What to speak of others who are created by me. Though I committed offense, you showed mercy to me, “Let his bewilderment go away.” You are controlled by the desires of yourdevotees (svecchā-amayasya). You fulfilled my desire to see your sweet glories because I too am your servant.

“That body you saw somehow or other was made of māyā.” That body is not made of māyā (na tu bhūtamayasya). It is made of knowledge and bliss as stated in satya-jñānānantānanda: the Lord is existence, knowledge, unlimited and bliss. (SB [10.13.54](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/13.54)) Even by controlled mind (manasāntareṇa) I cannot understand the greatness of you, the cowherd boy, directly the aṁśī what to speak of describing you. He is further described. You experience extraordinary happiness arising from playing with cowherds and cows (ātmā-sukhānubhūteḥ) since the śruti says, gopa-gopī- gavāvītam: he is surrounded by cowherds, gopīs and cows. (Gopāla- tāpanī Upaniṣad)

I cannot understand the greatness of your svāṁśas. How can I understand the greatness of you in your svayaṁ-rūpa, as the aṁśī.

### Text 3

*jñāne prayāsam udapāsya namanta eva*  
*jīvanti san-mukharitāṁ bhavadīya-vārtām*  
*sthāne sthitāḥ śruti-gatāṁ tanu-vāṅ-manobhi*  
*r ye prāyaśo ’jita jito ’py asi tais tri-lokyām*

**Перевод:**

**Those who give up attempts to understand your powers, who live constantly in devotional association, and who pass their lives respecting topics about you and your associates with the ear, by body, mind and words, which they proclaim loudly, bring you under control, though you cannot be controlled by anyone in the three worlds.**

**Комментарий:**

“If even you cannot understand my glory, then how can the ignorant cross saṁsāra? Śruti says that it can be crossed by knowledge,jñātvā devaṁ sarva-pāśāpahāni: Knowing the Lord, destroying all piety and sin, he destroys all karmas. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad [1.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sveta-bs/1.11))”

O unconquered one! Though not conquered in the three worlds, you are generally controlled by those who have faith in your topics (taiḥ), who — giving up (udapāsya) endeavor for complete knowledge concerning your svarūpa with unlimited forms, qualities and powers, offering respects by words to your topics, by which saints, though having taken vows of silence, are made talkative — only live, i.e., they do nothing else, and who stay in their own places, not travelling to tīrthas. Those topics enter the ear by nature, just by contact (śruti-gatām). Since one is delivered from saṁsāra by understanding your topics, and since what is the use of knowledge of all topics as the person is incapable of knowing it all.

### Text 4

*śreyaḥ-sṛtiṁ bhaktim udasya te vibho*  
*kliśyanti ye kevala-bodha-labdhaye*  
*teṣām asau kleśala eva śiṣyate*  
*nānyad yathā sthūla-tuṣāvaghātinām*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! If fools give up bhakti, the all-inclusive path, and suffer to attain realization of ātmā without bhakti, they simply attain suffering and nothing else. They are like fools who beat empty husks.**

**Комментарий:**

Not performing easy bhakti, those who attempt complete jñāna experience suffering. Those who give up your bhakti, a flow ofauspiciousness of liberation, which is commencing (śreya-sṛtim), suffer. It is like a waterfall from an inexhaustible lake. That bhaktiis composed of hearing your topics. Giving up bhakti they suffer to attain understanding of oneness. That understanding gives suffering (kleśalam). Just as leaving a small pile of rice and threshing a pile empty husk gives suffering.

### Text 5

*pureha bhūman bahavo ’pi yoginas*  
*tvad-arpitehā-nija-karma-labdhayā*  
*vibudhya bhaktyaiva kathopanītayā*  
*prapedire ’ñjo ’cyuta te gatiṁ parām*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord possessing unlimited glory! O Lord who does not fail his devotee! Many yogīs in the past, offering their activities to you and developing realization through devotional activities, easily attained your association.**

**Комментарий:**

He shows the proper conduct. O powerful lord (bhūman)! In this world (iha) many yogīs previously (purā), not attaining you directly by yoga methods, by bhakti accompanied with (labdhayā) offering their karmas and actions (īhā) to you, by increasing topics concerning you (kathopanītayā), realizing (vibhudhya) you, easily attained your supreme shelter. Īhā refers to material actions andnija-karma refers to Vedic karmas like agni-hotra.

### Text 6

*tathāpi bhūman mahimā-guṇasya te*  
*viboddhum arhaty amalāntar-ātmabhiḥ*  
*avikriyāt svānubhavād arūpato*  
*hy ananya-bodhyātmatayā na cānyathā*

**Перевод:**

**O great Lord! The greatness of one among your qualities may be realized by persons with pure hearts but not otherwise, according to his realization, without material sense objects and without material desires, and only through the Upaniṣads.**

**Комментарий:**

“You said that I am realized by bhakti. That depends on knowledge. How can one give up the attempts of jñāna?”

O powerful lord (bhūman)! Though that is so, some learned person who endeavors extremely can know, by pure (amala) functions ofhis antaḥkaraṇa, the wealth of glory of one of your qualities such as mercy, like one bud among many, but not everyone.

*catur-mukhāyur yadi ko ‘pi vaktā bhaven naraḥ kvāpi viśuddha-cetāḥ*  
*\| sa te guṇānāṁ ayutaikam aṁśaṁ vaden na vā devavara prasīda*

**If someone for the life of Brahmā and having a pure heart speaks, he may not speak one portion of your millions of qualities. O Lord! Be pleased with me. (Varāha Purāṇa)**

“Like seeing form with the eye, cannot a person understand your glory with his mind?” Without purity one cannot do so (nacānyatha). Purity of mind is required since the śruti says:

*āhāra-śuddhau sattva-śuddhiḥ*  
*, sattva-śuddhau dhruvā smṛtiḥ*

**If food is pure, the mind is pure. If the mind is pure, memory of the Lord is steady. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad** [**7.26**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/chan-upa/part-7.chapter-26.7261)**)**

What is the cause of the understanding? It is one’s own realization (svānubhavāt). One understands in accordance to one’s realization, but not entirely. The understanding is without sense objects (arūpataḥ). It is devoid of contact with material sound, touch, etc. It is devoid of desire for other qualities. The type of that realization is described. The svarūpa (ātmatayā) of the realization is understood only by the evidence of Upaniṣads (ananya-bodhā). The Lord’s qualities are understood by the Upaniṣads, just as fragrance is understood by smelling.

Thus, giving up attempts at complete knowledge, one should perform even one aṅga of bhakti. By the knowledge within that bhakti, like the fiber in a lotus stem, after purification of the heart, one will attain the Lord’s feet.

### Text 7

*guṇātmanas te ’pi guṇān vimātuṁ*  
*hitāvatīrṇasya ka īśire ’sya*  
*kālena yair vā vimitāḥ su-kalpair*  
*bhū-pāṁśavaḥ khe mihikā dyu-bhāsaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In time, skilled people might be able to count all the atoms of the earth, the particles of snow, or perhaps even the photons in the sky. But who could possibly count the unlimited transcendental qualities possessed by you, the possessor of all qualities, who have descended to display those qualities for the benefit of all living entities?**

**Комментарий:**

No persons can know all your qualities since they are unlimited. Thus he speaks this verse. The qualities are the self (guṇāḥ ātmanaḥ)since it is said, samasta-kalyāṇa-guṇātmako ‘sau: the Lord is endowed with all auspicious qualities. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) Who can even count your qualities, which are non-different from your svarūpa? Īśāṁ cakrire becomes īśire by poetic license. What to speak of realizing them? You have appeared to benefit the world (hita).

“But what is impossible for skillful people over time?” Vā indicates questioning. The atoms of earth, snowflakes in the sky or stars in the heavens may be counted over a long time by skillful people (sukalpaiḥ). But even Śeṣa cannot count your qualities.

### Text 8

*tat te ’nukampāṁ su-samīkṣamāṇo*  
*bhuñjāna evātma-kṛtaṁ vipākam*  
*hṛd-vāg-vapurbhir vidadhan namas te*  
*jīveta yo mukti-pade sa dāya-bhāk*

**Перевод:**

**One who earnestly waits for you to bestow your mercy upon him, all the while patiently suffering the reactions of his past misdeeds and passes his life by offering you respectful obeisances with his heart, words and body, is the rightful claimant of you, the shelter of liberation.**

**Комментарий:**

Therefore, giving up attempts at jñāna, one should perform bhakti according to one’s ability. One who waits patiently thinking, “When will you show me mercy?” while experiencing happiness and suffering, the results of karma (vipākam) earned by one’s own previous actions, and which are given by the Lord with a desire to benefit the person, like a father who gives both sweet rice and nīma juice, and who offers respect by his heart, words and body to the Lord and does not suffer by excessively performing vratas, such a person, situated in an authorized sampradāya (jīveta), becomes the recipient of liberation and service to the Lord’s feet (mukti-padam).

While living, one is entitled to the father’s inheritance. One cannot receive it if one is not living. Similarly, remaining on the path ofbhakti as described in the Vedas, one becomes the recipient of the Lord’s lotus feet, and not otherwise.

### Text 9

*paśyeśa me ’nāryam ananta ādye*  
*parātmani tvayy api māyi-māyini*  
*māyāṁ vitatyekṣitum ātma-vaibhavaṁ*  
*hy ahaṁ kiyān aiccham ivārcir agnau*

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, just see my uncivilized impudence! To test your power I tried to extend my māyā over you, the unlimited power, my father, the master of māyā. What am I compared to you? I am just like a small spark in the presence of a great fire.**

**Комментарий:**

The devotee is the rightful recipient of your mercy. But I am an offender. Brahmā speaks with regret.

O Lord! See my wickedness and foolishness. Considering this, punish or forgive me. He shows his wickedness and foolishness. You, my father (ādye) due to being my cause, were enjoying with your friends. This shows his wickedness. You possess unrestrictedpowers (anante), the bewilderer (māyini) of even other bewilderers. This shows his foolishness. In this way, I desired to see your powers (ātma-vaibhavam), spreading bewildering māyā to you. Ah! I can do nothing to you just as a spark can do nothing to the fire from which it arose.

### Text 10

*ataḥ kṣamasvācyuta me rajo-bhuvo*  
*hy ajānatas tvat-pṛthag-īśa-māninaḥ*  
*ajāvalepāndha-tamo-’ndha-cakṣuṣa*  
*eṣo ’nukampyo mayi nāthavān iti*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O infallible Lord, kindly excuse my offenses. I have taken birth in the mode of passion, ignorant, presuming myself a controller independent of you. My eyes are blinded by pride and ignorance, which causes me to think of myself as the unborn creator of the universe. You should think, “Since Brahmā is my servant, dedicated to me, he is worthy of my compassion.”**

**Комментарий:**

You will forgive me, though I deserve to be punished, since you are most merciful.

O Lord who never deviates from mercy (acyuta)! Forgive my offence of thinking I am a controller independent of you. I am the shelter of rajoguṇa (rajo-bhuvaḥ) and thus ignorant, with eyes blinded by deep darkness in the form of pride (avalepa), thinking “I am the son of the unborn Lord and I am the creator of the universe.”

“For what reason should I forgive you?”

This Brahmā is the object of my mercy since he, though existing independently elsewhere, is a servant (nāthavān) near me, he is aservant dependent on me. Nāthavān means dependent according to Amara-kośa.

### Text 11

*kvāhaṁ tamo-mahad-ahaṁ-kha-carāgni-vār-bhū-*  
*saṁveṣṭitāṇḍa-ghaṭa-sapta-vitasti-kāyaḥ*  
*kvedṛg-vidhāvigaṇitāṇḍa-parāṇu-caryā-*  
*vātādhva-roma-vivarasya ca te mahitvam*

**Перевод:**

**What am I, a small creature measuring seven spans of my own hand, enclosed in a potlike universe composed of material nature, the total material energy, false ego, ether, air, fire, water and earth? And what is your glory, when unlimited universes pass through the pores of your body just as particles of dust pass through the openings of a screened window when you create and destroy?**

**Комментарий:**

“You, Brahmā, the form of the universe, the creator of everything, are also the supreme controller.”

What am I? I have a body measuring just seven hands, in the pot- like universe with planets from Pātāla to Satya-loka, surrounded by the elements of earth, water (vār), fire, air (cara), ether (kha), ahaṅkāra, mahat-tattva and prakṛti (tamas). And what is your power? You have hair pores which act as air passages for uncountable such universes wandering in and out like atoms, during creation and destruction. This refers to Karaṇodaśayī Viṣṇu. My powers over you are like a grasshopper’s on Garuḍa.

### Text 12

*utkṣepaṇaṁ garbha-gatasya pādayoḥ*  
*kiṁ kalpate mātur adhokṣajāgase*  
*kim asti-nāsti-vyapadeśa-bhūṣitaṁ*  
*tavāsti kukṣeḥ kiyad apy anantaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O controller of the senses! Does a mother take offense when the child within her womb kicks with his legs? And is there anything in existence—whether designated by various philosophers as real or as unreal—that is actually outside your form known as Hiraṇyagarbha antaryāmī?**

**Комментарий:**

You must necessarily tolerate my offense to you. Does the kicking of the child’s feet in the womb become an offense to the mother? No. So what is my offense since I came from your womb? Nothing of the world of jīvas and matter situated in objects designated as conscious or unconscious exists outside (anantaḥ) your womb. The subject of existing and non-existing is discussed in Viṣṇu Purāṇa:

*jyotīṁṣi viṣṇur bhuvanāni viṣṇur*  
*vanāniviṣṇur girayo diśaś ca*  
*nadyaḥ samudrāś ca sa eva sarvaṁ*  
*yad asti yan nāsti ca vipra-varya*

**Viṣṇu is the planets. Viṣṇu is the worlds. Viṣṇu is the forests, mountains and directions. He is the rivers and oceans. He alone is everything which is conscious and unconscious, O best of the vipras. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa** [**2.12.38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/2.12.38)**)**

Since being within the universe, I am also within your womb, you should tolerate my offense. You have said:

*pitāham asya jagto mātā dhātā pitāmaha*

**I am the father of the universe, the mother, the maintainer and the grandfather. (BG** [**9.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.17)**)**

Here Kṛṣṇa is considered one with Garbhodaśayī Viṣṇu.

### Text 13

*jagat-trayāntodadhi-samplavode*  
*nārāyaṇasyodara-nābhi-nālāt*  
*vinirgato ’jas tv iti vāṅ na vai mṛṣā*  
*kintv īśvara tvan na vinirgato ’smi*

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord! It is said that Brahmā came out of the lotus in the navel on Nārāyaṇa’s belly in the water of devastation of the universe. Certainly, these words are not false. Thus am I not born from you?**

**Комментарий:**

“The son comes out of the womb of the mother. When did you come out of my womb?”

At the time of destruction of the three worlds, in the waters which became one, Brahmā (ajaḥ) came out of the stem in the navel on the belly of Nārāyaṇa. These words are certainly (vai) not false. O Lord! That being so, did I not come from you? Yes, I did.

### Text 14

*nārāyaṇas tvaṁ na hi sarva-dehinām*  
*ātmāsy adhīśākhila-loka-sākṣī*  
*nārāyaṇo ’ṅgaṁ nara-bhū-jalāyanāt*  
*tac cāpi satyaṁ na tavaiva māyā*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, Svayam Bhagavān! Nārāyaṇa is definitely you. You pervade all beings. You are the knower of all planets. Nārāyaṇa is your aṁśa since he is the source of all the elements. That form is real, not created by your material māyā. Nor is the third puruṣa, dwelling within all beings, nor is the second puruṣa, the witness of all planets. Mahā-viṣṇu, called Nārāyaṇa because he is the shelter of the Kāraṇa Ocean, which gives rise to material creation, is simply your expansion. That expansion of yours is real, not illusory.**

**Комментарий:**

“Let you be the son of Nārāyaṇa. How did I, the son of Nanda, become part of this topic?”

You are not at all Nārāyaṇa? This is uttered in lamentation. This means “Yes, you become Nārāyaṇa.” Why? You pervade (ātmā) allbeings. The derivation of the word Nārāyaṇa is he who pervades (āyana) all jīvas (nāra). You directly see all the worlds (akhila-loka- sākṣī). Another derivation of Nārāyaṇa is “he who knows (āyana) all jīvas (nāram).”

“The derivation of the word Nārāyaṇa is something else.”

He who is famous as Nārāyaṇa, the first puruṣa, is your svāṁśa (aṅgaṁ) since he is the source of all tattvas such as mahat-tattva(nara-bhū) and water (jalāyanāt) of Kāraṇa ocean which arise from him. Smṛti says:

*narāj jātāni tattvāni nārāṇīti vidur budhāḥ \|*  
*tasya tāny ayanaṁ pūrvaṁ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ*

**The elements of creation that arise from the Lord (nara) are known by wise as nāra. They acted first as his shelter (ayanam). Thus the puruṣa is known as Nārāyaṇa. (Mahābhārata 13.124.22)**

*āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai nara-sūnavaḥ \|*  
*ayanaṁ tasya tāḥ pūrvaṁ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ*

**The word āpaḥ and nārā are synonymous for “water” since the waters are considered the sons of Nara, the primeval male or Mahā-viṣṇu. Since these waters act as the bed (ayana) of Mahā-viṣṇu from the ancient past, he is called Nārāyaṇa. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa** [**1.4.6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/1.4.6)**)**

O lord of lords, Svayam Bhagavān (adhīśa)! Kāraṇodaśāyī, within whom are situated mahat-tattva and other elements, is my fatherwho lies on the Garbhoda ocean. Since he is an aṁśa of your aṁśa, I am your offspring. Thus, you should forgive my offense. Moreover, Nārāyaṇa, your svāṁśa is spiritual (satyaṁ), and condensed knowledge in all time and space, but not products of your māyā. It is not material like the universal form. The word api indicates appropriateness, meaning, “this is appropriate.”

### Text 15

*tac cej jala-sthaṁ tava saj jagad-vapuḥ*  
*kiṁ me na dṛṣṭaṁ bhagavaṁs tadaiva*  
*kiṁ vā su-dṛṣṭaṁ hṛdi me tadaiva*  
*kiṁ no sapady eva punar vyadarśi*

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord, if your body, which shelters the entire universe, lies on the water, then why were you not seen by me when I searched for you? And why did you appear clearly in my heart? Why did you not then appear to my external vision?**

**Комментарий:**

“Garbhodaśayī is not spiritual entity since he is limited. The all- pervading and infinitesimal are also accepted like that. In this way Kāraṇodaśayī (his source) must also be material.”

If your body called Nārāyaṇa, which resembles the existing universe, is situated on water, then why was it not seen then by me who entered within through the lotus-stem meditating for a hundred years? O Lord endowed with inconceivable powers!

“Because of ignorance, you did not see me situated on that water.” When I meditated, why then did I see you excellently in my heart. Then in a moment why did I not again see you? In this way though that body is situated in the water, it is all-pervading having theuniverse situated in the belly. Thus, it is spiritual entity and rests on the Kāraṇa ocean. Your mercy and indifference are the reasons for seeing and not seeing you.

### Text 16

*atraiva māyā-dhamanāvatāre*  
*hy asya prapañcasya bahiḥ sphuṭasya*  
*kṛtsnasya cāntar jaṭhare jananyā*  
*māyātvam eva prakaṭī-kṛtaṁ te*

**Перевод:**

**O subduer of māyā! Appearing in this incarnation, you manifested the whole universe, in your abdomen to your mother, even though it was clearly visible externally as well.**

**Комментарий:**

“It is contradictory to be a form situated in the water, within the universe, and to have the universe in its womb.”

O controller of prakṛti (māyā-dhamana)! In your appearance as Svayam Bhagavān (atra avatāre), you have manifested your acintya-śakti (māyātvam) by showing to your mother inside your belly the entire universe which is seen outside your belly. I have understood this. Your body being situated within the universe and the universe being situated within you — both are accomplished by your acintya-śakti. Now also, since I am situated in your belly, like a mother, tolerate my offense.

### Text 17

*yasya kukṣāv idaṁ sarvaṁ sātmaṁ bhāti yathā tathā*  
*tat tvayy apīha tat sarvaṁ kim idaṁ māyayā vinā*

**Перевод:**

**Just as this entire universe, including you, was exhibited within your abdomen, so it is now manifested here externally within you. How could such things happen unless arranged by your māyā?**

**Комментарий:**

“But my mother saw a reflection of the external universe on my shining body, like a face seen in a mirror. It was not actually inside me.”

Just as this universe exists in your belly, it exists here, outside your belly also. It exists along with you (sātmaṁ). Thus the reflection is rejected. One does not see the mirror within the mirror. The universe situated in your belly (tvayi), supported by you, is alsooutside you. Therefore (tad), because the two forms are not different at all, these two displays cannot take place except by acintya-śakti (māyayā).

### Text 18

*adyaiva tvad ṛte ’sya kiṁ mama na te māyātvam ādarśitam*  
*eko ’si prathamaṁ tato vraja-suhṛd-vatsāḥ samastā api*  
*tāvanto ’si catur-bhujās tad akhilaiḥ sākaṁ mayopāsitās*  
*tāvanty eva jaganty abhūs tad amitaṁ brahmādvayaṁ śiṣyate*

**Перевод:**

**Today, apart from you, the calves and cowherd boys and four- armed forms you manifested, all that I saw of the material realm and the beings worshipping you was nothing but your māyā. First you were alone, then you were all the calves and boys and then you became the four-armed forms in all the universes which were worshipped by persons all in the universe including me. Then you remained as the unlimited Brahman different from jīva and prakṛti.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, your mother saw the universe inside your belly and outside as well. Millions of universes wander in the hair pores of your Kāraṇodaśāyī form. All this is created by your māyā made of the three guṇas. This is what I believed till now. But today I realize that it is an unchanging creation composed of knowledge and bliss from your spiritual acintya-śakti. With hairs standing on end, Brahmā makes this statement.

Can the covered forms related to the group of Vāsudeva seen in this sweet glory arise without you? Rather everything is of your nature. You showed me the māyā of parā-śakti related to the group of Vāsudevas. How was this? First you were standing alone. Then you became all the cowherd boys and all the calves. Then covering them up, you became those many four-armed forms that manifested, which were worshipped by Lakṣmī (mayā) and all the tattvas (akhiliaḥ sākam). You became those many universes, globes full of knowledge. Then, covering all of that, immeasurable advaya (different from jīva and prakṛti) Brahman remained. It isimmeasurable (amita), all-pervading because everything is within you.

Like before expect you what did you become? Since it is said, “you became” and since iti not said, “by māyā you became,” Brahmā shows that the appearance of Nanda’ son along with the cowherd boys and the universe arose by the superior śakti alone (The versedoes not state that Kṛṣṇa became all these by material māyā). This is called śuddha-sarga in Nārada-pañcarātra.

*śuddha-sargam ahaṁ deva jñātum icchāmi tattvataḥ*  
*sarga-dvayasya caivāsya yaḥ paratvena vartate*

**O Lord! I desire to know in truth about the pure creation which is superior to the two creations (jīva and matter).**

### Text 19

*ajānatāṁ tvat-padavīm anātmany*  
*ātmātmanā bhāsi vitatya māyām*  
*sṛṣṭāv ivāhaṁ jagato vidhāna*  
*iva tvam eṣo ’nta iva trinetraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**For persons ignorant of your actual position, you appear in the material world, spreading māyā. For the creation of the universe you appear like me \[Brahmā\], for its maintenance you appear like Viṣṇu, and for its annihilation you appear like Śiva.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Brahmā! Others do not speak about me in the way that you speak.”

That is true. Those to whom you show great mercy speak in this way. Others know you as follows: there is some controller; he for the sake of the world, as Brahmā, etc., performs creation, etc., and as Vāmana, etc., helps the devatās. They know only this much, not more. This is expressed in two verses.

For those who do not know the method and conclusion of the pastimes of your superior śakti, not worshipping those who do know, you who are engaged as the controller (ātmā) of prakṛti (anātmani), spreading māyā independently (ātmanā), shine. How? Like for creation, you are me, Brahmā (ahaṁ), and for maintenance (vidhāne) you are Viṣṇu (eṣaḥ). And for destruction you are Śiva(trinetraḥ). Viṣṇu’s name is not mentioned since he is nondifferent from Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 20

*sureṣv ṛṣiṣv īśa tathaiva nṛṣv api*  
*tiryakṣu yādaḥsv api te ’janasya*  
*janmāsatāṁ durmada-nigrahāya*  
*prabho vidhātaḥ sad-anugrahāya ca*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! O supreme creator! You have no material birth, yet to defeat the false pride of the faithless demons and show mercy to your devotees, you take birth among the devatās, sages, human beings, animals and even the aquatics.**

**Комментарий:**

You are devoid of contact with a previous body (ajanasya). You take birth among the devatās as Vāmana, among the sages as Bhārgava (i.e. Paraśurāma), among men as Śrī Rāmacandra, among animals as Varāha and among fish as Matsya.

### Text 21

*ko vetti bhūman bhagavan parātman*  
*yogeśvarotīr bhavatas tri-lokyām*  
*kvāho kathaṁ vā kati vā kadeti*  
*vistārayan krīḍasi yoga-māyām*

**Перевод:**

**O unrestricted Lord! O Lord endowed with all powers! O Supersoul! O Lord spread throughout all time! Who knows where, how, how many, and when your pastimes will take place in the universe? Spreading yoga-māyā, you play.**

**Комментарий:**

“My creation full of knowledge produced by superior yogamāyā as previously described takes place in how much area, by what method, in how much time? How extensive is it? Do you know or not?”

O Lord of unlimited forms spread throughout the universe (bhūman)! O Lord full of all six opulences (bhagavan)! O antaryāmī of all jīvas in bondage or liberated (parātman)! O master of supreme yoga (yogeśvara)! Who knows your pastimes of, birth, etc., (ūtī),accomplished within the material creation (tri-lokyam)? No one knows since where, how, when or how many you perform. How do these pastimes occur simultaneously by your unlimited forms full of the six opulences? That is answered. You distribute your yoga-māyā.

*svarūpa-bhūtayā nitya-śaktyā māyākhyayā yutaḥ \|*  
*ato māyāmayaṁ viṣṇuṁ pravadanti sanātanam*

**The Lord is endowed with his eternal śakti called māyā arising from his svarūpa. Thus, the wise call eternal Viṣṇu māyā-mayam, made of māyā. (Caturveda-śikhā)**

Everything is carried out by your śakti, described in the above śruti, which is inconceivable.

### Text 22

*tasmād idaṁ jagad aśeṣam asat-svarūpaṁ*  
*svapnābham asta-dhiṣaṇaṁ puru-duḥkha-duḥkham*  
*tvayy eva nitya-sukha-bodha-tanāv anante*  
*māyāta udyad apiyat sad ivāvabhāti*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore this entire universe, which like a dream is by nature unreal, nevertheless appears real, and thus it covers one’s consciousness and assails one with repeated miseries. This universe appears real because it is manifested by the potency of illusion emanating from you, whose unlimited form is full of eternal happiness and knowledge.**

**Комментарий:**

But this universe controlled by me is temporary since it is material. Apart from the creation full of knowledge, there is this unlimited universe, an unattractive form (asat-svarūpam), temporary like a dream (svapnābham). It is where knowledge is lost (asta-dhiṣaṇam).Thus it is the very form of suffering (puru-duḥkha) for even its happiness is full of suffering, like honey mixed with poison. Where did it come from? It arises (udyat) from the three guṇas of māyā (māyātaḥ) situated in your shelter (tvayi), and it disappears (apiyat) into the three guṇas, yet for the ignorant it appears to be glorious (sat). It is situated in you who have a body of Brahman, in the form of eternal joy and knowledge (nitya-sukha-bodha-tanau).

### Text 23

*ekas tvam ātmā puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ*  
*satyaḥ svayaṁ-jyotir ananta ādyaḥ*  
*nityo ’kṣaro ’jasra-sukho nirañjanaḥ*  
*pūrṇo’dvayo mukta upādhito ’mṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You are the one supreme soul, the supreme person, the oldest, the truth, self-manifested, unlimited, the beginning, eternal, indestructible, unlimited happiness, pure, full, without a second, free of upādhis and deathless.**

**Комментарий:**

The svarūpa of the universe of jīvas and matter is not glorious: it is like a dream full of suffering. It arises from māyā under yourshelter. In this verse Brahmā distinguishes the svarūpa of Bhagavān from that. You are one ātmā, since though taking the forms of many cowherd boys, you have not given up being one. Śruti says:

*eko ‘pi san bahudhā yo ‘vabhāti*

**Though one he appears as many. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

Smṛti says:

*ekāneka-svarūpāya*

**I offer respects to the Lord who has one and many forms. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa)**

“Is this ātmā without form as propounded by the logicians.” No. You are a person (puruṣaḥ) possessing face, feet, hands and belly. This is called puruṣa-vidha in Taittarīya Upaniṣad [2.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/taittiriya/2.5).

“Is this form recent like those of ordinary people?” No. It is ancient (purāṇaḥ).

“Since I am the son of Nanda, I am recent.” No. You in all three aspects of time (satyaḥ) and previously also were his son.

“Am I manifested like other people by time, etc.?” No, you are self-manifesting (svayaṁ jyotiḥ).

“Am I limited then like a lamp?” No. You are unlimited, in all places (anantaḥ).

“Matsya and other avatāras are also like that. Which among them am I?” You are the avatārī, svayaṁ-rūpa (ādyaḥ) since the smṛtisays: kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam. (SB [1.3.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/3.28))

“Will I remain like that even at mahā-pralaya?” You are eternal (nityaḥ) always existing in your form. Even then you will exist as you are now.

“Seeing transformations of states of things with form, would I also transform?” You are without transformation (akṣaraḥ).

“Seeing persons sometimes subject to suffering, would I also suffer?” No. You have eternal happiness.

“In infancy I was greedy for yogurt. During paugaṇḍa age, I became angry at Kāliya. During kaiśora age I had passion for the young gopīs. I am contaminated with these.” No. You are spotless (nirañjanaḥ). You are pure since these qualities arise from your svarūpa.

“Since I depend on yogurt and the young gopīs, I am not complete in myself.” No. You are complete (pūrṇaḥ) since they are all yourvibhūtis. You are different from jīva and prakṛti (advayaḥ).

“Others say that I have upādhis.” No. You are free from upādhis since the śruti says:

*sākṣāt prakṛti-paro ‘yam ātmā gopālaḥ*  
*Kṛṣṇa is above prakṛti. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)*

**Being worshipped, because of you there is no death(amṛtaḥ). You give liberation.**

*govindān mṛtyur bibheti*

**Death fears Govinda. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

### Text 24

*evaṁ-vidhaṁ tvāṁ sakalātmanām api*  
*svātmānam ātmātmatayā vicakṣate*  
*gurv-arka-labdhopaniṣat-sucakṣuṣā*  
*ye te tarantīva bhavānṛtāmbudhim*

**Перевод:**

**Those who realize by obtaining clear vision of the Upaniṣads from the guru who is like the sun, and realize you as described previously, the highest person, as the soul of all souls, easily cross the false ocean of material existence.**

**Комментарий:**

Those who worship you easily attain liberation. They meditate (vicakṣate) on you, the splendid (su) ātmā of all kṣetra-jñas (jīvas)since you are the attractive puruṣa, as their antaryāmī and as their master (ātmātmatayā). How? They meditate by discernment(cakṣusā) arising from the Upaniṣad statement, eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛta: The ātmā, full of knowledge and bliss is your eternal (amṛtaḥ) antaryāmī (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad), which is learned from a guru who is indeed the sun. In the Upaniṣad statement, the meaning is that the Lord’s nature of antaryāmī is eternal. The word te (your) is connected not to ātmā but to antaryāmī since if it were not so, there would be the fault of the sixth case becoming figurative.

They cross the ocean of bad karmic results (bhavānṛtāmbudhim). The word ṛtam is used to mean good karmic results as in ṛtaṁ pibantau: experiencing good karmas. (Kena Upaniṣad) The word iva is used to suggest that they cross saṁsāra easily like steppingover the water in a calf’s hoofprint.

### Text 25

*ātmānam evātmatayāvijānatāṁ*  
*tenaiva jātaṁ nikhilaṁ prapañcitam*  
*jñānena bhūyo ’pi ca tat pralīyate*  
*rajjvām aher bhoga-bhavābhavau yathā*

**Перевод:**

**A person who mistakes a rope for a snake becomes fearful, but he then gives up his fear upon realizing that the so-called snake does not exist. Similarly, for those who fail to recognize the Lord who pervades them, by aversion to you, the world of saṁsāra is produced. That is destroyed by knowledge of you.**

**Комментарий:**

It is very difficult for persons ignorant of this knowledge of the Upaniṣads to cross saṁsāra. Ātmā means what manifests, what is attained (atati) by the liberated souls. For those who do not know you, who are full of knowledge and bliss (ātmānam) as their master and as one who pervades them (ātmatayā), by that lack of knowledge, by that aversion to you (tena), possessiveness of house and body and identity as “I” are manifested (nikhilaṁ prapañcitaṁ jātaṁ) again and again (bhūyaḥ) since it is said:

*bhayaṁ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād*  
*īśād apetasya viparyayo ‘smṛtiḥ*

**For the jīva averse to the Lord, there will be saṁsāra consisting of identity with body and lack of identity with the soul, because of his absorption in the material coverings on the soul, arising from the Lord’s māyā. (SB** [**11.2.37**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.37)**)**

That is destroyed by jñāna concerning you as described previously.

An example is given. Just as because of ignorance of the nature of a rope, one thinks it to be a snake, but with knowledge, oneunderstands that it is not a snake. Some say that Brahmā taught vivarta-vāda, with the appearance of an something unreal, because of using the example of the rope and snake. They say that from ignorance (mistake) concerning a rope a snake appears, and from knowledge of it, it disappears. Even while it manifests, it is an illusion only. Similarly, from ignorance that the self (ātmā) is non-dual consciousness alone (cin-mātrā) the material world appears. From knowledge of it, it disappears. During its manifestation that world is called an illusion. The persons who claim this should be questioned. Where does this ignorance exist? Whom does it belong to? If you say it manifest in Brahman, that cannot be. This contradicts the śruti, satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ brahma: Brahman is existence, infinite and knowledge. (Taittīrya Upaniṣad) yaḥ sarva- jñaḥ sarva-vit: the Lord knows everything generally and specifically. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) By everything other than ātmā being false, by equating the statements of Vedas such as yato va imāni bhūtāni: from the Lord arises all beings (Taittirīya Upaniṣad), to statements like “this is the son of a barren women,” there is the difficulty that these philosophers are ultimately atheists. And because of claiming the falsity of the world that philosophy also runs the risk of being voidism.
