Rather this example just teaches this much that saṁsāra arises because of being averse to the Lord. But by recognizing the Lord saṁsāra is destroyed. One should see the details in the commentary on the ananyatvādhikaraṇa in the Govinda-bhāṣya of Brahma-sūtras and in Siddhānta-ratnam.

### Text 26

*ajñāna-saṁjñau bhava-bandha-mokṣau*  
*dvau nāma nānyau sta ṛta-jña-bhāvāt*  
*ajasra-city ātmani kevale pare*  
*vicāryamāṇe taraṇāv ivāhanī*

**Перевод:**

**Bondage and liberation are defined as ignorance and nothing more since the jīva is real and has the capacity for knowledge. When one reflects on the Lord, who is separate from matter, pure, constantly omniscient, untouched by matter, these states no longer exist, just as, day and night do not exist for the sun.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of lack of knowledge about you as Paramātmā, the jīva end up in saṁsāra as described. That saṁsāra is destroyed by knowledge of you in truth. But Paramātmā is eternally beyond saṁsāra. That is explained in this verse. The jīva is an object (bhāvāt) which is real (ṛta) and has knowledge as its quality (jña). Ablative can express a missing verb particle ending in ya. Thus, the meaning of ṛta-jña- bhāvāt is “concerning the jīva which is real and a knower.”

Ajñāna-saṁjñau means understood or discerned by the destruction of true knowledge, by knowledge that you are similar to otherobjects. Saṁsāra, with possessiveness of body and house (bhava- bandha) and its destruction (mokṣau) are discerned out of ignorance and nothing else, since they promote and oppose ignorance. They are not independent of ignorance in the jīva.

But by realizing Paramātmā they no longer exist. Paramātmā is continually omniscient (ajasra-citi),

*yaḥ sarva-jñaḥ sarva-vit*

**The Lord knows everything generally and specifically. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)**

It is not that there is a contrary idea in oneself about Paramātmā by which saṁsāra will appear and not that from its absence, its destruction or liberation also will appear. That Paramātmā is all-pervading and the master of all (ātmani). He is pure (kevale) and though within all beings, is untouched by anything (pare). When this all-pervading master, untouched by matter, constantly omniscient, is contemplated by persons desiring the highest goal (vicāryamāne), these two states no longer exist.

An example is given. For the sun, day and night do not exist.

### Text 27

*tvām ātmānaṁ paraṁ matvā param ātmānam eva ca*  
*ātmā punar bahir mṛgya aho ’jña-janatājñatā*

**Перевод:**

**Considering that you, Paramātmā to be an ordinary jīva, a person seeks Paramātmā elsewhere. How astonishing is the ignorance of people who think themselves learned.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Brahmā! You speak of me as Paramātmā. I do not think so.” He objects to this in this verse.

In this verse the word ca means api. Considering you to be an ātmā filled with māyā (param) though you are Paramātmā (paramātmānam eva ca), a person seeks Paramātmā (ātmā) elsewhere (bahir). Aho indicates astonishment. How astonishing is the ignorance (ajñatā) of those who think themselves in knowledge (jña-janatā). Though they are learned in scriptures they cannot overcome saṁsāra.

### Text 28

*antar-bhave ’nanta bhavantam eva*  
*hy atat tyajanto mṛgayanti santaḥ*  
*asantam apy anty ahim antareṇa*  
*santaṁ guṇaṁ taṁ kim u yanti santaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O unlimited Lord, the discriminating people seek you out within the universe by rejecting things other than you. How can discriminating persons appreciate the real nature of a rope lying before them until they refute the illusion that it is a snake?**

**Комментарий:**

My nature of Paramātmā is hidden in this world. O unlimited Lord (ananta)! The devotees meditate (mṛgayanti) on you, the son of Nanda, as Paramātmā in the heart within the body (antar-bhave), giving up the variety of māyā (atat), different from Paramātmā, perceived as similar to other objects by your distinguishing features of giving liberation to Pūtanā and the marks on your feet. In the meditation, giving up māyā is necessary. An example is given. Without negating (antareṇa) the snake which is not present (asantam) nearby (ante), do the wise (santaḥ) know a rope which is actually present? No they do not.

Though a snake is not present in a rope, without giving up that thought of the snake, the real nature of the rope will not manifest. Without giving up the idea of matter in you, one cannot realize you as Paramātmā. Thus one must give up everything material (atat). Rejecting variegated matter perceived by misconceptions, they preach your nature as Paramātmā. Thus they become confident.

### Text 29

*athāpi te deva padāmbuja-dvaya-*  
*prasāda-leśānugṛhīta eva hi*  
*jānāti tattvaṁ bhagavan-mahimno*  
*na cānya eko ’pi ciraṁ vicinvan*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, revealer of everything! O Lord endowed with all qualities! Such persons, receiving a particle of mercy from your lotus feet, realize to some degree your greatness. Others cannot understand even after reflecting for a long time.**

**Комментарий:**

“Knowing me as Paramātmā, by the antaryāmī Upaniṣad received through guru, people cross saṁsāra. What is the use of strongbhakti with hearing about me as stated in the following verse?

*vibudhya bhaktyaiva kathopanītayā*  
*prapedire ‘ñjo ‘cyuta te gatiṁ parām*

**Through such devotional service, perfected by the processes of hearing and chanting about you, they came to understand you. (SB** [**10.1.45**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.45)**)”**

Though that knowledge is attained by the Upaniṣad, still being blessed by obtaining even a particle of mercy from your lotus feet, whose cause is hearing about you, people know the svarūpa (tattvaṁ) of your greatness. Not a person, important due to his exterme learning, devoid of a particle of mercy caused by hearing, can understand even though deliberating for a long time on that Upaniṣad. By bhakti one becomes delivered. Knowledge is generated in it, like the fiber in a lotus stem. Why be anxious for that knowledge?

### Text 30

*tad astu me nātha sa bhūri-bhāgo*  
*bhave ’tra vānyatra tu vā tiraścām*  
*yenāham eko ’pi bhavaj-janānāṁ*  
*bhūtvā niṣeve tava pāda-pallavam*

**Перевод:**

**Let that be, O Lord! My greatest fortunate, in this birth or born as an animal elsewhere, or preferably in Vraja, is to take birth as one among your devotees and serve your lotus feet with full devotion.**

**Комментарий:**

Having praised the Lord for his sweetness and powers, Brahmā prays for bhakti to Kṛṣṇa, defining it as the main method.O master of the cowherds (nātha)! May I have the good fortune that in this life as Brahmā, or in birth among animals (tiraścām), or even someother birth, I should become one among your people and serve your lotus feet.

He mentions animal birth due to remembrance of bhakti even in animal birth. Gajo gṛdhro vanīkpatha: Gajendra, Jaṭāyu, Tulādhāra (SB [11.12.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/12.6))

Bhakti increases in low birth. Thus tiraścām (among animals) is spoken. Being born anywhere may I have bhakti to you. In Jitānta- stotra, speaking to Nārada it is said:

*yatra kutra kule vāso yeṣu keṣu bhavo ‘stu me*  
*tava dāsyaika-bhāve syāt sadā savatra me ratiḥ*

**Whatever birth I may take, in whatever family, among any people, may I have always every rati for you, as your servant.**

### Text 31

*aho ’ti-dhanyā vraja-go-ramaṇyaḥ*  
*stanyāmṛtaṁ pītam atīva te mudā*  
*yāsāṁ vibho vatsatarātmajātmanā*  
*yat-tṛptaye ’dyāpi na cālam adhvarāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O almighty Lord, how greatly fortunate are the cows and ladies of Vṛndāvana, the nectar of whose breast-milk you have happily drunk to your full satisfaction, taking the form of their calves and children! All the Vedic sacrifices performed from time immemorial up to the present day have not given you as much satisfaction.**

**Комментарий:**

The position of being your follower is difficult for me to achieve. I will only praise it. This is expressed in two verses. The cows andgopīs (ramaṇyaḥ) situated in Vraja are most fortunate. Their good fortune cannot be described (aho)! O powerful Lord (vibho)! Theirbreast milk was drunk by you, condensed knowledge, with great joy, when you took the form of the calves and boys. Like you, the cows and gopīs were also condensed knowledge. Milk from their breasts was drunk as if it were the very essence of taste, like fragrance is the essence of earth. There was no part of that milk which was not of the same essence. The sacrifices performed by us from beginningless time till the present with their aṅgas are not able to satisfy (na alam) you like that.

### Text 32

*aho bhāgyam aho bhāgyaṁ nanda-gopa-vrajaukasām*  
*yan-mitraṁ paramānandaṁ pūrṇaṁ brahma sanātanam*

**Перевод:**

**How greatly fortunate are Nanda Mahārāja, the cowherd men and all the other inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi! There is no limit to their good fortune, because Kṛṣṇa gave them prema, which is the highest bliss, eternal and complete.**

**Комментарий:**

Aho bhāgyam is repeated twice to express great bliss and astonishment and great respect. What good fortune for the people of King Nanda’s Vraja. This is most, most astonishing. That good fortune is explained. Their friend is Svayam Bhagavān (pūrṇam), Brahman, the highest bliss. Using neuter gender (paramānandaṁ) is poetic license. This hints at the śruti statement vijñānam ānandam brahma: Brahman is knowledge and bliss. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) To refute that the friendship is temporary the word sanātanam (eternal) is used. Moreover, the people of Vraja are also eternal. Sanātanam does not modify Brahman.

By attaining the tattva of Brahman in its complete form, the friendship is eternal. In the statement “This is the best scholar” the excellence of the scholar is indicated. Similarly, the eternality of the friendship is indicated in this verse. The word mitra expressesmutual friendship since the suffix (kta) to the verb mid (to be affectionate) is used in both locative and doer ans since later it is said:

*dustyajaś cānurāgo ‘smin sarveṣāṁ no vrajaukasām*  
*nanda te tanaye ‘smāsu tasyāpy autpattikaḥ katham*

**Dear Nanda, how is it that we and all the other residents of Vraja cannot give up our constant affection for your son? And how is it that he is so spontaneously attracted to us? (SB** [**10.26.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/26.13)**)**

The exchange of friendship in the bhāvas of inhabitants of Vraja down to animals because of his mischievous nature was the same friendship in the Lord’s bhāvas since his bhāvas follow theirs.

### Text 33

*eṣāṁ tu bhāgya-mahimācyuta tāvad āstām*  
*ekādaśaiva hi vayaṁ bata bhūri-bhāgāḥ*  
*etad-dhṛṣīka-caṣakair asakṛt pibāmaḥ*  
*śarvādayo ’ṅghry-udaja-madhv-amṛtāsavaṁ te*

**Перевод:**

**O infallible Lord! What can be said of the great fortune of the people of Vraja? We, the deities of the directions, are also fortunate. Headed by Śiva, we constantly drink through the cups of our senses the nectar and liquor from your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā hails his own good fortune because of sometimes attaining the Lord’s sweetness.

Let the glory of the good fortune of the people of Vraja remain so. Who can one describe it since it is one (ekā) incomparable? Theten of us dik-pālas starting with Śiva, are very fortunate. Why? He touches with his index finger his eyes and ears (etat). With the drinking cups of our senses we constantly drink the sweetness of your lotus feet. With the cups of our eyes we constantly drink the honey of your feet. With the cups of our ears we constantly drink the sweetness of your jingling anklets. Since those feet are tasty and intoxicating, they are the form of sweet nectar (amṛtāsavam). Thus Śiva and others often come to Vraja to see Kṛṣṇa. This will berevealed later in the song sung in pairs of verses (Chapter thrity- five).

The interpretation, “We devatās, who are the presiding deities of their senses, drink that nectar through the cups of the senses of the people of Vraja” is made since it is not accepted that the sense devatās are enjoyers.

### Text 34

*tad bhūri-bhāgyam iha janma kim apy aṭavyāṁ*  
*yad gokule ’pi katamāṅghri-rajo-’bhiṣekam*  
*yaj-jīvitaṁ tu nikhilaṁ bhagavān mukundas*  
*tv adyāpi yat-pada-rajaḥ śruti-mṛgyam eva*

**Перевод:**

**My greatest possible good fortune would be to take any birth whatever in this forest of Gokula and have my head bathed by the dust falling from the lotus feet of any of its residents. Their entire life and soul is the Lord, Mukunda, the dust of whose lotus feet is sought even today by the Upaniṣads.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā prays with thirst for the path of ruci-bhakti, with the glory of seeing Vṛndāvana. If Kṛṣṇa is generous, he will mercifully glance upon me. May I attain that good fortune. What is that fortune? May I be born as dūrva grass in Vṛndāvana, where the feet of you with your friends walk. If this is not approved, then let me be born as a stone slab at the edge of Gokula, which will be bathed in the foot dust of some inhabitant.

“But why are the inhabitants glorious and why are you not ashamed to desire the foot dust since you, Brahmā, are lord of the universe, worshipped by the world?”

Mukunda means the smile on his face is like a kunda flower. Mukunda, Svayam Bhagavān, the embodiment of extreme sweetness, is the life of them all, since he is their only life. That is the glory of the inhabitants. And the dust from their feet is sought by the śrutiseven today but cannot be attained. What shame is there in this desire? I am worshipped by the world because I support the śrutis.

### Text 35

*eṣāṁ ghoṣa-nivāsinām uta bhavān kiṁ deva rāteti naś*  
*ceto viśva-phalāt phalaṁ tvad-aparaṁ kutrāpy ayan muhyati*  
*sad-veṣād iva pūtanāpi sa-kulā tvām eva devāpitā*  
*yad-dhāmārtha-suhṛt-priyātma-tanaya-prāṇāśayās tvat-kṛte*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! What can you give to the people of Vraja whose houses, possessions, friends, dear ones, bodies, sons, life airs and hearts are dedicated only to you, since there is nothing superior to you or Vraja (which you have already given)? Thinking of this, my mind becomes bewildered. You awarded yourself even to Pūtanā and her family members because she wore the disguise of a nurse.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing that the Lord is pleased with his desire for foot dust, wanting to hear his words, Brahmā asks him a question. O Lord! What reward can you give (rātā) to the people of this cowherd village? Uta indicates a question. I ask this. “Since you know the Vedas, deliberating, you can understand.”

The hearts of us—me, Śiva, and Nārada, and all the knowers of the Vedas—are bewildered, not obtaining (ayan) in any place and time a result superior than you, the svarūpa of all results? We become bewildere, “By giving what can he become free of debt?” Ayan is formed from yan, present participle of the root iṇ.

“But giving myself to them or person related to them, I can be free of debt.”

Because of wearing clothing of a nurse, Pūtanā with Baka and Agha, though she was most sinful, attained you by you. But to those whose all properties, etc., are engaged for serving you (tvad-kṛte), to these servants having anurāga for you, who are the crest jewels of the pious, giving yourself is not sufficient. You are always their debtor. Mercifully give me the dust of their lotus feet. I am not attracted to being lord of the universe.

### Text 36

*tāvad rāgādayaḥ stenās tāvat kārā-gṛhaṁ gṛham*  
*tāvan moho ’ṅghri-nigaḍo yāvat kṛṣṇa na te janāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Kṛṣṇa! Until people become your devotees, their material attachments and desires remain thieves, their homes remain prisons, and their affectionate feelings for their family members remain foot-shackles.**

**Комментарий:**

“The people of Vraja cannot be glorified since they were attached to house, wife and children.”

For householders living elsewhere, having obstacles of wife and children, the attachment, absorption, and aversion to wife, etc., become thieves, stealing wealth of knowledge, etc. Even the house becomes a prison. Bewilderment concerning matters related of house, etc., become shackles on the feet as long as they do not become your devotees.

But when they become devotees, they become attached to your devotees, they become absorbed in you or in things related with you and they show aversion to enemies of bhakti. Giving knowledge about you, they become devotees who give the highest help. The house, becoming useful for bhakti with service to the Lord, become cause for perceiving your eternal dhāma. Since wife and children are your devotees, the illusion related to them becomes spiritual. Thus because of relation with you, like the touch of a cintāmaṇi, theattachment, etc., of sannyāsīs ends in that. What to speak of these friends of yours and this dhāma engaged in your service? The glory which is shown is theirs.

### Text 37

*prapañcaṁ niṣprapañco ’pi viḍambayasi bhū-tale*  
*prapanna-janatānanda-sandohaṁ prathituṁ prabho*

**Перевод:**

**My dear master! Although you have nothing to do with material existence, you come to this earth and imitate material life just to expand the varieties of ecstatic enjoyment for your surrendered devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Brahmā! These people, extermely affectionate because of relationship, care for me, a human form. I have not given to them any wealth at all which is amazing and praiseworthy.”

You, who are beyond matter, have appeared on earth along with those cowherds who are also beyond matter but you put on a show of being material. Acting like a human, you deride the human form by actions full of power hidden within. What is the purpose of those human-like actions? It is to spread abundant bliss arising from such actions to surrendered people on earth. It is to give an experience of the extreme glory of your activities like a group of lamps at night. The human appearance of you and your devotees is actually spiritual bliss by nature. Powers, however, follow these devotees.

### Text 38

*jānanta eva jānantu kiṁ bahūktyā na me prabho*  
*manaso vapuṣo vāco vaibhavaṁ tava go-caraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Let the people who think they know, think in that way! What more can be said, O Lord! The powers of your mind, body, and words are not accessible to me.**

**Комментарий:**

Having praised the Lord according to his intelligence, mocking those who think themselves learned, he says the Lord cannot be understood. O master! The powers, in the form of having vibhūtis according to desire (vaibhavaṁ), of your mind, body and words are beyond my understanding.

### Text 39

*anujānīhi māṁ kṛṣṇa sarvaṁ tvaṁ vetsi sarva-dṛk*  
*tvam eva jagatāṁ nātho jagad etat tavārpitam*

**Перевод:**

**O Kṛṣṇa, endowed with attractive qualities! I now humbly request permission to leave. Actually, you are the knower and seer of all things. You are the Lord of all the universes. You have offered this universe to me for creating.**

**Комментарий:**

“You may not know my powers. Don’t I also know your powers?” Brahmā speaks with shame and regret. Please give me permissionto leave (anujānīhi)! The causative meaning is included in the verb. I am an offender for interrupting your meal and playing. I haveprayed with tad bhūri-bhāgya (SB [10.14.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.34)). This was not accepted by your feet or even your glance. I request in plenty. I serve from far off. You now all that I desire since you see everything (sarva- dṛk).

“You are the lord of the universe. Please do your duties for the universe.”

You are the master of many universes. This is a small universe, created by me on your order. You have offered it to me. It may be given to whom you desire. I have no need of this. What I desire is supplied by the ocean of mercy.

### Text 40

*śrī-kṛṣṇa vṛṣṇi-kula-puṣkara-joṣa-dāyin*  
*kṣmā-nirjara-dvija-paśūdadhi-vṛddhi-kārin*  
*uddharma-śārvara-hara kṣiti-rākṣasa-dhrug*  
*ā-kalpam ārkam arhan bhagavan namas te*

**Перевод:**

**O Kṛṣṇa! O sun making the families of Nanda and Vasudeva blossom! O nourishing moon for the cows, brāhmaṇas, devatās and earth. O dispeller of the dense darkness of irreligion! O destroyer of the demons who have appeared on this earth! O Svayam Bhagavān! Along with your decorations such as guñja berries and the arka tree, I offer my obeisances unto you, worthy of worship.**

**Комментарий:**

Though you will not speak with sinful me, still without your glance of mercy it is difficult for me to live. With this intent Brahmā offers respects. O sun now making the lotus, which is the Vṛṣṇi family, blossom! Since I arose from a lotus, make me blossom also. O moon now increasing the ocean, which is the earth, devatās, brāhmaṇas and cows. Make me, a devatā and brāhmaṇa, flourish also. Now you injure the demons like Agha on earth. You give them your lotus feet by this violence. Purifying me, a brahma-rakṣasa, interrupting your meal, by punishing, give me your lotus feet. Give up indifference, for it is difficult for me to live.

Ignorantly I thought it was improper for the Supreme Lord, master of unlimited Lakṣmīs to wear guñja berries, herd calves, and make friendship with cowherd boys. Thinking in that way, I committed offense. I ask pardon for that now. I offer respects to you, including your guñja berry decorations (ākalpa) and with the Vraja arka tree bearing unsuitable flowers (ārkaṁ). I should worship them since they are related to you and full of condensed knowledge. O lord worthy of worship (arhan)!

*paramaiśvarya-mādhurya-bhakti-bhṛd-brahmaṇoditā \|*  
*jīyād gokula-māhātmya-dhātrī nanda-sutas tatiḥ \|*

**May the praise of Nanda’s son, holding the glory of Gokula, spoken by Brahmā, possessing bhakti appreciating Kṛṣṇa’s sweetness and power, remain victorious.**

### Text 41

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity abhiṣṭūya bhūmānaṁ triḥ parikramya pādayoḥ*  
*natvābhīṣṭaṁ jagad-dhātā sva-dhāma pratyapadyata*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus offered his prayers to the unlimited Lord, Brahmā circumambulated him three times and then bowed down at his lotus feet. The appointed creator of the universe then returned to his own residence according to Kṛṣṇa’s desire.**

**Комментарий:**

Being glanced upon with mercy by the Lord who was satisfied with Brahmā’s desire for prideless prema of Vraja expressed in his prayers, he again praised Kṛṣṇa (bhūmānam) again and three times circumambulating, offering respects to Kṛṣṇa’s feet, and returned to his abode, being told by the Lord, “Now perfrom your duties related to the world. At the end your desire will come true, according to the principle of yāvad adhikāram avasthitir ādhikārikāṇām: the rulers of the universe remain in the universe till the end of their designated period. (Brahma-sūtra 3.3.3)”

### Text 42

*tato ’nujñāpya bhagavān sva-bhuvaṁ prāg avasthitān*  
*vatsān pulinam āninye yathā-pūrva-sakhaṁ svakam*

**Перевод:**

**After granting his son Brahmā permission to leave, the Lord took the previous calves and brought them to the riverbank, where he had been taking his meal and where previous cowherd boyfriends remained just as before.**

**Комментарий:**

Remaining silent, the Lord by his glance permitted Brahmā to leave, i.e. ordered him to go to his planet. He brought his calves whichate the grass as previously (prāk) to the bank where he was having his meals (svakaṁ) and where the real boys were sitting before the ones manifested by Kṛṣṇa (pūrva-sakhaṁ).

### Text 43

*ekasminn api yāte ’bde prāṇeśaṁ cāntarātmanaḥ*  
*kṛṣṇa-māyāhatā rājan kṣaṇārdhaṁ menire ’rbhakāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King! Although the boys had passed an entire year apart from the Lord of their very lives, they had been covered by Kṛṣṇa’s illusory potency and thus considered that year to be merely half a moment.**

**Комментарий:**

The lack of awareness of the time that had passed, and the conclusion of their meal with Kṛṣṇa, who returned, holding yogurt rice in his hand, were the manifestions of his inconceivable yoga- māyā. This is described in four verses. Without Kṛṣṇa (antarā), the lord of their lives (ātmanaḥ praṇeśam), the boys covered (āhatā) by yoga-māyā, thought that year was five palas, half a kṣaṇa.

### Text 44

*kiṁ kiṁ na vismarantīha māyā-mohita-cetasaḥ*  
*yan-mohitaṁ jagat sarvam abhīkṣṇaṁ vismṛtātmakam*

**Перевод:**

**What is not forgotten by those whose minds are bewildered by the Lord’s illusory potency? By that power of māyā, this entire universe remains in perpetual bewilderment, and in this atmosphere of forgetfulness, no one can understand his own identity.**

**Комментарий:**

An example is given comparing the illusion of yogamāyā to the illusion created by the three guṇas due to their similarity inbewildering. In this world (iha), what do those whose minds are bewildered by the three guṇas (māyā-mohita-cetasaḥ) not forget repeatedly? Thus the world makes one forget the ātmā (vismṛtātmakam) though understanding in deep sleep or through scriptures that one is apart from the gross and subtle bodies.

Similarly lasting one year, the friends did not remember the suffering of separation from Kṛṣṇa because of yoga-māyā.

### Text 45

*ūcuś ca suhṛdaḥ kṛṣṇaṁ sv-āgataṁ te ’ti-raṁhasā*  
*naiko ’py abhoji kavala ehītaḥ sādhu bhujyatām*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd boyfriends said to Kṛṣṇa: you have returned so quickly! We have not eaten even one morsel in your absence. Please come here and take your meal to full satisfaction.**

**Комментарий:**

You have returned in a half a kṣaṇa, happily. Thinking one ghaṭikā has passed, we have not eaten a morsel of food without you. Therefore, come here.

### Text 46

*tato hasan hṛṣīkeśo ’bhyavahṛtya sahārbhakaiḥ*  
*darśayaṁś carmājagaraṁ nyavartata vanād vrajam*

**Перевод:**

**Then Kṛṣṇa, smiling, finished his lunch in the company of his friends. Showing them the skin of Aghāsura, he returned from the forest to Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa smiled because they showed joy, and though a year had passed, the food had not spoilt since he returned quickly and their food was full of rasa. The dried up skin showed that the demon had died immediately. In order to announce to Vraja the events of the killing, he returned to Vraja from playing in the forest.

### Text 47

*barha-prasūna-vana-dhātu-vicitritāṅgaḥ*  
*proddāma-veṇu-dala-śṛṅga-ravotsavāḍhyaḥ*  
*vatsān gṛṇann anuga-gīta-pavitra-kīrtir*  
*gopī-dṛg-utsava-dṛśiḥ praviveśa goṣṭham*

**Перевод:**

**His body was decorated with peacock feathers and flowers and painted with forest minerals, and his flute, horn and instruments made from leaves loudly and festively resounded. His cowherd boyfriends purified the whole world by sweetly chanting his glories. Thus Kṛṣṇa entered the cow pasture of his father, Nanda Mahārāja, and seeing him produced a great festival for the eyes of all the cowherd women.**

**Комментарий:**

Endowed with a festival of loud flutes, his limbs colorful with minerals such as gairika (red chalk), his fame in killing Agha, which purifies the Lord, sung by the boys, herding the calves, calling them with fondness, a festival on seeing him for the eyes of Yaśodā and other gopīs, he entered Vraja.

### Text 48

*adyānena mahā-vyālo yaśodā-nanda-sūnunā*  
*hato ’vitā vayaṁ cāsmād iti bālā vraje jaguḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As the cowherd boys reached the village of Vraja, they sang, “Today Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda and Yaśodā, saved us by killing a great serpent!”**

**Комментарий:**

Today a great serpent was killed by him and we were saved (avitāḥ). He is the son of Yaśodā and Nanda. Those who favored Yaśodā said son of Yaśodā (yaśodā-sūnuḥ). Those who favored Nanda said son of Nanda (nanda-sūnuḥ).

### Text 49

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*brahman parodbhave kṛṣṇe iyān premā kathaṁ bhavet*  
*yo ’bhūta-pūrvas tokeṣu svodbhaveṣv api kathyatām*

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: O brāhmaṇa, how could the cowherd women have developed for Kṛṣṇa, someone else’s son, such unprecedented pure love—love they never felt even for their own children? Please explain this.**

**Комментарий:**

Previously it was shown that the people of Vraja had more love from Kṛṣṇa than for their own sons (in SB [10.13.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/13.26)). Parīkṣit inquires about this. How is it that they had love for Kṛṣṇa and even their own children which was unprecedented, which was not manifest previous to Brahmā’s bewilderment? Why is that? Please say. It is seen in this world that people have more love from their own children though they may be lesser in qualities than the son of another person, having great qualities. Since this contradicts what is seen in the world I ask.

### Text 50

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*sarveṣām api bhūtānāṁ nṛpa svātmaiva vallabhaḥ*  
*itare ’patya-vittādyās tad-vallabhatayaiva hi*

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, for every created being the dearest thing is certainly his own self. The dearness of everything else—children, wealth and so on—is due only to the dearness of the self.**

**Комментарий:**

This is the conclusion by examination of love in this world. One’s ātmā, the controller of the body and senses, is dear to the jīva since it is full of knowledge and bliss. Thus, other things like children are dear because they are related to the ātmā.

### Text 51

*tad rājendra yathā snehaḥ sva-svakātmani dehinām*  
*na tathā mamatālambi-putra-vitta-gṛhādiṣu*

**Перевод:**

**For this reason, O best of kings, the embodied soul is self- centered: he is more attached to his own body and self than to his so-called possessions like children, wealth and home.**

**Комментарий:**

Therefore (tat), affection for one’s self (sva-svakātmani), full of knowledge and bliss, with a sense of “I” does not exist in relation to sons, etc., objects of one’s possessiveness. Affection for wife and sons is not the main affection since, though equal to affection for one’s self, its true nature is unmanifest being covered by bodies, etc., and is not more than affection for one’s self.

### Text 52

*dehātma-vādināṁ puṁsām api rājanya-sattama*  
*yathā dehaḥ priyatamas tathā na hy anu ye ca tam*

**Перевод:**

**Even for persons who think the body is the self, O best of kings, those things whose importance lies only in their relationship to the body are never as dear as the body itself.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking another viewpoint, the self as object of love is shown. From the belief that “I am pale in complexion or I am huge” those who think that the body is the self, the Lokāyatikas, take the body as ātmā, and thus dearest. Children, etc., following the body, are not as dear as the body. The self is dear.

### Text 53

*deho ’pi mamatā-bhāk cet tarhy asau nātma-vat priyaḥ*  
*yaj jīryaty api dehe ’smin jīvitāśā balīyasī*

**Перевод:**

**If a person comes to the stage of considering the body “mine” instead of “me,” he will certainly not consider the body as dear as his own self. After all, even as the body is growing old and useless, one’s desire to continue living remains strong.**

**Комментарий:**

When people develop some discrimination by association with a knower of tattva, if the body is seen as the object of possession, it does not become as dear as the self but as something related to the self. This is proved by ordinary experience. When the body withers from sickness, seeing the extreme suffering in the body, thinking, “I, the ātmā, should not have such extreme suffering,” the desire to live in the body becomes stronger, from affection to the ātmā.

### Text 54

*tasmāt priyatamaḥ svātmā sarveṣām api dehinām*  
*tad-artham eva sakalaṁ jagad etac carācaram*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore it is his own self that is most dear to every embodied living being, and it is simply for the satisfaction of this self that the whole material creation of moving and nonmoving entities exists.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse summarizes. Moving beings like sons and immovable objects like houses are all for the ātmā. The ātmā (self) is dearest,the object of greatest affection by the individual according to material vision.

### Text 55

*kṛṣṇam enam avehi tvam ātmānam akhilātmanām*  
*jagad-dhitāya so ’py atra dehīvābhāti māyayā*

**Перевод:**

**You should know Kṛṣṇa to be the soul of all living entities. For the benefit of the whole universe, out of his causeless mercy he has appeared as an ordinary human being by the strength of his māyā.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse returns to the main subject.

*kṛṣir bhū-vāckaḥ śabdo ṇaś ca nirvṛti-vācakaḥ*  
*tayor aikyaṁ paraṁ brahma kṛṣṇa ity abhidīyate*

**Kṛṣ means “existence” and ṇa means “bliss.” Combined together, the two roots indicate the Supreme Brahman addressed as Kṛṣṇa.**

Understand that Kṛṣṇa, whose name is explained above, who is full of great knowledge and bliss, the son of Nanda (enam), is the ātmā of all, even the pure jīvas (ākhilātmanām). Just as affection for sons is seen by their in relation to the body and affection for the body by its relation to the ātmā, similarly there is affection for the jīva, which is compared to Kṛṣṇa’s body, by its relation to Kṛṣṇa (ātmā). Thus there was more affection for Kṛṣṇa than one’s son since Kṛṣṇa was the only object of their great affection.

The following should be understood. Prema or happiness is seen in conscious beings. It is fixed in the being in a visible way. Since discriminating person finds happiness from material objects to be useless, that happiness of prema is concluded to be the svarūpa of the jīva. The jīva must offer his manifested happiness to the most excellent self-manifesting happiness, which by its nature is not infinitesimal. For the jīva of this nature, prema develops. Param brahma is a similar entity.

*satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ brahma*

**Brahman is existence, knowledge and infinite. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)**

*vijñānam ānandaṁ brahma rātir dātuḥ parāyaṇam*

**The Lord is knowledge and bliss, the giver, the goal of the sacrificer. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad** [**3.9.28**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bau/3.9.28)**)**

*etad dhy evākṣaraṁ jñātvā yo yad icchati tasya tat*

**Meditating on this syllable one attains whatever one desires. (Kaṭha Upaniṣad)**

*eko bahūnāṁ yo vidadhāti kāmān \|*

**One entity, he fulfills the desires of many. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad)**

Thus, it is shown that the Lord is superior to the jīva, like honey is superior to raw sugar or the ocean is superior to a drop of water.

This is also shown by the writer of the Brahma-sūtras in the setu adhikaraṇa. That Parabrahman is Kṛṣṇa:

*sākṣāt prakṛti-paro yo’yam ātmā*  
*gopālaḥ kathaṁ tv avatīrṇo bhūmyāṁ hi vai*

**Why has this Gopāla, who is beyond prakṛti, made his appearance on earth? (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

*yo ‘sau paraṁ brahma gopālaḥ*

**Param brahman is Kṛṣṇa. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

Kṛṣṇa appeared in Vraja to benefit the world. By māyā, he appears to possess a body. Actually, that body is himself according to śruti.

### Text 56

*vastuto jānatām atra kṛṣṇaṁ sthāsnu cariṣṇu ca*  
*bhagavad-rūpam akhilaṁ nānyad vastv iha kiñcana*

**Перевод:**

**For those who know, in this universe there is no other object than Kṛṣṇa. He is all animate and inanimate objects and all forms of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa is not only ātmā for the jīvas, but even for material objects. In truth, in this world those who meditate on Kṛṣṇa (jānatām),those who are wise, for them all moving and nonmoving objects are the form of Bhagavān alone, since they are dependent on him, and since he pervades them. This is understood in the discussion on prāṇa.

*sa vāsudevo na yato ‘nyad asti*

**There is one Supreme Lord Vāsudeva. Nothing else exists. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

### Text 57

*sarveṣām api vastūnāṁ bhāvārtho bhavati sthitaḥ*  
*tasyāpi bhagavān kṛṣṇaḥ kim atad vastu rūpyatām*

**Перевод:**

**Real existence of all this is situated in the jīva. Its cause is the Lord endowed with all powers in the form of Kṛṣṇa. Can anything be found without Kṛṣṇa?**

**Комментарий:**

The suggested meaning (bhāvārthaḥ) of all objects, such as bodies and senses, understood by their tendencies, is the fixed jīvātmāsince it is unchanging. Since the jīva too is an aṁśa, its suggested cause the aṁśī is determined as Kṛṣṇa alone. An object differentfrom him (atat) cannot be determined.

### Text 58

*samāśritā ye pada-pallava-plavaṁ*  
*mahat-padaṁ puṇya-yaśo murāreḥ*  
*bhavāmbudhir vatsa-padaṁ paraṁ padaṁ*  
*padaṁ padaṁ yad vipadāṁ na teṣām*

**Перевод:**

**For those who have accepted the boat of the lotus feet of the Lord, killer of Mura, the ocean of the material world is like the water contained in a calf’s hoof-print. Their goal is Vaikuṇṭha, the place of the eternal associates, not the material world.**

**Комментарий:**

By taking shelter of the feet of Kṛṣṇa, the master of all, who bestows all means of living, one attains liberation. This is the summary. For those who take exclusive shelter of the boat of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, whose fame is attractive (puṇya-yaśaḥ), which is the shelter for the great devotees (mahat-padam), the ocean saṁsāra, though hard to cross, becomes like a calf’s hoofprint. It becomes spiritual sky (param padam) where there is no danger (vipadām) for those who take shelter (teṣām) since śruti says na ca punar āvartate: he does not return. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)

### Text 59

*etat te sarvam ākhyātaṁ yat pṛṣṭo ’ham iha tvayā*  
*tat kaumāre hari-kṛtaṁ paugaṇḍe parikīrtitam*

**Перевод:**

**Since you inquired from me, I have fully described to you those activities of the Lord that were performed in kaumāra period but not celebrated until his paugaṇḍa period.**

### Text 60

*etat suhṛdbhiś caritaṁ murārer*  
*aghārdanaṁ śādvala-jemanaṁ ca*  
*vyaktetaraṁ rūpam ajorv-abhiṣṭavaṁ*  
*śṛṇvan gṛṇann eti naro ’khilārthān*

**Перевод:**

**Any person who hears or chants these pastimes of the Lord performed with his cowherd friends—the killing of Aghāsura, the taking of lunch on the forest grass, the Lord’s manifestation of transcendental forms, and the wonderful prayers offered by Brahmā—is sure to achieve all his desires.**

**Комментарий:**

Activities with his friends were described:

*muṣṇanto ‘nyonya-śikyādīn jñātān ārāc ca cikṣipuḥ*  
*tatratyāś ca punar dūrād dhasantaś ca punar daduḥ*

**All the cowherd boys used to steal one another’s lunch bags. When a boy came to understand that his bag had been taken away, the other boys would throw it farther away, to a more distant place, and those standing there would throw it still farther. When the proprietor of the bag became disappointed, the other boys would laugh, the proprietor would cry, and then the bag would be returned. (SB** [**10.12.5**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/12.5)**)**

Hearing about eating (jemanam) on the grass and manifesting forms beyond the material (vyaktetarad-rūpam), calves and boys full of condensed knowledge and the great (uru) prayers of Brahmā (aja) uttered earnestly (abhistvam), one attains all desires. The non-t- ending on itara is poetic license (should have been vyaktetarat).

### Text 61

*evaṁ vihāraiḥ kaumāraiḥ kaumāraṁ jahatur vraje*  
*nilāyanaiḥ setu-bandhair markaṭotplavanādibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In this way the boys spent their childhood in the land of Vṛndāvana playing hide-and-go-seek, building play bridges, jumping about like monkeys and engaging in many other such games.**

**Комментарий:**

Thus explaining the kaumāra pastimes, the concluding verse repeats what was previously described.

## Chapter 15 - The Killing of Dhenuka, the Ass Demon

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*tataś ca paugaṇḍa-vayaḥ-śritau vraje*  
*babhūvatus tau paśu-pāla-sammatau*  
*gāś cārayantau sakhibhiḥ samaṁ padair*  
*vṛndāvanaṁ puṇyam atīva cakratuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa attained the age of paugaṇḍa in Vṛndāvana, the cowherd men allowed them to take up the task of tending the cows. Engaging thus in the company of their friends, the two boys rendered the land of Vṛndāvana most auspicious by imprinting upon it the marks of their lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

*dhenūnāṁ pālanaṁ pañca-daśe saṅkarṣaṇa-stutiḥ \|*  
*svaiḥ krīḍā dhenuka-dhvaṁsas trāṇaṁ ca viṣato’bhavat*

**In the fifteenth chapter, there is herding cows, there is praise of Balarāma, playing with the cowherd boys, the death of Dhenuka and deliverance from poison.**

After playing in the fifth year (tataḥ) Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma displayed paugaṇḍa age, the stage of sixth year, and were permitted to herdthe cows. That day is called Gopāṣṭamī:

*śuklāṣṭamī kārtike tu smṛtā gopāṣṭamī budhaiḥ*  
*tad-dinād vāsudevo ’bhūd gopaḥ pūrvaṁ tu vatsapaḥ*

**The eighth lunar day of the bright fortnight of the month of Kārtika is known by authorities as Gopāṣṭamī. From that day, Kṛṣṇa served as a cowherd, whereas previously he had tended the calves. (Padma Purāṇa, Kārtika-māhātmya)**

They made Vṛndāvana very attractive (puṇya) by the marks of flag, thunderbolt, etc., on their feet. At this time the markings became very distinct and more beautiful.

“Though Kṛṣna was a cowherd, because he was the son of the king he should not have herded cows.” Because he is the Supreme Lord, this was suitable. He is the lord of sacrifice. Sacrifices are accomplished by oblations of cow products and with mantras. Herding cows establishes his position as the lord of sacrifice.

### Text 2

*tan mādhavo veṇum udīrayan vṛto*  
*gopair gṛṇadbhiḥ sva-yaśo balānvitaḥ*  
*paśūn puraskṛtya paśavyam āviśad*  
*vihartu-kāmaḥ kusumākaraṁ vanam*

**Перевод:**

**Thus desiring to enjoy pastimes, Mādhava, sounding his flute loudly, surrounded by cowherd boys who were chanting his glories, and accompanied by Baladeva, kept the cows before him and entered the Vṛndāvana forest, which was full of flowers and rich with nourishment for the animals.**

**Комментарий:**

Mādhava means Kṛṣṇa, but as a pun refers to spring. Like spring, he gave joy to the forest.

### Text 3

*tan mañju-ghoṣāli-mṛga-dvijākulaṁ*  
*mahan-manaḥ-prakhya-payaḥ-sarasvatā*  
*vātena juṣṭaṁ śata-patra-gandhinā*  
*nirīkṣya rantuṁ bhagavān mano dadhe*

**Перевод:**

**Gazing at that forest, which resounded with the charming sounds of bees, animals and birds, and which was served by a breeze carrying the fragrance of hundred-petaled lotuses carrying water particles from lakes whose clear water resembled the minds of great souls, Kṛṣṇa decided to enjoy.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the forest, the Lord decided to enjoy there. The forest is described. It was filled with (ākulam) attractively humming bees, deer, birds, pleasing to the ears by the sweet sounds. It was served by wind, which took shelter of pools whose water was clear, sweet and cool like the hearts of great devotees. The winds were pleasing to the sense of touch because of the gentle cooling effect and pleasing to the tongue by sweetness. It was served by the fragrance of hundred petal lotuses. The fragrance was pleasing to the nose and the beauty of the lotuses was pleasing to the touch. Thus it is indicated that the forest gave joy to the five senses.

### Text 4

*sa tatra tatrāruṇa-pallava-śriyā*  
*phala-prasūnoru-bhareṇa pādayoḥ*  
*spṛśac-chikhān vīkṣya vanaspatīn mudā*  
*smayann ivāhāgra-jam ādi-pūruṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the primeval Lord saw that the stately trees, with their beautiful reddish buds and their heavy burden of fruits and flowers, were bending down to touch his feet with the tips of their branches he smiled gently and addressed his elder brother.**

**Комментарий:**

Wandering here and there, the son of Nanda (sa), the ādi-puruṣa, seeing the trees, as if smiling, spoke to Balarāma. The trees are described. With the beauty of downward facing reddish buds, their branches touched his feet because of the heavy load of fruit. The excellence of the trees indicates ultimately the excellence of Kṛṣṇa.

Since it was not proper to indicate his own excellence, he addressed his brother. It is not a fault for him, to address his brother who is endowed with secrecy, since he had great friendship with him. He smiled as if in joy. He was unable to remain without uttering something very profound.

### Text 5

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*aho amī deva-varāmarārcitaṁ*  
*pādāmbujaṁ te sumanaḥ phalārhaṇam*  
*namanty upādāya śikhābhir ātmanas*  
*tamo-’pahatyai taru-janma yat-kṛtam*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O greatest of Lords, just see how these trees are bowing their heads at your lotus feet, which are worshipable by the devatās, by offering you their fruits and flowers, having taken birth as trees to eradicate the dark ignorance of others by their actions.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks to his brother, informing the trees, his devotees, “I know your intention is, ‘We will worship the feet of our master, Nanda’s son by our flowers.’” O best of Lords! These trees, bowing their heads, holding their fruits as gifts, offer respect to your lotus feet which are worshipped by Brahmā and other devatās. What is the purpose? They do this to destroy ignorance of those who hear how they respect us. They accepted birth in order to worship your feet with flowers. Or they do this in order to destroy their suffering caused by inability to take your association (unlike the birds and animals). They have taken birth as trees because of your lotus feet. One cannot say that they are ignorant because they possessed such bhāva and because Brahmā prayed to take birth as a tree.

### Text 6

*ete ’linas tava yaśo ’khila-loka-tīrthaṁ*  
*gāyanta ādi-puruṣānupathaṁ bhajante*  
*prāyo amī muni-gaṇā bhavadīya-mukhyā*  
*gūḍhaṁ vane ’pi na jahaty anaghātma-daivam*

**Перевод:**

**O original person! These bees must all be great sages and your most elevated devotees, for they are following you along the path and chanting your glories, which are themselves a holy place for the entire world. Though you have disguised yourself within this forest, O sinless one, they refuse to abandon you, their worshipable Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

He praises the animals living in Vṛndāvana in two verses. O original person (ādi-puruṣa). These bees, singing your glories, are worshipping you by following your bodily fragrance. They do not give you up, their worshippable deity, though you are hidden fromyour friends for secret pastimes. Therefore, they must be great sages like Śukadeva, among your followers, contemplating your secrets. O person without sin! You do not accept their sins when they come here. His approval is indicated.

### Text 7

*nṛtyanty amī śikhina īḍya mudā hariṇyaḥ*  
*kurvanti gopya iva te priyam īkṣaṇena*  
*sūktaiś ca kokila-gaṇā gṛham āgatāya*  
*dhanyā vanaukasa iyān hi satāṁ nisargaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O worshipable Balarāma! These peacocks are dancing before you out of joy, these doe are pleasing you with affectionate glances, just as the gopīs do, and these cuckoos are honoring you with Vedic prayers, as the inhabitants of the forest welcome you to their house. This is the nature of cultured people.**

**Комментарий:**

They welcome you who have come to their house (gṛham āgatāya). The cuckoos please you with Vedic prayers (sūktaiḥ). It is the nature of good people (iyān satāṁ nisargaḥ) to respect by dancing, joyful glances and pleasing words, a saintly person, who has come to their home.

### Text 8

*dhanyeyam adya dharaṇī tṛṇa-vīrudhas tvat-*  
*pāda-spṛśo druma-latāḥ karajābhimṛṣṭāḥ*  
*nadyo ’drayaḥ khaga-mṛgāḥ sadayāvalokair*  
*gopyo ’ntareṇa bhujayor api yat-spṛhā śrīḥ*

**Перевод:**

**This earth has now become most fortunate by the touch of your feet. The grass and bushes are most fortunate for the same reason, and the trees and creepers have been touched by your fingernails .The rivers and mountains are fortunate, being touched by your feet. The birds and animals have been touched with your merciful glances. But above all, you have embraced the young cowherd women between your two arms—a favor hankered after by the goddess of fortune herself.**

**Комментарий:**

The land of Vṛndāvana and other items there are praised by Kṛṣṇa as recipients of Balarāma’s mercy.

This land of Vṛndāvana (dharaṇī) is praiseworthy (dhanyā) today. Your touch gives the earth greater joy than when you touched the earth as Varāha avatāra. The creepers in the form of dūrva grass, which grow there, are praiseworthy because of the touch of your feet. The trees and creepers are praiseworthy because you touched them with your fingers to pick flowers. The rivers and mountains are praiseworthy because of your merciful glance. Seeing the śyāma- latā, moved by the wind, touching Balarāma’s chest, Kṛṣṇa speaks.

The śyāma creepers (gopyaḥ) or the gopīs are praiseworthy, on your chest (bhujayor anatarena) which is desired by Lakṣmī. This indicates the pūrva-rāga of the young gopīs for Kṛṣṇa as will be spoken by the Nāga-patnis:

*yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo*  
*vihāya kāmān su-ciraṁ dhṛta-vratā*

**The goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. (SB** [**10.16.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/16.36)**)**

### Text 9

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*evaṁ vṛndāvanaṁ śrīmat-prītaḥ prīta-manāḥ paśūn*  
*reme sañcārayann adreḥ sarid-rodhaḥsu sānugaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus expressing his satisfaction with the beautiful forest of Vṛndāvana and its inhabitants, Kṛṣṇa enjoyed in Vṛndāvana, tending the cows and other animals with his friends on the banks of the river Yamunā below Govardhana Hill.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way, by praising Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa enjoyed (reme) in Vṛndāvana. A place becomes the object of the verb which is intransitive. Balarāma and others delighted in him (śrīmat-prītaḥ). With his servants (sānugaḥ) he herded the cows on the banks of Mānasa Gaṅgā near Govardhana. The secret meaning is this. Having praised Balarāma in this way, Kṛṣṇa became stimulated with amorous love when he mentioned gopyāntareṇa (the śyāma- latā was embraced by Balarāma’s arms). Then informing Balarāma, “Keeping the cows and friends here, I, along with Subala, will see the beauty of Govardhana and return,” he herded the cows in Vṛndāvana through Balarāma. He was the object of prema of Śrīmatī (śrīmat-prītaḥ). Thus, his mind filled with prema (prīta-manāḥ), he enjoyed on the bank of Mānasa Gaṅgā near Govardhana, with her followers (sānugaḥ).”

### Text 10

*kvacid gāyati gāyatsu madāndhāliṣv anuvrataiḥ*  
*upagīyamāna-caritaḥ pathi saṅkarṣaṇānvitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In the company of Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa, whose pastimes are praised, sang along with his followers when the highly intoxicated bees began humming.**

### Text 11

*anujalpati jalpantaṁ kala-vākyaiḥ śukaṁ kvacit*  
*kvacit sa-valgu kūjantam anukūjati kokilam*  
*kvacic ca kāla-haṁsānām anukūjati kūjitam*  
*abhinṛtyati nṛtyantaṁ barhiṇaṁ hāsayan kvacit*

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes Kṛṣṇa sweetly imitated what the parrot uttered, using soft words. Sometimes he sweetly cooed in imitation of the cooing pigeons. Sometimes he sweetly imitated the cooing of the swans. Sometimes he made his friends laugh by imitating the dancing peacocks.**

**Комментарий:**

He imitated the dancing peacocks and made his friends laugh.

### Text 12

*megha-gambhīrayā vācā nāmabhir dūra-gān paśūn*  
*kvacid āhvayati prītyā go-gopāla-manojñayā*

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes he affectionately called the cows which had wandered far off, with a voice like rumbling clouds, using their names.**

### Text 13

*cakora-krauñca-cakrāhva-bhāradvājāṁś ca barhiṇaḥ*  
*anurauti sma sattvānāṁ bhīta-vad vyāghra-siṁhayoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes he would cry out in imitation of birds such as the cakoras, krauñcas, cakrāhvas, bhāradvājas and peacocks, as if in fear of tigers and lions among all the animals.**

**Комментарий:**

He imitated the cakoras and other birds. Sometimes, he seemed to show fear (bhītavat) of tigers and lions among the living beings (sattvānāṁ), and he would flee when other animals fled. By the suffix vat (in bhītavat) it is shown that he was actually not afraid since he is himself very brave. This was for fun since even his brave friends ran away.

### Text 14

*kvacit krīḍā-pariśrāntaṁ gopotsaṅgopabarhaṇam*  
*svayaṁ viśramayaty āryaṁ pāda-saṁvāhanādibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When his elder brother, fatigued from playing, would lie down with his head upon the lap of a cowherd boy, Kṛṣṇa would help him relax by personally massaging his feet and offering other services.**

**Комментарий:**

He made Balarāma relax, arranging the lap of a boy as a pillow for his head.

### Text 15

*nṛtyato gāyataḥ kvāpi valgato yudhyato mithaḥ*  
*gṛhīta-hastau gopālān hasantau praśaśaṁsatuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes, as the cowherd boys danced, sang, moved about and playfully fought with each other, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, standing nearby hand in hand, would glorify their friends’ activities and laugh.**

**Комментарий:**

Laughing Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma would praise the cowherd boys who were dancing, etc.

### Text 16

*kvacit pallava-talpeṣu niyuddha-śrama-karśitaḥ*  
*vṛkṣa-mūlāśrayaḥ śete gopotsaṅgopabarhaṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes Kṛṣṇa grew tired from fighting and lay down at the base of a tree, resting upon a bed made of soft twigs and buds and using the lap of a cowherd friend as his pillow.**

**Комментарий:**

Tired from wrestling with friends (niyuddha), he seemed to become thin, with beads of beautiful perspiration like pearls on his forehead. This indicates that he and the boys equally showed prowess in fighting. It is said gopaiḥ samāna-guṇa-śīla-vayo-vilāsa- veśaiḥ: the boys had similar qualities, character, age, actions and dress. (Krama-dīpikā) The fatigue in the boys arose from the desireto serve. They relished the service since it is free from the eighteen faults.

### Text 17

*pāda-saṁvāhanaṁ cakruḥ kecit tasya mahātmanaḥ*  
*apare hata-pāpmāno vyajanaiḥ samavījayan*

**Перевод:**

**Some of the cowherd boys, who were all great souls, would then massage his lotus feet, and others, qualified by being free of all sin, would expertly fan him.**

**Комментарий:**

Their service is described. They were free of all sins eternally (hata- pāpmānaḥ) like dahara, the space in the heart. They fanned using tāla leaf fans and cāmaras.

### Text 18

*anye tad-anurūpāṇi manojñāni mahātmanaḥ*  
*gāyanti sma mahā-rāja sneha-klinna-dhiyaḥ śanaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, other boys would sing enchanting songs appropriate to the occasion, and their hearts would melt out of love for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

They sang songs suitable to his fame.

### Text 19

*evaṁ nigūḍhātma-gatiḥ sva-māyayā*  
*gopātmajatvaṁ caritair viḍambayan*  
*reme ramā-lālita-pāda-pallavo*  
*grāmyaiḥ samaṁ grāmya-vad īśa-ceṣṭitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In this way the Supreme Lord, whose soft lotus feet are personally attended by the goddess of fortune when he takes other forms, whose sweetness cannot be understood by anyone, acted like the son of a cowherd to show mercy to his parents. Yet even while enjoying like a village boy in the company of other village residents, he often exhibited feats only the Lord could perform.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse summarizes the pastimes. He enjoyed by such playing in Vṛndāvana. This indicates that such enjoyment is not there in the pastimes of Vaikuṇṭha. Out of mercy to his devotees (sva-māyayā), he establishes his pure powers within human-like actions in ahidden way (nigūḍha ātmā-gatiḥ), like a picture below a mirror, since his pure powers do not please his devotees. Though he was the son of a cowherd, by his activities such as killing Pūtanā, he rejected his role as son of a cowherd, or as son of a king since in those activities even a trace of being the son of cowherd or king were absent. Kṛṣṇa’s feet were desired (lālita) by Mahā-lakṣmī (ramā) of Gokula who was referred to in verse 9. Though he hides his powers, sometimes these become evident when he kills demons. That is explained in this verse. His actions are filled with power (īśa-ceṣṭitaḥ). He did not reveal these in playing with his friends. He was like a village friend (grāmya-vat) acting with village friends (grāmyaiḥ).

### Text 20

*śrīdāmā nāma gopālo rāma-keśavayoḥ sakhā*  
*subala-stokakṛṣṇādyā gopāḥ premṇedam abruvan*

**Перевод:**

**Once, some of the cowherd boys—Śrīdāmā, the very close friend of Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, along with Subala, Stokakṛṣṇa and others—lovingly spoke the following words.**

**Комментарий:**

His actions showing power are described. Śrīdāmā was Rādhā’s older brother and a pīṭha-marda sakha. He spoke with love, so that Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma could taste the tāla fruit, though superficially indicating his own interest in the fruit.

### Text 21

*rāma rāma mahā-bāho kṛṣṇa duṣṭa-nibarhaṇa*  
*ito ’vidūre su-mahad vanaṁ tālāli-saṅkulam*

**Перевод:**

**O Rāma, Rāma, mighty-armed one! O Kṛṣṇa, destroyer of the miscreants! Not far from here is a very great forest filled with rows of palm trees.**

**Комментарий:**

The place is not far from Govardhana, within a yojana.

*asti tāla-vanaṁ nāma dhenakāsura-rakṣitam*  
*mathurā-paścime bhāge adūrād eka-yojanam*

**Not far from the western side of Mathurā, one yojana away \[eight miles\], is the forest known as Tālavana, which was guarded by Dhenukāsura. (Varāha Purāṇa)**

Western portion means south-west. But the forest was blocked by Dhenuka. O Balarāma! Your great strength, and O Kṛṣṇa! your ability to kill the wicked will be tested today. Sending Kṛṣṇa to a fearful place does not diminish Śrīdāmā’s prema, since he knew Kṛṣṇa’s great prowess because of his great friendship. Rather his prema increased by stimulating vīra-rasa.

### Text 22

*phalāni tatra bhūrīṇi patanti patitāni ca*  
*santi kintv avaruddhāni dhenukena durātmanā*

**Перевод:**

**In that Tālavana forest many fruits are falling from the trees, and many are already lying on the ground. But all the fruits are being guarded by the evil Dhenuka.**

### Text 23

*so ’ti-vīryo ’suro rāma he kṛṣṇa khara-rūpa-dhṛk*  
*ātma-tulya-balair anyair jñātibhir bahubhir vṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Rāma, O Kṛṣṇa! Dhenuka is a most powerful demon and has assumed the form of an ass. He is surrounded by many friends who have assumed a similar shape and who are just as powerful as he.**

**Комментарий:**

He says that Dhenuka is very powerful to stimulate the prowess of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.

### Text 24

*tasmāt kṛta-narāhārād bhītair nṛbhir amitra-han*  
*na sevyate paśu-gaṇaiḥ pakṣi-saṅghair vivarjitam*

**Перевод:**

**The demon Dhenuka has eaten men alive, and therefore all people and animals are terrified of going to the tāla forest. O killer of the enemy, even the birds are afraid to fly there.**

**Комментарий:**

“What is his power over us?” You should go there. Destroying him will benefit the people.

### Text 25

*vidyante ’bhukta-pūrvāṇi phalāni surabhīṇi ca*  
*eṣa vai surabhir gandho viṣūcīno ’vagṛhyate*

**Перевод:**

**In the tāla forest are sweet-smelling fruits no one has ever tasted. Indeed, even now we can smell the fragrance of the tāla fruits spreading all about.**

**Комментарий:**

“How far is this place?” The fragrance of the fruit can be smelled, spreading everywhere (viṣūcīnaḥ).

### Text 26

*prayaccha tāni naḥ kṛṣṇa gandha-lobhita-cetasām*  
*vāñchāsti mahatī rāma gamyatāṁ yadi rocate*

**Перевод:**

**O Kṛṣṇa! Please get those fruits for us. Our minds are so attracted by their aroma! Dear Balarāma, our desire to have those fruits is very great. If you think it’s a good idea, go to that tāla forest.**

**Комментарий:**

Give those fruits to us. We have desire for them.

### Text 27

*evaṁ suhṛd-vacaḥ śrutvā suhṛt-priya-cikīrṣayā*  
*prahasya jagmatur gopair vṛtau tālavanaṁ prabhū*

**Перевод:**

**Hearing the words of their dear companions, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma laughed and, desiring to please them by showing their abilities, set off for the Tālavana surrounded by their cowherd boyfriends.**

**Комментарий:**

They smiled. We will even touch donkeys to make our friends happy.

### Text 28

*balaḥ praviśya bāhubhyāṁ tālān samparikampayan*  
*phalāni pātayām āsa mataṅ-gaja ivaujasā*

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma entered the tāla forest first. Then, with his two arms, he began forcefully shaking the trees with the power of a maddened elephant, causing the tāla fruits to fall to the ground.**

### Text 29

*phalānāṁ patatāṁ śabdaṁ niśamyāsura-rāsabhaḥ*  
*abhyadhāvat kṣiti-talaṁ sa-nagaṁ parikampayan*

**Перевод:**

**Hearing the sound of the falling fruits, the ass demon Dhenuka ran forward to attack, making the earth and mountains tremble.**

**Комментарий:**

Sa-nagam means with mountains.

### Text 30

*sametya tarasā pratyag-dvābhyāṁ padbhyāṁ balaṁ balī*  
*nihatyorasi kā-śabdaṁ muñcan paryasarat khalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The powerful demon rushed up to Baladeva and sharply struck the Lord’s chest with the hooves of his hind legs. Then Dhenuka began to run about, braying loudly.**

**Комментарий:**

The demon struck Balarāma with his two hind (pratyag) legs. Kā is an imitation of the sound of a donkey. He ran around (paryasarat).

### Text 31

*punar āsādya saṁrabdha upakroṣṭā parāk-sthitaḥ*  
*caraṇāv aparau rājan balāya prākṣipad ruṣā*

**Перевод:**

**O King! Moving again toward Balarāma while braying, the furious ass situated himself with his back toward him. Then the demon kicked him in anger.**

**Комментарий:**

Angry (saṁrabdhaḥ), braying nearby (upakroṣṭā), turning around (parāk-sthitaḥ), he kicked with his back (aparau) legs.

### Text 32

*sa taṁ gṛhītvā prapador bhrāmayitvaika-pāṇinā*  
*cikṣepa tṛṇa-rājāgre bhrāmaṇa-tyakta-jīvitam*

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma seized Dhenuka by his hooves whirled him about with one hand, and threw the demon, who died because of being whirled around, into the top of a palm tree.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma (saḥ) grabbed the ends of the donkey’s two feet (prapadoḥ) and threw him on top of a tāla tree (tṛṇa-rājāgre).

### Text 33

*tenāhato mahā-tālo vepamāno bṛhac-chirāḥ*  
*pārśva-sthaṁ kampayan bhagnaḥ sa cānyaṁ so ’pi cāparam*

**Перевод:**

**Being struck by the demon’s body, a huge tāla tree with a huge top began shaking and then broke, causing others to shake and break.**

### Text 34

*balasya līlayotsṛṣṭa-khara-deha-hatāhatāḥ*  
*tālāś cakampire sarve mahā-vāteritā iva*

**Перевод:**

**When Balarāma’s casually threw the body of the ass demon into the top of the tallest palm tree, all the trees even at a distance began shaking as if blown about by powerful winds.**

**Комментарий:**

The trees were struck (āhatāḥ) by the tree struck (hata) by the donkey’s body thrown casually by Balarāma.

### Text 35

*naitac citraṁ bhagavati hy anante jagad-īśvare*  
*ota-protam idaṁ yasmiṁs tantuṣv aṅga yathā paṭaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear Parīkṣit! That Balarāma killed Dhenukāsura is not such a wonderful thing, considering that he is Bhagavān, the unlimited and the controller of the entire universe. In him, the entire cosmos rests as cloth depends on its threads.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma’s valor was not astonishing. In him this universe (idam) is woven like a cloth which is woven in lengthwise threads and crosswise threads (ota-protam). The universe is uninterruptedly sewed in him everywhere.

### Text 36

*tataḥ kṛṣṇaṁ ca rāmaṁ ca jñātayo dhenukasya ye*  
*kroṣṭāro ’bhyadravan sarve saṁrabdhā hata-bāndhavāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The other ass demons, close friends of Dhenukāsura, were enraged upon seeing his death, and thus they all immediately ran to attack Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.**

### Text 37

*tāṁs tān āpatataḥ kṛṣṇo rāmaś ca nṛpa līlayā*  
*gṛhīta-paścāc-caraṇān prāhiṇot tṛṇa-rājasu*

**Перевод:**

**O King, as the demons attacked, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma easily seized them one after another by their hind legs and threw them all into the tops of the palm trees.**

**Комментарий:**

O King (nṛpa)!

### Text 38

*phala-prakara-saṅkīrṇaṁ daitya-dehair gatāsubhiḥ*  
*rarāja bhūḥ sa-tālāgrair ghanair iva nabhas-talam*

**Перевод:**

**The earth then appeared beautifully covered with heaps of fruits and with the dead bodies of the demons, which were entangled in the broken tops of the palm trees. The earth shone like the sky decorated with clouds.**

**Комментарий:**

The earth shone with the demons’ bodies, and the tops of tāla trees, just as it was spread with heaps of fruit. Because the trees were black and blood was sprinkled around, the earth appeared like the sky (nabhas-talam) with black and red clouds. Talam means asupport according to Viśva.

### Text 39

*tayos tat su-mahat karma niśamya vibudhādayaḥ*  
*mumucuḥ puṣpa-varṣāṇi cakrur vādyāni tuṣṭuvuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Observing this magnificent feat of the two brothers, the devatās and other elevated living beings rained down flowers and offered music and prayers in glorification.**

### Text 40

*atha tāla-phalāny ādan manuṣyā gata-sādhvasāḥ*  
*tṛṇaṁ ca paśavaś cerur hata-dhenuka-kānane*

**Перевод:**

**People without fear then ate the fruits of the palm trees. Also, the cows could now graze freely upon the grass in the forest where Dhenuka was killed.**

**Комментарий:**

The local people, the śabaras, ate the fruit, but the cowherds did not. They did not accept the fruit on that day since they were sprinkled with the blood of the donkey.

### Text 41

*kṛṣṇaḥ kamala-patrākṣaḥ puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ*  
*stūyamāno ’nugair gopaiḥ sāgrajo vrajam āvrajat*

**Перевод:**

**Lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, whose glories are most auspicious to hear and chant, returned home to Vraja with his elder brother, Balarāma, praised by the cowherd boys who followed behind.**

**Комментарий:**

The pastime of entering Vraja from the forest is described in three verses.

### Text 42

*taṁ go-rajaś-churita-kuntala-baddha-barha-*  
*vanya-prasūna-rucirekṣaṇa-cāru-hāsam*  
*veṇum kvaṇantam anugair upagīta-kīrtiṁ*  
*gopyo didṛkṣita-dṛśo ’bhyagaman sametāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa’s hair, covered with the dust raised by the cows, was decorated with a peacock feather and forest flowers. He glanced charmingly and smiled beautifully, playing upon his flute while his companions chanted his glories. The young gopīs, all together, came forward to meet him, their eyes very eager to see him.**

**Комментарий:**

He particularly attracted the young girls. The young gopīs came forward to meet Kṛṣṇa. They climbed the terraces of buildings located along the path of his arrival.

Their eyes had developed the desire to see him. Though the eyes are intruments by designating them as the doers in the desire to see, it is implied that they did not consider restraining it even out of shame and fear. Thus their eyes were not in their control.

It indicates that the eyes were in pursuit of attaining his form, as if in envy of the ears and nose which had attained the sound of the flute and the fragrance of his limbs. They went together to see him. Thus they did not mind their mothers-in-law.

Kṛṣṇa’s locks of hair were powdered with the dust raised by the cows and decorated with forest flowers and a peacock feather, and who glanced charmingly and smiled attractively.

### Text 43

*pītvā mukunda-mukha-sāragham akṣi-bhṛṅgais*  
*tāpaṁ jahur viraha-jaṁ vraja-yoṣito ’hni*  
*tat sat-kṛtiṁ samadhigamya viveśa goṣṭhaṁ*  
*savrīḍa-hāsa-vinayaṁ yad apāṅga-mokṣam*

**Перевод:**

**With their cup-like eyes, the women of Vṛndāvana drank the honey of the beautiful face of Mukunda, and thus they gave up the distress they had felt during the day because of separation from him. The young Vṛndāvana ladies cast sidelong glances at the Lord—glances filled with bashfulness, laughter and submission—and he, completely accepting these glances as a proper offering of respect, entered his house in the village.**

**Комментарий:**

What they did after approaching Kṛṣṇa is described. Mukunda here signifies that he would deliver them from all suffering. They drank the honey of the smile on the lotus face of Mukunda, who would deliver them from the pain of separation, with their eyes which were bees (bhṛṅgaiḥ) and not by the bees of their sidelong glances.

By mentioning pītvā, the idea is that before Kṛṣṇa saw them, they drank his naturally perfect smile without fear. By this they removed the longing arising from separation from him during the day. They removed the longing caused by separation at night by seeing him in the morning. Thus receiving their respects, Kṛṣṇa entered his house.

Here sa-vrīḍa-hāsa-vinayaṁ (bashful smiles and submission) modifies the action sat-kṛti (to respect) and yad-apāṅga-mokṣammodifies the action samadhigamya (to receive). Thus, their respect was in such a way where the bashful smiles and submission were. Kṛṣṇa received their respect in such a way that receiving the respect, his sidelong glances were released from them.

When they gazed at Kṛṣṇa’s moon-like face and Kṛṣṇa noticed, they smiled in joy (hāsa). Or on seeing his smile they covered their lotus faces out of shyness (lajjā) arising then. They became submissive (vinaya) which indicated their good character. Kṛṣṇa accepted their offering of submission permeated with fragrance, their offering of flower clusters consisting of smiles glances held in the hands of their lips and eyes.

Glancing at them, he went home. They would hide their feelings out of shyness when they glanced with their two eyes. Thus, he honored them in order to gain their side glance. Placing those glance, similar to a wealth of precious gems, in the treasure box of his heart, he went home.

Or the women of Vraja gave up pain during the day. Those women are then described. Their side glances are famous. Receiving those glances graciously, he went home. Their response is then described. The glances were filled with shyness, laughter and submission. Here since the word yat here comes later in the sentence, it is not linked to the word tat that comes earlier.

### Text 44

*tayor yaśodā-rohiṇyau putrayoḥ putra-vatsale*  
*yathā-kāmaṁ yathā-kālaṁ vyadhattāṁ paramāśiṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Mother Yaśodā and mother Rohiṇī, acting most affectionately toward their two sons, offered all the best things to them in response to their every desire and at the various appropriate times.**

**Комментарий:**

Mother Yaśodā and Rohiṇī offered wonderful food and clothes (param āśiṣaḥ) not ignoring their sons’ desires (yathā-kāmaṁ). They also made sure the boys ate at the proper time (yathā-kālaṁ), rather than forbidden times like sunset.

### Texts 45-46

*gatādhvāna-śramau tatra majjanonmardanādibhiḥ*  
*nīvīṁ vasitvā rucirāṁ divya-srag-gandha-maṇḍitau*

*janany-upahṛtaṁ prāśya svādy annam upalālitau*  
*saṁviśya vara-śayyāyāṁ sukhaṁ suṣupatur vraje*

**Перевод:**

**By being bathed and massaged, the two young boys were relieved of the weariness caused by walking on the country roads. Then they were dressed in attractive robes and decorated with transcendental garlands and fragrances. After dining sumptuously on the delicious food given them by their mothers and being pampered in various ways, the two brothers lay down upon their excellent beds and happily went to sleep in the village of Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verse go together. Their fatigue arising from the path (adhvāna) was gone (gata). Nīvīm is an upper garment. They slept on the best bed, covered with jewels and which was soft like the foam of milk. They went into yoga-nidrā, experiencing the bliss of their svarūpa, endowed with varous pastimes (suñupatuḥ).

### Text 47

*evaṁ sa bhagavān kṛṣṇo vṛndāvana-caraḥ kvacit*  
*yayau rāmam ṛte rājan kālindīṁ sakhibhir vṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa thus wandered about the Vṛndāvana area, performing his pastimes. Once, surrounded by his boyfriends, he went without Balarāma to the Yamunā River.**

**Комментарий:**

After finishing the description of the Gopāṣṭamī pastimes in Kārtika, the pastimes of a day in the summer of that year are told. Balarāma was kept at home by his mother because on that day was the conjuction of his birth constellation.

### Text 48

*atha gāvaś ca gopāś ca nidāghātapa-pīḍitāḥ*  
*duṣṭaṁ jalaṁ papus tasyās tṛṣṇārtā viṣa-dūṣitam*

**Перевод:**

**At that time the cows and cowherd boys were feeling acute distress from the glaring summer sun. Afflicted by thirst, they drank the water of the Yamunā River. But it had been contaminated with poison.**

**Комментарий:**

Ignoring Kṛṣṇa, who was walking slowly behind, the cows ran quickly due to their intense thirst and drank the water.

### Text 49

*viṣāmbhas tad upaspṛśya daivopahata-cetasaḥ*  
*nipetur vyasavaḥ sarve salilānte kurūdvaha*

**Перевод:**

**O descendant of the Kurus! Their minds bewildered by the Lord’s śakti, the boys, sipping the poisonous water, fell down on the bank of the river as if dead.**

**Комментарий:**

This is was the power of the līlā-śakti (daivaṁ) of Kṛṣṇa, the Lord. They were lifeless (vyasavaḥ) since their lifeairs were made to faint by those powers for the sake of the pastime, like how Balarāma’s intelligence was in illusion.

### Text 50

*vīkṣya tān vai tathā-bhūtān kṛṣṇo yogeśvareśvaraḥ*  
*īkṣayāmṛta-varṣiṇyā sva-nāthān samajīvayat*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the boys who had no Lord other than him in such a condition, Kṛṣṇa, the master of all masters of mystic potency, immediately brought them back to life by showering his nectarean glance upon them.**

**Комментарий:**

He brought them to life completely (samajīvayat).

### Text 51

*te sampratīta-smṛtayaḥ samutthāya jalāntikāt*  
*āsan su-vismitāḥ sarve vīkṣamāṇāḥ parasparam*

**Перевод:**

**Regaining their full consciousness, the cows and boys stood up on the bank of the river and began to look at one another in great astonishment.**

**Комментарий:**

Returning to consciousness, the cowherd boys thinking, “By whom were we revived?” were looking at each other. They remembered completely the enemy of Aghāsura and were astonished.

### Text 52

*anvamaṁsata tad rājan govindānugrahekṣitam*  
*pītvā viṣaṁ paretasya punar utthānam ātmanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King, the cowherd boys then surmised that although they had drunk poison and in fact had died, simply by the merciful glance of Govinda they had regained their lives.**

**Комментарий:**

Then (anu) they surmised that it was the glance of mercy of Govinda that brought them back to life.

## Chapter 16 - Kṛṣṇa Chastises the Serpent Kāliya

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*vilokya dūṣitāṁ kṛṣṇāṁ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇāhinā vibhuḥ*  
*tasyā viśuddhim anvicchan sarpaṁ tam udavāsayat*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Śrī Kṛṣṇa, manifesting his power, seeing that the Yamunā River had been contaminated by the black snake Kāliya, desired to purify the river, and thus banished him from it.**

**Комментарий:**

*ṣoḍaśe kāliyaṁ kṛṣṇo nyagṛhṇāt tad-vadhū-stutaḥ \|*  
*anugṛhya tam utsārya yamunāṁ nirviṣāṁ vyadhāt*

**In the sixteenth chapter Kṛṣṇa arrests Kāliya, shows mercy to his wives, releases Kāliya and makes Yamunā free of poison.**

Yamunā (kṛṣṇām) is his friend because of similarity in name and color. He must certainly help his friend. The river was contaminated by the black snake Kāliya. He drove him from the river.

### Text 2

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*katham antar-jale ’gādhe nyagṛhṇād bhagavān ahim*  
*sa vai bahu-yugāvāsaṁ yathāsīd vipra kathyatām*

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit inquired: O learned sage, please explain how the Lord subdued the serpent Kāliya within the unfathomable waters of the Yamunā, and how it was that Kāliya had been living there for so many ages.**

**Комментарий:**

How did he subdue the snake in the deep water? Please explain how the snake lived in the water for many yugas, though snakes do not live in water? O brāhmaṇa, expert at knowledge(vipra)! Yājñavalkya says:

*janmanā brāhmaṇo jñeyaḥ saṁskārair dvija ucyate*  
*vidyayā yāti vipratvaṁ tribhiḥ śrotriya-lakṣaṇam*

**A person is known as a brāhmaṇa by birth and as a dvija by saṁskāras. By knowledge he is becomes a vipra and by these three he becomes a śrotriya.**

### Text 3

*brahman bhagavatas tasya bhūmnaḥ svacchanda-vartinaḥ*  
*gopālodāra-caritaṁ kas tṛpyetāmṛtaṁ juṣan*

**Перевод:**

**O brāhmaṇa, the unlimited Bhagavān, freely acts according to his own desires. Who could be satiated when hearing the nectar of the blissful pastimes he performed as a cowherd boy in Vṛndāvana?**

**Комментарий:**

He gives happiness by nourishing the cows and the ears (go) of his devotees (gopālodāra).

### Text 4

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*kālindyāṁ kāliyasyāsīd hradaḥ kaścid viṣāgninā*  
*śrapyamāṇa-payā yasmin patanty upari-gāḥ khagāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Within the river Kālindī was a lake inhabited by the serpent Kāliya, whose fiery poison constantly boiled its waters. Because of its vapors, birds flying high above would fall into it.**

**Комментарий:**

The lake was in the southern portion of the river, untouched by the current and measuring a yojana according to Hari-vaṁśa. By the touch of such water flowing, the water would have become unusable by the people of Mathurā. Its water was boiled by fire of the poison. Birds would fall into it, afflicted by the poisonous fire.

### Text 5
