*vipruṣmatā viṣadormi-mārutenābhimarśitāḥ*  
*mriyante tīra-gā yasya prāṇinaḥ sthira-jaṅgamāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Touched by the wind blowing over that deadly waves of the lake, filled droplets of that water, all vegetation and creatures on the shore died.**

**Комментарий:**

Touched by the wind carrying drops of the poisonous water (vipruṣmatā), creatures would die.

### Text 6

*taṁ caṇḍa-vega-viṣa-vīryam avekṣya tena*  
*duṣṭāṁ nadīṁ ca khala-saṁyamanāvatāraḥ*  
*kṛṣṇaḥ kadambam adhiruhya tato ’ti-tuṅgam*  
*āsphoṭya gāḍha-raśano nyapatad viṣode*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing how the Kāliya serpent had polluted the Yamunā River with his terribly powerful poison, Kṛṣṇa who had descended from the spiritual world specifically to subdue envious demons, climbed to the top of a very high kadamba tree, tied his belt tightly, slapped his arms and then jumped into the poisonous water.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the snake (tam), Kṛṣṇa climbed a kadamba tree and from a very high point jumped into the poisonous water. This kadamba tree did not dry up because of the future good fortune of being touched by the Lord’s feet or because Garuḍa who was carrying nectar had perched upon it. He tightened his belt (rasanaḥ). This also indicted he prepared his hair and turban. He slapped his left arm with the palm of his right hand.

### Text 7

*sarpa-hradaḥ puruṣa-sāra-nipāta-vega-*  
*saṅkṣobhitoraga-viṣocchvasitāmbu-rāśiḥ*  
*paryak pluto viṣa-kaṣāya-vibhīṣaṇormir*  
*dhāvan dhanuḥ-śatam ananta-balasya kiṁ tat*

**Перевод:**

**Kāliya’s lake overflowed with water swelling with the snake’s poison on being agitated by the shock when the best among men fell into the water. Terrifying waves discolored with poison spread everywhere, overflowing for a hundred dhanus. What was this for Kṛṣṇa of unlimited strength?**

**Комментарий:**

The lake, increasing with the poison of snakes agitated by the force of the strong fall of the Lord, had fearful waves colored red andyellow (kaṣāya) by the poison and overflowed, spreading a hundred dhanus. A dhanu is measured as follows:

*aṣṭabhir yava-madhyaiḥ syād aṅgulaṁ*  
*tais tribhir bhavet tālam tri-tālako*  
*hasto hastau dvau kiṣkur ucyate*  
*kiṣku-dvayam dhanuḥ proktam*

**Eight yava-madhyas make an aṅgula. Three aṅgulas make a tāla. Three tālas make a hasta. Two hastas make a kiṣku. Two kiṣkus make a dhanu.**

### Text 8

*tasya hrade viharato bhuja-daṇḍa-ghūrṇa-*  
*vār-ghoṣam aṅga vara-vāraṇa-vikramasya*  
*āśrutya tat sva-sadanābhibhavaṁ nirīkṣya*  
*cakṣuḥ-śravāḥ samasarat tad amṛṣyamāṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa began sporting in Kāliya’s lake like a lordly elephant. When Kāliya heard the sound of his mighty arms churning the water, he understood that someone was trespassing in his lake. Not tolerating this, the snake immediately approached.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing the loud noise of the water churned by arms of Kṛṣṇa as he played by swimming and making various noises with the water, seeing that his abode was trespassed by this fault, not tolerating it (amṛsyamāṇaḥ), the snake (cakṣuḥ-śravāḥ) approached.

### Text 9

*taṁ prekṣaṇīya-sukumāra-ghanāvadātaṁ*  
*śrīvatsa-pīta-vasanaṁ smita-sundarāsyam*  
*krīḍantam apratibhayaṁ kamalodarāṅghriṁ*  
*sandaśya marmasu ruṣā bhujayā cachāda*

**Перевод:**

**Kāliya saw that Kṛṣṇa, who wore yellow silken garments, was very delicate, shining like a cloud. His chest bore the mark of Śrīvatsa, his face had a beautiful smile and his feet resembled the whorl of a lotus flower. The Lord was playing fearlessly in the water. Kāliya furiously bit his limbs and then completely enwrapped him in his coils.**

**Комментарий:**

The attractive form of Kṛṣṇa was opposite to that of Kāliya. He shone like a cloud (ghanāvādātam). His chest was marked with the line of Lakṣmī. He wore yellow cloth. Kāliya surrounded him with his coils (bhujayā).

### Text 10

*taṁ nāga-bhoga-parivītam adṛṣṭa-ceṣṭam*  
*ālokya tat-priya-sakhāḥ paśupā bhṛśārtāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇe ’rpitātma-suhṛd-artha-kalatra-kāmā*  
*duḥkhānuśoka-bhaya-mūḍha-dhiyo nipetuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the members of the cowherd community, who had accepted Kṛṣṇa as their dearest friend, who had offered him themselves, their friends, their wealth, their wives and goals of life, saw him enveloped in the snake’s coils, motionless, they were filled with pain. Overwhelmed by sorrow, lamentation and fear they fainted and fell on the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

They saw him surrounded by the snake’s coils, motionless. “Let me be surrounded by your coils as you desire now and then later I will show my prowess.” He remained with pride in his prowess.

Some of the cowherds situated in the fields, and those ploughing, quickly came. They are described. They had offered everything— themselves, their friends, etc., and enjoyment (kāmāḥ) to Kṛṣṇa to care for him. Lamenting because of sorrow they thought, “How can we exist without him?” Losing power of discrimination because of lamentation and fear, they fell on the ground like uprooted trees.

### Text 11

*gāvo vṛṣā vatsataryaḥ krandamānāḥ su-duḥkhitāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇe nyastekṣaṇā bhītā rudantya iva tasthire*

**Перевод:**

**The cows, bulls and female calves, in great distress, called out piteously to Kṛṣṇa. Fixing their eyes on him, they stood still in fear, shedding tears as if they were humans.**

**Комментарий:**

The cows seemed to cry, since their tears had dried up from disturbance of fear.

### Text 12

*atha vraje mahotpātās tri-vidhā hy ati-dāruṇāḥ*  
*utpetur bhuvi divy ātmany āsanna-bhaya-śaṁsinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In the Vṛndāvana area there then arose all three types of fearful omens—those on the earth, those in the sky and those in the bodies of living creatures—which announced imminent danger.**

**Комментарий:**

There were three types of omens: on earth, such as earthquakes; in the sky, such as comets; and in the self, such as twitching of the left eye. These omens of inauspiciousness were arranged by the līlā-śakti only at this place for attracting the people of Vraja by the omens disturbing their minds. They are not actually possible in the Lord or his devotees.

### Text 13

*tān ālakṣya bhayodvignā gopā nanda-purogamāḥ*  
*vinā rāmeṇa gāḥ kṛṣṇaṁ jñātvā cārayituṁ gatam*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the inauspicious omens, Nanda Mahārāja and the other cowherd men were fearful, for they knew that Kṛṣṇa had gone to herd the cows that day without Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the omens, everyone left Gokula, understanding that Kṛṣṇa had gone without Balarāma. Three verses are taken together.

### Text 14

*tair durnimittair nidhanaṁ matvā prāptam atad-vidaḥ*  
*tat-prāṇās tan-manaskās te duḥkha-śoka-bhayāturāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thinking of his destruction because of the omens, with minds dedicated to him alone, accepting him as their very life, but not know his powers, they became afflicted with grief, lamentation and fear.**

**Комментарий:**

They thought he was dead (nidhanam). But meaning indicated by Sarasvatī devī is this. The phrase can mean “great treasure” (nitarām + dhanam). The lake was his place of pastimes, a great treasure. They were not aware of the actions of his līlā-śakti (atad-vidaḥ).

### Text 15

*ā-bāla-vṛddha-vanitāḥ sarve ’ṅga paśu-vṛttayaḥ*  
*nirjagmur gokulād dīnāḥ kṛṣṇa-darśana-lālasāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana, including the children, women and elderly persons, thinking of Kṛṣṇa just as a cow thinks of her helpless young calf, suffering and falling down, rushed out of the village, intent upon seeing him.**

**Комментарий:**

Out of great lamentation they were like cows, devoid of understanding the remedy.

### Text 16

*tāṁs tathā kātarān vīkṣya bhagavān mādhavo balaḥ*  
*prahasya kiñcin novāca prabhāva-jño ’nujasya saḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma, full of all powers, the master of all knowledge, smiled and said nothing, even though he saw the residents of Vṛndāvana in such distress, since he understood the extraordinary power of his younger brother.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma smiled. “He does not like to play with my avatāra, his great devotee Śeṣa, but he plays with this hostile lowly snake.” Though it is possible that Balarāma’s knowledge of Kṛṣṇa’s powers, like that of Nanda, would be covered because of great attraction to Kṛṣṇa, his knowledge was not covered by the līlā-śakti, devoted to the Lord’s desire, in order to prevent them from entering the lake. Infering from his smile that Kṛṣṇa would be auspicious, they did not even desire to give up their lives.

### Text 17

*te ’nveṣamāṇā dayitaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ sūcitayā padaiḥ*  
*bhagaval-lakṣaṇair jagmuḥ padavyā yamunā-taṭam*

**Перевод:**

**The residents hurried toward the banks of the Yamunā in search of their dear Kṛṣṇa, following the path marked by his footprints, which bore the unique signs of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

They followed the path marked by his footprints endowed with symbols of lotus and goad which indicated Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 18

*te tatra tatrābja-yavāṅkuśāśani-*  
*dhvajopapannāni padāni viśpateḥ*  
*mārge gavām anya-padāntarāntare*  
*nirīkṣamāṇā yayur aṅga satvarāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear King Parīkṣit! Seeing on the path, mixed with the footprints of cows, the footprints of the master of the entire cowherd community, marked with the lotus flower, barleycorn, elephant goad, thunderbolt and flag, the residents of Vṛndāvana rushed along in great haste.**

**Комментарий:**

Looking at the footprints of the master of the cowherds (viśpateḥ), by rejecting the footprints of others with which they were mixed, they went quickly. Just as how the discerning yogis (satvarāḥ), follow the path of the Vedas (gavām) in pursuance of the highesttattva while rejecting all illusory appearances of truth.

### Text 19

*antar hrade bhujaga-bhoga-parītam ārāt*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ nirīham upalabhya jalāśayānte*  
*gopāṁś ca mūḍha-dhiṣaṇān paritaḥ paśūṁś ca*  
*saṅkrandataḥ parama-kaśmalam āpur ārtāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**They saw from a distance that Kṛṣṇa was in the lake, motionless within the coils of the serpent. They further saw that unconscious cowherd boys scattered on the bank and animals crying out for Kṛṣṇa. Seeing all this, the residents of Vṛndāvana were overwhelmed with anguish and confusion.**

**Комментарий:**

Having arrived there, seeing from a distance Kṛṣṇa motionless, the cowherd boys unconscious (mūḍha-dhiṣaṇān) and the cows wailing, they were stupefied.

### Text 20

*gopyo ’nurakta-manaso bhagavaty anante*  
*tat-sauhṛda-smita-viloka-giraḥ smarantyaḥ*  
*graste ’hinā priyatame bhṛśa-duḥkha-taptāḥ*  
*śūnyaṁ priya-vyatihṛtaṁ dadṛśus tri-lokam*

**Перевод:**

**The young gopīs, whose minds were constantly attached to Kṛṣṇa, the unlimited Supreme Lord, held in the snake’s coils, became filled with intense grief for their dear most and remembered his loving friendship, his smiling glances and his talks with them. They saw that the entire universe, having lost its senses because of the condition of their beloved, had become completely empty.**

**Комментарий:**

The state of the young gopīs is described. Their minds were attracted to Kṛṣṇa, most beautiful (bhagavati), endowed with great qualities (anante).

*mahad-guṇatvād yam anantam āhuḥ*

**He is called unlimited because he manifests unlimited qualities to the devotee. (SB** [**1.18.19**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/18.19)**)**

They remembered his secret talks (giraḥ), his smiling glances, his friendliness to them (sauhrḍa). They saw the three worlds to be vacant of their beloved, because of being burned by the fire of his absence.

### Text 21

*tāḥ kṛṣṇa-mātaram apatyam anupraviṣṭāṁ*  
*tulya-vyathāḥ samanugṛhya śucaḥ sravantyaḥ*  
*tās tā vraja-priya-kathāḥ kathayantya āsan*  
*kṛṣṇānane ’rpita-dṛśo mṛtaka-pratīkāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Although the elder gopīs were feeling just as much distress and were pouring forth a flood of sorrowful tears, they had to forcibly hold back Kṛṣṇa’s mother, who wanted to enter the lake on seeing him there. These gopīs each took turns recounting the pastimes of the darling of Vraja. Fixing their eyes on his face, they then stood like corpses.**

**Комментарий:**

The condition of those with vātsalya is described. The gopīs famous for maternal love (tā) held back with their arms Yaśodā who wasabout to enter the water near (anu) Kṛṣṇa (apatyam). Having similar pain, they were shedding tears of grief. They narrated stories about Kṛṣṇa, such as killing Agha. They told her, “Your son will return after killing the snake, similar to Agha. How will he feel if we are drowned in the poison?” They appeared to be like corpses.

### Text 22

*kṛṣṇa-prāṇān nirviśato nandādīn vīkṣya taṁ hradam*  
*pratyaṣedhat sa bhagavān rāmaḥ kṛṣṇānubhāva-vit*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that Nanda Mahārāja and the other cowherd men, who had dedicated their very lives to Kṛṣṇa, were beginning to enter the serpent’s lake, Balarāma, giver of joy and full of power, knowing Kṛṣṇa’s actual power, restrained them.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma prevented Nanda and others from entering the water. O respectable elders! Have you forgotten Garga’s words: “You will be saved from all obstacles by this son. (SB [10.8.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.16)) Protect him with care. (SB [10.8.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.19))”? What is overcoming the obstacle of Kāliya for that mahā-puruṣa, my younger brother? You have seen his power many times. If you all drown in the poison who will care for him? With these words he prevented them.

### Text 23

*ittham sva-gokulam ananya-gatiṁ nirīkṣya*  
*sa-strī-kumāram ati-duḥkhitam ātma-hetoḥ*  
*ājñāya martya-padavīm anuvartamānaḥ*  
*sthitvā muhūrtam udatiṣṭhad uraṅga-bandhāt*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the people of Gokula in that condition, having no other protector, understanding completely the extreme suffering of everyone including women and children because of him, after remaining in the coils for a moment, to follow the path proper conduct, Kṛṣṇa then released himself from the snake’s coils.**

**Комментарий:**

Having shown inaction in order to increase Kāliya’s enthusiasm and to show the splendor of the bhāva of the people of Vraja, now he showed his prowess. Seeing the people of Gokula who had no other resort than bewilderment, understanding that they along with the women and children were grieving because of him, following the human codes of conduct that, “Whoever is to be punished, his faults should be visible in the world,” staying in the snake’s coils for a moment, he then released himself from the bondage of thesnake.

### Text 24

*tat-prathyamāna-vapuṣā vyathitātma-bhoga*  
*s tyaktvonnamayya kupitaḥ sva-phaṇān bhujaṅgaḥ*  
*tasthau śvasañ chvasana-randhra-viṣāmbarīṣa-*  
*stabdhekṣaṇolmuka-mukho harim īkṣamāṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**His coils tormented by the expanding body of the Lord, Kāliya released him. In great anger the serpent then raised his hoods high and stood still, breathing heavily. His nostrils appeared like vessels for cooking poison, and the staring eyes were like frying pans. His mouths were like firebrands. Thus the serpent looked at the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Showing the way he emerged, the fatigue of Kāliya is described. Kāliya’s body (bhogaḥ) was pained, as if broken, by the expandingarms, thighs and shanks of Kṛṣṇa. Bhoga means the snake’s body or hoods according to Viśva. Giving up squeezing him, the snake raising his hoods, breathing heavily, remained glaring at Kṛṣṇa. His nostrils were full of poison. His glaring eyes were like fiery frying pans (ambarīṣa). His mouths emitted poisonous flames.

### Text 25

*taṁ jihvayā dvi-śikhayā parilelihānaṁ*  
*dve sṛkkaṇī hy ati-karāla-viṣāgni-dṛṣṭim*  
*krīḍann amuṁ parisasāra yathā khagendro*  
*babhrāma so ’py avasaraṁ prasamīkṣamāṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Playing with Kāliya who licked his lips with his bifurcated tongues and whose eyes were like terrible poisonous fires, Kṛṣṇa circled him like Garuḍa. Kāliya watched intently at every step for an opportunity to bit him.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa playing with him, circled around the snake in order to confuse him. Kāliya, waiting for an opportunity to bite Kṛṣṇa, circled him. He did not get an opportunity to bite since Kṛṣṇa moved swiftly. Kṛṣṇa defeated him by playfully circling him horizontally.

### Text 26

*evaṁ paribhrama-hataujasam unnatāṁsam*  
*ānamya tat-pṛthu-śiraḥsv adhirūḍha ādyaḥ*  
*tan-mūrdha-ratna-nikara-sparśāti-tāmra-*  
*pādāmbujo ’khila-kalādi-gurur nanarta*

**Перевод:**

**Having severely depleted the serpent’s strength with his relentless circling, Kṛṣṇa, the first being, pushed down Kāliya’s raised shoulders and mounted his broad serpentine heads. Thus Kṛṣṇa, the original master of all fine arts, began to dance, his lotus feet deeply reddened by the touch of the numerous jewels upon the serpent’s heads.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa pushed down his shoulders which were raised. He pushed down the serpent’s heads with one hand, since the snake had tired by the circling and was unable to move about any longer. Then he climbed on those heads and danced. His lotus feet became very red by touching the many jewels on the snake’s head.

*kāliya-phaṇi-māṇikya-rañjitaḥ śrī-padāmbujaḥ*

**His lotus feet were colored by the gems on Kāliya’s hoods. (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa 2.36.39)**

“But how did he dance on the moving hoods?” Dancers, knowledgeable of arts, dance on plates, suspended ropes. Because he was the supreme teacher of all arts, this show of arts was not astonishing. He did this to delight those who were attracted to him.

### Text 27

*taṁ nartum udyatam avetya tadā tadīya-*  
*gandharva-siddha-muni-cāraṇa-deva-vadhvaḥ*  
*prītyā mṛdaṅga-paṇavānaka-vādya-gīta-*  
*puṣpopahāra-nutibhiḥ sahasopaseduḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the Lord anxious to dance, his associates like Garuḍa, the Gandharvas, Siddhas, sages, Cāraṇas and wives of the demigods—immediately served by playing drums such as mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas and ānakas, singing, showering flowers and reciting prayers.**

**Комментарий:**

There was no lack of ingredients for dancing. Seeing that the Lord, in order to dance, was saying thai-tathai (imitative sound ofmusical instruments) without accompaniment of mṛdaṅgas, etc., (udyataṁ), his servants (tat-tadīya), the Gandharvas and others, played drums.

### Text 28

*yad yac chiro na namate ’ṅga śataika-śīrṣṇas*  
*tat tan mamarda khara-daṇḍa-dharo ’ṅghri-pātaiḥ*  
*kṣīṇāyuṣo bhramata ulbaṇam āsyato ’sṛṅ*  
*nasto vaman parama-kaśmalam āpa nāgaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King! When one of Kāliya’s hundred prominent heads would not bow down, Kṛṣṇa, who inflicts punishment on cruel wrong- doers, would crush that head by striking it with his feet. Almost dead, wandering in confusion, the serpent experienced extreme pain, vomiting profuse blood from his mouths and nostrils.**

**Комментарий:**

Kāliya had a hundred chief (eka) heads among many more, since in verse 30 it will be said that he had thousands of hoods. Kṛṣṇa climbed forcibly on the head which remained high and did not bow down and crushed it with beating of his feet by keeping rhythm with the music. From his mouths (āsyataḥ) and nostrils (nastaḥ) Kāliya vomited blood.

### Text 29

*tasyākṣibhir garalam udvamataḥ śiraḥsu*  
*yad yat samunnamati niḥśvasato ruṣoccaiḥ*  
*nṛtyan padānunamayan damayāṁ babhūva*  
*puṣpaiḥ prapūjita iveha pumān purāṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Exuding poisonous waste from his eyes, breathing heavily with anger, Kāliya would occasionally dare to raise up one of his heads. Forcing it to bow down with his foot, the Lord, satisfied as if worshipped with flowers, would dance on it and subdue it.**

**Комментарий:**

Dancing on Kāliya’s heads, Kṛṣṇa forced down any head which raised itself up by beating it with his feet. Pleased as if being worshipped with flowers by the Gandharvas, he subdued the snake for their benefit.

### Text 30

*tac-citra-tāṇḍava-virugna-phaṇā-sahasro*  
*raktaṁ mukhair uru vaman nṛpa bhagna-gātraḥ*  
*smṛtvā carācara-guruṁ puruṣaṁ purāṇaṁ*  
*nārāyaṇaṁ tam araṇaṁ manasā jagāma*

**Перевод:**

**O King! His thousand hoods broken by Kṛṣṇa’s wonderful, powerful dancing, with broken limbs, the serpent, profusely vomiting blood from his mouths, finally recognized Kṛṣṇa to be the supreme guru of all moving and nonmoving beings, the first person, Nārāyaṇa. Thus within his mind Kāliya took shelter of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he heard the Lord’s glories from his wives, who received devotion to the Lord due to the mercy of Lord Śeṣa, they did not manifest due to cruelty and other faults in his heart. But at this time, since he had been purified of his faults by the touch of Kṛṣṇa’s feet and by the punishment of being crushed, those glories manifested. Contemplating (smṛtvā) the Lord’s glories which he heard from his wives, he took shelter (araṇam) of the Lord.

### Text 31

*kṛṣṇasya garbha-jagato ’ti-bharāvasannaṁ*  
*pārṣṇi-prahāra-parirugna-phaṇātapatram*  
*dṛṣṭvāhim ādyam upasedur amuṣya patnya*  
*ārtāḥ ślathad-vasana-bhūṣaṇa-keśa-bandhāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When Kāliya’s wives saw how the serpent had become so fatigued from the excessive weight of Kṛṣṇa, who carries the entire universe in his abdomen, and how Kāliya’s umbrella-like hoods had been shattered by the striking of Kṛṣṇa’s heels, they felt great distress. With their clothing, ornaments and hair scattered in disarray, they then approached the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Before Kāliya surrendered, his wives stood there, indifferent to him. “Averse to the Lord, he should die by the Lord’s punishment. We will worship the Lord as widows.” But by seeing marks of humility, etc., (in their husband who was) surrendered to the Lord’s feet, they approached in order to save Kāliya’s life. Kṛṣṇa held the universe in his stomach. Thus, they saw the snake, their husband, suffering from the great weight. They approached (upaseduḥ) the feet of Kṛṣṇa (ādyam).

### Text 32

*tās taṁ su-vigna-manaso ’tha puraskṛtārbhāḥ*  
*kāyaṁ nidhāya bhuvi bhūta-patiṁ praṇemuḥ*  
*sādhvyaḥ kṛtāñjali-puṭāḥ śamalasya bhartur*  
*mokṣepsavaḥ śaraṇa-daṁ śaraṇaṁ prapannāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Their minds very much disturbed, those loyal wives, placing their children before them, bowed down to the Lord of all creatures, laying their bodies flat upon the ground. Folding their hands, desiring that he free their wicked husband, they surrendered to Kṛṣṇa, who gives shelter to all.**

**Комментарий:**

They placed their children in front in order to invoke the Lord’s mercy. They placed their bodies on the earth. There was some island in the middle of the lake where Kāliya had wrapped his coils around Kṛṣṇa. They desired that their offending (śamalasya) husband be freed.

### Text 33

*nāga-patnya ūcuḥ*  
*nyāyyo hi daṇḍaḥ kṛta-kilbiṣe ’smiṁs*  
*tavāvatāraḥ khala-nigrahāya*  
*ripoḥ sutānām api tulya-dṛṣṭir*  
*dhatse damaṁ phalam evānuśaṁsan*

**Перевод:**

**The wives of the Kāliya serpent said: The punishment this offender has been subjected to is certainly just. After all, you have incarnated within this world to curb down envious and cruel persons. You are so impartial that you look equally upon your enemies and your own sons, for when you impose a punishment it is praiseworthy.**

**Комментарий:**

*ṣaḍbhir daṇḍasya yuktatvaṁ daśabhiḥ prabhoḥ*  
*pañcabhiḥ prārthanā ceti stutiḥ kāliya-yoṣitām*

**In six verses the wives of Kāliya say that his punishment was proper. In ten verses they offer respects to the Lord. In five verses they pray.**

Among them first, in order to pacify the Lord’s anger, they say that punishing their husband was proper. A wicked person must obtain the results of his wicked deeds. You who protect the good and punish the wicked, show no prejudice. You see equally the sons of your enemy and your own sons. You delivered the saintly Prahlāda, son of an enemy and you destroyed wicked Bhauma, your own son. There is no prejudice in punishing a wicked person. By that punishment the person will become good in the future. Praising the result you give punishment.

### Text 34

*anugraho ’yaṁ bhavataḥ kṛto hi no*  
*daṇḍo ’satāṁ te khalu kalmaṣāpahaḥ*  
*yad dandaśūkatvam amuṣya dehinaḥ*  
*krodho ’pi te ’nugraha eva sammataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**What you have done here is actually mercy for us, since the punishment you give to the wicked certainly drives away all their contamination. Because this conditioned soul, our husband, is so sinful he has assumed the body of a serpent. Even his anger is your mercy, approved by you.**

**Комментарий:**

Having spoken of punishment for giving mercy, now they say that Kāliya’s punishment is mercy.

The punishment of this snake is an act of mercy since your punishment of the wicked destroys their wicked nature. Because of a wicked nature, this jīva (dehinaḥ) has become a snake. Thus though perceived as your anger, your punishment is mercy. This is approved by the devotees. Thus it is said:

*aroṣaṇo hy asau deva*

**The Lord is not angry. (Mahābhārata)**

### Text 35

*tapaḥ sutaptaṁ kim anena pūrvaṁ*  
*nirasta-mānena ca māna-dena*  
*dharmo ’tha vā sarva-janānukampayā*  
*yato bhavāṁs tuṣyati sarva-jīvaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Did our husband carefully perform austerities in a previous life, with his mind free of pride and full of respect for others? Or did he in some previous existence carefully execute religious duties with compassion for all living beings, and is that why you, the life of all living beings, are now satisfied with him?**

**Комментарий:**

They imagine some previous puṇya he has done to attain mercy through punishment. Was it absence of the desire to be respected(nirasta-mānena) or was it giving respect to others? Thus they indicate that the austerity is aimed at Viṣṇu since is other types of austerity such a condition (of no desire for respect and giving respect to others) is not seen, and since it is said, nāham vedair na tapasā: the form you are seeing with your transcendental eyes cannot be understood simply by studying the Vedas, nor by undergoing serious penances (BG [11.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/11.53)), and since by the other types of austerity the Lord’s mercy does not occur.

Or was it dharma with mercy to all beings? That dharma should also aim at Viṣṇu, since the Lord’s mercy is not attained by dharmaaiming at Svarga. Because of his austerity or dharma, you are pleased. You joyfully dance using his hoods as your arena. Giving life to all jīvas (sarva-jīvaḥ), you should give life to him also at this time.

### Text 36

*kasyānubhāvo ’sya na deva vidmahe*  
*tavāṅghri-reṇu-sparaśādhikāraḥ*  
*yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo*  
*vihāya kāmān su-ciraṁ dhṛta-vratā*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Kāliya has attained this great opportunity of being touched by the dust of your lotus feet. For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows.**

**Комментарий:**

This good fortune did not arise by austerity or dharma, but by your mercy alone. This is expressed in three verses. We do not know what sādhana (kasya) produced this result (anubhāvaḥ). What is the result he attained? It is his qualification to touch the dust of your lotus feet, though he is wicked. They emphasize that it is mercy alone that caused this good fortune. With a desire to touch Kṛṣṇa’s feet, Lakṣmī, queen of Vaikuṇṭha, worshipped even by Brahmā, gave up enjoyments on Vaikuṇṭha and performed austerities, but did not attain those feet. The place of her austerities famous by the name Śrīvana.

### Text 37

*na nāka-pṛṣṭhaṁ na ca sārva-bhaumaṁ*  
*na pārameṣṭhyaṁ na rasādhipatyam*  
*na yoga-siddhīr apunar-bhavaṁ vā*  
*vāñchanti yat-pāda-rajaḥ-prapannāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Those who are surrendered to the dust of your lotus feet never hanker for the kingship of heaven, limitless sovereignty on earth, the position of Brahmā or rulership over lower planets. They are not interested even in the perfections of yoga or in liberation itself.**

**Комментарий:**

“What is the result of attaining the dust from my feet?” These are not the causes of the results, rather they are the highest results.Those who have surrendered to the dust of your feet, but not yet attained them, even they do not desire Svarga, etc., or even liberation predominated by happiness and powers (apunar-bhavam).

### Text 38

*tad eṣa nāthāpa durāpam anyais*  
*tamo-janiḥ krodha-vaśo ’py ahīśaḥ*  
*saṁsāra-cakre bhramataḥ śarīriṇo*  
*yad-icchataḥ syād vibhavaḥ samakṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord who asks the suffering to make requests! Although this Kāliya, the king of the serpents, has taken birth in the mode of ignorance and is controlled by anger, he has achieved that which is difficult for others to achieve. Embodied souls, who are full of desires and are thus wandering in the cycle of birth and death, can have all benedictions manifested before their eyes simply by receiving the dust of your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

He has attained what is difficult for others, even Lakṣmī, to receive. The jīva with desire can attain wealth directly from the dust of your feet. “May I serve that dust.” From that desire or expectation, the expected wealth will directly manifest.

### Text 39

*namas tubhyaṁ bhagavate puruṣāya mahātmane*  
*bhūtāvāsāya bhūtāya parāya paramātmane*

**Перевод:**

**We offer our obeisances unto you, Bhagavān, the supreme lord with human form, pervading everywhere, dwelling in all jīvas, eternally perfect, the best, situated in Lakṣmī.**

**Комментарий:**

They offer respects in ten verses. We offer respects to Bhagavān, eternally complete with six opulences, with human form (puruṣāya), but still pervades everywhere (mahātmane), and thus who resides in all living entities’ hearts (bhūtāvāsāya), who is eternally perfect (bhūtāya), who is the best of all (parāya) and who pervades spiritual Lakṣmī or mā (para-mā ātmane).

### Text 40

*jñāna-vijñāna-nīdhaye brahmaṇe ’nanta-śaktaye*  
*aguṇāyāvikārāya namas te prākṛtāya ca*

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances unto the form of knowledge and specialized knowledge, unto Brahman, unto the possessor of unlimited energies, unto the unchangeable Lord devoid of guṇas, unto the instigator of prakṛti.**

**Комментарий:**

We offer obeisances to the cause of jñāna and vijñāna, having great qualities (brahmane), who possesses unlimited śaktis, who has no material guṇas like sattva, etc. (aguṇāya), who is devoid of the sixteen transformations (avikārāya), and beyond matter (aprākṛtāya).

### Text 41

*kālāya kāla-nābhāya kālāvayava-sākṣiṇe*  
*viśvāya tad-upadraṣṭre tat-kartre viśva-hetave*

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances unto you, who are time itself, the shelter of time, the witness of time in all its phases, the universal form, the antaryāmī of the universe, its creator, and also the totality of all its causes.**

**Комментарий:**

You are the agitator of the guṇas. I offer respects to you. The verbal root is kal (to throw). “But time agitates the guṇas.” You are theshelter of time (kāla-nabhāya). Nābhāya instead of nābhaye is poetic license. By time you agitate the guṇas. You are the direct witness of all portions of time such as creation (kālāvayava-sākṣiṇe). You are the form of the universe with its śaktis of jīva and matter. You are the seer of the universe from close-up (tad-upadraṣṭre). You are not just a seer but the creator of the universe (tat-kartre). You are not just the creator but the form of all causes of the universe (viśva- hetave). You are not different from the universe since everything in it is dependent on you.

### Text 42

*bhūta-mātrendriya-prāṇa-mano-buddhy-āśayātmane*  
*tri-guṇenābhimānena gūḍha-svātmānubhūtaye*

**Перевод:**

**You are the giver of knowledge (ātmane) or awareness to the elements, sense objects, senses, prāṇa, mind, intelligence and citta. You give knowledge (anubhūti) of the ātmā to the jīvas covered by māyā.**

**Комментарий:**

Not only are you the cause of the universe but the giver of conscious to elements, etc. You also take away the knowledge of the jīva. You cover the glorious knowledge of the jīva (ātma) by ahaṅkāra of the three guṇas (tri-guṇenābhimānena).

*tvatto jñānaṁ hi jīvānāṁ pramoṣas te ‘tra śaktitaḥ*

**From you alone the knowledge of the living beings arises, and by your potency that knowledge is stolen away. (SB** [**11.22.28**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/22.28)**)**

### Text 43

*namo ’nantāya sūkṣmāya kūṭa-sthāya vipaścite*  
*nānā-vādānurodhāya vācya-vācaka-śaktaye*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the biggest and smallest, to the fixed one, to the teacher of all arts, to the inspiration for many philosophies, to the giver of power to words and meanings.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respect to you, who is devoid of the limitation of ahaṅkāra (anantāya), an internal form (sūkṣmāya), always existing in one form (kūṭasthāya), omniscient (vipaścite). You manifest for the sake of pleasure various philosophies such being devoid of, non-different from and different from the guṇas, having no body, having eternal body and having self as body. They clarify this. From you arise the powers of notions of words and their meanings to establish those philosophies.

### Text 44

*namaḥ pramāṇa-mūlāya kavaye śāstra-yonaye*  
*pravṛttāya nivṛttāya nigamāya namo namaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**We offer our obeisances again and again to you, who are the source of all authoritative evidence, who are Vyāsa, who are revealed in scripture, who have manifested literatures encouraging sense gratification as well as in those encouraging renunciation of the material world, and their source the Vedas.**

**Комментарий:**

“If that is so, then the true meaning is lost.” We offer respects to you, the root of all proof in the form of the Vedānta-sūtras, by which proofs are established. Among them śruti is the chief proof. Pratyakṣa and anumāna which are approved by it are also proof. Śrutes tu śabda-mūlatvāt: scripture declares it and scripture is the root of all knowledge. (Brahma-sūtra 2.1.17)

We offer respects to you, who manifest those scriptures (kavaye), Vyāsa, to the source of instruction (śāstra-yonaye), i.e. to you from whom all instructions arise, to the form of jyotiṣṭoma etc. (pravṛttāya), to the form of śama, dama, etc. (nivṛttāya), to the Vedas (nigamāya) which reveal these processes.

### Text 45

*namaḥ kṛṣṇāya rāmāya vasudeva-sutāya ca*  
*pradyumnāyāniruddhāya sātvatāṁ pataye namaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**We offer our obeisances to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, the son of Vasudeva, and to Pradyumna and Aniruddha. We offer our respectful obeisances unto the one master of all worshippers.**

**Комментарий:**

They offer respects while showing the forms to be worshipped which are revealed in the scriptures. We offer respects to Kṛṣṇa, to Balarāma, who is also Nanda’s son, to the protector of Śūra, Parjanya and others arising in the Sātvata dynasty.

### Text 46

*namo guṇa-pradīpāya guṇātma-cchādanāya ca*  
*guṇa-vṛtty-upalakṣyāya guṇa-draṣṭre sva-saṁvide*

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances to you, who reveal spiritual qualities to the devotees and hide qualities of power by these qualities, who is inferred by manifesting generous qualities, who sees the devotee’s faults as good qualities and who understands the devotee.**

**Комментарий:**

We offer respects to the revealer of the qualities such as being dependent on prema in these forms (guṇa-pradīpāya), who covers your powers by these revealed qualities, like a painting covering a mirror, who are understood (upalakṣāya) to be Svayam Bhagavān by manifesting qualities like giving happiness to demons you kill, who sees the good qualities of a devotee but not the faults, who isexperienced in his devotees (sva-saṁvide).

### Text 47

*avyākṛta-vihārāya sarva-vyākṛta-siddhaye*  
*hṛṣīkeśa namas te ’stu munaye mauna-śīline*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord Hṛṣīkeśa, master of the senses, please let us offer our obeisances unto you, whose pastimes are beyond matter, whose pastimes are proclaimed everywhere, unto you who are ātmārāma but not ātmārāma.**

**Комментарий:**

We offer respects to you whose pastimes are condensed knowledge (avyākṛta). Material objects having name and form are calledvyākṛta. Your pastimes are different from them (i.e. free of material names and forms). They are eternally free of māyā. I offer respects to you having eternal pastimes. Since the śruti says, eko devo nitya-līlānuraktaḥ: the one Lord is engaged in eternal pastimes. (Puruṣa-bodhinī śruti) From you arise all manifested elements from mahat-tattva to earth, which have a name and form (sarva-vyākrṭa- siddhaye). O master of the senses! I offer respects to Kapila, the son of Devahūtī (munaye), who did not speak to even Brahmā who was proud (mauna-śīline).

### Text 48

*parāvara-gati-jñāya sarvādhyakṣāya te namaḥ*  
*aviśvāya ca viśvāya tad-draṣṭre ’sya ca hetave*

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances unto you, who know the destination of the jñānīs and karmīs and who are perceived by all, who do not hold the universe inside you, but who held it within your belly, who remained as witness of the universe but was also its cause.**

**Комментарий:**

You know what is achieved by jñānīs (para) and karmīs (avara). You are the controller of the results such as Svarga or mokṣa. You give results according to sādhana. You are devoid of contact with the universe (aviśvāya). But you also enter the universe (viśvāya)since viśva means to enter (viśati).

*etad īśanam īśasya prakṛti-stho ’pi tad-guṇaiḥ*  
*na yujyate sadātma-sthair yathā buddhis tad-āśrayā*

**This is the power of the Lord: though he is situated in prakṛti, he is not affected by the guṇas which are situated in him, just as the intelligence of the devotee remembering the Lord is not affected by the guṇas. (SB** [**1.11.38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/11.38)**)**

You are the cause of the universe. To transform pradhāna you glance upon it (tad-draṣṭre). Sa aikṣata lokān nu sṛjā: he glanced and created the universe. (Aitareya Upaniṣad) The dative (hetave) is used according to kriyārthopapadasya (Pāṇini 2.3.14).

### Text 49

*tvaṁ hy asya janma-sthiti-saṁyamān vibho*  
*guṇair anīho ’kṛta-kāla-śakti-dhṛk*  
*tat-tat-svabhāvān pratibodhayan sataḥ*  
*samīkṣayāmogha-vihāra īhase*

**Перевод:**

**O almighty Lord! Without desire, you act on behalf of the devotee, possessing by your nature the power of time, glancing at pradhāna during creation, maintenance and destruction, and you simultaneously awaken the impressions of previous karmas of others characterized by the guṇas. Your every action is useful.**

**Комментарий:**

By showing that the Lord is merciful, they pray for deliverance of their husband in five verses.

“What is the result of my transforming pradhāna?” By glancing upon pradhāna (sataḥ), awakening the various natures such as ferocity, in the universe which had become subtle at the destruction of the previous universe, you cause (īhase) creation, etc., by the guṇas beginning with rajas. You possess the eternal (akṛta) kāla-śakti. You are devoid (anīha) of the desire for results of actions of creating the universe. “Then my glancing at pradhāna and endeavoring to transform it would be useless.” The pastime is fruitful (amogha) since it is for the enjoyment of the jīva. Since you are merciful like that, it is appropriate that you free even this snake.

### Text 50

*tasyaiva te ’mūs tanavas tri-lokyāṁ*  
*śāntā aśāntā uta mūḍha-yonayaḥ*  
*śāntāḥ priyās te hy adhunāvituṁ satāṁ*  
*sthātuś ca te dharma-parīpsayehataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore all material bodies throughout the three worlds— those that are peaceful, in the mode of goodness; those that are agitated, in the mode of passion; and those that are foolish, in the mode of ignorance—all are your creations. Still, those living entities whose bodies are in the mode of goodness are especially dear to you, and it is to maintain them and protect their religious principles that you are now present on the earth.**

**Комментарий:**

All these types of bodies are yours, who are the form of the universe by śakti and mentioned previously. Tanu means things by which the pastimes are able to take place. The bodies are instruments of the pastimes. They are sāttvika (śāntāḥ), rājasika (aśāntaḥ) andtāmasika (mūḍha). However those in sattva are dear to you because you act (īhataḥ) with a desire to protect their dharma, and whoare situated (sthātuḥ) to protect and maintain them. Similarly, this snake is incapable of himself giving up his cruel nature created by you. By your mercy he can give it up.

### Text 51

*aparādhaḥ sakṛd bhartrā soḍhavyaḥ sva-prajā-kṛtaḥ*  
*kṣantum arhasi śāntātman mūḍhasya tvām ajānataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**At least once, a master should tolerate an offense committed by his child or subject. O supreme peaceful Soul, you should therefore forgive our foolish husband, who did not understand who you are.**

**Комментарий:**

The offense of acting against the sāttvika persons should be tolerated one time. If the act is committed again it should not be tolerated. You should forgive our husband. They repeat themselves out of great confusion. By the word śāntātman (who has peaceful nature) they give the reason for the Lord to forgive. By the word mūḍhasyājānataḥ (fool and ignorant) they give the reason why their husband should be forgiven.

### Text 52

*anugṛhṇīṣva bhagavan prāṇāṁs tyajati pannagaḥ*  
*strīṇāṁ naḥ sādhu-śocyānāṁ patiḥ prāṇaḥ pradīyatām*

**Перевод:**

**O Supreme Lord, please be merciful. It is proper for the saintly to feel compassion for women like us. This serpent is about to give up his life. Please restore our husband to life, with no injuries.**

**Комментарий:**

“If you permit, the remaining faults of the snake can be removed by kicking five or six times.” By your mercy, the remainder of his faults will be removed. He will give up his life if you kick him more. “Why are you, my devotees, so eager to save this wicked snake’s life?” This husband should be given to us women. He is equal to our lives now, since he has surrendered to you. We will be lamented by Lord Śeṣa and other devotees (sādhu) when we are made widows by his death. It will not be pleasing to them.

### Text 53

*vidhehi te kiṅkarīṇām anuṣṭheyaṁ tavājñayā*  
*yac-chraddhayānutiṣṭhan vai mucyate sarvato bhayāt*

**Перевод:**

**Now please tell us, your maidservants, what we should do. Certainly anyone who faithfully executes your order is automatically freed from all fear.**

**Комментарий:**

“I will give you your husband, but he must follow my order.” They accept with great reverence. He will give the order to leave this place quickly, which is evident ahead.

### Text 54

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*itthaṁ sa nāga-patnībhir bhagavān samabhiṣṭutaḥ*  
*mūrcchitaṁ bhagna-śirasaṁ visasarjāṅghri-kuṭṭanaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus praised by the Nāga-patnīs, satisfied with their praises, Kṛṣṇa released the serpent Kāliya, who had fallen unconscious, his heads battered by the striking of the Lord’s lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Quickly Kṛṣṇa jumped from his heads and stood in front of him.

### Text 55

*pratilabdhendriya-prāṇaḥ kāliyaḥ śanakair harim*  
*kṛcchrāt samucchvasan dīnaḥ kṛṣṇaṁ prāha kṛtāñjaliḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kāliya slowly regained his vital force and sensory functions. Then, breathing loudly and painfully, the poor serpent addressed Kṛṣṇa, with hands folded in humility.**

**Комментарий:**

With difficulty Kāliya folded his hands. Because he was in pain from the beating, he could not bow down on the ground.

### Text 56

*kāliya uvāca*  
*vayaṁ khalāḥ sahotpattyā tamasā dīrgha-manyavaḥ*  
*svabhāvo dustyajo nātha lokānāṁ yad asad-grahaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The serpent Kāliya said: I am evil, ignorant and constantly angry by the nature of my species. O my Lord, it is so difficult for people to give up their conditioned nature, because of false identity.**

**Комментарий:**

By nature of the species (saha utpattyā) I am evil. Because of which nature (yat), even learned hold on to attraction and repulsion(asad-grahaḥ). What to speak of us fools.

### Text 57

*tvayā sṛṣṭam idaṁ viśvaṁ dhātar guṇa-visarjanam*  
*nānā-svabhāva-vīryaujo-yoni-bījāśayākṛti*

**Перевод:**

**O supreme creator! You have created this universe, composed of the variegated arrangement of the material modes, various natures, physical strength, sensory strength, mothers, fathers, desires and forms.**

**Комментарий:**

This universe is created with variety by the guṇas dependent on you (guṇa-visarjanam). In that it has various natures, etc. Svabhāvameans śānta (sattva), etc. Vīrya and ojas are different due to difference between śakti of body (vīrya), and śakti of senses (ojas). Yoni and bīja are different due to difference in mothers (yoni) and fathers (bīja). Āśaya means desires. Ākṛti means forms.

### Text 58

*vayaṁ ca tatra bhagavan sarpā jāty-uru-manyavaḥ*  
*kathaṁ tyajāmas tvan-māyāṁ dustyajāṁ mohitāḥ svayam*

**Перевод:**

**O Supreme Lord! Among all the species within your material creation, we serpents are by nature always enraged. Being thus deluded by your illusory energy, which is very difficult to give up, how can we possibly give it up on our own?**

**Комментарий:**

Snakes by birth have very angry natures. How can we give up that nature on our own?

### Text 59

*bhavān hi kāraṇaṁ tatra sarva-jño jagad-īśvaraḥ*  
*anugrahaṁ nigrahaṁ vā manyase tad vidhehi naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, since you are the omniscient Lord you are the actual cause of giving up māyā. Please arrange for us whatever you consider proper, whether it be mercy or punishment.**

**Комментарий:**

You are the cause for giving up māyā (tatra).

### Text 60

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity ākarṇya vacaḥ prāha bhagavān kārya-mānuṣaḥ*  
*nātra stheyaṁ tvayā sarpa samudraṁ yāhi mā ciram*  
*sva-jñāty-apatya-dārāḍhyo go-nṛbhir bhujyate nadī*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After hearing Kāliya’s words, the Supreme Lord, who appeared in his human form to benefit all replied: O serpent, you may not remain here any longer. Go to the ocean immediately, accompanied by your retinue of children, wives, other relatives and friends. Let this river be enjoyed by the cows and humans.**

**Комментарий:**

“He will do what I say.” The Lord understood the intention of his speech. The Lord performs pastimes among humans (kārya- mānuṣaḥ) to make them happy. Or he makes humans prosperous with his special prema (kārya) since humans were most prominentin his avatāra among them. The river will be enjoyed by cows and humans since the water, fruits, grass on its banks are suitable for enjoyment.

### Text 61

*ya etat saṁsmaren martyas tubhyaṁ mad-anuśāsanam*  
*kīrtayann ubhayoḥ sandhyor na yuṣmad bhayam āpnuyāt*

**Перевод:**

**If a mortal being attentively remembers my command to you—to leave Vṛndāvana and go to the ocean—and narrates this account at sunrise and sunset, he will never be afraid of you.**

**Комментарий:**

The fame of your being touched by my feet and punishment given to you by me will always remain. The last two lines of verse 60 and this verse are a mantra to ward off snakes.

### Text 62

*yo ’smin snātvā mad-ākrīḍe devādīṁs tarpayej jalaiḥ*  
*upoṣya māṁ smarann arcet sarva-pāpaiḥ pramucyate*

**Перевод:**

**If one bathes in this place of my pastimes and offers the water of this lake to the devatās and other worshipable personalities, or if one observes a fast and duly worships and remembers me, he is sure to become free from all sinful reactions.**

**Комментарий:**

You should leave this place for the following reasons. If you remain here, this cannot happen.

### Text 63

*dvīpaṁ ramaṇakaṁ hitvā hradam etam upāśritaḥ*  
*yad-bhayāt sa suparṇas tvāṁ nādyān mat-pāda-lāñchitam*

**Перевод:**

**Out of fear of Garuḍa, you left Ramaṇaka Island and came to take shelter of this lake. But because you are now marked with my footprints, Garuḍa will no longer afflict you.**

**Комментарий:**

You will have no fear of Garuḍa.

### Text 64

*śrī-ṛṣir uvāca*  
*mukto bhagavatā rājan kṛṣṇenādbhuta-karmaṇā*  
*taṁ pūjayām āsa mudā nāga-patnyaś ca sādaram*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: My dear King, having been released by Kṛṣṇa, Bhagavān, whose activities are astonishing, Kāliya joined his wives in worshiping him with great joy and prema.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa had performed astonishing activities (adbhuta-karmaṇā) since he crushed Kāliya’s head covered with heaps of gems with his delicate feet and he maintained his artistic movements amidst the wandering unsteady heads and gave auspiciousness to both the victims of violence by delivering Vraja from Kāliya and to the violent snake by delivering Kāliya from Garuḍa.

### Texts 65-66

*divyāmbara-sraṅ-maṇibhiḥ parārdhyair api bhūṣaṇaiḥ*  
*divya-gandhānulepaiś ca mahatyotpala-mālayā*

*pūjayitvā jagan-nāthaṁ prasādya garuḍa-dhvajam*  
*tataḥ prīto ’bhyanujñātaḥ parikramyābhivandya tam*  
*sa-kalatra-suhṛt-putro dvīpam abdher jagāma ha*

**Перевод:**

**Kāliya worshiped the Lord of the universe by offering him fine garments, along with necklaces, jewels and other valuable ornaments, wonderful scents and ointments, and a large garland of lotus flowers. Having thus pleased the Lord, whose flag is marked with the emblem of Garuḍa, Kāliya felt satisfied. Receiving the Lord’s permission to leave, Kāliya circumambulated him and offered him obeisances. Then, taking his wives, friends and children, he went to his island in the sea.**

**Комментарий:**

It was said that Kāliya worshipped Kṛṣṇa (sādaram) (verse 64). O merciful Lord! Since you gave your footprints rare even for Brahmā to my head, please accept us decorating you. Sitting the Lord on an attractive seat, decorating him, receiving the Lord’s mercy, he left the lake.

They offered him excellent (parārdhyaiḥ) ornaments. The kaustubha which had been on Kṛṣṇa’s chest at the time of his birth, had entered Kāliya’s treasury. It was offered to the Lord by Kāliya’s wives along with his collection of jewels. Being pleased with Kāliya, Kṛṣṇa placed his lotus hand which removes fear on Kāliya’s head and removed all his pain. His fear of Garuḍa also disappeared.

### Text 67

*tadaiva sāmṛta-jalā yamunā nirviṣābhavat*  
*anugrahād bhagavataḥ krīḍā-mānuṣa-rūpiṇaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The very moment Kāliya left, the Yamunā was immediately restored to her original condition, free from poison and full of nectarean water by the mercy of the Lord, who was manifesting a humanlike form to enjoy his pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

Even though the lake became free of poison, it is said that Yamunā became free of poison because it was part of the Yamunā. He hadbeauty (rūpiṇaḥ) of a human with limbs all arranged properly which was predominated by pastimes (krīḍā-mānuṣa-rūpiṇaḥ). This was an eternal endowment, expressed by the suffix on rūpiṇaḥ.

## Chapter 17 - The History of Kāliya

### Text 1

*śrī-rājovāca*  
*nāgālayaṁ ramaṇakaṁ kathaṁ tatyāja kāliyaḥ*  
*kṛtaṁ kiṁ vā suparṇasya tenaikenāsamañjasam*

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit inquired: Why did Kāliya leave Ramaṇaka Island, the abode of the serpents, and what offense did he do to Garuḍa?**

**Комментарий:**

*kāliyasya bhayaṁ tārkṣyā-cchāpoktis tatra saubhareḥ \|*  
*hary-āptir go-duhāṁ dāvād rakṣā saptadaśe’bhavat*

**This chapter relates the reasons for Kāliya’s fear of Garuḍa, Saubhari Muni’s curse on Garuḍa, Kṛṣṇa’s reunion with the Vrajavāsīs, and saving the boys from the forest fire.**

Asamañjasam means not pleasing.

### Text 2-3

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*upahāryaiḥ sarpa-janair māsi māsīha yo baliḥ*  
*vānaspatyo mahā-bāho nāgānāṁ prāṅ-nirūpitaḥ*

*svaṁ svaṁ bhāgaṁ prayacchanti nāgāḥ parvaṇi parvaṇi*  
*gopīthāyātmanaḥ sarve suparṇāya mahātmane*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: To avoid being eaten by Garuḍa, the serpents would each make monthly offering of tribute at the base of a tree. O mighty-armed King Parīkṣit, every fortnight each serpent would duly make his offering to that powerful carrier of Viṣṇu to protect themselves.**

**Комментарий:**

The offering made by the snakes using gifts of food for Garuḍa every month was decided ahead of time by people in the form of snakes to avoid being killed by Garuḍa. It was offered at the base of a tree. There all the snakes gave every fifteen days their share, to protect themselves.

### Text 4

*viṣa-vīrya-madāviṣṭaḥ kādraveyas tu kāliyaḥ*  
*kadarthī-kṛtya garuḍaṁ svayaṁ taṁ bubhuje balim*

**Перевод:**

**One serpent—the arrogant Kāliya, son of Kadrū, proud because of his strength and poison—would eat all these offerings, disrespecting Garuḍa.**

**Комментарий:**

Kāliya did not give a share but rather ate the offerings given by others, thereby disrespecting Garuḍa.

### Text 5

*tac chrutvā kupito rājan bhagavān bhagavat-priyaḥ*  
*vijighāṁsur mahā-vegaḥ kāliyaṁ samapādravat*

**Перевод:**

**O King, the greatly powerful Garuḍa, who is very dear to the Supreme Lord, became angry when he heard of this. Desiring to kill Kāliya, he rushed toward the serpent with tremendous speed.**

**Комментарий:**

Garuḍa heard this from a treacherous snake.

### Text 6

*tam āpatantaṁ tarasā viṣāyudhaḥ*  
*pratyabhyayād utthita-naika-mastakaḥ*  
*dadbhiḥ suparṇaṁ vyadaśad dad-āyudhaḥ*  
*karāla-jihvocchvasitogra-locanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As Garuḍa swiftly fell upon him, Kāliya, who had the weapon of poison, raised his numerous heads to counterattack. Showing his ferocious tongues, breathing heavily and expanding his horrible eyes, Kāliya then bit Garuḍa with the weapons of his fangs.**

**Комментарий:**

Having a weapon of poison, from far off he would spit the poison. Close up, he bit with his teeth. He had a formidable tongue, breathed heavily and had fierce eyes.

### Text 7

*taṁ tārkṣya-putraḥ sa nirasya manyumān*  
*pracaṇḍa-vego madhusūdanāsanaḥ*  
*pakṣeṇa savyena hiraṇya-rociṣā*  
*jaghāna kadru-sutam ugra-vikramaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The angry son of Tārkṣya moved with overwhelming speed in repelling Kāliya’s attack. That terribly powerful carrier of Madhusūdana struck the son of Kadrū with his left wing, which shone like gold.**

**Комментарий:**

Garuḍa was Kasyapa’s son. On him was Viṣṇu’s seat.

### Text 8

*suparṇa-pakṣābhihataḥ kāliyo ‘tīva vihvalaḥ*  
*hradaṁ viveśa kālindyās tad-agamyaṁ durāsadam*

**Перевод:**

**Beaten by Garuḍa’s wing, Kāliya was extremely distraught, and thus he took shelter of a lake adjoining the river Yamunā. Garuḍa could not enter this lake. Indeed, it was difficult to enter even for others.**

### Text 9

*tatraikadā jala-caraṁ garuḍo bhakṣyam īpsitam*  
*nivāritaḥ saubhariṇā prasahya kṣudhito ‘harat*

**Перевод:**

**In that very lake Garuḍa had once desired to eat a fish. Although forbidden by the sage Saubhari, Garuḍa took courage and, feeling hungry, seized the fish.**

**Комментарий:**

The reason Garuḍa could not enter is explained. Previous to the twenty-four yuga cycle, when Māndhātā, ancestor of Rāma, ruled the earth (ekadā), though forbidden by Sauabhari, “Do not eat the fish,” Garuḍa took fish by force (prasahya).

### Text 10

*mīnān su-duḥkhitān dṛṣṭvā dīnān mīna-patau hate*  
*kṛpayā saubhariḥ prāha tatratya-kṣemam ācaran*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing how the unfortunate fish in that lake had become most unhappy at the death of their leader, Saubhari uttered the following curse under the impression that he was mercifully acting for the benefit of the lake’s residents.**

**Комментарий:**

The protector of the fish (mīna-patau) died. Saubhari acted for the auspiciousness of those living there (tatratya).

### Text 11

*atra praviśya garuḍo yadi matsyān sa khādati*  
*sadyaḥ prāṇair viyujyeta satyam etad bravīmy aham*

**Перевод:**

**If Garuḍa ever again enters this lake and eats the fish here, he will immediately lose his life. What I am saying is the truth.**

**Комментарий:**

If Garuḍa enters the lake (atra) and eats fish, he will immediately (sadya) lose his life. If he does not eat the fish then after some time he will die. The curse is for merely entering the lake. If he eats fish then the curse is even more. Using the word aham (I say this) indicates his pride in the strength of his austerities. Saubari committed three offenses: ordering Garuḍa – the Lord’s eternal associate, opposing what was desired by him and expressing anger in being merciful to fish. Thus, the long accrued results of his austerity was destroyed by bad desires arising from associating with fish which should be shown mercy and he obtained a body for experiencing material happiness. Because he was a great offender, even his mercy in the form of wanting to help the fish had opposite effect, since by Kāliya coming to the Yamunā, those situated in the water, on the bank and the birds which flew over the lake near were destroyed. Liberation of Saubhari after his enjoyment of material objects occurred because of the power of his serving Vṛndāvana and Yamunā.

Garuḍa made no offense by breaking Saubari’s order and by killing fish since he possessed greater powers than Saubhari. However, he did not enter the lake, in order to follow the words of the great sage, as the Lord also does.

### Text 12

*tat kāliyaḥ paraṁ veda nānyaḥ kaścana lelihaḥ*  
*avātsīd garuḍād bhītaḥ kṛṣṇena ca vivāsitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Of all the serpents, only Kāliya came to know of this affair, and in fear of Garuḍa, he took up residence in that Yamunā lake. Later Kṛṣṇa drove him out.**

**Комментарий:**

Lelihaḥ means snake.

### Text 13-14

*kṛṣṇaṁ hradād viniṣkrāntaṁ divya-srag-gandha-vāsasam*  
*mahā-maṇi-gaṇākīrṇaṁ jāmbūnada-pariṣkṛtam*

*upalabhyotthitāḥ sarve labdha-prāṇā ivāsavaḥ*  
*pramoda-nibhṛtātmāno gopāḥ prītyābhirebhire*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa rose up out of the lake wearing shining garlands, fragrances and garments, covered with many fine jewels, and decorated with gold. When the cowherds saw him they all stood up immediately like the life airs, having gained their life. Filled with great joy, the cowherd boys affectionately embraced him.**

**Комментарий:**

Having finished the anecdote, Śukadeva returns to the story. Two verses go together. Kṛṣṇa came out of the water in a special way (vi- niṣkrāntam). He came on top of the water, using his feet, swimming lightly. Some say that he climbed on some snake, unseen under the water, which was ordered by Kāliya. Otherwise his attractive garlands and clothing would have become wet. These items would not have been described in this verse in that case. Asavaḥ means senses. The cowherd boys embraced him first since they were unsteady (in conduct).

### Text 15

*yaśodā rohiṇī nando gopyo gopāś ca kaurava*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ sametya labdhehā āsan śuṣkā nagā api*

**Перевод:**

**Having regained their vital functions, Yaśodā, Rohiṇī, Nanda and all the other cowherd women and men went up to Kṛṣṇa. O descendant of Kuru, even the dried-up trees came back to life.**

**Комментарий:**

“O child! Like a creeper burned by a forest fire, suffering in separation from you, like a cloud, bringing back to life, you are welcome.” Yaśodā, surrounded by her similar friends who had arrived there, came to Kṛṣṇa. Rohiṇī also came overwhelmed with prema in the crowd. Giving up his seriousness, Nanda, along with the cowherds like Upananda and their wives, approached Kṛṣṇa and embraced him. The word ca indicates the young gopīs whoembraced him from a distance using their eyes. They had their desires fulfilled (ladbhehāḥ). The trees of Vṛndāvana and mountains like Govardhana had dried up from not seeing Kṛṣṇa. Seeing him again, they became full of sprouts, leaves, flowers and waterfalls.

### Text 16

*rāmaś cācyutam āliṅgya jahāsāsyānubhāva-vit*  
*premṇā tam aṅkam āropya punaḥ punar udaikṣata*  
*nagā gāvo vṛṣā vatsataryo lebhire paramāṁ mudam*

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma embraced his infallible brother and laughed, knowing well the extent of Kṛṣṇa’s potency. Out of great feelings of love, Balarāma lifted Kṛṣṇa up on his lap and repeatedly looked at him. The cows, bulls and young female calves also achieved the highest pleasure.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma laughed. O master, ocean of variegated pastimes! Though expert at exiling the snake by other means and making the well-known love of the people of Vraja increase, how is it that you performed this most attractive pastime on the hoods of Kāliya acting as a dancing arena, which gave your people pain, to fulfill these two purposes? Though he knew Kṛṣṇa’s actions, he repeatedly gazed at him because of the nature of prema. He looked to see if there were any injuries from the wicked snake on Kṛṣṇa’s limbs.

The line beginning with nagā is a verse of one line.

### Text 17

*nandaṁ viprāḥ samāgatya guravaḥ sa-kalatrakāḥ*  
*ūcus te kāliya-grasto diṣṭyā muktas tavātmajaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All the respectable brāhmaṇas, gurus, together with their wives, came forward to greet Nanda Mahārāja. They said to him, “Your son was in the grips of Kāliya, but by good fortunate he is now free.”**

**Комментарий:**

Guruvaḥ refers to the priests like Bhāguri.

### Text 18

*dehi dānaṁ dvi-jātīnāṁ kṛṣṇa-nirmukti-hetave*  
*nandaḥ prīta-manā rājan gāḥ suvarṇaṁ tadādiśat*

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇas then advised Nanda Mahārāja, “On the occasion of Kṛṣṇa being saved, you should give charity to the brāhmaṇas.” With a satisfied mind, O King, Nanda Mahārāja then very gladly gave them gifts of cows and gold.**

### Text 19

*yaśodāpi mahā-bhāgā naṣṭa-labdha-prajā satī*  
*pariṣvajyāṅkam āropya mumocāśru-kalāṁ muhuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The greatly fortunate mother Yaśodā, having lost her son and then regaining him, placed him on her lap. That chaste lady cried constant torrents of tears as she repeatedly embraced him.**

**Комментарий:**

Having first lost prāṇas in fainting (naṣṭā) and Yaśodā then attained her son (labdha-prajā). She embraced him and placed him on her lap. She had not been satisfied previously in embracing him as much as she desired, because of great crowds.

### Text 20

*tāṁ rātriṁ tatra rājendra kṣut-tṛḍbhyāṁ śrama-karṣitāḥ*  
*ūṣur vrayaukaso gāvaḥ kālindyā upakūlataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O best of kings \[Parīkṣit\], because the residents of Vṛndāvana were feeling very weak from hunger, thirst and fatigue, they and the cows spent the night where they were, lying down near the bank of the Kālindī.**

**Комментарий:**

Another astonishing pastime is related in the course of the topics. Since the day came to an end in the people of Vraja meeting Kṛṣṇa individually, they stayed at that place when the night came. Though Kāliya had gone, they thought he may return remembering his enmity. “We will prevent him, using sticks. We will not return home since then we cannot see Kṛṣṇa.” Thus, they remained there. They left the vicinity of the bank, since they feared the poisonous water of the lake. Otherwise the forest fire could not have completely surrounded them. They were hungry and thirsty. Thus they ate the attractive fruit of Vṛndāvana that Vṛndā devī brought by her wish. The cows ate grass.

### Text 21

*tadā śuci-vanodbhūto dāvāgniḥ sarvato vrajam*  
*suptaṁ niśītha āvṛtya pradagdhum upacakrame*

**Перевод:**

**During the night, while all the people of Vṛndāvana were asleep, a great fire blazed up within the dry summer forest. The fire surrounded the inhabitants of Vraja on all sides and began to scorch them.**

**Комментарий:**

That night (tadā) a fire arising from a dry forest of summer (śuci) arose. The fire was some friend of Kāliya, a demon follower of Kaṁsa.

### Text 22

*tata utthāya sambhrāntā dahyamānā vrajaukasaḥ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ yayus te śaraṇaṁ māyā-manujam īśvaram*

**Перевод:**

**Then the residents of Vṛndāvana woke up, extremely disturbed by the great fire threatening to burn them. Thus they took shelter of Kṛṣṇa, who was the Supreme Lord, though by his spiritual potency he appeared like an ordinary human being.**

**Комментарий:**

Confused, they wandered about to escape from that. Garga had said, “He will protect you from all dangers.” (SB 10.8.16) Remembering that statement, they surrendered to Kṛṣṇa. He is described. He had a human form by svarūpa-śakti (māyā-manujam). Catur-veda-śikhā says:

*svarūpa-bhūtayā nitya-śaktyā māyākhyayā yutaḥ*  
*ato māyāmayaṁ viṣṇuṁ pravadanti sanātanam*

**Because the Lord is endowed with his eternal śakti arising from his svarūpa, eternal Viṣṇu is called māyā-maya (made of māyā).**

Smṛti says:

*narākṛti paraṁ brahma*

**Kṛṣṇa is Brahman in human form. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa)**

### Text 23

*ṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-bhaga he rāmāmita-vikrama*  
*eṣa ghoratamo vahnis tāvakān grasate hi naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, from whom good fortune arises! O Rāma, possessor of unlimited power! This most terrible fire is about to devour us, devotees of you two!**

**Комментарий:**

They called to Balarāma since they understood his prowess in killing Dhenuka.

### Text 24

*su-dustarān naḥ svān pāhi kālāgneḥ suhṛdaḥ prabho*  
*na śaknumas tvac-caraṇaṁ santyaktum akuto-bhayam*

**Перевод:**

**O Kṛṣṇa who can do anything! We are your true friends and your relatives. Please protect us from this insurmountable fire of death. We can never give up your lotus feet, which drive away all fear.**

**Комментарий:**

Protect us from this fire which is a form of death (kālāgneḥ). When we die we will be separated from your feet. We cannot tolerate that separation.

### Text 25

*itthaṁ sva-jana-vaiklavyaṁ nirīkṣya jagad-īśvaraḥ*  
*tam agnim apibat tīvram ananto ‘nanta-śakti-dhṛk*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing his devotees so disturbed, Kṛṣṇa, the infinite Lord of the universe and possessor of infinite power, then swallowed the terrible forest fire.**

**Комментарий:**

“How could the tender child swallow the fire?” He possesses unlimited śakti. Though he did not endeavor, his śakti of destroying the wicked swallowed the fire.

## Chapter 18 - Lord Balarāma Slays the Demon Pralamba

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*atha kṛṣṇaḥ parivṛto jñātibhir muditātmabhiḥ*  
*anugīyamāno nyaviśad vrajaṁ gokula-maṇḍitam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Surrounded by his blissful companions, who constantly chanted his glories, Kṛṣṇa then entered the village of Vraja, which was decorated with herds of cows.**

**Комментарий:**

*aṣṭādaśe’vahat kṛṣṇaḥ śrīdāmānaṁ jitaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*balaḥ pralambam āruhya muṣṭinā tam amārayat*

**In the eighteenth chapter, Kṛṣṇa carried his friend Śrīdāmā, being defeated by him, and Balarāma killed demon Pralamba with his fist after riding on him.**

In the morning (atha) Kṛṣṇa entered. Vraja is said to be decorated with herds of cows since they had already entered Vraja. The cow had entered Vraja already in the early morning, desiring to return from an untimely journey.

### Text 2

*vraje vikrīḍator evaṁ gopāla-cchadma-māyayā*  
*grīṣmo nāmartur abhavan nāti-preyāñ charīriṇām*

**Перевод:**

**While Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were thus enjoying life in Vṛndāvana on the pretext of herding the cows, the summer season fully appeared. This season is not very pleasing to embodied souls.**

**Комментарий:**

They played in the forest with hidden amorous desire in which herding cows was also full of desire for other pastimes (chadma).They had pastimes with the young gopīs. It will later be revealed during the spring rāsa dance that Balarāma also has gopī lovers. Summer was not too pleasing. It was a little pleasing however because there was opportunity for water sports.

### Text 3

*sa ca vṛndāvana-guṇair vasanta iva lakṣitaḥ*  
*yatrāste bhagavān sākṣād rāmeṇa saha keśavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Nevertheless, even summer manifested the qualities of spring. Such are the features of the land of Vṛndāvana where Kṛṣṇa, full of all qualities, killer of Keśī, plays eternally along with Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

Vṛndāvana’s qualities bring about closeness to ever-lasting spring. How much may be its glory!

### Text 4

*yatra nirjhara-nirhrāda-nivṛtta-svana-jhillikam*  
*śaśvat tac-chīkararjīṣa-druma-maṇḍala-maṇḍitam*

**Перевод:**

**In Vṛndāvana, the loud sound of waterfalls covered the crickets’ noise, and clusters of trees constantly moistened by spray from those waterfalls beautified the entire area.**

**Комментарий:**

The similarity to spring is described in four verses. Vṛndāvana (yatra), is a place where there are crickets which become quitemistaking the sound (nirhrāda) of waterfalls from the mountains, for rain. Jhillika is a small insect with a harsh sound. In Vṛndāvana apart from Girirāja, there were small and large mountains made of jewels for the purpose of Lord’s pastimes. The place was constantly decorated with trees shining with drops of water from the waterfalls.

### Text 5

*sarit-saraḥ-prasravaṇormi-vāyunā*  
*kahlāra-kañjotpala-reṇu-hāriṇā*  
*na vidyate yatra vanaukasāṁ davo*  
*nidāgha-vahny-arka-bhavo ’ti-śādvale*

**Перевод:**

**Because the wind wafting over the waves of the lakes and flowing rivers carried away the pollen of many varieties of lotuses and water lilies, and because of the green grass, the people of Vṛndāvana did not feel intense heat of the summer sun.**

**Комментарий:**

The wind, which caused the waves of lakes and rivers, was cool. By silently stealing pollen from lotuses the wind was fragrant and gentle. The burning heat of forest fire of the summer did not exist as in other places. It was full of grass most soft and green (atiśādvale).

### Text 6

*agādha-toya-hradinī-taṭormibhir*  
*dravat-purīṣyāḥ pulinaiḥ samantataḥ*  
*na yatra caṇḍāṁśu-karā viṣolbaṇā*  
*bhuvo rasaṁ śādvalitaṁ ca gṛhṇate*

**Перевод:**

**With their flowing waves the deep rivers drenching their banks, making them damp and muddy in all places, the rays of the sun, which were as fierce as poison, could not evaporate the earth’s sap causing green grass.**

**Комментарий:**

The reason for lack of the sun’s heat is explained. The place was flowing with mud at all times, because of waves that touched the banks of the lakes. The fierce rays of the sun could not touch the essence of the earth. Purīṣyāḥ is a feminine form of purīṣa (mud) following Pāṇini 4.1.41. The rasa is described it had green grass with muddy banks. Śādvalitam comes from śādvala applying the suffixes ṇic and kta in passive impersonal.

### Text 7

*vanaṁ kusumitaṁ śrīman nadac-citra-mṛga-dvijam*  
*gāyan mayūra-bhramaraṁ kūjat-kokila-sārasam*

**Перевод:**

**Flowers beautifully decorated the forest of Vṛndāvana, and many varieties of animals and birds filled it with sound. The peacocks and bees sang, and the cuckoos and cranes cooed.**

### Text 8

*krīḍiṣyamāṇas tat krṣṇo bhagavān bala-saṁyutaḥ*  
*veṇuṁ viraṇayan gopair go-dhanaiḥ saṁvṛto ‘viśat*

**Перевод:**

**Intending to engage in pastimes, Kṛṣṇa, endowed with all qualities, accompanied closely by Balarāma and surrounded by the cowherd boys and the cows, entered the forest of Vṛndāvana as he played his flute with special attention.**

### Text 9

*pravāla-barha-stabaka-srag-dhātu-kṛta-bhūṣaṇāḥ*  
*rāma-kṛṣṇādayo gopā nanṛtur yuyudhur jaguḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Decorating themselves with newly grown leaves, along with peacock feathers, garlands, clusters of flower buds, and colored minerals, Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa and their cowherd friends danced, wrestled and sang.**

**Комментарий:**

Gopāḥ is used since even Balarāma identified himself as a cowherd.

### Text 10

*kṛṣṇasya nṛtyataḥ kecij jaguḥ kecid avādayan*  
*veṇu-pāṇi-talaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ praśaśaṁsur athāpare*

**Перевод:**

**As Kṛṣṇa danced, some of the boys accompanied him by singing, and others by playing flutes, hand cymbals and buffalo horns, while still others praised his dancing.**

**Комментарий:**

Among Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, dressed like dancers from another region, who came with their group to Śrīdāmā’s gathering Kṛṣṇa’s dance is described first since he is most important. When Kṛṣṇa was dancing others sang. It is understood the Balarāma also danced. Some played instruments like flutes and hand cymbals others, Śrīdāmā and others praised the dancing profusely. They gave gifts like flower ornaments for the expert dancing.

### Text 11

*gopa-jāti-praticchannā devā gopāla-rūpiṇaḥ*  
*īḍire kṛṣṇa-rāmau ca naṭā iva naṭaṁ nṛpa*

**Перевод:**

**O King, devatās, who had taken birth as cowherds and had cowherd forms, praised Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma just as dramatic dancers praise a dance.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiva, Nārada and others came there to see the dancing. Among the friends, devatās disguised in the clothing of boys who did not come that day, praised Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma who were holding horns and flutes. Rūpiṇaḥ expresses constant connection with that form.

### Text 12

*bhramaṇair laṅghanaiḥ kṣepair āsphoṭana-vikarṣaṇaiḥ*  
*cikrīḍatur niyuddhena kāka-pakṣa-dharau kvacit*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, with their hair in kāka-pakṣa style, played at wrestling with their cowherd friends by whirling about, leaping, insult each other.**

**Комментарий:**

Their fun in fighting is now shown. Holding each other’s hands, the boys whirled around (bhramaṇaiḥ). They would jump down and climb up again (laṅghanaiḥ). They would insult as a joke (kṣepaiḥ), slap their base of their arms, and pull each other. In this way they arm-wrestled. Kāka-pakṣa is hair dressed with three braids. According to others it means crooked locks of hair falling in front of the ears.

### Text 13

*kvacin nṛtyatsu cānyeṣu gāyakau vādakau svayam*  
*śaśaṁsatur mahā-rāja sādhu sādhv iti vādinau*

**Перевод:**

**While the other boys were dancing, O King, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma would sometimes accompany them with song and instrumental music, and sometimes the two Lords would praise the boys, saying, “Very good! Very good!”**

**Комментарий:**

After wrestling, the dancing of Śrīdāmā and others who were being praised by Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, who sat and acted as ācāryas of the arts for fun, and who would make songs is described. They gave gifts of jeweled necklaces etc.

### Text 14

*kvacid bilvaiḥ kvacit kumbhaiḥ kvacāmalaka-muṣṭibhiḥ*  
*aspṛśya-netra-bandhādyaiḥ kvacin mṛga-khagehayā*

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes the cowherd boys would play with bilva or kumbha fruits, and sometimes with handfuls of āmalaka fruits. At other times they would cover the eyes of a friend from behind and play tag, and sometimes they would imitate animals and birds.**

**Комментарий:**

Other pastimes such as fighting are summarized in three verses.

They competed by throwing two bilva fruits and hitting them by the other or similarly with kumbha fruits. Aspṛśya is a game played by trying to touch another boy while the other boy avoids being touched, and the one who touches wins and the one who is touched is defeated. Netra-bandha is a game of approaching a boy unnoticed from behind and covering his eyes with the hands. If the boy recognizes who it is then the boy who covered the eyes loses. In all contests of winning and losing, the prize was a flute or stick. Disguising themselves as birds they would compete at warbling. The verb is in verse 16: krīḍābhiś ceratuḥ.

### Text 15

*kvacic ca dardura-plāvair vividhair upahāsakaiḥ*  
*kadācit syandolikayā karhicin nṛpa-ceṣṭayā*

**Перевод:**

**They would sometimes jump around like frogs, sometimes play various jokes, sometimes ride on swings and sometimes imitate monarchs.**

**Комментарий:**

They would sometimes play at jumping like frogs leaping across the waterfalls and sometimes joke, imitating various things. Starting on the waxing tṛtīyā of Śrāvaṇa month they would swing. Sometimes one of them would sit on a throne fashioned from the rock of a hill and others would serve him with cāmara and umbrella made of flowers, in the form of a leader and his attendents.

### Text 16

*evaṁ tau loka-siddhābhiḥ krīḍābhiś ceratur vane*  
*nady-adri-droṇi-kuñjeṣu kānaneṣu saraḥsu ca*

**Перевод:**

**In this way, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma played all sorts of well-known games as they wandered among the rivers, valleys of hills, bushes, trees and lakes of Vṛndāvana.**

**Комментарий:**

Adri-droṇi means among the valleys of hills. This pastime of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, with boys of similar qualities manifested inVṛndāvana, which had sweetness prominently. This one cause of satisfaction is rare in Vaikuṇṭha dhāma where his powers are prominent. It is seen that a king of the world, though strict, sometimes goes to a solitary, attractive place, with five-six friends, and sports in various ways. This is the cause of great happiness. Otherwise, the withering of the elements in the limbs will lead tomelancholy.

### Text 17

*paśūṁś cārayator gopais tad-vane rāma-kṛṣṇayoḥ*  
*gopa-rūpī pralambo ‘gād asuras taj-jihīrṣayā*

**Перевод:**

**While Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, with their cowherd friends were thus tending the cows in that Vṛndāvana forest, the demon Pralamba entered their midst. He had assumed the form of a cowherd boy with the intention of kidnapping Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**
