While Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma herded cows, one cowherd, on that day stayed home to do some duties. Pralamba, in that cowherd’s dress, came to steal the two brothers.

### Text 18

*taṁ vidvān api dāśārho bhagavān sarva-darśanaḥ*  
*anvamodata tat-sakhyaṁ vadhaṁ tasya vicintayan*

**Перевод:**

**Since the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who had appeared in the Daśārha dynasty, sees everything, he understood who the demon was. Still, Kṛṣṇa pretended to accept the demon as a friend, while at the same time seriously considering how to kill him.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa (dāśārhaḥ) considered how to kill Pralamba. He decided to kill him by this method.

### Text 19

*tatropāhūya gopālān kṛṣṇaḥ prāha vihāra-vit*  
*he gopā vihariṣyāmo dvandvī-bhūya yathā-yatham*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, who knows all sports and games, then called together the cowherd boys and spoke as follows: “Hey cowherd boys! Let’s play now! We’ll divide ourselves into two even teams.”**

### Text 20

*tatra cakruḥ parivṛḍhau gopā rāma-janārdanau*  
*kṛṣṇa-saṅghaṭṭinaḥ kecid āsan rāmasya cāpare*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd boys chose Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma as the leaders of the two parties. Some of the boys were on Kṛṣṇa’s side, and others joined Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were the two leaders (parivṛḍhau). Some were on Kṛṣṇa’s side, in his group.

### Text 21

*ācerur vividhāḥ krīḍā vāhya-vāhaka-lakṣaṇāḥ*  
*yatrārohanti jetāro vahanti ca parājitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The boys played various games. In these games the winners would climb up on the backs of the losers, who would have to carry them.**

**Комментарий:**

The meaning of the games of carrier and carried is described. If anyone in Balarāma’s group being touchers, touched anyone in Kṛṣṇa’s group, then Balarāma’s group was the winner and they all climbed on Kṛṣṇa’s group, which was defeated, and carried them. If Kṛṣṇa’s group won, they would be carried by Balarāma’s group.

### Text 22

*vahanto vāhyamānāś ca cārayantaś ca go-dhanam*  
*bhāṇḍīrakaṁ nāma vaṭaṁ jagmuḥ kṛṣṇa-purogamāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus carrying and being carried by one another, and at the same time tending the cows, the boys followed Kṛṣṇa to a banyan tree known as Bhāṇḍīraka.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhāṇḍīrakam means named Bhāṇḍīra. The suffix kan is in the sense of name. The banyan tree was made the place where they would climb off the shoulders. But they climbed on shoulders near this place.

### Text 23

*rāma-saṅghaṭṭino yarhi śrīdāma-vṛṣabhādayaḥ*  
*krīḍāyāṁ jayinas tāṁs tān ūhuḥ kṛṣṇādayo nṛpa*

**Перевод:**

**O King! When Śrīdāmā, Vṛṣabha and the other members of Balarāma’s party were victorious in these games, Kṛṣṇa and his followers had to carry them.**

### Text 24

*uvāha kṛṣṇo bhagavān śrīdāmānaṁ parājitaḥ*  
*vṛṣabhaṁ bhadrasenas tu pralambo rohiṇī-sutam*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa carried Śrīdāmā. Bhadrasena carried Vṛṣabha, and Pralamba carried Balarāma, the son of Rohiṇī.**

**Комментарий:**

By saying bhagavān, a joke is implied, “Your Bhagavān has been defeated by us people of Vraja.”

### Text 25

*aviṣahyaṁ manyamānaḥ kṛṣṇaṁ dānava-puṅgavaḥ*  
*vahan drutataraṁ prāgād avarohaṇataḥ param*

**Перевод:**

**Considering Kṛṣṇa invincible, that foremost demon quickly carried Balarāma far beyond the spot where he was supposed to put his passenger down.**

**Комментарий:**

The demon thought that Kṛṣṇa could not be conquered. Thus, desiring to take Balarāma, he became part of Kṛṣṇa’s group. He carried Balarāma and went beyond the place of putting him down. Avarohaṇaṁ means the place where one alights. It was the base of the Bhāṇḍīra tree. He went beyond that for deceiving Kṛṣṇa’s sight.

### Text 26

*tam udvahan dharaṇi-dharendra-gauravaṁ*  
*mahāsuro vigata-rayo nijaṁ vapuḥ*  
*sa āsthitaḥ puraṭa-paricchado babhau*  
*taḍid-dyumān uḍupati-vāḍ ivāmbudaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As the great demon carried Balarāma, the Lord became as heavy as massive Mount Sumeru, and Pralamba had to slow down. The demon then resumed his actual form—an effulgent body that was covered with golden ornaments and that resembled a cloud flashing with lightning and carrying the moon.**

**Комментарий:**

When the great demon Pralamba, carrying Balarāma because he was very strong, went beyond the place of alighting, Balarāma became heavy like Meru and manifested power, Pralamba, because he could not carry him, slowed down and manifested his demon form to show his great power. He wore gold ornaments. He was like a cloud flashing with lightning (his ornaments) carrying the moon (Balarāma).

### Text 27

*nirīkṣya tad-vapur alam ambare carat*  
*pradīpta-dṛg-bhru-kuṭi-taṭogra-daṁṣṭrakam*  
*jvalac-chikhaṁ kaṭaka-kirīṭa-kuṇḍala-*  
*tviṣādbhutaṁ haladhara īṣad atrasat*

**Перевод:**

**When Balarāma, who carries the plow, saw the gigantic body of the demon as he moved swiftly in the sky—with his blazing eyes, fiery hair, terrible teeth reaching toward his scowling brows, and an amazing effulgence generated by his armlets, crown and earrings—he seemed to become a little frightened.**

**Комментарий:**

His eyes shone brightly. He had a frown and terrifying teeth. Seeing his body, Balarāma became a little frightened. Due to absorption in childhood pastimes, he just made a show of fright since it was previously said that he was heavier than Meru.

### Text 28

*athāgata-smṛtir abhayo ripuṁ balo*  
*vihāyasārtham iva harantam ātmanaḥ*  
*ruṣāhanac chirasi dṛḍhena muṣṭinā*  
*surādhipo girim iva vajra-raṁhasā*

**Перевод:**

**Remembering the actual situation, the fearless Balarāma understood that the demon was trying to kidnap him and take him away from his companions. He then became furious and struck the demon’s head with his hard fist, just as Indra, the king of the devatās, strikes a mountain with his thunderbolt weapon.**

**Комментарий:**

His memory was not lost, but according to Viṣṇu Purāṇa he regained his memory when Kṛṣṇa spoke to him. Then understanding hisavatāra was to kill the wicked, he struck the demon with his fist. He was like Indra striking a mountain with his thunderbolt. The demon was like someone stealing his (Balarāma’s) obtained treasure by going through the sky.

### Text 29

*sa āhataḥ sapadi viśīrṇa-mastako*  
*mukhād vaman rudhiram apasmṛto ’suraḥ*  
*mahā-ravaṁvyasur apatat samīrayan*  
*girir yathā maghavata āyudhāhataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus smashed by Balarāma’s fist, Pralamba’s head immediately cracked open. The demon vomited blood from his mouth and convulsed with fits. Then, with a great noise he fell lifeless on the ground, like a mountain devastated by Indra’s weapon.**

**Комментарий:**

Apasmṛtaḥ means he lost his memory as if he was afflicted with epilepsy. Making a great noise, he fell lifeless (vyasuḥ) on theground.

### Text 30

*dṛṣṭvā pralambaṁ nihataṁ balena bala-śālinā*  
*gopāḥ su-vismitā āsan sādhu sādhv iti vādinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd boys were most astonished to see how the powerful Balarāma had killed the demon Pralamba, and they exclaimed, “Excellent! Excellent!”**

**Комментарий:**

They were astonished by the demon’s disguise as a cowherd.

### Text 31

*āśiṣo ‘bhigṛṇantas taṁ praśaśaṁsus tad-arhaṇam*  
*pretyāgatam ivāliṅgya prema-vihvala-cetasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**They offered Balarāma profuse benedictions and then glorified Balarāma, who deserved all glorifications. Their minds overwhelmed with ecstatic love, they embraced him as if he had come back from the dead.**

**Комментарий:**

They proclaimed, “Play joyfully along with your younger brother and protect us.” Balarāma was worthy of their praise.

### Text 32

*pāpe pralambe nihate devāḥ parama-nirvṛtāḥ*  
*abhyavarṣan balaṁ mālyaiḥ śaśaṁsuḥ sādhu sādhv iti*

**Перевод:**

**The sinful Pralamba having been killed, the devatās felt extremely happy, and they showered flower garlands upon Lord Balarāma and praised the excellence of his deed.**

**Комментарий:**

The devatās also praised Balarāma. Pralamba was most wicked (pāpe), causing violence to the world.

*nāga-mūrdhasu tuṅgeṣu nartitvā madhusūdanaḥ*  
*\| pralamba-skandham atyuccaṁ balam ārohayat prabhuḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa having danced on the snake’s high heads, put Balarāma on Pralambha’s high shoulders (before killing him).**

## Chapter 19 - Swallowing the Forest Fire

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*krīḍāsakteṣu gopeṣu tad gāvo dūra-cāriṇīḥ*  
*svairaṁ carantyo viviśus tṛṇa-lobhena gahvaram*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Then while the cowherd boys were completely absorbed in playing, their cows wandered far away. They hungered for more grass, and with no one to watch them they entered a dense forest.**

**Комментарий:**

*dāvān muñja-vane rakṣan pihitākṣān sakhīn hariḥ \|*  
*vyadhād bhāṇḍīram ānīya muktākṣān ūnaviṁśake*

**The nineteenth chapter describes how Kṛṣṇa saved the cowherd boys from a great fire in the Muñjā forest while their eyes were closed and brought them to Bhāṇḍīra where they opened their eyes.**

Tad means after that. Accusative (dūra-cāriṇīḥ) is used for the nominative.

### Text 2

*ajā gāvo mahiṣyaś ca nirviśantyo vanād vanam*  
*īṣīkāṭavīṁ nirviviśuḥ krandantyo dāva-tarṣitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Passing from one part of the great forest to another, the goats, cows and buffalo eventually entered an area overgrown with sharp canes. Thirsty because of the heat of the summer sun, they cried out in distress.**

**Комментарий:**

The goats belonged to Gurjaras, the cows to the cowherds and the buffaloes to both. Entering a reed forest, the cows became thirsty because of the heat of the summer sun.

### Text 3

*te ’paśyantaḥ paśūn gopāḥ kṛṣṇa-rāmādayas tadā*  
*jātānutāpā na vidur vicinvanto gavāṁ gatim*

**Перевод:**

**Not seeing the cows before them, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and their cowherd friends suddenly felt repentant for having neglected them. The boys searched all around, but could not discover where they had gone.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa-rāmādayas is a compound of the atad-guṇa-saṁvijñāna type. The cowherds other than Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma (those who were followers of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma) did not see the animals and felt sorry. They did not know where the cows had gone.

Or their knowledge disappeared by increase of affection for the cows if it is accepted as tad-guṇa-saṁvijñāna (Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma also did not see the cows).

### Text 4

*tṛṇais tat-khura-dac-chinnair goṣ-padair aṅkitair gavām*  
*mārgam anvagaman sarve naṣṭājīvyā vicetasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then the boys began tracing out the cows’ path by noting their hoof prints and the blades of grass the cows had broken with their hooves and teeth. They were in great anxiety because they had lost their source of livelihood.**

**Комментарий:**

They followed the path characterized by areas of land marked with hoofprints of cows (goṣ-padaiḥ) and by the grass cut by their teeth and hooves. They lost sight of the source of their livelihood(naṣṭājīvyā).

### Text 5

*muñjāṭavyāṁ bhraṣṭa-mārgaṁ krandamānaṁ sva-godhanam*  
*samprāpya tṛṣitāḥ śrāntās tatas te sannyavartayan*

**Перевод:**

**Within the sedge thicket, the cowherd boys finally found their valuable cows, who had lost their way and were crying. Then the boys, thirsty and tired, herded the cows onto the path back.**

**Комментарий:**

They attained the cows who had lost their way in the reed thicket and made the cows return.

### Text 6

*tā āhūtā bhagavatā megha-gambhīrayā girā*  
*sva-nāmnāṁ ninadaṁ śrutvā pratineduḥ praharṣitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord called out to the animals in a voice that resounded like a rumbling cloud. Hearing the sound of their own names, the cows were overjoyed and called out to the Lord in reply.**

**Комментарий:**

How did he find the cows? Showing himself, he called to them. The cows called back mooing.

### Text 7

*tataḥ samantād dava-dhūmaketur*  
*yadṛcchayābhūt kṣaya-kṛd vanaukasām*  
*samīritaḥ sārathinolbaṇolmukair*  
*vilelihānaḥ sthira-jaṅgamān mahān*

**Перевод:**

**Suddenly a great forest fire appeared on all sides, threatening to destroy all the forest creatures. The fire was agitated by the wind, shooting sparks like meteors in all directions. Spreading everywhere it burned all moving and nonmoving creatures.**

**Комментарий:**

At that time (tataḥ), suddenly (yadṛcchayā) there arose (abhūt) a forest fire. Some say that this fire was some demon friend of Pralamba. The fire increased by the wind (sārathinā). It afflicted the creatures by hits sparks which were like sharp meteors since itspread everywhere (mahān).

### Text 8

*tam āpatantaṁ parito davāgniṁ*  
*gopāś ca gāvaḥ prasamīkṣya bhītāḥ*  
*ūcuś ca kṛṣṇaṁ sa-balaṁ prapannā*  
*yathā hariṁ mṛtyu-bhayārditā janāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As the cows and cowherd boys stared at the forest fire attacking them on all sides, they became fearful. They then spoke to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, having taken their shelter, just as people who are disturbed by fear of saṁsāra approach Viṣṇu. The boys addressed them as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

The boys spoke, remembering Garga’s words (SB [10.8.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.16)) that Kṛṣṇa would protect them from all disasters. “The cows spoke” means in confusion they mooed. That is their speaking. Harim means Viṣṇu.

### Text 9

*kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-vīra he rāmāmogha vikrama*  
*dāvāgninā dahyamānān prapannāṁs trātum arhathaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[The cowherd boys said:\] O Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Most powerful one! O Rāma! You whose prowess never fails! You can save your devotees, who are about to be burned by this forest fire and have surrendered to you!**

### Text 10

*nūnaṁ tvad-bāndhavāḥ kṛṣṇa na cārhanty avasāditum*  
*vayaṁ hi sarva-dharma-jña tvan-nāthās tvat-parāyaṇāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa! Certainly even those with a little relationship to you should not fall into grief. O knower of our nature and yours! We especially have taken shelter of you. We have surrendered unto you alone!**

**Комментарий:**

It is certain (nūnam). O Kṛṣṇa! Your friends do not even deserve to behave like suffering people. Why should they experience the heat of the forest fire? Avasāditum means to act in a state of complete defeat. It is formed by applying the suffixes kvip (Pāṇini 3.1.11) and then tumun. Protect the cows too. You know all dharma.

### Text 11

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*vaco niśamya kṛpaṇaṁ bandhūnāṁ bhagavān hariḥ*  
*nimīlayata mā bhaiṣṭa locanānīty abhāṣata*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Hearing these pitiful words from his friends, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa told them, “Just close your eyes and do not be afraid.”**

**Комментарий:**

Since I desire the benefit of devotees, I can drink even fire but since they cannot tolerate my drinking fire, it should be done without their seeing it. Moreover in the same way (with their eyes closed) they, who are fully tired and fully scorched, should be carried to the cool base of Bhāṇḍīra tree. Thinking thus he asked them to close their eyes. “O crest jewel of playing! By closing the eyes, how will the fire be destroyed?” Do not be afraid. There is no other way of destroying the fire apart from this.

### Text 12

*tatheti mīlitākṣeṣu bhagavān agnim ulbaṇam*  
*pītvā mukhena tān kṛcchrād yogādhīśo vyamocayat*

**Перевод:**

**“All right,” the boys replied, and immediately closed their eyes. Then the Supreme Lord, the master of all mystic power, swallowed the terrible fire in his mouth, saving his friends from danger.**

**Комментарий:**

“O friends! This great person Hari knows the method of pacifying the poison of the fire. This will not happen unless there are no people around. Therefore, in the place with people, closing the eyes is having no people around.” Thinking thus, when they tightly closed their eyes, the lord of yoga, Bhagavān, drank the fire though fierce, by the means of a portion of yoga-māyā, and freed his friends from difficulty. Mukha means method according to Medinī. When he desired to drink the fire, the śakti of destroying the wicked, impelled by yoga-māyā, drank it.

### Text 13

*tataś ca te ’kṣīṇy unmīlya punar bhāṇḍīram āpitāḥ*  
*niśamya vismitā āsann ātmānaṁ gāś ca mocitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd boys then opened their eyes and were amazed that they had been saved and had all been brought back to the Bhāṇḍīra tree.**

**Комментарий:**

Then they were brought by the Lord to Bhāṇdīra. O friends! Open your eyes. I have counteracted the fire. By his saying this they opened their eyes. Seeing themselves and the cows saved, they were astonished. They stood like painted pictures, realizing the inconceivable śakti in their friend Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 14

*kṛṣṇasya yoga-vīryaṁ tad yoga-māyānubhāvitam*  
*dāvāgner ātmanaḥ kṣemaṁ vīkṣya te menire ’maram*

**Перевод:**

**When the cowherd boys saw that they had been saved from the forest fire by the Lord’s mystic power, which is manifested by his internal potency, they began to think that Kṛṣṇa must be a devatā.**

**Комментарий:**

Even though seeing such power of Kṛṣṇa, the boys’ friendship remained steady. Being made to experience by Kṛṣṇa’s yoga-māyā the power which causes astonishing things (yoga-vīryam), and seeing that they were saved from the forest fire, they considered their friend amara, someone who destroys death for those who surrender to him. Yoga means that which causes something astonishing according to Viśva. They thought, “Our friend is directly īśvara, the cause of bhukti for those who worship him.”

### Text 15

*gāḥ sannivartya sāyāhne saha-rāmo janārdanaḥ*  
*veṇuṁ viraṇayan goṣṭham agād gopair abhiṣṭutaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**It was now late in the afternoon, and Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Balarāma, turned the cows back toward home. Playing his flute in a special way, Kṛṣṇa returned to the cowherd village in the company of his cowherd friends, who chanted his glories.**

### Text 16

*gopīnāṁ paramānanda āsīd govinda-darśane*  
*kṣaṇaṁ yuga-śatam iva yāsāṁ yena vinābhavat*

**Перевод:**

**The young gopīs took the greatest pleasure in seeing Govinda, since for them even a moment without his association seemed like a hundred ages.**

**Комментарий:**

When he entered Vraja though everyone was blissful, yet it was previously described that particularly those with vātsalya had more bliss as in gopī-dṛg-utsava-dṛśiḥ: seeing him produced a great festival for the eyes of all the cowherd women. (SB [10.14.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.47)) Now, the abundance of bliss of the young gopī lovers is described. The bliss of these gopīs was thoroughly more by type and quantity. “Please tell the defining, extraordinary characteristics of them.” Kṣaṇam in the neuter is poetic license. Without him (yena) a moment becamea hundred yugas for them, because of mahābhāva. This indicates Rādhā and others. Their such behavior is indicated in the following:

*aṭati yad bhavān ahni kānanaṁ*  
*truṭi yugāyate tvām apaśyatām*  
*kuṭila-kuntalaṁ śrī-mukhaṁ ca te*  
*jaḍa udīkṣatāṁ pakṣma-kṛd dṛśām*

**When you go off to the forest during the day, a tiny fraction of a second becomes like a millennium for us because we cannot see you. And even when we can eagerly look upon your beautiful face, so lovely with its adornment of curly locks, our pleasure is hindered by our eyelids, which were fashioned by the foolish creator. (SB** [**10.31.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/31.15)**)**

Even Śukadeva in order to show the highest prema refers to them and says:

*yat-prekṣaṇe dṛśiṣu pakṣma-kṛtaṁ śapanti*

**While gazing at their beloved Kṛṣṇa, the young gopīs used to condemn the creator of their eyelids, \[which would momentarily block their vision of him\]. (SB** [**10.82.39**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/82.39)**)**

## Chapter 20 - The Rainy Season and Autumn in Vṛndāvana

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*tayos tad adbhutaṁ karma dāvāgner mokṣam ātmanaḥ*  
*gopāḥ strībhyaḥ samācakhyuḥ pralamba-vadham eva ca*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: To the women of Vṛndāvana, the cowherd boys then related in full detail Kṛṣṇa’s and Balarāma’s wonderful activities of delivering them from the forest fire and killing the demon Pralamba.**

**Комментарий:**

*upādeyatva-heyatve vastūnām upamānataḥ\|*  
*bodhayan viṁśake brūte prāvṛṭ-śarad-ṛtu-śriyaṁ*

**In the twentieth chapter Śukadeva reveals the beauty of the monsoon and autumn seasons through comparisons of excellent and inferior objects.**

The cowherd boys told the pastimes to their mothers (strībhyaḥ).

### Text 2

*gopa-vṛddhāś ca gopyaś ca tad upākarṇya vismitāḥ*  
*menire deva-pravarau kṛṣṇa-rāmau vrajaṁ gatau*

**Перевод:**

**The elder cowherd men and ladies were amazed to hear this account, and they concluded that Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma must be exalted devatās who had appeared in Vṛndāvana.**

**Комментарий:**

The mothers-in-law and those gopīs considered that the two boys were directly Supreme Lords, the best of all the devas. This did notweaken the vātsalya but nourished it since when one’s son is the controller of the whole earth, it was observed that the mothers, etc., increased their vātsalya for them.

### Text 3

*tataḥ prāvartata prāvṛṭ sarva-sattva-samudbhavā*  
*vidyotamāna-paridhir visphūrjita-nabhas-talā*

**Перевод:**

**Then the rainy season began, giving life and sustenance to all living beings. The sky began to rumble with thunder, and the horizons glowed.**

**Комментарий:**

In twenty-two verses there is a description of the monsoon season. After the summer (tataḥ) the monsoon began in which there was increase of all creatures arising from birth and sustenance. The haloes of the sun and moon flashed and the sky trembled.

### Text 4

*sāndra-nīlāmbudair vyoma sa-vidyut-stanayitnubhiḥ*  
*aspaṣṭa-jyotir ācchannaṁ brahmeva sa-guṇaṁ babhau*

**Перевод:**

**The sky shone with weak light from the sun and moon since it was covered by dense blue clouds accompanied by lightning and thunder, just as the spirit soul is covered by the three modes of material nature.**

**Комментарий:**

The sky was covered with dark blue clouds with lightning and thunder and the constellations were not clearly visible. This was like the totality of jīvas in the material world (saguṇa-brahma). The lighting, thunder and clouds are compared to sattva, rajas and tamas.

This comparison is excellent for the worshippers of Hiraṇyagarbha. As the sky was covered by clouds, etc., so Hiraṇyagarbha is covered by the guṇas.

### Text 5

*aṣṭau māsān nipītaṁ yad bhūmyāś coda-mayaṁ vasu*  
*sva-gobhir moktum ārebhe parjanyaḥ kāla āgate*

**Перевод:**

**With its rays, the sun had for eight months drunk up the earth’s wealth in the form of water. Now that the proper time had arrived, the sun began releasing this accumulated wealth.**

**Комментарий:**

The sun (parjanyaḥ) with is rays (sva-gobhiḥ) drank the earth’s water and then gave back at the proper time. By atiśayokti acomparison to a king is indicated. This is an excellent comparison for kings. The king takes taxes from the citizens and then gives it to them at the proper time.

### Text 6

*taḍidvanto mahā-meghāś caṇḍa-śvasana-vepitāḥ*  
*prīṇanaṁ jīvanaṁ hy asya mumucuḥ karuṇā iva*

**Перевод:**

**Flashing with lightning, great clouds were shaken by fierce winds. Just like merciful persons give their lives for others, the clouds released water for the pleasure of this world.**

**Комментарий:**

The huge clouds, shaken by the wind (śvasana) flashing with lightning like eyes, seeing the world scorched, released water(jīvanaṁ), which causes welfare (prīṇanam), just like compassionate people. For them, sighing and trembling are two anubhāvas.Compassionate people seeing the suffering of people give up their lives, like how Rantideva gave away his water which maintained his life and like how Dadhīci gave up his life. These is an excellent comparison for dānavīra and dayāvīra.

### Text 7

*tapaḥ-kṛśā deva-mīḍhā āsīd varṣīyasī mahī*  
*yathaiva kāmya-tapasas tanuḥ samprāpya tat-phalam*

**Перевод:**

**The earth had been emaciated by the summer heat, but she became fully nourished again when moistened by the god of rain, just a body attains its results by performing an austerity for a material goal.**

**Комментарий:**

The earth, thin from the summer heat, being sprinkled with water by Indra (deva-mīḍhā) becomes prosperous (varṣīyasī), just as the body of one who does austerity for personal benefit (and becomes thin) attains enjoyment as the result of that austerity. This isdetestable for those who see transformation (pariṇāma-vāda).

### Text 8

*niśā-mukheṣu khadyotās tamasā bhānti na grahāḥ*  
*yathā pāpena pāṣaṇḍā na hi vedāḥ kalau yuge*

**Перевод:**

**In the evening twilight during the rainy season, the fireflies shone but the planets did not, because of the darkness, just as in the age of Kali because of sin, atheistic scriptures doctrines prevail, but the Vedas do not.**

**Комментарий:**

Pāṣaṇḍāḥ refers to those contrary to the Vedas such as the path of Buddha. This comparison is detestable.

### Text 9

*śrutvā parjanya-ninadaṁ maṇḍūkā vyasṛjan giraḥ*  
*tūṣṇīṁ śayānāḥ prāg yadvad brāhmaṇā niyamātyaye*

**Перевод:**

**The frogs, which had all along been lying silent, suddenly began croaking when they heard the rumbling of the rain clouds, in the same way that brāhmaṇa students, after meditating in silence begin reciting their lessons.**

**Комментарий:**

Previously silent, sleeping and inactive, the frogs released croaking sounds, like brāhmaṇas who after performing nitya-karmas, become silent for meditating on the Ṛg Veda, hearing the call of the teacher, recite their lessons. This is excellent comparison for brahmacārīs.

### Text 10

*āsann utpatha-gāminyaḥ kṣudra-nadyo ’nuśuṣyatīḥ*  
*puṁso yathā svatantrasya deha-draviṇa-sampadaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The insignificant streams were sometimes off course and sometimes were dried up, like the bodily wealth and wealth of properties of a man who follows scripture with an independent mind.**

**Комментарий:**

The small streams dried up in other seasons. They go off course even by the small amount of water that rains. This is like the wealth of youthful body (deha) and wealth of leadership of five or six villages (draviṇa) of a person who transgresses the scriptural injunctions (svatantrasya). Such wealth causes distress to others. This comparison is detestable.

### Text 11

*haritā haribhiḥ śaṣpair indragopaiś ca lohitā*  
*ucchilīndhra-kṛta-cchāyā nṛṇāṁ śrīr iva bhūr abhūt*

**Перевод:**

**The newly grown grass made the earth emerald green, the indragopa insects added a reddish hue, and mushrooms added further color. Thus the earth appeared like the wealth of army of kings.**

**Комментарий:**

The earth in some places became green because of the sprouting green grass. In some places the earth became red because of the redindragopa insects. Sprouting mushrooms created shade. It became the like the wealth of troops (śrīḥ) of the kings (nṛṇām), endowedwith tents colored green and red. This is an excellent comparison for kings.

### Text 12

*kṣetrāṇi śaṣya-sampadbhiḥ karṣakāṇāṁ mudaṁ daduḥ*  
*māninām anutāpaṁ vai daivādhīnam ajānatām*

**Перевод:**

**With their wealth of grains or lack of it, the fields gave joy or grief to the farmers since, identifying with their bodies, they did not know that everything is under the control of karma, just as others in the same ignorance rejoice on attaining wealth and grieve on losing it.**

**Комментарий:**

Land, by having shining sprouting grass in continuous rain, gives joy to farmers with material identity but in cessation of rain by drying grass it gives sorrow. They do not know that their joy and sorrow are dependent on karma, just as bodies (kṣetrāṇi) nourishedby wealth, give joy to the those who identify with the bodies and when wealth is lost, their bodies become thin and give sorrow. This comparison is detestable by the devotees.

### Text 13

*jala-sthalaukasaḥ sarve nava-vāri-niṣevayā*  
*abibhran ruciraṁ rūpaṁ yathā hari-niṣevayā*

**Перевод:**

**As all creatures of the land and water took advantage of the newly fallen rainwater, their forms became attractive and pleasing, just as a devotee becomes radiant by engaging in the service of the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Abibhrat stands for abibharuḥ: they accepted. All those who engage in the Lord’s service attain attractive forms by wearing the marks of a Vaiṣṇava. This was like that. This is favorable example.

### Text 14

*saridbhiḥ saṅgataḥ sindhuś cukṣobha śvasanormimān*  
*apakva-yoginaś cittaṁ kāmāktaṁ guṇa-yug yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Where the rivers joined the river Sindhu it became agitated, its waves blown about by the wind, just as the mind of an immature yogī, filled with desire, becomes agitated when engaged with the guṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

Sindhu here refers to a river west of Mathurā. The mind of the yogī filled with desire for enjoyment (kāmāktam) is compared to the waves blown by the wind. Engaging with material senses objects (guṇa-yug) is compared to meeting the rivers. This is a negative example.

### Text 15

*girayo varṣa-dhārābhir hanyamānā na vivyathuḥ*  
*abhibhūyamānā vyasanair yathādhokṣaja-cetasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The mountains in the rainy season do not at all feel pain by the repeated striking of torrential rains just as devotees whose minds are absorbed in the Lord remain peaceful even when attacked by all sorts of dangers.**

**Комментарий:**

The mountains do not feel pain when struck by the rain but rather appear beautiful with the disappearance of dust just as the minds of devotees do not feel pain when afflicted by the three types of suffering according to the following statement:

*mad-āśrayāḥ kathā mṛṣṭāḥ śṛṇvanti kathayanti ca*  
*tapanti vividhās tāpā naitān mad-gata-cetasaḥ*

**Engaged constantly in chanting and hearing about me, the sādhus do not suffer from material miseries because they are always filled with thoughts of my pastimes and activities. (SB** [**3.25.23**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.23)**)**

Rather, due to increase of humility, due to disappearance of pride and envy, they become most beautiful. This is a positive example for those attracted to the Lord.

### Text 16

*mārgā babhūvuḥ sandigdhās tṛṇaiś channā hy asaṁskṛtāḥ*  
*nābhyasyamānāḥ śrutayo dvijaiḥ kālena cāhatāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**During the rainy season the roads, not being cleansed, became covered with grass and debris and were thus difficult to discern. These roads were like Vedas that brāhmaṇas no longer study and have been destroyed by the influence of Kali-yuga.**

**Комментарий:**

The roads, overgrown, covered with grass, became difficult to discern (sandigdhāḥ). Roads overgrown are compared to the Vedas not studied. The roads covered by grass are compared to the Vedas destroyed by time. This is an unfavorable comparison for youngbrahmacārīs.

### Text 17

*loka-bandhuṣu megheṣu vidyutaś cala-sauhṛdāḥ*  
*sthairyaṁ na cakruḥ kāminyaḥ puruṣeṣu guṇiṣv iva*

**Перевод:**

**Though the clouds are the well-wishing friends of all living beings, the lightning, fickle in its affinities, moved from one group of clouds to another, like lusty women who are unfaithful even to virtuous men.**

**Комментарий:**

Lusty women are not loyal even to men who are knowledgeable of all arts. This is a negative example.

### Text 18

*dhanur viyati māhendraṁ nirguṇaṁ ca guṇiny abhāt*  
*vyakte guṇa-vyatikare ’guṇavān puruṣo yathā*

**Перевод:**

**The curved bow of Indra \[the rainbow\] without a string appeared in the thundering sky, just as the Lord devoid of material qualities appears in the world made of guṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

The bow of Indra, a rainbow, shone in the rumbling (guṇini) sky (viyati) without a string (nirguṇam), just like Viṣṇu (puruṣaḥ) beyond material guṇas (aguṇavān) shines in the world (vyakte) made of guṇas (guṇa-vyatikare) through various pastimes. This is favorable for those who know the Lord’s svarūpa.

### Text 19

*na rarājoḍupaś channaḥ sva-jyotsnā-rājitair ghanaiḥ*  
*ahaṁ-matyā bhāsitayā sva-bhāsā puruṣo yathā*

**Перевод:**

**The moon, covered by clouds which are revealed by the cool light of the moon, did not shine, just as the soul covered by ahaṅkāra, revealed by consciousness coming from the soul, does not show itself.**

**Комментарий:**

The moon, covered by clouds which are revealed and increased by its own cool moonlight, did not shine, just as the jīva (puruṣaḥ),covered by conception of ‘I’ in the form of, “I am a brāhmaṇa or I am huge,” revealed and enlarged by the soul’s nature of consciousness (sva-bhāsā), does not shine. This is favorable for the jñānī.

### Text 20

*meghāgamotsavā hṛṣṭāḥ pratyanandañ chikhaṇḍinaḥ*  
*gṛheṣu tapta-nirviṇṇā yathācyuta-janāgame*

**Перевод:**

**The peacocks became festive and made a joyful greeting when they saw the clouds arrive, just as householders devoted to devotees welcome the devotees when they arrive.**

**Комментарий:**

The peacocks, festive with the coming of clouds, welcome the clouds, just as householders, detached and associating with devotees, become joyful by the coming of devotees and welcome them. This is favorable for those who serve devotees.

### Text 21

*pītvāpaḥ pādapāḥ padbhir āsan nānātma-mūrtayaḥ*  
*prāk kṣāmās tapasā śrāntā yathā kāmānusevayā*

**Перевод:**

**The trees, after they drinking the newly fallen rainwater through their roots, took on various bodily features. Similarly, those whose bodies have grown thin and weak from austerity again exhibit healthy bodily features upon enjoying the material objects.**

**Комментарий:**

Drinking water with their roots, trees (pādapāḥ) assumed various forms with thick leaves and flowers, etc., just as those who previously were thin (kṣāmāḥ) and fatigued by performing austerities with material desires, after the austerity take on various natures by delighting in its result such as drinking, eating, and dallying (kāmānusevayā). This is unfavorable for the niṣkāma practitioners.

### Text 22

*saraḥsv aśānta-rodhaḥsu nyūṣur aṅgāpi sārasāḥ*  
*gṛheṣv aśānta-kṛtyeṣu grāmyā iva durāśayāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cranes continued dwelling on the shores of the lakes, although the shores were agitated during the rainy season, just as materialistic persons with contaminated minds always remain at home, despite the many disturbances there.**

**Комментарий:**

Cranes continued to stay (nyūṣuḥ) on the muddy (aśānta) banks of lakes just as materialists with no discrimination, thinking the house provides all comforts (durāśayā) remain in their houses though there are unending duties there (aśānta-kṛtyeṣu). O King (aṅga)! This is unfavorable.

### Text 23

*jalaughair nirabhidyanta setavo varṣatīśvare*  
*pāṣaṇḍinām asad-vādair veda-mārgāḥ kalau yathā*

**Перевод:**

**When Indra sent forth his rains, the floodwaters broke through the irrigation dikes in the agricultural fields, just as the atheists’ false theories break down the boundaries of Vedic injunctions in the Kali-yuga.**

**Комментарий:**

Indra is called īśvara who gives excess rain due to identifying himself as a controller. This is compared to Kali-yuga. This is an unfavorable description.

### Text 24

*vyamuñcan vāyubhir nunnā bhūtebhyaś cāmṛtaṁ ghanāḥ*  
*yathāśiṣo viś-patayaḥ kāle kāle dvijeritāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The clouds, impelled by the winds, released their nectarean water for the benefit of all living beings, just as kings, instructed by their brāhmaṇa priests, dispense charity to the citizens.**

**Комментарий:**

The clouds were impelled (nunnāḥ) by the wind. Kings (viśpatayaḥ) instructed by brāhmaṇas, distribute desirables. This is favorable for kings.

### Text 25

*evaṁ vanaṁ tad varṣiṣṭhaṁ pakva-kharjura-jambumat*  
*go-gopālair vṛto rantuṁ sa-balaḥ prāviśad dhariḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the Vṛndāvana forest had thus become resplendent, filled with ripe dates and jambu fruits, Kṛṣṇa, surrounded by his cows and cowherd boyfriends and accompanied by Balarāma, entered that forest to enjoy.**

**Комментарий:**

After describing the monsoon season, the Lord’s pastimes during that time are described in seven verses. Varṣiṣṭham means thriving.

### Text 26

*dhenavo manda-gāminya ūdho-bhāreṇa bhūyasā*  
*yayur bhagavatāhūtā drutaṁ prītyā snuta-stanīḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cows had to move slowly because of their weighty milk bags, but they quickly ran to the Lord as soon as he called them, their affection for him causing their udders to become wet.**

**Комментарий:**

In snuta-stanīḥ, the accusative case stands for the nominative. Their wet milk bags were a sign of their affection for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 27

*vanaukasaḥ pramuditā vana-rājīr madhu-cyutaḥ*  
*jala-dhārā girer nādād āsannā dadṛśe guhāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord saw the joyful aborigine girls of the forest, the trees dripping sweet sap, and the mountain waterfalls, and caves which were detected by echoes.**

**Комментарий:**

He saw the joyful Pulinda women (vanaukasaḥ), the groves of trees flowing with honey, waterfalls from the mountains, which were far away but close because of echoes and caves.

### Text 28

*kvacid vanaspati-kroḍe guhāyāṁ cābhivarṣati*  
*nirviśya bhagavān reme kanda-mūla-phalāśanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When it rained, the Lord would sometimes enter a cave or the hollow of a tree to play and to eat roots and fruits.**

**Комментарий:**

When the clouds rained everywhere, Kṛṣṇa ran into the hollows of trees or into caves and enjoyed round roots (kanda) and long roots (mūla) and fruits.

### Text 29

*dadhy-odanaṁ samānītaṁ śilāyāṁ salilāntike*  
*sambhojanīyair bubhuje gopaiḥ saṅkarṣaṇānvitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa would eat boiled rice and yogurt, sent from home, in the company of Saṅkarṣaṇa and the cowherd boys who were made to eat with him. They would all sit down to eat on a large stone near the water.**

**Комментарий:**

He ate rice and yogurt brought by people from the house along with his friends whom he made eat while sitting on a sone slab nearthe water. Sam in saṁbhojanīyaiḥ means together with, as in the word samvāda (conversation).

### Text 30

*śādvalopari saṁviśya carvato mīlitekṣaṇān*  
*tṛptān vṛṣān vatsatarān gāś ca svodho-bhara-śramāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa watched the contented bulls, calves and cows sitting on the green grass and chewing with closed eyes, and he saw that the cows were tired from the burden of their heavy milk bags.**

**Комментарий:**

They chewed because they were ruminating. He ate as he saw these cows and bulls. This sentence is connected with the previous verse.

### Text 31

*prāvṛṭ-śriyaṁ ca tāṁ vīkṣya sarva-kāla-sukhāvahām*  
*bhagavān pūjayāṁ cakre ātma-śakty-upabṛṁhitām*

**Перевод:**

**Thus observing the beauty of Vṛndāvana’s rainy season, filled with the happiness of all seasons, the Lord considered that season, which was surcharged with his hlādini-śakti, to be proper.**

**Комментарий:**

He worshipped the season filled with his hlādinī śakti.

### Text 32

*evaṁ nivasatos tasmin rāma-keśavayor vraje*  
*śarat samabhavad vyabhrā svacchāmbv-aparuṣānilā*

**Перевод:**

**While Balarāma and Keśava were thus dwelling in Vṛndāvana, the fall season arrived-- when the sky is cloudless, the water clear and the wind gentle.**

**Комментарий:**

Now autumn is described in eighteen verses. Its water was clear and its wind was mild.

### Text 33

*śaradā nīrajotpattyā nīrāṇi prakṛtiṁ yayuḥ*  
*bhraṣṭānām iva cetāṁsi punar yoga-niṣevayā*

**Перевод:**

**The autumn season, when the lotus flowers blossomed, also restored the various bodies of water to their original purity, just as the minds of those who fall from spiritual practice become pure by again practicing yoga.**

**Комментарий:**

The water became clear with the arrival of autumn, the season in which lotuses bloomed. This is a favorable example.

### Text 34

*vyomno ’bhraṁ bhūta-śābalyaṁ*  
*bhuvaḥ paṅkam apāṁ malam*  
*śaraj jahārāśramiṇāṁ*  
*kṛṣṇe bhaktir yathāśubham*

**Перевод:**

**Autumn cleared the sky of clouds, let the animals get out of their crowded living conditions, cleaned the earth of its covering of mud, and purified the water of contamination, in the same way that loving service rendered to Kṛṣṇa frees the members of the four spiritual orders from their respective troubles.**

**Комментарий:**

Autumn (śarat) took away the four contaminations such as clouds from the four objects starting with the sky just as bhakti arising from association of devotees takes away the difficulties from the āśramas. Just as bhakti removes difficulties of the brahmacārī such as carrying water for the guru while living with him, so autumn removed the clouds of the sky. As bhakti removes the householder’s difficulties of mixing with wife and others in repaying his three debts (to ṛṣis, devatās and pitṛs), so autumn removed the crowded condition of animals, caused by rains. As bhakti removes the suffering from not cutting nails and hair of the vānaprastha, so autumn removed the mud from the earth. As bhakti removes the desire for enjoyment in the sannyāsī, so autumn removed the contamination in water.

In the presence of bhakti one gives up the dharmas of the āśramas, since bhakti removes all anarthas and since it is the final result itself. This is a favorable example.

### Text 35

*sarva-svaṁ jaladā hitvā virejuḥ śubhra-varcasaḥ*  
*yathā tyaktaiṣaṇāḥ śāntā munayo mukta-kilbiṣāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The clouds, having given up all they possessed, shone forth with purified effulgence, just like peaceful sages who are free of all sinful propensities and thus have given up all material desires.**

**Комментарий:**

Giving up desires for sons, wealth, and followers (tyaktaiṣaṇāḥ), the sages become peaceful. This is a favorable example.

### Text 36

*girayo mumucus toyaṁ kvacin na mumucuḥ śivam*  
*yathā jñānāmṛtaṁ kale jñānino dadate na vā*

**Перевод:**

**During this season the mountains sometimes released their pure water and sometimes did not, just as jñānis sometimes give the nectar of knowledge and sometimes do not.**

**Комментарий:**

The ācāryas teach brahma-vidyā to the qualified person not just to anyone. The mountains sometimes release pure water and sometimes not. The writer of the sūtras says:

*anāviṣkurvann anvayāt*

**The teacher should not reveal vidyā to the unqualified person, since that is directly stated in śruti. (Brahma-sūtras 3.4.50)**

But they teach karma-vidyā (knowledge of karmas) to all, just like rain in monsoon is available to all. This is a favorable example.

### Text 37

*naivāvidan kṣīyamāṇaṁ jalaṁ gādha-jale-carāḥ*  
*yathāyur anv-ahaṁ kṣayyaṁ narā mūḍhāḥ kuṭumbinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The fish swimming in the increasingly shallow water did not at all understand that the water was diminishing, just as foolish family men cannot see how the time they have left to live is diminishing with every passing day.**

**Комментарий:**

Fish swimming in shallow (gādha) water did not know the water is decreasing just family people dedicated to maintaining their members do not know their life is decreasing. This is an unfavorable example.

### Text 38

*gādha-vāri-carās tāpam avindañ charad-arka-jam*  
*yathā daridraḥ kṛpaṇaḥ kuṭumby avijitendriyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The fish swimming in the shallow water had to suffer the heat of the autumn sun, just as a poverty-stricken person overly absorbed in family life and trying to earn money suffers because he cannot control his senses.**

**Комментарий:**

The fish in shallow water experiences the heat of the sun just as miserable, poor person without sense control suffers. However poverty becomes an ornament for a person who controls his senses.

### Text 39

*śanaiḥ śanair jahuḥ paṅkaṁ sthalāny āmaṁ ca vīrudhaḥ*  
*yathāhaṁ-mamatāṁ dhīrāḥ śarīrādiṣv anātmasu*

**Перевод:**

**Gradually the different areas of land gave up their muddy condition and the plants grew past their unripe stage, in the same way that sober sages give up egotism and possessiveness concerning the body which is different from the self.**

**Комментарий:**

Places gave up mud gradually and plants gave up their unripe state just as the devotees of Hari (dhīrāḥ) give up identity with bodyand possessiveness of house, since the body, not being the ātmā is useless and houses, etc., are dependent on the Lord. This is a favorable example.

### Text 40

*niścalāmbur abhūt tūṣṇīṁ samudraḥ śarad-āgame*  
*ātmany uparate samyaṅ munir vyuparatāgamaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**With the arrival of autumn, the lakes became silent, their water still, just like a sage who has desisted from all material activities and given up his recitation of Vedic mantras.**

**Комментарий:**

With the coming of autumn, the lake water became still just as the sage, his mind (ātmani) absorbed in the Lord (uparate), becoming silent, stops chanting the Vedas (vyuparatāgamaḥ). This is a favorable example.

### Text 41

*kedārebhyas tv apo ’gṛhṇan karṣakā dṛḍha-setubhiḥ*  
*yathā prāṇaiḥ sravaj jñānam tan-nirodhena yoginaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The farmers erected strong mud banks to keep the water within their rice fields from draining out, in the same way that the practitioners of yoga maintain knowledge from flowing out through the agitated senses by withdrawing the senses.**

**Комментарий:**

The farmers maintained (agṛhṇan) water flowing to the fields by firm embankments just as yogīs maintain knowledge which flows through the senses agitated by sense objects (prāṇaiḥ) by pratyāhāra, withdrawal of the senses (tat-nirodhena). This is a favorable example.

### Text 42

*śarad-arkāṁśu-jāṁs tāpān bhūtānām uḍupo ’harat*  
*dehābhimāna-jaṁ bodho mukundo vraja-yoṣitām*

**Перевод:**

**The autumn moon relieved all creatures of the suffering caused by the sun’s rays, just as wisdom relieves a person of the misery caused by his identifying with his material body and as Mukunda relieves Vṛndāvana’s ladies of the distress caused by their separation from him.**

**Комментарий:**

The moon took away the heat caused the rays of the autumn sun just as knowledge (bodhaḥ) takes away suffering caused by identity with the body and just as Mukunda takes away the suffering of the young gopīs. This is a favorable example.

### Text 43

*kham aśobhata nirmeghaṁ śarad-vimala-tārakam*  
*sattva-yuktaṁ yathā cittaṁ śabda-brahmārtha-darśanam*

**Перевод:**

**Free of clouds and filled with clearly visible stars and the moon, the autumn sky shone brilliantly, just as the heart endowed with sattva-guṇa shines with realization through the Vedas.**

**Комментарий:**

The heart having knowledge (darśanam) of the meaning of the Vedas (śabda-brahma)— niṣkama-karma, jñāna and bhakti— becomes endowed with purity (sattva). Here the sky is compared to the heart, cloudlessness to being endowed with purity, autumn to Vedas, stars to niṣkāma-karma and jñāna, and the controller of stars, referent of the word tāra, to bhakti. This is a favorable example.

### Text 44

*akhaṇḍa-maṇḍalo vyomni rarājoḍu-gaṇaiḥ śaśī*  
*yathā yadu-patiḥ kṛṣṇo vṛṣṇi-cakrāvṛto bhuvi*

**Перевод:**

**The full moon shone in the sky, surrounded by stars, just as Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the Yadu dynasty, shone brilliantly on the earth, surrounded by all the Vṛṣṇis.**

**Комментарий:**

The unfragmented nature of the disk (of the full moon) is compared to the quality of Svayam Bhagavān, the moon to Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the Yadus, and the stars to the circle of Vṛṣṇis such as Nanda, Upananda, Vasudeva, Akrūra and others. This is favorable for meditation.

### Text 45

*āśliṣya sama-śītoṣṇaṁ prasūna-vana-mārutam*  
*janās tāpaṁ jahur gopyo na kṛṣṇa-hṛta-cetasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Except for the gopīs, whose hearts had been stolen by Kṛṣṇa, the people could forget their suffering by embracing the wind coming from the flower-filled forest, which was neither hot nor cold.**

**Комментарий:**

The gopīs, embracing the wind from the flowering forest which was neither hot nor cold did not give up their suffering since they felt separation, their hearts being stolen by Kṛṣṇa. Rather they obtained pain.

### Text 46

*gāvo mṛgāḥ khagā nāryaḥ puṣpiṇyaḥ śaradābhavan*  
*anvīyamānāḥ sva-vṛṣaiḥ phalair īśa-kriyā iva*

**Перевод:**

**By the influence of the autumn season, all the cows, doe, women and female birds became fertile and were followed by their respective mates in search of sexual enjoyment, just as activities performed for the service of the Supreme Lord are automatically followed by all beneficial results.**

**Комментарий:**

Use of masculine forms (mṛgāḥ khagāḥ) instead of feminine (mṛgyaḥ khagyaḥ) is poetic license. Being forcefully approached by their mates (sva-vṛṣaiḥ), though they were unwilling, became pregnant just as actions for the Lord, characterized by worship of the Lord, performed even without material desires, are followed by results of happiness and enjoyment, which are present in it. This is a favorable example.

### Text 47

*udahṛṣyan vārijāni sūryotthāne kumud vinā*  
*rājñā tu nirbhayā loka yathā dasyūn vinā nṛpa*

**Перевод:**

**O King Parīkṣit, when the autumn sun rose, all the lotus flowers blossomed happily, except the night-blooming kumuda, just as in the presence of a strong ruler everyone becomes fearless, except the thieves.**

**Комментарий:**

With the rising of the sun the lotuses became jubilant except for the kumudas (which bloom at night). No ending on kumud is poetic license. Kumuda is also known as kumud according to Viśva.

The kumudas are compared to thieves, since wicked people are happy with kumudas (which bloom at night and indicate that the time is appropriate for theft). People are without fear because of a king ruling from the throne, except for thieves. This is favorable for kings.

### Text 48

*pura-grāmeṣv āgrayaṇair indriyaiś ca mahotsavaiḥ*  
*babhau bhūḥ pakva-śaṣyāḍhyā kalābhyāṁ nitarāṁ hareḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Abundant with ripe grains, the earth, a śakti of the Lord, was glorious with festivals for Indra and the new rice ceremony in the towns and villages, in the constant presence of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

The earth shone with Vedic karmas like ceremony of eating new grains.

*navānna naiva nandāyām na ca supte janardane*  
*kṛṣṇa-pakṣe dhanuṣi tulāyām naiva kārayet*

**The new rice ceremony should not be done on pratipada, ṣaṣṭhi, or ekādaṣī, or when the Lord sleeps, or in the waning moon phase of Kārtika or Pauṣa months.**

It takes place after the Lord sleeping on the Milk Ocean wakes up, when the sun is in Scorpio. It is a custom of the autumn season since it ends in autumn season. Earth became glorious with festivals for the senses and with ordinary festivals (indriyaiḥ). The earth, a śakti (kalā) of the Lord was glorious with Rāma and Kṛṣṇa (ābhyām).

### Text 49

*vaṇiṅ-muni-nṛpa-snātā nirgamyārthān prapedire*  
*varṣa-ruddhā yathā siddhāḥ sva-piṇḍān kāla āgate*

**Перевод:**

**The merchants, sages, kings and householders, kept indoors by the rain, were at last free to go out and attain their desired objects, just as those who achieve perfection in this life can, when the proper time comes, leave the material body and attain their respective forms.**

**Комментарий:**

The merchants, sages, kings and brahmacārīs (who have returned home after studies) who were confined during the rains, after the monsoon, went out to attain wealth, independence, conquest of countries and knowledge, just as siddhas, confined by years of lifespan, when the end comes, attain the form of an associate of the Lord (svapiṇḍān). This is a favorable example.

*varṣā-śaradayoḥ krīḍan prajaharṣa janārdanaḥ\|*  
*tayos tad-varṇanaṁ vidvān vidadhau vividhopamam*

**Kṛṣṇa, giving joy to everyone, played during the monsoon and autumn seasons. The wise one gives various analogies in the descriptions of these seasons.**

## Chapter 21 - The Gopīs Glorify the Song of Kṛṣṇa’s Flute (venu-gīta)

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*itthaṁ śarat-svaccha-jalaṁ padmākara-sugandhinā*  
*nyaviśad vāyunā vātaṁ sa-go-gopālako ’cyutaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The infallible Lord, accompanied by his cows and cowherd boyfriends, entered that Vṛndāvana forest filled with transparent autumnal waters and cooled by breezes perfumed with the fragrance of lotus flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

*ekaviṁśe veṇu-nāda-mattā gopyaḥ smarārditāḥ \|*  
*vṛndāṭavyāṁ jaguḥ kīrtiṁ mṛgyādīnāṁ muhur muhuḥ*

**This twenty-first chapter describes how the gopīs, intoxicated by Kṛṣṇa’s flute song, pained by love, repeatedly sang the glories of animals and other beings in Vṛndāvana.**

While he will be describing the pastime of flute-playing in Vṛndāvana after describing the autumn, he first describes Kṛṣṇa entering Vṛndāvana forest adorned by autumn. He entered the forest followed by the gentle breeze which was cool and fragrant because of the lotuses. Vāyunā is in the singular to suggest the gentleness of the breeze. The sentence is connected to the next verse.

### Text 2

*kusumita-vanarāji-śuṣmi-bhṛṅga*  
*dvija-kula-ghuṣṭa-saraḥ-sarin-mahīdhram*  
*madhupatir avagāhya cārayan gāḥ*  
*saha-paśu-pāla-balaś cukūja veṇum*

**Перевод:**

**The lakes, rivers and hills of Vṛndāvana resounded with the sounds of maddened bees and flocks of birds moving about the flowering trees. In the company of the cowherd boys and Balarāma, the master of spring entered that forest, and while herding the cows with them, he began to vibrate his flute.**

**Комментарий:**

The forest had mountains, rivers and lakes filled with the cries of flocks of maddened birds and bees in the flowering groves. Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda, the master of the cowherds who were also members of the Madhu dynasty (madhu-patiḥ) by being Yādavas,entering (avagāhya) that forest, played his flute. He was also the master of spring (madhu-patiḥ). By his entrance the forest became completely beautiful. He entered the forest with the cowherds and with them herded the cows, but he did not play the flute together with them, since it is explained that he played the flute song in the nextverse.

### Text 3

*tad vraja-striya āśrutya veṇu-gītaṁ smarodayam*  
*kāścit parokṣaṁ kṛṣṇasya sva-sakhībhyo ‘nvavarṇayan*

**Перевод:**

**When the young ladies in the cowherd village of Vraja heard the song of Kṛṣṇa’s flute, which arouses the influence of Cupid, some of them privately began describing Kṛṣṇa’s qualities to their intimate friends.**

**Комментарий:**

Some gopīs, his beloveds headed by Rādhā, hearing that flute song of Kṛṣṇa, described it to their friends. The song was in a such a way that their love arose (smarodayam). Thus others are excluded (i.e. elders or Balarāma’s gopīs since they did not feel any increase of conjugal love hearing the song). They did so in private (parokṣam) since they were situated in Vraja.

### Text 4

*tad varṇayitum ārabdhāḥ smarantyaḥ kṛṣṇa-ceṣṭitam*  
*nāśakan smara-vegena vikṣipta-manaso nṛpa*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd girls began to speak about Kṛṣṇa, but when they remembered his activities, O King, the power of Cupid disturbed their minds, and thus they could not speak.**

**Комментарий:**

Though they began to describe the song, they could not describe it, since their minds were confused by the impetus of love.

### Text 5

*barhāpīḍaṁ naṭa-vara-vapuḥ karṇayoḥ karṇikāraṁ*  
*bibhrad vāsaḥ kanaka-kapiśaṁ vaijayantīṁ ca mālām*  
*randhrān veṇor adhara-sudhayā pūrayan gopa-vṛndair*  
*vṛndāraṇyaṁ sva-pada-ramaṇaṁ prāviśad gīta-kīrtiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Wearing a peacock-feather ornament upon his head, yellow karṇikāra flowers on his ears, a yellow garment as brilliant as gold, and the Vaijayantī garland, Kṛṣṇa exhibited his form as the greatest of dancers as he entered the forest of Vṛndāvana, beautifying it with the marks of his footprints. He filled the holes of his flute with the nectar of his lips, and the cowherd boys sang his glories.**

**Комментарий:**

“What were Kṛṣṇa’s activities that disturbed their minds with love?” Kṛṣṇa entered Vṛndāvana with the cowherd boys. He is described. He had the body of the best dancer, with a peacock feather head ornament and wore in his ears one karṇikāra flower, sometimes on the left ear and sometimes on the right ear. This suggests his intoxication with his youth. He wore two golden cloth and a garland woven with five differently colored flowers (Vaijayantī). The word bibhrat (maintaining) is used to suggest that he constantly nourished the love with the manifestation of his beauty. He filled the holes of his flute with the wealth of notes filled with the nectar of his lips. Those notes were soft sounds, with syllables of an enchanting mantra, in various rāgas, tālas, songs and mūrchanas. The sweetness of his lips filling the flute, coming out of the flute, and entering the gopīs’ minds through their ears, showed his own bewildering gestures to their minds.

Vṛndāvana was pleasurable to his feet, suitable for the rāsa dance or with soft dust and flower pollen. This is distinguished it from Vraja town. He was glorified by the devatās as he entered the forest. This is repetition of the description in verse 1 and 2, to nourish what is already stated.

### Text 6

*iti veṇu-ravaṁ rājan sarva-bhūta-manoharam*  
*śrutvā vraja-striyaḥ sarvā varṇayantyo ’bhirebhire*

**Перевод:**

**O King, when the young ladies in Vraja heard the sound of Kṛṣṇa’s flute, which captivates the minds of all living beings, they all embraced one another and began describing it.**

**Комментарий:**

The previous description ends (iti). After some moments, when the gopīs’ impetus of love which caused the remembrance of Kṛṣṇa’s activities ended, they while describing the song of the flute, all embraced each other. They spoke into the ears of others what was in their minds while embracing. Or they embraced Kṛṣṇa in their minds. The song was attractive to all beings, unlike the song at the time of the rāsa dance, which stole only the minds of his beloveds.

### Text 7

*śrī-gopya ūcuḥ*  
*akṣaṇvatāṁ phalam idaṁ na paraṁ vidāmaḥ*  
*sakhyaḥ paśūn anuviveśayator vayasyaiḥ*  
*vaktraṁ vrajeśa-sutayor anu-veṇu juṣṭaṁ*  
*yair vā nipītam anurakta-kaṭākṣa-mokṣam*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd girls said: O friends! We do not know any other success for those with eyes than the face of the younger one who plays the flute—the face experienced as he casts a side glance of love, the face tasted by people with eyes—as the two sons of Nanda take the cows from forest to forest along with their friends.**

**Комментарий:**

Some gopīs spoke. We know that this is the result for living beings with eyes. There is nothing hihgher than this. What is that? It is the face of the two sons of Nanda, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, seen by them with thirst (nipītaṁ) and served by an agreeable flute. It was well known in Vraja that even Balarāma was the son of Nanda. Vasudeva says:

*tātaṁ bhavantaṁ manvāno bhavadbhyām upalālitaḥ*

**My son Baladeva, being raised by you and your wife, Yaśodādevī, considers you his father. (SB** [**10.5.27**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/5.27)**)**

Śukadeva says:

*rāmo ‘bhivādya pitarāv āśīrbhir abhinanditaḥ*

**Lord Balarāma offered respects to his parents (Nanda and Yaśodā), and they joyfully greeted him with prayers. (SB** [**10.65.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/65.2)**)**

That face releases side glances directed towards his attracted devotees. The two boys herd cows (anuviveśayatoḥ) with their friends. Kṛṣṇa is mentioned with Balarāma to hide their love for Kṛṣṇa. The intended meaning is this: “O friends! Of the two sons of Nanda, the face of the one following behind (anu), endowed with a flute, which is drunk by those with eyes.” “But let it be seen and heard, but how can we respectable girls drink that face?” His face releases arrows of glances after aiming in such a way that being agitated by that you give up shyness and control and and drink that.

### Text 8

*cūta-pravāla-barha-stavakotpalābja*  
*mālānupṛkta-paridhāna-vicitra-veśau*  
*madhye virejatur alaṁ paśu-pāla-goṣṭhyāṁ*  
*raṅge yathā naṭa-varau kvaca gāyamānau*

**Перевод:**

**Dressed attractively in cloth with garlands, with peacock feathers mango buds entwined in clusters of flowers on their heads, with water lilies in their ears and play lotuses in their hands, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma shine forth magnificently among the assembly of cowherd boys, and sometimes sing. They look just like the best of dancers appearing on a dramatic stage.**

**Комментарий:**

O friends! We cannot go near him because he is with Balarāma. But experiencing through the holes in the creepers, his extreme sweetness due to the nectar of his beauty, singing, and dancing, we will come back quickly. Other gopīs speak. They have new branches of mango, peacock feathers and flower clusters in their hair. They have water lilies decorating their ears. They have play lotuses in their right hands and flower garlands on their necks. They have clothing, with various colors of cloth suitable for dancing touching their bodies. Through all these they have an appearance which causes astonishment. Among cowherd boys of equal beauty, they shine on a stage like the best of dancers. Sometimes they dance among friends who sing and play instruments and sometimes they sing (gāyamānau) or are respected by all when they sing. In this way they shine nicely (alam), since it is impossible to shine or exist in Vraja due to absence of such singing, etc., out of inhibition.

### Text 9

*gopyaḥ kim ācarad ayaṁ kuśalaṁ sma veṇur*  
*dāmodarādhara-sudhām api gopikānām*  
*bhuṅkte svayaṁ yad avaśiṣṭa-rasaṁ hradinyo*  
*hṛṣyat-tvaco ’śru mumucus taravo yathāryāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear gopīs! What auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of Dāmodara’s lips independently and leave only a taste for us gopīs, for whom that nectar is actually meant! The rivers have their hairs standing on end and its relatives the trees shed tears of pleasure just as forefathers shed tears of joy on seeing the good fortune of their descendents.**

**Комментарий:**

Other gopīs speak. O gopīs! What auspicious acts did this flute perform because of which the flute enjoys even the nectar of his lips which is the wealth of gopīs? Knowing this, we also will perform those acts to attain that. If the flute were a woman then she could enjoy the nectar of her husband’s lips with great attachment. But how does this flute, a male, enjoy that nectar? They mock the the flute, since it is a masculine gender word (veṇu). And he enjoys personally (svayam). It is impossible for any gopī to attain even anatom of that nectar. That is most astonishing.

Hear about another injustice. The most pure Yamunā and other water bodies (hradinyaḥ), having enjoyed the remaining rasa left after the enjoyment by the flute, is seen to be abounding in flowers, with a deceptive appearance of blossoming lotuses. Moreover, seeing the glory of the flute, its related species, the trees also have their hairs standing on end, out of joy, with the deceptive appearance of unfurling of sprouts and shed tears with the deceptive appearance of streams of honey. They do not even consider the flute’s conduct to be improper. Some respectable people, by seeing the greatness of their dynasty, develop those respective feelings. But these trees are not like that (āryāḥ). Using the genitive form gopikānām suggests that the nectar of his lips is theirs alone since they relate to him as their husband.

### Text 10

*vṛndāvanaṁ sakhi bhuvo vitanoti kīṛtiṁ*  
*yad devakī-suta-padāmbuja-labdha-lakṣmi*  
*govinda-veṇum anu matta-mayūra-nṛtyaṁ*  
*prekṣyādri-sānv-avaratānya-samasta-sattvam*

**Перевод:**

**O friend, Vṛndāvana is spreading the glory of the earth, having obtained the treasure of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, with peacocks dancing madly when they hear Govinda’s flute, with all other creatures remaining stunned on the top of the hills as they watch the dancing.**

**Комментарий:**

“Vṛndāvana, being the place of his pastimes, is most charming. If we go there with the desire to see it, and see our lover from adistance, then there is no worry.” Others speak with this mood.

O friend! Vṛndāvana particularly spreads the glory of the earth, such that it is now more glorious than even Svarga, because it has attained the beauty of the symbols such as flag, thunderbolt and goad on the lotus feet of Yaśodā’s son (devakī-suta), which is not on other planets. It is not possible for other places to have this excellence. Seeing the dancing of peacocks mad for the sound of Govinda’s flute, on the plateaus of the mountains other animals such as deer and doves, coming there, give up all action. Going there, we will see these amazing features. This is not possible to see that in the village.

### Text 11

*dhanyāḥ sma mūḍha-matayo ’pi hariṇya etā*  
*yā nanda-nandanam upātta-vicitra-veśam*  
*ākarṇya veṇu-raṇitaṁ saha-kṛṣṇa-sārāḥ*  
*pūjāṁ dadhur viracitāṁ praṇayāvalokaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Blessed are all these foolish deer because, on hearing the sound of his flute, they, with their husbands, perform the best worship while glancing with affection at Mahārāja Nanda’s son, who is gorgeously dressed.**

**Комментарий:**

Though intelligent, we make our births unsuccessful, not meeting our lover because of shame and fear of dharma, but devoid of shame, even the foolish make their lives successful. Other gopīs speak. Sma indicates astonishment and lamentation. Though these does are foolish, they are fortunate. Hearing the sound of Kṛṣṇa’s flute, they nourished (dadhuḥ) worship of him by affectionately glancing at him. By their glances he considers his worship nourished. What to speak of our glances? Moreover, they nourish his worship along with their husbands. They are fortunate and we are unfortunate since we lack such a situation.

### Text 12

*kṛṣṇaṁ nirīkṣya vanitotsava-rūpa-śīlaṁ*  
*śrutvā ca tat-kvaṇita-veṇu-vivikta-gītam*  
*devyo vimāna-gatayaḥ smara-nunna-sārā*  
*bhraśyat-prasūna-kavarā mumuhur vinīvyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the devatās’ wives flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of Kṛṣṇa, whose nature and form bring joy to all women, and when they hear the pure song when he plays the flute, their hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair and their skirts loosen.**

**Комментарий:**

Others speak. The wives of devatās, flying in the sky on airplanes, situated on the laps of devatās, seeing Kṛṣṇa and hearing the pure(viviktam) song of the flute played by him, their composure (sārāḥ) agitated (nunna) by Cupid, become bewildered. Kṛṣṇa is described. His character and form cause joy in women whose attraction for him has arisen. The nature of the bewilderment is described. The flowers fall from their hair and their skirts become loose. Though they are devatā women, different from humans, being unobstructed by their husbands, they show attraction to Kṛṣṇa. Then why should we, who are similar to Kṛṣṇa, not show our attraction? This shows their perseverance of their love for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 13

*gāvaś ca kṛṣṇa-mukha-nirgata-veṇu-gīta*  
*pīyūṣam uttabhita-karṇa-puṭaiḥ pibantyaḥ*  
*śāvāḥ snuta-stana-payaḥ-kavalāḥ sma tasthur*  
*govindam ātmani dṛśāśru-kalāḥ spṛśantyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Using their upraised ears as vessels, the cows are drinking the nectar of the flute-song flowing out of Kṛṣṇa’s mouth. The calves, their mouths full of milk from their mothers’ moist nipples, with tear-filled eyes, stand still as they embrace him within their hearts.**

**Комментарий:**

This attraction is not caused by lust but caused by svarūpa. Other gopīs speak. The cows drink the sweet song of the flute emanating from the moon of Kṛṣṇa’s mouth through their ears, which are raised up, out fear the nectar will spill away. They stand there, not eating the grass. The calves also, which were busy drinking milk, immediately on hearing the flute song, drinking the nectar by their upraised ears, becoming stunned, stand with their mouths full of the milk from the cows udders because of being unable to drink the milk. The cows are described. Seeing Govinda, bringing him, they touch him in their minds (ātmani) and release tears from their eyes. The calves do the same.

The cause of the prema of all beings for Kṛṣṇa is caused by svarūpa and for us also, but the cows and calves, associating with him, are fortunate whereas we are unfortunate, being separated from him.

### Text 14

*prāyo batāmba vihagā munayo vane ’smin*  
*kṛṣṇekṣitaṁ tad-uditaṁ kala-veṇu-gītam*  
*āruhya ye druma-bhujān rucira-pravālān*  
*śṛṇvanti mīlita-dṛśo vigatānya-vācaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O mother! In this forest all the birds have risen onto the budding branches of the trees to see Kṛṣṇa. With closed eyes, like sages, they are simply listening in silence to the sweet vibrations of his flute, and they speak of nothing except Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Other gopīs strengthen the point that the prema is caused by svarūpa. Bata indicates surprise. Amba is an address to a sakhī. O sakhī (amba)! The birds in this forest must be mostly sages. They listen to the soft song of the flute arising from Kṛṣṇa, which is seen in Kṛṣṇa but not in Brahmā, Śiva or others. Resting (āruhya) on tree branches with attractive buds, by that happiness they close their eyes and do not speak any words. They are silent. Sages, by rejecting the results of karmas mentioned in the Vedas have climbed on the branch of the tree of the Vedas. While accepting to some degree niṣkāma-karmas, which are mentioned in the Vedas and which are compared to attractive buds, they listen to Kṛṣṇa’s song. Due to possessing such qualities the birds must be sages.

*yasmin dyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣam*  
*otaṁ manaḥ saha prāṇaiś ca sarvaiḥ \|*  
*tam evaikaṁ jānatha ātmānam anyā*  
*vāco vimuñcathāmṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ*

**Know the one ātmā within whom heaven, earth, antarikṣa and mind are woven along with all the prāṇas. Give up all other words. He is the bridge of immortality. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad** [**2.2.5**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/mundaka/2.2.5)**)**

The birds have prema arising from svarūpa.

### Text 15

*nadyas tadā tad upadhārya mukunda-gītam*  
*āvarta-lakṣita-manobhava-bhagna-vegāḥ*  
*āliṅgana-sthagitam ūrmi-bhujair murārer*  
*gṛhṇanti pāda-yugalaṁ kamalopahārāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the rivers hear the flute-song of Kṛṣṇa, the flow of their currents is broken and their waters are agitated out of desire, moving around in whirlpools. Presenting offerings of lotus flowers with the arms of their waves, the rivers grasp Murāri’s lotus feet, covering them in their embrace.**

**Комментарий:**

Others speak. Let us not speak any longer of people with knowledge. Even the rivers, currents of water, hearing Mukunda’s song, break their currents out of love (manobhāva), marked with whirlpools. Thus losing composure and shame, the rivers stop flowing to the ocean, their husband, and thus form waves by the increase of water. They hold to their bodies the feet of Murārī, standing on the shore, which have become immobile by the embrace of their arms—the waves produced from the increased water, while offering lotuses. Having shyness, we have been cheated. We are most unfortunate.

### Text 16

*dṛṣṭvātape vraja-paśūn saha rāma-gopaiḥ*  
*sañcārayantam anu veṇum udīrayantam*  
*prema-pravṛddha uditaḥ kusumāvalībhiḥ*  
*sakhyur vyadhāt sva-vapuṣāmbuda ātapatram*

**Перевод:**

**In the company of Balarāma and the cowherd boys, Kṛṣṇa plays his flute loudly as he herds all the animals of Vraja, even under the full heat of the summer sun. Seeing this, the cloud in the sky has expanded himself out of love, rises high and constructs out of his own body, with its multitude of flower-like droplets of water,an umbrella for the sake of his friend.**

**Комментарий:**

Others speak. Even the cloud, seeing Kṛṣṇa herding the Vraja cows with the cowherds and Balarāma in the hot sun, rising above him,swelling due to prema, increasing as much by which the heat will be extinghuished, produces an umbrella with its body for Kṛṣṇa, who is its friend because of being similar in showering rasa (water), destroying heat (suffering) and being the same color (dark blue). The umbrella is described. It was distinguished by small drops of water (kusumāvalībhiḥ) since megha-puṣpa (“cloud blossom”) andghana-rasa (water) are equivalent. Even the cloud in the sky acts favorably to Kṛṣṇa. We however cannot do so and are unfortunate.

### Text 17

*pūrṇāḥ pulindya urugāya-padābja-rāga*  
*śrī-kuṅkumena dayitā-stana-maṇḍitena*  
*tad-darśana-smara-rujas tṛṇa-rūṣitena*  
*limpantya ānana-kuceṣu jahus tad-ādhim*

**Перевод:**

**The aborigine women of the Vṛndāvana area become disturbed when they see the grass marked with reddish kuṅkuma powder. Endowed with the color of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts of his beloved, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they feel fully satisfied and give up all their anxiety.**

**Комментарий:**

The sakhīs of Rādhā indicate the mahābhāva called mādana as they speak among themselves. O friends! The wives of the śabaras(pulindyaḥ), are complete (pūrṇāḥ), whereas we are incomplete. We want to do such austerities. By what are they complete? By the shining saffron (śrī-kuṅkumena) in which is the color of the lotus feet of Nanda’s son, who sings in various ways using his flute (urugāya). Where did the kuṅkuma on his feet come from? It decorated the breast of his beloved. The Pulinda women are praised by us who have not attained that kuṅkuma. What is the use of the kuṅkuma to the Pulindas? It was stuck to the grass. After enjoying with his lover, Kṛṣṇa played in the forest. The kuṅkuma then stuck to the grass from his feet.

Then what did they do? Seeing the kuṅkuma stuck to the grass, they became pained with love. They spread it on their faces, desiring to smell the fragrance of Kṛṣṇa’s limbs and spread it on their breasts, with a desire for enjoyment with him. Thinking of that enjoyment, they gave up the pain caused by love (ādhim). Oh! What power there is in that kuṅkuma! We, though amidst them, however have not attained that even once. The effect of mādana is to praise those with a shadow of that enjoyment even though there is always enjoyment for oneself.

### Text 18

*hantāyam adrir abalā hari-dāsa-varyo*  
*yad rāma-kṛṣṇa-caraṇa-sparśa-pramodaḥ*  
*mānaṁ tanoti saha-go-gaṇayos tayor yat*  
*pānīya-sūyavasa-kandara-kandamūlaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Of all the servants, this Govardhana Hill is the best! O my friends! This hill, blissful with the touch of the feet of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, along with their calves, cows and cowherd friends, gives respect with all kinds of necessities—water for drinking, honey, very soft grass, caves, bulbs and roots.**

**Комментарий:**

O friends! Without taking shelter of the great devotees, one cannot attain Kṛṣṇa, dear to devotees. The great devotee is Govardhana. Thus, let us go there to see him. We will attain Kṛṣṇa there. With this intention some other gopīs speak.

This mountain Govardhana is the best servant of Kṛṣṇa. Yudhiṣthira is called hari-dāsa:

*hari-dāsasya rājarṣe rājasūya-mahodayam*  
*praśaṁsantaḥ piban martyo ‘mṛtaṁ yathā*

**As they all glorified the wonderful Rājasūya-yajña performed by that great saintly King and servant of Lord Hari, they were not satiated, just as an ordinary man is never satiated when drinking nectar. (SB** [**10.75.27**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/75.27)**)**

Uddhava is also called hari-dāsa:

*sarid-vana-giri-droṇīr vīkṣan kusumitān drumān*  
*saṁsmārayan reme hari-dāso vrajaukasām*

**That servant of Lord Hari, seeing the rivers, forests, mountains, valleys and flowering trees of Vraja, enjoyed inspiring the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana by reminding them of Lord Kṛṣṇa. (SB** [**10.47.56**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.56)**)**

But Govardhana is the best hari-dāsa, servant of the Lord. Why is it the best? Because by the touch of Kṛṣṇa’s and Balarāma’s feet Govardhana derives great pleasure indicated by the melting of rocks. Because of that pleasure, Govardhana worships (mānam) him along with the cows and his friends, using water (pānīya) in the form of foot water and ācamana, waterfalls with sweet, cooling water, as well as drinks made of honey and mangoes, etc., offered as naivedya, using dūrva grass (sūyavasas) an ingredient of arghya, and as well, tender grass used to nourish the cows as food, to increase the milk. Sūyavasa is poetic license for suyavasa. He offers caves used for sitting, for happiness when it is cold or hot. Govardhana offers roots for eating which are sweet and tasty. Govardhana is the best because he worships his master using these items which are part of his body.

### Text 19

*gā gopakair anu-vanaṁ nayator udāra*  
*veṇu-svanaiḥ kala-padais tanu-bhṛtsu sakhyaḥ*  
*aspandanaṁ gati-matāṁ pulakas taruṇāṁ*  
*niryoga-pāśa-kṛta-lakṣaṇayor vicitram*

**Перевод:**

**My dear friends!
