When Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma pass from forest to the forest with their cowherd friends, with their cows, carrying ropes to bind the cows’ rear legs at the time of milking, by the generous sound of his flute, among all living beings, those which move become inert and trees which cannot move sprout shoots in ecstasy. This is most amazing.**

**Комментарий:**

Do not delay in going there, for that cowherd may go elsewhere. Gopakaiḥ indicates compassion with the suffix kan. The cowherds were objects of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. Gopa also means that the boys protected Kṛṣṇa out of affection. The two boys herd the cows from forest to forest with their friends. This is amazing. Why? By the songs of the flute which give pleasure (udāra) by sweet melodies (kala- padaiḥ), among living beings, those which move about like animals become stunned and those without movement such as trees take on features of moving beings by their hairs standing on end. The two boys are described. They were distinguised (kṛta-lakṣaṇayoḥ) by carrying ropes for restraining the legs of uncontrollable cows. It was a yellow silk with pearls on the two ends and splendid like ornaments on their turbans. Thus they shone with increased strength as cowherds.

### Text 20

*evaṁ-vidhā bhagavato yā vṛndāvana-cāriṇaḥ*  
*varṇayantyo mitho gopyaḥ krīḍās tan-mayatāṁ yayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus narrating to one another the playful pastimes of the Lord who wandered in the Vṛndāvana forest, the gopīs became fully absorbed in those pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse summarizes. Describing the pastimes of the Lord as he wandered in Vṛndāvana, the gopīs became absorbed in him (tan- mayatām). “The mutual attraction between Kṛṣṇa and the young cowherd girls, who knew the meaning of scriptures, is improper from the point of good conduct. It shows bad character.” This is a foolish assertion since this is not stated in the scriptures. Rather, the conclusion of scriptures is that they had the highest bhakti, and he had with affection for devotees. That will be shown in the five chapters on the rāsa dance.

*yad-yac-cakāra govindo vṛndāraṇye viceṣṭitam \|*  
*prema-netrais tad-ālokya procur gopyo gṛhasthitāḥ*

**Seeing with eyes of prema, the gopīs, situated in their houses, spoke of whatever activities Govinda performed in the Vṛndāvana forest.**

## Chapter 22 - Kṛṣṇa Steals the Garments of the Unmarried Gopīs

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*hemante prathame māsi nanda-vraja-kamārikāḥ*  
*cerur haviṣyaṁ bhuñjānāḥ kātyāyany-arcana-vratam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: During the first month of the winter season, the young unmarried girls of Gokula observed the vow of worshiping goddess Kātyāyanī. For the entire month they ate only unspiced khichrī.**

**Комментарий:**

*dvāviṁśe’bhyarcitā durgā kanyābhir vāsasāṁ hṛtiḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇena vara-dānaṁ ca taru-stotraṁ ca kathyate*

**In the twenty-second chapter Durgā is worshipped by the young girls, their clothing is stolen by Kṛṣṇa, he gives them blessings and praises the trees.**

Having described the attraction of married gopīs for Kṛṣṇa in the autumn, now the attraction of unmarried girls is described. In the first month of winter, Mārgaśīrṣa, though they were eternal associates of Kṛṣṇa, they performed this worship of Kātyayānī according to local custom. The superior śakti of the Lord who is described in Nārada-pañcarātra (with the following verse) is to be understood to be Kātyāyanī.

*jānāty ekā parā-kāntaṁ saiva durgā tad-ātmikā\|*  
*yā parā paramā śaktir mahā-viṣṇu-svarūpiṇī*

**The supreme lover of Viṣṇu, called Durgā, knows. She is the supreme śakti, the counterpart of Mahā-viṣṇu.**

### Texts 2-3

*āplutyāmbhasi kālindyā jalānte codite ’ruṇe*  
*kṛtvā pratikṛtiṁ devīm ānarcur nṛpa saikatīm*

*gandhair mālyaiḥ surabhibhir balibhir dhūpa-dīpakaiḥ*  
*uccāvacaiś copahāraiḥ pravāla-phala-taṇḍulaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, after they had bathed in the water of the Yamunā just as the sun was rising, the gopīs on the riverbank worshiped an earthen deity of goddess Durgā with aromatic substances such as sandalwood pulp, garlands, other ingredients, lamps, incense, and great variety of offerings including fruits, newly grown leaves and rice.**

**Комментарий:**

They made a deity out of sand and worshipped Kātyāyinī. They worshipped using various types of cloth (uccāvacaiḥ), food offerings (upahāraiḥ), and rice, fruits and shoots (pravāla). Pravāla means young sprouts according to Medinī.

### Text 4

*kātyāyani mahā-māye mahā-yoginy adhīśvari*  
*nanda-gopa-sutaṁ devi patiṁ me kuru te namaḥ*  
*iti mantraṁ japantyas tāḥ pūjāṁ cakruḥ kamārikāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Each of the young unmarried girls performed her worship while chanting the following mantra. “O goddess Kātyāyanī, O great potency of the Lord, O possessor of great mystic power and mighty controller of all, please make the son of Nanda Mahārāja my husband. I offer my obeisances unto you.”**

**Комментарий:**

The mantra that those girls performing vrata chanted is described in two lines. O Kātyāyanī! Manifestor of the Kātyāyana’s dynasty! Bestower of the highest dharma! Make the son of King named Nanda accept my hand in marriage. “Your parents, inspired by me, will do this.” O great yoginī (joiner)! You should make this union quickly, not by the intervention of parents since tolerating the delay is difficult. Make him our husband through Gandharva rites. It is not impossible for you to do this. You are the controller (adhīśvari).

“Without the witness of guru, brāhmaṇas and fire, the relationship with him as husband will not be for the purpose of freely associating with him.” O Mayāmāyā! Spread your māyā so that my parents will not arrange my marriage to some other cowherd boy and will not know of my association with Kṛṣṇa.” O devī, maker of pastimes! You should accomplish this one pastime.

### Text 5

*evaṁ māsaṁ vrataṁ ceruḥ kumāryaḥ kṛṣṇa-cetasaḥ*  
*bhadrakālīṁ samānarcur bhūyān nanda-sutaḥ patiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus for an entire month the girls carried out their vow and properly worshiped the goddess Bhadrakālī, fully absorbing their minds in Kṛṣṇa and meditating upon the following thought: “May the son of King Nanda become my husband.”**

**Комментарий:**

They decided that Kṛṣṇa should be their husband.

### Text 6

*uṣasy utthāya gotraiḥ svair anyonyābaddha-bāhavaḥ*  
*kṛṣṇam uccair jagur yāntyaḥ kālindyāṁ snātum anvaham*

**Перевод:**

**Each day they rose at dawn. Calling out to one another by name, they all held hands and loudly sang the glories of Kṛṣṇa while going to the Kālindī to take their bath.**

**Комментарий:**

Remembering the sequence pervious to the description given in verse 2, he speaks this verse. They called each other by name(gotraiḥ). “O Dhanyā! Why are you late? Come quickly!” Hearing this, placing their arms on another’s shoulders (ābaddha-bāhavaḥ), going to the Yamunā, giving up shyness, they sang about Kṛṣṇa loudly.

### Text 7

*nadyāḥ kadācid āgatya tīre nikṣipya pūrva-vat*  
*vāsāṁsi kṛṣṇaṁ gāyantyo vijahruḥ salile mudā*

**Перевод:**

**One day they came to the riverbank and, putting aside their clothing as they had done before, happily played in the water while singing the glories of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

One day (kadācid) means on the full moon day at the end of the month since it is said that they performed the vrata for a month (SB [10.22.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.5)). With Rādhā and others, who had similar desires and who had been invited and brought there, they played in the water aftercompleting the worship of Durgā at the place of their avabhṛtha- snāna (sacred bathing after the end of a vow).

### Text 8

*bhagavāṁs tad abhipretya kṛṣno yogeśvareśvaraḥ*  
*vayasyair āvṛtas tatra gatas tat-karma-siddhaye*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord and master of all masters of yoga, was aware of what the gopīs were doing, and thus he went there surrounded by his young companions to award the gopīs the perfection of their endeavor.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was endowed with all the six opulences beginning with aiśvarya (power) and ending with vairāgya (detachment) (Bhagavān). The ending vān indicates a constant endowment of those qualities. Knowing that they were performing a vrata whose result is himself, he went there with some friends three or four years old, who were devoid of seeing difference between man and woman, who were naked. This is understood since it is said bālaiḥ (with infants) in the next verse.

*jaṅghānta-pīvara-kaṭīra-taṭī-nibaddha-vyālola-kiṅkiṇi-ghaṭā-ghaṭitair aṭadbhiḥ mugdhais tarakṣu-nakha-kalpita-kaṇṭha-bhūṣair avyakta-mañju-vacanaiḥ pṛthukaiḥ parītam*

**Kṛṣṇa was surrounded by babies who spoke in broken language, who wore tiger nails around their necks and tinkling bells around their waists, and who had fat thighs. (Krama-dīpikā)**

If they were not young, there would be no rasa. Surrounded by those young boys, Kṛṣṇa came there to give the results of their actions. Since he was Bhagavān, he was the lord of masters of yoga. He was capable of knowing the inclinations of all their hearts, and in order to fulfil their desires, he was capable of stealing their clothes placed within his sight, removing their shyness, making them offer respects by coming out of the water, and desisting from embracing them at that time, whose all limbs were seen by him, who were obtained in a secluded place and who were in his control.

### Text 9

*tāsāṁ vāsāṁsy upādāya nīpam āruhya satvaraḥ*  
*hasadbhiḥ prahasan bālaiḥ parihāsam uvāca ha*

**Перевод:**

**Taking the girls’ garments, he quickly climbed to the top of a kadamba tree. Then, as he laughed loudly and his companions also laughed, he addressed the girls jokingly.**

**Комментарий:**

He acted quickly (satvaraḥ) in order to avoid them seeing. Because the children were very young, their laughter was without cause. With them, Kṛṣṇa laughed. By the sound of their laughter, he revealed himself to the girls. He spoke in a joking way. “O young girls! Who kept these clothes on the branches of this kadamba tree? Do you know or not? Looking from a distance, is my kadamba treeholding flowers and fruit like colorful cloth? In great joy, to see the astonishing sight, I quickly came and climbed the tree.”

“It is our clothing.”

“Why are they clothes so high in the branches?”

“You stole the clothes and put them there.”

“True, other than you all, who has the power to cast accusation such as this on me, the king’s son?”

“Do not become angry. Do you not recognize them as women’s clothing?”

“Are you the only women in this world? Do not other women also exist”?

“Which other girls than us young girls of Vraja come to this solitary spot to play?”

“Are there no other women except you who play in a solitary place?”

“We did not come to play but to worship Durgā, the devatā of the kadamba tree.”

“Are there no other worshippers of her?” Apsaras who worship Durgā every night, who will worship her tonight, have put their clothing in these branches to wear after bathing.

### Text 10

*atrāgatyābalāḥ kāmaṁ svaṁ svaṁ vāsaḥ pragṛhyatām*  
*satyaṁ bravāṇi no narma yad yūyaṁ vrata-karśitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] My dear girls, you may each come here as you wish and take back your garments. I’m telling you the truth and am not joking with you, since I see you’re fatigued from executing austere vows.**

**Комментарий:**

“O crest jewel of rasikas! Those are our clothes. Making a vow to Durgā for fulfilling our desires, we put the cloth in the branches of the kadamba during the day while we worshipped her. We will wear them again.” He speaks this verse in reply.

If they are your clothes, come here and take your clothing, individually recognizing what is yours.

“Close your eyes and we will come to get the clothes. But we do not believe your words, a cheater.”

He answers with the second line. I swear that I tell the truth. I am not joking. I will give you your clothing since you are thin. My mercy, bhakti and fear of breaking dharma have arisen on you who have been doing austerities during the vrata.

### Text 11

*na mayodita-pūrvaṁ vā anṛtaṁ tad ime viduḥ*  
*ekaikaśaḥ pratīcchadhvaṁ sahaiveti su-madhyamāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**I have never before spoken a lie, and these boys know it. Therefore, O slender-waisted girls, please come forward, either one by one or all together, and pick out your clothes.**

**Комментарий:**

“We do not believe your words, as you are a false accuser.” In response, biting his tongue he speaks. Certainly (vai), I have never told a lie before this time. Udita-pūrvam means pūrvam uditam. “How can we respect your words?” These boys (ime) who accept what is seen, know this. “It is not proper for us being without clothing to come before you. Therefore, from far away, throw us the clothing. Or the small children can give them.” Come one by one. Which is whose cloth, I do not recognize. Thus you come here and take them. They will be given with my eyes closed. If you still do not believe my words, then when one of you takes the clothing, carries it and goes away, then all, having gotten faith, can come together and take the clothing. He desires to see their thin waists (su-madhyamāḥ).

### Text 12

*tasya tat kṣvelitaṁ dṛṣṭvā gopyaḥ prema-pariplutāḥ*  
*vrīḍitāḥ prekṣya cānyonyaṁ jāta-hāsā na niryayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing how Kṛṣṇa was joking with them, the gopīs became fully immersed in love for him, and as they glanced at each other they began to laugh and joke among themselves, even in their embarrassment. But still they did not come out of the water.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the secret joke of Nanda’s son, their master, filled with prema for him, thinking of doing anything for him, the gopīs looked ateach other. “You go first. He is attracted to you. You go first.” They stood laughing but did not come out of the water.

### Text 13

*evaṁ bruvati govinde narmaṇākṣipta-cetasaḥ*  
*ā-kaṇṭha-magnāḥ śītode vepamānās tam abruvan*

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa, expert at speaking, spoke to the gopīs in this way, with minds captivated by his joking words, they spoke to him, but submerged up to their necks in the cold water, they began to shiver.**

**Комментарий:**

Govinda means “he who has (vindati) attractive joking words (go).” He spoke jokes. O moon faced girls! If you do not come, then I will make a swing by tying your clothing to the branch of the kadamba tree. I will stay awake all night in the bed and pillow I have made by your clothing. Now I will sleep, since I am sleepy.”

“O jewel of cowherds! Your cows, greedy for grass, have entered a cave. Fetch them.”

O young girls! If you go very late to your houses, your parents will think something inauspicious has happened.

“O crest jewel of rasikas! We, who have begun this vrata as ordered by our parents, will live in this water for one month.”

O girls performing vratas! By the power of seeing you, I have become detached from my house, have no hunger or thirst, and desire to perform a vrata under the sky here if there is mercy. Coming down from here I will perform a vrata in the water with you.

Their hearts overwhelmed by his jokes, up to their throats in water, trembling in the cold water, they spoke to him. They trembled from worry, joy and eagerness.

### Text 14

*mānayaṁ bhoḥ kṛthās tvāṁ tu nanda-gopa-sutaṁ priyam*  
*jānīmo ‘ṅga vraja-ślāghyaṁ dehi vāsāṁsi vepitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[The gopīs said:\] Dear Kṛṣṇa, don’t be unfair! We know that you are the respectable son of Nanda and that you are honored by everyone in Vraja. You are also very dear to us. Please give us back our clothes. We are shivering in the cold water.**

**Комментарий:**

First they spoke with sāma, pacifying words. Do not do what is improper.

“You are accusing me of the fault of injustice.” We know that you are the son of the king of the cowherd called Nanda, are praiseworthy in all of Vraja, and are dear to everyone there.

“If that is so, why did you accuse me of injustice?” We are shivering. Forgive our offense and give us our clothing. Not awakening mercy in him, using intelligence of women, they say, “Do not now commit injustice.”

### Text 15

*syāma sundara te dāsyaḥ karavāma tavoditam*  
*dehi vāsāṁsi dharma-jña no ced rājñe bruvāma he*

**Перевод:**

**O beautiful boy, we are your maidservants and must do whatever you say. But give us back our clothing. You know what the religious principles are, and if you don’t give us our clothes we will have to tell the king.**

**Комментарий:**

They show dāna, giving offerings to appease him. O beautiful boy (sundara)! We will be (syāma) your servants. In some versions, the words are śyama-sundara. It is fitting that we, your citizens serve you, the son of the king. Actually, however, we are your servants and will offer ourselves to you. Since we are the servants of you, so beautiful, we will do what you say.

Some rough girls among them then spoke using bheda (dissension). O knower of dharma! You will commit adharma by stealing theproperty of women. If you do not fear adharma, there is fear present now. If you do not give the clothing, we will tell Nanda your father, the king. There are two types of bheda but punishment is not prescribed since that is unsuitable for a dear person.

From verse 12 till the present verse the anubhāva called kilakiñcita has been shown. Its characteristics are:

*garvābhilāṣa-rudita-smitāsūyā-bhaya-krudhām \|*  
*saṅkarī-karaṇaṁ harṣād ucyate kila-kiñcitam*

**When pride, desire, weeping, smiling, envy, fear and anger manifest together because of joy, these symptoms are called kilakiñcita. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 11.44)**

### Text 16

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*bhavatyo yadi me dāsyo mayoktaṁ vā kariṣyatha*  
*atrāgatya sva-vāsāṁsi pratīcchata śuci-smitāḥ*  
*no cen nāhaṁ pradāsye kiṁ kruddho rājā kariṣyati*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: If you girls are actually my maidservants, and if you will really do what I say, then come here with your innocent smiles and let each girl pick out her clothes. If you don’t do what I say, I won’t give them back to you. And even if the king becomes angry, what can he do?**

**Комментарий:**

Making them speachless by defeating them with his words he then spoke. “This is the test of your dharma, whether there is no deviation from truth.” Smile purely (śuci-smitāḥ). “If in this test, your smiles are not withered.” I will not give the clothing to those who deviate from truth and to those whose smiles are withered. Actually śuci means mādhurya rasa according to the dictionary. Thus he asks them to smile with amorous love.

### Text 17

*tato jalāśayāt sarvā dārikāḥ śīta-vepitāḥ*  
*pāṇibhyāṁ yonim ācchādya protteruḥ śīta-karśitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then, shivering from the painful cold, all the young girls rose up out of the water, covering their pubic area with their hands.**

**Комментарий:**

“O friends! We have been defeated by our own words. What shall we do? If some man comes here, we will sink in the ocean of shame. Moreover, for whom we performed this vow, preserving the obstinacy of that dear lover, saying goodbye to our shame, covering our bodies with the clothing of darkness attained by closing our eyes, we should come out of the water to the bank. Deciding in this way together, they approached Kṛṣṇa, coming out of the water (protteruḥ).

### Text 18

*bhagavān āhatā vīkṣya śuddha-bhāva-prasāditaḥ*  
*skandhe nidhāya vāsāṁsi prītaḥ provāca sa-smitam*

**Перевод:**

**When the Supreme Lord saw how the gopīs were struck with embarrassment, he was satisfied by their pure loving affection. Putting their clothes on his shoulders, the Lord smiled and spoke to them with a smile.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing them approach (āhatā) or seeing that they had overcome shame, completely beaten (āhatā), he was pleased with their purelove, which desired him alone. Bhagavān placed the clothing on his shoulders. By this he conveyed the idea that their limbs were not different from his limbs. By attaining the fragrance of their limbs, understanding that “these girls will become completely dedicated to me,” he was pleased (prītaḥ) and spoke with a smile. I will test them since they accepted to be my servants and said, “We will do what you say.” (SB [10.22.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.15)) I will give clothing along with my mind to those who pass the test.

### Text 19

*yūyaṁ vivastrā yad apo dhṛta-vratā*  
*vyagāhataitat tad u deva-helanam*  
*baddhvāñjaliṁ mūrdhny apanuttaye ’ṁhasaḥ*  
*kṛtvā namo ’dho-vasanaṁ pragṛhyatām*

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] You girls bathed naked while executing your vow, and that is certainly an offense against the devatās. To counteract your sin you should offer obeisances while placing your joined palms above your heads. Then you should take back your lower garments.**

**Комментарий:**

“O master! Let the test be done.”  
Your bathing naked in the water, is definitely (u) an offense (helanam) to Varuṇa the controller of water.

“But this is the local custom.” You made a vow (dhṛta-vratāḥ) but this will not bear fruit. Seeing them depressed, being merciful, he immediately showed a light atonement. To negate the offense to the water devatā, offer respects and take your lower cloth. Since I, a male, have no use for them, I will give them alone. But I will keep the upper cloth. He saw them offering respects with their heads and one hand. Since that was not first class, and since the second hand had commited a fault, he ordered them to fold their hands and put them on their heads. By saying on the head (mūrdhni) he negated folding the hands below the waist.

### Text 20

*ity acyutenābhihitaṁ vrajābalā*  
*matvā vivastrāplavanaṁ vrata-cyutim*  
*tat-pūrti-kāmās tad-aśeṣa-karmaṇāṁ*  
*sākṣāt-kṛtaṁ nemur avadya-mṛg yataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus the young girls of Vṛndāvana, considering what he had told them, accepted that they had suffered a fault in their vow by bathing naked in the river. But they still desired to successfully complete their vow, and they offered their obeisances to their future husband, who thus cleansed them of sin.**

**Комментарий:**

Let us forget about shame. Our vrata should not be faulty. Determining this, they followed the order of their master. Due to the fault, they offered respects to their master Kṛṣṇa, the real result indicated by Acyuta (karmaṇāṁ sāksāt-krṭam), not to Varuṇa, since they were the best knowers of truth and it is said:

*kim alabhyaṁ bhagavata prasanne śrī-niketane*  
*tathāpi tat-parā rājan na hi vāñchanti kiñcana*

**My dear King, what is unattainable for one who has satisfied the Supreme Lord, the shelter of the goddess of fortune? Even so, those who are dedicated to his devotional service never want anything from him. (SB** [**10.39.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.15)**)**

One should not say that unlimited faults cannot destroyed just by offering respects. By offering respects to the Lord (yataḥ) there isdestruction (mṛk) of all faults and all offenses.

### Text 21

*tās tathāvanatā dṛṣṭvā bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ*  
*vāsāṁsi tābhyaḥ prāyacchat karuṇas tena toṣitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing them bow down like that, the Supreme Lord, the son of Devakī, gave them back their garments, feeling compassionate toward them and satisfied by their act.**

**Комментарий:**

The son of Yaśodā (devakī-sutaḥ), seeing them bow down (avanatā) as he instructed (tathā), gave them all the clothing. Seeing them shivering from the cold, being merciful, he was satisfied by their pure devotion (tena).

### Text 22

*dṛḍhaṁ pralabdhās trapayā ca hāpitāḥ*  
*prastobhitāḥ krīḍana-vac ca kāritāḥ*  
*vastrāṇi caivāpahṛtāny athāpy amuṁ*  
*tā nābhyasūyan priya-saṅga-nirvṛtāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Although the gopīs had been thoroughly cheated, deprived of their modesty, ridiculed and made to act just like toy dolls, and although their clothing had been stolen, they did not feel at all inimical toward Kṛṣṇa. Rather, they were simply joyful to have this opportunity to associate with their beloved.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he had mocked them, he rejoiced at their compliance to him, hard to do for others. They had been cheated extremely by him (pralabdhāḥ) (you are naked, SB [10.22.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.19)), made to give up their modesty (trapayā hāpitāḥ) (come here and get your cloths, SB [10.22.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.16)), ridiculed roughly (I tell the truth, not a joke, SB [10.22.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.10)), and made to act like dolls (put your hands on your head, SB [10.22.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.19)) but they did not see any fault in him. Kāritāḥ has the affix ṇic, used in the meaning of itself. Rather, though he had done this, they became blissful by his association. They considered everything that he had done as the spiritual goal, since he was dear to them. A material intelligence will worry that the Lord full of bliss becomes dependent on objects like women for bliss, like a jīva. This is refuted, since these women were his svarūpa-śakti. Their forms were expansions of his form, as Brahmā-saṁhitā explains:nija-rūpatayā kalābhiḥ: the gopīs were his own forms. Moon only becomes complete with its digits.

### Text 23

*paridhāya sva-vāsāṁsi preṣṭha-saṅgama-sajjitāḥ*  
*gṛhīta-cittā no celus tasmin lajjāyitekṣaṇāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After they had dressed, the gopīs, attracted to his association, and attracting him, did not move. The simply glanced at him shyly.**

**Комментарий:**

They became attached to his association. They accepted his heart or feelings (gṛhīta-cittāḥ). They had mutual prema. They glanced at him with shyness. They did not move because they were stunned. Due to the perception that Kṛṣṇa is attracted to them, the shyness which though had deparated, returned exceedingly to their limbs.

### Text 24

*tāsāṁ vijñāya bhagavān sva-pāda-sparśa-kāmyayā*  
*dhṛta-vratānāṁ saṅkalpam āha dāmodaro ’balāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Dāmodara, understanding the determination of the gopīs in executing their strict vow with a desire to touch his feet, spoke to them as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding their words, “Hearing the order to us your servants to serve you, we will return home,” he revealed his decision.Understanding their determination of having him as their husband (sva-pāda-sparśa-kāmyayā) Dāmodara spoke. Starting with this pastime, he had love for them.

### Text 25

*saṅkalpo viditaḥ sādhvyo bhavatīnāṁ mad-arcanam*  
*mayānumoditaḥ so ’sau satyo bhavitum arhati*

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] O saintly girls, I understand that your real motive in this austerity has been to worship me. That intent of yours is approved by me and must come true.**

**Комментарий:**

O chaste girls! Your desire (saṅkalpaḥ) characterized by worship of me, in which you offer yourselves for my happiness, though not stated because of your shyness, is known and approved by me. It must come true since it is devoid of deception. There is no doubt at all about this since you are dedicated to my happiness and I am controlled by your prema.

### Text 26

*na mayy āveśita-dhiyāṁ kāmaḥ kāmāya kalpate*  
*bharjitā kvathitā dhānāḥ prāyo bījāya neśate*

**Перевод:**

**The desire of those who fix their minds on me does not lead to material desire for sense gratification, just as barleycorns burned by the sun and then cooked can no longer grow into new sprouts.**

**Комментарий:**

Your bhakti is the result. It is not that bhakti has some other result. For those who understand me as the supreme goal, who have absorbed their intelligence in me, desire to serve me in prema (kāmaḥ) does not produce desire for different material results (kāmāya). Rather it becomes tasty itself. An example is given. Dhānā means roasted barley corns according to Viśva. By their nature they are roasted. Then roasted again in ghee and cooked with sugar syrup cannot produce any other result (bījāya). This is like that (prāyaḥ). Use of the singular verb is poetic license. Prāya means most or equal according to Viśva.

### Text 27

*yātābalā vrajaṁ siddhā mayemā raṁsyatha kṣapāḥ*  
*yad uddiśya vratam idaṁ cerur āryārcanaṁ satīḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Go now, girls, and return to Vraja. Your desire is fulfilled, for in my company you will enjoy the coming nights. After all, this was the purpose of your vow to worship goddess Kātyāyanī, O pure-hearted ones.**

**Комментарий:**

He fulfills their desire. O young girls (abalāḥ)! Go to Vraja. You are perfected. Your performance of a vrata in the form of pastimes is complete from customary perception. You will enjoy the coming nights (ime kṣapāḥ) with me. You performed the vrata with thepurpose of enjoyment as wives. It is understood that Gandharva marriage had taken place for them. O pure women!

### Text 28

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity ādiṣṭā bhagavatā labdha-kāmāḥ kumārikāḥ*  
*dhyāyantyas tat-padāmbhojam kṛcchrān nirviviśur vrajam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus instructed by the Supreme Lord, the young girls, their desire now fulfilled, could bring themselves only with great difficulty to return to the village of Vraja, meditating all the while upon his lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

They returned with difficulty because their minds and eyes had been stolen by him.

### Text 29

*atha gopaiḥ parivṛto bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ*  
*vṛndāvanād gato dūraṁ cārayan gāḥ sahāgrajaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After some time, Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, surrounded by his cowherd friends and accompanied by his elder brother, Balarāma, went a good distance away from Vṛndāvana, herding the cows.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the mercy given to the young girls, now Śukadeva begins to speak of mercy given to the wives of the brāhmaṇasperforming sacrifice, which manifested in his heart at this time. At another time, in the summer season (atha) this occurred.

### Text 30

*nidaghārkātape tigme chāyābhiḥ svābhir ātmanaḥ*  
*ātapatrāyitān vīkṣya drumān āha vrajaukasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the sun’s heat became intense, Kṛṣṇa saw that the trees growing in Vraja were acting as umbrellas by shading him, and thus he spoke.**

### Texts 31-32

*he stoka-kṛṣṇa he aṁśo śrīdāman subalārjuna*  
*viśāla vṛṣabhaujasvin devaprastha varūthapa*

*paśyataitān mahā-bhāgān parārthaikānta-jīvitān*  
*vāta-varṣātapa-himān sahanto vārayanti naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] O Stoka Kṛṣṇa and Aṁśu, O Śrīdāmā, Subala and Arjuna, O Viśāla, O Vṛṣabha, Ojasvī, Devaprastha and Varūthapa, just see these greatly fortunate trees, whose lives are completely dedicated to the benefit of others. Even while tolerating the wind, rain, heat and snow, they protect us from these elements.**

**Комментарий:**

These trees are better than the brāhmaṇas absorbed in killing animals, since they help others. He calls to his friends Stoka- kṛṣṇa and others in order to praise the trees. The first eight boys, very strong, are in the eight directions to protect Kṛṣṇa, the son of a king. Devaprastha by holding an umbrella above him and Varūthapa by cleaning the path (in front of him) are in upward and downward directions. The eleventh boy was Bhadrasena who was the commander-in-chief of the boys. He was situated at a distance, looking over everything. Tolerating the wind themselves, the trees check them for us.

### Text 33

*aho eṣāṁ varaṁ janma sarva -prāṇy-upajīvanam*  
*su-janasyeva yeṣāṁ vai vimukhā yānti nārthinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Just see how these trees are maintaining every living entity! Their birth is successful. Their behavior is just like that of great personalities, for anyone who asks anything from a tree never goes away disappointed.**

**Комментарий:**

The trees are like generous persons (sujanasya) who are intent on serving guests, giving to those who ask (arthinaḥ).

### Text 34

*patra-puṣpa-phala-cchāyā-mūla-valkala-dārubhiḥ*  
*gandha-niryāsa-bhasmāsthi-tokmaiḥ kāmān vitanvate*

**Перевод:**

**These trees fulfill one’s desires with their leaves, flowers and fruits, their shade, roots, bark and wood, and also with their fragrance, sap, ashes, seeds, pulp and shoots.**

**Комментарий:**

Niryāsaḥ means thick sap. Asthi means the essential portion. Tokmāḥ means sprouts.

### Text 35

*etāvaj janma-sāphalyaṁ dehinām iha dehiṣu*  
*prāṇair arthair dhiyā vācā śreya-ācaraṇaṁ sadā*

**Перевод:**

**It is the duty of every living being to perform welfare activities for the benefit of others with his life, wealth, intelligence and words. To this extent is the success of life.**

**Комментарий:**

Success of birth is to this extent. Whatever beneficial actions are done for jīvas (dehiṣu) with prāṇas, etc.

### Text 36

*iti pravāla-stabaka-phala-puṣpa-dalotkaraiḥ*  
*tarūṇāṁ namra-śākhānāṁ madhyato yamunāṁ gataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus moving among the trees, whose branches were bent low by their abundance of twigs, flower bunches, fruits, flowers and leaves, Kṛṣṇa came to the Yamunā River by a middle road.**

**Комментарий:**

The branches bent over because of their twigs, etc.

### Text 37

*tatra gāḥ pāyayitvāpaḥ su-mṛṣṭāḥ śītalāḥ*  
*śivāḥ tato nṛpa svayaṁ gopāḥ kāmaṁ svādu papur jalam*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd boys let the cows drink the clear, cool and wholesome water of the Yamunā. O King Parīkṣit, the cowherd boys themselves also drank that sweet water to their full satisfaction.**

### Text 38

*tasyā upavane kāmaṁ cārayantaḥ paśūn nṛpa*  
*kṛṣṇa-rāmāv upāgamya kṣudhārtā idam abravan*

**Перевод:**

**Then, O King, the cowherd boys began herding the animals in a leisurely way within a small forest along the Yamunā. But soon they became afflicted by hunger and, approaching Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

They were herding the cows in grove on the Yamunā (tasyāḥ). The grove was mostly aśoka trees since it is mentioned as such later. Thus there were no fruits. The boys were afflicted by hunger (kṣudhārtā). The boys were particularly hungry by thinking that Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were also hungry. Saying that they were hungry is an arrangement of prema. They later say to the brāhmaṇas, “Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma are hungry.” (SB [10.23.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/23.7)) The Lord’s and the boys’ hunger was impelled by the brāhmaṇas’ wives who were devotees and was the form of appetite for the food and nothing else for it is said vijigatso ’pipāsa: there is no hunger or thirst in the spiritualworld. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) On that day, they did not bring yogurt and rice from home. This was arranged on some pretext by the Lord. By his desire there was offering of fruits, etc., which took shelter of Vṛndā. Its result was mercy on the brāhmaṇas’ wives.

## Chapter 23 - The Brāhmaṇas’ Wives Blessed

### Text 1

*śrī-gopa ūcuḥ*  
*rāma rāma mahā-bāho kṛṣṇa duṣṭa-nibarhaṇa*  
*eṣā vai bādhate kṣun nas tac-chāntiṁ kartum arhathaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd boys said: O Rāma, Rāma, mighty-armed one! O Kṛṣṇa, chastiser of the wicked! We are being harassed by this hunger, and you should do something about it.**

**Комментарий:**

*trayoviṁśe tv anna-yācñā gopair viprān prati prabhoḥ \|*  
*tat-patnīnāṁ parā bhaktis teṣāṁ tāpaś ca varṇyate*

**In the twenty-third chapter, the cowherd boys asking the brāhmaṇas for food for Kṛṣṇa and the elevated bhakti of the wives as well as the brāhmaṇas repentance is described.**

We are afflicted by this hunger. We will know that you two are “mighty-armed” (mahā-bāho) and “chastiser of the wicked” (duṣṭa- nirbarhaṇa) only when you destroy this hunger. This is their joke.

### Text 2

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*iti vijñāpito gopair bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ*  
*bhaktāyā vipra-bhāryāyāḥ prasīdann idam abravīt*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus entreated by the cowherd boys, Kṛṣṇa, endowed with all powers, the son of Devakī, replied as follows, desiring to be merciful to brāhmaṇas’ wives who were devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhāryāyāḥ is in the singular to denote a type since he gave mercy to all the wives.

### Text 3

*prayāta deva-yajanaṁ brāhmaṇā brahma-vādinaḥ*  
*satram āṅgirasaṁ nāma hy āsate svarga-kāmyayā*

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] Please go to the sacrificial arena where a group of brāhmaṇas, learned in the Vedic injunctions, are now performing the Āṅgirasa sacrifice to gain promotion to heaven.**

**Комментарий:**

There can be no mercy by mere dharmas such as performing saṁskāras like donning the scared thread but by bhakti alone. In order to teach this gradually among one brāhmaṇa lineage, Kṛṣṇa first sent the cowherd boys to such brāhmaṇas. Go to the sacrificial arena (deva-yajanam). Those brāhmaṇas speak the Vedas (brahma- vādinaḥ).

### Text 4

*tatra gatvaudanaṁ gopā yācatāsmad-visarjitāḥ*  
*kīrtayanto bhagavata āryasya mama cābhidhām*

**Перевод:**

**When you go there, my dear cowherd boys, simply request some food. Declare to them the name of my elder brother, the powerful Balarāma and my name, and explain that you have been sent by us.**

**Комментарий:**

You who have been sent by us (visarjitāḥ) should ask for food. “How can brāhmaṇas give food to cowherds? And how can we accept what is given? Since cowherds are not worthy recipients.” Kṛṣṇa answers. You should glorify the names of Baladeva and me since we are worthy recipients.

*ataḥ pātrataraḥ ko ‘nyas triṣu lokeṣu vidyate*  
*kṛṣṇāt kamala-patrākṣād deva-devāj janārdanāt*

**Who else is a more worthy recipient of charity than lotus eyed Kṛṣṇa, the head of the devatās, in the three worlds? (Hari-vaṁśa)**

### Text 5

*ity ādiṣṭā bhagavatā gatvā yācanta te tathā*  
*kṛtāñjali-puṭā viprān daṇḍa-vat patitā bhuvi*

**Перевод:**

**Respecting Kṛṣṇa’s instructions they stood before the brāhmaṇas with palms joined in supplication and falling flat on the ground to offer respect they submitted their request.**

**Комментарий:**

They fell on the earth. They, due to good etiquette, had devotional sentiments directed to the brāhmaṇas.

### Text 6

*he bhūmi-devāḥ śṛṇuta kṛṣṇasyādeśa-kāriṇaḥ*  
*prāptāñ jānīta bhadraṁ vo gopān no rāma-coditān*

**Перевод:**

**\[The cowherd boys said:\] O earthly gods, please hear us. We cowherd boys are executing the orders of Kṛṣṇa, and we have been sent here by Balarāma. We wish all good for you. Please acknowledge our arrival.**

**Комментарий:**

O brāhmaṇas (bhūmi-devāḥ)! Know that we have been sent by Balarāma, and carry the order of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 7

*gāś cārayantāv avidūra odanaṁ*  
*rāmācyutau vo laṣato bubhukṣitau*  
*tayor dvijā odanam arthinor yadi*  
*śraddhā ca vo yacchata dharma-vittamāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma and Acyuta are tending their cows not far from here. They are hungry and want you to give them some of your food. Therefore, O best of the knowers of religion, if you have faith please give some food to us to give them.**

**Комментарий:**

Desiring (laṣataḥ) your food they beg because they are hungry (bubhukṣitau). One should not ask how they can be given food before the brāhmaṇas have eaten due to the statement, annasya kṣudhitaḥ pātram: one who is hungry should be given food. The hidden meaning is this. O brāhmaṇas! Since you are silent even after hearing that Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, givers of bliss to all, afflicted by hunger beg, you appear to be born from two parents only (dvijā), not twice-born. Dharma-vittamā (best knowers of religion) is used without its original meaning.

### Text 8

*dīkṣāyāḥ paśu-saṁsthāyāḥ sautrāmaṇyāś ca sattamāḥ*  
*anyatra dīkṣitasyāpi nānnam aśnan hi duṣyati*

**Перевод:**

**Except during the interval between the initiation of the performer of a sacrifice and the actual sacrifice of the animal, O most pure brāhmaṇas, it is not contaminating for even the initiated to partake of food, at least in sacrifices other than the sautrāmaṇi.**

**Комментарий:**

“Being initiated into the sacrifice, we cannot eat.” Dīkṣitānnaṁ na bhuñjīta: being initiated one should not eat food. Thinking thebrāhmaṇas would say this the boys reply. Eating is contaminating from the initiation until killing of the animal in the agnīṣoma sacrifice but in other cases eating food does not contaminate. And after the killing, eating is not contaminating. The idea is that the animal sacrifice has taken place. Similarly, in sacrifices other than sautrāmaṇi it is not contaminating but in the sautrāmaṇi sacrifice eating is always contaminating. Since they were associates of the Lord, they spontaneously knew scriptures even though they had not studied scriptures.

### Text 9

*iti te bhagavad-yācñāṁ śṛṇvanto ’pi na śuśruvuḥ*  
*kṣudrāśā bhūri-karmāṇo bāliśā vṛddha-māninaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇas heard this supplication from the Lord full of all powers, yet they refused to pay heed. They were full of petty desires and entangled in elaborate rituals because of ignorance, though presuming themselves advanced in Vedic learning.**

**Комментарий:**

Though they knew the Vedas, why did they not listen to the Lord’s request? Though they had studied the Vedas, they were fools. With anger Śukadeva criticizes the brāhmaṇas. They had desires for insignificant Svarga (kṣudra). They were very proud (vṛddha- māninaḥ), but not great in knowledge.

### Texts 10-11

*deśaḥ kālaḥ pṛthag dravyaṁ mantra-tantrartvijo ‘gnayaḥ*  
*devatā yajamānaś ca kratur dharmaś ca yan-mayaḥ*

*taṁ brahma paramaṁ sākṣād bhagavantam adhokṣajam*  
*manuṣya-dṛṣṭyā duṣprajñā martyātmāno na menire*

**Перевод:**

**Although the ingredients of sacrificial performance—the place, time, particular paraphernalia, mantras, rituals, priests, fires, demigods, performer, offering and the as yet unseen beneficial results—are all simply his byproducts, the brāhmaṇas, by mortal vision, did not respect Kṛṣṇa though he was the Absolute Truth, Bhagavān, and beyond the material senses because they lacked discrimination, because of false identification with the material body.**

**Комментарий:**

“Overlooking the time, place, recipient etc. prescribed in the Vedas, why should food meant for other be given to another?” Thevarious ingredients, the caru, proḍāśa, etc. (dravyaṁ), the method (tantraḥ), and the results in the future (dharma) are a portion of aportion of Kṛṣṇa’s powers (yan-mayaḥ).

The reason for the ingredients being portion of portion of his powers is that he is paramaṁ brahman, since the śaktimān has all thosevarious forms, or because all the ingredients depend on him and he pervades everything all of them. He is full of the six opulences(bhagavān). He is beyond the material senses (adhokṣajam). However, by mercy he can be seen.

Those who identify with the body (martyātmānaḥ) by thinking the Lord is a special jīva, do not respect this Bhagavān.

### Text 12

*na te yad om iti procur na neti ca parantapa*  
*gopā nirāśāḥ pratyetya tathocuḥ kṛṣṇa-rāmayoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the brāhmaṇas failed to reply even with a simple yes or no, O chastiser of the enemy \[Parīkṣit\], the cowherd boys returned disappointed to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma and reported this to them.**

**Комментарий:**

Oṁ is used in the sense of acceptance. Om ity anumatau proktam: Om means consent according to Viśva.

They did not say, “We will give the food,” and they did not say, “We will not give the food,” because of excessive disrespect arising from their absorption in intolerable pride. The boys spoke to Kṛṣṇa what they said and the actions of the brāhmaṇas.

### Text 13

*tad upākarṇya bhagavān prahasya jagad-īśvaraḥ*  
*vyājahāra punar gopān darśayan laukikīṁ gatim*

**Перевод:**

**Hearing what had happened, the Lord of the universe, invested with all powers simply laughed. Then he again addressed the cowherd boys, showing them how to act in this world.**

**Комментарий:**

He laughed since it was not proper to become angry at ignorant brāhmaṇas. He taught worldly conduct (laukikīṁ gatim): those who are begging should not become despondent. Sometimes the beggar is defeated.

### Text 14

*māṁ jñāpayata patnībhyaḥ sa-saṅkarṣaṇam āgatam*  
*dāsyanti kāmam annaṁ vaḥ snigdhā mayy uṣitā dhiyā*

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] Tell the wives of the brāhmaṇas that I have come here with Saṅkarṣaṇa. They will certainly give you all the food you want, for they are most affectionate toward me, thinking of me always.**

**Комментарий:**

Tell the wives that I have come, not that I am hungry, because they will be pained. “But how will they give food without telling that you are hungry?” Being most affectionate to me, they will give as much food as you want because it is related to me. “Their husbands will prevent them.” They live in me by their intelligence. They live in their husband’s houses with only their bodies. They will not consider being prevented by their husbands.

### Text 15

*gatvātha patnī-śālāyāṁ dṛṣṭvāsīnāḥ sv-alaṅkṛtāḥ*  
*natvā dvija-satīr gopāḥ praśritā idam abruvan*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd boys then went to the house where the brāhmaṇas’ wives were staying. There the boys saw those chaste ladies sitting, nicely decorated with fine ornaments. Bowing down to the brāhmaṇa ladies, the boys addressed them in all humility.**

**Комментарий:**

Praśritā means they were very polite.

### Text 16

*namo vo vipra-patnībhyo nibodhata vacāṁsi naḥ*  
*ito ’vidūre caratā kṛṣṇeneheṣitā vayam*

**Перевод:**

**\[The cowherd boys said:\] Obeisances unto you, O wives of the learned brāhmaṇas! Kindly hear our words. We have been sent here by Kṛṣṇa, who is passing by not far from here.**

**Комментарий:**

Iṣitāḥ means “were sent.”

### Text 17

*gāś cārayan sa gopālaiḥ sa-rāmo ’dūram āgataḥ*  
*bubhukṣitasya tasyānnaṁ sānugasya pradīyatām*

**Перевод:**

**He has come near with the cowherd boys and Balarāma, tending the cows. Now he is hungry, so some food should be given for him and his companions.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing Kṛṣṇa’s name, they will faint in bliss. To make them recover, details are given. They have come and are near you (adūram).

### Text 18

*śrutvācyutam upāyātaṁ nityaṁ tad-darśanotsukāḥ*  
*tat-kathākṣipta-manaso babhūvur jāta-sambhramāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The wives of the brāhmaṇas were always eager to see Kṛṣṇa, for their minds had been enchanted by descriptions of him. Thus as soon as they heard that he was hungry, they became very excited.**

**Комментарий:**

The wives began criticizing their minds on hearing that Kṛṣṇa was hungry: “O you low mind! Although you have heard that yourmaster is suffering from hunger, why did you not wake up from fainting?”

### Text 19

*catur-vidhaṁ bahu-guṇam annam ādāya bhājanaiḥ*  
*abhisasruḥ priyaṁ sarvāḥ samudram iva nimnagāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Taking along in large vessels the four kinds of foods, full of fine tastes and aromas, all the ladies went forth to meet their beloved, just as rivers flow toward the sea.**

**Комментарий:**

They brought four types of food: which are not chewed (i.e. swallowed), those which are chewed, those which are licked and those which are sucked. The food had many good qualities: hot, cold, soft, fragrant, etc. Bringing the food, they approached their beloved, as rivers flow to the sea, without considering obstacles. Mādhurya-bhāva had arisen in them.

### Texts 20-21

*niṣidhyamānāḥ patibhir bhrātṛbhir bandhubhiḥ sutaiḥ*  
*bhagavaty uttama-śloke dīrgha-śruta-dhṛtāśayāḥ*

*yamunopavane ’śoka nava-pallava-maṇḍite*  
*vicarantaṁ vṛtaṁ gopaiḥ sāgrajaṁ dadṛśuḥ striyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Although their husbands, brothers, sons and other relatives tried to forbid them from going, their hope of seeing Kṛṣṇa, cultivated by extensive hearing of his qualities, prevailed. Along the river Yamunā, within a garden decorated with buds of aśoka trees, they caught sight of him playing with the cowherd boys and Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

They approached Kṛṣṇa (previous verse), though forbidden by their husbands, etc. The reason is given. They had desire for the Lordby hearing about him for a long time (dīrgha-śruta-dhṛtāśayāḥ). Coming, they saw Kṛṣṇa immediately.

### Text 22

*śyāmaṁ hiraṇya-paridhiṁ vanamālya-barha-*  
*dhātu-pravāla-naṭa-veṣam anuvratāṁse*  
*vinyasta-hastam itareṇa dhunānam abjaṁ*  
*karṇotpalālaka-kapola-mukhābja-hāsam*

**Перевод:**

**His complexion was dark blue and his belt was golden. Wearing a peacock feather, colored minerals, sprigs of flower buds, and a garland of forest flowers and leaves, he was dressed just like a dramatic dancer. He rested his left hand upon the shoulder of a friend and with the other twirled a lotus. Lilies graced his ears, his hair hung down over his cheeks, and his lotus-like face was smiling.**

**Комментарий:**

He wore gold colored cloth. He had the dress of an actor, with garland made of leaves and flowers reaching to his feet, a peacockfeather head ornament, minerals made into fragrant ointments, and ear ornaments made of fresh shoots (pravāla). His left hand rested gracefully like an embrace on the shoulder of a friend (anuvrata). This was a particular anubhāva which informed the women of his feelings. In his right hand he twirled a play lotus. He informed them, “By your love, you make my mind dizzy.” He had fickle locks of hair which spread over his cheeks. He wore water lilies in his ears. He had a smile.

### Text 23

*prāyaḥ-śruta-priyatamodaya-karṇa-pūrair*  
*yasmin nimagna-manasas tam athākṣi-randraiḥ*  
*antaḥ praveśya su-ciraṁ parirabhya tāpaṁ*  
*prājñaṁ yathābhimatayo vijahur narendra*

**Перевод:**

**O ruler of men, for a long time those brāhmaṇa ladies had made their ears successful by hearing about Kṛṣṇa and their minds were always absorbed in him. Through the apertures of their eyes they now forced him to enter within their hearts, and then they embraced him within for a long time. In this way they finally gave up the pain of separation from him, just as materialists give up the pain of the waking state on embracing Paramātmā in deep sleep.**

**Комментарий:**

Their minds were absorbed in Kṛṣṇa because of the ear ornaments (karṇa-pūraiḥ) consisting of the excellence of Nanda’s son heard many times. Now through the apertures of their eyes they brought him into the lotus of their hearts and gave up the pain of separationfrom him by embracing him tightly. An example is given. Persons who identify with ‘I’ and ‘mine’ in relation to body and house give up the pain of the waking state on attaining Paramātmā (prājñam) in deep sleep.

### Text 24

*tās tathā tyakta-sarvāśāḥ prāptā ātma-didṛkṣayā*  
*vijñāyākhila-dṛg-draṣṭā prāha prahasitānanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, who witnesses the thoughts of all creatures, understood how those ladies had abandoned all worldly hopes and come there simply to see him. Thus he addressed them as follows with a smile upon his face.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding that these women had brought plates of food to him and were fainting, the witness of everyone’s intelligence (dṛg-draṣṭā), with smiling face indicating his sweet cleverness in cheating, spoke.

### Text 25

*svāgataṁ vo mahā-bhāgā āsyatāṁ karavāma kim*  
*yan no didṛkṣayā prāptā upapannam idaṁ hi vaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] Welcome, O most fortunate ladies. Please sit down and make yourselves comfortable. What can I do for you? That you have come here to see me is most appropriate.**

**Комментарий:**

He spoke to them, who were full of great prema, like the gopīs. O fortunate women! I welcome you. You have come, desiring to see me, though scolded by husbands who are difficult to give up. It is proper that you have come. Sit down for a moment to see me. What can I do for you? Please instruct me. I will do that here. He uses the plural (naḥ, us) in forder to hide their attachment to him alone and to show indifference. The phrase “coming with a desire to see us” negates any other desires that may arise after seeing him.

### Text 26

*nanv addhā mayi kurvanti kuśalāḥ svārtha-darśinaḥ*  
*ahaituky avyavahitāṁ bhaktim ātma-priye yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Certainly expert personalities, who can see their own true interest, render unmotivated and uninterrupted devotional service directly unto me, just as materialists show affection for objects dear to them.**

**Комментарий:**

He clarifies the appropriateness of their coming. Those with discrimination (kuśalāḥ), who know what is best for themselves (svārtha-darśinaḥ), perform direct (addhā) bhakti to me, which isdevoid of seeking results (ahaitukī) and is constant (avyavahitām), just as materialists show affection for material bliss, which is dearto them (ātma-priye).

### Text 27

*prāṇa-buddhi-manaḥ-svātma-dārāpatya-dhanādayaḥ*  
*yat-samparkāt priyā āsaṁs tataḥ ko nv aparaḥ priyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**It is only by contact with me that one’s vital breath, intelligence, mind, friends, body, wife, children, wealth and so on are dear. Therefore what object can possibly be dearer than me?**

**Комментарий:**

A gross example was given to stimulate the intellect. Actually, I, full of bliss, am most dear since I am purer and unlimited than them. That is explained in this verse. Prāṇa, intelligence, mind, body (sva), jīva (ātmā), wife, children and wealth are dear because of relationship with me, because of remembrance of me (yat- samparkāt). I am dearest since I am the cause of dearness in prāṇa, etc.

### Text 28

*tad yāta deva-yajanaṁ patayo vo dvijātayaḥ*  
*sva-satraṁ pārayiṣyanti yuṣmābhir gṛha-medhinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You should thus return to the sacrificial arena, because your husbands, the learned brāhmaṇas, are householders and need your assistance to finish their sacrifices.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of attraction to me you are successful. Go to the place of sacrifice. “But why should the successful return?” Your husbands, householders, will complete the sacrifice with you, the cause of household-life. Assist your husbands. Since the sacrifices and other karmas are taught by me by the body of the Vedas, respecting my actions, go there. You will see me manifest there.

### Text 29

*śrī-patnya ūcuḥ*  
*maivaṁ vibho ’rhati bhavān gadituṁ nṛ-śaṁsaṁ*  
*satyaṁ kuruṣva nigamaṁ tava pada-mūlam*  
*prāptā vayaṁ tulasi-dāma padāvasṛṣṭaṁ*  
*keśair nivoḍhum atilaṅghya samasta-bandhūn*

**Перевод:**

**The wives of the brāhmaṇas replied: O almighty one, please do not speak such cruel words. Rather, you should fulfill your promise to us. Giving up all material relationships, we have attained your service, in order to carry upon our heads tulasī leaves fallen from your feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Like the gopīs, they speak. O Lord! You should not speak such hard- hearted words. Prove your own words, ye yathā māṁ prapadyante taṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham: I respond to persons according to how they surrender to me. (BG [4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11))

“How will you brāhmaṇa wives be fixed me?” Overcoming all friends, we have attained the soles of your feet. We do not have pride in our families.

“But where is your use?” Our service is to carry with our hair, tulasī leaves which have fallen at the base of your seat from your feet or from contact with your beloved’s feet when you embrace her and which given to us by mercy by them. Let us not have physical association with you, but let us, who live in the Vṛndāvana forest with Vana-devīs have just that much service. This is like Pulindawomen wearing the kuṅkuma (fallen from the Lord’s feet). Here they indicate Kṛṣṇa’s great powers by mentioning the tulasī leavesfalling from his feet and suggest that his service is what they desire.

The svarūpa of the jīva is being your servant on account of the jīva’s characteristics described in Padma Purāṇa:

*dāsa-bhūto harer eva nānyasyaiva kadācana*

**The jīva is always subordinate to Hari and no one else. (Padma Purāṇa)**

It is not improper to give up household-dharma by the following:

*sarva-dharmān parityajya māṁ ekaṁ saraṇam vraja*

Give up all dharmas and surrender only to me. (BG [18.66](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.66))

### Text 30

*gṛhṇanti no na patayaḥ pitarau sutā vā*  
*na bhrātṛ-bandhu-suhṛdaḥ kuta eva cānye*  
*tasmād bhavat-prapadayoḥ patitātmanāṁ no*  
*nānyā bhaved gatir arindama tad vidhehi*

**Перевод:**

**Our husbands, fathers, sons, brothers, other relatives and friends will no longer take us back, and how could anyone else be willing to give us shelter? Therefore, since we have surrendered to your lotus feet, we have no other shelter. Please, O chastiser of enemies, grant our desire.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, we have become attracted to you by hearing your attractive qualities from puberty. Therefore, our husbands will not accept us for enjoyment. We are wives for the sake of completing sacrifices. According to Pāṇini (4.1.33), patyur no yajña-saṁyoge: the definition of patnī is a wife, who takes part in the sacrifices of her husband.

We will not enjoy the results of the sacrifice performed by them because of no desire for those results. Fathers and others do not even want to talk to us. They criticize us saying, “They are crazy.” Suta means sons of cowives. What to speak of others who are neutral (anye)?

Remembering his words, “Go to the sacrifice,” (verse 28) the wives speak with agitation. Please arrange so that there is no object of surrender other than you for us who offering respects with eight limbs (patitātmanām) to the tips of your feet (prapadayoḥ), since we have given up our husbands. O destroyer of obstacles to attaining you (arindama)! O compassionate one!

### Text 31

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*patayo nābhyasūyeran pitṛ-bhrātṛ-sutādayaḥ*  
*lokāś ca vo mayopetā devā apy anumanvate*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord replied: Rest assured that your husbands will not find fault with you, nor will your fathers, brothers, sons, other relatives or the general populace, though you have closely associated with me. Even the devatās present in the sacrifice will recognize me as the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

“Ignoring our husbands, we came to you. They will not accept us. Rather, being angry, they will chastise us.” Seeing them who will say this, Kṛṣṇa speaks. Husbands and others will not hate you. They will not find fault in your good qualities of offering me food,speaking to me and seeing me. The devatās, being made to appear in the sacrifice by your husbands, will recognize you, permitted to leave by me. They will approve of what you did. You are my devotees. Even Indra will welcome you, what to speak of others.

### Text 32

*na prītaye ’nurāgāya hy aṅga-saṅgo nṛṇām iha*  
*tan mano mayi yuñjānā acirān mām avāpsyatha*

**Перевод:**

**For you to serve me directly in this life would certainly not please people in this world, what to speak of being attractive to them. Therefore, you should fix your minds on me, and very soon you will achieve me.**

**Комментарий:**

“But we cannot give you up.” In your birth as wives of brāhmaṇas (iha), physical association with me will not produce happiness and attraction of people. Therefore, concentrating your minds on me, go to your houses. Very soon you will attain me by in a different body. I, bound by morality, do not trespass the moral boundaries. You, my devotees should not act against me. You will attain me quickly in the future, with forms of gopīs.

### Text 33

*śravaṇād darśanād dhyānān mayi bhāvo ’nukīrtanāt*  
*na tathā sannikarṣeṇa pratiyāta tato gṛhān*

**Перевод:**

**It is by hearing about me, seeing my deity form, meditating upon me and chanting my names and glories that love for me develops, not by physical proximity. Therefore please go back to your homes.**

### Text 34

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*ity uktā dvija-patnyas tā yajña-vāṭaṁ punar gatāḥ*  
*te cānasūyavas tābhiḥ strībhiḥ satram apārayan*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus instructed, the wives of the brāhmaṇas returned to the place of sacrifice. The brāhmaṇas did not find any fault with their wives, and together with them they finished the sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

Having thus being spoken to, knowing the Lord’s love for them, they went to the place of sacrifice (yajña-vāṭam).

Vāṭam means place according to Medini. But the gopīs however, knowing his love, will remain (at the beginning of rāsa dance). Theway of prema follows the tendency in the lover’s heart.

### Text 35

*tatraikā vidhṛtā bhartrā bhagavantaṁ yathā-śrutam*  
*hṛḍopaguhya vijahau dehaṁ karmānubandhanam*

**Перевод:**

**One of the ladies had been forcibly kept back by her husband. When she heard the others describe Kṛṣṇa, she embraced him within her heart and gave up her material body, the basis of bondage to material activity, and attained her spiritual body.**

**Комментарий:**

He not only gave them just hope, rather he also would offer himself. An example is given. At the sacrificial grounds one left after all others and was thus held back by her husband. Embracing Nanda’s son within her heart of whom she had heard, she gave up herbody, caused by prārabdha-karma, burnt by the fire of separation. Immediately she became a young gopī and attained Kṛṣṇa, as istestified in ye yathā mām prapadyante: as they surrender to me, I respond. (BG [4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11))

### Text 36

*bhagavān api govindas tenaivānnena gopakān*  
*catur-vidhenāśayitvā svayaṁ ca bubhuje prabhuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Though he was the Supreme Lord, the cowherd Kṛṣṇa fed the cowherd boys with that food of four varieties and then personally partook of the preparations, showing mercy to the wives because he was capable of unlimited mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he was Bhagavān, he personally ate their food. What good fortune for the brāhmaṇas’ wives!

### Text 37

*evaṁ līlā-nara-vapur nṛ-lokam anuśīlayan*  
*reme go-gopa-gopīnāṁ ramayan rūpa-vāk-kṛtaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Thus, appearing like a human being to perform his pastimes, he taught devotion to himself to the human world. He enjoyed by pleasing his cows, cowherd boyfriends and cowherd girlfriends with his beauty, words and actions.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord, with human form predominated with pastimes enjoyed (reme), while giving enjoyment (ramayan) to the cows, boys andyoung gopīs, but not to the brāhmaṇa’s wives because there would not be excellence in pastimes by that. He did this by dressing as a dancer (rūpa), by sweet words (vāk) and by actions (kṛtaiḥ), following human actions of this world (nṛ-lokam anuśīlayan).

### Text 38

*athānusmṛtya viprās te anvatapyan kṛtāgasaḥ*  
*yad viśveśvarayor yācñām ahanma nṛ-viḍambayoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇas then came to their senses and began to feel great remorse. They thought, “We have sinned, for we have denied the request of the two Lords of the universe, who are engaged in spreading human pastimes.”**

**Комментарий:**

By seeing their wives, the brāhmaṇas felt remorse. Since we have denied the request of the lords of the universe, we have committed offense. They cheated (viḍambayoḥ) us humans (nṛ) by begging for food. Remembering the Lord, they repented.

### Text 39

*dṛṣṭvā strīṇāṁ bhagavati kṛṣṇe bhaktim alaukikīm*  
*ātmānaṁ ca tayā hīnam anutaptā vyagarhayan*

**Перевод:**

**Taking note of their wives’ pure, unworldly devotion for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, and seeing their own lack of devotion, the brāhmaṇas felt most sorrowful and began to condemn themselves.**

**Комментарий:**

They received their wives as if they were gurus. They criticized themselves as being devoid of bhakti. Their wives’ bhakti was impossible in the world (alaukikīm).

### Text 40

*dhig janma nas tri-vṛd yat tad*  
*dhig vrataṁ dhig bahu-jñatām*  
*dhik kulaṁ dhik kriyā-dākṣyaṁ*  
*vimukhā ye tv adhokṣaje*

**Перевод:**

**\[The brāhmaṇas said:\] To hell with our threefold birth, our vow of celibacy and our extensive learning! To hell with our aristocratic background and our expertise in the rituals of sacrifice! These are all condemned because we were inimical to the Lord who has appeared many times.**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇas said, “Our three births: 1) physical birth, 2) initiation as twice-born, and 3) initiation into the performance of Vedic sacrifice are all useless. Our vow of celibacy is useless. Our profound study of the meaning of the Vedas is useless. Our pure family lines, maternal and paternal, are useless. Our skill in performing rites like nitya and naimittika acts are useless. All are lamentable since we are inimical to the Lord. That by which Lord is satisfied is productive and everything else is useless.

### Text 41

*nūnaṁ bhagavato māyā yoginām api mohinī*  
*yad vayaṁ guravo nṛṇāṁ svārthe muhyāma he dvijāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The illusory potency of the Supreme Lord certainly bewilders even the great mystics, what to speak of us. As brāhmaṇas we are supposed to be the spiritual masters of all classes of men, yet we have been bewildered about our own real interest.**

**Комментарий:**

Definitely, the Lord’s māyā is the cause since (yat) we, brāhmaṇas, gurus of all humans, though teachers of tattva, do not know ourown interest.

### Text 42

*aho paśyata nārīṇām api kṛṣṇe jagad-gurau*  
*duranta-bhāvaṁ yo ‘vidhyan mṛtyu-pāśān gṛhābhidhān*

**Перевод:**

**Just see the unlimited love these women have developed for Kṛṣṇa, the spiritual master of the entire universe! This love has broken their bondage to death—their attachment to family life.**

**Комментарий:**

Aho indicates astonishment. See the love characterized by saying, “Kṛṣṇa” in choked voice, tears and hairs standing on end for Kṛṣṇa, love that we cannot understand (durantam), hard to attain, of these women who should not even be suitable for this. “But a women’s love for a man other than her husband is condemned.” It was for Kṛṣṇa, the guru for the whole world. By his order the wives considered their husbands their gurus. What need be considered when they had love for him directly. This love immediately (avidhyat) cut the ropes of death, called home. They have become our gurus because of destroying their attachment to house and husband.

### Texts 43-44

*nāsāṁ dvijāti-saṁskāro na nivāso gurāv api*  
*na tapo nātma-mīmāṁsā na śaucaṁ na kriyāḥ śubhāḥ*

*tathāpi hy uttamaḥ-śloke kṛṣṇe yogeśvareśvare*  
*bhaktir dṛḍhā na cāsmākaṁ saṁskārādimatām api*

**Перевод:**

**These women have never undergone the purificatory rites of the twice-born classes, nor have they lived as brahmacārīs in the āśrama of a spiritual master, nor have they executed austerities as vānaprasthas, or speculated on the nature of the self as sannyāsīs, followed the formalities of cleanliness or engaged in pious rituals. Nevertheless, they have firm devotion for Kṛṣṇa, whose glories are chanted by all and who is the supreme master of all devotes. We, on the other hand, have no such devotion for the Lord, although we have executed all these processes.**

**Комментарий:**

It is impossible to understand the cause of their attachment to Kṛṣṇa. They never had the saṁskāra of the twice-born such as receiving the sacred thread (upanāyana). They did not live with the guru and serve him, study scriptures (tapas), deliberate on the true nature of their ātmā (ātma-mīmāṁsā), bathe three times a day (śaucaṁ) or perform rituals like sandhyopāsana (śubhāḥ kriyāḥ). We on the other hand performed the saṁskāras, etc. By this, saṁskāras, etc., are denied to be the cause of bhakti by positive (themselves) and negative examples (their wives who did not perform these acts). The cause of their bhakti was association with women garland makers who went from Nandīśvara to Mathurā, who relaxing in the courtyard outside the houses, would sing the glories of Kṛṣṇa, since it said dīrgha-śruta-dhṛtāśayāḥ: they developed hope from hearing for a long time (verse 20). The husbands however did not know this and thus did not mention it.

### Text 45

*nanu svārtha-vimūḍhānāṁ pramattānāṁ gṛhehayā*  
*aho naḥ smārayāmāsa gopa-vākyaiḥ satāṁ gatiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Indeed, infatuated as we are with our household affairs, we have deviated completely from the real aim of our life. But the Lord, the shelter of the devotees, through the words of these simple cowherd boys, has made us remember him.**

**Комментарий:**

Where is the Lord’s kindness and where is our wickedness! By the words of the cowherd boys we remembered the form of the Lord.

### Text 46

*anyathā pūrṇa-kāmasya kaivalyādy-aśiṣāṁ pateḥ*  
*īśitavyaiḥ kim asmābhir īśasyaitad viḍambanam*

**Перевод:**

**What else could be his purpose? Since he is complete in his desires and fully capable of awarding all blessings including liberation and prema, what other purpose would he have in approaching us, since we are incapable of doing anything? Begging food was the Lord’s criticism of us.**

**Комментарий:**

If it is not his kindness, then what was the purpose of him, full in his desires, with us? Nothing at all. Thus the Lord’s begging us for food was just a criticism (viḍambanam) of us.

### Text 47

*hitvānyān bhajate yaṁ śrīḥ pāda-sparśāśayāsakṛt*  
*svātma-doṣāpavargeṇa tad-yācñā jana-mohinī*

**Перевод:**

**Hoping for the touch of his lotus feet, Lakṣmī perpetually serves only him, leaving aside all others without being touched by the faults of fickleness. In that condition, his begging for food makes us think he is not the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

One should not say that he begged food because of hunger, not to show mercy, and that he is not full in his desires since he herds cows.

Śrī, personification of wealth, serves him always, giving up Indra and others. By rejecting (apavargeṇa) her own fault of fickleness, she remains steady. Nanda gave two niyutas of cows as donation at Kṛṣṇa’s birth festival. His begging food bewilders people like us. It convinces us that he is not the Lord of all.

### Texts 48-49

*deśaḥ kālaḥ pṛthag dravyaṁ mantra-tantrartvijo‘ gnayaḥ*  
*devatā yajamānaś ca kratur dharmaś ca yan-mayaḥ*

*sa eva bhagavān sākṣād viṣṇur yogeśvareśvaraḥ*  
*jāto yaduṣv ity āśṛṇma hy api mūḍhā na vidmahe*

**Перевод:**

**The place, time, particular paraphernalia, mantras, rituals, priests, fires, devatās, performer, offering and the as yet unseen beneficial results—are all simply his by-products. Yet even though we had heard that he had appeared directly in the Yadu dynasty, showing all powers, spreading them everywhere to please his devotees, we were ignorant of the scriptural conclusion and did not recognize him.**

**Комментарий:**

They explain their bewilderment. Yan-mayaḥ means he pervades it all or it is all dependent on him. Though we heard about him, being ignorant, we do not know him.

### Text 50

*tasmai namo bhagavate kṛṣṇāyākuṇṭha-medhase*  
*yan-māyā-mohita-dhiyo bhramāmaḥ karma-vartmasu*

**Перевод:**

**Let us offer our obeisances unto Kṛṣṇa endowed with all powers, and possessing unfailing intelligence. Confused by his power of illusion, we repeatedly become absorbed in the path of karma.**

**Комментарий:**

Very disturbed by their committing offense they offer respects to the Lord.

### Text 51

*sa vai na ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ sva-māyā-mohitātmanām*  
*avijñatānubhāvānāṁ kṣantum arhaty atikramam*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, who is also the first puruṣa, should forgive us brāhmaṇas who were ignorant of his glory since we were bewildered by his māyā.**

**Комментарий:**

They ask Kṛṣṇa for forgiveness for their offense. Atikramam means offense.

### Text 52

*iti svāgham anusmṛtya kṛṣṇe te kṛta-helanāḥ*  
*didṛkṣavo vrajam atha kaṁsād bhītā na cācalan*

**Перевод:**

**Thus reflecting on the sin they had committed by neglecting Kṛṣṇa, they became very eager to see him. But being afraid of Kaṁsa, they did not take one step towards Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why did they not go to see Kṛṣṇa?” Having neglected Kṛṣṇa, they remembered their offense. Having developed fixed faith andbhakti from seeing their wives, though they desired to see the Lord, because they had not developed prema they did not go, since they feared Kaṁsa. Learning from spies that we are favorable to Kṛṣṇa, Kaṁsa will stop our maintenance. Thus, they remained in their houses and worshipped Kṛṣṇa. The wives did not consider this since they had developed prema, but the husbands made such considerations, since they had not developed prema.

## Chapter 24 - Worshiping Govardhana Hill

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*bhagavān api tatraiva baladevena saṁyutaḥ*  
*apaśyan nivasan gopān indra-yāga-kṛtodyamān*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: While staying near Govardhana with Baladeva, Kṛṣṇa watched the cowherd men busily arranging for a sacrifice to Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

*caturviṁśe vinirdhūya pūjām indrasya hetubhiḥ \|*  
*prāvartayat sva-bhaktasya giri-rājasya tāṁ hariḥ*

**In the twenty-fourth chapter the Lord rejects the worship Indra using logic and promotes the worship of Govardhana, his devotee.**

In the assembly, sitting with his brothers, Nanda ordered the cowherds to gather ingredients for worship of Indra. Staying there, the Lord also saw the cowherds preparing for the worship of Indra.

### Text 2

*tad-abhijño ’pi bhagavān sarvātmā sarva-darśanaḥ*  
*praśrayāvanato ’pṛcchad vṛddhān nanda-purogamān*

**Перевод:**

**Being the omniscient Supersoul, Kṛṣṇa, full of all good qualities, with his own purpose in mind, humbly inquired from the elders, headed by his father, Nanda Mahārāja.**

**Комментарий:**

Though knowing this was effort for worshipping Indra, from seeing it in previous years, and though he inspired them to do this, by being present in their bodies as their antaryāmī, bowing with humility he asked. He saw the whole future (sarva-darśanaḥ): deflating Indra’s pride and for seven days living with his dear associates. Being Bhagavān, eternally full of six opulences, he was capable of deflating Indra’s pride.

### Text 3

*kathyatāṁ me pitaḥ ko ’yaṁ sambhramo va upāgataḥ*  
*kiṁ phalaṁ kasya voddeśaḥ kena vā sādhyate makhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] My dear father, kindly explain to me your flurry of activity which is being done so close at hand. What is it meant to accomplish? Who is it for? How and by whom will it be executed?**

**Комментарий:**

A sacrifice is going to take place. This great preparation (sambhramaḥ) is for accomplishing that sacrifice. What is the result of this? Who is it for? Which devatā is it meant to be worshiped? By whom or by what means is it accomplished?

### Text 4-5

*etad brūhi mahān kāmo mahyaṁ śuśrūṣave pitaḥ*  
*na hi gopyaṁ hi sādhūnāṁ kṛtyaṁ sarvātmanām iha*  
*asty asva-para-dṛṣṭīnām amitrodāsta-vidviṣām*  
*udāsīno ’ri-vad varjya ātma-vat suhṛd ucyate*

**Перевод:**

**Please tell me about it, O father. I have a great desire to know. Certainly, no secrets are to be kept by saintly personalities, who see Paramātmā everywhere in the universe, who have no conception of “mine” or “another’s” and who do not consider who is a friend, who is an enemy and who is neutral. One who is neutral may be avoided like an enemy, but a friend should be considered like one’s own self.**

**Комментарий:**

“You are a boy. Play with your friends. Why do you ask this question?” This is my great desire. Therefore, tell me as I am eager to hear. It will please me. “As it is secret, it should not be spoken to a child.” He then showing his wisdom by his colorful statement, speaks. One who thinks of all beings (sarvātmanaḥ) and thus who do not see his relatives as intimate, they have no friends, neutralparties or enemies. Such saintly persons have no secret activities in this world.

“Though we are saintly persons, because we are householders, we cannot reveal secrets.”

The neutral person should be avoided like an enemy. The neutral person has qualities similar to the enemy because of having desire to harm by being the enemy’s friend but he does not harm.

*yo vipakṣa-suhṛt-pakṣaḥ sa taṭastha ihocyate*

**The group which is friendly with the opposing group is called borderline. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 9.7)**

The neutral person is not on either side. He is not avoided but is not accepted. One should however accept the friend as oneself. Since I am your son, keeping secrets from me is not suitable.

### Text 6

*jñatvājñātvā ca karmāṇi jano ’yam anutiṣṭhati*  
*viduṣaḥ karma-siddhiḥ syād yathā nāviduṣo bhavet*

**Перевод:**

**When people in this world perform activities like sacrifice or agriculture, sometimes they understand present and future results and sometimes they do not. Those who know achieve success in their work, and accordingly, ignorant people do not.**

**Комментарий:**

Deliberating with friends, a person understands and performs karmas. Others however, not deliberating, do not understand andperform karmas. Just as the person in knowledge attains success in his karmas the ignorant person does not. Thus, one must deliberate with friends.

### Text 7

*tatra tāvat kriyā-yogo bhavatāṁ kiṁ vicāritaḥ*  
*atha vā laukikas tan me pṛcchataḥ sādhu bhaṇyatām*

**Перевод:**

**In these actions, have you considered the future results with scriptural proofs or is it merely a local custom? You should clearly explain this to me, since I am asking.**

**Комментарий:**

Has this work of yours been deliberated according to scriptures or has it been attained by family custom? Tell me, your son, withproofs (sādhu).

### Text 8

*śrī-nanda uvāca*  
*parjanyo bhagavān indro meghās tasyātma-mūrtayaḥ*  
*te ’bhivarṣanti bhūtānāṁ prīṇanaṁ jīvanaṁ payaḥ*

**Перевод:**
