**Nanda Mahārāja replied: Indra is the controller of the rain. The clouds are his personal representatives, and they directly provide rainwater, which gives happiness and sustenance to all creatures.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda explains with reasoning that the ceremony is from family tradition. Parjanya means one who sprinkles (pṛṣ). The clouds are Indra’s form, equal to himself. They shower water which satisfies (prīṇanam) all beings and makes dried up plants grow (jīvanam).

### Text 9

*taṁ tāta vayam anye ca vārmucāṁ patim īśvaram*  
*dravyais tad-retasā siddhair yajante kratubhir narāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Not only we, my dear son, but also many other men worship him, the lord and master of the rain-giving clouds. We offer him grain and other paraphernalia of worship produced through his rain.**

**Комментарий:**

We and others worship Indra, lord (patim) of the clouds (vār- mucām). We and others worship by sacrifices with materials produced from rain.

### Text 10

*tac-cheṣeṇopajīvanti tri-varga-phala-hetave*  
*puṁsāṁ puruṣa-kārāṇāṁ parjanyaḥ phala-bhāvanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**By accepting the remnants of sacrifices performed to Indra, people sustain their lives and accomplish the threefold aims of religiosity, economic development and sense gratification. Thus Indra is the agent responsible for the success of people’s efforts.**

**Комментарий:**

By food which is remnants of sacrifice to him (tac-cheṣeṇa), men maintain their lives, and not for living for sense enjoyment as they desire, but for accomplishing dharma, artha, and kāma. “They maintain themselves by farming. What is the use of Indra?” Indra is the producer (bhāvanaḥ) of tri-vargas (phalam), which is the result of efforts undertaken for their (i.e. trivargas’) sake (puruṣa- kārānām) for men. From Indra comes rain. From rain comes food and from food comes life. From life comes dharma. Thus, since Indra is the root cause, he should be worshipped.

### Text 11

*ya enaṁ visṛjed dharma paramparyāgataṁ naraḥ*  
*kāmād dveṣād bhayāl lobhāt sa vai nāpnoti śobhanam*

**Перевод:**

**Anyone who rejects this religious principle which is based on sound tradition out of lust, enmity, fear or greed will certainly fail to achieve good fortune.**

**Комментарий:**

The fault of doing the opposite is explained. One who rejects this dharma out of personal desire (kāmād), because of fearful persons(bhayāt), hatred towards devatās (dveṣād), or thinking that by spending he will be lacking (lobhāt), does not attain good fortune.

### Text 12

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*vaco niśamya nandasya tathānyeṣāṁ vrajaukasām*  
*indrāya manyuṁ janayan pitaraṁ prāha keśavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When Keśava heard the statements of his father, Nanda, and other senior residents of Vraja, he addressed his father as follows, to arouse anger in Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

He produced anger in Indra in order to remove his pride. Even though Indra, like Agni, is created by the Lord, was a devatādescribed in the Vedas, and was given a share in sacrifices by the Lord, still because Indra manifested pride, Kṛṣṇa disrespected him to purify him by removing the pride, because Kṛṣṇa is Svayaṁ Bhagavān, later it is said śakra-darpa-jighāṁsayā: Kṛṣṇa desired to destroy Indra’s pride. (verse 31) He also disrespected Indra to have yearly celebration of Govardhana, his best devotee.

### Text 13

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*karmaṇā jāyate jantuḥ karmaṇaiva pramīyate*  
*sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ bhayaṁ kṣemaṁ karmaṇaivābhipadyate*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa said: It is by the force of karma that a living entity takes birth, and it is by karma alone that he meets his destruction. His happiness, distress, fear and sense of security all arise as the effects of karma.**

**Комментарий:**

The Supreme Lord, personification of the Vedas, the son of Nanda, internally accepting the devatās described in the Vedas, begins to reject by karma-vāda Indra devatā described by his father. Karma- vādīs disrespect the devatās in this way. Yathākārī yathācārī tathābhavati: as one acts according to scripture and as one conducts (ācārī) oneself in general, one takes birth. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad [4.4.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bau/4.4.5)) One should not object, “How can material actions be agents of production, etc.?” since one sees that there is agency even in matter. Water flows and trees fructify.

### Text 14

*asti ced īśvaraḥ kaścit phala-rūpy anya-karmaṇām*  
*kartāraṁ bhajate so ’pi na hy akartuḥ prabhur hi saḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Even if there is some supreme controller who awards all others the results of their activities, he must also depend upon a performer’s engaging in activity since it is not possible to give results without the performer.**

**Комментарий:**

Some think that devatās give results. The karma-vādīs reject them in this way. If there is an īśvara who gives results for our actions, he also is dependent on action and thus responds to the performer of actions since (hi) the master does not give results for actions which are not performed. Otherwise there would be the fault of inequality. In this way when results arise by karma alone, what is the need of a useless devatā? They say, “But the devatā-kāṇḍa exists in order to urge those who lack faith in the independence of karmas, to perform karmas on the pretext that devatās are independent, just as jñāna-kāṇḍa does (i.e. urges one to perform jñāna) by revealing the svarūpa of the sacrificer (as ātmā).”

### Text 15

*kim indreṇeha bhūtānāṁ sva-sva-karmānuvartinām*  
*anīśenānyathā kartuṁ svabhāva-vihitaṁ nṛṇām*

**Перевод:**

**Living beings in this world are forced to experience the consequences of their own particular actions. What can useless Indra do to change the natures of humans?**

**Комментарий:**

“Let the devatā not be the giver of results, but the devatā should be accepted for inspiring (performance of karmas).” What is the use of Indra who is powerless to alter karma, which is ordained by ancient saṁskāras (svabhāva) called śīla, of men who follow their individual karmas. He can do nothing. Svabhāva means śīla or nature according to Dhanañjaya. Living beings are inspired to subsequent actions because of previous saṁskāras. From that there is karma and from that the results. What is the use of saying that conscious devatās inspire for material actions?

### Text 16

*svabhāva-tantro hi janaḥ svabhāvam anuvartate*  
*svabhāva-stham idaṁ sarvaṁ sa-devāsura-mānuṣam*

**Перевод:**

**Every individual is under the control of his own conditioned nature, and thus he must follow that nature. This entire universe, with all its devatās, demons and human beings, is based on the conditioned nature of the living entities.**

**Комментарий:**

This is further described. Since the inclination to act dependence on previous saṁskāras, acceptance of devatās is nor approved.

### Text 17

*dehān uccāvacāñ jantuḥ prāpyotsṛjati karmaṇā*  
*śatrur mitram udāsīnaḥ karmaiva gurur īśvaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because it is action that causes the conditioned living entity to accept and then give up different high-and low-grade material bodies, action (karma) is his enemy, friend and neutral witness, his teacher and controlling lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Because all goals are achieved by karmas arising from saṁskāras, karma should be performed with high respect. High and low bodies all depend on karma.

### Text 18

*tasmāt sampūjayet karma svabhāva-sthaḥ sva-karma-kṛt*  
*anjasā yena varteta tad evāsya hi daivatam*

**Перевод:**

**Because action is the teacher and controller, situated in one’s nature, one spontaneously acts. Therefore one should worship work itself, since that by which one can live comfortably is one’s deity.**

**Комментарий:**

Being situated in varṇa such as brāhmaṇa (svabhāva-sthaḥ), performing one’s prescribed karmas (sva-karma-kṛt), a person should accept (sampūjayet) karmas and not devatās. “Since karmas like sacrifices consist of reliquishing objects as in relation to devatās,how can those karmas be accomplished without the devatās?” People live (varteta) easily by karmas such as begging, conquering or farming. That is one’s devatā. No other devatā than this is seen. Since it was previously stated that karma is guru and the Lord (verse 17), acceptance of devatās such as Indra is the svarūpa of karma for the ignorant.

### Text 19

*ājīvyaikataraṁ bhāvaṁ yas tv anyam upajīvati*  
*na tasmād vindate kṣemaṁ jārān nāry asatī yathā*

**Перевод:**

**If one thing is actually sustaining our life but we take shelter of something else, how can we achieve any real benefit? We would be like an unfaithful woman, who can never achieve any actual benefit by consorting with her paramour.**

**Комментарий:**

The karma-vādīs will say that it is a fault to take shelter of devatās and perform karmas for maintaining one’s life. Taking support(bhāvam) of a means of living, the person who takes shelter of another means such as Indra does not achieve benefit because of ingratitude.

### Text 20

*varteta brahmaṇā vipro rājanyo rakṣayā bhuvaḥ*  
*vaiśyas tu vārtayā jīvec chūdras tu dvija-sevayā*

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa maintains his life by studying and teaching the Vedas, the member of the royal order by protecting the earth, the vaiśya by trade, and the śūdra by serving the higher, twice-born classes.**

**Комментарий:**

People accept occupations as a means of living. The brāhmaṇa (vipraḥ) subsists by teaching and studying the Veda (brahmaṇā).

### Text 21

*kṛṣi-vāṇijya-go-rakṣā kusīdaṁ tūryam ucyate*  
*vārtā catur-vidhā tatra vayaṁ go-vṛttayo ’niśam*

**Перевод:**

**The occupational duties of the vaiśya are conceived in four divisions: farming, commerce, cow protection and lending money. Out of these, we are always engaged in cow protection.**

**Комментарий:**

The different occupations within the vaiśya varṇa are described. There are said to be four occupations of the vaiśya: farming, trading,cow protection and money lending. Among them we have the occupation of protecting cows since we are vaiśyas. This is constant(aniśam) since even in difficult circumstances we do not take to agriculture, etc. In this way even karma-vādīs state that protecting cows is our occupation. Thus what is the use of Indra? The devatā accepted by Nanda is disregarded by the karma-vādīs in this way.

### Text 22

*sattvaṁ rajas tama iti sthity-utpatty-anta-hetavaḥ*  
*rajasotpadyate viśvam anyonyaṁ vividhaṁ jagat*

**Перевод:**

**The causes of creation, maintenance and destruction are the three modes of nature—namely goodness, passion and ignorance. In particular, the mode of passion creates this universe and through sexual combination causes it to become full of variety.**

**Комментарий:**

His father says, “Protecting cows is dependent on Indra.” This is rejected by followers of Sāṅkhya in two verses. Anyonyam means by union of woman and man.

### Text 23

*rajasā coditā meghā varṣanty ambūni sarvataḥ*  
*prajās tair eva sidhyanti mahendraḥ kiṁ kariṣyati*

**Перевод:**

**Impelled by the material mode of passion, the clouds pour down their rain everywhere, and by this rain all creatures gain their sustenance. What has the great Indra to do with this arrangement?**

**Комментарий:**

Since it seen that clouds sprinkle water everywhere (sarvataḥ), even on the ocean, rockes and desert, the rains are not connected with intelligence (since if there was intelligence they would rain only where Indra is worshipped). Creatures live (sidhyanti) by the clouds (taiḥ). The explanation of Nanda that Indra worship is necessary for maintaining life is wrong since it is refuted by scholars of Kapila’s school and karmīs.

### Text 24

*na naḥ puro janapadā na grāmā na gṛhā vayam*  
*vanaukasas tāta nityaṁ vana-śaila-nivāsinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear father, our home is not in the cities, villages or permanent houses. Being forest dwellers, we always live in the forest and on the hills.**

**Комментарий:**

“O child! May you live long! Why do you, son of a devotee, form of the Vedas, Svayaṁ Bhagavān, promote karma-vāda and pradhāna- vāda, contrary to the Vedas when the great sage Vyāsa has refuted these in Brahma-sūtras? Thus you should accept the devatās described in the Vedas, who are created by the Lord and give a share of sacrifice.”

No, I accept these atheistic philosophies. But giving up a devatā who give direct results, some other invisible devatā, accepted by father is refused by these philosophies.

“Okay, you specify that devatā who gives direct results.” That devatā approved by me is this Govardhana. That is explained in this verse.

Our cities in Bṛhadvana and Nandīśvara, towns connected to them, as ornaments on both the banks of the Yamunā, villages existing there and houses within the villages are not for our livelihood. We do not live by their taxes but we accept the folded hands of their residents as tax. Our citizens live happily. O father! We are always forest dwellers since we are situated generally in the forests of Govardhana for herding cows. We live there because of Govardhana which is decorated with desire trees, with forests and hills filled with gems and by them provides all desired objects. We like how others live happily in the cities. This mountain is our devatā since it supplies everything and protects us. We partake of the attractive flowers, etc., it offers and taking shelter of it, we conquer enemies. Hoarding for unexpected events is foolish since it will be against the description that Nanda is the king of Vraja, that various instruments, chariots, gems, gold ornaments, kuṅkuma and ointments were described and that in Vraja there was all prosperity. Also since in Brahma-saṁhitā it is stated cintāmaṇi- prakara-sadmasu: the houses are made of cintāmaṇi.

### Text 25

*tasmād gavāṁ brāhmaṇānām adreś cārabhyatāṁ makhaḥ*  
*ya indra-yāga-sambhārās tair ayaṁ sādhyatāṁ makhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore may a sacrifice for the pleasure of the cows, the brāhmaṇas and Govardhana Hill begin! With all the paraphernalia collected for worshiping Indra, let this sacrifice be performed instead.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa explains the devatās approved by him. Fruit, milk and wealth of cows with blessings, grass, water, attractive flowers and fruits should be used. It is not that this sacrifice described by me should use separate articles. Sambārāḥ means ingredients.

### Text 26

*pacyantāṁ vividhāḥ pākāḥ sūpāntāḥ pāyasādayaḥ*  
*saṁyāvāpūpa-śaṣkulyaḥ sarva-dohaś ca gṛhyatām*

**Перевод:**

**Let many different kinds of food be cooked, from sweet rice to vegetable soups! Many kinds of fancy cakes, both baked and fried, should be prepared. And all the available milk products should be taken for this sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

Rice and vegetables (pākāḥ) should be cooked. Dhal (sūpa) should be cooked in the end and rice cooked in pure milk (pāyasa) shouldbe cooked in the beginning, since dhal needs to be hot and milk- rice cool. Saṁyāvāḥ refers to preparations made of wheat flour.Sarva-doha refers to products of milk of all people of Vraja such as milk and yogurt.

### Text 27

*hūyantām agnayaḥ samyag brāhmaṇair brahma-vādibhiḥ*  
*annaṁ bahu-guṇaṁ tebhyo deyaṁ vo dhenu-dakṣiṇāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇas who are learned in the Vedic mantras must properly invoke the sacrificial fires. Then you should feed the priests with nicely prepared food and reward them with cows and other gifts.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks to produce faith and for the magnificence of the sacrifice. Gifts with cows should be given by you.

### Text 28

*anyebhyaś cā śva-cāṇḍāla-patitebhyo yathārhataḥ*  
*yavasaṁ ca gavāṁ dattvā giraye dīyatāṁ baliḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After giving the appropriate food to others, including fallen souls such as dogs and dog-eaters, you should give grass to the cows and then present your respectful offerings to Govardhana Hill.**

**Комментарий:**

In his opinion after favoring the brāhmaṇas, all others living in Vraja should be satisfied. Since it is said, annasya kṣudhitaḥ pātram: one should give food to the hungry, it should not be given to Indra. You should give grass (yavasam) to the cows. Offering (baliḥ) of scents, flowers, etc., should be given to Govardhana.

### Text 29

*sv-alaṅkṛtā bhuktavantaḥ sv-anuliptāḥ su-vāsasaḥ*  
*pradakṣiṇāṁ ca kuruta go-viprānala-parvatān*

**Перевод:**

**After everyone has eaten to his satisfaction, you should all dress and decorate yourselves handsomely, smear your bodies with sandalwood paste and then circumambulate the cows, the brāhmaṇas, the sacrificial fires and Govardhana Hill.**

**Комментарий:**

Decoration is described.

### Text 30

*etan mama mataṁ tāta kriyatāṁ yadi rocate*  
*ayaṁ go-brāhmaṇādrīṇāṁ mahyaṁ ca dayito makhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**This is my idea, O father, and you may carry it out if it appeals to you. Such a sacrifice to the cows, the brāhmaṇas and Govardhana Hill will be very beneficial for me.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks so that everyone agrees. The sacrifice is beneficial for me.

### Text 31

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*kālātmanā bhagavatā śakra-darpa-jighāṁsayā*  
*proktaṁ niśamya nandādyāḥ sādhv agṛhṇanta tad-vacaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Kṛṣṇa, who is himself powerful time, desired to destroy the false pride of Indra. When Nanda and the other senior men of Vṛndāvana heard Kṛṣṇa’s statement, they accepted his words as proper.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was the destroyer of Indra’s sacrifice (kālātmanā).

### Texts 32-33

*tathā ca vyadadhuḥ sarvaṁ yathāha madhusūdanaḥ*  
*vācayitvā svasty-ayanaṁ tad-dravyeṇa giri-dvijān*

*upahṛtya balīn samyag ādṛtā yavasaṁ gavām*  
*go-dhanāni puraskṛtya giriṁ cakruḥ pradakṣiṇam*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd community then did all that Madhusūdana had suggested. They arranged for the brāhmaṇas to recite the auspicious Vedic mantras, and using the paraphernalia that had been intended for Indra’s sacrifice, they presented offerings to Govardhana Hill and the brāhmaṇas and were respected by Kṛṣṇa. They also gave grass to the cows. Then, placing the cows, bulls and calves in front of them, they circumambulated Govardhana.**

**Комментарий:**

They gave to the mountain and the brāhmaṇas using the ingredients of Indra’s sacrifice (tad-dravyena). They were respected (ādṛtāḥ) by Kṛṣṇa. They gave grass to the cows.

### Text 34

*anāṁsy anaḍud-yuktāni te cāruhya sv-alaṅkṛtāḥ*  
*gopyaś ca kṛṣṇa-vīryāṇi gāyantyaḥ sa-dvijāśiṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As the beautifully ornamented cowherd ladies followed along, riding on wagons drawn by oxen, they sang the glories of Kṛṣṇa, and their songs mingled with the brāhmaṇas’ chanting of benedictions.**

**Комментарий:**

Mounting chariots yoked to oxen, the cowherds headed by Nanda and the women headed by Yaśodā, having blessing of brāhmaṇas(sa-dvijāśiṣaḥ), circumambulated Govardhana.

### Text 35

*kṛṣṇas tv anyatamaṁ rūpaṁ gopa-viśrambhaṇaṁ gataḥ*  
*śailo ’smīti bruvan bhūri balim ādad bṛhad-vapuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then assumed an unprecedented, huge form to instill faith in the cowherd men. Declaring, “I am Govardhana Mountain!” he ate the abundant offerings.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa showed the devatā of Govardhana that they worshipped to instill faith in people concerning the sacrifice he had described. In the center of the people of Vraja, Kṛṣṇa manifested an excellent form on top of Govardhana. It was a huge body, like a mountain, most excellent with attractive eyes and ears, a thousand arms and most effulgent, and in whom the cowherds had faith that it is a mountain. “I am the mountain, king of this place. Pleased with your worship, choose what you desire from me.” He ate all the many offerings that they gave.

### Texts 36-37

*tasmai namo vraja-janaiḥ saha cakra ’tmanātmane*  
*aho paśyata śailo ’sau rūpī no ’nugrahaṁ vyadhāt*

*eṣo ’vajānato martyān kāma-rūpī vanaukasaḥ*  
*hanti hy asmai namasyāmaḥ śarmaṇe ātmano gavām*

**Перевод:**

**Together with the people of Vraja, the Lord bowed down to this form of Govardhana Hill, thus in effect offering obeisances to himself. Then he said, “Just see how this hill has appeared in person and bestowed mercy upon us! This Govardhana Hill, assuming any form he wishes, will kill any residents of the forest who neglect him. Therefore let us pay our obeisances to him for the safety of ourselves and our cows.”**

**Комментарий:**

He offered respects to himself, the form of the mountain (ātmane), with the people of Vraja, using his body (ātmanā). The long ā at the beginning of ātmanā is elided as in the case of gūḍhotma due to being pṛṣodarādi (a class of words formed irregularly).

Oh! See this hill which has manifested the form of devatā (rūpī). Govardhana assuming the forms of snakes, etc., (kāma-rūpī) will kill those who disrespect him. Let us offer respects for the auspiciousness (śarmane) of ourselves and the cows.

### Text 38

*ity adri-go-dvija-makhaṁ vāsudeva-pracoditāḥ*  
*yathā vidhāya te gopā saha-kṛṣṇā vrajaṁ yayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The members of the cowherd community, having thus been inspired by Vāsudeva to properly execute the sacrifice to Govardhana Hill, the cows and the brāhmaṇas, returned with Kṛṣṇa to their village, Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

The people, along with Kṛṣṇa, went to the capital, Nandīśvara (vrajam).

## Chapter 25 - Lord Kṛṣṇa Lifts Govardhana Hill

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*indras tadātmanaḥ pūjāṁ vijñāya vihatāṁ nṛpa*  
*gopebhyaḥ kṛṣṇa-nāthebhyo nandādibhyaś cukopa ha*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King Parīkṣit, when Indra understood that his sacrifice had been diverted, he became furious with Nanda Mahārāja and the other cowherd men, who were accepting Kṛṣṇa as their Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

*pañca-viṁśe’tikopena śakre nāśāya varṣati \|*  
*gokulasyākarod rakṣāṁ girim uddhṛtya keśavaḥ*

**In the twenty-fifth chapter Kṛṣṇa, holding up the mountain, protected Gokula when Indra poured rain to destroy the place out of anger.**

Indra became angry at those who had accepted Kṛṣṇa as the Lord. This shows his foolishness and futility of his anger.

### Text 2

*gaṇaṁ sāṁvartakaṁ nāma meghānāṁ cānta-kārīṇām*  
*indraḥ pracodayat kruddho vākyaṁ cāheśa-māny uta*

**Перевод:**

**Angry Indra sent forth the clouds of universal destruction, known as Sāṁvartaka. Imagining himself to be the supreme controller, he spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

His anger is described. Sāmvartakam were those clouds used at pralaya. The word ca indicates other clouds like āvaha and pravahawinds as well. Indra thought that he was the supreme controller (īśa-mānī).

### Text 3

*aho śrī-mada-māhātmyaṁ gopānāṁ kānanaukasām*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ martyam upāśritya ye cakrur deva-helanam*

**Перевод:**

**\[Indra said:\] Just see how these cowherd men living in the forest have become so greatly intoxicated by their prosperity! They have surrendered to an ordinary human being, Kṛṣṇa, and thus they have offended the gods.**

**Комментарий:**

Such self-importance (māhātmyam) of these forest dwellers due to pride in wealth (śrī-mada)! They do not even live in a fort. They have taken shelter of a human, Kṛṣṇa and have disregarded me, Indra, king of the devatās by stopping my worship. But the Goddess of speech reveals the following meaning. What beauty (śrī), joy (mada) and glory worshipped by Brahmā and others (māhātyaṁ) inthe residents of Vṛndāvana, the Lord’s body! Śrī-mada-māhātmyaṁ is a dual compound in singular. They surrendered to Kṛṣṇa, theform of eternity, knowledge and bliss, who is Parabrahman who performs human pastimes for the benefit of humans (matryam).Martyam is formed by the suffix yat applied in the sense of tasmai hitaṁ (for the benefit of that). They have disrespected me, his son.

### Text 4

*yathādṛḍhaiḥ karma-mayaiḥ kratubhir nāma-nau-nibhaiḥ*  
*vidyām ānvīkṣikīṁ hitvā titīrṣanti bhavārṇavam*

**Перевод:**

**Their taking shelter of Kṛṣṇa is just like the foolish attempt of men who abandon knowledge of the self and instead try to cross over the great ocean of material existence in the false boats of ritual sacrifices.**

**Комментарий:**

Foolish people, giving up knowledge of Brahman and ātmā, desire to cross the ocean of saṁsāra by the apparent boat named sacrifices, which are full of karma alone (karma-mayaiḥ), which are powerless (adṛḍhaiḥ), though they cannot actually cross by this means. Anvīkṣa means to constantly contemplate Upaniṣads. Arising from that is ānvīkṣikī. It means brahmātma-vidyā. Similarly, giving me up, they desire prosperity by Kṛṣṇa.

But the Goddess of speech reveals the following meaning. Intelligent people, giving up knowledge that seeks out tvam-padārtha(ānvīkṣikīm) along with giving up sacrifices, though purifiying the heart, taking shelter of Kṛṣṇa, desire to cross the ocean of saṁsāra.

*pibanti ye bhagavata ātmanaḥ satāṁ*  
*kathāmṛtaṁ śravaṇa-puṭeṣu sambhṛtam*  
*punanti te viṣaya-vidūṣitāśayaṁ*  
*vrajanti tac-caraṇa-saroruhāntikam*

**Those who drink through aural reception, fully filled with the nectarean message of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the beloved of the devotees, purify the polluted aim of life known as material enjoyment and thus go back to Godhead, to the lotus feet of the Lord. (SB** [**2.2.37**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.37)**)**

### Text 5

*vācālaṁ bāliśaṁ stabdham ajñaṁ paṇḍita-māninam*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ martyam upāśritya gopā me cakrur apriyam*

**Перевод:**

**These cowherd men have acted inimically toward me by taking shelter of this ordinary human being, Kṛṣṇa, who thinks himself very wise but who is simply a foolish, arrogant, talkative child.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks profusely contrary to mīmāṁsā scriptures (vācālam). Vācāla means a gossiper according to Amara-kośa. He is a fool because of not studying those scriptures (bāliśam). Bāliśam means a fool according to Viśva-kośa.

He is stabdha (poorly cultured) because he speaks boldly even in the presence of his own father. He knows nothing at all (ajñaṁ),since he constantly herds cows. Still he thinks himself a learned man (paṇḍita-māninam). He is just a human being (martyam). Taking shelter of this Kṛṣṇa, they have offended me, king of the devatās (apriyam cakruḥ).

But Sarasvatī devī suggests another meaning. Due to him even children like Dhruva (bāliśaṁ) are ornamented with skillful words (vācālam). He does not bow down to others (stabdham) because he is the lord of everyone.

*vṛkṣa iva stabdho divi tiṣṭhaty ekas*  
*tenedaṁ pūrṇaṁ puruṣeṇa sarvam*

**He alone stands firm in the sky like a tree. The universe is pervaded by this person. (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad 13)**

He is omniscient (ajñam). The nirukti says, na jño yasmād, there is no one more learned than him. The śruti says, yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit: the Lord is omniscient. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) His worship takes place among the learned (paṇḍita-māninam). He is worshippable for all.

*yaṁ sarve devā namanti mumukṣavo brahmavādinaś ca*

**All the devatās, persons desiring liberation and persons established in Brahman, offer respects to the Lord. (Nṛsiṁha-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

Kṛṣṇa is the form of eternity, knowledge and bliss. He is Parabrahman, performing human pastimes.

### Text 6

*eṣāṁ śriyāvaliptānāṁ kṛṣṇenādhmāpitātmanām*  
*dhunuta śrī-mada-stambhaṁ paśūn nayata saṅkṣayam*

**Перевод:**

**\[To the clouds of destruction King Indra said:\] The prosperity of these people has made them mad with pride since they have become bold because of Kṛṣṇa. Now go and remove their pride and bring their animals to destruction.**

**Комментарий:**

They are proud (avaliptānām) because of wealth since their minds are enflamed by Kṛṣṇa (dhmāpitātnanām). The rest is clear in meaning.

But Sarasvatī devī reveals the following meaning. Their limbs are anointed with catuḥsama pulp (śrīyā). They have glorious wealth since they follow scriptures.

Remove their glorious activeness. Now they are thoroughly active because of the heat with no cold. Make them immovable (stambham) with cold by adequate rain, by which the heat will be destroyed.

When the Lord holds up Govardhana, bring the cows to live at the base of Govardhana which gives happiness (saṅkṣayam nayata). Become the cause of their residence at the base of Govardhan.

### Text 7

*ahaṁ cairāvataṁ nāgam āruhyānuvraje vrajam*  
*marud-gaṇair mahā-vegair nanda-goṣṭha-jighāṁsayā*

**Перевод:**

**I will follow you to Vraja, riding on my elephant Airāvata and taking with me the swift and powerful wind-gods to with a desire to decimate the cowherd village of Nanda Mahārāja.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks to the clouds who are frightened. I will follow you with a host of devatās. Marut means devatās according to Amara-kośa.Nanda-goṣṭha-jighāṁsayā can mean “with a desire to go to Nanda’s place.” This is revealed by Sarasvatī devī.

### Text 8

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*itthaṁ maghavatājñaptā meghā nirmukta-bandhanāḥ*  
*nanda-gokulam āsāraiḥ pīḍayām āsur ojasā*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: On Indra’s order the clouds of universal destruction which were released untimely from their bonds went to the cowherd pastures of Nanda Mahārāja. There they began to torment the inhabitants by powerfully pouring torrents of rain upon them.**

**Комментарий:**

The clouds were released from bondage. They are normally released to make everything one ocean at the time of destruction. Now they were released by Indra who was angry and not discerning the truth. The clouds went to Nanda’s village and not to Mathurā.

### Text 9

*vidyotamānā vidyudbhiḥ stanantaḥ stanayitnubhiḥ*  
*tīvrair marud-gaṇair nunnā vavṛṣur jala-śarkarāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Propelled by the fearsome wind-gods, the clouds, blazing with intense lightning bolts and roaring with intense thunder, showered down water and hailstones.**

**Комментарий:**

The clouds rumbled with thunder and lightning, pushed by the winds like āvaha and pravaha. They showered hail (jala-śarkarāḥ).

### Text 10

*sthūṇā-sthūlā varṣa-dhārā muñcatsv abhreṣv abhīkṣṇaśaḥ*  
*jalaughaiḥ plāvyamānā bhūr nādṛśyata natonnatam*

**Перевод:**

**As the clouds released torrents of rain as thick as massive columns, the earth was submerged in the flood, and high ground could no longer be distinguished from low.**

**Комментарий:**

The clouds poured down torrents of rain in sheets as thick as pillars of a house (sthūṇā). When the clouds released rain, the earth became flooded and high and low regions could not be seen.

### Text 11

*aty-āsārāti-vātena paśavo jāta-vepanāḥ*  
*gopā gopyaś ca śītārtā govindaṁ śaraṇaṁ yayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cows and other animals, shivering from the excessive rain and wind, and the cowherd men and women, pained by the cold, all approached Govinda for shelter.**

**Комментарий:**

“Having disrespected Indra, by your order, we worshipped the cows, brāhmaṇas and Govardhana. Now Indra, angry because of the disrespect, attacks the cows, your devatās. what auspiciousness has been done by this boy?” Due to the dearness of this scolding, the cowherds, who had heard and experienced Kṛṣṇa’s powers, though not fully manifested in him, took shelter of him. Jāta- vepanāḥ means they were shivering.

### Text 12

*śiraḥ sutāṁś ca kāyena pracchādyāsāra-pīḍitāḥ*  
*vepamānā bhagavataḥ pāda-mūlam upāyayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Trembling from the distress brought about by the severe rainfall, and trying to cover their heads and calves with their own bodies, the cows and people approached the lotus feet of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

The cows covered their heads and their calves (sutān) with their own bodies.

### Text 13

*kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-bhāga tvan-nāthaṁ gokulaṁ prabho*  
*trātum arhasi devān naḥ kupitād bhakta-vatsala*

**Перевод:**

**\[The cowherd men and women addressed the Lord:\] Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, O most fortunate one, please deliver the cows and us from the wrath of Indra! O Lord, you are most affectionate to your devotees!**

**Комментарий:**

They pray for destruction of suffering. Devāt means “from Indra.”

### Text 14

*śilā-varṣāti-vātena hanyamānam acetanam*  
*nirīkṣya bhagavān mene kupitendra-kṛtaṁ hariḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the inhabitants of his Gokula rendered practically unconscious by the onslaught of hail and blasting wind, the Supreme Lord understood that this was the work of angry Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

Even before being informed that the rain was created by angry Indra, Kṛṣṇa understood that Indra was responsible. The severe distress of the residents of Vṛndāvana was an arrangement made by Kṛṣṇa’s pastime potency (līlā-śakti) so that Kṛṣṇa could taste the rasa in a future pastime. Just as hunger enhances the pleasure of food of the eaters.

### Text 15

*apartv aty-ulbaṇaṁ varṣam ati-vātaṁ śilā-mayam*  
*sva-yāge vihate ‘smābhir indro nāśāya varṣati*

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa said to Himself:\] Because we have stopped his sacrifice, Indra has caused this unusually fierce, unseasonable rain, together with terrible winds and hail.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding that it was Indra’s work, Kṛṣṇa spoke to himself in five verses. The fierce rain full of hailstones (śilā-mayam) wasunseasonal, belonging to a season already passed.

### Text 16

*tatra pratividhiṁ samyag ātma-yogena sādhaye*  
*lokeśa-mānināṁ mauḍhyād dhaniṣye śrī-madaṁ tamaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**By my mystic power I will completely counteract this disturbance. I will destroy the ignorance, the intense pride in wealth of these devatās, who out of foolishness consider themselves the controllers of planets.**

**Комментарий:**

I will remedy the situation through my potency (ātma-yogena), which is inconceivable. Due to foolishness, these devatās think ofthemselves as lords. Plural is used (lokeśa-māninām) to indicate Varuṇa and the other devatās.

### Text 17

*na hi sad-bhāva-yuktānāṁ surāṇām īśa-vismayaḥ*  
*matto ’satāṁ māna-bhaṅgaḥ praśamāyopakalpate*

**Перевод:**

**Since the devatās are endowed with sentiments for me and should not have the false pride of considering themselves lords, I will break their false prestige to create auspiciousness for them.**

**Комментарий:**

It is not that I compete with tiny Indra, but I will take away his false pride that has arisen in him as he is my devotee. Since (hi) thedevatās like Indra who are endowed with bhakti for me (sad-bhāva) should not have pride thinking, “We are lords,” therefore due to the sickness of pride, removal of their respect (māna-bhaṅgaḥ) by me is for producing dedication to me, without pride.

### Text 18

*tasmān mac-charaṇaṁ goṣṭhaṁ*  
*man-nāthaṁ mat-parigraham*  
*gopāye svātma-yogena*  
*so ’yaṁ me vrata āhitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**I must therefore protect the cowherd community by my natural powers for I am their shelter, I am their protector, and indeed I am everything to them. I have taken a vow to protect my devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

“The people of Vraja who live only for me, must be protected even if by the means of despising the devatās.” I will protect (gopāye)Vraja (goṣṭhaṁ) from angry Indra. The place is my home (śaraṇam). Śaraṇam means house according to Amara-kośa. I am its master(mat-nātham). It is the place of my family (parigraham), where my parents, siblings and beloved gopīs live. Not only will I protect it from angry Indra, but even from final destruction. This is the famous rule (vrataḥ) held (āhitaḥ) by me.

### Text 19

*ity uktvaikena hastena kṛtvā govardhanācalam*  
*dadhāra līlayā viṣṇuś chatrākam iva bālakaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Having said this, Kṛṣṇa picked up Govardhana Hill with one hand and held it aloft just as easily as a child holds up a mushroom.**

**Комментарий:**

Having thus spoken to himself, Kṛṣṇa held up Govardhana like a small mushroom by his left hand as mentioned in Hari-vaṁśa:

*sa dhṛtaḥ saṅgato megahir giriḥ savyena*  
*pāṇinā -bhāvaṁ gatas tatra grḥākāreṇa varcasā*

**He held the mountain up to the clouds with his left hand. It became like a dwelling, with the form of a splendid house. (Hari-vaṁśa)**

O king of mountains! After eating plenty, in the end do you just see your worshippers suffering from wicked Indra? Wake up and protect them. Conquer Indra. Thus in order to wake him up, Kṛṣṇa touched him with his left hand and in order to protect them he personally remained on the hand and due to his vow became like a flower ball. Thus he held Govardhan like a mushroom.

### Text 20

*athāha bhagavān gopān he ’mba tāta vrajaukasaḥ*  
*yathopajoṣaṁ viśata giri-gartaṁ sa-go-dhanāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord then addressed the cowherd community: O Mother, O Father, O residents of Vraja, if you wish, you may now come under this hole in the hill with your cows.**

**Комментарий:**

Come comfortably (yathopajoṣam). This is the inconceivable power of the mountain, the best of the Lord’s servants. At the base of the mountain measuring three krośas, all the people of Vraja with their belongings entered leisurely. Kṛṣṇa says in Hari-vaṁśa:

*śailotpāṭana-bhūr eṣā mahatī nirmitā mayā*  
*apy utsahate rakṣituṁ kiṁ punar vrajam*

**Raising Govardhana I have created this huge area. This is adequate for the three worlds, what to speak of protecting Vraja.**

By its power, the colorful birds and animals on its peaks, did not feel any suffering at all by the hard rains which were like showers of flowers, and the flowering trees and creepers did not interrupt giving off fragrance. Rather they became fully joyful. The heavy rains became hanging strings of pearls on the golden umbrella of the mountain. Due to interrupting the thunderbolts, Govardhana revealed the true meaning of govardhana (increasing the cows).

### Text 21

*na trāsa iha vaḥ kāryo mad-dhastādri-nipātanāt*  
*vāta-varṣa-bhayenālaṁ tat-trāṇaṁ vihitaṁ hi vaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You should have no fear that this mountain will fall from my hand. And don’t be afraid of the wind and rain, for your deliverance from these afflictions has already been arranged.**

**Комментарий:**

This devatā of the mountain, being pleased, remains on my hand like a flower-ball. Do not fear. Your deliverance has been arrangedby that devatā.

### Text 22

*tathā nirviviśur gartaṁ kṛṣṇāśvāsita-mānasaḥ*  
*yathāvakāśaṁ sa-dhanāḥ sa-vrajāḥ sopajīvinaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Their minds thus pacified by Kṛṣṇa, they all entered beneath the hill, where they found ample room for themselves along with their cows, wagons, servants and priests, and all other members of the community as well.**

**Комментарий:**

They entered with their wealth of cows and various articles (sa- dhanāḥ), with chariots, carts (sa-vrajāḥ) and with priests and servants (sopajīvinaḥ).

### Text 23

*kṣut-tṛḍ-vyathāṁ sukhāpekṣāṁ hitvā tair vraja-vāsibhiḥ*  
*vīkṣyamāṇo dadhārādriṁ saptāhaṁ nācalat padāt*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, forgetting hunger and thirst and putting aside all considerations of personal pleasure, stood there holding up the hill for seven days without moving as the people of Vraja gazed upon him, forgetting hunger and thirst and putting aside all considerations of personal pleasure.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa and the Vraja-vāsīs gave up the pain of hunger and thirst and dependence on happiness arising from sleeping, sitting, etc. The reason and purpose of giving them up was seeing him. That became like an assistance to hold the mountain, since by that they were constantly filled with joy. This is stated in Viṣṇu Purāṇa:

*kṛṣno ’pi taṁ dadhāraiva śailam atyanta-niścalam*  
*vrajaika-vāsibhir harṣa-vismitākṣair nirīkṣitaḥ*  
*gopa-gopī-janair hṛṣṭaiḥ prīti-visphāritekṣaṇaiḥ*  
*saṁstūyamāna-caritaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śailam adhārayat*

**Kṛṣṇa held up the unmoving mountain while his praises were chanted by the residents of Vraja, all of whom now had the opportunity to dwell together with him, and who glanced at him with joyful and amazed eyes, with eyes opened wide out of affection. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa)**

Kṛṣṇa faced them all. By drinking the nectar of his beauty while looking at him, the people’s hunger and thirst disappeared and by drinking the nectar of the gopīs’ beauty, Kṛṣṇa’s hunger and thirst disappeared. Though the sāmvartaka clouds showered for seven days, the place was not submerged in water, since by the śakti of the Lord the water immediately dried up.

### Text 24

*kṛṣṇa-yogānubhāvaṁ taṁ niśamyendro ‘ti-vismitaḥ*  
*nistambho bhraṣṭa-saṅkalpaḥ svān meghān sannyavārayat*

**Перевод:**

**When Indra observed this power of Kṛṣṇa’s śakti, he became most astonished. His pride destroyed, his determination to cause havoc thwarted, he ordered his clouds to desist.**

**Комментарий:**

His pride deflated, Indra withdrew his clouds. He was fearful of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 25

*khaṁ vyabhram uditādityaṁ vāta-varṣaṁ ca dāruṇam*  
*niśamyoparataṁ gopān govardhana-dharo ‘bravīt*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that the fierce wind and rain had now ceased, the sky had become clear of rainclouds, and the sun had risen, the lifter of Govardhana Hill spoke to the cowherd community as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing (niśamya) that the sky was cloudless (vyabhram) and the wind and rain had stopped (uparatam), he spoke to the people.

### Text 26

*niryāta tyajata trāsaṁ gopāḥ sa-strī-dhanārbhakāḥ*  
*upārataṁ vāta-varṣaṁ vyuda-prāyāś ca nimnagāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa said:\] My dear cowherd men, please go out with your wives, children, cows and possessions. Give up your fear. The wind and rain have stopped, and the rivers’ high waters have subsided.**

**Комментарий:**

There is little water (vyuda-prāyāḥ). The king of mountains is giving the order. Therefore, go out now. (niryāta).

### Text 27

*tatas te niryayur gopāḥ svaṁ svam ādāya go-dhanam*  
*śakaṭoḍhopakaraṇaṁ strī-bāla-sthavirāḥ śanaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After collecting their respective cows, wealth and carts, the cowherd men, women, children and elderly persons slowly went out.**

**Комментарий:**

Mounting on their carts, they went out in such a way that their wealth was mounted on the carts.

### Text 28

*bhagavān api taṁ śailaṁ sva-sthāne pūrva-vat prabhuḥ*  
*paśyatāṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ sthāpayām āsa līlayā*

**Перевод:**

**While all living creatures looked on, the Lord easily put down the hill in its original place, just as it had stood before.**

**Комментарий:**

He placed the mountain down in the place where it had been resting and where he lifted it up, as if the mountain was going fromwaking to sleeping state.

### Text 29

*taṁ prema-vegān nirbhṛtā vrajaukaso*  
*yathā samīyuḥ parirambhaṇādibhiḥ*  
*gopyaś ca sa-sneham apūjayan mudā*  
*dadhy-akṣatādbhir yuyujuḥ sad-āśiṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All the residents of Vṛndāvana, overwhelmed with ecstatic love, came to Kṛṣṇa with embraces and other acts of affection according to their individual relationships with him. The cowherd women affectionately presented water mixed with yogurt and unbroken barleycorns as a token of honor, and they showered auspicious benedictions upon him in joy.**

**Комментарий:**

Govardhana with embraces, etc., according to their positions (yathā). They were full (nibhṛtāḥ) of intense prema because of hisendeavors for them (prema-vegān). Elders worshipped him with auspicious blessings, smelling his head, kissing him, massaging his left hand, praising him and asking about his fatigue. Friends worshipped him with jokes. Younger persons worshipped him by falling at his feet, massaging his feet, etc. The elder gopīs with vātsalya worshipped him with yogurt and grains. The word ca in this verse indicates that the wives of the brāhmaṇas joined with the cowherd ladies (gopyaḥ) and worshipped him with auspicious items like yogurt and unbroken grains. They gave blessings (āśiṣaḥ yuyujuḥ) to Kṛṣṇa by saying, “May you subdue the wicked, protect the decent people, be enriched with six opulences and give pleasure to your parents.”

### Text 30

*yaśodā rohiṇī nando rāmaś ca balināṁ varaḥ*  
*kṛṣṇam āliṅgya yuyujur āśiṣaḥ sneha-kātarāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Mother Yaśodā, mother Rohiṇī, Nanda Mahārāja and Balarāma, the greatest of the strong, all embraced Kṛṣṇa. Overcome with affection, they offered him their blessings.**

**Комментарий:**

The details of his mother and others is given. Because Balarāma was elder, he is grouped with the elders, having vātsalya. Though Balarāma was the best of the strong and most affection to his younger brother, it was proper that he did not participate in holding up the mountain since Kṛṣṇa desired to perform this pastime alone.

### Text 31

*divi deva-gaṇāḥ siddhāḥ sādhyā gandharva-cāraṇāḥ*  
*tuṣṭuvur mumucus tuṣṭāḥ puṣpa-varṣāṇi pārthiva*

**Перевод:**

**In the heavens, O King, all the devatās, including the Siddhas, Sādhyas, Gandharvas and Cāraṇas, sang the praises of Kṛṣṇa and showered down flowers in great satisfaction.**

**Комментарий:**

Not only the people of Vraja became joyful, but the inhabitants of heaven also celebrated. This is described in two verses.

### Text 32

*śaṅkha-dundubhayo nedur divi deva-pracoditāḥ*  
*jagur gandharva-patayas tumburu-pramukhā nṛpa*

**Перевод:**

**My dear Parīkṣit, the conch shells and kettledrums played by the devatās in heaven sounded, and the best of the Gandharvas, led by Tumburu, began to sing.**

### Text 33

*tato ’nuraktaiḥ paśupaiḥ pariśrito*  
*rājan sva-goṣṭhaṁ sa-balo ’vrajad dhariḥ*  
*tathā-vidhāny asya kṛtāni gopikā*  
*gāyantya īyur muditā hṛdi-spṛśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Surrounded by loving cowherd boyfriends and Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa entered his house within Vraja. The cowherd girls returned to their homes, singing joyfully about the lifting of Govardhana Hill and other glorious deeds performed by Kṛṣṇa, who had so deeply touched their hearts.**

**Комментарий:**

From the place of Govardhana (tataḥ) Kṛṣṇa went to his house. The gopīs met him unseen by others, by glances from a distance. They sang about the activities of he who touched their hearts and minds (hṛdi-spṛśaḥ) with prema on returning home.

## Chapter 26 - Wonderful Kṛṣṇa

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*evaṁ-vidhāni karmāṇi gopāḥ kṛṣṇasya vīkṣya te*  
*atad-vīrya-vidaḥ procuḥ samabhyetya su-vismitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The cowherd men, astonished when they saw Kṛṣṇa’s powerful activities, and unable to understand his potency, approached Nanda Mahārāja with devotion and spoke with affection.**

**Комментарий:**

*karmāṇy aiśvarya-garbhāṇi vīkṣya kṛṣṇe ’bhiśaṅkitān \|*  
*gopān ṣaḍ-viṁśake nando gargoktyā ca samādadhat*

**In the twenty-sixth chapter, by the words of Garga, Nanda resolved the cowherds doubts about Kṛṣṇa on seeing his powerful actions.**

They saw activities such as in killing Pūtanā which were superhuman and following the ways of humans (evaṁ vidhāni). They approached Nanda and spoke. They did not understand his powers because their friendly affection covered knowledge of his powers. They were most astonished because by human actions he accomplished great feats of power.

The meaning is this. He who always exists with us in a friendly manner in Gokula, the highest place, has come with his abode and associates to this material world, was born to Nanda and Yaśodā, did amazing activities, and gave us bliss. We know that he is Svayam Bhagavān full of powers and sweetness. Going to his father we will understand other things as they are. One cannot say that they did not know about Kṛṣṇa’s powers since as his eternal friends they knew this from the praise of the devatās when he had killed Baka and others. Thus they spoke of surrender to him when in danger.

### Text 2

*bālakasya yad etāni karmāṇy aty-adbhutāni vai*  
*katham arhaty asau janma grāmyeṣv ātma-jugupsitam*

**Перевод:**

**\[The cowherd men said:\] Since this boy performs such extraordinary activities, how could he warrant a birth among worldly men like us — a birth that for him would seem contemptible?**

**Комментарий:**

By his astonishing activities as a human being, which appear like those of a divinity, he must be īśvara (Lord). How could he take birth among us, who are of gross intelligence? It would be proper to take birth among the devatās having fine intelligence. It is notproper for him (ātmā-jugupsitam). They call themselves gross out of good character though it is not actually true, since it is said that as cowherds they were of similar form and qualities as the Lord (Krama-dīpika). By addressing Kṛṣṇa as asau (that person),indicating beyond visibility, it is understood that he had gone to the forest since there would be conflict of rasa if he were present.

### Text 3

*yaḥ sapta-hāyano bālaḥ kareṇaikena līlayā*  
*kathaṁ bibhrad giri-varaṁ puṣkaraṁ gaja-rāḍ iva*

**Перевод:**

**How could this seven-year-old boy playfully hold up the great hill Govardhana with one hand, just as a mighty elephant holds up a lotus flower?**

**Комментарий:**

If he were not the Lord, how could these activities be possible? This is expressed in twelve verses. How did hold up the mountain and stand there for seven days? The word yaḥ changes in case to suit the meaning in the following verses.

### Text 4

*tokenāmīlitākṣeṇa pūtanāyā mahaujasaḥ*  
*pītaḥ stanaḥ saha prāṇaiḥ kāleneva vayas tanoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As a mere infant who had his eyes completely closed, he drank the breast milk of the powerful demoness Pūtanā and then sucked out her very life air as well, just as the force of time sucks out the youth of one’s body.**

**Комментарий:**

The milk was drunk by him with half closed eyes (āmilitākṣena). The invisible actions are described by an example. Invisibly time drinks up youth of one’s body.

### Text 5

*hinvato ’dhaḥ śayānasya māsyasya caraṇāv udak*  
*ano ’patad viparyastaṁ rudataḥ prapadāhatam*

**Перевод:**

**Once, when only three months old, little Kṛṣṇa was crying and kicking up his feet as he lay beneath a huge cart. Then the cart fell and turned upside-down simply because it was struck by the tip of his toe.**

**Комментарий:**

The word māsyasya in this verse means three months. It is formed by the rule, māsād vayasi yat khañau (Pāṇini 5.1.81). Being slightly struck by the tip of the feet being thrown up, of the three month old, who was lying under the cart, the cart turned over. How was that?

### Text 6

*eka-hāyana āsīno hriyamāṇo vihāyasā*  
*daityena yas tṛṇāvartam ahan kaṇṭha-grahāturam*

**Перевод:**

**At the age of one, while sitting peacefully he was taken up into the sky by the demon Tṛṇāvarta. But baby Kṛṣṇa grabbed the demon’s neck, causing him great pain, and thus killed him.**

**Комментарий:**

Taken away the demon (daityena) he killed the demon.

### Text 7

*kvacid dhaiyaṅgava-stainye mātrā baddha udūkhale*  
*gacchann arjunayor madhye bāhubhyāṁ tāv apātayat*

**Перевод:**

**Once, his mother tied him with ropes to a mortar because she had caught him stealing butter. Then, crawling on his hands, he dragged the mortar between a pair of arjuna trees and pulled them down.**

**Комментарий:**

He stole butter (haiyaṅgave-stainye). Crawling, he made the trees fall.

### Text 8

*vane sañcārayan vatsān sa-rāmo bālakair vṛtaḥ*  
*hantu-kāmaṁ bakaṁ dorbhyāṁ mukhato ’rim apāṭayat*

**Перевод:**

**Another time, when Kṛṣṇa was tending the calves in the forest together with Balarāma and the cowherd boys, the demon Bakāsura came with the intention of killing Kṛṣṇa. But Kṛṣṇa seized this inimical demon starting from the mouth and tore him apart.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking him by his arms, starting from his mouth (mukhataḥ) how did he tear Baka apart?

### Text 9

*vatseṣu vatsa-rūpeṇa praviśantaṁ jighāṁsayā*  
*hatvā nyapātayat tena kapitthāni ca līlayā*

**Перевод:**

**Desiring to kill Kṛṣṇa, the demon Vatsa disguised himself as a calf and entered among Kṛṣṇa’s calves. But Kṛṣṇa killed the demon and, using his body, enjoyed the sport of knocking kapittha fruits down from the trees.**

### Text 10

*hatvā rāsabha-daiteyaṁ tad-bandhūṁś ca balānvitaḥ*  
*cakre tāla-vanaṁ kṣemaṁ paripakva-phalānvitam*

**Перевод:**

**Together with Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa killed the jackass demon and all his friends, thereby securing the safety of the Tālavana forest, which abounded with fully ripened palm fruits.**

**Комментарий:**

Rāsabha-daiteyam is Dhenukāsura. In his killing Kṛṣṇa was most prominent (balāvitah—with Balarāma).

### Text 11

*pralambaṁ ghātayitvograṁ balena bala-śālinā*  
*amocayad vraja-paśūn gopāṁś cāraṇya-vahnitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After arranging for the mighty Balarāma to kill the terrible demon Pralamba, Kṛṣṇa saved Vraja’s cowherd boys and their animals from a forest fire.**

### Text 12

*āśī-viṣatamāhīndraṁ damitvā vimadaṁ hradāt*  
*prasahyodvāsya yamunāṁ cakre ’sau nirviṣodakām*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa chastised the most poisonous serpent, Kāliya, and after humbling him he drove him forcibly from the lake of the Yamunā. In this way the Lord made the water of that river free of the snake’s powerful poison.**

**Комментарий:**

He restrained (damitvā) the king of the snakes having severe poison (āśī-viṣatama).

### Text 13

*dustyajaś cānurāgo ’smin sarveṣāṁ no vrajaukasām*  
*nanda te tanaye ’smāsu tasyāpy autpattikaḥ katham*

**Перевод:**

**Dear Nanda, how is it that we and all the other residents of Vraja cannot give up our constant affection for your son? And how is it that he is so spontaneously attracted to us?**

**Комментарий:**

Having described his powerful activities, they describe his sweetness.

O Nanda! How do we, the people of Vraja, babies, aged and youths as well as animals and birds, all have such affection (anurāgaḥ)for Kṛṣṇa at every moment though it is certain that he is your son. We cannot give up that affection though he is not even our son, as it is spontaneous. How is it so? Let our attraction for him be! He also has such natural, constant affection for us though he is the supreme Lord, full of powerful actions, since he is our protector, and full of knowledge and bliss. We have experienced that also. How is that possible?

Making us doubtful by his godly powers, he begs from us in a friendly mood and strenghtens that. But he does not show any powers. How can he be the Supreme Lord? His begging is made clear in Viṣṇu Purāṇa and Hari-vaṁśa. This was shown in the commentary on tasmān nandātma-jo ’yaṁ te (SB [10.8.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.19))

### Text 14

*kva sapta-hāyano bālaḥ kva mahādri-vidhāraṇam*  
*tato no jāyate śaṅkā vraja-nātha tavātmaje*

**Перевод:**

**On the one hand this boy is only seven years old, and on the other we see that he has lifted the great hill Govardhana. Therefore, O King of Vraja, a doubt about your son arises within us.**

**Комментарий:**

Though his lifting Govardhana was already mentioned, because it is topic in question, they describe it with amazement. We havedeveloped a doubt (śaṅkāḥ). Since you know the truth you tell us the real nature of his svarūpa.

### Text 15

*śrī-nanda uvāca*  
*śrūyatāṁ me vaco gopā vyetu śaṅkā ca vo ’rbhake*  
*enam kumāram uddiśya gargo me yad uvāca ha*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja replied: O cowherd men, just hear my words and let all your doubts concerning my son be gone. Some time ago Garga Muni spoke to me as follows about this boy.**

**Комментарий:**

Being asked, Nanda, taking shelter of what Garga said exactly about him, spoke to enlighten them.

### Text 16

*varṇās trayaḥ kilāsyāsan gṛhṇato ’nu-yugaṁ tanūḥ*  
*śuklo raktas tathā pīta idānīṁ kṛṣṇatāṁ gataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Your son Kṛṣṇa appeared in previous yugas (according to the avatāra he worshipped) with three different colors—white, red and yellow—and now he has appeared in a blackish color.**

**Комментарий:**

The meaning of the next seven verses was previously explained. The essence is stated here. The yuga-avatāras starting with Śuklahave entered into eternally perfect Śyamasundara who has appeared from you now.

### Text 17

*prāgayaṁ vasudevasya kvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ*  
*vāsudeva iti śrīmān abhijñāḥ sampracakṣate*

**Перевод:**

**This beautiful son of yours somewhere appeared previously as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore, those who are learned sometimes call this child Vāsudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

He also appeared from Vasudeva as he has appeared from you.

### Text 18

*bahūni santi nāmāni rūpāṇi ca sutasya te*  
*guṇa-karmānurūpāṇi tāny ahaṁ veda no janāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**For this son of yours there are many forms and names according to his qualities and activities. These are known to me, but people in general do not understand them.**

**Комментарий:**

He is the avatārī of the puruṣa and other avatāras. They have also entered him. He is Svayam Bhagavān.

### Text 19

*eṣa vaḥ śreya ādhāsyad gopa-gokula-nandanaḥ*  
*anena sarva-durgāṇi yūyam añjas tariṣyatha*

**Перевод:**

**By his nature increasing the bliss of the cowherd men of Gokula, this child will always act most auspiciously for you. And by his grace only, you will surpass all difficulties.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he is of such nature, he is controlled by your prema. He will follow your orders.

### Text 20

*purānena vraja-pate sādhavo dasyu-pīḍitāḥ*  
*arājake rakṣyamāṇā jigyur dasyūn samedhitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In a previous birth, when Indra was dethroned, and the devatās were afflicted by the demons, they were rescued by Kṛṣṇa, conquered the demons and then flourished.**

**Комментарий:**

He always protects the devotees. Now also he will protect you.

### Text 21

*ya etasmin mahā-bhāge prītiṁ kurvanti mānavāḥ*  
*nārayo ’bhibhavanty etān viṣṇu-pakṣān ivāsurāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Enemies cannot harm the devotees who show affection for this greatly fortunate child, just as the demons cannot harm the devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

His devotees are always happy.

### Text 22

*tasmān nanda kumāro ’yaṁ nārāyaṇa-samo guṇaiḥ*  
*śriyā kīrtyānubhāvena tat-karmasu na vismayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O Nanda Mahārāja, this child of yours is as good as Nārāyaṇa by his qualities, opulence, name, fame and influence. Thus you should not be astonished by his activities.**

**Комментарий:**

He cannot be compared to anyone except the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha since he is Kṛṣṇa’s vilāsa-rūpa. Though there is no differencebetween him and the puruṣa-avatāras since they are his svāṁśas, distinctions are made by viśeṣa. Though he is Svayam Bhagavān he desires your affection of seeing him as a your child, since by that there is intense joy arising from svarūpa. You should not be astonished by the activities of Svayam Bhagavān (tat-karmasu). In his seemingly worldly actions in which he is greedy for your love in friendly manner, you should give him blessing for long life. But there should not be any restriction by seeing his powers, because it does not give him joy. Masters are seen to enjoy sporting with his friends of equal stature. In this way, he consequently quoted Garga’s words, “Protect him carefully” (SB [10.8.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.19)). This child is my and your son too since the words kumāro ‘yam do not express a particular relationship.

### Text 23

*ity addhā māṁ samādiśya garge ca sva-gṛhaṁ gate*  
*manye nārāyaṇasyāṁśaṁ kṛṣṇam akliṣṭa-kāriṇam*

**Перевод:**

**After Garga Ṛṣi spoke these words to me and returned home, I began to consider that Kṛṣṇa, who keeps us free from trouble, is empowered by Nārāyaṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Thus, I consider Kṛṣṇa to be an avatāra (aṁśa) of my Lord Nārāyaṇa. He said this to hide the powers of his son. Actually however, the meaning is “aṁśas (divisions) are present in him,” using the rule arśa-ādibhyo ‘c (Pāṇini 5.2.127). He is the aṁśī of Nārāyaṇa. Otherwise there would be contradiction to the previous statements varṇās trayaḥ kilāsyāsan: he had three colors (verse 16), and bahūni santi rūpāni: he had many forms (verse 18). And since the statement kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam (SB [10.3.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.28)) must be remembered.

### Text 24

*iti nanda-vacaḥ śrutvā garga-gītaṁ taṁ vrajaukasaḥ*  
*muditā nandam ānarcuḥ kṛṣṇaṁ ca gata-vismayāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Having heard Nanda Mahārāja relate the statements of Garga Muni, the residents of Vṛndāvana became enlivened. Their perplexity was gone, and they worshiped Nanda and Kṛṣṇa with great respect.**

**Комментарий:**

All the cowherds were overjoyed on hearing the conclusion which established his nature. They worshipped Nanda with attractive clothing, ornaments and gold coins. They worshipped Kṛṣṇa too who had returned from the forest by decorating him with yellow cloth, necklaces, bracelets, and arm bands. May you remain victorious. O tilaka of the land of Gokula! Live long! Prosper with ease. Protect us.

### Text 25

*deve varṣati yajña-viplava-ruṣā vajrāsma-varṣānilaiḥ*  
*sīdat-pāla-paśu-striy ātma-śaraṇaṁ dṛṣṭvānukampy utsmayan*  
*utpāṭyaika-kareṇa śailam abalo līlocchilīndhraṁ yathā*  
*bibhrad goṣṭham apān mahendra-mada-bhit prīyān na indro gavām*

**Перевод:**

**Indra became angry when his sacrifice was disrupted, and thus he caused rain and hail to fall on Gokula, accompanied by lightning and powerful winds, all of which brought great suffering to the cowherds, animals and women there. When Kṛṣṇa, who is by nature always compassionate, saw the condition of those who had only him as their shelter, he smiled broadly and lifted Govardhana Hill with one hand, just as a small child picks up a mushroom to play with it. Holding up the hill, he protected the cowherd community. May He, Govinda, the Lord of the cows and the destroyer of Indra’s false pride, be pleased with us.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to remove obstacles in completing the scripture, even though it is in the middle, Śukadeva utters a maṅgalācaraṇa(auspicious invocation), praying for the mercy of his worshippable deity.

When Indra showered rain because of anger at disruption of his sacrifice, seeing the village where the animals, cowherds and women were being afflicted by the thunder hail and harsh winds, for whom he was personally the shelter, being very merciful, smiling (utsmayan), Kṛṣṇa raised the mountain with his left hand alone and holding it protected (apāt) the village, just as a child picks up a mushroom playfully with one hand and holds it. May son of Nanda, king of the cows, be pleased with me, Parīkṣit and all the listeners.

Due to being the kind of cows he destroyed the pride of Indra. Being the king of cows is more power than Indra’s.

*gobhyo yajñāḥ pravartante gobhyo devāḥ samutthitāḥ \|*  
*gobhir vedāḥ samudgīrṇāḥ sa-ṣaḍ-aṅga-pada-kramāḥ*

**Sacrifices take place because of cows. The devatās appear because of cows. The Vedas with their six aṅgas appear because of the cows. (Go-sūkta)**

He easily destroyed Indra’s pride. By lifting the king of mountains, he protected Vraja from Indra’s thunderbolt. Similarly, he will protect you, Parikṣit, from the thunderbolts of the brāhmaṇa’s curse, by Bhāgavatam extracted from the Vedas.

## Chapter 27 - Lord Indra and Mother Surabhi Offer Prayers

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*govardhane dhṛte śaile āsārād rakṣite vraje*  
*go-lokād āvrajat kṛṣṇaṁ surabhiḥ śakra eva ca*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After Kṛṣṇa had lifted Govardhana Hill and thus protected the inhabitants of Vraja from the terrible rainfall, Surabhi, the mother of the cows, came from her planet to see Kṛṣṇa. She was accompanied by Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

*stuvatīndre prasanno’bhūt surabhyā tena ca prabhuḥ*  
*\| sapta-viṁśe’bhiṣiktaśca govindākhyāṁ dadhau hariḥ*

**In the twenty-seventh chapter, when Indra offered praises, the Lord was pleased with Surabhi and Indra. Bathed, he accepted the name Govinda.**

Indra went to Kṛṣṇa, with Surabhi, sent by Brahmā on Meru, on his request to assist him. She came from material Goloka, not from the spiritual Goloka, a special manifestation of Gokula, because Indra could not associate with the spiritual Surabhi.

### Text 2

*vivikta upasaṅgamya vrīḍitaḥ kṛta-helanaḥ*  
*pasparśa pādayor enaṁ kirīṭenārka-varcasā*

**Перевод:**

**Indra, ashamed of having offended the Lord, approached him in a solitary place, and touched his crown, whose effulgence was as brilliant as the sun, upon the Lord’s lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa had gone alone to check the condition of Govardhan according to Hari-vaṁśa. He was sitting on jeweled slab on Govardhana with Garuḍa’s wings giving shade from the sky. On the advice of Surabhi Indra came without attendants. He was miserable, ashamed from committing offense. Meeting in that private place he touched his crown to Kṛṣṇa’s feet and offered full respects on the ground.

### Text 3

*dṛṣṭa-śrutānubhāvo ’sya kṛṣṇasyāmita-tejasaḥ*  
*naṣṭa-tri-lokeśa-mada idam āha kṛtāñjaliḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Indra had now heard of and seen the power of omnipotent Kṛṣṇa, and his false pride in being the lord of the three worlds was thus defeated. Holding his hands together in supplication, he addressed the Lord as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Indra experienced Kṛṣṇa who had unlimited powers. He had heard from scriptures about him. Eko vaśī sarvagaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ: Kṛṣṇa is the one controller, pervading everything. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) He folded his hands and spoke. Though Indra’s crown had the effulgence of the sun, in front of Kṛṣṇa, he was like a firefly and thus his pride was destroyed.

### Text 4

*indra uvāca*  
*viśuddha-sattvaṁ tava dhāma śāntaṁ*  
*tapo-mayaṁ dhvasta-rajas-tamaskam*  
*māyā-mayo ’yaṁ guṇa-sampravāho*  
*na vidyate te ’grahaṇānubandhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Indra said: Your form, a manifestation of pure goodness, is undisturbed by change, shines with knowledge and is devoid of passion and ignorance. This is a succession of qualities made of māyā. You have no desire to accept them.**

**Комментарий:**

To beg forgiveness for his offense Indra speaks in four verses indicating that the Lord’s punishment is mercy. I surrender to your svarūpa (dhāma). The svarūpa is described. It is gentle (śāntam), viśuddha-sattvam. Is it material? It is the svarūpa of jñāna(tapomayam): it is eternally endowed with the self-manifesting saṁvit śakti. Material sattva is mixed with tamas and rajas.

*anyonya-mithunāḥ sarve*

**The guṇas, tamas, rajas and sattva, are invariably mixed with each other. (Mahābhārata, Aśvamedha Parva)**

This was said previously also:

*sattvaṁ na ced dhātar idaṁ nijaṁ bhaved*  
*vijñānam ajñāna-bhidāpamārjanam*  
*guṇa-prakāśair anumīyate bhavān*  
*prakāśate yasya ca yena vā guṇaḥ*

**O Lord, cause of all causes, if your transcendental body were not beyond the modes of material nature, one could not understand the difference between matter and transcendence. Only by your presence can one understand the transcendental nature of your Lordship, who are the controller of material nature. Your transcendental nature is very difficult to understand unless one is influenced by the presence of your transcendental form. (SB** [**10.2.35**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.35)**)**

By you rajas and tamas are destroyed (dhvasta-raja-tamaskam). Sattva is not mentioned as being destroyed by Lord (i.e. he does not say dhvasta-sattva-raja-tamaskam) since it is a door to manifestation of knowledge related to Lord. What was said in sattvaṁ yad brahma- darśanam: Sattva is favorable for realizing the Lord (SB [1.2.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.24)), is explained here in this way.

The Lord is free from material sattva, consisting of two inferior guṇas, by him rajas and tamas are destroyed, and remembering him one surpasses all the guṇas. You are the svarūpa of consciousness (tapomayam). Thus saṁsāra (guṇa-sampravāhaḥ), which is relatedto jīvas like us, which is full of māyā, does not exist for you.

“Okay, let me not accept the guṇas like the jīvas. What is the fault in accepting them as a pastime?” You have no desire to accept them since you are full of pure bliss.

### Text 5

*kuto nu tad-dhetava īśa tat-kṛtā*  
*lobhādayo ye ’budha-linga-bhāvāḥ*  
*tathāpi daṇḍaṁ bhagavān bibharti*  
*dharmasya guptyai khala-nigrahāya*

**Перевод:**

**O controlling Lord! Where is the fault if you are the cause of māyā? The greed and other qualities are the effects and produce signs of ignorance. The Lord punishes in order to protect dharma and chastise the wicked.**

**Комментарий:**

Being so, O Lord! Where did the causes of saṁsāra, i.e sattva and other guṇas, arise from? The effects of saṁsāra (tat-kṛtāḥ) aregreed, etc., difficult to approach which produce signs of ignorance (abudha). Then why was your worship disturbed? Though devoid of greed and anger, the Lord punishes in order to protect dharma and chastise the wicked.

### Text 6

*pitā gurus tvaṁ jagatām adhīśo*  
*duratyayaḥ kāla upātta-daṇḍaḥ*  
*hitāya cecchā-tanubhiḥ samīhase*  
*mānaṁ vidhunvan jagad-īśa-māninām*

**Перевод:**

**You are the father and spiritual master of this entire universe, and also its supreme controller. You are insurmountable time, imposing punishment upon the sinful for their benefit. In your various incarnations, selected by your own free will, you act decisively to remove the false pride of those who presume themselves masters of this world.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why is it necessary for me, full of bliss to protect dharma and punish the wicked?” For those who follow dharma in the world(jagatām) you are the protector (pitā), the teacher (guru) and the giver of happiness and deliverer from suffering (adhīśaḥ). You are like insurmountable time for the wicked, purifying them by punishing them (upātta-daṇḍaḥ). In this way, for the benefit of both you perform pastimes (samīhase) through avatāras, dependent on your will (icchā-tanubhiḥ). Your pastime such as killing Pūtanā destroyed the wicked and protected the righteous. The purpose of you, engaged in protecting dharma and punishing the wicked, is the welfare of the world. But even for qualified persons such as Brahmā and others who become proud because of the wealth given by you, your actions destroy their pride.

### Text 7

*ye mad-vidhājñā jagad-īśa-māninas*  
*tvāṁ vīkṣya kāle ’bhayam āśu tan-madam*  
*hitvārya-mārgaṁ prabhajanty apasmayā*  
*īhā khalānām api te ’nuśāsanam*

**Перевод:**

**Even fools like me, who proudly think themselves universal lords, quickly give up their conceit and directly take to the bhakti when they see you are fearless even in the face of time. Your pastimes are punishment for the wicked.**

**Комментарий:**

Among those who think themselves lords of the world, I am the most foolish. People like me are ignorant. They are of my kind and they are ignorant (mad-vidhājñāḥ). Since I am an object of comparison of even the ignorant, I am most ignorant. Though like that, those who think themselves controllers of the world, they, seeing you fearless at the time of fearful showers of lightning (kāle), giving up the conception of being lords of the world, losing their pride (apasmayāḥ), they take to the path of your devotees (ārya-mārgam). Thus, your pastime (īhā) of lifting Govardhana is punishment for wicked people like me.

### Text 8

*sa tvaṁ mamaiśvarya-mada-plutasya*  
*kṛtāgasas te ’viduṣaḥ prabhāvam*  
*kṣantuṁ prabho ’thārhasi mūḍha-cetaso*  
*maivaṁ punar bhūn matir īśa me ’satī*

**Перевод:**

**Engrossed in pride over my ruling power, ignorant of your majesty, I offended you. O capable Lord, may you forgive me. My intelligence was bewildered, but let my consciousness never again be so impure.**

**Комментарий:**

“By lifting Govardhana I protected Gokula. Now I should punish you.”

Indra speaks while trembling. You are famous as the father and guru. Since you are in truth an ocean of mercy, you should forgive my offense, though I was fully intoxicated with my power. Forgive me by mercy, and not by punishment. Give mercy so that my intelligence does not become again polluted like this. This is the prayer of a person who realizes his incapability as expressed in theprevious verse: being fearful of you only when I am fearful (kale tvam bhayaṁ vīkṣya), but not one made with pure feelings. Thus, he will again forget when Kṛṣṇa takes the pārijāta tree.

### Text 9

*tavāvatāro ’yam adhokṣajeha*  
*bhuvo bharāṇām uru-bhāra-janmanām*  
*camū-patīnām abhavāya deva*  
*bhavāya yuṣmac-caraṇānuvartinām*

**Перевод:**

**You descend into this world, O invisible Lord, to destroy the warlords who burden the earth and create many terrible disturbances. O Lord worthy of worship! You simultaneously act for the auspiciousness of those who faithfully serve your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

“Being capable, how can I forgive such a great offense?” You descend to destroy the wicked (camū-patīnām), the very form of a burden to the earth (bharāṇāṁ), who commit (janma) many sins (uru-bhāra). You appear also for increasing (bhavāya) those whodwell at your feet. Thus, you should forgive my offense.

### Text 10

*namas tubhyaṁ bhagavate puruṣāya mahātmane*  
*vāsudevāya kṛṣṇāya sātvatāṁ pataye namaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances to Svayam Bhagavān, known only as Kṛṣṇa, possessing extraordinary motives, full of all glories, the son of Vasudeva and protector of the Yadus.**

**Комментарий:**

Revealing his obedience, he offers respects in two verses. I offer respects to the lord of the spiritual sky (bhagavate), to the creator of mahat-tattva (puruṣāya), to the antaryāmī of the total material world (mahātmane), to he who appeared from Vasudeva (vāsudevāya), to the son of Nanda (kṛṣṇāya), to the master of the cowherds and Yadus (sātvatām pataye).

### Text 11

*svacchandopātta-dehāya viśuddha-jñāna-mūrtaye*  
*sarvasmai sarva-bījāya sarva-bhūtātmane namaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Unto him who assumes bodies according to the desires of his devotees, unto him whose form is pure consciousness, unto him who is the universe, who is Mahā-viṣṇu and the antaryāmī, I offer my obeisances.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to you who have assumed body according to the desires of the devotees in dāsya, sakhya, etc., who is the seed ofeverything in the form of the śaktis of matter and jīva (sarva- bījāya), who is everything because of having that form, and whoinspires all jīvas (sarva-bhūtātmane).

### Text 12

*mayedaṁ bhagavan goṣṭha- nāśāyāsāra-vāyubhiḥ*  
*ceṣṭitaṁ vihate yajñe māninā tīvra-manyunā*

**Перевод:**

**My dear Lord, when my sacrifice was disrupted, I became fiercely angry because of false pride. Thus I tried to destroy your cowherd community with severe rain and wind.**

**Комментарий:**

Being sincere, he explains his offense. “Why did the servant not tolerate the disruption of the sacrifice done by the master?” My intelligence was stolen by pride in my powers (māninā).

### Text 13

*tvayeśānugṛhīto ’smi dhvasta-stambho vṛthodyamaḥ*  
*īśvaraṁ gurum ātmānaṁ tvām ahaṁ śaraṇaṁ gataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, you have shown mercy to me by shattering my false pride and defeating my foolish attempts. To you, the controller, the guru and the cause of all beings, I have now come for shelter.**

**Комментарий:**

Still, like a sick person cured by a good doctor, even if disrespected, I have been purified by the merciful Lord. My pride (stambha) has been destroyed. My attempts at throwing thunderbolts has been destroyed. I surrender to you, īśvara due to being the controller,guru due to being the benefactor, and ātmā due to being full of great knowledge and bliss.

### Text 14

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*evaṁ saṅkīrtitaḥ kṛṣṇo maghonā bhagavān amum*  
*megha-gambhīrayā vācā prahasann idam abravīt*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus glorified by Indra, Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, smiled and then spoke to him as follows in a voice resonant like the clouds.**

### Text 15

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*mayā te ’kāri maghavan makha-bhaṅgo ’nugṛhṇatā*  
*mad-anusmṛtaye nityaṁ mattasyendra-śriyā bhṛśam*

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear Indra, it was out of mercy that I stopped the sacrifice meant for you. You were greatly intoxicated by your opulence as King of heaven, and I wanted you to always remember me.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord replies to what Indra said in verse 12, suitable to the Lord’s position.

### Text 16

*mām aiśvarya-śrī-madāndho daṇḍa-pāṇiṁ na paśyati*  
*taṁ bhraṁśayāmi sampadbhyo yasya cecchāmy anugraham*

**Перевод:**

**A man blinded by intoxication with his power and opulence cannot see me nearby with the rod of punishment in my hand. If I desire his real welfare, I destroy his materially fortune.**

### Text 17

*gamyatāṁ śakra bhadraṁ vaḥ kriyatāṁ me ’nuśāsanam*  
*sthīyatāṁ svādhikāreṣu yuktair vaḥ stambha-varjitaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Indra, you may now go. Execute my order and remain in your appointed position as king of heaven. But be sober, without false pride.**

**Комментарий:**

You (vaḥ) is in plural to indicate Varuṇa and others. You should remain (shtīyatām) without pride, with care (yuktaiḥ), so that you do not get punished again. It is suggested that since the Lord did not say, “(remain such that) pride do not appear again,” Indra will again develop pride when Kṛṣṇa takes away the pārijāta tree.

### Text 18

*athāha surabhiḥ kṛṣṇam abhivandya manasvinī*  
*sva-santānair upāmantrya gopa-rūpiṇam īśvaram*

**Перевод:**
