**Mother Surabhi, along with her progeny, the cows, then offered her obeisances to Kṛṣṇa. Respectfully requesting his attention, the gentle lady addressed the Lord, who was present before her as a cowherd boy.**

**Комментарий:**

Surabhi approached with the cows of Vraja (sva-santānaiḥ). Surabhi thought of those cows as her children, since they appeared in the same dynasty, just as Kṛṣṇa appeared in the moon dynasty. (The material moon often thinks of Kṛṣṇa as his offspring.) “Why did she not previously speak in order to assist Indra?” She was wise (manasvinī). She thought, “In going I will be perceived as favoring Indra. Since the Lord is omniscient, understanding my coming, he will forgive him because he is merciful.”

### Text 19

*surabhir uvāca*  
*kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-yogin viśvātman viśva-sambhava*  
*bhavatā loka-nāthena sa-nāthā vayam acyuta*

**Перевод:**

**Mother Surabhi said: O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, greatest of mystics! O Soul and origin of the universe! You are the master of the world, and by your grace, O infallible Lord, we have you as our master.**

**Комментарий:**

She repeats Kṛṣṇa’s name out of joy. O great yogī! By your acintya- śakti you lifted Govardhana and protected my offspring. In you we have a master (sa-nāthāḥ).

### Text 20

*tvaṁ naḥ parama-kaṁ daivaṁ tvaṁ na indro jagat-pate*  
*bhavāya bhava go-vipra-devānāṁ ye ca sādhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You are our worshipable deity. Therefore, O Lord of the universe, for the benefit of the cows, the brāhmaṇas, the demigods and all other saintly persons, please become our Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

You give the highest happiness (parama-kam). Thus, you become our Indra. Enough with this Indra as our master, as he has committed violence against my offspring, the cows. O master of the universe! You are fit to be Indra since though the master of the universe, you are a cowherd, and though a cowherd, you destroyed the pride of Indra. You are Indra of even the other virtuous people(the brāhmaṇas, and devatās).

### Text 21

*indraṁ nas tvābhiṣekṣyāmo brahmaṇā coditā vayam*  
*avatīrṇo ’si viśvātman bhūmer bhārāpanuttaye*

**Перевод:**

**As ordered by Brahmā, we shall perform your bathing ceremony to coronate you as our Indra. O Soul of the universe, you descend to this world to relieve the burden of the earth.**

**Комментарий:**

We will perform abhiṣeka of you as our Indra. “Is this your own idea, or the instruction from someone?” It was ordered by Brahmā.Requested for help by Indra who was extremely frightened, Brahmā, remembering his own offense, did not come. Brahmā said, “O Surabhi! Being the protector of your progeny, seeing you, the Lord will be merciful. Thus you should go and get forgiveness for Indra’s offense. Enthrone Kṛṣṇa as the Indra of the cows.” Ordered by him, we have come. Being merciful to us, forgive his offense. O all-pervading Lord (viśvātman)! As Indra of the cows your position as the Indra of millions of universes is accomplished from beginningless time. Yet we will properly enthrone you with an abhiṣeka for our excellence.

### Texts 22-23

*śṛī-śuka uvāca*  
*evaṁ kṛṣṇam upāmantrya surabhiḥ payasātmanaḥ*  
*jalair ākāśa-gaṅgāyā airāvata-karoddhṛtaiḥ*

*indraḥ surarṣibhiḥ sākaṁ codito deva-mātṛbhiḥ*  
*abhyasiñcata dāśārhaṁ govinda iti cābhyadhāt*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus appealed to Kṛṣṇa, mother Surabhi performed his bathing ceremony with her own milk, and Indra, ordered by Aditi and other mothers of the devatās, anointed the Lord with heavenly Gaṅgā water from the trunk of Indra’s elephant carrier, Airāvata in the company of the devatās and great sages and gave the descendant of Daśārha the name Govinda.**

**Комментарий:**

Payasā means with milk. Ordered by the devatā mothers such as Aditi, Indra performed the abhiṣeka also. Thinking himself low, he was reluctant to do the abhiṣeka initially, but, ordered by the devatā mothers, and thus gaining qualification, he did so. He gave the descendant of Daśārha the name Govinda.

He said, “You are who known by the cows, the earth and the Vedas.”

### Text 24

*tatrāgatās tumburu-nāradādayo*  
*gandharva-vidyādhara-siddha-cāraṇāḥ*  
*jagur yaśo loka-malāpahaṁ hareḥ*  
*surāṅganāḥ sannanṛtur mudānvitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Tumburu, Nārada and other Gandharvas, along with the Vidyādharas, Siddhas and Cāraṇas, came there to sing the glories of Kṛṣṇa, which purify all people of faults in their bhakti. And the wives of the devatās, filled with joy, danced together in the Lord’s honor.**

### Text 25

*taṁ tuṣṭuvur deva-nikāya-ketavo*  
*hy avākiraṁś cādbhuta-puṣpa-vṛṣṭibhiḥ*  
*lokāḥ parāṁ nirvṛtim āpnuvaṁs trayo*  
*gāvas tadā gām anayan payo-drutām*

**Перевод:**

**The most eminent devatās chanted the praises of the Lord and scattered wonderful showers of flowers all around him. All three worlds felt supreme satisfaction, and the cows drenched the surface of the earth with their milk.**

**Комментарий:**

The leaders (ketavaḥ) of the devatās included persons like Varuṇa. They covered (āvakiran) him with remarkable showers of flowers. The cows made the earth (gām) wet (drutām) with milk.

### Text 26

*nānā-rasaughāḥ sarito vṛkṣā āsan madhu-sravāḥ*  
*akṛṣṭa pacyauṣadhayo girayo ’bibhran un maṇīn*

**Перевод:**

**Rivers flowed with various kinds of tasty liquids, trees exuded honey, edible plants came to maturity without cultivation, and hills gave forth jewels formerly hidden in their interiors.**

**Комментарий:**

The rivers flowed with various tasty liquids, such as milk. The mountains where herbs ripened without cultivation (akṛṣṭa-pacya),manifested attractive gems (unmaṇīn).

### Text 27

*kṛṣṇe ’bhiṣikta etāni sarvāṇi kuru-nandana*  
*nirvairāṇy abhavaṁs tāta krūrāṇy api nisargataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Parīkṣit, beloved of the Kuru dynasty, upon the ceremonial bathing of Kṛṣṇa, all living creatures, even those cruel by nature, became entirely free of enmity.**

**Комментарий:**

All living beings became friendly.

### Text 28

*iti go-gokula-patiṁ govindam abhiṣicya saḥ*  
*anujñāto yayau śakro vṛto devādibhir divam*

**Перевод:**

**After he had ceremonially bathed Govinda, who is the master of the cows and the cowherd community, Indra took the Lord’s permission and, surrounded by the devatās and other higher beings, returned to his heavenly abode.**

**Комментарий:**

Indra left with permission along with Surabhi.

## Chapter 28 - Kṛṣṇa Rescues Nanda Mahārāja

### Text 1

*śrī-bādarāyaṇir uvāca*  
*ekādaśyāṁ nirāhāraḥ samabhyarcya janārdanam*  
*snātuṁ nandas tu kālindyāṁ dvādaśyāṁ jalam āviśat*

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bādarāyaṇi said: Having worshiped Lord Janārdana, Nanda Mahārāja, who fasted on the Ekādaśī day, entered the water of the Kālindī on the Dvādaśī to take his bath.**

**Комментарий:**

*aṣṭāviṁśe tu nandasyānayanaṁ varuṇa-stutiḥ \|*  
*gopān prati svagoloka-darśanaṁ cābhidhīyate*

**In the twenty-eighth chapter, Varuṇa taking Nanda, Varuṇa’s praise of Kṛṣna, and showing Goloka to the cowherds are described.**

Nanda woke up and offered special worship according to the rules. He fasted in order to spread bhakti to the Lord, though he hadalready achieved the highest success.

### Text 2

*taṁ gṛhītvānayad bhṛtyo varuṇasyāsuro ’ntikam*  
*avajñāyāsurīṁ velāṁ praviṣṭam udakaṁ niśi*

**Перевод:**

**Because Nanda Mahārāja entered the water in the dark of night, disregarding that demonic time, a demoniac servant of Varuṇa seized him and brought him to his master.**

**Комментарий:**

Varuṇa’s servant who was demonic, seized Nanda and brought him to Varuṇa. The reason for that is that not knowing the demonic timing, ignoring it, Nanda had entered the water in the night. Nanda, who knew scriptures, bathed on dvādaśī, whose only a kalā (a unit of time) was remaining, for breaking the fast.

*kalārdhāṁ dvādaśīṁ dṛṣṭvā niśīthād urdhvam eva hi*  
*āmadhyāhnāḥ kriyāḥ sarvāḥ kartavyāḥ śambhu-śāsanāt*

**Seeing half a kalā of Dvādaśī, from the end of night onwards one should perform all rituals to be performed up till noon according to the order of Śiva.**

By the strength of this scripture, Nanda, who was desirous of following this rule, entered the water at night to bathe. A servant of Varuṇa, not knowing this rule took Nanda.

*varuṇasya jaleśasya garva-nāśaṁ kṛpāṁ tathā \|*  
*kariṣyatā pitus tejaḥ stambhitaṁ pūtanāriṇā*

**Kṛṣṇa gave mercy to Varuṇa after destroying his pride. He established his power in the eyes of his father.**

### Text 3

*cukruśus tam apaśyantaḥ kṛṣṇa rāmeti gopakāḥ*  
*bhagavāṁs tad upaśrutya pitaraṁ varuṇāhṛtam*  
*tad-antikaṁ gato rājan svānām abhaya-do vibhuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King, not seeing Nanda Mahārāja, the cowherd men loudly cried out, “O Kṛṣṇa! O Rāma!” Lord Kṛṣṇa heard their cries and understood that his father had been captured by Varuṇa. Therefore the almighty Lord, who makes his devotees fearless, went to the court of Varuṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The cowherds, protectors of Nanda, who had gone to take bath at night, cried out. Kṛṣṇa, though sleeping far off on a bed of flowers, heard the shouts from close (upa) since he is all-pervasive. He understood that his father had been taken by Varuṇa. He asked, “Where did my father sink in the water?” The guards pointed out the place where he had sunk. From the bank, he jumped into the water and went to Varuṇa. Kṛṣṇa was the giver of fearlessness to his relatives. Bringing his father from Varuṇa, he would make his relatives fearless.

### Text 4

*prāptaṁ vīkṣya hṛṣīkeśaṁ loka-pālaḥ saparyayā*  
*mahatyā pūjayitvāha tad-darśana-mahotsavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that the Lord had arrived, Varuṇa worshiped him with elaborate offerings since he was joyful upon seeing the Lord. He spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Varuṇa (loka-pālaḥ) saw Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 5

*śrī-varuṇa uvāca*  
*adya me nibhṛto deho ’dyaivārtho ’dhigataḥ prabho*  
*tvat-pāda-bhājo bhagavann avāpuḥ pāram adhvanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Varuṇa said: O Lord! Now my body has attained fulfillment since I have attained the greatest treasure. O Supreme Lord, those who accept your lotus feet easily attain liberation from saṁsāra.**

**Комментарий:**

My body is fulfilled today by seeing you. Before this, my bodies were uselessly held, since I did not see you. Though Lord of a jeweled palace, I have today become successful since everything I previously gained was insignificant. O Lord! Persons who worship your feet obtain the destruction (pāraṁ) of saṁsāra (adhvanaḥ). But I have seen you. Thus I am greatly fortunate.

### Text 6

*namas tubhyaṁ bhagavate brahmaṇe paramātmane*  
*na yatra śrūyate māyā loka-sṛṣṭi-vikalpanā*

**Перевод:**

**My obeisances unto Bhagavān, Paramātmā and Brahman within whom there is no trace of the illusory energy, which orchestrates the creation of this world.**

**Комментарий:**

The words bhagavate, brahmaṇe, and paramātmane were explained in verse SB [1.2.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.11). Those explanations should be seen. In you,māyā, which makes arrangements for creation the world, is not perceived.

### Text 7

*ajānatā māmakena mūḍhenākārya-vedinā*  
*ānīto ’yaṁ tava pita tad bhavān kṣantum arhati*

**Перевод:**

**Your father, who is sitting here, was brought to me by a foolish, ignorant servant of mine who did not understand his proper duty. Therefore, please forgive us.**

**Комментарий:**

“Though Nanda, true to his vows was taken by force, since you have praised me, you should not have shame.’

This servant did not know the scriptural rule that one can enter the water for bathing at the end of night for completing nitya-kriyāswhen a little of the dvādaśī remains. Thus, he is a fool. By the offense of the servant, I also have committed offense. He brought your father, the king of Vraja, here not knowing what is to be done. Nanda was sitting on jeweled seat. Varuṇa pointed him out with his folded hands, as he, absorbed in remembering Nārāyaṇa, was being worshipped by Varuṇa. You, being an ocean of mercy, should forgive me as you forgave Indra. Otherwise punish me as you please.

### Text 8

*mamāpy anugrahaṁ kṛṣṇa kartum arhasy aśeṣa-dṛk*  
*govinda nīyatām eṣa pitā te pitṛ-vatsala*

**Перевод:**

**O Kṛṣṇa, O seer of everything, please give your mercy even to me. O Govinda! You are most affectionate to your father. Please take him home.**

**Комментарий:**

He suggests that Kṛṣṇa had given great mercy to Indra. You gave great mercy to Indra. This is understood by mentioning Govinda.

### Text 9

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*evaṁ prasāditaḥ kṛṣṇo bhagavān īśvareśvaraḥ*  
*ādāyāgāt sva-pitaraṁ bandhūnāṁ cāvahan mudam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus satisfied by Varuṇa, Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, Lord of lords, returned with his father, giving joy to all their friends.**

**Комментарий:**

“How can Kṛṣṇa be pleased just by that, for such great offense?” He was Bhagavān, omniscient. He knew that actually there as no fault in Varuṇa. He returned with Nanda before the sun rose.

### Text 10

*nandas tv atīndriyaṁ dṛṣṭvā loka-pāla-mahodayam*  
*kṛṣṇe ca sannatiṁ teṣāṁ jñātibhyo vismito ’bravīt*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja had been astonished to see for the first time the great opulence of Varuṇa, the ruler of the ocean planet, and also to see how Varuṇa and his servants had offered such humble respect to Kṛṣṇa. Nanda described all this to his fellow cowherd men.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the great wealth (mahodayam) of loka-pālas, which astonishes the senses (atīndriyam), Nanda described it to his relatives.

### Text 11

*te cautsukya-dhiyo rājan matvā gopās tam īśvaram*  
*api naḥ sva-gatiṁ sūkṣmām upādhāsyad adhīśvaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[Hearing about Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes with Varuṇa,\] the cowherd men considered that Kṛṣṇa must be the Supreme Lord, and their minds, O King, were filled with eagerness. They thought, “Will the Supreme Lord bestow upon us his abode?”**

**Комментарий:**

The cowherds, relatives (te), became eager (autsukya-dhiyaḥ). They, whose conception of supreme opulence had sprung up because of the respect given by the loka-pālas, thought that Kṛṣṇa was the Supreme Lord. Will the Lord have us attain his abode beyond māyā (sūkṣmām). This was their eagerness.

Since it is always said that the cowherds were his friends, and since it is said that he was similar to the cowherds in qualities andforms (Krama-dīpikā), even though without doubt the cowherds had knowledge of the Lord’s planet, still by the Lord’s līlā-śakti that knowledge was covered, for accomplishing a display of that planet now, as in Baladeva being covered during the pastime of bewildering Brahmā and Arjuna when Gītā was spoken.

### Text 12

*iti svānāṁ sa bhagavān vijñāyākhila-dṛk svayam*  
*saṅkalpa-siddhaye teṣāṁ kṛpayaitad acintayat*

**Перевод:**

**Because he sees everything, Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, automatically understood what the cowherd men were conjecturing. Wanting to show his compassion to them by fulfilling their desires, the Lord thought as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Svānām means “of his relatives.” The Lord, fully capable of fulfilling all desires (bhagavān), understanding his relatives’ decision, since he is omniscient (akhila-dṛk), to fulfill their desire he thought as follows.

### Text 13

*jano vai loka etasminn avidyā-kāma-karmabhiḥ*  
*uccāvacāsu gatiṣu na veda svāṁ gatiṁ bhraman*

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa thought:\] My eternal associates, wandering in this world among people who take higher and lower bodies because of karma, desire and ignorance, do not recognize my eternal abode.**

**Комментарий:**

By their omniscience covered by my līlā-śakti, these people act as if not knowing my actual svarūpa, though they know. In this world, materialistic people, by actions instigated by desire for objects arising from ignorance, the cause of material intelligence here,wandering in various bodies (gatiṣu) such as devatā or human, do not know the tripāda-vibhūti world (svāṁ gatiṁ) attainable by their puruṣārtha, though they are in front of me. That is correct. These friends of mine, the cowherds, though omniscient because of being my eternal associates and having qualities equal to mine, desire to see my abode because of the līlā-śakti, most inconceivable, covering their knowledge. One should not say that the statement of this verse is directed to his devotees since this would contradict statements saying that they are completely devoted to him. One should see these statements:

*tāsām avirataṁ kṛṣṇe kurvatīnāṁ sutekṣaṇam*  
*na punaḥ kalpate rājan saṁsāro ‘jñāna-sambhavaḥ*

**These cows and women who took Kṛṣṇa as their son constantly were not qualified for saṁsāra, which produces ignorance. (SB** [**10.6.39**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/6.39)**)**

*aho bhāgyam aho bhāgyaṁ nanda-gopa-vrajaukasām*  
*yan-mitraṁ paramānandaṁ pūrṇaṁ brahma sanātanam*

**How greatly fortunate are Nanda Mahārāja, the cowherd men and all the other inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi! There is no limit to their good fortune, because the Absolute Truth, the source of transcendental bliss, the eternal Supreme Brahman, has become their friend. (SB** [**10.14.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.33)**)**

*yat-pāda-pāṁsur bahu-janma-kṛcchrato dhṛtātmabhir yogibhir apy alabhyaḥ*  
*sa eva yad-dṛg-viṣayaḥ svayaṁ sthitaḥ kiṁ varṇyate diṣṭam ato vrajaukasām*

**Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, whose foot dust cannot be seen by yogīs, who have focussed minds, though they have controlled their mind by severe hardship for many births, is eternally situated here, directly visible to the eyes of the people of Vraja. Ah! How can the good fortune of the people of Vraja be described? (SB** [**10.12.12**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/12.12)**)**

*kṛṣṇe ‘rpitātma-suhṛd-artha-kalatra-kāmā*

**They had offered Kṛṣṇa everything—their very selves, their families, their wealth, wives and all pleasures. (SB** [**10.16.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/16.10)**)**

Thus what is said is proper.

### Text 14

*iti sañcintya bhagavān mahā-kāruṇiko hariḥ*  
*darśayām āsa lokaṁ svaṁ gopānāṁ tamasaḥ param*

**Перевод:**

**Thus, deeply considering the situation, the he showed the planet of the cowherds.**

**Комментарий:**

He showed to the cowherds their own planet (svaṁ lokaṁ). The Gokula that they were perceiving was manifested within that.

### Text 15

*satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ yad brahma-jyotiḥ sanātanam*  
*yad dhi paśyanti munayo guṇāpāye samāhitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa revealed the place which was existence, knowledge, infinity, eternity, and self-effulgent. Sages see that place in trance, when their consciousness is free of the modes of material nature.**

**Комментарий:**

That planet is described. It exists in past, present and future (satyam). It reveals other things (jñānam). It is unlimited (anantam). It is full of great qualities (brahma). It is self-manifesting (jyotiḥ). It is unchanging (sanātanam), devoid of restriction of qualities.

In Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad beginning with divye brahma-pure hy eṣa vyomany ātmā pratiṣṭitaḥ: The Lord resides in the spiritual sky inVaikuṇṭha, the city is described:

*brahmaivedam amṛtaṁ purastād brahma paścād brahma dakṣiṇataś cottareṇa*  
*adhaś cordhvaṁ ca prasṛtaṁ brahmaivedaṁ viśvam idaṁ variṣṭham*

**Brahman is spread in front. Brahman is spread behind. Brahman is spread to the right and to the left. Brahman is spread above and below. The whole world is excellent Brahman. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)**

In the Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad it is said:

*tāsāṁ madhye sākṣāt brahma-gopāla-puri*

**Among them is the city of Gopāla, directly brahman. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

By acintya-śakti it takes the form of such a city due to the following sūtra:

*antarā bhūta-grāmavat svātmanaḥ*

**In the city of Brahman, objects which seem to be made of the elements appear to the devotee. (Brahma-sūtra)**

The sages in the state of being devoid of guṇas (guṇāpāye) see this place.

*tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṁ padaṁ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ*

**Devotees always see the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. (Ṛg Veda)**

### Text 16

*te tu brahma-hradam nītā magnāḥ kṛṣṇena coddhṛtāḥ*  
*dadṛśur brahmaṇo lokaṁ yatrākrūro ’dhyagāt purā*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa brought the cowherd men to Brahma-hrada, made them enter the water, and then lifted them up from it. Where Akrūra saw Vaikuṇṭha previously, the cowherd men saw Goloka.**

**Комментарий:**

The method for seeing the abode, in order to teach that that is highest goal, is described. The cowherds (te) were brought by Kṛṣṇa to Brahma-hrada. They were immersed in it and brought out. They then saw Kṛṣṇa’s planet (brahmaṇo lokam), which was described assatyam jñānam anantam (verse 15).

“What is this Brahma-hrada?” It is called Akrūra-tīrtha. It is described in the past tense since Akrura saw Vaikuṇṭha there, previous to the conversation between Śukadeva and Parīkṣit. This indicates that Vaikuṇṭha along with Viṣṇu exist there.

### Text 17

*nandādayas tu taṁ dṛṣṭvā paramānanda-nirvṛtāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ ca tatra cchandobhiḥ stūyamānaṁ su-vismitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja and the other cowherd men felt the greatest happiness when they saw that abode. They were especially amazed to see Kṛṣṇa there, surrounded by the personified scriptures, who were offering him prayers.**

**Комментарий:**

The master of that planet was Kṛṣṇa! Seeing that planet and there Kṛṣṇa being praised by the śrutis like Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad withmantras such as eko vaśī sarvagaḥ kṛṣnā iḍya, they experienced the highest bliss, natural to their prema but were most astonishedbecause of seeing Kṛṣṇa’s friendly nature. Just by bathing in the tīrtha they could see his planet as the manner described. Having their desire fulfilled, being free of doubt, they came back with Kṛṣṇa to their own places.

## Chapter 29 - Kṛṣṇa and the Gopīs Meet for the Rāsa Dance

### Text 1

*śrī-bādarāyaṇir uvāca*  
*bhagavān api tā rātṛīḥ śāradotphulla-mallikāḥ*  
*vīkṣya rantuṁ manaś cakre yoga-māyām upāśritaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bādarāyaṇi said: Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, upon seeing those autumn nights scented with blossoming jasmine flowers, taking shelter of his yogamāya, decided to fulfill the desires of the gopīs.**

**Комментарий:**

*rasaṁ yam āhuḥ śrutayaḥ pareśaṁ guṇārṇavaṁ cid-ghanam ambudābhaṁ*  
*\| pītāmbaraṁ veṇu-dharaṁ kiśoraṁ sa nanda-sūnus tanutāṁ mudaṁ naḥ*

**May the son of Nanda, whom the śrutis call rasa, who is the Supreme Lord, an ocean of good qualities, condensed knowledge, endowed with the complexion of a cloud, who wears yellow cloth, plays the flute, and is of kaiśora age, bestow to us bliss.**

*jānāti yāṁ nanda-sutaḥ pumarthaṁ svayaṁ pumartho’pi nijaṁ pareśaḥ \|*  
*sā rādhikā śrī-nikarādhikāme rāseśvarī hṛt-kamale cakāstu*

**May Rādhikā, queen of rāsa dance, the essence of beauty, whom Kṛṣṇa knows as the goal of life, thought he himself is the Supreme Lord and goal, manifest in the lotus of my heart which is extremely eager.**

*kṛṣṇaṁ ca rādhāṁ ca tayor viśuddhāṁ līlāṁ ca yo vetti budho yathāvat \|*  
*virakta-cūḍāmaṇir iddha-bhāvaḥ sa māṁ munir vyāsa-sutaḥ punātu*

**May intelligent Śukadeva, son of Vyāsa, who knows Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā and their pure pastime as it is, who is the crest jewel of renunciates and who shines with prema, purify me.**

*una-triṁśe veṇu-nādo rukṣatābhāsikā giraḥ \|*  
*vikrīḍitaṁ tato’ntardhi-kautukaṁ ceti varṇyate*

**In the twenty-ninth chapter Kṛṣṇa playing the flute, his apparently rough words to the gopīs, sporting with them and then disappearing for fun are described.**

Kṛṣṇa endowed with his parā śakti, who is known as Parabrahman, is the essence of rasa due to the following śruti statements:

parākya-śaktir vividhaiva śruyate: the parā śakti takes various forms. (Śvetāśvtara Upaniṣad)

raso vai saḥ: the Lord is rasa. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)

Rasa is rati for the Lord combined with vibhāva and other elements. That rasa is distinct from material rasa and unlimited since it isestablished in śrutis and smṛtis that rati for the Lord is the essence of the hlādinī and saṁvit śaktis, and that the ālambanas and uddīpanas (vibhāvas) – the Lord, his associates, his abodes and his vibhūtis – are the form of knowledge and bliss, and since by positive and negative logic anubhāvas and sañcārī-bhāvas are not too different from rati. It is chiefly manifested in Kṛṣṇa and his associates as ālambanas since they are free from material limitation of fear, etc. By the Lord’s mercy a portion of this rasa is spread to cultured people.

Kṛṣṇa, the essence of rasa, appearing here, experienced and had others experience pastimes in vātsalya, sakhya and dāsya with devotees in those rasas. These have been described. Now, revealing his pastimes of mādhurya, the king of rasas, which he performed with his beloveds, his devotees, there was an occasion for embarrassment in experiencing and having them experienced. Thus Śukadeva beings to describe this in five chapters, the life airs of the scripture (i.e. comparing the five chapters to the five prāṇas). Api indicates aggregation in the phrase bhagavān api (i.e. Bhagavān and his beloveds had made up their mind to enjoy).

*pītvā mukunda-mukha-sāragham akṣi-bhṛṅgais*  
*tāpaṁ jahur viraha-jaṁ vraja-yoṣito ‘hni*  
*tat sat-kṛtiṁ samadhigamya viveśa goṣṭhaṁ*  
*savrīḍa-hāsa-vinayaṁ yad apāṅga-mokṣam*

**With their beelike eyes, the women of Vṛndāvana drank the honey of the beautiful face of Lord Mukunda, and thus they gave up the distress they had felt during the day because of separation from Him. The young Vṛndāvana ladies cast sidelong glances at the Lord—glances filled with bashfulness, laughter and submission—and Śrī Kṛṣṇa, completely accepting these glances as a proper offering of respect, entered the cowherd village. (SB** [**10.15.43**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/15.43)**)**

Rādhā’s friends filled with attraction, had decided to enjoy. The Lord, though also attracted, delayed but, seeing the proper time, also decided to enjoy. Or bhagavān api means though he was full of the six opulences, he decided to enjoy. Thus he becomes complete in his svarūpa by that rati. That internal rati had attained its fruit. In Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad there is a question: by knowing whatperson is everything known? The answer is: by knowing the lover of the gopīs everything is known.

In this way, the explanations of the dull-minded that the rati with the gopīs is imitation of humans or to attract people’s hearts, are rejected.

The uddīpana of rati in the pastime is mentioned. He saw the nights. Going home in the evening of the full moon, after his mother left the room, he went out by the opening for moonlight in the bedroom. Tā (in tā rātrīr) are the devatās of the night who come for service, whom he had either promised to enjoy (in SB [10.22.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.27)) or who were famous for their qualities such as clearness. This is the excellence of the nights.

Because of the autumn those nights were full of blossoming jasmines even in autumn. There were also kunda flowers:

*kunda-srajaḥ kula-pater iha vātigandhaḥ*

**blowing this way is the fragrance of his garland of kunda flowers. (SB** [**10.30.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/30.11)**)**

Lotus bloomed even in the night:

*juṣṭaṁ tat-taralānandi kumudāmoda-vāyunā*

**the wind, enlivened by the river’s waves, bore the fragrance of lotuses. (SB** [**10.29.45**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.45)**)**

This is the excellence of Vṛndāvana. Nights is in the plural to suggest that in one night there was a night of Brahmā, otherwise within three yāmās there could not be the mutual experience of the beauty, sweetness, fragrance, and three types of instrumental music of the unlimited gopīs and a mine of gem-like qualities of his, the best hero. It will be said brahma-rātra upāvṛtte: after an entire night of Brahmā had passed, Lord Kṛṣṇa advised the gopīs to return to their homes. (SB [10.33.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/33.38)) Thus, the night of Brahmā fit within the three yāmās of one night for the completion of the great festival of the rāsa dance and there was an arrangement for spreading a screen to keep the pastime private. How could that happen? He took shelter of yoga-māyā, his parā śakti who makes the impossiblepossible. This means he ordered yoga-māyā to adjust everything.

### Text 2

*tadoḍurājaḥ kakubhaḥ karair mukhaṁ*  
*prācyā vilimpann aruṇena śantamaiḥ*  
*sa carṣaṇīnām udagāc chuco mṛjan*  
*priyaḥ priyāyā iva dīrgha-darśanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The moon then rose, anointing the face of the eastern horizon with the reddish hue of his comforting rays, and thus dispelling the pain of all who watched him rise. The moon was like a beloved husband who returns after a long absence and adorns the face of his beloved wife with red kuṅkuma.**

**Комментарий:**

After these uddīpanas, the moon personally appeared. The full moon (uḍurājaḥ) rose (udagāt) then. What did it do? It tinged with red by its joyful rays the face (middle) of the eastern direction.

Seeing after a long time, or with long eyes (dīrgha-darśanaḥ), gazing with unblinking eyes out of great thirst, the lover anoints the face of his beloved with red kuṅkuma by his hands (rays). It removed (mṛjan) the fatigue from the autumn sun (śucaḥ) for people (carṣaṇīnāṁ).

The gopīs, who were dedicated to Kṛṣṇa’s happiness alone, worried (śucaḥ) from separation arising from pride. They were like the eastern direction, wives of the moon, attracted to him. Just as the moon, the beloved, colored the face of his lover using his rays, I will color the faces of the gopīs attracted to me, by taking kuṅkuma in my hand. This was the bhāva of Kṛṣṇa, stimulated by the night. Hands is in the plural to indicate many actions.

### Text 3

*dṛṣṭvā kumudvantam akhaṇḍa-maṇḍalaṁ*  
*ramānanābhaṁ nava-kuṅkumāruṇam*  
*vanaṁ ca tat-komala-gobhī rañjitaṁ*  
*jagau kalaṁ vāma-dṛśāṁ manoharam*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa saw the unbroken disk of the full moon glowing with the red effulgence of newly applied vermilion, as if it were the face of Rādhā. He also saw the kumuda lotuses opening in response to the moon’s presence and the forest gently illumined by its rays. Thus the Lord began to play sweetly on his flute, attracting the minds of the beautiful-eyed gopīs.**

**Комментарий:**

Having gone to Vṛndāvana and remembering the faces of his beloveds on seeing the disk of the moon, he devised a method forcalling them.

He saw the moon (kumudavantam), which had lotus which had to be blossomed, a full disk (akhaṇḍa-maṇḍalaṁ), which had the effulgence (ābham) of the faces of Rādhā, Mahālakṣmī of Gokula and her friends, the gopīs (ramānā), red like ball of fresh kuṅkumaas it rose. The face becomes red by applying kuṅkuma. He also saw the forest colored by the soft rays of the moon.

On the other hand, since the modifier and the noun are not specified, the following can be said. He saw himself as the giver of joy forthe earth (kumudvantaṁ) and due to whom the complexion which indicated inner amorous feelings of the women was completelymature (akhaṇḍa-maṇdalam). It was red from application of unguents made of kuṅkuma. The forest was colored by the soft effulgence of his limbs. Seeing theses two types vibhāvas – the uddīpanas and ālambanas, he sang sweet, indistinct sounds on his flute. They were sweet to attract the gopīs and they were indistinct so that each would think it was calling them by name. He played the flute in such a way as to attract the minds of the gopīs endowed with crooked glances (vāma-dṛśām).

And esoterically even the kāma-bīja is indicated by the combination kala (k + l) with vāma-dṛśāṁ representing ī. Mana is anusvāra and hara is candrabindu. Thus, he sang the kāma-bīja, arising from himself.

### Text 4

*niśamya gītāṁ tad anaṅga-vardhanaṁ*  
*vraja-striyaḥ kṛṣṇa-gṛhīta-mānasāḥ*  
*ājagmur anyonyam alakṣitodyamāḥ*  
*sa yatra kānto java-lola-kuṇḍalāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When the young women of Vṛndāvana heard Kṛṣṇa’s flute song, which arouses romantic feelings, their minds were captivated by the Lord. They came to where their lover waited, each unknown to the others, moving so quickly that their earrings swung back and forth.**

**Комментарий:**

Then what happened? The beloveds of Kṛṣṇa (vraja-striyaḥ), hearing that flute song which stimulated prema which desired only their lover’s happiness (anaṅga-vardhanaṁ), which was composed of the kāma-bīja, their minds, with their composure, memory andshyness (gṛhīta-mānasāḥ) stolen by Kṛṣṇa, came to him.

*premaiva gopa-rāmānāṁ kāma ity agamat prathām*

**The pure love of the gopīs has become celebrated by the name kāma. (BRS)**

Remembering the song, they came to him like puppets strung on the thread of the flute’s soft song.

“They came”, is stated with the conception that he (Śukadeva) is situated close to Kṛṣṇa. Where did they come? They came to where Kṛṣṇa, their lover, most attractive, or who is full of happiness. Their ornaments like earrings, necklaces and bracelets swung by their fast pace. They made attempts unseen by others since they lost discrimination when their minds became attracted to the flute.

### Text 5

*duhantyo ’bhiyayuḥ kāścid dohaṁ hitvā samutsukāḥ*  
*payo ’dhiśritya saṁyāvam anudvāsyāparā yayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Some of the gopīs were milking cows when they heard Kṛṣṇa’s flute. They stopped milking and went off to meet him. Some left milk on the stove, and others left cakes burning in the oven.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses describe how they came to him. Some gave up milking cows and went to him because of intense longing. Others left milk in pots on the stove without waiting for the milk to boil. Others left without taking wheat cakes off the fire though they were cooked. These were Dhanyā and other kanyās (unmarried girls).

### Texts 6-7

*pariveṣayantyas tad dhitvā pāyayantyaḥ śiśūn payaḥ*  
*śuśrūṣantyaḥ patīn kāścid aśnantyo ’pāsya bhojanam*

*limpantyaḥ pramṛjantyo ’nyā añjantyaḥ kāś ca locane*  
*vyatyasta-vastrābharaṇāḥ kāścit kṛṣṇāntikaṁ yayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Some of them were serving servants and friends food, feeding milk to their infants or rendering personal service to their husbands, or taking their evening meals, but they all gave up these duties and went to meet Kṛṣṇa. Others were putting on cosmetics, cleansing themselves or applying kajjala to their eyes. But all the gopīs stopped these activities at once and, though their clothes and ornaments were in complete disarray, rushed off to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Others gave up serving food. Others gave up feeding milk to nephews. Others gave up serving water, etc., to apparent husbands.These were gopīs who were qualified for giving up the body. Others gave up eating their meal.

Others were putting catuḥsama on their bodies. Some were rubbing their bodies with ungents (pramṛjantyaḥ). Others were applying eye ointment and stopped with one eye only decorated. These were nitya-siddha sakhīs. Some put on their clothing and ornaments in opposite manner and went to Kṛṣṇa. This is the anubhāva calledvibhrama.

*vallabha-prāpti-velāyāṁ madanāveśa-sambhramāt\|*  
*vibhramo hāra-mālyādi-bhūṣā-sthāna-viparyayaḥ*

**When, at the time of going to meet her lover, the heroine places necklaces, flower-garlands and other ornaments in the wrong places, when agitated by the onslaught of intense passion, it is called vibhrama. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 11.39)**

Due to these symptoms, these were leaders of groups to be served by the sakhīs. All of these gopīs, endowed with clothing by yoga- māyā, with proper eye ointments, with fickle, shining, creeper like bodies, with eyes extending to their ears, with waists narrow as fists, with bimba lips and with ruby-like teeth, beckoned their lover, black like a cloud.

### Text 8

*tā vāryamāṇāḥ patibhiḥ pitṛbhir bhrātṛ-bandhubhiḥ*  
*govindāpahṛtātmāno na nyavartanta mohitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Their husbands, fathers, brothers and other relatives tried to stop them, but they had lost all discrimination, since Kṛṣṇa had already stolen their hearts. They refused to turn back. Thus they could not be prevented.**

**Комментарий:**

“One sees even sādhakas giving up all dependence on others because scriptural orders of the Lord. It is not remarkable then insiddhas. But why did the husbands give up dependence on them?” Though prevented by husbands they did not return because Kṛṣṇa had stolen their hearts.

Sādhakas, hearing topics of Govinda, cannot be made to return from that path, then by whom can the siddhas, having seen his beauty, being very strong like monsoon rivers, be prevented? For those whose minds attracted to the Lord, obstacles have no power. Moreover, they were enchanted (mohitāḥ).

Seeing their replicas which were manifested by yogamāyā, they left. The husbands saw these forms and remained calm. This will be made clear later.

### Text 9

*antar-gṛha-gatāḥ kāścid gopyo ’labdha-vinirgamāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ tad-bhāvanā-yuktā dadhyur mīlita-locanāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Some of the gopīs, however, could not manage to get out of their houses, and instead they remained home with eyes closed, meditating upon him in pure love.**

**Комментарий:**

In the pure pastimes of Kṛṣṇa’s, Parabrahma’s mādhurya-rāsa, also called ujjvala or śuci, the gopīs with pure forms went out. But those with some contamination, though having bhāva did not go.

Some gopīs, with impure bodies remained within their houses. Due to being locked up by husbands, they could not go outside.Though previously they were engaged in thinking of him, now they meditated on him internally.

### Texts 10-11

*duḥsaha-preṣṭha-viraha-tīvra-tāpa-dhutāśubhāḥ*  
*dhyāna-prāptācyutāśleṣa-nirvṛtyā kṣīṇa-maṅgalāḥ*

*tam eva paramātmānaṁ jāra-buddhyāpi saṅgatāḥ*  
*jahur guṇa-mayaṁ dehaṁ sadyaḥ prakṣīṇa-bandhanāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**For those gopīs who could not go to see Kṛṣṇa, intolerable separation from their beloved caused an intense agony that burns away the pain of temporary separation. By meditating upon him they realized his embrace and experienced the bliss of a sudden internal realization of meeting him. Although Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Soul, these girls simply thought of him as an illicit lover and associated with him in that intimate mood. Thus the bondage of the house was nullified and they give up gross material bodies.**

**Комментарий:**

Giving up their impure bodies, they quickly attained him. This is explained in two verses. They purify those who listen to this pastime of inauspicious elements by the intense pain of separation from Kṛṣṇa. They experienced highest bliss by embraces of Kṛṣṇa who was attained by meditation. The auspicious elements of those who listen to this pastime are destroyed by that highest bliss. The pain of separation from him and the bliss of his embrace destroy the listeners’ prārabdhas both auspicious and inauspicious. They arefreed from saṁsāra. One should not say, “the gopīs’ sin and piety which begin with material bodies are destroyed by the sufferingand happiness arising from separation and union with the Lord since these can only by destroyed by experiencing their results.” Since separation and union with the Lord are not the results of sin or piety. Devotees have their prārabdha-karmas destroyed at the stage of anartha-nivṛtti. They remain in their bodies by the Lord’s will, whose result is preaching bhakti, like a burned-up rope. This is the conclusion of those who know the truth.

Then they associated with their master (paramātmānam) Kṛṣṇa along with thinking of him as jāra (illicit lover). They attained him in a special manifestation of Gokula seen by the cowherds after Varuṇa stole Nanda since Uddhava says that the message is that they attained the rāsa dance:

*yā mayā krīḍatā rātryāṁ vane ‘smin vraja āsthitāḥ*  
*alabdha-rāsāḥ kalyāṇyo māpur mad-vīrya-cintayā*

**O fortunate ladies! Although some gopīs had to remain in the cowherd village and so could not join the rāsa dance to sport with me at night in the forest, they attained me by thinking of my potent pastimes. (SB** [**10.47.37**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.37)**)**

Api indicates collection of all those mentioned. The conception of him as an illicit lover should be added in the following verses too (i.e. all the gopīs thought of Kṛṣṇa as an illicit lover, not just the gopīs who were restrained) since Kṛṣṇa says in the Eleventh Canto:

*mat-kāmā ramaṇaṁ jāram asvarūpa-vido ‘balāḥ*  
*brahma māṁ paramaṁ prāpuḥ saṅgāc chata-sahasraśaḥ*

**All those hundreds of thousands of gopīs, understanding me to be their most charming lover and ardently desiring me in that way, were unaware of my actual position. Yet by intimately associating with me, the gopīs attained me, the Supreme Brahman. (SB** [**11.12.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/12.13)**)**

It should not be said, “Their feelings towards him as illicit lover are lowly like that described in, jigāṁsayāpi haraye stanaṁ dattvāpa sad-gatiḥ: Putanā attained a spiritual destination though giving the Lord her breast with the intention of killing him (SB [10.6.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/6.35)) and since it will later be said, jugupsitaṁ ca sarvatra hy aupapatyaṁ kula- striyā: For a woman from a respectable family, petty adulterous affairs are always condemned (SB [10.29.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.26)).”

The gopīs were excellent because their feelings were in conformity to the Lord, and since they were free from adultery in its true sense (i.e. they never had relationships with their husbands in the first place for their relationship with Kṛṣṇa to qualify as adultery) and since the verse beginning with jugupsitaṁ ca (SB [10.29.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.26)) is for the sake of apparently tricking them.

“But could they associate with Kṛṣṇa when they had contaminated bodies?”

Deham (body) is in the singular to represent a class. Immediately giving up bodies made of the guṇas they associated with Kṛṣṇa. Their bodies’ contamination was lifted out of Gokula since it is said that they gave up their material bodies, and then associated with the Lord. They manifested bodies of knowledge and bliss suitable for enjoyment with the Lord, by the parā śakti of the Lord since it is said:

*aśva iva romāṇi vidhūya dhūtvā śarīram*  
*akṛtaṁ kṛtātmā brahma-lokam abhisambhavāni*

**Shedding the material body like a horse shaking his mane, I, being successful, attain the spiritual world. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad** [**8.13.1**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/chan-upa/part-8.chapter-13.8131)**)**

Those bodies which were given up merged into the causal elements by the Lord’s will. Since there was not a particle of impurity in this most auspicious pastime, the gopīs are described as most auspicious (kalyāṇyaḥ) (SB [10.47.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.37)). It was previously explained that by the parā śakti the husbands, who were led to believe in those gopīs’ replicas, were composed. Their bondage of being confined to their houses was destroyed on attaining those pure forms.

### Text 12

*śrī-parīkṣid uvāca*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ viduḥ paraṁ kāntaṁ na tu brahmatayā mune*  
*guṇa-pravāhoparamas tāsāṁ guṇa-dhiyāṁ katham*

**Перевод:**

**Parīkṣit Mahārāja said: O sage, the gopīs knew Kṛṣṇa only as their lover, not as the Supreme Brahman with no qualities. So how could these girls, their minds absorbed in his qualities, give up their spiritual qualities and take another body?**

**Комментарий:**

Since the Supreme Lord was paramour, though worshipped by that conception, the Lord gave them bodies suitable for himself and gave them the result of closeness to himself after they gave up their material bodies. Though knowing this Parīkṣit asks to remove doubts in ignorant people. O sage! Those gopīs knew Kṛṣṇa, as the highest (param) most attractive form giving rati (kāntaṁ), not as Brahman, the form full of knowledge and bliss and unlimited qualities such as being the creator of the universe. Thus how could these gopīs, absorbing their intelligence in the Kṛṣṇa’s qualities of beauty, sweetness, loveliness, friendliness and intelligence, give up bodies made of material guṇas like sattva since we hear thatliberation is attained by brahma-jñāna?

*brahmavid āpnoti paraṁ tad eṣābhyuktā*  
*satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ brahma*

Knowing Brahman one attains the supreme. This verse is uttered by students concerning Brahman:

**Brahman is eternity and infinite knowledge. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)**

*yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante*

**From the Lord all these beings arise. (Taittrīya Upaniṣad)**

*yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukma-varṇam kartāram īśam puruṣam brahma-yoniṁ nirañjanaḥ paramaṁ sāmyam upaiti*

**When the observer sees the golden person, the cause, the agent, the Lord, the source of Brahmā, the person, being pure, attains a form similar to the Supreme Lord. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)**

### Text 13

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*uktaṁ purastād etat te caidyaḥ siddhiṁ yathā gataḥ*  
*dviṣann api hṛṣīkeśaṁ kim utādhokṣaja-priyāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: This point was explained to you previously. Since even Śiśupāla, who hated Kṛṣṇa, again achieved his spiritual body as an associate by thinking of him, then what to speak of the Lord’s dear devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva, knowing that the king knew the conclusion, but chastising those who are not aware through him speaks this verse. Previously, in the seventh canto it was explained to you that Śiśupāla, whose envy had dissipated due to power of his absorption in the Lord and whose demoniac tendency was destroyed, attained perfection of becoming an associate of the Lord, though he hated the Lord. It was said:

*vairānubandha-tīvreṇa dhyānenācyutasātmatāṁ \|*  
*nītau punar hareḥ pārśvaṁ jagmatur viṣṇu-pārṣadāv*

**These two associates of Lord Viṣṇu—Jaya and Vijaya—by meditation with intense, continuous hatred of the Lord, entered Kṛṣṇa, and then went to the side of the Lord as his two associates in Vaikuṇṭha. (SB** [**7.1.47**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/1.47)**)**

But these gopīs, his beloveds who love him, by their meditation on him gaving up their material bodies, having spiritual bodies,attained him. This is not astonishing (kimuta). Kim uta means strong, very good, excessive. In this way since the Lord’s beauty, etc., are also qualities of Brahman just as his being the creator of the universe is, their absorption in him is also brahma-vidyā. Thus by being free from upādhis, liberation in the form of attaining him was accomplished since śruti says brahmavid āpnoti paraṁ: Knowing Brahman one attains the supreme (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) and by the knowledge which was different from material guṇas they hadintelligence since they did address the Lord as Varadeśvara (giver of benedictions, in SB [10.29.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.33)).

### Text 14

*nṛṇāṁ niḥśreyasārthāya vyaktir bhagavato nṛpa*  
*avyayasyāprameyasya nirguṇasya guṇātmanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O King, the Supreme Lord is inexhaustible and immeasurable, and he is untouched by the material modes because he is their controller. His personal appearance in this world is meant for bestowing the highest benefit on humanity.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa descended to deliver persons who have a slight relationship with him. This is expressed in two verses. O King! Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, has appeared to give the supreme goal (niḥśreyasāya) to persons with a slight relationship to him, though being devoid of sādhana, not to relieve the earth of her burden, since that is possible even by some jīva without special qualities. The Lord is devoid of change though he gives himself to each devotee (avyayasya). How can he do this? He is unknowable (aprameyasya). It is impossible to know him. Those who have take shelter of the followng śruti are not dependent on logic.

*dhyāyen mama priyo nityaṁ mokṣam adhigacchati \|*  
*sa mukto bhavati tasmai ātmānaṁ ca dadāmi vai*

**Meditating in this way, he who is dear to me attains eternal liberation. He gives up material bondage. More than that, I give myself to him. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad** [**2.73**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/gopala-tapani/2.73)**)**

“What devotees?” He is beyond the guṇas and creator of the guṇas of māyā (nirguṇasya). He is full of qualities such as omniscience, power, mercy sand affection to devotees (guṇātmanaḥ).

### Text 15

*kāmaṁ krodhaṁ bhayaṁ sneham aikyaṁ sauhṛdam eva ca*  
*nityaṁ harau vidadhato yānti tan-mayatāṁ hi te*

**Перевод:**

**Persons who constantly direct their lust, anger, fear, protective affection, and friendship and goodwill towards the Lord are sure to attain realization of him.**

**Комментарий:**

Thouse who attained him just by a relationship are shown. An example of kāma are the personified Vedas and sages who becamegopīs. An example of anger and hatred is Śiśupāla. Kaṁsa is an example of fear. An example of affection, vātsalya, is Droṇa, Dharā and Nanda. Examples of one-hearted sakhya are Śrīdāma and Subala (aikyam sauhrḍam). Aikyam here means friendship, being ofone heart, due to usages such as hyo-vivādināv etāvad aikyaṁ gatāv: these two who had a quarrel yesterday, have become united (rather than merging). Goodwill is seen in Kratha, Kauśika and others. The Vṛṣṇis, Pāṇḍavas and others constantly showed such relationship. Those who are doing so now, they also attain absorption in him (tan-mayatām), just as a lusty man becomes absorbed in women.

### Text 16

*na caivaṁ vismayaḥ kāryo bhavatā bhagavaty aje*  
*yogeśvareśvare kṛṣṇe yata etad vimucyate*

**Перевод:**

**You should not be so astonished since he is Bhagavān, unborn, the unborn master of all masters of mystic power, endowed with the complete manifestation of qualities, and liberates this world.**

**Комментарий:**

Others may be astonished about the Lord but you should not be astonished about Kṛṣṇa, Bhagavān, endowed with knowledge, power and fame to do the impossible, since from the time in the womb you have known his svarūpa, qualities, pastimes and powers in truth. Though he herds cows, he punishes Brahmā and others. Though born from Devakī’s womb, he is unborn. Though the lover of many young girls, he is known as the master of yoga. He gives position devoid of māyā to those who serve him, though thinking of him as an illicit lover. You should have no doubt in this meaning since by him the world even now becomes liberated by meditating on him with kāma, krodha, etc.

The following should be understood. There are two types of gopīs: the nitya-siddhas and the sādhana-siddhas. The nitya-siddhas areequal to Kṛṣṇa. These are understood in the following statements of śruti and smṛti:

*gopa-gopī-gavāvītaṁ*

**He is surrounded by cowherds, gopīs and cow. (Gopāla- tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

*ānanda-cinmaya-rasa-pratibhāvitābhiḥ*

**He resides in Goloka exclusively with the young gopīs, who are embodiments of madhura-rasa. (Brahma-saṁhitā)**

There are three types of sādhana-siddhas: those who were previously śrutis, those who were previously sages and those who were daughters of devatās. The first type is described in Bṛhad-vāmana Purāṇa:

*kandarpa-koṭi-lāvaṇye tvayi dṛṣṭe manāṁsi naḥ*  
*kāminī-bhāvam āsādya smara-kṣubdhāny asaṁśayāḥ*

**Seeing you with more beauty than millions of Cupids, our minds, undoubtedly agitated by love, assume the mood of the gopīs.**

The second type is described in Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa:

*purā maharṣayaḥ sarve daṇḍakāraṇya-vāsinaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā rāmaṁ hariṁ tatra bhoktum aicchat suvigraham*  
*te sarve strītvam āpannāḥ samudbhūtās tu gokule \|*  
*hariṁ samprāpya kāmena tato muktā bhavārṇavāt*

**Previously, all the sages living in Daṇḍakāraṇya forest, who after seeing Lord Rāma, desired enjoyment with his form, attained forms of women and appeared in Gokula. Attaining the Lord by that kāma, they became liberated from the ocean of the material world. (Padma Purāṇa 6.245.164)**

The third type are described as follows by Kśīrodakaśāyī:

*vasudeva-gṛhe sākṣād bhagavān puruṣaḥ paraḥ*  
*janiṣyate tat-priyārthaṁ sambhavantu sura-striyaḥ*

**The Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who has full potency, will personally appear as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore all the wives of the demigods should also appear in order to satisfy him. (SB** [**10.1.23**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.23)**)**

These four types are described in Padma Purāṇa:

*gopyas tu śrutayo jñeyā ṛṣi-jā gopa-kanyakāḥ*  
*deva-kanyāś ca rājendra na mānuṣyaḥ kathañcana*

**O best of kings! The gopīs, consisted of śrutis, the sages, the nitya-siddha gopīs, and the daughters of the devatās. They are not at all human.**

They are not material human beings (na mānuṣyaḥ). Gopa-kanyā refers to the nitya-siddhas gopīs who are the chief since they are described in the method of worship in the eternal eighteen-syllable mantra and they are never heard of as doing sādhana. But thosegopīs who were kept in their house were daughters of cowherds who came from the bordering places on seeing the increase of happiness in Nanda’s kingdom and had been born in those bordering places.

### Text 17

*tā dṛṣṭvāntikam āyātā bhagavān vraja-yoṣitaḥ*  
*avadad vadatāṁ śreṣṭho vācaḥ peśair vimohayan*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that the girls of Vraja, attracted by his flute, had arrived, Kṛṣṇa, the best of speakers, greeted them with charming words that bewildered their minds.**

**Комментарий:**

Having given the conclusion concerning the contradiction, he continues the story.

He saw that his beloveds, the girls of Vraja, attracted by the flute, had come (āyatā) to him and surrounded him. Facing them all, he spoke. The Lord, the best among skillful speakers who know how to speak according to time, place and candidate, who is endowedwith natural knowledge to the utmost, spoke to bewilder them who were already by the flute (vimohayan) with parts of words. Peśaiḥ is formed from the root piś (to divide), by applying the affix ghañ. Some of the words were affectionate, other parts were rough expressed directly, indirectly and by hint.

By his rough words they understood his indifference, but this did not decrease their affection at all. This showed the purity of their affection. As a hero, he looked at their manifestation of eagerness. He heard their internal words which were disguised by avahittha(hiding emotions). He took away their stubborn mood which was concealed as heroines. These were his goals. Actually, he was not indifferent to them since it was said that he had decided to enjoy with them (verse 1).

He made them blush with the affectionate portion of words also. He bewildered them to determine what was in their minds by wordsrevealing many meanings.

The names of the gopīs are not mentioned. This is expressed in a verse.

*asmat-kathāḥ sadasi no kathayeti tābhir*  
*ukto muniḥ pratijagāda natiṁ dadhānaḥ*  
*līlāḥ pathāmi na tu vaḥ khalu nāma-dheyā*  
*nīty evam artha-parikīrtanataḥ pratītam*

**They said, “Do not relate our topics publicly.” Śukadeva offering respects, answered, “I will recite pastimes but not your names, but these will be known from the glorification of the meaning.”**

### Text 18

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*svāgataṁ vo mahā-bhāgāḥ priyaṁ kiṁ karavāṇi vaḥ*  
*vrajasyānāmayaṁ kaccid brūtāgamana-kāraṇam*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa said: O most fortunate ladies, welcome. What may I do to please you? Is everything well in Vraja? Please tell me the reason for your coming here.**

**Комментарий:**

First Kṛṣṇa seemingly resorting to indifference, speaks following cultured conduct. O most fortunate women! Have you, bearing the burden of dharma such being chaste to husband, come here comfortably (svāgatam)? What can I do to please you? I am asking you. Please order me. In the dear conduct of greatly fortunate women I also should perform special dharma. Having said what is obligatory in welcoming people who have come, taking shelter of proper conduct for fun, seeing them come with confusion, he inquires with deceit, while seeming to have fear and confusion. Is everything well (anāmayam) in Vraja?

“O crest jewel of the clever! If something were wrong, all the cowherds would come.”

“True. Some disaster concerning young girls must have surely occurred.” Guessing in this way by his shrewdness, he replies haughtily. “Please tell me the cause or the purpose of your coming. I will find a solution.” He seemingly shows indifference with a portion of roughness in his words.

However, there is another meaning, which attracts them by an affectionate portion of his words.

(Another meaning)

In sweet interpretation of his words he says, “O most fortunate women! Your fortune is great that such a moonlight, and that too such a forest, and that too such youthfulness of yours, and that too a person like I are all compliant. You have auspiciously come(svāgatam) to me, dear and compliant. Please reveal what is dear to you. Without doubt, I will accomplish it. He speaks the reason for being free of worry. “Vraja is safe since I have destroyed the demons. Please tell me what should be undertaken to begin your pastimes.” This should be considered in latter verses also.

### Text 19

*rajany eṣā ghora-rūpā ghora-sattva-niṣevitā*  
*pratiyāta vrajaṁ neha stheyaṁ strībhiḥ su-madhyamāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**This night is quite frightening, and frightening creatures are lurking about. Return to Vraja, slender-waisted girls. This is not a proper place for women.**

**Комментарий:**

“We have come to pick flowers blossoming in the night.” This night is frightening because it is frequented by ferocious animals. Therefore, turning back, go to Vraja. Delaying is not appropriate. “Why do you remain here?” O beautiful waisted women! It is not proper for beautiful women to stay in the forest at night.

(Another meaning)

Because the full moon has risen, the night is gentle (aghora-rūpā). Since it excites love of people, it is night (ra-janī). It is served by peaceful creatures (aghora-sattva) like bees and cuckoos. Or the night is served by me, whose strength (sattva) gives fear to thewicked (ghora-) and gives fearlessness to the cultured (aghora-). Thus, you should not return at all. You should stay here since the place is suitable for your pastimes. O beautiful waisted women! Such beautiful women should stay with me.

### Text 20

*mātaraḥ pitaraḥ putrā bhrātaraḥ patayaś ca vaḥ*  
*vicinvanti hy apaśyanto mā kṛḍhvaṁ bandhu-sādhvasam*

**Перевод:**

**Not finding you at home, your mothers, fathers, sons, brothers and husbands are certainly searching for you. Don’t cause anxiety for your family members.**

**Комментарий:**

“There should be no worry if many women come to the forest at night.” Not seeing you, your mothers and other will search for you. The sons of your cowives will look for you. Do not create fear in your relatives arising from not seeing you. Therefore, return to Vraja.

(Another meaning)

Your mothers, not seeing you, will just search for you, but they will not see you in this dense forest far away. Thus do not be afraid of them. Perform pastimes with me here in the middle of the night.

### Texts 21-22

*dṛṣṭaṁ vanaṁ kusumitaṁ rākeśa-kara-rañjitam*  
*yamunānila-līlaijat taru-pallava-śobhitam*

*tad yāta mā ciraṁ goṣṭhaṁ śuśrūṣadhvaṁ patīn satīḥ*  
*krandanti vatsā bālāś ca tān pāyayata duhyata*

**Перевод:**

**Now you have seen this Vṛndāvana forest, full of flowers and resplendent with the light of the full moon. You have seen the beauty of the trees, with their leaves trembling in the gentle breeze coming from the Yamunā. So now go back to the cowherd village. Don’t delay. O chaste ladies, serve your husbands and give milk to your crying babies and calves.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks to those who look around in shyness. “I understand you have come to see the forest.” When they look upwards he says, “You have seen the forest is lit by the moon.” When they glance towards the Yamunā, he says, “The forest is beautiful with the sprouts for trees trembling in the gentle (līlā) breeze which touched the Yamunā. Having seen the forest as your desired, return to Vraja.

(Another meaning)

The forest laughs at you about to return home by blossoming with flowers and spreading rays of the moon. Even the Yamunā, yourfriend, forbids you from going by waving the buds on the trees on its bank, by the fickle wind. This forest is most excellent. Moreover it is the full moon night. Moreover it is surrounded by the Yamunā with of wind. These are the three uddīpanas. I am the ālambana of rati. This is the opportunity to manifest your nature as rasikas.

Therefore (tat) because your desire to see the forest is satisfied, go to the village. Do not delay. Serve your husbands. O chaste women! If you do not, your chastity will be broken.

“Giving up chastity we should serve you.” Fearing such a response he replies. The calves and young children are crying. Take care of them. Feed them milk. Milk the cows. Being merciful to them, to the village.

(Another meaning)

Thus (tat), do not go for long time (ciram), the whole night. Do not milk the cows or care for the children or serve the husband.

### Text 23

*atha vā mad-abhisnehād bhavatyo yantritāśayāḥ*  
*āgatā hy upapannaṁ vaḥ prīyante mayi jantavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**On the other hand, perhaps you have come here out of your great love for me, which has taken control of your hearts. This is of course quite commendable on your part, since all living entities possess natural affection for me.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking that imagining any other cause is useless, he says he understands the cause of their coming. Your hearts controlled(yantritāśayāḥ) by intense general affection for me (mad- abhisnehaḥ), you have come here. It has been accomplished (upapannam) by seeing me. That is not surprising because (hi) all living beings, including animals and birds have affection for me. Thus, it is proper that you friendly women have come to see me. It is my natural good fortune that I am the object of everyone’s affection. Therefore, go now.

(Another meaning)

You have controlled my heart by your prema with the mood of a beloved (abhisnehāt). I am attracted by the control of your prema. Thus your coming is proper (upapannam). All beings are attracted to me, what to speak of you, having prema.

### Text 24

*bhartuḥ śuśrūṣaṇaṁ strīṇāṁ paro dharmo hy amāyayā*  
*tad-bandhūnāṁ ca kalyāṇaḥ prajānāṁ cānupoṣaṇam*

**Перевод:**

**The highest religious duty for a woman is to sincerely serve her husband, behave well toward her husband’s family and take good care of her children.**

**Комментарий:**

“If our affection for you is true, then it is also suitable that we serve you.” Fearing this response, he instills fear in them through scriptures on dharma. It is women’s dharma to serve husbands, not someone other than them such as me. Serving husbands is the supreme dharma (paraḥ) compared to other dharmas. “We are doing that properly.” Do it sincerely (amāyayā). Serving the another person is māyā, spoiled by deceit. Your affection for me is against women’s dharma.

(Another meaning)

Since the rule concerns ordinary women, gopīs serving husbands is not the highest dharma but is svakīya. Therefore, that dharma should not be undertaken. Since I am Viṣṇu, for you who have taken Vaiṣṇava dīkṣā, bhakti to me, while giving up other dharmas, is proper.

*ājñāyaivaṁ guṇān doṣān mayādiṣṭān api svakān*  
*dharmān santyajya yaḥ sarvān māṁ bhajeta sa tu sattamaḥ*

**A person who, understanding good and bad aspects of dharma as taught by me gives up all his duties and simply worships me is the best of all. (SB** [**11.11.32**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/11.32)**)**

Or since I, your husband have accepted you by Gāndharva rites like Duṣmanta (refer SB [9.20.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/20.16)), serving this husband is your highest dharma. This should be done sincerely, not using crooked words. Rest is clear.

### Text 25

*duḥśīlo durbhago vṛddho jaḍo rogy adhano ’pi vā*  
*patiḥ strībhir na hātavyo lokepsubhir apātakī*

**Перевод:**

**Women who desire a good destination in the next life should never abandon a husband who has not fallen from his religious standards, even if he is obnoxious, unfortunate, old, inactive, sickly or poor.**

**Комментарий:**

“How can we, who have affection for you, serve husbands who are unfavorable!”

Husbands who are sinless should not be given up by women who desire happiness of pati-loka, however he may be, since smṛti says,patiṁ tv apatitaṁ bhajet: one should serve a husband who is not fallen. (SB [7.11.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/11.28))

He may have cruel nature (duḥśīlaḥ). He may be without good fortune (durbhagaḥ), failing in his attempts.

He may be old (vṛddhaḥ) or incapable of activity (jaḍaḥ). He may be sick (rogī) or poor (adhanaḥ). Since your husbands, residents of Vraja, are not sinful, how can you reject them?

(Another meaning)

The husband should not be given up by those who desire insignificant fame and happiness in this life and the next life. But husbands should be given up by you, who consider this world and the next to be like grass and take me as the only goal.

### Text 26

*asvargyam ayaśasyaṁ ca phalgu kṛcchraṁ bhayāvaham*  
*jugupsitaṁ ca sarvatra hy aupapatyaṁ kula-striyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**For a woman from a respectable family, petty adulterous affairs are always condemned. They bar her from heaven, ruin her reputation and bring her difficulty and fear.**

**Комментарий:**

You have great affection for me. But special affection which is against dharma, is completely rejectable. One cannot attain Svarga. “We do not care for Svarga.” It leads to infamy. “We do not care for fame.” It is useless (phalgu). “It is not useless since we have experienced that is the best of all.” It brings difficulties (kṛcchram) since your husbands will reject you. “No one will know about this.” It will make you fearful. You will fear your husbands who will get to know sometime.

“Bharata Muni has said that the love which causes great opposition because of being against normal dharma, which necessitates the love being kept secret, and which makes it hard for the lovers to meet is the highest type of love. Love with the king of rasa is themost excellent.”

It is condemned (jugupsitam). Everywhere, at all times, actions of the upapati (paramour) with a well-bred woman is criticized. Even though you may tolerate the criticism because your desires are fullfilled, how can I do this to you, the objects of my love? Therefore, go to the village.

All this which is condemned is actually not condemend for you but is praiseworthy. It is beyond auspicious and inauspicious since I am the Supreme Lord.

### Text 27

*śravaṇād darśanād dhyānān mayi bhāvo ’nukīrtanāt*  
*na tathā sannikarṣeṇa pratiyāta tato gṛhān*

**Перевод:**

**Love for me arises by the devotional processes of hearing about me, seeing my form, meditating on me and faithfully chanting my glories. The same result is not achieved by mere physical proximity. So please go back to your homes.**

**Комментарий:**

“O most intelligent prince! Do you think our minds will pleased by something else? We have not come with desire for physical association with you but to serve you, Viṣṇu, the Supreme Lord. Placing us near you in this night, let us serve you through your feet.”

First hear about me. Then see my deity form. Then meditate on my form. Then glorify me with excitement. This is my instruction. Bhāva for me arises in my pure devotees by hearing, etc., not by being near me. Thus, they do not desire proximity to me.

*sālokya-sārṣṭi-sāmīpya-sārūpyaikatvam apy uta*  
*dīyamānaṁ na gṛhṇanti vinā mat-sevanaṁ janāḥ*

**A pure devotee does not accept any kind of liberation— sālokya, sārṣṭi, sāmīpya, sārūpya or ekatva—even though they are offered by the Supreme Lord. (SB** [**3.29.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.13)**)**

Thus, go home to perfect this procedure.

(Another meaning)

By hearing, etc., amorous feelings (bhāvaḥ) for me does not arise to the extent (na) that it does by being near me (sannikarṣeṇa). Forthis reason, go to the bower houses, similar to houses (agṛhān). The particle na is connected with the noun (gṛhān) and not the verb (pratiyāta).

### Text 28

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*iti vipriyam ākarṇya gopyo govinda-bhāṣitam*  
*viṣaṇṇā bhagna-saṅkalpāś cintām āpur duratyayām*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Hearing these unpleasant words spoken by Govinda, the gopīs became morose. Their great hopes were frustrated and they began to think deeply.**

**Комментарий:**

Govinda can mean he who possesses words which have direct, indirect and hinted meanings (go), i.e. one who is greatly learned. They heard his words having the previously mentioned characteristics (iti), which were not pleasing (vipriyam). Words indicating his attraction would be pleasing and words indicating his indifference are not pleasing. Since by the first meaning of his words doubts arose in them and by the second meaning, humility arose in them, they became disappointed. Then they felt pain because their long-held desire to physically associate with him was thwarted. They became filled with thoughts which could not besuppressed (duratyayām).

Though he is soft with prema for us, now he is hard. Our good fortune has disappeared. Should we win him with miserable voices and holding his feet or by a rejoinder? Should we carefully maintain our composure? Should we return to the village because of his deceit? We should fathom the mood of his heart which is deep like an ocean. Should we enter the lake of the Yamunā in front of him? If we do that, how can we see his moon-like face? They became bewildered about what to do.

### Text 29

*kṛtvā mukhāny ava śucaḥ śvasanena śuṣyad*  
*bimbādharāṇi caraṇena bhuvaṁ likhantyaḥ*  
*asrair upātta-masibhiḥ kuca-kuṅkumāni*  
*tasthur mṛjantya uru-duḥkha-bharāḥ sma tūṣṇīm*

**Перевод:**

**Their heads hanging down and their heavy, sorrowful breathing drying up their reddened lips, the gopīs scratched the ground with their toes. Tears flowed from their eyes, carrying their kajjala and washing away the vermilion smeared on their breasts. Thus they stood, silently bearing the burden of their unhappiness.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks the anubhāvas of their thoughtfulness. They remained silent for a moment since words could not appear, because of their absorption in deep thinking. Their situation is described. Their bimba-like red lips dried up by their breathing arising fromlamentation.

They hung their heads down. His lotus eyes closed, he will not recognize us when the moons of our faces arise. Will our hearts not break by his words attempting to remove our illusion? They hung down their heads, waiting for his glance. This is conjectured.

By the words śucaḥ, it is suggested that their breathing was hot and drawn out. By the word śuṣyad, ending in the suffix śatṛ, it is suggested that their lamentation was continuous. By the word bimba, it is suggested that their lips were red and soft but extremelydried up and faded. They scratched the earth with their big toes. “O earth! Split open and we will enter.” The kuṅkuma on theirbreasts was washed away by their tears which took away (upātta) their collyrium. Their tears flowed in streams since they had great suffering (uru-duḥkha-bharāḥ). Though not mentioned, it is understood that they also experienced pain and exhaustion. By seeing their state, the heart of even Kṛṣṇa, the crest jewel of rasikas, melted. Still their desire to hear his reply was in order to disclose his honest words.

### Text 30

*preṣṭhaṁ priyetaram iva pratibhāṣamāṇaṁ*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ tad-artha-vinivartita-sarva-kāmāḥ*  
*netre vimṛjya ruditopahate sma kiñcit*  
*saṁrambha-gadgada-giro ’bruvatānuraktāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Although Kṛṣṇa was their beloved, and although they had abandoned all other objects of desire for his sake, he had been speaking to them unfavorably. Stopping their crying, they wiped their eyes and began to speak, their voices stammering with anger, because of their great attachment to him.**

**Комментарий:**

“O lotus-eyed women! O those who have seen the prosperity of the forest! Why stay longer? With happy faces go home and sleep soundly.” Regaining consciousness by his words, they spoke to him something. This is related in this verse.

They spoke to Kṛṣṇa consequently. The heads of groups, situated in the eight directions, all facing him, spoke one after the other, not simultaneously, since if they spoke simultaneously then due to the noise there would be no relishment. He was most dear (preṣṭham) since he was their master. Without reason, he spoke displeasing words like a person who does not like them. He had spoken roughly to them ordering them to serve their husbands.

“Perceiving the harsh treatment, why did their minds not withdraw from him?” For Kṛṣṇa’s sake, they had specially rejected all other desires that were different from him. They gave up all engagements for his happiness. It was not possible to withdraw their minds from him.

Why could they not speak, though they were overcome with great grief? Their grief was covered by great anger arising from his words which were causelessly indifferent to them. They rubbed their eyes in order to retort, after glancing at his face, because of the nature of anger in love. It is understood that by their great pain, their shyness reduced.

### Text 31

*śrī-gopya ūcuḥ*  
*maivaṁ vibho ’rhati bhavān gadituṁ nṛśaṁsaṁ*  
*santyajya sarva-viṣayāṁs tava pāda-mūlam*  
*bhaktā bhajasva duravagraham mā tyajāsmān*  
*devo yathādi-puruṣo bhajate mumukṣūn*

**Перевод:**

**The beautiful gopīs said: O all-powerful one, you should not speak in this cruel way. Do not reject us, who have renounced all material enjoyment to render devotional service to your lotus feet. Reciprocate with us, O stubborn one, just as the primeval Lord, Nārāyaṇa, reciprocates with his devotees in their endeavors for liberation.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks the gopīs’ replies, which had two meanings following Kṛṣṇa’s example.

Here, the meanings which prohibit the dear request of the gopīs, being direct and the meanings which express his request for his most desirable object, and which nourish the rasa, being indicative, there is no conflict in rasa. Thus, Śukadeva speaks in that way.

Mā (in maivaṁ) is used in the sense of refusing his request. Those who giving up all objects including husbands, worshiped the soles of your feet, respond to those persons freely (duravagraham) accordingly. Mentioning soles indicates their low position. Reject us (asmān) completely (ātyaja) even in seeing and speaking. An example of responding to others and giving up them (gopīs) is given. The Lord responds to those seekers of liberation who have given up material objects such as karmas and not others.

(Another meaning)

O lord supremely capable! You should not speak such cruel words, what to speak of acting cruelly. Nṛśaṁsa means cruel or harming according to Amara-kośa. Do not kill us women with the arrows of your indifferent words. If you do not desire to kill women then accept us (bhajasva), who have given up all objects, and serve your feet.

“Why do you not serve your husbands?” O difficult obstacle (duravagraha)! O creator of droughts! O person who gives rough treatment! Do not give us up (mā tyaja). Otherwise you contradict your promise to respond to the devotee, ye yathā mam prapadnyante: as they surrender to me, I respond. (BG [4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11)) The example nourishes what they say. The ādi-puruṣa, the Lord who who is your vilāsa-aṁśa, lord of Vaikuṇṭha, responds to those seekers of liberation who even desire to give up all material objects for worshipping the Lord in order to supply what they desire. But we have given up everything for you (not just desire to give up). Why would you not respond?

### Text 32

*yat paty-apatya-suhṛdām anuvṛttir aṅga*  
*strīṇāṁ sva-dharma iti dharma-vidā tvayoktam*  
*astv evam etad upadeśa-pade tvayīśe*  
*preṣṭho bhavāṁs tanu-bhṛtāṁ kila bandhur ātmā*

**Перевод:**

**Our dear Kṛṣṇa, as an expert in religion you have advised us that the proper religious duty for women is to faithfully serve their husbands, children and other relatives. We agree that this principle is valid, but actually you should do the same since you give instructions. After all, O Lord, you are the dearest friend of all embodied souls. You are their most intimate friend and their very self.**

**Комментарий:**

They refute what was said in verse 24 that highest dharma of women is to serve their husbands.

O Kṛṣṇa (aṅga)! It is fine dharma for women to obey their husbands, etc. This is a statement of trickery since it is can be constructed differently. The phrase dharma-vit (knower of dharma) is a sarcastic statement since calling us with the sound of your flute, to enjoy with you, you then teach us about serving husbands. This is an instruction to destroy adharma. May that instruction be enacted by you, the Lord, the independent avatāra, the teacher. Destroy adharmas. Previously as Ajita, you became a woman, Mohinī. Now becoming a woman, you should serve a husband.

“Then what will you do?” You, who are the friend and the beautiful intelligence (ātmā), are dear to all living beings. Thus by your conduct in dharma, we all will experience auspiciousness.

(Another meaning)
