Previously the Lord spoke taking support of Pūrva-mīmāṁsa in saying that serving husbands was the highest dharma for women.They refute that with Uttara-mīmāṁsa. Such words should be directed to you. The reason for your being the object of all instructions is that you are the Lord (īśe) since the śrutis say:

*namo vedānta-vedyāya*

**I offer respects to one who is known by the Upaniṣads. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

*aupaniṣadaḥ puruṣaḥ*

**The lord is revealed by the Upaniṣads. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)**

And due to the logic:

*śāstra-yonitvāt*

**The Lord cannot be known by reasoning because the source of understanding the Lord is the Upaniṣads. (Brahma- sūtras)**

Giving up service to husbands, one should serve you only, since this is obtained from scriptures. “I am the Lord. But why serve me?” You are the dearest to all beings, since you are full of knowledge and bliss. Yet you are not indifferent but perform beneficial acts(bandhuḥ) and spread in the heart (ātmā). You are the master who is always present nearby.

### Text 33

*kurvanti hi tvayi ratiṁ kuśalāḥ sva ātman*  
*nitya-priye pati-sutādibhir ārti-daiḥ kim*  
*tan naḥ prasīda varadeśvara mā sma chindyā*  
*āśāṁ dhṛtāṁ tvayi cirād aravinda-netra*

**Перевод:**

**Expert transcendentalists always direct their affection toward you because they recognize you as their true self and eternal beloved. What use do we have for these husbands, children and relatives of ours, who simply give us trouble? Therefore, O giver of benedictions grant us your mercy. O lotus-eyed one, please do not cut down our long-cherished hope to have your association.**

**Комментарий:**

They refute what was said in verse 23 that they have come here on account of affection for Kṛṣṇa.

Why would those women who become prosperous while remaining in their eternally dear bodies due to husbands who destroysuffering, have feelings as lovers for you? Rather they would not. Thus bless us. Give up this obstinacy. O Lord of benedictions! This is an address indicating criticism. Give us this boon. May we not pervade the desire that has been held in you for long. We are not the objects of your desire. Thus destroy that desire (in you). O lotus-eyed Lord! Crookedness is not proper for such eyes. Māsma is in the imperfect tense of the root as (to be) connected with the particle māṅ (expressing prohibition). Āśā is the object of the verb as (though it is classified as intransitive) like the usage go-doham asti: he remains for as long as the cows are being milked. (It means: destroy the desire as long as it stays).

(Another meaning)

Since you were to be served by all, you are to be served by us.

*harir eva sadārādhyaḥ sarva-deveśvareśvaraḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa, or Hari, is the master of all devatās, and therefore he is always worshipable. (Padma Purāṇa)**

Those who are skillful at scriptures (kuśalāḥ) such as the above verse, show rati for you, our husband (sve), the form full of all knowledge and bliss (ātman for ātmani), and thus eternally dear. Thus, what significance are husbands, etc.? They are detestable.

“They should be dear to you, since they are my servants.” No, they give pain (ārti-daiḥ) since they obstruct our meeting with you.Ārti-daiḥ is a modifier (of pati-sutādibhir) with the reason implicit in it. Therefore, be merciful to us. O giver of benedictions! Do not forget to give benedictions. You said, “You will enjoy those nights with me.” (SB [10.22.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.27)) O Lord, capable of fulfilling the desires of your devotees! Do not cut the desire creeper of our aspiration from childhood which is now bearing fruit. A fruiting creeper should not be cut down by a gentleman. O lotus-eyed one! Do you not see our beauty with those two eyes? If you do not, it injures your position as the king of rasikas.

### Text 34

*cittaṁ sukhena bhavatāpahṛtaṁ gṛheṣu*  
*yan nirviśaty uta karāv api gṛhya-kṛtye*  
*pādau padaṁ na calatas tava pāda-mūlād*  
*yāmaḥ kathaṁ vrajam atho karavāma kiṁ vā*

**Перевод:**

**Until today our minds were absorbed in household affairs, but you easily stole both our minds and our hands away from our housework. Now our feet won’t move one step from your lotus feet. How can we go back to Vraja? What would we do there?**

**Комментарий:**

They conceal the awakening of their bhāva, which was indicated by verse 27 that bhakti is established through hearing, seeing the deity and meditation. Our hearts remain happy, not stolen by you, since they were absorbed in household affairs. The sign is that even our hands (karau) were absorbed in household affairs. In verse 19, by calling them sumadhyamā (slender-waisted girls) it was suggested that in going home quickly there is fatigue. They answer that. Will our feet not move away from your feet by one step? Rather they move far away too. Thus should we not go to Vraja? Yes, we will go now. “You should not go to Vraja but should stay here.” What will we do here?

(Another meaning)

Our hearts are attracted to you. You stole our hearts easily, just by the sound of your flute. Because of this we do not enter the house. Even our hands do not perform household tasks.

Without our hearts, our feet do not move even one step from your feet. Why should we go to Vraja? Going there, without you, what will we do?

### Text 35

*siñcāṅga nas tvad-adharāmṛta-pūrakeṇa*  
*hāsāvaloka-kala-gīta-ja-hṛc-chayāgnim*  
*no ced vayaṁ virahajāgny-upayukta-dehā*  
*dhyānena yāma padayoḥ padavīṁ sakhe te*

**Перевод:**

**Dear Kṛṣṇa, please pour the nectar of your lips upon the fire within our hearts—a fire you ignited with your smiling glances and the sweet song of your flute. If you do not, we will consign our bodies to the fire of separation from you, O friend, and thus like yogīs attain to the abode of your lotus feet by meditation.**

**Комментарий:**

They respond to his eager request to go to the bowers (in verse 27). O lover! Extinguish the fire of love ignited by the soft song of your flute combined with our natural smiling glances with the full nectar of your lips, since the nectar of our lips is difficult to obtain.Usually, a person greedy for rasa, not attaining the desired object, licks his own lips. This joke is suggested. The reason is given,starting with no cet. Because we will certainly (yadi) not become bodies suitable for your fire arising from separation, and thus wewill not go to your feet even in meditation. Cet is a synonym for yadi used in the sense of certainty as in yadi vedāḥ pramāṇaṁ syuḥ(Certainly the Vedas should be pramāṇas). O friend (sakhe)! This suggests mutual friendship of playing in dust during infancy.

(Another meaning)

“What do you women want?” O Kṛṣṇa! Sprinkle the nectar of your lips on the fire of love which has arisen from the soft sound of your flute and your smiling glances. The smiles and flute sound are compared to ghee and wind respectively. Otherwise it will become one fire because of separation from you. Our bodies will be burned by that fire. Like yogīs by meditation, we will go to your feet. This display of frightening him, is a direct request for enjoyment, and is not rasābhāsa because it is expressed by hint.

### Text 36

*yarhy ambujākṣa tava pāda-talaṁ ramāyā*  
*datta-kṣaṇaṁ kvacid araṇya-jana-priyasya*  
*asprākṣma tat-prabhṛti nānya-samakṣam añjaḥ*  
*sthātuṁs tvayābhiramitā bata pārayāmaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed one, the goddess of fortune considers it a festive occasion whenever she touches the soles of your lotus feet. You are very dear to the residents of the forest, and therefore when we touched those lotus feet, from that time on we have been unable even to stand in the presence of others, for we will have been fully satisfied by you.**

**Комментарий:**

“During childhood, while playing in the dust, you showed envy. Now why are you all indifferent to me?” They reply.

O lotus-eyed one! At some time you, who have made friendship with the animals and birds of the forest as a child, had given the opportunity to a beloved to become inclined to follow your feet, from that time onwards we did not touch those feet, what to speak of other limbs. Though we previously enjoyed with you in infant pastimes with persistence, now we can easily stand still before the elders. Bata indicates doubt. Otherwise we would be rejected by them too.

(Another meaning)

“If your minds are agitated by my beauty, and your hands cannot engage in household actions, still it is proper for you well-bred women to remain in your houses”

O lotus-eyed one! Immediately on seeing the beauty of your eyes, we develop attraction to you.

The moment we touched your feet – which gave a joy to Lakṣmī, queen of Vaikuṇṭha – with our breasts in a bower somewhere at Govardhana

*yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo*  
*vihāya kāmān su-ciraṁ dhṛta-vratā*

**For the dust of your lotus feet, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. (SB** [**10.16.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/16.36)**)**

Laksṁī was given a festival by her desire to enjoy those feet. “How are you qualified for something desired by Lakṣmī?” You have affection for cowherd people situated in Vṛndāvana. By that, we have qualification. From that moment (tat-prabhṛti), we cannot stay in front of our husbands. We serve them from a distance. Moreover, not only did we touch your feet but we were enjoyed by you. We were enjoyed as you like, by being made to take the role of a man. Giving us, your wives, pain by your indifferent words, you are not ashamed.

### Text 37

*śrīr yat padāmbuja-rajaś cakame tulasyā*  
*labdhvāpi vakṣasi padaṁ kila bhṛtya-juṣṭam*  
*yasyāḥ sva-vīkṣaṇa utānya-sura-prayāsas*  
*tadvad vayaṁ ca tava pāda-rajaḥ prapannāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Goddess Lakṣmī, whose glance is sought after by the devatās with great endeavor, has achieved the unique position of always remaining on the chest of her Lord, Nārāyaṇa. Still, she desires the dust of his lotus feet, even though she has to share that dust with Tulasī-devī and with the Lord’s many other servants. Similarly, we have approached the dust of your lotus feet for shelter.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking the example of Lakṣmī, they reject his proposition that it is proper to show affection for him as lovers on the pretext that all beings have affection for him (which was stated in verse 23).

Though Lakṣmī has attained a place on Viṣṇu’s chest, she, along with Vṛndā desired the foot dust of the king of Gokula situated in Vṛndāvana since it is well known that starting from your birth, Vraja became the playground of Lakṣmī in Vraja and Vṛndā-devī, another form of Tulasī, eternally lived in Vṛndāvana. She desired any kind of dust, even the dust served by persons related to Vraja(bhrṭya) by placing on their heads. Is she glorious in any way? Even devatās and their followers strive to attain her glance of mercy on themselves. And we too are glorious like her. The particle ca has the meaning of api (too) and indicative of complaint. Thus like Lakṣmī and Vṛndā we too are mugdhā (innocently charming girls) but are not surrendered to your foot dust.

(Another meaning)

We, your lovers, desire to serve your feet. They explain with an example. Lakṣmī desired your foot dust along with tulasī, like thatwe also have surrendered to your foot dust. The rest is clear. Lakṣmī has a place on Viṣṇu’s chest, thus you, king of rasikas, should also give us a place on your chest.

### Text 38

*tan naḥ prasīda vṛjinārdana te ’nghri-mūlaṁ*  
*prāptā visṛjya vasatīs tvad-upāsanāśāḥ*  
*tvat-sundara-smita-nirīkṣaṇa-tīvra-kāma*  
*taptātmanāṁ puruṣa-bhūṣaṇa dehi dāsyam*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O vanquisher of all distress, please show us mercy. To approach your lotus feet we abandoned our families and homes, and we have no desire other than to serve you. Our hearts are burning with intense desires generated by your beautiful smiling glances. O jewel among men, please make us your maidservants.**

**Комментарий:**

They summarize what was stated previously.

O one who removes all distress! Vṛjinārda is formed according to the sūtra, karmaṇy aṇ (Pāṇini 3.2.1). Thus have mercy on us. Give up these fickle glances. “But you all have come here by giving up your homes, and like Lakṣmī are surrendered to the dust of my feet”. They reply with na te’ṅghri-mūlam. Giving us such homes, maintaining desire for your worship, we have not achieved your feet. But we have come for fun in order to see the forest of Vṛndāvana in moon-light. Thus give your service to those who are scorched by the intense desire aroused by seeing things related to you, but not to us who are not like that. O jewel among men! You decorate your friends (puruṣa), but not any of the young girls of Gokula even now. Thus, even the young women who are afflicted by desire are absorbed in imagination. You are the best of harsh!

(Another meaning)

Due to the previously stated reason give us your mercy. We have given up our houses and have come near your feet. We have given us desire for other types of happiness.

But how can I give mercy when there is an impediment, a bad prārabdha which causes suffering? Even then removing the badprārabdha, give us your mercy.

“What type of mercy are you requesting?” Give us service as we are pained by sharp love pains because of your glances. We do not pray to become your wives.

“You who desire happiness of getting relief from the pain of love previously requested for a sprinkling of the nectar from my lips (in verse 35). Being a friend of niṣkāma bhaktas, I do not desire you, who are full of desire (i.e. sakāma).”

We desire only to serve you (tvad-upāsanāśāḥ). Our worship is satisfying you, the king of rasikas, by embracing your body full of softness, beauty, grace and fragrance. What fault is there if we develop happiness knowing that you are happy? The fire in our hearts is also caused by you, since it arises from your beautiful smiling glances. Moreover, we desire only to serve you. You make us mad with love by such glances in order to engage us in your service. A rasika does not experience joy when he embraces young women devoid of amorous love. O ornament in the form of a male! Be an ornament like the sapphire on all the limbs of us golden gopīs.

### Text 39

*vīkṣyālakāvṛta-mukhaṁ tava kuṇḍala-śrī-*  
*gaṇḍa-sthalādhara-sudhaṁ hasitāvalokam*  
*dattābhayaṁ ca bhuja-daṇḍa-yugaṁ vilokya*  
*vakṣaḥ śriyaika-ramaṇaṁ ca bhavāma dāsyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing your face encircled by curling locks of hair, your cheeks beautified by earrings, your lips full of nectar, and your smiling glance, and also seeing your two imposing arms, which take away our fear, and your chest, which is the only source of pleasure for the goddess of fortune, we must become your maidservants.**

**Комментарий:**

In verse 27, by the phrase darśanān mayi bhāvaḥ the power his beauty was shown. They speak about that. The latter word ca,indicates a plaintive cry (implying a negation). The former word ca, is used in the sense of aggregation of the what all has been said(describing him in this verse). Seeing all this (ca) we must become your servants? Not by any means.

(Another meaning)

“You are not new servants purchased by me for a price. Then, why do you remain as maidservants?”

We have been purchased for millions of times the price than our suitable price. Seeing your face not covered, slightly covered and fully covered by locks, we should become your maidservants. Your face is not covered by locks whose tips are seen on your forehead, since your colorful tied turban covers them. It is slightly covered by small curled locks on the front, right and left sides of your tied topknot. Your face is fully covered by locks which have fallen due to rubbing unguents at the time of love battles. That particle of beauty is our price. The face is described. It has cheeks reflecting the beauty of swinging large, round pearl earrings and sweet lips. This is a single word (in the verse). The face has glances endowed with a smile. With the locks shining on top, the beauty of the earrings on the two sides, and the glances with similes in the middle and below – his face is laden with beauty everywhere. By the comparison to place (sthala) the cheeks are broad. By the reference to mirror in kuṇḍala-śrī the cheeks are shining. The inference of nectar in his lips is due to the arousal of special greed merely on seeing them and due to the experience of special fragrance. His arms give fearlessness to those who take shelter by killing demons. Seeing them, by his cleverness our fear of husbands disappears. By the tight embraces of those arms, fear of Cupid disappears. The arms are compared to sticks, to indicate their roundness, thickness and length. His chest is where Lakṣmī, a golden line on the left side of his chest, can experience the best enjoyment (ramaṇa). It is a shelter endowed with the highest beauty.

The word ca is used twice and seeing is mentioned twice (vīkṣya, vilokya). This indicates special shelter of the arms and chest in their rasa. In the world, the price of a servant is some material object. This is accomplished in you however with your great beauty, the sweetness of your lips, the touch of your attractive arms, and your chest, the shelter of Lakṣmī. By these things we have become your maidservants.

### Text 40

*kā stry aṅga te kala-padāyata-veṇu-gīta-*  
*sammohitārya-caritān na calet tri-lokyām*  
*trailokya-saubhagam idaṁ ca nirīkṣya rūpaṁ*  
*yad go-dvija-druma-mṛgāḥ pulakāny abibhran*

**Перевод:**

**Dear Kṛṣṇa, what woman in all the three worlds wouldn’t deviate from religious behavior when bewildered by the sweet, drawn- out melody of your flute? Your beauty makes all three worlds auspicious. Even the cows, birds, trees and deer manifest the ecstatic symptom of bodily hair standing on end when they see your beautiful form.**

**Комментарий:**

“If you have determined vows, then why do you not stay here all night?” Fearing such an objection, they reply with fear. Though we are like that still O Kṛṣṇa, playing the flute softly (aṅga)! O bewildered one! who are bewildered by the arrow of Cupid calledsammohana! what young woman in the three worlds would not go away from you because of good conduct (ārya-caritāt), since (yat) even cows and other creatures develop hairs standing on end, seeing that form which is auspicious for the three worlds. Who would not deviate because of that? Everyone would. Thus we will not stay here, since beautiful women staying near a handsome man is criticized.

(Another meaning)

“If you become my servants, other women will mock you.” They speak with anger and humility.

Who is the woman in the three worlds who would not deviate? All would deviate, since even the devatā women deviate. (SB [10.21.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/21.12)) On not seeing you (i.e. on only hearing your flute) this is the situation, and even on seeing you it is so. Thus in every way you kill. They speak as if with fear. Seeing that extraordinary form which is auspicious for upper, middle and lower planets, animals, etc., have hairs standing on end. Just by hearing about you, bewilderment will arise for women. This is stated by kaimutya. Even you, a man, are bewildered. Uddhava says:

*vismāpanaṁ svasya ca saubhagarddheḥ*

**These pastimes were wonderful for everyone, even for those proud of their own opulence, including the Lord himself in his form as the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha. (SB** [**3.2.12**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.12)**)**

Oh! Let these talks of those endowed with knowledge remain because even the cows and other creatures develop hairs standing on end from your flute song and your form. This is the gopīs’ answer to:

*duḥśīlo durbhago vṛddho jaḍo rogy adhano ’pi vā*  
*patiḥ strībhir na hātavyo lokepsubhir apātakī*

**Women who desire a good destination in the next life should never abandon a husband who has not fallen from his religious standards, even if he is obnoxious, unfortunate, old, unintelligent, sickly or poor. (SB** [**10.29.25**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.25)**)**

Thus, by your flute song and form everyone is bewildered (so even the husbands become bewildered and are thus “fall from dharma,” so they are fit to be abandoned). None of us will be mocked.

### Text 41

*vyaktaṁ bhavān vraja-bhayārti-haro ’bhijāto*  
*devo yathādi-puruṣaḥ sura-loka-goptā*  
*tan no nidhehi kara-paṅkajam ārta-bandho*  
*tapta-staneṣu ca śiraḥsu ca kiṅkarīṇām*

**Перевод:**

**Clearly you have taken birth in this world to relieve the fear and distress of the people of Vraja, just as the primeval Lord protects the domain of the devatās. Therefore, O friend of the distressed, kindly place your lotus hand on your maidservants’ heads and burning breasts.**

**Комментарий:**

Fearing that he would forcibly make them stay with him as expressed in verse 19 and others that they should stay with a hero like him, they pray while praising him.

You have taken birth in this world to relieve the fear and distress of the people of Vraja. Therefore (tat), O friend of the distressed! Even out of fear of deviating from dharma, do not put your lotus hand on the heads of residents of Vraja, our servant girls who should be protected, what to speak of us cultured women, what to speak of putting your hand on our breasts. O boy whose heart is burning with lust (tapta)! We do not trust you, a lusty person.

(Another meaning)

Taking away fear and pain of Vraja, you were born in Nanda’s house just as Nārāyaṇa, protecting the devatās’ planets, was born to Aditi. This is well known (vyaktam). The people of Vraja fear demons and have pain from rain and wind.

“What is your desire?” Place your lotus hand on burning breasts of us, your servants, to test them and cool them. And on our heads too. Thus do not speak words of extreme indifference, since they are not real.

Starting with verse 18 till this verse the verbal anubhāva called saṁlāpa has been shown.

*ukti-pratyuktimad-vākyaṁ saṁlāpa iti kīrtyate*

**Statements with replies and counter replies are called saṁlāpa. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 11.85)**

### Text 42

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*iti viklavitaṁ tāsāṁ śrutvā yogeśvareśvaraḥ*  
*prahasya sa-dayaṁ gopīr ātmārāmo ’py arīramat*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Smiling upon hearing these despondent words from the gopīs, Kṛṣṇa, the supreme master of all masters of mystic yoga, mercifully enjoyed with them, although he is self-satisfied.**

**Комментарий:**

Having his desire fulfilled on hearing (śrutvā) the words of fearlessness and great distress (viklavitam) of his beloveds as stated (iti) he smiled. You, who consider yourselves very intelligent have been conquered by me – who desiring to hear the words of great honesty from you whose stubbornness and depth belittles an ocean – showed words of seeming indifference, similar to Agastya swallowing the ocean of your depth and stubbornness. Thus because of giving up unfavorableness in the form of shyness and stubbornness, becoming a golden pearl necklace on my heart, a person dark like a sapphire, you should make me drink the nectar of your lips for which I have been eager for a long time. Thus smiling, he enjoyed pastimes with the gopīs. Seeing their choked voices and dried lips because of tears, he became merciful (sa-dayam), or he enjoyed with affection which carried auspiciousness (sad-ayam). He enjoyed with them while being ātmārāma (who enjoys with himself). Api is for restriction since the smṛtis say:

*ballavyo me mad-ātmikā*

**my gopīs are of my nature. (SB** [**10.46.6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/46.6)**)**

*ānanda-cinmaya-rasa-pratibhāvitābhiḥ*

**he is surrounded by gopīs endowed with equal rasa full of bliss and knowledge. (Brahma- saṁhitā)**

It is not that in enjoying with those who were non-different from himself he had to give up his nature of being ātmārāma.

“It is not possible to enjoy with millions of gopīs at the same time for it will be said vanitā-śata-yūthapaḥ: he was the leader of hundreds of women (verse 44).” He is yogeśvareśvara. He is the controller (īśvara) of even controllers like Śiva who are controllers of yogīs like Saubhari. They enjoy simultaneously with many women through their expanded forms. But Kṛṣṇa, only one person, by his acintya-śakti, enjoyed with each of them in various manifestations(prakāśa forms). It will be said citraṁ bataitad ekena vapuṣā: it is amazing that he enjoyed with one body. (SB [10.69.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/69.2))

### Text 43

*tābhiḥ sametābhir udāra-ceṣṭitaḥ*  
*priyekṣaṇotphulla-mukhībhir acyutaḥ*  
*udāra-hāsa-dvija-kunda-dīdhatir*  
*vyarocataiṇāṅka ivoḍubhir vṛtaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Surrounded by the assembled gopīs whose faces blossomed by his glance, Kṛṣṇa, who responded to each of them without fail, whose activities were most attractive, whose smile revealed his shining rows of teeth, white like jasmine buds, increased in beauty, like the moon surrounded by stars.**

**Комментарий:**

His beauty with the gopīs is described. He was endowed with pastimes which were great or which gave prema (udāra-ceṣṭitaḥ). He did not fail to enjoy with each gopī (acyutaḥ). He had teeth beautiful like jasmine buds with smiles that gave happiness (udāra).

### Text 44

*upagīyamāna udgāyan vanitā-śata-yūthapaḥ*  
*mālāṁ bibhrad vaijayantīṁ vyacaran maṇḍayan vanam*

**Перевод:**

**With the gopīs singing his praises, that leader of hundreds of groups of women sang loudly. He wandered in the forest wearing his Vaijayantī garland, beautifying the Vṛndāvana forest.**

**Комментарий:**

He wandered with them to see the beauty of the forest washed by the moonlight. He was praised profusely by the gopīs (upagīyamānaḥ), because of his having great valor, beauty, grace and being controlled by prema, through songs they composed using rāga and tāla, and he himself sang loudly (udgāyan), dedicated to the happiness of his beloveds, endowed with a mine of good qualities like beauty. He wore a garland of five differently colored flowers (vaijayantīm).

### Text 45

*nadyāḥ pulinam āviśya gopībhir hima-vālukam*  
*juṣṭaṁ tat-taralānandi kamalāmoda-vāyunā*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa went with the gopīs to the bank of the Yamunā, where the sand was cooling and the wind, enlivened by the river’s waves, bore the fragrance of lotuses.**

**Комментарий:**

He came to Yamunā’s bank, which was furnished by Yamunā as the place for the rāsa dance, and enjoyed with the gopīs because of the wind giving joy to the lotuses blossoming even in the night, delightful with its coolness and gentleness caused by Yamunā’s waves. Kumudāmoda is alternate reading.

### Text 46

*bāhu-prasāra-parirambha-karālakoru*  
*nīvī-stanālabhana-narma-nakhāgra-pātaiḥ*  
*kṣvelyāvaloka-hasitair vraja-sundarīṇām*  
*uttambhayan rati-patiṁ ramayāṁ cakāra*

**Перевод:**

**There Kṛṣṇa threw his arms around the gopīs and embraced them tightly. He aroused Cupid in the beautiful young ladies of Vraja by touching their hands, hair, thighs, belts and breasts, by playfully scratching them with his fingernails, and also by joking with them, glancing at them and laughing with them. In this way the Lord enjoyed his pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

Their amorous play is described. By spreading his arms, by embraces, by touching (ālabhanam) hands, thighs, etc., by jokes (namra), by scratching their breasts, by playful conversations (kṣveli), by glances, and by laughing, he stimulated his and their lust, a form of prema (rati-patim) and enjoyed with them through as many prakāśa forms.

“How could the amorous pastimes take place with a crowd of millions of gopīs on just that much bank of the Yamunā without beds, scents, garlands and betel nut, without concealment?” Since even a small bank is expansive by the acintya-śakti. Nothing was lacking even a bit since everything was supplied by yogamāyā and after the pastime everything was again concealed. What is impossible for the śakti of the Supreme Lord?

### Text 47

*evaṁ bhagavataḥ kṛṣṇāl labdha-mānā mahātmanaḥ*  
*ātmānaṁ menire strīṇāṁ māninyo hy adhikaṁ bhuvi*

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs became proud of themselves for having received such special attention from Kṛṣṇa, the greatest hero and Svayam Bhagavān. Each of them thought herself the best woman on earth.**

**Комментарий:**

*na vinā vipralambhena sambhogaḥ puṣṭim aśnute \|*  
*kaṣāyite hi vastrādau bhūyān rāgo’bhivardhate*

**The happiness of conjugal love cannot reach it’s fullness without separation of the lovers. It increases in strength just as cloth increase in beauty by repeatedly dying with red color. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 15.3, quoted from Bharata Muni’s Nātya-śāstra)**

Now the seed of vipralambha, manifested by the līlā-śakti for nourishing sambhoga, is described.

Having received respect (labdha-mānāḥ) from Bhagavān, Kṛṣṇa, the crest jewel of heroes (mahātmanaḥ), each among the heroines situated on earth considered herself to be superior to the others. They became proud thinking, “I alone have gained great fortune.”

### Text 48

*tāsāṁ tat-saubhaga-madaṁ vīkṣya mānaṁ ca keśavaḥ*  
*praśamāya prasādāya tatraivāntaradhīyata*

**Перевод:**

**Keśava, seeing the gopīs too proud of their good fortune and the anger of Rādhā, wanted to relieve them of this pride and show mercy to Rādhā. Thus he immediately disappeared.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of enjoying equally, Rādhikā, Mahā-lakṣmī of Gokula, the chief most among all the gopīs, because sulky due to the suddenly developed envy. The others remained proud of their good fortune. The action of the Lord to resolve the conflict among them is described. Seeing the intoxication with good fortune in the gopīs and the anger in Rādhā (tāsām), to relieve them of intoxication with good fortune and to give mercy to angry Rādhā, he disappeared taking Rādhā by force. Antardhīyate is poetic license from antardadhāt. Or the verbal root is dhiñ, belonging to the fourth class of roots, which means to disrespect. Keśava means he who controls Brahmā and Śiva or he who arranges Rādhā’s hair. He disappeared to relieve them of pride and to give mercy to Rādhā.

## Chapter 30 - The Gopīs Search for Kṛṣṇa

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*antarhite bhagavati sahasaiva vrajāṅganāḥ*  
*atapyaṁs tam acakṣāṇāḥ kariṇya iva yūthapam*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When Kṛṣṇa disappeared so inexplicably, the gopīs felt great sorrow at losing sight of him, like a group of female elephants who have lost their mate.**

**Комментарий:**

*gopyā viccheda-santaptāḥ kṛṣṇaṁ pṛṣṭvā vanaspatīn \|*  
*triṁśe tu cakrus tal-līlāḥ sambhujya sa jahau ca tāṁ*

**In the thirtieth chapter the gopīs pained by separation ask the trees about Kṛṣṇa, enact his pastimes. But Kṛṣṇa, enjoying with Rādhā, leaves her.**

When Kṛṣṇa unexpectedly disappeared, the women of Vraja, other than Rādhā, did not see him.

### Text 2

*gatyānurāga-smita-vibhramekṣitair*  
*mano-ramālāpa-vihāra-vibhramaiḥ*  
*ākṣipta-cittāḥ pramadā ramā-pates*  
*tās tā viceṣṭā jagṛhus tad-ātmikāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As the cowherd women remembered Kṛṣṇa, their hearts were overwhelmed by his movements and loving smiles, his playful glances and enchanting talks, and by the many other pastimes he would enjoy with them. Thus absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Rādhā, the gopīs began acting out his various pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

Not seeing him, searching for him the gopīs became insane (unmāda). Their actions are described in two verses. Their hearts agitated by the movements, etc., of Kṛṣṇa, the master of all wealth of Vraja (ramā-pateḥ), the women enacted his pastimes. They were agitated by his gait, like an intoxicated elephant, his loving smile, his playful glances with moving pupils, attractive talks, hispastimes and other play (vibhramaiḥ). Their minds and intelligence (ātma) were like his (tad-ātmikāḥ). They were completely absorbed in him.

### Text 3

*gati-smita-prekṣaṇa-bhāṣaṇādiṣu*  
*priyāḥ priyasya pratirūḍha-mūrtayaḥ*  
*asāv ahaṁ tv ity abalās tad-ātmikā*  
*nyavediṣuḥ kṛṣṇa-vihāra-vibhramāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Because the beloved gopīs were absorbed in thoughts of their beloved Kṛṣṇa, their bodies imitated his way of moving and smiling, his glances, his speech and other distinctive features. Deeply identifying with and maddened by remembering his pastimes, they declared to one another, “I am Kṛṣṇa!”**

**Комментарий:**

Their condition in deep unmāda is described. Their bodies imitated (prati-rūḍha) his gait, etc. Previously his gait, etc., entered into each of their forms made of mind and senses and then those forms imitated his gait and other mannerisms. Then just as an iron ball which is heated, they became one with him and thought, “I am Kṛṣṇa.” They became completely absorbed in him (tad-ātmikāḥ). They said this to each other. The reason is given. They became insane by memory of his pastimes (kṛṣṇa-vihāra-vibhramāḥ). Oneshould not say that this mentality arose from thinking themselves one with his svarūpa since it is said in this verse priyāḥ priyasya pratirūḍha-mūrtayaḥ: the beloveds imitated the lover. This is ananubhāva of bhakti like tears and trembling. The conception of so ’ham (I am he) (in Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) is not with the intention of identity with his svarūpa according to Vedānta-sūtra:

*pūrva-vikalpaḥ prakaraṇāt syāt kriyā mānasavat*

**So ’ham means a type of bhakti because of the context. It is just like deity worship and meditation. (Vedānta-sūtra** [**3.3.46**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vs/3.3.46)**)**

### Text 4

*gāyantya uccair amum eva saṁhatā*  
*vicikyur unmattaka-vad vanād vanam*  
*papracchur ākāśa-vad antaraṁ bahir*  
*bhūteṣu santaṁ puruṣaṁ vanaspatīn*

**Перевод:**

**Singing loudly of Kṛṣṇa, they searched for him throughout the Vṛndāvana forest like a band of madwomen. They even asked the trees about him, who as the Supersoul is present inside and outside of all created things, just like the sky.**

**Комментарий:**

He describes their activities, who had half inclination to search for him externally, when their unmāda slackened.

They sang loudly to attract their lover who was fond of songs, and so that he would hear of their suffering. Together they went from forest to forest. They searched for him (vicikyuḥ) and like madwomen asked the trees about him. Though he had given them pain by rejecting them, they still searched for him. Pained by separation from Kṛṣṇa, we women of Vraja will search for him. This is their external search. They asked the trees. This is a sign of unmāda. Unmāttaka means slightly unmāda.

“Kṛṣṇa was mad with happiness, being with Rādhā, the chief among all gopīs. Did he know the questioning of the trees in madness of the other gopīs?”

That is described. He is inside and outside all beings like ether. Though he was playing with Rādhā and, though mad with happiness, he was also situated with the other gopīs unseen and could hear them since he will say:

*mayā parokṣaṁ bhajatā tirohitaṁ*

**Even when I removed myself from your sight by suddenly disappearing, I never stopped loving you. (SB** [**10.32.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.21)**)**

By his acintya-śakti he was with everyone simultaneously.

### Text 5

*dṛṣṭo vaḥ kaccid aśvattha plakṣa nyagrodha no manaḥ*  
*nanda-sūnur gato hṛtvā prema-hāsāvalokanaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[The gopīs said:\] O aśvattha tree, O plakṣa, O nyagrodha, have you seen Kṛṣṇa? That son of Nanda Mahārāja has gone away after stealing our minds with his loving smiles and glances.**

**Комментарий:**

Their questioning is described in nine verses. In the land of Vraja shining like a mirror, pippala and other trees with leaves and fruit effulgent like sapphires, rubies, diamonds and various other gems shine. The trees can see Kṛṣṇa though he is far away because they were very tall. Thus the gopīs asked the trees. “Have you seen him? Though the son of Nanda, a great devotee, he has stolen the minds of us women and gone away. Have you seen the thief who stole the jewels of our minds?” By what did he steal your minds? “He stole them by sending off smiling glances of prema.”

### Text 6

*kaccit kurabakāśoka-nāga-punnāga-campakāḥ*  
*rāmānujo māninīnām gato darpa-hara-smitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O kurabaka tree, O aśoka, O nāga, punnāga and campaka, has Balarāma’s younger brother, whose smile removes the pride of respectable women, passed this way?**

**Комментарий:**

These trees are proud. They do not respect us. We should not bother with trees with no flowers or with insignificant fruits, with no knowledge of helping others. They entered a flower garden and asked. The kuravaka is red Amaranthus tree. Nāga is the nāgakesara. At night they protect the bees with their honey. They will help us. “What do you ask for?” If you have seen where the younger brother of Balarāma, who has a smile that steals the pride of us women with a wealth of pride, has gone, then please tell.

### Text 7

*kaccit tulasi kalyāṇi govinda-caraṇa-priye*  
*saha tvāli-kulair bibhrad dṛṣṭas te ’ti-priyo ’cyutaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O most kind Tulasī, to whom the feet of Govinda are so dear, have you seen that infallible one walk by, wearing you and encircled by swarms of bees?**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the wind move the branches, the trees, shaking their heads, say, “We have not seen him.” We should not concern ourselves with these callous males. We will ask the females who side with us. They go elsewhere and, approaching tulasī, ask her. O Tulasī, dear to Govinda’s feet! Most auspicious (kalyāni), due to touching his feet. We are not fortunate, since we do not associate with his feet. They explain that association. Most affectionate to you (te’tipriyaḥ), he wears you, along with even the bees, greedy for your fragrance.

The pun is, he has disregarded us beloveds (atipriyaḥ). Thus you must have seen him. Please tell us his whereabouts. Later they will say that the fragrance of tulasī in the pastime forest is intense.

*divya-gandha-tulasī-madhu-mattaiḥ*  
*ali-kulai alaghu gītām abhīṣṭam*

**Maddened by the divine, honeylike aroma of the tulasī flowers on the garland Kṛṣṇa wears, swarms of bees sing loudly for him. (SB** [**10.35.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/35.10)**)**

### Text 8

*mālaty adarśi vaḥ kaccin mallike jāti-yūthike*  
*prītiṁ vo janayan yātaḥ kara-sparśena mādhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O mālati, O mallikā, O jāti and yūthikā, has Mādhava gone by here, giving you pleasure with the touch of his hand?**

**Комментарий:**

Proud of her good fortune she does not speak to us. We will ask those who have no pride. Going elsewhere they speak. He went from here, gaving you pleasure by touching you with his hand when picking your flowers. Because you saw him, you should tell us. Mālatī and jāti are different species of jasmine.

### Text 9

*cūta-priyāla-panasāsana-kovidāra*  
*jambv-arka-bilva-bakulāmra-kadamba-nīpāḥ*  
*ye ’nye parārtha-bhavakā yamunopakūlāḥ*  
*śaṁsantu kṛṣṇa-padavīṁ rahitātmanāṁ naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O cūta, O priyāla, O panasa, āsana and kovidāra, O jambu, O arka, O bilva, bakula and āmra, O kadamba and nīpa and all you other plants and trees living by the banks of the Yamunā who have dedicated your very existence to the welfare of others, we gopīs have lost our minds, so please tell us where Kṛṣṇa has gone.**

**Комментарий:**

Though they have seen Kṛṣṇa they will not show him to us since they forbidden by him. Let us not ask them since they are dependent. Going elsewhere, they ask trees situated on the bank of the Yamunā. Cūta is a mango creeper and amra is a mango tree.Nīpa is, a big tree with huge flowers tree and kadamba is a small tree with small fragrant flowers. Priyāla is a type of śāla tree. Asanais the yellow śāla tree. Kovidāra is a type of kāñcanāra. Arka is hara- priya. “Others” refers to coconut and betel nut. They dwell at the tīrtha of the Yamunā and because they do not move, it is inferred they are meditating on Viṣṇu. They will not tell a lie.

Please tell us where Kṛṣṇa is since we are devoid of consciousness. (rahitātmanām).

“What is the purpose of us speaking?” You live on the bank of the Yamunā, for the welfare of others (parārtha-bhavakā).

### Text 10

*kiṁ te kṛtaṁ kṣiti tapo bata keśavāṅghri-*  
*sparśotsavotpulakitāṅga-ruhair vibhāsi*  
*apy aṅghri-sambhava urukrama-vikramād vā*  
*āho varāhava-puṣaḥ parirambhaṇena*

**Перевод:**

**O mother earth, what piety did you perform to attain the touch of Keśava’s lotus feet, which has brought you such great joy that your bodily hairs are standing on end? You appear very beautiful in this condition. Was it perhaps when then two embraced in the best battle of love?**

**Комментарий:**

Because they are absorbed in Viṣṇu, they do not hear our question. Or they do not answer us since they have become hard-heartedfrom living in a tīrtha. Or they did not see him. Therefore, we will search by ourselves. Looking at the earth, the priya-narma-sakhīs,thinking the soft sprouts of dūrva grass are her hairs standing on end from the touch of his feet, they ask the earth, understanding her to be on their side. This is expressed in three verses.

O earth, holding up the bowers of Vṛndāvana! Kṣitiḥ and kṣitī are equivalent according to Śabda-bheda-prakāśa. Wherever he maybe, you know where our beloved is. What austerity did you perform? We have a desire to do that austerity.

“How do you infer that I did austerities?” Bata indicates joy. Keśavā means she who has excellent hair. Keśavā is Kṛṣṇa’s beloved. Keśava is Kṛṣṇa. You are beautiful, joyful with the touch of their feet as they walked slowly upon your surface. You cannot conceal that joy. Your hairs are standing on end in the form of the dūrva grass sprouts. Without the touch of his feet this would not happen. Details of being touched by the Lord’s feet are given. Api vā means kiṁ vā (perhaps).

In picking flowers, competing, “I will be first,” the couple made big steps (urukrama) with their feet together, pressing down the earth (vikrama), making foot marks. Because of that deep touch of their feet, your hairs are standing on end. This is the ornament called keli.

*vihāre saha kāntena krīḍitaṁ kelir iṣyate*

**Playing with the lover during pastimes is called keli. (Sāhitya-darpaṇa)**

We understand this, not because of those bold actions but there is the highest cause. Nourishing the best battle of love (vara āhava puṣ), the Lord and his beloved with embraces were situated upon you. Your hairs stood on end by experiencing bliss in sheltering the couple mad with love and experiencing their own bliss. Knowing about the two, please direct us.

### Text 11

*apy eṇa-patny upagataḥ priyayeha gātrais*  
*tanvan dṛśāṁ sakhi su-nirvṛtim acyuto vaḥ*  
*kāntāṅga-saṅga-kuca-kuṅkuma-rañjitāyāḥ*  
*kunda-srajaḥ kula-pater iha vāti gandhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O friend, wife of the deer, has Acyuta been here with his beloved, bringing great joy to your eyes by her limbs? Indeed, blowing this way is the fragrance of his garland of kunda flowers, which was smeared with the kuṅkuma from the breasts of his girlfriend when he embraced her.**

**Комментарий:**

O friends! The earth, proud of its good fortune to touch the Lord’s feet always, does not speak to us. We will ask others. Seeing an impassioned doe in front of them they inquire.

O wife of a deer! Has the son of Nanda come here with his beloved, giving great joy to your eyes just by showing their limbs which have attained special beauty by associating with each other? Do not say that you have not seen him since we have obtained some indication of him. The fragrance of a jasmine garland tinged with kuṅkuma from her breasts from their physical association comes here. Our nostrils recognize the scent of the garland, the kuṅkuma from her breasts and her limbs. This is the garland from the ornament of the dynasty of Nanda (kula-pateḥ). The pun in calling him acyuta is: has he come here separated from her?

### Text 12

*bāhuṁ priyāṁsa upadhāya gṛhīta-padmo*  
*rāmānujas tulasikāli-kulair madāndhaiḥ*  
*anvīyamāna iha vas taravaḥ praṇāmaṁ*  
*kiṁ vābhinandati caran praṇayāvalokaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O trees! When the younger brother of Rāma walked by here, followed by intoxicated bees swarming around the tulasī buds decorating his garland, his arm on the shoulder of his beloved, holding a lotus in his right hand, did he acknowledge your obeisances with his affectionate glances?**

**Комментарий:**

They surmise that the doe cannot speak because of joy on seeing Kṛṣṇa, or from suffering on being separated from him now. Not verifying the meeting of the couple, they describe Kṛṣṇa’s special pastime suitable at that time with great joy. Regarding the trees’ bending over with the weight of fruit, as their offering of respects in the mood of being the Lord’s assisting servants, and again inquiring from those trees about their particular good fortune arising from being close to the Lord, they describe the particular pastime of the couple.

O trees! Did the younger brother of Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa, wandering near you, acknowledge your obeisances with loving glances or not? He is described. Putting his arm on his beloved’s shoulder, he, holding a lotus, is followed by bees blind with intoxication of tulasī. Her limbs slack from amorous enjoyment, he makes his left arm into a pillow for her. He is followed by bees which have given up a tulasī forest out of greed for the fragrance of her face. He holds a play lotus to drive them away. In this way there were opportunities for him absorbed in serving her, to see elsewhere.

### Text 13

*pṛcchatemā latā bāhūn apy āśliṣṭā vanaspateḥ*  
*nūnaṁ tat-karaja-spṛṣṭā bibhraty utpulakāny aho*

**Перевод:**

**Let us ask these creepers about Kṛṣṇa. Even though they are embracing the arms of their husband, this tree, they certainly must have been touched by Kṛṣṇa’s fingernails, since out of joy they are manifesting eruptions on their skin.**

**Комментарий:**

They infer association with Kṛṣṇa from the black complexion of the creeper. Certainly, being touched by his fingernails, the creeper’s hairs are standing on end. Without the touch of his fingernail your hairs would stand on end in this way. Though you are embracing the arms of the tree, i.e though associating with your husband, he touched you because of an abundance of good fortune.

### Text 14

*ity unmatta-vaco gopyaḥ kṛṣṇānveṣaṇa-kātarāḥ*  
*līlā bhagavatas tās tā hy anucakrus tad-ātmikāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Having spoken these words, the gopīs, distraught from searching for Kṛṣṇa, began to act out his various pastimes, fully absorbed in thoughts of him.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described in this way their inquiry like madwomen in these verses, now Śukadeva describes their imitating his pastimes which was mentioned before (in verse 3). “There should be no disturbance to the couple’s playing on being met by these gopīs. Forthat purpose, yoga-māyā made arrangements for them to imitate his pastimes.” In those imitations, yoga-māyā imitated the roles ofthe contrary portions taking their forms since it was previously said:

*ādiṣṭā prabhuṇāṁśena kāryārthe sambhaviṣyati*

**At the request of her master, she will appear with her different potencies in order to execute the work of the Lord. (SB** [**10.1.25**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.25)**)**

The gopīs themselves imitated the favorable roles in the pastimes. Otherwise rasābhāsa would occur. With words like madwomen,the gopīs disheartened in searching for Kṛṣṇa, being incapable of searching for him due to the pain of separation, enacted the various pastimes of the Lord who disappeared, to pass the time. This is the anubhāva called līlā.

*priyānukaraṇaṁ līlā ramyair veśa-kriyādibhiḥ*

**Imitating the lover by attractive garments and actions is called līlā. (Ujjvalā-nīla-manī)**

### Text 15

*kasyācit pūtanāyantyāḥ kṛṣṇāyanty apibat stanam*  
*tokayitvā rudaty anyā padāhan śakaṭāyatīm*

**Перевод:**

**One gopī imitated Pūtanā, while another acted like infant Kṛṣṇa and pretended to suck her breast. Another gopī, crying in imitation of infant Kṛṣṇa, kicked a gopī who was taking the role of the cart demon, Śakaṭāsura.**

**Комментарий:**

That imitation is explained in four verses. One gopī acted like Pūtanā (pūtanāyantyaḥ). Another acted like Kṛṣṇa (kṛṣṇāyantī) anddrank. Another made herself like a baby (tokayitvā).

### Text 16

*daityāyitvā jahārānyām eko kṛṣṇārbha-bhāvanām*  
*riṅgayām āsa kāpy aṅghrī karṣantī ghoṣa-niḥsvanaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**One gopī took the role of Tṛṇāvarta and carried away another, who was acting like infant Kṛṣṇa, while yet another gopī crawled about, her ankle bells tinkling as she pulled her feet.**

**Комментарий:**

One gopī made herself like the demon Tṛṇāvarta (daityāyitvā) and took away another taking the role of baby Kṛṣṇa. Another crawled around, pulling her feet with the sound of bells.

### Text 17

*kṛṣṇa-rāmāyite dve tu gopāyantyaś ca kāścana*  
*vatsāyatīṁ hanti cānyā tatraikā tu bakāyatīm*

**Перевод:**

**Two gopīs acted like Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa in the midst of several others, who took the role of cowherd boys. One gopī enacted Kṛṣṇa’s killing of the demon Vatsāsura, represented by another gopī, and a pair of gopīs acted out the killing of Bakāsura.**

### Text 18

*āhūya dūra-gā yadvat kṛṣṇas tam anuvartatīm*  
*veṇuṁ kvaṇantīṁ krīḍantīm anyāḥ śaṁsanti sādhv iti*

**Перевод:**

**When one gopī perfectly imitated how Kṛṣṇa would call the cows who had wandered far away, how he would play his flute and how he would engage in various sports, the others congratulated her with exclamations of “Well done! Well done!”**

**Комментарий:**

She imitated the way Kṛṣṇa would call the cows which were far away and stand.

### Text 19

*kasyāñcit sva-bhujaṁ nyasya calanty āhāparā nanu*  
*kṛṣṇo ’haṁ paśyata gatiṁ lalitām iti tan-manāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Another gopī, her mind fixed on Kṛṣṇa, walked about with her arm resting on the shoulder of a friend and declared, “I am Kṛṣṇa! Just see how gracefully I dance!”**

**Комментарий:**

They imitate other pastimes in four verses. One gopī put her arm on another gopī and walked around. What did she say? “I am Kṛṣṇa with my arm on Subala’s shoulder. Look at my attractive movements.”

### Text 20

*mā bhaiṣṭa vāta-varṣābhyāṁ tat-trāṇaṁ vihitaṁ maya*  
*ity uktvaikena hastena yatanty unnidadhe ’mbaram*

**Перевод:**

**“Don’t be afraid of the wind and rain,” said one gopī. “I will save you.” And with that she lifted her shawl above her head.**

**Комментарий:**

Making efforts (yatantī) one gopī held her upper cloth above (unnidadhe).

### Text 21

*āruhyaikā padākramya śirasy āhāparāṁ nṛpa*  
*duṣṭāhe gaccha jāto ’haṁ khalānām nanu daṇḍa-kṛt*

**Перевод:**

**O King, one gopī climbed on another’s shoulders and, putting her foot on the other’s head, said, “Go away from here, O wicked snake! You should know that I have taken birth in this world just to punish the wicked.”**

**Комментарий:**

Some gopī climbed on another and put her foot on her head. O evil snake Kāliya! Go from here.

### Text 22

*tatraikovāca he gopā dāvāgniṁ paśyatolbaṇam*  
*cakṣūṁṣy āśv apidadhvaṁ vo vidhāsye kṣemam añjasā*

**Перевод:**

**Then another gopī spoke: My dear cowherd boys, look at this raging forest fire! Quickly close your eyes and I will easily protect you.**

**Комментарий:**

Apidadhvaṁ means close your eyes.

### Text 23

*baddhānyayā srajā kācit tanvī tatra ulūkhale*  
*badhnāmi bhāṇḍa-bhettāraṁ haiyaṅgava-muṣaṁ tv iti*  
*bhītā su-dṛk pidhāyāsyaṁ bheje bhīti-viḍambanam*

**Перевод:**

**One gopī tied up her slender companion with a flower garland and said, “Now I will bind this boy who has broken the butter pots and stolen the butter to this mortar.” The second gopī then covered her face, pretending to be afraid by movements of her eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

One slender gopī, imitating breaking pots, was tied up by yoga- māyā who manifested the nature of Yaśodā (anyayā) to a mortarenacted by another gopī. She covered her eyes imitating frightened Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 24

*evaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ pṛcchamānā vrṇdāvana-latās tarūn*  
*vyacakṣata vanoddeśe padāni paramātmanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**While the gopīs were thus imitating Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes and asking Vṛndāvana’s creepers and trees, in part of the forest they happened to see footprints of he who is attracted to Rādhā.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way, enquiring the various entities, they saw the foot prints of Kṛṣṇa, attracted to the Mahālakṣmī of Gokula, Rādhā, in whomhis soul is (paramā ātmanaḥ).

### Text 25

*padāni vyaktam etāni nanda-sūnor mahātmanaḥ*  
*lakṣyante hi dhvajāmbhoja- vajrāṅkuśa-yavādibhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**\[The gopīs said:\] The marks of a flag, lotus, thunderbolt, elephant goad, barleycorn and so forth on these footprints clearly distinguish them as belonging to that great soul, the son of Nanda Mahārāja.**

**Комментарий:**

They talk to each other. The markings on the feet of Kṛṣṇa, Svayam Bhagavān, the master are clearly seen as nineteen in number. Himeans famous. These are described by Brahmā to Nārada in Padma Purāṇa:

*ṣoḍaśaiva tu cihnāni mayā dṛṣṭāni tat-pade \|*  
*dakṣiṇe cāṣṭa-cihnāni itare sapta eva ca*  
*dhvajā padmaṁ tathā vajram aṅkuśo yava eva ca \|*  
*svastikaṁ cordhva-rekhā ca aṣṭa-koṇas tathaiva ca*  
*saptānyāni pravakṣyāmi sāmprataṁ vaiṣṇavottama \|*  
*indra-cāpaṁ trikoṇaṁ ca kalasaṁ cārdha-candrakam*  
*ambaraṁ matsya-cihnaṁ ca goṣpadaṁ saptamaṁ smṛtam \|*  
*ṣoḍaśaṁ tu tathā cihnaṁ śṛṇu devarṣi-saptam \|*  
*jambū-phala-samākāraṁ dṛśyate yatra kutracit*

**I have seen sixteen marks on his feet. On his right foot are eight marks and on his left foot are seven marks. O best of Vaiṣṇavas! On his right foot can be seen the marks of the flag, lotus, thunderbolt, goad, barley corn, svastika, an upward line and an octagon. O best of the Vaiṣṇavas! Now I will tell you about the seven marks on his left foot. There is a rainbow, a triangle, a pot, a crescent moon, sky, a fish and a hoof print of a cow. Hear about the sixteen marks, O best of the sages among the devatās. Sometimes a markresembling a jambu fruit is seen. (Padma Purāṇa)**

*śaṅkha-dhvajātapatrais tu cihnitaṁ caraṇa-dvayam*

**He is endowed with two feet marked with conch, flag and umbrella. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

Ādi-varāha Purāṇa says:

*yatra kṛṣṇena saṁkīrṇaṁ krīḍitaṁ ca yathā-sukham \|*  
*cakrāṅkita-padā tena sthāne brahma-maye śubhe*

**In that auspicious place, purely spiritual, Krsna, his feet marked with the cakra, played continually in joy.**

The nineteen marks, including the three additional marks – cakra, conch, umbrella – are summarized by the best of his devotees (i.e. Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura):

*candrārdham kalasaṁ trikoṇa-dhanuṣī khaṁ*  
*goṣpadaṁ proṣṭhikāṁ śaṅkhaṁ savya-pade ’tha*  
*dakṣiṇa-pade koṇāṣṭakaṁ svastikaṁ cakraṁ*  
*chatra-yavāṅkuśaṁ dvaja- pavī jambūrdha-*  
*rekhāmbujaṁ bibhrāṇaṁ harim ūnaviṁsati-*  
*mahālakṣmārcitāṅghriṁ bhaje*

**I worship Kṛṣṇa, whose feet are worshipped with nineteen great mark: a crescent moon, water pot, triangle, bow, sky, cow’s hoofprint, fish, conch on his left foot: an eight pointed star, svastika, cakra, umbrella, barley corn, goad, flag, thunderbolt, jambu fruit, line going upwards, and lotus on his right foot. (Rūpa-cintāmaṇi, Stavāmṛta-laharī)**

The three additional marks are of Kṛṣṇa since in the section on the sixteen marks in Padma Purāṇa, it is said:

*aṅkāny etāni bho vidvan dṛśyante tu yadā kadā*  
*kṛṣṇākhyaṁ tu paraṁ brahma bhuvi jātaṁ na saṁśayaḥ \|*  
*dvayaṁ vātha trayaṁ vātha catvāraḥ pañca eva vā*  
*dṛśyante vaiṣṇava-śreṣṭha avatāre kathañcana*

**O wise man! Whenever these signs are seen, Parabrahman known as Kṛṣṇa has appeared on earth without doubt. O best of devotees! Two, three, four or five of these marks are sometimes seen in an avatāra.**

### Text 26

*tais taiḥ padais tat-padavīm anvicchantyo ’grato’balāḥ*  
*vadhvāḥ padaiḥ su-pṛktāni vilokyārtāḥ samabruvan*

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs began following Kṛṣṇa’s path, as shown by his many footprints, but when they saw that these prints were thoroughly intermixed with those of his dearest consort, they became perturbed and spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Rādhā’s footprints along with Kṛṣṇa’s footprints, the various gopīs—opposing group, supportive group and Rādhā’s own group became depressed, happy and overjoyed respectively.

The opposing party is described. Following the path of the footprints, the women (abalāḥ), weak from separation and from searching, seeing those footprints nicely mixed with Rādhā’s footprints, became pained (ārtāḥ) due to being competitors. The opposing party spoke.

Rādhā’s marks are described by the best of the devotees (i.e. Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura) who see the proof that it is indeed Rādhā:

*chatrāri-dhvaja-valli-puṣpa-valayān padmordhva-rekhāṅkuśān*  
*ardhenduṁ ca yavaṁ ca vamam anu yā śaktiṁ gadaṁ syandanaṁ*  
*vedī-kuṇḍala-matsya-parvata-daraṁ datte ‘nv asavyaṁ padaṁ tāṁ*  
*rādhāṁ ciram ūnaviṁśati-mahā-lakṣmyārcitāṅghriṁ bhaje*

**I worship Rādhā, whose feet are endowed with nineteen great marks: umbrella, cakra, flag, vine, flower, bracelet, lotus, upwards line, goad, half-moon, and barley corn on her left foot; and spear, club, chariot, altar, earring, fish, mountain, and conch on her right foot. (Rūpa-cintāmaṇi, Stavāmṛta-laharī)**

### Text 27

*kasyāḥ padāni caitāni yātāyā nanda-sūnunā*  
*aṁsa-nyasta-prakoṣṭhāyāḥ kareṇoḥ kariṇā yathā*

**Перевод:**

**\[The gopīs said:\] Here we see the footprints of some gopī who must have been walking along with the son of Nanda Mahārāja. Her arm is on his shoulder, just as an elephant is accompanied by a she-elephant.**

**Комментарий:**

Recognizing that the footprints are of a woman because there were lightly depressed prints, they speak with envy. We should knowwho the son of Nanda went with, but who was not led by him, and whose footprints these are. Who is this on whose shoulder, he is resting his arm? Actually, she rested her arm on his shoulder because of her good fortune.

### Text 28

*anayārādhito nūnaṁ bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ*  
*yan no vihāya govindaḥ prīto yām anayad rahaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Certainly this particular gopī has perfectly worshiped the all- powerful Lord who takes away distress, Govinda, since he was so pleased with her that he abandoned the rest of us and brought her to a secluded place.**

**Комментарий:**

Not able to tolerate the envious words of the opposing party, the friendly group and Rādhā’s sakhīs spoke little audibly to agitatethem.

Considering that the friendly group speaks: The Lord was worshipped by that young woman. He destroys suffering (hariḥ). He can cheat us all (īśvaraḥ) since he gave us up, being pleased with her worship, and brought her to a solitary spot. She is most fortunate, controlling the son of Nanda!

Considering that the sakhīs speak: O persons devoid of the ways of Kṛṣṇa’s love (anayā)! Or O persons with wrong conceptions dueto thinking yourselves equal to she who is the best! Hari attained Rādhā (rādhitaḥ). Rādhā is his wife. Rādhitaḥ comes from rādhām itaḥ (obtained), but is contracted like the word śakandhu from śakan andhu. He is Bhagavān, most beautiful, intoxicated with love and announces his fame, knowledge and affection. Bhaga means beauty, love, and fame according to Nānārtha-varga. He is capableof fulfilling her desires (īśvaraḥ) since, giving us up, he led her to a solitary place. He hears her words uttered at the time of pastimes(govindaḥ). He enjoys with her. He is most pleased (prītaḥ).

Śukadeva, due to being forbidden by the gopīs, decided not name them. But he indicated Rādhā indirectly. Thus, he produced a scripture indicating her name. He also indicated her name at the beginning of the scripture.

*nirasta-sāmyātiśayena rādhasā*  
*sva-dhāmani brahmaṇi raṁsyate namaḥ*

**I continually offer respects to you, who are the enjoyer with Rādhā in your spiritual abode with your devotees, displaying powers that are unequalled and unsurpassed. (SB** [**2.4.14**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.14)**)**

In bliss himself, giving bliss to her worshippers, he hinted at her name only since he was disturbed by the sages whose minds were overwhelmed by various philosophies in the assembly. But elsewhere her glory is recorded like the sounding of drums. Starting with gokulākhye māthura-maṇḍale in Puruṣa-bodhini Upaniṣad of the Atharva Veda and then saying:

*govindo ’pi śyāmaḥ pītāmbaro dvibhujaḥ*

**Dark Kṛṣṇa wears yellow cloth and has two arms.**

It then says dve pārśve candrāvalī rādhikā ceti yasyā aṁśo lakṣmī- durgādikā-śaktir: on his two sides are Candrāvalī and Rādhikā,whose expansions are Lakṣmī, Durgā and other śaktis.

Bṛhad-gautamīya-tantra says:

*devī kṛṣṇamayī proktā rādhikā para-devatā \|*  
*sarva-lakṣmī-mayī sarva-kāntiḥ sammohinī parā*

**Rādhikā is the supreme worshippable person, non-different from Kṛṣṇa. She is the embodiment of all opulence and all beauty. She is the supreme enchanter.**

She is the chief of all gopīs. the queen of the king of the bowers.

*vāmāṅga-sahitā devī rādhā vṛndāvaneśvarī*

**Rādhā situated on his left is the queen of Vṛndāvana. (Kṛṣṇa Upaniṣad)**

The other gopīs are her aṁśas. They are all Lakṣmīs. Brahmā says:

*lakṣmī-sahasra-śata-sambhrama-sevyamānam*

**Govinda is served by millions of Lakṣmīs (gopīs). (Brahma- saṁhitā)**

The envy of those gopīs was created by the līlā-śakti for giving Kṛṣṇa happiness. It is an ābhāsa of envy only. This is explained in detail elsewhere.

### Text 29

*dhanyā aho amī ālyogovindāṅghry-abja-reṇavaḥ*  
*yān brahmeśau ramā devī dadhur mūrdhny agha-nuttaye*

**Перевод:**

**O friends! The dust of Govinda’s lotus feet is so sacred that even Brahmā, Śiva and Lakṣmī take that dust upon their heads to dispel sinful reactions.**

**Комментарий:**

The neutral group, seeing the Lord’s footprints, inattentive to them, speak. Brahmā and others place that dust on their heads to destroy the suffering of separation from him since daily in the afternoon, at the time when Kṛṣṇa returns to Vraja, they are seen taking the dust and since the wives of Kāliya mentioned that Lakṣmī desires that dust. But we are suffering separation since we do not hold that dust on our heads out of shyness.

### Text 30

*tasyā amūni naḥ kṣobhaṁ kurvanty uccaiḥ padāni yat*  
*yaikāpahṛtya gopīnām raho bhunkte ‘cyutādharam*  
*na lakṣyante padāny atra tasyā nūnaṁ tṛṇāṅkuraiḥ*  
*khidyat sujātāṅghri-talām unninye preyasīṁ priyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**These footprints of that special gopī cause us great pain. She alone has taken him away to a secluded place, where she is enjoying the lips of Kṛṣṇa, which belong to all of us. Look, we can’t see her footprints over here! The lover lifted up his beloved whose tender feet were pained by the spouts.**

**Комментарий:**

The opposing party speaks. They do not mention her name out of envy as competitors. The footprints of that person cause us great sorrow. She has stolen that nectar of his lips, the treasure of all the gopīs and enjoys it alone. He was made to give up all us gopīs who have prema by some bewitching mantra and was brought by her far away. Thus, she is our enemy.

“O envious ones! Do not be depressed. Her footprints are not else where. Cool your hearts (burning with envy)!” Friends of Rādhā speak again. Other friends speak to them in low voices while glancing with joy. He lifted her up with his arms, holding her to his chest (unninye) because her feet were pained by the grass and he could not tolerate it since she was the object of his abundant prema(preyasīṁ). The friends became happy in two ways: by seeing the good fortune of their mistress and from seeing the burning heartsof the opponents.

### Text 31

*imāny adhika-magnāni padāni vahato vadhūm*  
*gopyaḥ paśyata kṛṣṇasya bhārākrāntasya kāminaḥ*  
*atrāvaropitā kāntā puṣpa-hetor mahātmanā*

**Перевод:**

**Please observe, my dear gopīs, how in this place lusty Kṛṣṇa’s footprints are pressed more deeply into the ground because of carrying the weight of his beloved. Over here that intelligent boy must have put her down to gather some flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

The opposing party, even on not seeing Rādhā’s footprints, felt great pain and spoke.

O unobservant talkative gopīs! See Kṛṣṇa’s footprints sinking deeper into the earth from carrying her weight.

Being controlled by her, he gives us great pain. He is a lusty person (kāminaḥ), not an affectionate person. He carries her out of lust, not affection. That being so, he should not give us up, who are affectionate. They show displeasure even towards their beloved Kṛṣṇa. There is another meaning to their words however by the grace of Sarasvatī devī. The word kāminaḥ can mean “of he who desires constantly the happiness of his beloved.” This will be made clear later.

Again, the sakhīs spoke. He brought her down from his chest in order to pick flowers. Kāntā means she who is loving and who has attained great happiness by the best of rasikas (mahātmanā), or by he whose intelligence (ātmā) is joyful (maha) on pleasing her.

### Text 32

*atra prasūnāvacayaḥ priyārthe preyasā kṛtaḥ*  
*prapadākramaṇa ete paśyatāsakale pade*

**Перевод:**

**Just see how in this place dear Kṛṣṇa collected flowers for his beloved. Here he has left the impression of only the front part of his feet because he was standing on his toes to reach the flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

See how he picked flowers for his beloved with incomplete footprints (asakale pade) as he sought most attractive flowers on the topmost branches since the earth is pressed down (ākramaṇ) by the tips of his feet.

### Text 33

*keśa-prasādhanaṁ tv atra kāminyāḥ kāminā kṛtam*  
*tāni cūḍayatā kāntām upaviṣṭam iha dhruvam*

**Перевод:**

**Certainly this lusty person arranged the hair of the lusty woman here. He must have sat here making a crown for his beloved.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing marks of her sitting in between Kṛṣṇa’s knees, the opposing group felt anguish and again spoke.

That woman lusty but not affectionate since, cheating even her own friends, she took that lusty man to a solitary place. Her hair was arranged by that man, who is lusty but not affectionate because he does not even think of us affectionate women suffering in separation from him. He used a comb supplied by a forest deity. He made a crown for the lusty women with her hair and flowers.

He was situated firmly (upaviṣṭam) with her after making the crown for her and himself, because of tasting playful conversations with her. The words kāminyāḥ and kāminā have a duel meaning as explained previously according to Sarasvatī devī. Cūḍayatā is formed by deleting the suffix matup by the rule vin-mator luk (Pāṇiṇi 5.3.65).

### Text 34

*reme tayā cātma-rata ātmārāmo ’py akhaṇḍitaḥ*  
*kāmināṁ darśayan dainyaṁ strīṇāṁ caiva durātmatām*

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Kṛṣṇa enjoyed constantly with that gopī, although he enjoys only within, and although he satisfied with his many eternal consorts. Thus by contrast he showed the wretchedness of ordinary lusty men and hardheartedness of ordinary women.**

**Комментарий:**

Having great good fortune of Rādhā through the words of the gopīs, Śukadeva himself speaks.

His heart agitated by speaking with her, touching her, dressing her hair, glancing at her limbs and strolling in the forest washed by the moonlight, Kṛṣṇa enjoyed with dearest Rādhā in the bower made of various gems, served by gentle, cool, fragrant breeze, furnished with attractive garlands, betel nut and scents, filled with shining moon-light and hanging with pearls, on a bed strewn with jewels.

Shining on a bed, he enjoyed with embraces, with garlands offered by her, etc. He is ātmārāma, delighting in his svarūpa alone. Api is used in the sense of restriction. “How could a person delighting in a young women, be so (i.e. ātmārāma)?” He was absorbed in(rataḥ) Rādhā, who was nondifferent from himself since she was the svarūpa-śakti (ātmani) of himself, the form of sac-cid-ānanda, the Supreme Lord. This is described in the Tantras:

*hlādinī yā mahā-śaktiḥ sarva-śakti-*  
*varīyasī tat-sāra-bhūtā rādheyam*

**That great śakti, hlādinī is the best of all śaktis. Its essence is Rādhā. (Sanat-kumāra Saṁhitā)**

Thus engaging with she who is nondifferent from him, endowed with prema whose essence is hlādinī and saṁvit is not damaging to being ātmārāma. This is stated in Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad:

*yo ha vai kāmena kāmān kāmayet sa kāmī bhavati \|*  
*yo ha vai tv akāmena kāmān kāmayate so’kāmī bhavati \|*

**He who desires objects with desire to enjoy them is an enjoyer. He who desires objects without a desire to enjoy them is not an enjoyer.**

Akāmena means similar to kāma. It means prema. He is continuously attracted to her (akhaṇḍitaḥ). By that his trembling, loss of composure, etc, are suggested. What did he accomplish by that enjoyment?

He showed the lack of the wealth of rasa (dainyaṁ), due to being devoid of a such ingredients, of the material persons like Indra dedicated to their own sensual happiness (kāmināṁ) and the wickedness of hearts (durātmatām), due to having false stubbornness, of material women like Indra’s wife, who are similarly dedicated to their own sensual happiness (strīnāṁ).

The usage of darśayan is similar to:

*darśayad vidhu-parājayaṁ ramā-vaktraṁ ullasati dhūta-lāñchanam*

**The face of Lakṣmī, showing its victory over the moon, being devoid of stains, rejoices.**

Ordinary men and women for their own happiness, enjoy material objects mutually. Thus they perceive prīti (affection) due to happiness arising from sense objects. But this is not so in real prīti since real prīti results in attaining their svarūpas and bliss. The jīva, a particle of consciousness and bliss, whose svarūpa is covered by ignorance, depends on a bliss manifested by serving young women by touching, hearing, etc., but one cannot say that the Lord, whose svarūpa is complete consciousness and bliss, depends on serving women to attain bliss. However, to attract the hearts of people, the Lord imitates the actions of men. Thus, the false conceptions of the unintelligent are refuted.

### Texts 35-36

*ity evaṁ darśayantyas tāś cerur gopyo vicetasaḥ*  
*yāṁ gopīm anayat kṛṣṇo vihāyānyāḥ striyo vane*

*sā ca mene tadātmānaṁ variṣṭhaṁ sarva-yoṣitām*  
*hitvā gopīḥ kāma-yānā mām asau bhajate priyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As the gopīs wandered about, their minds completely bewildered, they pointed out various signs of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. The particular gopī whom Kṛṣṇa had led into a secluded forest when he had abandoned all the other young girls began to think herself the best of women. She thought, “My beloved has rejected all the other gopīs, even though they are driven by Cupid himself. He has chosen to reciprocate with me alone.”**

**Комментарий:**

Making each other understand the facts as above described, the gopīs wandered about.. Having described a portion of enjoyment which describes the supreme good fortune of Rādhā, their mistress, to describe a portion of separation which nourishes the enjoyment, Śukadeva explains the reason for separation. Previously all the gopīs were proud of their good fortune. Now Rādhā was proud of her good fortune. Giving up the other gopīs, who desired my beloved for themselves (kāmayānāḥ).

### Text 37

*tato gatvā vanoddeśaṁ dṛptā keśavam abravīt*  
*na pāraye ’haṁ calituṁ naya māṁ yatra te manaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**As the two lovers passed through one part of the Vṛndāvana forest, the special gopī began feeling proud of herself. She told Kṛṣṇa who had tied up her hair, “I cannot walk any further. Please lead me wherever you want to go.”**

**Комментарий:**

Though their mistress was very satisfied with her such good fortune, she deliberated in her heart, “All my sakhīs, being pained without us two, are dejected. And so are the opposing groups and the neutral groups without Kṛṣṇa. Thus I and my lover are faulty of hard behavior. Now, to remedy that I should enact some stubbornness by which Kṛṣṇa, who understands my mind, may go there to resolve the issue quickly. They will all meet with him and by that his and my fault will be dissipated. My sponsored rāsa dance will also take place.”

Thus because of the deliberation (tataḥ), the word tat (in tataḥ) referring to thoughts, Rādhā came to raised area in the forest, being situated where all could see, and spoke to Kṛṣṇa, undoing her hair which had been arranged while joking. Kṛṣṇa had tied up (vaya) that hair (keśa) in an attractive braid. That is the meaning of Keśava. Proud of her good fortune, since the pride of the svādhina-bhartṛkā nourishes rasa, she spoke. “I cannot walk because of fatigue from wandering in the forest.”

“Dear! You should give me the order. I will take you far from here to another attractive place, a flower garden for flower ornaments or to a flower cottage in bower for resting comfortably.” Take me somewhere, carrying me on your chest. One should not say that she had bad character in ordering the hero since it is spoken out of anubhāva of pure prema of sakhya, in the form of intimacy filled with control and devoid of reverence.

### Text 38

*evam uktaḥ priyām āha skandha āruhyatām iti*  
*tataś cāntardadhe kṛṣṇaḥ sā vadhūr anvatapyata*

**Перевод:**

**Thus addressed, Kṛṣṇa replied, “Just climb on my shoulder.” But as soon as he said this, he disappeared. His beloved consort then immediately felt constant remorse.**

**Комментарий:**

Addressed by his beloved with words indicating fake fatigue suitable to her svādhīna-bhartṛkā mood, he spoke to his beloved in a joking way. Get on my shoulders. This is not roughness since he addressed her as dear (priyām) and since stubbornness in both members of the couple is for nourishing the rasa.

*yo ’anya-mukhe durvādaḥ priyatam vadane sa eva parihāsaḥ*  
*itarendhana-jo dhūmaḥ so ’guru-janmā bhaved dhūpaḥ*

**What is harsh speech in others’ mouths becomes a joke in the beloved’s mouth. Smoke arising from burning wood when it arises from aguru becomes incense.**

Or skandha can mean the body, chest or the group of sakhīs. This is according to Viśva-kośa.

On saying this, Kṛṣṇa disappeared for a reason (tataḥ). This was because of the considerations in his mind (tataḥ) since he thought as follows:

The sakhīs’ lamentation because of Rādhā’s absence could be dissipated when they attain her. The opposing group showed hatred saying that lusty woman enjoys, having alone taken Kṛṣṇa, who was pleasure for all. The opposing group should not show this envy. Rather they should be indignant of me thinking “That lusty Kṛṣṇa took her by force and went away.” Seeing her good fortune in uniting with me and her becoming overwhelmed by extreme prema in separation from me, they should become prideless.

The particle ca indicates that Kṛṣṇa disappeared even from her heart, because he understood the situation should be resolved, to accomplish his goal. He remained however hiding in the shadows near her. Not seeing Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā, forgetting her own reasoning, being pained by the separation, lamented constantly (anu), “What did I say!” Vadhū means she carries multitudes of prema or she ties her lover with the rope of prema. It means she is the dear most beloved of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 39

*hā nātha ramaṇa preṣṭha kvāsi kvāsi mahā-bhuja*  
*dāsyās te kṛpaṇāyā me sakhe darśaya sannidhim*

**Перевод:**

**She cried out: O master! My lover! O dearest, where are you? Where are you? Please, O mighty-armed one, O friend, just show that you are nearby since I am just your servant, suffering intolerably!**

**Комментарий:**

The lamentation is described. Ha indicates extreme sorrow.  
O my lord (nātha)! Or O person from who people request the highest benefit.

“My nature as lord is distributed to everyone without distinction.”

O my beloved (ramaṇa)!

“My nature as lover is distributed to all the dear gopīs without distinction.”

“O giver of the greatest affection (preṣṭha)! You bestow the greatest fortune.”

Where are you? Where are you? She repeats this out of bewilderment. O might-armed one! She desires that he embrace her tightly.

“I am near you. Why are you disturbed?”

She speaks with humility arising from great pain. Show your presence to me, your most miserable servant. Though you are near I cannot see you. Be merciful and show yourself.

This is the anubhāva called audārya since its symptoms are:

*audāryaṁ vinayaṁ prāhuḥ sarvāvasthāgataṁ budhā*

**Audārya means having a kind nature in all circumstances. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 11.23)**

Some say that these are conclusive statements because she is the essence of the hlādinī-śakti and since Puruṣa-bodhinī śruti and theTantras say:

*tasyādyā prakṛtī rādhikā nityā nirguṇā sarvālaṅkāra-śobhitā prasannāśeṣa-lāvaṇya-sundarī*

**Rādhā is the original prakṛti. Rādhā is eternally without material qualities and beautiful with all ornaments. She is merciful and possesses unlimited grace and beauty. (Puruṣa-bodhinī śruti)**

*hlādinī yā mahā-śakti*

**She is hlādinī, the great śakti. (Sanāt-kumāra Saṁhitā)**

Thus, due to being dependent on him, like light, her statement that she is his miserable servant (dāsyās te) is not unsuitable and since in separation, lordship falters.
