The word prakṛtī (in the Puruṣa- bodhinī quote above) does not refer to others, nor does it harm even explaining the nature of Rādhā’s svarūpa. But in accepting the word, it is hard to deny her role as subservient.

“Since you are my beloved, using miserable worlds is not pleasing to me.”

O friend (sakhe)! If I am your friend, then accept me. Sakhi means a someone who is called an equal by people.

### Text 40

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*anvicchantyo bhagavato mārgaṁ gopyo ’vidūritaḥ*  
*dadṛśuḥ priya-viśleṣān mohitāṁ duḥkhitāṁ sakhīm*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: While continuing to search out Kṛṣṇa’s path, the gopīs discovered their unhappy friend close by, suffering and fainting because of separation from her lover.**

**Комментарий:**

They all saw her, fallen on the ground like a streak of lightning, at some distance. The word sakhīm is used because on seeing her rejected, they envy went away and friendliness manifested. They all served her with fanning, and scented water.

### Text 41

*tayā kathitam ākarṇya māna-prāptiṁ ca mādhavāt*  
*avamānaṁ ca daurātmyād vismayaṁ paramaṁ yayuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**She told them how Mādhava had given respect, but how she then suffered dishonor because of her pride. The gopīs were extremely amazed to hear this.**

**Комментарий:**

When she recovered a little by their service, they inquired from her. She, their mistress, having simple nature spoke. She gained respect from Mādhava and was disrespected due to separation from him. Hearing these two facts, they were most astonished. Daurātmyam means her condition of being at a distance (dūra) from Kṛṣṇa the personification of knowledge and bliss (ātmā). Due to separation from Kṛṣṇa, she was thus dishonored in the form of being away from him. They spoke among themselves. How astonishing that she, all alone, having great prema, was rejected by the king of rasikas, the ocean of mercy.

### Text 42

*tato ’viśan vanaṁ candra jyotsnā yāvad vibhāvyate*  
*tamaḥ praviṣṭam ālakṣya tato nivavṛtuḥ striyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In search of Kṛṣṇa, the gopīs then entered the depths of the forest as far as the light of the moon shone. But when they found themselves engulfed in darkness, they decided to turn back.**

**Комментарий:**

Then taking support of friends’ hands, they entered the forest to search for him. They went as far as moonlight was visible, then, not finding him there, not understanding that he was hidden in the thick shadows, they turned back.

This is described in Viṣṇu Purāṇa:

*praviṣṭo gahanaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ padam atra na lakṣyate*  
*nivartadhvaṁ śaśāṅkasya naitad dīdhiti-gocaraḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa has entered such a dark part of the forest that we cannot possibly see his footprints. Therefore, let us turn back from this area, which even the light of the moon cannot reach.**

O friends! Dear Kṛṣṇa has disappeared in the thick darkness. Do not restrict him. Leaving you who destroy darkness by the moonlight of your faces, the young boy will get tired. Thinking thus they gave up searching for him.

### Text 43

*tan-manaskās tad-alāpās tad-viceṣṭās tad-ātmikāḥ*  
*tad-guṇān eva gāyantyo nātmagārāṇi sasmaruḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Their minds absorbed in thoughts of him, they conversed about him, they engaged in actions to help him out of the forest, and made efforts only for him. They completely forgot about themselves and their homes as they sang about Kṛṣṇa’s qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

Again they attained a state of unmāda. Due to being absorbed in him, when the state of unmāda was weak they spoke of him like “O aśvattha tree, have you seen him?” (verse 5) When unmāda wasmedium, they performed actions like acting as Kṛṣṇa drinking breast milk (verse 15). When unmāda was deep forgetting themselves,they became filled with Kṛṣṇa (tad-ātmikāḥ) like, “I am Kṛṣṇa. See me move about.” (verse 19) They sang about his qualities (as in verse 4) based on previous impressions.

### Text 44

*punaḥ pulinam āgatya kālindyāḥ kṛṣṇa-bhāvanāḥ*  
*samavetā jaguḥ kṛṣṇaṁ tad-āgamana-kāṅkṣitāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs again came to the bank of the Yamunā. Meditating on Kṛṣṇa and eagerly hoping he would come, they sat down together to sing of him.**

**Комментарий:**

“Friend! Staying here we will sing. By singing only he will meet us since singing is dear to him.”

Mad-bhaktā yatra gāyanti, tatra tiṣṭhāmi nārada: O Narada! I reside where my devotees sing. Considering in this way, they again came to the bank, the place of previous pastimes and gathered together. In one voice they sang about Kṛṣṇa, desiring that he come.

## Chapter 31 - The Gopīs Songs of Separation (Gopī-gītā)

### Text 1

*gopya ūcuḥ*  
*jayati te ’dhikaṁ janmanā vrajaḥ*  
*śrayata indirā śaśvad atra hi*  
*dayita dṛśyatāṁ dikṣu tāvakās*  
*tvayi dhṛtāsavas tvāṁ vicinvate*

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs said: O beloved, by your birth the land of Vraja has become exceedingly glorious, and thus Lakṣmī always resides here. Let our suffering be known to you. Offering ourselves to you, we search for you everywhere. We maintain our lives only in the hope of attaining you.**

**Комментарий:**

*eka-triṁśe gopikā-gīti-padma-śreṇī*  
*śuddha-prema-mādhvīka-pūrṇā*  
*sausvaryābhā-rāga-tālādi-gandhā*  
*govindālyākarṣiṇī sandidīpe*

**In the thirty-first chapter the song of the gopīs, a line of lotuses, full of the honey of pure prema, fragrant with pleasing svaras, rāgas and tālas, attracting the bee of Govinda, shines.**

In all the verses of this chapter, every line generally has the same second syllable (ya in the first verse). Similarly the first syllable and the seventh syllable are the same in a line. This feature is generally present here and there for other verses too. The verses are not composed by intelligence, since they were disturbed by separation. They arose by the gopīs’ natural skills. Their expression of prayers for enjoyment with him in some verses should not be considered to be rasābhāsa since the prayers are for his happiness. Just as in cooking food for one’s friend sometimes one speaks of it for oneself, in prema one praises oneself. Some say that, when prema appears, there is loss of discrimination because of the pain of separation. Others say that there is no fault because the words are not spoken in his presence.

This verse is a statement made by gopīs who think of themselves as his, who are dedicated to praise and modesty. O beloved! By your birth Vraja remains more glorious (adhikam jayati). It is superior to even Vaikuṇṭha since there your birth pastimes do not occur. It is excellent by another sign. In Vraja, Lakṣmī always serves (śrayate), whereas in Vaikuṇṭha she is served. But in Vraja full of great happiness, we are suffering intensely.

“Why do you suffer?” It should be seen by you in the directions. Your gopīs search for you. It should not be asked, “Why do they not die from such pain?” because maintaining life with the hope of attaining you, they do not die. Or by offering themselves to you they do not die.

### Text 2

*śarad-udāśaye sādhu-jāta-sat-*  
*sarasijodara-śrī-muṣā dṛśā*  
*surata-nātha te ’śulka-dāsikā*  
*vara-da nighnato neha kiṁ vadhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord of love, in beauty your glance excels the whorl of the finest, most perfectly formed lotus within the autumn pond. O bestower of benedictions, you are killing the maidservants who have given themselves to you freely, without any price. Will you not kill us?**

**Комментарий:**

“I do not desire to give you suffering. What did you do with your lives in relation to me who am extremely handsome to remain there suffering?” This is a statement of those with mixed emotions. O Kṛṣṇa, asking us for enjoyment with your glance (surata-nātha)! O giver of benedictions (varada)! You gave blessings such as “You will enjoy with me the nights.” (SB [10.22.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/22.27))

You kill us by the arrows of sidelong glances. Why is this not your violence? The glance is described. It steals the treasure of beautywithin the blossoming (sat) lotus, which by its species is excellent and is excellently born in the lake full of clear, deep water of the autumn season. This indicates the beauty and fragrance of the glance. Surpassing the moats of water, stealing the wealth of our such lotuses, the glance also takes our life airs and offers them to you. You are the cause of our suffering. The gopīs (who are killed by his glances) are described. Without price we have become maidservants. We are attracted to you. Do not contradict the obedient words of Śruti and Purāṇas.

### Text 3

*viṣa-jalāpyayād vyāla-rākṣasād*  
*varṣa-mārutād vaidyutānalāt*  
*vṛṣa-mayātmajād viśvato bhayād*  
*ṛṣabha te vayaṁ rakṣitā muhuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O greatest of personalities, you have repeatedly saved us from all kinds of danger—from poisoned water, from the terrible man-eater Agha, from the wind mixed with rains and the fiery thunderbolt of Indra, from Ariṣṭāsura and from Vyomāsura.**

**Комментарий:**

If you desire to kill us, why did you protect us for danger many times? This is a statement of those with friendliness predominated by dāsya. We were protected from destruction due to poisonous water, from the snake demon Agha, from the rain created by Indra, from the whirlwind of Tṛṇāvarta, from the thunderbolts of Indra, from Ariṣṭāsura (vṛṣa), from Vyomāsura (mayātmajād), and from many other fears. We were protected many times by crushing Kāliya, etc. O best of men (ṛṣabha)! Because of protecting yourself, we who depend on you alone for life, were saved, but we were directly protected by you from the rain and the lightning. Though Ariṣṭa and Vyomāsura would be killed in the future, past tense is used, since it was considered accomplished as the prediction was made from his birth chart (Garga). Here by referring to Aghāsura’s killing (vyāla-rākṣasād), the allegation that the chapter has been inserted are dismissed. It is not that it is an insertion since it is not mentioned at the end of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam (in the twelfth chapter of Twelfth Canto), for if it were so then the any of the topics of the Seventh Canto which are respected will also be at the risk of being insertions.

### Text 4

*na khalu gopīkā-nandano bhavān*  
*akhila-dehinām antarātma-dṛk*  
*vikhanasārthito viśva-guptaye*  
*sakha udeyivān sātvatāṁ kule*

**Перевод:**

**You are the son of the gopī Yaśodā, O friend, and the indwelling witness in the hearts of all embodied souls. Because Brahmā prayed for you to come and protect the universe, you have now appeared in the Sātvata dynasty.**

**Комментарий:**

“Speaking harshly, you accuse me of killing women, though I shine with fame in the moonlight, as the Supreme Lord and son of Yasodā. I will leave this place and live somewhere alone, so that even between lifetimes you do not see my face even once.” Fearing this response, they speak with criticism. This is a statement of those filled with vāmya-prākharya, who think of him as belonging to them.

Since the particle na is placed first, it is connected with each of the lines. O enemy (asakhe)! Khalu indicates conjecture. You are not the son of Vraja’s queen. Otherwise, you could not neglect us by that relationship to her. You are not the person who inspires the hearts of all embodied beings or the witness (antarātma-dṛk). Otherwise you would understand our suffering. You were not even requested by Brahmā (vikhanasā), destroyer of doubts about the Vedas, to protect the world. Otherwise you would be able to protect us, situated within this universe. You have not appeared in the family of devotees (sātvatām). Otherwise you would have causeless mercy by that relationship. We do not know who are you and from where you have come. With heart as hard as a thunderbolt, mischievous, announcing yourself as the son of Nanda you give us pain.

Or fear such a response from him, those who are extremely distressed praise him to please him. Khalu indicates forbiddance, like in the sentence khalūktvā (do not speak). It is not that you are not the son of Yaśodā. Rather you are her son from beginning time. You are the witness and ātmā of all beings by your aṁśa. You are the Lord. May you be pleased and give up your anger. We know the reason for your appearing in Gokula within the universe. Requested by Brahmā to protect the universe you were born in the womb of Yaśodā in the family of Yadus. O person who makes friends with us (sakhe)! It is suitable that you protect us by your nature of being Yaśodā’s son, etc.

### Text 5

*viracitābhayaṁ vṛṣṇi-dhurya te*  
*caraṇam īyuṣāṁ saṁsṛter bhayāt*  
*kara-saroruhaṁ kānta kāma-daṁ*  
*śirasi dhehi naḥ śrī-kara-graham*

**Перевод:**

**O best of the Vṛṣṇis, your lotus-like hand, which is held by the hand of the goddess of fortune, grants fearlessness to those who approach your feet out of fear of material existence. O lover, please place that wish-fulfilling lotus hand on our heads.**

**Комментарий:**

“O beloveds! In order to drink the honey of your statements uttered in affectionate anger I became invisible near you. Having drunk them since I am satisfied, please choose a benediction from me.” Thinking of his pleasing reply, being comforted, those with dāsyapredominated by friendliness pray for a boon in four verses.

O best of your dynasty (vṛṣṇi-dhurya)! O beloved! Place your lotus hand on our heads. Why? Those hands destroy Cupid, being frightened of whose arrows we have come to you, the shelter. The hidden meaning is those hands also fulfill amorous desire. It should not be said that his hands are incapable of this. Your hand bestows fearlessness to men who have surrendered to your feet out of fear of material existence. For he who destroys fear of saṁsāra, to destroy fear of Cupid is a petty task.

“I will place my hands on your breasts.” No. You hand is held by the hands of Lakṣmī in order to prevent you from placing your hands on her breasts. We must also prevent that.

### Text 6

*vraja-janārti-han vīra yoṣitāṁ*  
*nija-jana-smaya-dhvaṁsana-smita*  
*bhaja sakhe bhavat-kiṅkarīḥ sma no*  
*jalaruhānanaṁ cāru darśaya*

**Перевод:**

**Show us your beautiful lotus face since you destroy the suffering of Vraja’s people. O hero of all women, your smile shatters the false pride of your devotees. Please, dear friend, accept us as your maidservants.**

**Комментарий:**

Other gopīs who consider themselves his equals, speak. O destroyer of pain of Vraja’s people. You destroy the suffering of everyone who lives there. O hero! You are full capable of destroying that suffering. Your smile destroys the pride of your devotees among women. Since just by your smile you destroy our pride, you should not stay hidden.

“What do you say?”

O friend! Accept us as your maidservants. Come close to us.

“I am close to you.”

Show your lotus like face. That face destroys all suffering. Seeing it, we will speak everything else and attain everything.

Or “Please choose what you desire.”

Serve us your maidservants.

“If you are servants, how can you engage me in serving?” O friend! “Tell me how to serve you?”

Show your lotus like face.

### Text 7

*praṇata-dehināṁ pāpa-karṣaṇaṁ*  
*tṛṇa-carānugaṁ śrī-niketanam*  
*phaṇi-phaṇārpitaṁ te padāmbujaṁ*  
*kṛṇu kuceṣu naḥ kṛndhi hṛc-chayam*

**Перевод:**

**Your lotus feet destroy the past sins of all embodied souls who surrender to them. Those feet follow after the cows in the pastures and are the eternal abode of the goddess of fortune. Since you once put those feet on the hoods of the great serpent Kāliya, please place them upon our breasts and destroy the lust in our hearts.**

**Комментарий:**

Some fully dedicated to his happiness speak. Place your lotus feet on our breasts! By that destroy the amorous desire causing pain.

“Why should I place my feet on the breasts of you who are impure with pride and anger?”

You should destroy the sin of us, who bow down to you, like you did for Kāliya.

“Why should I place my tender feet on your hard breasts?”

Those feet follow the cows. Our breasts are not as rough as the rough places where you walk on the grass. Rather they are for your pleasure.

“It is improper to put my feet on your breasts ornamented with many decorations.”

Those feet are the abode of beauty (śrī). They will be the best ornaments on our breasts.

Nothing undesirable will happen to you by doing so. You put your feet on Kāliya’s hoods and gained fame. Destroying the torment in hearts of your people will bring fame.

Or “I fear your husbands.” You were not afraid of wicked Kāliya. Why do you fear those who are attracted to you? Though they know about this, they will not say anything.

There is no fault in their praying for enjoyment directly since it is for Kṛṣṇa’s pleasure. One should not forget that they were dedicated to his happiness alone. This is clear later in the statement yat te sujāta. (verse 19)

### Text 8

*madhurayā girā valgu-vākyayā*  
*budha-manojñayā puṣkarekṣaṇa*  
*vidhi-karīr imā vīra muhyatīr*  
*adhara-sīdhunāpyāyayasva naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed one, by your sweet voice and charming words, which attract the minds of the intelligent, we have fainted. Our dear hero, please revive your maidservants with the nectar of your lips.**

**Комментарий:**

“O beloveds who are beautiful in every way! I am not indifferent to you auspicious women. Why do you not have faith in me, boundby the golden ropes of prema to you? Have faith in me. Know that I am a fine ornament for your body like an ornament for your hand.” Some, with the mood of being his, speak. They had heard his words in an internal vision.

O lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa! O hero, capable of giving the impossible (vīra)! By making us drink the nectar of your lips, make us, who are bewildered (muhyatīḥ) by your words, bewildered more. The words are described. They are pleasing to hear, woven with syllables suggesting sweetness, with sentences, having words declined as nouns or conjugated as verbs and filled with excellence of ākāṅkṣā(mutual expectancy of words to complete the meaning), yogyatā (appropriateness of words) and āsatti (proximity of words) (valgu),and which give bliss to intelligent people by the depth of vastu (content), rasa, bhāva, alaṅkāra, produced by the direct, indirect and allusive interpretations. Here also their requesting the nectar of his lips is not for their happiness since by his giving, he tastes nectar.

### Text 9

*tava kathāmṛtaṁ tapta-jīvanaṁ*  
*kavibhir īḍitaṁ kalmaṣāpaham*  
*śravaṇa-maṅgalaṁ śrīmad ātataṁ*  
*bhuvi gṛṇanti ye bhūri-dā janāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The nectar of your topics is the life of those suffering in this material world. These narrations, praised by learned sages, eradicate one’s sinful reactions and bestow good fortune upon whoever hears them. These narrations are most excellent and are broadcast all over the world. Those who speak these topics are the greatest benefactors.**

**Комментарий:**

Who can describe the sweetness of topics spoken by you? Even the sweetness of topics about you spoken by others are much greaterthan the famous amṛta (which the devatās have in possession). Gopīs having friendliness filled with dāsya speak. Your topics areamṛta. The reason for that is described. Your topics bring to life persons suffering in saṁsāra, but the famous amṛta only brings to life persons suffering from sickness.

They are thus praised (īḍitaṁ) more than the famous amṛta by Parāśara and other poets (kavibhir), who have minimized the famous amṛta. Your topics being heard destroy sins up to prārabdha- karmas (kalmaṣāpaham), but the famous amṛta does not destroyprārabdha-karmas, rather it produces more karma since it increases lust, etc.

Your topics are auspicious just by hearing them since they are relishable and they fulfil the desires. But the famous amṛta, beingheard of, is inauspicious since one desires to die for attaining it.

Your topics are full of wealth (śrīmat) because they enable one to attain the treasure in the highest abode and they are spread (ātataṁ)since they are broadcast at every moment by the speakers. But the famous amṛta is not like that. Those who glorify (gṛṇanti) thesesweet topics on earth are great benefactors (bhūri-dā). The hearers cannot pay-off their favor even if they give everything to them. Just by hearing your topics they live for a moment.

Or some gopīs with mixed bhāva, predominated by friendliness and possessiveness of him, speak that your words are sweet only when accompanied by seeing you, or else they produces misfortune.

Your topics are a cause of death. Why? Life becomes distressed by them. The hidden meaning is your topics give life like water in boiling oil.

“They why are the topics praised in the Purāṇas?”

Your poets alone praise (īḍitaṁ) them as destroyers of sin. Moreover only in hearing them are they auspicious, but not in experiencing them. By experiencing them, one dies. The topics are spread from place to place by reciters of Purāṇas, satisfied with money, who do not now your svarūpa and qualities, who are intoxicated with beauty (śrīmada ātataṁ). Those who glorify your topics on earth destroy the profuse happiness of the house (bhūri-dā) since they renounce the house believing in their meanings. They utter this in great pain (since the gopīs themselves left their houses believing those topics).

If one desire to live for a moment, then enough with those topics.

### Text 10

*prahasitaṁ priya prema-vīkṣaṇaṁ*  
*viharaṇaṁ ca te dhyāna-maṅgalam*  
*rahasi saṁvido yā hṛdi spṛśaḥ*  
*kuhaka no manaḥ kṣobhayanti hi*

**Перевод:**

**Your excellent smiles, your sweet, loving glances, your pastimes worthy of meditation and confidential talks we enjoyed with you, which touch our hearts, give grief to our minds. O cheater!**

**Комментарий:**

“Spend your time remembering previous pastimes, my smiles, etc. Henceforth meeting me directly cannot happen.” Gazing at him when he says this, some gopīs having friendship with possessiveness speak.

O beloved! Your excellent smiles, which are a little more that natural smiles (pra-hasitam), and on top of that your glances of prema and special pastimes (viharaṇam) in seclusion are auspicious for meditation. Your joking conversations (samvidaḥ) stick to the mind (hṛdi-spṛśaḥ). Here the word yāḥ is for the sake of denoting wonder. O cheater!

Your conversations along with your excellent smiles and other items agitate our minds. Manifested by you with a mind embraced by deception, they have entered our minds and after giving happiness, they give great suffering. Just as flour cakes, fried in ghee, given by a cheater are tasty at first but later create a burning sensation. O beloved (priya)! Still giving up our affection for you is difficult. This indicates their extreme attachment. Naḥ (in plural) shows the proof that this is the experience of many of them. In this way, without meeting you, your smiles and glances cause us such great suffering.

### Text 11

*calasi yad vrajāc cārayan paśūn*  
*nalina-sundaraṁ nātha te padam*  
*śila-tṛṇāṅkuraiḥ sīdatīti naḥ*  
*kalilatāṁ manaḥ kānta gacchati*

**Перевод:**

**Dear master, dear lover, when you leave the cowherd village to herd the cows, our minds are disturbed with the thought that your feet, more beautiful than a lotus, will be pricked by the spiked husks of grain and the rough grass and plants.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, you are known to make great efforts to give us pain, since even after making yourself also suffer, you cause us to suffer.Some other gopīs with same nature speak.

When you go from Vraja to the forest to herd the cows, your feet, softer and more beautiful than lotuses, suffer from spikes of corn or sharp tips of grass. Thinking this, our minds become disturbed (kalitatām). O person who destroys happiness (kānta)! O giver of suffering! Though there are no particles of spikes, etc., in Vṛndāvana, they say this according to the mood that a relative or intimate friend is always fearful of some injury to his beloved. (Abhijñāna-śakuntalā-nāṭaka)

### Text 12

*dina-parikṣaye nīla-kuntalair*  
*vanaruhānanaṁ bibhrad āvṛtam*  
*dhana-rajasvalaṁ darśayan muhur*  
*manasi naḥ smaraṁ vīra yacchasi*

**Перевод:**

**At the end of the day you repeatedly show us your lotus face, covered with dark blue locks of hair and thickly powdered with dust. Thus, O hero, you arouse desires in our minds.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, even in meeting you want to give us suffering. With this intention other gopīs, similar to the previous ones, speak. In the evening, you show your lotus like face surrounded by black locks of hair, laden with dust from cows (dhana-rajasvalam), fromherding cows and looking for friends. Dhana means cow according to Viśva-kośa. Showing your face constantly (muhuḥ) on the pretext of gathering the cows and searching for your friends, you impart love to our minds.

During the whole day the sight of your lotus like face cannot be had and even in the evening, due to being covered by hair and dust of cows, the sight of your face does this occur completely. By muhur the idea is that we are not satisfied by seeing you interruptedly. By smaram the idea is that giving us amorous desires, remembering which we are agitated, you cause us great suffering. But you do not meet us. Thus you make all attempts to give us suffering.

### Text 13

*praṇata-kāma-daṁ padmajārcitaṁ*  
*dharaṇi-maṇḍanaṁ dhyeyam āpadi*  
*caraṇa-paṅkajaṁ śantamaṁ ca te*  
*ramaṇa naḥ staneṣv arpayādhi-han*

**Перевод:**

**Your lotus feet, which are worshiped by Brahmā, fulfill the desires of all who bow down to them. They are the ornament of the earth, in times of danger they are the appropriate object of meditation and they give the highest satisfaction. O destroyer of anxiety! O bestower of joy! Please put those lotus feet upon our breasts.**

**Комментарий:**

“If I am so unsteady, then give me up.” Worried that he would say this, some gopīs with secondary friendliness and predominantdāsya speak.

O lover! Offer your lotus feet to our breasts.

O destroyer of suffering (ādhi-han)! By that destroy our mental pain. What all don’t the beloveds pained by separation, speak to their lovers? Forgive our rough words.

His feet are described. They give what surrendered persons like Kāliya and his wives desired, even though he had committed offense (praṇata-kāma-dam). Those feet are worshipped by Brahmā (padmaja) in order that he get forgiveness for his offense. Their forgiving nature is famous. They decorate the surface of the earth. Their mercy is famous. What harm is there if you decorate even our breasts with those feet? Those feet are the object of meditation when one is in danger (āpadi). Those feet are famous for destroying all pain. Those feet are the very form of happiness (śāntamam). They are the form of the highest goal. Your lotus feet have qualities of forgiveness, mercy, etc. May they show forgiveness and mercy to us also.

### Text 14

*surata-vardhanaṁ śoka-nāśanaṁ*  
*svarita-veṇunā suṣṭhu cumbitam*  
*itara-rāga-vismāraṇaṁ nṛṇāṁ*  
*vitara vīra nas te ’dharāmṛtam*

**Перевод:**

**O hero! Kindly distribute to us the nectar of your lips, which enhances conjugal pleasure and vanquishes grief. That nectar is thoroughly relished by your vibrating flute and makes people forget any other attachment.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking that he is pleased by their humble words, other similar gopīs speak. Give the nectar of your lips, a great medicine to us, who are suffering from the sickness of amorous desire. The nectar of lips are described.

It increases amorous love (surata-vardhanaṁ). It is nourishing. It destroys lamentation caused by not attaining you (śoka-nāśanaṁ). It takes away misery.

“Why should I give what is most valuable without a price?”

It is tasted (cumbitam), even by the lifeless flute, which is played. Since you are a dāna-vīra (valiant in charity) you should give it to persons like the flute.

“It is given to unfortunates attached to family and house.”

Once tasted in the form of chewing betel nut, it makes even men forget other attachments. What to speak of women. Since it is most astonishing, it makes them give up such attachments. O dāna-vira! You must certainly give the nectar of your lips. This desire for their own happiness is not a fault, as previously explained. Or they have lost all discrimination out of extreme pain according to others.

### Text 15

*aṭati yad bhavān ahni kānanaṁ*  
*truṭi yugāyate tvām apaśyatām*  
*kuṭila-kuntalaṁ śrī-mukhaṁ ca te*  
*jaḍa udīkṣatāṁ pakṣma-kṛd dṛśām*

**Перевод:**

**When you go off to the forest during the day, a tiny fraction of a second becomes like a millennium for us because we cannot see you. And even when we can eagerly look upon your beautiful face, so lovely with its adornment of curly locks, we think the creator was foolish in making eyelids.**

**Комментарий:**

Some other gopīs say that the suffering of not seeing him is extremely intolerable. When you wander in the forest during the day, not seeing you, for us gopīs, a twenty-seventh part of a kṣaṇa (truti) becomes a yuga. Neuter (in truṭi) is poetic license. All people of Vraja experience suffering in separation for three yāmas. But we experience those three yāmas like millions of yugas. This is most difficult for us. The creator of eyelids of us gopīs who somehow, at the end of the day, see with longing your face with curly locks, has become the creator of obstacles.

“Why did he make the eyelids?”

He is foolish (jaḍaḥ), without intelligence. He does not know other’s suffering.

### Text 16

*pati-sutānvaya-bhrātṛ-bāndhavān*  
*ativilaṅghya te ’nty acyutāgatāḥ*  
*gati-vidas tavodgīta-mohitāḥ*  
*kitava yoṣitaḥ kas tyajen niśi*

**Перевод:**

**Who but a cheater like you would abandon young women who come to see you in the middle of the night, enchanted by the loud song of your flute, though you know the nature of your flute, and though we have completely rejected our husbands, children, mothers, fathers, and brothers to come to you, O Acyuta!**

**Комментарий:**

Though you know of our love and though you make great efforts to glance at us, you appear to be ignorant of your own welfare, disturbing us, your exclusive devotees, by your actions. Some prakharā gopīs with prominent friendliness speak.

We are your women (yoṣitaḥ) having love only for you, accepted by you by Gāndharva rites.

We have obtained your wandering here and there (gati-vidaḥ) constantly on the road to our houses in order to see us. We, suchwomen, have been invited here while mentioning our names (mohitā) by the sound of your flute.

Thus overcoming husbands, etc., giving them up completely we came to you in the night. We gave up those who consideredthemselves husbands (pati), the sons of cowives (suta), their connections (anvaya), the brothers and are other relatives — all of them. Who would give up such women in the night? But you, being, merciless, gave us up. O cheater (kitava)! O madman! Kitava means a cheater or madman according to Medinī. O Kṛṣṇa, who do not falling from the dharma of cheating (acyuta)! Giving us up, you, who cheated us, are cheated. Who would give up women (yoṣitaḥ) in the night? This suggests, “Why did you not become the daughter of Nanda?” (since a daughter of Nanda would not be found in such circumstances).

### Text 17

*rahasi saṁvidaṁ hṛc-chayodayaṁ*  
*prahasitānanaṁ prema-vīkṣaṇam*  
*bṛhad-uraḥ śriyo vīkṣya dhāma te*  
*muhur ati-spṛhā muhyate manaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Our minds filled with desire are repeatedly bewildered on seeing the arousal of your desire, the intimate conversations we had with you in secret, on seeing the remarkable smile on your face, your loving glances and your broad chest, the resting place of the goddess of fortune.**

**Комментарий:**

Though we know you are a cheater, still we cannot give you up. Other gopīs of same bhāva speak.

Seeing your private conversations in which you request amorous enjoyment, your arousal of love caused by our glances, your face with excellent smile, your glance endowed with prema, and your broad chest, the abode of beauty (śriyaḥ), our minds, full of desirebecome bewildered. Spṛhā if formed by saṁpad-ādibhyaḥ kvip (Vārttika 3.3.94).

These five items enter our minds and pierce us like arrows of Cupid.

### Text 18

*vraja-vanaukasāṁ vyaktir aṅga te*  
*vṛjina-hantry alaṁ viśva-maṅgalam*  
*tyaja manāk ca nas tvat-spṛhātmanāṁ*  
*sva-jana-hṛd-rujāṁ yan niṣūdanam*

**Перевод:**

**O beloved, you appear to destroy completely the distress of those living in Vraja and the forests and to bestow upon them all happiness to the highest degree. With minds longing for your association, please give to us just a bit of that medicine, which counteracts the disease in your devotees’ hearts.**

**Комментарий:**

You do not desire to give us suffering but happiness, but that you should do now. Some gentle gopīs predominated with sakhya speak.

O beloved (aṅga)! Your appearance (vyaktiḥ) destroys the suffering of all people of Vraja, and is in such a way that it is auspicious for the entire universe. Our minds want to satisfy the desire aroused in you by seeing us (tvat-sṛphātmanām). Give us a little of that which destroys (niṣūdanam) the pain in the hearts of your devotees (sva- jana-hṛd-rujām). You know that by which your desire is fulfilled and our suffering is destroyed. Or O kinsman (sva-jana)! (i.e. sva- jana is in vocative and not a part of the compound).

### Text 19

*yat te sujāta-caraṇāmburuhaṁ staneṣu*  
*bhītāḥ śanaiḥ priya dadhīmahi karkaśeṣu*  
*tenāṭavīm aṭasi tad vyathate na kiṁ svit*  
*kūrpādibhir bhramati dhīr bhavad-āyuṣāṁ naḥ*

**Перевод:**

**O dearly beloved! Your lotus feet are so soft that we place them gently on our breasts, fearing that your feet will be hurt. Our life rests only in you. Our minds, therefore, are filled with anxiety that your tender feet might be wounded by pebbles as you roam about on the forest path.**

**Комментарий:**

Showing themselves completely dedicated to his happiness, they all speak of their complete bewilderment caused by not seeing their beloved.

We place your soft lotus feet on our breasts in fear. The cause of fear is the rough stones.

Why do you do this? O beloved (priya)! In putting your feet on our breasts, you become pleased. It is for your pleasure. Though you experience happiness, we will place them there gently since understanding the roughness of our breasts, we do not want your tender feet to be hurt.

By the feet which we protect in this way, you wander in the forest.

Even then what about in the night? Are your feet not in pain from the stones and grass tips. They certainly are.

“I do as I please. What can you do?”

Our minds become completely bewildered by that (dhīḥ bhramati). Why are you bewildered? You are our life (bhavad-āyuṣām naḥ). Our life is in your safety.

## Chapter 32 - The Reunion

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*iti gopyaḥ pragāyantyaḥ pralapantyaś ca citradhā*  
*ruruduḥ su-svaraṁ rājan kṛṣṇa-darśana-lālasāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, having thus loudly sung and intensely spoken in various ways, the gopīs began to weep loudly because of their eagerness to see Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

*dvātriṁśe tv āgataḥ kṛṣṇas tābhiḥ premṇā samarcitaḥ \|*  
*pratyarcya tāḥ sa tad-bhāvair ṛṇitāṁ prabhur āvahat*

**In thirty-second chapter Kṛṣṇa comes, is worshipped by the gopīs with love, worships them in return and bears the debt of their love.**

They sang about Kṛṣṇa with various amazing rāgas and tālas (citradhā). Out of control, they talked and cried with loud voices(susvaram).

### Text 2

*tāsām āvirabhūc chauriḥ smayamāna-mukhāmbujaḥ*  
*pītāmbara-dharaḥ sragvī sākṣān-manmatha-manmathaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then Kṛṣṇa, a smile on his lotus face, appeared before the gopīs, wearing a garland and a yellow garment. He directly appeared as one who can bewilder the mind of Cupid, though Cupid himself bewilders the minds of ordinary people.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa (śauriḥ) appeared in the midst of the gopīs while they were crying. Śukadeva criticizes Kṛṣṇa by using the word śauriḥ. Thequality of hard-heartedness due to appearing in kṣatriya family was shown to the gopīs who had soft hearts and prema. You are praiseworthy! The lotus of his face had a smile in order to give the gopīs joy. The lotus of his heart was however suffering. Yellow upper cloth was hanging from his two shoulders in front. He wore it in such a way that they would forgive his offense. He wore a garland put on by his beloved. He manifested himself with great beauty to remove the suffering in their hearts: he was directly the bewilderer of Cupid. Among the various catur-vyūhas which begin with Vāsudeva, the forms of called Pradyumna are directly Cupids. Kṛṣṇa was the cupid of those Cupids, the manifestor of their nature of Cupid. The usage is similar to tad devā jyotiṣāṁ jyoti: the Lord is the light of light. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) Thus he is worshipped as the greatest Cupid in the kāma-gāyatrī. In this way it is indicated that the Cupid of the Lord caused agitation in Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs. By the mutual glances of Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs, the Cupid of the Lord who caused this became glorious. This is the opinion of those who know the secret.

### Text 3

*taṁ vilokyāgataṁ preṣṭhaṁ prīty-utphulla-dṛśo ’balāḥ*  
*uttasthur yugapat sarvās tanvaḥ prāṇam ivāgatam*

**Перевод:**

**When the gopīs saw that their dearest Kṛṣṇa had returned to them, they all stood up at once, and out of their affection for him their eyes bloomed wide. It was as if the air of life had reentered their bodies.**

**Комментарий:**

Their bodies with hands, feet and other limbs rose up like prāṇaṣ returning from fainting. Āgatam is used twice to show that the suffering women would not have stood up without his coming.

### Text 4

*kācit karāmbujaṁ śaurer jagṛhe ’ñjalinā mudā*  
*kācid dadhāra tad-bāhum aṁse candana-rūṣitam*

**Перевод:**

**One gopī joyfully took Kṛṣṇa’s hand between her folded palms, and another placed his arm, anointed with sandalwood paste, on her shoulder.**

**Комментарий:**

The natural actions of prema of some gopīs who were leaders of groups among all of them are described in five verses. One gopī grasped with her cupped hands his right lotus-like hand (understood from later descriptions). This is Candrāvalī since she was eager to touch him and due to friendliness with prominent courtesy. She had prominence of being his. She was foremost in being subservient to him, was ornamented with modesty, praises and compliance. Kṛṣṇa had great respect for her.

One gopī placed on her shoulder his left arm smeared with sandalwood since it is appropriate that one who is similar to the lover (in terms of facing and positioning) be situated on his left side. This was Śyāmalā with mixed bhāva. Due to putting his arm on her shoulder, more than similarity with the portion of compliance of the previous gopī, she had similarity with the portion of possessiveness of the latter gopī. She was a friend of Rādhā, because of this greater portion of possessiveness (Kṛṣṇa is mine).

### Text 5

*kācid añjalināgṛhṇāt tanvī tāmbūla-carvitam*  
*ekā tad-aṅghri-kamalaṁ santaptā stanayor adhāt*

**Перевод:**

**A slender gopī respectfully took in her joined hands the betel nut he had chewed, and another gopī, burning with desire, put his lotus feet on her breasts.**

**Комментарий:**

One slender gopī held in her cupped hands his chewed betel nut. She was a compliant gopī, subservient to her lover, with friendliness having prominent dāsya. Another gopī, sitting on the earth, held his right lotus-like foot with her two hands and placed them on her breasts because she was burning with desire. But Kṛṣṇa taking support of beloved’s shoulder with his left arm he stood leaning on the ground with his left foot. At this point he was standing since it will be said later that he sat down. She is a compliant gopī, with dāsya having prominent friendliness and subservient to her lover. These two, thinking themselves his, are Padmā and Śaibyā, Candrāvalī’s sakhīs.

### Text 6

*ekā bhru-kuṭim ābadhya prema-saṁrambha-vihvalā*  
*ghnantīvaikṣat kaṭākṣepaiḥ sandaṣṭa-daśana-cchadā*

**Перевод:**

**One gopī, filled with loving anger, bit her lips and stared at him with frowning eyebrows, as if to wound him with her harsh glances.**

**Комментарий:**

The chief among all gopīs (ekā) frowned and looked at Kṛṣṇa with arrows of her harsh glances as if to wound him. She wasoverwhelmed with anger in love (prema-saṁrambha). She bit her lips which were covered with the edge of her cloth. She was angry that he had deceived even her. This is Rādhā, situated in the middle due to being described in the middle. Most difficult to attain, she regards him as hers (possessiveness). Her frowns, etc, which reveal this are clear.

### Text 7

*aparānimiṣad-dṛgbhyāṁ juṣāṇā tan-mukhāmbujam*  
*āpītam api nātṛpyat santas tac-caraṇaṁ yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Another gopī looked with unblinking eyes upon his lotus face, but even after deeply relishing its sweetness she did not feel satiated, just as peaceful devotees are never satiated when meditating upon the Lord’s feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Another gopī again and again dranking his lotus face with her two eyes, which were unblinking because of being stunned with bliss, though she had already drunk them, since she was not satisfied. She was given the opportunity to gaze at him thoroughly, because his mind and eyes were absorbed by Rādhā’s shower of side glances.

### Text 8

*taṁ kācin netra-randhreṇa hṛdi kṛtvā nimīlya ca*  
*pulakāṅgy upaguhyāste yogīvānanda-samplutā*

**Перевод:**

**One gopī took the Lord through the aperture of her eyes and placed him within her heart. Then, with her eyes closed and her bodily hairs standing on end, filled with bliss, she continuously embraced him within. She resembled a yogī meditating upon the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking him into her heart she closed his eyes because she worried he would escape, since he was fickle. Because she was thinking of enjoying with him without obstacles, her hairs stood on end. She embraced him since she lost composure with the appearance of great thirst on attaining him after a great separation. She was like a yogī, uniting with the Lord because of extreme absorption.

The last two gopīs (in verse 7 and 8) are Rādhā’s sakhīs Lalitā and Viśākhā, having possessiveness. Because these three did not gonear him, they are vāma (non-cooperative). He should come to us. They have the mood that Kṛṣṇa is theirs.

These seven are described by Śukadeva. Bhadrā is the eighth gopī understood from Viṣṇu Purāṇa:

*kācid āyāntam ālokya govindam atiharṣitā*  
*krṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇeti prāha nānyad udairayat*

**One gopī in great bliss glanced at Kṛṣṇa when he arrived. Saying his name repeatedly she said nothing else. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa** [**5.13.44**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/5.13.44)**)**

These are the principle gopīs among them all. They are named in Bhaviṣya and other Purāṇas and will be shown in the verse jayati jana-nivasaḥ. (SB [10.90.48](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/90.48))

### Text 9

*sarvās tāḥ keśavāloka- paramotsava-nirvṛtāḥ*  
*jahur viraha-jaṁ tāpaṁ prājñaṁ prāpya yathā janāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**All the gopīs enjoyed the greatest festivity when they saw their beloved, most beautiful Kṛṣṇa again. They gave up the distress of separation, just as people in general forget their misery when they gain the association of a great devotee.**

**Комментарий:**

There were similar to householders who meet knowers of bhagavat- tattva, since it was said previously gṛheṣu tapta-nirviṇṇā yathācyuta- janāgame: the householders, who have suffered and are detached, become happy on meeting devotees of the Lord (SB [10.20.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/20.20)).

### Text 10

*tābhir vidhūta-śokābhir bhagavān acyuto vṛtaḥ*  
*vyarocatādhikaṁ tāta puruṣaḥ śaktibhir yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Encircled by the gopīs, who were now relieved of all distress, Kṛṣṇa, perfect in himself, without fault, shone forth more splendidly than previously. My dear King, Kṛṣṇa thus appeared like the a king encircled by his powers.**

**Комментарий:**

Surrounded by the gopīs who had become united due to pacification of their anger and pride (tābhiḥ), Bhagavān, towards who the attachment of the gopīs was without interruption (acyutaḥ), shone even more just as a king (puruṣaḥ) surrounded by his powers fully manifested or like a worshipper of the Lord (puruṣaḥ) surrounded by jñāna, vairāgya, and meditation. Thus just as king or a worshipper does not shine when those respective elements are imperfect similarly, when the gopīs were suffering Bhagavān did not shine. Thus they are described as the śaktis of the Lord.

### Texts 11-12

*tāḥ samādāya kālindyā nirviśya pulinaṁ vibhuḥ*  
*vikasat-kunda-mandāra surabhy-anila-ṣaṭpadam*

*śarac-candrāṁśu-sandoha- dhvasta-doṣā-tamaḥ śivam*  
*kṛṣṇāyā hasta-taralā cita-komala-vālukam*

**Перевод:**

**The almighty Lord then took the gopīs with him to another the bank of the Kālindī and entered its middle area with a breeze bearing the fragrance of blooming kunda and mandāra flowers, attracting many bees. The abundant rays of the autumn moon dispelled the darkness of night and the hands of the waves scattered piles of soft sand upon the shore.**

**Комментарий:**

They attained a place suitable for the rāsa dance. This is described in two verses. He came to the bank by holding their hands. In this manner he shone. The bank is described in three lines.

There were bees because of the wind fragrant with blossoming jasmine and mandāra flowers. The breeze was cool due to its connection with the bank and it was gentle because the bees hoovered in it. The darkness of night was dissipated by the mass of rays of the autumn moon. It was a form of happiness (śivam). It had soft sand brought together by hand-like waves of the Yamunā(kṛṣṇāyā).

### Text 13

*tad-darśanāhlāda-vidhūta-hṛd-rujo*  
*manorathāntaṁ śrutayo yathā yayuḥ*  
*svair uttarīyaiḥ kuca-kuṅkumāṅkitair*  
*acīkḷpann āsanam ātma-bandhave*

**Перевод:**

**Their heartache vanquished by the joy of seeing Kṛṣṇa, the gopīs had their desires completely fulfilled, just as the Vedas become fulfilled by revealing Kṛṣṇa. For their dear friend Kṛṣṇa they arranged a seat with their shawls which were smeared with the kuṅkuma powder from their breasts.**

**Комментарий:**

The gopīs rendered service befitting their friendship. Their mental anguish had been dissipated by the intense bliss on seeing Kṛṣṇaand the bank, and had their desires fulfilled (manorathāntam), just as the śrutis, propagating various philosophies like karma, on revealing Kṛṣṇa’s svarūpa endowed with such pastimes, giving up the low condition of various philosophies, attained bliss of the highest essence of themselves. With happy hearts they made a seat for him in order to establish him as the ācārya of prema aboutwhich they would inquire.

The seat is described. The used the cloth (shawls) they wore on their upper bodies, which were used as covering as will be stated bykuca-paṭṭikām vā (SB [10.33.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/33.17)). The cloth was very fine, with edges of golden lines. Their shawls were marked with kuṅkuma fromtheir breast because of the falling streams of tears from weeping due to separation. Why did they give him as their tribute their shawls, suitable for their own wear, with seeming slackening of shame? Because of the feeling that he was their close friend (ātmā-bandhave). It is understood that individual seats were made by different groups.

### Text 14

*tatropaviṣṭo bhagavān sa īśvaro*  
*yogeśvarāntar-hṛdi kalpitāsanaḥ*  
*cakāsa gopī-pariṣad-gato ’rcitas*  
*trailokya-lakṣmy-eka-padaṁ vapur dadhat*

**Перевод:**

**Though masters of yoga fix a seat for him by intense concentration of their minds, Kṛṣṇa, full of all powers and capable of revealing those powers, took his seat on that stained cloth, in the assembly of gopīs and revealed impossible beauty. He revealed in front of them a manifestation which gave exclusive shelter to the wealth of all types of beauty of all objects existing until his appearance in all the three worlds and even Mahāvaikuṇṭha.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa appeared most beautiful being situated on the seats they made. This is described.

How could he sit simultaneously on all the seats? He was capable of manifesting many forms (īśvaraḥ). Why did he sit on them? He was Bhagavān (possessed of desire). He desired to sit on them. Bhaga can means desire according to Amara-kośa.

Moreover, a seat is made for him in the hearts of Śiva, Sanaka and others masters of yoga (yogeśvara). He who shines with difficulty on the unimpaired seats created in the lotus hearts of the yogeśvaras shone while sitting on the seats made of second-hand cloth of the gopīs by his desire. Previously he held their lower cloths on his shoulders. He went by himself among the gopīs (pariṣad-gataḥ), though he is brought into the minds by yogeśvaras with difficulty. He was served (arcitaḥ) by offerings of betelnut, etc. He had a body which was the main shelter (padam) of the wealth of beauty (lakṣmī) of all objects including his svāṁśas in the three worlds. He was nourished by drinking the sweet smiling glances of the gopīs. Or sitting there endowed with all that beauty, he was brought by the yogeśvaras into each of their hearts by meditation the seats they had prepared in their hearts.

### Text 15

*sabhājayitvā tam anaṅga-dīpanaṁ*  
*sahāsa-līlekṣaṇa-vibhrama-bhruvā*  
*saṁsparśanenāṅka-kṛtāṅghri-hastayoḥ*  
*saṁstutya īṣat kupitā babhāṣire*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa had awakened romantic desires within the gopīs, and they honored him by glancing at him with playful smiles, gesturing amorously with their eyebrows, and massaging his hands and foot as they held them in their laps. Even while worshiping him, however, they felt somewhat angry, and thus they addressed him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

They honored Kṛṣṇa – who stimulated desire in himself or in them by his playful eyebrows and smiling glances –with bhāvas suitable to those.

“Previously you left us and went away. Now you are acting in this manner.” To hide that affectionate anger, they praised him whilesoftly massaging his foot and hands (aṅghri-hastayoḥ, spoken in dual with the idea that they are similar), having taken them into their laps.

“Your hands and foot are very cool. Just by touching them our pain is destroyed. You are a moon and do not know our pain.” They praised him sarcastically and while having a little anger arising from natural affection they spoke to him.

### Text 16

*śrī-gopya ūcuḥ*  
*bhajato ’nubhajanty eka eka etad-viparyayam*  
*nobhayāṁś ca bhajanty eka etan no brūhi sādhu bhoḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs said: Some people reciprocate the affection only of those who are affectionate toward them, while others show affection even to those who are indifferent or inimical. And yet others will not show affection toward anyone. Dear Kṛṣṇa, please properly explain this matter to us.**

**Комментарий:**

It is confirmed many times that Kṛṣṇa has great affection for us. Why did he today leave us in a very painful and difficult situation?Hearing from his mouth the reason for this, we will be without doubt and will serve him. The gopīs with this deep intention inquired from him.

They speak a riddle. O Kṛṣṇa, most wise! Some persons respond to people worshiping them according to their worship. Other persons are the opposite. Not considering being worshipped, they respond to everyone. Others do not respond to persons who worship them or who do not worship them. Tell us correctly about this. Who are these people? What is their worshipping and not worshipping. Please explain this. The person responding and the object of response are combined in etat, neuter according to the rule napuṁsakam anapuṁsakena-ekavac cāsyānyatarasyām (Pāninī 1.2.69). Tell us about them. They address him with the vocative bhoḥ in order to check the inattention caused by the riddle. Do not become stifled, fearing some fault in yourself.

### Text 17

*śrī-bhagavān uvāca*  
*mitho bhajanti ye sakhyaḥ svārthaikāntodyamā hi te*  
*na tatra sauhṛdaṁ dharmaḥ svārthārthaṁ tad dhi nānyathā*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: O friends! Those who show affection for each other only to benefit themselves are actually selfish. They have no true friendship, nor are they following the true principles of religion. They expect benefit for themselves alone and nothing else.**

**Комментарий:**

Knowing their intentions Bhagavān spoke. O friends! Those who, expecting rewards for helping others, respond to others, are very selfish. Their efforts are constantly fixed on their own goals. They worship themselves, not others. There is no love (sauhṛdam), norfaultless dharma.

### Text 18

*bhajanty abhajato ye vai karuṇāḥ pitarau yathā*  
*dharmo nirapavādo ’tra sauhṛdaṁ ca su-madhyamāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear slender-waisted gopīs, some people are genuinely merciful or, like parents, naturally affectionate. Such persons, who devotedly serve even those who fail to reciprocate with them, are following the true, faultless path of religion, and they are true friends.**

**Комментарий:**

He answers the second question. Those who respond to person who do not worship them are of two types: without relationship and with relationship. A merciful person responds to persons who are not his relatives and a parent responds to an offspring who is a relative. Among them, the first type are pure devotees like Prahlāda since one sees unconditional mercy in them. The second type are mothers and fathers, who not expecting any recompense, experiencing happiness or suffering due to the beneficiary’s happiness or suffering, they do not give up responding properly in all ways. Among them, the first type is excellent and the second type inferior. The dharma of both types is indestructible (nirapavādaḥ) because there is no desire for results. And prema (sauhṛdaṁ) too isindestructible.

Manu speaks of dharma of the householder in raising children, etc.:

*vṛddhau ca mātā-pitarau sādhvī bhāryā sutaḥ śiśuḥ*  
*apy akārya-śataṁ kṛtvā bhartavyā manur abravīt*

**Manu has said that the elders, mother, father, the chaste wife, sons and babies should be protected even if one commits hundreds of sins to do so. (Manu-smṛti 11.10)**

O girls with beautiful waists (sumadhyamā)! As a pun he refers to the beauty of their middle question. O women whose middlequestion is beautiful! The first and last questions are not beautiful since beautiful examples are not given for these. Or O women to whom I answer the middle question beautifully. You are the examples for this.

### Text 19

*bhajato ’pi na vai kecid bhajanty abhajataḥ kutaḥ*  
*ātmārāmā hy āpta-kāmā akṛta-jñā guru-druhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Those individuals who are spiritually self-satisfied, those materially satisfied, those who are ignorant, and those who intentionally offend those who act for others’ welfare do not respond even those who love them, what to speak of those who are inimical.**

**Комментарий:**

The answer to the third question is given. Persons who do not respond, though worshipped are of four types from best to worst. The ātmārāmas, enjoying in themselves, devoid of external vision, do not respond. Another type are the full satisfied persons (āpta-kāmāḥ). Though having external vision, they do not desire enjoyment from others since they are fully satisfied. Others are ungrateful. Though desiring enjoyment from others, they do not acknowledge the help rendered by others. They are ignorant or foolish. Some are offenders to persons who help (guru-druhaḥ). A person who does a favor is definitely a guru on account of the statement sa pitā yas tu poṣaka: One who nourishes is the father (Lakṣmī-nārāyaṇa saṁhitā). Not considering the person’s help, they commit violence to that person. They are most hard-hearted. Or the person is considered guru because he protects. The person who offends his trusting protector is a guru-druhaḥ.

### Text 20

*nāhaṁ tu sakhyo bhajato ’pi jantūn*  
*bhajāmy amīṣām anuvṛtti-vṛttaye*  
*yathādhano labdha-dhane vinaṣṭe*  
*tac-cintayānyan nibhṛto na veda*

**Перевод:**

**But the reason I do not immediately reciprocate the affection of living beings even when they worship me, O gopīs, is that I want to intensify their loving devotion. They then become like a poor man who has gained some wealth and then lost it, and who thus becomes so anxious about it that he can think of nothing else.**

**Комментарий:**

Because he gives pain in separation, he cannot be the type of person that responds to those who worship them or not (mentioned inverses 17 and 18). Because he enjoys various pastimes with us he cannot be an ātmārāma or an āpta-kāma. He is not ungrateful, since he knows such answers. Rather this mahāpuruṣa must be the last type. Gazing at them as they looked at each other with smiling glances he spoke.

O friends! I am not a guru-druḥ. It is improper to label me a guru- druḥ just by giving you up for a moment for I constantly show affection through a variety of pastimes, having mercy on you, and am sold to you for very little (in return). “If you are not a guru- druḥ, then why did you give us up?”

If I do not respond to living beings (jantūn) who worship me, it is for increasing the bhakti (anuvṛtti-vṛttaye) of those who are worshiping (amīṣāṁ). An example is given.

Just like a poor man gaining wealth somehow and then losing it, becomes full (nibhṛtaḥ) of thoughts about that wealth and does not now anything else like hunger and thirst. He thinks only of that wealth.

### Text 21

*evaṁ mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda*  
*svānām hi vo mayy anuvṛttaye ’balāḥ*  
*mayā parokṣaṁ bhajatā tirohitaṁ*  
*māsūyituṁ mārhatha tat priyaṁ priyāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear girls, understanding that simply for my sake you had rejected the authority of worldly opinion, of the Vedas and of your relatives, I acted as I did only to increase your attachment to me. Even when I removed myself from your sight by suddenly disappearing, I never stopped loving you. Therefore, my beloved gopīs, please do not harbor any bad feelings toward me, your beloved.**

**Комментарий:**

He continues from that example (evam). For me you did not consider criticism of others (loka), you did not consider dharma (veda) and did not consider relatives (sva) since you gave up affection for them. To increase your attraction to me, I, having a goal,disappeared (tirohitam) without being visible (parokṣam), though you worshipped me. I was situated in your shadows, listening to your conversations. I left you in order to accomplish the rāsa dance by uniting you all and to destroy their envy of Rādhā. He did not however reveal these internal goals.

“O crest jewel of the learned! We are fully dedicated to you and are full of attraction to you. Considering us among the living entities, you show us your great powers but not affection. A full water pot cannot be filled nor does even the sky increase.” What was arranged in this way in order to not wound that affection, which could have been accomplished by prayers as well, was done by me without considering thoroughly and was great. Thus you should not hate me, seeing fault in me since I am dear to you (priyam). And you are dear to me (priyāḥ). The dear person does not find fault in the object of affection. Therefore, you should forgive me.

### Text 22

*na pāraye ’haṁ niravadya-saṁyujāṁ*  
*sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṁ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ*  
*yā mābhajan durjara-geha-śṛṅkhalāḥ*  
*saṁvṛścya tad vaḥ pratiyātu sādhunā*

**Перевод:**

**I am not able to repay my debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmā. Your connection with me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped me, cutting off all domestic ties, which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing them unpleased, he explains his nature to them.

You have faultless connection with me since you do not expect your own happiness and aim only for my happiness in your actions. I cannot repay (pāraye) your actions which are glorious in themselves (sva-sādhu-kṛtyam), not by some contact with an object which produces glory. I cannot repay your actions in the unlimited time (āyuṣā) beyond the calculation of the wise (vibhudha). Thus I am your debtor.

“According to your words ye yathā mām prapadyante (BG [4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11)) you respond to us. So how can you be a debtor?” I have not excluded that. Cutting off completely (saṁvṛścya) the shackles of the house, hard to cut, in the form of affection for husband and brothers, you worshipped me (mām abhajan). I did not respond (mā abhajam) to you who cut your shackles. Here abhajam is inferred from abhajan by the phonetic combination of n and d.

But I respond to you, while maintaining affection for my parents, etc. Thus I cannot repay. Thus may your excellent actions be repaid by your good character. By that I will not be a debtor. But actually, I am a debtor.

## Chapter 33 - The Rāsa Dance

### Text 1

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*itthaṁ bhagavato gopyaḥ śrutvā vācaḥ su-peśalāḥ*  
*jahur viraha-jaṁ tāpaṁ tad-aṅgopacitāśiṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When the gopīs heard the Lord speak these most charming words, they forgot their distress caused by separation from him. Touching his limbs, they felt all their desires fulfilled.**

**Комментарий:**

*trayas-triṁśe rāsa-nṛtya-sambhoga-vana-kelayaḥ \|*  
*parīkṣic-chukayor āsan praśnottara-vacāṁsi ca*

**In the thirty-third chapter the rāsa dance, enjoyment and playing in the forest, and questions and answers between Parīkṣit and Śukadeva are described.**

Hear the Lord’s words as previously described, the gopīs gave up their pain. His words were most pleasing (supeśalāḥ). Peśala meansattractive according to Medinī. Their desires were fulfilled (upacita) by their touching his body. His desires were fulfilled by touching their bodies. Tad-aṅgopacitāśiṣaḥ is a modifier for both Kṛṣṇa and gopīs.

### Text 2

*tatrārabhata govindo rāsa-krīḍām anuvrataiḥ*  
*strī-ratnair anvitaḥ prītair anyonyābaddha-bāhubhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**When their minds were in harmony, Govinda then began the pastime of the rāsa dance in the company of those best among women, who were dedicated only to him, who joyfully linked their arms together with him.**

**Комментарий:**

Govinda began the rāsa dance with the jewels among women in Vṛndāvana (tatra). Rising from his seat he was inclined to perform the dance. The characteristics of the rāsa dance are described:

*naṭair gṛhīta-kaṇṭhinām anyo’nyātta-kara-śriyāṁ*  
*nartakīnām bhaved rāso maṇḍalī-bhūya nartanam*

**Rāsa is the dance with women forming a circle holding each other’s hands and their necks being held by the male dancers.**

The etymological meaning is a collection of rasas such as dancing, singing, embracing, etc. The word is formed according to the sūtra, tasya samūha (Pāṇini 4.2.37). They bound their arms together mutually among themselves with favorable attitude towards each other due to unanimity. The mutuality was amongst themselves and not with him. They thought, “He should remain in this circle and not leave.” Thus, they held their hands tightly (ābaddha). This was their deep intention.

### Text 3

*rāsotsavaḥ sampravṛtto gopī-maṇḍala-maṇḍitaḥ*  
*yogeśvareṇa kṛṣṇena tāsāṁ madhye dvayor dvayoḥ*  
*praviṣṭena gṛhītānāṁ kaṇṭhe sva-nikaṭaṁ striyaḥ*  
*yaṁ manyeran nabhas tāvad vimāna-śata-saṅkulam*  
*divaukasāṁ sa-dārāṇām autsukyāpahṛtātmanām*

**Перевод:**

**The festive rāsa dance commenced, with the gopīs arrayed in a circle. Kṛṣṇa expanded himself and entered between each pair of gopīs, placing his arms around their necks. As that master of yoga-māyā each girl thought he was standing next to her alone. The devatās and their wives were overwhelmed with eagerness to witness the rāsa dance, and they soon crowded the sky with their hundreds of celestial airplanes.**

**Комментарий:**

The manner of congregating is described in three lines less six syllables (i.e. till kaṇṭhe). The rāsa dance began in its entirety with Kṛṣṇa. He entered between each pair of gopīs situated in a circle. Here it is suggested that the state of an independent doer was given to the rāsa dance by the Lord who took the role of an instrument, or else the word sampravartitaḥ (made to undertake by someone) would have been used instead of sampravṛttaḥ. In this way it became the more excellent than all pastimes and thus even Lakṣmī desired to enter it but could not as will be stated by, nāyaṁ śriyo ’ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ: the gopīs received benedictions from the Lord that neither Lakṣmī devī nor the most beautiful dancers in the heavenly planets could attain. (SB [10.47.60](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.60))

Thus the rāsa dance astonished even the Lord, who is the guru of all arts since the Lord has said:

*santi yadyapi me prājyā līlās tās tā manoharāḥ \|*  
*na hi jāne smṛte rāse mano me kīdṛśaṁ bhavet*

**Though all my major pastimes are attractive, I do not know what would happen to my mind when I think of the rāsa dance. (Bṛhad-vāmana Purāṇa)**

The gopīs were served by Sarasvatī, were expert in all arts. They are described as jewel among women. The dance was adorned with three circles of these young women of Vraja.

“How did Kṛṣṇa enter between each pair of gopīs, hold hands with each of them simultaneously and appear to be near each gopī?”He was the master of yoga (yogeśvareṇa). He manifested forms near each gopīs by his acintya-śakti (yoga-māyā). And the women thought he was near each one of them.

They are described. They were held by him around the neck. They were embraced by him on both sides.

The circle is described. It was a wheel with three rims, covered with gems whirling around, like a sixteen petalled lotus, on a jeweledpivot measuring a vitasti. The gopīs climbed on that wheel first and later Kṛṣṇa. In the middle was Kṛṣṇa with Rādhā and on the rims were his other beloveds. They were the heads of the groups, the sakhīs and sādhana-siddhas sequentially. All of them were with Kṛṣṇa:

*nṛtyan nitambinīnāṁ tad-vaidagdhya-pada-cālanaiḥ*  
*kulāla-cakravac cakraṁ bhramad āsīd dvayor api*

**The disc and Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa rotated like a potter’s wheel by the dancing gopīs’ skilful footsteps.**

*laghu-bhramac-cakra-gateḥ samā tāsāṁ gatiḥ kvacit*  
*kvacin-mandā kvacic-chīghrāḥ sa-priyasya tathā hareḥ*

**Their gait matched the speed of the turning wheel. When the wheel turned fast or slow they moved at the same speed. (Govinda-līlāmṛta)**

This is a moving circle is described in Krama-dīpikā. There is another nonmoving circle, shining like a mirror with a huge circumference.

*sthire bhramiḥ kartṛ-gatā bhavet savyāpasavyayoḥ*  
*asthire tu cakra-jā sā prātilomyānulomya-bhāk*

**In a fixed circle the revolution happens by the left and right movements of the dancers. In an unfixed circle the revolution happens by a wheel having clockwise and counter clockwise motions.**

The fixed circle is understood since it will later be said madhye maṇīnām (SB [10.33.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/33.7)).

At that very moment (tāvat), the sky became crowded with hundreds of vehicles, arranged in a circle, of the devatās who were with their wives. When Kṛṣṇa engaged in the rāsa dance, Brahmā, Śiva, Indra and other devatās approached to render service individually and to experience the bliss of the rāsa dance according to their qualification. These special devatās, celestial followers of the Lord are always in the sky and depend on doing their assigned services. The males were eager to see the dancing of Kṛṣṇa, but not the intimate portions of the pastime since they were not qualified for that and since yogamāyā covered it from them. Their wives however saw even the dancing of the gopīs since it was not improper for them.

### Text 4

*tato dundubhayo nedur nipetuḥ puṣpa-vṛṣṭayaḥ*  
*jagur gandharva-patayaḥ sa-strīkās tad-yaśo ’malam*

**Перевод:**

**Kettledrums then resounded in the sky while flowers rained down and the chief Gandharvas and their wives sang his spotless glories.**

**Комментарий:**

In the sky, drums sounded by themselves, with the proper tāla and rāga since the drummers could not beat, being overcome by bliss. Showers of flowers fell from the sky. The head Gandharvas like Tumburu with their wives sang the glories of the Supreme LordKṛṣṇa engaged in the rāsa dance, which destroyed material desires (amalam).

### Text 5

*valayānāṁ nūpurāṇāṁ kiṅkiṇīnāṁ ca yoṣitām*  
*sa-priyāṇām abhūc chabdas tumulo rāsa-maṇḍale*

**Перевод:**

**A tumultuous sound arose from the armlets, ankle bells and waist bells of the gopīs as they sported with their beloved Kṛṣṇa in the circle of the rāsa dance.**

**Комментарий:**

Havin described the festival made by the devatās in the sky, now the music is described first in order to describe the singing, etc., suitable for the dance. The sound arose from the women each of whom had Kṛṣṇa with them (sa-priyānām). The tumultuous soundwas their arrangement, as they desired it.

### Text 6

*tatrātiśuśubhe tābhir bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ*  
*madhye maṇīnāṁ haimānāṁ mahā-marakato yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, though naturally endowed with all powers, appeared most brilliant in the midst of the dancing gopīs, like a sapphire in the midst of golden gems.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was most beautiful in the circle of the rāsa dance. The son of Yaśodā (devakī-sutaḥ), though full of the six opulences (bhagavān), exceedingly shone amidst the gopīs (tatra). An example is given. Though of the color of sapphire, he became the color of an emerald because of contact with the complexion of the golden gopīs. Mahat suggests that the gem has extraordinary beauty.

### Text 7

*pāda-nyāsair bhuja-vidhutibhiḥ sa-smitair bhrū-vilāsair*  
*bhajyan madhyaiś cala-kuca-paṭaiḥ kuṇḍalair gaṇḍa-lolaiḥ*  
*svidyan-mukhyaḥ kavara-rasanāgranthayaḥ kṛṣṇa-vadhvo*  
*gāyantyas taṁ taḍita iva tā megha-cakre virejuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**With feet perform dance steps on the ground, with hands gesturing, with smiles and movements of their brows, with their braids and belts tied tight, their waists bending, their faces perspiring, the garments on their breasts moving this way and that, and their earrings swinging on their cheeks, Kṛṣṇa’s young consorts, singing, shone like streaks of lightning in a mass of clouds.**

**Комментарий:**

Just as he was most beautiful with the gopīs, they were most beautiful with him. They moved their feet according to the tāla, rasa and song, making various dance steps which did not repeat. They shook their arms in various ways though locked in each other’s arms. Or giving up holding hands, they gestured gracefully with their hands to illustrate the song. They playfully moved their brows while smiling, showing skill at dancing which indicated various rasas. They were most skillful at expressing rati through dance due to being thin by their nature. Earrings danced on their cheeks. The earrings became dancers, making their cheeks into a dancing arena, imitating the rāsa dance. Suitable sāttvika-bhāvas manifested. Their faces perspired. They had small knots on their braids and belts. This indicates that their hair and belts became loosened. These consorts of Kṛṣṇa singing about him shone. There were like lightning in a group of clouds. Without lighting the cloud does not exist nor does it rain. Without the cloud the lighting does not exist. Similarly, this indicates the eternal relationship of Kṛṣṇa with the gopīs, and that he is made to experience extreme bliss only by them.

### Text 8

*uccair jagur nṛtyamānā rakta-kaṇṭhyo rati-priyāḥ*  
*kṛṣṇābhimarśa-muditā yad-gītenedam āvṛtam*

**Перевод:**

**Their throats impassioned to please their lover, the gopīs sang loudly while they danced, overjoyed by Kṛṣṇa’s touch. This singing spread throughout the entire universe.**

**Комментарий:**

Respected by Kṛṣṇa for their dancing (nṛtya-mānāḥ), astonishing Kṛṣṇa by their dancing, they sang loudly. Their throats were colored by the colorful rāgas that they sang (rakta-kaṇṭhyaḥ).

Rāgas are described in Saṅgīta-sāra:

*tāvanta eva rāgāḥ syur yāvatyo jīva-jātayaḥ*  
*teṣu ṣoḍaśa-sāhasrī purā gopī-kṛtā varā*

**There are as many musical rāgas as there are species of life. Among these rāgas, sixteen thousand principal ones were performed by the gopīs previously.**

The reason for singing loudly was that Kṛṣṇa’s pleasure was dear to them (rati-priyāḥ). Because of contact with Kṛṣṇa they did not tire from dancing. The universe became filled with their singing. Or the universe sings about them even today.

### Text 9

*kācit samaṁ mukundena svara-jātīr amiśritāḥ*  
*unninye pūjitā tena prīyatā sādhu sādhv iti*  
*tad eva dhruvam unninye tasyai mānaṁ ca bahv adāt*

**Перевод:**

**One gopī, joining Mukunda in his singing, sang pure melodious tones that rose harmoniously above his voice. Kṛṣṇa was pleased and showed great appreciation for her performance, saying “Excellent! Excellent!” When another gopī sang in the dhruva style, Kṛṣṇa praised her even more.**

**Комментарий:**

One gopī, along with Kṛṣṇa, sang (unnīnye) svara-jātīs which were unmixed with those uttered by Kṛṣṇa or which though pure were untouched by other jātis. Unnīnye means she lead excellently because of expertise in knowledge of svaras and jātis.

There are seven svaras:

*rañjakāḥ śrotṛ-cittānām svarāḥ sapta-vidhā*  
*smṛtāḥ ṣaḍja-rṣabhau ca gāndhāro madhyamaḥ*  
*pañcamas tathā dhaivatāś ca niṣādaś ca sarve syuḥ*  
*śruti-sambhavāḥ mayūra-cātaka-cchāga-krauñca-kokila-*  
*dardurāḥ mātaṅgaś ca krameṇāha svarānetān sudurgamān*

**Notes attractive to the listeners are of seven types difficult to comprehend: ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, madhyama, pañcama, dhaivata, and niṣāda. They all arise from the śrutis. They resemble respectively the cries of the peacock, cātaka, goat, curlew, cuckoo, frog, and elephant.**

Among them the jātis, the cause of production of rāgas are eighteen:

*rāgas tu jāyate yasyāḥ sā jātir abhidhīyate*  
*śuddhā ca vikṛtā ceti sā dvidhā parikīrtitā*  
*śuddhāḥ syur jātayaḥ sapta tāḥ ṣaḍjādi-svarābhidhāḥ*  
*tā eva vikrṭāḥ satyo jātā vikṛta-saṁjñayā*  
*ṣāḍjā rṣabhī ca gāndhārī madhyamā pañcamī tathā*  
*dhaivatī cātha naiṣādī śuddhā etās tu jātayaḥ*

**That which gives rise to rāga is called jāti. There are two types: pure and altered. The pure jātis are of seven types, defined according to the seven svāras (seven notes of scale). When these are modified they are called vikṛta (altered). The pure jātis are ṣāḍjā, ṛṣabhī, gāndhārī, madhyamā, pañcamī, dhaivatī and naiṣādī.**

Kṛṣṇa was pleased with the singing of the unfathomable songs. Saying, “Excellent, excellent,” he honored her with his yellow top cloth. They say that the singer was Viśākhā.

A jāti was sung to Dhruva tāla. Kṛṣṇa respected the singer and gave many ornaments like lockets and rings. The singer was Lalitā.

### Text 10

*kācid rāsa-pariśrāntā pārśva-sthasya gadā-bhṛtaḥ*  
*jagrāha bāhunā skandhaṁ ślathad-valaya-mallikā*

**Перевод:**

**When one gopī grew tired from the rāsa dance, she turned to Kṛṣṇa, standing at her side, and grasped his shoulder with her arm. The dancing had loosened her bracelets and the flowers in her hair.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described two sakhīs with prominence of good qualities, Rādhā, their mistress, is described with prominence of good fortune. She was tired. This indicates her tender form, rather than fatigue, since that was impossible in her. She held Kṛṣṇa’s shoulder with her right arm, taking his support. Her bracelets and flowers became loose. She was a svādhīna lover. He nourished (bhṛtaḥ)discussion (gadā) about the degrees of good qualities of her two singing friends. Gadā is formed by the sūtra, ṣid-bhid-ādibhyo ’ṅ (Pāṇini 3.3.104). Some say that gadā-bhṛtaḥ means “of Kṛṣṇa.” Others say that gadā means flute, (gadābhṛt: he who holds a flute) due to the etymology, gadati madhuram: it sounds sweet.

### Text 11

*tatraikāṁsa-gataṁ bāhuṁ kṛṣṇasyotpala-saurabham*  
*candanāliptam āghrāya hṛṣṭa-romā cucumba ha*

**Перевод:**

**Upon the shoulder of one gopī Kṛṣṇa placed his arm, whose natural blue-lotus fragrance was mixed with that of the sandalwood pulp anointing it. As the gopī relished that fragrance, her bodily hair stood on end in jubilation, and she kissed his arm.**

**Комментарий:**

One gopī smelled and kissed his arm, which was kept on her shoulder, which had the fragrance of a blue lotus, though anointed with sandalwood. Due to similarity in the actions as indicated in the previous chapter (SB [10.32.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.4)) this indicates Śyāmalā.

### Text 12

*kasyāścin nāṭya-vikṣipta kuṇḍala-tviṣa-maṇḍitam*  
*gaṇḍaṁ gaṇḍe sandadhatyāḥ prādāt tāmbūla-carvitam*

**Перевод:**

**Next to Kṛṣṇa’s cheek one gopī put her own, beautified by the effulgence of her earrings, which glittered as she danced. Kṛṣṇa then carefully gave her the betel nut he was chewing.**

**Комментарий:**

He gave his chewed betel nut to one gopī who, on the pretext of being tired, placed her cheek, on which was the reflection of her earrings moving about from dancing, and which was thus decorated, on his cheek, which was similar. He gave it, making her face come in front of his face (prādāt).
