The gopī described in this verse must be Śaibyā, being similar to the gopī described in SB [10.32.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.5).

### Text 13

*nṛtyatī gāyatī kācit kūjan nūpura-mekhalā*  
*pārśva-sthācyuta-hastābjaṁ śrāntādhāt stanayoḥ śivam*

**Перевод:**

**Another gopī, with the bells on her ankles and waist tinkling, became fatigued as she danced and sang. Another placed upon her breasts the comforting lotus hand of Acyuta, who was standing by her side.**

**Комментарий:**

One gopī, dancing and singing, took the lotus hand of Acyuta, who was by his side. This is Candrāvalī because of similarity the gopīwho took his hand in the previous chapter.

One gopī however placed his lotus-like hand on her breasts. In the previous chapter just as she placed his lotus-like feet on her breasts, now she placed the lotus-like hands. In either case it removed the pain in her breasts. (This is Padmā as in SB [10.32.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.5).) The eighth gopī, namely Bhadrā, though not mentioned here, is to be understood as previously.

### Text 14

*gopyo labdhvācyutaṁ kāntaṁ śriya ekānta-vallabham*  
*gṛhīta-kaṇṭhyas tad-dorbhyāṁ gāyantyas tam vijahrire*

**Перевод:**

**Having attained as their intimate lover Acyuta, their exclusive consort, the gopīs, goddesses of fortune, enjoyed great pleasure. They sang his glories as he held their necks with his arms.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the pastimes of the main gopīs, the pastimes of all according to their individual natures is described. Having attained attractive (kāntam) Kṛṣṇa, their exclusive consort, the gopīs enjoyed pastimes. They were Lakṣmīs (śriyaḥ). Brahma-saṁhitāsays lakṣmī-sahasra-śata-sambhrama-sevyamānam: Govinda is served by hundreds of thousands of Lakṣmīs. Śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ: the gopīs are Lakṣmīs and Kṛṣna is the supreme Puruṣa. Thus the gopīs were a expansions of the Mahā-lakṣmī of Gokula. Śriyaḥ should not be connected with ekānta-vallabhaṁ acyutam (Kṛṣṇa, the exclusive consort of Lakṣmī) since Lakṣmī of Vaikuṇṭha is not related to this pastime and since it is said:

*yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo*  
*vihāya kāmān su-ciraṁ dhṛta-vratā*

**The goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. (SB** [**10.16.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/16.36)**)**

*nāyaṁ śriyo ’ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ*  
*svar-yoṣitāṁ nalina-gandha-rucāṁ kuto ’nyāḥ*

**When Kṛṣṇa was dancing with the gopīs in the rāsa-līlā, the gopīs were embraced by the arms of the Lord. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or other consorts in the spiritual world. (SB** [**10.47.50**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.50)**)**

### Text 15

*karṇotpalālaka-viṭaṅka-kapola-gharma-*  
*vaktra-śriyo valaya-nūpura-ghoṣa-vādyaiḥ*  
*gopyaḥ samaṁ bhagavatā nanṛtuḥ sva-keśa-*  
*srasta-srajo bhramara-gāyaka-rāsa-goṣṭhyām*

**Перевод:**

**The beauty of the gopīs’ faces was enhanced by the lotus flowers behind their ears with locks of hair and drops of perspiration decorating their cheeks. With their armlets and ankle bells making a loud musical sound, with their chaplets scattered, the gopīs danced with their sweet lover in the arena of the rāsa dance as swarms of bees sang in accompaniment.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described individually the beauty of their singing and dancing, the beauty of their faces caused by the dancing is described. Their faces were beautiful with lotus-shaped ear ornaments, with cheeks decorated by locks of hair, and with drops of perspiration. With ankle bells and bracelets and musical instruments they danced with the Lord, while garlands fell from their hair. Their hair,satisfied by the tāla and movements, offered a reward by sprinkling flowers at their feet. Where did this take place? It took place in the assembly (goṣṭhyām) of the rāsa dance where the singers were bees.

When the Gandharvas and their wives, singers and musicians, became stunned by bliss, the bracelets acted as instrumental music and the bees acted as singers to perfect the ingredients of the rāsa dance without break.

### Text 16

*evaṁ pariṣvaṅga-karābhimarśa-*  
*snigdhekṣaṇoddāma-vilāsa-hāsaiḥ*  
*reme rameśo vraja-sundarībhir*  
*yathārbhakaḥ sva-pratibimba-vibhramaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In this way Kṛṣṇa, though he is the master of Lakṣmī, took pleasure in the company of the young women of Vraja by embracing them, caressing them and glancing lovingly at them as he smiled playfully, while acting boldly, as child plays with his reflection.**

**Комментарий:**

The limbs of enjoyment were accomplished for the Lord by the limbs of the rāsa dance.

The Lord enjoyed with them by embraces as he danced becoming one with each one of them, and by touching them with his hand(abhimarśa). When he finished dancing, he touched their left breast with his right hand. He glanced lovingly at their concealed limbs.On the pretext of taking a reward he kissed them (uddāma-vilāsa). After kissing them his face became joyful with a smile. By these means the master of Gokula’s Mahā-lakṣmī (rameśaḥ), the son of Nanda played (reme) with women of Vraja, the expansions of Mahā-lakṣmī. In playing with them, he did not manifest a particle of his lordly powers.

A person dependent on prema, he was like a small child who is foolish. Even a particle of power difficult to behold did not manifest.

“How did he, one person, enjoy with millions of gopīs?” Pratibimbam means ‘with each replica (bimba)’ or with each svarūpa. He for whom each of his replica is his pastime (sva-pratibimba-vibhramaḥ) enjoyed with each gopī by an individual svarūpa. He played using as many prakāśas (manifestations).

*kṛtvā tāvantam ātmānaṁ yāvatīr gopa-yoṣitaḥ*  
*reme sa bhagavāṁs tābhir ātmārāmo ‘pi līlayā*

**Expanding himself us many times as there were cowherd women to associate with, the Supreme Lord, though self- satisfied, playfully enjoyed their company. (SB** [**10.33.19**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/33.19)**)**

### Text 17

*tad-aṅga-saṅga-pramudākulendriyāḥ*  
*keśān dukūlaṁ kuca-paṭṭikāṁ vā*  
*nāñjaḥ prativyoḍhum alaṁ vraja-striyo*  
*visrasta-mālābharaṇāḥ kurūdvaha*

**Перевод:**

**O hero of the Kuru dynasty! Their senses overwhelmed by the joy of having his physical association, the gopīs could not prevent their hair, their dresses and the cloths covering their breasts from becoming disheveled. Their garlands and ornaments loosened.**

**Комментарий:**

By the pastimes of the Lord the gopīs became overwhelmed with happiness. Their senses were overwhelmed by the great bliss of associating with Kṛṣṇa’s limbs. They were not able (alam) to keep (prativyoḍhum) their hair, etc., easily in order as previously. Their garlands of flowers and jeweled ornaments loosened.

### Text 18

*kṛṣṇa-vikrīḍitaṁ vīkṣya mumuhuḥ khe-cara-striyaḥ*  
*kāmārditāḥ śaśāṅkaś ca sa-gaṇo vismito ’bhavat*

**Перевод:**

**The wives of the devatās, observing Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, were bewildered and became agitated with desire. The moon and his entourage of stars became astonished.**

**Комментарий:**

The wives of the devatās became overwhelmed at seeing Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. The moon along with the stars became astonished. They remained stationary in the sky all night. The zodiac (śiśumāra- cakra) also stopped moving.

### Text 19

*kṛtvā tāvantam ātmānaṁ yāvatīr gopa-yoṣitaḥ*  
*reme sa bhagavāṁs tābhir ātmārāmo ’pi līlayā*

**Перевод:**

**Expanding himself as many times as there were cowherd women to associate with, the Supreme Lord, though self-satisfied, playfully enjoyed their company.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa then enjoyed in bower houses ornamented with attractive canopies and beds, furnished with garlands, betel nut, and drinks. He revealed as many forms of himself as there were gopīs by his līlā-śakti and enjoyed with them, though he is self-satisfied(ātmārāmaḥ).

### Text 20

*tāsāṁ rati-vihāreṇa śrāntānāṁ vadanāni saḥ*  
*prāmṛjat karuṇaḥ premṇā śantamenāṅga pāṇinā*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that the gopīs were fatigued from conjugal enjoyment, my dear King, merciful Kṛṣṇa lovingly wiped their faces with his comforting hand.**

**Комментарий:**

He was affectionate to his beloveds.

He wiped the withered faces of the gopīs, tired from intense pastimes after giving up amorous play. He was naturally compassionate because of prema, not lust. He used his hand which was full of joy (śantamena). He also fanned them, applied ointments, offered betel nut, and arranged their dresses and each of their limbs, etc.

### Text 21

*gopyaḥ sphurat-puraṭa-kuṇḍala-kuntala-tviḍ-*  
*gaṇḍa-śriyā sudhita-hāsa-nirīkṣaṇena*  
*mānaṁ dadhatya ṛṣabhasya jaguḥ kṛtāni*  
*puṇyāni tat-kara-ruha-sparśa-pramodāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs honored their hero with smiling glances sweetened by the beauty of their cheeks and the effulgence of their curly locks and glittering golden earrings. Overjoyed from the touch of his fingernails, they chanted the glories of the all-auspicious pastimes of their husband.**

**Комментарий:**

The independent lovers, decorated with the jewels offered by Kṛṣṇa, left the bowers and joined with each other. They sang auspicious invocations indicating the completion of the rāsa festival.

They gave respect to their master, the best of men, the son of Nanda, by the effulgence of their locks with golden earrings, by the beauty of their cheeks and by their smiling glances filled with nectar and sang about the attractive (puṇyāni) actions of their hero, which destroy ignorance in the listener. They were joyful with the touch of his sharp fingernails.

### Text 22

*tābhir yutaḥ śramam apohitum aṅga-saṅga-*  
*ghṛṣṭa-srajaḥ sva-kuca-kuṅkuma-rañjitāyāḥ*  
*gandharva-pālibhir anudruta āviśad vāḥ*  
*śrānto gajībhir ibha-rāḍ iva bhinna-setuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**To dispel the fatigue, with the gopīs whose garlands had been crushed during conjugal dalliance and who were colored vermilion by the kuṅkuma powder on their breasts, Kṛṣṇa entered the water of the Yamunā, followed swiftly by bees who were singing like the best of the Gandharvas. He appeared like a lordly elephant entering the water to relax in the company of his consorts, as if breaking the dikes in a paddy field.**

**Комментарий:**

For the sake of completeness of rāsa dance, playing in the water comparable to the avabhṛtha bath after a sacrifice is described.

With the gopīs, Kṛṣṇa entered Yamunā’s water. Why? To take away fatigue, to remove the pains arising from the rāsa dance and amorous play. The fatigue was the desire to play in water, since otherwise, fatigue was not present in rāsa dance or amorous play.

The gopīs are described. They were colored by the kuṅkuma from their breasts, due to absorption in amorous play all their limbs hadcome in contact with the kuṅkuma, and their jasmine garlands had been crushed by close contact with the Lord’s limbs. The garland is of jasmine since though they are actually quite pale in complexion, they were colored red by the kuṅkuma. Kṛṣṇa was followed bybees, the best singers (gandharva-pa). Gandharva can mean a singer according to Viśva. Or he was followed by assistants, the bees, skillful at singing suitably for the water play. He was like the king of the elephants with female elephants, breaking all boundaries. This indicates the great beauty of the pastime. In terms of Kṛṣṇa, breaking all boundaries means he surpassed normal human conduct.

### Text 23

*so ’mbhasy alaṁ yuvatibhiḥ pariṣicyamānaḥ*  
*premṇekṣitaḥ prahasatībhir itas tato ’ṅga*  
*vaimānikaiḥ kusuma-varṣibhir īdyamāno*  
*reme svayaṁ sva-ratir atra gajendra-līlaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, in the water Kṛṣṇa was splashed on all sides by the laughing gopīs, who looked at him with love. As the devatās worshiped him by showering flowers from their airplanes, the self-satisfied Lord took pleasure in playing like the king of the elephants.**

**Комментарий:**

He had pastimes like the king of the elephants and for him the wealth was the amorous pastimes (sva-ratiḥ).

### Text 24

*tataś ca kṛṣṇopavane jala-sthala*  
*prasūna-gandhānila-juṣṭa-dik-taṭe*  
*cacāra bhṛṅga-pramadā-gaṇāvṛto*  
*yathā mada-cyud dviradaḥ kareṇubhiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Then the Lord strolled through a small forest on the bank of the Yamunā. This forest was filled to its limits with breezes carrying the fragrances of all the flowers growing on the land and in the water. Followed by his entourage of bees and beautiful women, Kṛṣṇa appeared like an elephant flowing with mada in the company of she-elephants.**

**Комментарий:**

After playing in the water (tataḥ) and after putting on clothing and ornaments offered by Vṛndā devī (ca), Kṛṣṇa wandered about in a grove of the Yamunā, beautiful with thousands of jeweled pavilions. He also performed the pastime of sleeping. That grove was served in all directions by breeze fragrant with flowers of the water and land. Kṛṣṇa was surrounded by groups of intoxicated bees. He was like the king of elephants flowing with mada.

### Text 25

*evaṁ śaśāṅkāṁśu-virājitā niśāḥ*  
*sa satya-kāmo ’nuratābalā-gaṇaḥ*  
*siṣeva ātmany avaruddha-saurataḥ*  
*sarvāḥ śarat-kāvya-kathā-rasāśrayāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**With gopīs firmly attached to him with anurāga, Kṛṣṇa, whose desires are always pure, who had fixed in his mind enjoyment with them, served the nights lit by the rays of the moon — all the nights which give shelter to poetic topics or rasa in autumn.**

**Комментарий:**

He had various pastimes with the gopīs on other nights, as he did on this night in the autumn.

That is expressed this verse.

He served respectfully (siṣeva) all the nights, which were lit by the rays of the moon by the power of yoga-māyā, as described previously in the rāsa dance. He is described. He had desires and amorous play which were spiritual like his svarūpa (satya-kamaḥ). He was accompanied by girls who enjoyed him after he enjoyed them (anu- ratābalā-ganaḥ). It is not that the secret meaning is revealed here, since it is not contrary to the rule, dvy-arthaiḥ padaiḥ piśunayec ca rahasya-vastu: Secrets should be revealed through phrases with two meanings, and since the second meaning is “He was attracted (anurata) to the girls always.” One should seek such meanings elsewhere too. Actually the Lord became attached completely to those pastimes. This is further described.

He had restrained and established (avaruddha) bhāva, hāva and other amorous acts (saurataḥ) in his mind (ātmani).

During the day he meditated on whatever actions were revealed to him in the nights by the gopīs. Some explain the words saurataḥ to mean actions related to amorous love since that usage is seen in the story of Rukmiṇī, evaṁ saurata-saṁlāpaiḥ: engaging in talks of amorous love (SB [10.60.58](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/60.58)). The nights are described. They are the shelter of tasty topics of poets which occur in a year (śarat)composed of six seasons. Śarat can mean year according to Amara- kośa.

He served the pastimes related to spring and other seasons too in the nights. Thus the nights were very deep. The events are summarized:

*vaṁśī-sañjalpitam anurataṁ rādhāyāntardhi-keliḥ*  
*prādurbhūyāsanam adhipaṭaṁ praśna-kūṭottaraṁ ca*  
*nṛtyollāsaḥ punar api rati-krīḍitaṁ vāri-khelā*  
*kṛṣṇāraṇye viharaṇam iti śrīmatī rāsa-līlā*

**The rāsa pastimes consist of the following: playing the flute, conversing with the gopīs, playing with them, disappearing with Rādhā for pastimes, appearing again, sitting down on cloth, engaging in questions and answers, dancing in bliss, again engaging in amorous acts, playing in the water, and playing in the forest on the bank of the Yamunā.**

### Text 26

*śrī-parīkṣid uvāca*  
*saṁsthāpanāya dharmasya praśamāyetarasya ca*  
*avatīrṇo hi bhagavān aṁśena jagad-īśvaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Parīkṣit Mahārāja said: O brāhmaṇa, though full of all powers, the lord of the universe, he has descended to this earth along with Balarāma to destroy irreligion and reestablish religious principles.**

**Комментарий:**

Though Parīkṣit, who knew the true nature of the Lord and his devotees, had no doubts, however he asks so that there are not doubts in the members of the assembly, who were practicing harsh jñāna and yoga, regarding his teacher Śukadeva, that giving up topics of internal Brahman and speaking topics about women of the external world, though highly renounced why is Śuka opposing realization?

Bhagavān appeared with Balarāma (aṁśena) in order to propagate dharma which was lost, and to protect what was continuing and to completely uproot adharma (itara).

### Text 27

*sa kathaṁ dharma-setūnāṁ vaktā kartābhirakṣitā*  
*pratīpam ācarad brahman para-dārābhimarśanam*

**Перевод:**

**He is the original speaker, follower and guardian of moral laws. How, then, could he have violated them by touching other men’s wives?**

**Комментарий:**

Being the teacher (vaktā), preacher (kartā) and the protector (abhirakṣitā) of the limits of dharma, how can Kṛṣṇa be going against it by performing adharma which is contrary? “What is that?” Touching others wives since the statements of you, the Lord and the gopīs respectively are:

Śuśūrṣantyaḥ patīn: they were serving their husbands. (SB [10.29.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.6)) Bhartuḥ śuśrūṣaṇam strīṇām: serving husbands is the highest dharma. (SB [10.29.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.24))

Pati-sutānvaya: we have completely rejected our husbands, children, ancestors, brothers and other relatives. (SB [10.31.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/31.16))

It is certainly not just adharma such as eating onions, but the very bold act of associating with other’s wives. O form of the Vedas (brahman)! O son of Vyāsa! If one says the Lord acted independently, then by accepting this relaxation just as he accepted its result (enjoyment with the gopīs), in the same way accepting adharma he should have borne the results. This is the objection.

### Text 28

*āpta-kāmo yadu-patiḥ kṛtavān vai jugupsitam*  
*kim-abhiprāya etan naḥ śaṁśayaṁ chindhi su-vrata*

**Перевод:**

**O faithful upholder of vows, please destroy our doubt by explaining to us what purpose the self-satisfied Lord of the Yadus had in mind when he behaved so contemptibly.**

**Комментарий:**

If you say that adharma does not touch him since he is the Supreme Lord, still it is contemptible. With what intention did he do this? It is not possible to say that he acts in this way to fulfill his amorous desires since he is full in his desires (āpta-kāmaḥ). Nor can one say that he descended to perform contemptible acts since that would be contrary to his position as the lord of the Yadus. The Yadus performed pious acts. Seeing even you who are the best of persons of good conduct (suvrata) are absorbed in this pastime, a doubt arises for all people.

### Text 29

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*dharma-vyatikramo dṛṣṭa īśvarāṇāṁ ca sāhasam*  
*tejīyasāṁ na doṣāya vahneḥ sarva-bhujo yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The status of powerful controllers is not harmed by any apparently audacious transgression of morality we may see in them, for they are just like fire, which devours everything fed into it and remains unpolluted.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to show by kaimutya-nyāya that the Lord has no fault in accepting the gopīs if they are other’s wives, Śukadeva, knowing Parīkṣit’s intentions, speaks of the conduct of devotees of the Lord to whom he has shown mercy. Thus, what can be said of the Lord?

Some transgression of dharma is seen in persons with opulence such as austerity, knowledge, etc., such as Brahmā (īśvarāṇāṁ), such as Brahmā’s lust for his daughter and Bṛhaspati approaching Utathya’s (his brother’s) wife, who are powerful, do not produce fault for them. Just as fire, though devouring everything, does not become impure.

### Text 30

*naitat samācarej jātu manasāpi hy anīśvaraḥ*  
*vinaśyaty ācaran mauḍhyād yathārudro ’bdhi-jaṁ viṣam*

**Перевод:**

**One who is not a great controller should never imitate the behavior of ruling personalities, even mentally. If out of foolishness an ordinary person does imitate such behavior, he will simply destroy himself, just as a person who is not Rudra would destroy himself if he tried to drink an ocean of poison.**

**Комментарий:**

“But even others should act this way according to the principle, ‘Whatever the leader does, others follow.” (BG [3.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/3.21))

That is not so. Jīvas who are devoid of austerity, knowledge and power, and controlled by karma, should never, not even in their minds, act in this way, even partially. If he acts in this way out of foolishness, he will fall down. The ignorance about the powers of great controllers and ignorance about one’s lack of powers is the foolishness. Just as a person other than Śiva while drinking the kālakūṭa poison is immediately destroyed. But the powerful person is not destroyed. Rather, because of his powers, he becomes glorious, like Śiva with his blue throat.

### Text 31

*īśvarāṇāṁ vacaḥ satyaṁ tathaivācaritaṁ kvacit*  
*teṣāṁ yat sva-vaco-yuktaṁ buddhimāṁs tat samācaret*

**Перевод:**

**The statements of the Lord’s empowered servants are authoritative, and the acts they perform are exemplary when consistent with those statements. Therefore one who is intelligent should carry out their instructions.**

**Комментарий:**

“Then, the correct actions of the great are not authoritative for others.” The words of great are for the benefit of devotees and should be accepted as proof (satyaṁ) and their actions are like that (i.e. for the benefit of others) sometimes as in the case of Rāmacandra and others. Therefore this arrangement. Their conduct (yad) which is not contradictory (yuktam) to their injunctions (sva-vacas) should alone be practiced by the intelligent. By the word buddhimān it is stated that the action too should be done after deliberation. For instance, “that sinful person should be killed.” (SB [1.7.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/7.39)) Though these words of the Lord prescribed killing Āśvatthāmā, they were not carried out by Arjuna.

### Text 32

*kuśalācaritenaiṣām iha svārtho na vidyate*  
*viparyayeṇa vānartho nirahaṅkāriṇāṁ prabho*

**Перевод:**

**O Parīkṣit, you can understand! When these great persons who are free from false ego act piously in this world, they have no selfish motives to fulfill, and even when they act in apparent contradiction to the laws of piety, they are not subject to sinful reactions.**

**Комментарий:**

“Then why do they act rashly?” For persons endowed with austerity, knowledge and powers, who are devoid of bodily identity (nirahaṅkāriṇām), there is no happiness (arthaḥ) by performing sat-karmas and no suffering (anarthaḥ) caused by performing asat-karmas. Those good and bad karmas, occurring sometimes, do not cling to the person expert at brahma-vidyā, just as water drops do not cling to the lotus leaf.

### Text 33

*kim utākhila-sattvānāṁ tiryaṅ-martya-divaukasām*  
*īśituś ceśitavyānāṁ kuśalākuśalānvayaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**How, then, could the Lord of all created beings—animals, men and devatās—have any connection with the piety and impiety that affect his controlled creatures?**

**Комментарий:**

The current topic is discussed. If those who have received the mercy of the Lord have no relationship with good or bad karmas, thenwhat to speak of the Lord having any relationship to those karmas.

Kim uta means “excessively, strong, well” according to Amara-kośa. The controller (iśituḥ) of those controlled (īśitavyānām), creatures in tamas, rajas and sattva, animals, humans and devatās respectively is not regulated by good and bad karma for certain (kim uta).

### Text 34

*yat-pāda-paṅkaja-parāga-niṣeva-tṛptā*  
*yoga-prabhāva-vidhutākhila-karma-bandhāḥ*  
*svairaṁ caranti munayo ’pi na nahyamānās*  
*tasyecchayātta-vapuṣaḥ kuta eva bandhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The devotees, filled with prema, continually meditating on the particles of beauty emanating from his lotus feet, having destroyed all karma by the power of his bhakti-yoga, wander about performing actions without accruing bondage. So how could there be any question of bondage for the Lord himself, who accepts the bodies of the gopīs by his own sweet will?**

**Комментарий:**

This is described in detail. Even sages like Parāśara and Viśvāmitra who destroy the bondage of karmas of people who see them (vidhutākhila), what to speak of their own karmas, by the power of bhakti (yoga-prabhāva) are not bound by good or bad karmas (nahyamānāḥ) which may occur somehow. They wander about as they choose. What is the bondage of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, who accepts the bodies of the gopīs by his independent will? There will be bondage for those who doubt about his bondage.

### Text 35

*gopīnāṁ tat-patīnāṁ ca sarveṣām eva dehinām*  
*yo ’ntaś carati so ’dhyakṣaḥ krīḍaneneha deha-bhāk*

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, appearing directly in this world, moves among the gopīs and their apparent husbands as well as the other inhabitants of Vraja, in his eternal spiritual body performing his pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

The fault in the Lord for touching others’ wives is rejected. Now it is stated that for Kṛṣṇa there are no “others.” If Kṛṣṇa, the bodymeasuring a pradeśa, who wanders about internally within the gopīs and their husbands, and who is the seer of their intelligence(adhyakṣaḥ), in Gokula (iha) because of playing enjoys the bodies of the gopīs by embraces externally and sees externally their bodies privately (deha-bhāk), then what is the fault? Nothing. One who finds fault in him commits a fault.

### Text 36

*anugrahāya bhaktānāṁ mānuṣaṁ deham āśritaḥ*  
*bhajate tādṛśīḥ krīḍā yāḥ śrutvā tat-paro bhavet*

**Перевод:**

**When the Lord assumes a humanlike body to show mercy to his devotees, he engages in such pastimes. Hearing about those pastimes a person becomes dedicated to him.**

**Комментарий:**

“If that is so, what is the Lord’s intention in playing with the gopīs with the mood that they are other’s wives, which is contemptible?”

To show mercy to the devotees who are in this world, who long to see that pastime, who are agitated without it, Kṛṣṇa, manifesting(deham āśritaḥ or āsthitaḥ) his form which appears human, or which is filled with human-like actions (mānuṣam), reveals (bhajate) such pastimes. Āśritaḥ means manifesting as in the sentence cakṣur āśritya rūpe sthite: manifesting the eye he is situated in form. Similar is the usage here. One should not explain the meaning to be “he accepted a human form,” since one who is himself the body cannot take a body and since the śruti says:

*sākṣāt prakṛti-paro ’yam ātmā gopālaḥ*

**Kṛṣṇa is ātmā, superior to prakṛti. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)**

Hearing his pastimes (yāḥ), the devotees become absorbed in them (tat-paraḥ). Or the Lord himself on hearing about those previously performed pastimes, he becomes absorbed in enacting those pastimes again. This indicates that those pastimes are most astonishing to himself.

The following has been said. I said that there is no fault in touching other’s wives for Kṛṣṇa, who is supreme, for the sake of crushing those who criticize. But actually the gopīs were of four types such as nitya-siddha, etc. Thus they were forms of the essence of hlādinī- śakti. By Gāndharva rites they were married to Kṛṣṇa and were his wives and not wives of other men since it is said, sa vo hi svāmī bhavati: he is the husband of all of you (Gopāla tāpanī Upaniṣad) and since it is said:

*aneka-janma-siddhānāṁ gopīnāṁ patir eva vā yaḥ \|*  
*nanda-nandana ity uktas trailokyānanda-vardhanaḥ*

**The master of many cowherd women who achieved perfection after many births, is called Nanda-nandana, the son of Nanda. He increases the bliss of the three worlds. (Gautamīya-tantra)**

Also, in Bhāgavatam it is said kṛṣṇa-vadhvaḥ (wives of Kṛṣṇa) (SB [10.33.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/33.7)). Still for nourishing Kṛṣṇa’s mādhurya-rasa, they appeared as others’ wives by the arrangement of līlā-śakti. And by their being other’s wives, Kṛṣṇa became excellent, like a diamond by polishing. Since the cowherds to whom the gopīs were given in marriage by their fathers, interacted only with some counter forms of gopīs manifested by yogamāyā, just as Sūrya interacts with Chāyā, the counter form of Saṁjñā (his wife), the cowherds had no tinge of hatred towards Kṛṣṇa and since it will be said nāsūyan: they did not hate him (verse 37).

In this way, the gopīs did not even speak a word to those who considered themselves husbands. The Lord’s parents considered to gopīs to be daughters-in-law since they understood the svarūpa of Bhagavān accompanied by his associates and since the gopīsgenerally stayed in the Lord’s home and their own homes within the enclosure. Even the gopīs’ parents understood about the Lord’ssvarūpa and had the conception that he was their daughters’ protector. The Lord’s relatives thought that they were wives of cowherds but that conception was annulled by knowledge of the truth, as if perceiving objects in a dream. All necessary explanation has been given.

But what is said regarding the suitability of the meaning of the statement, sa vo hi svāmī bhavati: he is your husband (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad), since they were married to Kṛṣṇa when he became the cowherds during the pastime of Brahmā’s bewilderment — that is not harmonious since later when all those cowherd boys merged into Kṛṣṇa and when the real boys returned home, the gopīs’ fame as his wives would go against the evident meaning, and since better than marriage with aṁśas of his svarūpa through fire rituals is marriage with the aṁśī through Gāndharva rites without fire rituals, and since that was desired by the gopīs (during Kātyāyanī vrata) and since there is no proof of the marriage with the aṁśas through fire rituals. This is the conclusion of the wise who have no envy.

Those who speak of these topics in terms of external material objects by equating the gopīs with women they have seen, are notfavored by anyone. Those having clear vision do not see equality of women and gold simply because they are both yellowish. The yogīs who cultivate coarse jñāna cannot realize this as it truly is. They are like frogs who serve a salt water well. They are like worms of an udumbara fruit in the milk ocean. They uselessly try to smell the fragrance of pārijāta flowering on Kailāsa.

The Lord’s svarūpa is not complete without the gopīs since at the beginning of Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad his svarūpa is stated to becomplete with them alone. Thus his svarūpa endowed with the gopīs is worshippable and is pure, full of knowledge and bliss. This is understood by the learned.

### Text 37

*nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya*  
*mohitās tasya māyayā*  
*manyamānāḥ sva-pārśva-sthān*  
*svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherd men, bewildered by Kṛṣṇa’s yogamāyā, thought their wives had remained home at their sides. They did not harbor any jealous feelings against him at any time.**

**Комментарий:**

There was not a particle of opposition to the pastime. The apparent husbands, the people of Vraja, had no hatred of Kṛṣṇa, who hadpastimes with the gopīs every night, because they were put into samādhi by yoga-māyā. The samādhi is described. They consideredthat their wives, who were imitation forms made by yogamāyā, were by their sides.

### Text 38

*brahma-rātra upāvṛtte vāsudevānumoditāḥ*  
*anicchantyo yayur gopyaḥ sva-gṛhān bhagavat-priyāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**After a night of Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa advised the gopīs to return to their homes. Although they did not wish to do so, the Lord’s beloved consorts complied with his command.**

**Комментарий:**

Another amazing feat, the supreme power of Kṛṣṇa, is explained. In the word brahma-rātre, the suffix at the end of the compound is poetic license.

After one night of Brahmā, measuring a thousand yuga cycles, had completely passed, the consorts of the Lord, though not willing to go, but advised by Nanda’s son (vāsudevena), who had manifested through viśuddha-sattva, with the understanding that there would again be such pastimes, returned home.

By yoga-māyā, one night of Brahmā entered into three yāmās of the ordinary night. Otherwise the millions of gopīs with unlimitedastonishing qualities and Kṛṣṇa, jewel among heroes, a mine of infinite qualities, would not be able to experience each other’s qualities.

### Text 39

*vikrīḍitaṁ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṁ ca viṣṇoḥ*  
*śraddhānvito ’nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ*  
*bhaktiṁ parāṁ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṁ*  
*hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Anyone who faithfully and continually hears or describes the Lord’s playful affairs with the young gopīs of Vṛndāvana will attain the highest type of prema to the Lord, quickly destroy lust, the disease of the heart, and immediately become steady.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of hearing, etc., of the rāsa pastimes is described.

The intelligent, faithful person who hears repeatedly, and who recites repeatedly as well, this pastime and also other spiritual pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, son of Nanda, who spreads everywhere (viṣṇoḥ) and who is capable of remaining close to all the gopīs simultaneously, with the gopīs, attains supreme bhakti in the form of prema very quickly and destroys quickly the sickness of the heart, kāma. Hearing and reciting repeatedly indicates great attachment (āsakti).

The suffix ktvā (in pratilabhya), indicates that when kāma is present, due to the power hearing this pastimes, prema appears and thusthe sickness disappears completely. After destroying ignorance, the attainment of Kṛṣṇa is the result of hearing, etc. Thus this worship produces the highest human goal.

*vraja-strīṇāṁ bhāvān amṛta-madhurān āśu*  
*dadhatīn ṛtā śrī-rādhāyā mahima-nikareṇātiguruṇā \|*  
*iyaṁ pañcādhyāyī vivṛtir amitārthā śikhariṇī*  
*jagannātha-prātyai kim u viśada-varṇā na bhavitā*

**Depicting nicely the sweet honey of the bhāvas of the gopīs, with the great qualities of Rādhā, the commentary on the five chapters, a mountain peak with unlimited meanings, what clear syllables does this not have for the pleasure of Jagannātha?**

*pañcādhyāyī-ṭippaṇī bhāva-ratnaiś*  
*citrā vidyā-bhūṣaṇena pragītā \|*  
*etāṁ śrī-govinda-pādābja-bhṛṅgāḥ*  
*kāruṇyārdrāḥ sādhavaḥ śodhayadhvaṁ*

**The colorful commentary on the five chapters has been sung with gems of bhāva, by Vidyābhuṣaṇa. The devotees, bees at the lotus feet of Govinda, with soft hearts, should purify this work.**

## Chapter 34 - Nanda Mahārāja Saved and Śaṅkhacūḍa Slain

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: One day the cowherd men, eager to take a trip to worship Śiva, traveled by bullock carts to the Ambikā forest.**

**Комментарий:**

In the thirty-fourth chapter, by touching it with his foot, Kṛṣṇa delivered the snake which swallowed Nanda’s foot. After killing Śaṅkhacūḍa he took his jewel. Having described the rāsa dance in the autumn, while about to speak about the rāsa dance in the spring, first the celebration of Śiva rātri and deliverance of Sudarśana there are described. At the festival of Śiva on the dark caturdaśī of Phālguna month, the cowherds by Kṛṣṇa’s desire became eager and went to the forest of Ambikā at the edge of Mathurā by chariots and carts, carrying provisions and wealth since their eagerness followed Kṛṣṇa’s desire.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**O King, after arriving there, they bathed in the Sarasvatī and then devotedly worshiped with various paraphernalia the powerful Śiva and his consort, goddess Ambikā.**

**Комментарий:**

They worshipped Śiva (paśupatim) called Gokarṇa, the king of the devotees of Viṣṇu.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**All the cowherd men gave the brāhmaṇas gifts of cows, gold, clothing and cooked grains mixed with honey, with the prayer, “May the Lord be pleased with us.”**

**Комментарий:**

They gave cows, etc. Madhu madhu means that it was sweeter than honey. The usage is like madhura-madhuram. Welcomed by the brāhmaṇas of the temple, they gave them cows, etc. They requested that Śiva or Viṣṇu (devaḥ) be pleased.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Nanda, Sunanda and the other greatly fortunate cowherds spent that night on the bank of the Sarasvatī, strictly observing their vows. They fasted, taking only water.**

**Комментарий:**

Because it was Śiva-rātri they drank only water and spent (ūṣuḥ) the night there.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**During the night a huge and extremely hungry snake appeared in that thicket. Slithering on his belly up to the sleeping Nanda Mahārāja, the snake began swallowing him.**

**Комментарий:**

A huge serpent swallowed Nanda who was sleeping in a tent. The snake crawled on its belly (uraga) and thus was not seen.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**In the clutches of the snake, Nanda Mahārāja cried out, “Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, my dear boy! This huge serpent is swallowing me! Please save me, as I am surrendered to you!”**

**Комментарий:**

Prapannam means surrendered.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**When the cowherd men heard the cries of Nanda, they immediately rose up and saw that he was being swallowed. Distraught, they beat the serpent with blazing torches.**

**Комментарий:**

They beat the snake with flaming sticks.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**But even though the firebrands were burning him, the serpent would not release Nanda Mahārāja. Then the Supreme Lord, master of his devotees, came to the spot and touched the snake with his foot.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa, who was playing among the young gopīs making lamps, came there because of the cries of Nanda and the uproar of the people and touched the serpent with his foot.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**The snake had all his sinful reactions destroyed by the touch of the Supreme Lord’s divine foot, and thus he gave up his serpent body and appeared in the form of a worshipable Vidyādhara.**

**Комментарий:**

The snake’s sin of being born as a snake was destroyed by the touch of the Lord’s divine foot. He took the form of a chief among the Vidyādharas, who was worshipped.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Hṛṣīkeśa then questioned this personality, who was standing before him with his head bowed, his brilliantly effulgent body bedecked with golden necklaces.**

**Комментарий:**

As if not knowing, in order to show his powers to his relatives, Kṛṣṇa inquired from this person standing with a shining body.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] My dear sir, you appear so wonderful, glowing with such great beauty. Who are you? And who forced you to assume this terrible body of a snake?**

**Комментарий:**

You shine with beauty (lakṣmyā). How or by whom were you made to get this low born body beyond your control?

### Text 12-13

**Перевод:**

**The serpent replied: I am the well-known Vidyādhara named Sudarśana. I was very wealthy and beautiful, and I used to wander freely in all directions in my airplane. Once I saw some deformed sages of the lineage of Aṅgirā Muni. Proud of my beauty, I ridiculed them, and because of my sin they made me assume this lowly form.**

**Комментарий:**

I was famous (śrutaḥ) as Sudarśaṇa, endowed with beauty (svarūpasampattyā). Proud of my beauty, I laughed at the deformed sages. Because of my sin, I was given this snake birth by them who had been mocked (pralabdhaiḥ).

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**It was actually for my benefit that those merciful sages cursed me, since now I have been touched by the foot of the lord of all the worlds and have thus been relieved of all inauspiciousness.**

**Комментарий:**

I was cursed by the sages whose minds (ātmā) were merciful. Because of the curse, I have been touched by the foot of the guru of the worlds. Thus, all inauspiciousness has been destroyed.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, you destroy all fear for those who, fearing this material world, take shelter of you. By the touch of your feet I am now freed from the curse of the sages. O destroyer of distress, please let me return to my planet.**

**Комментарий:**

I beg (āpṛcche) for the order to return to Svarga. O destroyer of suffering (amīvahan)!

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**O master of mystic power, O great personality, O Lord of the devotees, I surrender to you. Please command me as you will, O supreme God, Lord of all lords of the universe.**

**Комментарий:**

O lord with acintya-śakti (mahā-yogin)! O Supreme Lord (mahāpuruṣa)! O protector of the devotees (sat-pate)!

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**O infallible one, I was immediately freed from the brāhmaṇas’ punishment simply by seeing you. Anyone who chants your name purifies all who hear his chanting, as well as himself. How much more, then, will I purify others, having been touched by your lotus feet?**

**Комментарий:**

I was freed from the curse of the Aṅgīrasā (brahma-daṇḍāt). The person who chants your name purifies immediately the hearers of the name and himself. What to speak of me who have been touched by you and have seen you!

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Thus receiving the permission of Kṛṣṇa, the devatā Sudarśana circumambulated him, bowed down to offer him homage and then returned to his heavenly planet. Nanda Mahārāja was thus delivered from peril.**

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**The inhabitants of Vraja were not astonished to see the mighty power of Kṛṣṇa. Dear King, they then completed their worship of Śiva and returned to Vraja, along the way respectfully describing Kṛṣṇa’s powerful acts.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing from the mouth of Sudarśana, they were not astonished. Svayaṁ Bhagāvan is our friend. It is not amazing for him. They had a rule (niyamam) of staying two nights at that place.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Once Govinda and Balarāma, the performers of wonderful feats, were playing in the forest at night with the young girls of Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

Now the spring rāsa dance is described. One time, after Śiva-rātrī, in night with moonlight, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma played in the middle of the women of Vraja, since in horikā pastime that was the practice. In this mādhurya-rasa pastime, Balarāma was accompanying since the mood of sakhya manifested in him at this time. Thus mādhuryarasa does not shine with vātsalya and dāsya (but it does with sakhya).

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma wore flower garlands and spotless garments, and their limbs were beautifully decorated and anointed. The women sang their glories in a charming way, bound to them by affection.**

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**The two Lords praised the nightfall, signaled by the rising of the moon and the appearance of stars, a lotus-scented breeze and bees intoxicated by the fragrance of jasmine flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

The two greeted the night, with moon and stars, and with a breeze of lotuses.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma sang, producing the entire range of musical sounds simultaneously. Their singing brought happiness to the ears and minds of all living beings.**

**Комментарий:**

They produced mūrchanas of all the svaras simultaneously. The characteristics are mentioned in Saṅgīta-sāra: When the seven notes ascending and descending are sung in order, it is called mūrcchana. These are played or sung in three grāmas (basic scales) making twenty-one mūrcchanas.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs became stunned when they heard that song. O King, they did not notice that their fine garments were becoming loose and their hair and garlands disheveled.**

**Комментарий:**

The respective beloveds of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma (gopyaḥ) were not aware of their own bodies.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**While Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma thus played and sang according to their own sweet will and with excitement, a servant of Kuvera named Śaṅkhacūḍa came upon the scene.**

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**O King, even as the two Lords looked on, Śaṅkhacūḍa brazenly began driving the women off toward the north. The women, who had accepted Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma as their Lords, began to cry out to them.**

**Комментарий:**

While the two looked on, being ignored by Śaṅkhacūḍa, he drove the women north, where he lived, waving a stick. He did not touch them. Pramadā-janam is in the singular to represent a class (jāti). They cried out, “Please save us from him!”

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Hearing their devotees crying out, “Kṛṣṇa! Rāma!” and seeing that they were just like cows being stolen by a thief, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma began to run after the demon.**

**Комментарий:**

Just as on seeing cows taken by a thief and driven to his own place to make them his own, the cowherds pursued him.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**The Lords called out in reply, “Do not fear! “Then they picked up logs of the śala tree and running immediately, quickly caught up with that lowest of Guhyakas.**

**Комментарий:**

Abhayārāvau means they said “Do not be afraid.”

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**When Śaṅkhacūḍa saw the two of them coming toward him like the personified forces of time and death, he was filled with anxiety. Confused, he abandoned the women and fled for his life.**

**Комментарий:**

The two were like time and death. The analogy is made with the idea of inspirer and inspired respectively. Time is the inspirer which produces death (the inspired). Balarāma was the inspirer, saying, “Quickly kill him.” The inspired, Kṛṣṇa, like death itself, said, “I will kill him.”

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Govinda chased the demon wherever he ran, eager to take his crest jewel. Meanwhile Balarāma stayed with the women to protect them.**

**Комментарий:**

The women were tired due to fleeing away. Balarāma, steadying them there and reassuring them, remained there protecting them.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The mighty Lord overtook Śaṅkhacūḍa from a great distance as if from nearby, my dear King, and then with his fist the Lord removed the wicked demon’s head, together with his crest jewel.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the demon was far away, Kṛṣṇa overtook him as if he were near.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Having thus killed the demon Śaṅkhacūḍa and taken away his shining jewel, Kṛṣṇa gave it to his elder brother with great satisfaction as the gopīs watched.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the gopīs were all anxious, thinking, “He will give the gem to me, the dearest,” he did not give it to any of them but gave it to his brother, so that they would not become proud or angry, since Balarāma was worthy of respect and protected them. By giving it to him everyone was satisfied. Balarāma, due to being highly knowledgeable, placed it on a place cherished by Kṛṣṇa.

## Chapter 35 - The Gopīs Sing of Kṛṣṇa as He Wanders in the Forest (Yugala-gītā)

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Whenever Kṛṣṇa went to the forest, the minds of the gopīs would run after him, and thus the young girls sadly spent their days singing of his pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

In the thirty-fifth chapter, the gopīs sing the flute song made of twelve pairs of verses and like Kṛṣṇa, spend their days in separation. At night, the gopīs, playing with Kṛṣṇa became blissful by union with him but in the daytime, drinking the nectar of descriptions of the flute, attaining association with him in the mind, they experienced bliss of separation from him. Their minds moved quickly after him as he went to the forest. They spent their days singing about him in separation (duḥkhena). Though singing about him is a form of happiness, the word duḥkha is used because like chewing hot sugar-cane, it was intolerable, but not that because it was unfavorable.

### Text 2-3

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs said: When Mukunda vibrates the flute he has placed to his lips, stopping its holes with his tender fingers, he rests his left cheek on his left arm and makes his eyebrows dance. At that time the demigoddesses traveling in the sky with their husbands become amazed. As those ladies listen, they are embarrassed to find their minds yielding to the pursuit of desire, and in their distress they are unaware that the belts of their garments are loosening.**

**Комментарий:**

When Kṛṣṇa played his flute to announce his coming to the trees, creepers, birds and animals of Vṛndāvana, who were pained by separation during the night, the gopīs speak twelve pairs of verses describing the sound of the flute to their friends situated in their own groups. O gopīs! When Mukunda, having left his house and going to the forest, plays his flute placed on his lips, then the wives of Siddhas in airplanes, though with their husbands, on hearing the sound of the flute, become astonished by it. Their hearts, offered to the paths of amorous love, they become embarrassed and bewildered. The sign of that is that they forget that their skirts are loosening. Kṛṣṇa is described. His left cheek rests on the base of his left arm by which he can easily produce the ascending and descending notes with gamakas. By this, he also bewilders the women who see him. He places his right shank over his left shank. This is the grace of his bending in three places. His attractive brows dance in order to make his friends in front of him understand the skill of his singing. Bhruḥ instead of bhrūḥ is poetic license. The flute is described. It has seven holes which are covered by his soft fingers. The word komala (modifying aṅguli – fingers) means soft with affection or soft in comparison to the limbs of other people. According to Sāmudrika, hands of a great person are hard without work, which means that compared to their other limbs their hands are slightly hard. If this is the condition of even the devatā women who are with their husbands, then his beloveds think “How can we exist without Kṛṣṇa?” This should be understood at the end of each couplet.

### Text 4-5

**Перевод:**

**O girls! This son of Nanda, who gives joy to the distressed, bears motionless lightning on his chest and has an attractive smile. Now please hear something wonderful. When he vibrates his flute, bulls, deer and cows of Vraja and the forest are all captivated by the sound, and they stop chewing the food in their mouths and cock their ears. Stunned, they appear as if asleep, or like figures in a painting.**

**Комментарий:**

“What to speak of those devatā women who are so intelligent, please hear about the bewilderment of even the animals.” Hanta expresses that it is extraordinary. O girls! Listen! Kṛṣṇa is described. His chest has the appearance of a smile of necklaces resembling white cranes (hāra). He has stationary lightning, Lakṣmī, on his chest which resembles a cloud. He destroys the summer of your chastity by his cloud-like chest ornamented with the lightning and flying cranes. He makes us who are in pain, mocked by society (narma-daḥ). When this son of Nanda having gone to the forest, plays the flute, then the oxen attached to carts in the village and the deer in the forest and the cows near him going to the forest, joyful on hearing the flute, hold their chewed grass in their mouths and raise their ears. Because their hearts are stolen, they seem to be sleeping, like painted pictures. Some astonishing artist has drawn these pictures on the canvas of the sky. This indicates vismaya-rasa (astonishment). This Kṛṣṇa’s flute playing is for gathering all the cows and the cowherd boys as he goes to the forest.

### Text 6-7

**Перевод:**

**My dear gopī, sometimes Mukunda imitates the appearance of a wrestler by decorating himself with leaves, peacock feathers and colored minerals. Then, in the company of Balarāma and the cowherd boys, he plays his flute to call the cows. At that time the rivers stop flowing, their water stunned by the ecstasy they feel as they eagerly wait for the wind to bring them the dust of his lotus feet. But like us, the rivers are not very pious, and thus they merely wait with their arms trembling out of love.**

**Комментарий:**

What to speak of conscious beings, even unconscious rivers become stunned on hearing the flute’s sound. Please hear. O friends (āli)! Tied with clusters of peacock feathers (barhiṇastavaka) or with peacock feathers (barhiṇa) and flower clusters (stabaka), with blue and yellow mineral pigments (dhātu) and with young shoots (palāśa), he derides a wrestler’s costume by his splendor. When he calls the cows in the company of Balarāma and the other boys using his flute, “O Gaṅgā! O Yamunā! O Sarasvatī!” then the water bodies like Mānasa Gaṅgā and Yamunā, becoming conscious by that call, desiring the dust from his lotus feet brought by the wind, surpassing their banks with intense flow, though desiring to approach him, become stunned, their waves, like arms, waving due to prema. Like us, they are most unfortunate. Just as we are stopped from meeting Kṛṣṇa being obstructed by our husbands, and our eyes become moist with tears. This flute sound is for the sake of calling the cows for drinking their first water after he wrestles with friends on entering the forest and dressing like a wrestler.

### Text 8-9

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa moves about the forest in the company of his friends, who vividly chant the glories of his magnificent deeds. He thus appears as the most outstanding person, exhibiting his inexhaustible sweetness. When the cows wander onto the mountainsides and Kṛṣṇa calls out to them with the sound of his flute, the trees and creepers in the forest respond by becoming so luxuriant with fruits and flowers that they seem to be manifesting Kṛṣṇa, spread everywhere, within their hearts. As their branches bend low with the weight, the filaments on their trunks and vines stand erect out of prema, and both the trees and the creepers release sweet sap.**

**Комментарий:**

See something amazing among the non-moving entities. When Mukunda, whose valor is praised by the cowherds and devatās, who like lord of the spiritual world is fixed in power, and yet wanders in the forest out of attraction to the jīvas there, then the trees and creepers in the forest, like household devotees, release tears in the form of streams of honey as if teaching about Viṣṇu situated in their minds. Sasṛjuḥ (release) and vavṛṣuḥ (shower) are alternative versions of the verb. The branches of the trees bow down with the weight of flowers, compared to joy, and fruits, compared to rati, and the trees’ hairs stand on end in joy. This sound of his flute is to bring close the cows which, having drunk water, have wandered far off when he becomes absorbed in hearing his friends glorify his activities.

### Text 10-11

**Перевод:**

**Maddened by the divine, sweet aroma of the tulasī flowers on the garland Kṛṣṇa wears, swarms of bees sing loudly for him, and Kṛṣṇa, decorated with new tilaka, acknowledges their song by taking his flute to his lips. At that very moment the cranes, swans and other lake-dwelling birds, their minds overcome by the attractive song, approach attractive Kṛṣṇa, close their eyes and, maintaining strict silence, fix their consciousness upon him.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the devotion of the trees and creepers, they describe the devotion of the birds. He wears attractive tilaka or he is the chief person among all those who should be seen (darśanīya-tilakaḥ). Hearing with respect the favorable (abhīṣṭam) song loudly sung by swarms of bees intoxicated by the honey of fragrant tulasī in his forest garland, when he places his flute to his lips, at that time the cranes and other birds in the lake, their minds attracted by the song of the flute, coming from the lake, worship Kṛṣṇa or sit near him (upāsata). How amazing (hanta)! They close their eyes, their minds absorbed in the song. At noon sometimes wearing tilaka and forest garland, having eaten food sent by his mother along with his friends, sending friends to gather the cows, he sits in the shade of a huge tree on a huge jewel slab and with associates of bees attracted by the fragrance of his garland, he attracts the cranes and other birds from the lake by the sound of his flute.

### Text 12-13

**Перевод:**

**O goddesses of Vraja, when Kṛṣṇa is enjoying himself with Balarāma on the mountain slopes, charming in appearance with a flower crown. He gives joy to all with the resonant vibrations of his flute. Thus he delights the entire world. At that time the nearby cloud, afraid of offending a great personality, thunders very gently in accompaniment. The cloud showers flowers onto his dear friend and shades him from the sun like an umbrella.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the joy of entities situated on earth, they now describe the joy of entities in the sky. O gopīs of Vraja! Mukunda with Balarāma resplendent with earrings of huge, round pearls and with garlands on his chest, shining on the plateau of Govardhana (kṣti-bhṛtaḥ), joyful himself, gives joy to the universe as he fills it with the sound of his flute (uparambhati). Parasmaipada form of the verb rabh and the addition of the suffix num (m in uparambhati) are poetic licenses. At that time, a cloud in the sky, worried about offending a great soul, Mukunda, rumbles gently, following the sound of the flute. The cloud showers his friend, being similar in color and in relieving the world of suffering, with flowers in the form of fine particles of snow, while freeing him from the heat of the sun by becoming an umbrella (pratāpa trayate = pratapa-tram) with his shade. This sound of the flute filled with mallāra-rāga is to give joy to the cloud, as the cloud acts as shade when Kṛṣṇa, decorated with flower garland brought by a friend, wanders on the plateaus of Govardhana devoid of shade, responding to the cows.

### Text 14-15

**Перевод:**

**O pious mother Yaśodā, your son, who is expert in all the arts of herding cows, has invented many new styles of flute-playing. When he takes his flute to his bimba-red lips and sends forth the tones of the harmonic scale in variegated melodies, Brahmā, Śiva, Indra and other chief devatās listen repeatedly to the sound. Although they are the most learned authorities, with hearts in submission, they cannot ascertain the meaning and forget everything.**

**Комментарий:**

Some gopīs, longing to see their beloved Mukunda after a long time, go to Yaśodā’s house. There, they speak to Yaśodā – who is hearing about the qualities, actions and powers of her son along with various women there – the powerful sweetness of the flute’s sound to give her joy. O Yaśodā, worshippable by all (sati)! O queen! When your son, skillful in the actions of the cowherds, such as herding and milking cows, puts the flute to his red lips and produces eighteen jātīs of the seven svāras, which contained many types of teachings which are comparable to themselves, the devatās headed by Indra, hearing the svara-jātis at the time of sacrifices (savanaṣaḥ), become bewildered (kaśmalam). Indra, Upendra, Agni, and Yama, Śiva, Pārvatī and Gaṇeśa, Brahmā, the Kumāras and Nārada, all omniscient (kavayaḥ), though composers of songs, lower their necks and hearts when hearing that sound. They experience a taste of the song’s sweetness. They cannot determine the nature of the rāgas, tālas and tānas. Thus, they become bewildered due to uncertainty of that and due to the great sweetness of the flute’s sound. If the devatās are bewildered, what to say of others? Your son bewilders the universe. The sound of his flute is to bewilder all the devatās dwelling in the sky who have come to see Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 16-17

**Перевод:**

**As Kṛṣṇa strolls through Vraja with his lotus-petal-like feet, marking the ground with the distinctive emblems of flag, thunderbolt, lotus and elephant goad, he relieves the distress the ground feels from the cows’ hooves. As he plays his renowned flute, his body moves slowly with the grace of an elephant. Thus we gopīs, who become agitated by Cupid when Kṛṣṇa playfully glances at us, stand as still as trees, unaware that our hair and garments are slackening.**

**Комментарий:**

Some gopīs describe their own bewilderment from the flute’s sound to their sakhīs. By the lotus petals of his feet, marked with astonishing signs (lalāmaiḥ) of flag, etc., he relieves the earth of pain caused by the cows’ hooves as they walk in front of Kṛṣṇa. Lalāma means a sign according to Jaya-kośa. Feet is in the plural out of respect or to indicate that each step was incomparable. To relieve the earth of pain by the touch of his lotus feet, he walks while playing his flute. He walks like an elephant (varṣma-dhuryagatiḥ). At that time we, to whom are offered the urges of amorous love by his playful glances as he walks, become like trees and do not know that our hair and clothing have become loose because of bewilderment. He relieved the earth of pain from the cows’ hooves by placing on it his lotus feet. But by placing his lotus glance on the women of Vraja he produces pain of love. What can we do? This verse describes the flute sound as experienced by some gopīs, whose afternoon was ruined after speaking various topics about him, and who went to the forest on the pretext of picking flowers when cowherd boys were returning back in the third yāma of the afternoon, and who saw their lover Kṛṣṇa and then related this scene on another day to their friends.

### Text 18-19

**Перевод:**

**Now Kṛṣṇa is standing somewhere counting his cows on a string of gems, calling them with his flute. He wears a garland of tulasī leaves that bear the fragrance of his beloved, and he has thrown his arm over the shoulder of an affectionate cowherd boyfriend. As Kṛṣṇa plays his flute and sings, the music attracts the black deer’s wives, who approach that ocean of qualities and sit down beside him. Just like us cowherd girls, they have given up all hope for happiness in family life.**

**Комментарий:**

They describe how the flute’s sound bewilders the does in the forest, just as it bewilders the gopīs in Vraja. Situated somewhere, he holds a string of gems colored white, red, black and yellow to count the cows. Counting the cows by their color when it is time to return to Vraja, wearing a tulasī garland bearing the fragrance of his beloved, throwing his arm on a friend’s shoulder, he plays his flute. At that time, the wives of the Kṛṣṇa-sāra deer, their hearts stolen by the sound of the flute, approach him (anvāsata), an ocean of beauty, sweetness, omniscience and mercy. The does have given up desire for the house, like the gopīs. We are in the same situation. A gopīs describes to her sakhīs the does that go near by hearing the sound of the flute, as Kṛṣṇa desiring to go home in the afternoon, gathers the cows by the sound of his flute and counts them with his jeweled beads.

### Text 20-21

**Перевод:**

**O sinless Yaśodā, your darling child, the son of Mahārāja Nanda, has festively enhanced his attire with a jasmine garland, and he is now playing along the Yamunā in the company of the cows and cowherd boys, amusing his dear companions. The gentle breeze honors him with its soothing fragrance of sandalwood, while the various minor devatās, standing on all sides like panegyrists, offer their music, singing, and gifts of tribute.**

**Комментарий:**

Going to Yaśodā’s assembly, the gopīs console her by explaining the reason for the delay, since she laments that her son is late in coming. O Yaśodā of great puṇya (anaghe)! Your son, bathing in the Yamunā to get relief from the fatigue of wandering in the forest, sitting on the bank of the river, wearing clothing indicating a festival, with jasmine garlands, necklaces and bracelets, to give joy to his relatives with whom he will meet, plays his flute (vijahāra) and moves about. At that time, a gentle breeze blows. He thwarts and promotes mutual jokes with his friends. He is the son of Nanda who is the topmost pious person. You should not at all be worried about him as he is the son of two most pious parents. Do not worry about his slight delay. Hear the cause of his delay. He is honored favorably by the breeze, touching him with the Malaya sandalwood, fragrant and cooling, which cannot move quickly because of the weight. Moreover, minor devatās, praisers, Gandharvas and others, reveal his qualities. They surround him with songs and gifts of cloth etc. Because he accepts these offerings, he is late. Do not lament. He is almost here. Some gopīs, who went to Yaśodā with a desire to see their beloved as he returns home, wearing flower ornaments after bathing and making the cows drink water a second time, describe the sound of the flute to her.

### Text 22-23

**Перевод:**

**Out of great affection for the cows of Vraja, Kṛṣṇa became the lifter of Govardhana Hill. At the end of the day, having rounded up all his cows, he plays a song on his flute, while exalted devatās standing along the path worship his lotus feet and the cowherd boys accompanying him chant his glories. He wears a garland covered with dust raised by the cows’ hooves, and his beauty, enhanced by his fatigue, creates joy for everyone’s eyes. Eager to fulfill his friends’ desires, he arrives. Kṛṣṇa is the moon which has arisen from the womb of mother Yaśodā.**

**Комментарий:**

‘His heart attracted to the songs of Gandharvas, my son does not come even though evening has passed. I am worried.” When Yaśodā said this, some gopīs, reassuring her explain the reason her son has not come quickly. Your son has affection for the cows, bulls and oxen staying in Vraja. Because of that affection, giving up the songs of the Gandharvas, he will come quickly. He lifted Govardhana (aga) to protect them. “If that is so, why is he late?” His feet are respected on the way by Brahmā and others (vṛddhaiḥ) who have gathered. Because of that obligation he is late. “O girls! Climb on the roof of the palace and see how far my son is.” When they do as she says, some gopīs speak, pointing with their fingers. Your son desires to fulfill (ditsayaiti) the desires of his friends. Gathering all the cows in the evening, while playing the flute, he produces great joy for the eyes of people by his beauty due to fatigue, with his garland covered with dust raised by the cows’ hooves. He wears the garland sent by Rādhā, though it is covered by dust, since he has great affection for her. He is the moon (uḍu-rājaḥ) which has risen in the milk ocean of your womb (devakī-jaṭhara-bhūḥ). Some gopīs describe the sound of the flute, as they desire to see him and give joy to Yaśodā by speaking about her son, whose feet are worshipped by Brahmā and others on the road as he returns home.

### Text 24-25

**Перевод:**

**As Kṛṣṇa respectfully greets his well-wishing friends, his eyes roll slightly as if from intoxication. He wears a flower garland, and decorates his tender cheeks with the brilliance of his golden earrings. His face is pale as a badara berry. With cheerful face, the master of the cowherds, moving with the grace of a regal elephant, like the rising moon in the evening, returns in the evening, relieving the cows and Vraja from the pain experienced during the day.**

**Комментарий:**

Other gopīs who have climbed on the roof of the palace speak on seeing him. His eyes roll about slightly because of the appearance of youth (mada-vighūrṇita-locanaḥ). He respects his relatives who have gathered by offering respects and embraces. He respects the gopīs on the roof who worship him with smiling glances like blue lotuses by his side glance. His face is pale like a ripe badari fruit because of fatigue from wandering in the forest. Or his face is pale because of pain of separation from his beloveds. He decorates his soft cheeks with the beauty of swaying gold earrings with huge round, shining pearls. Singular gaṇḍam is used to indicate a type. The protector of the cowherds (yadu-patiḥ), walking like the king of elephants, like the rising moon, arrives (upayāti) in the evening. It was established previously that the cowherds too are Yadus. He has a joyful face (mudita-vaktraḥ). By the skill of his flute playing he relieves the cows of Vraja and the eyes of the people of Vraja of endless suffering during the day. The sound of the flute gives bliss to everyone.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, thus during the daytime the women of Vṛndāvana took pleasure in continuously singing about the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, and those ladies’ minds and hearts, absorbed in him, were filled with great festivity.**

**Комментарий:**

O King! Thus the women of Vraja, his beloveds, singing about Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, enjoyed the days. Their hearts concentrated on Kṛṣṇa, the gopīs, who were on Kṛṣṇa’s mind, became joyful. They mutually became the viṣaya and āśraya.

## Chapter 36 - The Slaying of Ariṣṭa, the Bull Demon

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The demon Ariṣṭa then came to the cowherd village. Appearing in the form of a bull with a large hump, he made the earth tremble as he tore it apart with his hooves.**

**Комментарий:**

In the thirty-sixth chapter, after the killing of Ariṣṭa, Kaṁsa, understanding through Nārada about the parents of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, gives orders to Akrūra, after imprisoning the parents. In the evening, when Kṛṣṇa came home from the forest (tarhi), Ariṣṭa arrived since Viṣṇu Purāṇa says: Once, midway through the period of dusk, when Kṛṣṇa was eager to perform the rāsa dance, Ariṣṭāsura madly entered the cowherd village, terrifying everyone. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) After finishing his dinner, he left his bedroom to go for the rāsa dance and went beyond the village of Vraja. The demon named Ariṣṭa, having the form of a bull, came within the village. He had a huge hump and body.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Ariṣṭāsura bellowed very harshly and pawed the ground. With his tail raised and his eyes glaring, he began to tear up the embankments with the tips of his horns, every now and then passing a little stool and urine.**

**Комментарий:**

Bellowing like a bull, splitting the earth with his sharp hooves, raising his tail, tearing up the banks with his horns, every now and then he passed a little stool and urine. His eyes were unblinking.

### Text 3-4

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, clouds hovered about sharp-horned Ariṣṭāsura’s hump, mistaking it for a mountain, and when the cowherd men and ladies caught sight of the demon, they were struck with terror. Indeed, the strident reverberation of his roar so frightened the pregnant cows and women that they lost their fetuses in miscarriages.**

**Комментарий:**

The women and cows had miscarriages because of the cruel sound (nirhrāditena). Up to the fourth month a premature delivery is called srāva, in the fifth and sixth months it is called pāta, and after this it is considered a birth (prasūti).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**The domestic animals fled the pasture in fear, O King, and all the inhabitants rushed to Lord Govinda for shelter, crying, “Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa!”**

**Комментарий:**

All of them, the gopīs and others, crying, “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Protect us,” surrendered to him.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**When the Supreme Lord saw the cowherd community distraught and fleeing in fear, he calmed them, saying, “Don’t be afraid.” Then he called the bull demon towards him, away from Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

Saying, “Do not fear,” the Lord, Kṛṣṇa, pacified all Gokula and called to the demon bull.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**You fool! What do you think you’re doing, you wicked rascal, frightening the cowherd community and their animals when I am here just to punish corrupt miscreants like you!**

**Комментарий:**

O fool! O worst being! Why are you terrorizing the cowherds? I destroy the pride of wicked beings like you. Therefore, come and face me.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Having spoken these words, without moving an inch, Kṛṣṇa slapped his arms with his palms, further angering Ariṣṭa with the loud sound. Then appearing most attractive, he casually threw his mighty, serpentine arm over the shoulder of a friend and stood facing the demon.**

**Комментарий:**

Speaking thus, Acyuta, striking his arms with his hands strongly (āsphoṭya), making the demon angry by that, put his snake-like arm on the shoulder of a friend and remained there, fearless.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Thus provoked, Ariṣṭa pawed the ground with one of his hooves and then, dispersing clouds with his upraised tail, angrily charged at Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The verse is clear.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Pointing the tips of his horns straight ahead and glaring menacingly at Kṛṣṇa from the corners of his bloodshot eyes, Ariṣṭa rushed toward him at full speed, like a thunderbolt hurled by Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

Pointing the tips of his horns in front, his eyes bloodshot, throwing glances, he charged at Acyuta quickly.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa seized Ariṣṭāsura by the horns and threw him back eighteen steps, just as an elephant might do when fighting a rival elephant.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhagavān, Kṛṣṇa, grabbed him by the horns and threw him backwards (pratyapovāha) eighteen feet.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Thus repulsed by the Supreme Lord, the bull demon got up and, breathing hard and sweating all over his body, again charged at him in a mindless rage.**

**Комментарий:**

Being thrown back the bull perspired in all his limbs. He became inundated (mūrcchitaḥ) with anger.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**As Ariṣṭa attacked, Kṛṣṇa seized him by the horns and knocked him to the ground with his foot. He then thrashed him as if he were a wet cloth, and finally uprooted one of the demon’s horns and struck him with it until he died.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking him by his horns, Acyuta threw him on the ground. Stepping on him with his foot, he crushed him as if he were some wet cloth. Uprooting his left horn, he struck him with it since according to Hari-vaṁśa uprooting his right horn, he beat him with it. He then died (apatat).

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Vomiting blood and profusely excreting stool and urine, kicking his legs and rolling his eyes about, Ariṣṭāsura thus went painfully to the abode of death. After this, the devatās honored Kṛṣṇa by scattering flowers upon him.**

**Комментарий:**

How did he die? He vomited blood and discharged stool with urine. He kicked up his legs. His eyes rolled (anavasthitekṣaṇaḥ). He died painfully (kṛcchram jagāma) and then went to the abode (kṣayam) of the Lord because of his death (nirṛtteḥ). He achieved liberation since it was previously said pralamba-khara-dardura-keśy-ariṣṭa: the demons attained liberation. (SB [2.7.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.34)) Showering Kṛṣṇa with flowers, the devatās praised (īḍire) him.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Having thus killed the bull demon Ariṣṭa, he who is joy for the gopīs’ eyes entered the cowherd village with Balarāma, being praised by his friends.**

**Комментарий:**

Having killed Ariṣṭāsura (kakudminam), praised by the cowherds (svajātibhiḥ), Kṛṣṇa entered the village. He was the form of joy for the eyes of the gopīs. Details are given as follows in the Ādi-varāha Purāṇa, while circumambulating Govardhana: North of Manasa-gaṅgā (gaṅgāyāḥ) the Lord marked with cakras on his hand (cakriṇaḥ), endowed with all powers and sweetness (devadevasya) fought a fierce battle with Ariṣṭa. Killing the demon with the body of a bull at that place, in anger (because the demon had disturbed Vraja) Kṛṣṇa produced a great tīrtha by striking the ground with his heel. He brought this great tīrtha from Pātāla. vṛṣabhasya vadho jñeya ātmanaḥ śuddham icchatā snātas tatra tadā krṣṇo vṛṣaṁ hatvā sa-gopakaḥ Knowing he had killed a bull, he desired purification. He bathed in the tīrtha along with his friends after killing the bull. His purification was an imitation. He bathed using it as a pretext to broadcast the glory of his tīrtha. Then he bathed in it. Then he spoke to Rādhā. He spoke to Rādhā. O fortunate Rādhā! How can you be as pious? I am sinless. I have killed the sinful bull Ariṣṭa. Rādhā embraced him, who relieves all fatigue. She made another tīrtha nearby named after her. I do not have any sin. Because of manifesting such a tīrtha, I have achieved my goals. How can you be pious since you do not manifest such a tīrtha? He explained how he is sinless. This demon, disguised as a bull was killed by me. This does not make me faulty. Being spoken to, Rādhā, embracing him, made a kuṇḍa right next to it and gave it her name. It is famous as Rādhā-kuṇḍa. By bathing in these two kuṇḍas, one achieves auspicious results and all sins are destroyed. The same effect cannot be achieved by a rājasūya or aśvamedha sacrifice. It destroys the sin of killing a cow or a brāhmaṇa. There is no doubt about this.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**After Ariṣṭāsura had been killed by Kṛṣṇa, who acts wonderfully, Nārada Muni went to speak to King Kaṁsa. That powerful sage of godly vision addressed the king as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Nārada, desiring that Kaṁsa be killed quickly, went to speak to him. Seeing him was like seeing the Lord (deva-darśanaḥ). Or for him the Lord was perceptible (deva-darśanaḥ).

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**\[Nārada told Kaṁsa:\] Yaśodā’s child was actually a daughter, and Kṛṣṇa is the son of Devakī. Also, Balarāma is the son of Rohiṇī. Out of fear, Vasudeva entrusted Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma to his friend Nanda Mahārāja, and it is these two boys who have killed your men.**

**Комментарий:**

What Nārada spoke is described. The daughter famous as being the eighth child of Devakī was Yaśodā’s daughter. Kṛṣṇa, famous as the son of Yaśodā is actually the son of Devakī. Balarāma, the son of Rohinī is actually the seventh son of Devakī. If they are both sons of Vasudeva, how did they get to Nanda’s house? They were entrusted by Vasudeva, who was afraid of you, to Nanda, who was his friend and relative. Because he was afraid, you should not kill him. Vai means it is well known. All this you do not know as you are a fool. I say this since I desire your wellbeing. Your men were killed by Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. By this he confirms what he has said.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Upon hearing this, the master of the Bhojas became furious with agitated senses. He picked up a sharp sword to kill Vasudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

His heart was disturbed (pracalitendriyaḥ).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**But Nārada restrained Kaṁsa by reminding him that it was the two sons of Vasudeva who would cause his death. Kaṁsa then had Vasudeva and his wife shackled in iron chains.**

**Комментарий:**
