Nārada prevented Kaṁsa from killing Vasudeva. If he is killed, his two sons will flee. Therefore, do not kill him. In this way he gave advice to Kaṁsa. Knowing that Vasudeva’s two sons would be his death, he chained him up along with his wife with iron shackles.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**After Nārada left, King Kaṁsa summoned Keśī and ordered him, “Go kill Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa.”**

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**The King of the Bhojas next called for his ministers, headed by Muṣṭika, Cāṇūra, Śala and Tośala, and also for his elephantkeepers. The King addressed them as follows.**

### Text 22-23

**Перевод:**

**My dear heroic Cāṇūra and Muṣṭika, please hear this. Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, the sons of Vasudeva, are living in Nanda’s cowherd village. It has been predicted that these two boys will be the cause of my death. When they are brought here, kill them on the pretext of engaging them in a wrestling match.**

**Комментарий:**

My death by those two has been announced by voice from the sky and by Nārada. He speaks to Cāṇūra and Muṣṭika who are eager to go to Vraja. They should be killed bringing them here. However, Sarasvatī devī gives another meaning to his words. You both will be liberated.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Erect a wrestling ring with many surrounding viewing stands, and bring all the residents of the city and the outlying districts to see the open competition.**

**Комментарий:**

Make a high stand with pillars (mañcāḥ) surrounding the sides of the wrestling arena. What is the purpose? The residents of the city and the people of the state may see the wrestling match which is arranged by free will, not by force.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**You, elephant-keeper, my good man, should position the elephant Kuvalayāpīḍa at the entrance to the wrestling arena and have him kill my two enemies.**

**Комментарий:**

What is the use of exhausting the dear wrestlers? Kṛṣṇa can be easily killed by a mad elephant. Externally he suggested this, but internally he was fearful. O skillful one (bhadra)! He encourages the elephant driver. You should bring the elephant to the gate of the arena and kill my two enemies through the elephant. But Sarasvatī devī says, “Become liberated and attain my two enemies.”

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Commence the bow sacrifice on the Caturdaśī day in accordance with the relevant Vedic injunctions. In ritual slaughter offer the appropriate kinds of animals to the magnanimous Śiva.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the material means, Kaṁsa speaks of more religious means. Bring the two on the pretext of a festival of the bow sacrifice. Kill animals suitable for sacrifice (medhyān) to please Śiva (bhūta-rājāya), the protector of Mathurā, also called Bhūteśvara, whose bow was also celestial and who is generous (mīḍhuṣe from the root mih to scatter or give). He makes this statement in fear.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Having thus commanded his ministers, Kaṁsa next called for Akrūra, the most eminent of the Yadus. Kaṁsa knew scriptures concerning material gain, and thus he took Akrūra’s hand in his own and spoke to him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa was skillful only in artha-śāstra. “Akrūra is trusted by all the Yadus including Nanda,” thinking thus he took Arkūra’s hand as a show of affection. Akrūra was necessary for attaining his goals.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**My dear Akrūra, most charitable one, please do me a friendly favor, since I respect you. Among the Bhojas and Vṛṣṇis, there is no one else as kind to us as you.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa repeats bho bho to show respect. O best of the generous (dāna-pate)! My desires will be fulfilled by you. Do something as a friend. “O king of the Bhojas! Why do you send me among all the people?” You are respected (ādṛtaḥ).

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Gentle Akrūra, I am depending on you to accomplish this important task, just as powerful Indra took shelter of Viṣṇu to achieve his goals.**

**Комментарий:**

Thus taking shelter of you to achieve my important work, I will achieve my goal (svārtham). Just as Indra, taking shelter of Viṣṇu, achieved his goal.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Please go to Nanda’s village, where the two sons of Vāsudeva are living, and without delay bring them here on this chariot.**

**Комментарий:**

Bring them on a chariot studded with jewels, in order to give them joy.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The devatās, who are under the protection of Viṣṇu, have sent these two boys as my death. Bring them here, and also have Nanda and the other cowherd men come with gifts of tribute.**

**Комментарий:**

The two boys were made (nisṛṣṭaḥ) as my death by the devatās who take shelter of Viṣṇu (vaikuṇṭha-saṁśrayaiḥ). Bring the boys with the cowherds bearing gifts. He spoke this in order to cheat them by convincing about the truth of the bow sacrifice.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**After you bring Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, I will have them killed by my elephant, which is as powerful as death itself. And if by chance they escape from him, I will have them killed by my wrestlers, who are as strong as lightning.**

**Комментарий:**

The purpose of bringing them is stated. I will kill them by the elephant which is equal to death (kāla-kalpena). If the two escape the elephant I will have them killed by wrestlers, equal to lightning.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**When these two have been killed, I will kill Vasudeva and all their lamenting relatives—the Vṛṣṇis, Bhojas and Daśārhas.**

**Комментарий:**

“I will be in danger from their relatives.” I will kill their relatives like Vasudeva. Do not feel insecure because of them. But Sarasvatī devī gives another meaning. “Having attained the two boys in liberation, I will also attain his associates.”

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**I will also kill my old father, Ugrasena, who is greedy for my kingdom, and I will kill his brother Devaka and all my other enemies as well.**

**Комментарий:**

I will also kill all others who side with them.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Then, my friend, this earth will be free of thorns.**

**Комментарий:**

“But am I also their friend among the Bhojas?” No, you are my friend. You are my benefactor. I will even give a part of my kingdom to you.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**My elder relative Jarāsandha and my dear friend Dvivida are firm well-wishers of mine, as are Śambara, Naraka and Bāṇa. I will use them all to kill off those kings who are allied with the devatās, and then I will rule the earth.**

**Комментарий:**

I will kill all those who side with the devatās such as the Kauravas . Then I will rule the earth. Sarasvatī devī intends another meaning however. I will enjoy the earth in my state of liberation, since liberation includes all enjoyment (figuratively).

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Now that you understand my intentions, please go at once and bring Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma to watch the bow sacrifice and see the wealth of the Yadus’ capital.**

**Комментарий:**

By you the two can be fooled and brought here (arbhakau). He informs the way this is to be done. The bow sacrifice and the splendor of the city will definitely be attractive to children.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Akrūra said: O King, you have expertly devised a process to free yourself of misfortune. Still, one should be equal in success and failure, since it is certainly destiny that produces results.**

**Комментарий:**

After hearing this, with a desire to accomplish his two desires of seeing the Lord and as a result, to bring about the death of Kaṁsa and a desire to announce his being a confidant of Kaṁsa he praises Kaṁsa’s words. That is expressed in two verses. O King! What you desire is correct (sadhryak) for freeing yourself of death. You should execute this plan to rid yourself of death. Otherwise there is the fault of suicide. But in success or failure you should act without change because (hi) ancient karmas produce the result. Because he was a devotee, he spoke the truth to him.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**An ordinary person is determined to act on his desires even when fate prevents their fulfillment. Therefore he encounters both happiness and distress. Yet even though such is the case, I will execute your order.**

**Комментарий:**

Describing his reliability he speaks the truth. A man performs actions as a method to fulfil his desires even though they are destroyed by the Lord, but he does not enjoy the results. Since the result is already destroyed, he rejoices during the actions to attain it and laments when he does not get the result. Though that is so, I will follow your order.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus instructed Akrūra, King Kaṁsa dismissed his ministers and retired to his quarters, and Akrūra returned home.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa went into the inner chambers (gṛhaṁ) and Akrūra went to his house.

## Chapter 37 - The Killing of the Demons Keśī and Vyoma

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The demon Keśī, sent by Kaṁsa, appeared in Vraja as a great horse. Running with the speed of the mind, he tore up the earth with his hooves. The hairs of his mane scattered the clouds and the demigods’ airplanes throughout the sky, and he terrified everyone present with his loud neighing.**

**Комментарий:**

In the thirty-seventh chapter, when Kṛṣṇa kills Keśī, he is praised by Nārada who recites his future exploits, plays and kills Vyomāsura easily. Keśī breaking the earth with his hooves, running at the speed of the mind, scattering the clouds and airplanes in the sky by shaking his mane, frightened everyone in the airplanes, etc., by his neighing, came to Vraja.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**He had wide eyes and a frightening gaping mouth. He had a huge neck and was dark like a huge cloud. With evil intentions, he desired to benefit Kaṁsa. He came to Vraja, shaking the earth. When the Lord saw how the demon was frightening his village of Gokula, the Lord came forward to meet him, as he shook the clouds with his tail, searching for Kṛṣṇa. When Kṛṣṇa stood before him, he called the horse, and Keśī replied, roaring like a lion.**

**Комментарий:**

He had a gaping mouth which was frightening. He had bad intentions (durāśayaḥ). The Lord called him close (upāhvayat). Keśī is described. He terrorized Gokula by his rough neighing. He agitated the clouds by his tail (bāla). He was searching for Kṛṣṇa in order to fight (ājau). Kṛṣṇa, leaving the cowherds, came in front of him. Seeing him, Keśī roared like a lion.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the Lord standing before him, Keśī ran toward him in extreme rage, his mouth gaping as if to swallow up the sky. Rushing with furious speed, the unconquerable and unapproachable horse demon tried to strike the lotus-eyed Lord with his two front legs.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa, Keśī, as if drinking the sky with his mouth, angered (aty-amarṣaṇaḥ) or not tolerating the enemy in front of him, ran towards him. He struck Kṛṣṇa with his two front legs. Others could not conquer him (durāsadaḥ). He was eager, and difficult to surpass since he ran quickly.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**But the Lord dodged Keśī’s blow and then with his arms angrily seized the demon by the legs, whirled him around in the air and contemptuously threw him the distance of one hundred bowlengths, just as Garuḍa might throw a snake, and remained in the same spot.**

**Комментарий:**

Avoiding his kick, to kill Keśī, Kṛṣṇa grabbed his spread out legs by his hands, whirled him around and threw him a hundred bow lengths away, while he himself remained there without moving.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Upon regaining consciousness, Keśī angrily got up, opened his mouth wide and again rushed to attack Kṛṣṇa. But the Lord just smiled and thrust his left arm into the horse’s mouth as easily as one would make a snake enter a hole in the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

Opening his mouth, Keśī swiftly attacked the Lord. Kṛṣṇa put his left arm in Keśī’s mouth, without worry, as a snake enters a hole.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Keśī’s teeth immediately fell out when they touched the Supreme Lord’s arm, which to the demon felt as hot as molten iron. Within Keśī’s body the Supreme Lord’s arm then expanded greatly, like a diseased stomach swelling because of neglect.**

**Комментарий:**

Keśī’s teeth touched the Lord’s arm in order to bite it. When he opened his mouth, the teeth were exposed. The teeth then fell out. It was like the touch of very hot iron. The Lord’s arm seemed to take up that nature by the śakti of his anger. His arm expanded like an untreated disease in the stomach.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**As Kṛṣṇa’s expanding arm completely blocked Keśī’s breathing, his legs kicked convulsively, his body became covered with sweat, and his eyes rolled around. The demon then passed stool and fell on the ground, dead.**

**Комментарий:**

Leṇḍam means stool.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**The mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa withdrew his arm from Keśī’s body, which now appeared like a long karkaṭikā fruit. Without the least display of pride at having so effortlessly killed his enemy, the Lord accepted the devatās’ worship in the form of flowers which rained down many times.**

**Комментарий:**

Withdrawing his arm from the life-less body torn like a karkaṭikā fruit, Kṛṣṇa remained there without pride (avismitaḥ), having killed his enemy without effort. He was praised by the devatās who gave up their astonishment at the killing, since they understood the truth about the Lord’s nature and were smiling. They showered flowers profusely.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, thereafter Kṛṣṇa was approached in a solitary place by the great sage among the devatās, Nārada Muni. That most exalted devotee spoke as follows to the Lord, who effortlessly performs his pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

Not able to tolerate the suffering of Vasudeva and others, Nārada met Kṛṣṇa secretly and spoke to him as follows since he was a devotee (bhāgavata).

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**\[Nārada Muni said:\] O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, unlimited Lord, source of all yogamāyā, Lord of the universe, spread everywhere, the shelter of all beings, best of the Yadu kṣatriyas and cowherds, the master of time!**

**Комментарий:**

“You revealed to the enemy Kaṁsa my secret.” You should not worry about that. O Kṛṣṇa who removes fear in the devotees! The meaning is this. You are the Lord of everyone and have appeared to destroy the demons who burden the world. Thus protect the universe by pastimes favorable for that purpose. You have no worry of fear. O Lord with indivisible svarūpa! O shelter of all beings! O best of the Yadus. O master!

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**You are the Paramātmā of all beings, Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and Karaṇodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, sitting unseen within the cave of the heart like the fire dormant within kindling wood, the witness.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why do you speak like this to me, the son of Nanda?” You are the one ātmā, full of knowledge and bliss, strung together within all beings, but not limited like the jīva. An example is given of being strung together within all beings. You are like fire within wood. “Why am I not known by these beings?” You are unseen (guḍhaḥ) since you reside in the heart as the witness. Situated within intelligence you witness directly. Moreover, as the mahāpuruṣa you are the form of all-pervading consciousness. In that form how can you be known by the jīvas? “But being within them, how can I be respected?” You are the lord (īśvara). Without the Lord, dependent living beings cannot function. I told Kaṁsa that you, the son of Nanda, have appeared at the request of Brahmā to remove the burden of the earth. This was told by me in accordance with your activities and not with malice.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**You are your own shelter, and being the supreme controller, you fulfill your desires simply by your will. By your personal creative potency you manifested in the beginning the primal modes of material nature, and through their agency you create, maintain and then destroy this universe.**

**Комментарий:**

He explains Kṛṣṇa as the Lord. You are the shelter of yourself (ātmāśrayaḥ). By yourself, by your will in your mind (ātmanā) you create the guṇas like sattva by māyā. So ’kāmayata bahusyām: the Lord desired, “May I become many.” (Taittirīya Upaniṣad [2.6.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/taittiriya/2.6.2)) You create the universe by the three guṇas. “How is this possible?” Your actions arise from your unobstructed mind (satya-sañkalpaḥ).

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**You, that very same creator, have now descended on the earth to annihilate the Daitya, Pramatha and Rākṣasa demons, and also to protect the bounds of dharma.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks of the present context. You have appeared to destroy the Daityas, etc., who accept the earth as their own (bhū-dhara) and to protect the laws (setūnām) of dharma.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**The horse demon was so terrifying that his neighing frightened the devatās into leaving their heavenly kingdom. But by our good fortune you have enjoyed the sport of killing him.**

**Комментарий:**

Keśī was killed by you (te). Animiṣā means devatās.

### Text 15-20

**Перевод:**

**In just two days, O almighty Lord, I will see the deaths of Cāṇūra, Muṣṭika and other wrestlers, along with those of the elephant Kuvalayāpīḍa and King Kaṁsa—all by your hand. Then I will see you kill Kālayavana, Mura, Naraka and Pañcajana, and I will also see you steal the pārijāta flower and defeat Indra. I will then see you marry many daughters of heroic kings after paying for them with your valor. Then, O Lord of the universe, in Dvārakā you will deliver King Nṛga from a curse and take for yourself the Syamantaka jewel, together with another wife. You will bring back a brāhmaṇa’s dead son from the abode of your servant Yamarāja, and thereafter you will kill Pauṇḍraka, burn down the city of Kāśī and annihilate Dantavakra and the King of Cedi during the great Rājasūya sacrifice. I shall see all these heroic pastimes, along with many others you will perform during your residence in Dvārakā. These pastimes are glorified on this earth in the songs of poets.**

**Комментарий:**

In two days, you will kill the wrestlers. Today, Akrūra will come. Tomorrow you will go to Mathurā. Then two days from now I will see Cāṇūra and others killed. The great devotees inform by speaking like Siddhas. After that (anu) I will see the killing of Pañcajana (śaṅkha) and others. This is a description of the future, without the events told in sequence. In Dvārakā you will marry the daughters imprisoned by Naraka and will liberate Nṛga. You will take for yourself the Syamantaka jewel, together with Jāmbavatī as a wife. You will bring the brāhamaṇa’s son from Mahākāla-pura (sva-dhāmataḥ). You will burn Kāśī (dīpanam). I will see whatever activities you perform while you live in Dvārakā.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Subsequently I will see you destroy entire armies of soldiers when you appear as the universe, capable of destroying it, serving as Arjuna’s chariot driver.**

**Комментарий:**

I will see the destruction of the armies by you, possessing the śakti of time, as you destroy the burden of the earth (kṣapayiṣṇoḥ).

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Let me surrender to you, Bhagavān. You are the condensed form of pure knowledge and you are bliss itself, you have forms with many qualities. Your desires are always fulfilled. Because of your svarūpa-śakti you are never touched by the material guṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

Informing Kṛṣṇa, he offers respects to Kṛṣṇa after praising him in two verses. You are the form of pure consciousness (viśuddhavijñāna-ghanam). You obtain all enjoyment by your parā śakti (svasaṁsthayā). This refers to lord’s nature as āptakāma. Your desires come true (amogha-vāñchitam). This refers to lord’s nature as satya-saṅkalpa. “If I have desires, I will transmigrate within the material world.” You are devoid of the influence of the guṇas arising as effects of māyā eternally by your supreme, spiritual form (sva-tejasā). Dhāmnā svena sadā nirasta-kuhakam: the lord is devoid of māyā by his spiritual śakti. (SB [1.1.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.1)) You are full of the six opulences (bhagavantam) as described earlier. I surrender (īmahi) to you.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**I bow down to you, the supreme controller, dependent only on yourself. By your potency you have constructed the unlimited particular arrangements of this universe. Now you have appeared as the greatest hero among the Yadus, Vṛṣṇis and Sātvatas and with human form, manifest pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why do you praise me, a human being, like this?” You control those other than yourself (īśvaram). You take shelter of yourself, not controlled by others (svāśrayaṁ). You create (kalpana) the various elements like mahat-tattva made of māyā, which are dependent on you. You have a human form brought facing the devotee (abhyātta) for performing variegated pastimes (krīḍārtham).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus addressed Kṛṣṇa, the chief of the Yadu dynasty, Nārada bowed down. Then that great sage and most eminent devotee took his leave from the Lord and went away, feeling great joy at having directly seen him.**

**Комментарий:**

Nārada was in a festival of joy by seeing him (tad-darśanotsavaḥ).

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**After killing the demon Keśī in battle, though he was Bhagavān, as Govinda, he continued to tend the cows and other animals in the company of his joyful cowherd boyfriends. Thus he brought happiness to all the residents of Vṛndāvana.**

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**One day the cowherd boys, while grazing their animals on the mountain slopes, played the game of stealing and hiding, acting out the roles of rival thieves and herders.**

**Комментарий:**

Now begins the description of killing Vyoma. The cows grazed on a plateau of a mountain in Kāmya-vana.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**In that game, O King, some acted as thieves, others as shepherds and others as sheep. They played their game happily, without fear of danger.**

**Комментарий:**

Tatra means “in that game.”

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**A powerful magician named Vyoma, son of the demon Maya, appeared on the scene in the guise of a cowherd boy. Pretending to join the game as a thief, he proceeded to steal most of the cowherd boys who were acting as sheep.**

**Комментарий:**

Vyoma, acting as a thief (corāyitaḥ), took away many boys acting as sheep (meṣāyitān).

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Gradually the great demon abducted more and more of the cowherd boys and cast them into a mountain cave, which he sealed shut with a boulder. Finally only four or five boys acting as sheep remained in the game.**

**Комментарий:**

He covered (pidadhe) the door with a rock.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, who shelters all saintly devotees, understood perfectly well what Vyomāsura was doing. Just as a lion grabs a wolf, Kṛṣṇa forcefully seized the demon as he was taking away cowherd boys.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa, who gives himself as shelter (śarana-daḥ) to all devotees (satām), seized him. He was like a lion (hariḥ).

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The demon changed into his original form, as big and powerful as a great mountain. But try as he might to free himself, he could not do so, suffering from being held in the Lord’s tight grip.**

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Acyuta, clutching Vyomāsura between his arms, threw him to the ground. Then, while the devatās in the sky looked on, Kṛṣṇa killed him in the same way that one kills a sacrificial animal.**

**Комментарий:**

He killed the demon like slaughtering sacrificial animal by blocking his breath (paśu-māram amārayat).

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then smashed the boulder blocking the cave’s entrance and led the trapped cowherd boys to safety. Thereafter, as the devatās sang his glories, he returned to his cowherd village, Gokula, with the cowherd boys.**

**Комментарий:**

He rescued the boys from danger (kṛcchrataḥ). Some say that the killing of Vyomāsura took place before killing Śaṅkhacūḍa, since the event is mentioned in relation to wearing disguises (playing with boys).

## Chapter 38 - Akrūra’s Arrival in Vṛndāvana

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After passing the night in the city of Mathurā, the high-minded Akrūra mounted his chariot and set off for the cowherd village of Nanda Mahārāja.**

**Комментарий:**

In the thirty-eighth chapter after Keśī is killed, Akrūra arrives in Vraja and is greeted by Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, according to his mood. Kṛṣṇa became eager to go to Mathurā when he heard from Nārada that he would kill Kaṁsa. And at that time, Akrūra also came to Vraja.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**As he traveled on the road, the great soul Akrūra felt intense devotion for the lotus-eyed Personality of Godhead, and thus he began to consider as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

He began to consider as follows.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**\[Śrī Akrūra thought:\] What pious deeds have I done, what severe austerities undergone, what worship performed or charity given so that today I will see Keśava?**

**Комментарий:**

What charity (dattam) was given to a suitable candidate? Api is used in the sense of possibility.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Since I am a materialistic person absorbed simply in sense gratification, I think it is as difficult for me, absorbed in material consciousness, to have gotten this opportunity to see he whose fame destroys saṁsāra as it would be for one born a śūdra to be allowed to recite the Vedic mantras.**

**Комментарий:**

Worried that it would be impossible for him to see Kṛṣṇa, he again thinks of the possibility in two verses. For a mind absorbed in material sense objects such as sound, touch, etc. (viṣaya), for a materialist, to see the Lord is very difficult, like a śūdra reciting the Vedas (brahma-kirtanam). One should not recite the Vedas in front of a śūdra, since he is like a moving cremation ground. Therefore the śūdra, like an animal, is unfit for sacrifices. (Quoted in Govindabhāṣya) By trying to understand the syllables of the Veda, the śūdra immediately degrades himself. (Parāśara-smṛti)

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**But enough of such thoughts! After all, even a fallen soul like me can have the chance to behold the infallible Supreme Lord, for one of the conditioned souls being swept along in the river of time may sometimes reach the shore (the Lord).**

**Комментарий:**

The chance to behold the infallible Supreme Lord is possible even for me, who is abominable due to close association with Kaṁsa. Why? One of the conditioned souls being swept along in the river of time may sometimes reach the shore (the Lord). Just as one blade of grass among a bunch of grass swept away by the river, reaches the shore, similarly among all the jīvas taken by time under the control of karma, one jīva by the mercy of the Lord crosses to the shore. This is possible.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Today all my sinful reactions have been eradicated and my birth has become worthwhile, since I will offer my obeisances to the Supreme Lord’s lotus feet, which mystic yogīs meditate upon.**

**Комментарий:**

By this action, my inauspicious elements, my karmas of bondage from beginningless time will be destroyed. My birth (bhavaḥ) will be successful. Why? Since I will offer respects to the Lord.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Indeed, today Kaṁsa has shown me extreme mercy by sending me to see the lotus feet of he who takes away all inauspiciousness, of he who has now appeared in this world. Simply by the effulgence of his toenails, many souls in the past have transcended the insurmountable darkness of material existence and attained the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

After indicating destruction of karma, he speaks again on the subject. Bata indicates astonishment. Though he is most wicked, Kaṁsa has shown me mercy because, sent by him, I will see the Lord’s lotus feet. If he had sent some other servant, I would not have been able to see the Lord’s lotus feet. Thus, I think it is Kaṁsa’s mercy. By the manifestation of the effulgence of his toenail in the heart, previously Prahlāda and others crossed the darkness of saṁsāra.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Those lotus feet are worshiped by Brahmā, Śiva and all the other devatās, by Lakṣmī and her associates and by devotees in this world, as well as the followers of Pañcarātra. Upon those lotus feet the Lord walks about the forest while herding the cows with his companions, and those feet are smeared with the kuṅkuma from the gopīs’ breasts.**

**Комментарий:**

He meditates on the Lord’s lotus feet. Those feet are worshipped by Brahmā and others. This shows that he gives them the power to create and destroy the universe. They are worshipped by Lakṣmī. This shows that he gives great good fortune. They are worshipped by sages along with devotees. This shows that they are the highest puruṣārtha. He walks using those feet to herd cows. This shows his mercy. They are marked with kuṅkuma from the gopīs’ breasts. This shows that those feet are attained easily by prema alone. Since he is absorbed in only these thoughts (and not more) it does not conflict with his dāsya-rasa.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Surely I shall see the face of Kṛṣṇa whose smile is like jasmine buds, since the deer are now walking past me on my right. That face, framed by his curly hair, is beautified by his attractive cheeks and nose, his smiling glances and his reddish lotus eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

Certainly, I will see Mukunda’s lotus face since the deer are crossing me from left to right (considered auspicious). The face is described. It has two beautiful cheeks and beautiful nose. It has a smiling glance. It has eyes like red lotuses. The modifiers are karma-dhāraya compounds. The face is surrounded by curly (guḍa) locks of hair.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**I am going to see Kṛṣṇa, who spreads his powers everywhere, who is the reservoir of all beauty, and who by his own sweet will has now assumed a humanlike form to relieve the earth of her burden. If I see him, will not my eyes be successful? No, certainly they will.**

**Комментарий:**

Today I will see (bhavitā upalambhanam) Viṣṇu. He is described. He has manifested (īyuṣaḥ) a human body by his own will for lightening the burden of the earth. Para-brahma narākṛtiḥ: Kṛṣṇa is Parabrahman in human form. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) He is the shelter of beauty like the center jewel of a pearl necklace. If that is so (api), then will my eyes not be successful easily? Yes, they will be.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**He who creates the world by his glance alone, inducing cause and effect, who is devoid of absorption in that action, who destroys ignorance, difference and illusion by his cit-śakti, can be perceived in the gopīs’ houses and in the forest by those persons created by his māyā acting under his will, and endowed with action senses, knowledge senses and antaḥkaraṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

“How can he be Viṣṇu if he has qualities of being a doer and enjoyer like us?” Three verses answer. Just by his glance, Kṛṣṇa is the creator of the subtle and gross (asat-satoḥ). Sa aikṣata lokān nu sṛjā: he glanced and created the worlds. (Aitareya Upaniṣad) Though he is the creator, he is without pride (ahaṁ-rahitaḥ). By his superior śakti he removes ignorance (tamaḥ), duality and illusion from himself. From ignorance of oneself comes duality and from duality comes abhiniveśa, etc. (bhramaḥ). The jīva endowed with ego and possessiveness exists with absorption in bodies with prāṇas, senses and intelligence, created in its support of the ātmā by the Lord’s glance which awakens māyā, dependent on him. Although he is the cause of everything, he is very different from the jīva, since he is devoid of ego and possessiveness.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Words that describe the Supreme Lord’s qualities, activities and appearances, which destroy all sins and create all auspiciousness, animate, beautify and purify the world. On the other hand, words bereft of his glories are like a corpse decorated with cloth and ornaments. Devotees do not accept those words.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the Lord’s pastimes, which have commenced, are devoid of material identity, still because of abundance of bliss, they are for the auspiciousness of the world. The topics of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, mixed with his qualities, activities and birth, which destroy all sins (amīvāni), give life to the world, make the world beautiful and purify the world. The opposite is stated. Words devoid of his qualities and pastimes are considered by the wise to be decorations of cloth and ornaments on a corpse. They will not be touched or accepted by the wise.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**That same Supreme Lord, having descended into the dynasty of the Sātvatas to benefit the exalted devatās who maintain bhagavatdharma and spread his fame, which the devatās glorify in song and which brings auspiciousness to all, is residing in Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa has appeared in the Sātvata dynasy and, spreading his fame, is now in Vraja. He gives happiness to Brahmā and other devatās who protect the laws made by him and whose unlimited auspicious fame the devatās sing.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Today I shall certainly see the Lord who is attainable by great devotees and gives instructions, who is joy to all people having eyes, who is the most beautiful in all the worlds, whom even Lakṣmī desires as her shelter. Now all the mornings of my life have become auspicious.**

**Комментарий:**

Certainly, I will see him today. He is the shelter (gatim) of the best of the devatās (mahatām). He is the teacher. He is attractive (kāntam) to the three worlds. He causes great joy to those with eyes. He is the abode of desires of Lakṣmī. He nourishes beauty (rūpaṁ dadhānam) by his various cloths and ornaments. The sign that I will see that person today is that the dawn now indicates auspiciousness for me.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Then I will at once alight from my chariot and bow down to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, the Supreme Lords, which yogīs contemplate by intense practice in order to attain realization of self. I will also offer my obeisances to the Lords’ cowherd boyfriends and to all the other residents of Vṛndāvana.**

**Комментарий:**

On seeing him, I will immediately alight from my chariot. I will offer respects to the feet of Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, who are the chief persons (pradhāna-puṁsoḥ). Those feet are the object of meditation by yogīs for attaining realization of the svarūpa of the jīva endowed with qualities like being free of sin, etc. But I will directly offer respects to those feet. I will offer respects to the friends situated in Vṛndāvana, accompanying the two.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**And when I have fallen at his feet, my master will place his lotus hand upon my head — a hand which destroys fear in all people who are greatly disturbed by the powerful serpent of time and who desire shelter.**

**Комментарий:**

He expresses another desire. He will offer his lotus hand on my head. The lotus-like hand is described. It gives fearlessness to men afraid of the force of the snake of time.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**By offering water to that lotus hand, Purandara and Bali earned the status of Indra, or during the pastimes of the rāsa dance, the Lord relieved the gopīs’ fatigue instantly by the touch of his fragrant hand.**

**Комментарий:**

Giving water (samarhaṇam) to that hand at the time of offering the earth measuring three steps of land, Bali attained the status of Indra. Indra also offered a little water to his hand and received material blessings. For those who desire liberation, he destroys saṁsāra. For those having material desires, he gives material prosperity. For those who are attracted to him however, the Lord offers the highest bliss. The word vā indicates conjecture. That hand, having fragrance of a special type of lotus, relieved the gopīs of fatigue during the rāsa dance.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**The infallible, omniscient Lord will not consider me an enemy, even though Kaṁsa has sent me here as his messenger. After all, he is the actual knower of the field of this material body, and with his perfect vision he witnesses, both externally and internally, all the endeavors of the conditioned soul’s heart.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking of the Lord’s mercy, again worrying, he finally concludes. Acyuta will not think (buddhim upaisyati) of me as an enemy. How is such a thought possible? Since I am sent by Kaṁsa. Why would he not think of me as a messenger sent by Kaṁsa? Because he is omniscient (viśva-dṛk) since the śruti says Yaḥ sarva-jñaḥ sarvavit: he is omniscient. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) He who is inside and outside my consciousness, knows my actions by his omniscience (amalena cakṣuṣā). He is also my antaryāmī (kṣetra-jñaḥ). The meaning is this. I follow Kaṁsa externally, but I follow Kṛṣṇa internally. Kṛṣṇa knows this. Thus, he will not think of me as an enemy, but will give great mercy.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Thus he will cast his smiling, affectionate glance upon me as I remain fixed with joined palms, fallen with respect at his feet. Then all my contamination will at once be dispelled, and I will give up all fears and feel the most intense bliss.**

**Комментарий:**

If he sees me with a glance of mercy as I fold my hands and approach his lotus feet, then immediately I will have all my contaminations destroyed and will attain (voḍhā) the highest bliss (ūrjitām mudam).

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Recognizing me as an intimate friend and relative, Kṛṣṇa will deeply embrace me with his arms, instantly sanctifying my body and diminishing to nil all my material bondage, which is due to karma.**

**Комментарий:**

When he embraces me, a great friend, with his huge arms, only then my body (ātmā) will become purified (tīrthī-kriyate). From the embrace, the bondage of karma will be destroyed (ucchvasiti).

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Having been embraced by the all-famous Kṛṣṇa, I will humbly stand before him with bowed head and joined palms, and he will address me, “My dear Akrūra.” At that very moment my life’s purpose will be fulfilled. Indeed, the life of anyone whom the Supreme Lord fails to recognize is simply pitiable.**

**Комментарий:**

When famous Kṛṣṇa speaks to me, “O dear Akrūra!” I will become successful in birth. He who is not respected by the Lord, his birth is useless.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord does not consider a person dear or despised, the object of gratitude, the object of hatred or the object of indifference. All the same, he lovingly reciprocates with his devotees in whatever manner they worship him, just as the trees of heaven fulfill the desires of whoever approaches them.**

**Комментарий:**

“Embracing and speaking together as friends are human actions. How is it proper for the Lord to do this?” For the Lord, no one is dear (dayitaḥ) or the opposite, disliked (apriyaḥ), no one is a friend, giving benefit, and no one is an enemy. He is neutral, separate from all. That is true. However, he worships the devotees as they worship him. Ye yathā mām prapadyante: as they surrender to me, I respond. (BG [4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11)) Though he is neutral, he does not give results to non-devotees. An example is given of the desire tree.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa’s elder brother, the foremost of the Yadus, will grasp my joined hands while I am still standing with my head bowed, and after embracing me he will take me to his house. There he will honor me with all items of welcome and inquire from me about how Kaṁsa has been treating his family members.**

**Комментарий:**

Even Balarām (kiṁ ca), holding my folded hands, will take me into his house. He will ask me, who has been given a welcome with items like arghya (āpta-samasta-sat-kṛtam) about the sufferings created by Kaṁsa for his relatives.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: My dear King, while the son of Śvaphalka, traveling on the road, thus meditated deeply on Kṛṣṇa, he reached Gokula as the sun came to Sunset Mountain.**

**Комментарий:**

Absorbed in Kṛṣṇa, Akrūra, even though devoid of external awareness, arrived in Gokula in the evening by the chariot controlled by the driver.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**In the cowherd pasture Akrūra saw the footprints of those feet whose pure dust the rulers of all the planets in the universe hold on their crowns. Those extraordinary footprints of the Lord, distinguished by such marks as the lotus, barleycorn and elephant goad, made the earth joyful.**

**Комментарий:**

He saw in the village the footprints whose pure dust is placed in their crowns by all the devatās. The footprints gave joy to the earth. Thus, they were preserved by the earth. The footprints were distinguished by marks of the lotus, etc.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Increasingly agitated by ecstasy at seeing the Lord’s footprints, his bodily hairs standing on end because of his pure love, and his eyes filled with tears, Akrūra jumped down from his chariot and began rolling about among those footprints, exclaiming, “Ah, this is the dust from my master’s feet!”**

**Комментарий:**

He became increasingly agitated with joy from seeing the footprints. His hairs stood on end in prema. His eyes became full of tears. Alighting from the chariot, Akrūra rolled on the footprints, saying, “What good fortune! This is the dust from the lotus feet of my master.”

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**The very goal of life for all embodied beings is this ecstasy, which Akrūra experienced when, upon receiving Kaṁsa’s order, he put aside all pride, fear and lamentation and absorbed himself in seeing, hearing, and describing the things that reminded him of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why did he roll in Kṛṣṇa’s foot dust?” There is no regards for result in the confusion of prema. This much is only the puruṣārtha (highest goal) for those having bodies (deha-bhṛtām), which has been described about Akrūra by hearing about and seeing signs of the Lord, starting from the order of Kaṁsa, while he was devoid of pride, fear and lamentation. It said here that bhakti is the puruṣārtha.

### Text 28-33

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra then saw Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma in the village of Vraja, going to milk the cows. Kṛṣṇa wore yellow garments, Balarāma blue, and their eyes resembled autumnal lotuses. One of those two mighty-armed youths, the shelters of the goddess of fortune, had a dark-blue complexion, and the other’s was white. With their fine-featured faces they were the most beautiful of all persons. As they walked with the gait of young elephants, glancing about with compassionate smiles, those two exalted personalities beautified the cow pasture with the impressions of their feet, which bore the marks of the flag, lightning bolt, elephant goad and lotus. The two Lords, whose pastimes are most magnanimous and attractive, were ornamented with flower garlands and necklaces, anointed with auspicious, fragrant substances. They were freshly bathed and dressed in spotless raiment. They were the primeval Lords, the masters and original causes of the universes, Keśava and Balarāma who had for the welfare of the earth now descended with their expansions. O King Parīkṣit, they resembled two goldbedecked mountains, one of emerald and the other of silver. With their effulgence they dispelled the sky’s darkness in all directions.**

**Комментарий:**

Six verses together. He saw them at the gośāla (go-dohanam). The etymology of go-dohanam is gāvo duhyate’atra: the place where cows are milked. Their glances were shining with mercy (anukrośa). They were decorated with jeweled necklaces (sragviṇau). Their bodies were anointed with attractive (puṇya) scents. They were the principal forms of the Lord (pradhāna-puruṣau) and thus are the original (ādyau). They had appeared with other different forms for relieving the earth of its burden. They were like two mountains decorated with ornaments (kanakācitau).

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra, overwhelmed with affection, quickly jumped down from his chariot and fell at the feet of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma like a rod.**

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**The joy of seeing the Supreme Lord flooded Akrūra’s eyes with tears and decorated his limbs with eruptions of ecstasy. He felt such eagerness that he could not speak to present himself, O King.**

**Комментарий:**

His eyes were full of tears from the joy of seeing the Lord. He was not even able to say, “I am Akrūra. I offer respects to you.”

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Recognizing Akrūra, Kṛṣṇa drew him close with his hand, which bears the sign of the chariot wheel, and then embraced him. Kṛṣṇa felt pleased, for he is affectionate toward his surrendered devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Knowing that Akrūra had come here for this purpose, as if hinting, “Do not worry how Kaṁsa will be killed,” Kṛṣṇa, drawing him close with his hand marked with the cakra, embraced him.

### Text 37-38

**Перевод:**

**As Akrūra stood with his head bowed, Balarāma grasped his joined hands, and then Balarāma took him to Nanda’s house in the company of Kṛṣṇa. After inquiring from Akrūra whether his trip had been comfortable, Balarāma offered him a first-class seat, bathed his feet in accordance with the injunctions of scripture and respectfully served him madhuparka.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma grasped his hands (pāṇī) which were joined together. Offering an excellent seat to Akrūra, washing his feet, he brought (āharat) and offered madhuparka or all items appropriate to offer.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**The almighty Balarāma, in devotion, presented Akrūra with the gift of a cow, massaged him to relieve him of fatigue and then with great respect and faith fed him suitably prepared food of various fine tastes.**

**Комментарий:**

He relieved Akrūra of fatigue by massaging him with fragrant oils. With respect, Balarāma, though he was the Lord (vibhuḥ), offered pure foods. By these sweet actions Akrūra, who was inwardly conscious of their powers, developed a similar sweet mood.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**When Akrūra had eaten to his satisfaction, Balarāma, the knower of devotion, offered him aromatic herbs for sweetening his mouth, along with fragrances and flower garlands for his great satisfaction.**

**Комментарий:**

He pleased Akrūra with betel nut prepared with cardamom and clove (mukha-vāsa).

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja asked Akrūra, who had been welcomed: O descendant of Daśārha, how are all of you maintaining yourselves while that merciless Kaṁsa remains alive? You are just like sheep under the care of a butcher.**

**Комментарий:**

After Akrūra had been welcomed, Nanda inquired from him. O Akrūra! While merciless Kaṁsa is alive, how do you maintain your life? You are like sheep under the protection of a killer of animals (sauna).

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**That cruel, self-serving Kaṁsa murdered the infants of his own sister in her presence, even as she cried in anguish. Can we imagine how much well-being those dependent on him have?**

**Комментарий:**

The cruelty of Kaṁsa is described. He killed the children of his own sister Devakī. He is wicked, who satisfies his life by his sinful actions (asu-tṛp). How can we imagine the well-being of you, his citizens?

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Honored by Nanda Mahārāja with these true and pleasing words of inquiry, Akrūra forgot the fatigue of saṁsāra.**

**Комментарий:**

Honored by the sweet words of Nanda, by the questions, Akrūra gave up the sufferings of saṁsāra (adhva-pariśramam).

## Chapter 39 - Akrūra’s Vision

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having been honored so much by Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, Akrūra, seated comfortably on a couch, felt that all the desires he had contemplated on the road were now fulfilled.**

**Комментарий:**

In the thirty-nineth chapter when Kṛṣṇa goes to Mathurā, the gopīs’ words and the praise by Akrūra and seeing Viṣṇu and his planet are described. Indicating that the Lord fulfills the desires of his devotees, Śukadeva speaks this verse. When Nanda returned and entered his house for performing night duties, Akrūra was respected profusely with fine scents, etc., by Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma who were seated with him on a jeweled couch offered by servants. When the two entered their own quarters, feeling less reverence, Akrūra felt that his desires had been achieved. He felt complete.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, what is unattainable for one who has satisfied the Supreme Lord, the shelter of the goddess of fortune? Even so, those who are dedicated to his devotional service never want anything from him.**

**Комментарий:**

“How is it that he did not have desires for dharma, artha, etc.?” That is answered in this verse.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**After the evening meal, Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, asked Akrūra how Kaṁsa was treating their dear relatives and friends and what the King was planning to do.**

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear, gentle Uncle Akrūra, was your trip here comfortable? May all good fortune be yours. Are our well-wishing friends and our relatives, both close and distant, happy and in good health?**

**Комментарий:**

O father (tata)! O gentle one! I hope your journey was comfortable. Are your friends (sva), close relatives (jñāti) and distant relatives (bāndhu) free of suffering (anamīvam) and in good health (anāmayam)?

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**But, my dear Akrūra, as long as Kaṁsa—that disease of our family who goes by the name “maternal uncle”—is still prospering, why should I even bother to ask about the well-being of our family members and his other subjects?**

**Комментарий:**

My question is actually not possible. O Akrūra! While the disease of our family prospers, how can I ask about the welfare of relatives and subjects? He laments.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Just see how much suffering I have caused my offenseless parents! Because of me, their sons were killed and they themselves imprisoned.**

**Комментарий:**

O dear one! My faultless parents have suffered a lot (vṛjinam) because of me. Thus all this suffering has arisen due to me.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**By good fortune we have today fulfilled our desire to see you, our dear relative. O gentle uncle, please tell us why you have come.**

**Комментарий:**

My desire of seeing you, my relative has been fulfilled by good fortune (diṣṭyā).

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: In response to the Supreme Lord’s request, Akrūra, the descendant of Madhu, described the whole situation, including Kaṁsa’s enmity toward the Yadus and his attempt to murder Vasudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Mādhavaḥ means born in the dynasty of Madhu.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra relayed the message he had been sent to deliver. He also described Kaṁsa’s real intentions and how Nārada had informed Kaṁsa that Kṛṣṇa had been born as the son of Vasudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

He gave the message with the pretext of the bow sacrifice, and explained how the wrestlers were arranged to kill him, as well as what Nārada had told Kaṁsa, that Kṛṣṇa had been born to Vasudeva. Hearing of the birth of the one with unlimited avatāras, in the form of Kṛṣṇa, Kaṁsa sent me as a messenger.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, the vanquishers of heroic opponents, laughed when they heard Akrūra’s words. The Lords then informed their father, Nanda Mahārāja, of King Kaṁsa’s orders.**

**Комментарий:**

They laughed. “Death has quickly come for so called uncle.” They particularly informed their father going close to him. Vijajñatuḥ has a causative sense (made him know).

### Text 11-12

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja then issued orders to the cowherd men by having the village constable make the following announcement throughout Nanda’s domain of Vraja: “Go collect all the available milk products. Bring valuable gifts and yoke your wagons. Tomorrow we shall go to Mathurā, present our milk products to the king and see a very great festival. The residents of all the outlying districts are also going.”**

**Комментарий:**

Though dedicated to caring for his son, the father, as in Kṛṣṇa’s stopping Indra’s sacrifice, followed the desire of his son thinking that the wicked Kaṁsa should not die by the power of his son, which he experienced, and desiring the happiness of the Yadus, his relatives, he ordered the very strong cowherds. We will give ghee, etc., (rasān) to the king. Or as a pun it can mean medicines that will cure his disease. Take all these excellent substances and yoke the chariots (śakatāni). Nanda, the king of Vraja, spread the message everywhere (aghoṣayat) by his servant (kṣattrā), responsible for protecting Gokula.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**When the young gopīs heard that Akrūra had come to Vraja to take Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma to the city, they became extremely distressed.**

**Комментарий:**

Among the people of Vraja, the gopīs’ intense prema is described. Hearing that Akrūra had come to take Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma to Mathurā, they became distressed.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Some gopīs felt so pained at heart that their faces turned pale from their heavy breathing. Others were so anguished that their dresses, bracelets and braids became loose.**

**Комментарий:**

The signs of their distress are described. The beauty of their faces faded by their heavy breathing due to the pain of their hearts caused by what they heard. Their clothing became loose. The thinness that is attained by fasting for a month, they attained by just hearing the news.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Other gopīs entirely stopped their sensory activities and became fixed in meditation on Kṛṣṇa. They lost all awareness of the external world, just like those who attain the platform of selfrealization.**

**Комментарий:**

Others such as Candrāvalī became unaware of their own bodies (imam lokam) as if they had achieved realization of ātmā in asaṁprajñāta-samādhi by perfection of yoga.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**And still other young women fainted simply by remembering the words of Kṛṣṇa. These words, decorated with wonderful phrases and expressed with affectionate smiles, would deeply touch the young girls’ hearts.**

**Комментарий:**

Other gopīs fainted on remembering his word, spoken with smiles born of affection, most attractive (hṛdi spṛśaḥ), and which had various literary ornaments such as alliterations (citra-padā).

### Text 17-18

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs were frightened at the prospect of even the briefest separation from Mukunda, so now, as they remembered his graceful gait, pastimes, affectionate, smiling glances, his joking words, and his intimate pastimes with them, they were beside themselves with the fright of the great separation. They gathered in groups and spoke to one another, their faces covered with tears and their minds fully absorbed in Acyuta.**

**Комментарий:**

They remembered his pastimes (ceṣṭām) and joking words (narmāni), disturbed by the separation, their hearts attached to Kṛṣṇa (acyutāśayaḥ), they spoke.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs said: O Providence, you have no mercy! You bring embodied creatures together in friendship and love and then senselessly separate them before they fulfill their desires. This whimsical play of yours is like a child’s game.**

**Комментарий:**

The gopīs scold the creator for arranging association with Kṛṣṇa and then destroying it. O creator (vidhātaḥ)! You do not have any mercy. You bring people together by friendly behavior (maitryā) and affection (praṇayena) and then separate them who have got desires. You are foolish. Your actions are useless like those of a child.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Having shown us Mukunda’s face, framed by dark locks and beautified by his fine cheeks, raised nose and gentle smiles, which eradicate all misery, you are now making that face invisible. This behavior of yours is not at all good.**

**Комментарий:**

Your actions are to be criticized. Showing Mukunda’s beautiful face with a secret smile which destroys lamentation, you make it disappear. Thus your action is to be criticized.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**O Providence, though you come here with the name Akrūra, you are indeed cruel (krūra), for like a fool you are taking away what you once gave us—those eyes with which we have seen, the perfection of your entire creation in just one feature of Kṛṣṇa’s form, which derides all other sweetness.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover you are most cruel, since you take away what was given. “But it is Akrūra who is taking away not I.” You gave us our eyes and coming in name of Akrūra (not cruel) you take them away. Definitely no one except for you, can do that. “But I am taking Kṛṣṇa away, not your eyes.” No, by those eyes which were given by you, we saw your skill of entire creation in the limbs, face to feet, of Kṛṣṇa. We saw in a portion of a portion of the nectar ocean of beginningless beauty, the perfection of the beauty of the moon, lotus, etc. Our eyes are the receptacle of that. As if with the anger that, “All my skill of creation is known by these gopīs,” you take away Kṛṣṇa and blind us.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Alas, Nanda’s son, who breaks loving friendships in a second, will not even look directly at us. Forcibly brought under his control, we abandoned our homes, relatives, children and husbands just to serve him, but he is nevertheless exceptionally pleasing in appearance while he leaves.**

**Комментарий:**

Giving up the creator, the gopīs talk among themselves. Bata indicates lamentation. Having unsteady friendship, breaking it in a moment, the son of Nanda does not even glance at us. They describe themselves. Suffering from his smiles and glances we fell under his control. Giving up house, etc., we approached him directly as servants. His mind is absorbed in new girls (nava-priyaḥ).

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**This night will certainly bring joy to the women of Mathurā. All their hopes will now be fulfilled, for as the Lord of Vraja enters their city, they will be able to drink from his face the nectar of the smile emanating from the corners of his eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

They speak with envy. All the desires of the Mathurā women will be fulfilled when Kṛṣṇa, the sole object of enjoyment for the people of Vraja (vrajas-pateḥ), enters the city. The “s” in vrajas is poetic license. They will drink or see (pāsyanti) his face, having a smile, which is honey, emanating from the edges of his eyes. They imagine that the face is a beverage.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**O gopīs, although our Mukunda is intelligent and very obedient to his parents, once he has fallen under the spell of the honey-sweet words of the women of Mathurā and been enchanted by their alluring, shy smiles, how will he ever return to us unsophisticated village girls?**

**Комментарий:**

“Spending two or three days there, attracted by his parents, etc., he will return to Vraja.” His heart will be captivated by the sweet words of the city women and bewildered by their shy, smiling gestures. Though Mukunda is subservient to his parents (para-vān) and intelligent, how will he come to us? He will not come, O girls (abalāḥ)! Because we are village girls and not skillful. They utter this in wretchedness, since their skill was shown in the five chapters on the rāsa dance. Later he will also say tāḥ kiṁ niṣāḥ smaratī: do you remember those nights? (SB [10.47.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.43))

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**When the Dāśārhas, Bhojas, Andhakas, Vṛṣṇis and Sātvatas see the son of Devakī in Mathurā, they will certainly enjoy a great festival for their eyes, as will all those who see him traveling along the road to the city. After all, he is the darling of the goddess of fortune and the reservoir of all qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

Others will experience our joy. In the city there will be a great festival for the eyes (dṛśaḥ) of the Dāśārhas and others. Eye is in the singular, representing a type. Ātmanepada form of the verb (bhaviṣyate) is poetic license. Those who see the son of Devakī going on the road will also experience joy for their eyes, since they will see the lord of Rādhā (śrī-ramaṇam).

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**He who is doing this merciless deed should not be called Akrūra. He is so extremely cruel that without even trying to console the sorrowful residents of Vraja, he is taking away Kṛṣṇa, who is dearer to us than life itself to a far off place.**

**Комментарий:**

They curse Akrūra. The person who does such a deed, being most cruel, should not have the auspicious name of Akrūra (not cruel). The reason is given. Being most cruel, he will take Kṛṣṇa dearer than the self, far off (pāram) on the road.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Hard-hearted Kṛṣṇa has already mounted the chariot, and now the foolish cowherds are hurrying after him in their bullock carts. Even the elders are saying nothing to stop him. Today fate is working against us.**

**Комментарий:**

How unfortunate is our life! Kṛṣṇa, with hard intelligence (anārdradhīḥ), has mounted the chariot. Seeing his hard intelligence, he is not prevented (upekṣitam) by the elders (sthaviraiḥ). The cowherds, revering him, urge him ahead with their carts. They had taken to valor (durmadāḥ) since Hari-vaṁśa describes them as bhavanto bhīma-vikramā: the cowherds were all ferocious and courageous. Otherwise they would have discrimination. Therefore, fate is against us. If fate were in our favor, there would be some sudden obstacle (to prevent Kṛṣṇa’s departure).

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Let us directly approach Mādhava and stop him from going. What can our family elders and other relatives do to us? Now that fate is separating us from Mukunda, our hearts are already wretched, for we cannot bear to give up his association even for a fraction of a second.**

**Комментарий:**

Consulting each other they speak. Together we will stop Kṛṣṇa. What will the elders and friends do to us, whose hearts are miserable being separated from association with Mukunda by fate? Even if we, who are of such condition. die, there is no worry.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**When he brought us to the assembly of the rāsa dance, where we enjoyed his affectionate and charming smiles, his delightful secret talks, his playful glances and his embraces, we passed many nights as if they were a single moment. O gopīs, how can we possibly cross over the insurmountable darkness of his absence?**

**Комментарий:**

Because of this, we should be bold. O gopīs! We passed the nights as moments in the rāsa dance with Kṛṣṇa’s charming smile, confidential conversations, playful glances and affectionate embraces. How can we cross the insurmountable darkness, the suffering of separation, without Kṛṣṇa? We cannot in anyway.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**How can we exist without Kṛṣṇa, who in the evening would return to Vraja in the company of the cowherd boys and Balarāma, his hair and garland powdered with the dust raised by the cows’ hooves? As he played his flute, he would captivate our minds with his smiling sidelong glances.**

**Комментарий:**

What to speak of crossing darkness, we cannot live without him. In the evening, entering Vraja, he attracts (kṣinoti) our hearts with his smiling side glances. Without that Kṛṣṇa, how can we live (bhavema)? To maintain our lives, giving up shame, we should stop his departure.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After speaking these words, the ladies of Vraja, who were so attached to Kṛṣṇa, felt extremely agitated by their imminent separation from him. They forgot all shame and loudly cried out, “O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!”**

**Комментарий:**

They whose minds were attracted to Kṛṣṇa (kṛṣṇa-viṣakta-mānasāḥ), cried out loudly (susvaram).

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**But even as the gopīs cried out in this way, Akrūra, having at sunrise performed his morning worship and other duties, began to drive the chariot.**

**Комментарий:**

Ignoring the crying gopīs, Akrūra urged on the chariot, after performing morning rites like sandhyopāsana related to the devatā Mitra (maitrādikam).

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Led by Nanda Mahārāja, the cowherd men followed behind Kṛṣṇa in their wagons. The men brought along many offerings for the king, including clay pots filled with ghee and other milk products.**

**Комментарий:**

The cowherds followed (anvasajjanta).

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa somewhat pacified the gopīs, and they also followed behind for some time. Then, hoping he would give them some instruction, they stood still.**

**Комментарий:**

The gopīs were somewhat happy (anurañjitāḥ) by his glancing back at them. They desired some answer from him.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**As he departed, that best of the Yadus saw how the gopīs were lamenting, and thus he consoled them by sending messengers with this loving promise: “I will return.”**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the suffering gopīs, he consoled them by words through messengers, “I will return quickly.” He sent many messengers (dautyakaiḥ). This indicates his own anguish.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Sending their minds after Kṛṣṇa, the gopīs stood as motionless as figures in a painting. They remained there as long as the flag atop the chariot was visible, and even until they could no longer see the dust raised by the chariot wheels.**

**Комментарий:**

As long as they could see the flag and the dust, they stood like painted dolls. They made their minds (ātmanaḥ) follow Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs then turned back, without hope that Govinda would ever return to them. Giving up sorrow, they began to spend their days and nights chanting about the pastimes of their beloved.**

**Комментарий:**

They gave up hope that he would not go to Mathurā and would return on the path. Thus, they left from there. They sang about his activities, in which he keeps his promise: tasmān mac-charaṇaṁ goṣṭhaṁ man-nāthaṁ mat-parigraham gopāye svātma-yogena so ’yaṁ me vrata āhitaḥ I must therefore protect the cowherd community by my natural powers for I am there shelter, I am their protector, and indeed I am everything to them. I have taken a vow to protect my devotees. (SB [10.25.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/25.18)) Their lamentation disappeared by his sphurti through singing. Thus, without lamentation, they spent two days in separation because that much time entered in it like a night of Brahmā entered three yāmās. This is elaborated elsewhere.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, traveling as swiftly as the wind in that chariot with Balarāma and Akrūra, arrived at the river Kālindī, which destroys all sins.**

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**The river’s sweet water was more effulgent than brilliant jewels. After Kṛṣṇa had performed ācamana, he drank some. Then he had the chariot moved near a grove of trees and climbed back on, along with Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

He performed ācamana (upaspṛśya) and then drank the clear water which shone with the color of sapphire. Then going to a thicket of trees, as if afraid of enemies he climbed back on the chariot (āviśat).

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra asked the two Lords to take their seats on the chariot. Then, taking their permission, he went to a pool in the Yamunā and took his bath as enjoined in the scriptures.**

**Комментарий:**

He took permission from the two seated on the chariot.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**While immersing himself in the water and reciting Gāyatrī mantra, Akrūra suddenly saw Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa before him.**

**Комментарий:**

He chanted Gāyatrī (brahma), characterized by having three lines, and saw the two boys. He worried how the two very young boys would fight with the wrestlers. Thus, the Lord showed Akrūra his powers.

### Text 42-43

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra thought, “How can the two sons of Vasudeva, who are sitting in the chariot, be standing here in the water? They must have left the chariot.” But when he came out of the river, they were on the chariot, just as before. Asking himself, “Was the vision I had of them in the water an illusion?” Akrūra reentered the pool.**

**Комментарий:**

“How did the two come here? Then they are not on the chariot.” Worrying in this way, he got out of the water and looked at the chariot. Svid indicates conjecture. Seeing that they were even on the chariot, he again went into the water. “Was my seeing them in the water an illusion?”

### Text 44-45

**Перевод:**

**In the water, Akrūra now saw Ananta Śeṣa, the Lord of the serpents, receiving praise from Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas and demons, who all had their heads bowed. He had thousands of heads, thousands of hoods and thousands of helmets. Worthy of worship by the universe, he wore blue garment, and was as white as the filaments of a lotus stem, like white Kailāsa Mountain with its many peaks.**

**Комментарий:**

To Akrūra who was not diving into the magnificence of his sweetness and who was afraid of Kaṁsa, Kṛṣṇa made him realize his aṁśa Viṣṇu. Going into the water, Akrūra saw the Lord of the snakes, praised by Siddhas, etc. On his thousand hoods he had crowns. Maulinam is formed by the suffix ini according to vrīhy-ādibhyaś ca (Pāṇini 5.2.116). He was white like lotus stem filaments. He was situated like white Kailāsa with many peaks.

### Text 46-48

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra then saw the Lord lying peacefully on the lap of Ananta. His complexion was like a dark-blue cloud. He wore yellow garments and had four arms and reddish lotus-petal eyes. His face looked attractive and cheerful with its smiling, endearing glance and lovely eyebrows, its raised nose and finely formed ears, and its beautiful cheeks and reddish lips. The Lord had broad shoulders and his chest was marked with the line of Lakṣmī. His arms were long and thick. His neck had three lines like conch shell, his navel was deep, and his abdomen bore lines like those on a banyan leaf.**

**Комментарий:**

Twelve verses describe the Lord lying on Ananta comfortably. The verb occurs in the eleventh verse: seeing the Lord situated on the lap of the king of snakes. He had lovely eyebrows, a raised nose, beautiful cheeks and reddish lips. The Lord had broad shoulders and his chest was marked with the line of Lakṣmī. He had deep horizontal lines (valimat) on his navel. His abdomen resembled a banyan leaf.

### Text 49-50

**Перевод:**

**He had large loins and hips, thighs tapering like an elephant’s trunk, and shapely knees and shanks. His raised ankles reflected the brilliant effulgence emanating from the nails on his tender, petal-like toes, which beautified his lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

He had wide hips, wide loins and wide thighs, whose shape was like an elephant trunk (karabha). His ankles were slightly raised and his toenails were red. His lotus feet shone brightly with the light of the tender toes, toenails and ankles.

### Text 51-52

**Перевод:**

**Adorned with a helmet, bracelets and armlets, which were all bedecked with many priceless jewels, and also with a belt, a sacred thread, necklaces, ankle bells and earrings, the Lord shone with dazzling effulgence. In one hand he held a lotus flower, in the others a conch, discus and club. Gracing his chest were the Śrīvatsa mark, the brilliant Kaustubha gem and a flower garland.**

**Комментарий:**

He shone with crowns having valuable gems, with a belt of bells (kaṭi-sūtra), with a sacred thread (yajña-sūtra). He held a lotus in his hand. He had Śrīvatsa on his chest. The form of Śrīvatsa is described in Hari-vaṁśa: On his broad chest shines beautiful Śrīvatsa, a curved hair raising up with stripes, which is honored by his nipples. (Hari-vaṁśa)

### Text 53-55

**Перевод:**

**Encircling the Lord and worshiping him were Nanda, Sunanda and his other personal attendants; Sanaka and the other Kumāras; Brahmā, Rudra and other chief devatās; the nine chief brāhmaṇas; and the best of the saintly devotees, headed by Prahlāda, Nārada and Uparicara Vasu. Each of these great personalities was worshiping the Lord by chanting sanctified words of praise in his own unique mood. Also in attendance were the Lord’s principal internal potencies—Śrī, Puṣṭi, Gīr, Kānti, Kīrti, Tuṣṭi, Ilā and Ūrjā—as were his material potencies Vidyā, Avidyā and Māyā, and his internal pleasure potency, Śakti.**

**Комментарий:**

He was surrounded by nine brāhmaṇas such as Marīci. Vasu means Uparicara Vasu. Each of these great personalities was worshiping the Lord by chanting sanctified words of praise in his own unique prema or unique desire (pṛthag-bhāvaiḥ). These are eternal āvaraṇa deities who give life to the devatās in the material world. nityāḥ sarve pare dhāmni ye cānye ca divaukasaḥ te vai prākṛta-nāke’smin anityās tridaśeśvarāḥ te ha nākaṁ mahimānaḥ sacanta iti vai śrutir All the other devatās in the spiritual world are eternal. Those in the material heavenly planets are temporary devatās. The śruti says that devatās associate with the Lord in the spiritual world. (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa) He was served by the superior śakti. That śakti is divided. He was served by Lakṣmī (śriyā), Sarasvatī (girā), Bhūmi (ilayā), and māyā. Māyā is divided into vidyā, by causing liberation of jīvas, and avidyā by causing saṁsāra of jīvas since it will be said: vidyāvidye mama tanū viddhy uddhava śarīriṇām mokṣa-bandha-karī ādye māyayā me vinirmite O Uddhava, both knowledge (vidyā) and ignorance (avidyā), being products of māyā, are expansions of my potency. Both knowledge and ignorance are beginningless and perpetually award liberation and bondage to embodied living beings. (SB [11.11.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/11.3)) The word ca indicates other śaktis like time.

### Text 56-57

**Перевод:**

**As the great devotee Akrūra beheld all this, he became extremely pleased and felt enthused with devotion. His intense ecstasy caused his bodily hairs to stand on end and tears to flow from his eyes, drenching his entire body. Somehow managing to steady himself, Akrūra bowed his head while within the water. Then he joined his palms in supplication and, in a voice choked with emotion, very slowly and attentively began to pray.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa of this nature, Akrūra was greatly pleased since he understood Kṛṣṇa’s powers. His mind (ātma) and eyes were moist from bhāva. Though overcome with prema, regaining control (sattvam), the devotee (sātvataḥ) praised the Lord, while being within the water.

## Chapter 40 - Akrūra’s Prayers

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Akrūra said: I bow down to you, the cause of all causes, the original and inexhaustible Supreme Person, Nārāyaṇa. From the whorl of the lotus born from your navel, Brahmā appeared, and by his agency this universe has come into being.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fortieth chapter Akrūra, understanding that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Lord, praises him with the highest devotion, offering respects. O Kṛṣṇa! I offer respects to you. “But you are an elder. Why do you offer respects to me, a child?” You are the original puruṣa, unchanging (avyayaṁ), even the cause of Brahmā, who is the cause of the universe (akhila-hetu-hetuṁ). From your navel came Brahmā who created the universal form (eṣa lokaḥ).

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Earth; water; fire; air; ether and its source, false ego; the mahattattva, the total material nature and the jīva; the mind; the senses; the sense objects; and the senses’ presiding deities—all these causes of the cosmic manifestation are born from your transcendental body.**

**Комментарий:**

This explains how the Lord is the cause of the cause of everything. Kham is ether and its origin (ādi) is ahaṅkāra. Ajā is prakṛti. Ādi indicates time. Artha means sense objects. Vibudhāḥ means the presiding deities of the senses. All the causes of the universe function under your control (aṅga-bhūtāḥ).

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**The total material nature and these other elements of creation certainly cannot know you as you are, for they are manifested in the realm of dull matter. Since you are beyond the modes of nature, even Brahma, who is bound up in these modes, does not know your true identity.**

**Комментарий:**

Prakṛti, etc., do not know your (ātmanaḥ) svarūpa because they are accepted as material (nātmatayā) in the scriptures. “Matter cannot know me, but why cannot the conscious jīvas know me?” The jīva (ajaḥ), bound by the guṇas of prakṛti, does not know your svarūpa, which is beyond the guṇas of prakṛti. Though you are beyond the senses, by mercy you show yourself.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Pure yogīs worship you, the Supreme lord, by conceiving of you in the threefold form comprising the living entities, the material elements that constitute the living entities’ bodies, and the controlling deities of those elements.**

**Комментарий:**

“If no one knows me, how can jīvas become liberated from saṁsāra?” Yogīs who are situated in asaṁaprajñāta-samādhi, worship you directly. They see you by the yajña of yoga. You are the mahāpuruṣa, witness of adhyātmā, adhibhūta and adhidaiva.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Brāhmaṇas who follow the regulations concerning the three sacred fires, worship you by chanting mantras from the three Vedas and performing elaborate fire sacrifices for the various devatās, who have many forms and names.**

**Комментарий:**

Some saniṣṭhā niṣkāma-karmīs (vaitānikas), worship you by the sacrifices profusely mentioned in the three Vedas. “They worship Indra and others, not me.” They worship you by the names of the devatās who have various forms such as holding a thunderbolt (Indra), etc. The meaning is this. The devatās like Indra are revealed as the controller of all beings by sūktas dedicated to them, but the controllers of all beings are not multiple. Thus as their antaryāmī, you are only to be worshipped by their names.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**In pursuit of spiritual knowledge, some persons renounce all material activities and, having thus become peaceful, perform the sacrifice of philosophic investigation to worship you, the original form of all knowledge.**

**Комментарий:**

The jñānīs, endowed with discriminatory knowledge arising from reflecting on Vedānta, giving up all karmas, wandering everywhere (upaśamam gatāḥ), see you by such yajña of jñāna arisen from that.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**And yet others—those whose intelligence is pure—follow the injunctions of Vaiṣṇava scriptures promulgated by you. Absorbing their minds in thought of you, they worship you as the one Supreme Lord manifesting in multiple forms.**

**Комментарий:**

Those having knowledge of Pañcarātra, having taken dīkṣā (saṁskṛtātmanas) according to the rules given there, taking you as the main object (tvan-mayāḥ), worship you having many forms such as the expansions like Vāsudeva, etc., and having one form such as Nārāyaṇa.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**There are still others, who worship you, the Supreme Lord, in the form of Śiva. They follow the path described by him and interpreted in various ways by many teachers.**

**Комментарий:**

Others, the followers of Śiva, worship you alone, who is Śiva’s antaryāmī (śiva-rūpiṇam) by the path explained by Śiva. Brahmā says to Śiva in Nārāyaṇīya: He is the soul of you, me and others who are defined in terms of bodies. He is the witness of all beings. He is not understood by anyone in any circumstance. The path is explained in many ways such as Śaiva, Pāśupata, etc., by various ācāryas.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**
