**But all these people, my Lord, even those who have turned their attention away from you and are worshiping other deities, are actually worshiping you alone, the embodiment of all the devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

O antaryāmī of all devatās (sarva-deva-maya)! Those who are even devoted to other devatās, worshippers of Sūrya, etc., having other intelligence, desiring quick cure for diseases, etc., still worship you alone, the Supreme Lord. The meaning is this. Those who worship thinking that the Lord is the antaryāmī of the devatās, get the result of worshipping the Lord. Those who worship thinking only of the devatās attain trifling results. The Lord says in Gītā: Those who are devoted to other gods and with faith worship them, worship me by the wrong method, O son of Kuntī. (BG [9.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.23)) The results obtained by these foolish persons are temporary. Those who worship devas attain the devas, and those who worship me attain me. (BG [7.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.23))

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**As rivers born from the mountains and filled by the rain, flow from all sides into the sea, so do all the antaryāmīs of the paths in the end reach you, O master.**

**Комментарий:**

Thus all paths end in you. He describes this with an example. All the rivers that flow from a mountain, being increased by the cloud, enter the ocean alone. Similarly, the paths (gatayaḥ) enter you alone. Their antaryāmīs enter you, since they focus on you. My greatest possible good fortune would be to take any birth whatever in this forest of Gokula and have my head bathed by the dust falling from the lotus feet of any of its residents. Their entire life and soul is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Mukunda, the dust of whose lotus feet is still being searched for in the Vedic mantras. (SB [10.14.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.34))

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Goodness, passion and ignorance, the qualities of your material nature, entangle all conditioned living beings, from Brahmā down to the nonmoving creatures.**

**Комментарий:**

“Brahmā and others cause creation, etc., independently. How am I their antaryāmī?” Sattva, etc., are the guṇas of your prakṛti. All beings from Brahmā to nonmoving entities possessing subtle bodies are entangled in the guṇas. You are the controller of Brahmā and other jīvas and their senses and bodies. Thus, they are not independent.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**I offer my obeisances to you, who, as the Supreme Soul of all beings, witness everyone’s consciousness with unbiased vision. The force of your material modes, produced by the force of ignorance, flows strongly among the living beings who assume identities as devatās, humans and animals.**

**Комментарий:**

“By saying that prakṛti belongs to me, I too am not distinguished from the jīvas due to relation with prakṛti.” I offer respects to you, having uncontaminated vision (aviṣakta) since you inspire all beings (sarvātmane), and since you are the witness of all intelligence, seeing neutrally. O Lord! The influence of the guṇas created by ignorance takes place in the jīvas who identify themselves as human or animal and does not take place in you. Jīva’s saṁsāra is caused by ignorance. It is never your nature since you are always without ignorance. This is the great difference between you and the jīva.

### Text 13-14

**Перевод:**

**Fire is said to be your mouth, the earth your feet, the sun your eye, and the sky your navel. The directions are your sense of hearing, the chief demigods your arms, and the oceans your abdomen. Heaven is considered to be your head and the wind your vital air and physical strength. The trees and plants are the hairs on your body, the clouds the hair on your head, and the mountains your bones and nails. The passage of day and night is the blinking of your eyes, the progenitor of mankind your genitals and the rain your semen.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord is praised as the source of the universe. Your mouth is Agni! Your feet are earth! Your eyes are Sūrya. Your navel is ether. Your ears are the directions. Your head is the heavens. Your arms are Indras. Your stomach is the oceans! Your prāṇas and strength are Marut. The body hairs of you, the supreme are the trees and herbs. Your head hair is the clouds. Your nails and bones are the mountains. The blinking of your eyes is day and night. Your genital is Prajāpati. Your semen is the rain. One should think of Agni, etc., being caused by the Lord’s mouth, etc. since by that the excellence of the Lord’s mouth, etc., is shown. The author of Brahma-sūtras says so: One should think of the Lord’s limbs as the cause of the sun etc. because this demonstrates the excellence of the Lord. (Brahma-sūtra) One should think of the Lord’s limbs such as eyes as the cause of the sun, etc., since by that the excellence of the Lord’s limbs is established.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**All the worlds, with their presiding devatās and teeming populations, originate in you, the inexhaustible Supreme Lord. These worlds travel within you, the basis of the mind and senses, just as aquatics swim in the sea or tiny insects burrow within an udumbara fruit.**

**Комментарий:**

The whole material world is just one of your portions. All the planets along with their protectors, crowded with many jīvas are arranged within you, who are the unchanging (avyayātmani) puruṣa and move about within you, who are to be sought only by the mind (manomaye) since the śruti says: The Lord must be realized by the mind alone. (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaṇiṣad [4.4.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bau/4.4.19)) They move within you just like fish in the water or bugs in an udumbara fruit, unaware of their svarūpas.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**To enjoy your pastimes you manifest yourself in various forms in this material world, and these incarnations cleanse away all the unhappiness of those who joyfully chant your glories.**

**Комментарий:**

Your forms like Matsya are for the auspiciousness of the world. By repeatedly thinking about all the forms like Matsya that you manifest (bibharṣi), people whose lamentation is destroyed chant your glories in bliss. They become liberated by that.

### Text 17-18

**Перевод:**

**I offer my obeisances to you, the cause of the creation, Matsya, who swam about in the ocean of dissolution, to Hayagrīva, the killer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, to the immense Kūrma, who supported Mandara Mountain, and to the boar incarnation Varāha, who enjoyed lifting the earth.**

**Комментарий:**

He offers respects to those forms. I offer respects to Matsya who performed actions like rescuing Satyavrata, etc. (kāraṇa). Akūpāra means the ocean and the king of turtles according to Viśva. I offer respects to the giant turtle and to Varāha who performed the pastime of lifting the earth.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances to you, the amazing lion Nṛsiṁha, who remove your saintly devotees’ fear, and to the dwarf Vāmana, who stepped over the three worlds.**

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances to you, lord of the Bhṛgus, who cut down the forest of the conceited royal order, and to Rāma, the best of the Raghu dynasty, who put an end to the demon Rāvaṇa.**

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances to you and to your forms of Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha, protectors of the Sātvatas.**

**Комментарий:**

He offers respects to the catur-vyūha.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances to your form as the faultless Buddha, who will bewilder the Daityas and Dānavas, and to Kalki, the annihilator of the meat-eaters posing as kings.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to faultless Buddha. He rejected the sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas to bewilder the demons.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**O Supreme Lord, the living entities in this world are bewildered by your illusory energy. Becoming involved in the false concepts of “I” and “my,” they are forced to wander along the paths of karma.**

**Комментарий:**

Having praised the Lord, he prays for liberation. The jīva is strongly attached to the body, wife, etc., which are despicable (asad-grāhaḥ).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**I too am deluded in this way, O almighty Lord, foolishly thinking my body, children, home, wife, money and followers to be real, though they are actually as unreal as a dream.**

**Комментарий:**

“Let the world be deluded. But you know me very well.” I too am bewildered thinking that impermanent things like body (ātma), wealth (artha), relatives will last forever.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Thus mistaking the temporary for the eternal, my body for the self, and sources of misery for sources of happiness, I have tried to take pleasure in material dualities. Covered in this way by ignorance, I could not recognize you as the real object of my love.**

**Комментарий:**

He explains his foolishness. I think that the impermanent results of karma like animals, food and sons, are eternal, that the body, which is not the self, is the self, and that house, etc., forms of grief, are happiness. Thus I have opposite intelligence. I take pleasure in dualities like heat and cold. “But how so?” Covered with ignorance, I do not know you, the abode of prema (ātmanaḥ priyam).

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Just as a fool overlooks a body of water covered by the vegetation growing in it and chases a mirage, so I have turned away from you.**

**Комментарий:**

An example is given. A fool overlooks water covered by grass which has grown from the water (udbhavaiḥ) and chases a mirage. Similarly, I give up you, residing in my heart but covered by my ignorance, and turn towards body, wife, etc.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**My intelligence is so crippled that I cannot find the strength to curb my mind, which is disturbed by material desires and activities and constantly dragged here and there by my obstinate senses.**

**Комментарий:**

“If you know this, why do you not give affection up for your body, etc.?” Having feeble intelligence, I do not have the power (utsahe) to control the fickle mind which is overcome by kāma-karmas. The mind is pulled to sense objects like sound, touch, etc., here and there by the harassing (pramāthibhiḥ) senses like ears, etc. (akṣaiḥ). I cannot control the mind which follows the senses which accept sense objects.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Being thus fallen, I am approaching your feet for shelter, O Lord, because although the impure can never attain your feet, I think it is nevertheless possible by your mercy. Only when one’s material life has ceased by serving your pure devotees, O lotus-naveled Lord, one develops bhakti to you.**

**Комментарий:**

“Then will you also like the ordinary jīvas of this world, remain opposed to the Lord?” Though I am of that nature (so ’ham), I approach your feet. “How can a person like you approach my feet?” O Lord! I think that I can attain your feet by your mercy. “This will happen by service to devotees.” When the jīva’s saṁsāra may be destroyed, then the mind may be fixed in you by association with your devotees (sad-upāsanayā). Bhaved and syāt are used in the sense of supposition. By association with Nārada, my mind has become fixed in you. I am thus successful.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances to the embodiment of pure knowledge, the source of all kinds of awareness, and the controller of Brahmā and other, the Brahman, the possessor of unlimited energies.**

**Комментарий:**

Falling at his feet, Akrūra prays. I offer respects to you, consciousness alone, from head to foot (vijñāna-mātrāya), to the cause of all types of knowledge (prayaya), since it will be said, tvatto jñānaṁ hi jīvānām: from you alone the knowledge of the living beings arises (SB [11.22.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/22.28)). To the controller (pradhānāya) of Brahmā and others (puruṣeśa), to the cause of this, Brahman, full of great qualities, to he who possesses unlimited śaktis (ananta-śaktaye).

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**O son of Vasudeva, obeisances to you, within whom all living beings reside. O Lord of the mind and senses, again I offer you my obeisances. O master, please protect me, who am surrendered unto you.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to you, the abode of all beings (sarva-bhūta-kṣayāya).

## Chapter 41 - Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma Enter Mathurā

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: While Akrūra was still offering prayers Kṛṣṇa withdrew his form that he had revealed in the water just as an actor winds up his performance.**

**Комментарий:**

In the forty-first chapter Kṛṣṇa kills the washerman and being pleased gives many gifts to Sudāmā, the weaver. Having shown his form as the Lord to Akrūra to dispel his doubts, Kṛṣṇa withdrew that form of power. An example is given to show its astonishing nature. He withdrew the form like an actor discards his role.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**When Akrūra saw the vision disappear, he came out of the water and quickly finished his various ritual duties. He then returned to the chariot, astonished.**

**Комментарий:**

He came out (unmajya) of the water.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa asked Akrūra: Have you seen something wonderful on the earth, in the sky or in the water? From your appearance, we think you have.**

**Комментарий:**

We think you have seen something astonishing.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra said: Whatever wonderful things the earth, sky or water contain, all exist in you. Since you encompass everything, when I am seeing you, what have I not seen?**

**Комментарий:**

Whatever astonishing objects exist on earth, water and air are in you. What is unseen by me who has seen you that way? I saw everything in you, the form of everything (viśvātmake).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**And now that I am seeing you, O Supreme Absolute Truth, in whom reside all amazing things on the earth, in the sky and in the water, what amazing things could I see in this world?**

**Комментарий:**

“But before meeting me your face was without astonishment. Thus whatever you saw astonishing on the earth, etc., describe that.” Seeing you, in whom (yatra) all astonishing things exist, what else can I see that is amazing on earth, etc.? Nothing, since except you nothing else is astonishing.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**With these words, Akrūra, the son of Gāndinī, began driving the chariot onward. At the end of the day he arrived in Mathurā with Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Gāndinī-sutaḥ is Akrūra.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Wherever they passed along the road, O King, the village people came forward and looked upon the two sons of Vasudeva with great pleasure. In fact, the villagers could not withdraw their eyes from them.**

**Комментарий:**

The village people, seeing the two sons of Vasudeva on the road, could not withdraw their eyes from them. Their eyes went with the boys.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja and the other residents of Vṛndāvana, having reached Mathurā ahead of the chariot, had stopped at a garden on the outskirts of the city to wait for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda and others waited (pratīkṣantaḥ) until Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma arrived.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**After joining Nanda and the others, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, the controller of the universe, took humble Akrūra’s hand in his own and, smiling, spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

He joined Nanda and others (tān). Kṛṣṇa spoke to Akrūra politely (praśritam).

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa said:\] Take the chariot and enter the city ahead of us. Then go home. After resting here a while, we will go to see the city.**

**Комментарий:**

Go with your chariot (sahayānaḥ). After resting (avamucya) here we will see the city.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra said: O master, without the two of you I shall not enter Mathurā. I am your devotee, O Lord, so it is not fair for you to abandon me, since you are always affectionate to your devotees.**

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Come, let us go to my house with your elder brother, the cowherd men and your companions. O best of friends, O transcendental Lord, in this way please grace my house with its master.**

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**I am simply an ordinary householder attached to ritual sacrifices, so please purify my home with the dust of your lotus feet. By your foot water, my forefathers, the sacrificial fires and the devatās will all become satisfied continually.**

**Комментарий:**

By the foot water (śaucena) which will remain in the yard of the house, the forefathers will be satisfied.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**By bathing your feet, the exalted Bali Mahārāja attained not only unequaled power but also the final goal of pure devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Avanijya means bathing. Ślokyaḥ means worthy of glorification.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**The water of the river Ganges has purified the three worlds, by having bathed your feet. Śiva accepted that water on his head, and by that water’s grace the sons of King Sagara attained heaven.**

**Комментарий:**

The water that washed your feet purified the three worlds. Śiva (śarvaḥ) put that water (yāḥ) on his head. By that water (yābhiḥ) the sons of Sagara attained Svarga (svar yātaḥ).

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**O Lord of lords, master of the universe, O You whose glories are most pious to hear and chant! O best of the Yadus, O whose fame is recounted in excellent poetry! O Supreme shelter of the jīvas! I offer you my obeisances.**

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: I will come to your house with my elder brother, but first I must satisfy my friends and well-wishers by killing the enemy of the Yadu clan.**

**Комментарий:**

First, killing Kaṁsa, I will give (vitariṣye) satisfaction (priyam) to my dear friends. Later I will come to your house.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus addressed by the Lord, Akrūra entered the city with a heavy heart. He informed King Kaṁsa of the success of his mission and then went home.**

**Комментарий:**

Seemingly sad (vimanā iva) without Kṛṣṇa, since his heart was attached to him, Akrūra entered the city. He was not actually sad because he was internally full of bliss from the Lord’s words. Informing Kaṁsa that he had brought Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma (karma āvedya), he went to his house to prepare it for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa desired to see Mathurā, so toward evening he took Lord Balarāma and the cowherd boys with him and entered the city.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa went into the city surrounded by (parivāritaḥ) his friends.

### Text 20-23

**Перевод:**

**The Lord saw Mathurā, with its tall gates and household entrances made of crystal, its immense archways and main doors of gold, its granaries and other storehouses of copper and brass, and its impregnable moats. Beautifying the city were pleasant gardens and parks. The main intersections were fashioned of gold, and there were mansions with private pleasure gardens, along with guildhalls and many other buildings. Mathurā resounded with the calls of peacocks and pet turtledoves, which sat in the small openings of the lattice windows and on the gem-studded floors, and also on the columned balconies and on the ornate rafters in front of the houses. These balconies and rafters were adorned with vaidurya stones, diamonds, crystal quartz, sapphires, coral, pearls and emeralds. All the royal avenues and commercial streets were sprinkled with water, as were the side roads and courtyards, and flower garlands, newly grown sprouts, parched grains and rice had been scattered about everywhere. Gracing the houses’ doorways were elaborately decorated pots filled with water, which were bedecked with mango leaves, smeared with yogurt and sandalwood paste, and encircled by flower petals and ribbons. Near the pots were flags, rows of lamps, bunches of flowers and the trunks of banana and betel-nut trees.**

**Комментарий:**

The city is described in four verses. He saw Mathurā with city and house gates made of crystal, with huge road arches and doors made of gold, with grain storerooms made of brass and copper, with insurmountable moats, consisting of the Yamunā on the east and north sides, beautified with gardens situated far away and groves within the city. Or the city had walls (koṣṭhā) made of copper and brass and the city was beautiful with gardens and attractive groves. The order is gardens, groves, moat, walls, city gates and other gates, and golden doors. It had intersections (śṛṅgāṭaka), wealthy persons’ houses (harmya), and house gardens (niṣkutaiḥ) all made of gold. It was beautiful with the resting halls of different types of craftsmen and other halls. The roof ridges were made of vaidurya, diamond, crystal, sapphire, coral, pearls and emeralds. The city resounded with cries of peacocks and doves perched on houses having roof ridges, lattice work holes, floor inlaid with jewels. The city had main roads, markets, side roads and yards sprinkled with fragrant water. The city was decorated with garlands, sprouts, popped rice and white rice. Understanding that their two Lords had come, the citizens, unafraid of Kaṁsa, decorated the city. The city had houses whose doors were well decorated with full water pots anointed with yogurt, sandalwood and musk, with bunches of flowers and lamps and fresh mango leaves, banana trees and betel nut, with flags, banners and strips of cloth. The manner of arrangement was as follows. On either sides of the door there were pots sitting on piles of white rice. Around the pots were flower clusters. On the throat of the pots were cloth strips. On the mouth of the pots were mango leaves. On top were groups of lamps on different leaves. Nearby were fruiting banana trees, betel nut trees, flags and arches.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**The women of Mathurā hurriedly assembled and went forth to see the two sons of Vasudeva as they entered the city on the King’s road, surrounded by their cowherd boyfriends. Some of the women, my dear King, eagerly climbed to the roofs of their houses to see them.**

**Комментарий:**

The city women approached to see the two sons of Vasudeva who had entered the city on the main road (naradeva-vartmanā).

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Some of the ladies put their clothes and ornaments on backwards or forgot one piece, others forgot one of their earrings or ankle bells, and others applied makeup to one eye but not the other.**

**Комментарий:**

The women’s eagerness is described in two verses. Their clothing and ornaments were put on in opposite manner. Others forgot to wear one bangle or earring and came. They put on one ear ornament or one anklet. Others put collyrium on one eye only and came.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Those who were taking their meals abandoned them, others went out without finishing their baths or massages, women who were sleeping at once rose when they heard the commotion, and mothers breast-feeding their infants simply put them aside.**

**Комментарий:**

Some, eating alone, gave up eating. Others, having their bodies oiled by maidservants came without bathing. Others rose from sleep on hearing the commotion of the lord coming (niḥsvanam). Mothers gave up (apohya) feeding their infants.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**The lotus-eyed Lord, walking with the gait of a lordly elephant in rut, creating joy for their eyes with his body, which is the source of pleasure for the divine goddess of fortune, captivated those ladies’ minds with playful, bold, smiling glances.**

**Комментарий:**

Then what happened? Lotus eyed Kṛṣṇa attracted their minds by his bold pastimes and smiling glances. He gave joy to the eyes by his beautiful form (śrī-ramaṇātmanotsavam).

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**The ladies of Mathurā had repeatedly heard about Kṛṣṇa, and thus as soon as they saw him their hearts melted. They felt honored that he was sprinkling upon them the nectar of his glances and attractive smiles. Taking him into their hearts through their eyes, they embraced him, the embodiment of all ecstasy, and as their bodily hairs stood on end, O subduer of enemies, they forgot the unlimited distress caused by his absence.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing suddenly the person of whom they had constantly heard previously, the city women, their hearts melted (anudruta), who received respect from him being sprinkled by the nectar of his glances and smiles, embraced that form of bliss, attained in their hearts through their eyes. If their eyes were filled with tears, or they closed them from shyness or fainting, they were still able to embrace him directly since he appeared in their minds as a sphūrti. They gave up the pain in their hearts by seeing him. O Parikṣit (arindama)!

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Their lotus faces blooming with affection, the ladies who had climbed to the roofs of the mansions rained down showers of flowers upon Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

They sprinkled him with flowers (saumanasyaiḥ).

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Brāhmaṇas standing along the way honored the two Lords with presentations of yogurt, unbroken barleycorns, pots full of water, garlands, fragrant substances such as sandalwood paste, and other items of worship.**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇas, unafraid of Kaṁsa, worshipped him with yogurt and other items. “He will kill Kaṁsa.”

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The women of Mathurā exclaimed: Oh, what severe austerities the gopīs must have performed to be able to see continually Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, who are the greatest source of pleasure for all mankind!**

**Комментарий:**

Paurāḥ refers to the women of Mathurā. Paurāḥ instead of pauryaḥ is poetic license.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Seeing a washer man approaching who had been dyeing some clothes, Kṛṣṇa asked him for the finest laundered garments he had.**

**Комментарий:**

Raṅga-kāra is a washerman who washes new cloths and dyes them.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa said:\] Please give suitable garments to the two of us, who certainly deserve them. If you grant this charity, you will undoubtedly receive the greatest benefit.**

**Комментарий:**

O washerman (aṅga)! Please give both of us suitable clothing. We are qualified to wear them. There will be great benefit for you, the giver of the clothing.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Thus requested by the Supreme Lord, who is perfectly complete in all respects, that arrogant servant of the King became angry and replied insultingly.**

**Комментарий:**

Requested by the Lord who was complete in all ways, who did this just to please his friends and to instill fear in Kaṁsa, the washerman became angry.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**\[The washer man said:\] You impudent boys! You’re accustomed to roaming the mountains and forests, and yet you would dare put on such clothes as these! You desire the king’s possessions.**

**Комментарий:**

O arrogant boys (udvṛttā)! You wanderers in the forests and mountains, would wear such clothing! Imperative (paridhatta) is used to express supposition. Do you desire the king’s items? He says this because of his demonic nature. But actually by being complete in all respects due to the statement, śyāmaṁ hiraṇya-paridhim: Kṛṣṇa’s complexion was dark blue and his belt was golden (SB [10.23.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/23.22)), his clothing was excellent in all respects. Thus, Sarasvatī devī speaks: O boys having excellent pastimes (udvṛttāḥ)! Wandering in the forests of Govardhana eternally why would you wear such clothing. Rather you would wear something much superior to this. Do you desire the king’s cloth? Of course not. You are asking for this cloth as a trick.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Fools, get out of here quickly! Don’t beg like this if you want to stay alive. When someone is too bold, the king’s men arrest him and kill him and take all his property.**

**Комментарий:**

O fools! Go from here. If you want to live, do not ask like this. The king’s men will plunder such a proud person, taking his property. But Sarasvatī devī speaks as follows. Oh those who have understood my nature of fickleness (yātāśu bāliśā)! If you desire to show strength, then you should not ask like this. The verb jīv means bearing strength and life airs. “How can warriors test their strength on a washer man?” Persons like you, coming in a royal family, tie up persons filled with pride.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**As the washer man thus spoke brazenly, the son of Devakī became angry, and then with the tip of his hand he separated the man’s head from his body.**

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**The washer man’s assistants all dropped their bundles of clothes and fled down the road, scattering in all directions. Kṛṣṇa, remaining at that place, then took the clothes.**

**Комментарий:**

They dropped their bags of clothing (vāsaḥ-kośān).

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma put on pairs of garments that especially pleased them, and then Kṛṣṇa distributed the remaining clothes among the cowherd boys, leaving some scattered on the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

They each put on two pieces of cloth (vastre), upper and lower. Scattering on the ground other pieces not regarded as clothing, they gave the remainder to the cowherds.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Thereupon a tailor came forward and, feeling affection for the Lords, nicely adorned their attire with cloth ornaments of various colors.**

**Комментарий:**

The tailor with his assistants quickly made attire using cloth ornaments suitable to the boys.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma looked resplendent, each in his own unique, wonderfully ornamented outfit. They resembled a pair of young elephants, one white and the other dark, decorated for a festive occasion.**

**Комментарий:**

They were like two young elephants, crystal white and sapphire blue, at a festival.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Pleased with the weaver, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa gave him a form like the Lord’s, and that while in this world he enjoyed supreme affluence, physical strength, influence, memory and sensory vigor.**

**Комментарий:**

He gave him immediately a form similar to his own, as in the case of Kubjā in this life (loke) as well as great wealth (śriyaṁ), strength of body (bala), power, memory of the Lord at all times (smṛti) and sharpness of senses (indriyaṁ).

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**The two Lords then went to the house of the garland-maker Sudāmā. When Sudāmā saw them he at once stood up and then bowed down, placing his head on the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the two, Sudāmā fell on the ground and offered respects with his head.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**After offering them seats and bathing their feet, Sudāmā worshiped them and their companions with arghya, garlands, betel, sandalwood paste and other presentations.**

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**\[Sudāmā said:\] O Lord, now that you both have come here my birth is now sanctified and my family free of contamination, my forefathers, the devatās and the great sages are certainly all satisfied with me.**

**Комментарий:**

My birth is successful by your (vām) coming and my family is purified. Forefathers, etc., are pleased with me.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**You two Lords are the ultimate cause of this entire universe. To bestow sustenance and prosperity upon this realm, you have descended with your plenary expansions.**

**Комментарий:**

You are the final cause of the whole (viśvasya) universe (jagataḥ). You have appeared in Mathurā area (iha) with the cowherds and Yadus (aṁśena) for protection (kṣemāya) and prosperity (bhavāya).

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**Because you are the well-wishing friends and Supreme Soul of the whole universe, you regard all with unbiased vision. Therefore, although you reciprocate your devotees’ loving worship, you always remain equally disposed toward all living beings.**

**Комментарий:**

You do not have distorted vision like the jīvas, either by killing the washerman or by rewarding the tailor, since you are benefactors (suhṛdoḥ) and are antaryāmīs of the universe. Thus like a desire tree, you both respond equally to all different types of beings who worship you.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**Please order me, your servant, to do whatever you wish. To be engaged by you in some service is certainly a great blessing for anyone.**

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] O best of kings, having spoken these words, Sudāmā could understand what Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma wanted. Thus with great pleasure he presented them with garlands of fresh, fragrant flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

Speaking in this way, Sudāmā understanding that they needed garlands after putting on their clothing, gave the two boys garlands.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**Beautifully adorned with these garlands, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were delighted, and so were their companions. The two Lords then offered the surrendered Sudāmā, who was bowing down before them, whatever benedictions he desired.**

**Комментарий:**

Tābhiḥ means “with the garlands.”

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**Sudāmā chose unshakable devotion for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul of all existence; friendship with his devotees; and compassion for all living beings.**

**Комментарий:**

He chose bhakti to the antaryāmī of all beings (akhilātmani).

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**Not only did Kṛṣṇa grant Sudāmā these benedictions, but he also awarded him strength, long life, fame, beauty and ever-increasing prosperity for his family. Then Kṛṣṇa and his elder brother took their leave.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa gave him prosperity of his family (anvaya-vardhinīm).

## Chapter 42 - The Breaking of the Sacrificial Bow

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: As he walked down the King’s road, Mādhava then saw a young hunchback woman with an attractive face, who carried a tray of fragrant ointments as she walked along. The bestower of the ecstasy of love smiled and inquired from her as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

In the forty-second chapter Kṛṣṇa straightens Kubjā, breaks the bow and destroys the protectors of the arena, Kaṁsa sees bad omens and the festivity of the arena is described. Kubjā was holding containers of sandalwood, etc. Kṛṣṇa, who offers happiness (rasa-pradaḥ), saw her. She was the daughter of a vaiśya, a minister of Kaṁsa. Requested by Kaṁsa she was engaged in preparing sandalwood, etc. In previous birth she was the daughter of a king, a devotee of the Lord by the mercy of Nārada. She became a hunch back in order to be touched by the Lord.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa said:\] Who are you, O beautiful-thighed one? Ah, ointment! Who is it for, my dear lady? Please tell us truthfully. Give us both some of your finest ointment and you will soon gain a great boon.**

**Комментарий:**

O beautiful woman with beautiful thighs! He referred to her as one with auspicious limbs in a joking manner and asked: Who are you? Who is the ointment for? Please tell us. U ha are particles indicating conjecture, with intentional moving of his brow. Let it be for anyone, still give it to us. Service to us gives results immediately.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**The maidservant replied: O handsome one, I am a servant of King Kaṁsa, who respects me highly for the ointments I make. My name is Trivakrā. Who else but you two deserve my ointments, which the lord of the Bhojas likes so much?**

**Комментарий:**

O beautiful one! I am called Trivakrā, due to being bent at the neck, chest and waist. I am a servant much respected by Kaṁsa, engaged in ointments. Or saying, “I am your servant,” she answers the latter question (who is the ointment for) with “Kaṁsa.” She calls him “beautiful” in order to reveal that she is attracted to him. Showing the result she says, “Except for you two, who deserves these ointments.”

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Her mind overwhelmed by Kṛṣṇa’s beauty, charm, sweetness, smiles, words and glances, Trivakrā gave both Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma generous amounts of ointment.**

**Комментарий:**

Her heart was overwhelmed (dharṣitātmā) by his beauty characterized by proper placement of limbs (rūpa), his youthfulness (peśala), his smile, his speech and glances, since bhāva manifests in the heart. She gave the ointments to the two, who were qualified, by the Lord’s desire. She gave the ointments to their hands. Viṣṇu Purāṇa says: śrutvā tam āha sā kṛṣṇaṁ gṛhyatām iti sādaram anulepanaṁ pradadau gātra-yogyam athobhayoḥ Hearing this, she respectfully replied to Lord Kṛṣṇa, ‘Please take it,’ and gave both of them ointment suitable for applying to their bodies. Sāndram means thick.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Anointed with these most excellent cosmetics, which adorned them with hues that contrasted with their complexions, the two Lords appeared extremely beautiful.**

**Комментарий:**

Anointed with the ointments which they applied above the waist (para-bhāgena), or by which they became extremely beautiful (parabhāga) with colors of black and yellow, different from their white and blue complexions, made into attractive patterns, they appeared beautiful. Their friends anointed them on their cheeks, chest and arms.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Since Kṛṣṇa was pleased with Trivakrā, he decided to straighten that hunchbacked girl with the lovely face just to demonstrate the immediate result of seeing him.**

**Комментарий:**

Pleased, he showed the immediate result of seeing him. He decided to make her straight.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Pressing down on her toes with both his feet, Kṛṣṇa placed two upward-pointing fingers under her chin and straightened up her body.**

**Комментарий:**

Pressing the tips of her feet with his two feet, with his right hand, using the stretched out forefinger and middle finger he grasped her chin, supporting her back with his left hand and made her body (adhyātmam) straight (udanīnamat).

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Simply by the touch of Kṛṣṇa, who awards liberation easily, Trivakrā was suddenly transformed into an exquisitely beautiful woman with straight, evenly proportioned limbs and large hips and breasts.**

**Комментарий:**

She at that moment became a beautiful woman. All her limbs became normal. The main cause was his touch and pulling her up by the chin was just an amusement. He who just by remembering removes saṁsāra and even gives a form equal to himself, then how much more can he give by touching a person?

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Now endowed with beauty, character and generosity, Trivakrā began to feel desire for Keśava. Taking hold of the end of his upper cloth, she smiled and addressed him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

She developed amorous desire (jāta-hṛc-chayaḥ).

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**\[Trivakrā said:\] Come, O hero, let us go to my house. I cannot bear to leave you here. O best of males, please take pity on me, since you have agitated my mind.**

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Thus entreated by the woman, Kṛṣṇa first glanced at the face of Balarāma, who was watching the incident, and then at the faces of the cowherd boys. Then with a laugh Kṛṣṇa replied to her as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Being entreated by the women full of desire while Balarāma and his friends watched, Kṛṣṇa looked at the faces of Balarāma and his friends and then laughing loudly in amusement and spoke to her with secret intention.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa said:\] O lady with beautiful eyebrows, as soon as I fulfill my purpose I will certainly visit your house, where men can relieve their anxiety. Indeed, you are the best refuge for us homeless travelers.**

**Комментарий:**

Your house relieves men of their mental pain (ādhi-vikarṣaṇam). But my objective should be accomplished (sādhita-arthaḥ): killing Kaṁsa for my friends. You are the shelter for travellers having no wives (agṛhāṇām). He uses the plural to fool those present.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Leaving her with these sweet words, Kṛṣṇa walked further down the road. The merchants along the way worshiped him and his elder brother by presenting them with various respectful offerings, including betel nut, garlands and fragrant substances.**

**Комментарий:**

With sweet words Kṛṣṇa left her, sending her home and walking on the main road, he was worshipped by merchants with garlands of jewels and pearls and sandalwood, etc. He was with Balarāma and others.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**The sight of Kṛṣṇa aroused Cupid in the hearts of the city women. Thus agitated, they forgot themselves. Their clothes, braids and bangles became disheveled, and they stood as still as figures in a painting.**

**Комментарий:**

The women’s bodies were like painted pictures.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then asked the local people the location of the arena where the bow sacrifice would take place. When he went there he saw the amazing bow, which resembled Indra’s bow.**

**Комментарий:**

He asked about the place of the bow sacrifice. It was like Indra’s bow (rainbow) because it was colorful with imbedded gems and huge. Thus it was astonishing.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**That most valuable bow was guarded by a large company of men, who were respectfully worshiping it. Kṛṣṇa pushed his way forward and, despite the guards’ attempts to stop him, picked it up.**

**Комментарий:**

He picked it up with force (prasahya).

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Easily lifting the bow with his left hand, Kṛṣṇa strung it in a fraction of a second as the king’s guards looked on. He then powerfully pulled the string and snapped the bow in half, just as an excited elephant might break a stalk of sugar cane.**

**Комментарий:**

He broke the bow in a blink of an eye, like an elephant breaking sugar cane.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**The sound of the bow’s breaking filled the earth and sky in all directions. Upon hearing it, Kaṁsa was struck with terror.**

**Комментарий:**

Then the sound spread to Svarga and earth (rodasī).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**The enraged guards then took up their weapons and, wanting to seize Kṛṣṇa and his companions, surrounded them and shouted, “Seize them! Imprison them!”**

**Комментарий:**

The guards, with weapons in their hands (ātatāyinaḥ), saying “Seize them, imprison them!” surrounded Kṛṣṇa. Seize him to offer him to Kaṁsa. Catch them alive. Then imprison them. Bind them with chains. These were the statements of the wrestlers. But Sarasvatī devī says, “Persons like us should be seized and imprisoned.”

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the guards coming upon them with evil intent, angry Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa took up the two halves of the bow and began striking them down.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing their wicked intentions, the two, in anger, taking up the broken bow, beat them.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**After killing a contingent of soldiers sent by Kaṁsa, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma left the sacrificial arena by its main gate, and became joyful on seeing the wealth of the city and continued to walk about.**

**Комментарий:**

Killing the soldiers (balam) sent by Kaṁsa or defeating the ability (balam) of Kaṁsa, they left from the gate of the arena and, seeing the wealth of the city, became joyful, and then wandered about casually in the city again.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Having witnessed the amazing deed Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma had performed, and seeing their strength, boldness and beauty, the people of the city thought they must be the best of devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing their ability to defeat all (tejaḥ), their vigor (prāgalbhyam) and their astonishing beauty (rūpam), the people thought they were the best of all devatās.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**As they strolled about at will, the sun began to set, so they left the city with the cowherd boys and returned to the cowherds’ wagon encampment.**

**Комментарий:**

The sun began to set — the idea is that it was unable to tolerate Kṛṣṇa’s prowess manifested at that time. Having said that they would see the rest in the morning, they left the town (purāt) and went to the camp where the carts were parked.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**At the time of Mukunda’s departure from Vṛndāvana, the gopīs had foretold that the residents of Mathurā would enjoy many benedictions, and now the gopīs’ predictions were coming true, for those residents were gazing upon the beauty of Kṛṣṇa, the jewel among men. The goddess of fortune desired the shelter of that beauty so much that she abandoned many others, although they worshiped her.**

**Комментарий:**

When Kṛṣṇa left Vraja, the blessings which the gopīs, pained in separation, spoke of in verses such as SB [10.39.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/39.23)—the objects which they desired that amorous women of Mathurā should definitely obtain—that had now come true in Mathurā for its residents who were seeing the beauty of the limbs of the ornament among men. The verb śās means to desire. The beauty is described. Giving up Brahmā and others who worship her, Lakṣmī desired to take shelter of that beauty.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**After Kṛṣṇa’s and Balarāma’s feet were bathed, the two Lords ate rice with milk. Then, although knowing what Kaṁsa intended to do, they spent the night there comfortably.**

**Комментарий:**

Having had their feet washed by servants, they ate rice mixed with milk and passed the night comfortably. Though knowing from the people that Kaṁsa desired to arrange for the wrestling match, they did not worry about his killing.

### Text 26-27

**Перевод:**

**Wicked King Kaṁsa, on the other hand, was terrified, having heard how Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma had broken the bow and killed his guards and soldiers, all simply as a game. He remained awake for a long time, and both while awake and while dreaming he saw many bad omens, messengers of death.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma breaking the bow was just their play. It was not a show of their prowess. In waking and dreaming (ubhayathā), Kaṁsa saw omens indicating death.

### Text 28-31

**Перевод:**

**When he looked at his reflection he could not see his head; for no reason the moon and stars appeared double; he saw a hole in his shadow; he could not hear the sound of his life air; trees seemed covered with a golden hue; and he could not see his footprints. He dreamt that he was being embraced by ghosts, riding a donkey and drinking poison, and also that a naked man smeared with oil was passing by wearing a garland of nalada flowers. Seeing these and other such omens both while dreaming and while awake, Kaṁsa was terrified by the prospect of death, and out of anxiety he could not sleep.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses describe what he saw. Though seeing his reflection in a mirror, he did not see his head. He saw double moons and stars in the absence of any obstruction to the eye (such as a finger). He saw his shadow with a hole in it. He could not hear the sound of his prāṇas (prāna-ghoṣā) when covering his ears with his palms. Trees appeared golden. He could not see his footprints in the dust and mud. These were the bad omens while awake. Omens in his dreams are described. He was embraced by ghosts. He rode a donkey. He drank poison. He saw a naked man smeared with oil was passing by wearing a garland of japā flowers. He did not get sleep.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**When the night had finally passed and the sun rose up again from the water, Kaṁsa set about arranging for the grand wrestling festival.**

**Комментарий:**

When night passed somehow with difficulty, when the sun rose from the water (adbhyaḥ), he arranged the festival, the means of his death. The mention of the sun rising from water is conventional explanation as mentioned in śruti, adbhyo vā eṣa prātar udeti apaḥ sāyaṁ praviśati: the sun rises from the water in the morning and enters it at night. (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa) In order to show his foolishness in arranging the means of his own death, Śukadeva calls out to Parīkṣit (kauravya).

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**The king’s men performed the ritual worship of the wrestling arena, sounded their drums and other instruments and decorated the viewing galleries with garlands, flags and arches made of cloth.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa’s servants decorated (ānarcuḥ) the wrestling arena (raṅgam) by placing auspicious pots, etc.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**The city-dwellers and residents of the outlying districts, led by brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas, came and sat down comfortably in the galleries. The royal guests received special seats.**

**Комментарий:**

They sat as they liked (yathopajoṣam).

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Surrounded by his ministers, Kaṁsa took his seat on the imperial dais. But even as he sat amidst his various provincial rulers, his heart trembled.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa sat in his gallery, which was very high, with burning (vidūyatā) heart.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**While the musical instruments loudly played and the wrestlers kept the rhythm by slapping their arms, the lavishly ornamented wrestlers proudly entered the arena with their coaches and sat down.**

**Комментарий:**

The wrestlers sat with their coaches (sopādyāyāḥ) amidst the drum playing in which was heard the loud slapping of the wrestlers’ arms.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Enthused by the pleasing music, Cāṇūra, Muṣṭika, Kūṭa, Śala and Tośala sat down on the wrestling mat.**

**Комментарий:**

The wrestlers are described. They came to the arena (upasthānam). Upasthānam means the arena due to the etymology, upatiṣṭhanti ārādhayanti kaṁsam atra: the place where they worshipped Kaṁsa.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja and the other cowherds, summoned by the King of the Bhojas, presented him with their offerings and then took their seats in one of the galleries.**

**Комментарий:**

Called by Kaṁsa, Nanda, presenting his offerings, became situated in a gallery on his order.

## Chapter 43 - Kṛṣṇa Kills the Elephant Kuvalayāpīḍa

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O chastiser of enemies, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, having executed all necessary purification, then heard the kettledrums resounding at the wrestling arena, and they went there to see what was happening.**

**Комментарий:**

In the forty-third chapter, after killing the excellent elephant at the gate, the two brothers entered the arena and spoke to Cāṇūra. The two purified themselves. Though showing our powers by breaking the bow, if he does not free our parents and desires to kill us both then though he is our uncle there is no fault in killing, for he afflicts devatās and brāhmaṇas. They took bath to cancel any fault. Hearing the sounds of the drums and wrestlers, they went into the arena on the pretext of seeing.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa reached the entrance to the arena, he saw the elephant Kuvalayāpīḍa blocking his way at the urging of his keeper.**

**Комментарий:**

The elephant was goaded by its keeper (ambaṣṭha).

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Securely binding up his sash and tying back his curly locks, Kṛṣṇa addressed the elephant-keeper with words as grave as the rumbling of a cloud.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking off his jacket, he bound a sash around his dhoti and put on a long garland over his shoulders as an upper garment. This is the meaning since his garland will be described in verse 19. Though his naturally curly long hair had been tucked beneath a turban, fearing that they would be scattered while wrestling, he bound his locks tightly with his upper cloth as well.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa said:\] O driver, move aside at once and let us pass! If you don’t, this very day I will send both you and your elephant to the abode of Yamarāja!**

**Комментарий:**

O elephant driver! Give us a path. Move off the road immediately (apakrama). If you do not, I will take you to the abode of death today. I will kill you.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Thus threatened, the elephant-keeper became angry. He goaded his furious elephant, who appeared equal to time, death and Yamarāja, into attacking Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

He goaded his elephant, angry because of the goad, who was comparable to the cause of death (kāla), death (antaka), and the killer (yama).

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**The lord of the elephants charged Kṛṣṇa and violently seized him with his trunk. But Kṛṣṇa slipped away, struck him a blow and disappeared from his view among his legs.**

**Комментарий:**

The elephant seized Kṛṣṇa by his trunk. Kṛṣṇa, escaping from the trunk, struck the elephant with his fist and disappeared between his legs.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Infuriated at being unable to see Keśava, the elephant sought him out with his sense of smell. Once again Kuvalayāpīḍa seized him with the end of his trunk, only to have the Lord forcefully free himself.**

**Комментарий:**

Not seeing Kṛṣṇa, the elephant used his nose to smell him. It is well known that animals not seeing with the eyes, can know by smell. Though not seeing Kṛṣṇa, the elephant grasped him with the tip of his trunk. Kṛṣṇa forcibly escaped.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then grabbed the powerful Kuvalayāpīḍa by the tail and playfully dragged him twenty-five bow-lengths as easily as Garuḍa might drag a snake.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa grabbed the elephant by his tail and pulled him twenty-five bow-lengths just as Garuḍa drags a snake.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**As Kṛṣṇa held on to the elephant’s tail, the animal tried to twist away to the left and to the right, making the Lord swerve in the opposite direction, as a young boy would swerve when pulling a calf by the tail.**

**Комментарий:**

To catch Kṛṣṇa, who was holding his tail, if the elephant turned to the right, it made Kṛṣṇa go to the left just as a boy holding a calf’s tail whirls around with a whirling calf.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then came face to face with the elephant, slapped him and chased him. Touched by the elephant, Kṛṣṇa made him trip and fall.**

**Комментарий:**

He hit the elephant with his hand. Running in all directions he made it fall. He ran by fooling it in such a way that it would fall.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**As Kṛṣṇa dodged about, he playfully fell on the ground and quickly got up again. The raging elephant, thinking Kṛṣṇa was down, tried to gore him with his tusks but struck the earth instead.**

**Комментарий:**

Running about Kṛṣṇa fell on the earth for fun and immediately got up. Thinking he was down on the ground the angry elephant struck the earth with his tusks.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**His prowess foiled, the lordly elephant Kuvalayāpīḍa went into a frenzied rage out of frustration. But the elephant-keepers goaded him on, and he furiously charged Kṛṣṇa once again.**

**Комментарий:**

Mahāmātraiḥ means by the elephant trainers.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord, killer of the demon Madhu, confronted the elephant as he attacked. Seizing his trunk with one hand, Kṛṣṇa threw him to the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

Hastam means the tip of the trunk.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then climbed onto the elephant with the ease of a mighty lion, pulled out a tusk, and with it killed the beast and his keepers.**

**Комментарий:**

He beat the elephant with the tusk (tena).

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Leaving the dead elephant aside, Kṛṣṇa held on to the tusk and entered the wrestling arena. With the tusk resting on his shoulder, drops of the elephant’s blood and sweat sprinkled all over him, and his lotus face covered with fine drops of his own perspiration, the Lord shone with great beauty.**

**Комментарий:**

He entered the arena. Beautiful in revealing his prowess, he shone.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, Baladeva and Kṛṣṇa, each carrying one of the elephant’s tusks as his chosen weapon, entered the arena with several cowherd boys.**

**Комментарий:**

The two boys, surrounded by a few greatly valorous cowherd friends, entered the arena. The elders were already in the galleries. The two boys held excellent weapons in the form of elephant tusks.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**The various groups of people in the arena regarded Kṛṣṇa in different ways when he entered it with his elder brother. The wrestlers saw Kṛṣṇa as a lightning bolt, the men of Mathurā as the best of males, the women as Cupid in person, the cowherd men as their relative, the impious rulers as a chastiser, his parents as their child, the King of the Bhojas as death, the unintelligent as the Supreme Lord’s universal form, the yogīs as the Absolute Truth and the Vṛṣṇis as their supreme worshipable Deity.**

**Комментарий:**

Due to the acintya-śakti, the Lord manifested as the viṣaya of all rasas for the various spectators in the arena. Known in twelve forms such as lightning bolt for the spectators of ten types starting with the wrestlers, Kṛṣṇa entered the arena with his brother. This is the alaṅkāra called ullekha since its mark is — bahubhir bahudhollekhād ullekhaḥ syād alaṅkṛtiḥ: due to many descriptions of an object by many people the alaṅkāra is called ullekha. Though he was a young boy, etc., with tender skin he appeared like a thunderbolt, etc., to the wrestlers and others. This was caused by his krūra (ferocity) and other śaktis. This will be explained in the verse jayati jana-nivāsa (SB [10.90.48](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/90.48)). The wrestlers showed raudra-rasa whose sthāyī-bhāva is krodha (anger) because for the wrestlers, who were proud due to their prowess, Kṛṣṇa, though previously disrespected, manifested limbs similar to thunderbolts and entered the arena disregarding the opposition like thunderbolt. The people of the city, who were different from those who hated him and who were different from those who were related to him, by seeing his astonishing actions showed adbhuta-rasa whose sthāyībhāva is vismaya (astonishment). The women, other than the elders, due to Kṛṣṇa’s manifestation as Cupid showed śṛṅgāra-rasa whose sthāyī-bhāva is rati (amorous love) filled with the mood of a lover. The cowherds like Śrīdāmā and Subala thought of him as a friend and relative (sva-jana). They had sakhya-rasa whose sthāyī-bhāva is maitrī (friendship). Seeing him dressed with drops of blood from the elephant tusk, with unrestricted hearts, they showed hāsyarasa whose sthāyī-bhāva is hāsa (laughter). The demonic kings (asatām) favoring Kaṁsa saw him as a punisher, due to seeing his great valor. They had vīra-rasa whose sthāyī-bhāva is utsāha (fortitude). Nanda and Vasudeva saw him as a baby. This was vatsala-rasa whose sthāyī-bhāva is vātsalya (parental affection). Due to manifestation of his infancy, by understanding his tenderness and worrying about the cruelty of the wrestlers, they showed karuṇa-rasa whose sthāyībhāva is śoka (anguish). Kaṁsa saw him as the cause of his death. He had bhayānaka-rasa whose sthāyī-bhāva is bhaya (fear). The ignorant priests of Kaṁsa saw him as material (virāḍ), though the learned see him as a form full of consciousness and bliss. Due to concluding him to be material by thinking of him as imperfect in body, they showed bibhatsa-rasa whose sthāyī-bhāva is jugupsā (disgust). Yogīs situated in the heavenly sky, who possess tattvajñāna saw him as the supreme tattva. They had śānta-rasa whose sthāyī-bhāva is śānta (tranquility). The Vṛṣnis saw him as the most worshippable supreme devatā. They had dāsya-rasa whose sthāyībhāva is bhakti. There is this verse: There are twelve rasas listed: raudra, adbhuta, śṛṅgāra (śuciḥ), hāsya with sakhya, vīra, karuṇa with vatsala, bhayānaka, bībhatsa, śānta and dāsya. This is Śukadeva’s conclusion. According to Bharata Muni there are nine rasas in the order described, but the last one (śānta) is described as bhāva. There is this verse: The rasas are raudra, adbhuta, śṛṅgāra, hāsya, vīra, karuṇa, bhāyanaka, bībhatsa and the ninth, śānta is a bhāva. But the description of rasas in the commentary is according to the order in the above verse though the various elevated and low people saw him at that time in the order as given in the main verse. Śānta, dāsya, sakhya, vatsala and śṛṅgāra are the five principal rasas. But the seven rasas, adbhuta and others, which appear in the devotees are secondary since they are equal to sañcārī-bhāvas. In this way Kṛṣṇa is the embodiment of the twelve rasas. This is stated by the śrutis, raso vai saḥ rasaṁ hy evāyaṁ labdhānandī bhavatī: the Lord is rasa and a jīva, attaining rasa becomes blissful. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**When Kaṁsa saw that Kuvalayāpīḍa was dead and the two brothers were invincible, he was overwhelmed with anxiety, though he was a hero, O King.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he was a hero (manasvī), Kaṁsa was frightened (udvivije) on seeing Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma (tau).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Arrayed with variegated ornaments, garlands and garments, just like a pair of excellently costumed actors, the two mighty-armed Lords shone splendidly in the arena, agitating the minds of all onlookers with their beauty.**

**Комментарий:**

Yathā naṭau (like actors) denotes that they were unafraid. They agitated (kṣipantau) the minds of the spectators.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**O King, as the citizens of the city and the people from outlying districts gazed upon those two lords from their seats in the galleries, the force of the people’s happiness caused their eyes to open wide and their faces to blossom. They drank in the vision of the Lords’ faces without becoming satiated.**

**Комментарий:**

Their faces blossomed and eyes opened wide because of the extreme joy. They were not satisfied when they drank their face with their eyes. They saw them with unblinking eyes, with respect.

### Text 21-22

**Перевод:**

**The people seemed to be drinking Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma with their eyes, licking them with their tongues, smelling them with their nostrils and embracing them with their arms. Reminded of the Lords’ beauty, character, charm and bravery, the members of the audience began describing these features to one another according to what they had seen and heard.**

**Комментарий:**

Their lack of full satisfaction is described. Two verses go together. The word iva indicates a comparison. They seemed to drink the two boys with their wide open eyes. They seemed to lick them with their tongues, by describing their sweetness. They seemed to inhale them through their nostrils by facing them and by opening their nostrils wide out of greed for their fragrance. By waving their hands in order to mutually see them (i.e. they were trying to grab the attention of the two), they seemed to embrace them with their arms. They became absorbed in them by their external and internal senses. They spoke about what they had seen such as killing the elephant and what they had heard, such as his lifting Govardhana, etc. They spoke only according to that without going beyond what they saw and heard (i.e. they did not speculate). They seemed to be remembering their forms with them carrying the elephant tusks, etc., which were directly visible, their qualities such as beauty and others, their sweetness such as their smiles and talks and their boldness. Forgetting their own behaviour, they loudly discussed these.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**\[The people said:\] These two boys are certainly expansions of the Supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa who have descended to this world in the home of Vasudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

The statements of persons who were astonished are described in eight verses. They speak according to their perception (and not according to the truth).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**This one \[Kṛṣṇa\] took birth from mother Devakī and was brought to Gokula, where he has remained concealed all this time, growing up in the house of Nanda.**

**Комментарий:**

In this verse they repeat what was heard from Nārada.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**He made Pūtanā and the whirlwind demon meet with death, pulled down the twin Arjuna trees and killed Śaṅkhacūḍa, Keśī, Dhenuka and similar demons.**

**Комментарий:**

Guhyakaḥ means Śaṅkhacūḍa.

### Text 26-27

**Перевод:**

**He saved the cows and the cowherds from a forest fire and subdued the serpent Kāliya. He removed Indra’s false pride by holding up the best of mountains with one hand for an entire week, thus protecting the inhabitants of Gokula from rain, wind and hail.**

**Комментарий:**

Since he defeated Indra, he does not need to exert any effort to kill the wrestlers.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Because of joy, the gopīs easily overcame all kinds of distress by constantly seeing his face, with talks and smiles, which was without fatigue.**

**Комментарий:**

Constantly seeing his face which was without fatigue, which had his eyes along with talks and smiles, the gopīs crossed over various sufferings. We however see his face endowed with fatigue (due to the fighting). We are most unfortunate.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**It is said that under his full protection the Yadu dynasty will become extremely famous and attain wealth, glory and power.**

**Комментарий:**

Protected by him, the Yadu dynasty, becoming very famous, will attain wealth, etc. This has been said by Nārada and others.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**This lotus-eyed elder brother, Balarāma, is the proprietor of all beauty. He has killed Pralamba, Vatsaka, Baka and other demons.**

**Комментарий:**

They mention that Balarāma killed Vatsa and Baka, because of the uncertainty of the rumours they heard.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**While the people talked in this way and the musical instruments resounded, the wrestler Cāṇūra addressed Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma with the following words.**

**Комментарий:**

While they were speaking, Cāṇūra became intolerant and spoke words full of pride.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**\[Cāṇūra said:l O son of Nanda, O Rāma, you two are well respected as being courageous and are both skilful at wrestling. Having heard of your prowess, the king has called you here, wanting to see for himself.**

**Комментарий:**

You are skilful at wrestling (niyuddha).

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Subjects of the king who try to please him with their thoughts, acts and words are sure to achieve good fortune, but those who fail to do so will suffer the opposite fate.**

**Комментарий:**

Not pleasing the king brings misfortune.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**It is well known that cowherd boys are always joyful as they tend their calves, and that the boys playfully wrestle with each other while grazing their animals in the various forests.**

**Комментарий:**

“But we cowherds do not know how to wrestle.”

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Therefore let us and you do what the king wants. Everyone will be pleased with us, for the king embodies all living beings.**

**Комментарий:**

If the king is pleased, everyone would become happy.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Hearing this, Kṛṣṇa, who liked to wrestle and welcomed the challenge, replied with words appropriate to the time and place.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa welcomed the words of the servant. “It is proper that the king’s servant please the king.”

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] Although forest-dwellers, we are also subjects of the Bhoja king. We must gratify his desires, for such behaviour will confer upon us the greatest benefit.**

**Комментарий:**

We who live in Vṛndāvana, wandering in the forest and you (because of the ca) are the citizens of the Bhoja king. But we always please the king by killing and liberating his associates such as Pūtanā and others. Your request to fight with us (tad) is great mercy on us since it will bestow fame.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**We are just young boys and should play with those of equal strength. The wrestling match must go on properly so that irreligion does not taint the respectable members of the audience.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks words to bewilder the demons. It is proper to fight with young boys, those of equal strength. O people watching the match! Adharma should not touch the people. We will play with cowherds like us of great strength, not with you low class fools. That is the hidden meaning.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Cāṇūra said: You aren’t really a child or even a young man, and neither is Balarāma, the strongest of the strong. After all, you casually killed an elephant who had the strength of a thousand other elephants.**

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Therefore you two should fight powerful wrestlers. There’s certainly nothing unfair about that. You, O descendant of Vṛṣṇi, can show your prowess against me, and Balarāma can fight with Muṣṭika.**

**Комментарий:**

It is not improper that you fight with strong persons like me. O descendent of Vṛṣṇi! Show your prowess against me. Muṣṭika should show prowess against Balarāma.

## Chapter 44 - The Killing of Kaṁsa

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus addressed, Kṛṣṇa made up his mind to accept the challenge. He grabbed Cāṇūra, and Balarāma confronted Muṣṭika.**

**Комментарий:**

In the forty-fourth chapter the wrestlers and Kaṁsa are killed, Kaṁsa’s wives are consoled and the parents are released from prison. Kṛṣṇa made up his mind to kill Cāṇūra (carcita-saṅkalpaḥ). He grabbed him.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Seizing each other’s hands and locking legs with each other, the opponents struggled powerfully, eager for victory.**

**Комментарий:**

Prasahya means with force.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**They each struck fists against fists, knees against knees, head against head and chest against chest.**

**Комментарий:**

Aratni refers to the fist excluding the little finger as defined by knowers of dictionaries. Though it is difficult to fight with the fists like that, still the Lord taught in that way.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Each fighter contended with his opponent by dragging him about, shoving and crushing him, throwing him down and approaching from the front and back.**

**Комментарий:**

Grasping with the hands they would drag the opponent around (paribhrāmaṇa). They would push by the hands (vikṣepa), squeeze the opponent with the arms (parirambha), throw the opponent down (avapātaṇaiḥ), get loose and come in front (utsarpaṇa) and approach from behind (apasarpaṇaiḥ). In this way they restrained the opponent. The addition of the letter n is poetic license in the aorist tense used in the verb pratyarundathāṁ.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Forcefully lifting and carrying each other, pushing each other away and holding each other down, the fighters hurt even their own bodies in their great eagerness for victory.**

**Комментарий:**

They would lift up (utthāpanaiḥ) an opponent holding the earth by acting like a turtle. They would raise the opponent in their arms (unnayanaiḥ), drag the opponent by holding his neck, etc. (cālanaiḥ), pound with the hands and feet (sthāpanaiḥ). In this way they injured the body (ātmanaḥ). Though Kṛṣṇa was not actually injured, this is the description according to the understanding of the spectators.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, all the women present, gathering in groups, feeling compassion, said that the match was an unfair fight between the strong and the weak.**

**Комментарий:**

The women of the city in a group (varūthaśaḥ) said that it was an unequal fight between the strong on one side and the weak on the other side because they had natural affection for Kṛṣṇa. This is the nature of affection, even though the object of affection is greatly powerful still there is fear of mishap.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**\[The women said:\] Alas, what a greatly irreligious act the members of this royal assembly are committing! As the king watches this fight between the strong and the weak, they also want to see it.**

**Комментарий:**

Ten verses describe what they said. It is great injustice on the part of the king’s assembly since, while the king watches, they do not stop the match. Rather they also want to see it.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**What comparison can there be between these two professional wrestlers, with limbs as strong as lightning bolts and bodies resembling mighty mountains, and these two young, immature boys with exceedingly tender limbs?**

**Комментарий:**

They point with their forefingers at the strong and the weak.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Religious principles have certainly been violated in this assembly. One should not remain for even a moment in a place where irreligion is flourishing.**

**Комментарий:**

Dharma has certainly been transgressed in this assembly.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**A wise person should not enter an assembly if he knows the participants there are committing acts of impropriety. It is a sin if, recognizing the faults in an assembly, he remains silent, or even in ignorance speaks falsely.**

**Комментарий:**

We have been at fault in entering this arena today. The fault of the assembly is expressed in this verse. A person of the assembly obtains sin, who though knowing does not speak (abruvan), or speaks the opposite (vibhruvan), vidharma, or says he does not know though he actually does (ajñaḥ). Therefore, a wise person should not enter this assembly.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Just see the moon-like face of Kṛṣṇa as he darts around his foe! That face, covered with drops of perspiration brought on by the strenuous fight, resembles the whorl of a lotus covered with dew.**

**Комментарий:**

“By not seeing their fatigue, since it may be inferred that they are strong, there is no question of fault.” Fearing this objection they described Kṛṣṇa’s fatigue. See the moon-like face (vadanāmbujam) of Kṛṣṇa covered with perspiration as he runs around Cāṇūra. Abja can mean moon according to Amara-kośa . The neuter gender for vadanāmbujam is poetic licence.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Don’t you see the face of Balarāma, with its eyes copper-red from his anger toward Muṣṭika and its beauty enhanced by his absorption in laughter?**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāmā is angry (sāmarṣaṁ) due to fatigue arising from the blows of Muṣṭika. He is beautiful with absorption in fighting with a laugh arising from his anger.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**How pious are the tracts of land in Vraja, for there the oldest person, disguising himself with human traits, wanders about, enacting his many pastimes! Adorned with wonderfully variegated forest garlands, he whose feet are worshiped by Śiva and Lakṣmī vibrates his flute as he tends the cows in the company of Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇas’ wives, who had gone there or other women, with desires like theirs, knowing Kṛṣṇa’s svarūpa, not tolerating the injustice, praise the people of Vraja, indicating that Mathurā is inferior. The places in Vraja are glorious where (yat) he wandered with various pastimes (vikrīḍayā). Fie on Mathurā for here we see his suffering. (In Vraja) He hides his powers from people with external vision by his human characteristics and wears a colorful forest garland. The pastimes are herding the cows and playing the flute. Seeing that, the people of Vraja are most fortunate. He is the ancient person since his feet are worshipped by Śiva and Lakṣmī.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**What worship must the gopīs have performed! With their eyes they always drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s form, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equalled or surpassed. That loveliness is the only abode of beauty, fame and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and extremely rare.**

**Комментарий:**

Among the people of Vraja the young gopīs are most fortunate. What austerity did they perform so that they can see with respect (pibanti) his beauty (rūpam) with their eyes? Having stated that seeing him is the result of such austerity, they suggest an indescribable reason for embracing him, etc. If we know the austerity we will also perform it. Or what austerities did the gopīs perform? None, since it is impossible to get such results from any austerity. Thus this manifestation is suitable only for his nitya-preyasīs. That form is the essence of all types of shining beauty or the fixed portion of all beauty (lāvanya-sāraḥ). “But if such a form exists even on earth, which is inferior than Svarga, etc, then in Maha-vaikuṇṭha which is beyond everything, there should be his form of Nārāyaṇa, which is superior than this form also.” There is no equal to this form (asamordhvam) there what to speak of anything superior. Thus it is heard that even Lakṣmī, Nārāyaṇa’s consort desires this form. “Then where did Kṛṣṇa obtain this form from?” It is natural to him (ananya-siddham). “But if they see him all the time, it will not be astonishing at all times.” It is constantly fresh (anasavābhinavam), manifesting more at every moment due to the mutual increase of prema and the form’s manifestation. “Others should be able to see this.” It is rare (durāpam). Without such prema, it cannot be seen. “His excellence is due to beauty and Nārāyaṇa’s excellence is due to opulence.” That form is the sole abode (dhāma) of the six opulence such as fame, etc. (yaśasaḥ) and is the root bhagavat-tattva. Kaṁsa will be killed in a moment.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**The ladies of Vraja are the most fortunate of women because, with their minds fully attached to Kṛṣṇa and their throats always choked up with tears, they constantly sing about him while milking the cows, winnowing grain, churning butter, gathering cow dung for fuel, riding on swings, taking care of their crying babies, sprinkling the ground with water, and cleaning their houses. He was always in their hearts.**

**Комментарий:**

Like in seeing him even in not seeing him, his form manifests to them. While milking cows, threshing grains (avahanane), swinging (preṅkheṅkhana), sprinkling water (ukṣaṇa), the gopīs sang. The word ca indicates that they sometimes see him. By that sweetness their chores did not act as an obstacle. He carried them always in his heart. Others like Brahmā however carry the Lord in their hearts. This shows his great attachment to them. Another version has cinta-yānā: they thought of him.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**When the gopīs hear Kṛṣṇa playing his flute as he leaves Vraja in the morning with his cows or returns with them at sunset, the young girls quickly come out of their houses to see him. They must have performed many pious activities to be able to see him as he walks on the road, his smiling face mercifully glancing upon them.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing the flute of Kṛṣṇa when he leaves Vraja for the forest in the morning with the cows and entering Vraja from the forest in the evening, the gopīs would quickly leave their houses and see him at the edge of the forest on a path for bringing the cows. He had a smiling face and a glance laden with mercy indicating he would fulfil their desires. They are most fortunate, and we see his face when we are having problems. We are unfortunate.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] As the women spoke thus, O hero of the Bhāratas, Kṛṣṇa, the master of all mystic power, made up his mind to kill his opponent.**

**Комментарий:**

When the women spoke with afflicted hearts, the Lord decided to kill the enemy to remove their suffering.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Out of affection for the two Lords, their parents became overwhelmed with sorrow when they heard the women’s fearful statements. They grieved, not knowing their sons’ strength.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda and Vasudeva, who were cast into lamentation because of affection for their sons, felt great repentance. Why was Akrūra not clever enough that he would not bring the two boys here? How is it that I did not keep them, locking them in the house? In this way they repented. They did not know the strength of their sons in conquering the wrestlers since their knowledge was covered by the manifestation of their vātsalya.
