Abudhau does not take the genitive (rather takes the accusative – balam) since the usage of genitive is optional by the usage in the sūtra, tad arham (Pāṇini 5.1.117).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma and Muṣṭika, expertly displaying numerous wrestling techniques, battled each other in the same way that Kṛṣṇa and his opponent did.**

**Комментарий:**

They fought similar to Kṛṣṇa and Cāṇūra (acyutetarau).

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**The harsh blows from the Supreme Lord’s limbs fell like crushing thunder bolts upon Cāṇūra, breaking every part of his body and causing him more and more pain and fatigue.**

**Комментарий:**

By the blows of Kṛṣṇa’s elbows, knees, etc., cruel as crushing thunderbolts, Cāṇūra’s limbs broke.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Furious, Cāṇūra attacked Kṛṣṇa with the speed of a hawk and struck his chest with both fists.**

**Комментарий:**

Cāṇūra struck him (abādhata) on the chest.

### Text 22-23

**Перевод:**

**No more shaken by the demon’s mighty blows than an elephant struck with a flower garland, Kṛṣṇa grabbed Cāṇūra by his arms, swung him around many times and hurled him onto the ground with great force. His clothes, hair and garland scattered, the wrestler fell down dead, like a huge festival column collapsing.**

**Комментарий:**

He threw Cāṇūra on the ground and agitated him (pothayām āsa). The Indra-dhvaja (flag staff of Indra) is famous in the eastern provinces.

### Text 24-25

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, Muṣṭika struck Balabhadra with his fist and was slain. Receiving a violent blow from the mighty Lord’s palm, the demon trembled all over in great pain, vomited blood and then fell lifeless onto the ground, like a tree blown down by the wind.**

**Комментарий:**

Talena means with the open hand. Muṣṭika fell lifeless on the ground (urvy-upasthe).

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Confronted next by the wrestler Kūṭa, Balarāma, the best of fighters, effortlessly and with paying attention killed him with his left fist, O King.**

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Then Kṛṣṇa struck the wrestler Śala in the head with his toes and tore him in half. The Lord dealt with Tośala in the same way, and both wrestlers fell down dead.**

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Cāṇūra, Muṣṭika, Kūṭa, Śala and Tośala having been killed, the remaining wrestlers all fled for their lives.**

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma then called their young cowherd boyfriends to join them, and in their company the Lords jumped about and sported, their ankle bells resounding as musical instruments played.**

**Комментарий:**

Calling the cowherd boys who were of equal strength, meeting with them (saṁsṛjya), the two boys danced while their ankle bells jingled, to increase Kaṁsa’s anger.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Everyone except Kaṁsa rejoiced at the wonderful feat Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma had performed. The exalted brāhmaṇas and great saints exclaimed, “Excellent! Excellent!”**

**Комментарий:**

The chief brāhmaṇas who were saintly praised them, saying, “Excellent, excellent!” Those who were impious, the priests of Kaṁsa, lamented, “Alas, alas!”.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The Bhoja king, seeing that his best wrestlers had all been killed or had fled, stopped the musical performance originally meant for his pleasure and spoke the following words.**

**Комментарий:**

He stopped the music which he had commissioned (sva-tūryānī), not the devatā music which he could not stop since he became powerless at that time. Or he could not stop the music which played by itself since he was powerless to stop it. Viṣṇu Purāṇa explains that the music stopped previously. Seeing the destruction of Cāṇūra’s strength and the success of Kṛṣṇa, Kaṁsa, full of anger stopped the music. When the mṛdaṅgas and other instruments stopped, at that moment in the sky the devatās’ many instruments began to sound together. Hari-vaṁśa having stated both (Kaṁsa’s stopping his instruments and the playing of the devatās instruments) says: svayam eva pravādyanta tūrya-ghoṣāś ca sarvaśaḥ All the instruments began playing on their own.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**\[Kaṁsa said:\] Drive the two wicked sons of Vasudeva out of the city! Confiscate the cowherds’ property and arrest that fool Nanda!**

**Комментарий:**

The meaning is clear. But Sarasvatī devī speaks as follows: Give these boys of unfathomable pastimes the best position in the city. Protect Kṛṣṇa, the treasure of the cowherd men here. He has tied up (badhnīta) Nanda whose mind is difficult to understand with the ropes of love and has affection for him.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Kill that most evil fool Vasudeva! And also kill my father, Ugrasena, along with his followers, who have all sided with our enemies!**

**Комментарий:**

The other meaning is as follows. Everyone should go to and take shelter (hanyatāṁ) of Vasudeva, whose intelligence is hard to understand. There is no one equal to him in purity (asattamaḥ). Bring Ugrasena and his followers, who are loyal to the Lord (para), who are devotees.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**As Kaṁsa thus raved so audaciously, the infallible Kṛṣṇa, intensely angry, quickly and forcefully leaped onto the high royal dais.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa who is famous by the name Avyaya, being devoid of fatigue, etc., was visibly angry (prakupitaḥ). By his śakti called laghimā, he quickly ascended the gallery.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Kṛṣṇa approaching like death personified, the quickwitted Kaṁsa instantly rose from his seat and took up his sword and shield.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was the cause of his death (mṛtyum). Kaṁsa was frightened (manasvī) (literally censured by the wise). The suffix vin is used in the sense of censure (Kāśikā vṛtti 5.2.94).

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Sword in hand, Kaṁsa moved quickly from side to side like a hawk in the sky. But Kṛṣṇa, whose fearsome strength is irresistible, powerfully seized the demon just as the son of Tārkṣya might capture a snake.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was endowed with great, intolerable ferocity (durviṣahogratejā). He quickly grabbed Kaṁsa just as Garuḍa catches a snake. Kaṁsa was moving left and right like a hawk in the sky.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Grabbing Kaṁsa by the hair and knocking off his crown, the lotus-naveled Lord threw him off the elevated dais onto the wrestling mat. Then the independent Lord, the support of the entire universe, threw himself upon the king.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa thew him from the gallery and fell upon him without being injured by the ground, in order to kill him with his own weight since he was the shelter of the universe. The cause of falling on top of Kaṁsa was that he was independent (ātmā-tantraḥ).

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**As a lion drags a dead elephant, the Lord then dragged Kaṁsa’s dead body along the ground in full view of everyone present. O King, all the people in the arena tumultuously cried out, “Oh! Oh!”**

**Комментарий:**

To make Nanda and others understand that Kaṁsa was dead and had not just fainted, he pulled the corpse around. Cries of astonishment arose because of disrespecting a great warrior, who had just been killed. Then the entire arena became filled with cries of astonishment as the people saw that the master of Mathurā had been contemptuously killed by Kṛṣṇa. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) After offering respects to his fathers, Kṛṣṇa personally dragged Kaṁsa to the bank of the Yamunā since it was impossible for others, as Kaṁsa was heavy as a mountain. Kaṁsa’s body produced a huge channel when Kṛṣṇa forcefully dragged it to the Yamunā. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) This place is known as Kaṁsa-khāta.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Kaṁsa had always been disturbed by the thought that the Supreme Lord was to kill him. Therefore when drinking, eating, moving about, sleeping or simply breathing, the King had always seen the Lord before him with the disc weapon in his hand. Thus Kaṁsa achieved the rare boon of attaining a form like the Lord’s.**

**Комментарий:**

Kaṁsa obtained liberation because his offenses were destroyed by absorption in Kṛṣṇa out of fear. He obtained the form that he saw then like an insect trapped by a bee. Previously as Kālanemi he had been killed by the Lord Ajita but did not attain liberation. Now, being killed by Kṛṣṇa, he obtained liberation since svayam rūpa Kṛṣṇa bestows this benediction on the enemies he kills. In this sense it is rare (duravāpam).

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Kaṁsa’s eight younger brothers, led by Kaṅka and Nyagrodhaka, then attacked the Lords in a rage, seeking to avenge their brother’s death.**

**Комментарий:**

They wanted to pay their debt to their brother (nirveśa-kāriṇāḥ).

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**As they ran swiftly toward the two Lords, ready to strike, the son of Rohiṇī slew them with his club just as a lion easily kills other animals.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma killed the brothers who were as quick as Kaṁsa (tathātirabhasān), with a club taken from them, or with the elephant tusk resembling a club.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Kettledrums resounded in the sky as Brahmā, Śiva and other devatās, the Lord’s expansions, rained down flowers upon him with pleasure. They chanted his praises, and their wives danced.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā and others, endowed with powers (vibhūtayaḥ) given by the Lord, and thus his servants, showered flowers. Women means Urvaśī and others.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, the wives of Kaṁsa and his brothers, aggrieved by the death of their well-wishing husbands, came forward with tearful eyes, beating their heads.**

**Комментарий:**

The wives of Kaṁsa and others (teṣām) approached (abhīyuḥ).

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Embracing their husbands, who lay dead on the battlefield, the sorrowful women loudly lamented while shedding constant tears.**

**Комментарий:**

They embraced their husbands, lying down as if sleeping on the ground where they were killed in battle (vīra-śayāyām). The word śocatīḥ stands for śocantyaḥ (lamenting).

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**\[The women cried out:\] Alas, O master, O dear one, O knower of religious principles! O kind and compassionate protector of the shelterless! By your being slain we have also been slain, together with your household and offspring.**

**Комментарий:**

The daughters of Jarāsandha, objects of their husband’s affection speak in two verses. We have been killed along with the house and children (sa-gṛha-prajāḥ).

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**O great hero among men, bereft of you, its master, this city has lost its beauty, just as we have, and all festivity and good fortune within it have come to an end.**

**Комментарий:**

The city is separated from its master (patyā).

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**O dear one, you have been brought to this state because of the terrible violence you committed against innocent creatures. How can one who harms others attain happiness?**

**Комментарий:**

Some women, of pure hearts, who were not like them, speak in two verses.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa causes the appearance and disappearance of all beings in this world, and he is their maintainer as well. One who disrespects him can never prosper happily.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa is the cause of appearance and destruction of all beings. He is the protector (goptā), the Supreme Lord, the cause of the production, maintenance, destruction of the universe. Those who offend him (avadhyāyī) can never prosper.

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After consoling the royal ladies, Kṛṣṇa, sustainer of all the worlds, arranged for the prescribed funeral rites to be performed.**

**Комментарий:**

He consoled the wives of Kaṁsa, saying, “I will protect you aunts.” He performed the funeral rites (saṁsthām) of the dead according to scriptures, which the knowers of scriptures describe (yām āhuḥ).

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**Then Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma released their mother and father from bondage and offered obeisances to them, touching their feet with their heads.**

**Комментарий:**

Releasing their father and mother, touching their feet with their heads, they offered respects (vavandāte).

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**Devakī and Vasudeva, knowing Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma to be the Lords of the universe, simply stood with joined palms. Being apprehensive, they did not embrace their sons.**

**Комментарий:**

Remembering Kṛṣṇa’s birth and seeing his power in killing Kaṁsa, frightened due to respect, they did not embrace their sons who were related to them. Instead they folded their hands and stood there. Viṣṇu Purāṇa says: Vasudeva and Devakī raised Kṛṣṇa from the ground and remembering the words spoken at his birth, they offered respects to him. In the same Purāṇa their long prayer is also described.

## Chapter 45 - Kṛṣṇa Rescues His Teacher’s Son

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Understanding that his parents were becoming aware of his powers, the Supreme Lord thought that this should not be allowed to happen. Thus he expanded his Yogamāyā, which bewilders his devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

In the forty-fifth chapter Kṛṣṇa pacifies his parents, enthrones Ugrasena, resolves issues with Nanda, resides in his guru’s āśrama and returns to Mathurā. Upalabdha here means his parents realized Kṛṣṇa devoid (upa) of sentiments of his being their son, appreciating instead his powerful aspect. Kṛṣṇa realized this when he offered them his respects (SB [10.44.50](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/44.50)), after releasing them. He thought, “This should not happen.” He then spread his mercy (māyām) in the form of vātsalya with parental affection for him (nijām), which bewilders his devotees, to increase his own bliss. By that understanding they attained bewilderment in prema. For those who are recipients of my mercy, understanding of my great powers is secondary. Thus, they had less respect in dealing with him.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, the greatest of the Sātvatas, approached his parents with his elder brother. Humbly bowing his head and gratifying them by respectfully addressing them as “My dear mother” and “My dear father,” Kṛṣṇa spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

After freeing them, he sent them home, and then came there himself. Then he spoke. He engaged others to perform the rites for Kaṁsa and others.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa said:\] Dear Father, because of us, your two sons, you and mother Devakī always remained in anxiety and could never enjoy our childhood, boyhood or youth.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of us, though longing, you did not experience the intense bliss of childhood, etc., of us two. The kaiśorāḥ instead of kaiśorāṇi is poetic license. It is said by the city women that the two boys had attained kaiśora period. Kiśorau nāpta-yauvanau: they attained kaiśora period, but did not enter yauvana period. (SB [10.44.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/44.8)) Here however it is said that they had passed kaiśora. How is that to be reconciled with this verse? In this verse the kaiśora mentioned is the first part of kaiśora not the ending. Thus it is not contradictory. Kaiśora period lasts till fifteen years since it is said, kaiśoram ā pañca-daśād: Kaiśora extends till fifteen years. But Kṛṣṇa was eleven years old when he killed Kaṁsa since it is said, ekādaśa-samās tatra vraje’vātsīt sahāgrajaḥ: He lived for eleven years with his elder brother, Baladeva (SB [3.2.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.26)).

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Deprived by fate, we could not live with you and enjoy the pampered happiness most children enjoy in their parents’ home.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover we both are devoid of good fortune. Our destiny was weak. In daiva-hatayoḥ, the genitive stands for instrumental. But Sarasvatī devī speaks as follows. We are obtained by good fortune. You did not obtain the happiness that is caused by parental care of children staying with their parents.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**With one’s body one can acquire all goals of life, and it is one’s parents who give the body birth and sustenance. Therefore no mortal man can repay his debt to his parents, even if he serves them for a full lifetime of a hundred years.**

**Комментарий:**

A human cannot repay the debt to parents in a hundred lives since they have given birth to the body by which one can manifest all goals such as dharma, etc.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**A son who, though able to do so, fails to provide for his parents with his physical resources and wealth is forced after his death to eat his own flesh.**

**Комментарий:**

For the son who, though able (kalpaḥ) to give according to scriptural rules, being situated on the path of karma, does not provide for his parents, the servants of Yama force him after death to eat his own flesh.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**A man who, though able to do so, fails to support his parents, elders of the family, chaste wife, young child or spiritual master, or who neglects a brāhmaṇa or anyone who comes to him for shelter, is considered dead, though breathing.**

**Комментарий:**

Abibhrat means not supporting. The person lives uselessly (śvasan mṛtaḥ).

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Thus we have wasted all these days, unable as we were to properly honor you because our minds were always disturbed by fear of Kaṁsa.**

**Комментарий:**

Therefore (tat), we have wasted our days since we did not serve you, because we were disturbed by fear of Kaṁsa. We were incapable (akalpayoḥ). The real meaning is, “There is no one capable for these two (akalpayoḥ). We spent all these days uselessly. After hearing from Kaṁsa (kaṁsāt) we were always eager and joyful to fight (nityamud) and thus we had decided to go to Mathurā (vigna-cetaso).” In this case vigna means moving or going (the root is vij). Kṛṣṇa’s saying that he spent his days uselessly (mogham) is an expression of regret.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Dear Father and Mother, please forgive us for not serving you. You were not independent and have been greatly frustrated by cruel Kaṁsa.**

**Комментарий:**

You should forgive us. You were under the control of (paratantrayoḥ) and afflicted by evil Kaṁsa (durhṛdā).

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus beguiled by the words of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul of the universe, whose illusory potency acts on humans, his parents joyfully raised the two boys on their laps and embraced them.**

**Комментарий:**

His illusion acts on men (māyā-manuṣyasya). Since māyā-manuṣya is a word belonging to gaḍv-ādi group, the locative (manuṣya) is placed later. His parents were bewildered by his words which were filled with affection and forgot his powers. Vasudeva and others had bhakti predominated with aiśvarya-jñāna. The Lord was not too attracted to such bhakti suitable for śānta bhaktas performing austerities. Thus, he gave them awareness with vātsalya to increase his own bliss.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Pouring out a shower of tears upon the Lord, his parents, who were bound up by the rope of affection, could not speak. They were overwhelmed, O King, and their throats choked up with tears.**

**Комментарий:**

They were bound by ropes of vātsalya.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Thus having comforted his mother and father, the Lord, appearing as the son of Devakī, installed his maternal grandfather, Ugrasena, as king of the Yadus.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda was not present when he consoled his parents and enthroned Ugrasena. He had gone to his encampment for some daily duties, understanding that the people, free of Kaṁsa, would take his son to the palace to honor him.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**The Lord told him: O mighty King, we are your subjects, so please command us, even though, because of the curse of Yayāti, no Yadu may sit on the royal throne.**

**Комментарий:**

Even though by the curse of Yayāti, Yadus should not sit on the throne, by my order, there is no fault.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Since I am present in your entourage as your personal attendant, all the devatās and other exalted personalities will come with heads bowed to offer you tribute. What, then, to speak of others, the rulers of men?**

**Комментарий:**

“But I am not capable of bearing the responsibility of the kingdom.” Kṛṣṇa answers.

### Text 15-16

**Перевод:**

**The Lord then brought all his close family members and other relatives back from the various places to which they had fled in fear of Kaṁsa. He received the Yadus, Vṛṣṇis, Andhakas, Madhus, Dāśārhas, Kukuras and other clans with due honor, and he also consoled them, for they were weary of living in foreign lands. Then Kṛṣṇa, the creator of the universe, resettled them in their homes and gratified them with valuable gifts.**

**Комментарий:**

The topics of future are described. Two verses are taken together. He caused all the families who had fled out of fear of Kaṁsa to be brought back.

### Text 17-18

**Перевод:**

**The members of these clans, protected by the arms of Kṛṣṇa and Saṅkarṣaṇa, felt that all their desires were fulfilled. Thus, they enjoyed perfect happiness while living at home with their families. Because of the presence of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, they no longer suffered from the fever of material existence. Every day these loving devotees could see Mukunda’s ever-cheerful lotus face, continually increasing in beauty and continually displaying compassionate, smiling glances.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Siddhāḥ means they were successful.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Even the most elderly inhabitants of the city appeared youthful, full of strength and vitality, for with their eyes they constantly drank the elixir of Mukunda’s lotus face.**

**Комментарий:**

The elders, ancient members of the Andhakas, etc., became young.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Then, O exalted Parīkṣit, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, along with Balarāma, approached Nanda Mahārāja. The two Lords embraced him and then addressed him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

The word atha is used to speak some difficult to understand topics, the day after killing Kaṁsa. Kṛṣṇa approached Nanda, thinking of himself as a son. The two boys embraced Nanda, since there was no opportunity to offer respects, since seeing his sons come, Nanda immediately stood up, and held them both to his chest at the same time. Thus they also embraced him (and are stated as the subject of the action of embracing in the verse). They spoke. Being embraced by his arms while sitting on a seat, through questions and answers indicating the remaining tasks of the Yadus, they made a request humbly with some reserve.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma said:\] O Father, you and mother Yaśodā have affectionately maintained us and cared for us so much, since parents love their children more than themselves.**

**Комментарий:**

First Balarāma, being elder, spoke in two verses. O father! We two were nourished by you two parents, Nanda and Yaśodā with food and pampered in plenty with bathing, etc. Using the dual he indicates that as you are affectionate to Kṛṣṇa, your son, you are affectionate to me, your brother’s son. I know you two as my parents. It is appropriate that you cared for us so much, since parents have more affection for their children than for their own bodies (ātmanaḥ). It is difficult for me to stay in the house of my father without my brother, dearest Kṛṣṇa and you two who cared for me.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**They are the real father and mother who care for, as they would their own sons, children abandoned by relatives unable to maintain and protect them.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Balarāma! You are the son of my brother Vasudeva. In difficulty, he left you with us. Vasudeva is now free of problems. Why would he give you up? Thus stay with your father. We will tolerate that separation by deliberation. It is not possible to see a brother suffer.” Balarāma speaks. The person is a father of babies or mother of babies who nourishes those children as his own. You are like that. The person who impregnates and the woman who bears the child in the womb are not the parents. If a child born from them are not nourished they will die, then whose parents are they? Thus the wise consider you as parents who nourished us. I will go with you and Kṛṣṇa to Vraja.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Now you should all return to Vraja, dear father. We shall come to see you, our dear relatives who suffer in separation from us, as soon as we have given some happiness to your well-wishing friends.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding Balarāma’s words and his mood, Nanda thought. “If I take him also and go home, then there will be an increase of happiness in Vraja. But it will be a great bad mark on me and a very painful breach of friendship with my brother Vasudeva, whose many sons were killed by Kaṁsa and whose only one son was saved (i.e. Balarāma). Thus what should I do?” Nanda was cast into an ocean of thought and stood there silently. Kṛṣṇa then aroused him with logic. O father! You return to Vraja now. I, Balarāma and Madhumaṅgala and others (vayam) will come to see you, my relatives. Do not worry. “When will you come?” Having given happiness to our friends such that your friends, having obtained Balarāma will have faith that “Leaving us he will not go to Vraja.” By doing that, your friendship will not be broken and you will not get a tinge of bad reputation. What remaining work has to be done?

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Thus consoling Nanda Mahārāja and the other men of Vraja, Kṛṣṇa, who was capable of doing anything and who would not fail to keep his promise, respectfully honored them with gifts of clothing, jewelry, household utensils and so on.**

**Комментарий:**

He consoled Nanda. “I will be delayed a few days. Do not worry.” He honored them with gifts of attractive utensils made of gold, silver, and bell metal.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja was overwhelmed with affection upon hearing Kṛṣṇa’s words, and his eyes brimmed with tears as he embraced the two Lords. Then he went back to Vraja with the cowherd men.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda was overwhelmed with affection. This indicates that he fainted because of separation from his son.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, then Vasudeva, the son of Śūrasena, arranged for a priest and other brāhmaṇas to perform his two sons’ second-birth initiation.**

**Комментарий:**

Dvija-saṁskṛtim means upanayanam. This was done by Garga (purodhasā).

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva worshipped the brāhmaṇas and, after offering them ornaments, gave them well-ornamented cows with their calves. All these cows wore gold necklaces and linen wreaths.**

**Комментарий:**

The cows received garlands made of threads of atasi (kṣaumam).

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**The magnanimous Vasudeva then remembered the cows he had mentally given away on the occasion of Kṛṣṇa’s and Balarāma’s birth. Kaṁsa had stolen those cows, and Vasudeva now recovered them and gave them away in charity also.**

**Комментарий:**

Remembering the cows that he gave away mentally at the birth constellations of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, he gave those cows which had been stolen by Kaṁsa by adharma. They were his cows since they were property of a conquered king.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**After attaining twice-born status through initiation, the Lords, sincere in their vows, took the further vow of celibacy from Garga Muni, the spiritual master of the Yadus.**

**Комментарий:**

They took brahmacarya vows (gāyatram).

### Text 30-31

**Перевод:**

**Concealing their innately perfect knowledge by their humanlike activities, those two omniscient Lords of the universe, themselves the origin of all branches of knowledge, next desired to reside at the school of a spiritual master. Thus they approached Sāndīpani Muni, a native of Kāśī living in the city of Avantī.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Covering (gūhamanau) their natural (nānyasiddha) knowledge of all subjects (amalaṁ) by human behavior, and though they were like that, desiring to live in the guru-kula to teach people, they approached Sāndīpani, born in Kāśī, living in Avantī. Desiring association of Kṛṣṇa, Sāndīpani gave up Kāśī and lived in Avantī.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**According to the rules they approached the guru, and with controlled senses, accepting faultless conduct towards the guru, respecting him as the Lord, they performed service with devotion.**

**Комментарий:**

Duly (yathā), approaching him, they taught people service to guru (gurau vṛttim). They approached (upetau) guru and respected him as if he were the Lord.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**That best of brāhmaṇas, the spiritual master Sāndīpani, was satisfied with their submissive behavior, and thus he taught them the entire Vedas with its aṅgas, together with the Upaniṣads.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Pleased by their service (anuvṛttibhiḥ) in which there was pure bhakti (śuddha-bhāva), the guru taught them all the Vedas, with their aṅgas, and the Upaniṣads. The aṅgas of the Vedas are six: The six aṅgas of the Vedas are known by the wise as śikṣā, kalpa, grammar, astrology, meter, and derivation of words.

### Text 34-35

**Перевод:**

**He also taught them the Dhanur-veda, with its most confidential secrets; the standard books of law; the methods of logical reasoning and philosophical debate; and the sixfold science of politics. O King, those best of persons, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, being themselves the original promulgators of all varieties of knowledge, could immediately assimilate each and every subject after hearing it explained just once.**

**Комментарий:**

Sa-rahasyam means with knowledge of the devatās of the mantras. Dharmān means dharma-scriptures such as those spoken by Manu, etc. Nyāya-pathān means karma-mīmāṁsa and brahma-mīmāṁsa. Anvīkṣikīm means logic. The six-fold political science includes (1) sandhi, making peace; (2) vigraha, war; (3) yāna, marching; (4) āsana, sitting tight; (5) dvaidha, dividing one’s forces; and (6) śraya, seeking the protection of a more powerful ruler. They imitated learning all scriptures just by hearing once.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**They learned the sixty-four arts and skills in as many days and nights. Thereafter, O King, They satisfied their spiritual master by offering him guru-dakṣiṇā.**

**Комментарий:**

They learned all these sixty-four arts in sixty-four days and nights. These arts should be seen in Śaiva-tantra. They satisfied their guru. Please accept this donation. Then they manifested what he desired. Chanda means desire according to Amara-kośa.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**O King, the learned brāhmaṇa Sāndīpani carefully considered the two Lords’ glorious and amazing qualities and their superhuman intelligence. Then, after consulting with his wife, he chose as his remuneration the return of his young son, who had died in the ocean at Prabhāsa.**

**Комментарий:**

The child was swallowed by the conch demon while playing in the water as a child at Prabhāsa.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**“So be it,” replied those two great charioteers of limitless might, and they at once mounted their chariot and set off for Prabhāsa. When they reached that place, they walked up to the shore and sat down. In a moment the deity of the ocean, recognizing them to be the Supreme Lords, approached them with offerings of tribute.**

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa addressed the lord of the ocean: Let the son of my guru be presented at once—the one you seized here with your mighty waves.**

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**The ocean replied: O Kṛṣṇa, it was not I who abducted him, but a demonic descendant of Diti named Pañcajana, who travels in the water in the form of a conch.**

**Комментарий:**

Pañcajana took him away. I cannot defeat him (mahān).

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**“Indeed,” the ocean said, “that demon has taken him away.” Hearing this, Lord Kṛṣṇa entered the ocean, found Pañcajana and killed him. But the Lord did not find the boy within the demon’s belly.**

### Text 42-44

**Перевод:**

**Janārdana took the conch shell that had grown around the demon’s body and went back to the chariot. Then he proceeded to Saṁyamanī, the beloved capital of Yamarāja, the lord of death. Upon arriving there with Balarāma, he loudly blew his conch shell, and Yamarāja, who keeps the conditioned souls in check, came as soon as he heard the resounding vibration. Yamarāja elaborately worshiped the two Lords with great devotion, and then he addressed Kṛṣṇa, who lives in everyone’s heart: “O Supreme Lord Viṣṇu, what shall I do for you two, who are playing the part of ordinary humans?”**

**Комментарий:**

He took the shell which was present conspicuously in the body of the demon (tad-aṅga-prabhavam). Avantī-khaṇḍa, Skanda Purāṇa says: Killing Pañcajana, the great demon in the form of a shark, who had swallowed a conch previously, Kṛṣṇa took it from within his body. Like the Kaustubha, which was given with other jewels by Kāliya, since his own conch had entered the demon’s body, Kṛṣṇa entered the water to take it back. The chariot was parked on the shore. He went to the chariot where Balarāma was waiting. Blowing the conch, he delivered the jīvas from hell by the sound of the conch. The blades in Asipatra hell broke. Raurava lost its cruelty. The hell called Bhaivara lost its fearful nature. Kumbhipāka hell did not cook anyone. (Avantī-khaṇḍa) Yamaḥ was the punisher of the sinful (prajā-saṁyamanaḥ). O Viṣṇu! What can I do for you two who are in the form of humans with predominant pastimes (līlā-manuṣyayoḥ)?

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: Suffering the bondage of his past activity, my spiritual master’s son was brought here to you. O great King, obey my command and bring this boy to me without delay.**

**Комментарий:**

Bring the son of my guru even though he must definitely suffer his prārabdha-karma. “How can I bring him if he has prārabdha?” Since by my order (śāsana), his prārabdha is destroyed. According to the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam ([11.31.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/31.12)): martyena yo gurusutaṁ yama-loka-nītaṁ: “Śrī Kṛṣṇa brought the son of his guru back from the planet of the lord of death in the boy’s self-same body.” Here martyena means in the appearance of a human. The boy had received a spiritual body in place of his material body.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**Yamarāja said, “So be it,” and brought forth the guru’s son. Then those two most exalted Yadus presented the boy to their spiritual master and said to him, “Please select another boon.”**

**Комментарий:**

The guru’s son was brought by Yama (tena). They spoke to their guru (tam).

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**The spiritual master said: My dear boys, you two have completely fulfilled the disciple’s obligation to reward his spiritual master. Indeed, with disciples like you, what further desires could a guru have?**

**Комментарий:**

O dear boy (vatsa)! He addresses both of them individually. What desire remains among all desires for a guru of persons similar to you (yuṣmad-vidha), what to speak of me, the guru of you two? No desire remains. All his desires were fulfilled by their association.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**O heroes, now please return home. May your fame sanctify the world, and may the Vedic hymns be ever fresh in your minds, both in this life and the next.**

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**O son! Thus, receiving their guru’s permission to leave, the two Lords returned to their city on their chariot, which moved as swiftly as the wind and resounded like a cloud.**

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**All the citizens rejoiced upon seeing Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, whom they had not seen for many days. The people felt just like those who have lost their wealth and then regained it.**

## Chapter 46 - Uddhava Visits Vṛndāvana

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The supremely intelligent Uddhava was the best of the Vṛṣṇi dynasty, a counselor, beloved of Kṛṣṇa, his intimate friend and a direct disciple of Bṛhaspati.**

**Комментарий:**

In the forty-sixth chapter, intelligent Uddhava goes to Gokula and becomes astonished on seeing the pain of Nanda and Yaśodā because of separation from Kṛṣṇa. When Kṛṣṇa was thinking of a suitable person to send a message to the people of Vraja when his mind was attracted by their prema, at that moment Uddhava came there. Taking him to a solitary place the Lord instructed him. Thus, Śukadeva begins to speak, and describes Uddhava. He was accepted by the Vṛṣṇis. Coming from Vraja, everyone would trust him when he described the great glories of the people of Vraja, since his words and actions were regarded as authoritative by the Vṛṣṇis. He was an advisor (mantra). By his advice the people of Vraja would be pacified completely. He was skillful in that. He was dear to Kṛṣṇa. He was qualified to taste the confidential prema of Vraja. He was a friend. He was skillful at speaking about mādhurya- rasa like Subala, Ujjvala, and others since he is stated to be equal to Kṛṣṇa in the Third Canto: noddhavo ‘ṇv api man-nyūno yad guṇair nārditaḥ prabhuḥ Uddhava is not inferior to me in any way because he is never affected by the modes of material nature. (SB [3.4.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/4.31)) He was a good messenger since he was a second image of Kṛṣṇa. He was directly the disciple of Bṛhaspati. He would be able to understand what the gopīs taught concerning the scriptures of prema since his intelligence was sharp. Since he was most intelligent (buddhi-sattamaḥ), he was fit to understand their scriptures. Kṛṣṇa too will explain to him that scripture alone amidst the queens (later on). Thus a desire for their bhāva would appear in the queens since they said: We desire the same contact with the Supreme Lord’s feet that the young women of Vraja, the cowherd boys and even the aborigine Pulinda women desire. (SB [10.83.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/83.43)) This Uddhava was the son of Vasudeva’s brother Devabhāga: uddhavo devabhāgasya mahā-bhāgaḥ suto ’bhavat. (Hari-vaṁśa) “But Uddhava is described as a friend and servant. Thus, it is not proper for a servant to give messages to the gopīs, the Lord’s beloveds.” It is not rasābhāsa since according to the pastimes of the Lord, with the appearance of friendship, dāsya becomes covered. This should be considered similar to the case of Balarāma.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who relieves the distress of all who surrender to him, once took the hand of his fully devoted, dearest friend Uddhava and addressed him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa spoke to Uddhava, who was a devoted bhakta and even in that, he was dear to the Lord. In a solitary place, he took Uddhava’s hand in his right hand. This indicates his own confusion. He destroys pain in only those who surrender to him. Thus, what to speak of the people of Vraja who were dearest to him.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] Dear gentle Uddhava, go to Vraja and give pleasure to our parents. And also relieve the gopīs, suffering in separation from me, by giving them my message.**

**Комментарий:**

Give full satisfaction to Yaśodā and Nanda, our parents. Relieve the gopīs of affliction because of separation from me. Release that pain tied by tight knot in their hearts. This will not happen by the skill of your words but by the many messages that I have written in letters.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**The minds of those gopīs are always absorbed in me, and their very lives are ever devoted to me. For my sake they have abandoned everything related to their bodies, as well as dharma and other people. I alone am their dear beloved and, indeed, their very self. Therefore I take it upon myself to sustain them in all circumstances.**

**Комментарий:**

You must particularly pacify the gopīs. This is expressed in three lines. Their minds, whose function is determination, are in me. I am their prāṇās. To attain me they give up husbands and bodily concerns. Their minds go towards me, most dear (preṣṭham ātmānam), Paramātmā, not to their husbands, as their lover. I protect those sādhakas who give up worldly dharma for me. What to speak of these gopīs.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**My dear Uddhava, for those women of Gokula I am the most cherished object of love. Thus when they remember me, who am so far away, they are overwhelmed by the anxiety of separation.**

**Комментарий:**

“If they have the characteristics of thinking of only you, etc., why do they not come here to see you, since you are not far away?” These women of Gokula shine in Gokula with me as the young prince of the cowherds, wearing cowherd dress, not in this city of the Yadus, with kṣatriya clothing. Thus even I do not bring them here. Since I, dear to the dear ātmās, Paramātmā (preṣṭhe preyasām), am far away, they faint greatly. All objects of possession are very dear. Dearer however than that is the ātmā, the shelter of “I.” Dearer than that however is the all-pervading Paramātmā, full of consciousness and bliss, and that is I.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Simply because I have promised to return to them, my fully devoted cowherd girlfriends struggle to maintain their lives somehow or other.**

**Комментарий:**

They maintain their prāṇas with great difficulty. Since their bodies, senses and prāṇas are eternal, they will not leave. But the pain, a form of experience of bliss in separation, difficult to bear, like chewing hot sugar cane, is great. The method of maintaining their lives is described. They hope that I will return since I gave the message through messengers that I would quickly return when I left Gokula. “O master! Why do you have great attraction to them?” They are my lovers (ballavyaḥ). They, who are famous as the wives of gopās, were not touched by them, and were married to me by Gandharava rules. They are dearest to me. Rādhā and other nityasiddhas, have me as their svarūpa (mad-ātmikāḥ). The sādhanasiddhas, who were previously sages, have their minds in me (madātmikāḥ). Or they are the persons who are always on my mind. The suffix ka indicates that this is his mercy. You should know that the relationships with their husbands was resolved by imitation forms manifested by my yoga-māyā.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus addressed, O King, Uddhava respectfully accepted his master’s message, mounted his chariot and set off for Nanda-gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

Accepting his master’s (bhartuḥ) message written as a letter, he went to Gokula.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**The fortunate Uddhava reached Nanda Mahārāja’s pastures just as the sun was setting, and since the returning cows and other animals were raising dust with their hooves, his chariot passed unnoticed.**

**Комментарий:**

Six verses describe his arrival in Vraja. He reached Nanda-vraja when the sun was setting (vibhāvasau nimlocati). His chariot was unnoticed (channaḥ).

### Text 9-13

**Перевод:**

**Gokula resounded on all sides with the sounds of bulls in rut fighting with one another for fertile cows; with the mooing of cows, burdened by their udders, chasing after their calves; with the noise of milking and of the white calves jumping here and there; with the loud reverberation of flute-playing; and with the singing of the all-auspicious deeds of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma by the cowherd men and women, who made the village resplendent with their wonderfully ornamented attire. The cowherds’ homes in Gokula appeared most charming with garlands, incense and lamps, for worship of the sacrificial fire, the sun, unexpected guests, the cows, the brāhmaṇas, the forefathers and the demigods. On all sides lay the flowering forest, echoing with flocks of birds and swarms of bees and beautified by its lakes crowded with swans, kāraṇḍava ducks and bowers of lotuses.**

**Комментарий:**

Then the Lord’s śakti called yoga-māyā covered the prakaṭa manifestation of Vraja filled with separation from Kṛṣṇa, distressful with regret, lamentation, misery, etc., and displayed the aprakaṭa manifestation of Vraja, having Kṛṣṇa’s presence, attractive with joy, eagerness, enthusiasm, etc., in order to give bliss to Uddhava. That is described in five verses. The place was filled with the sounds of bulls in rut fighting with one another for fertile cows; with the mooing of cows, burdened by their udders, chasing after their calves. There were the calves jumping and the noise of milking along with sounds such as, “Bring that here, release that, be quick, take this.” The place was resplendent (suvirājitam) with the sound of flutes. The place was attractive with the cowherds’ houses (gopāvāsaiḥ), having incense, lamps and garlands, and with worship of fire, etc. They worshiped the fire and sun by daily homa, service, etc, the cows by feeding mouthfuls of food, etc., and guests, brāhmaṇas, Pitṛs, devatās by honoring, etc. The cowherds performed agnihotra, etc., because they were twice born.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**As soon as Uddhava, the dear devotee of Kṛṣṇa, arrived at Nanda Mahārāja’s door, Nanda came forward to meet him. The cowherd King embraced him in great happiness and worshiped him as nondifferent from Vāsudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way, seeing the manifestation of Vraja having Kṛṣṇa’s presence, Uddhava was satisfied and entered Nanda’s house where separation was manifested. He had come from the palace to Nanda’s presence. Thinking of Uddhava as, “my worshippable Nārāyaṇa, coming in the body of a guest”, Nanda worshipped him with footwater, etc.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**After Uddhava had eaten first-class food, been seated comfortably on a bed and been relieved of his fatigue by a foot massage and other means, Nanda inquired from him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

He fed him sweet-rice. Though, bewildered by separation from Kṛṣṇa, the people of Vraja did not cook sweet-rice, etc., still for the sake of Uddhava they cooked. The washing of feet was done by servants, since he was a nephew.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**\[Nanda Mahārāja said:\] My dear most fortunate one, does Vasudeva, the son of Śūra, fare well, now that he is free and has rejoined his children and other relatives?**

**Комментарий:**

Worrying that asking about Kṛṣṇa would make his voice choke, Nanda first asks about the welfare of Vasudeva, his brother. Is he free from all dangers?

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Fortunately, because of his own sins, the sinful Kaṁsa has been killed, along with all his brothers. He always hated the saintly and righteous Yadus.**

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Does Kṛṣṇa remember us? Does he remember his mother and his friends and well-wishers? Does he remember the cowherds and their village of Vraja, of which he is the master? Does he remember the cows, Vṛndāvana forest and Govardhana Hill?**

**Комментарий:**

He mentions mother to indicate, pointing his finger, “You can see her miserable condition.” He is the master of Vraja (ātma-nātham). See! Without him, this Vraja is without a master, and its splendor is destroyed. Gāvaḥ should be gāḥ.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Will Govinda return even once to see his family? When may we glance upon his beautiful face, with its beautiful eyes, nose and smile?**

**Комментарий:**

O Uddhava! Will Govinda come to see at least once us, his relatives and parents who are burning in the fire of separation? Since you are dear to him, reveal his mood. O master of Vraja! “Why speak of once? Know that he is almost ready to come.” When (karhi) will we see his face? This indicates the great desire to see him. Drakṣyāma should be drakṣyāmaḥ.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**We were saved from the forest fire, the wind and rain, the bull and serpent demons—from all such insurmountable, deadly dangers—by Kṛṣṇa whose nature was very affectionate.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda remembers Kṛṣṇa’s powers. Su-mahātmanā means having very affectionate nature.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**As we remember the wonderful deeds Kṛṣṇa performed, his playful sidelong glances, his smiles and his words, O Uddhava, we forget all our material engagements.**

**Комментарий:**

Without seeing his face, we become disturbed. The actions like bathing and eating, become slack, though performed due to impressions like in the case of jīvan-muktas. Now how should we exist?

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**When we see the places where Mukunda enjoyed his sporting pastimes—the rivers, hills and forests he decorated with his feet—our minds become totally absorbed in him.**

**Комментарий:**

“Until he comes, pass your time looking at the Yamunā and Govardhana.” Seeing the places (uddeṣa) decorated with his feet, our minds see his sphūrti (tad-ātmatām) but again in external consciousness we feel difficulty in separation without him.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**In my opinion, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma must be two exalted devatās who have come to this planet to fulfill some great mission of the devatās. Such was foretold by Garga Ṛṣi.**

**Комментарий:**

For a moment Nanda becomes as if aware of Kṛṣṇa’s powers because of separation. I think the two who had appeared in my house (iha) in the form of sons by the good fortune of me and Vasudeva, are the Lords (surottamau). “Why did they come as your sons?” They came to benefit the devatās, by killing Kaṁsa, etc. Just as Garga spoke words with deep meaning, in the same way they manifest great powers, denying that they are not our sons. Thus he indicates his extreme misery.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**After all, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma killed Kaṁsa, as well as the wrestlers Cāṇūra and Muṣṭika and the elephant Kuvalayāpīḍa who was as strong as ten thousand elephants, just as a lion easily kills small animals.**

**Комментарий:**

His powers are described.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**With the ease of a royal elephant breaking a stick, Kṛṣṇa broke a powerful, giant bow three tālas long. He also held a mountain aloft for seven days with just one hand.**

**Комментарий:**

Tāla means a tāla tree which is 60 hastas high. He held the mountain with his left hand.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Here in Vṛndāvana, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma easily destroyed demons like Pralamba, Dhenuka, Arista, Tṛṇāvarta and Baka, who had themselves defeated both devatās and other demons.**

**Комментарий:**

These demons were killed by Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa (yena).

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus intensely remembering Kṛṣṇa again and again, Nanda Mahārāja, his mind completely attached to the Lord, felt extreme anxiety and fell silent, overcome by the strength of his vātsalya.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way, though remembering his powers, Nanda lamented, “Alas! I am separated from the mine of such qualities.” Because of the merging of the flow of Sarasvatī of their powers with the huge flow of Gaṅgā and Yamunā of his stirred up vātsalya for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, he, absorbed in vātsalya became silent. He was overwhelmed by the flow of vātsalya (prema-prasara).

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**As mother Yaśodā heard the descriptions of her son’s activities, she poured out her tears, and milk flowed from her breasts out of love.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda, who was a very sober father, because of his serious nature maintained self-control and welcomed Uddhava as a guest, asked about his welfare and spoke about Kṛṣṇa’s powers. But Yaśodā a mother, incapable of maintaining self-control, could not do any of that. She released tears completely drenching her clothes, etc., Drowning in waves of prema, she remained silent.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava then joyfully addressed Nanda Mahārāja, having clearly seen the supreme loving attraction he and Yaśodā felt for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing their attraction for Kṛṣṇa, understanding it, he spoke to Nanda, excellent (paramam) with prema superior to Vasudeva’s and Devaki’s by its type and quantity. He was joyful thinking himself fortunate to know their attraction to Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Uddhava said: O respectable Nanda! Certainly you and mother Yaśodā are the most praiseworthy persons in the entire world, since you have developed such a loving attitude toward Kṛṣṇa or Nārāyaṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

He praised them for their attraction to Kṛṣṇa. In this world, Vasudeva and Devakī are praiseworthy among the Lord’s devotees but I have understood from your attraction, etc., that you two are most praiseworthy, more than them, because you are always thinking of Kṛṣṇa (nārāyaṇe) like this. Nanda just said that he thought of his sons as the best of devatās (verse 23). Understanding that Nanda knew the power of his sons, he pacified them by speaking of their powers.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**These two Lords, Mukunda and Balarāma, are each the cause of the universe — the nimitta and upadāna cause. The independent, eternal lords enter the hearts of living beings and control their awareness of Brahman.**

**Комментарий:**

The two are Nārāyaṇa and gurus of the whole world. Possessing the śaktis of jīva and pradhāna, they are nimitta and upādāna (bīja-yonī) of the universe. They are jīva (puruṣaḥ) and matter (pradhāna) since the two śaktis are not different from the possessors of the śaktis. By svarūpa they are nimitta and by śakti they are upādāna. In this way, there is transformation in the śakti but not in the svarūpa. sa-viśeṣaṇe vidhi-niṣedhau viśesaṇam upasaṁkrāmataḥ sati viśeṣye bādhe Statements of affirmation and denial change the meaning of their particular descriptive elements if there is a contradiction to the principal subject. (Nyāya-vartikatātparya by Vācaspati Miśra). They enter the jīvas (bhūteṣu) as antaryāmī (anvīya) and can give high and low knowledge by their mercy. prajñā ca tasmāt prasṛtā purāṇi Because of the Lord, the jīva’s eternal knowledge spreads out everywhere. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad [4.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sveta-bs/4.18))

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Anyone, even a person in an impure state, who absorbs his mind in Kṛṣṇa for just a moment at the time of death, burns up all traces of sinful reactions and immediately attains the spiritual world with a spiritual body, which is self-illuminating.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa, the object of meditation for persons desiring liberation, keeps meditating on you both. With this mood he speaks in two verses. Having burned up (nirhṛtya) the subtle body (karmāśayam), one attains a spiritual body (brahma-mayaḥ), bright like the sun (arka-varṇaḥ) and goes to Vaikuṇṭha (parāṁ gatiṁ).

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**O great soul! You two have shown the highest anurāga to Kṛṣṇa, the revealer of all forms of God and jīvas, the shelter of Mahāviṣṇu, who appears in human form. What remains for you to do?**

**Комментарий:**

You two have shown the highest anurāga (bhāvaṁ) to Kṛṣṇa, who is the cause of (hetau) giving the highest auspiciousness (kāraṇe) to all living beings, and who is in a human form. Thus what remains for you to do? Nothing at all. The word tu means that all that remains is for Kṛṣṇa to pacify you. Sva-kṛtyam is an alternative version.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Infallible Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the devotees, will soon return to Vraja to satisfy his parents.**

**Комментарий:**

He reveals what he means in saying that the remaining action for Kṛṣṇa is to pacify them. Kṛṣṇa had promised Nanda, “We will come to see you, our relatives.” (SB [10.45.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/45.23)) That is without fail (acyutaḥ). Coming here, he will fulfill the desires (priyam) of his parents. He is lord of the Yadus (sātvatāṁ). Staying here, he will protect them.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Having killed Kaṁsa, the enemy of all the Yadus, in the wrestling arena, Kṛṣṇa will now surely fulfill his promise that he spoke to you by coming back.**

**Комментарий:**

What he promised to you in verse SB [10.45.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/45.23), he will fulfil. Present tense (karoti) is used to show that he is most trustworthy and that he speaks the truth.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**O most fortunate ones, do not lament. You will see Kṛṣṇa again very soon. He is present within you just as Paramātmā is in the hearts of all living beings, or as fire lies dormant in wood.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing his words that Kṛṣṇa would return, Yaśodā glanced at him. Still, seeing the two disturbed at heart, he speaks. O most fortunate couple, having perfect affection for your son! Do not lament. You will see Kṛṣṇa close by. “When will we see him?” He prospers in the hearts of all beings as conscious Paramātmā, the size of a thumb (jyotiḥ), manifesting like fire in wood. And even here he exists being invisible (aprakaṭaḥ). I inferred his presence when I entered Vraja from seeing the great joy of the place. He sees you from close up and you see him through bhāva. But soon you will see him with your eyes.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**For him no one is especially dear or despicable, superior or inferior, and yet he is not indifferent to anyone since he is free from false identity and equal in all circumstances.**

**Комментарий:**

“He does not come since he has obtained dear associates in Mathurā.” Fearing this objection he speaks with the idea that the way dear or inimical, superior or inferior – caused by karma – exist for the jīvas, they do not exist for Kṛṣṇa for he is free of karma. This is expressed in three verses. The verb asti is understood for all the negative statements. No one is especially dear to him by doing him favors. Not at all. No one is disfavored by him if they do offenses. A person is not praised (uttamaḥ) by Kṛṣṇa because of good qualities such as learning, nor is a person condemned (adhamaḥ) by him because of faults such as stupidity. Nor is anyone completely ignored (āsama) by him because they have neither good nor bad qualities. The proper cause for all this is that he does not have any false pride of having good qualities and no faults (amāninaḥ), being equal to all.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**He has no mother, no father, no wife, children or other relatives. No one is related to him, and yet no one is a stranger to him. He has no material body and no birth.**

**Комментарий:**

Since he has no cause arising from material elements, he has no mother or father. Thus, he has no children. He is not related by marriage to a wife (since Kṛṣṇa hasn’t married any princesses yet). Nor does he have relatives (whom he considers his own) because he is the cause of all effects. There is no stranger too because he has no relatives. He has no body generated from matter. And since he has no material body, he has no birth.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**He has no karma. Yet to enjoy his pastimes and deliver his saintly devotees, he manifests himself in different species.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, he does not have karma characterized by pious and impious acts which are the cause of attaining dear ones, etc. (as mentioned in verse 37). No one is dear than us. The repeated negatives are to establish their denial. However, he sees some as dear because of their devotional qualities and sees others as detestable because of their violence to devotees. That is explained in this verse. Appearing in his svarūpa forms similar to devatā, human or animal without regard for respectable or unrespectable species, he is fit to deliver the devotees. “He can deliver them just by his will. Why does he manifest in this world?” He does this for the sake of pastime (krīḍārtham). We can only speculate about the cause of your appearance. It has no cause except your desire for pastimes. (SB [10.2.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.39)) This should be said. Devotional qualities are attractive to the Lord, an ocean of good qualities. sādhavo hṛdayaṁ mahyam: the devotees are my heart. (SB [9.4.68](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/4.68)) Dependent on the devotees, he plays for his happiness, which is filled with the devotees’ happiness. Mad-bhaktānāṁ vinodārthaṁ karomi vividhāḥ kriyāḥ: I perform various actions to the pleasure of my devotees. (Padma Purāṇa) This being his nature, he will come here to perform suitable pastimes because you have greater vātsalyaprema than Vasudeva and Devakī. He is the friend of devotion. bhāva-grāhyam anīḍākhyam The Lord, being without body, is understood only by devotion. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad). Without beginning he is your son because of your love and now he is your son by birth. He himself says: gacchoddhava vrajaṁ saumya pitror naḥ prītam āvaha O Uddhava! Go to Vraja and satisfy our parents. (SB [10.46.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/46.3)) The apparent meaning cannot be insincere, for if it so then taking Uddhava’s hand to give him the responsibility of pacifying his parents, and asking him to go to Vraja would be futile.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Although beyond the three modes of material nature—goodness, passion and ignorance—the Lord accepts association with them as his play. Thus the unborn Supreme Lord utilizes the material modes to create, maintain and destroy.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of his nature to play, he even accepts the guṇas of prakṛti. Though beyond the guṇas he accepts the guṇas, bringing them to active state by his glance. But he is not overcome by them. He is beyond the guṇas by his qualities like his knowledge arising from his svarūpa (guṇaiḥ). Playing, he creates, maintains and destroys since he is devoid of changes like birth (ajaḥ).

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Just as a person who is whirling around perceives the ground to be turning, one who is affected by false ego thinks himself the doer, when actually only his mind is acting.**

**Комментарий:**

“Then why does it appear that the Lord is overcome by the guṇas?” By vision, when one turns around, the earth appears to be turning. When citta, matter which has become conscious by proximity to the jīva becomes the doer by thinking, “I am the matter (citta),” the pure ātmā appears to be the performer of actions like yajña and fighting. Similarly, the Lord appears to be overcome by creation in the guṇas. But he is never under their control since matter as the doer and the pure jīva as the doer of actions like yajña are refuted.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord is certainly not your son alone. Rather, since he is the ātmā of all beings and the Lord, he is the son, father and mother.**

**Комментарий:**

The sentiment of vātsalya makes one identify him as your son. It is not just a bodily relationship. If it were only bodily relationship then Kṛṣṇa would be the son of Brahmā or the universal form (since he manifests with the material world). That bhāva is in you two principally and not in Devakī and Vasudeva. Though he goes elsewhere for work, he will come to you. Uddhava explains this with philosophy in two verses. The Lord, full of six opulences (bhagavān), who takes away all suffering (hariḥ), is not your son alone. For those who show love for him as their son such as Upananda, he is their son. He is the form of complete knowledge and bliss (ātmā) and is the father for those with love for him as a father, etc. Or he is principally your son since you take him as your son with pure vātsalya, but not for others (na eva) since they lack such a mood. Thus, he is the creator of all (pitā), the maintainer of all (mātā) and the giver of results of karma (īśvaraḥ).

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Nothing can be said to exist independent of Acyuta—nothing heard or seen, nothing in the past, present or future, nothing moving or unmoving, great or small. He alone is everything, for he is the basis of everything.**

**Комментарий:**

O lord of Vraja! You know bhagavat-tattva since you said, “Son! A snake is swallowing me. Rescue one who is surrendered to you.” (SB [10.34.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/34.6)) Thus, do not lose your composure becoming overwhelmed due to separation. Control your emotions and deliberate. Your son is here as well since he is all-pervading. He consoles Nanda in this way. Everything seen and heard, everything in past, present and future, everything moving and nonmoving, great or small cannot be described (vācyam) at all (tarām) without Acyuta. He is everything since it is said: sarvaṁ samāpnoṣi tato ’si sarvam Since you extend over everything, you are everything. (BG [11.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/11.40)) He is fixed (paramārtha-bhūtaḥ): The wise accept the eternal spiritual goal. Without doubt temporary ingredients produce temporary products. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.14.21) He will manifest here because of both of your vātsalya. Do not lament.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**While Kṛṣṇa’s messenger continued speaking with Nanda, the night ended, O King. The women of the cowherd village rose from bed and, lighting lamps, worshiped their household deities. Then they began churning the yogurt into butter.**

**Комментарий:**

The night completely ended in this way. Nanda’s grief and Uddhava’s words to allay his grief did not stop. Then Uddhava went out to take a bath, but Nanda however reflected in his mind as follows. “I know that Kṛṣṇa is, Svayam Bhagavān, but I worship him, seeing him as my son. I know his vilāsa expansion Nārāyaṇa as my master and worship him with that bhāva. Kṛṣṇa knows us as his parents since he said to me, “O father! Go to Vraja,” (SB [10.45.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/45.23)) and he said to Uddhava, “Satisfy our parents” (verse 3). He was joyful with us acting as parents, offering chewed betel nut, climbing on our laps, embracing and kissing the face, etc., and without them he was not joyful. We experienced that repeatedly. When tied up by his mother for the offense of breaking the pot, his face withered. And when released by me, his face became joyful. We saw that at that time. Though he is the supreme Lord, he accepted being tied up, being scolded and being instructed by us, who were acting as parents. He was overjoyed internally and externally by these actions. Therefore, after performing remaining duties, the friend of bhāva will return since he said vidhāya suhrḍāṁ sukham as soon as we have given some happiness to your well-wishing friends. (SB [10.45.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/45.23)) Let us two spend a few days in difficulty till then.” The gopīs rising at brāhma-muhūrta, lighting lamps, worshipping the entrances (vāstūn), churned yogurt.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**As they pulled on the churning ropes with their bangled arms, the women of Vraja shone with the splendor of their jewels, which reflected the lamps’ light. Their hips, breasts and necklaces moved about, and their faces, anointed with reddish kuṅkuma, glowed radiantly with the luster of their earrings reflecting from their cheeks.**

**Комментарий:**

The beauty of the gopīs churning yogurt is described. The gopīs especially shone with radiant jewels of their bracelets and medallions more than even the lamps. Lighting lamps is for creating auspiciousness. Another reason is given for shining. The gopīs had groups of bracelets on their arms which pulled the churning ropes. Their necklaces, breasts and hips trembled. Their cheeks shone with earrings. They had red kuṅkuma from Bāhlīka province (Balkh) on their faces.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**As the ladies of Vraja loudly sang the glories of lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, their songs blended with the sound of their churning, ascended to the sky and dissipated all inauspiciousness in every direction.**

**Комментарий:**

They sang with great absorption. Mention of his lotus-eyes indicate his prominent beauty. Their singing, most skillful touched the sky. Another reason is given. It was mixed with the sound of churning. The sound spread to the ten directions. Yoga-māyā, the śakti of the Lord, as previously, at the end of night, showed this manifestation related to the Lord’s presence, to give bliss to Uddhava. Otherwise it would have been impossible to wear attractive kuṅkuma, ornaments and clothing since it would indicate bliss for persons grieving in separation.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**When the powerful sun had risen, the people of Vraja noticed the golden chariot in front of Nanda Mahārāja’s doorway. “Who does this belong to?” they asked.**

**Комментарий:**

Vrajaukasaḥ (people of Vraja) refers to the gopīs who were in separation.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**“Perhaps Akrūra has returned—he who fulfilled Kaṁsa’s desire by taking lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa to Mathurā.**

**Комментарий:**

They speak in anger. He fulfills the desires of Kaṁsa, his master — he caused his death. He is cruel.

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**“Is he going to use our flesh to offer funeral oblations for his master, who is dead?” As the women were speaking in this way, Uddhava appeared, having finished his early-morning duties.**

**Комментарий:**

Having already done his job, why has he come again? Thinking thus they speculate about his task. Will he accomplish the dead Kaṁsa’s funeral rites through us? Will he offer piṇḍa using our flesh?

## Chapter 47 - The Song of the Bee (Bhramara-gītā)

### Text 1-2

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The young women of Vraja smiled upon seeing Kṛṣṇa’s servant, who had long arms, whose eyes resembled a newly grown lotus, who wore a yellow garment and a lotus garland, and whose lotus-like face glowed with brightly polished earrings. “Who is this handsome man?” the gopīs asked. “Where has he come from, and whom does he serve? He is wearing Kṛṣṇa’s clothes and ornaments!” Saying this, the gopīs eagerly crowded around Uddhava, whose shelter was the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

In the forty-seventh chapter, Uddhava hears the gopīs’ citra-jalpa, makes the gopīs blissful by the messages, praises them and returns to Mathurā. Having pacified the parents, he met with the gopīs in a solitary place after waiting for an opportunity. Two verses describe this. These verses are related to the third verse starting with rahasi. They saw Uddhava, the follower of Kṛṣṇa. They concluded that he was Kṛṣṇa’s follower because he wore yellow cloth. When Uddhava had departed, Kṛṣṇa had given him his own upper cloth and lotus garland. They determined that he was a follower of Kṛṣṇa because in Vraja too his associates wore attire similar to his. They had pure smiles (śuci-smitāḥ) because of the joy of seeing dress that reminded them of Kṛṣṇa. Another version has suvismitāḥ: they were astonished how someone else could look like Kṛṣṇa. He is attractive to see (apīvya-darśanaḥ). Where has he come from? Whose follower is he? He is wearing clothing, tilaka, hair band, etc., (veṣa), bracelets, and earrings (bhūṣaṇaḥ) similar to Kṛṣṇa’s. Saying this they surrounded him immediately without reserve, because they were eager (utsukāḥ). They lost discrimination because they could not tolerate the time. Later also, the reason for lack of reserve is that they had ascertained him to be a leading associate of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Bowing their heads in humility, the gopīs duly honored Uddhava with their shy, smiling glances and pleasing words. They took him to a quiet place, seated him comfortably and began to question him, for they recognized him to be a messenger from Kṛṣṇa, the master of the goddess of fortune.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding that Uddhava had come secretly as a message bearer of Kṛṣṇa they inquired from him. Politely they bowed their heads. Kṛṣṇa was the master of the wealth of Vraja (ramā-pateḥ) but now he was situated in Mathurā. Uddhava is described. He was welcomed as guest by their shyness, characterized by covering their heads which was natural to well-bred women. Along with that they smiled because they understood that he was a follower of their lover. They glanced and uttered fine words (sūnṛtam). “Welcome. Hope you are well!” They also welcomed him as guest with what was available, as appropriate, such as foot water. He was seated on a seat which was offered as an aṅga of the worship.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**\[The gopīs said:\] We know that you are the personal servant of Kṛṣṇa, the chief of the Yadus, and that you have come here on the order of your master, who desires to give pleasure to his parents.**

**Комментарий:**

We know you. What need is there to ask questions? The reason for his coming is explained: you have been sent by your master (bhartrā). What is the purpose? To please (priya-cikīrṣayā) his parents. Not coming personally, he sent you because of fearing criticism from the public. But he does not love his parents.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**We see nothing else he might consider worth remembering in these cow pastures of Vraja. But the bonds of affection for one’s family members are difficult to break, even for a sage.**

**Комментарий:**

Except for desiring to please his parents, we do not see anyone worthy of Kṛṣṇa’s remembrance in Gokula. “Why should the parents be remembered?” Bondage of affection to parents and others are difficult to give up even for those who have taken sannyāsa (muneḥ). They can be forgotten only with difficulty. But he suddenly gave up such attachments. Thus, he is hard-hearted.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**The friendship shown toward others—those who are not family members—is motivated by personal interest, and thus it is a pretense that lasts only until one’s purpose is fulfilled. Such friendship is just like the interest men take in women, or bees in flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

“O women of Vraja! I have been sent by Kṛṣṇa to please you too who are like the very life of my master.” Friendship with others who are not relatives are motivated by self-interest. It is a disregard of all mutual interests (yāvad-arthaviḍamanam). Yāvat means “all” according to Amara-kośa. Such friendship is a criticism of all goals of mutual interest for everyone — the person who does the friendship, the person with whom the friendship is done and the person who caused the friendship — since in absence of a common goal, the friendship is given up. They indicate their intended embarrassment on the pretext of an example. Friendship made by men with women who are similar to flowers (sumanaḥsv iva), having beauty, fragrance and softness, or as a pun, friendship made by men with women who have splendid minds and who are singly devoted to them is like that made by the six-legged bees with flowers. The bees, one and half animals, drink once the flowers with fragrance and other qualities and then give them up because of their own fault of being fickle in nature. Similarly, men also enjoy and give up women though dedicated to those men, and though they have beauty and other qualities for his enjoyment. This is criticized because friendship is given up. Since later we married Kṛṣṇa by Gandharva rites, we are his relatives. That is famous in the world. Thus there is no fear of giving up friendship.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Prostitutes abandon a penniless man, subjects an incompetent king, students their teacher once they have finished their education, and priests a man who has remunerated them for a sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

Examples are given of friendship which ceases when self-interest ceases in two verses. The prostitute abandons the man with no money (niḥsvam). The citizens give up a king who is incapable of ruling. The hotṛ and other priests (ṛtvijaḥ) give up the sponsor once he pays the donation.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Birds abandon a tree when its fruits are gone, guests a house after they have eaten, animals a forest that has burnt down, and lovers the woman they have enjoyed, even though she remains attached to them.**

**Комментарий:**

Birds give up the tree whose fruits are over. The paramour gives up a woman though she has love for him (ratām). Singular (striyam) is used to indicate a type. “Kṛṣṇa is the paramour of the gopīs. Why do they give an example of a paramour?” True, he is just famous as being that. But actually, he married them by Gāndharva rites. The prostitute and others give up a lusty man when they do not receive money, etc. Paramours give up women who materially love them. But we having developed prema for Kṛṣṇa from childhood, not having material love, we were still rejected by him. This shows his extreme cruelty.

### Text 9-10

**Перевод:**

**Thus speaking, the gopīs, whose words, bodies and minds were fully dedicated to Govinda, put aside all their regular work now that Kṛṣṇa’s messenger, Uddhava, had arrived among them. Constantly remembering the activities their beloved Kṛṣṇa had performed in his childhood and youth, they sang about them and cried without shame.**

**Комментарий:**

The gopīs gave up their regular work because they began to manifest mādhurya-bhāva for Kṛṣṇa through their words in private. They cried on remembering his activities starting from childhood to kaiśora age. Because prema manifested from childhood, it is shown that his svarūpa is the only cause of their prema. By that even in kaiśora they had prema.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**One of the gopīs, while meditating on her previous association with Kṛṣṇa, saw a honeybee before her and imagined it to be a messenger sent by her beloved. Thus she spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

This gopī (kācit) is the chief among them, Śrī Rādhā-devī. Kācit can mean “she who has knowledge (cit) completely (ā) in the happiness of prema (ke).” Or it means “she who increases (ācinoti) the happiness of prema (kam) to everyone.” She meditated on association of Kṛṣṇa with the city women. While in this mental state she saw a bee whose whiskers were tinged with yellow pollen suddenly appear. Imagining the bee to be a messenger sent by Kṛṣṇa to please her, she spoke. On this pretext she spoke to Uddhava. Some say that Kṛṣṇa had come in the form of bee to hear her prema-jalpa.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**The gopī said: O honeybee, O friend of a cheater, don’t touch my feet with your whiskers, which are smeared with the kuṅkuma that rubbed onto Kṛṣṇa’s garland when it was crushed by the breasts of a rival lover! Let Kṛṣṇa satisfy the women of Mathurā. One who sends a messenger like you will certainly be ridiculed in the Yadus’ assembly.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to Rādhikā-devī, the supreme queen of Vṛndāvana. By her mercy I can understand the meaning of her words. Full of sulky anger, experiencing divyonmāda, she speaks to the bee. O bee (madhupa)! Or as a pun: O drunkard! Madhu can mean liquor or flower sap according to Amara-kośa. O friend of cheaters (kitava-bandho)! You are a friend of the cheater Kṛṣṇa, who said, “I cannot repay your debt. You are faultless.” (SB [10.32.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.22)) “I will come.” (SB [10.39.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/39.35)) The bee is a friend of Kṛṣṇa because it is his messenger, because they both have same color, they have similar names (madhupa and Madhupati) and because they have similar activities since drunkards and cheaters are generally friends. She speaks again thinking the bee is touching her feet to please her when the bee thinks her feet are raṅgaṇa flowers and desires to drink their honey. Do not touch my feet. Let independent women who are rich in sulky anger be pleased by you. Why touch my feet? In forbidding the bee to touch her feet, she gives details. Do not touch my feet with your whiskers laden with kuṅkuma from his garland which was crushed (vilulita) by the kuṅkuma-dusted breasts of a rival woman whom he has now accepted as a beloved in Mathurā. Vi in vilulita indicate very tight embraces. Naḥ (we) is in the plural to indicate her own group of gopīs or it indicates her pride. By the touch of a person who has drunk wine, my feet will become impure. Remain at a distance. You have come to please me without even washing off that kuṅkuma. How thoughtless of you.
