Seeing that kuṅkuma only increases the anger. This is the symptom of an intoxicated person like you. “Since you are offended, I will go to Mathurā. He will only come and please you.” Garga Muni said that previously Kṛṣṇa was the son of Vasudeva (SB [10.8.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.14)). Sometime previously he was Vasudeva’s son. Now, hiding that he is the son of Nanda, as the lord of the Yādavas (madhu-patiḥ), let him please those angry women (māninīnām) who understand that he is a cheater of women who are attached to him in this way. What chance does he have to please me? Madhu-pati can also mean master of intoxication. This indicates his lack of discrimination and lack of friendship. We have nothing to do with him. She shows disrespect. His attempts at pleasing though considered as his own glorification, will have opposite effect. He will be mocked in the Yadu assembly. That is not so in the assembly of cowherds since the cowherds have offered him their lives. She does not mention his secret pastimes which are sometimes known. “How would the Yadus know?” You are his messenger, bearing marks of his enjoyment with women. It is not surprising that you reveal his mercy. This is called prajalpa: When a woman utters rough words filled with envy, hatred and pride, with indications of insult, it is called prajalpa. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 14.199) Words like cheater indicate envy. Rival women (sapatnya) indicate hatred. “Don’t touch my feet” indicates pride. Insult is indicated by “please the city women.” Rough words are indicated with “You will be mocked in the Yadu assembly.”

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**After making us drink the enchanting nectar of his lips only once, Kṛṣṇa suddenly abandoned us, just as you might quickly abandon some flowers. How is it, then, that Goddess Padmā willingly serves his lotus feet? Alas! The answer must certainly be that her mind has been stolen away by his deceitful words.**

**Комментарий:**

“O mistress! This is my natural yellow color. It is not the marks of kuṅkuma from his amorous acts. He, whose mind is fixed only on you, does not associate with other young women even in dreams. Why are you angry with him like this?” He made us drink just once the extraordinary sweet nectar of his lips. The causative (he made us drink) indicates that he made us the recipients by force and trickery. Then he gave us up suddenly. Though they drank many times, she says once indicating the great thirst due to attraction. That nectar was bewildering (mohinīm), destroying the intelligence producing intolerable greed. Due to having no example of drinking she only gives an example of giving up. He is like you, the bee, that, having once drunk the nectar from a jasmine flower, out of fickleness, gives it up. Enjoying us once, he gave us up. Why should we not become angry? Saying that he does not associate with other women even in dreams is a false statement. Why does Lakṣmī, queen of Vaikuṇṭha, desiring him, come to him who is separated from us in Mathurā, and serve his lotus feet? Her heart has been stolen by talks about him. She, being innocent, is bewildered by the talks of those who do not know his nature. But we, being intelligent, are not like that. This is an example of parijalpa. When the woman reveals her cleverness with wit by revealing her lover’s cruelty, cunning, unsteadiness, and other qualities as well, it is called parijalpa. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 14.201) His cunningness is revealed by making them drink once and having bewildering lips. Suddenly giving them up is his cruelty. Fickleness is illustrated by taking other women, like the bee. Ādi (in cāpalyādi) indicates his ungratefulness and his lack of love. Their cleverness is illustrated in citing Lakṣmī’s simple conduct.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**O bee, why do you sing here so much about the Lord of the Yadus, in front of us homeless people? These topics are old news to us. Better you sing about your friend Kṛṣṇa in front of his new girlfriends, the burning desire in whose breasts he has now relieved. Those ladies will surely give you the charity you are begging.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the bee which hummed and came to her was brushed away, it did not go away. Rādhā speaks thinking that the bee wants to please her by its quality of singing. O six-legged creature! Why do you sing in our assembly? And why sing so much here? And why do you sing about the lord of the Yadus here? Why do you sing old news here? Does the old news about the lord of the Yadus please you? And why do you sing in front of us at this place? As an animal and a half, you are very ignorant, since by singing about our prince of Vraja as the lord of the Yadus you make us suffer. “O mistress! Since I am coming from your lover in Mathurā, give me something.” We are now living in the forest, having given up our houses because of him. Thus, we cannot give anything to you. However, we are not angry with you, a fool. Since you live by singing, we will show a place for singing. Vijaya means he who is endowed or devoid of victory in love battle. Kṛṣṇa is vijaya and a friend (sakha). You should sing in front of the beloveds of that Lord of Yadus. Your friend Kṛṣṇa, wins over them in love battle or is won over by them. Sing infront of those city women who are attracted to him. Then the pain in their breasts destroyed, they will give you what you desire. You should worship (iṣṭāḥ) those women by your song. This is vijalpa. The wise consider vijalpa to be leering statements directed to Kṛṣna with evident indignation containing indications of deep pride. The last half of the verse shows envy and pride. The whole verse mocks Kṛṣṇa with a scornful side glance.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**In heaven, on earth or in the subterranean sphere, what women are unavailable to him? He simply arches his eyebrows and smiles with deceptive charm, and they all become his. The supreme goddess herself worships the dust of his feet, so what is our position in comparison? But at least those who are wretched can chant his name, Uttamaḥśloka.**

**Комментарий:**

“O mistress! Crowning jewel of his beloveds! Thinking of you day and night, he is pained by love. He does not feel any joy within except for your mercy.” She answers with envy. What women in the three worlds are not available to him? None. Tad is an indeclinable. He is described. He expands his attractive brows and smiles with deception. The deceiver controlling them by that brow and smile, enjoying them once, gives them up just like us, since he always like new lovers. What to speak of devatā women, Lakṣmī (bhūtiḥ) is controlled by his smile and brow. She worships the dust of his feet. This is a statement indicating accepting a low position to serve him. If that is so, what to speak of us humans? What will happen to us, situated in Vṛndāvana? This is a statement of humility. This indicates hatred clothed in pride, with increasing quivering of her voice while smiling. Moreover (api ca), the word uttama-śloka can be applied to the person who is merciful to wretched, suffering people. It is false to describe Kṛṣṇa like that since he lacks that. This is ujjalpa. The wise say ujjalpa is abusing Kṛṣna with indignation for his deception, through jealousy and pride. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 14.205) The first part of the verse expresses his deception. The third line shows envy with pride. The fourth line shows abuse with envy.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Keep your head off my feet! I know what you’re doing. You expertly learned diplomacy from Mukunda, and now you come as his messenger with flattering words. But he abandoned those persons who for his sake alone gave up their children, husbands and all other relations. He’s simply ungrateful. Why should I make up with him now?**

**Комментарий:**

The bee, buzzing softly, approaches her pink, fragrant lotus feet, greedy for its fragrance. O mistress! Do not be angry. Once hear my plea. Thinking that the bee begs, seeming to offer respects, she speaks. Give up my foot which you have held on your head. Go far from here. You have learned entreaty by acting as a messenger with pleasing words from Mukunda. Thus I know his and your conduct. I cannot be cheated like Lakṣmī. “O devī! Do not quarrel with your beloved, who is most dear to yourself. Forgiving once his offense, you should meet with him using me, sent by him.” He has given up us, who have given up husbands, children and others, in-laws, etc., for his sake. He is ungrateful, he does not know the favor that is done. Or he did not give his heart to us who are devoted to him (akṛta-cetāḥ): he is merciless. Or making (akṛtaḥ) us give up our husbands for his own purpose, he attained us (itāḥ) and gave us up. Is such a cruel cheater (asmin) worthy of reconciling with? Not at all. This is sañjalpa. The wise say sañjalpa is utterances about Kṛṣṇa’s ungratefulness and other bad qualities, through deeply sarcastic words with indications of censure. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 14.207) The first two lines show sarcasm and censure. The last two lines describe his ungratefulness and merciless nature.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Like a hunter, he cruelly shot the king of the monkeys with arrows. Because he was conquered by a woman, he disfigured another woman who came to him with lusty desires. And even after consuming the gifts of Bali Mahārāja, he bound him up with ropes as if he were a crow. So let us give up all friendship with this dark-complexioned boy, even if we can’t give up talking about him.**

**Комментарий:**

“Kṛṣṇa is not hard-hearted. Rather he is very soft-hearted and very affectionate. He is meditating on you only.” Not only now is he like this but previously also. This is understood from previous actions of avatāras. That Kṛṣṇa previously also as Rāma, killed Vāli, king of the monkeys, like a hunter. He did this devoid of dharma of a hunter (alubdha-dharmā). A hunter does not kill a monkey since his flesh is inedible. It is not that since he is the king of the world, his killing Vāli who has engaged in injustice is proper since killing him while hiding is adharma. He disfigured a woman, Śūrpaṇakhā, though she was full of desire (kāmayānāṁ), cutting off her ear and nose so that others could not enjoy her since he is extremely cruel. He was not detached though he had matted locks and wore bark clothing. He was controlled by a woman (strī-jitaḥ). He was attached to Sītā. Though he was a kṣatriya he did not follow kṣatriya dharma of following justice. Previous to that also, as Vāmana, though taking (attvā) the gift of the three worlds given by Bali, he tied up Bali who followed dharma. He was like a crow that takes food and then surrounds the person who gave the food. Acting as a brāhmaṇa he did not follow brāhmaṇa conduct of being peaceful and free of fraud. One should not say that since he was worshipped by Aditi, the result of that worship, which is taking the kingdom from Bali, is proper, since using trickery in doing it is adharma. Therefore one should not make friendship with Kṛṣṇa, who is black inside and outside. Black means extremely impure. Since by them one will definitely become afraid. “Then remain silent.” It is difficult to give up speaking about him, though he has been given up. This is avajalpa. Statements which show that attachment to him is unadvisable because of his hard nature, his lust and his cheating behavior, along with expressions of malice and fear is called avajalpa. (Ujjvala-nīla-maṇi 14.209) His hard nature is shown by his killing Bali. His lust is indicated by his attachment to Sītā. His cheating is in dealing with Bali Mahārāja. Not dealing with a black person indicates his being unqualified for being attached to, fear and malice. Rādhā’s words of knowledge of her lover as Svayaṁ Bhagavān arise from her feelings of separation.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**To hear about the pastimes that Kṛṣṇa regularly performs is nectar for the ears. For those who relish just a single drop of that nectar, even once, their dedication to material duality is ruined. Many such persons have suddenly given up their wretched homes and families and, themselves becoming wretched, traveled here to Vṛndāvana to wander about like birds, begging for their living.**

**Комментарий:**

It is not surprising that we suffer in making friendship with him. Even topics of his pastimes cause pain to the world. His pastimes performed at every moment are independent play, like actions of a child. They are nectar for the ears, giving pleasure to the ear by their sound but the meaning is not pleasing to the mind. Even a drop (vipruṭ) of that nectar, not plenty, tasted once, even from far off, destroys the dualities (dvandva-dharmā) of experiencing hot and cold or the conduct of couples. Hearing about the activities of the hard-hearted person, approaching his hardness, men and women give up mutual affection and become devoid of enjoying happiness. It is like complete destruction. “O mistress! How can that be understood?” Just hearing about him, people, giving up house and family, father, etc., who are distressed (dīnaṁ) since they do not obtain food because of lack of livelihood, and becoming miserable themselves, carrying just a copper bowl because of disturbed minds, pained from not obtaining food, many thousands of people, not two or three, beg for grains of wheat and wander like birds. Just as birds take shelter of trees, they take shelter of the base of trees and stay. Seeing them, one can understand. His pastimes are like cool drink mixed with powdered dhustūra seeds. Śukadeva, the speaker, is the killer dressed as a saint. His father Vyāsa is the constructor of the net of the Purāṇa (to catch the birds). Kṛṣṇa is their instructor since he is the Supreme Lord. Giving grief to all people is his supreme lordship. There are many suggestions in this verse. Here comparing devotees to birds, it is suggested that they give him up because of the pain. These are statements filled with regret. This is called abhijalpa: Remorseful statements to give up Kṛṣṇa because of his inflicting pain on innocent people treating them like birds are called abhijalpa. (Ujjvala-nīla-maṇi 14.211) Not desiring anything except Kṛṣṇa, worshipping him, they quickly attain him. This is suggested in this verse by the ācārya of the path of bhakti, Rādhā-devī.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Faithfully taking his deceitful words as true, we became just like the black deer’s foolish wives, who trust the cruel hunter’s song. Thus we repeatedly felt the sharp pain of lust caused by the touch of his nails. O messenger, please talk about something besides Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

“O devī! If you know he is like this, why did you make friendship with him?” We, his wives, accepting his deceitful words such as “I cannot repay you,” (SB [10.32.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.22)) as truth (ṛtaṁ) with faith (śraddadhānāḥ), became ignorant. This is like the deer’s wives who have faith in the sweet song of the hunter, which is their death. As the deer’s wives feel (dadṛśuḥ) the shot of the arrow, the result of Text 20\] The Song of the Bee 269 the song, we also by the touch of his nails experienced the sharp pains of love. Therefore, O messenger, jester! Speak other news. Give up speaking about him which causes suffering. This is called ājalpa. Where there is discussion of his crooked nature and how that gives sorrow, whereas other persons give happiness, with disgust, it is called ājalpa. (Ujjvala-nīla-maṇi 14.213) In this verse that his crookedness, his talks giving grief, and other topics giving happiness are clear.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**O friend of my dear one, has my beloved sent you here again? I should honor you, friend, so please choose whatever boon you wish. But why have you come back here to take us to him, who finds it difficult to give up his relationships in Mathurā? After all, gentle bee, his consort is the goddess Śrī, and she is always with him, staying upon his chest.**

**Комментарий:**

Due to her unmāda, not recognizing the bee which was wandering around there, thinking that it had gone to Mathurā because of being disrespected and then returned because of being sent back by Kṛṣṇa, she speaks. O friend of our beloved (priya-sakha)! Though struck by the arrow of my rough words, because of your good qualities, you have returned. This I have understood. Have you been sent by my beloved who is most affectionate, not considering my offenses? Then choose something (varaya). What do you want (anurundhe)? I will do it. You are respected by me. “O devī! I choose that you come to Mathurā.” Saying, “I will come to you,” she speaks further. Why do you take me to him, whose amorous relationships are difficult to give up? Seeing him who is like that, my anger will arise again. Taking me there would be unsuitable. “Since there is no woman there, how can he have relationships with women there?” O gentle one with simple mind! His consort Lakṣmī, who has come to him who is without us, is with him, on his chest always, dominating him. This is pratijalpa. Humble statements expressing respect for the messenger, but with refusal to meet Kṛṣṇa, who has permanent relationships with other women is called pratijalpa. (Ujjvala-nīla-maṇi 14.215) Respecting the messenger, accepting his words, and then not accepting his words on understanding that Kṛṣṇa is unsuitable are clear in the verse.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava, does Kṛṣṇa now reside in Mathurā? Does he remember his father’s houses, his relatives and the cowherd boys? O great soul! Does he ever talk about us, his maidservants? When will he lay on our heads his aguru-scented hand?**

**Комментарий:**

Ah! What have I been saying? I have not asked what I should have asked. With repentance she speaks with reverence. Api indicates a question. O messenger (bata)! By convention ārya-putra refers to the son of King Nanda. But he is actually our husband. Is he in Mathurā? Does he not desire to go elsewhere from there? Staying close to Mathurā there is possibility of coming to Vraja. Or does he stay there to fulfill his duties, while overwhelmed with memories of our affection for him? Does he remember his father’s house, nicely cleansed and decorated, its members overcome with confusion by separation? Does he remember relatives like Upananda, fainting in separation, and cowherds like Subala? Does he sometimes talk of us maidservants? When city women do not know how to serve him using clothing, ornaments, garlands, rasa and fragrance, and various types of music and deep riddles, which are attractive to him, does he speak of us, skillful at such service? Longing for our service, when will our beloved, coming here, place his arm, anointed with aguru by us, on our heads, pacifying us by saying, “There are no persons such as you, skillful at serving in prema and thus I will not go anywhere at any time, giving you up?” This is sujalpa. Sujalpa refers to asking about Kṛṣṇa with simplicity, gravity, humility, unsteadiness and eagerness. (Ujjvalanīla-maṇi 14.217) The first line expresses simplicity. The second line expresses gravity, by not mentioning herself. The third line expresses humility by speaking of being his maidservants. The fourth line expresses unsteadiness and eagerness. Their statements of anger out of pride, which are their experience of love for him are very attractive to him, who is portrayed as unfit for friendship. na tathā rocate vedaḥ purāṇādyās tathetare yathā tāsāṁ tu gopīnāṁ bhartsanāgarbhitaṁ vacaḥ I am not attracted to the Vedas, Purāṇas and other scriptures as I am to the words of the gopīs cloaked in scolding. In this way, citra-jalpa, a type of divyonmāda, is of ten types. When the friendliness of the lover who has gone far away, is perceived, then there is a manifestation of deep anger, filled with emotion and with intense longing, with an appearance of illusion. That is divyonmāda, a special vilāsa of mohana, the excellent portion of mahābhāva. It is generally manifested in Rādhā. This is the conclusion of the knowers of bhāva.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having heard this, Uddhava then tried to pacify the gopīs, who were most eager to see Kṛṣṇa. He thus spoke the following with the message of their beloved.**

**Комментарий:**

Directly hearing the talks, as described, which are a transformation of prema, which were not heard previously even indirectly from others, when Rādhā had stopped speaking, he began speaking to the other gopīs, unable to speak directly to Rādhā due to respect. He spoke to check their intense disturbance of prema by informing them of the greatness of Kṛṣṇa’s powers and prema, and to ally their feelings of wretchedness by praising them. Otherwise it would be impossible for them to hear the message.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Uddhava said: Certainly you gopīs are all-successful and are universally worshiped because you have dedicated your minds in this way to the Supreme Lord, Vāsudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

Aho indicates astonishment. This is something never seen or heard before. You are certainly (sma) successful (pūrnārthāḥ). You have Svayam Bhagavān (pūrṇa) as wealth (arthaḥ). Thus, you are worshipped by Brahmā and others. He uses yūyam and bhavatyaḥ (which have the same meaning) repeatedly for them out of great respect. The reason why they are worshipped is given. You have offered your minds to Kṛṣṇa in a way not seen in other devotees.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Devotional service unto Kṛṣṇa is attained by charity, strict vows, austerities, fire sacrifices, japa, study of Vedic texts, controlling the senses and by the performance of many other auspicious practices.**

**Комментарий:**

Your bhakti is very rare. Bhakti, a taste for hearing topics of the Lord, is accomplished by charity, etc., which are performed without material desire. This is shown by positive concomitance by the verse sa vai puṁsāṁ paro dharmaḥ (SB [1.2.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.6)) and by negative concomitance by the verse dharmaḥ svanuṣṭhitaḥ puṁsāṁ (SB [1.2.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.8)) in the First Canto. Among them, vrata refers to niyamas. Tapas means austerity. Samyama is control of the senses. Others auspicious practices indicates yoga, etc.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**By your great fortune you have established an unexcelled standard of pure devotion for the Lord, most worthy of praise—a standard even the sages can hardly attain.**

**Комментарий:**

Your bhakti is the best of all. That bhakti has been performed by you. Āśaṁsāyāṁ bhūtavac ca: desire for a future event can be expressed using the past tense. (Pāṇini 3.3.132) This did not exist before now. From now on it will be preached to the people. Diṣṭyā means “by good fortune to the people.”

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**It is good fortune that you have left your sons, husbands, bodily comforts, relatives and homes in favor of the Supreme Lord, who is known as Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Their manner of engaging in bhakti is clearly explained in this verse. Giving up attachment to sons, etc., which are objects of possession and ‘I’-ness you accepted Supreme Lord known as Kṛṣṇa as your lover. This is good fortune for the people. Seeing and hearing of such actions of yours, which are the good fortune of the world, people will practice similarly. He says, “You gave up your bodies,” to include those who were kept back in their houses (during the rāsa dance and thus gave up their bodies).

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**You possess the highest prema for the Lord, O most glorious gopīs. Your separation from Kṛṣṇa has shown me great mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing your bhakti, I have attained perfect good fortune. You have mahā-bhāva for Kṛṣṇa, who cannot even be seen by others. Prema for him is rare for others, but your prema has been made qualified for mahā-bhāva (sarvātma-bhāva), the seventh stage of prema, by the Lord. The prema of Lakṣmī and others is not qualified (as mahābhāva). Just as the sun spreads heat to all as its dharma and the moon spreads coolness to all by its dharma, that bhāva spreads everywhere as its nature (sarvātma-bhāvaḥ). Your separation is greatly merciful to me since you made me hear your citra-jalpa of divyonmāda. If your separation did not take place, I would not be sent here and neither would I hear this.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**My good ladies, now please hear your beloved’s message, which I, the confidential servant of my master, have come here to bring you.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Uddhava! Stop praising us and yourself. Tell us some message that he has given to us.” He then showed the written letter and spoke. “But what is the use of his message, by which we will not attain him quickly? I have come here for that purpose since he will definitely come quickly. He produces respect. I do confidential work for my master. This indicates that since Uddhava is so intimate to him, he is qualified to give his message and that the message is also confidential. O chaste women! You are the sole recipients of this message.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: You are never actually separated from me, for I am the Soul of all creation. Just as the elements of nature—ether, air, fire, water and earth—are present in every created thing, so I am present within everyone’s mind, life air and senses, and also within the physical elements and the modes of material nature.**

**Комментарий:**

Uddhava speaks what the Lord said. Perfect tense (uvāca) is used in the sense of “beyond one’s comprehension”. I will repeat his message. But I cannot understand what he said (uvāca). You gopīs should try to understand its meaning. Being the cleverest, he wrote a letter with two meanings for the clever gopīs. The first meaning is a statement according to adhyātma scriptures, but the second one hints according to rasa scriptures. Just as at the beginning of the rāsa dance he gave instructions on dharma as the external meaning. The instructions on amorous enjoyment were the second meaning hidden within. These instructions are similar. You are not separated from me. Then why are you disturbed? “How can this be?” Because I am the antaryāmī of everyone (sarvātmanā). The Lord enters all and is the ruler of men. (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 3.11) sarvasya cāhaṁ hṛti sanniviṣṭaḥ I am situated in everyone’s heart. (BG [15.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.15)) Thus you are not separated from me as the antaryāmī. Rather you are united with the antaryāmī by the mind and intelligence, forms of the body (sarvātmānā). Ātmā means body, mind and intelligence according to Viśva. When you are fixed in your mind and intelligence, you will definitely meet me quickly. You should be confident, not disturbed. I am everywhere since I am the cause of upādāna (material cause). Why do you think you are separate from me? Just as ether and other elements exist in moving and nonmoving beings (bhūteṣu), I am the shelter of the effects like mind, etc., and the guṇas such as sattva, etc., their cause, since I am their chief cause. I am spread through them. Why do you think of separation? (Another meaning) I take shelter of the mind, prāṇas, intelligence, and sense objects such as sound, etc., (indriya-guṇa) of you, who always meditate on me. Taking shelter of them, I always manifest myself in them. Thus you should be convinced of this.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**By myself I create, sustain and withdraw myself within myself by the power of my personal energy, which comprises the material elements, the senses and the modes of nature.**

**Комментарий:**

“Pradhāna is the support of the universe made of elements and senses. Brahmā is the creator. Viṣṇu is the preserver. Śiva is the destroyer. How are you spread everywhere?” I create, preserve and destroy the universe made of elements, senses and guṇas (ātmānam) in myself (ātmani), the support, by myself (ātmanā). “How are you, who are condensed consciousness, in the form of the universe made of dull matter?” By the nature of prakṛti, which is in my control(ātmā-māyā). Prakṛti’s nature is to transform into various forms. Since pradhāna, though the support of the universe, is supported by me, I am the support of the material world. Since Brahmā and Śiva are given powers by me, I am the creator and destroyer. I am Viṣṇu, the maintainer. There is nothing illogical here. (Another meaning) I manifest myself (ātmānam) in your minds (ātmani) by effort (ātmanā). There is a similar statement tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham: I manifest myself. (BG [4.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.7)) I shine with real (bhūta) senses such as eyes, and qualities like beauty (guṇātmanā). I establish (anupālayāmi) that form to play for a moment. Then I disappear (hanmi). I do it by the power (anubhāvena) of my desire (ātmā-māyā). I am controlled by your prema. When I cannot tolerate separation then I, desiring you, do this. Thus you should be convinced of this. Unperceived words are not a fault, since they are covered because of the secret meaning.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Being composed of pure knowledge, this ātmā is pure, distinct from everything material, though connected with the guṇas. We can perceive the soul through the three functions of material nature known as wakefulness, sleep and deep sleep.**

**Комментарий:**

“How can people know you if you are of this nature?” The allpervading Lord (ātmā) has a svarūpa of consciousness (jñānamayaḥ). Because of his acintya-śakti, he is devoid of a relationship with the world (śuddhaḥ) though he creates through the gunās. He is different from the body of the living entity though he dwells in the body (vyatiriktaḥ). Though he enters the guṇas he has no contact with them (aguṇānvayaḥ). He, who is of such nature, is inferred by people through the mental functions of sleep, dreaming and waking states as stated by the devatās: You can be inferred by sattva-guṇa, for one can realize that sattva-guṇa is related to you and that by you alone does it function. (SB [10.2.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/2.35)) (Another meaning) I (ātmā), being chiefly omniscient (jñāna-mayaḥ), never forget you. I am devoid of association with the Mathurā women (śuddhaḥ) because I am situated far from them (vyatiriktaḥ). “How do you spend your time?” I realize your qualities like beauty and friendliness (guṇānvayaḥ) by constant meditation. This is how I spend my time. My ātmā is understood by your mental functions of sleep, waking and dreaming. In deep sleep, my form and qualities, which were seen in past, are seen in a general way. In dream there is some distinction. In waking state appearing before you, you experience speaking and embracing me. Why are you disturbed?

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**As a person just arisen from sleep may continue to meditate on a dream even though it is illusory, so by the agency of the mind one meditates on the sense objects, which the senses can then obtain. Therefore one should become fully alert and bring the mind under control.**

**Комментарий:**

“The meaning of adhyātmā scriptures that you teach does not stay fixed in the heart.” This cannot take place without controlling the mind. You should control the mind. The senses attain the useless (mṛṣābhūtān) sense objects previously experienced, upon which one meditates by the mind, just as a person, rising from dream, without proper sleep, meditates on objects falsely experienced in a dream. If one controls the mind, then an object becomes fixed in the heart. (Another meaning) Rising from a fainting state, (utthitaḥ) people like you consider objects of senses like seeing me, embracing and kissing me (indriyārthān), which exist since I appear there, to be false objects in a dream produced by the mind and by controlling the mind, they dismiss it as not factual. Because, being without proper sleep, like you, the sense such as your eyes, etc., without collyrium (eyes), without sandalwood, without redness (lips), perceive directly. Thus I have sent this message in order that you believe that my union with you, that you think is false, is actually true since your reasoning is affected by longing in separation.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**According to intelligent authorities, this is the ultimate conclusion of all the Vedas, as well as all practice of yoga, Sāṅkhya, renunciation, austerity, sense control and truthfulness, just as the sea is the ultimate destination of all rivers.**

**Комментарий:**

Among the causes of jñāna, controlling the mind is final cause. All Vedas (samāmnāyaḥ) have this as the end, the result – controlling the mind (etad-antaḥ) since they conclude in this. There is one conclusion in the various paths of aṣṭāṅga-yoga, distinguishing matter and spirit (sāṅkhyaṁ), sannyāsa (tyāgaḥ), following svadharma (tapaḥ), controlling the senses (damaḥ), and speaking the truth (satyaṁ). An example is given. The rivers end in the ocean. Just as by controlling the mind, one crosses the suffering of saṁsāra, by controlling the mind, you cross the suffering of separation from me. They are equal.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**But the actual reason why I, your beloved, have stayed far away from your eyes is that I wanted to intensify my meditation upon you and thus draw my mind closer to you.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Uddhava! Why do you cheat us with statements with two meanings? Having extreme attraction for him, we see him close in dreams and waking state, with extreme absorption. But the fire of separation does not extinguish by this. If there is even something spoken by him which has only one meaning and which extinguishes that fire, please reveal it.” Being thus spoken to, Uddhava reveals a second letter from inside the turban and speaks. If I, though dear to your eyes, now stay far away from them, it is because of a desire that you meditate on me constantly. That meditation is to draw the mind close. Now I exist near your minds. In this way, though you are dear to my eyes, you, situated far from my eyes, exist close to my mind. Thus though something is close to the eye, if it is not close in the mind, it will not produce attachment. Thus being close in mind is what I desire and may you also desire this.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**When her lover is far away, a woman thinks of him more than when he is present before her.**

**Комментарий:**

He explains this according to the experience of men and women. The word ca indicates men as well as women. The mind of a man becomes absorbed in a dear women situated far away. This is not so if the woman is situated near, within sight.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Because your minds are totally absorbed in me and free from all other engagement, remembering me always, you will very soon have me again in your presence eternally.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Uddhava! What does the Lord who knows our love teach by saying that men and women increase their love by staying far away?” Since you give this teaching though you are Bṛhaspati’s disciple, you do not know us, who, though Kṛṣṇa is situated close to our eyes, consider even a second of interruption to be like a yuga of being away from the eyes. Thus he enjoys with city women today. When he will be separated from them, you can describe this to him and those women. We do not accept those words of his. Hearing this, he gives another message from Kṛṣṇa. Absorbing your minds, which have completely given up (vimukta) all interest in duties related to house, husband, etc., in me, Kṛṣṇa, Śyāmasundara, the son of Nanda, remembering me constantly, you will very soon attain me, who am situated close (upa) to you.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**O fortunate ladies! Although some gopīs had to remain in the cowherd village and so could not join the rāsa dance to sport with me at night in the forest, they attained me by thinking of my potent pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

The gopīs who were kept in their houses are the proof of this statement. Those who could not participate with me who was sporting at night in Vṛndāvana, visible to the eyes (asmin), since they were prevented by their husbands, remaining in their houses, attained me in another manifestation by thinking of my heroism. O auspicious gopīs! You will directly attain me, not by giving up your bodies as described in SB [10.29.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/29.11).

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The women of Vraja were pleased to hear this message from their dear Kṛṣṇa. His words having revived their memory, they addressed Uddhava as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing the instructions of Kṛṣṇa as described, the women of Vraja, pleased, spoke to Uddhava, their memories revived by the message. Their words whose syllables announced the first meaning were like the marks of a bookworm (i.e. they were superficial). Their words whose syllables announced the second meaning was his approved meaning. They became pleased because of remembering union with him by understanding the true meaning of the message, since he was their beloved and the last four verses (34-37) of his letter showed were unambiguous in meaning.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs said: It is very good that Kaṁsa, the enemy and persecutor of the Yadus, has now been killed, along with his followers. And it is also very good that Acyuta is living happily in the company of his well-wishing friends and relatives, whose every desire is now fulfilled.**

**Комментарий:**

It is good (diṣṭyā) that the enemy (ahitaḥ), Kaṁsa has been killed.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Gentle Uddhava, is the elder brother of Gada now bestowing on the city women the pleasure that actually belongs to us? We suppose those ladies worship him with excellent glances full of affectionate, shy smiles.**

**Комментарий:**

Different gopīs speak these verses with envy. Does Kṛṣṇa give pleasure to the city women? He is the elder brother of Gada. He is now a resident of Mathurā. Gada was the first son of Devarakṣitā, a wife of Vasudeva. Kṛṣṇa is Gadāgraja (elder brother of Gada) since he thinks himself the son of Vasudeva now. He who was previously worshipped by our excellent glances with shy smiles of affection has now become their worshipper! They lament.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa is expert in all kinds of conjugal affairs and is the darling of the city women. How can he not become entangled, now that he’s constantly adored by their enchanting words and gestures?**

**Комментарий:**

O fools! There is no doubt at all. Others speak with sarcasm and inner anger. Because he knows about amorous love he is now dear to the city women. How can he not become attracted by their words? He is worshipped constantly by their playful gestures (vibhramaiḥ). Attracted to them, he will not come here. You should know this!

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**O honest Uddhava, does the king of Gokula ever remember us village girls during his free conversations with the city women?**

**Комментарий:**

Out of longing some gopīs ask with sarcasm. Does the king of Gokula on some occasion remember us? O truthful Uddhava (sādho)! You will not speak a lie. The occasion is described. In the assembly of city women during free conversations (svaira-kathā) does he remember us, who are devoid of skills (grāmyāḥ)? “O city women! You know jokes and riddles. Gopīs know very little.” Does he talk about us in this way, about our village culture? This is criticism of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Does he, whose is the subject of attractive talks praised by devatā women, recall those nights in the Vṛndāvana forest, lovely with lotus, jasmine and the bright moon? He enjoyed with us, his beloved girlfriends, in the circle of the rāsa dance, which resounded with the music of ankle bells.**

**Комментарий:**

Not tolerating what others said, other gopīs ask, revealing their skill. Let other things such as our skill be forgotten! How can he forget his rāsa dance? He played with us, his lovers in the rāsa in which ankle bells tinkled in Vṛndāvana in those nights. Does he not remember those nights in Vṛndāvana sometimes or not? Vṛndāvana is described. It was attractive with lotuses, jasmines and the moon, making it white. Kṛṣṇa is described. His topics are praised by wives of devatās in airplanes. The women of Svarga praised the topics of our rāsa dance. Do the low city women know this? All of his wealth is hidden from everyone. Thus, we lament.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Will that descendant of Daśārha return here and by the touch of his limbs bring back to life those who are now burning with the grief he has caused, just as Lord Indra brings a forest back to life with his water-bearing clouds?**

**Комментарий:**

Other gopīs speak. O friends! Though he is king of the Daśārhas, Kṛṣṇa, filled with longing on remembering the rāsa dance, will come here relieving us of pain, caused by his actions, bringing us to life by his limbs, just as Indra gives life to the forest by clouds. Since the pain is caused by him, his touch is the only relief. Since he brings us to life by his limbs, his touch is full of nectar. That is made clear in the example of the forest.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**But why should Kṛṣṇa come here after winning a kingdom, killing his enemies? He will be pleased on marrying the daughters of kings, and will be surrounded by all his friends and well-wishers?**

**Комментарий:**

Others having vāmya nature speak. Because of what happiness will Kṛṣṇa come to Vraja, for he has attained a kingdom which is free of problems? His relatives, who depend on him for their lives, due to absorption in friendship will not accept his coming here for ruling Vraja though he was made prince by his father. He will live among the Yadus who are situated in governing. “He will come since he cannot give up dependence on the happiness of our association.” He will marry the daughters of kings. It is stated like this since staying in Mathurā, he will marry Rukminī and others. This is also stated in Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad. Those statements are reconciled here since they are concerning another kalpa. “He will come since he cannot give up dependence on the friendship of his father and others.” He is surrounded there by all friends. He obtains all of them there. He stays there considering Vasudeva and others as his father, etc. The meaning is this. What wealth is not there in Vraja. Bṛhad-vana and Nandīśvara — these are Nanda’s two capitals. There are houses made of jewels there. There is Vṛndāvana served by all seasons. There are areas for play. There are mountains like Govardhana and many desire trees made of gems. There are waterfalls with sweet water. There are rivers like Yamunā with pure water. In that Vraja the prince is Kṛṣṇa. Brahmā and others come there constantly for pleasing him. We, his beloveds worship him with service in prema. Yet giving up Vraja, he stays in Mathurā with the Yadus, who are order carriers of the king. He enjoys with the city women. We know that. Desiring lordship, he does not feel the rasa of friendship.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**What use does this person who thinks himself great have for forest people or any others, since he is the master of Lakṣmī, has all possessions, and is fully satisfied?**

**Комментарий:**

Others, taking shelter of renunciation, speak. What goal will be accomplished for clever Kṛṣṇa through the city women (anyābhiḥ) or through us women of Vraja (asmābhiḥ), who live in the forest, giving up houses because of separation from him (vanaukobhiḥ)? He is the husband of Lakṣmī who has come from Vaikuṇṭha. He is satisfied and full in his svarūpa with her (kṛtātmanaḥ). Kṛta means full according to Amara-kośa. How will the Lord who is complete in himself, whose feet Lakṣmī serves, be attracted to friends who are dealt with as equals, in a friendly mood? Or why would he be attracted to us charming women?

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**The greatest happiness is to renounce all desires, as even the prostitute Piṅgalā has declared. Yet even though we know this, we cannot give up our longing for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

“Then you should withdraw your mind from him.” That longing (āśā) is hard to give up.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**Who can bear to give up the experience of Kṛṣṇa? Although he shows no interest in her, Lakṣmī never moves from her place on his chest.**

**Комментарий:**

Whether attaining a desired object or not, the greedy person cannot give up desire for the object. Who can give up the experience (saṁvidam) of his beauty, etc.? No one can. Though he does not desire her, Lakṣmī does not leave (cyavate) his chest (aṅgāt) as a golden line.

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**Dear Uddhava, when Kṛṣṇa was here in the company of Balarāma, he served all these rivers, hills, forests, cows and flute sounds.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover when we forget him, our longing for him should decrease, but the longing constantly increases because of a reason. This is explained in two verses. The rivers, etc., were constantly used by him (ācaritāḥ). Even the sound of the flute is played by some others. We want him to return along with Balarāma as well (saṅkārṣaṇa).

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**All these remind us constantly of Nanda’s son. Because we see Kṛṣṇa’s footprints, which are marked with fine symbols, we can never forget him.**

**Комментарий:**

We like to remember him as the son of the king of the cowherds, Nanda. Even now we see his footprints marked with the divine symbols of a flag and thunderbolt, abodes of beauty, which remain on the stones even today.

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**O Uddhava, how can we forget him when our intelligence has been stolen away by the charming way he walks, his excellent smile and playful glances, and his honeylike words?**

**Комментарий:**

“As long as he does not come, take your intelligence away from the rivers and stones. Then you can forget him.” He stole our intelligence with his sweet words. Our intelligence is stuck to those items. How can we forget him?

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**O master, O master of the goddess of fortune, O master of Vraja! O destroyer of all suffering, Govinda, please lift Gokula out of the ocean of distress in which it is drowning!**

**Комментарий:**

Having said this, overwhelmed by remembering Kṛṣṇa, they all called out to him with wretchedness while weeping. O Kṛṣṇa, attractor of our hearts! O lord of Lakṣmī, having an attractive form, desired by Lakṣmī! O master of Vraja, desired by the people of Gokula! O destroyer of the great distress created by Indra! Deliver Gokula drowning in an ocean of pain caused by separation from you, by returning personally. What is the use of sending messengers? O Govinda, enjoy the cows that you protect!

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Kṛṣṇa’s messages having relieved their fever of separation, the gopīs then worshiped Uddhava, lowering their eyes, after having experienced the highest bliss.**

**Комментарий:**

Pleased by the written messages, their hearts slackened. Uddhava made them joyful with another message. Their fever of separation was relieved by messages other than the one which was written since messages is in the plural (sandeśaiḥ). These are the messages. O women! As you stand in front of my dear Uddhava with closed eyes, I will deliver you from the fire of separation just as I delivered my friends from the fire of reeds. Just see the power of my inconceivable yoga. By these messages spoken by his dear friend, the gopīs closed their eyes. Within that moment a yuga of time entered, like a night of Brahmā entering three yāmās and Kṛṣṇa performed the rāsa dance and other pastimes with the gopīs, unseen by others. By those pastimes their fire of separation was extinguished. Uddhava saw their joyful limbs and said, “O ladies! Open your eyes.” Being like that, realizing themselves (ātmānam) as born again with the attainment of the highest bliss by closing the eyes (adhoḥ aksa), they worshipped him, dear to Kṛṣṇa, according to the rules.

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava remained there for several months, dispelling the gopīs’ sorrow by chanting the topics of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. Thus he brought joy to all the people of Gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

By Kṛṣṇa’s messages he again removed their suffering which arose by their external consciousness. He pleased the people of Gokula.

### Text 55

**Перевод:**

**All the days that Uddhava dwelled in Nanda’s cowherd village seemed like a single moment to the residents of Vraja, for Uddhava was always discussing Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The days passed like a moment since Uddhava was true to the meaning of his name (festival). That was since Kṛṣṇa gave him the power to give bliss.

### Text 56

**Перевод:**

**That servant of Kṛṣṇa was satisfied by giving them direct association with Kṛṣṇa and seeing the rivers, forests, mountains, valleys and flowering trees of Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

The trees flowered as previously, before Kṛṣṇa left Vraja.

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**Seeing how the gopīs were always showing extreme symptoms because of their total absorption in Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava was supremely pleased. Offering them all respect, he sang as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the conduct of the gopīs as described (evam-ādi), whose minds (ātma) were in divyonmāda (viklava) by absorption in Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava, though a kṣatriya, though recognized by the Vṛṣṇis as a counsellor, offered respects to the gopīs, understanding their supreme position, that they were the internal śaktis of the Supreme Lord, his master, and loudly sang the following song.

### Text 58

**Перевод:**

**\[Uddhava sang:\] Among all persons on earth, these cowherd women alone have attained prefect bodies, for they have achieved mahābhava for Govinda, the source of all forms of the Lord. Their pure love is desired by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as well. For one who has tasted the narrations of the infinite Lord, what is the use of taking birth as a high-class brāhmaṇa, or even as Brahmā himself?**

**Комментарий:**

He describes their glories which are more than all others. These cowherd women alone (param) are successful in their birth (tanubhṛtaḥ), who possess mahā-bhāva (rūḍha-bhāvāḥ) as previously described, for Govinda, the ātmā of all beings, which sages desiring liberation (bhava-bhiyaḥ), liberated sages (munayaḥ) and we, his associates, desire. Understanding that the Lord is controlled extremely by this bhāva, we desire a small degree of it but do not attain it. For one who has attachment to Kṛṣṇa’s unlimited pastimes, what is the use of the three births—seminal, gāyatri and yajñika? There is no use at all since attachment for those topics is the cause of being superior to all else. Lack of attachment to the topics is the cause of everything being useless.

### Text 59

**Перевод:**

**How amazing it is that these simple women who wander about the forest, seemingly spoiled by improper behavior, have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul! Still, it is true that the Supreme Lord himself awards his blessings even to an ignorant worshiper, just as the best medicine works even when taken by a person ignorant of its ingredients.**

### Text 60

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa was dancing with the gopīs in the rāsa-līlā, the gopīs were embraced by the arms of the Lord. This favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune, though she was intensely attracted to him, or to other consorts in the spiritual world whose bodily luster and aroma resemble the lotus flower. And what to speak of worldly women?**

### Text 61

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs of Vṛndāvana have given up the association of their husbands, sons and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken their relatives and the path of dharma to obtain the lotus feet of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa, which even the Vedas pursue. Oh, let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers or herbs in Vṛndāvana, because the gopīs bless them with the dust of their lotus feet.**

### Text 62

**Перевод:**

**The goddess of fortune herself, along with Brahmā and all the other devatās, and the best of yogīs, can worship the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa only within their minds. But during the rāsa dance Kṛṣṇa placed those feet upon these gopīs’ breasts, and by embracing those feet, the gopīs gave up all distress.**

**Комментарий:**

Again, he states the gopīs’ supreme position. Vai indicates that it is certain. The gopīs (yāḥ) embraced those lotus feet of Svayaṁ Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, which were placed on their breasts and gave up their pain during the rāsa dance. Those feet are worshipped in the mind (ātmani) by Lakṣmī, Brahmā and others, but cannot be directly touched by them since it is said, yad vāñchayā śrī: with desire for those feet Lakṣmī performed austerities. (SB [10.16.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/16.36)) Since they are qualified for what was rare for Lakṣmī and others, they are superior to everyone.

### Text 63

**Перевод:**

**I repeatedly offer my respects to the dust from the feet of the women of Nanda Mahārāja’s cowherd village. When these gopīs loudly chant the glories of Kṛṣṇa, the vibration purifies the three worlds.**

**Комментарий:**

Having praised the gopīs as greatly excellent, he offers respects on the ground with eight limbs. I offer respects at every moment (abhīkṣṇaśaḥ), not once or twice, as long as I do not take birth as a bush that can easily see them. Their singing purifies the three worlds of the fault of ignorance. Noddhavo ‘ṇv api man nyūnaḥ: Uddhava is not less than me at all. (SB [3.4.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/4.31)) Tvaṁ tu bhāgavateṣv aham: you, Uddhava, represent me among the devotees. (SB [11.16.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/16.29)) By these statements of the Lord, since even Uddhava, the best among all devotees, respected the gopīs, they are the best of all. This is the intention of Vyāsa and others.

### Text 64

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Uddhava, the descendant of Daśārha, then took permission to leave from the gopīs and from mother Yaśodā and Nanda Mahārāja. He bade farewell to all the cowherd men and, about to depart, mounted his chariot.**

**Комментарий:**

Begging their permission, asking about (āmantrya) the cowherds, he left.

### Text 65

**Перевод:**

**As Uddhava was about to leave, Nanda and the others approached him bearing various items of worship. With tears in their eyes they addressed him as follows with anurāga.**

**Комментарий:**

Holding in their hands, various items such as gold bracelets and jeweled necklaces gathered for Kṛṣṇa, they approached Uddhava to offer them. The word ādi means that Yaśodā also was there, with modaka sweets tasting like nectar. Upananda and others, with their wives, as well as Śrīdāma and other cowherd boys, holding fragrant, gold-colored gairika, were there. The gopīs were also there with head ornaments having special marks indicating themselves. They also had gifts for Balarāma and others as appropriate.

### Text 66

**Перевод:**

**\[Nanda and the other cowherds said:\] May our mental functions always take shelter of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, may our words always chant his names, and may our bodies always bow down to him and serve him.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Uddhava! Kṛṣṇa does not come to us, his parents because of our faults only. Why should the friend of bhāva come to persons devoid of bhāva? Thus since those who have affection for their real son have heart-breaking emotions arising from the fire of separation from a son like him. How unfortunate for us, with false affection, with iron hearts! May we have devotion for him, the Lord, though we are devoid of real love. Uddhava should convey our words to him.” With this mood they speak. Our mental functions should take shelter of his feet. Our words should utter his name. Our bodies should offer respects to him. May we have bhakti to his feet, etc., seeing him as the Lord.

### Text 67

**Перевод:**

**Wherever we are made to wander about this world by the Supreme Lord’s will, in accordance with the reactions to our fruitive work, may our good works and charity always grant us love for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Due to manifestation of humility, he speaks. May we, wandering somewhere by continuing karmas by Kṛṣṇa’s will, have rati for Kṛṣṇa, the lord of those with clean hearts, by auspicious karmas and charities. The prayer is in potential mood. This is the nature of persons having sakhya, vātsalya or mādhurya bhāvas. When separation occurs, or an indifferent attitude is inferred, dāsya towards him is accepted by their not-so-strong dainya. Balarāma says: Who is this mystic power, and where has she come from? Is she a demigod or a demoness? She must be the illusory energy of my master, Lord Kṛṣṇa, for who else can bewilder me? (SB [10.13.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/13.37)) Nanda says: May our mental functions take shelter of Kṛṣṇa’s feet. (SB [10.47.66](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.66)) The gopīs say: Does he ever talk about us, his maidservants? When will he lay on our heads his aguru-scented hand? (SB [10.47.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.21)) But Vasudeva and Devakī, even on meeting their son, say: You are not our sons but the very Lords of both material nature and its creator \[Mahā-Viṣṇu\]. As you yourself have told us, you have descended to rid the earth of the rulers who are a heavy burden upon her. (SB [10.85.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/85.18)) This statement is because of thinking of their son as the Lord and is to reject their parental relationship with Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 68

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] O ruler of men, thus honored by the cowherd men with attachment to Kṛṣṇa and Vṛndāvana, Uddhava went back to the city of Mathurā, which was under Kṛṣṇa’s protection.**

**Комментарий:**

Uddhava was worshipped with bhakti having the form of great anurāga for Kṛṣṇa (bhaktyā). Since Mathurā was protected by Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava went there even though he was attracted to Vraja.

### Text 69

**Перевод:**

**After falling down to pay his homage, Uddhava described to Kṛṣṇa the immense devotion of the residents of Vraja. Uddhava also described it to Vasudeva, Lord Balarāma and King Ugrasena and presented to them the gifts of tribute he had brought with him.**

**Комментарий:**

Uddhava described the bhakti of the people of Vraja which was millions of times greater in type and quantity than that of the people of Mathurā. O master! Giving up those devotees with such bhakti and living here has made statements about your being controlled by bhakti become devoid of object of reference (i.e. now they do not seem to be referring to anyone). Make those words have an object of reference. Nanda, your father, is an ocean of vātsalya. You should think of his words “Our mental functions take shelter of your feet.” (verse 66) Those statements were difficult for me to understand. Your mother Yaśodā dampens her cloth with a river of tears. She remains silent. Hearing this, the Lord became unsettled and wept loudly in the assembly full with the best of the Yadus. The whole assembly became full of tears and astonishment. But the vāḍava fire of separation for the gopīs was revealed at night in a solitary place. Thinking only of them, he burned the whole night and made the whole universe burn. Those who maintain their lives by the nectar of bhāvas in the message have attained greatness. By the power of his mercy I have drunk a little of the remnants.

## Chapter 48 - Kṛṣṇa Pleases His Devotees

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Next, after assimilating Uddhava’s report, Kṛṣṇa, the soul of all beings and seer of everything, desired to satisfy the serving girl Trivakrā, who was troubled by desire. Thus he went to her house.**

**Комментарий:**

In the forty-eighth chapter, Kṛṣṇa enjoys with Kubjā, is praised by Akrūra, and sends him to Hastināpura. Due to Uddhava’s arrival, passing many days, understanding that his father and the people of Vraja had been pacified by Uddhava, the Lord (bhagavān), full of inconceivable powers, while remaining in Mathurā, went in another form to Vraja. He spread to all places (sarvātmā). He showed to Uddhava his manifestation in Vraja, meeting everyone there. “I cannot reject even Kubjā, what to speak of the people of Vraja.” In order to teach this, he went with Uddhava to her house. What did he desire? He desired to please her, who was burning with desire, just as he had promised.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Trivakrā’s home was decorated with expensive furnishings and replete with sensual accoutrements meant to inspire amorous desire. There were banners, rows of strung pearls, canopies, fine beds and sitting places, fragrant with incense, oil lamps, flower garlands and aromatic sandalwood paste.**

**Комментарий:**

By the Lord’s mercy, her house had become very attractive. That is described in three lines. It was filled with valuable accessories. It was filled with articles to increase amorous desire such as paintings, honey and betel nut. Within the house were strings of pearls. On top were flags. There were canopies (vitāna).

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**When Trivakrā saw him arriving at her house, filled with joy, she at once rose from her seat excitedly. Coming forward graciously with her girlfriends, she respectfully greeted Kṛṣṇa, by offering him an excellent seat and other articles of worship.**

**Комментарий:**

She greeted him properly (yathā). Kṛṣṇa did not deviate from his promise (acyutaṁ).

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Uddhava was also worshipped properly, but he simply touched his seat and sat on the floor. Then Kṛṣṇa, imitating the manners of human society, quickly made himself comfortable on a luxurious bed.**

**Комментарий:**

Touching with his hand a seat offered by Kubjā by her hands, Uddhava sat on the ground since he was a servant, though he sat on the seat given by the gopīs, since friendship had arisen at that time. Kṛṣṇa quickly sat on the bed, made of valuable gems, which was within the house. He sat on a seat for worship, then rose up and himself went to the bed within the room. He was eager to accept the devotional acts (ācaritāni) of his devotees (loka).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Trivakrā prepared herself by bathing, anointing her body, and dressing in fine garments, by putting on jewelry, garlands and perfume, and also by chewing betel nut, drinking honey, and so on. She then approached the consort of Lakṣmī with shy, playful smiles and coquettish glances.**

**Комментарий:**

She prepared her body (ātmā) with sandalwood (ālepa), honey which was like nectar (sudhāsava) suitable for pastimes. She approached Kṛṣṇa with glances endowed with coquetry and shy, playful smile arisen from the pastime.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Calling forward his beloved, who was anxious and shy at the prospect of this new contact, the Lord pulled her by her bangled hands onto the bed. Thus he enjoyed with that beautiful girl, who became master of devotees by offering ointment as a puṇya.**

**Комментарий:**

She was shy at the new meeting. She had not touched a man previously. By the previous touch of the Lord, her body developed the bhāva of an unmarried young girl. The reason for that mercy was her bhakti. She attained puṇya by offering ointments to Kṛṣṇa. He enjoyed with that girl who was the best among devotees (īśayā) who offered (la) ointment (anulepārpaṇa-puṇya). She was best because at a special time she offered directly to Svayam Bhagavān.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Simply by smelling the fragrance of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, Trivakrā cleansed away the burning desire Cupid had aroused in her breasts, chest and eyes. With her two arms she embraced between her breasts her lover, Kṛṣṇa, the personification of bliss, and thus she gave up her long-standing distress.**

**Комментарий:**

She removed the pain of her breasts, chest and eyes burning with desire by his foot endowed with unlimited sweetness (ananta) and smelled the fragrance of his feet.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Having thus gotten the hard-to-get Supreme Lord by the simple act of offering him body ointment, unfortunate Trivakrā submitted to the bestower of bhakti the following request.**

**Комментарий:**

She requested him who is her Lord exclusively (kaivalya-nāthaṁ). She prayed, “Enjoy only with me and not with any others.” She was unfortunate because the Lord did not grant that boon.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**\[Trivakrā said:\] O beloved, please stay here with me for a few days more and enjoy. I cannot bear to give up your association, O lotus-eyed one!**

**Комментарий:**

O beloved! Stay with me for some days within the house and enjoy.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Promising her the fulfillment of this desire, considerate Kṛṣṇa, Lord of all beings, paid Trivakrā his respects and then returned with Uddhava to his own supremely opulent residence.**

**Комментарий:**

Having given her the boon she desired (kāma-varam) to enjoy with him fully, he promised, “I will come and enjoy with you, though I have other women.” Taking her permission (mānayitvā), he went to his own house with Uddhava. He was with Uddhava in order to avoid rumours from the public since Uddhava was famous for his proper behavior. This pastime took place in the night.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, endowed with all qualities and powers, able to bestow all benedictions, is ordinarily difficult to approach. One who has properly worshiped him and then chooses the benediction of material enjoyment is certainly of poor intelligence, for he is satisfied with an insignificant result.**

**Комментарий:**

Enjoyment with the Lord, which is predominated with one’s own happiness is criticized. The person who chooses his own sense enjoyment (mano-grāhyam) is foolish. Why? Since giving up the Lord who is the form of complete happiness he asks for happiness different from the Lord.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Then Kṛṣṇa, wanting to have some things done, went to Akrūra’s house with Balarāma and Uddhava. The Lord also desired to please Akrūra.**

**Комментарий:**

Wanting to please Akrūra, Kṛṣṇa went to his house. How would he please him? He wanted Akrūra to do something for him since orders of the master are dear to the servant. He went with Uddhava and Balarāma. Previously he said: yāsye bhavato geham aham arya-samanvitaḥ I will come to your house with my elder brother. (SB [10.41.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/41.17)) It was improper to go without Uddhava for undertaking such actions, since Uddhava was the best councilor.

### Text 13-14

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra stood up in great joy when he saw them, his own relatives and the greatest of exalted personalities, coming from a distance. After embracing them and greeting them, Akrūra bowed down to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma and was greeted by them in return. Then, when his guests had taken their seats, he worshiped them in accordance with scriptural rules.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing them from a distance, while sitting on the roof top, he became joyful. He stood up and approached, embraced them and greeted them. He offered respects to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma in order with devotion due to manifestation of svarūpa. He welcomed Uddhava, with what was suitable for friends. vaiṣṇave bandhu-sat-kṛtyā: one should worship me within the Vaiṣṇavas by offering loving friendship to them and honoring them in all respects. (SB [11.11.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/11.44))

### Text 15-16

**Перевод:**

**O King, Akrūra bathed the feet of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma and then poured the bath water on his head. He presented them with gifts, fine clothing, aromatic sandalwood paste, flower garlands and excellent jewelry. After thus worshiping the two Lords, he bowed his head to the floor. He then began to massage Kṛṣṇa’s feet and Balarāma’s feet, placing them on his lap, and with his head bowed in humility he addressed Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. He placed the water which had bathed their feet on his head completely (ā). He worshipped them with four types of food (arhaṇa), ending with betel nut. At the start of massaging the feet of them as they were resting, he touched (ānamya) their feet to his head, and then gently massaged one foot and then the other.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**\[Akrūra said:\] It is our good fortune that you two have killed the evil Kaṁsa and his followers, thus delivering your dynasty from endless suffering and causing it to flourish.**

**Комментарий:**

You saved your (vām) family from difficulties and made it prosperous.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**You both are prakrṭi and jīva, the cause of the universe and its very substance. Not the slightest subtle cause or manifest product of creation exists apart from you.**

**Комментарий:**

What to speak of this family! The whole universe belongs to you. You two are prakrti (pradhāna) and jīva (puruṣau) since they depend on you and you pervade them. You are the causes of the universe (jagad-dhetū) and its effects (jagan-mayau). Stated in another way, without you two, cause (param) and effect (aparam) do not exist at all.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**O Supreme Absolute Truth, with your personal energies you create this universe and then enter into it. Thus one can perceive you in many different forms being understood from scripture and direct experience.**

**Комментарий:**

The universe is your effect. You enter into the universe after the creation. O Brahman! You are perceived as many by your antaryāmī expansions. You are then subject to hearing and seeing (śrutapratyakṣa-gocaram). The neuter form (gocaram) is poetic license.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Just as the primary elements—earth and so on—manifest themselves in abundant variety among all the species of mobile and immobile life, so you, the pure one, independent, appear to be manifold among the variegated objects of your creation.**

**Комментарий:**

An example of one becoming many is given. Just as the causes such as earth, etc., appear variously in the moving and nonmoving beings in various species (yoniṣu), similarly, you who is one, appear as many in the places manifested by you (ātma-yoniṣu). You are independent (ātma-tantraḥ).

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**You create, destroy and also maintain this universe with your personal energies—the modes of passion, ignorance and goodness—yet you are never entangled by these modes or the activities they generate. Since you are the original source of all knowledge, what could ever cause you to be bound by illusion?**

**Комментарий:**

You are the cause of material creation, maintenance and destruction but because you are devoid of identity as their doer, you do not experience the results of that karma. Yet you are not bound by the guṇas and karma like the jīva. “Why am I not bound up?” How can the cause of bondage, the false identity exist for you, who are omniscient without restriction (jñānātmanaḥ) like it does for the jīva? Darkness never enters the sun.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Since it has never been demonstrated that you are covered by material, bodily designations, it must be concluded that for you there is neither birth in a literal sense nor any duality. Therefore you never undergo bondage or liberation, and if you appear to, it is only because of your desire that we see you in that way, or simply because of our lack of discrimination.**

**Комментарий:**

“The cause of my body, which is born from Vasudeva, is ignorance characterized by pride.” Since it is not determined by writers of scripture that you have ignorance, the upādhi of body or senses, you do not have a birth like the jīva having seminal birth. But your body is simply a manifestation of a body which is previously perfected and there is no difference of ātmā and body as in the case of jīva. You are your body. The Lord does not possess a form since his form is his very self. (Brahma-sūtra [3.2.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vs/3.2.14)) Since your body is yourself, you have an extraordinary form with body and senses. It is not bound nor liberated. “I was bound by my mother around my belly and released from bondage by my father. My bondage and liberation are famous.” That may be. You appear like this because of the desires (nikāmaḥ) of dear devotees such as us. We meditate on these events since you have a form of knowledge, not one of ignorance (avivekaḥ).

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**You enunciated the eternal Vedas for the benefit of the whole universe. Whenever that path becomes obstructed by wicked persons following the path of atheism, you nourish sattva-guṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Though you are of that nature, in order to protect the righteous you appear while nourishing sattva-guṇa by protecting the path of dharma.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**You are that very same Supreme Person, my Lord, and you have now appeared in the home of Vasudeva with your plenary portion. You have done this to relieve the earth’s burden by killing hundreds of armies led by kings who are expansions of the devatās’ enemies, and also to spread the fame of our dynasty.**

**Комментарий:**

You whose body is yourself, have appeared with Balarāma (svāṁśena) to relieve the burden of the earth by killing hundreds of armies of kings who were aṁśas of demons and to spread the fame of the Yadu dynasty (amuṣya).

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Today, O Lord, my home has become most fortunate because you have entered it. As the Supreme Truth, you embody the forefathers, ordinary creatures, human beings and devatās, and the water that has washed your feet purifies the three worlds. O omniscient Lord, you are supreme among all universes.**

**Комментарий:**

Our house which you, who are the embodiment of deities of pañcayajñas (devas, pitrṣ, kings and other living entities), have entered is most fortunate.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**What learned person would approach anyone but you for shelter, when you are the affectionate, grateful and truthful well-wisher of your devotees? To those who worship you in sincere friendship you reward everything they desire, even your own self, yet you never increase or diminish.**

**Комментарий:**

You are the object of surrender. What learned person is he who surrenders (śaraṇaṁ samīyāt) to someone else other than you? He is a fool (kaḥ paṇdītaḥ), since you are affectionate, friendly (suhṛdaḥ), grateful and truthful (ṛta-girāt). You said, “After killing Kaṁsa I will come to your house.” You kept that promise. You do what is beneficial for your servant (suhṛdaḥ). You recognize the service that your devotee does (abhijñāt). You give all desired things to the person with splendid heart (suhrḍaḥ) who worships you. Here genitive (suhṛdo bhajataḥ) has the meaning of dative. And you do not cease even by giving that much. You give yourself also. “In giving myself, there is a great decrease.” You have no increase when you are worshipped by the leaders of the universe using all the materials of the universe and you have no decrease when you give even yourself to the devotees, since you have infinite powers.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**It is by our great fortune, Janārdana, that you are now visible to us, for even the masters of yoga and the foremost devatās can achieve this goal only with great difficulty. Please quickly cut the ropes of our illusory attachment for children, wife, wealth, friends, home and body. All such attachment is simply the effect of your illusory material energy.**

**Комментарий:**

It is good fortune (diṣṭyā) that you who are difficult to approach by the masters of yoga and devatās, are directly visible to us in our house. Quickly cut the ropes of affection for sons and family, your māyā. This means, “Increase our bhakti to you.”

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Thus worshiped and fully glorified by his devotee, Kṛṣṇa, full of all powers and attractive with pastimes, smilingly addressed Akrūra, completely bewildering him with his words.**

**Комментарий:**

He spoke to Akrūra as if covering (sammohayann) him by his words, which will be presented. He did not completely bewilder him (iva).

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: You are our praiseworthy teacher, praiseworthy paternal uncle and praiseworthy friend, and we are like your sons, always dependent on your protection, sustenance and compassion.**

**Комментарий:**

We are like your sons (prajāḥ).

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Exalted souls like you are the true objects of service and the most worshippable authorities for those who desire the highest good in life. Devatās are generally concerned with their own interests, but saintly devotees never are.**

**Комментарий:**

You are honorable by us according to the path of ordinary behavior and are worshippable by us according to the path of spiritual pursuit. You are most worshippable, being the best of Vaiṣṇavas (arha-sattamāḥ). You are worthy of service by people desiring the highest good. “But the men who desire the highest good should serve the devatās.” The devatās are absorbed in their own duties. The devotees are not like that but merciful to others.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**No one can deny that there are holy places with sacred rivers, or that the devatās appear in deity forms made of earth and stone. But these purify the soul only after a long time, whereas saintly persons purify just by being seen.**

**Комментарий:**

“One gets the greatest benefit by serving tīrthas, and devatās.” He disagrees by shaking his head. Do not the tīrthas made of water also purify? Yes, they do and the devatās also do, but there is a great difference between them and the devotees. Tīrthas and devatās purify after a long time but devotees purify even by seeing them.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**You are indeed the best of us Yadus and our relatives, so please go to Hastināpura and, as the well-wisher of the Pāṇḍavas, find out how they are doing.**

**Комментарий:**

Because you are dear to us by being our paternal uncle and because you help others by your saintly nature, you should do this. Among our friends, you are the best. Go (gaccha) to Hastināpura with a desire to know about the Pāṇḍavas’ welfare. O my dear devotee (sva)!

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**We have heard that when their father passed away, the young Pāṇḍavas were brought with their anguished mother to the capital city by King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and that they are now living there.**

**Комментарий:**

The Pāṇḍavas were brought to Hastināpura by Dhṛtarāṣṭra and live there.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**It seems that weak-minded Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the son of Ambikā, has come under the control of his wicked sons, and therefore that blind king is not treating his brother’s sons fairly.**

**Комментарий:**

Dhṛtarāṣṭra was pained. “If the Pāṇḍavas prosper, my sons will not obtain the kingdom.” He was blinded (andha-dṛk).

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Go and see whether Dhṛtarāṣṭra is acting properly or not. When we find out, we will make the necessary arrangements to help our dear friends.**

**Комментарий:**

We will make arrangements so that our friends, the Pāṇḍavas will be happy.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Thus fully instructing Akrūra, the Supreme Lord then returned to his residence, accompanied by Saṅkarṣaṇa and Uddhava.**

**Комментарий:**

Akrūra then departed from the house following them. His departure is not mentioned indicating his haste.

## Chapter 49 - Akrūra’s Mission in Hastināpura

### Text 1-2

**Перевод:**
