**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Akrūra went to Hastināpura, the city distinguished by the glory of the Paurava rulers. There he saw Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Bhīṣma, Vidura and Kuntī, along with Bāhlika and his son Somadatta. He also saw Droṇācārya, Kṛpācārya, Karṇa, Duryodhana, Aśvatthāmā, the Pāṇḍavas and other close friends.**

**Комментарий:**

In the forty-ninth chapter, Akrūra went to Hastināpura, and, understanding that the king was persecuting his brother’s sons, returned from there. The phrase “marked with the fame” (yaśo-aṅkitam) means that because of the fame of the rulers of the Puru dynasty, Hastināpura was decorated with temples and homes for the devatās and brāhmaṇas. Akrūra saw Dhṛtarāṣṭra (ambikeyaḥ), Bāhlika with his son Somadatta, Drona (bhāradvājaṁ), Kṛpa (gautamam) and the rest.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**After Akrūra, the son of Gāndinī, had appropriately greeted all his relatives and friends, they asked him for news of their family members, and he in turn asked about their welfare.**

**Комментарий:**

Akrūra asked about their welfare (avyayam).

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**He remained in Hastināpura for several months to scrutinize the conduct of the weak-willed king, who had bad sons and who was inclined to give in to the whims of mischievous advisers.**

**Комментарий:**

Akrūra wanted to observe the behavior of the king, who had wicked sons (duṣprajasya), who was weak-willed (alpa-sārasya), and whose nature was to follow the desires (chanda) of mischievous men (khala) like Karṇa.

### Text 5-6

**Перевод:**

**Kuntī and Vidura described to Akrūra in detail the evil intentions of Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s sons, who could not tolerate the great qualities of Kuntī’s sons—such as their powerful influence, military skill, physical strength, bravery and humility—or the intense affection the citizens had for them. Kuntī and Vidura also told Akrūra about how the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra had tried to poison the Pāṇḍavas and carry out other such plots.**

**Комментарий:**

The sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra could not tolerate the influence (tejaḥ), skill with weapons (oja), courage (vīryam) and the other good qualities of the Pāṇḍavas. Kuntī and Vidura also described to Akrūra (asmai) the unjust (apeśalam) acts committed by them and what they desired to commit thereafter against the Pāṇḍavas, such as the house of lac.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Kuntīdevī approached him, her brother, confidentially when he came to her house. While remembering her birthplace, she spoke with tears flowing from her eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse and those following describe events previous to Kuntī’s description to Akrūra in verses five and six. Approaching her brother, remembering her birthplace, she spoke.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**\[Queen Kuntī said:\] O gentle one, do my parents, brothers, sisters, nephews, family women and others with similar character still remember us?**

**Комментарий:**

Jāmayaḥ means women of the family.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Does my nephew lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord and the compassionate shelter of his devotees, still remember his aunt’s sons? And does Balarāma remember them also?**

**Комментарий:**

Bhrātreyaḥ means the son of my brother, Vasudeva. Kuntī’s phrase, “His father’s sister’s sons” (paitṛ-ṣvasreyān) means “my sons.”

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Now that I am suffering in the midst of my enemies like a doe in the midst of wolves, will Kṛṣṇa come to console me and my fatherless sons with his words?**

**Комментарий:**

Kuntī said, “Will Kṛṣṇa console me who am lamenting among enemies, like a doe among wolves (vṛkānām) by his words?”

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa! O great yogī! O Supreme Soul and protector of the universe! O Govinda! Please protect me, who have surrendered to you. I and my sons are being overwhelmed by trouble.**

**Комментарий:**

She knows her brother’s son is the Supreme Lord. She desires to surrender to him. O great yogī (mahā-yogin)! Even though you are situated in Mathurā, hear my words of lamentation. O soul of the universe (viśvātman), being also in my heart, you can certainly hear me! You protect even the whole universe (viśva-bhāvana), so what trouble is it for you to protect me? O Govinda, pleasure of the senses, please become visible before my eyes, so that I may see you!

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**For persons fearful of death and rebirth, I see no shelter other than your lotus feet, which award liberation, for you are the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

“But your other relatives are great warriors and protectors. Why not pray to them?” She answers. Apavargika means who gives liberation.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**I offer my obeisances unto you, Kṛṣṇa, the embodiment of dharma, Brahman, Paramātmā, the complete in all aspects and the source of all knowledge. I have come to you for shelter.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to Kṛṣṇa, dark like a tamāla tree. You are beyond māyā, although visible before the eyes (śuddhāya). You are full of great qualities like omniscience (brahmaṇe). You are the husband of Lakṣmī (paramātmane). You are the object of meditation for yogīs. You are the svarūpa of methods to attain you (yogāya). You give the means.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus meditating on her family members and also on Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the universe, your greatgrandmother Kuntīdevī began to cry out in grief, O King.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhavatāṁ prapitāmahī means Kuntī.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Both Akrūra, who shared Queen Kuntī’s distress and happiness, and the illustrious Vidura consoled the Queen by reminding her of the extraordinary way her sons had taken birth.**

**Комментарий:**

Vidura and Akrūra, who shared Queen Kuntī’s distress and happiness, consoled Queen Kuntī by reminding her of the extraordinary way her sons took birth as expansions of Dharma, Vāyu, Indra and the Aśvinī Kumāras. They told Kuntī of their power, “Who can possibly vanquish your powerful sons, who are aṁśas of Dharma, Vāyu, etc.?”

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**The ardent affection King Dhṛtarāṣṭra felt for his sons had made him act unjustly toward the Pāṇḍavas. Just before leaving, Akrūra approached the king, who was seated among his friends and supporters, and related to him the message that his relatives— Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma—had sent out of friendship.**

**Комментарий:**

While going to Mathurā, Akrūra, approaching Dhṛtarāṣṭra who was situated among his relatives (suhṛdāṁ) such as Bhīṣma, spoke friendly words from Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa (bandhubhiḥ).

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra said: O my dear son of Vicitravīrya, O enhancer of the Kurus’ glory, your brother Pāṇḍu having passed away, you have now assumed the royal throne.**

**Комментарий:**

“Bho bho” indicates a leer, “Though the young sons of Pāṇḍu are present, you occupy the throne.”

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**By religiously protecting the earth, delighting your subjects with your noble character, and treating all your relatives equally, you will surely achieve success and glory.**

**Комментарий:**

Even so, you will attain success, if you are equal to your sons and the Pāṇḍavas (sveṣu).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**If you act otherwise, however, people will condemn you in this world, and you will suffer greatly in this life and in the next life you will enter the darkness of hell. Remain equally disposed, therefore, toward Pāṇḍu’s sons and your own.**

**Комментарий:**

Tamaḥ means hell.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**In this world no one has any permanent relationship with anyone else, O King. We cannot stay forever even with our own body, what to speak of our wife, children and the rest.**

**Комментарий:**

“But how are others’ sons and one’s own sons equal?” He answers in this verse. No one can live permanently with anyone. O King! One cannot stay with one’s own body permanently, what to speak of staying with sons. Though one’s sons are very dear, they can go anywhere after dying.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Every creature is born alone and dies alone, and alone one experiences the just rewards of his good and evil deeds.**

**Комментарий:**

This is clarified. One experiences heaven (sukṛtam) and hell (duskṛtam) alone. There is no company of anyone in birth and death, and in happiness and suffering?

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**In the guise of dear dependents, strangers steal the sinfully acquired wealth of a foolish man, just as the offspring of a fish drink up the water that sustains the fish.**

**Комментарий:**

When other people live with you, then also they give suffering by depleting the hard-earned wealth. Sons steal the wealth of a foolish man by claiming, “we should be maintained (sambhojanīyāḥ)”, just as the offspring of the fish, growing in size take away the water which sustains life of the fish.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**A fool indulges in sin to maintain his life, wealth and children and other relatives, for he thinks, “These things are mine.” In the end, however, these very things all abandon him, leaving him frustrated.**

**Комментарий:**

Life, sons and wealth (rāyaḥ) which he nourishes, thinking these are my sons (sva-buddhyā), reject that fool, who has not fulfilled his desires (akṛtārtham).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Abandoned by his so-called dependents, ignorant of the actual goal of life, indifferent to his real duty, and having failed to fulfill his purposes, the foolish soul enters the blindness of hell, taking his sinful reactions with him.**

**Комментарий:**

Not fulfilling his desires, he mounts the chariot of sin and goes to hell.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O King, looking upon this world as a dream, a magician’s illusion or a flight of fancy, please control your mind with intelligence and become equipoised and peaceful, my lord.**

**Комментарий:**

O King! For the reasons mentioned, seeing this world as equal to a dream because of its impermanence, controlling your mind (ātmānam) by intelligence (ātmanā), while fixing your meditation on the Lord (śāntaḥ), become equal in vision to your sons’ and the sons’ of your brother. You are the son of Vyāsa.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: O master of charity, I can never be satiated while hearing your auspicious words. Indeed, I am like a mortal who has obtained the nectar of the gods.**

**Комментарий:**

O master of charity, Akrūra! I cannot be satisfied with your words.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Even so, gentle Akrūra, because my unsteady heart is prejudiced by affection for my sons, these pleasing words of yours cannot remain fixed there, just as lightning cannot remain fixed in a cloud.**

**Комментарий:**

Your pleasing words do not remain fixed in my fickle heart, just as lightning which is in the direction of a crystal mountain (saudāmanī) suddenly flashes and disappears.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Who can defy the injunctions of the Supreme Lord, who has now descended in the Yadu dynasty to diminish the earth’s burden?**

**Комментарий:**

“Knowing this, why are you in illusion?” Who can change the Lord’s arrangement? No one can. You cannot instill proper judgement in me by all your instructions. The Lord is in your house. That Lord, who is wise, cannot direct my intelligence through you in this way.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**I offer my obeisances to the Supreme Lord, who creates this universe by the inconceivable activity of his material energy and then distributes happiness and distress after entering within the creation. He puts in motion the entangling cycle of birth and death whose chief cause is his pastimes caused by his inexplicable will.**

**Комментарий:**

He offers respects thinking, “Thus let there be auspiciousness for me.” By an inconceivable path (durvimarśa-pathayā), the Supreme Lord (yaḥ) creates this universe by his māyā, distinguishes the guṇas as peacefulness, ferocity and dullness and then enters them, regulating them. I offer respects to the Lord whose goal is inconceivable pastimes, and who is the deliverance (gati) from the wheel of saṁsāra. Sending you to enlighten me, he drowns my intelligence in ignorance. Who can understand the goal of that irregular pastime?

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus apprised himself of the king’s attitude, Akrūra, the descendant of Yadu, took permission from the Pāṇḍavas and returned to the capital of the Yādavas.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding that the king would not give up his prejudice, he returned to Mathurā.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Akrūra reported to Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa how Dhṛtarāṣṭra was behaving toward the Pāṇḍavas. Thus, O descendant of the Kurus, he fulfilled the purpose for which he had been sent.**

**Комментарий:**

He reported the various actions of Dhṛtarāṣṭra towards the Pāṇḍavas, for obtaining which knowledge (yad-artham) he had been sent. May the son of Yaśodā by whose mercy the first half of the tenth canto has been explained shine in my heart always.

## Chapter 50 - Kṛṣṇa Establishes the City of Dvārakā

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When Kaṁsa was killed, O heroic descendant of Bharata, his two queens, Asti and Prāpti, went to their father’s house in great distress.**

**Комментарий:**

May the son of Devakī, Govinda, remain victorious. By his glance of mercy, may the second part of the tenth canto be easily explained. In the fiftieth chapter, though defeating Jarāsandha eighteen times, as if in fear of him, Kṛṣṇa takes his people to Dvārakā. The two queens of Kaṁsa named Asti and Prātpi went to the house of their father Jarāsandha when their husband Kaṁsa was killed.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**The sorrowful queens told their father, King Jarāsandha of Magadha, the cause of their becoming widows.**

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Hearing this odious news, O King, Jarāsandha was filled with sorrow and anger, and he began the greatest possible endeavor to rid the earth of the Yādavas.**

**Комментарий:**

With lamentation at Kaṁsa’s death and anger at Kṛṣṇa, Jarāsandha acted.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**With a force of twenty-three akṣauhiṇī divisions, he laid siege to the Yadu capital, Mathurā, on all sides.**

### Text 5-6

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa, full of all powers, the cause of all elements and possessing a human-like form, saw Jarāsandha’s assembled army surrounding his city like a great ocean overflowing its shores, and when he saw how this army was striking fear into his subjects, he considered what was suitable according to the time, place and specific purpose of his current incarnation.**

**Комментарий:**

Velā means shore according to Amara-kośa. He saw the army like an ocean overflowing the shore (udvelam). Tena means “by the army.” Kṛṣṇa has a human-like form (mānuṣaḥ) and is composed of the Brahman, which is the cause of everything (kāraṇa) and which is stated in the śruti statement, yato vā imāni bhūtāni: from the Lord comes all living beings. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) This means he is Para-brahman. Viṣṇu Purāṇa says paraṁ brahma narākṛtiḥ: Kṛṣṇa is Para-brahman in human form. He thought of the goal of his avatāra in accordance with the place and time. Since Mathurā is blocked on all sides, it is suitable to kill Jarāsandha here right now.

### Text 7-8

**Перевод:**

**\[The Supreme Lord thought:\] Since it is such a burden on the earth, I will destroy Jarāsandha’s army, consisting of akṣauhiṇīs of foot soldiers, horses, chariots and elephants, which the King of Māgadha has assembled from all subservient kings and brought together here. But Jarāsandha himself should not be killed, since in the future he will certainly assemble another army (which should also be destroyed).**

**Комментарий:**

He elaborates his thoughts in two verses. I will destroy the army assembled by Jarāsandha with all the kings he controls, numbering in akṣauhinis of foot soldiers, etc., which were assembled from the kings under his control. Bhīṣma and others who are not under his control have not come (and are not included). Jarāsandha should not be killed now since he will again attempt to make an army. If he is killed who will bring the army in front of me?

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**This is the purpose of my present incarnation—to relieve the earth of its burden, protect the pious and kill the impious.**

**Комментарий:**

My appearance is for this purpose. That purpose is to rid the earth of its burden: to kill the non-devotees (anyeṣām) and protect the devotees.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**I also assume other bodies to protect religion and to end irreligion whenever it flourishes in the course of time.**

**Комментарий:**

Other bodies also (api) such as Varāha are manifested (saṁbhriyate) by me. What to speak of this form of Kṛṣṇa, full of all powers.

### Text 11-12

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] As Kṛṣṇa, protector of the earth, was thinking in this way, two chariots as effulgent as the sun suddenly descended from the sky. They were complete with drivers and equipment. Eternal divine weapons also appeared spontaneously. Seeing these, Kṛṣṇa, Lord of the senses, addressed Saṅkarṣaṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Govinda means he who visits the earth (go) for relieving its burden. Two chariots arrived from Vaikuṇṭha and remained in front of him. The weapons were new though ancient (purāṇāni). They are eternal. They came on their own without any effort to bring them (yadṛcchayā).

### Text 13-14

**Перевод:**

**\[The Supreme Lord said:\] See this danger which has beset your dependents, the Yadus! And see, dear master, how your personal chariot and favorite weapons have come before you. Situated in your chariot, destroy the armies. Deliver the devotees from danger since the purpose for which we have taken birth, My Lord, is to secure the welfare of all devotees. Please now remove from the earth the burden of these twenty-three armies.**

**Комментарий:**

See danger to the Yadus of whom you are the master (tvāvatām). O master (prabho)! Tvāvatāṁ instead of tvadvatāṁ is poetic license. Our birth is for giving happiness (śarma-kṛt) to the devotees. O Lord (īśa)! He encourages Balarāma with this utterance.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**After Kṛṣṇa had thus invited his brother, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, wearing armor and displaying their resplendent weapons, drove out of the city in their chariots. Only a very small contingent of soldiers accompanied them.**

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**As Kṛṣṇa came out of the city with Dāruka at the reins of his chariot, he blew his conch, taking away their courage, and the enemy soldiers’ hearts began to tremble with fear.**

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Jarāsandha looked at the two of them and said: O Kṛṣṇa, lowest of men! I do not wish to fight alone with you, since it would be a shame to fight with a mere boy. You fool who keep yourself hidden, O murderer of your relatives! Go away! I will not fight with you.**

**Комментарий:**

Sarasvatī devī speaks as follows: O Kṛṣṇa, men are inferior to you (puruṣādhamā)! O best of men! I will not fight with you, in whose hair pores resides Brahmā (bālenaikena), i.e., with the Supreme Lord. I am ashamed (lajjayā) to fight with you because I am lowest of the beings. Out of fear of me you kept yourself hidden after killing Kaṁsa. Having gone for the sake of studies, you were not visible. O fool (manda), O killer of your uncle (bandhu-han)! But Sarasvatī devī says, “Since you are situated inside the heart, it is not possible to see you. O best of all (amanda)! O destroyer of jīva’s ignorance (bandhu-hān).”

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**You, Balarāma, should gather your courage and fight with me, if you think you can do it. You may either give up your body when it is cut to pieces by my arrows, and thus attain to heaven, or else kill me.**

**Комментарий:**

But Sarasvatī devī says, “O Balarāma! Kill me.” How? “Having thrown here my body cut by arrows, having attained your objective, from me (mat) go to Vaikuṇṭha, your abode.”

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: Real heroes do not simply boast but rather show their prowess in action. We cannot take seriously the words of one who is full of anxiety and who wants to die.**

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Just as the wind covers the sun with clouds or a fire with dust, the son of Jarā marched toward the two descendants of Madhu and with his huge assemblage of armies surrounded them and their soldiers, chariots, flags, horses and charioteers.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma are called descendants of Madhu dynasty (mādhavau). The example is given just to show that the two could not be seen. As winds cover the sun with clouds or covers fire with dust, so the troops covered Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**The women stood in the watchtowers, palaces and high gates of the city. When they could no longer see Kṛṣṇa’s and Balarāma’s chariots, identified by banners marked with the emblems of Garuḍa and a palm tree, they were struck with grief and fainted.**

**Комментарий:**

Not seeing the chariots of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, the women lamented and fainted since they had more affection for them than the men had.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Seeing his army tormented by the relentless and savage rain of arrows from the massive opposing forces gathered like clouds about him, Kṛṣṇa twanged his excellent bow, Śārṅga, which both gods and demons worship.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing his troops afflicted by the shower of fierce arrows from the clouds of the opposing forces, Kṛṣṇa twanged his excellent bow called Śārṅga.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa took arrows from his quiver, fixed them on the bowstring, pulled the bow, and released endless torrents of sharp shafts, which struck the enemy’s chariots, elephants, horses and infantrymen. The Lord shooting his arrows resembled a blazing circle of fire.**

**Комментарий:**

What was he doing? Taking arrows one by one from his quiver (niṣāṅgāt), he fixed them on the string and pulled the bow. He released a torrent of sharp arrows, striking the chariots, etc., constantly (nirantaram). Nirantara (constantly), an adverb modifying the actions of grabbing the bow, etc., indicates that though the actions took place in sequence the viewers saw them happening simultaneously. Millions of arrows were released within a moment. As a flaming stick when whirled about appears to be a circle, he whirled around facing the troops encircling Mathurā and twanged the bow.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Unlimited elephants fell to the ground, their foreheads split open, cavalry horses fell with severed necks, chariots fell with their horses, flags, drivers and masters all shattered, and foot soldiers collapsed with severed arms, thighs and shoulders.**

**Комментарий:**

Nāyakā means the warriors in the chariots.

### Text 25-28

**Перевод:**

**On the battlefield, hundreds of rivers of blood flowed from the limbs of the humans, elephants and horses who had been cut to pieces. In these rivers arms resembled snakes; human heads, turtles; dead elephants, islands; and dead horses, crocodiles. Hands and thighs appeared like fish, human hair like waterweeds, bows like waves, and various weapons like clumps of bushes. The rivers of blood teemed with all of these. Chariot wheels looked like terrifying whirlpools, and precious gems and ornaments resembled stones and gravel in the rushing red rivers, which aroused fear in the timid and joy in the warrior. With the blows of his plow weapon, the immeasurably powerful Balarāma destroyed Magadhendra’s military force. And though this force was as unfathomable and fearsome as an impassable ocean, for the two sons of Vasudeva, the Lords of the universe, the battle was supreme play.**

**Комментарий:**

Caused by Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, rivers of blood flowed from the severed limbs of humans and other beings. Three verses are connected. A famous analogy is used. In that river, the arms were like snakes. The dead elephants were like islands, raised areas in the middle of the blood. Horses were like crocodiles. The river was spread (ākulāḥ) with these. Hands and thighs were like fish. Men’s hair, being fine, was like śaivala weed in the river. Bows were like waves and the weapons were like bushes. The river was crowded with these (saṅkulāḥ). The river was fearful with wheels or shields (acchūrikā) which were like whirlpools. Huge fine gems and ornaments were like the rocks and pebbles in the river. The troops, though diminished by Balarāma, were unsurpassable and fearsome (bhairavaṁ) like the ocean and without an opposite shore. Antas means depth and pāram means extent. By valor the array was very deep and in area it was without borders. “But the two showed great valor.” It was just play for Vasudeva’s sons but not a fit object for valor.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**For him who orchestrates the creation, maintenance and destruction of the three worlds and who possesses unlimited spiritual qualities, it is hardly amazing that he subdues insignificant opponents because he is playing a human role in his pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

“If he is the Lord of the universe, then how can he have rasa in fighting with insignificant jīvas, very different from him? Otherwise why have this description?” He answers in the first two lines. “Then why is it described as amazing?” Yet he performs human-like pastimes. If he who creates the universe conquers Jarāsandha, there is no rasa when Jarāsandha is so different. But by taking a human-like form, in fighting, there is rasa by having similar forms.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Powerful Jarāsandha, with his chariot lost and all his soldiers dead, was left with only his breath. At that point Balarāma forcibly seized the powerful warrior, just as one lion takes hold of another with speed.**

**Комментарий:**

He seized Jarāsandha who had all troops killed and had only his life remaining.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**With the divine noose of Varuṇa and other, mortal ropes, Balarāma began tying up Jarāsandha, who had killed so many foes. But Kṛṣṇa, protector of the earth, still had a purpose to fulfill through Jarāsandha, and thus he asked Balarāma to stop.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa protected Jārasandha, who had killed many enemies (hatārātim), and was being tied up with Varunā’s ropes, because he wanted to achieve another purpose—gathering the wicked armies.

### Text 32-33

**Перевод:**

**Jarāsandha, whom fighters had highly honored, was ashamed after being released by the two Lords of the universe, and thus he decided to undergo penances. On the road, however, several kings convinced him with both spiritual wisdom and mundane arguments that he should give up his idea of self-abnegation. They told him, “Your defeat by the Yadus was simply the unavoidable reaction of your past karma.”**

**Комментарий:**

Jarāsandha was ashamed because he was honored by heroes (vīrasammataḥ). They give teachings on dharma through material logic (nayanaiḥ prākṛtaiḥ) which had words endowed with teachings of dharma (pavitrārtha). “Your defeat by a few Yadus was because of some ancient karma. Otherwise how could it happen?” By suggested meaning they speak material logic. “You should not be ashamed because of being defeated which was caused by ancient karmas. In battle with equals, there is pride by victory and humility by defeat. In battle with inferiors, there is no pride or humility, in victory or defeat. Thus, you should not be ashamed.”

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**All of his armies having been killed, and himself neglected by the Lord, Jarāsandha, son of Bṛhadratha, then sadly returned to the kingdom of the Magadhas.**

**Комментарий:**

Jarāsandha was the son of Bṛhadratha.

### Text 35-36

**Перевод:**

**Mukunda had crossed the ocean of his enemy’s armies with his own military force completely intact. He received congratulations from the denizens of heaven, who showered him with flowers. The people of Mathurā, relieved of their feverish anxiety and filled with joy, came out to meet him as professional bards, heralds and panegyrists sang in praise of his victory.**

**Комментарий:**

Mukunda also left (yayau from the previous verse).

### Text 37-38

**Перевод:**

**As the Lord entered his city, conches and kettledrums sounded, and many drums, horns, vīṇās, flutes and mṛdaṅgas played in concert. The boulevards were sprinkled with water, there were banners everywhere, and the gateways were decorated festively. The citizens were elated, and the city resounded with the chanting of Vedic hymns.**

**Комментарий:**

The city is described.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**As the women of the city affectionately looked at the Lord, their eyes wide open with love, they scattered flower garlands, yogurt, parched rice and newly grown sprouts upon him.**

**Комментарий:**

He was sprinkled (nicīyamānaḥ) with flowers by the women.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then presented to the Yadu king all the wealth that had fallen on the battlefield—namely, the countless ornaments of the dead warriors.**

**Комментарий:**

He gave everything to Ugrasena (yadu-rājāya).

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Seventeen times the King of Magadha met defeat in this very way. And yet throughout these defeats he continued to fight using his akṣauhiṇī divisions against the forces of the Yadu dynasty who were protected by Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Each time he brought twenty-three akṣauhiṇīs (tāvatī). Tāvatī should actually be masculine.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**By the power of Kṛṣṇa, the Vṛṣṇis would invariably annihilate all of Jarāsandha’s forces, and when all his soldiers had been killed, the king, released by his enemies, would again go away.**

**Комментарий:**

They destroyed (akṣiṇvan) his army. Released by the Yadus (aribhiḥ), he would go to his country.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Just as the eighteenth battle was about to take place, a barbarian warrior named Kālayavana, sent by Nārada, appeared on the battlefield.**

**Комментарий:**

Just before the eighteenth battle, suddenly Kālayavana was seen (pratyadṛśyate) at the edge of Mathurā. He was sent by Nārada. Viṣṇu Purāṇa explains the story as follows: Once, Gārgya was ridiculed by his brother-in-law as a eunuch, and when the Yadus heard this they laughed heartily. Infuriated at them, he pleased Śiva and attained a boon of a son who would terrify the Yadus. Then while returning home, he was requested by the childless king of the Yavanas to give birth to a son through his fertile wife. He produced Kālayavana in wife of the king of Yavanas. He inquired from Nārada, “Presently on this earth who are the most powerful?” Nārada said, “The Yadus are the most powerful.” Being told this, Kālayavana ran to Mathurā.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Arriving at Mathurā, this Yavana laid siege to the city with thirty million barbarian soldiers. He had never found a human rival worth fighting, but he had heard that the Vṛṣṇis were his equals.**

**Комментарий:**

He had heard that the Vṛṣṇis were his equals in prowess (ātmasammitān).

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa and Saṅkarṣaṇa saw Kālayavana, Kṛṣṇa thought about the situation. “Ah, a great danger now certainly threatens the Yadus from two sides.”**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing him, out of affection for the Yadus, acting like a human, Kṛṣṇa began to think thus. It is not that his omniscience is harmed by his thinking like a human, since being omniscient he thought like that. Also this is not a pretense since it is not described like that. Thus the nature of his svarūpa is direct consciousness like his spiritual body having the appearance of nails and hair, since he has no ignorance at all. Yaḥ sarva-jñaḥ sarva-vit: he is omniscient. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**“This Yavana is besieging us already, and the mighty King of Magadha will soon arrive here, if not today then tomorrow or the next day.**

**Комментарий:**

He thinks as follows. He has completely surrounded (nirundhe) us. Mahābala implies that it is impossible to escape from here. “Today or tomorrow” is an expression of common speech.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**“If powerful Jarāsandha comes while we two are busy fighting Kālayavana, Jarāsandha may kill our relatives or else take them away to his capital.**

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**“Therefore we will immediately construct a fortress that no human force can penetrate. Let us settle our family members there and then kill the barbarian king.”**

**Комментарий:**

We will place the Yadus there comfortably (samādhāya).

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**After thus discussing the matter with Balarāma, the Lord had a fortress measuring twelve yojanas built within the sea. Inside that fort he had a city built containing all kinds of wonderful things.**

**Комментарий:**

He had a city built by Viśvakarma (acīkarat) where there all the things were astonishing (kṛtsnādbhutam).

### Text 50-53

**Перевод:**

**In the construction of that city could be seen the full knowledge and skill of craftsmanship of Viśvakarmā. There were wide avenues, commercial roads and courtyards laid out on ample plots of land; there were splendid parks, and also gardens stocked with trees and creepers from the heavenly planets. The gateway towers were topped with golden turrets touching the sky, and their upper levels were fashioned of crystal quartz. The gold-covered houses were adorned in front with golden pots and on top with jeweled roofs, and their floors were inlaid with precious emeralds. Beside the houses stood treasury buildings, warehouses, and stables for fine horses, all built of silver and brass. Each residence had a watchtower, and also a temple for its household deity. Filled with citizens of all four social orders, the city was especially beautified by the palaces of Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the Yadus.**

**Комментарий:**

At that place was seen the knowledge of Viśvakarma, the skill of his craftmanship. The details of the city are described. It had main roads (rathyā) and secondary roads (vīthībhiḥ). It was constructed without overstepping the places for houses, etc. (yathā-vāstu). It had colorful groves and gardens of trees and creepers of the devatās, golden spires which touched the sky, and crystal roof tops and arches. It has horse stables, made of silver and brass, with ornamented golden pots, houses with rubied golden spires and emerald floors. It had temples of devatās (vāstoṣpatīnām), roof top pavilions, and shone with the houses of Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma, Vasudeva, Ugrasena (yadu-deva-gṛhollasat). The surroundings of the city were as follows. Kuśasthalī was surrounded by sweet water of the ocean, and had a wall measuring twelve yojanas in length, made of gold. Outside it were areas decorated with trees and creepers for relaxing, with water bodies. In the walls there were huge enclosures at various places. On their top were jeweled pavilions and on their top were golden spires and flags. In the eight directions were eight arched gates and on their top were crystal watchtowers to look outside. Within the fort were plazas, and within them gardens, ponds and wells. Inside were sheds for sacrifices for devatās, and inside at suitable places, horse stables. In the eastern part were houses of brāhmaṇas, in the west were those of śūdras, in the north were houses of vaiśyas and in the south were houses of kṣatriyas. In the center was the Sudharmā. In front of that were the houses of the Yadus. Starting from the Sudharmā were the main roads and side roads.

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**Indra brought to Kṛṣṇa the Sudharmā assembly hall, standing within which a mortal man is not subject to the laws of mortality. Indra also gave the pārijāta tree.**

**Комментарий:**

A mortal was not affected by the six urges — hunger, thirst, illusion, lamentation, old-age and death (martya-dharmaiḥ).

### Text 55

**Перевод:**

**Varuṇa offered horses as swift as the mind, some of which were pure dark-blue, others white. Kuvera gave his eight mystic treasures, and the rulers of various planets each presented their own opulences.**

**Комментарий:**

Kuvera gave his eight treasures. padmaś caiva mahāpadmo matsya-kūrmau tathaudakaḥ nīlo mukundaḥ śaṅkhaś ca nidhayo ’ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ The eight mystic treasures are called Padma, Mahāpadma, Matsya, Kūrma, Audaka, Nīla, Mukunda and Śaṅkha. Loka-pālaḥ gave their famous individual powers (nijodayān).

### Text 56

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord having come to the earth, O King, these devatās now offered him whatever powers of control he had previously delegated to them for the exercise of their particular authority.**

**Комментарий:**

He had given them their powers since he is himself complete.

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**After transporting all his subjects to the new city by the power of his yogamāyā, Kṛṣṇa consulted with Balarāma, who had remained in Mathurā to protect it. Then, wearing a garland of lotuses but bearing no weapons, Kṛṣṇa went out of Mathurā by its main gate.**

**Комментарий:**

By the power of his inconceivable śakti (yoga-prabhāvena) he transferred all the people of Mathurā to Dvārakā without their knowing it along with their belongings. Sleeping in Mathurā they woke up in Dvārakā and became astonished. This is told in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of Padma Purāṇa. He consulted with Balarāma and deliberated, “Stay here for a moment. By this means I will kill the king of the Yavanas.”

## Chapter 51 - The Deliverance of Mucukunda

### Text 1-6

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Kālayavana saw the Lord come out from Mathurā like the rising moon. The Lord was most beautiful to behold, with his dark-blue complexion and yellow silk garment. Upon his chest he bore the mark of Śrīvatsa, and the Kaustubha gem adorned his neck. His four arms were sturdy and long. He displayed his ever-joyful lotus-like face, with eyes pink like lotuses, beautifully effulgent cheeks, a pristine smile and glittering shark-shaped earrings. The barbarian thought, “This person must indeed be Vāsudeva, since he possesses the characteristics Nārada mentioned: he is marked with Śrīvatsa, he has four arms, his eyes are like lotuses, he wears a garland of forest flowers, and he is extremely handsome. He cannot be anyone else. Since he goes on foot and unarmed, I will fight him without weapons.” Resolving thus, he ran after the Lord, who turned his back and ran away. Kālayavana hoped to catch Kṛṣṇa, though great mystic yogīs cannot attain him.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fifty-first chapter the Lord burns Kālayavana by the glance of Mucukunda and gets rid of him. Satisfied with Mucukunda, offers him a boon. He saw the Lord like the rising moon. The demons cannot appreciate the sweetness of the Lord, though manifest before them, because of their inimical attitude. In order to teach this Śukadeva describes the Lord. The description is according to what Nārada explained to him. He was smiling constantly, nourished by joy of destroying the enemy. Seeing him, the king of the Yavanas began to consider, “This must be Vāsudeva.” He followed Kṛṣṇa who turned and ran (dravantam) somewhat (ā) quickly as a special pastime (pra), to fulfill the words of Śiva to Kālayavana. He wanted to catch Kṛṣṇa. This shows his pride. Kṛṣṇa was rare even for yogīs (durāpam). This shows Kālayavana’s foolishness, making him a laughing stock.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Appearing virtually within reach of Kālayavana’s hands at every moment, the Lords led the King of the Yavanas far away to a mountain cave.**

**Комментарий:**

Kālayavana was led by Kṛṣṇa, almost in his hands, far away to a mountain cave.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**While chasing the Lord, the Yavana cast insults at him, saying “You took birth in the Yadu dynasty. It’s not proper for you to run away!” But still Kālayavana could not reach Kṛṣṇa, because his sinful reactions had not been cleansed away.**

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Although insulted in this way, the Supreme Lord entered the mountain cave. Kālayavana also entered, and there he saw another man lying asleep.**

**Комментарий:**

Entering the cave, the Lord stood near Mucukunda’s head, so that Kālayavana would be in the line of sight of Mucukunda and to hide himself. Kṛṣṇa, the best of the intelligent, stood near the head of King Mucukunda without being visible. He did so to make room for Kālayavana and to hide himself. He did not see the Lord, but someone else. (Hari-vaṁśa)

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**“So, after leading me such a long distance, now he is lying here like some saint!” Thus thinking the sleeping man to be Kṛṣṇa, the deluded fool kicked him with all his strength.**

**Комментарий:**

He kicked that person (tam).

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**The man awoke after a long sleep and slowly opened his eyes. Looking all about, he saw Kālayavana standing beside him.**

**Комментарий:**

Mucukunda saw Kālayavana (tam).

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**The awakened man was angry and cast his glance at Kālayavana, whose body burst into flames. In a single moment, O King Parīkṣit, Kālayavana was burnt to ashes.**

**Комментарий:**

As soon as Mucukunda glanced, Kālayavana burst into flames arising from his own body, and immediately turned to ashes. prasuptaṁ bodhayed yo māṁ taṁ daheyam ahaṁ surāḥ cakṣuṣā krodha-dīptena evam āha punaḥ punaḥ evam astv iti taṁ śakra uvāca tridaśaiḥ saha Again and again Mucukunda said, “O devatās, with eyes blazing with anger, may I incinerate anyone who awakens me from sleep.” Indra along with the devatās then agreed. (Hari-vaṁśa) proktaś ca devaiḥ saṁsuptaṁ yas tvām utthāpayiṣyati deha-jenāgninā sadyaḥ sa tu bhasmī-kariṣyati The devatās declared, “Whoever awakens you from sleep will suddenly be burnt to ashes by a fire generated from his own body.” (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) By asking for a benediction and by receiving a benediction, his prayer for sleep was till the time that he could see Kṛṣṇa, according to the words of Vṛddha-garga with the idea that, “It is impossible for me, full of longing, to spend that long time in a waking state. Thus, by deeply sleeping, the time would pass in an instance.” He prayed for burning anyone who would awaken him in order to destroy demons as previously with the idea that, “Let even Indra not wake me up.”

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: Who was that person, O brāhmaṇa? To which family did he belong, and what were his powers? Why did that destroyer of the barbarian lie down to sleep in the cave, and whose son was he?**

**Комментарий:**

Ko nāma should correctly be kiṁ nāma (which name). Who is this person by lineage and what is his power? This means “What is his seminal lineage?” Who is this person who afflicts the yavana?

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Mucukunda was the name of this great devotee, who was born in the Ikṣvāku dynasty as the son of Māndhātā. He was devoted to brahminical culture and always true to his vow in battle.**

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Begged by Indra and the other devatās to help protect them when they were terrorized by the demons, Mucukunda defended them for a long time.**

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**When the devatās obtained Kārttikeya as their general, they told Mucukunda, “O King, you may now give up your troublesome duty of guarding us.**

**Комментарий:**

Guham means Kārtikeya.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**“Abandoning an unopposed kingdom in the world of men, O valiant one, you neglected all your personal desires while engaged in protecting us.**

**Комментарий:**

Kāma means enjoyment.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**“The children, queens, relatives, ministers, advisers and subjects who were your contemporaries are no longer alive.**

**Комментарий:**

Amātya and mantrin are different due to their different functions. They have all been swept away (kālitāḥ) by time.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**“Inexhaustible time, stronger than the strong, is non-different from the controlling Lord. Like a herdsman moving his animals along, time moves mortal creatures as his pastime.**

**Комментарий:**

By what are they swept away? Time is the Lord since it is figuratively non-different from him by being his śakti. Time takes all beings elsewhere (kālayate).

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**“All good fortune to you! Now please choose a benediction from us—anything but liberation. Viṣṇu alone is capable of giving it, since he is endowed with all powers and is inexhaustible.”**

**Комментарий:**

The lord (īśvaras) of liberation (tasya) means the giver of liberation, since Śiva says in Hari-vaṁśa: mukti pradātā sarveṣāṁ viṣṇur eva na saṁśayaḥ The giver of liberation is Viṣṇu alone. There is no doubt about this. (Hari-vaṁśa)

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Addressed thus, King Mucukunda took his respectful leave of the devatās and went to a cave, where he lay down to enjoy the sleep they had granted him.**

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**After the Yavana was burnt to ashes, the Supreme Lord, chief of the Sātvatas, revealed himself to the wise Mucukunda.**

### Text 23-26

**Перевод:**

**As he gazed at the Lord, King Mucukunda saw that he was dark blue like a cloud, had four arms, and wore a yellow silk garment. On his chest he bore the Śrīvatsa mark and on his neck the brilliantly glowing Kaustubha gem. Adorned with a Vaijayantī garland, the Lord displayed his handsome, peaceful face, which attracts the eyes of all mankind with its shark-shaped earrings and affectionately smiling glance. The beauty of his youthful form was unexcelled, and he moved with the nobility of an angry lion. The highly intelligent king was overwhelmed by the Lord’s effulgence. Expressing his uncertainty, Mucukunda hesitantly questioned Kṛṣṇa who could not be questioned.**

**Комментарий:**

He began to inquire slowly with a doubt which had come (śaṅkitaḥ), “Is this the Lord?” because it was hard to question the Lord (durdharṣam). Iva is ornamental.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Mucukunda said: Who are you who have come to this mountain cave in the forest, having walked on the thorny ground with feet as soft as lotus petals?**

**Комментарий:**

Who are you, who have come to a mountain cave to the forest, after walking on ground profuse with thorns, with soft lotus feet. This indicates the Lord’s affection for his devotee and doubts about his powers.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Perhaps you are the potency of all potent beings. Or maybe you are the powerful god of fire, or the sun-god, the moon-god, the king of heaven or the ruling devatās of some other planet.**

**Комментарий:**

Svit indicates conjecture. Perhaps you are the personified effulgence of effulgent people. Because of your extreme effulgence, you may be the Lord’s vibhūti of fire (bhagavān) or the sun. Seeing his nature of giving joy, he says: maybe you are Soma. Seeing his power, he thought: you may be Indra.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**I think you are the Supreme Lord among the three chief gods, since you drive away the darkness of this cave as a lamp dispels darkness with its light.**

**Комментарий:**

Not satisfied with these options, since the Lord had such power, he speaks again. Among the three chief gods, I consider you to be Viṣṇu, the Supreme Lord. You dispel (bādhase) the external darkness of the cave and the internal darkness of ignorance. You are a lamp made of jewels and consciousness.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**O best among men, if you like, please truly describe your birth, activities and lineage to us, who are eager to hear.**

**Комментарий:**

Plural is used to express his own importance in order to receive an answer, since in expressing his inferiority, he would not be eligible for it.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**As for ourselves, O tiger among men, we belong to a family of fallen kṣatriyas, descendants of King Ikṣvāku. My name is Mucukunda, my Lord, and I am the son of Yauvanāśva.**

**Комментарий:**

He introduces himself. He calls himself a fallen kṣatriya (kṣatrabandhavaḥ) to show his lack of pride. Among those whose importance has ended, I am known as Mucukunda, the son of Māndhātā (yauvanāśva), the son of Yuvanāśva.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**I was fatigued after remaining awake for a long time, and my senses were overwhelmed by sleep. Thus I slept comfortably here in this solitary place until, just now, someone woke me.**

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**The man who woke me was burned to ashes by the reaction of his sins. Just then I saw you, possessing a glorious appearance and the power to chastise your enemies.**

**Комментарий:**

The enemy has been destroyed by you through me.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Your unbearably brilliant effulgence overwhelms our strength, and thus we cannot fix our gaze upon you. O exalted one, you are to be honored by all embodied beings.**

**Комментарий:**

Since our strength is defeated by your power, we cannot even see you, what is the question of asking questions?

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Thus addressed by the king, the Supreme Lord, protector of all beings, smiled and then replied to him in a voice as deep as the rumbling of clouds.**

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear friend, I have taken thousands of births, lived thousands of lives and accepted thousands of names. In fact my births, activities and names are limitless, and thus even I cannot count them.**

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**After many lifetimes someone might count the dust particles on the earth, but no one can ever finish counting my qualities, activities, names and births.**

### Text 38-40

**Перевод:**

**O King, the greatest sages enumerate my births and activities, which take place throughout the three phases of time, but never do they reach the end of them. Nonetheless, O friend, listen as I will tell you about my current birth, name and activities. Some time ago, Brahmā requested me to protect the devotees and destroy the demons who were burdening the earth. Thus I descended in the Yadu dynasty, in the home of Vāsudeva. Because I am the son of Vasudeva, people call me Vāsudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

The first three lines go together. The next three go together. The last line goes alone.

### Text 41-43

**Перевод:**

**I have killed Kālanemi, reborn as Kaṁsa, as well as Pralamba and other enemies of the pious. And now, O King, this barbarian has been burnt to ashes by your piercing glance. Since in the past you repeatedly prayed to me, I have personally come to this cave to show you mercy, for I am affectionately inclined to my devotees. Now choose some benedictions from me, O saintly King. I will fulfill all your desires. One who surrenders to me need never again lament.**

**Комментарий:**

The first three lines go together. The next three go together. I was previously requested with extreme purity (pra arthitaḥ pracuram) to be seen by you. One should not lament again since the benedictions given by me are indestructible.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Mucukunda bowed down to the Lord when he heard this. Remembering the words of the sage Garga, he joyfully recognized Kṛṣṇa to be the Supreme Lord, Nārāyaṇa. The king then addressed him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

He remembered ancient Garga’s words that the Lord would appear in the twenty-eighth cycle of four yugas and then he would see the Lord.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Mucukunda said: O Lord, the people of this world, both men and women, are bewildered by your illusory energy. Unaware of their real benefit, they do not worship you but instead become attached to family affairs, which are actually sources of misery and are cheated.**

**Комментарий:**

Giving up you, the highest goal, accepting other material enjoyments is your māyā. O Lord! Both men and women are cheated.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**O Lord who destroys all suffering! That person , despite having somehow or other automatically obtained the rare and highly evolved human form of life, does not worship your lotus feet even inattentively since he is devoid of discrimination, like an animal. He falls into the blind well of material life.**

**Комментарий:**

Material happiness is obtained even in birth as an animal. But worship of you cannot take place without human birth. Thus though becoming a human, not worshipping you, one is a fool. Having attained human birth in Bhārata, without deformation of limbs (avyaṅgam), the persons fixed in material happiness (asanmatiḥ) who does not worship you falls, like an animal greedy for grass that falls into a well which is covered with grass.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! You have not brought me under your control! I have wasted all this time, becoming more and more intoxicated by my domain and opulence as an earthly king. Misidentifying the mortal body as the self, becoming attached to children, wives, treasury and land, I suffered endless anxiety.**

**Комментарий:**

I am the person whom I have criticized. I think that I am this mortal body (martyātma-buddhiḥ), absorbing in maintaining it.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**With deep arrogance I took myself to be the body, which is a material object like a pot or a wall. Thinking myself a god among men, I traveled the earth surrounded by my charioteers, elephants, cavalry, foot soldiers and generals, disregarding you in my deluding pride.**

**Комментарий:**

Increase of pride is described. I took myself to be the body, which is similar to a pot or a wall (kuḍya). I proudly thought of myself as a king (naradevaḥ). Thus, I became proud (durmadaḥ). In this way I wasted my time (previous verse).

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**A man, not thinking at all of you, with thoughts of what he thinks needs to be done, intensely greedy, and delighting in sense enjoyment, is suddenly confronted by you, who are ever alert. Like a hungry snake licking its fangs before a mouse, you appear before him as death.**

**Комментарий:**

Time, your śakti, devours the person who does not recognize you. You confront the person who ignores you because of material attachment (pramattam), who thinks “I must do this,” whose greed for objects has increased because of many desires (pravṛddhalobham), who is eager for them though his desires are thwarted. In the form of time, being always attentive (apramattaḥ), without his seeing, you subdue him like a hungry snake licking its tongue in front of a mouse.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**The body that at first rides high on fierce elephants or chariots adorned with gold and is known by the name “king” is later, by your invincible power of time, called “feces,” “worms,” or “ashes.”**

**Комментарий:**

The body devoured by time becomes as follows. That body that rides on chariots or elephants, that is called a king, is devoured by invincible time and becomes disgusting with names like feces, worms, or ashes.

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**Having conquered the entire circle of directions and being thus free of conflict, a man sits on a splendid throne, receiving praise from leaders who were once his equals. But when he enters the women’s chambers, where sex pleasure is found, he is led about like a pet animal, O Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way he described how those similar to him are kings and then stool, etc., by passage of time. He describes how simultaneously they are conquerors of all directions and also plaything of women. Being free of war (abhūta-vigrahaḥ), though respected by all kings, a person becomes led around as the plaything in the houses of women by her friends.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**A king who desires even greater power than he already possesses strictly performs his duties, carefully practicing austerity and forgoing sense enjoyment. But he whose urges are so rampant, thinking, “I am independent and supreme,” cannot attain happiness.**

**Комментарий:**

Just as the material enjoyment of those who are turned away from you is condemned, the endeavor to attain it is also condemned. A king performs sacrifice, etc., (karmāṇi) and becomes steady in sleeping on the ground, brahmacārya, etc., and gives charity with expectation of enjoyment. He thinks he will become Indra or some king (svarāṭ). Overwhelmed by those desires, he cannot be happy. He becomes distressed, worried about falling from his position.

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**When the material life of a wandering soul has ceased, O Acyuta, he may attain the association of your devotees. And when he associates with them, there awakens in him devotion unto you-- who take shelter of your devotees and are independent of higher and lower beings.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described that saṁsāra (transmigration) of the jīva opposed to the Lord, it is now described that the saṁsāra is destroyed for a person due to recognizing the Lord. When there is destruction (apavarga) of saṁsāra for the person wandering in various births, association with devotees occurs. This is the fourth type of literary ornament called atiśayokti. The cause is association with devotee and the result is destruction of saṁsāra but cause and effect are reversed in the statement indicating that the cause gives quick effect. When there is association with devotees, only then a person develops the desire (matiḥ) to concentrate on you, the Supreme Lord, dependent on your devotee (sad-gatau). And by the Lord’s mercy follows. Thus there is no partiality in the Lord. By association with devotees, one concentrates on you and receives mercy.

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, I think you have shown me mercy, since my attachment to my kingdom has spontaneously ceased. Rulers of vast empires who desire to enter the forest for a life of solitude because of making proper discrimination pray for that mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

After my association with your devotee Garga, suddenly disinterest in my kingdom arose. I know that it is due to your mercy only. That mercy which caused detachment from kingdom is desired by devotee kings who desire to go to the forest in solitude by thinking of you without interruption.

### Text 55

**Перевод:**

**O all-powerful one, I desire no boon other than service to your lotus feet, the boon most eagerly sought by those who reject liberation as insignificant. O Hari, what enlightened person who worships you, the giver of bhakti, would choose a boon that causes his own bondage?**

**Комментарий:**

Having considered the destinations of the person opposed to the Lord and favorable to the Lord, he answers the Lord’s request to ask for a boon. (verse 44) O Lord! I do not even desire liberation with prominence of one’s own happiness, a boon other than service to your feet. Prayer for affection for you is better but the best prayer (prarthyatamam) is for your service. What discriminating person (kaḥ), worshipping you, would choose a boon other than you, such as Svarga, even if given by you, who give pure bhakti (apavarga-dam) since it covers one’s svarūpa (ātma-bandhanam)? Apavarga means bhakti as in the following: That liberation, whose essential nature is unmotivated bhakti-yoga to the Lord full of qualities, who attracts the minds of all beings, who is not the object of merging, who is not described by material words, who remains beyond destruction of the universe, who is the most excellent ātmā, who is the son of Vasudeva, takes place by destruction of the knot of ignorance which causes various material goals, when there is association with devotees of the Lord. (SB [5.19.19-20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/19.19))

### Text 56

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O Lord, having put aside all objects of material desire, which are bound to the modes of passion, ignorance and goodness, I am approaching you, in human form, for shelter. You are not covered by mundane designations; are beyond the guṇas, non-dual, and pure consciousness.**

**Комментарий:**

“Choose what you want.” Since everything other than you covers your svarūpa, I give up all desires (āśiṣaḥ). I, your devotee, choose (vrajāmi) you. The desires are all māyā, bound by the guṇas. You are beyond māyā (nirañjanam) and endowed with definite qualities (nirguṇam) such as omniscience. Ni means certainty according to Amara-kośa. You are different from the jīva and prakṛti (advayam). You are pure knowledge (jñāpti-mātram). You are the Lord with human form (puruṣam).

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**For so long I have been pained by troubles in this world and have been burning with lamentation. My six enemies are never satiated, and I can find no peace. Therefore, O giver of shelter, O Supreme Soul, please protect me. O Lord, in the midst of danger I have by good fortune approached your lotus feet, which are the truth and which thus make one fearless and free of sorrow.**

**Комментарий:**

“After enjoying wealth, I will give you service to my feet.” Seeing the Lord says this, Mucukunda speaks with misery. Pained by problems in this world (iha), longing to conquer Indra, etc., burning with the regret that I did not worship Kṛṣṇa till this time and having the six senses as enemies which are unsatiated even by enjoying wealth, having not obtained peace by discrimination arising from self or others somehow, I have approached your lotus feet. O giver of bhakti (śaraṇa-da)! O antaryāmī (parātman)! O lord (īśa)! Protect me who have approached you at your lotus feet, which destroy fear of time (abhayam), which destroy lamentation caused by separation from you (aśokam) since you are always situated with your devotees (ṛtam).

### Text 58

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O emperor, great ruler, your mind is pure and potent since your mind is not overcome by material desires or benedictions belonging to a greedy person.**

**Комментарий:**

O conqueror of the world (sārvabhauma), O emperor (mahā-rāja)! In this way the Lord shows his good character by praising him. Your mind is strong because it cannot be disturbed (ūrjitā), because of which it is not overcome by material benedictions.

### Text 59

**Перевод:**

**Understand that I enticed you with benedictions just to prove that you would not be deceived. The intelligence of my unalloyed devotees is never diverted by material blessings.**

**Комментарий:**

To see and show other worshippers your non-deviation, I tempted you.

### Text 60

**Перевод:**

**The minds of nondevotees who attain samādhi using practices as prāṇāyama are not fully cleansed of material desires. Thus, O King, material desires are again seen to arise in their minds.**

**Комментарий:**

Those who are devoid of bhakti to me get disturbed. Sometimes tendency to enjoy objects is seen in them (akṣīna-vāsanam).

### Text 61

**Перевод:**

**Wander this earth at will, with your mind fixed on me. May you always possess such unfailing devotion for me.**

**Комментарий:**

Your bhakti should increase even now.

### Text 62

**Перевод:**

**Because you followed the principles of a kṣatriya, you killed living beings while hunting and performing other duties. You must vanquish the sins thus incurred by carefully executing penances while remaining surrendered to me.**

**Комментарий:**

“Destroy sin by austerity.” This is only for teaching that a devotee kṣatriya should not become absorbed in hunting, since having seen Kṛṣṇa, he did not have these tendencies and since he was previously (in verse 47) addressed as anagha (sinless).

### Text 63

**Перевод:**

**O King, in your very next life you will become an excellent brāhmaṇa, the greatest well-wisher of all creatures, and certainly come to me alone.**

**Комментарий:**

“When will I attain you?” In this very birth (anantare) you will come to me. O King! O kṣatriya twice born! Becoming the best (varaḥ) by increased prema because of separation from me, you will attain me at the end of life.

## Chapter 52 - Rukmiṇī’s Message to Lord Kṛṣṇa

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King, thus receiving Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, Mucukunda circumambulated him and bowed down to him. Then Mucukunda, the beloved descendant of Ikṣvāku, exited through the mouth of the cave.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fifty-second chapter, Kṛṣṇa, while seeing bad omens, enters the city. He accepts the message read by the brāhmaṇa sent by Rukmiṇī. Offering full respects on the ground repeatedly (sannamya), gaining permission from Kṛṣṇa, Mucukunda departed.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that the size of all the human beings, animals, trees and plants was severely reduced, and thus realizing that the age of Kali was at hand, Mucukunda left for the north.**

**Комментарий:**

Kali-yuga had arrived (prāptaṁ) means it had almost arrived due to its proximity.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**The discriminating king, free of doubt through scripture, devoid of material desires, faithfully concentrating on the Lord, absorbed his mind in Kṛṣṇa and came to Gandhamādana Mountain.**

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**There he arrived at Badarikāśrama, the abode of Nara-Nārāyaṇa, where, remaining tolerant of all dualities, he peacefully worshiped the Supreme Lord by performing severe austerities.**

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**The Lord returned to Mathurā, which was still surrounded by Yavanas. Then he destroyed the army of barbarians and began taking their valuables to Dvārakā.**

**Комментарий:**

He took their valuables (ninye) and went to Mathurā (purīṁ).

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**As the wealth was being carried by oxen and men under Kṛṣṇa’s direction, Jarāsandha appeared at the head of twenty-three armies.**

**Комментарий:**

The word ca indicates that their camels were also used.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**O King, seeing the fierce waves of the enemy’s army, the two Mādhavas, imitating human behavior, ran away swiftly.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the swift army of the enemy, the two ran away, like humans (manuṣya-ceṣṭām). This is a nature of the Lord but not imitation fear since Uddhava says: My Lord, even the learned sages become disturbed in their intelligence when they see that your greatness engages in fruitive work although you are free from all desires, that you take birth although you are unborn, that you flee out of fear of the enemy and take shelter in a fort although you are the controller of invincible time, and that you enjoy householder life surrounded by many women although you enjoy in yourself. (SB [3.4.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/4.16)) Thus only a natural pastime like this is filled with joy.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Abandoning the abundant riches, fearless but feigning fear, they went many yojanas on their lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

As if very afraid, they went many yojanas.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**When he saw them fleeing, powerful Jarāsandha laughed loudly and then pursued them with charioteers and foot soldiers. He could not understand the exalted position of the two Lords.**

**Комментарий:**

He did not know the extent of their powers (apramāṇavit).

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Apparently exhausted after fleeing a long distance, the two Lords climbed a high mountain named Pravarṣaṇa, upon which Indra showers incessant rain.**

**Комментарий:**

Running quickly, the two who delight in the dear services of servants (saṁśrāntau), climbed a mountain, eleven yojanas high. It was called Pravarṣaṇa since Indra (bhagavān) used to pour lots of rain on it.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Although he knew they were hiding on the mountain, Jarāsandha could find no trace of them. Therefore, O King, he placed firewood on all sides and set the mountain ablaze.**

**Комментарий:**

He could not find their footprints (padam).

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**The two of them then suddenly jumped from the edge of the burning mountain, which was eleven yojanas high, and fell to the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

From the mountain (tataḥ) avoiding the array of Jarāsandha’s troops, they fell to the ground.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Unseen by their opponent or his followers, O King, those two most exalted Yadus returned to their city of Dvārakā, which had the ocean as a protective moat.**

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Jarāsandha, moreover, mistakenly thought that Balarāma and Keśava had burned to death in the fire. Thus he withdrew his vast military force and returned to the Magadha kingdom.**

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**As ordered by Brahmā, Raivata, the wealthy ruler of Ānarta, gave Balarāma his daughter Raivatī in marriage. This has already been discussed.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to describe Kṛṣṇa’s marriage, the marriage of Balarāma mentioned in the Ninth Canto is remembered.

### Text 16-17

**Перевод:**

**O hero among the Kurus, the Supreme Lord, Govinda, married Bhīṣmaka’s daughter, Vaidarbhī, who was a direct expansion of the goddess of fortune. The Lord did this by her desire, and in the process he beat down Śālva and other kings who took Śiśupāla’s side. Indeed, as everyone watched, Kṛṣṇa took Rukmiṇī just as Garuḍa boldly stole nectar from the devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmiṇī is called śriyo mātrām: all wealth and qualities (śriyo) enter (māti) into her since she is Svayam bhagavān’s dear consort, the complete counterpart of the aṁśī. While the others watched (paśyatām), Kṛṣṇa took Rukmiṇī. The genetive (paśyatām) indicates that he took her while disregarding the onlookers.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: The Supreme Lord married Rukmiṇī, the beautiful-faced daughter of Bhīṣmaka, in the Rākṣasa style—or so I have heard.**

**Комментарий:**

The word rākṣasena is used due to the smṛti statement: The rākṣasa style of marriage involves stealing the bride from a battle.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**My lord, I wish to hear how the immeasurably powerful Kṛṣṇa took away his bride while defeating such kings as Māgadha and Sālva.**

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**What experienced listener, O brāhmaṇa, could ever grow satiated while listening to the pious, charming and ever-fresh topics of Kṛṣṇa, which cleanse away the world’s contamination?**

**Комментарий:**

Puṇyā means attractive. Mādhvīḥ means sweet. Śṛṇvānaḥ should be śṛṇvan (while listening).

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bādarāyaṇi said: There was a king named Bhīṣmaka, the ruler of Vidarbha, endowed with great qualities. He had five sons and one daughter of lovely countenance.**

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Rukmī was the first-born son, followed by Rukmaratha, Rukmabāhu, Rukmakeśa and Rukmamālī. Their sister was the excellent Rukmiṇī.**

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Hearing of the beauty, prowess, character and opulence of Mukunda from visitors to the palace who sang his praises, Rukmiṇī decided that he would be the perfect husband for her.**

**Комментарий:**

She thought he would be a suitable (sadṛśaṁ) husband for herself.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa knew that Rukmiṇī possessed intelligence, auspicious bodily markings, beauty, proper behavior and all other good qualities. Concluding that she would be a suitable wife for him, he made up his mind to marry her.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa heard about Rukmiṇī from other people.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Because Rukmī envied the Lord, O King, he forbade his family members to give his sister to Kṛṣṇa, although they wanted to. Instead, Rukmī decided to give Rukmiṇī to Śiśupāla.**

**Комментарий:**

The relatives such as her father wanted to give her to Kṛṣṇa, but Rukmī disregarding them, forbidding them from Kṛṣṇa, he thought that Śiśupāla should be the groom since he hated Kṛṣṇa (kṛṣṇadviṭ).

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Dark-eyed Vaidarbhī was aware of this plan, and it deeply upset her. Analyzing the situation, she quickly sent a trustworthy brāhmaṇa to bring Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

She sent the brāhmaṇa to bring Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Upon reaching Dvārakā, the brāhmaṇa was allowed inside by the gatekeepers and saw Kṛṣṇa, the source of all avatāras, sitting on a golden throne.**

**Комментарий:**

He was given permission to enter by the gatekeepers (pratīhāraiḥ).

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the brāhmaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Lord of the brāhmaṇas, came down from his throne and seated him. Then the Lord worshiped him just as he himself is worshiped by the devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

He worshipped brāhmaṇa with great devotion just as the devatās worship Kṛṣṇa (yathā ātmānam) with great devotion.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**After the brāhmaṇa had eaten and rested, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the goal of saintly devotees, came forward, and while massaging the brāhmaṇa’s feet with his hands, he gently questioned him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa massaged (abhimṛśan) the brāhmaṇa’s feet gently. He remained steady in heart (avyagraḥ), though distracted about the marriage.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**\[The Supreme Lord said:\] O best of exalted brāhmaṇas, are your religious practices, sanctioned by senior authorities, proceeding without great difficulty? Is your mind always fully satisfied?**

**Комментарий:**

Is your dharma accomplished without too much suffering (nātikṛcchreṇa)? Since dharma cannot be accomplished without some suffering, he does not ask whether he is able to accomplish dharma comfortably.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**When a brāhmaṇa is satisfied with whatever comes his way and does not fall away from his religious duties, those very religious principles fulfill all his wishes.**

**Комментарий:**

When he does not deviate from his own dharma by collecting fallen grains from the field, his svadharma (saḥ) yields all desired results.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**An unsatisfied brāhmaṇa wanders restlessly from one planet to another, even if he becomes king of heaven. But a satisfied brāhmaṇa, though he may possess nothing, rests peacefully, all his limbs free of distress.**

**Комментарий:**

He wanders from planet to planet, not staying in one place happily, though he becomes Indra. Another version has nāpnoti. Though he attains heavenly planets, due to being overcome by desire he does not attain them.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**I repeatedly bow my head in respect to those brāhmaṇas who are satisfied with their lot. Saintly, prideless and peaceful, they are the best well-wishers of all living beings.**

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**O brāhmaṇa, is your king attending to your welfare? That king in whose country the citizens are happy and protected is very dear to me.**

**Комментарий:**

O brāhmaṇa! Are you happy with the king? That king whose citizens live happily in that place (viṣaya) is dear to me.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Whence have you come, crossing the impassable sea, and for what purpose? Explain all this to us if it is not a secret and tell us what we may do for you.**

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Thus questioned by the Supreme Lord, who incarnates to perform his pastimes, the brāhmaṇa told him everything.**

**Комментарий:**

Asked about what should be asked (saṁpṛṣtaḥ saṁpraśnaḥ) by Kṛṣṇa (paremeṣṭhinā), the brāhmaṇa described everything, the feelings of the relatives and the activities of Rukmī. The Lord is called parameṣṭhī in Viṣṇu-sahasra-nāmā-stotra. The Lord has a body which is the shelter of the līlā-śakti (līlā-gṛhīta-dehena).

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Rukmiṇī said: O beauty of the worlds, having heard of your qualities, which enter the ears of those who hear and remove their bodily distress, and having also heard of your beauty, which fulfills all desires of those who see, I have fixed my shameless mind upon you, O Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Opening the seal on the letter of seven verses written by Rukmiṇī in a solitary place, showing it to Kṛṣṇa, he read it aloud on Kṛṣṇa’s order. O Acyuta! Hearing about your qualities and form, my heart has become shameless and has become absorbed (āviśati) in you. Even after making my heart shameless by your qualities, you do not retire from that. I do not know what else you want to do. My heart having become shameless, is absorbed in you, I do not know what else it wishes to become. Your qualities are omniscience, omnipotence, friendliness, softness, worthy of surrender, being affectionate to those who take shelter, etc. Those qualities, being heard, entering the ears of the girls who hear, destroy all suffering. O lord (aṅga)! The complexion of your body (rūpam), the color of your limbs, lips and nails, is a more sweeter attainment than all sense objects of the eyes of the seers, such as the colors of the sapphire, ruby and moonstone. She calls out accordingly. O most beautiful person in the universe! You are more beautiful than anything in all spiritual worlds up to Mahāvaikuṇṭha and all material worlds. You are pleasing both by nature and by form. Thus your qualities which make my heart shameless are alone to be blamed, not I.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**O Mukunda, you are equal only to yourself in lineage, character, beauty, knowledge, youthfulness, wealth and influence. O lion among men, you delight the minds of all mankind. What aristocratic, sober-minded and marriageable girl of a good family would not choose you as her husband when the proper time has come?**

**Комментарий:**

“This is very bold for you, a cultured girl.” O Mukunda, with a smile like a jasmine (kunda) on your face (mukha). You have had the opportunity to smile at me! What girl endowed with great beauty and qualities, sober minded, and born in a good family, would not choose you as a husband? Rather all would choose you. Many equal to me will choose you. You are incomparable (ātma-tulyam) in family, character, beauty, knowledge, youthfulness, wealth and influence. You delight the minds of the universe. What then is the offense of my mind? O best of men (nṛ-siṁha) at the time of the marriage (kāle)!

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, my dear Lord, I have chosen you as my husband, and I surrender myself to you. Please come swiftly, O almighty one, and make me your wife. My dear lotus-eyed Lord, let Śiśupāla never touch the hero’s portion like a jackal stealing the property of a lion.**

**Комментарий:**

Therefore, you have been chosen by me as my husband. O Lord! I have offered myself to you (ātmārpitaḥ). Thus coming here, make me your wife (jāyām). She finds fault in the opponent. May Śiśupāla not come close (ārāt) and touch me, the portion meant for you, the hero, like the jackal taking the food of the lion. I will enter fire if he approaches. And you will lose your fame.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**If I have sufficiently worshiped the Supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa by pious works, sacrifices, charity, rituals and vows, and also by worshiping the devatās, brāhmaṇas and gurus, then may Kṛṣṇa come and take my hand, and not Damaghoṣa’s son or anyone else.**

**Комментарий:**

O Lord! If you say you are rarely attained, but attained by pious acts, then let this happen because of even my pious actions previously performed. If I have worshiped the Lord profusely (alam) by digging wells (purta), by sacrifices (iṣṭa), by giving charity (dātta), by regulations (niyama) directed to the Lord, by vratas such as bathing in holy places, observing vows of fasting like Ekādaśī, and by worshiping the devatās, brāhmaṇas and gurus, which are corollaries to the worship of the Lord himself, then may Svayam bhagavān, the elder brother of Gada, come here and accept me. Others like Śiśupāla should not come for marrying me. She mentions Śiśupāla since the occasion is marriage with him.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**O unconquerable one, tomorrow when my marriage ceremony is about to begin, you should arrive unseen in Vidarbha and surround yourself with the leaders of your army. Then crush the forces of Caidya and Magadhendra and marry me in the Rākṣasa style, winning me with your valor.**

**Комментарий:**

“What should I do now for you, since you have been offered by relatives to Śiśupāla?” O one who is unconquerable for all (ajita)!
