Thus since you are fearless, when the marriage takes place tomorrow, first come unseen by others, enter Kuṇḍinapura, and then, surround yourself with leaders of armies for your own glory. Otherwise it is difficult to enter the city, since Rukmī may fight using brave soldiers outside the city. But in entering the city, since they will not fight with you thinking that you have come in order to see the beauty of the wedding, you can then easily take me away. If they start fighting with you, worrying that something undesirable will occur, you can show your prowess. Crushing the armies of Śiśupāla and others with force (prasahya), marry me by Rākṣasa method paying the valor as the price for me. Previously also you churned the milk ocean and attained me (as Lakṣmī).

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Since I will be staying within the inner chambers of the palace, you may wonder, “How can I carry you away without killing some of your relatives?” But I shall tell you a way: On the day before the marriage there is a grand procession to honor the royal family’s deity, and in this procession the new bride goes outside the city to visit Goddess Girijā.**

**Комментарий:**

“Let Śiśupāla’s army be harassed. But in taking you from the inner chambers however, your relatives may get killed.” If you say this, then I will explain. The procession will take the bride to the Durgā temple outside the city. If you steal me from there, the relatives will not get killed.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed one, great souls like Śiva hanker to bathe in the dust of your lotus feet and thereby destroy their ignorance. If I cannot obtain your mercy, I shall simply give up my vital force, which will have become weak from the severe penances I will perform. Then, after hundreds of lifetimes of endeavor, I may obtain your mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

“O princess! What is the use of such obstinacy which only cause problems? You may also choose Śiśupāla whose family rituals are famous.” Great souls desire to bath in the dust of your lotus feet in order to destroy their ignorance (tamaḥ), even Śiva desires. If I do not attain your mercy, I will give up my life airs made faint by fasting. And I will give up my life airs multiple times for even as many hundreds of lives till your mercy is obtained. Thus she shows her deep conviction since she actually has eternal life. Giving up you, the Supreme Lord, how can I accept some low jīva?

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa said: This is the confidential message I have brought with me, O Lord of the Yadus. Please consider what must be done in these circumstances and do it at once.**

**Комментарий:**

This message should not be revealed anywhere. For if it is, she will be a shame (to the family). Therefore, you should consider what should be done and then do that. There can be no delay.

## Chapter 53 - Kṛṣṇa Kidnaps Rukmiṇī

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus hearing the confidential message of Rukmiṇī, Kṛṣṇa, giver of joy to the Yadus, took the brāhmaṇa’s hand and, smiling, spoke to him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fifty-third chapter, having gone to Kuṇḍina and being worshipped by Bhīṣmaka, he forcibly takes Rukmiṇī as she sets out to worship Durgā. He smiled, showing his self-control though he was anxious to attain Rukmiṇī.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: Just as Rukmiṇī’s mind is fixed on me, my mind is fixed on her. I can’t even sleep at night. I know that Rukmī, out of envy, has forbidden our marriage.**

**Комментарий:**

He cannot sleep because of attachment to her, which is for his own purpose, and not for attracting other’s minds. Veda stands of vedmi.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**She has dedicated herself exclusively to me, and her beauty is flawless. I will bring her here after thrashing those worthless kings in battle, just as a blazing flame is produced from firewood.**

**Комментарий:**

An example of thrashing the kings and bringing Rukmiṇī is given. Just as the flame, increased by firewood, turns the firewood to ashes, she, surrounded by wicked armies, manifesting herself, will destroy them. I am merely an instrument of that.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of demons, also understood the exact lunar time for Rukmiṇī’s wedding. Thus he told his driver, “Dāruka, make my chariot ready immediately.”**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding (vi-jñāya) from the brāhmaṇa that the constellation for the marriage was in the evening two days later, leaving that evening he arrived in Vidarbha in the morning since she had asked him to be there the next day (SB [10.52.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/52.41)).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Dāruka brought the Lord’s chariot, yoked with the horses named Śaibya, Sugrīva, Meghapuṣpa and Balāhaka. He then stood before Kṛṣṇa with joined palms.**

**Комментарий:**

The four horses are described in Padma Purāṇa. Śaibya was green like a parrot’s wings, Sugrīva yellow-gold, Meghapuṣpa the color of a cloud, and Balāhaka whitish.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa mounted his chariot and had the brāhmaṇa do likewise. Then the Lord’s swift horses took them from the Ānarta district to Vidarbha in a single night.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord reached Vidarbha in a single night. Hearing Rukmiṇī’s message in the evening, mounting his chariot and going, he arrived the next morning in Kuṇḍina.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**King Bhīṣmaka, the master of Kuṇḍina, having succumbed to the sway of affection for his son, was about to give his daughter to Śiśupāla. The king saw to all the required preparations.**

**Комментарий:**

The king followed his son, controlled by affection for him. It is understood that Rukmī had attempted suicide, retirement to forest, etc. The king saw to the decoration, etc., of the city.

### Text 8-9

**Перевод:**

**The king had the main avenues, commercial roads and intersections thoroughly cleaned and then sprinkled with water, and he also had the city decorated with triumphant archways and multicolored banners on poles. The men and women of the city, arrayed in spotless raiment and anointed with fragrant sandalwood paste, wore precious necklaces, flower garlands and jeweled ornaments, and their homes decorated with canopies were filled with the aroma of aguru.**

**Комментарий:**

It had men and women decorated with garlands, scents and necklaces.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**O King, in accordance with prescribed rituals, Bhīṣmaka worshiped the forefathers, devatās and brāhmaṇas, feeding them all properly. Then he had the traditional mantras chanted for the well-being of the bride.**

**Комментарий:**

He had them chant those auspicious prayers which are to be chanted for a daughter on the occasion of the wedding (yathā-nyāyam).

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**The bride cleaned her teeth and bathed, after which she put on the auspicious wedding necklace. Then she was dressed in brandnew upper and lower garments and adorned with most excellent jeweled ornaments.**

**Комментарий:**

She was made auspicious by the wedding necklace (kṛta-kautukamaṅgalām). Āhata means cloth which has been freshly taken from the loom since that is auspicious. It is said by Brahmā that clothing fresh off the loom is best during auspicious ceremonies. The verb (cakruḥ) is in the next verse.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**The best of brāhmaṇas chanted mantras of the Ṛg, Sāma and Yajur Vedas for the bride’s protection, and a famous priest learned in the Atharva Veda offered oblations to pacify the controlling planets.**

**Комментарий:**

The priest learned in the Atharva Veda offered oblations using Atharva mantras to pacify the planets.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Outstanding in his knowledge of regulative principles, the king rewarded the brāhmaṇas with gold, silver, clothing, cows and sesame seeds mixed with raw sugar.**

**Комментарий:**

Rājā refers to Bhīṣmaka.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Damaghoṣa, lord of Cedi, had also engaged brāhmaṇas expert in chanting mantras to perform all rituals necessary to assure his son’s prosperity.**

**Комментарий:**

Just like Bhīṣmaka (evam), the king of Cedi performed karmas for the marriage of his son. His actions took place not too far from Kuṇḍina since they were performed the previous day.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**King Damaghoṣa traveled to Kuṇḍina accompanied by armies of elephants exuding mada, chariots hung with golden chains, and numerous cavalry and infantry soldiers.**

**Комментарий:**

The king went with elephants which had mada flowing from them.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Bhīṣmaka, the lord of Vidarbha, came out of the city dutifully and met King Damaghoṣa, offering him tokens of respect. Bhīṣmaka then settled Damaghoṣa in a residence especially constructed for the occasion.**

**Комментарий:**

He joyfully settled the king in another place at a river crossing which was decided.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Śiśupāla’s supporters—Śālva, Jarāsandha, Dantavakra and Vidūratha—all came, along with Pauṇḍraka and thousands of other kings.**

### Text 18-19

**Перевод:**

**To secure the bride for Śiśupāla, the kings who envied Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma came to the following decision among themselves: “If Kṛṣṇa comes here with Balarāma and the other Yadus to steal the bride, we shall band together and fight him.” Thus those envious kings went to the wedding with their entire armies and a full complement of military conveyances.**

**Комментарий:**

The kings were prepared (yattāḥ) to insure (sādhitum) that Rukmiṇī was given to Śiśupāla.

### Text 20-21

**Перевод:**

**When Balarāma heard about these preparations of the inimical kings and how Kṛṣṇa had set off alone to steal the bride, he feared that a fight would ensue. Immersed in affection for his brother, he hurried to Kuṇḍina with a mighty army consisting of infantry and of soldiers riding on elephants, horses and chariots.**

**Комментарий:**

Through word of mouth, Balarāma heard of this. Though omniscient he became worried that a quarrel was certain. He worried out of affection. That affection covered his natural omniscience, for it is human nature to worry about the dangers imminent for a friend: aniṣṭāśaṅkīni bandhu-hṛdayāni bhavanti: friends always worry that their friend is in danger.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**The lovely daughter of Bhīṣmaka anxiously awaited the arrival of Kṛṣṇa, but when she did not see the brāhmaṇa return she thought as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Pratyāpattim means return.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**\[Princess Rukmiṇī thought:\] Alas, my wedding is to take place when the night ends! How unlucky I am! Lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa does not come. I don’t know why. And even the brāhmaṇa messenger has not yet returned.**

**Комментарий:**

Her thoughts are described. Three yāmās (nine hours) are remaining for my wedding. Tomorrow is the fixed time for the wedding. There can be no other cause than my misfortune.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Perhaps the faultless Lord, even while preparing to come here, saw something contemptible in me and therefore has not come to take my hand.**

**Комментарий:**

Perhaps (api) seeing some fault in me, the boldness in the form of the love letter, Kṛṣṇa has not come even though he was prepared to come. Since Kṛṣṇa was ready to come, (and because the brāhmaṇa would accompany him) he did not send the brāhmaṇa ahead. However, coming close, understanding some fault in me, he gave up his plan to come here. Being unsuccessful, the brāhmaṇa too has not come to see me, out of fear that I would give up my body upon hearing the bad news.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**I am extremely unfortunate, for the creator is not favorably disposed toward me, nor is the great Śiva. Or perhaps Śiva’s wife, Devī, who is known as Gaurī, Rudrāṇī, Girijā and Satī, has turned against me.**

**Комментарий:**

She worries about other things. Kṛṣṇa has not come, being obstructed by Śiva and the creator, unfavorable to me. But it is not possible for the Supreme Lord to be angry with me, a mere girl. Maybe Devī is angry with me. Why would she dislike me, though I worship her? Śiva, her husband, makes the whole world cry. His wife (rudrānī) makes me cry. That is her nature. She has a hard heart. She is the daughter of stone (girijā). And she is anger. In a previous birth, angrily she entered the sacrificial fire (satī). She will make even me enter the fire due to being unsuccessful. She thought profusely. These statements of omniscient MahāLakṣmī arose due to her omniscience being covered by the līlāśakti, promoted by Kṛṣṇa’s desire.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**As she thought in this way, the young maiden, whose mind had been stolen by Kṛṣṇa, closed her tear-filled eyes, remembering that there was still time.**

**Комментарий:**

Knowing the time that the Lord should come had not passed, she closed her eyes to meditate on him.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**O King, as the bride thus awaited the arrival of Govinda, she felt a twitch in her left thigh, arm and eye. This was a sign that something desirable would happen.**

**Комментарий:**

Her limbs on the left quivered as a sign of auspiciousness (priyabhāṣiṇaḥ). Priya-bhāṣiṇaḥ, being an eka-śeṣa compound, should be in the neuter (priya-bhāṣīni) to agree with netram (which it is modifying) but is in the masculine as poetic license.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Just then the purest of learned brāhmaṇas, following Kṛṣṇa’s order, came to see the Rukmiṇī, shining with ornaments, within the inner chambers of the palace.**

**Комментарий:**

She saw the brāhmaṇa named Sunanda who had been ordered by Kṛṣṇa, situated in grove in the city, “Tell her that I have come.”

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Noting the brāhmaṇa’s joyful face and serene movements, saintly Rukmiṇī, who could expertly interpret such symptoms, inquired from him with a pure smile.**

**Комментарий:**

Her meditation was broken by the brāhmaṇa saying, “I have come from Kṛṣṇa.” The confusion in her mind calmed on seeing his joyful face and due to whom the mind is free from agitation (avyagrātmagatiṁ). She remembered the quivering of her left limbs and his joy which indicated fulfillment of the task.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa announced to her the arrival of Yadunandana and relayed the Lord’s promise to marry her.**

**Комментарий:**

He informed her that Kṛṣṇa had arrived. He announced Kṛṣṇa’s promise (verse 3) to take her.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Princess Vaidarbhī was overjoyed to learn of Kṛṣṇa’s arrival. Not finding anything at hand suitable to offer the brāhmaṇa, she simply bowed down to him.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding that Kṛṣṇa had come, but not seeing a proper object to give him since she considered giving everything of hers to be insufficient for his excellent duty, she just offered respects to him and by that indicated, “I am controlled by your family lineage.” It is understood that his house immediately became filled with all wealth.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**The king, upon hearing that Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma had come and were eager to witness his daughter’s wedding, went forth with abundant offerings to greet them as music resounded.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhīṣmaka heard about Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma’s arrival.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Presenting them with madhu-parka, new clothing and other desirable gifts, he worshiped them according to standard rituals.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding the Lord had come for his daughter’s wedding, he worshipped them suitably since he is called mahā-matiḥ in the next verse.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Generous King Bhīṣmaka arranged opulent accommodations for the two Lords, and also for their army and entourage. In this way he afforded them proper hospitality.**

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Bhīṣmaka gave all desirable things to the kings who had assembled for the occasion, honoring them as befitted their political power, age, their armies and wealth.**

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**When the residents of Vidarbha heard that Kṛṣṇa had come, they all went to see him. With the cupped palms of their eyes they drank the honey of his lotus face.**

**Комментарий:**

They drank the sweetness of his lotus face. Mentioning his lotus face in singular indicates its unlimited nature and astonishing nature.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**\[The people of the city said:\] Rukmiṇī, and no one else, deserves to become his wife, and he also, possessing such flawless beauty, is the only suitable husband for Princess Rukmiṇī.**

**Комментарий:**

The words of the citizens are repeated. The word eva is repeated. 1. She is suitable for Kṛṣṇa alone (asya eva), and no one else. 2. She is suitable as his wife alone (bhāryaiva), not as an object to be enjoyed. 3. Rukmiṇī alone (rukmiṇy eva) is suitable to be his wife, no one else. 4. She is definitely suitable (arhaty eva) and not that she is unsuitable. 5. He alone (asāv eva) and no other is most suitable (samucitaḥ) as a husband for Rukmiṇī. 6. He is suitable for her alone (bhaiṣmyā eva) and for no one else. 7. He is completely suitable for her (samyag evocitaḥ) and not even a little bit unsuitable. Among the seven, in one sentence distinction is shown (in not having eva) by the word aparā, for the sake of implying it in the other sentences. Since there are many people speaking here, there are many statements. Thus it is understood that seven sentences are combined in one. Here “Rukmiṇī should certainly be Kṛṣṇa’s wife only, and no one else’s,” is statement of some. “Rukminī should be his only wife,” is statement of others. “Rukmiṇī alone and no one else should be his wife,” is of some others. In this way the other four statements may be construed. In this way since it can be taken as one composite sentence there is no fault of vākya-bheda .

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**May Acyuta, the creator of the three worlds, be satisfied with whatever pious work we may have done and show his mercy by taking the hand of Vaidarbhī.**

**Комментарий:**

Satisfied with whatever good works we have done, Kṛṣṇa should accept Rukmiṇī’s hand. We offer all our pious credits to Rukmiṇī so she can marry Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Bound by their swelling love, the city’s residents spoke in this way. Then the bride, protected by guards, left the inner palace to visit the temple of Ambikā.**

**Комментарий:**

Controlled by increasing love (prema-kalā-baddhā) for Rukmiṇī, they spoke. Kal means increase. Kal and val are the kāma-dhenus of poets (i.e. words made with them can take a wide range of meanings).

### Text 40-41

**Перевод:**

**Rukmiṇī silently went out on foot to see the lotus feet of the deity Bhavānī. Accompanied by her mothers and girlfriends and protected by the King’s valiant soldiers, who held their upraised weapons at the ready, she simply absorbed her mind in the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. And all the while mṛdaṅgas, conch shells, paṇavas, horns and other instruments resounded.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmiṇī was carried in a palanquin from the city palace to the temple complex of Durgā. Then she walked into the temple room on her feet. But the guards stood around the temple. Drums were struck and other instruments played (jaghnire).

### Text 42-43

**Перевод:**

**Behind the bride followed thousands of prominent courtesans bearing various offerings and presents, along with well-adorned brāhmaṇas’ wives singing and reciting prayers and bearing gifts of garlands, scents, clothing and jewelry. There were also professional singers, musicians, bards, chroniclers and heralds.**

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Upon reaching the goddess’s temple, Rukmiṇī first washed her lotus feet and hands and then sipped water for purification. Thus sanctified and peaceful, she came into the presence of mother Ambikā.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmiṇī performed ācamana (upaspṛśya) and entered the inner sanctum (deva-sadanaṁ). The masculine is used for deva (in devasadanam) by the rule, kukkuṭy-ādīnām aṇḍādiṣu puṁvadbhāvo vaktavyaḥ (Vārtika 6.3.42). There was a jeweled pavilion within the huge temple complex.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**The older wives of brāhmaṇas, expert in the knowledge of rituals, led young Rukmiṇī in offering respects to Bhavānī, wife of Śiva, who was with him always.**

**Комментарий:**

The elderly wives of the brāhmaṇas had her offer respects to Śiva’s wife. They prayed, “O Durgā, just as you, the wife of Śiva, are always with Śiva, please make her Kṛṣṇa’s wife and be with him always,” since they had also previously prayed in verse 38 on seeing Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**\[Princess Rukmiṇī prayed:\] O mother Ambikā, wife of Lord Siva, I repeatedly offer my obeisances unto you, together with your children. May Kṛṣṇa become my husband! Please grant this!**

**Комментарий:**

They had her recite this mantra. Offering respects to the offspring indicates, “May Gaṇeśa remove all the obstacles now facing me.” Please agree to this (anumodatām).

### Text 47-48

**Перевод:**

**Rukmiṇī worshiped the goddess with water, scents, whole grains, incense, clothing, garlands, necklaces, jewelry and other prescribed offerings and gifts, and also with arrays of lamps. The married brāhmaṇa women each performed worship simultaneously with the same items, also offering savories and cakes, prepared betel nut, sacred threads, fruit and sugar-cane juice.**

**Комментарий:**

Srak refers to flower garlands and mālya refers jeweled necklaces. Lavaṇa-āpūpa (savory cakes) refers to what is known as salted mung bean cakes.

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**The ladies gave the bride the remnants of the offerings and then blessed her. She in turn bowed down to them and the deity and accepted the garland remnants as prasādam.**

**Комментарий:**

Śeṣāṁ means garland remnants.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**The princess then gave up her vow of silence and left the Ambikā temple, holding on to a friend with her hand, which was adorned with a jeweled ring.**

**Комментарий:**

Muni-vratam means silence.

### Text 51-55

**Перевод:**

**Rukmiṇī appeared as enchanting as the Lord’s illusory potency, which enchants even the sober and grave. Thus the kings gazed upon her virgin beauty, her shapely waist, and her lovely face adorned with earrings. Her hips were graced with a jewelstudded belt, her breasts were just budding, and her eyes seemed apprehensive of her encroaching locks of hair. She smiled sweetly, her jasmine-bud teeth reflecting the glow of her bimbared lips. As she walked with the motions of a royal swan, the effulgence of her tinkling ankle bells beautified her feet. Seeing her, the assembled heroes were totally bewildered. Lust tore at their hearts. Indeed, when the kings saw her broad smile and shy glance, they became stupefied, dropped their weapons and fell unconscious to the ground from their elephants, chariots and horses. On the pretext of the procession, Rukmiṇī displayed her beauty for Kṛṣṇa alone. Slowly she advanced the two moving lotus-whorls of her feet, awaiting the arrival of the Supreme Lord. With the fingernails of her left hand she pushed some strands of hair away from her face and shyly looked from the corners of her eyes at the kings standing before her. At that moment she saw Kṛṣṇa. Then, while his enemies looked on, the Lord seized the princess, who was eager to mount his chariot.**

**Комментарий:**

As she returned to the palanquin outside the temple wall, the warriors saw an ābhāsa of her śakti and fainted. This is described in three verses and a line (of verse 54). The word iva is for restriction. The warriors, seeing her as only the deva-māyā, fainted (three verses later). They thought she was the Lord’s material māyā. That deva-māyā alone is described. The śyāmā woman has a golden complexion. Her breasts were just becoming visible (vyañjat), she was in the first part of kaiśora period. She had fickle glances, seemingly fearing her locks of hair. She had teeth like jasmine buds tinted red by the reflection of her bimba fruit lips. She moved with feet made beautiful by the shining of her jingling ankle bells crafted with great skill. Padā in the singular indicates a type. Seeing that māyā of the Lord, the kings, though famous for qualities like self-control, etc., (yaśasvinaḥ), became afflicted by lust produced from seeing her (tat-kṛta). This pain of lust was produced by thinking of her to be the Lord’s māyā, but not by thinking of her as the daughter of Bhīṣmaka. Not only did they faint but even fell on the ground. Here too devamāyām iva needs to be supplied. Seeing Rukmiṇī as deva-māyā, the kings fell on the ground. Rukmiṇī is described in five lines. On the pretext of pilgrimage, she offered to Kṛṣṇa her beauty, and not to others. Desiring to see Kṛṣṇa she looked shyly at the kings present. Thinking, “These are other men,” shyness arose in her glances. Among them she saw Acyuta, who never disappeared from her heart.

### Text 56

**Перевод:**

**Lifting the princess onto his chariot, whose flag bore the emblem of Garuḍa, Mādhava drove back the circle of kings. With Balarāma in the lead, he slowly exited, like a lion removing his prey from the midst of jackals.**

**Комментарий:**

He went slowly since he was without fear.

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**The proud kings inimical to the Lord, headed by Jarāsandha, could not tolerate this humiliating defeat. They exclaimed, “Oh, damn us! Though we are mighty archers, mere cowherds have stolen our honor, just as puny animals might steal the honor of lions!”**

**Комментарий:**

The shouts of the intolerant kings like Jarāsandha are described. What misfortune (aho)! For our fame is stolen by cowherds. The other meaning of gopaiḥ is as suggested by Sarasvatī devī is “by kings.” The plural gopaiḥ (by cowherds) is used since the Yadus following Kṛṣṇa, were many.

## Chapter 54 - The Marriage of Kṛṣṇa and Rukmiṇī

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus spoken, all those infuriated kings donned their armor and mounted their conveyances. Each king, bow in hand, was surrounded by his own army as he went after Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fifty-fourth chapter Kṛṣṇa defeats the enemy, disfigures Rukmī, enligthens Rukminī and marries her in Dvārakā. Surrounded by their troops (parikrāntāḥ) they pursued him.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**The commanders of the Yādava army, seeing the enemy racing to attack, turned to face them and stood firm, O King, twanging their bows.**

**Комментарий:**

They sounded their bows.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Mounted on the backs of horses, the shoulders of elephants and the seats of chariots, the enemy kings, expert with weapons, rained down arrows upon the Yadus like clouds pouring rain on mountains.**

**Комментарий:**

The arrows did not injure the Yadus. Rather the arrows nourished their desire to fight.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Rukmiṇī, of thin waist, seeing her Lord’s army covered by torrents of arrows, shyly looked at his face with fear-stricken eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmiṇī looked at her husband’s face (tad-vaktram).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**In response the Lord laughed and assured her, “Do not be afraid, beautiful-eyed one. This enemy force is about to be destroyed by our troops.”**

**Комментарий:**

Do not be afraid (mā sma bhaiḥ). Using tāvakaiḥ (your) indicates his great affection for Rukmiṇī.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**The heroes of the Lord’s army, headed by Gada and Saṅkarṣaṇa, could not tolerate the aggression of the opposing kings. Thus with iron arrows they began to strike down the enemy’s horses, elephants and chariots.**

**Комментарий:**

Tat can mean at that time or can mean “that” aggression (tadvikramam).

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**The heads of soldiers fighting on chariots, horses and elephants fell to the ground by the millions; some heads wore earrings and helmets, others turbans.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Lying all around were thighs, legs and fingerless hands, along with hands clutching swords, clubs and bows, and also the heads of horses, donkeys, elephants, camels, wild asses and humans.**

**Комментарий:**

Karabhā means “from the wrist to the little finger,” according to Amara-kośa.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Seeing their armies being struck down by the Vṛṣṇis, who were behaving like victors, the kings headed by Jarāsandha were discouraged and left the battlefield.**

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**The kings approached Śiśupāla, who was disturbed like a man who has lost his wife. His complexion was drained of color, his enthusiasm was gone, and his face appeared dried up. The kings spoke to him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiśupāla, who had not obtained a wife, was disturbed like a man who has lost his wife.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**\[Jarāsandha said:\] Listen, Śiśupāla, O tiger among men, give up your depression. After all, embodied beings’ happiness and unhappiness is never seen to be permanent, O King.**

**Комментарий:**

Niṣṭhā means permanent.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Just as a puppet in the form of a woman dances by the desire of the puppeteer, so this world, controlled by time, struggles in both happiness and misery.**

**Комментарий:**

The puppet is controlled by the puppeteer (kuhakaḥ). Jarāsandha and others, proponents of time, think that time is the controller (īśvara), rather than considering Kṛṣṇa, the regulator of even time, as the controller. Thus they are demons.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**In battle with Kṛṣṇa I and my twenty-three armies lost seventeen times; only once did I defeat him.**

**Комментарий:**

He gives an example of himself in two verses. When time was unfavorable seventeen times, I was defeated by Kṛṣṇa. When time was favorable one time, at the end I defeated him.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**But still I never lament or rejoice, because I know this world is driven by time and fate.**

**Комментарий:**

The world is disturbed (vidrāvitam) by time, impelled by karma.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**And now all of us, great commanders of military leaders, have been defeated by the Yadus and their small entourage, who are protected by Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

We are defeated by the meager entourage (phalgu-tantraiḥ) of the Yadus.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Now when time is favorable to them, our enemies have conquered but in the future, when time is auspicious for us, we shall conquer.**

**Комментарий:**

When time is favorable to them (ātma-ānusārinī), they win. We will win when time is favorable to us (pradakṣiṇaḥ).

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus persuaded by his friends, Śiśupāla took his followers and went back to his capital. The surviving warriors also returned to their respective cities.**

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Powerful Rukmī, however, was especially envious of Kṛṣṇa. He could not bear the fact that Kṛṣṇa had carried off his sister to Texts 19–20\] Marriage of Kṛṣṇa and Rukmiṇī 431 marry her in the Rākṣasa style. Thus he pursued the Lord with an entire military division.**

**Комментарий:**

Marriage in Rākṣasa style means “taking by force.”

### Text 19-20

**Перевод:**

**Intolerant and enraged, mighty-armed Rukmī, dressed in armor and wielding his bow, had sworn before all the kings, “I shall not again enter Kuṇḍina if I do not kill Kṛṣṇa in battle and bring Rukmiṇī back with me. I swear this to you.”**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmī was intolerant (amarṣī) and very angry (su-saṁrabdhaḥ). Apratyūhya means not bringing back. The other meaning spoken by Sarasvatī devī is “Even in ignorance I will not free Rukmiṇī from Kṛṣṇa.”

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Having said this, he had mounted his chariot and told his charioteer, “Drive the horses quickly to where Kṛṣṇa is. He and I must fight.**

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**“This wicked-minded cowherd boy has violently abducted my sister. But today I will remove his pride in his prowess with my sharp arrows.”**

**Комментарий:**

The other meaning spoken by Sarasvatī devī is this. My prowess will be removed by the sharp arrows of he who protects the Vedas and earth (gopālasya) and whose beautiful mind is compassionate even toward the wicked (durmateḥ).

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Boasting thus, foolish Rukmī, ignorant of the true extent of the Supreme Lord’s power, in his lone chariot, approached the Lord who had appeared on earth and challenged him. “Just stand and fight!”**

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Rukmī drew his bow with great strength and struck Kṛṣṇa with three arrows. Then he said, “Stand here for a moment, O defiler of the Yadu dynasty!**

**Комментарий:**

The other meaning spoken by Sarasvatī devī is: O protector of the Yadu dynasty (kula-pa)! O killer of enemies (aṁsana)! Aṁs means to kill. “Stand in such a way that I may quickly glance upon you (arekṣaṇam tistha).”

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**“Where do you go, carrying off my sister like a crow stealing sacrificial butter? This very day I shall relieve you of your false pride, you fool, you deceiver, you cheater in battle!**

**Комментарий:**

Having stolen my sister like a crow stealing offerings, where can you flee? You do not deserve her. Today I will take away your pride. O fool! The other meaning as spoken by Sarasvatī devī is: Taking my sister properly, who, being Lakṣmī, belongs to you where do you go? You do not need to go anywhere since there is no fear. The word dhvāṅkṣa means “having one eye.” The opposite adhvāṇkṣa means “having many eyes.” This ultimately means “having a thousand eyes”, i.e. like Indra. I will give you joy today by fighting. You spread your māyā-śakti (māyinaḥ) to people who are averse to you (manda) and remove the mass of ignorance of those who remain favorable to you (kūta-yodhinaḥ).

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**“Release the girl before you are struck dead by my arrows and made to lie down!” In response to this, Kṛṣṇa smiled, and with six arrows he struck Rukmī and broke his bow.**

**Комментарий:**

Yāvat is used in the meanings of limit and restriction. Before being struck by my arrows and lying on the battlefield, release the girl. But Sarasvatī devī speaks as follows: Because you are not killed by my arrows (ahataḥ), do not release the girl. You will gain satisfaction with her.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**The Lord struck Rukmī’s four horses with eight arrows, his chariot driver with two, and the chariot’s flag with three. Rukmī grabbed another bow and struck Kṛṣṇa with five arrows.**

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Although hit by these many arrows, Acyuta again broke Rukmī’s bow. Rukmī picked up yet another bow, but the infallible Lord broke that one to pieces as well.**

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Iron bludgeon, three-pointed spear, lance, sword and shield, pike, javelin—whatever weapon Rukmī picked up, the Lord who destroys the wicked smashed it.**

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Then Rukmī leaped down from his chariot and, sword in hand, rushed furiously toward Kṛṣṇa to kill him, like a bird flying into the wind.**

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**As Rukmī attacked him, the Lord shot arrows that broke Rukmī’s sword and shield into small pieces. Kṛṣṇa then took up his own sharp sword and prepared to kill Rukmī.**

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Lord Kṛṣṇa ready to kill her brother, saintly Rukmiṇī was filled with alarm. She fell at her husband’s feet and piteously spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

She was frightened that the public would gossip that the brother was killed in front of his sister. She was not alarmed out of affection for her brother. The prema of the city women with regard for common morality is called samañjasa. But the prema of the women of Vraja, which has no regard for such morality is called samartha.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Rukmiṇī said: O controller of all mystic power, immeasurable one, Lord of lords, master of the universe! O all auspicious and mighty-armed one, please do not kill my brother!**

**Комментарий:**

O master of acintya-śakti (yogeśvara)! What is use of killing a person with no power? O Kṛṣṇa who is without limit! What is the use of killing this limited insect? O lord of lords! What is the use of killing this lowest of men? O protector of the universe! You should protect this inhabitant of the universe. O auspicious one! Killing him is inauspicious. O mighty-armed! You should not kill a person who is devoid of strength of arms.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Rukmiṇī’s utter fear caused her limbs to tremble and her mouth to dry up, while her throat choked up out of sorrow. And in her agitation her golden necklace scattered. She grasped Kṛṣṇa’s feet, and the Lord, feeling compassionate, desisted.**

**Комментарий:**

Her mouth was dried up due to lamentation. Her throat was choked. She was agitated. The Lord was compassionate that she should not face public defamation. In such a state she grasped his feet.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa tied up the evil-doer with a strip of cloth. He then proceeded to disfigure Rukmī by comically shaving him, leaving parts of his mustache and hair. By that time, the Yadu heroes had crushed the extraordinary army of their opponents, just as elephants crush a lotus flower.**

**Комментарий:**

Compassionate to Rukmiṇī, Kṛṣṇa gave up the idea of killing him but he thought of marking him a little to crush his wicked nature. Thus, he acted. He bound Rukmī around the neck with his own cloth. Holding with his left hand the ends of the cloth and grasping a knife in his right hand, he took off Rukmī’s turban and shaved off his moustache and hair so that patches of his moustache and hair remained. He shaved him with a lot of blood flowing (pravapan). In this way he disfigured him.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**As the Yadus approached Kṛṣṇa, they saw Rukmī in this sorry condition, practically dying of shame. When the all-powerful Balarāma saw Rukmī, he compassionately released him and spoke the following to Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma released him, by removing the two ends of the cloth bound around his neck from Kṛṣṇa’s left hand.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Balarāma said:\] My dear Kṛṣṇa, you have acted improperly! This deed will bring shame on us, for to disfigure a close relative by shaving off his mustache and hair is as good as killing him.**

**Комментарий:**

He externally pacified Rukmiṇī a little by scolding Kṛṣṇa. It is improper to disfigure your relative your brother-in-law, giving him opposite features of an enemy. But for an enemy this disfiguring is appropriate.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Saintly lady, please do not be displeased with us out of anxiety for your brother’s disfigurement. No one but oneself is responsible for one’s joy and grief, for a man experiences the result of his own deeds.**

**Комментарий:**

He quotes scripture to relieve Rukmiṇī’s grief. Do not attribute fault to Kṛṣṇa and others (asmān). Some ancient karma has caused this disfigurement.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**\[Again addressing Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma said:\] A relative should not be killed by his friend even if his wrongdoing warrants capital punishment. Rather, he should be thrown out of the family. Since he has already been killed by his own sin, why kill him again?**

**Комментарий:**

Since her grief did not disappear still, Balarāma chastises Kṛṣṇa to lessen her grief. The brother-in-law should not be killed by the husband of his sister. Rather he should be rejected. It is not that the fault in protecting someone who deserves being killed is as much as killing someone who does not deserve to be killed, for he is killed by his sin.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**The code of sacred duty for warriors established by Prajāpati enjoins that one should kill even his own brother in a just war. That is a most dreadful law.**

**Комментарий:**

He enlightens her with sva-dharma when she still does not give up her grief. Because of dharma, even a brother should kill his own brother. Because of killing brothers, this dharma is dreadful. But since Prajāpati has stated that the brother can be killed in a fight, there is no fault of us in killing a brother-in-law.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**\[Again Balarāma addressed Kṛṣṇa:\] Blinded by conceit with their personal wealth, proud men offend others for the sake of such things as kingdom, land, wealth, women, honor and power.**

**Комментарий:**

He again scolds Kṛṣṇa to pacify Rukmiṇī. Because of kingdom, land, worship (mānasya), beauty or strength (tejasaḥ) and other things like food and drink, proud people who become blinded by pride and wealth cause destruction. We should not do this, since we are not like that.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**\[To Rukmiṇī Balarāma said:\] Your attitude of thinking that what is actually beneficial is always inauspicious for your friends, who have wicked hearts among all living entities, is unfair like an ignorant person.**

**Комментарий:**

“An enemy even if a relative should be killed by the kṣatriya. But he should not be disfigured like an insignificant person.” Understanding her feelings, he speaks. You think that the punishment given by Kṛṣṇa, though it is beneficial, to be always unbeneficial for your relatives (suhṛdām). This is wrong intelligence like that of a fool. Thinking something is not beneficial (when it is beneficial) is not proper for you. It is foolish. Among all living beings they (your relatives) have wicked hearts.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord’s māyā makes men forget their real selves, and thus, taking the body for the self, they consider others to be friends, enemies or neutral parties.**

**Комментарий:**

The ignorant person is explained. For those who identify with the body, who consider the body to be the ātmā, illusion of thinking of friends and enemies of the self is created by the Lord’s māyā. This does not happen for knowledgable people.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Those who are bewildered perceive the ātmā, residing in all embodied beings, as many, just as one may perceive reflections of light or sky in pots.**

**Комментарий:**

The nature of the ātmā is explained. Every ātmā in all embodied beings, though in different bodies such as devatā, human, etc., and though in differing stages of infancy, boyhood, etc., is only one but not that accepting all these bodies and stages is different. This is because ātmā is different from them and devoid of birth and other transformations (paraḥ). However ātmā is accepted as many according to different bodies and stages by those who are foolish, who identify body as self, just as the sun appears to be many in many reflections in water, by thinking the sun and reflection are the same. Or as the sky appears various by differently colored clouds. This statement does no propound oneness of all jīvas since birth, death and senses are alloted to the jīvas individually and since the activities of the jīvas are not simultaneous.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**This material body, which has a beginning and an end, is composed of the physical elements, the senses and the sense devatās. The body, imposed on the self by material ignorance, causes one to experience the cycle of birth and death.**

**Комментарий:**

The nature of the body is explained. The body is endowed with six transformations, having a beginning and end. It is composed of matter (dravya) or adhibhūta, senses (prāṇa) or adhyātmā, and guṇa or adhidaiva. That body, attached by sense of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ to the jīva (ātmani) due to aversion to the Lord (avidyayā), which is different from the jīva, causes the jīva identifying with the body to enter saṁsāra. It becomes the cause in attaining birth in various bodies such as devatā, etc.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**O intelligent lady, the soul never undergoes contact with or separation from insubstantial, material objects, because the soul is the cause of matter’s energy. Thus the soul resembles the sun, which neither comes in contact with nor separates from the eye and form.**

**Комментарий:**

“How can one destroy the relationship with the body which is made by beginningless ignorance?” It can be done by being favorable to the Lord. The jīva (ātmanaḥ), which is subtle (asataḥ) has no natural relationship with the gross (anyena) bodies. Similarly, it has no separation from those bodies since separation is to be preceded by relationship. Thus, since the relationship is unnatural, the relationship with the body is destroyed by becoming favorable to the Lord, just as possession by ghosts is destroyed by mantras. O chaste woman (sati)! Another cause of difference of the ātmā from the body is explained. Because the cause of manifesting (hetutvāt) the state (prasiddheḥ) of the material body and senses (tat), is the ātma, they are different. An example is given. The manifestation of the states of revealer (sun) and revealed (eye, form) from the eye and the form is caused due to the sun. As the sun is different from the eye and the form, so the ātmā is different from the body and senses.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**Birth and other transformations are undergone by the body but never by the self, just as change occurs for the moon’s phases but never for the moon, though the new-moon day may be called the moon’s “death.”**

**Комментарий:**

To explain the difference between the body and ātmā, as the revealed and the revealer, they are explained as having transformation and having no transformation. The six transformations starting with birth exist for the body only, they never take place for the ātmā. Then how can the perceptions of transformations such as “I am born, I am a child, I am old, I am dying,” exist in the ātmā? Just as there is birth, etc., of the phases of the moon, but not the birth, etc., of the moon which has a phase called amā. Just as we call the termination of the phases of the moon (kuhūḥ), “the death” of the moon similarly the destruction of the body is called the destruction of the ātmā. Kuhū means dark moon according to Amara-kośa. The transformations fixed in the body are imposed figuratively on the ātmā.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**As a sleeping person perceives himself, the objects of sense enjoyment and the fruits of his acts within the illusion of a dream, so one who is unintelligent undergoes material existence.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why does saṁsāra continue if there is no connection of ātmā with the body?” Just like because of the influence of saṁskāras of the body (asataḥ arthe), a sleeping person experiences a dream body, dream objects such as form, taste, etc., (viṣayān) and results like happiness and distress (phalam). Similarly a persons with no discrimination (abudhaḥ), because of absorption in identifying himself with the body which is different from himself, attains saṁsāra (bhavam). Asaṅgo hy ayaṁ puruṣaḥ: the jīva is not connected with matter. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad) On account of this śruti statement, though ātmā is devoid of connection with the body, by ignorance, the Lord’s śakti, a fault arising from aversion to the Lord, a relationship with the body takes place.

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, with true knowledge dispel the grief that is weakening and confounding your mind. Please resume your natural mood, O princess with a joyful heart!**

**Комментарий:**

Dispel the grief which causes bewilderment (vimohanam) by lack of discrimination and which dries up the body (ātmā).

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus enlightened by Balarāma, slender Rukmiṇī forgot her depression and steadied her mind by spiritual intelligence.**

**Комментарий:**

Giving up worry of what other people would say about her, she controlled her mind by discrimination (buddhyā).

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**Left with only his life air, freed from bondage and deprived of his strength, armies and bodily radiance by his enemies, Rukmī could not forget how he had been disfigured. In frustration he constructed for his residence a large city, which he called Bhojakaṭa.**

**Комментарий:**

He was released by Kṛṣṇa and went on foot. He had been mocked by the Yadus. Thus, they were enemies. Rukmī experienced suffering (bhoja). Kaṭa means an agreement or oath according to Nānārthavarga. Thus, the meaning of Bhoja-kaṭa is the place where the Bhoja king made an oath.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**Because he had promised “I will not reenter Kuṇḍina until I have killed wicked Kṛṣṇa and brought back my younger sister,” in a mood of angry frustration Rukmī took up residence at that very place.**

**Комментарий:**

Another meaning spoken by Sarasvatī devī is “Not knowing (ahatvā) Kṛṣṇa, most intelligent (adurmatim) and not seeing my sister, I will not enter the city.” He settled there (tatra), at the place of his disfigurement.

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**Thus defeating all the opposing kings, the Supreme Lord brought the daughter of Bhīṣmaka to his capital and married her according to the Vedic injunctions, O protector of the Kurus.**

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**At that time, O King, there was great rejoicing in all the homes of Dvārakā, whose citizens had prema for only Kṛṣṇa, chief of the Yadus.**

**Комментарий:**

They had exclusive devotion to Kṛṣṇa (ananya-bhāvānām).

### Text 55

**Перевод:**

**All the men and women, full of joy and adorned with shining jewels and earrings, brought wedding presents, which they reverently offered to the exquisitely dressed groom and bride.**

**Комментарий:**

Varayoḥ means bridegroom and bride.

### Text 56

**Перевод:**

**The city of the Vṛṣṇis appeared most beautiful: there were tall, festive columns, and also archways decorated with flower garlands, cloth banners and precious gems. Arrangements of auspicious, full water pots, aguru-scented incense, and lamps graced every doorway.**

**Комментарий:**

There were colorful flags flying high in the sky (uttambhitendraketubhiḥ).

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**The city’s streets were soaked with the mada of intoxicated elephants belonging to the beloved kings who were guests at the wedding, and the city was made additionally beautiful by trunks of plantain and betel-nut trees decorating all the doorways.**

**Комментарий:**

The streets were soaked by elephants which were emitting mada. The city became more beautiful with the betel and banana trees raised (parāmṛṣṭa) by men.

### Text 58

**Перевод:**

**Those who belonged to the royal families of the Kuru, Sṛñjaya, Kaikeya, Vidarbha, Yadu and Kuntibhoja clans joyfully met one another in the midst of the crowds of people excitedly running here and there.**

**Комментарий:**

Associating with each other, the Kurus, Sṛñjayas and others became joyful amidst relatives running around.

### Text 59

**Перевод:**

**The kings and their daughters were totally astonished to hear the story of Rukmiṇī’s abduction, which was being glorified in song everywhere.**

### Text 60

**Перевод:**

**Dvārakā’s citizens were overjoyed to see Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Lakṣmī, united with Rukmiṇī, within whom Lakṣmī had merged.**

**Комментарий:**

After the marriage, because of seeing their two happy together, all the people of Dvārakā became filled with bliss. That is described in this verse. Seeing Kṛṣṇa, Svayam Bhagavān, the husband of the Mahā-lakṣmī (śriyaḥ patiḥ) who is the eligible shelter for all, they said that Mahā-lakṣmī had now attained him (ramayoptem).

## Chapter 55 - The History of Pradyumna

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Kāma-deva \[Cupid\], an expansion of Vāsudeva, had previously been burned to ashes by Rudra’s anger. Now, to obtain a new body, he merged back into the body of Vāsudeva.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fifty-fifth chapter Pradyumnya is born in Rukmiṇī from Kṛṣṇa. Kidnapped by Śambara, he kills him and returns home with his wife. Pradyumna was born before Kṛṣṇa’s marriages to Jāmbavati and others. Then their marriages took place. Then Pradyumna returned from Śambara’s house. This is the sequence. In mentioning his birth, his activities should also be described. Thus that is told in this chapter. By describing his being stolen, swallowed by a fish, and again being attained, his indestructible nature is shown. The appearance of Svayaṁ Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa and his associates in this world is glorified taking shelter of the fame of his svāṁśas and his vibhūtis who enter into him by his desire, by the logic of parokṣa-vāda but not by their respective fame. Just as Svayaṁ Bhagavān’s appearance is glorified through the fame of Vāmana, Nārāyaṇa-ṛṣi, etc., who had entered the Lord. Nanda and Yaśodā’s appearance through the Droṇa and Dharā’s fame. Vasudeva and Devakī’s appearance through Sutapa and Pṛśni’s fame. Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma and Arjuna’s appearance through the fame of Dharma, Vāyu and Indra. By this it is established that conclusions concerning the Lord depends on the teachings of guru and the destruction of materialistic ideas is also accomplished. This being so, the appearance of even Pradyumna of the third vyūha is described through the fame of Kāma-deva, his vibhūti who had entered him. Prajanaś cāsmi kandarpa: of causes of procreation I am Kāmadeva. (BG [10.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.28)) Thus Kāma-deva is Vāsudeva’s vibhinnāṁśa (i.e. a jīva) having vibhūti. Previously he had been burned by Śiva’s anger. In order to obtain a body by entering the body of his shelter, Pradyumna, he attained him, who has variegated pastimes, by Pradyumna’s desire and not by his own power. In this way, Pradyumna manifested with the fame of Cupid, who had entered him. Another meaning (that Pradyumna was burned by Śiva) is not possible, since in Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Nārada teaches Vyāsa a mantra indicating Pradyumna as the Supreme Lord, and thus it is impossible that he was burned by Śiva’s anger and since Garbodhakaśāyī is Pradyumna’s aṁśa and from him Śiva arises. Thus the explanation is right.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**He took birth in the womb of Vaidarbhī from the seed of Kṛṣṇa and received the name Pradyumna. In no respect was he inferior to his father.**

**Комментарий:**

He who appears as an aṁśa of Kṛṣṇa in every kalpa (kṛṣṇa-vīrya- samudbhavaḥ), and is famous (vikhyatah) as Pradyumna among the catur-vyūha, appeared (jātaḥ) from Rukmiṇī. The material Kāmadeva, servant of Indra, burned up by Śiva, had merged into him, just as the world is merged in the Lord since having been made limbless by Śiva, he could not independently attain a new body. The reason that it was the member of the catur-vyūha Pradyumna that was born is that in all ways (sarvataḥ), he was not less than his father. He was his equal. This is not possible for the material Kāma .deva, servant of Indra

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**The demon Śambara, who could assume any form he desired, kidnapped the infant before he was even ten days old. Understanding Pradyumna to be his enemy, Śambara threw him into the sea and then returned home.**

**Комментарий:**

A curious pastime of Kṛṣṇa is shown. The story continues for the rest of the chapter. Śambara took the form of a nurse and stole him before he was ten days old. O sage! On the sixth day after birth Kāla-śambara stole Pradyumna from the confinement room since he recognized him as his killer. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) Thus, it was the sixth day from his birth. He learned from Nārada, who wanted the demon killed, that Pradyumna would kill him. Throwing him in the ocean (udanvati) he returned home. Kṛṣṇa though knowing this, did not catch the demon since his killing, a work of the devatās, would be accomplished by Pradyumna.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**A powerful fish swallowed Pradyumna, and this fish, along with others, was caught in a huge net and seized by fishermen.**

**Комментарий:**

The fish swallowed him (nirjagāra). By Kṛṣṇa’s will, he developed the power to swallow him.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**The fishermen presented that extraordinary fish to Śambara, who had his cooks bring it to the kitchen, where they began cutting it up with a butcher knife.**

**Комментарий:**

They cut it open with a knife (sudhitinā). The sudhitinā instead of svadhitinā is poetic license. It was astonishing because of its huge size. For that reason, the fish was gifted to Śambara.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Seeing a male child in the belly of the fish, the cooks gave the infant to Māyāvatī, who was astonished. Nārada Muni then appeared and explained to her everything about the child’s birth and his entering the fish’s abdomen.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the astonishing child, they gave him to Rati who was called Māyāvatī due to manifesting her knowledge regarding illusions. How did this attractive child, similar in form to my husband, come out of the fish? This was the doubt in her mind (śaṅkita-cetasaḥ). Nārada told her everything. This child is Lord Pradyumna, and your husband, Kāma-deva, has merged in his body. This is his svarūpa (tattvaṁ). He was born to Rukmiṇī (utpattim) and entered the fish. He explained the reason for this. Since she worshipped Pradyumna as being non-different from her husband, her vow did not break. But the mother of Aniruddha was Pradyumna’s direct śakti.

### Text 7-8

**Перевод:**

**Māyāvatī was in fact Kāma-deva’s renowned wife, Rati. While waiting for her husband to obtain a new body—his previous one having been burnt up—she had been assigned by Śambara to prepare vegetables and rice. Māyāvatī understood that this infant was actually Kāma-deva, and thus she began to feel love for him.**

**Комментарий:**

There is story in Matsya Purāṇa. When her husband was burned to ashes by Śiva, Rati worshipped Śiva for a long time so that her husband would get another body. Śambara who was also worshipping Śiva for a different benediction, was addressed by Śiva, “Ask for a benediction.” On seeing Rati, he, pained with lust, asked Śiva for her as a result of his worship. Śiva said to Rati, “Go with him. There you will attain your desire.” She having gone to his house, bewildered him by her illusory powers and remained there being untouched by him. Bewildered by her illusory powers he did not recognize the child. She was given responsibility for preparing soups and vegetables.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**After a short time, this son of Kṛṣṇa—Pradyumna—attained paugaṇḍa. He caused amorous feelings in all women who gazed upon him.**

**Комментарий:**

He attained paugaṇḍa age very quickly. He attracted the women who saw him, what to speak of talking to him. He filled them with passion (vibhramam).

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, with a bashful smile and raised eyebrows, Māyāvatī exhibited various gestures of conjugal attraction as she lovingly approached her husband, whose eyes were broad like the petals of a lotus, whose arms were very long and who was the most beautiful of men.**

**Комментарий:**

She approached him with affection, with shy smiles and dancing eyebrows and other conjugal (saurataiḥ) gestures. O King (aṅga)!

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Pradyumna told her, “O mother, your attitude has changed. You are overstepping the proper feelings of a mother and behaving like a lover.”**

**Комментарий:**

Most beautiful (bhagavān), the son of Kṛṣṇa (kārṣṇiḥ) spoke to her. His omniscience was covered by the will of Kṛṣṇa. The nurse told him that Māyāvatī is his mother. The meaning is clear. According to Hari-vaṁśa Rati and Pradyumna did not know their identities. The real meaning of his statement is this. You should not have any other tendency than this ecstatic loving attraction you are displaying. After all, you have surpassed the mood of a mother, your present limited condition, and are actually my lover in conjugal rasa. You desire to cover my limbs with your limbs. Pradyumna said this to her because he was Bhagavān, always filled with omniscience.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Rati said: You are the son of Nārāyaṇa and were kidnapped from your parents’ home by Śambara. I, Rati, am your legitimate wife, O master, because you are Kāma-deva.**

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**That demon, Śambara, threw you into the sea when you were not even ten days old, and a fish swallowed you. Then in this very place we recovered you from the fish’s abdomen, O master.**

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Now kill this dreadful Śambara, your formidable enemy. Although he knows hundreds of magic spells, you can defeat him with bewildering magic and other techniques.**

**Комментарий:**

He is formidable because he knows hundreds of magic spells. “Then how can he be killed?” By bewildering magic.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Your poor mother, having lost her son, cries for you like a kurarī bird. She is overwhelmed with love for her child, just like a cow that has lost its calf.**

**Комментарий:**

You should not delay.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Speaking thus, Māyāvatī gave to the great soul Pradyumna the mystic knowledge called Mahāmāyā, which vanquishes all other deluding spells.**

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Pradyumna approached Śambara and called him to battle, hurling intolerable insults at him to foment a conflict.**

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Offended by these harsh words, Śambara became as agitated as a kicked snake. He came out, club in hand, his eyes red with rage.**

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Śambara whirled his club swiftly about and then hurled it at the wise Pradyumna, producing a sound as sharp as a thunder crack.**

**Комментарий:**

He whirled (āvidhya) his club and threw it at Pradyumna. The club made a special sound (vyanadan), harsher than the sound of grinding thunder. The phrase vyanadan nādam, “creating a resonance” is a valid statement in the same way as the phrase vacanam avocat, “he spoke a statement.”

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**As Śambara’s club came flying toward him, Pradyumna knocked it away with his own. Then, O King, Pradyumna angrily threw his club at the enemy.**

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Resorting to the black magic of the Daityas taught to him by Maya Dānava, Śambara suddenly appeared in the sky and released a downpour of weapons upon Kṛṣṇa’s son.**

**Комментарий:**

While situated in the sky (vaihayasaḥ) Śambara released weapons on him.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Harassed by this rain of weapons, Pradyumna, the greatly powerful warrior, made use of the mystic science called Mahāmāyā, which was created from the mode of goodness and which could defeat all other mystic power.**

**Комментарий:**

Kāmadeva used sāttvika weapons. The verb of the sentence, prāyuṅkta (he used) is found in the next verse.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**The demon then unleashed hundreds of mystic weapons belonging to the Guhyakas, Gandharvas, Piśācas, Uragas and Rākṣasas, but Pradyumna struck them all down.**

**Комментарий:**

He destroyed (vyadhamayat) all the māyā weapons.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Drawing his sharp-edged sword, Pradyumna forcefully cut off Śambara’s head, complete with red mustache, helmet and earrings.**

**Комментарий:**

He cut off his head which had a red moustache.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**As the residents of the higher planets showered Pradyumna with flowers and chanted his praises, his wife, who could float in the air, transported him through the heavens, back to the city of Dvārakā.**

**Комментарий:**

Being covered (ākīryamāṇaḥ) by the flowers and praises of the devatās, he was taken to Dvārakā by his wife.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**O King, Pradyumna and his wife resembled a cloud accompanied by lightning as they descended from the sky into the inner quarters of Kṛṣṇa’s most excellent palace, which were crowded with lovely women.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmiṇī’s palace was the best among all palaces. He was like a cloud with lightning.

### Text 27-28

**Перевод:**

**The women of the palace thought he was Kṛṣṇa when they saw his dark-blue complexion the color of a rain cloud, his yellow silk garments, his long arms and red-tinged eyes, his charming lotus face adorned with a pleasing smile, his fine ornaments and his thick, curly blue hair. Thus the women became bashful and hid themselves here and there.**

**Комментарий:**

His eyes were red at the edges (tāmrākṣaṁ). Pradyumna had abundant locks (ālaka-alibhiḥ), which was both dark-blue and curly. The women became shy (hrītāḥ).

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Gradually, from the slight differences between his appearance and Kṛṣṇa’s, the ladies realized he was not the Lord. Delighted and astonished, they approached Pradyumna and his consort, who was a jewel among women.**

**Комментарий:**

He was slightly different by being slightly less in his color and other features as well as age, and by his polite glances. Thus they understood he was not Kṛṣṇa and approached him, who was accompanied by Rati, a jewel among women.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Pradyumna, sweet-voiced, dark-eyed Rukmiṇī remembered her lost son, and her breasts became moist out of affection.**

**Комментарий:**

After he had come (atha), among the women were looking at him, Rukmiṇī remembered her son, on seeing the similarity of form.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**\[Śrīmatī Rukmiṇī-devī said:\] Who is this lotus-eyed jewel among men? What man’s son is he, and what woman carried him in her womb? And who is this woman he has taken as his wife?**

**Комментарий:**

Who is this best among men like a vaidūrya gem? Who is he or whose son is he?

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**If my lost son, who was kidnapped from the maternity room, were still alive somewhere, he would be of the same age and appearance as this young man.**

**Комментарий:**

My son had disappeared (nāstaḥ). Possibly he was taken by a demon (api). If he is possibly alive somewhere, he would be the same age and form. She spoke like this though she is omniscient, since her omniscience was covered by Kṛṣṇa’s will.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**But how is it that this young man so much resembles my own Lord, Kṛṣṇa, the wielder of Śārṅga, in his bodily form and his limbs, in his gait and the tone of his voice, and in his smiling glance?**

**Комментарий:**

The word tu indicates astonishment. She shows how he is exactly like Kṛṣṇa (samprāptam).

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Yes, he must be the same child I bore in my womb, since I feel great affection for him and my left arm is quivering.**

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**As Rukmiṇī conjectured in this way, Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, arrived on the scene with Vasudeva and Devakī.**

**Комментарий:**

Devaky-ānakadundubhyām instead of devaky-ānakadundubhibhyām is poetic license. Kṛṣṇa came with Vasudeva and Devakī because he had come from their house.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Although Janārdana knew perfectly well what had transpired, he remained silent. The sage Nārada, however, explained everything, beginning with Śambara’s kidnapping of the child.**

**Комментарий:**

The reason he was silent is explained though he knew. The devotees (jana) pray (ardana) for variegated pastimes (janārdana). It was possible Rukmiṇī would be displeased with him since she was lamenting for a long time. At that moment Nārada came by Kṛṣṇa’s desire.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**When the women of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s palace heard this most amazing account, they joyfully greeted Pradyumna, who had been lost for many years but who had now returned as if from the dead.**

**Комментарий:**

They welcomed him. He had disappeared and was thus as if dead. Now he had again returned.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Devakī, Vasudeva, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and all the women of the palace, especially Queen Rukmiṇī, embraced the young couple and rejoiced.**

**Комментарий:**

Devakī and Vasudeva are mentioned first since they had special affection as the paternal grandparents. Balarāma is mentioned later since he arrived later. The ‘women’ means the queens (striyaḥ). Rukmiṇī is mentioned at the end because she desired everyone’s blessings on the two and since she desired to embrace the two for a long time.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Hearing that lost Pradyumna had come home, the residents of Dvārakā declared, “Ah, providence has allowed this child to return as if from death!”**

**Комментарий:**

Ha is an indeclinable, expressing contemplation of the previous events.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**It is not astonishing that the palace women, felt ecstatic attraction for him with vātsalya, as if he were their own Lord. After all, the son exactly resembled his father. Indeed, Pradyumna was a perfect reflection of the beauty of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of the goddess of fortune, and reminded them of Kṛṣṇa. What to speak of seeing Kṛṣṇa. Other women could not develop such feelings.**

**Комментарий:**

Pradyumna’s beauty is shown. Gazing at him constantly, because of beauty similar to his father’s, they experienced emotions related to their master Kṛṣṇa. They thought, “How did he attain the same form as Kṛṣṇa?” (Verse 33) The mothers headed by Rukmiṇī developed greater vātsalya-bhāva for him in privacy before learning of his identity. “I feel great affection for him and my left arm is quivering” (Verse 34) The doubt was now confirmed. “Yes, he must be the same child I bore in my womb.” (Verse 34) With tears, they smelled his head and rubbed his limbs. This love for him was not surprising for the mothers. He was a reflection of the abode of wealth of all beauty, Kṛṣṇa. He was an uncovered reflection like a rainbow because they confirmed that he was the son of Kṛṣṇa due to being similar to him and since they experienced it. Moreover only the mothers had such vātsalya not the others. Reminding their lover (kāme smare), he invoked their conjugal love for Kṛṣṇa even when Kṛṣṇa was not present. What to speak of when he was present. Other women could not have such bhāva rather they only became disturbed.

## Chapter 56 - The Syamantaka Jewel

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having offended Kṛṣṇa, Satrājit tried as best he could to atone by presenting him with his daughter and the Syamantaka jewel.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fifty-sixth chapter, getting a bad name because of false rumors, by finding a jewel the Lord attains the daughter of Jambavān and then the daughter of Satrājit. With the jewel Satrājit gave his daughter. The name Satrājit sometimes ends in a-kāra (“a”) and sometimes in ta-kāra (“ta”).

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Mahārāja Parīkṣit inquired: O brāhmaṇa, what did King Satrājit do to offend Kṛṣṇa? Where did he get the Syamantaka jewel, and why did he give his daughter to the Supreme Lord?**

**Комментарий:**

Hareḥ (genetive) means “to Hari” (dative).

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Sūrya, the sun-god, felt great affection for his devotee Satrājit. Acting as his greatest friend, the devatā gave him the jewel called Syamantaka as a token of his satisfaction.**

**Комментарий:**

The sun-god, his master, pleased with Satrājit, treated him as a friend.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Wearing the jewel on his neck, Satrājit entered Dvārakā. He shone as brightly as the sun itself, O King, and thus he went unrecognized because of the jewel’s effulgence.**

**Комментарий:**

He could not be recognized as Satrājit (na upalakṣitaḥ).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**As the people looked at Satrājit from a distance, his brilliance blinded them. They presumed he was the sun-god, Sūrya, and went to tell Kṛṣṇa, who was at that time playing at dice.**

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**\[The residents of Dvārakā said:\] Obeisances unto you, O Nārāyaṇa, shelter of the jīvas! O holder of the conch, disc and club, O lotus-eyed Dāmodara, O Govinda, O giver of joy to the Yadu!**

**Комментарий:**

By chanting his names, the Dvārakāvāsīs caught the attention of Kṛṣṇa, who was absorbed in a dice game.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**The sun god has come to see you, O Lord of the universe. He is blinding everyone’s eyes with his intensely effulgent rays.**

**Комментарий:**

Lord Savitā is blinding our eyes with the network of his intense (tigma-guḥ) rays (gabhasti-cakreṇa).

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**The most exalted devatās in the three worlds are certainly anxious to seek you out, O Lord, now that you have hidden yourself among the Yadu dynasty. Thus the unborn sun-god has come to see you here.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why does the sun-god want to see me, who am a mere mortal?” Ajaḥ means savitā.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Hearing these innocent words, the lotus-eyed Lord smiled broadly and said, “This is not the sungod, but rather Satrājit, who is glowing because of his jewel.”**

**Комментарий:**

He heard their ignorant words (bāla-vacanam). Satrājit was shining (jvalan).

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**King Satrājit entered his opulent home, endowed with auspiciousness and joy. He had qualified brāhmaṇas install the Syamantaka jewel in the house’s temple room.**

**Комментарий:**

The house was made auspicious with festivity. He had brāhmaṇas install the gem.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**O master! Each day the gem would produce eight bhāras of gold and the place in which it was kept and properly worshiped would be free of calamities such as famine or untimely death, and also of evils like snake bites, mental and physical disorders and the presence of deceitful persons.**

**Комментарий:**

The bhāra is defined as follows: Four rice grains are called one guñjā; five guñjās, one paṇa; eight paṇas, one dharaṇa or karṣa; four karṣas, one pala; and one hundred palas, one tulā. Twenty tulās make up one bhāra. Mārī means untimely death. Ariṣṭāni means inauspicious events. Aśubhāḥ means causes of suffering.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**On one occasion Kṛṣṇa requested Satrājit to give the jewel to the Yadu king, Ugrasena, but Satrājit was so greedy that he refused. He gave no thought to the seriousness of the offense he committed by denying the Lord’s request.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa asked him to give the jewel to Ugrasena. Satrājit did not consider it a fault to deny the request of the Lord.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Once Satrājit’s brother, Prasena, having hung the brilliant jewel about his neck, mounted a horse and went hunting in the forest.**

**Комментарий:**

Prasena was the younger brother of Satrājit. He tied the gem around his neck.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**A lion killed Prasena and his horse and took the jewel. But when the lion entered a mountain cave he was killed by Jāmbavān, who wanted the jewel.**

**Комментарий:**

The lion took (ācchidya) the jewel.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Within the cave Jāmbavān made the jewel into a toy for his son. Meanwhile Satrājit, not seeing his brother return, became deeply troubled.**

**Комментарий:**

Saḥ means Jāmbavān.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**He said, “Kṛṣṇa probably killed my brother, who went to the forest wearing the jewel on his neck.” Satrājit’s supporters heard this accusation and began whispering it in one another’s ears.**

**Комментарий:**

These wicked people had the same mentality as Satrājit.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa heard this rumor, he wanted to remove the stain on his reputation. So he took some of Dvārakā’s citizens with him and set out to retrace Prasena’s path.**

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**In the forest they found Prasena and his horse, both killed by the lion. Further on they found the lion dead on a mountainside, slain by Jāmbavān.**

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**The Lord stationed his subjects outside the terrifying, pitch-dark cave of the king of the bears, and then he entered alone.**

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**There Kṛṣṇa saw that the most precious of jewels had been made into a child’s plaything. He waited for an opportunity to take the gem, situated near the child.**

**Комментарий:**

He saw the jewel made into a toy for the child’s playing.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**The child’s nurse cried out as if in fear upon seeing that extraordinary person standing before them. Jāmbavān, strongest of the strong, heard her cries and angrily ran toward the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa wanting to take the jewel, the nurse shouted. She seemed afraid but she shouted because of arousal of bliss due to seeing him, but not because she became afraid.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Unaware of his true position and thinking him an ordinary man, Jāmbavān angrily began fighting with the Supreme Lord, his master.**

**Комментарий:**

He thought Kṛṣṇa to be a human. Jāmbavān did not gain happiness from fighting with the army of Rāvaṇa which was meager in strength and neither did I gain happiness from fighting with Cānūra, etc., who were similarly of meager strength. Thus by fighting with him who is of equal strength both will gain happiness. Thus, by this decision of the Lord, his servant’s knowledge that the Lord was his master was covered.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**The two fought furiously in single combat, each determined to win. Contending against each other with various weapons and then with stones, tree trunks and finally their bare arms, they struggled like two hawks battling over a piece of flesh.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. The fighting was intense (sutumulam). They fought like hawks fighting for meat (kravyārthe).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**The fight went on without rest for twenty-eight days, the two opponents striking each other with their fists, which fell like the cracking blows of lightning.**

**Комментарий:**

They fought continuously for twenty-eight days and nights (aharniṣam). Viṁśa should be viṁśati. They fought without a moment of rest (aviśramam). Niṣpeṣa means the noise of a blow.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**His bulging muscles pummeled by the blows of Kṛṣṇa’s fists, his strength faltering and his limbs perspiring, Jāmbavān, greatly astonished, finally spoke to the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

The joints of his large limbs were pulverized by Kṛṣṇa’s fists. Since he had previously determined, “There is no one stronger than me except Rāmacandra,” he was astonished, “Is he that same person?” Having resolved, he spoke.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**\[Jāmbavān said:\] I know now that you are the life air and the sensory, mental and bodily strength of all living beings. You are all-pervading, the original person, the supreme, all-powerful controller.**

**Комментарий:**

I know that you are the sum total of prāṇa of all jīvas in the millions of universes and you are the total of all the strengths of all the senses (oja), minds (saha) and bodies (bala) – special prāṇa – of all beings since they both are your vibhūtis. How can your strength be opposed by that of mine, one person? I am like a fly against an elephant. I know you are he who spreads everywhere (viṣṇum), eternally perfect (purāṇaṁ puruṣam), most powerful (prabhaviṣṇum) and the ruler (adhīśvaram). How can you be fought by me, pervaded by you, a recent being, without power, and meant to be ruled? Please forgive the offense of your servant.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**You are the ultimate creator of all creators of the universe, and of everything created you are the underlying substance. You are the subduer of all subduers, the Supreme Lord and Supreme Soul of all souls.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, you alone are the creator of all creators such as Brahmā. You alone are the cause (sat) such as ether, etc., of all planets created by them since you pervade them. They are not the cause of the universe. To repeat, you are their creator. You alone are the destroyer (kālaḥ) of all destroyers (kalayatām). You alone are the aṁśī (para ātmā) of all jīvas (ātmanām). How can you be fought by me?

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**You are he who impelled the ocean to give way when his sidelong glances, slightly manifesting his anger, disturbed the crocodiles and timiṅgala fish within the watery depths.
