You are he who built a great bridge to establish his fame, who burned down the city of Laṅkā, and whose arrows severed the heads of Rāvaṇa, which then fell to the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

My master Rāmacandra is this person. He makes his conviction clear. By glances slightly manifesting anger, disturbing the crocodiles and timiṅgala fish, the ocean made a path to go to Laṅkā. Still he made a bridge which is his fame and, by that bridge, put Laṅkā in flames through his servant Hanumān and made the heads of the demons such as Rāvaṇa, cut off by his arrows, fall on the ground. I know that he, my master, is you.

### Text 29-30

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] O King, Lord Kṛṣṇa then addressed the king of the bears, who had understood the truth. The lotus-eyed son of Devakī touched Jāmbavān with his hand, which bestows all blessings, and spoke to his devotee with sublime compassion, his grave voice deeply resounding like a cloud.**

**Комментарий:**

He spoke to Jāmbavān who understood the svarūpa of the Lord (vijñāta-vijñānam). Vijñānam ānandam brahma: the Lord is consciousness and bliss. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad) He touched him with his auspicious hand, thus removing the pain in his devotee’s limbs. He then spoke (vyājahāra).

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] It is for this jewel, O lord of the bears, that we have come to your cave. I intend to use the jewel to disprove the false accusations against me.**

**Комментарий:**

Many of us came to the door of your cave for the jewel and among them I entered to remove (pramṛjan) the false accusations.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Thus addressed, Jāmbavān happily honored Kṛṣṇa by offering him his maiden daughter, Jāmbavatī, together with the jewel.**

**Комментарий:**

Arhaṇārtham means for worship along with the jewel.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**After Śauri had entered the cave, the people of Dvārakā who had accompanied him had waited twelve days without seeing him come out again. Finally they had given up and returned to their city in great sorrow.**

**Комментарий:**

They did not have prema like the people of Vraja.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**When Devakī, Rukmiṇī-devī, Vasudeva and the Lord’s other relatives and friends heard that he had not come out of the cave, they all lamented.**

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Cursing Satrājit, the sorrowful residents of Dvārakā approached the Durgā deity who was situated alone and prayed to her for Kṛṣṇa’s return.**

**Комментарий:**

Durgā is mahāmāyā, who was situated alone.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**When the citizens had finished worshiping her, the blessings came true. Kṛṣṇa, who had achieved his purpose, appeared suddenly before them in the company of his new wife, filling them with joy.**

**Комментарий:**

Durgā became visible to their eyes and she gave the blessings that Kṛṣṇa has almost come. The Lord appeared simultaneously with the blessings she gave. This is the ornament called sahokti.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Hṛṣīkeśa return as if from death, accompanied by his new wife and wearing the Syamantaka jewel on his neck, all the people were roused to jubilation.**

**Комментарий:**

When he gave his daughter, Jāmbavān put the jewel on Kṛṣṇa’s neck.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Lord Kṛṣṇa summoned Satrājit to the royal assembly. There, in the presence of King Ugrasena, Kṛṣṇa announced the recovery of the jewel and then formally presented it to Satrājit.**

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Hanging his head in great shame, Satrājit took the gem and returned home from the assembly, all the while feeling remorse for his sinful behavior.**

**Комментарий:**

Satrājit was repentant (anutapyamānaḥ) for his offensive behavior (svena pāpmanā).

### Text 40-42

**Перевод:**

**Pondering over his grievous offense and worried about the possibility of conflict with the Lord’s mighty devotees, King Satrājit thought, “How can I cleanse myself of my contamination, and how may Acyuta become satisfied with me? What can I do to regain my good fortune and avoid being cursed by the populace for being so short-sighted, miserly, foolish and avaricious? I shall give my daughter, the jewel of all women, to the Lord, together with the Syamantaka jewel. That, indeed, is the only proper way to pacify him.”**

**Комментарий:**

He was overcome with anxiety about conflict (vigraha) with the powerful Lord (balavat) or his devotees because of spreading the rumor. Thus, he thought continually, “How can I purify myself?”

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Having thus intelligently made up his mind, King Satrājit personally arranged to present Kṛṣṇa with his fair daughter and the Syamantaka jewel.**

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**The Lord married Satyabhāmā in proper religious fashion. Possessed of excellent behavior, along with beauty, broadmindedness and all other good qualities, she had been sought by many men.**

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord told Satrājit: We do not care to take this jewel back, O King. You are the sun-god’s devotee, so let it stay in your possession. Thus we will also enjoy its benefits.**

**Комментарий:**

We will enjoy the results of you, the worshipper of the sun (devabhaktasya). The logic — “because you have no sons, the wealth is ours only,” is suggested.

## Chapter 57 - Satrājit Murdered, the Jewel Returned

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bādarāyaṇi said: Although Govinda was fully aware of what had actually occurred, when he heard reports that the Pāṇḍavas and Queen Kuntī had burned to death, he went with Balarāma to the kingdom of the Kurus to fulfill the family obligations expected of him.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fifty-seventh chapter Śatadhanva kills Satrājit, Kṛṣṇa kills Śatadhanva, and then obtains the jewel from Akrūra. Though understanding that the Pāṇḍavas had escaped from the lac house from an underground hole, on hearing that they had been burned up, he went with Balarāma for the sake of handling family rites. In private he confirmed the news of Hastināpura with Balarāma.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**The two Lords met with Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, Vidura, Gāndhārī and 484 Vaiṣṇavānandinī \[Ch.57 Droṇa. Showing sorrow equal to theirs, they cried out, “Alas, how painful this is!”**

**Комментарий:**

Since others were not grief-stricken over the burning, it is said that he met with Bhīṣma, etc. They imitated having similar grief.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Taking advantage of this opportunity, O King, Akrūra and Kṛtavarmā went to Śatadhanvā and said, “The Syamantaka jewel cannot be taken by an unqualified person.”**

**Комментарий:**

They found an opportunity. “Since Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa are absent from Dvārakā, by killing Satrājit, it is possible to take the jewel. Since you are a greater warrior than even us, you should kill him.”

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**“Satrājit promised his jewel-like daughter to us but then gave her to Kṛṣṇa instead, contemptuously neglecting us. Satrājit should follow his brother’s path, since he has no heirs.”**

**Комментарий:**

They describe the offense of Satrājit. Since previously it was said that Satyabhāmā had been desired by many (SB [10.56.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/56.44)), it follows that even they had individually requested her as a bride and Satrājit too promised to give her. Rejecting us by attributing some fault he gave the jewel of daughter to Kṛṣṇa. Why should he not follow his brother, dead Prasena? Rather he should follow. He should die. The two devotees engaged Śatadhanva since they were angry that Satrājit had cast allegations on the Lord.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**His mind thus influenced by their advice, wicked Śatadhanvā murdered Satrājit in his sleep simply out of greed. In this way the sinful Śatadhanvā shortened his own life span.**

**Комментарий:**

With his mind cheated (bhinna-matiḥ) because he was demonic by nature (asattamaḥ), he killed Satrājit, though he was sleeping, out of greed for the jewel.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**As the women of Satrājit’s palace screamed and helplessly wept, Śatadhanvā took the jewel and left, like a butcher after he has killed some animals.**

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**When Satyabhāmā saw her dead father, she was plunged into grief. Lamenting, “My father, my father! Oh, I am killed!” she became bewildered out of affection for him.**

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Queen Satyabhāmā put her father’s corpse in a large vat of oil and went to Hastināpura, where she sorrowfully told Kṛṣṇa, who was already aware of the situation, about her father’s murder.**

**Комментарий:**

She actually did not have affection for her father who was opposed to Kṛṣṇa. Yet she showed grief to dispel rumors of the public. “Why would she not bring him back to life through her husband on some pretext?” She went to make Kṛṣṇa also grieve. As I am grieving you also should make a show of grieving.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma heard this news, O King, they exclaimed, “Alas! This is the greatest tragedy for us!” Thus imitating the ways of human society, they lamented, their eyes brimming with tears.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing her words (tat), they imitated human behavior.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord returned to his capital with his wife and elder brother. After arriving in Dvārakā, he readied himself to kill Śatadhanvā and retrieve the jewel from him.**

**Комментарий:**

Satyabhāma said to her relatives, “The two brothers, unable to bring my father back to life, lamented with tears.”

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Upon learning that Kṛṣṇa was preparing to kill him, Śatadhanvā was struck with fear. To save his life he approached Kṛtavarmā and begged him for help, but Kṛtavarmā replied as follows.**

### Text 12-13

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛtavarmā said:\] I dare not offend the Supreme Lords, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. How can one who troubles them expect any good fortune? Kaṁsa and all his followers lost both their wealth and their lives because of enmity toward them, and after battling them seventeen times Jarāsandha was left without even a chariot.**

**Комментарий:**

How can one who offended them (vṛjinam) have good fortune? The meaning is this. You are against Satrājit, not the Lord. Thus you should surrender to him. If you do not, I will not become opposed to him like you. Kaṁsa died (apītaḥ). Due to seventeen battles, Jarāsandha was left without a chariot.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**His appeal refused, Śatadhanvā went to Akrūra and begged him for protection. But Akrūra similarly told him, “Who would oppose the two Lords if he knew their strength?**

**Комментарий:**

Not getting help from Kṛtavarmā, he went to Akrūra. Pārṣṇi-grāham means help.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**“It is the Supreme Lord who creates, maintains and destroys this universe without effort. The cosmic creators cannot even understand his purpose, bewildered as they are by his illusory māyā.**

**Комментарий:**

The singular is used instead of the dual since Balarāma is included in Kṛṣṇa. Mohitājayā should be mohitā ajayā.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**As a child of seven, Kṛṣṇa uprooted an entire mountain and held it aloft as easily as a young boy picks up a mushroom.**

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**“I offer my obeisances to the Lord whose actions are amazing, since he is endowed with all powers in full, and is the supreme Brahman in human form, who is thus without end and without Satrājit Murdered, the Jewel Returned 489 beginning, and remains unchanged since he dwells within all beings. I offer respects to him.”**

**Комментарий:**

Ātmane means to the form which is the self (ātmā) .

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**His appeal thus rejected by Akrūra also, Śatadhanvā placed the precious jewel in Akrūra’s care and fled on a horse that could travel one hundred yojanas \[eight hundred miles\].**

**Комментарий:**

Nyasya means placing (the jewel) as a nyāsa. This shows his great possessiveness for the jewel. He went on a horse capable of going a hundred yojanas. That was the horse’s nature. In dangerous circumstances it could go further. He went from Dvārakā to a grove near Mithilā.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, mounting Kṛṣṇa’s chariot, with Garuḍa as the flag, and which was yoked with tremendously swift horses, pursued their elder’s murderer.**

**Комментарий:**

They pursued the killer of their father-in-law.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**In a garden on the outskirts of Mithilā, the horse Śatadhanvā was riding collapsed. Terrified, he abandoned the horse and began to flee on foot, with Kṛṣṇa in angry pursuit.**

**Комментарий:**

“If he was fleeing, it is not correct to chase him.” Kṛṣṇa was angry. Since anger on someone who killed an elder is correct.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**As Śatadhanvā fled on foot, the Supreme Lord, also going on foot, cut off his head with his sharp-edged disc. The Lord then searched Śatadhanvā’s upper and lower garments for the Syamantaka jewel.**

**Комментарий:**

It is understood that the jewel was with Akrūra. This is done as a pastime meant for illusion.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Not finding the jewel, Lord Kṛṣṇa went to his elder brother and said, “We have killed Śatadhanvā uselessly. The jewel isn’t here.”**

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**To this Lord Balarāma replied, “Indeed, Śatadhanvā must have placed the jewel in the care of someone. You should return to our city and find that person.**

**Комментарий:**

“Search for him (anveṣa).”

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**“I wish to visit King Videha, who is most dear to me.” O King, having said this, Balarāma, the beloved descendant of Yadu, entered the city of Mithilā.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking that “Even though Kṛṣṇa is omniscient, he is acting like this to fool me,” because he was bewildered by Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma, concealing his anger, spoke this verse. I will not enter your Dvārakā. Stay there as you please.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**The King of Mithilā immediately rose from his seat when he saw Balarāma approaching. With great love the king honored the supremely worshipable Lord by offering him elaborate worship, as stipulated by scriptural injunctions.**

**Комментарий:**

The king rose suddenly because Balarāma came unexpectedly and alone. He worshipped him with the articles for worship (samarhaṇaiḥ).

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**The almighty Balarāma stayed in Mithilā for several years, honored by his affectionate devotee Janaka Mahārāja. During that time Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s son Duryodhana learned from Balarāma the art of fighting with a club.**

**Комментарий:**

The words mānitaḥ and vibhuḥ are linked. The Lord (vibhuḥ) stayed there for some time honored (mānitaḥ) by his devotee.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Keśava arrived in Dvārakā and described the demise of Śatadhanvā and his own failure to find the Syamantaka jewel. He spoke in a way that would please his beloved, Satyabhāmā.**

**Комментарий:**

Keśava comforted his beloved (priyāyāḥ priya-kṛd) by affectionately saying, “I was unable to revive your father because he did not have the karma for living, but I have cut off the head of his murderer with my own hands.” Keśava is used to show that he fooled Satyabhāmā.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then had the various funeral rites performed for his deceased relative, Satrājit, along with well-wishers of the family.**

**Комментарий:**

Bandhoḥ refers to Satrājit. Sāmparāyikāḥ means funeral rites.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**When Akrūra and Kṛtavarmā, who had originally incited Śatadhanvā to commit his crime, heard that he had been killed, they fled Dvārakā in terror and took up residence elsewhere.**

**Комментарий:**

They fled from Dvārakā to some other place since they instigated (prayojakau) Śatadhanvā to take the jewel by killing Satrājit.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**In Akrūra’s absence ill omens arose in Dvārakā, and the citizens began to suffer continually from physical and mental distresses, as well as from disturbances caused by higher powers and by creatures of the earth.**

**Комментарий:**

Due to his offense of taking Kṛṣṇa away from the gopīs without pacifying them, Akrūra was forced to experience separation from the Lord for a long time and had to live in Kāśī (Benares) which was filled with people who were averse to Kṛṣṇa. Hearing how Akrūra was giving charity to many brāhmaṇas and doing sacrifices on a gold altar in Kāśī, the Dvārakāvāsīs gossiped that Akrūra was there with Kṛṣṇa’s approval. When Satyabhāmā, Balarāma and others also did not have faith in Kṛṣṇa, to dispel this stain on his reputation which arose again, the various calamities in Dvārakā which were the cause of bringing back Akrūra were created by Kṛṣṇa’s desire. After stating the sages’ proposition that Dvārakā was suffering due to the influence of time (as mentioned in this verse), Śukadeva Gosvāmī refutes it in the next verse.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Some men proposed that the troubles were due to Akrūra’s absence, but they had forgotten the glories of the Supreme Lord, which they themselves had so often described. Indeed, how can calamities occur in a place where the Lord, the residence of all the sages, resides?**

**Комментарий:**

Some like Vaiśampāyana, forgetting what they had previously said in praise of the Lord, attributed the calamities to Akrūra’s absence. In whichever city even one sage lives calamities cannot be visible there. How could calamities happen in Dvārakā where Kṛṣṇa, the shelter (vāsa) of all the sages, resided (nivāse)? Rather no calamity could occur.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**\[The elders said:\] Previously, when Indra had withheld rain from Kāsī \[Benares\], the king of that city gave his daughter Gāndinī to Śvaphalka (Akrūra’s father), who was then visiting him. It soon rained in the kingdom of Kāśī.**

**Комментарий:**

Again the opinion of the sages is described. Deve refers to Indra. Akrūra went to Kāśī because of his relationship with his maternal grandfather, the King of Kāśī.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Wherever his equally powerful son Akrūra stays, Indra will provide sufficient rain. Indeed, that place will be free of miseries and untimely deaths.**

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Hearing these words from the elders, Janārdana, though aware that the absence of Akrūra was not the only cause of the evil omens, had him summoned back to Dvārakā and spoke to him.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing the words of the elders glorifying Akrūra in order to bring him back, Kṛṣṇa thought within himself, “Akrūra’s absence is not the cause of the calamity, but rather my own desire is the real cause,” and then had Akrūra brought back from Kāśī.

### Text 35-36

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa honored Akrūra, greeted him confidentially and spoke pleasant words with him. Then the Lord, who was fully aware of Akrūra’s heart by virtue of his being the knower of everything, smiled and addressed him: “O master of charity, surely the opulent Syamantaka jewel was left in your care by Śatadhanvā and is still with you. Indeed, we have known this all along.**

**Комментарий:**

He spoke by asking questions about welfare, etc. He spoke dear topics (priya-kathāḥ) concerning how Akrūra had stayed near Kaṁsa in order to favor Vasudeva and others, how he internally endeavored to kill Kaṁsa, how he came to Vraja on the pretext of following Kaṁsa’s order, how he became blissful on seeing Kṛṣṇa and how he brought Kṛṣṇa to Mathurā to kill Kaṁsa. He also spoke to Akrūra about the recent lamentable events brought about by destiny. He knew the heart of Akrūra since he knew everything (vijñāta). Kṛṣṇa understood that “Since he is a great devotee, though I gave him the jewel, he does not care for it because being called, bringing the jewel, he has come.” Kṛṣṇa smiled. You had no enmity against Satrājit, nor did you steal the jewel. Śatadhanvā merely entrusted it to you. So why are you afraid of me? Why do I ask you? I anyway know. Then he speaks.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**“Since Satrājit had no sons, his daughter’s sons should receive his inheritance. They should pay for memorial offerings of water and piṇḍa, clear their grandfather’s outstanding debts and keep the remainder of the inheritance for themselves.**

**Комментарий:**

“Then what?” He speaks. Since Satrājit had no sons, and since his wives all died along with him, and since his daughter Satyabhāmā is not interested in the Syamantaka jewel, her sons should accept the jewel which is the inheritance, after offering water and piṇḍa to their maternal grandfather and clearing his remaining debts. The law of inheritance is defined in the Smrti scriptures: patnī duhitaraś caiva pitarau bhrātaras tathā tat-sutā gotra-jā bandhuḥ śiṣyāḥ sa-brahmacāriṇaḥ The inheritance goes first to the wife, then \[if the wife has passed away\] to the daughters, then to the parents, then to the brothers, then to the brothers’ sons, then to family members of the same gotra as the deceased, then to his disciples, and then to those who were his fellow students (sabrahmacārīs). (Yājñavalkya-dharma-śāstra 2.135)

### Text 38-39

**Перевод:**

**“Nevertheless, the jewel should remain in your care, O trustworthy Akrūra, because no one else can keep it safely. But please show the jewel just once, since my elder brother does not fully believe what I have told him about it. In this way, O most fortunate one, you will pacify my relatives. \[Everyone knows you have the jewel, for\] you are now continually performing sacrifices on altars of gold.”**

**Комментарий:**

“Should the jewel be brought?” Still it is difficult to keep by others who are devoid of vratas. Balarāma had just been brought from Mithilā. Satisfying Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa had him brought to Dvārakā by great warriors of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas. (Hari-vaṁśa) Due to this statement of Harivaṁśa, it is understood that Balarāma and Akrūra were absent from Dvārakā for the same time. Everyone knows you have the jewel since you perform continuous (avyucchinnā) sacrifices.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Thus shamed by Kṛṣṇa’s conciliatory words, the son of Śvaphalka brought out the jewel covered by this cloth, and which shone like the sun and gave it to the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Censured by those words or being touched to the heart by those words (ālabdhaḥ), he gave the gem.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**After the almighty Lord had shown the Syamantaka jewel to his relatives, thus dispelling the false accusations against him, he returned it to Akrūra.**

**Комментарий:**

Clearing the accusations (rajaḥ) created by the jewel, he returned it affectionately to his best devotee on the pretext that no one else was capable of possessing it. Akrūra placed the jewel around his neck and went away. Hari-vaṁśa says: Taking the gem from Kṛṣṇa’s hand Akrūra put it on his neck and walked like the sun.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Anyone who recites, hears or remembers this narration, rich with descriptions of the prowess of Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, capable of all actions and spread everywhere by his powers—stories which destroy saṁsāra and increase bhakti, destroys his sins and becomes happy.**

**Комментарий:**

All this was just the Lord’s desire for pastimes but not Lord’s being under someone’s control. Destroying his infamy, and the sin which is its cause, one attains happiness (śāntim). Even a protective amulet kills his wearer if he offends Kṛṣṇa. The jewel teaches this from the killing of Satrājit.

## Chapter 58 - Kṛṣṇa Marries Five Princesses

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Once, glorious in being accompanied by Sātyaki and others, the best of men went to Indraprastha to visit the Pāṇḍavas, who had again appeared in public.**

**Комментарий:**

In fifty-eighth chapter, Kṛṣṇa obtains five wives: Kālindī, Mitravindā, Satyā, Bhadrā and Lakṣmaṇā. The Pāṇḍavas were seen by everyone in the house of Drupada though they were lost (pratītān), Kṛṣṇa visited them with Sātyaki (yuyudhānaḥ) and others.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**When the Pāṇḍavas saw that Mukunda had arrived, those heroic sons of Pṛthā all stood up at once, like the senses responding to the return of the life air.**

**Комментарий:**

The senses such as ears, etc., (prāṇāḥ) become active when the prāṇa (mukhyam) having five functions, which was in a fainting state, again starts to function.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**The heroes embraced Acyuta, and the touch of his body freed them from grief. Looking at his affectionate, smiling face, they were overwhelmed with joy.**

**Комментарий:**

Their suffering of not attaining him (enasaḥ) was destroyed by the touch of his body.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**After the Lord bowed down at the feet of Yudhiṣṭhira and Bhīma and firmly embraced Arjuna, he accepted obeisances from the twin brothers, Nakula and Sahadeva.**

**Комментарий:**

Out of bliss, both parties forgot proper etiquette. Then they carefully followed the etiquette. He offered respects to the two elder cousins. He was embraced by his equal (Arjuna). He was offered respects by the two youngest cousins.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Faultless Draupadī, the Pāṇḍavas’ newly married wife, slowly Text 6\] Kṛṣṇa Marries Five Princesses 503 and somewhat timidly approached Kṛṣṇa, who sat on an exalted seat, and offered him her obeisances.**

**Комментарий:**

Draupadī (kṛṣṇā) was not criticized though she was the wife of all five Pāṇḍavas but was praised as chaste. She was newly married by the five sons of Pṛthā. When Kṛṣṇa suddenly came within the palace, she offered respects.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Sātyaki also accepted a seat of honor after receiving worship and welcome from the Pāṇḍavas, and the Lord’s other companions, being duly honored, sat down in various places.**

**Комментарий:**

Other associates of Kṛṣṇa sat around Sātyaki in the four directions, close (pari upāsata).

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**The Lord then went to see his aunt, Queen Kuntī. He bowed down to her and she embraced him, her eyes moist with great affection. Kṛṣṇa inquired from her along with her daughter-inlaw, Draupadī, about their welfare, and they in turn questioned him at length about his relatives \[in Dvārakā\].**

**Комментарий:**

Going within the rooms attached to the palace, he then bowed, etc., to Kuntī. Her eyes moistened with extreme love (ati-hārdena), Kuntī embraced Kṛṣṇa and smelled his head, saying, “I worship the moon of your face with a million life airs.” Priyatā and hārdam are synonyms for pure love according to Amara-kośa. They asked him about his relatives such as brother (Akrūra).

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**So overcome by love that her throat choked up and her eyes filled with tears, Queen Kuntī remembered the many troubles she and her sons had endured. Thus she addressed Kṛṣṇa, who appears before his devotees to drive away their distress.**

**Комментарий:**

Having symptoms of being overcome with prema, etc., she spoke to Kṛṣṇa. Remembering the many troubles inflicted by Duryodhana and others, such as giving poison, she spoke to Kṛṣṇa whose sight in the mind destroys all sufferings.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**\[Queen Kuntī said:\] My dear Kṛṣṇa, our welfare was assured only when you remembered us, your relatives, and gave us your protection by sending my brother to visit us.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhrātā means Akrūra.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**For you, the well-wishing friend and Supreme Soul of the universe, there is never any illusion of “us” and “them.” Yet even so, residing within the hearts of all, you eradicate the sufferings of those who remember you constantly.**

**Комментарий:**

She indicates Kṛṣṇa’s affection for his devotees. You are friend of the universe, benefitting the world by bestowing your jñāna and kriyā śaktis and its soul, spreading everywhere (ātmā). You have no illusion about “mine” or “others” (sva-para-bhrāntiḥ) since all belong to you. Still you reside in the hearts of those who think of you as the shelter of qualities like compassion, appearing to them manifesting those qualities. You always destroy suffering just as the sun, though having the nature of helping others due to invoking the vision of blind, also destroys darkness for persons with eyes.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**King Yudhiṣṭhira said: O supreme controller, I do not know what pious deeds we, devoid of bhakti, have done so that we can see you, whom even the masters of bhakti rarely see.**

**Комментарий:**

Yudhiṣṭhira, taking shelter of humility, describes the Lord’s affection for the most fallen. Though you are like this, the fact that we see you is that you are affectionate to the most fallen.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Requested by the king to stay with them, the almighty Lord remained happily in Indraprastha during the months of the rainy season, giving joy to the eyes of the city’s residents.**

**Комментарий:**

He stayed there (verb omitted) happily.

### Text 13-14

**Перевод:**

**Once Arjuna, the slayer of powerful enemies, donned his armor, mounted his chariot flying the flag of Hanumān, took up his bow and his two inexhaustible quivers, and went to sport with Kṛṣṇa in a large forest filled with fierce animals.**

**Комментарий:**

A story related to seeing Kālindī is told. This event took place after the burning of the Khāṇḍava forest since Arjuna now had Gāṇḍīva bow, which he obtained from that incident.

### Text 15-16

**Перевод:**

**With his arrows Arjuna shot tigers, boars and buffalo in that forest, along with rurus, śarabhas, gavayas, rhinoceroses, black deer, rabbits and porcupines. A crew of servants carried for King Yudhiṣṭhira the slain animals fit to be offered in sacrifice on some special occasion. Then, feeling thirsty and tired, Arjuna went to the bank of the Yamunā.**

**Комментарий:**

The servants took those animals which were pure (medhyān), suitable for sacrifice, to make the king offer them in sacrifice (rājñe). By killing the violent animals, it prevented them from killing others and those violent animals which were unsuitable for sacrifice got benefit by being killed by them. Bibhatsur is Arjuna. Since they rode on a single chariot (verse 13) it was Kṛṣṇa’s.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**After the two Kṛṣṇas bathed there, they drank the river’s clear water. The great warriors then saw an attractive young girl walking nearby.**

**Комментарий:**

The two, Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, saw the girl who was performing austerities.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Sent by his friend, Arjuna approached the exceptional young woman, who possessed beautiful hips, fine teeth and a lovely face, and inquired from her as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

He was sent by Kṛṣṇa, to teach Arjuna of her attraction to him (Kṛṣṇa) alone.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**\[Arjuna said:\] Who are you, O fine-waisted lady? Whose daughter are you, and where do you come from? What are you doing here? I think you must be looking for a husband. Please explain everything, O beautiful one.**

**Комментарий:**

Who are you—are you a devatā or human being and what is your name? Whose daughter are you? From which place (kutaḥ) have you come? Or, for what purpose (kutaḥ) are you here? What do you desire to do? I think you, unmarried, must be looking for a husband. Please tell everything.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Kālindī said: I am the daughter of the sun-god. I desire to get as my husband the most excellent and munificent person who spreads himself everywhere, and to that end I am performing severe penances.**

**Комментарий:**

Fearing that “He desires me,” she speaks.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**I will accept no husband other than him, the abode of the goddess of fortune. May that Mukunda, the Supreme Lord, the shelter of the helpless, be pleased with me.**

**Комментарий:**

She expresses her convictions by stating the negative. He is the abode of a wealth of all beauty and other qualities (śrī-niketam). He is the only protector of me, a young girl performing austerities in the forest (anātha-saṁśrayaḥ). Thus I do not fear anything.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**I am known as Kālindī, and I live in a mansion my father built for me within the water of the Yamunā. There I will stay until I meet Acyuta.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described her lineage, she tells her name. “Why do you live in the water like an aquatic?” I live in a house made by my father the sun god, by some mystic power. No one can harm me, who am the daughter of sun god. I will live here until I see he who does not waver from affection for devotees (acyuta).

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Arjuna repeated all this to Vāsudeva, who was already aware of it. The Lord then took Kālindī onto his chariot and went back to see King Yudhiṣṭhira.**

**Комментарий:**

“Ah, my dear beautiful one, I am your most desirable Viṣṇu. You should recognize me from the descriptions of Viṣṇu taught by your father. Climb on the chariot.” The idea is that he aroused her desire to climb the chariot since it is not said, “He caught her and made her climb the chariot.” Kṛṣṇa knew this (vidvān): he went to bring her knowing that she had prema for him. Then he approached Yudhiṣṭhira and told him that he had obtained Kālindī. He (Yudhiṣṭhira) entrusted her to his mother (Kuntī). She entrusted her to her daughter-in-law (Draupadī).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**\[Describing a previous incident, Śukadeva Gosvāmī said:\] Upon the request of the Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇa had Viśvakarmā build them a most wonderful and amazing city.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord acted for the benefit of the Pāṇḍavas in another way. This is a previous incident. “We should have a city where you with all your associates can live.” Requested by the Pāṇḍavas, he built a city embedded with jewels. The order of events is this. The city was built. Then the Khāṇḍava forest was burned. Then Arjuna took the assembly hall. Finally, Kṛṣṇa accepted Kālindī.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord stayed in that city for some time to please his devotees. On one occasion, Kṛṣṇa wanted to give the Khāṇḍava forest as a gift to Agni, and so the Lord became Arjuna’s charioteer.**

**Комментарий:**

He became Arjuna’s charioteer so Arjuna could gain the Gāṇḍīva bow, etc. The forest belonged to Indra.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Being pleased, O King, Agni presented Arjuna with a bow, a set of white horses, a chariot, a pair of inexhaustible quivers, and armor that no fighter could pierce with weapons.**

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**When the demon Maya was saved from the fire, Maya presented to his friend an assembly hall, in which Duryodhana would later mistake water for a solid floor.**

**Комментарий:**

Maya gave the hall to his friend (sakhye), Arjuna.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Then Kṛṣṇa, given leave by Yudhiṣṭhira and other well-wishing relatives and friends, returned to Dvārakā with Sātyaki and the rest of his entourage.**

**Комментарий:**

He took permission from Yudhiṣṭhira (tena), who knew of Kṛṣṇa’s desire to marry Kālindī.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**The supremely auspicious Lord then married Kālindī on a day when the season, the lunar asterism and the configurations of the sun and other heavenly bodies were all propitious. In this way he brought the greatest pleasure to his devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

The season and constellation were suitable for marriage (supuṇya).

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Vindya and Anuvindya, who shared the throne of Avantī, were followers of Duryodhana’s. When the time came for their sister \[Mitravindā\] to select her husband in the svayaṁvara ceremony, they forbade her to choose Kṛṣṇa, although she was attracted to him.**

**Комментарий:**

The fifth marriage to Mitravindā is described in two verses. The brothers were kings of Avantī.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, Kṛṣṇa forcibly took away Princess Mitravindā, the daughter of his aunt Rājādhidevī, before the eyes of the rival kings.**

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**O King, Nagnajit, the very pious King of Kauśalya, had a lovely daughter named Satyā, or Nāgnajitī.**

**Комментарий:**

The sixth marriage is described. Nagnajit means he who conquered by proper discrimination even the naked Jains who were beyond the rules of the Veda. He did this because he was a follower of Vedic dharma. He was king of Ayodhya (kauśalyaḥ). His daughter was named Satyā.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**The kings who came as suitors were not allowed to marry her unless they could subdue seven sharp-horned bulls. These bulls were extremely vicious and uncontrollable, and they could not tolerate even the smell of warriors.**

**Комментарий:**

Without taming the best among the cattle (go-vṛṣān), most wicked, violent bulls, having the nature of demons they could not marry her. In the Second Canto these bulls are counted among the demons. (SB [2.7.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.34)) It is stated there that after being killed, by the power of the Lord’s touch, they attained liberation.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**When the Lord, the protector of the devotees, heard of the princess who was to be won by the conqueror of the bulls, he went to the capital of Kauśalya with a large army.**

**Комментарий:**

He heard of her, who could be attained by conquering the bulls (vṛṣa-jil-labhyām).

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**The King of Kośala, pleased to see Kṛṣṇa, worshiped him by rising from his throne and offering him a seat of honor and substantial gifts. Kṛṣṇa also greeted the king respectfully.**

**Комментарий:**

The king worshipped Kṛṣṇa and was also respected by Kṛṣṇa (pratinanditaḥ).

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**When the king’s daughter saw her chosen suitor arrive, she immediately desired to have him, the husband of Rukmiṇī. She prayed, “May he become my husband. If I have kept my vows, may the sacred fire bring about the fulfillment of my hopes.”**

**Комментарий:**

She saw him from lattice holes in the roof pavilion. He was the master of all wealth (ramā-patim).

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**King Nagnajit first worshiped the Lord properly and then addressed Him: “O Nārāyaṇa, Lord of the universe, you are full in your own spiritual pleasure. Therefore what can this insignificant person do for you?”**

**Комментарий:**

Taking shelter of humility he speaks.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**“Lakṣmī, Brahmā, Śiva and the rulers of the various planets place the dust of his lotus feet on their heads, and to protect the codes of religion, which he has created, he assumes pastime incarnations at various times. By what sādhana will Kṛṣṇa, Svayam Bhagavān, become pleased with me?” She describes him with a humble mood, indicating his special glory.**

**Комментарий:**

He specifically describes his glories. With the desire to follow (parīpsayā) the laws he has made, he accepts forms having various pastimes (līlā-tanuḥ) at appropriate times. Nourished with the beauty of the Kaustubha, he has now come to my house. By what worship performed by me, who am insignificant, may he be satisfied?

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O beloved descendant of Kuru, the Supreme Lord was pleased, and after accepting a comfortable seat he smiled and addressed the king in a voice as deep as the rumbling of a cloud.**

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O ruler of men, learned authorities condemn begging for a person in the royal order who is executing his religious duties. Even so, desiring your friendship, I ask you for your daughter, though we offer no gifts in exchange.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he is the Lord, he speaks from the position of kṣatriya obligations. O ruler of men! He addresses the king with a title suitable for his father-in-law. For a person engaged in kṣatriya dharma, even if he is a low kṣatriya, begging is condemned by Vyāsa and other learned sages (kavibhiḥ). Still I, the best of kṣatriyas, beg for your daughter, with a desire for friendship with you. Or by the prema you have for me consider the gift as my desire. He makes a profound joke. We kṣatriyas do not give gifts.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**The King said: My Lord, who could be a better husband for my daughter than you, the exclusive abode of all qualities? On your body the goddess of fortune herself resides, never leaving you for any reason.**

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**But to ascertain the proper husband for my daughter, O protector of the devotees, we previously set a condition to test the prowess of her suitors.**

**Комментарий:**

We too do not accept a dowry. But I have made a rule (samayaḥ) to test the strength of any groom desiring my daughter as his bride. Otherwise all the kings would ask for her and how could I refuse all of them? The actual purpose in setting up this test, however, is to attain you, most suitable, as my daughter’s husband.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**These seven bulls are impossible to tame and stubborn, O hero. They have defeated many princes, breaking their limbs.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing him accept the challenge, the king went with Kṛṣṇa to the place where the bulls lived and pointed them out. They are untrained and difficult to restrain. Why? They have defeated many princes, breaking their limbs.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Since you can subdue them, O descendant of Yadu, you will certainly be the appropriate bridegroom for my daughter, O Lord of Śrī.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the visible meaning of yad seems to be yadi (if), but the real meaning of yad is yasmāt (because). O lord of Lakṣmī! You can easily tame them. You alone have been decided as the groom.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Upon hearing these terms, the Lord tightened his clothing, revealed seven forms and easily subdued the bulls.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa revealed seven forms (ātmānaṁ saptadhā kṛtvā), to show Princess Satyā that she would not have to suffer competing with his other queens, since manifesting himself multiplely he could enjoy with all of them simultaneously.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**Śauri tied up the bulls, whose pride and strength were now broken, and pulled them with ropes just as a child playfully pulls wooden toy bulls.**

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**Then King Nagnajit, pleased and astonished, presented his daughter to Kṛṣṇa. The Supreme Lord accepted this suitable bride in the proper Vedic fashion.**

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**The king’s wives felt the greatest ecstasy upon attaining Kṛṣṇa as the dear husband of their daughter, and a mood of great festivity arose.**

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**Conch shells, horns and drums resounded, along with vocal and instrumental music and the sounds of brāhmaṇas, invoking blessings. The joyful men and women adorned themselves with fine clothing and garlands.**

### Text 50-51

**Перевод:**

**As the dowry, powerful King Nagnajit gave ten thousand cows, three thousand young maidservants wearing golden ornaments on their necks and bedecked in fine clothing, nine thousand elephants, a hundred times as many chariots as elephants, a hundred times as many horses as chariots, and a hundred times as many male servants as horses.**

**Комментарий:**

He gave three thousand maid servants well dressed with ornaments on their necks. In addition, he gave 9,000 elephants, 900,000 chariots, 90 million horses and 9 billion soldiers! Nāgāt and other words are in singular denoting a class.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**The King of Kośala, his heart melting with affection, had the bride and groom seated on their chariot, and then he sent them on their way surrounded by a great army.**

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**When the intolerant kings who had been rival suitors heard what had happened, they tried to stop Kṛṣṇa on the road as he took his bride home. But just as the bulls had broken the kings’ strength before, the Yadu warriors broke it now.**

**Комментарий:**

The kings whose pride was previously broken by the bulls in anger caused obstruction. They had not forgotten the incident. Their pride was now broken by the Yadus.

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**Arjuna, wielder of the Gāṇḍīva bow, was always eager to please his friend Kṛṣṇa, and thus he drove back those opponents, who were shooting torrents of arrows at the Lord. He did this just as a lion drives away insignificant animals.**

**Комментарий:**

Arjuna drove them away.

### Text 55

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, the chief of the Yadus, then took his dowry and Satyā to Dvārakā and continued to live there happily.**

### Text 56

**Перевод:**

**Bhadrā was a princess of the Kaikeya kingdom and the daughter of Kṛṣṇa’s paternal aunt Śrutakīrti. The Lord married Bhadrā when her brothers, headed by Santardana, offered her to him.**

**Комментарий:**

The seventh marriage is described. He married Bhadrā, the daughter of Kṛṣṇa’s paternal aunt Śrutakīrti. She was born in Kaikeya.

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**Then the Lord married Lakṣmaṇā, the daughter of the King of Madra. Kṛṣṇa appeared at her svayaṁvara ceremony and took her away by himself, just as Garuḍa once stole the devatās’ nectar.**

**Комментарий:**

The eighth marriage is described. The eight queens Rukmiṇī, Jāmbavatī, Satyabhāmā, Kālindī, Mitravindā, Satyā, Bhadrā and Lakṣmaṇā have been described.

### Text 58

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa also acquired thousands of other wives equal to these when he killed Bhaumāsura and freed the beautiful maidens the demon was holding captive.**

**Комментарий:**

Sahasraśa is thousands and thousands. It means 16,000 beautiful maidens. He took them from the palace of Bhauma (tan-nirodhāt).

## Chapter 59 - The Killing of the Demon Naraka

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**\[King Parīkṣit said:\] How was Bhaumāsura, who kidnapped so many women, killed by the Supreme Lord? Please narrate this adventure of Lord who holds the Śārṅga bow.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fifth-ninth chapter Kṛṣṇa kills Bhauma, obtains thousands of girls stolen by him, and takes pārijāta tree from Svarga. Please explain the Lord’s valor by which Bhauma, by whom the women were imprisoned, was killed and for what reason (ca).

### Text 2-3

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After Bhauma had stolen the earrings belonging to Indra’s mother, along with Varuṇa’s umbrella and the devatās’ playground at the peak of Mandara mountain, Indra went to Kṛṣṇa and informed him of these misdeeds. The Lord, taking his wife Satyabhāmā with him, then rode on Garuḍa to Prāgjyotiṣa-pura, which was surrounded on all sides by fortifications consisting of hills, unmanned weapons, water, fire and wind, and by obstructions of mura-pāśa wire.**

**Комментарий:**

Indra went to Dvārakā and informed of Bhauma’s activities to Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa then went to Prāgjyotiṣa-pura. Indra is described. Indra’s umbrella had been stolen by Bhauma. The umbrella was actually Varuṇa’s but Indra’s pride was broken by the theft, since he was the king of the devatās. His mother’s earrings were also stolen. Mandara mountain’s peak, called Maṇi-parvata, made of gems situated in Svarga was also stolen. He related these actions of Bhauma to Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa went with his wife Satyabhāmā. Prāgjyotiṣa was Bhauma’s city. Satyabhāmā had been miffed when the heavenly pārjiāta flower, brought by Nārada Muni, had been given to Rukmiṇī. At that time Kṛṣṇa, who was pacifiying Satyabhāmā, promised her, “I will plant you a whole tree of these flowers.” Therefore Kṛṣṇa brought Satyabhāmā along to show her that he could take the tree from Indra and so that she would also be helpful. Or since he had given a boon to earth, that he would not kill her son without her permission, he took Satyabhāmā, who was her aṁśī. The fort was impenetrable with water, fire and wind weapons.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**With his club the Lord broke through the rock fortifications; with his arrows, the weapon fortifications; with his disc, the fire, water and wind fortifications; and with his sword, the mura-pāśa cables.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**With the sound of his conch shell Gadādhara then shattered the magic seals of the fortress, along with the hearts of its brave defenders, and with his heavy club he demolished the surrounding ramparts.**

**Комментарий:**

The walls had machines attached on top made of iron. The sound of the conch shattered the weapons and the hearts of the defenders.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**The five-headed demon Mura, who was sleeping in the city’s moat, awoke and rose up out of the water when he heard the vibration of Kṛṣṇa’s Pāñcajanya conch shell, a sound as terrifying as the thunder at the end of the cosmic age.**

**Комментарий:**

The sound was terrifying like thunder at the end of the yuga. Mura rose out of the oceanic water of the moat.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Shining with the blinding, terrible effulgence of the sun’s fire at the end of a millennium, Mura seemed to swallow up the three worlds with his five mouths. He lifted up his trident and attacked the Lord just as a snake attacks Garuḍa.**

**Комментарий:**

The subject is Mura.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Mura whirled his trident and then hurled it fiercely at Garuḍa, roaring from all five mouths. The sound filled the earth and sky, all directions and the limits of outer space, until it reverberated against the very shell of the universe.**

**Комментарий:**

He hurled his trident (āvidhya) and threw it at Garuḍa. He made a great sound (vyanadat).

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Then with two arrows the Lord struck the trident flying toward Garuḍa and broke it into three pieces. Next, the Lord hit Mura’s mouths with several arrows, and the demon angrily hurled his club at the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa broke the trident (triśikham). Mura released a club at the Lord.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**As Mura’s club sped toward him on the battlefield, Gadāgraja intercepted it with his own and broke it into thousands of pieces. Mura then raised his arms high and rushed at the unconquerable Lord, who easily sliced off his heads with his disc weapon.**

**Комментарий:**

The lord cut off the head of Mura who ran towards him with raised arms.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Lifeless, Mura’s decapitated body fell into the water like a mountain whose peak has been severed by the power of Indra’s thunderbolt. The demon’s seven sons, lamenting their father’s death, prepared to retaliate.**

**Комментарий:**

His body fell like a mountain cut by Indra’s thunderbolt . Overcome with grief at their father’s death, his sons prepared to fight. His seven sons, angry, prepared for revenge.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Ordered by Bhaumāsura, Mura’s seven sons—Tāmra, Antarikṣa, Śravaṇa, Vibhāvasu, Vasu, Nabhasvān and Aruṇa—followed their general, Pīṭha, onto the battlefield bearing their weapons.**

**Комментарий:**

They came out (niragat).

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**These fierce warriors furiously attacked invincible Kṛṣṇa with arrows, knives, clubs, spears, swords and tridents, but the Supreme Lord, with unfailing prowess, cut this mountain of weapons into tiny pieces with his arrows.**

**Комментарий:**

They attacked the Lord (ajite).

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**The Lord severed the heads, thighs, arms, legs and armor of these opponents led by Pīṭha by means of his arrows and cakra and sent them all to the abode of Yamarāja. Narakāsura, the son of the earth, could not contain his fury when he saw the fate of his military leaders. Thus he went out of the citadel with elephants born from the Milk Ocean who were exuding mada from their foreheads out of excitement.**

**Комментарий:**

Yama-kṣayaṁ means the abode of Yamarāja (death). The real meaning is that Kṛṣṇa gave them liberation, for yama indicates the aṣṭāṅga-yoga process ending with liberation. Bhauma, from top of the fort, saw his army destroyed. He emerged (nirakramat) from the fort with elephants born from the Milk Ocean. This means that the elephants came in the family of Airāvata. He was called Naraka because from birth he had a wicked nature, taking human heads in his mouth as soon as he was born.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa and his wife, mounted upon Garuḍa, looked like a cloud with lightning sitting above the sun. Seeing the Lord, Bhauma released his Śataghnī weapon at him, whereupon all of Bhauma’s soldiers simultaneously attacked with their weapons.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was situated with his wife and Garuḍa like a cloud with lightning above the sun. This is abhūta upamā (an analogy which is impossible). Or it is bimbānubimba upamā . Narakāsura threw his Śataghnī (name of his śakti spear) weapon at Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**At that moment Gadāgraja shot his sharp arrows at Bhaumāsura’s army. These arrows, displaying variegated feathers, soon reduced that army to a mass of bodies with severed arms, thighs and necks. The Lord similarly killed the opposing horses and elephants.**

**Комментарий:**

The arrows had variegated feathers.

### Text 17-19

**Перевод:**

**Hari then struck down all the missiles and weapons the enemy soldiers threw at him, O hero of the Kurus, destroying each and every one with three sharp arrows. Meanwhile Garuḍa, as he carried the Lord, struck the enemy’s elephants with his wings. Beaten by Garuḍa’s wings, beak and talons, the elephants fled back into the city, leaving Narakāsura alone on the battlefield to oppose Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Even before the weapons such as swords (śastrāṇi) and arrows (astrāṇi) employed by the warriors reached their target, Kṛṣṇa first killed the throwers of the weapons and then destroyed the missiles while they were still in the air, each with three arrows. Śukadeva Gosvāmī cried out in extreme amazement, “O kuru-udvaha!” (O hero of the Kurus, King Parīkṣit) Even among the Kurus, such personalities as Bhīṣma and Arjuna were not capable of such swiftness in using weapons. Naraka was alone.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Seeing his army driven back and tormented by Garuḍa, Bhauma attacked him with his spear, which had once defeated Indra’s thunderbolt. But though struck by that mighty weapon, Garuḍa was not shaken. Indeed, he was like an elephant hit with a flower garland.**

**Комментарий:**

Struck by the weapon, Garuḍa did not shake (he did not feel pain).

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Bhauma, frustrated in all his attempts, took up his spear to kill Kṛṣṇa. But even before he could release it, the Lord cut off his head with his razor-sharp cakra as the demon sat atop his elephant.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Bhauma with his invincible trident, Satyabhāmā said, “Kill him right away,” and Kṛṣṇa cut off his head with his cakra.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Fallen on the ground, Bhaumāsura’s head shone brilliantly, decorated as it was with earrings and an attractive helmet. As cries of “Alas, alas!” and “Well done!” arose, the sages and principal devatās worshiped Mukunda by covering him with flower garlands.**

**Комментарий:**

Some (who were very sinful at that place) shouted in condemnation “Hā, hā!” This is the meaning of hā hā is according to Kṣīrasvāmī. The sages said (verb should be added) in joy “It is good that the wicked fellow is dead (sādhu)!” They covered him with garlands.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**The goddess of the earth then approached Kṛṣṇa and presented him with Aditi’s earrings, which were made of glowing gold inlaid with shining jewels. She also gave him a Vaijayantī flower garland, Varuṇa’s umbrella and the peak of Mandara Mountain.**

**Комментарий:**

She offered him the earrings along with a vanamāla and vaijayanti garland and the mountain of jewels called Maṇi-parvata.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**O King, after bowing down to him and then standing with joined palms, the goddess, her mind filled with devotion, began to praise the Lord of the universe, whom the best of devatās worship.**

**Комментарий:**

She praised the Lord who is worshipped by the best devatās such as Brahmā.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Goddess Bhūmi said: I offer respects to you. O Lord of the chief devatās, O holder of the conch, disc and club! O Supreme Soul within the heart! I offer respects to you who assume various forms to fulfill your devotees’ desires.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to you who accept a form by the desire of the devotees. The form is dependent on the devotees’ desires.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**My respectful obeisances are unto you, O Lord, whose abdomen is marked with a depression like a lotus flower, who are always decorated with garlands of lotus flowers, whose glance is as cool as the lotus and whose feet are engraved with lotuses.**

**Комментарий:**

She offers respects with the mantra that Kuntī recited to please the Lord, indicating the Lord’s beauty.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances unto you, who, willingly revealing all your sweet qualities, act as the son of Vasudeva, spread your glories everywhere, produce prema for your devotees, and know their desires.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to you, unlimited in six qualities (bhagavate), dwelling in all beings (vāsudevāya), since you are all powerful (viṣṇave), since you exist before all others (puruṣāya) being their cause. Śruti says pūrvam evāham ihāsam iti tat-puruṣasya puruṣatvam: in the beginning I alone existed in this world as the best of the puruṣas. (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 1.23.4) You are the cause (bījāya) of prakṛti, the cause of the universe (ādi). Sa kāraṇaṁ karaṇādhipādhipaḥ: the Lord is the cause, the ruler of those who control causes. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad). He is omniscient (pūrṇa-bodhāya).

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances unto you of unlimited energies, the unborn progenitor of this universe, the Brahman. O Soul of the high and the low, O Soul of the created elements, O all-pervading Supreme Soul, obeisances unto you.**

**Комментарий:**

“But I cannot exist before my cause.” You are without birth (ajāya) but are the cause of the universe (asya) since it is said, na tasya kaścij janitā na cādhipaḥ: he has no lord or creator. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad [6.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sveta-bs/6.9)). Then two causes of having no birth are mentioned to indicate that he is without birth since he is Brahman, great (brahmaṇe) and he is the cause of the universe since he possesses unlimited śaktis (ananta-śaktaye). “But parents create sons. Before them there were other beings. And their cause was the elements and jīvas manifest by their karma. Who am I in this?” You are soul of all high and low beings. You are the instigator of all fathers, etc. Thus you alone are the generator of everything.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Desiring to create, O unborn master, you increase and then assume the mode of passion. You do likewise with the mode of ignorance when you wish to annihilate the universe and with goodness when you wish to maintain it. Nonetheless, you remain uncovered by these modes. You are time, the pradhāna, and the puruṣa, O Lord of the universe, yet still you are separate and distinct.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord as the cause of the universe is further explained. You alone support rajas (utkaṭam), tamas and sattva but are not contaminated by them (asaṁvṛtaḥ). You inspire rajas for creating the universe, tamas for destroying it (nirodhāya) and sattva for maintaining it (sthānāya). “But the causes of creation, etc., of the universe are the guṇas. By glancing at pradhāna, the puruṣa agitates it. Time is the efficient cause. What do I do in this?” You are time, māyā and the puruṣa since time and māyā are your śaktis and the puruṣa is your svāṁśa. Their activities are your activities. You are superior to time and pradhāna (paraḥ) and the aṁśī.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**This is illusion: that earth, water, fire, air, ether, sense objects, demigods, mind, the senses, false ego and the total material energy exist independent of you. In fact, they are all within you, my Lord, who are one without a second.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Bhū-devī! Because my form is the color of an atasī flower, it must be material. My senses and subtle body are related to ahaṅkāra. How then do you call me the puruṣa, and say that I am superior to time and pradhāna?” Those who think that earth (I, aham), the subtle sense objects such as sound (mātrāni), ahaṅkāra (kartā) — all moving (mind and senses) and nonmoving (gross elements) exist in you are mistaken since you have nothing different from your svarūpa (advitīye). Like a golden statue, you are only one essence. samāna evaṁ cābhedāt Though there are differences because of the Lord’s features, the Lord is still one entity, because his features are nondifferent from himself. (Vedānta Sūtra [3.3.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vs/3.3.20))

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Here is the son of Bhaumāsura. Frightened, he is approaching your lotus feet, since you remove the distress of all who seek refuge in you. Please protect him. Place your lotus hand, which dispels all sins, upon his head.**

**Комментарий:**

Having praised the Lord, Bhūmi prays. The son of Bhauma, Bhagadatta is afraid. I have made him surrender to your lotus feet. O Lord who destroys the suffering of the surrendered! Place your hand on his head.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus entreated by Goddess Bhūmi in words of humble devotion, the Supreme Lord bestowed fearlessness upon her grandson and then entered Bhaumāsura’s palace, which was filled with all manner of riches.**

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**There Lord Kṛṣṇa saw sixteen thousand royal maidens, whom Bhauma had taken by force from various kings.**

**Комментарий:**

There were actually 16,100 royal maidens taken from kings and devatās, etc. According to the Viṣṇu Purāṇa: kanyā-pure sa kanyānāṁ ṣoḍaśātulya-vikramaḥ śatādhikāni dadṛśe sahasrāṇi mahā-mate deva-siddhāsurādīnām nṛpāṇāṁ ca janārdana hatvā hi so’suraḥ kanyā rurodha nija-mandire Bhauma had stolen 16,100 women not only from kings, but he also kidnapped the unmarried daughters of demigods, sages and demons as well and kept them in his palace.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**The women became enchanted when they saw that most excellent of males, Kṛṣṇa, enter. In their minds they each accepted him, who had been brought there by destiny, as their chosen husband.**

**Комментарий:**

They achieved him by the fortune of previously practised bhakti (daivopasāditam).

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**With the thought “May providence grant that this man become my husband,” each and every princess absorbed her heart in contemplation of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Dhātā means Kṛṣṇa. It is the Lord’s name mentioned in Viṣṇu -sahasra-nāma-stotra: dhātā vidhātā dhātur uttamaḥ.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**The Lord had the princesses dressed in clean, spotless garments and then sent them in palanquins to Dvārakā, together with great treasures of chariots, horses and other valuables.**

**Комментарий:**

He had them dressed in clean clothing. This suggests that they had previously performed vratas for attaining him. Kṛṣṇa sent the women to Dvārakā in palanquins (narayānaiḥ). By saying mahākośān (great treasures) it is suggested that Bhauma had a wealth of jewels that even Kuvera had not seen.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa also dispatched sixty-four swift white elephants, descendants of Airāvata, who each sported four tusks, as well as many other elephants.**

**Комментарий:**

Due to the word ca it is understood from Viṣṇu Purāṇa that besides the sixty-four swift elephants fifty-nine thousand other elephants and twenty-one million horses from Kāmboja were also sent to Dvārakā by the servants of Naraka.

### Text 38-39

**Перевод:**

**The Lord then went to the abode of Indra and gave mother Aditi her earrings; there Indra and his wife worshiped Kṛṣṇa and his beloved consort Satyabhāmā. Then, at Satyabhāmā’s behest the Lord uprooted the heavenly pārijāta tree and put it on the back of Garuḍa. After defeating Indra and all the other devatās, Kṛṣṇa brought the pārijāta to his capital.**

**Комментарий:**

The details of going to Indra’s abode are given in Viṣṇu Purāṇa: Garuḍa very easily carried the umbrella of Varuṇa, the jeweled mountain, Kṛṣṇa and his wife and went to Svarga. The Lord blew his conch when he arrived at the gate of Svarga. The devatās arrived and worshipped Kṛṣṇa with arghya. After being worshipped, Kṛṣṇa entered Aditi’s abode, which resembled a shining peak, and saw her. He offered her respects along with Indra, and presented her with her excellent earrings. He described to her the killing of Naraka. Due to the word ca, it is understood that he gave the remaining items to Indra. Viṣṇu Purāṇa describes how his wife requested the pārijāta. Kṛṣṇa saw that pārijāta, filled with fragrance, laden with masses of buds, producing coolness and joy, decorated with pink, young shoots and golden bark. It has been produced from the churning of the Milk Ocean. On seeing that tree, Satyabhāmā spoke to Kṛṣṇa, O best of the brāhmaṇas! “O Kṛṣṇa! Why can this tree not be brought to Dvārakā? If your words are true and I am really dear to you, please bring that tree for the garden in my house. O Kṛṣṇa! You have many times said that you do not desire Jāmbavatī or Rukmiṇī as much as you desire me. O Govinda! If you have spoken true and your words are not just a decoration, then the pārijāta should decorate my house. Carrying a bud of the pārijāta in my hair, among all the co-wives I will be glorious. This is what I desire.” He completely conquered the devatās (nijitya) along with Indra. The details of this battle are found in Viṣṇu Purāṇa, etc.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Once planted, the pārijāta tree beautified the garden of Queen Satyabhāmā’s palace. Bees followed the tree all the way from heaven, greedy for its fragrance and sweet sap.**

**Комментарий:**

Sthāpitaḥ means planted. Details are given in Hari-vaṁśa. Near the tree people could hear various instruments and sweet singing coming from the tree and could smell whatever fragrance they desired. Sometime its branches covered the whole of Dvārakā. Sometimes it could be held in the hand, becoming as small as a thumb. The smell of the tree perfumed the earth for three furlongs, and on approaching it enabled everyone to recollect the events of a prior birth.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Even after Indra had bowed down to Acyuta, touched his feet with the tips of his crown and begged the Lord to fulfill his desire, that exalted devatā, having achieved his purpose, chose to fight with the Supreme Lord. What ignorance there is among the gods! To hell with their opulence!**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa should be served with a mentality of having no material possessions. Indra, bowing and touching the feet of the Lord with the tips of his crown, begged the Lord who does not fail to give what one wants (acyutam). Indra had requested the Lord to retrieve the umbrella, earrings, etc. Being fulfilled in his desires (siddharthaḥ) in obtaining these things, he fought (vigṛhyate) with the Lord. Though he is a great devatā (mahān), how astonishing is the anger (tamas) of the devatās! It is not proper for sāttvika devatās to show anger arising from ignorance. What to speak of Indra, their king. What use is their wealth (āḍhyatām)? It is the cause of anarthas and definitely despicable for devotees.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Then the imperishable Lord, assuming a separate form for each bride, duly married all the princesses simultaneously, each in her own palace.**

**Комментарий:**

Returning to Dvārakā (atha), Kṛṣṇa married all the women at the same time (muhūrta ekasmin) because the experts in astrology told that that very fixed time for marriage was most auspicious. Kṛṣṇa manifested as many forms as the brides by the acintya-śakti of his one form and was with all the brides. Later it will be said: It is quite amazing that in a single body Lord Kṛṣṇa simultaneously married sixteen thousand women, each in a separate palace. (SB [10.69.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/69.2)) This refutes the notion that it was like Saubhari and others expanding into many forms. By yathā (duly) it is suggested that Devakī and others were also similarly present with each bride. The forms were pūrṇa (avyayaḥ) everywhere, not that somewhere he was present as a svāṁśa.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**The Lord, performer of the inconceivable, constantly remained in each of his queens’ palaces, which were unequaled and unexcelled by any other residence. There, although fully satisfied within himself, he enjoyed with his pleasing wives, and like an ordinary husband he carried out his household duties.**

**Комментарий:**

His full pastimes with the queens are described. He stayed continually in their houses completely (ava) having come close to even their family members and enjoyed with them (ramābhiḥ), with smiles, glances and embraces. The houses were superior even to those of Vaikuṇṭha (nirasta-sāmyātiśayeṣu). Kṛṣṇa performed inconceivable actions of being simultaneously in the presence of all of them with one body (atarkya-kṛt). His heart was soft with his own desires for them (nija-kāma-saṁplutaḥ). The result was enjoying pastimes with them. He performed household dharmas such as agnihotra sacrifices. Thus his actions were mixed with sweetness like a kṣatriya king, etc. In the spiritual sky there are no houses like this. There there is one Ramā and her husband and their activities are filled with great powers only. Thus this indicates the excellence of Dvārakā compared to Vaikuṇṭha. The following should be understood. The eight forms of the hlādinīśakti combined with the essence of the saṁvit-śakti starting with Candrāvalī, who were previously described and their avatāras, the other gopīs, numbering in the millions, manifested in Gokula. But in Dvārakā, the eight gopīs manifested as the eight queens beginning with Rukmiṇī. Each of the eight had two forms and thus sixteen known as Lambinī, etc., were śaktis of Kṛṣṇa, forms of vidyā who are described in the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa of Skanda Purāṇa. For variety in their lord’s service each of the sixteen becomes a thousand. Thus they are all forms of Ramā. In this way, just as the Lord of Dvārakā is a pūrṇa (full) manifestation of Svayaṁ bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Gokula, so the queens in Dvārakā are a pūrṇa (full) manifestation of the gopīs. The Kārttikamāhātmya section of the Padma Purāṇa says: Those who were the daughters of cowherds in their early youth became royal princesses in their adolescence.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Thus those women obtained as their husband the husband of the goddess of fortune, although even great devatās like Brahmā do not know how to approach him. With ever-increasing pleasure they experienced loving attraction for him, exchanged smiling glances with him and reciprocated with him in ever-fresh intimacy, replete with joking and feminine shyness.**

**Комментарий:**

Those with crooked intelligence should not worry that the Lord is contaminated with māyā by associating with many women. The combination of the Lord full of consciousness and bliss with his śaktis full of sac-cid-ānanda is faultless like the combination of the moon with its rays. These women independently attained as their husband Kṛṣṇa, the husband of Rukmiṇī, the aṁśī of all Ramās. The women, Ramās, the svāṁśas of Rukmiṇī, increasing constantly their anurāga for him in bliss, enjoyed smiling glances, fresh association, conversations with him and shyness.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Although the Supreme Lord’s queens each had hundreds of maidservants, they chose to personally serve the Lord by approaching him humbly, offering him a seat, sprinkling handfuls of flowers and jewels, bathing and massaging his feet, giving him betel nut to chew, fanning him, anointing him with fragrant sandalwood paste, adorning him with flower garlands, dressing his hair, arranging his bed, bathing him, and presenting him with various gifts.**

**Комментарий:**

The variegated services are described. Hearing him, they would come in front of him (udgamana) just on hearing that he has arrived. They would massage his feet (viśramaṇa). They would dress his hair (keśa-prasāra). Though they had hundreds of maidservants, they personally performed services for their husband because this gave them the highest bliss. The author of the Brahma-sūtras also says so: Ānandamaya puruṣa is the Lord, because of repetition. (Brahma-sūtra)

## Chapter 60 - Lord Kṛṣṇa Teases Queen Rukmiṇī

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bādarāyaṇi said: Once, in the company of her maidservants, Queen Rukmiṇī was personally serving her husband, the spiritual master of the universe, by fanning him as he relaxed on her bed.**

**Комментарий:**

Her lotus heart crushed by the wheel of her husband’s words, Rukminī then becomes pacified and joyful by his words in the sixtieth chapter. Rukmiṇī, along with her maidservants was performing various services to her husband who relaxed on her bed. But later, she fanned him personally. The reason she fanned him as service was that her husband was guru of the universe.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**The unborn Lord, the supreme controller, who creates, maintains and then devours this universe simply as his play, took birth among the Yadus to preserve his own laws.**

**Комментарий:**

Just as in his pastimes of creating, maintaining and destroying the universe, pleasure is the only purpose, similarly even in disturbing Rukmiṇī’s rasa of service in prema, pleasure was the only purpose and nothing else. Śukadeva speaks this verse in order to convey this. For preserving the limits of dharma that he made, though unborn, the Lord appeared among the Yadus through birth and other pastimes.

### Text 3-6

**Перевод:**

**Rukmiṇī’s quarters were extremely beautiful, boasting a canopy hung with brilliant strings of pearls, as well as effulgent jewels serving as lamps. Garlands of jasmine and incense hung here and there, attracting swarms of humming bees, and the spotless rays of the moon shone through the holes of the lattice windows. As aguru incense drifted out of the window holes, my dear King, the breeze wafting the scent of the pārijāta grove carried the mood of a garden into the room. There the queen served her husband, the Supreme Lord of all the worlds, as he reclined upon an opulent pillow on her bed, which was as soft and white as the foam of milk.**

**Комментарий:**

In three verses, her place is described as being complete with ingredients for serving in prema. This is described in three verses. The room was bright with a canopy hung with strings of glistening pearls. All the words ending in instrumental case are connected with the word virājite (shining). Jasmine garlands were tied to the doors as reverence. Dhūpaiḥ indicates ordinary incense but in the next verse the incense is that of aguru. Evening pastimes are suggested with the red rays of the sun coming through the lattice holes. By the will of the Lord, the one pārijāta plant existed in all the queens’ gardens. There Rukmiṇī attentively served Kṛṣṇa, who was lying on the best of beds (kaśipūttame).

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**From her maidservant’s hand Rukmiṇī devī took a yak-hair fan with a jeweled handle, and then she began to worship her master by fanning him.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse describes how she served him.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Her hand adorned with rings, bangles and the cāmara fan, Rukmiṇī looked resplendent standing near Kṛṣṇa. Her jeweled ankle-bells tinkled, and her necklace glittered, reddened by the kuṁkuma from her breasts, which were covered by the end of her sāri. On her hips she wore a priceless belt.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukminī shone next to her husband with her jeweled anklets. Her anklets jingled as her limbs quivered by moving the long fan. She had rings and bangles on her hands. She shone with a priceless belt and the effulgence of a necklace reddened by kuṅkuma from her two breasts covered by her bodice and the edge of her red cloth.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**As he contemplated her, the actual goddess of fortune, who desires only him, Kṛṣṇa smiled. The Lord assumes various forms to enact his pastimes, and he was pleased with her form as it was just suitable for her to serve him. Her charming face was adorned with curling hair, earrings, a locket on her neck, and the nectar of her bright, happy smile. The Lord then spoke to her as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord spoke to her (babhāṣa). Ā indicates lamentation since speaking to her like this was not proper. Rukmiṇī later says atadarhām: this speech is improper (SB [10.60.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/60.28)). She had an excellent form (rūpinīm), superior to the queen of Vaikuṇṭha since she was the consort of Svayaṁ Bhagavān. She had a form corresponding to that of the Lord who accepted a body for pastimes (līlayā). Lakṣmī-stotra in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa says: devatve deva-deheyaṁ mānuṣyatve ca mānuṣī viṣṇor dehānurūpāṁ vai karoty eṣātmanas tanūm When Viṣṇu appears as a devatā, Lakṣmī takes the form of a devatā, and when he appears as a human being, she takes a human-like form. Thus, she assumes a form suitable to the form that the Lord assumes. She had a sweet smile shining on a face beautiful with a niṣka ornament on her neck and with earrings and locks of hair.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear princess, you were sought after by many kings as powerful as the rulers of planets. They were all abundantly endowed with political influence, wealth, beauty, generosity and physical strength. Giving them up why did you choose me, not equal to them?**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord jokes in two verses to experience the affectionate anger of his principal beloved Rukmiṇī. You are a king’s daughter, but I am the son of someone related to royalty. Though Kṛṣṇa is himself a king’s son since he tells Kuntī in Mahābhārata that she is the daughter of Śūra, a king (Śūra is also the father of Vasudeva), still he does not say this to Rukmiṇī for devastating her, and since Āhuka (Ugrasena) was the chief of all kings of the Yadus. Thus for what reason did you, the daughter of a king, choose me, a person related to kings? Though having a modifier, the plurality of asmad (asmān) is poetic license. Nor can you say that I was chosen by you out of no other option, for you were desired by kings. And not that they were without power, being like lokapalas. They had extreme power (mahānubhāvaiḥ) or beauty and learning (śrīmadbhiḥ).

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Since your brother and father offered you to them, why did you reject the King of Cedi and all those other suitors, who stood before you, maddened by Cupid? Why, instead, did you choose me, though I am not at all your equal?**

**Комментарий:**

They were not far away then. They personally came (prāptān). They were not rough with you. They entreated you (arthinaḥ). They were infatuated with you (smara-durmadān). This is a great joke. There was no disagreement of relatives in giving you to them. Why did you choose me, who cannot compare with them or you?

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Terrified of these kings, O lovely-browed one, I took shelter in the ocean. I have become enemies of powerful men, and I practically abandoned the royal throne.**

**Комментарий:**

He explains why he is not their equal. Even in this fearful state, I do not have particle of friendship with others. I have become enemies of powerful men. Only a few friends like Arjuna remain (prāyaḥ). I gave the throne to Ugrasena after killing Kaṁsa and after being enthroned as the king, as described in Hari-vaṁśa.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**O fine-browed lady, women are usually destined to suffer when they stay with men whose behavior is uncertain and who pursue a path not approved by society.**

**Комментарий:**

It is not proper for any woman to serve me.
