My unseen beneficiary conduct (vartma) is not easy to understand (aspaṣṭa) due to being perceived as both atheistic and theistic due to touching others’ wives and also following marriage norms, and due to being perceived as engaged in pravṛtti and nivṛtti due to hunting and criticizing hunting. Similarly I have no visible beneficiary conduct regarding wife and children (aloka-patham) due to disfiguring the wife’s brother in front of her and due to not protecting a newborn son. Women who have taken shelter of the feet of men like me generally suffer. Due to the word prāyas (generally) the idea is that some who do not suffer it is their good quality.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**I have no material possessions, and I am dear to those who similarly have nothing. Therefore, O slender one, the wealthy hardly ever worship me.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover wealthy people do not worship me. We are niṣkiñcana since we have no attachment to enjoying. Niṣkiñcana persons are dear to me or I am dear to them. Therefore, the wealthy, except for the wealthy who are internally detached (prāyeṇa), do not worship me. Since you have wealth as a king’s daughter and since it is not possible for you to renounce, you should not serve me.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Marriage and friendship are proper between two people who are equal in terms of their wealth, birth, influence, physical appearance and capacity for good progeny, but never between a superior and an inferior.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking you as my wife is against the nīti scriptures. Since you are king’s daughter you have plenty of wealth. I do not have ancestral wealth since I am the son of Vasudeva who had no money. The only wealth I have is what little I have been able to earn on my own. You are born in a good family. I have a low family, being a Yādava. You have jurisdiction over many towns in the Vidarbha state, whereas I have only Dvārakā in the ānarta state. Ākṛti means physical appearance. You are fair complexioned like lightning and I am very black. Aiśvaryākṛti means ākṛti along with aiśvarya. It is a śāka-pārthivādi compound . Your prosperity (bhava) is always auspicious, whereas mine is uncertain because I have many enemies. We are not well matched as a couple. Only matching couples should marry.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**O Vaidarbhī, not being farsighted, you didn’t realize this, and therefore you chose me as your husband, even though I have no good qualities and, being a fool, am glorified only by people desiring money.**

**Комментарий:**

He summarizes. Not carefully considering, not seeing the future, you chose me. “But I chose you from hearing of all your good qualities.” I am praised by people greedy for money (bhikṣubhiḥ) from you.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Now you should definitely accept a husband suitable to yourself, a first-class man of the royal order who can help you achieve everything you want, both in this life and the next.**

**Комментарий:**

“What are you saying?” I speak only beneficial words. You should accept the best kṣatriya suitable as a husband for yourself by which you will attain the highest desires (āśiṣaḥ satyāḥ).

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Kings like Śiśupāla, Śālva, Jarāsandha and Dantavakra all hate me, O beautiful-thighed one, and so does your elder brother Rukmī.**

**Комментарий:**

Expecting the question, “Why then did you bring me here?” he speaks. Mama in the genitive is for accusative (mām).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**It was to dispel the arrogance of these kings that I carried you away, my good woman, for they were blinded by the intoxication of power. My purpose was to curb the strength of the wicked.**

**Комментарий:**

I took you to destroy the pride of the kings, not for marriage.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**We care nothing for wives, children and wealth. Always satisfied within ourselves, we do not work for body and home, but remain detached like Paramātmā.**

**Комментарий:**

You shouldn’t worry that I will be unhappy if you accept another man. I am definitely (nūnaṁ) indifferent, not attached to anything. I do not desire wife, children or wealth. Indifferent to body and house, I am devoid of action, being a witness, like the light of a lamp. “Then how can there be increase of happiness?” I am full with happiness of my svarūpa. Taking the role of antaryāmī of the jīva, showing detachment to body, etc., which follow a jīva, he indicates that to Rukmiṇī. From the position of bhagavān however he does not act in this way since it was said: The Lord, performer of the inconceivable, constantly remained in each of his queens’ palaces, which were unequaled and unexcelled by any other residence. There, although fully satisfied within himself, he enjoyed with his pleasing wives, and like an ordinary husband he carried out his household duties. (SB 10.59.43) Though the antaryāmī and bhagavān are nondifferent, by viśeṣa, they should be accepted as different. This is the intention of the Lord. Satyābhāma became very angry when I gave one pārijāta flower to Rukmiṇī. She bathed me in the nectar of her angry words. Not being pacified by falling at her feet, she was satisfied only when I offered her a pārijāta tree. But Rukminī is very profound. She did not become angry even when I gave a whole tree to Satyabhāmā. I am attached to drinking the nectar of Rukmiṇī’s angry words. Thus I play in this way.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Rukmiṇī had thought herself especially beloved by the Lord because he never left her company. By saying these things to her he vanquished her pride, and then he stopped speaking.**

**Комментарий:**

Having said this to Rukmiṇī, the Lord stopped speaking. She is described. She thought of herself as the dearest wife (vallabhām), since he never left her. This is the meaning. Though she was the chief beloved, Rukmiṇī thought of herself as the servant of the Lord because of humility arising from intense bhakti. She also thought she was excellent because of the continuous association with him. He then destroyed her pride. He destroyed her pride due to carrying heap of dāsya by which she thinks, “He makes me full of good fortune by his good qualities, because he is friend of the devotees, though I do not deserve to be his wife because of being his servant. I am just his servant.” There is a possibility of becoming proud by thinking that there is nothing higher to being servant of the Supreme Lord. Though the words vallabhā is in apposition to ātmā it is not masculine. The word vallabhām (beloved) would normally be masculine to agree with ātmānaṁ, but here it does not give up its gender (rather it remains in the feminine) to follow conventional meaning of being his dearest wife.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Goddess Rukmiṇī had never before heard such unpleasant words from her beloved, the Lord of universal rulers, and she became frightened. A tremor arose in her heart, and with deep thoughts she began to cry.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing those words (iti) at the time of joyful play (tadā), though she was omniscient, her knowledge was now covered by his līlāśakti. She became frightened that he is capable of doing what he spoke since he is the Lord. Since she had dakṣiṇya prema she did not become angry. She began to tremble in her heart. She began to think deeply. Will I be rejected by him? She became absorbed in meditation.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**With her tender foot, effulgent with the reddish glow of her nails, she scratched the ground, and tears darkened by her eye makeup sprinkled her kuṅkuma-reddened breasts. There she stood, face downward, her voice choked up by extreme sorrow.**

**Комментарий:**

The signs of her contemplation are described. By her tender (sujātena) foot beautifully red with her toenails, she scratched the ground. Her foot was not suitable for this. Out of great sorrow, as if eating hot sweet rice, experiencing intolerable separation from her husband, in disappointment her voice choked up since in great sorrow one cannot speak.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Rukmiṇī’s mind was overwhelmed with unhappiness, fear and grief. Her bangles slipped from her hand, and her fan fell to the ground. In her bewilderment she suddenly fainted, her hair scattering all about as her body fell to the ground like a plantain tree blown over by the wind.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmiṇī became very unhappy (su-duḥkha) from hearing these unpleasant words. She became fearful (bhaya) with trembling heart that Kṛṣṇa might leave her. Due to this fear and sadness, Rukmiṇī then became remorseful (śoka). Her intelligence thus concealed (vinaṣṭa-buddher) by her remorse, Rukmiṇī could not understand that Kṛṣṇa was only joking. Her bracelets slipped off her hands (hastāc chlathad-valayato) because her body became thin due to the pain of impending separation. Then her body fell down. The reason is viklava-dhiyaḥ, she lost consciousness. Since it was said previously that her intelligence became concealed, here viklava-dhiyaḥ should mean that she lost consciousness. Then she was bewildered (muhyan). This was the ninth state. Her falling is pralaya (a sāttvika-bhāva), These sāttvika-bhāvas arose.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that his beloved was so bound to him in love that she could not understand the full meaning of his teasing, merciful Kṛṣṇa felt compassion for her.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the indescribable bondage of prema of his beloved, who did not understand that this was joke of the king of rasikas, who was not able to deliberate because of lack of vāmya prema, he immediately gave up his bold joking and felt compassion, because he should give mercy to the devotee.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**The Lord quickly got down from the bed. Manifesting four arms, he picked her up, gathered her hair and caressed her face with his lotus hand.**

**Комментарий:**

His mercy is shown. Lifting her up from the ground, placing her in his lap, he manifested four arms to lift her, embraced her, wiped her face and retied her hair simultaneously. He bound her hair (samuhya).

### Text 27-28

**Перевод:**

**Wiping her tear-filled eyes and her breasts, which were stained by tears of grief, the Supreme Lord, the goal of his devotees, embraced his chaste wife, who desired nothing but him, O King. Expert in the art of pacification, Kṛṣṇa tenderly consoled pitiable Rukmiṇī, whose mind was bewildered by his proud joking and who did not deserve to suffer so.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa wiped Rukmiṇī’s tear-filled eyes (aśru-kale) and her breasts, which were stained with tears of sorrow (śucā). He embraced her, who was devoted only to him (ananya-viṣayām). He consoled her, beautiful in that state (satīm), since he pacifies any devotee (satām gatiḥ), what to speak of her. She did not deserve such joking (atadarhāṁ) because she had a soft nature. The reason for consoling her is that she was miserable (kṛpanām) on thinking he would leave her. The reason for that was that her mind was bewildered by his proud joking. “How could he so quickly pacify her?” Kṛṣṇa was expert at pacification. His expertise was shown in wiping away her tears. etc.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O Vaidarbhī, do not be displeased with me. I know that you are fully devoted to me. I only spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say.**

**Комментарий:**

O Rukmiṇī! Do not be displeased with me (mā). In this sportive joking which is a good quality since it was a special display of play in prema, do not find fault with me of hurting your heart. I Know that you are devoted to me. “Then why do you hurt my heart?” I played this joke with a desire to hear your words while curling your lips. But actually, O woman with auspicious limbs (aṅgane)!

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**I also wanted to see your face with lips trembling in loving anger, the reddish corners of your eyes throwing sidelong glances and the line of your beautiful eyebrows knit in a frown.**

**Комментарий:**

He gives other reasons for joking with Rukmiṇī. I wanted to see your face with lips trembling (sphurita) with loving anger (prema-saṁrambha), with attractive eyebrows furrowed, and reddish eyes throwing angry side-long glances. This was the way to see her face like this, since his desire was powerless due to her dakṣiṇa prema.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The greatest pleasure worldly householders can enjoy at home is to spend time joking with their beloved wives, my dear timid and temperamental one.**

**Комментарий:**

“I am not attracted to you when you fan me in prema with your lotus-face smiling in joy. I am attracted to you when your face is discolored with rough words from anger.” What is this nature of the Lord. He answers.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, Queen Vaidarbhī was fully pacified by the Lord and understood that his words had been spoken in jest. Thus she gave up her fear that her beloved would reject her.**

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Smiling bashfully as she cast charming, affectionate glances upon the face of the Lord, the best of males, Rukmiṇī spoke the following, O descendant of Bharata.**

**Комментарий:**

She spoke to best of men exhibiting the height of beauty (bhagavat) while looking at his face. She looked at him with glances moist with prema, attractive with smiles along with shyness. She was shy because she had not known it was a joke. She smiled because now she knew.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Rukmiṇī said: Actually, what you have said is true, O lotuseyed one. I am indeed unsuitable for the almighty Lord. What comparison is there between that Supreme Lord, who is master of the three primal deities and who delights in his own glory, and myself, a woman of mundane qualities whose feet are grasped by fools?**

**Комментарий:**

Taking the same statements by which Kṛṣṇa previously denigrated himself and praised her, Rukmiṇī, having understood their respective intentions now explains them by giving an opposite meaning to those arguments to satisfy Kṛṣṇa. First Rukmiṇī responds that the inequality mentioned by Kṛṣṇa till kasmān no vavṛṣe ’samān, “Why did you select us, who are not equal to you? Such a marriage is not proper,” (verse 11) is not well said. O master! The intention with which you made the statement, “I am not equal to you,” is not like that. She explains. You are the master of the three vibhūtis existing in the eternal world (tryadhīśaḥ), absorbed in your greatness of omniscience, omnipotence, etc. Where do you exist? But you always exist as my shelter since all these are superior pastimes. My svarūpa (prakṛtiḥ) is qualities such as omniscience of you who are superior. Thus my feet are accepted by those who know (jña) your (a=viṣṇu) svarūpa. Where do I exist? I always exist under your shelter. They worship me as nondifferent from you. I am always surrendered to you. Since she is in a state of equality, words indicating inequality are useless. However, the words may be explained in terms of the three guṇas. “I am made of the three guṇas.” Since Lakṣmī is actually different from that. That form is different, being destructible. (Skanda Purāṇa)

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Yes, my Lord Urukrama, you lay down within the ocean as if afraid of the material modes, and thus in pure consciousness you appear within the heart as the Supersoul. You are always battling against the foolish material senses, and even your servants reject the privilege of royal dominion, which leads to the blindness of ignorance.**

**Комментарий:**

In Text 12 Kṛṣṇa said, rājabhyo bibhyataḥ su-bhru samudraṁ śaraṇaṁ gatān: “Out of fear of the kings, we took shelter in the ocean.” This is definitely true only according to the manner I say, and not according to what you intended. She speaks this verse. What you say is actually the fact (satyam). O Kṛṣṇa, endowed with great śakti (urukrama)! She indicates that he does not have fear. The Visva-kośa dictionary says the word krama can mean śakti. Due to the etymology that the sense objects such as sound (guṇa) shine (root=raj), guṇa means kings. You seem to have the same fear of kings that your devotees have since you are controlled by them. Thus as if out of that fear you lie down in the lotus hearts of the devotees, deep like the ocean. Thus in samudraṁ śaraṇaṁ gatān (verse 12), śaraṇaṁ means home since śaraṇa can mean home or protector. You are famous for taking shelter of your devotee’s lotus heart. nāpaiṣi nātha hṛdayāmburuhāt sva-puṁsām You are never separated from the lotus of their hearts. (SB [3.9.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.5)) You are pure awareness (upalambhana-mātra), self-manifesting, and a form of consciousness (ātmā). Balavadbhiḥ kṛta-dveṣān: I created enmity with the strong. (verse 12) You make war with the senses, directed to sense objects, of those who meditate on you. You take care so that the devotees are turned towards you since you have said: teṣām evānukampārtham aham ajñāna-jaṁ tamaḥ nāśayāmy ātma-bhāva-stho jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā To show them special mercy, I, dwelling in their hearts, destroy with the shining lamp of knowledge the darkness born of ignorance. (BG [10.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.11)) In the same verse Kṛṣṇa stated, tyakta-nṛpāsanān: we renounced the royal throne. Even those serving you reject the position of being kings, what to speak of you, since such positions are filled with ignorance because of lack of discrimination. Here due to the usage of tvat-sevakair, the previous lines (of this verse) have also been explained in relation with devotees. Since the Supreme Lord is never fearful, is free from opposition in battle and is free from desire for position as king, it is harmonious for those lines to be related to devotees.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Even the path of the sages who relish the honey of your lotus feet, which is covered by karmas is unclear. It is certainly incomprehensible for human beings who behave like animals. And just as your activities are transcendental, O all-powerful Lord, so too are those of your followers.**

**Комментарий:**

What was spoken by aspaṣṭa-vartmanāṁ (verse 13) is also similar. Even the path of the sages which is covered by karmas for the sake of the welfare of the world is unclear. Thus it is difficult to be understood (duvibhāvyaṁ) by men who are like animals, but is understood by persons with pure intelligence. Certainly (nanu), your path is unclear to a greater degree. It is true that you do not follow the customary path (aloka-patham). Since the endeavors even of those who follow you are seen as transcendental, your activities are also transcendental. O powerful lord! Āsthitāḥ padavīṁ: women are usually destined to suffer when they stay with men whose behavior is uncertain. This will be answered in verse 38.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**You possess nothing because there is nothing beyond you. Even the great enjoyers of tribute—Brahmā and other demigods— pay tribute to you. Those who are blinded by their wealth and absorbed in gratifying their senses do not recognize you in the form of death. But to the gods, the enjoyers of tribute, you are the dearest, as they are to you.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmiṇī replies to Kṛṣṇa’s statement in Text 14: niṣkiñcanā vayaṁ śaśvan, “We have no material possessions.” Certainly (nanu) there is nothing greater than you (niṣkiñcana). All wealth is dependent on you. Sarva-kāmaḥ sarva-rasaḥ: He has all enjoyable objects. He has spiritual fragrance and taste. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) Thus, the meaning of niṣkiñcana as poor is impossible to apply to you. Even the great enjoyers of tribute—Brahmā and other demigods—pay tribute to you. She replies to tasmāt prāyeṇa na hy āḍhyā māṁ bhajanti: the wealthy hardly ever worship me. (verse 14) Those who have lost all knowledge of tattva (andhā) by pride in their wealth and thus who satisfy their prāṇas (asutṛpaḥ), do not recognize you in the form of their death. My dear Lord, all living entities within this material world are mad after planning for things, and they are always busy with a desire to do this or that. This is due to uncontrollable greed. (SB [4.24.66](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.66)) How could they worship you? She then explains the phrase niṣkiñcana-jana-priyāḥ: I am dear to the niṣkiñcanas. (verse 14) Taking niṣkiñcana-jana-priyāḥ as a tat-puruṣa compound: you alone are dear to the devatās such as Brahmā (bali-bhujām) though they have material desires, what to speak of those having no desires, the niṣkiñcanas, who desire only you. Taking niṣkiñcana-jana-priyāḥ as a bahu-vrīhi compound: even the devatās with material desires are dear to you, what to speak of the devotees with no material desires at all. The essential nature of niṣkiñcanas is stated by the followers of Purāṇas: Those who do not desire to engage in anything else, acquire anything else or inquire into anything else other than worship of the Lord are called niṣkiñcana by the wise.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**You are the embodiment of all human goals and are yourself the final aim of life. Desiring to attain you, O all-powerful Lord, intelligent persons abandon everything else. It is they who are worthy of your association, not men and women absorbed in the pleasure and grief resulting from their mutual lust.**

**Комментарий:**

Whatever was stated in: yayor eva samaṁ vittaṁ janmaiśvaryākṛtir bhavaḥ tayor vivāho maitrī ca nottamādhamayoḥ kvacit, “Marriage and friendship are proper between two people who are equal in terms of their wealth, birth, influence, physical appearance and capacity for good progeny, but never between a superior and an inferior,” (verse 15) — it is certain in those other than you, but it is not possible in you. All the four puruṣārthas, dharma, etc. (samasta), are made of you: you bestow them to others. You are the very result, the svarūpa of full bliss. Raso vai saḥ ānando brahmeti vyajānāt: the Lord is rasa. One should know Brahman as bliss. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) Desiring you, the end result, the wise give up everything and become niṣkiñcana. Relationship, in the form of served and servant, of these persons, (samājaḥ) who have given up everything with a desire for you, with you who are affectionate to the niṣkiñcanas, alone is proper since they are similar to you by indifference to wealth, etc. That relationship, like the moon and moonlight, is appropriate between you and me, etc. But not between men and women attached to contaminated sense objects and consequently who are overcome with happiness and suffering caused by amorous pleasure.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Knowing that great sages who have renounced the sannyāsī’s daṇḍa proclaim your glories, that you are the Supreme Soul of all the worlds, and that you are so gracious that you give away even your own self, I chose you as my husband, rejecting Brahmā and the rulers of heaven, whose aspirations are all frustrated by the force of time, which is born from your eyebrows. What interest, then, could I have in any other suitors?**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmiṇī answers Kṛṣṇa’s statement: bhikṣubhiḥ ślāghitā mudhā, “I, a fool, am praised only by beggars,” (verse 16) on remembering the incident of churning the ocean of milk. Your prowess (anubhāvaḥ) is praised by sages, who have given up the staff (nyāsta-daṇḍa) and are thus called beggars (bhikṣu in verse 16). Those prowess are the highest spiritual attainment. By that she suggests that Kṛṣṇa’s words are only useless. You are the form of knowledge and bliss (ātmā) and give yourself (ātma-da) to the devotees living in the universe. Dadāty ātmānam apy ajaḥ: the Lord gives even himself. (SB [11.2.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.31)) Knowing this, I choose you. Giving up Brahmā, Śiva and others whose desires are destroyed by the force of time, which is pushed by your eyebrow, what to speak of others, absorbed in karmas of charity, etc. You said that I lacked foresight. (tvayādīrgha-samīkṣayā, verse16) That was spoken without considering my knowledge which has foresight.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, as a lion drives away lesser animals to claim his proper tribute, you drove off the assembled kings with the resounding twang of your Śārṅga bow and then claimed me, your fair share. Thus it is sheer foolishness, my dear Gadāgraja, for you to say you took shelter in the ocean out of fear of those kings.**

**Комментарий:**

Though she suggested that he has not recognized her knowledge and foresight, due to arousal of anger even by direct expression she speaks it in two verses. O brother of Gada! O Lord! As a lion drives away lesser animals to claim its proper tribute, you drove off the assembled kings with the resounding twang of your Śārṅga bow and claimed me, your fair share. Your words saying that you took shelter of the ocean out of fear of them are just foolish, full of deep ignorance.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Wanting your association, the best of kings—Aṅga, Vainya, Jāyanta, Nāhuṣa, Gaya and others—abandoned their absolute sovereignty and entered the forest. How could those kings, fixed at your feet suffer frustration in this world, O lotus-eyed one?**

**Комментарий:**

What was spoken by you by āsthitāḥ padavīṁ subhru! prāyaḥ sīdanti yoṣitaḥ: “O fine-browed lady, women are usually destined to suffer when they stay with such men” (verse 13) is also foolish. Aṅga who was the father of Vena (vainya), Bharata (jāyanta), Yayāti (nāhuṣa), Gaya and others, the best of kings, emperors, desiring you, giving up their kingdoms, on which they had absolute monarchy, entered the forest. How could those kings, fixed on your path (padavīm), suffer? Rather they were fixed in you, the highest bliss. Like them, we, princesses, are most intelligent. Your words are foolish. The desire of the Lord to see the beauty of her angry face and hear her angry words was thus fulfilled. tvad-vacaḥ śrotu-kāmena kṣvelyācaritam aṅgane I only spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say. (SB [10.60.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/60.29))

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**The aroma of your lotus feet, which is glorified by great saints, awards people liberation and is the abode of Lakṣmī. What woman would disregard that fragrance and take shelter of any other man after savoring that aroma, since you are the abode of unlimited qualities? The fools who concentrate on material wealth are filled with great fear.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmiṇī replies to Kṛṣṇa’s statement, “You should choose a husband suitable to yourself, who is the best of the royal order” (ātmano’nurūpaṁ bhajasva ksatriya-rṣabham, verse 17). What intelligent woman (kā), who has smelled the fragrance of your lotus feet or heard your glories praised by sages (sanmukharitam), despising them, would accept (śrayeta) anyone but you? No one would. The fragrance is described. It is praised by the devotees, like bees and cuts saṁsāra of all beings by hearing about that fragrance. It is the abode of all wealth (lakṣmy-ālayam). The fragrance gives wealth by hearing the glories of that fragrance. The others are described. They are mortal and humans, completely (ā) filled with fear at all times (sadā), swallowed by the snake of time. Discriminating woman (artha-vivikta-dṛṣtiḥ) would take shelter of no one else. But an inconsiderate blind woman would take shelter of someone other than you. What was stated as the Lord being devoid of good qualities (verse 16) is countered here. You are an ocean of qualities (guṇālayasya). In verse 16, guṇas indicated sattva, etc. (not good qualities).

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Because you are suitable for me, I have chosen you, the master and Supreme Soul of all the worlds, who fulfill our desires in this life and the next. May your feet, which give freedom from illusion by approaching their worshiper, give shelter to me, who have been wandering from one material situation to another.**

**Комментарий:**

I have chosen you, suitable for me, Lakṣmī. You are the all-pervading Viṣṇu (ātmānam). May your lotus feet which fulfill desires in this life (atra) and the next (paratra), be my shelter (araṇam). I have been following you here and there, manifesting a corresponding form when you manifest in this world (sṛtibhiḥ). devatve deva-deheyam mānuṣatve ca mānuṣi When Kṛṣṇa appears as a devatā, his consort appears as a devī and when he appears as a human she appears as a human also. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) Instead of sṛtibhiḥ, sometimes śrutibhiḥ is seen. Then the meaning is “I begin to worry on hearing about how you gave up Sītā in your other incarnation or how you gave up the gopīs, that the same will be heard regarding me.” Your feet, destroying (apavarga) all illusions (anṛtasya), personally go to the person who worships them. She states one-pointed surrender to his lotus feet. It is suggested that without that she does not speak of approaching his lotus face.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**O infallible Kṛṣṇa, let each of the kings you named become the husband of a woman whose ears have never heard your glories, which are sung in the assemblies of Śiva and Brahmā. After all, in the households of such women, these kings live like asses, oxen, dogs, cats and slaves.**

**Комментарий:**

She speaks gestures with her finger in hatred and cursing the kings described by the Lord in verse 16 as having good qualities. O Acyuta! Let the kings you mentioned become husbands of unfortunate women, whose ears have not heard your pastimes. The kings are described. In the houses of such women they are like asses, kicked by their feet, like oxen, bearing their wives’ heavy loads, like dogs who behave inimically toward outsiders in order to protect their home and like cats who eat left-overs of their wives, and are like slaves since they serve their wives.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**A woman who fails to relish the fragrance of the honey of your lotus feet becomes totally befooled, and thus she accepts as her husband or lover a living corpse covered with skin, whiskers, nails, head-hair and body-hair and filled with flesh, bones, blood, parasites, feces, mucus, bile and air.**

**Комментарий:**

The woman who worships anyone except you as her husband enjoys with a corpse. The body is externally covered by skin, etc., otherwise it would be covered by lakhs of flies attracted by the bad smell. Internally the body is composed of flesh, etc. The woman who thinks, “My husband is very attractive” is a fool and worships a living corpse made of flesh, etc., and covered by skin, etc. The foolishness is described. She does not smell the sweetness of the lotus feet of you, sac-cid-ānanda and full of mercy, which spreads everywhere by the wind of spiritual literary works. You, my master, the Supreme Lord, with sac-cid-ānanda form, should be served by wives with prema.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed one, though you are satisfied within yourself and thus rarely turn your attention toward me, please bless me with steady love for your feet. It is when you assume a predominance of passion in order to manifest attraction for me, you glance upon me, showing me what is indeed your greatest mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

Here Rukmiṇī replies to Kṛṣṇa’s statement regarding his indifference to family life, “Always satisfied within ourselves, we care nothing for wives, children and wealth.” (verse 20) Though you are indifferent to me, still may I have attraction to your lotus feet. You have attraction to me and yourself (mayi ātmān ratasya). You have attraction for me since you said to my messenger, tathāham api tac-citto nidrāṁ ca na labhe niśi, “I am also thinking about her so much that I cannot sleep at night.” (SB [10.53.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/53.2)). You have equal vision toward both (anatirikta-dṛṣteḥ). Your statement of indifference udāsīnā vayaṁ (verse 20) is thus meaningless. When for increasing attraction to me you accept an excess of passion, you glance at me. Making you repentful when you are criticized by that Satyabhāma, “Why did Vasudeva not have a daughter instead of you?” and are expelled from the house, you sometimes come to my house and glance at me. Then I feel your supreme mercy, I feel successful. I cannot give you pain like Satyabhāmā.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**Actually, I don’t consider your words false, Madhūsudana. Quite often an unmarried girl is attracted to a man, as in the case of Ambā.**

**Комментарий:**

She became pleased in refuting what all Kṛṣṇa had said. She answers in two verses his statement ātmano’nurūpaṁ bhajasva: Accept someone who is very suitable to you (verse 17). I do not consider your words indicating the nature of women to be irrelevant because (hi) in this world a young girl will be attracted to a single man in most cases (prāyas). She is chaste. Ambā, the daughter of the king of Kāśī, became attracted to Śālva.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**The mind of a promiscuous woman always hankers for new lovers, even if she is married. An intelligent man should not keep such an unchaste wife, for if he does, he will lose his good fortune both in this life and the next.**

**Комментарий:**

The mind of a promiscuous woman, even though she is married, hankers for newer and newer men. This indicates the attraction of ordinary women. But I, directly Lakṣmī, your eternal beloved, like the moon and its light, have been accepted by you, who are omniscient. Your words do not touch me. The intelligent man does not support a woman who desires many men. The person who supports this woman falls in this and the next world.

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O saintly lady, O princess, I deceived you only because I wanted to hear you speak like this. Indeed, everything you said in reply to my words is most certainly true.**

**Комментарий:**

O princess! I joked with you, desiring to hear your words with crooked lips. Everything you later explained about what I said, taking it in another way, is true.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**Whatever qualities you hope for in order to become free of material desires are eternally present in you, O angry woman, for you are my unalloyed devotee.**

**Комментарий:**

Since I am most pleased with you, what benediction should I give you? Whatever services you desire for pastimes of prema, different from kāma (akāmāya) are yours. I am controlled by your prema.

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**O sinless one, I have now seen firsthand the pure love and chaste attachment you have for your husband. Even though shaken by my words, your prema for me did not decrease.**

**Комментарий:**

Chastity to the husband has been attained to the extreme (upalabdham) since, though you were disturbed by my words, which devastated you, your intelligence fixed in me did not lessen (apakarṣitā) but remained steady. This is the quality of prema: When the relationship of love between the couple remains always without destruction even when there is causes for destroying it, it is called prema. (Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi 14.63)

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**Although I have the power to award prema, lusty couples worship me with penance and vows in order to get material enjoyment. Such persons are bewildered by my illusory energy.**

**Комментарий:**

Praising pure bhakti, he then criticizes sakāma-bhakti. Those who worship me by practice of sva-dharma (tapasā) and by performance of painful cāndrāyaṇa (vrata-caryayā), for attaining a good material husband, with desire for sexual enjoyment (kāmātmanaḥ) according to the statement of the Fifth Canto, are cheated by my māyā. Therefore all women who worship you by strictly observing vows because they wish to acquire a husband to satisfy their senses are surely under illusion. They do not know that such a husband cannot actually give protection to them or their children. Nor can he protect their wealth or duration of life, for he himself is dependent on time, fruitive results and the modes of nature, which are all subordinate to you. (SB [5.18.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/18.19)) The Lord is described. I award bhakti-yoga or liberation, since liberation removes all other desires opposed to me (apavargeśam).

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**O supreme reservoir of love, unfortunate are persons who even after obtaining me, the Lord of both liberation and material riches, hanker only for material treasures. These worldly gains can be found even in hell. Since such persons are obsessed with sense gratification, hell is a fitting place for them.**

**Комментарий:**

He explains the bewilderment by māyā. Taking shelter of me, who gives wealth along with liberation as mentioned, people desire wealth, material vibhūtis which cause material happiness because I am the giver of that enjoyment (patim). These people who desire that are most unfortunate. This enjoyment exists even in birth as a Rākṣasa, etc. (niraye). That hellish birth is suitable for living beings since they are fixed in material sense objects (mātrātmakatvāt). It is suitable since it produces degraded material happiness of sexual enjoyment. Worshipping me for that happiness is extremely foolish. O Rukminī, who are honorable (mānini)!

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**Fortunately, O mistress of the house, you have always rendered me faithful devotional service, which liberates one from material existence. This service is very difficult for the envious to perform, especially for a woman whose intentions are wicked, who lives only to gratify her bodily demands, and who indulges in duplicity.**

**Комментарий:**

Not satisfied with praising pure bhakti, he again praises Rukmiṇī, who possess that pure bhakti. O queen of the house! The service in prema rendered by you to me always is auspicious. That service destroys saṁsāra for the hearer. “Then hearing about it, everyone should become liberated.” That is impossible for the rascals since they cannot hear because of their low nature. “Then women, of same nature should become liberated.” Service of your nature is even more difficult for women, having evil desires (durāśiṣaḥ), who are absorbed in sensual enjoyment (asuṁbhārāyāḥ), and skilfull at cheating (nikṛtiṁ juṣaḥ). Qualification for your service is rare.

### Text 55

**Перевод:**

**In all my palaces I can find no other wife as loving as you, O most respectful one. When you were to be married, you disregarded all the kings who had assembled to seek your hand, and simply because you had heard authentic accounts concerning me, you sent a brāhmaṇa to me with your confidential message.**

**Комментарий:**

Though filled with prema, among all my wives, you are the best because of performing difficult actions for me. I do not see a wife like you endowed with prema in all my houses. By you a secret brāhmaṇa messenger (raho-vaho) named Sunanda was sent to me, about whom you had heard true facts. Raho means very secret according to Viśva. O Rukmiṇī, in whose heart anger has arisen (mānini)! You alone are like that, no one else is.

### Text 56

**Перевод:**

**When your brother, who had been defeated in battle and then disfigured, was later killed during a gambling match on Aniruddha’s wedding day, you felt unbearable grief, yet out of fear of losing me you spoke not a word. By this silence you have conquered me.**

**Комментарий:**

Because he was your brother, you had affection for him. His disfigurement was thus intolerable for you. He was defeated in battle. Since he was your brother, I should not have defeated him. And he should not have been killed on Aniruddha’s wedding day, in the gambling match. It was not proper to kill him then. Though you saw all that you did not express any grief out of fear that I would be separated from you. You worried, “My husband should never be insulted by me.” You experienced grief in which there was no strength to tolerate (asahaḥ). The grief was weak because it arose from consideration of public only. The grief arose (uttham) along with (sam) happiness because of the killing of the inimical brother. I am conquered by this. I and my people are controlled by you. In this way it is known that this joking took place after the wedding of Aniruddha.

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**When you sent the messenger with your most confidential plan and yet I delayed going to you, you began to see the whole world as void and wanted to quit your body, which could never have been given to anyone but me. May this greatness of yours remain with you always; I can do nothing to reciprocate except joyfully thank you for your devotion.**

**Комментарий:**

Remembering again the excellence of her pūrva-rāga he speaks. A Text 58\] Lord Kṛṣṇa Teases Queen Rukmiṇī 583 messenger was sent by you to attain me. When I was slightly late, because I was absorbed in hospitality to him and in hearing your message, considering the world empty though filled with father and others, you wanted to give up your most excellent body, which is unsuitable to be given to anyone except me (ananya-yogyam) in the fire. If I cannot obtain your mercy, I shall simply give up my vital force, which will have become weak from the severe penances I will perform. Then, after hundreds of lifetimes of endeavor, I may obtain your mercy. (SB 10.52.43) May that action remain in you alone. I cannot repay it. I can only praise it (pratinandayāmaḥ).

### Text 58

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: And so the self-satisfied Supreme Lord, son of Devakī, enjoyed with the goddess of fortune, engaging her in lovers’ talks, which resembled the ways of human society.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord who is ātmārāma himself (svarataḥ), since his consorts are nondifferent from him, thus enjoyed with Rukmiṇī (ramayā) with joking conversations related to amorous love, belittling (viḍambayan) the human world, which could never be compared to him because he acted like a human but with the greatest show of powers.

### Text 59

**Перевод:**

**The almighty Lord, preceptor of all the worlds, similarly behaved like a conventional householder in the palaces of his other queens, performing the dharmas of a family man.**

**Комментарий:**

By his one body he spread simultaneously in all houses. Thus he is vibhuḥ (all-pervading). Like other householders (gṛhavān iva) he performed (āsthitaḥ) household dharmas (gṛha-medhīyān) in all the houses because he was teaching this to the people (loka-guruḥ).

## Chapter 61 - Lord Balarāma Slays Rukmī

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Each of Kṛṣṇa’s wives gave birth to ten sons, who were not less than their father, having all his personal opulence.**

**Комментарий:**

In the sixty-first chapter, the sons and grandsons of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma’s killing Rukmī at Aniruddha’s wedding are described. Each of Kṛṣṇa’s wives manifested (ajījanan) ten sons. They had his powers and were not less than him, equal to their father (anavamān).

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Because each of these princesses saw that Acyuta never left her palace, each thought herself the Lord’s favorite. These women did not understand the full truth about him.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa, Acyuta, generally situated near them, not going from their house, each thought that she was the dearest to him. They did not know the truth: they did not know his svarūpa of being situated in all their houses at that time. Kṛtsnaṁ tad-jñānaṁ kasyāpi na bhavati: no one knows the Lord completely. (Kenopaniṣad)

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord’s wives were fully enchanted by his lovely, lotus face, his long arms and large eyes, his loving glances imbued with laughter, and his charming talks with them. But with all their charms these ladies could not conquer the mind of the allpowerful Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

It is refuted that he was a lusty man for not going out of their houses. The women, enchanted by the Lord’s lotus like face, his long eyes and arms, the taste of his loving smile, his glances and charming speech, could not completely (saṁ-aśakan) conquer his mind by their coquettish gestures. Having samañjasa-rati, they had bhāvas filled with prema and kāma. He was controlled by their bhāvas filled with prema and not by those filled with kāma. Thus the vi in vijetum and sam in samaśakan.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**The arched eyebrows of these sixteen thousand queens enchantingly expressed those ladies’ secret intentions through coyly smiling sidelong glances. Thus their eyebrows boldly sent forth conjugal messages. Yet even with these arrows of Cupid, and with other means as well, they could not agitate Lord Kṛṣṇa’s senses.**

**Комментарий:**

While describing the special gestures they displayed, what was spoken previously is stated. By their eyes (karaṇaiḥ), the arrows of Cupid, skillful in (śaunḍa) amorous mantras sent by the bent bows of their attractive (hāri) eyebrows with intentions (bhāva) shown by their glances endowed with deep smiles, they could not agitate his mind (yasya indriyam). By their bhāvas filled with prema however they could agitate his mind. Thus his prema is expressed distinctly by the phrase sa-prema (verse 3).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Thus these women obtained as their husband the master of the goddess of fortune, although even great devatās like Brahmā do not know how to approach him. With ever-increasing pleasure, they felt loving attraction for him, exchanged smiling glances with him, eagerly anticipated associating with him in ever-fresh intimacy and enjoyed in many other ways.**

**Комментарий:**

Their pastimes with him, whose mind was agitated by their bhāvas of prema are described. Attaining Kṛṣṇa, the lover of the Mahālakṣmī of Vraja (ramā-patim) or the master of all wealth, with continuously increasing joy, they enjoyed the pastimes that he and they performed, endowed with bhāvas never completely satisfying (lālasa) and ever-fresh, intimate association accompanied by smiling glances filled with anurāga. reme strī-ratna-kūṭastho bhagavān prākṛto yathā Living amongst the jewel among women, Kṛṣṇa played like an ordinary person. (SB [1.11.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/11.35)) Sa-prema-hāsa-rasa was mentioned in verse 3. Thus the Lord’s prema for them is shown. Though they associated intimately many times, it was always new, since that association is eternally everfresh.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Although the Supreme Lord’s queens each had hundreds of maidservants, they chose to personally serve the Lord by approaching him humbly, offering him a seat, worshiping him with excellent paraphernalia, bathing and massaging his feet, giving him betel to chew, fanning him, anointing him with fragrant sandalwood paste, adorning him with flower garlands, dressing his hair, arranging his bed, bathing him and presenting him with various gifts.**

**Комментарий:**

The anubhāvas of prema, services to him, are described. Pratyudgama was explained previously . Varārahṇa refers to sprinkling handfuls of flowers, and jewels.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Among Kṛṣṇa’s wives, each of whom had ten sons, I previously mentioned eight principal queens. I shall now recite for you the names of those eight queens’ sons, headed by Pradyumna.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described a related topic, now the main topic is introduced. I shall recite the sons headed by Pradyumna of the eight queens previously mentioned among all of them who had ten sons each. I do not present other sons for fear of making the work too large.

### Text 8-9

**Перевод:**

**The first son of Queen Rukmiṇī was Pradyumna, and also born of her were Cārudeṣṇa, Sudeṣṇa and the powerful Cārudeha, along with Sucāru, Cārugupta, Bhadracāru, Cārucandra, Vicāru and Cāru, the tenth. None of these sons of Kṛṣṇa was less than his father.**

**Комментарий:**

Vīryavān (strong) modifies each of them. Each of them was strong (vīryavān). Bhadracāru was younger (paraḥ) than Cārugupta.

### Text 10-12

**Перевод:**

**The ten sons of Satyabhāmā were Bhānu, Subhānu, Svarbhānu, Prabhānu, Bhānumān, Candrabhānu, Bṛhadbhānu, Atibhānu (the eighth), Śrībhānu and Pratibhānu. Sāmba, Sumitra, Purujit, Śatajit, Sahasrajit, Vijaya, Citraketu, Vasumān, Draviḍa and Kratu were the sons of Jāmbavatī. These ten, headed by Sāmba, were approved by their father.**

**Комментарий:**

First three lines go together (they list Satyabhāmā’s sons). The next three lines go together (they list Jāmbavatī’s sons).

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**The handsome sons of Nāgnajitī were Vīra, Candra, Aśvasena, Citragu, Vegavān, Vṛṣa, Āma, Śaṅku, Vasu and the Kunti.**

**Комментарий:**

Śrīmān (possessing beauty) modifies all the sons.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Śruta, Kavi, Vṛṣa, Vīra, Subāhu, Bhadra, Śānti, Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa were sons of Kālindī. Her youngest son was Somaka.**

**Комментарий:**

Among the sons of Kālindī, Bhadra was one (ekalaḥ) and Somaka was the youngest (avaraḥ).

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Lakṣmaṇā’s sons were Praghoṣa, Gātravān, Siṁha, Bala, Prabala, Ūrdhaga, Mahāśakti, Saha, Oja and Aparājita.**

**Комментарий:**

Mādrī (mādryāḥ) refers to Lakṣmaṇā.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Mitravindā’s sons were Vṛka, Harṣa, Anila, Gṛdhra, Vardhana, Unnāda, Mahāṁsa, Pāvana, Vahni and Kṣudhi.**

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Saṅgrāmajit, Bṛhatsena, Śūra, Praharaṇa, Arijit, Jaya and Subhadra were the sons of Bhadrā, together with Vāma, Āyur and Satyaka.**

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Dīptimān, Tāmratapta and others were the sons of Kṛṣṇa and Rohiṇī. Kṛṣṇa’s son Pradyumna fathered the greatly powerful Aniruddha in the womb of Rukmavatī, the daughter of Rukmī. O King, this took place while they were living in the city of Bhojakaṭa.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the sons of the eight chief queens now the sons of Rohiṇī, the chief of the other sixteen thousand one hundred queens, are described in one line. Sometimes Pradyumna used to reside in Bhojakaṭa due to being very dear to his maternal uncle. From him Aniruddha was born there.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, the sons and grandsons of Kṛṣṇa’s children numbered in the tens of millions. Sixteen thousand mothers gave rise to this dynasty.**

**Комментарий:**

One can only count the mothers of Kṛṣṇa’s offspring, but not the sons and grandsons. Kṛṣṇa’s queens numbered 16,108, though ṣoḍaśa-sahasrāṇi (sixteen thousand) is mentioned in the verse.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: How could Rukmī give his daughter to his enemy’s son? After all, Rukmī had been defeated by Kṛṣṇa in battle and was waiting for an opportunity to kill him. Please explain this to me, O learned one—how these two inimical parties became united through marriage.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaivāhikam means “for purpose of marriage.”

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Mystic yogīs can perfectly see that which has not yet happened, as well as things in the past or present, beyond the senses, remote or blocked by physical obstacles.**

**Комментарий:**

“How can we know the mind of Rukmī?” Yogīs can see the future and past and even the present, beyond perception of our senses (atīndriyaṁ)—at a great distance (viprakṛṣṭam) or with intervening obstacles like walls, etc. (vyavahitaṁ).

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: At her svayaṁ-vara ceremony, Rukmavatī herself chose Pradyumna, who was the re-embodiment of Cupid. Then, although he fought alone on a single chariot, Pradyumna defeated the assembled kings in battle and took her away.**

**Комментарий:**

The reason for choosing Pradyumna is that he who was without a body (anaṅgaḥ) by being uncontrolled in other places, was present here completely (sākṣāt) and with a body (aṅga-yutaḥ). Understanding that his daughter had chosen Pradyumna, he arranged the svayamvara to fool his own people, who could not tolerate it.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Though Rukmī always remembered his enmity toward Kṛṣṇa, who had insulted him, in order to please his sister he sanctioned his daughter’s marriage to his nephew.**

**Комментарий:**

The answer is given. Rukmī approved his daughter’s marriage to Kṛṣṇa’s son Pradyumna in order to please his sister, Rukmiṇī, who had saved his life.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**O King, Balī, the son of Kṛtavarmā, married Rukmiṇī’s young daughter, large-eyed Cārumatī.**

**Комментарий:**

Each queen had one daughter. To represent all the daughters the eldest daughter’s marriage is described.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Rukmī gave his granddaughter Rocanā to his daughter’s son, Aniruddha, despite Rukmī’s relentless feud with Kṛṣṇa. Although Rukmī considered this marriage irreligious, he wanted to please his sister, bound as he was by the ropes of affection.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukmī agreed to the marriage (yaunaṁ) of his grand-daughter to Rukmiṇī’s grandson Aniruddha, though he knew it would cause adharma. Since it contradicts normal custom. Dviṣad-annaṁ na bhoktavyaṁ dviṣantaṁ naiva bhojayet. “One should not eat an enemy’s food or feed an enemy.” And there is also the following prohibition. Asvargyaṁ lokavidviṣṭaṁ dharmam apy ācaren na tu: one should not execute dharma if it obstructs one’s elevation to heaven, or if it is condemned by human society.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**On the joyous occasion of that marriage, O King, Rukmiṇī, Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa and several of the Lord’s sons, headed by Sāmba and Pradyumna, went to the city of Bhojakaṭa.**

### Text 27-28

**Перевод:**

**After the wedding, a group of arrogant kings headed by the King of Kaliṅga told Rukmī, “You should defeat Balarāma at dice. He’s not expert at dice, O King, but still he’s quite addicted to it.” Thus advised, Rukmī challenged Balarāma and began a gambling match with him.**

**Комментарий:**

Deciding that it would be difficult to defeat Kṛṣṇa even in gambling, they told Rukmī to invite Balarāma (balam) to a game of dice.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**In that match Balarāma first accepted a wager of one hundred coins, then one thousand, then ten thousand. Rukmī won this first round, and the King of Kaliṅga laughed loudly at Balarāma, showing all his teeth. Balarāma could not tolerate this.**

**Комментарий:**

The wager was a hundred gold coins, etc. Rukmī won. Balarāma became inwardly angry (na amṛṣyat).

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Next Rukmī accepted a bet of one hundred thousand coins, which Balarāma won. But Rukmī tried to cheat, declaring, “I’m the winner!”**

**Комментарий:**

Glaham means wager.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Shaking with anger like the ocean on the full-moon day, handsome Balarāma, his naturally reddish eyes even redder in his fury, accepted a wager of one hundred million gold coins.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma accepted a wager of one hundred million gold coins (nyarbudam).

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma fairly won this wager also, but Rukmī again resorted to cheating and declared, “I have won! Let these witnesses here say what they saw.”**

**Комментарий:**

Resorting to deceit, Rukmī said, “I have won. The witnesses (prāśnikāḥ) can testify to this.”

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Just then a voice from the sky declared, “Balarāma has fairly won this wager according to the rules since he accepted the wager. Rukmī is surely lying.”**

**Комментарий:**

When the witness who are devoid of dharma were giving false testimony that Rukmī had won, a voice from the sky (nabho-vāṇī) proclaimed, “Balarāma speaks correctly and has won. Rukmī is lying.”

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Urged on by the wicked kings, Rukmī ignored the divine voice. In fact destiny itself was urging Rukmī on, and thus he ridiculed Balarāma as follows.**

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**\[Rukmī said:\] You cowherds who wander about the forests know nothing about dice. Playing with dice and sporting with arrows are only for kings, not for the likes of you.**

**Комментарий:**

But the meaning of his words as revealed by Sarasvatī devī are as follows. You protect (pālāḥ) the cows, the earth and the Vedas (go). You are the objects of meditation (gocarāḥ) in solitary forests (vane). But persons like you are not learned at gambling matches at all because persons intoxicated with wealth (rājānaḥ) enjoy committing violence to others by arrows and gambling. This is not seen in you or your devotees.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Thus insulted by Rukmī and ridiculed by the kings, Balarāma was provoked to anger. In the midst of the auspicious wedding assembly, He raised his club and struck Rukmī dead.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma killed him in the auspicious (nṛmṇa) assembly. The word nṛmṇa indicates Vedic auspiciousness.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**The king of Kaliṅga, who had laughed at Balarāma and shown his teeth, tried to run away, but the furious Lord quickly seized him on his tenth step and knocked out all his teeth.**

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Tormented by Balarāma’s club, the other kings fled in fear, their arms, thighs and heads broken and their bodies drenched in blood.**

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**When his brother-in-law Rukmī was slain, Kṛṣṇa neither applauded nor protested, O King, for he feared jeopardizing his affectionate ties with either Rukmiṇī or Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

Affection for Rukmiṇī would be disturbed by approving, and affection for Balarāma would be disturbed by disapproving. There would be crookedness, anger within their affection (sneha-bhāṅga). Worried about that he did not speak.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Then the descendants of Daśārha, headed by Balarāma, seated Aniruddha and his bride on a fine chariot and set off from Bhojakaṭa for Dvārakā. Having taken shelter of Madhusūdana, they had fulfilled all their purposes.**

**Комментарий:**

With all their desires fulfilled, they put Aniruddha on a chariot with his new bride (sūryayā) and departed for Dvārakā. Since Rukmiṇī is also included among Balarāma and others (rāmādi), she was also happy with her brother’s death.

## Chapter 62 - The Meeting of Ūṣā and Aniruddha

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: The best of the Yadus married Bāṇāsura’s daughter, Ūṣā, and as a result a great, fearsome battle occurred between Kṛṣṇa and Śiva. Please explain everything about this incident, O most powerful of mystics.**

**Комментарий:**

In the sixty-second chapter, Aniruddha meets Ūṣā and he is captured by angry Bāṇa. Parīkṣit inquires in three lines.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Bāṇa was the oldest of the hundred sons fathered by the great saint Bali Mahārāja, who gave the whole earth in charity to the Lord when he appeared as Vāmanadeva. Bāṇāsura, born from Bali’s semen, became a great devotee of Śiva. His behavior was always respectable, and he was generous, intelligent, truthful and firm in his vows. The beautiful city of Śoṇitapura was under his dominion. Because Śiva had favored him, the very devatās waited on Bāṇāsura like menial servants. Once, when Śiva was dancing, Bāṇa especially satisfied him by playing a musical accompaniment with his one thousand arms.**

**Комментарий:**

Bāṇa was skilfull at using his thousand arms for music.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**The lord and master of all created beings, the compassionate refuge of his devotees, gladdened Bāṇāsura by offering him the benediction of his choice. Bāṇa chose to have Śiva as the guardian of his city.**

**Комментарий:**

He asked Bāṇa to choose a gift (vareṇa chandayāmāsa). He chose to have Śiva as the protector of his city.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Bāṇāsura was intoxicated with his strength. One day, when Śiva was standing beside him, Bāṇāsura touched Śiva’s lotus feet with his helmet, which shone like the sun, and spoke to him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

He continually stayed with Bāṇa in his city as its protector.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**\[Bāṇāsura said:\] O Mahādeva, I bow down to you, the spiritual master and controller of the worlds. You are like the heavenly tree that fulfills the desires of those whose desires are unfulfilled.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to you who are equal to a desire tree fulfilling all desires.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**These one thousand arms you bestowed upon me have become merely a heavy burden. Besides you, I find no one in the three worlds worthy to fight.**

**Комментарий:**

From the boon given by you, I have ended up in sorrow. O Lord! Please give relief for my sorrow. I can find no one equal in the three worlds to fight except for you. Thus mercifully become my opponent. Defeating you, I will become world famous as the conqueror of all directions.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Eager to fight with the elephants who rule the directions, O primeval lord, I went forth, pulverizing mountains with my arms, which were itching for battle. But even those great elephants fled in fear.**

**Комментарий:**

Eager to fight with all my arms intensely itching for battle, I went (ayāṁ) to elephants of the directions. O primeval one (ādya)! When I crushed the mountains, the elephants, fearing the crushed mountains, fled. The intention is this. I conquered the nine directions, but not the northeast. Not conquering you, who preside over northeast, I cannot be ‘the conquerer of all-directions’. Thus my itching will be relieved by fighting with you. Become my opponent. Thus he showed great pride.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Hearing this, Śiva became angry and replied, “Your flag will be broken, fool, when you have done battle with one who is my equal. That fight will vanquish your conceit.”**

**Комментарий:**

The word kruddhaḥ (angry) implies that at first the desire to kill him arose in Śiva’s heart. Then Lord Śiva reflected, “It would be improper to kill my servant with my own hands. My master, who relieves the world of its burden, should take away his burden.” When your flag on your palace is broken, your pride will also be broken. Present tense is used since the future is near the present in this case. You will fight with someone equal to (samena) me. He states this to gratify Bāṇāsura. However, his internal meaning is “You will fight with Kṛṣṇa, due to whom I am splendorous (samena).” He spoke after he became angry.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Thus advised, unintelligent Bāṇāsura was delighted. The fool then went home, O King, to wait for that which Śiva had predicted: the destruction of his prowess.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiva, addressing me as “fool” said that there will be a battle in which my pride will be destroyed. That is meaningless. It is impossible that my pride can be destroyed. Thinking thus, he had bad judgement (kumatiḥ). Still due to his words thinking there would be someone strong who would come to fight he became joyful. He waited for the breaking of his flag as predicted by Śiva. He had bad intelligence (kudhīḥ) because of such a disastrous desire.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**In a dream Bāṇa’s daughter, the maiden Ūṣā, had an amorous encounter with the son of Pradyumna, though she had never before seen or heard of her lover.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse describes the incidents leading up to the battle predicted by Śiva. His daughter was a young girl (kanyā). Prādyumninā means “with Aniruddha.” Viṣṇu Purāṇa describes this: ūṣā bāṇasya duhitā pārvatīm śambhunā saha krīḍantīm upalakṣyoccaiḥ spṛhāṁ cakre tad-āśrayām “When Ūṣā, the daughter of Bāṇa, happened to see Pārvatī playing with her husband, Lord Śambhu, Ūṣā intensely desired to experience the same feelings.” tataḥ sakala-citta-jña gaurī tām aha bhāvinīm alam atyartha-tāpena bhartrā tvam api raṁsyase “At that time Goddess Gaurī \[Pārvatī\], who knows everyone’s heart, told the sensitive young girl, ‘Don’t be so disturbed! You will have a chance to enjoy with your own husband.’” “Hearing this, Ūṣā thought to herself, ‘But when? And who will my husband be?’ In response, Pārvatī addressed her once more.” “O princess, the man who approaches you in your dream on the twelfth lunar day of the bright fortnight of the month Vaiśākha will become your husband.”

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Losing sight of him in her dream, Ūṣā suddenly sat up in the midst of her girlfriends, crying out “Where are you, my lover?” She was greatly pained and embarrassed.**

**Комментарий:**

She was overcome with fatigue after amorous enjoyment with him. Thus she became embarrassed.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Bāṇāsura had a minister named Kumbhāṇḍa, whose daughter was Citralekhā. A companion of Ūṣā’s, she was filled with curiosity, and thus she inquired from her friend.**

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**\[Citralekhā said:\] Who are you searching for, O fine-browed one? What is this hankering you’re feeling? Until now, O princess, I haven’t seen any man take your hand in marriage.**

**Комментарий:**

Citralekhā said, “I do not see your husband (hasta-grāhaṁ) now, since you are not married.”

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**\[Ūṣā said:\] In my dream I saw a certain man who had a dark blue complexion, lotus eyes, yellow garments and mighty arms. He was the kind who touches women’s hearts.**

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**It is that lover I search for. After making me drink the honey of his lips, he has gone elsewhere, and thus he has thrown me, with my desire still unfulfilled, into the ocean of distress.**

**Комментарий:**

Ādharam means related to the lips.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Citralekhā said: I will remove your distress. If he is to be found anywhere in the three worlds, I will bring this future husband of yours who has stolen your heart. Please show me who he is by selecting the picture.**

**Комментарий:**

If the person who you seek and whose picture I draw exists in the three worlds then I will bring him to you. Point him out on seeing the pictures and say.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Saying this, Citralekhā proceeded to draw accurate pictures of various demigods, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Pannagas, Daityas, Vidyādharas, Yakṣas and humans.**

### Text 18-19

**Перевод:**

**O King, among the humans, Citralekhā drew pictures of the Vṛṣṇis, including Śūrasena, Vasudeva, Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa. When Ūṣā saw the picture of Pradyumna she became bashful, and when she saw Aniruddha’s picture she bent her head down in embarrassment. Smiling, she exclaimed, “He’s the one! It’s him!”**

**Комментарий:**

After Citralekhā told her to identify the person, on seeing Pradyumna she became bashful by her nature, thinking of him as a father-in-law. Seeing Aniruddha, she cast her head down in bashfulness because of her special love for him. “He is the person” she said in joy. You should know that such skill in drawing and recognizing another person by the drawing is not seen elsewhere (mahī-pate).

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Citralekhā, endowed with mystic powers, recognized him as Kṛṣṇa’s grandson \[Aniruddha\]. My dear King, she then traveled by the mystic skyway to Dvārakā, the city under Kṛṣṇa’s protection.**

**Комментарий:**

According to Hari-vaṁśa, she attained her powers (yoginī) from Nārada. Otherwise she could not have entered Dvārakā, protected by Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**There she found Pradyumna’s son Aniruddha sleeping upon a fine bed. With her yogic power she took him away to Śoṇitapura, where she presented her girlfriend Ūṣā with her beloved.**

**Комментарий:**

She then went to Śoṇitapura (missing verb).

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**When Ūṣā beheld him, the most beautiful of men, her face lit up with joy. She took the son of Pradyumna to her private quarters, which men were forbidden even to see, and there enjoyed with him.**

**Комментарий:**

Other men could not enter those quarters (duṣprekṣye).

### Text 23-24

**Перевод:**

**Ūṣā worshiped Aniruddha with faithful service, offering him priceless garments, along with garlands, fragrances, incense, lamps, sitting places and so on. She also offered him beverages, all types of food, and sweet words. As he thus remained hidden in the young ladies’ quarters, Aniruddha did not notice the passing of the days, for his senses were captivated by Ūṣā, whose affection for him ever increased.**

**Комментарий:**

Ūṣā honored Aniruddha with various services described in this verse.

### Text 25-26

**Перевод:**

**The guards eventually noticed unmistakable symptoms of romantic involvement in Ūṣā, who, having broken her maiden vow, was being enjoyed by the Yadu hero and showing signs of conjugal happiness. The guards went to Bāṇāsura and told him, “O King, we have detected in your daughter the kind of improper behavior that spoils the reputation of a young girl’s family.**

**Комментарий:**

The wives of the guards noticed signs of amorous union which were hard to conceal. They noticed her great joy. Hearing from their wives, the guards, frightened of Bāṇa, informed him of the girl’s actions.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**“We have been carefully watching over her, never leaving our posts, O master, so we cannot understand how this maiden, whom no man can even see, has been corrupted within the palace.”**

**Комментарий:**

They deny fault on their part. We do not know how the girl who cannot be seen by men, who cannot even flee, became spoiled. We can guess, but we cannot see him directly. Duṣpreṣyāyāḥ is another version: she has a wicked servant Citralekhā, who is the cause of this.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Very agitated to hear of his daughter’s corruption, Bāṇāsura rushed at once to the maidens’ quarters. There he saw the pride of the Yadus, Aniruddha.**

### Text 29-30

**Перевод:**

**Bāṇāsura saw before him Cupid’s own son, possessed of unrivaled beauty, with dark-blue complexion, yellow garments, lotus eyes and formidable arms. His face was adorned with effulgent earrings and hair, and also with smiling glances. As he sat opposite his most auspicious lover, playing with her at dice, there hung between his arms a garland of spring jasmines that had been smeared with kuṅkuma powder from her breasts when he had embraced her. Bāṇāsura was astonished to see all this.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses describe Aniruddha. He was playing dice with his beloved, the form of auspiciousness (abhinṛmnayā). His garland made of spring jasmines hung on his head and arms, which was smeared with kuṅkuma from her breasts from their physical association. He was sitting in front of her. The sandhi of tasyāḥ and agre is irregular. Bāṇa was surprised. “Who is this impudent person?”

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Bāṇāsura enter with many armed guards, Aniruddha raised his iron club and stood resolute, ready to strike anyone who attacked him. He resembled death personified holding his rod of punishment.**

**Комментарий:**

Mādhavaḥ means Aniruddha. He raised his club made of a special kind of iron called muru (maurvaṁ).

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**As the guards converged on him from all sides, trying to capture him, Aniruddha struck them just as the leader of a pack of boars strikes back at dogs. Hit by his blows, the guards fled her quarters, running for their lives with shattered heads, thighs and arms.**

**Комментарий:**

They desired to capture him but did not desire to kill him. They fled from Ūṣā’s quarters.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**But even as Aniruddha was striking down the army of Bāṇa, that powerful son of Bali angrily caught him with the mystic nāgapāśa ropes. When Ūṣā heard of Aniruddha’s capture, she was overwhelmed with grief and depression; her eyes filled with tears, and she wept.**

**Комментарий:**

Bāṇa was the son of Bali. Arautsīt means “she cried.” “But how could Aniruddha, the Supreme Lord, be tied up by the rascal?” It was by the will of Kṛṣṇa, the aṁśī, just as Pradyumna was stolen by Śambara.

## Chapter 63 - Lord Kṛṣṇa Fights with Bāṇāsura

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O descendant of Bharata, the relatives of Aniruddha, not seeing him return, continued to lament after the four rainy months passed.**

**Комментарий:**

In the sixty-third chapter, Kṛṣṇa is praised by Śiva and Jvāra, is victorious, returns to his city and makes it joyful. The word ca means “but” since there is a change of topic. Mārgaśīrṣa (December) had started. After Ūṣā’s dream which occurred on the Dvādaśī during waxing phase of Vaiśākha month, Aniruddha was brought to her on the first day of Jyeṣṭha month, according to Citralekhā’s words in Hari-vaṁśa. Sapta-rātreṇa te bhīru darśayiṣyāmy ahaṁ priyam: I will show you your beloved in seven nights’ time. Six months passed, including even the four months of the monsoon (vi-atīyuḥ).

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**After hearing from Nārada the news of Aniruddha’s deeds and his capture, the Vṛṣṇis, who worshiped Kṛṣṇa as their personal deity, went to Śoṇitapura.**

**Комментарий:**

Karma refers to battle, etc.

### Text 3-4

**Перевод:**

**With Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa in the lead, the chiefs of the Sātvata clan—Pradyumna, Sātyaki, Gada, Sāmba, Sāraṇa, Nanda, Upananda, Bhadra and others—converged with an army of twelve divisions and laid siege to Bāṇasura’s capital, completely surrounding the city on all sides.**

**Комментарий:**

Nanda and others were the best followers, excellent Yādavas.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Bāṇāsura became filled with anger upon seeing them destroy his city’s suburban gardens, ramparts, watchtowers and gateways, and thus he went out to confront them with an army of equal size.**

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Rudra, accompanied by his son Kārtikeya and the Pramathas, came riding on Nandi, his bull carrier, to fight Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa on Bāṇa’s behalf.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to allude to Bāṇa’s evil inclination, Śiva, though omniscient (bhagavān), fought to show to Bāṇa and others Kṛṣṇa’s powers by his own defeat.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**A most astonishing, tumultuous and hair-raising battle then commenced, with Kṛṣṇa matched against Śiva, and Pradyumna against Kārtikeya.**

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma fought with Kumbhāṇḍa and Kūpakarṇa, Sāmba with Bāṇa’s son, and Sātyaki with Bāṇa.**

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Brahmā and the other ruling devatās, along with Siddhas, Cāraṇas and great sages, as well as Gandharvas, Apsarās and Yakṣas, all came in their celestial airplanes to watch.**

### Text 10-11

**Перевод:**

**With sharp-pointed arrows discharged from his bow Śārṅga, Kṛṣṇa drove away the various followers of Śiva—Bhūtas, Pramathas, Guhyakas, Ḍākinīs, Yātudhānas, Vetālas, Vināyakas, Pretas, Mātās, Piśācas, Kuṣmāṇḍas and Brahma-rākṣasas.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa drove them away with arrows shot from the Śārṅga bow but did not kill them since they were the followers of his devotee Śiva.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Śiva, wielder of the trident, shot various weapons at Kṛṣṇa, wielder of Śārṅga. But Kṛṣṇa was not in the least perplexed: he neutralized all these weapons with appropriate counter-weapons.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa shot his arrows carefully (avismitaḥ).

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa counteracted a brahmāstra with another brahmāstra, a wind weapon with a mountain weapon, a fire weapon with a rain weapon, and Śiva’s personal pāśupatāstra weapon with his own personal weapon, the nārāyaṇāstra.**

**Комментарий:**

Each of the weapons is described. For a brahmāstra, a brahmāstra was used. Naijam (his own) means nārāyaṇāstra.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**After making Śiva faint by making him yawn with a yawning weapon, Kṛṣṇa proceeded to strike down Bāṇāsura’s army with his sword, club and arrows.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa made Śiva faint with his yawning weapon. Hari-vaṁśa says: Śiva, still holding his arrows and bow, suddenly yawned and lost consciousness because of the Lord’s weapon. The Lord was the conqueror of the demons.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Kārtikeya was distressed by the flood of Pradyumna’s arrows raining down from all sides, and thus he fled the battlefield on his peacock as blood poured from his limbs.**

**Комментарий:**

Skanda fled with his peacock (śikhinā).

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Kumbhāṇḍa and Kūpakarṇa, tormented by Balarāma’s club, fell down dead. When the soldiers of these two demons saw that their leaders had been killed, they scattered in all directions.**

**Комментарий:**

Kumbāṇḍa and Kūpakarṇa were afflicted by Balarāma’s club (musala).

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Bāṇāsura was furious to see his entire military force being torn apart. Leaving his fight with Sātyaki, he charged across the battlefield on his chariot and attacked Kṛṣṇa.**

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Proud on the battlefield, Bāṇa simultaneously pulled taut all the strings of his five hundred bows and fixed two arrows on each string.**

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa split every one of Bāṇāsura’s bows simultaneously, and also struck down his chariot driver, chariot and horses. The Lord then sounded his conch.**

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Just then Bāṇāsura’s mother, Koṭarā, desiring to save her son’s life, appeared before Kṛṣṇa naked and with her hair undone.**

**Комментарий:**

Koṭarā is some form of Pārvatī. She was Bāṇa’s mother. According to Hari-vaṁśa, Bāṇa became Śiva’s son by great austerities and thus Pārvatī became his mother. She is sometimes called Koṭarī.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Gadāgraja turned his face away to avoid seeing the naked woman, and Bāṇāsura—deprived of his chariot, his bow shattered—took the opportunity to flee into his city.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa avoiding looking at her, turned his head aside.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**After Śiva’s followers had been driven away, the Śiva-jvara, who had three heads and three feet, pressed forward to attack Kṛṣṇa. As the Śiva-jvara approached, he seemed to burn everything in the ten directions.**

**Комментарий:**

Jvara rushed forward to fight (last phrase is understood but not stated in the text). Hari-vaṁśa says: The terrible Śiva-jvara had three legs, three heads, six arms and nine eyes. Showering ashes, he resembled Yamarāja at the time of universal annihilation.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Seeing this personified weapon approach, Kṛṣṇa then released his own personified fever weapon, the Viṣṇu-jvara. The Śiva-jvara and Viṣṇu-jvara thus battled each other.**

**Комментарий:**

Immediately (atha) Kṛṣṇa released his own weapon, chilling fever—something more powerful than Śiva’s weapon.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**The Śiva-jvara, overwhelmed by the strength of the Viṣṇu-jvara, cried out in pain. But finding no refuge, the frightened Śiva-jvara approached Kṛṣṇa, the master of the senses, hoping to attain his shelter. Thus with joined palms he began to praise the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Wailing loudly (samākrandan), the Śiva-jvara fought. Then he became afflicted by the strength of Viṣṇu-jvara. Not finding fearlessness elsewhere, even in Śiva, he was followed by Viṣṇujvara, like Durvasā being followed by Sudarśaṇa. Then, fearful, desiring protection or shelter (śaraṇārthī), he folded his hands and praised the Lord Hṛṣīkeśa, the controller of even Śiva.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**The Śiva-jvara said: I bow down to you of unlimited potencies, the Supreme Lord, the Supersoul of all beings. You possess pure and complete consciousness and are the cause of cosmic creation, maintenance and dissolution. Perfectly peaceful, you are the Absolute Truth to whom the Vedas indirectly refer.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to you, having unlimited śaktis because you are the Supreme Lord, controlling Brahmā and others since you are their antaryāmī (sarvātmānam). Brahmā says to Śiva in Nārāyaṇīya: tavāntarātmā mama ca ye cānye dehi-saṁjñitāḥ sarveṣāṁ sākṣibhuto’sau na grāhyaḥ kenacit kvacit He is the soul of you, me and others who are defined in terms of bodies. He is the witness of all beings. He is not understood by anyone in any circumstance. (Mahābhārata) You are pure (kevalam).
