Though you are endowed with a form of consciousness (jñātpi-mātram), you are the cause of the universe through your two śaktis—prakṛti and time. “Brahman is said to be like this.” You are Brahman understood by the Vedas (brahmaliṅgam). You are devoid of agitation (praśāntam).

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Time, the agitator; fate; action, or cause; the conditioned jīva; impressions; the sense objects; the prakṛti; mahat-tattva; false ego; the eleven senses and five gross elements; the body—all this constitutes your material illusory energy, māyā, an endless cycle like that of seed and plant. I take shelter of you, the negation of this māyā.**

**Комментарий:**

He clarifies the Lord being pure (kevalam). Time is the agitator. Karma is the nimitta. When karma is about to bring the results it is called destiny (daiva). Propensities (svabhāva) are the subtle traces (saṁskāra) of karma. The jīva is the individual living entity who possesses this karma. Dravyaṁ refers to the subtle forms of the elements (tan-mātras). Kṣetram is matter (prakṛti). Prāṇa is the life air (sūtra), ātmā is the false ego (ahaṅkāra), and vikāraḥ (transformation) is sixteen-fold, comprising the eleven senses and the five gross elements (pañcamahā-bhūtas). Their combination is the body. From the body (bīja) is produced karma, and from that another body is produced. Their repeated sequence (bīja-roha-pravāhaḥ) is your māyā. Though the jīva is different from māyā still due to being captured by māyā it is included in māyā. I surrender to you, who are the negation of all this.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**With various intentions, you perform pastimes to maintain the devatās, the saintly persons and the codes of religion for this world. By these pastimes you also kill those who stray from the right path and live by violence. Your present incarnation is meant to relieve the earth’s burden.**

**Комментарий:**

“If I am pure, there will be material attachment and repulsion in me by giving mercy or punishing. This will contaminate my purity.” By manifesting through pastimes such as the battle with Bāṇa, with various intentions such as “I must protect devotees and kill those inimical to devotees,” you support the devotees, the devatās such as Indra, and the sages. You kill those who stray from the path. Because you have affection for the devotees you do not have material attachment and repulsion. This is what I understand: this birth of yours is to relieve the earth, your devotee, of its burden.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**I am tortured by the fierce power of your terrible fever weapon, which is cold yet burning. All embodied souls will not suffer as long as they remain bound to your lotus feet and serve them.**

**Комментарий:**

He begs for protection, the result of surrender. Suffering from the heat of your fever, I cannot praise you. Please protect me from it. It is cool but fierce, just as the moon is cooling everywhere but fierce to the lotuses. “Suffering is suitable for you who torment others.” Āśānubaddhāḥ means having thirst for your lotus feet. Therefore, suffering is not suitable for me, who am your devotee now. Fever is the presiding deity of suffering just as Yama is the presiding deity of hellish punishment.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O three-headed one, I am pleased with you. May your fear of my fever weapon be dispelled, and may whoever remembers our conversation here have no reason to fear you.**

**Комментарий:**

May the person have no suffering even though touched by you. He will quickly be relieved of the fever.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Thus addressed, the Māheśvara-jvara bowed down to the infallible Lord and went away. But Bāṇāsura then appeared, riding forth on his chariot to fight Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

His driver was Nandīśa according to Viṣṇu-Purāṇa.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Carrying numerous weapons in his thousand hands, O King, the terribly infuriated demon shot many arrows at Kṛṣṇa, the carrier of the disc weapon.**

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**As Bāṇa continued hurling weapons at him, the Supreme Lord began using his sharp-edged cakra to cut off Bāṇāsura’s arms as if they were tree branches.**

**Комментарий:**

Asyataḥ means throwing.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Śiva felt compassion for his devotee Bāṇāsura, whose arms were being cut off, and thus he approached Kṛṣṇa and spoke to him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

“Śiva had fought with Kṛṣṇa. Was he not ashamed to then praise him?” Śiva is omniscient (bhagavān). He understood that it was not surprising that the Supreme Lord bewildered him. What shame should the servant have in front of his master?

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Rudra said: You alone are the Absolute Truth, self-revealing, the mystery hidden within the Vedas. Those whose hearts are spotless can see you, for you are uncontaminated, like the sky.**

**Комментарий:**

You are self-revealing (jyotiḥ), Parabrahman. “Knowing this, why did you fight with me?” You are hidden in the Vedas (brahmaṇi) made of words. You are difficult to understand. “Then people will not be liberated.” Those whose minds are fixed in sattva can see you. I however have a mind fixed in tamas. How can I see you? This is an utterance in humility only. Otherwise the first part of the verse would be contradicted. You are pure like the sky. The sky remains pure though it is the substratum of māyā’s effects.

### Text 35-36

**Перевод:**

**The sky is your navel, fire your mouth, water your semen, and heaven your head. The cardinal directions are your sense of hearing, herbal plants the hairs on your body, and water-bearing clouds the hair on your head. The earth is your foot, the moon your mind, and the sun your vision, while I am your ego. The ocean is your abdomen, Indra your arm, Brahmā is your intelligence, the progenitor of mankind is your genitals, and dharma is your heart. You are indeed the original puruṣa, the creator of the worlds.**

**Комментарий:**

You are Parabrahman. The universe in the form of all of us is your vibhūti. Two verses go together. He for whom the various elements are the limbs, that person is you, the puruṣa, who creates the universe (loka-kalpah). This is the connection between the two verses. The sky is your navel. Fire is your mouth. Water is your semen. Heaven is your head. The directions (āśā) are your ears. Earth (urvī) is your feet. The moon is your mind. The sun is your eye. I, Siva, am your ahaṅkāra (ātmā). The ocean is your stomach. Indra is your arms. Herbs are your body hairs. Clouds are your hair on the head. Brahmā is your intelligence. Prajāpati is your genital. Dharma is your heart. The word yasya is repeated only for clarity. The various elements are the vibhūtis of your spiritual form. From your spiritual navel, etc., you make the material sky, etc.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Your current descent into the material realm, O Lord of unrestricted power, is meant for upholding the principles of bhakti and benefiting the entire universe. We devatās, each depending on your grace and authority, protect the seven planetary systems.**

**Комментарий:**

You manifest yourself to protect your bhakti, not just to protect the planetary systems. O Lord, living in your eternal planet (akuṇṭhadhāman)! To institute bhakti (dharmasya guptyai) by which there is auspiciousness (bhavāya) to the world, you descend. “Let me just manifest to protect the planetary systems.” All of us, the lords of the directions, given powers (anubhāvitā) by you protect the seven worlds. Thus, that is not the only reason for your appearance. It is a secondary reason.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**You are the original person, one without a second, transcendental and self-manifesting. Uncaused, you are the cause of all, and you are the ultimate controller. You are nonetheless perceived in terms of the transformations of matter effected by inconceivable energy—transformations you sanction so that the various material objects can fully manifest.**

**Комментарий:**

He confirms that the devatās are given powers by the Lord. You are the chief of all (ekaḥ), existing before all others (ādyaḥ), without a second (advitīyaḥ) since there is no one who is your equal, beyond the three states of consciousness (turyaḥ) since you are eternally omniscient (svadṛk), the cause of everything, capable of doing the inconceivable (īśaḥ). Though you have these qualities, you assist the insignificant guṇas of māyā. You are perceived as antaryāmī for accomplishing perfectly all the senses (guṇa) by your māyā in each body (yathā-vikāram). Without your acting as antaryāmī they could not function. You are the promoter of our senses. Tavāntarātmā mama ca ye cānye dehi-saṁjñitāḥ: He is the soul of you (Śiva), me (Brahmā) and others who are defined in terms of bodies. (Nārāyaṇīya). Being instigated by you, we are able to protect the worlds.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**O almighty one, just as the sun, though hidden by a cloud, illuminates the cloud and all other visible forms as well, so you, although hidden by the material qualities, remain self-luminous and thus reveal all those qualities, along with the living entities who possess them.**

**Комментарий:**

An example is given of the antaryāmī manifesting the guṇas of māyā though being invisible. Just as the sun, though hidden by the shade of a cloud reveals all objects covered by the cloud and the cloud itself, you reveal the jīvas (guṇinaḥ) and the senses (guṇān) though hidden by ahāṅkara, the effect of the guṇas, which covers the jīva.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Their intelligence bewildered by your māyā, fully attached to children, wife, home and so on, persons immersed in the ocean of material misery sometimes rise to the surface and sometimes sink down.**

**Комментарий:**

Without your mercy the jīvas cannot be delivered. The jīvas attached to sons, etc., sometimes rise in the ocean of saṁsāra by generation of puṇyas and sometimes sink by generation of sin.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**One who has attained this human form of life as a gift from God, yet who fails to control his senses and honor your feet, is surely to be pitied, for he is only cheating himself.**

**Комментарий:**

He criticizes those who do not worship the Lord in two verses. A person attains this human body (nṛ-lokam) given by you (devadattam).

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**That mortal who rejects you—his true self, dearest friend, and Lord—for the sake of sense objects, whose nature is just the opposite, refuses nectar and instead consumes poison.**

**Комментарий:**

The person rejects you, all-pervading, full of consciousness and bliss (ātmanāṁ), for the opposite of you, sense objects, which are material, not dear and not the Lord.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**I, Lord Brahmā, the other devatās and the pure-minded sages have all surrendered wholeheartedly unto you, our dearest self and Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

“You, Brahmā, Indra and others all oppose me. Who is my devotee?” We all surrender with our complete minds (sarvātmanā). Our opposition to you is because of your desire to produce pastimes.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Let us worship you, the Supreme Lord, to be freed from material life. You are the maintainer of the universe and the cause of its creation and demise. Equipoised and perfectly at peace, you are the true friend, self and worshipable Lord. You are one without a second, the shelter of all the worlds and all souls.**

**Комментарий:**

Showing the reason for the Lord being worshippable, he begs for liberation. Let us worship (bhajāma) you. The imperative form expresses a prayer. You are Parabrahman, the cause of creation, maintenance and destruction. You are equal to devotees (samam), though they have different qualities. You are devoid of anger though seeing your devotee’s offense (prasāntam). Others are not to be worshipped (ananyam) since you do not give up oneness, though becoming many. You are the shelter (ketum) of the universes and the jīvas. We worship you to destroy saṁsāra characterized by opposition to you. May we not oppose you again.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**This Bāṇāsura is my dear and faithful follower, and I have awarded him freedom from fear. Therefore, my Lord, please grant him your mercy, just as you showed mercy to Prahlāda, the lord of the demons.**

**Комментарий:**

“Choose a boon.” He chooses that his devotee Bāṇa have bhakti for Kṛṣṇa. When I danced with great devotion for you, he assisted me by playing instruments. Thus I developed affection for him (iṣṭaḥ). He is dear (dayitaḥ) since he is related to Prahlāda and Bali, your devotees. You should give him fearlessness. How? Please show mercy on him just as you showed mercy to Prahlāda, lord of the demons.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear lord, for your pleasure I must certainly do what you have requested of me. I fully agree with your conclusion.**

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**I will not kill this demonic son of Vairocani, for I gave Prahlāda Mahārāja the benediction that I would not kill any of his descendants.**

**Комментарий:**

Anvayaḥ means the dynasty.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**It was to subdue Bāṇāsura’s false pride that I severed his arms. And I slew his mighty army because it had become a burden upon the earth.**

**Комментарий:**

“Then why did you do this?” He answers.

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**This demon, who still has four arms, will be immune to old age and death, and he will serve as one of your principal attendants. Thus he will have nothing to fear on any account.**

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**Thus attaining freedom from fear, Bāṇāsura offered obeisances to Kṛṣṇa by touching his head to the ground. Bāṇa then seated Aniruddha and his bride on their chariot and brought them before the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Saḥ means Bāṇa. Vadhvā means “with Ūṣā”.

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**At the front of the party Kṛṣṇa then placed Aniruddha and his bride, both beautifully adorned with fine clothes and ornaments, and surrounded them with a full military division. Thus Kṛṣṇa took his leave of Śiva and departed.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa left with Ūṣā and Aniruddha (sa-patnīkam), having taken Śiva’s permission since Śiva approved of Bāṇa’s arms being severed.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**The Lord then entered his capital. The city was lavishly decorated with flags and victory arches, and its avenues and crossways were all sprinkled with water. As conchs, ānaka and dundubhi drums resounded, the Lord’s relatives, the brāhmaṇas and the general populace all came forward to greet him respectfully.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was approached by the citizens, etc., and welcomed (abhyudyātaḥ).

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**Whoever rises early in the morning and remembers Kṛṣṇa’s victory in his battle with Śiva will never experience defeat.**

## Chapter 64 - The Deliverance of King Nṛga

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva said: O King, one day Sāmba, Pradyumna, Cāru, Bhānu, Gada and other young boys of the Yadu dynasty went to a small forest to play.**

**Комментарий:**

In the sixty-fourth chapter, Kṛṣṇa frees Nṛga from a curse and teaches devotion to brāhmaṇas by explaining the fault of taking a brāhmaṇa’s property.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**After playing for a long time, they became thirsty. As they searched for water, they looked inside a dry well and saw a peculiar creature.**

**Комментарий:**

Sattvam means a living entity.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**The boys were astonished to behold this creature, a lizard who looked like a hill. They felt sorry for it and tried to lift it out of the well.**

**Комментарий:**

They saw a lizard (kṛkalāsam).

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**They caught on to the trapped lizard with leather thongs and then with woven ropes, but still they could not lift it out. So they went to Kṛṣṇa and excitedly told him about the creature.**

**Комментарий:**

They tried using leather ropes (carmabhiḥ) and thread woven ropes (tāntavaiḥ).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**The lotus-eyed Supreme Lord, maintainer of the universe, went to the well and saw the lizard. Then with his left hand he easily lifted it out.**

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Touched by the hand of the glorious Supreme Lord, the being at once gave up its lizard form and assumed that of a resident of heaven. His complexion was beautifully colored like molten gold, and he was adorned with wonderful ornaments, clothes and garlands.**

**Комментарий:**

He became a devatā of Svarga.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa understood the situation, but to inform people in general he inquired as follows: “Who are you, O greatly fortunate one? Seeing your excellent form, I think you must surely be an exalted devatā.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa asked the cause of his becoming a lizard (tan-nidānam).

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**“By what past activity were you brought to this condition? It seems you did not deserve such a fate, O good soul. We are eager to know about you, so please inform us about yourself—if, that is, you think this the proper time and place to tell us.”**

**Комментарий:**

If (yad) you think it suitable (kṣamam) tell us.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus questioned by Kṛṣṇa, whose forms are unlimited, the King, his helmet as dazzling as the sun, bowed down to Mādhava and replied as follows.**

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**King Nṛga said: I am a king known as Nṛga, the son of Ikṣvāku. Perhaps, Lord, you have heard of me when lists of charitable men were recited.**

**Комментарий:**

You may have heard my name when groups of bards sing ancient histories. The word yadi expresses some doubt even when there is no doubt, as in the usage, yadi vedāḥ pramāṇaṁ syuḥ which means “the Vedas must be authoritative evidence.”

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**What could possibly be unknown to you, O master? With vision undisturbed by time, you witness the minds of all living beings. Nevertheless, on your order I will speak.**

**Комментарий:**

What is unknown to you? You know everything.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**I gave in charity as many cows as there are grains of sand on the earth, stars in the heavens, or drops in a rain shower.**

**Комментарий:**

Yāvatya means uncountable.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Young, brown, milk-laden cows, who were well behaved, beautiful and endowed with good qualities, who were all acquired honestly, and who had gilded horns, silver-plated hooves and decorations of fine ornamental cloths and garlands—such were the cows, along with their calves, that I gave in charity.**

**Комментарий:**

He describes the excellence of what he gave. The cows were good natured, being under the control of their master (śīla). They were beautiful with good nourishment (rūpa). They always gave plentiful milk (guṇa).

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**I first honored the brāhmaṇas who were recipients of my charity by decorating them with fine ornaments. Those most exalted brāhmaṇas, whose families were in need, were young and possessed of excellent physical features and mental qualities. They were dedicated to vratas done sincerely, faithful to rituals, vastly learned in the Vedic scriptures, generous and dedicated to proper conduct.**

**Комментарий:**

Now he describes the good qualities of the recipients of charity. I gave to brāhmaṇas who were well known for austerity (tapaḥśruta), and who gave the Vedas to their disciples (brahma-vadānya).

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**I gave them bulls, land, gold and houses, along with horses, elephants and marriageable girls with maidservants, as well as sesame, silver, fine beds, clothing, jewels, utensils and chariots. In addition, I performed Vedic sacrifices and executed various pious welfare activities.**

**Комментарий:**

Other gifts are described. Caritam means performed.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Some cow belonging to a certain first-class brāhmaṇa wandered away and entered my herd. Unaware of this, I gave that cow in charity to a different brāhmaṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

“If you were so pious what was the sin that caused you to become a lizard?” I, ignorant that a cow which wandered into my heard belonged to a certain brāhmaṇa, gave it to another brāhmaṇa.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**When the cow’s first owner saw her being led away, he said, “She is mine!” The second brāhmaṇa, who had accepted her as a gift, replied, “No, she’s mine! Nṛga gave her to me.”**

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**As the two brāhmaṇas argued, each trying to fulfill his own purpose, they came to me. One of them said, “You gave me this cow,” and the other said, “But you stole her from me.” Hearing this, I was bewildered.**

**Комментарий:**

The second brāhmaṇa who had accepted the gift said, “You have given the cow to me.” The first owner said, “You took her away from me.” Hearing that, I was put in extreme perplexity (bhramaḥ).

### Text 19-20

**Перевод:**

**Finding myself in a terrible dilemma concerning my duty in the situation, I humbly entreated both the brāhmaṇas: “I will give one hundred thousand of the best cows in exchange for this one. Please give her back to me. Your good selves should be merciful to me, your servant. I did not know what I was doing. Please save me from this difficult situation, or I’ll surely fall into a filthy hell.”**

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**The present owner of the cow said, “I don’t want anything in exchange for this cow, O King,” and went away. The other brāhmaṇa declared, “I don’t want even ten thousand more cows \[than you are offering\],” and he too went away.**

**Комментарий:**

“I do not desire gifts from kings.” Saying this, the owner gave up his cow and left. The other brāhmaṇa was adamant saying, “I am not willing to give up this cow for the lakh of cows you mention or even for another ten thousand cows in addition to that.” He also left.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**O Lord of lords, O master of the universe, the agents of Yamarāja, taking advantage of the opportunity thus created, later carried me to his abode. There Yamarāja himself questioned me.**

**Комментарий:**

In this interval I died. I was taken to Yama’s abode, Saṁyamanī, by his servants, who have the power to take a person because of his sins.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**\[Yamarāja said:\] My dear King, do you wish to experience the results of your sins first, or those of your piety? Indeed, I see no end to your enjoyment in Svarga, shining with happiness and powers, because of your charity and sacrifices.**

**Комментарий:**

Will you experience the result of the sin arising from taking the cow (aśubham) first? Or the result of the piety arising from your charity (śubham)? I see no end of your staying in Svarga, shining with wondrous happiness and powers. There was no destruction of sin for Nṛga even though he had chanted the Lord’s name since in that name there was the offense of considering the name to be equal to pious karmas and since sins which are linked to offense are destroyed only along with the offense (and not independent of the destruction of offense).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**I replied, “First, my lord, let me suffer my sinful reactions,” and Yamarāja said, “Then fall!” “At once I fell, and while falling I saw myself becoming a lizard, O master.**

**Комментарий:**

O Yamarāja (deva)! I will experience my inauspicious results first. Yamarāja said “Fall!”

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**O Keśava, since I am your servant and am devoted to the brāhmaṇas and generous to them, I always hankered for your audience. Therefore even till now I have not lost my memory.**

**Комментарий:**

One time some devotee of Kṛṣṇa came to the house of Nṛga who was extremely generous. He was worshipped by Nṛga. The devotee was so satisfied that he blessed Nṛga: “O King, I give blessings that you may see Kṛṣṇa.” From that time on, Nṛga attained dāsya-bhāva and had a desire to see Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**O almighty one, how is it that my eyes see you here before me? You are the Supreme Soul, whom the greatest devotees can fix within their pure hearts only by employing the spiritual eye of the Vedas. Then how, O transcendental Lord, are you directly visible to me, since my intelligence has been blinded by the severe tribulations of material life? Only one who has finished his material entanglement in this world should be able to see you.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Kṛṣṇa, rare to see, astonished he praises his good fortune. O Lord (vibho)! How did you become directly visible to my eyes? Even masters of yoga can only meditate upon you through the eyes of the Upaniṣads in their purified hearts. Knowledge arising from the senses cannot approach you (adhokṣajam). You are seen by a person who has destroyed material existence. But you are visible to me though my intelligence is blinded by suffering of being a lizard (uru-vyasana).only due to the benedictions of your devotee.

### Text 27-28

**Перевод:**

**O Devadeva, Jagannātha, Govinda, Puruṣottama, Nārāyaṇa, Hṛṣīkeśa, Puṇyaśloka, Acyuta, Avyaya! O Kṛṣṇa, please permit me to depart for the world of the devatās. Wherever I live, O master, may my mind always take shelter of your feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Calling the Lord many times with great devotion, he desires bhakti. Though I have seen your feet, my portion of puṇyas has not been depleted by your will. I will enjoy the result in Svarga, like Prahlāda. Being situated there, may I attain bhakti to you and attain your feet after the enjoyment in Svarga.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**I offer my repeated obeisances unto you, Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vasudeva. You are the source of all beings, the Supreme Absolute Truth, the possessor of unlimited potencies, the master of all spiritual disciplines.**

**Комментарий:**

About to leave, he offers respects. I offer respects to you from whom Brahmā and others are born (bhāva) since you are Brahman. Yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante: from the Lord all beings arise. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) “Why are all the beings that arise from me not forms of consciousness?” You have unlimited śaktis. By your śakti, they take birth. I offer respects to Kṛṣṇa, the form of sac-cid-ānanda, the supreme person, the son of Vasudeva (vāsudevāya), the giver of results of karmas like iṣṭa-pūrta (yogānām pataye). Attaining you, I proceed to enjoy their results by your desire.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Having spoken thus, Mahārāja Nṛga circumambulated Kṛṣṇa and touched his crown to the Lord’s feet. Granted permission to depart, King Nṛga then boarded a wonderful celestial airplane as all the people present looked on.**

**Комментарий:**

He obtained permission to go. “After enjoying in Svarga, you will attain me.”

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī—who is especially devoted to the brāhmaṇas and who embodies the essence of dharma, then spoke to his personal associates and thus instructed the royal class in general.**

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] How indigestible is the property of a brāhmaṇa, even when enjoyed just slightly and by one more potent than fire! What then to speak of kings who try to enjoy it, presuming themselves to be lords.**

**Комментарий:**

Enjoyed even a little, the property of a brāhmaṇa is indigestible even to a person who is more powerful than fire .

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**I do not consider hālāhala to be real poison, because it has an antidote. But a brāhmaṇa’s property, when stolen, can truly be called poison, for it has no antidote in this world.**

**Комментарий:**

“It is like indigestible food?” It is more poisonous than poison. Śīva digested the hālāhala poison. But there is no antidote for enjoying a brāhmaṇa’s property.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Poison kills only the person who ingests it, and an ordinary fire may be extinguished with water. But the fire generated from the kindling wood of a brāhmaṇa’s property burns the thief’s entire family down to the root.**

**Комментарий:**

The lack of remedy is described. Poison affects the person who drinks it but does not destroy his sons, etc. Fire on a tree does not burn the root of the tree but is quelled by water. But the fire kindled from a brāhmaṇa’s property however burns up the dynasty, everyone related to the enjoyer of the property, to the very root (samūlam), upto ancient ancestors.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**If a person enjoys a brāhmaṇa’s property without receiving due permission, that property destroys three generations of his family. But if he takes it by force or gets the government or other outsiders to help him usurp it, then ten generations of his ancestors and ten generations of his descendants are all destroyed.**

**Комментарий:**

Burning to the root is described. “This is my relative, if he enjoys my wealth, then let him enjoy it.” Not being fully permitted like this (duranujñātam), enjoying in this way destroys oneself, one’s sons and one’s grandsons (tri-pūruṣa). If one enjoys by using force (prasahya) or the influence of the king, then ten generations in the past and future will suffer.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Members of the royal order fail to foresee their own downfall. Childishly hankering to enjoy a brāhmaṇa’s property, they are actually hankering to go to hell.**

**Комментарий:**

Those born in a royal family (rāja-kulyāḥ) who desire to take the property of a brāhmaṇa desire to go to hell. They are foolish, not seeing their downfall.

### Text 37-38

**Перевод:**

**For as many years as there are particles of dust touched by the tears of generous brāhmaṇas who have dependent families and whose property is stolen, uncontrolled kings who usurp a brāhmaṇa’s property are cooked, along with their royal families, in the hell known as Kumbhīpāka.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Whether he takes the brāhmaṇa’s wealth or it is given to him, he will take birth as a worm in feces for sixty thousand years.**

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**I do not desire brāhmaṇas’ wealth obtained by force or trickery and offered to me. Those persons become short-lived and are defeated. They lose their kingdoms and in the next life become snakes, who trouble others.**

**Комментарий:**

One loses life span just by hankering (ghṛdhvā) after a brāhmaṇa’s property, then what to speak of actually taking it. They become snakes (ahayaḥ).

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**My dear followers, never treat a learned brāhmaṇa harshly, even if he has sinned. Even if he attacks you physically or repeatedly curses you, always continue to offer him obeisances.**

**Комментарий:**

“If the brāhmaṇa steals our money or becomes hostile, what should be done then?” Two verses explain. Even if they are like that, I will give up my attachment to those (māmakatvāḥ) who disrespect the brāhmaṇas.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Just as I always carefully bow down to brāhmaṇas, so all of you should likewise bow down to them. I will punish anyone who acts otherwise.**

**Комментарий:**

I will punish that person.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**When a brāhmaṇa’s property is stolen, it certainly causes the person who takes it to fall down, even if he does so by accident, just as the brāhmaṇa’s cow did to Nṛga.**

**Комментарий:**

This is not an exaggeration to instill fear. There is direct proof as stated in this verse.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Having thus instructed the residents of Dvārakā, Mukunda, who wanted to purify all the people, entered his palace.**

## Chapter 65 - Lord Balarāma Visits Vṛndāvana

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O best of the Kurus, once Balarāma, eager to visit his well-wishing friends, mounted his chariot and traveled to Nanda Gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

In the sixty-fifth chapter Balarāma, going to Vraja, embraced by his friends, enjoys with his gopīs and pulls the Yamunā. Kṛṣṇa, the ocean of Vraja prema, many times went to Vraja directly and in his sphūrti as Uddhava expressed in his message: O lotus-eyed Lord, whenever you go away to Mathurā, Vṛndāvana or Hastināpura to meet your friends and relatives, every moment of your absence seems like a million years. O infallible one, at that time our eyes become useless, as if bereft of sun. (SB [1.11.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/11.9)) Now Balarāma also went there. It is understood that he carried a message from Kṛṣṇa. Hari-vaṁśa says: Remembering the deep friendship he once enjoyed with the cowherd folk, Balarāma went alone to Vraja, having taken Kṛṣṇa’s permission. Giving up his associates in the city, wearing cowherd dress, he was eager (utkaṇṭhaḥ). He had great desire for Vraja, which turned his ocean of sobriety into a handful of water.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Having long suffered the anxiety of separation, the cowherd men and their wives embraced Balarāma. The Lord then offered respects to his parents, and they joyfully greeted him with blessings.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma was embraced by elder gopīs (gopībhiḥ), friends of his mother. Pitarau (parents) is used since he had parental feelings towards the two.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**\[Nanda and Yaśodā prayed,\] “O descendant of Daśārha, O Lord of the universe, may you and your younger brother Kṛṣṇa ever protect us.” Saying this, they raised Balarāma onto their laps, embraced him and moistened him with tears from their eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

By using ciram they suggest that staying here and ruling relieves our pain, but not in intermittently coming and that it is not glorious for the parents to be not protected by their two sons, though they are lords of the universe. First Nanda placed Balarāma on his lap and then Yaśodā placed.

### Text 4-6

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma then paid proper respects to the elder cowherd men, and the younger ones all greeted him respectfully. He met them all with smiles, handshakes and so on, dealing personally with each one according to age, degree of friendship, and family relationship. Then, after resting, the Lord accepted a comfortable seat, and they all gathered around him. With voices faltering out of love for him, those cowherds, who had dedicated everything to lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, asked about the health of their dear ones \[in Dvārakā\], and Balarāma in turn asked about the cowherds’ welfare.**

**Комментарий:**

After greeting the elder cowherd men, Balarāma was welcomed by the younger men. Then (atha) on the second day, he met them all with smiles, handshakes and so on, dealing personally with each one according to age, degree of friendship, and family relationship. Going to their houses and meeting them, after he had taken food and rested, and then was sitting comfortably, the cowherds asked about his well-being (anāmayam). Balarāma asked them about their well being with choked voice. They had offered everything, bodies etc., to Kṛṣṇa for perfecting their affairs. From the day he left they had no interest in maintaining their lives.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**\[The cowherds said:\] O Rāma, are all our relatives doing well? And Rāma, do all of you, with your wives and children, still remember us?**

**Комментарий:**

The very elderly ask the first question. Bāndhavāḥ means the Yādavas. His friends ask the second question.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**It is our great fortune that sinful Kaṁsa has been killed and our dear relatives freed. And it is also our good fortune that our relatives have killed and defeated their enemies and found complete security in a great fortress.**

**Комментарий:**

Durgam refers to Dvārakā.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Honored to have the personal audience of Balarāma, the young gopīs, laughed and asked him, “Is Kṛṣṇa, the darling of the city women, living happily?**

**Комментарий:**

Desiring to hear news of their beloved, the beloveds of Kṛṣṇa (gopyaḥ) met with Balarāma and Uddhava after searching for them. They laughed out of unmāda. Otherwise laughter is impossible for such shy girls in front of an elder. “How can Kṛṣṇa be happy in separation from you?” Since even in the city there are women, he should be happy.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**“Does he remember his family members, especially his father and mother? Do you think he will ever come back even once to see his mother? And does mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa remember the service we always did for him?**

**Комментарий:**

Let him not remember us, but does he remember his uncles, etc. (bandhūn), and his father Nanda and mother Yaśodā or not? Let him enjoy with the city women. But does he constantly remember our services, which were dear to him? They suggest that city women are not so skillful in serving him.

### Text 11-12

**Перевод:**

**“For Kṛṣṇa’s sake, O descendant of Daśārha, we abandoned our mothers, fathers, brothers, husbands, children and sisters, even though these family relations are difficult to give up. But now, O Lord, that same Kṛṣṇa has suddenly abandoned us and gone away, breaking off all affectionate ties with us. And yet how could any woman fail to trust his promises?**

**Комментарий:**

“Dear beloveds of Kṛṣṇa! He is very affectionate to you. He remembers you.” For him we gave up dependence on mothers, etc. Giving up us, solely devoted to him, he left. Who can believe his affection? He completely broke our friendship like a blade of grass. “But ladies! Why did you make such friendship with him?” O Balarāma how can his words made with modesty, promises, etc., not be believed by simple-minded women? We were then cheated by words of false affection. Through messengers he sent words to give us hope. “Going to the city, I will return.” Now we are in pain.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**“How can intelligent city women possibly trust the words of one whose heart is so unsteady and who is so ungrateful? They must believe him because he speaks so wonderfully and also because his beautiful smiling glances arouse their lust.**

**Комментарий:**

Some gopīs, pained by prema, speak. Having simple minds, we were cheated by him. How can the city women, being intelligent, understanding how he cheated us, accept his words? He has an unsteady heart (anavasthitātmanaḥ) and thus will destroy the friendship he makes with others (kṛta-ghnasya). Other gopīs conclude. Vai indicates remembrance. They, like us, will be cheated by he whose talks produce amazing rasa though they are actually false (citra-kathasya). There is another reason for accepting his words. They become pained with amorous love which increases by his beautiful smiling glances. Filled with passion they will not give regard to his method of affection.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**“Why bother talking about him, dear gopīs? Please talk of something else. If he passes his time without us, then we shall similarly pass ours without him.”**

**Комментарий:**

Others, displeased due to agitation of prema, speak. There is no happiness by speaking about him, rather there is just sorrow. Speak about something else. By stopping to speak about him, there will not be the suffering that arises because of him. Others speak. But he will pass his time happily. We will pass our time in grief. That is the difference.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**While speaking these words, the young cowherd women remembered Kṛṣṇa’s laughter, his pleasing conversations with them, his attractive glances, his style of walking and his loving embraces. Thus they began to cry.**

**Комментарий:**

Pierced by the sweet rasa, by Kṛṣṇa’s laughter, talks, glances, walking and embraces — which are the five arrows of Cupid — holding hope by his words that he would return, they became overwhelmed and cried in front of Balarāma, his elder brother.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord Balarāma, the attractor of all, being expert at various kinds of conciliation, consoled the gopīs by relaying to them the confidential messages Kṛṣṇa had sent with him. These messages deeply touched the gopīs’ hearts.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord, learned in various types of conciliation, pacified the gopīs having intense prema for Kṛṣṇa as previously described by messages from Kṛṣṇa himself and made them give up their pain. He pacified them in this way. First, he described Kṛṣṇa’s tearful eyes. Then he described how Kṛṣṇa praised them and criticized himself. Then he spoke of his prema. He described their mercy to him. Then with remorse he described the reason for his delay in coming, the various troubles in Dvāraka. Then with logic, “I am not controlled by him like Uddhava. Rather he is controlled by me,” and vow, he made a promise to bring him back. Then he frightened them, “Hearing your present state, he will become very greatly distressed.” Viṣṇu Purāṇa describes his heart-rending message: Balarāma appeased the gopīs with Kṛṣṇa’s sweet, consoling attractive messages filled with prema and devoid of pride. With tears, by words which were pleasing (madhuraiḥ) due to pleasant statements along with praises such na pāraye ’ham: I cannot repay you (SB [10.32.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.22)), and which were filled with prema (prema-garbhaiḥ) such as the following: But the actual reason why I, the beloved object of your sight, have stayed far away from you is that I wanted to intensify your meditation upon me and thus draw your minds closer to me. (SB [10.47.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.34)) He quoted his words devoid of pride (agarvitaiḥ): Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation. (SB [10.32.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/32.22)) In this way he used words such as “Closing your eyes please experience his most desired association,” which were charming (atimanoharaiḥ) due to manifesting their realization of him. After pacifying them, he had pastimes with his own group of gopīs and not otherwise. In this way only by manifestation of a portion of sakhya, he gave them such messages. He did not reveal any other mood. His portion as an elder brother did not manifest in order to protect the lives of the gopīs who had reached the tenth state.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma resided there for the two months of Madhu and Mādhava, and during the nights he gave his cowherd girlfriends conjugal pleasure.**

**Комментарий:**

For the month of Caitra (madhuṁ) and Vaiśākha (mādhavaṁ), he stayed. Gopīs here refers to his gopīs who had been mentioned mixing with Kṛṣṇa’s gopīs at the spring rāsa-dance where Śaṅkhacūḍa was killed.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**In the company of numerous women, Balarāma enjoyed in a garden by the Yamunā River. This garden was bathed in the rays of the full moon and caressed by breezes bearing the fragrance of night-blooming lotuses.**

**Комментарий:**

The garden was bathed by the rays of full moon. “But for two months how could there be full-moon nights?” This happened by the will of Balarāma. The gopīs went to a spot in that forest. Kaumudī also indicates blossoming lotuses. The grove was served by winds carrying the scent of lotuses. This place is famous as Rāma-ghaṭṭa, which is far from the site of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s rāsa dance, which was avoided by Balarāma.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Sent by Varuṇa, the divine Vāruṇī liquor flowed from a tree hollow and made the entire forest even more fragrant with its sweet aroma.**

**Комментарий:**

Vāruṇī, the presiding deity of liquor was the daughter of Varuṇa. Varuṇa sent her to serve Balarāma. She fell from a hole of the kadamba tree in streams of liquor. She made the forest fragrant with her fragrance, more than previously. Hari-vaṁśa describes her words to Balarāma, samīpam preṣitā pitrā varuṇena tavānagha: O sinless one, Vāruṇī was sent to you by her father Varuṇa. She arose along with the nectar during the churning of the Milk Ocean. Like the nectar, the liquor was tasty and intoxicating.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**The wind carried to Balarāma the fragrance of that flood of sweet liquor, and when he smelled it he went to the tree. There he and his female companions drank.**

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**As the Gandharvas sang his glories, Balarāma enjoyed within the brilliant circle of young women. He appeared just like Indra’s elephant, the lordly Airāvata, enjoying in the company of sheelephants.**

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**At that time kettledrums resounded in the sky, the Gandharvas joyfully rained down flowers, and the great sages praised Balarāma’s heroic deeds.**

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**As his deeds were sung, Halāyudha wandered as if inebriated among the various forests with his girlfriends. His eyes rolled from the effects of the liquor.**

### Text 24-25

**Перевод:**

**Intoxicated with joy, Balarāma sported flower garlands, including the famous Vaijayantī. He wore a single earring, and beads of perspiration decorated his smiling lotus face like snowflakes. The Lord then summoned the Yamunā River so that he could play in her waters. She disregarded his command, thinking he was drunk. This angered Balarāma, and he began dragging the river with the tip of his plow.**

**Комментарий:**

His moon-like face had a smile like moonlight, and was ornamented with perspiration which was like snow. Angered at Yamunā who did not come having disrespected his words by thinking, “He is intoxicated for he is inviting even me, a river,” he pulled the river with the tip of his plough.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**\[Balarāma said:\] O sinful one disrespecting me, you do not come when I call you but rather move only by your own whim. Therefore with the tip of my plow I shall bring you here in a hundred streams!**

**Комментарий:**

You have been called (āhutāḥ). The short hu is poetic license. You are an unchaste woman (kāma-cāriṇīm). Actually for destroying the sins of the people she flows here and there independently in many streams (kāma-cāriṇīm).

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Thus scolded by the Lord, O King, the frightened river-goddess Yamunā came and fell at the feet of Balarāma, the beloved descendant of Yadu. Trembling, she spoke to him the following words.**

**Комментарий:**

This Yamunā in the form of a river, is the wife of the ocean and is a vibhūti of Kālindī (Kṛṣṇa’s wife) like Chāyā and Saṁjñā, since Hari-vaṁśa says praty-uvācārṇava-vadhuḥ: the wife of the ocean replied.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**\[Goddess Yamunā said:\] Rāma, Rāma, O mighty-armed one! I cannot know your full prowess. With a single portion of yourself you hold up the earth, O Lord of the universe.**

**Комментарий:**

With a portion of yourself called Śeṣa you hold up the earth.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, please release me. O soul of the universe, I didn’t understand your position as the Supreme Lord, but now I have surrendered unto you, O master, kind to your devotees!**

**Комментарий:**

Paraṁ bhāvaṁ refers to Balarāma’s position as the svarūpa of Mahāsaṅkarṣaṇa.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Upon being requested, Balarāma released the Yamunā and, like the king of the elephants with his entourage of she-elephants, entered the river’s water with his female companions.**

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The Lord played in the water to his full satisfaction, and when he came out Goddess Kānti presented him with blue garments, precious ornaments and a brilliant necklace.**

**Комментарий:**

Kānti is a different form of Lakṣmī and wife of Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa since Viṣṇu Purāṇa says: Sent by Varuṇa, Goddess Lakṣmī then presented Balarāma with a garland of unfading lotuses and a pair of garments colored blue like the sea.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma dressed himself in the blue garments and put on the gold necklace. Anointed with fragrances and beautifully adorned, he appeared as resplendent as Indra’s royal elephant.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma dressed himself, wore the necklace on his neck and was smeared with sandalwood. He appeared like Airāvata (vāraṇaḥ).

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Even today, O King, one can see how the Yamunā flows through the many channels created when it was dragged by the unlimitedly powerful Balarāma. This demonstrates his prowess.**

**Комментарий:**

The path marked by his pulling the plough starts from Rāmaghaṭṭa. Even today she flows by that path by the order of Balarāma and out of affection for him. Hari-vaṁśa describes his order: This path made by my plough should flood the beautiful place by spreading water. My fame shall remain as long as people remain.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Thus for Balarāma all the nights passed like a single night as he enjoyed in Vraja, his mind enchanted by the exquisite charm and beauty of Vraja’s young ladies.**

**Комментарий:**

All evenings passed like one night because of the ever-fresh experience. His mind was enchanted by the sweetness of the Vraja women. This indicates that the women of Dvārakā were not of the same nature. After two months Balarāma went to Dvārakā and related the well-being of Vraja to Kṛṣṇa who questioned while sitting in the assembly. This is known from the verses beginning with tathaivādhva-gaveṣeṇa in Hari-vaṁśa. In private Kṛṣṇa asked about the well-being of his gopīs. Balarāma leaving Vraja is not mentioned since he continued to go there in his mind according to some. About Śrī Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa Śrī Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa (Śrī Govinda Dasa) appeared in the 1600's near Remuna, Orissa. In his youth, he mastered Sanskrit grammar, poetry, and logic. After carefully studying the commentries of Sankara and Madhva he took initiation in the Tattva-vadi disciplic succession of Śrīpad Madhvacarya. Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa became a dig vijaya pandit (conqueror of all opponents) and began visiting the holy places. Wherever he went he defeated the local sages, scholars, and sannyasis. In Vrindavana, he studied Śrīmad Bhagavatam under Śrīla Vishvanatha Cakravarti Thakura and worshipped Radha-Syamasundara. In 1706 A.D. Vishvanatha Cakravarti Thakura sent him to Gulta (near Jaipur,Rajasthan) to uphold the credibility of Mahaprabhu's movement. The local Ramanandis (a branch of Śrī Vaishnavas) were claiming that the Bengali Vaishnavas had no right to worship Govindaji they had no commentary on the Vedanta-sutra. Lord Govindaji Himself directly revealed the Govinda-bhasya (a Vaishnava commentary on Vedanta) to Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa. Using it, Baladeva solidly established Gaudiya Vaishnavism as an independent philosophy. He also reinstated the Bengali Vaishnavas in Govindaji's service in Jaipura. Govinda-bhasya is the only bhakti commentary on Vedanta-sutra. Śrī Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa was a niskincana-parama bhagavata, fullyrenounced topmost Devotee of Lord Krishna. His more than twenty-four books and commentaries have helped thousands of Vaishnavas understand the sublime philosophy of Krishna consciousness and the intimate writings of the six Goswamis. Since he was devoid of false prestige, he never wrote about his birth, parents, lineage, personal life. According to Śrī Bhaktivinoda Thakura in Navadvipa-dhama mahatyam, in Chaitanya lila Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa is Śrī Gopinatha Acarya, the brother-in-law of Śrī Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya. In Vraja he serves as Śrī Radha's eternal maidservant Ratnavali Devi.

## Chapter 66 - Pauṇḍraka, the False Vāsudeva

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, while Balarāma was away visiting Nanda’s village of Vraja, the ruler of Karūṣa, foolishly thinking “I am the Supreme Lord, Vāsudeva,” sent a messenger to Lord Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

In the sixty-sixth chapter, the Lord kills Pauṇḍraka and the king of Kāśī is killed by Sudarśana. When Balarāma was in Vraja, Pauṇḍraka the king of Karūṣa thought knowing that Kṛṣṇa was alone, thinking that he himself was Vāsudeva, sent a messenger to Kṛṣṇa because he was a fool.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Pauṇḍraka was emboldened by the flattery of childish men, who told him, “You are Vāsudeva, the Supreme Lord and master of the universe, who have now descended to the earth.” Thus he imagined himself to be the infallible Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

His foolishness is described. Praised by fools with those words, he became excited. He considered himself Vāsudeva (acyutam).

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Thus slow-witted King Pauṇḍraka sent a messenger to the inscrutable Kṛṣṇa at Dvārakā. Foolish Pauṇḍraka thought himself to be the Lord just like an unintelligent child whom other children make a king thinks he is a king.**

**Комментарий:**

The facts are repeated out of astonishment at his foolishness. He sent a message to Kṛṣṇa, whose path is difficult to follow (avyaktavartmane). He was like a child who is made into a king in play.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Arriving in Dvārakā, the messenger found lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa in his royal assembly and relayed the King’s message to that almighty Lord.**

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**\[On Pauṇḍraka’s behalf, the messenger said:\] I am the one and only Lord Vāsudeva, and there is no other. It is I who have descended to this world to show mercy to the living beings. Therefore give up your false name.**

**Комментарий:**

The meaning suggested by Sarasvatī devī is as follows. According to Bhāguri, when there is deletion of the syllable ‘a’, there is no ‘n’ too (so the word avatīrṇaḥ is actually anavatīrṇaḥ). I am not Vāsudeva descended but rather to show mercy to the living beings you alone have descended and no one else since there cannot be two Supreme Lords. Please make me give up my false designation, which is like that of color on white. The verb tyaja has the causative sense in it and thus means “make me give up”. Thus the Lord will say to him “I will make you give up the name.” (verse 20)

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**O Sātvata, give up my personal symbols, which out of foolishness you now carry, and come to me for shelter. If you do not, then you must give me battle.**

**Комментарий:**

Because I do not restrain, you hold my symbols, conch, disk, etc., — artificial ones which exist only because of foolishness. But you do not remove them, this is unjust. Thus making me give up the symbols, come here to give me bhakti since you are the protector from suffering. Or killing me in battle, give me liberation.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: King Ugrasena and the other members of the assembly laughed loudly when they heard this vain boasting of unintelligent Pauṇḍraka.**

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**The Lord, after enjoying the jokes of the assembly, told the messenger \[to relay a message to his master:\] “You fool, I will indeed let loose the weapons you boast of in this way.**

**Комментарий:**

O fool! Since the meaning is “I will release these symbols on you,” it means“I will release them even upon those with whom you brag in this way”. Or, I will make you give up the artificial weapons by which you boast in this way.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**“When you lie dead, O fool, your face covered by vultures, herons and vaṭa birds, you will become the shelter of dogs.”**

**Комментарий:**

In reply to the message “Take shelter of me” (verse 6) Kṛṣṇa answers. The mouth with which you speak like this, closing that mouth, covered by vultures, etc., you will lie down dead. Vaṭa is a type of bird. Dogs will eat you.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**When the Lord had thus spoken, the messenger conveyed his insulting reply to his master in its entirety. Kṛṣṇa then mounted his chariot and went to the vicinity of Kāśī.**

**Комментарий:**

Pauṇḍraka was at that time living in Kāśī, his friend’s city.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Upon observing Kṛṣṇa’s preparations for battle, the mighty warrior Pauṇḍraka quickly went out of the city with two full military divisions.**

### Text 12-14

**Перевод:**

**Pauṇḍraka’s friend, the king of Kāśī, followed behind, O King, leading the rear guard with three akṣauhiṇī divisions. Kṛṣṇa saw that Pauṇḍraka was carrying the Lord’s own insignia, such as the conch, disc, sword and club, and also an imitation Śārṅga bow and Śrīvatsa mark. He wore a mock Kaustubha gem, was decorated with a garland of forest flowers and was dressed in upper and lower garments of fine yellow silk. His banner bore the image of Garuḍa, and he wore a valuable crown and gleaming, shark-shaped earrings.**

**Комментарий:**

He had protectors behind him (pārṣnī-grāhaḥ). He wore a red colored, round stone as a Kaustubha. He had a selfmade flag of Garuḍa. He had artificial crown which had little value and ornaments on his arms and other limbs.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa laughed heartily when he saw how the king had dressed up in exact imitation of his own appearance, just like an actor on a stage.**

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**The enemies of Kṛṣṇa attacked him with tridents, clubs, bludgeons, pikes, ṛṣtis, barbed darts, lances, swords, axes and arrows.**

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**But Kṛṣṇa fiercely struck back at the army of Pauṇḍraka and Kāśirāja, which consisted of elephants, chariots, cavalry and infantry. The Lord tormented his enemies with his club, sword, Sudarśana disc and arrows, just as the fire of annihilation torments the various kinds of creatures at the end of a cosmic age.**

**Комментарий:**

Huta-bhuk is the fire of devastation which attacks all types of living beings such as viviparous, etc (pṛthak-prajā).

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**The battlefield, strewn with the dismembered chariots, horses, elephants, humans, mules and camels that had been cut to pieces by the Lord’s disc weapon, shone like the gruesome playground of Śiva, giving pleasure to the wise.**

**Комментарий:**

The battleground (āyodhanam), strewn with chariots, etc., broken by the cakra (ariṇā), shone like the playground of Śiva (bhūtapateḥ).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then addressed Pauṇḍraka with laughter: My dear Pauṇḍraka, the very weapons you spoke of through your messenger, I now release unto you.**

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**O fool, now I shall make you renounce my name, which you have falsely assumed. And I will certainly take shelter of you if I do not wish to fight you.**

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Having thus derided Pauṇḍraka, Kṛṣṇa destroyed his chariot with his sharp arrows. The Lord then cut off his head with the Sudarśana disc, just as Indra lops off a mountain peak with his thunderbolt weapon.**

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**With his arrows, Kṛṣṇa similarly severed Kāśirāja’s head from his body, sending it flying into Kāśī city like a lotus flower thrown by the wind.**

**Комментарий:**

The head fell in the city of Kāśi. The king of Kāśī had promised the citizens “My dear residents of Kāśī, today I will bring the enemy’s head into the midst of the city.” The Lord, frustrating that, threw the king’s head into the city of Kāśī to astonish the inhabitants.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Having thus killed envious Pauṇḍraka and his ally, Kṛṣṇa returned to Dvārakā. As he entered the city, the jivanmuktas glorified his feat.**

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**By constantly meditating upon the Supreme Lord, Pauṇḍraka shattered all his material bonds. Indeed, by imitating Kṛṣṇa’s appearance, O King, he ultimately became absorbed in him.**

**Комментарий:**

Pauṇḍraka bearing a four-armed form like the Lord (hareḥ svarūpam), like the insect that meditates on a wasp, was absorbed in the Lord (tan-mayaḥ). Ca indicates the king of Kāśi also.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Seeing a head decorated with earrings lying at the gate of the royal palace, the people present were puzzled. Some of them asked, “What is this?” and others said, “It is a head, but whose is it?”**

**Комментарий:**

First they thought, “what is it?” Then they thought, “it is a head”. In this way they were puzzled.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**My dear King, when they recognized it as the head of their king— the lord of Kāśi—his queens, sons and other relatives, along with all the citizens of the city, began to cry pitifully: “Alas, we are killed! O my lord, my lord!”**

### Text 27-28

**Перевод:**

**After the king’s son Sudakṣiṇa had performed the obligatory funeral rituals for his father, he resolved within his mind: “Only by killing my father’s murderer can I avenge his death.” Thus the charitable Sudakṣiṇa, together with his priests, began worshiping Śiva with great concentration.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Sudakṣiṇa performed the death rites (saṁsthā-vidhim) for the king of Kāśī. I will take revenge (apacitim). He worshipped Śiva with concentrated mind (samādhinā).

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Satisfied by the worship, the powerful Śiva appeared in the sacred precinct of Avimukta and offered Sudakṣiṇa his choice of benedictions. The prince chose as his benediction a means to slay his father’s killer.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiva is also called Avimukta since he is the presiding deity at the tīrtha known by that name. Viṣṇu Purāṇa says avimukte mahākṣetre toṣitas tena śaṅkaraḥ: at Avimukta, Śiva became pleased with him. Śiva said, “Accept a boon.”

### Text 30-31

**Перевод:**

**Śiva told him, “Accompanied by brāhmaṇas, serve the Dakṣiṇa fire—the original priest—following the injunctions of the abhicāra ritual. Then the Dakṣiṇa fire, together with many Pramathas , will fulfill your desire if you direct it against someone inimical to the brāhmaṇas.” So instructed, Sudakṣiṇa strictly observed the ritualistic vows and invoked the abhicāra against Kṛṣṇa**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Lord Śiva said, “Serve the dakṣiṇa-agnim (the Dakṣiṇa fire), which like the priest (ṛtvijam), accomplishes that which it is employed for.” This is confirmed in the Ṛg Veda (1.1.1): yajñasya devam ṛtvijam, “The lord of the sacrifice is the ṛtvik priest.” The fire will not act against a person who respects brāhmaṇas. If directed to Kṛṣṇa, the mouth of the brāhmaṇas, it will destroy the persons who direct it. Sudakṣiṇa thought that Kṛṣṇa was not devoted to brāhmaṇas (abrahmaṇye), since he heard sometimes that brāhmaṇas offered Kṛṣṇa respect. Following strict rules (vratī), he directed the curse to Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of all beings, with intentions of violence.

### Text 32-33

**Перевод:**

**Thereupon the fire rose up out of the altar pit, assuming the form of an extremely fearsome, naked person. The fiery creature’s beard and tuft of hair were like molten copper, and his eyes emitted blazing hot cinders. His face looked most frightful with its fangs and terrible arched and furrowed brows. As he licked the corners of his mouth with his tongue, the demon shook his flaming trident.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses go together. His face (āsyaḥ) was frightening with ferocious teeth, crooked brows. He had a trident (trīśikham).

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**On legs as tall as palm trees, the monster raced toward Dvārakā in the company of ghostly spirits, shaking the ground and burning the world in all directions.**

**Комментарий:**

He ran towards Dvārakā, while burning the directions.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the approach of the fiery demon created by the abhicāra ritual, the residents of Dvārakā were all struck with fear, like animals terrified by a forest fire.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing him approaching Dvārakā from far off, they were like animals terrified of a forest fire.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Distraught with fear, the people cried out to the Lord, who was then playing at dice in the royal court: “Save us! Save us, O Lord of the three worlds, from this fire burning up the city!”**

**Комментарий:**

They said (verb omitted), “Save us! Save us”

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**When Kṛṣṇa heard the people’s agitation and saw that even his own men were disturbed, that most worthy giver of shelter simply laughed and told them, “Do not fear; I shall protect you.”**

**Комментарий:**

He heard the citizens’ agitation and saw the Yādavas, the protectors of the citizens (svānāṁ) panic because of not knowing the cause.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**The almighty Lord, the internal and external witness of all, understood that the monster had been produced by Śiva from the sacrificial fire. To defeat the demon, Kṛṣṇa dispatched his disc weapon, who was waiting at his side.**

**Комментарий:**

He dispatched the cakra because the cakra itself could destroy the demon. He did not want his dice game disturbed for the sake of the demon.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**That Sudarśana, the disc weapon of Mukunda, blazed forth like millions of suns. His effulgence blazed like the fire of universal annihilation, and with his heat he pained the sky, all the directions, heaven and earth, and also the fiery demon.**

**Комментарий:**

The heat spread (verb missing) in the heavens and on earth (rodasī). The cakra produced fire (agnim). Mukundāstram suggests that the cakra would liberate those burned by it.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Frustrated by the power of Kṛṣṇa’s weapon, O King, the fiery creature produced by black magic turned his face away and retreated. Created for violence, the demon then returned to Vārāṇasī, where he surrounded the city and then burned Sudakṣiṇa and his priests to death, even though Sudakṣiṇa was his creator.**

**Комментарий:**

The demon came back to the city with unfavorable intentions (pratisametya). He burned Sudakṣiṇa along with his priests (sartvig-janam) to ashes. The fire of death (abhicāraḥ) was his creation (sva-kṛtaḥ). The word sva-kṛtaḥ is used with astonishment and extreme joy. This is viṣama alaṅkāra .

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**The Lord’s cakra also entered Vārāṇasī, in pursuit of the fiery demon, and proceeded to burn the city to the ground, including all its assembly halls and residential palaces with raised porches, its numerous marketplaces, gateways, watchtowers, warehouses and treasuries, and all the buildings housing elephants, horses, chariots and grains.**

**Комментарий:**

The cakra burned up Vārāṇasī, filled with citizens opposed to the Lord. The verb is in the previous verse. Aṭṭa means raised platform.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**After burning down the entire city of Vārāṇasī, the Lord’s cakra returned to the side of Kṛṣṇa, whose actions are effortless.**

**Комментарий:**

The cakra was beautiful to behold (sudarśanam).

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Any mortal who recounts this heroic pastime of the praiseworthy Lord, or who simply hears it attentively, will become freed from all sins.**

**Комментарий:**

One who recounts this exploit of the Lord in which he punished the people of Kāśī who were opposed to the Lord (etad) will be freed from all sins.

## Chapter 67 - Lord Balarāma Slays Dvivida Gorilla

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: I wish to hear further about Balarāma, the unlimited and immeasurable Supreme Lord, whose activities are all astounding. What else did he do?**

**Комментарий:**

In the sixty-seventh chapter, Balarāma sporting at Raivata Mountain, intoxicated with his beloveds, kills wicked Dvivida. “Being fully attached to Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, Śukadeva Gosvāmī has not spoken other pastimes of Balarāma.” Therefore, Parīkṣit Mahārāja asks him this question. Balarāma’s activities were astonishing (adbhuta-karmaṇaḥ), unseen that someone pulled a river near him in order to take bath. One cannot say that these were his only activities because he is unlimited (anantasya). And one cannot say,“you know all his activities,” since it is impossible to measure them even with the intelligence (aprameyasya).

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**ŚrīŚukadeva Gosvāmī said: There was an ape named Dvivida who was a friend of Narakāsura’s. This powerful Dvivida, the brother of Mainda, had been an associate of King Sugrīva.**

**Комментарий:**

The cause of his enmity with the Lord was that he was a friend of Naraka. Sugrīva-saciva means he had the ability to counsel. He was the brother of Mainda. Thus he had great strength. Though Dvivida was a devotee of Lord Rāmacandra and also a minister of the great devotee Sugrīva, he became opposed to the Lord by the bad association of Naraka. Because he did not respect Lakṣmaṇa due to his strength, he got that bad association.“But how could a devotee become corrupted in mind?” This should be understood to be arranged by the Lord to teach the despicable nature of disrespecting devotees and association with the wicked. Or else the Lord’s affection for his devotee is lost. And since he arranged it only for some time for the purpose that the devotee recognize the Lord again.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**To avenge the death of his friend \[Naraka\], the ape Dvivida ravaged the land, setting fires that burned cities, villages, mines and cowherd dwellings.**

**Комментарий:**

Paying debt to his friend, he set fire to the cities, and other places such that the kingdom would be destroyed by it.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Once, Dvivida tore up a number of mountains and used them to devastate all the neighboring kingdoms, especially the province of Ānarta, wherein dwelt his friend’s killer, Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Saḥ refers to Dvivida. Mitra-hā refers to Kṛṣṇa, the killer of Dvivida’s friend.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Another time he entered the ocean and, with the strength of ten thousand elephants, churned up its water with his arms and thus submerged the coastal regions.**

**Комментарий:**

He submerged places on the shore of the ocean (velā-kūlān). Masculine kūlān is Vedic usage (it should have been kūlāni).

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**The wicked ape tore down the trees in the hermitages of exalted sages and contaminated their sacrificial fires with his feces and urine.**

**Комментарий:**

Agnīn refers to the āhavanīya and other fires.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Just as a wasp imprisons smaller insects, he arrogantly threw both men and women into caves in a mountain valley and sealed the caves shut with boulders.**

**Комментарий:**

He sealed (apyadhāt) the opening of the caves with stones. Peśaskārī is a wasp.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Once, while Dvivida was thus engaged in harassing the neighboring kingdoms and polluting women of respectable families, hearing very sweet singing coming from Raivataka Mountain, he went there.**

### Text 9-10

**Перевод:**

**There he saw Balarāma, the Lord of the Yadus, adorned with a garland of lotuses and appearing most attractive in every limb. He was singing amidst a crowd of young women, and since he had drunk vāruṇī liquor, his eyes rolled as if he were intoxicated. His body shone brilliantly as he behaved like an elephant in rut.**

**Комментарий:**

Prabhinnam means ruttish (elephant in rut).

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**The mischievous ape climbed a tree branch and then revealed his presence by shaking the trees and making an indistinct sound.**

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**When Baladeva’s consorts saw the ape’s impudence, they began to laugh. They were, after all, young girls who were fond of joking and prone to silliness.**

**Комментарий:**

The girls were by nature fickle (jāti-cāpalāḥ).

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Even as Balarāma looked on, Dvivida insulted the girls by making odd gestures with his eyebrows, coming right in front of them, and showing them his anus.**

**Комментарий:**

He insulted them by coming in front of them and urinating. He showed his anus to them (tāsām), while disrespecting Balarāma (expressed by the genitive form).

### Text 14-15

**Перевод:**

**Angered, Balarāma, the best of fighters, hurled a rock at him, but the cunning ape dodged the rock and grabbed the Lord’s pot of liquor. Further infuriating Balarāma by laughing and by ridiculing him, wicked Dvivida then broke the pot and offended the Lord even more by pulling at the clothing on the cot. Thus the powerful ape, puffed up with false pride, continued to insult Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

He disrespected Balarāma by touching him with his foot. The root heḍṛ which means “to disrespect” is used to denote excessive disrespect. The suffix ṇic is used in the sense of denoting the word’s own meaning. He pulled and tore up the cloth which was on the ot. Tormenting constantly (kadarthī-kṛtya), he insulted Balarāma.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma saw the ape’s rude behavior and thought of the disruptions he had created in the surrounding kingdoms. Thus the Lord angrily took up his club and his plow weapon, having decided to put his enemy to death.**

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Mighty Dvivida also came forward to do battle. Uprooting aśāla tree with one hand, he rushed toward Balarāma and struck him on the head with the tree trunk.**

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**But Saṅkarṣaṇa remained as motionless as a mountain and simply grabbed the log as it fell upon his head. He then struck Dvivida with his club, named Sunanda.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma grabbed the log. He struck Dvivida with his musala called Sunanda.

### Text 19-21

**Перевод:**

**Struck on the skull by the Lord’s club, Dvivida became brilliantly decorated by the outpour of blood, like a mountain beautified by red oxide. Ignoring the wound, Dvivida uprooted another tree, stripped it of leaves by brute force and struck the Lord again. Now enraged, Balarāma shattered the tree into hundreds of pieces, upon which Dvivida grabbed yet another tree and furiously hit the Lord again. This tree, too, the Lord smashed into hundreds of pieces.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma struck him on a particular part of the head (mastiṣkaḥ). Gaurikayā means “with iron mineral.” Dvivida ignored the wound. Dvivida attacked with another tree. Balarāma smashed that tree also.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Thus fighting the Lord, who again and again demolished the trees he was attacked with, Dvivida kept on uprooting trees from all sides until the forest was left treeless.**

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**The angry ape then released a rain of stones upon Balarāma, but the wielder of the club easily pulverized them all.**

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Dvivida, the most powerful of apes, now clenched his fists at the end of his palm-tree-sized arms, came before the son of Rohiṇī and beat his fists against the Lord’s chest.**

**Комментарий:**

He beat (arūrajat) with his fists.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**The furious Lord of the Yādavas then threw aside his club and plow and with his bare hands hammered a blow upon Dvivida’s collarbone. The ape collapsed, vomiting blood.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma then fought without weapons. Balarāma crushed the gorilla’s collarbone (jatrau).

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**When he fell, O tiger among the Kurus, Raivataka Mountain shook, along with its cliffs and trees, like a wind-tossed boat at sea.**

**Комментарий:**

Raivata shook with its cliffs (sa-ṭaṅkaḥ). Taṅka means the sides of a mountain according to Tri-kāṇda-śeṣa.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**In the heavens the devatās, jīvanmuktas and great sages cried out, “Victory to you! Obeisances to you! Excellent! Well done!” and showered flowers upon the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

The best (indrāṇām) of the devatās, siddhas and sages shouted “Very good!”

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Having thus killed Dvivida, who had disturbed the whole world, the Supreme Lord returned to his capital as the people along the way chanted his glories.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma was endowed with omniscience (bhagavān). Thus it is suggested that knowing that people were confined to the caves of mountains by Dvivida, he freed them. Dvivida had caused destruction (vyatikaram) of the world.

## Chapter 68 - The Marriage of Sāmba

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, Jāmbavatī’s son Sāmba, ever victorious in battle, kidnapped Duryodhana’s daughter Lakṣmaṇā from her svayaṁ-vara ceremony.**

**Комментарий:**

In the sixty-eighth chapter, after Sāmba is bound by the Kurus, Balarāma, angry at the insulting words of the Kurus, pulls Hastināpura to free Sāmba. Another pastime of Balarāma is related. Sāmba was ever victorious in battle (samitiṁ-jayaḥ). He was called Sāmba because he always stayed with his mother. They had great affection for each other. Thus in general the phrase jāmbavatī-sutaḥ modifies the word sāmba everywhere (in Bhāgavatam).

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**The angry Kurus said: This ill-behaved boy has offended us, forcibly kidnapping our unmarried daughter against her will.**

**Комментарий:**

The boy has not been taught by his parents (durvinītaḥ). It seemed that she did not want to marry him (akāmām), but actually, she had hidden love for him.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Arrest this ill-behaved Sāmba! What will the Vṛṣṇis do? By our grace they are ruling land that we have granted them.**

**Комментарий:**

Badhnīta (bind him) suggests that they forbade killing him. They enjoy land given by us. They are not kings.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**If the Vṛṣṇis come here when they learn that their son has been captured, we will break their pride. Thus they’ll become subdued, like bodily senses brought under strict control.**

**Комментарий:**

They will be under our control (śamaṁ yānti) like senses (prāṇāḥ) brought under control.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**After saying this and having their plan sanctioned by the senior member of the Kuru dynasty, Karṇa, Śala, Bhūri, Yajñaketu and Duryodhana set out to attack Sāmba.**

**Комментарий:**

Śala, Bhūri and Yajñaketu (Bhuriśravā) were sons of Somadatta. The elders like Bhīṣma approved.“Since Sāmba has touched this maiden already, he must be the husband, for it would be improper to marry her to anyone else. To show our bravery and his impropriety however, we should capture him but not kill him.” Actually he approved of the act so that Balarāma would break their false pride. There were a total of six of them (including Bhīṣma).

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Duryodhana and his companions rushing toward him, Sāmba, the great chariot-fighter, took up his splendid bow and stood alone like a lion.**

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Determined to capture him, the angry bowmen led by Karṇa shouted at Sāmba, “Stand and fight! Stand and fight!” They came straight for him and showered him with arrows.**

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**O best of the Kurus, as Kṛṣṇa’s astonishing son Sāmba was being unjustly harassed by the Kurus, that darling of the Yadu dynasty did not tolerate their attack, any more than a lion would tolerate an attack by puny animals.**

**Комментарий:**

Attacked unjustly (apa-viddhaḥ) Sāmba did not tolerate it. He was Kṛṣṇa’s son (acintyārbhaḥ). Thus only by Lord’s will, whose result was to show the prowess of Balarāma, was he bound. Otherwise who could bind his son?

### Text 9-10

**Перевод:**

**Twanging his wonderful bow, heroic Sāmba struck with arrows the six warriors headed by Karṇa. He pierced the six chariots with as many arrows, each team of four horses with four arrows, and each chariot driver with a single arrow, and he similarly struck the great bowmen who commanded the chariots. The enemy warriors congratulated Sāmba for this display of prowess.**

**Комментарий:**

Sāmba killed the four horses of each chariot with four arrows. This indicates pervasion (he did this to all six warriors). The six warriors praised this act of Sāmba.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**But they forced him down from his chariot, and thereupon four of them struck his four horses, one of them struck down his chariot driver, and another broke his bow.**

**Комментарий:**

Karṇa (ekaḥ) struck his chariot and Bhīṣma (anyaḥ) broke his bow.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Having deprived Sāmba of his chariot during the fight, the Kuru warriors tied him up with great difficulty and then returned victorious to their city, taking the young boy and their princess.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking (verb omitted) the boy and girl they returned to the city.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**
