**O King, when the Yādavas heard news of this from Nārada, they became angry. Urged on by King Ugrasena, they prepared for war against the Kurus.**

**Комментарий:**

They were urged on by Ugrasena, but not by Kṛṣṇa since he had given control of the kingdom to Ugrasena and it was not proper to make such efforts for his son while Ugrasena was present.

### Text 14-15

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma, however, cooled the tempers of the Vṛṣṇi heroes, who had already put on their armor. He who purifies the age of quarrel did not want a quarrel between the Kurus and Vṛṣṇis. Thus, accompanied by brāhmaṇas and family elders, he went to Hastināpura on his chariot, which was as effulgent as the sun. As he went, he appeared like the moon surrounded by the ruling planets.**

**Комментарий:**

Pacifying them, Balarāma went since he did not want a quarrel between the two families.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Upon arriving at Hastināpura, Balarāma remained in a garden outside the city and sent Uddhava ahead to probe King Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s intentions.**

**Комментарий:**

He sent Uddhava to inquire about their intentions.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**After he had offered proper respects to Dhṛtarāṣṭra and to Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Bāhlika and Duryodhana, Uddhava informed them that Balarāma had arrived.**

**Комментарий:**

The Pāṇḍavas are not mentioned since they were now living in Indraprastha.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Overjoyed to hear that Balarāma, their dearmost friend, had come, they first honored Uddhava and then went forth to meet the Lord, carrying auspicious offerings in their hands.**

**Комментарий:**

They honored Uddhava (arcayitvā).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**They approached Balarāma and worshipped him with gifts of cows and arghya, as was fitting. Those among the Kurus who understood his true power bowed down to him, touching their heads to the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

Meeting with Balarāma, those among them such as Bhīṣma and others, knowing Balarāma’s powers, offered respects.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**After both parties had heard that their relatives were doing well and both had inquired into each other’s welfare and health, Balarāma without fear spoke to the Kurus as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Having mutually asked and heard about their relatives’ welfare and health, when they remained there, Balarāma spoke without fear (aviklavaṁ).

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**\[Balarāma said:\] King Ugrasena is our master and the ruler of kings. With undivided attention you should hear what he has ordered you to do, and then you should do it at once.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing with attention what Ugrasena has ordered you, do it. Otherwise he may punish you. Ordering was appropriate since he is a ruler of even kings like you, because he is the master (prabhuḥ). He was a king because Yayati had forbidden the Yadus to be kings but he did not forbid them from being master of kings. Otherwise Indra and others would not have been his order-carriers.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**\[King Ugrasena has said:\] Even though by irreligious means many of you defeated and tied up a single opponent who follows the religious codes, still I am tolerating this for the sake of unity among family members.**

**Комментарий:**

Repeating what Ugrasena said, I tolerate (mṛṣye). Therefore, bringing him quickly, return him. He did not finish speaking because on hearing just that much, the Kauravas began to speak abusively.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Upon hearing Balarāma’s words, which were full of potency, courage and strength and were appropriate to his power, the Kauravas became furious and spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

They became angry upon hearing Balarāma’s words, which were filled with influence (vīrya), courage (śaurya) and strength (balam), befitting his position.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**\[The Kuru nobles said:\] Oh, how amazing this is! The force of time is indeed insurmountable: a lowly shoe now wants to climb on the head that bears the royal crown.**

**Комментарий:**

How amazing (aho)! But this is not surprising. By the sūtra beginning with supāṁ suluk (Pāṇini 7.1.29) kāla-gatyā instead of kāla-gatiḥ is Vedic usage. Time cannot be overcome. They give an example to illustrate the impossible situation. A leather shoe also desires to ascend to the head served by a crown.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**It is because these Vṛṣṇis are bound to us by marital ties that we have granted them equality, allowing them to share our beds, seats and meals. Indeed, it is we who have given them their royal thrones.**

**Комментарий:**

They explain further. By the marriage of Kunti to Pāṇdu, they are our brothers-in-law.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Only because we looked the other way could they enjoy the pair of yak-tail fans and the conch, white umbrella, throne, and royal bed.**

**Комментарий:**

It happened only because we neglected, giving up insistence that they should not use the cāmara, etc.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**No longer should the Yadus be allowed to use these royal symbols, which now cause trouble for those who gave them, like milk fed to poisonous snakes. Having prospered by our grace, these Yādavas have now lost all shame and are daring to command us!**

**Комментарий:**

The symbols of royalty now act unfavorably for us, the givers. They are like milk given to a serpent. Amṛtam instead of amṛtaiḥ is Vedic usage. They have prospered by our grace. We should take back the signs of the king from them.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**How would even Indra dare usurp anything that Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Arjuna or the other Kurus have not given him? It would be like a lamb claiming the lion’s kill.**

**Комментарий:**

“The cause of your anarthas is the pride that ‘Indra and others carry out our orders.’” Thinking thus they speak. How can he accept anything unless it is given by us? We regard even Indra to be a lamb. What are you (Yādavas)? Though Arjuna did not support them they mention his name for the sake of their self-respect.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bādarāyaṇi said: O best of the Bhāratas, after the arrogant Kurus, thoroughly puffed up by the opulence of their high birth and relations, had spoken these harsh words to Balarāma, they turned and went back to their city.**

**Комментарий:**

Greatly proud because of wealth in the form of their birth in good family (janma), friends like Bhīṣma, etc., (bandhu), those who were without courtesy (asabhyāḥ) such as Duryodhana, etc., making Balarāma hear harsh words, entered (āviśan) the city, quickly, completely turning their backs. Bhīṣma and some others remained however.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the bad character of the Kurus and hearing their nasty words, the infallible Balarāma became filled with rage. His countenance frightful to behold, he laughed repeatedly and spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing their anger (dauḥśīlyam), Balarāmā, full of eternal powers (acyutaḥ), overcome with anger, hard to look at because of his increasing frown (duṣprekṣyaḥ), laughed continuously from anger (pra-hasan).

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Balarāma said:\] “Clearly the many passions of these scoundrels have made them so proud that they do not want peace. Then let them be pacified by physical punishment, as animals are, with a stick.**

**Комментарий:**

They are proud because of good family, wealth, etc. Punishment is the only way to calm them, not conciliation.

### Text 32-33

**Перевод:**

**“Ah, only gradually was I able to calm the furious Yadus and Kṛṣṇa, who was also enraged. Desiring peace for these Kauravas, I came here. But they are so dull-headed, fond of quarrel and mischievous by nature that they have repeatedly disrespected me. Out of conceit they dared to address me with harsh words!**

**Комментарий:**

Although I am famous as their well-wisher, they have insulted me with bad words

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**“Is not King Ugrasena, the lord of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, fit to command, when Indra and other planetary rulers obey his orders?**

**Комментарий:**

He remembers their insulting words in six verses.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**“That same Kṛṣṇa who occupies the Sudharmā assembly hall and for his enjoyment took the pārijāta tree from the immortal devatās—that very Kṛṣṇa is not fit to sit on a royal throne?**

**Комментарий:**

Angry that the foolish Kurus have criticized Kṛṣṇa also by their words such asalaṁ yadūnām (verse 27), he speaks. Kṛṣṇa should not sit on the throne? He jokes.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**“The goddess of fortune herself, ruler of the entire universe, worships his feet. And does not the master of the goddess of fortune deserve the paraphernalia of a mortal king?**

**Комментарий:**

“How much of his glories can be described?”. Mahā-lakṣmī, his superior śakti (sākṣāt rīḥ), worships his two feet. What to speak of material Lakṣmī of Svarga?

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**The devatās with the best crowns take the dust of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, which is the source of holiness for all places of pilgrimage, on their heads. Great devatās like Brahmā and Śiva, and I, who are simply his part of parts, and even the goddess of fortune also carefully carry that dust on our heads. And still Kṛṣṇa is not fit to use the royal insignia or even sit on the royal throne?**

**Комментарий:**

The dust from his feet is held on the excellent crowns of devatās. That dust yields all desires (tīrtha) for the best of yogīs since he is the Lord of the universe. Brahmā, Śiva, who are greater than all, and more than them, I, who are aṁśas of his aṁśas (kalāyāḥ kalāḥ), carry his dust on our heads. Lakṣmī, the controller of all, carries that dust. Is such a person not fit for the throne? He laughs in anger.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**“We, Vṛṣṇis enjoy only whatever small parcel of land the Kurus allow us? And we are indeed shoes, whereas the Kurus are the head?**

**Комментарий:**

“The criticism was directed to the Yādvas, not to Kṛṣṇa.” He laughs and speaks. The land is given but even in that it is just a small piece. Because we are Yādavas, they also criticize us. Even angrier he says, “Are we the shoes?”

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**“Just see how these puffed-up Kurus are intoxicated with their so-called power, like ordinary drunken men! What actual ruler, with the power to command, would tolerate their foolish, harsh words?**

**Комментарий:**

Having joked with sarcastic words, Balarāma now speaks the truth. Which ruler, a punisher, would tolerate the words rough in sound and meaning, devoid of respect, of proud people, intoxicated as if with liquor? No one would.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**“Today I shall rid the earth of the Kauravas!” declared the furious Balarāma. Thus he took his plow weapon and rose up as if to set the three worlds ablaze.**

**Комментарий:**

This is what should be done.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**The Lord angrily dug up Hastināpura with the tip of his plow and began to drag it, intending to cast the entire city into the Ganges.**

**Комментарий:**

He dug up the city from the south with the tip of his plough which enlarged by his will and pulled it towards the current of Gaṅgā, digging up the foundation of the wall, in order to destroy it (prahariṣyan) by submerging it. He ordered the Ganges, “Except for Sāmba and his wife, you should destroy everyone in the city with your water,” since the purpose was to make them frightened. Some say that it foreboded their future danger.

### Text 42-43

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that their city was tumbling about like a raft at sea as it was being dragged away, and that it was about to fall into the Gaṅgā, the Kauravas became terrified. To save their lives they approached the Lord for shelter, taking their families with them. Placing Sāmba and Lakṣmaṇā in front, they joined their palms in supplication.**

**Комментарий:**

First, they saw the city wobbling, and then falling into the Gaṅga. Then they saw Balarāma pulling it. They desired to save their lives. This indicates that their pride was destroyed completely. They put Sāmba with Lakṣmaṇā in front to immediately please Balarāma.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**\[The Kauravas said:\] O bliss of the universe, shelter of everything! We know nothing of your power. Please excuse our offense, for we are ignorant and misguided.**

**Комментарий:**

They show his lordship.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**You alone cause the creation, maintenance and annihilation of the cosmos, and of you there is no prior cause. Indeed, O Lord, authorities say that the worlds are mere playthings for you as you perform your pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

You are Mahā-saṅkarṣaṇa. The worlds are your playthings. Lokavat tu līlā-kaivalyam: the Lord has pastimes similar to the activities of this world. (Brahma-sūtra [2.1.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vs/2.1.33))

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**O unlimited one of a thousand heads, as your pastime you carry this earthly globe upon one of your heads. At the time of annihilation you withdraw the entire universe within your body and, remaining all alone, lie down to rest.**

**Комментарий:**

It is proper that you, who are most merciful, protect us since you hold up the earth by your aṁśa called Śeṣa. O Ananta with a thousand heads! O Śeṣa! By one of your heads you easily hold up the earth. Even during naimittika-pralaya (at the end of every day of Brahmā), you protect the universe within your body as Garbhodakaśāyī and sleep. Even then you protect the universe. You are without a second (advitīyaḥ), since nothing else in the three worlds exists at that time.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**Your anger is meant for instructing everyone; it is not a manifestation of hatred or envy. O Supreme Lord, you sustain the pure mode of goodness, and you become angry only to maintain and protect this world.**

**Комментарий:**

Your anger is not out of hatred but for teaching everyone. You nourish (bibhrahtaḥ) sattva-guṇa, which is meant for maintenance, through the form of Kṣīrodakaśāyī. By establishing everyone within the rules of conduct you protect them. Otherwise the world would perish. The purpose of your anger is to protect observance of the good conduct.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**We bow down to You, O Soul of all beings, O wielder of all potencies, O tireless maker of the universe! Offering you obeisances, we take shelter of you.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing that he did not stop pulling the city, they bow down repeatedly by performing nāma-kīrtana, which is dear to him, and surrender. O antaryāmī of all jīvas (sarva-bhūtātman)! O supporter of all sensory functions of all jīvas (sarva-śakti-dhara)! O creator of the universe (viśva-karman)! O lord devoid of change such as fatigue (avyaya)! Since you are the father of the universe, you should protect us not destroy us.

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus propitiated by the Kurus, whose city was trembling and who were surrendering to him in great distress, Balarāma gave up his anger and was pleased with them. He said, “Do not be afraid.” He thus took away their fear.**

**Комментарий:**

Their city was shaking and moving (vepamānāyanaiḥ).

### Text 50-51

**Перевод:**

**Duryodhana, being very affectionate to his daughter, gave as her dowry 1,200 sixty-year-old elephants, 120,000 horses, 6,000 golden chariots shining like the sun, and 1,000 maidservants with jeweled lockets on their necks.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. He gave 1,200 sixty-year-old elephants and 120,000 horses.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord, chief of the Yādavas, accepted all these gifts and then took permission to leave with his son and daughter-inlaw after giving his devotees bliss.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhagavān refers to Balarāma.

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**Then Halāyudha entered Dvārakā and met his relatives, whose hearts were all bound to him in loving attachment. In the assembly hall he reported to the Yadu leaders everything about his dealings with the Kurus.**

**Комментарий:**

He entered his own city magnificently (pra-viṣṭaḥ), with singing and auspicious music and met his relatives Kṛṣṇa and others. Because of anurāga, they always watched the road for his return (anurakta-cetasaḥ). Among the leaders of the Yadus like Ugrasena, he told them all mainly about his valiant actions. He told only a little about the Kurus’ insulting words.

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**Even today the city of Hastināpura is visibly elevated on its southern side along the Ganges, thus showing the signs of Balarāma’s prowess.**

**Комментарий:**

Dakṣiṇataḥ means on the southern side of the city.

## Chapter 69 - Nārada Muni Visits Lord Kṛṣṇa’s Palaces in Dvārakā

### Text 1-6

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Hearing that Kṛṣṇa had killed Narakāsura and had alone married many brides, Nārada Muni desired to see the Lord in this situation. He thought, “It is quite amazing that in a single body Lord Kṛṣṇa simultaneously married sixteen thousand women, each in a separate palace.” Thus the sage of the devatās eagerly went to Dvārakā. The city was filled with the sounds of birds and bees flying about the parks and pleasure gardens, while its lakes, crowded with blooming indīvara, ambhoja, kahlāra, kumuda and utpala lotuses, resounded with the calls of swans and cranes. Dvārakā boasted nine hundred thousand royal palaces, all constructed with crystal and silver and decorated with huge emeralds. Inside these palaces, the furnishings were bedecked with gold and jewels. Traffic moved along a well laid-out system of boulevards, roads, intersections and marketplaces, and many assembly houses and temples graced the charming city. The roads, courtyards, yards and threshold altars were all sprinkled with water and shaded from the sun’s heat by banners waving from flagpoles.**

**Комментарий:**

In the sixty-ninth chapter, in each palace the Lord shows Nārada the nature of his one body to have many forms. Hearing about the death of Naraka, and how Kṛṣṇa married many brides, Nārada became astonished and wanted to see the Lord. His astonishment is described. This is most amazing. It is the manifestation of his śakti which is inconceivable to us. What is amazing? One person married sixteen thousand women.“But it is seen that others have had even more marriages than him. ” He has married them simultaneously. “But like Saubhari, Nārada could also expand himself into many forms simultaneously. Why was he surprised?” He married them all with one body. “But even in one body, since by having many long arms that is possible, why be surprised?” He was separately in each of the sixteen thousand palace yards surrounded by walls. With one body he married them all. Saubhari, and others, expanding their body enjoyed simultaneously with many women but not with one body. This is the difference between prakāśa and bodily expansions. For this reason (iti) he went to Dvārakā, endeavoring to fulfill his desire (utsukaḥ). Dvārakā is described in three and a half verses. It had lakes filled (churiteṣu) with lotuses. The palaces were beautiful (prakhyā) with sapphire embedded spires. The interiors had various furnishings made of gold and jewels (paricchadaiḥ). It had wide (vibhakta) main roads (rathyā) and other roads (patha), etc. It was attractive with horse stables (śāla) and individual assembly houses according to the various groups, as well as temples for the devatās. It had flapping flags which blocked the sun’s heat.

### Text 7-8

**Перевод:**

**In the city of Dvārakā was a beautiful private quarter worshipped by the planetary rulers. This district, where Viśvakarmā had shown all his divine skill, was the residential area of Kṛṣṇa, and thus it was gorgeously decorated by the sixteen thousand palaces of Kṛṣṇa’s queens. Nārada Muni entered an immense palace.**

**Комментарий:**

In Dvārakā, the palace of the Lord was worshipped by all the lokapālas. It was endowed with all wealth, where Viśvakarmā showed his skill completely. He manifested it by the instructions of the Lord but he did not make it by his own intelligence. It was decorated with sixteen thousand palaces. Nārada entered one house of the wives of the Lord. This was Rukmiṇī’s palace, very large (mahat) since in verse 14 it will be stated that the Lord immediately got up from Rukmiṇī’s bed (śrī-paryaṅkataḥ).

### Text 9-12

**Перевод:**

**Supporting the palace were coral pillars decoratively inlaid with vaiḍūrya gems. Sapphires bedecked the walls, and the floors glowed with perpetual brilliance. In that palace Tvaṣṭā had arranged canopies with hanging strands of pearls; there were also seats and beds fashioned of ivory and precious jewels. In attendance were many well-dressed maidservants bearing lockets on their necks, and also armor-clad guards with turbans, fine uniforms and jeweled earrings. The glow of numerous jewelstudded lamps dispelled all darkness in the palace. My dear King, on the ornate ridges of the roof danced loudly crying peacocks, who saw the fragrant aguru incense escaping through the holes of the latticed windows and mistook it for a cloud.**

**Комментарий:**

That palace is described in four verses. It had coral pillars with Vaiḍūrya inlay. It had sapphire walls. It has floors perpetually shining, that were never soiled. It had seats and beds. There were male servants in the form of young boys. The darkness in the house (missing word) was destroyed by lamps. Seeing the incense smoke from the rooms escape through the lattice holes and thinking it was a cloud, the peacocks danced on the colorful rooftops. O King!

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**In that palace the learned brāhmaṇa saw the Lord of the Sātvatas, Kṛṣṇa, together with his wife, who fanned him with a goldhandled yak-tail fan. She personally served him in this way, even though she was constantly attended by a thousand maidservants equal to her in personal character, beauty, youth and fine dress.**

**Комментарий:**

In that house Nārada saw Kṛṣṇa with Rukmiṇī, the mistress of the house. She was constantly attended by a thousand maidservants equal to her in qualities, beauty, age and fine dress.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**The Suprme Lord is the greatest upholder of dharma. Thus when he noticed Nārada, he rose at once from Rukmiṇī’s bed, bowed his crowned head at Nārada’s feet and, joining his palms, had the sage sit in his own seat.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing him with pleasant glance since he came suddenly, Kṛṣṇa immediately rose. He bowed his head to Nārada’s feet, touching them with attachment. The Lord did this because he was absorbed in the pastimes of instituting proper dharma. He made Nārada sit on his own jeweled seat.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**The Lord bathed Nārada’s feet and then put the water on his own head. Although Kṛṣṇa was most worthy of worship in the universe and the master of his devotees, and though the water that bathed the Lord’s own feet became the Ganges, the ultimate holy shrine, it was proper for him to behave in this way, for he favored the brāhmaṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The lord of the devotees bathed Nārada’s feet and holding the water on his own head, spoke, though he is the most worthy of worship in the universe (gurutamaḥ). The verb prāha (spoke) is in the next verse.“Is it not improper for him to wash the feet of his servant?” He served the brāhmaṇas (brahmaṇya-devaḥ). For he, whose names indicate his qualities, acting in this way was appropriate (yadguṇa-nāma-yuktam). He did not act like this for purifying himself. Because (yat) the water that bathes the Lord’s feet, the Gaṅgā, is perfect tīrtha. “But why did Nārada, his servant, accept this?” Because he is subservient to his master.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**After fully worshiping the great sage of the devatās according to Vedic injunctions, Kṛṣṇa, who is himself the original sage— Nārāyaṇa, the friend of Nara—conversed with Nārada, and the Lord’s measured speech was as sweet as nectar. Finally the Lord asked Nārada, “What may we do for you, our Lord and master?”**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa worshipped Nārada, best of sages, according to the rules described in scriptures. He spoke words of few syllables (mitayā), which were very sweet (amṛta-juṣṭayā). He said, “O master, since you are a brāhmaṇa, you are our master. What service can we do for your lordship? Please order us.” Kṛṣṇa was the seer of mantras (ṛṣiḥ), though ancient since he was the Supreme Lord, he was young (purāṇaḥ). He is Nārāyaṇa since he is the shelter of all tattvas. He performed pastimes with humans, he is Nara-sakha. It should not be said that “Nārāyaṇa of Badarīkāśrama, the friend of Nara (nara-sakhaḥ), appeared as Kṛṣṇa” since it is impossible that Svayaṁ Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa is an avatāra of his aṁśa, Kṣīrodakaśāyī. Kṛṣṇa is Nara-Nārāyaṇa since the two forms entered Kṛṣṇa when he appeared on earth. Others say that Kṛṣṇa is Nara-Nārāyaṇa since they are the aṁśa of his aṁśa.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Nārada said: O almighty Lord, it is no surprise that you, the ruler of all worlds, show friendship for all people and yet subdue the envious. As we well know, you descend by your sweet will in order to bestow bhakti and mukti to this universe by maintaining and protecting it. O most capable Lord! Thus your glories are widely sung.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way being subservient to the Lord’s will, though Nārada accepted worship by him, he is not distressed and explains that. O Lord! O master of all the planets! This is not astonishing for you, the master, who wishes well. Expecting, “What do you mean?” he speaks. You are the benefactor (maitrī) of all people. Sarvasya śaraṇaṁ suhṛt: the Lord is the shelter of all and the friend. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) Because you are the friend to all, you worship me, not because of respect.“Then why am I not the friend of Kaṁsa?” You subdue the wicked. This is not astonishing. Because you are master of all the planets, this also becomes a display of friendship. “How is that?” You descend on your own for giving the highest benefit (niḥśreyasāya) in the form of bhakti and liberation along with protecting and maintaining the universe. By your mercy, we know that properly. You manifest in the world to make some who are attracted into devotees and make others who are not attracted by bhakti seek liberation through distress. You worship me to make devotees.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Now I have seen your feet, which grant liberation to your devotees, which even Brahmā and other great personalities of unfathomable intelligence can only meditate upon within their hearts, and which those who have fallen into the well of material existence resort to for deliverance. Please favor me so that I may constantly think of you as I travel about.**

**Комментарий:**

“O best of heavenly sages! What is the purpose of suddenly coming here and seeing me? How many days will you stay?”

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Nārada then entered the palace of another of Kṛṣṇa’s wives, my dear King. He was eager to witness the yoga-māyā possessed by the master of all masters of mystic power.**

**Комментарий:**

After that, he entered the house of Satyabhāmā. It was previously mentioned that he thought of the Lord’s yogamāyā as most inconceivable (citraṁ bataitat). He wanted to experience without doubt that yoga-māyā by seeing its effects.

### Text 20-22

**Перевод:**

**There he saw the Lord playing at dice with his beloved consort and his friend Uddhava. Kṛṣṇa worshipped Nārada by standing up, offering him a seat, and so on, and then, as if he did not know, asked him, “When did you arrive? What can needy persons like us do for those who are full in themselves? In any case, my dear brāhmaṇa, please make my life auspicious.” Thus addressed, Nārada was astonished. He simply stood up silently and went to another palace.**

**Комментарий:**

In this house he saw Kṛṣṇa playing dice. Uddhava acted as the witness to the game of dice. Nārada was worshipped by the Lord. The Lord spoke to Nārada, who remained silent.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**This time Nārada saw that Kṛṣṇa was engaged as an affectionate father petting his small children. From there he entered another palace and saw Kṛṣṇa preparing to take his bath.**

**Комментарий:**

Nārada was praised and worshipped by the Lord even there. This should be understood in other verses as well. Since Kṛṣṇa was preparing for his bath, it was early morning. Fourteen and a half verses describe what Nārada observed (so the word observed has to be carried forward). Each sentence is generally just half a verse long.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**In one place the Lord was offering oblations into the sacrificial fires; in another, worshiping through the five mahā-yajñas; in another, feeding brāhmaṇas; and in yet another, eating the remnants of food left by brāhmaṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

Nārada saw Kṛṣṇa offering oblations (juhvantaṁ) into the sacrificial fires (vitāna-agnīn), the āhavanīya and other fires, through agnihotra in the forenoon. He was worshipping through mahā-yajñas— reciting the Vedas; offering oblations into the sacrificial fire; waiting on guests; making offerings to the forefathers; and offering a share of one’s food to living entities—in the noon. He fed the brāhmaṇas and ate the remnants in the afternoon.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Somewhere Kṛṣṇa was observing the rituals for worship at sunset by refraining from speech and quietly chanting the Gāyatrī mantra, and elsewhere he was moving about with sword and shield in the areas set aside for sword practice.**

**Комментарий:**

In some places he chanted the Gāyatrī silently. This is done at three times of the day beginning with morning. He was walking on the path meant for training in swordsmanship. This is a forenoon activity.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**In one place Gadāgraja was riding on horses, elephants and chariots, and in another place he was resting on his bed while bards recited his glories.**

**Комментарий:**

In some places he was moving about in various ways on horses, elephants and chariots. These are again activities of the forenoon. Lying on his bed while being praised is an activity at daybreak.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Somewhere he was consulting with royal ministers like Uddhava, and somewhere else he was enjoying in the water, surrounded by many society girls and queens.**

**Комментарий:**

Consulting was done in the evening. In other places he was surrounded by queens (abalā) and the best courtesans. This was in the afternoon.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Somewhere he was giving well-decorated cows to exalted brāhmaṇas, and elsewhere he was listening to the auspicious narration of epic histories and Purāṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

Giving cows in charity is an activity carried out in the forenoon. Smṛti says itihāsa-purāṇabhyaṁṣaṣṭha-saptamakau nayet: recitation of histories and Purāṇas takes place in the sixth and seventh parts of the day (afternoon). Maṅgalāni refers to Vedic sūktas expressing peace and sacred songs.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Somewhere Kṛṣṇa was found enjoying the company of a particular wife by exchanging joking words with her. Somewhere else he was found engaged, along with his wife, in religious ritualistic functions. Somewhere Kṛṣṇa was found engaged in matters of economic development, and somewhere else he was found enjoying.**

**Комментарий:**

Joking conversations (hāsa-kathayā) take place during the night. In some house he was engaged in dharma with faith (sevamāman). Elsewhere he was enjoying (kāmau) and elsewhere he was undertaking actions for attaining wealth (artha). These occur during both the day and the night, as appropriate.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Somewhere he was sitting alone, meditating on the Lord, who is transcendental to material nature, and somewhere he was rendering menial service to gurus, offering them desirable things and reverential worship.**

**Комментарий:**

The activity of meditation indicates the brāhma-muhūrta (dhyāyantam), the early morning hours before sunrise. The details in this regard are explained later. He was serving gurus like Garga as well as Vasudeva by offering all items they desired (kāmaiḥ) and all items suitable for enjoyment (bhogaiḥ) along with service.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**In one place he was planning battles in consultation with some of his advisers, and in another place he was making peace. Somewhere Keśava and Balarāma were together pondering the welfare of the pious.**

**Комментарий:**

In some places he was beginning to start battles or make peace. He was thinking, “How to create auspiciousness (śivam) for the Pāṇḍavas and other devotees (satām)?”

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Nārada saw Kṛṣṇa engaged in getting his sons and daughters married to suitable brides and bridegrooms at the appropriate time, and the marriage ceremonies were being performed with great pomp.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was having his sons and daughters married according to religious principles (vidhy-upayāpanam) to suitable brides and grooms. He was getting his sons married to wives suitable to them and his daughters married to husbands suitable to them using many opulent materials (vibhūtibhiḥ). Vibhūtibhiḥ is connected with the next verse too.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Nārada observed how Kṛṣṇa, the master of all yoga masters, arranged to send away his daughters and sons-in-law, and also to receive them home again, at the time of great holiday celebrations. All the citizens were astonished to see these celebrations.**

**Комментарий:**

At the end of festivals Kṛṣṇa was sending his daughters and their husbands from his home back to their own houses. At the beginning of the festivals, he was again bringing them from their houses. By that he was arranging great festivals. Seeing the festivals of the children of Kṛṣṇa, the master of great yogīs, even Indra and others (lokāḥ) became astonished (visismire).

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Somewhere he was worshiping all the devatās with elaborate sacrifices, and elsewhere he was fulfilling his religious obligations by doing public welfare work, such as the construction of wells, public parks and temples.**

**Комментарий:**

Sometimes Kṛṣṇa would worship the devatās (yajantaṁ devān), his vibhūtis (sva-kalāḥ) during Caitra (spring) or other auspicious times. At other times, such as the day commemorating the beginning of a yuga, Kṛṣṇa would perform works of public piety called pūrta by digging wells, constructing rest houses and temples. Ālaya refers to temples of Viṣṇu and the devatās.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**In another place he was on a hunting expedition. Mounted on his Sindhī horse and accompanied by the most heroic of the Yadus, he was killing animals meant for offering in sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

He rode horses from Sind province. He killed animals suitable for sacrifice (medhyān).

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Somewhere Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of mystic power, was moving about in disguise among the homes of ministers and other citizens in order to understand what each of them was thinking.**

**Комментарий:**

He was going in disguise amongst his ministers and in his own palaces since he was the master of yoga, capable of such disguises. He wanted to understand the intentions of his ministers and residents of his palaces because by the līlā-śakti his omniscience was covered and distinct ignorance was manifested.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Having thus seen this display of the Lord’s yogamāyā, Nārada mildly laughed and then addressed Hṛṣīkeśa, who was adopting the behavior of a human being.**

**Комментарий:**

Then (atha), seeing the appearance of the yogamāyā as described of the Lord endowed with human play, and who was also absorbed in those activities, Nārada smiled, since he was surprised at the Lord’s distinct ignorance, though he is omniscient, and on seeing within a moment various inverted timings. He covered the smile (iva) however, out of reverence understanding that he was his master.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**\[Nārada said:\] Now we understand your mystic potencies, which are difficult to comprehend, even for great mystics, O Supreme Soul, master of all mystic power. Only by serving your feet have I been able to perceive your powers.**

**Комментарий:**

“O great sage! What all did you see in wandering in my palaces?” O master of yoga! By serving your feet, may I know your yogamāyā. This is a prayer expressed in the imperative. I pray to know your yoga-māyā.“ But what is difficult to know for people like you?” The yoga-māyā is difficult to be seen even by yogīs like Śiva. What to speak of them knowing yoga-māyā and what at all of using yoga-māyā! That yoga-māyā manifests (nirbhātāḥ) only in you, the Supreme Lord (ātmani) since it is a feature of your svarūpa.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, please give me your leave. I will wander about the worlds, which are flooded with your fame, loudly singing about your pastimes, which purify the universe.**

**Комментарий:**

“Staying here, you will understand more”, Nārada then asks permission to leave. Seeing these astonishing pastimes of yours, I cannot maintain my steadiness. Thus I will go to tell this to the devotees situated in the fourteen worlds.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O brāhmaṇa, I am the speaker of dharma, its performer and sanctioner. I observe dharma to teach them to the world, my child, so do not be disturbed.**

**Комментарий:**

“I am greatly blissful in front of you, the Lord full of bliss. But I have experienced great sorrow because you have washed the feet of your servant. Thus I will meditate on you from far away. I cannot offend the Lord.” I am the speaker, performer of dharma, spoken by the Vedas and praise it when performed by others (tad-anumoditā). He shows that he is the ācārya of promoting dharma. Therefore (tat), a teaching the world which I have created, I, a householder kṣatriya, have enacted dharma by worshipping a brāhmaṇa according to the logic, yad yad ācarati sreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ: ‘Whatever a great person does, ordinary people follow.’ (BG [3.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/3.21)) Otherwise the world would be destroyed. Thus do not grieve. When I had not manifested my pastimes as the ācārya, you approached me after I killed Keśi and worshipped me profusely. Please remember that. Like creating the universe by my form with a thousand heads, this feature of an ācārya is fixed in my svarūpa during my human pastimes. I will enact it again. Please understand this. O son! He pacifies Nārada by showing affection. It is not an offense for the child to place his feet on his father’s lap.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus in every palace Nārada saw the Lord in his same personal form, executing the proper principles of religion that purify those engaged in household affairs.**

**Комментарий:**

By the order of the Lord, Nārada stayed five or six days. Every day he saw those pastimes. He saw the one form performing the pastimes in all the houses since it was said previously, ekena vapuṣā: in one body the Lord performed the pastimes (verse 2).

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Having repeatedly seen the vast mystic display of Kṛṣṇa, whose power is unlimited, the sage was amazed and filled with wonder.**

**Комментарий:**

This is further described. Nārada was constantly surprised. Because Nārada could travel at the speed of mind from being a master of yoga, in a moment he could be present in all the palaces. Still how could events of the whole day (60x24 minutes), not in order, manifest in an instant? How could the Lord appear ignorant when he is omniscient? Though Nārada was also omniscient, he was constantly astonished.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Nārada was greatly honored by Kṛṣṇa having faith related to artha, kāma and dharma. Thus fully satisfied, the sage departed, constantly remembering the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

He got permission to leave, in order to narrate everywhere this pastime. Nārada was worshipped by Kṛṣṇa who was filled with faith (śraddhitātmanā).

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**In this way the source of Nārāyaṇa imitated the ways of ordinary humans, manifesting his divine potencies for the benefit of all beings. Thus he enjoyed, dear King, in the company of his sixteen thousand exalted consorts. He was served by their shy, affectionate glances and laughter.**

**Комментарий:**

What was the Lord’s faith in artha, kāma and dharma? He who is the shelter of all tattvas, the Supreme Lord (nārāyaṇaḥ), imitated the pastimes which were in accordance with human beings. The pastimes are described. Possessing śakti characterized by mercy for the benefit of all (bhavāya), showing a human form by his mercy, easy to remember for humans by having a similar form, giving them liberation, he enjoyed pastimes easy to remember. He was served by smiles and friendly, shy glances of the queens.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa is the ultimate cause of universal creation, maintenance and destruction but in this avatāra, he performed activities which are non-different from himself. My dear King, anyone who chants about, hears about or simply appreciates the extraordinary activities will surely develop devotion for the Supreme Lord, the bestower of liberation.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes are not meant only to liberate everyone, but also to bestow prema-bhakti when undertaken by singing, etc. The Lord who is the cause of creation, maintenance (vṛtti) and destruction (vilaya) through his svāṁśas, manifested many activities as Kṛṣṇa. These activities were fixed in his svarūpa (ananya-viṣayāni). Prema (bhaktiḥ) develops in the person who chants or hears those activities.“But how to attain liberation?” One attains liberation on the path of glorifying the Lord’s activities (apavarga-mārge). Destruction of saṁsāra will happen by glorifying the Lord’s activities but being situated in a body happens according to the logic of snakeskin . Prema is the main result.

## Chapter 70 - Lord Kṛṣṇa’s Daily Activities

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: As dawn approached, the wives of Mādhava, each embraced around the neck by her husband, cursed the crowing roosters. The ladies were disturbed that now they would be separated from him.**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventieth chapter, Kṛṣṇa’s daily activities and deliberation in the Sudharma hall on hearing from a messenger and Nārada are described. In the previous chapter it was stated that Kṛṣṇa faithfully observed the principles of artha, dharma and kāma (SB [10.69.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/69.43)). In reply to the question on how Kṛṣṇa carried out dharma, this verse explains from brāhma-muhūrta. Patibhiḥ is in the plural since Kṛṣṇa had manifested many forms. Kṛṣṇa’s wives (madhavyaḥ) cursed the roosters, “You should become mute.”

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**The bees’ buzzing, caused by the fragrant breeze from the garden of mandāra trees, roused the birds from sleep. And when the birds began to sing loudly, they woke Kṛṣṇa like court poets reciting his glories.**

**Комментарий:**

When the bees hummed, awakened by the fragrance of the gentle breeze, the sleepless birds cooed like bards, waking up Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Lying in her beloved’s arms, Rukmiṇī did not like this most auspicious hour, for it meant she would lose his embrace.**

**Комментарий:**

Rukminī, representing other queens, could not tolerate this auspicious brāhma-muhūrta, understanding it as an obstacle (viśleṣāt) to Kṛṣṇa’s embrace.

### Text 4-5

**Перевод:**

**Mādhava would rise during the brahma-muhūrta period and touch water. With a clear mind he would then meditate upon himself, the single, self-luminous, unequaled and infallible Supreme Truth, known as Brahman (the greatest of all), who by his very nature ever dispels all contamination, and who through his personal energies, which cause the creation and destruction of this universe, manifests his own pure and blissful existence.**

**Комментарий:**

Rātreś caturdaśo bhāgo muhūrto brāhma ucyate: the fourteenth part of the night is called brāhma-muhūrta. At that time, rising from bed, performing ācamana, becoming stable in mind by prāṇāyāma (prasanna-karaṇaḥ), he meditated (dadhyau) on himself (ātmānam) beyond prakṛti (tamasaḥ param). Śruti says, āditya-varṇaṁtamasaḥ parastāt: the Lord, the color of the sun, is beyond prakṛti. (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad) This is further explained. He is one, since there are not multiple Supreme Lords. He manifests himself to himself (svayaṁjyotiḥ) since the śruti says: Ekam evādvayaṁ brahma: there is one Brahman alone. (Gopālatāpanī Upaniṣad) Ātma-prakāśam: the Lord is self-manifesting. (Nṛsiṁha-uttaratāpanīUpaniṣad) “But Śaṅkarṣaṇa and others are also the Supreme Lords.” They too are not different from him (ananyam). He is all forms, Svayaṁ Bhagavān, complete. He is devoid of change (avyayam). By his superior śakti (sva-saṁsthayā) he destroys all variety in māyā (kalmaṣaṁ). The reason for being beyond prakṛti (tamasaḥ paraṁ) is stated. Śruti says ayam ātmā apahata-pāpmā: the Lord is free of contamination. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) He is called brahman (brahmākhyaṁ). Brahmeti paramātmeti: he is called brahman and paramātmā. (SB [1.2.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.11)) His merciful nature is described. He produces bliss for the living beings (bhāva-nirvṛttim) which is known by his śaktis such as giving jñāna, etc., which cause destruction of saṁsāra (udbhava) of this world (asya). Imitating human activities, knowing all scriptures, people meditate on their ātmā and Paramātmā during brāhma-muhūrta. For Kṛṣṇa however, for whom this was a pastime, meditated on himself at that time, since there is no one superior to him. Mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat kiñcit asti dhanañjayaḥ: O Arjuna, there is no one superior to me.(BG 7.7) One should not be perplexed by the explanation that “he meditated on his impersonal self, his basis, at that time,” for there are no evidences for this. There are numerous evidences for the other explanation.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**That most saintly of personalities would then bathe in sanctified water, dress himself in lower and upper garments and perform the entire sequence of prescribed rituals, beginning with worship at dawn. After offering oblations into the sacred fire, Kṛṣṇa would silently chant the gāyatrī mantra.**

**Комментарий:**

He did many other activities. He was most learned in the activities beginning with sandhyopāsanam (sandyopagamādi-sattamaḥ). He chanted brahma-gāyatrī (brahma).

### Text 7-9

**Перевод:**

**Each day with attention the Lord worshipped the rising sun and propitiated the devatās, sages, forefathers, elders, brāhmaṇas and avatāra forms with worship. To those well-attired brāhmaṇas he would offer herds of tame and peaceful cows with gold-plated horns and pearl necklaces. These cows were also dressed in fine cloth, and the fronts of their hooves were plated with silver. Providers of abundant milk, they had each given birth only once and were accompanied by their calves. Daily the Lord gave many groups of 210,757, 072 cows to the learned brāhmaṇas, together with linen, deerskins and sesame seeds.**

**Комментарий:**

Three verses go together. He worshipped devatās, vibhūtis (kalās) of himself while being steady in those procedures (ātmavān). He offered cows which had given birth one time (gṛṣṭīnām), every day, every year, at every house. The word badvam ends in the conjunction of the consonants of d and v. The number badva is described: 1,400,000 divided by 107 is one badva or 13,084.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa would offer obeisances to the cows, brāhmaṇas and devatās, his elders and respected masters, and all living beings— all of whom are his expansions. Then he would touch auspicious things.**

**Комментарий:**

Devatā refers to śalagrāma and other forms. He would offer them respects though they are his own vibhūtis (ātma-saṁbhūtīḥ) for the purpose of honoring him as part of his human pastimes. Maṅgalāni refers to brown cow (which is very auspicious), etc.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**He would decorate his body, the very ornament of human society, with his own special clothes and jewelry and with unfading flower garlands and ointments.**

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**He would then look at ghee, a mirror, the best of cows, the brāhmaṇas and the devatās and see to it that the members of all the social classes living in the palace and throughout the city were satisfied with gifts. After this he would satisfy ministers by fulfilling all their desires. By this he became pleased.**

**Комментарий:**

Go-vṛṣa refers to the best of the cows. Though he had seen them during the worship, he sees them again for the auspiciousness of a journey. Prakṛtīḥ means ministers.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**After first distributing flower garlands, betel and sandalwood paste to the brāhmaṇas, he would give these gifts to his friends, ministers and wives, and finally he would partake of them himself.**

**Комментарий:**

He distributed garlands, etc., to brāhmaṇas and others in portions. Then he would accept them for enjoyment.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**By then the Lord’s driver would have brought his supremely wonderful chariot, yoked with Sugrīva and his other horses. His charioteer would bow down to the Lord and then stand before the city gate.**

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Holding on to his charioteer’s hands, Kṛṣṇa would mount the chariot, together with Sātyaki and Uddhava, just like the sun rising over the easternmost mountain.**

**Комментарий:**

He held the joined hands of the charioteer with his right hand. After sending off the brāhmaṇas he would mount the chariot.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**The palace women would look upon Kṛṣṇa with shy, loving glances, and thus he would get free from them only with difficulty. He would then set off, his smiling face captivating their minds.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse shows the situation before he mounted the chariot. The palace women glanced at him with shy loving glances hinting at their agitation. Their glances implied, “How can we tolerate the torment of being separated from you?” As he was about to move, he stopped. With difficulty freeing himself from the bondage of their glances, getting permission to leave, he smiled, suggesting a consolation, “My dear restless ladies, why are you so overwhelmed by this little bit of separation? After meeting my maternal grandfather, best of kings, I am quickly coming.” Attracting their minds by that smile, he left.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**The Lord, attended by all the Vṛṣṇis, would enter the Sudharmā assembly hall, which protects those who enter it from the six waves of material life, dear King.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way, exiting from all the huge palaces by his individual prakāśas (manifestations), in the jeweled courtyard amidst all the palaces, unseen by others, becoming one,Kṛṣṇa would enter the Sudharmā hall.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**As the almighty Supreme Lord would seat himself upon his exalted throne there in the assembly hall, he shone with his unique effulgence, illuminating all the quarters of space. Surrounded by the Yadus, lions among men, that best of the Yadus appeared like the moon amidst many stars.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was attended by the Yadus, who were best among men (nṛsiṁhair).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**And there, O King, jesters would entertain the Lord by displaying various comic moods, expert entertainers would perform for him, and female dancers would dance energetically.**

**Комментарий:**

Jesters in separate groups entertained (upatasthuḥ) the Lord.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**These performers would dance and sing to the sounds of mṛdaṅgas, vīṇās, murajas, flutes, cymbals and conchs, while professional poets, chroniclers and panegyrists would recite the Lord’s glories.**

**Комментарий:**

Some groups danced and others sang there. The professional poets (sūtas) offered praises.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Some brāhmaṇas sitting in that assembly hall would fluently chant Vedic mantras, while other persons recounted stories of past kings of pious renown.**

**Комментарий:**

Brāhmaṇas who were skillful at pronunciation of the Vedas (brahma-vādinaḥ), chanted them.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Once a certain person arrived in the assembly, O King, who had never been seen there before. The doorkeepers announced him to the Lord and then escorted him inside.**

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**That person bowed down to Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, and with joined palms he described to the Lord how a number of kings were suffering because Jarāsandha had imprisoned them.**

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Twenty thousand kings who had refused to submit absolutely to Jarāsandha during his world conquest had been forcibly imprisoned by him in the fortress named Girivraja.**

**Комментарий:**

Why did he imprison the kings? They did not submit (sannatim) to him by paying taxes. Twenty thousand kings (ayute dve), were in the fort named Girivraja. The purpose of imprisoning them is described by the Lord in Sabhā Parvā, Mahābhārata: Jarāsandha wanted to perform a sacrifice to Śiva, using all the kings. (Mahābhārata)

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**The kings said \[as related through their messenger\]: O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, O immeasurable Soul, destroyer of fear for those surrendered to you! Despite our separatist attitude, we have come to you for shelter out of fear of material existence.**

**Комментарий:**

Five verses explain their request to Kṛṣṇa. One expresses their surrender. We thought ourselves to be independent (pṛthagdhiyaḥ).

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**People in this world are always engaged in sinful activities and are thus bewildered about their real duty, which is to worship you according to your commandments. This activity would truly bring them good fortune. Let us offer our obeisances unto the all-powerful Lord, who is diligent and suddenly cuts down one’s stubborn hope for a long life in this world.**

**Комментарий:**

They describe their fear of material existence. People like us are absorbed in actions to attain material happiness (vikarmanirataḥ). They are negligent about the auspicious (kuśale) actions of worshipping you in the form of your bhakti described by you (udite) in verse such as, yat karosi yad aśnāsi: whatever you do and whatever you eat, do it for me. (BG [9.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.27)) This action is the real treasure (sve) of everyone, relieving one of material miseries and bestowing the pleasure of bliss in prema. The purpose for which people are engaged in vikarma, even that result is not achieved. You suddenly shatter (chinatty) our hopes for long life, being devoured by sickness and enemies. It is not possible to counteract this, for you are strong (balavān). We offer respects to you who are awake to cut down those hopes (animiṣāya). This is proper action for those opposed to you.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**You are the predominating Lord of the universe and have descended into this world with your personal power to protect the saintly and suppress the wicked. We cannot understand, O Lord, how anyone can transgress your law and still continue to enjoy the fruits of his work.**

**Комментарий:**

Though you, who are established in such conclusion, who have such nature, have appeared, it is greatly astonishing to us why those who are opposed to you are increasing in happiness. You are the Lord of the universe (jagad-inaḥ) and have appeared with your portion Saṅkarṣaṇa in this world. Yet others like Jarāsandha, the wicked, disregard your laws. O Lord! Why does a wicked person enjoy increase in happiness, the results of his karma (sva-kṛtam)? Or why does a person, though protected by you, experience suffering given by that wicked person, earned through his karmas (sva-kṛtam)? We cannot understand this. It is amazing that material karma is stronger than you.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, with this corpselike body, always full of fear, we bear the burden of the relative happiness of kings, which is just like a dream and dependent on others. Thus we have rejected the real happiness of the soul, which is obtained by your devotees. Being so very wretched, we simply suffer in this life under the spell of your illusory energy.**

**Комментарий:**

Even now, though suffering from Jarāsandha’s imprisonment, we maintain hopes of a kingdom because of your māyā. You who destroy the fear of the surrendered should not remove that hope. With bodies as if dead, filled with fear caused by continual diseases, etc., we carry the burden (dhuram) of attempts at conciliation and war, the happiness of kings produced by identity as a king, which is dependent on others due to being under the control of ministers and troops, and is like a dream due to being impermanent. Even now we do not give up those hopes. “Killing your enemy, I will give you your kingdoms.” Attaining kingdoms, attached to them because of your māyā, we will suffer. The present tense is used to indicate future since the future is near. We have rejected happiness which is famous, glorified in scriptures, not condemned like a king’s happiness. That happiness is naturally perfect in the ātmā, not generated by karma. It does not appear because of sense objects like sound or touch, but from you, who is satisfied by bhakti. It is obtained by lack of material desires (anīha) not by material desires. It is filled with the eight qualities of apahata-pāpma, etc.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, since your feet relieve the sorrow of those who surrender to them, please release us prisoners from the shackles of karma, manifest as the king of Magadha. Wielding alone the prowess of ten thousand maddened elephants, he has locked us up in his house just as a lion captures sheep.**

**Комментарий:**

They pray that “You alone should first release us from the bondage of karma created by your māyā.” Release us from the shackles of karma called Jarāsandha.“You should escape the shackles by your own valor.” That one person, wielding the power of ten thousand elephants has locked us kings in his house just as a lion captures sheep. We do not have prowess there.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**O wielder of the disc! Your strength is unlimited, and thus seventeen times you crushed Jarāsandha in battle. But then, absorbed in human affairs, you allowed him to defeat you once. Now he is so filled with pride that he dares to torment us, your subjects. O unconquerable one, please rectify this situation.**

**Комментарий:**

Hating you, he knows that we are surrendered to you and gives us even more pain now. O you who hold the Sudarśana cakra high! Fighting eighteen times with you, he was defeated seventeen times. He conquered you one time, since you were attached to running away in jest, acting like a human, though you have unlimited strength. Thus increased in his pride, he afflicts us, your citizens. O unconquered one! Please do what is proper in this situation.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The messenger continued: This is the message of the kings imprisoned by Jarāsandha, who all hanker for your audience, having surrendered to your feet. Please bestow good fortune on these poor souls.**

**Комментарий:**

The messenger continued. Please bestow good fortune of releasing the kings from his confinement and letting them see you (śaṁ).

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When the kings’ messenger had thus spoken, the sage of the devatās, Nārada, suddenly appeared. Bearing a mass of golden matted locks on his head, the supremely effulgent sage entered like the brilliant sun.**

**Комментарий:**

At this time Nārada, whose effulgence is like that of the supreme entity (parama-dyutiḥ), appeared playing his vīṇā before Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa is the worshippable master of even planetary rulers like Brahmā and Śiva, yet as soon as he saw that Nārada had arrived, he joyfully stood up along with his priest and ministers and retinue to receive the great sage and offer his respectful obeisances by bowing his head.**

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**After Nārada had accepted the seat offered to him, Kṛṣṇa honored the sage according to scriptural injunctions and, gratifying him with his affection, spoke the following truthful and pleasing words.**

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa said:\] Have the three worlds attained freedom from all fear today, for that is the influence of such a great personality as you, who travel at will throughout all the worlds?**

**Комментарий:**

Since it would be improper to ask you, who always possess auspiciousness, about your well being. Therefore, I will ask you if the three worlds are auspicious. Api svid indicates a question.“O Lord! How would I know of the well-being of the three worlds?” We attain great (bhūyān) news about events of all the worlds (guṇaḥ) from you who wander about in the worlds.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**There is nothing unknown to you within God’s creation. Therefore please tell us what the Pāṇḍavas intend to do.**

**Комментарий:**

Since you are omniscient, nothing is unknown to you in the planets created by the Lord. As a pastime, Kṛṣṇa indicates his humanness by this statement. For this reason, I ask what do the Pāṇḍavas intend to do? He suggests that among all people or planets, he has highest consideration for them.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Nārada said: I have seen many times the insurmountable power of your māyā, the creators of the universes and the possessors of māyā, O almighty one. O all-encompassing Lord, it does not surprise me serving your feet while covering my glory, moving among the created beings, as a fire covers its own light with smoke.**

**Комментарий:**

Nārada does not answer the proposition of the Lord that Nārada has made the three worlds fearless and the question concerning the Pāṇḍavas, but in response to the Lord’s statement that Nārada sees everything, he accepts that he has seen everything by being endowed with the śakti of the Lord. I have seen your māyā and in the planets made by your māyā, the creators of universes such as Brahmā, possessing a portion of that Like the sun, you (Nārada) can travel everywhere in the three worlds, and like the air you can penetrate the internal region of everyone. As such, you are as good as the allpervasive Supersoul. (SB [1.5.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/5.7)) Following this statement of Vyāsa, I have seen this by your śaktis, or by my śaktis filled with bhakti to you. O great Lord! It is not surprising to me, who serve your feet, wandering about among living entities like fire with its effulgence covered.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Who can properly understand your purpose since you expand and control this whole creation by your māyā. I offer respects to you, who manifests this universe in its present form, and are completely different from me.**

**Комментарий:**

Your question is part of your pastimes since you are omniscient. Who can properly understand your activities (īhitam)? No one can. Who are you? You create the universe having three worlds, which should be inquired about and set it into motion as a controller by your will (sva-māyayā). Your universe appears like a lump of crystal formed by your hand (vidyamānātmatayā). Therefore, I offer respects to you, different from the jīva (sva-vilakṣaṇātmane), inconceivable. Thus those questions of yours, are your pastime, difficult to understand since you are omniscient.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Therefore I surrender unto you, who lights the lamp of your fame through various pastimes of various avatāras for the benefit of the jīvas who do not know the method of becoming free from saṁsāra and the material body, which brings them grief.**

**Комментарий:**

But this question arises from your human pastimes. I surrender to you, who to show your tattva, shine the lamp, in the form of your fame, appearing as līlāvatāras for the jīva who wanders about in various species (saṁsārataḥ), not knowing about liberation from the bondage of a body (śarīrataḥ). I have seen that people averse to your glories in the three worlds are full of fear and people who are favorable to them to be without fear.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Nonetheless, O Supreme Truth playing the part of a human being, I shall tell you what your devotee Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja, the son of your father’s sister, intends to do.**

**Комментарий:**

Now Nārada answers Kṛṣṇa’s second question about the intentions of the Pāṇḍavas in five verses (41-45). Even though you know everything, I will tell you completely (āśrāvaye), since you are imitating the pastimes of an ordinary human being (nara-lokaviḍambanam).

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Desiring unrivaled sovereignty, King Yudhiṣṭhira intends to worship you with the greatest fire sacrifice, the Rājasūya. Please bless his endeavor.**

**Комментарий:**

Yudhiṣṭhira desires to preach your supremacy (pārameṣṭhyakāmaḥ) everywhere. It will be said: Therefore, O Lord of lords, let the people of this world see the power of devotional service rendered to your lotus feet. Please show them, O almighty one, the position of those Kurus and Sṛñjayas who worship you, and the position of those who do not. (SB [10.72.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/72.5)) The word pārameṣṭhya, is formed by applying the suffix aṇ in the sense of tasyedaṁ (Pāṇini 4.3.120) to the word parameṣṭhin (Kṛṣṇa) and then applying ṣyañ in the meaning of its own sense.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, exalted devatās and virtuous kings, eager to see you, will all come to that best of sacrifices.**

**Комментарий:**

Not only should you allow that while staying here, but you should also go there. O Lord (deva)! Yaśasvinaḥ means “having good conduct.”

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, even outcastes are purified by hearing and chanting your glories and meditating upon you, the Absolute Truth. What then to speak of those who see and touch you?**

**Комментарий:**

“What is the result of their desiring to see me?” People become purified of the fault of their birth, etc., by hearing of, chanting of and meditating on you, who are the form of Brahman (brahmamayasya) since the śruti says, brahmānadaika-vigrahaḥ: you are the spiritual form of bliss (Rāma-uttara-tāpanī Upaniṣad). What to speak of those viewers who possess the experience of touching you by seeing?

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Your purifying, most excellent fame is known throughout the universe, including the higher, middle and lower planetary systems. The water that washes your lotus feet, known in the higher planetary systems as the Mandākinī River, in the lower planetary systems as the Bhogavatī and in this earthly planetary system as the Ganges, purifies the entire universe.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why are they so eager to see me?” O auspiciousness for the world! Your pure fame, which is spread throughout heaven, earth and the subterranean region like a canopy decorating the universal directions (dig-vitānam), purifies the whole universe. In the same way the water of your feet purifies the whole universe, in the form of Mandākinī in heaven, as Bhogavatī in Pātālā and as Gaṅgā on earth. To show that these are the three main waters for purification, the word ca is repeated thrice. They desire to see you because their minds have been purified by this water.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When his supporters, the Yādavas, objected to this proposal out of eagerness to defeat Jarāsandha, Keśava turned to his servant Uddhava and, smiling, addressed him with fine words.**

**Комментарий:**

When the assembled Yādavas, Kṛṣṇa’s allies, were not interested in Nārada’s proposal because they were intent on conquering Jarāsandha, Kṛṣṇa, smiling by having spread to Uddhava’s heart the meanings of the words that he himself approved, spoke to Uddhava. Bhṛtyam indicates that he did this to show his servant’s (Uddhava’s) great intelligence.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: You are indeed our best eye and closest friend, for you know perfectly the relative value of various kinds of counsel. Therefore please tell us what should be done in this situation. We trust your judgment and shall do as you say.**

**Комментарий:**

You alone (hi) are the eye of the Yādavas since you act for our benefit without personal motives (suhṛt) and know thoroughly how to give counsel. You are more than the ordinary eye, for by your counsel we can see the future and distant things. For this reason, you should say which of these two actions should be done first. You should not say that they (the Yādavas) will not accept your words. We will accept your decision with faith and carry it out. This shows the great good fortune of his servant Uddhava.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Thus requested by his master, who, though omniscient, acted as if perplexed, Uddhava took this order upon his head and replied as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Being instructed with affection (upāmantritaḥ) with devotion he took the order on his head. This means he joined his hands and placed them on his head. His master was omniscient but acted as if ignorant.

## Chapter 71 - Lord Kṛṣṇa Travels to Indraprastha

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus heard the statements of Nārada, and understanding the opinions of both the assembly and Kṛṣṇa, the great-minded Uddhava began to speak.**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventy-first chapter, Kṛṣṇa, on Uddhava’s advice, goes to Indraprastha with his queens and his army to give joy. Uddhava heard the statements of Kṛṣṇa, Nārada Muni, the assembly members, and the messenger from the imprisoned kings (ca) and then spoke on Kṛṣṇa’s order. Nārada wanted Kṛṣṇa to go to Indraprastha. The assembly and the messenger wanted Kṛṣṇa to kill Jarāsandha and protect the kings, and Kṛṣṇa wanted both. Uddhava is called mahā-matiḥ (great-minded) since all became joyful by his supporting everyone’s opinion.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Uddhava said: O Lord, as the sage advised, you should help your cousin fulfill his plan for performing the Rājasūya sacrifice, and you should also protect the kings who are begging for your shelter.**

**Комментарий:**

You should help Yudhiṣṭhira, your cousin, who is performing the sacrifice (yakṣyataḥ), which was mentioned by Nārada. You should also protect those who desire your shelter, which is the opinion of the assembly and the messenger.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Only one who has conquered all opponents in every direction can perform the Rājasūya sacrifice, O almighty one. Thus, in my opinion, conquering Jarāsandha will serve both purposes.**

**Комментарий:**

The best strategy is that by which both purposes can be achieved by a single act. Both purposes, completion of the Rājasūya sacrifice and protecting the kings, will be accomplished by conquering all directions. Without conquering all the directions, the Rājasūya sacrifice cannot occur, and without killing Jarāsandha, one cannot conquer the directions. First the Lord should accept the invitation to the Rājasūya sacrifice. The request to protect the kings, on the other hand, will be fulfilled as a secondary result of fulfilling that first request.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**By this decision there will be great gain for us, and you will save the kings. Thus, Govinda, you will be glorified.**

**Комментарий:**

Even for us members of the assembly, in your going to the Rājasūya sacrifice there is a great gain – the death of Jarāsandha.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**The invincible Jarāsandha is as strong as ten thousand elephants. Other powerful warriors cannot defeat him. Only Bhīma is equal to him in strength.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing that the Yādavas were extremely eager to kill Jarāsandha, Uddhava speaks. Other warriors though stronger than him, cannot defeat Jarāsandha. For he is extremely skillful in battle and very deceptive. He can only be killed by Bhīma, who is his equal in strength. I have deduced this from astrological scriptures I learned from my guru, Bṛhaspati.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**He will be defeated in a single combat, not when he is with his hundred military divisions. Now, Jarāsandha is so devoted to brahminical culture that he never refuses requests from brāhmaṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

Jarāsandha should be defeated by Bhīma alone in single combat, because otherwise Jarāsandha is armed with one hundred akṣauhiṇīs. Dvai-rathe is derived from dvi-ratha which means “where only two bodies are the warriors.” It means combat between two single opponents. It is formed by adding the suffix aṇ to dvi-ratha by prajñādibhyaś ca (Pāṇini 5.4.38). Or it means “accomplished by two bodies,” by the rule tena nirvṛttam (Pāṇini 4.2.68). But Jarāsandha will engage his troops in the fight, then how can a fight in single combat be obtained? Requested by brāhmaṇas, he will not refuse. But rather he will oblige.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Bhīma should go to him disguised as a brāhmaṇa and beg charity. Thus he will obtain single combat with Jarāsandha, and in your presence Bhīma will no doubt kill him.**

**Комментарий:**

“But because of his strength and craftiness Jarāsandha could win sometimes.” If Bhīma fights in your presence, he will be able to kill Jarāsandha.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Even Brahmā and Śiva act only as your instruments in cosmic creation and annihilation, which are ultimately done by you, the Supreme Lord, in your invisible aspect of time.**

**Комментарий:**

“But what will be the effect of my merely being present without doing anything?” Time, formless is the śakti of Paramātmā (īśasya kālasya arūpinaḥ). The words īśasya and kālasya refers to different subjects though both are in genetive. Arūpinaḥ modifies kālasya. sva-kāla-śaktyā kṣapayaṁś cared bhuvi Lord moves on earth to diminish its burden by his own potency in the form of time. (SB [10.1.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.22)) Brahmā and Śiva, creating and destroying the universe, are only (param) the instruments (nimitta) of time. They are not the principal agents. Bhīma is only the nimitta in killing Jarāsandha. You, being nearby, are the chief killer, like time. You will give fame to Bhīma as you give to Brahmā and Śiva. This is the idea since such connection (of words) is possible in this verse.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**In their homes, the godly wives of the imprisoned kings sing of your noble deeds—about how you will kill their husbands’ enemy and deliver them. The gopīs also sing your glories—how you killed Śaṅkhacūḍa and delivered them from his hands. The surrendered souls sing of your killing the enemy of Gajendra. The sages sing of your killing the enemy of Sītā. We Yadus sing of your killing the enemies of Vasudeva and Devakī.**

**Комментарий:**

Though you are famous for punishing the wicked and protecting the righteous, now, in killing of Jarāsandha your glories will be even greater. The wives (devyaḥ) of the kings imprisoned by Jarāsandha sing about your splendid activities in their homes, while taking care of their children. What are those activities? They sing about your future killing of Jarāsandha and freeing of their husbands, having been informed of this by the sages. Their mothers tell them, “O child. Śrī Kṛṣṇa will kill Jarāsandha and release your father.” Uddhava gives examples. It is just as the gopīs, gathering together, sang about the enemy Śaṅkhacūḍa being killed and their deliverance from his captivity . O friends, Kṛṣṇa, comforting us, will kill the snake of separation just as he killed Śaṅkhacūḍa. Just as these women reunite with their husbands after the death of Jarāsandha, similarly you should reunite with the gopīs. Moreover, just as the wives and gopīs sing about you, those who have surrendered to you, the self-satisfied sages (labdha-śaraṇāḥ), and we, your servants (vayaṁ), also sing your glories comforting each other. “What is that?” You killed the crocodile enemy of the king of elephants and delivered him. You killed Rāvaṇa, the enemy of Sītā, and Kaṁsa, the enemy of your parents, Vasudeva and Devakī. And you delivered each of them from their enemies. O sages! O servants! Do not lament. Merciful Kṛṣṇa, after removing all anarthas, will bestow even to us, nearness to him and service to him as he did to Gajendra and others.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**O Kṛṣṇa, the killing of Jarāsandha, which is certainly a reaction of his past sins, will bring immense benefit. It will make possible the sacrificial ceremony you desire.**

**Комментарий:**

It is necessary to go for the purpose of the Rājasūya sacrifice. Previously two purposes were mentioned, now it is said “many purposes” (bhūry-arthāya), namely the previous two purposes (of protecting the kings and executing Rājasūya sacrifice); the killing of Śiśupāla easily—which you need to do, the special purposes that I indicated—the Bhārata war brought about by Kali due to Duryodhana’s pride being bruised in the assembly. All this will happen when the Lord goes there. The word prāyaḥ (certainly) is used to express conjecture. Killing Jarāsandha will be most beneficial by allowing the Rājasūya sacrifice to take place (pāka-vipākena). That which cooks (on its own) is pākaḥ. The word is formed by applying the affix ghañ after the root pac (to cook) in the sense of karma-kartari (the object being the subject of the verb) since it can be applied in multiple senses. Its thorough cooking or its perfection is vipāka. Some read it as pāpa-vipākena. It means “due to the transformation of the sins of Śiśupāla and Jarāsandha into their destruction.” Even you approve this sacrifice. Uddhava used equivocal words (pākavipākena) so that this meaning is confidential.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, Devarṣi Nārada, the Yadu elders and Kṛṣṇa all welcomed Uddhava’s proposal, which was entirely auspicious and infallible.**

**Комментарий:**

The word acyutam (infallible) indicates that Uddhava’s proposal was “without error,” since it was reasonable. The term yadu-vṛddhāḥ means that it was the senior members, not the junior ones, who welcomed the proposal. Young princes such as Aniruddha did not like Uddhava’s proposal, since they were eager to fight Jarāsandha’s army immediately.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**The almighty Lord, the son of Devakī, begged his superiors for permission to leave. Then he ordered his servants, headed by Dāruka and Jaitra, to prepare for departure.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa took permission from the elders such as Vasudeva.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**O slayer of enemies, after he had arranged for the departure of his wives, children and baggage and taken leave of Saṅkarṣaṇa and King Ugrasena, Kṛṣṇa mounted his chariot, which had been brought by his driver. It flew a flag marked with the emblem of Garuḍa.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa arranged for his wives (avarodhān) to go along, since they had also been invited to the Rājasūya sacrifice and were eager to attend.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**As the vibrations resounding from mṛdaṅgas, bherīs, kettledrums, conchs and gomukhas filled the sky in all directions, Kṛṣṇa set out on his journey. He was accompanied by the chief officers of his corps of chariots, elephants, infantry and cavalry and surrounded on all sides by his fierce personal guards.**

**Комментарий:**

Dvipā means elephants, bhaṭa means infantry soldiers and sādi means cavalry.
