Together with the leaders of his chariot corps and surrounded by his own fierce (karālayā) army, Kṛṣṇa went out of the city wherein all the directions (kakubhaḥ) were filled with musical vibrations of horns and mṛdaṅgas. The word kakubhā is found to end with even the feminine affix ṭāp.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Acyuta’s faithful wives, along with their children, followed the Lord on golden palanquins carried by powerful men. The queens were adorned with fine clothing, ornaments, fragrant oils and flower garlands, and they were surrounded on all sides by soldiers carrying swords and shields in their hands.**

**Комментарий:**

The faithful queens, with their sons, dressed in fine cloth, followed their husband in golden palanquins carried by men swift as horses (nṛ-vāji). Or they followed in palanquins, accompanied by men and horses.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**On all sides proceeded finely adorned women—attendants of the royal household, as well as courtesans. They rode on palanquins and camels, bulls and buffalo, donkeys, mules, bullock carts and elephants. Their conveyances were fully loaded with grass tents, blankets, clothes and other items for the trip.**

**Комментарий:**

Aśvatarī is a female mule born from a female donkey through a male horse. Parijana means attendants like barbers, washermen, etc. The wives of these attendants and the courtesans followed after him with palanquins, camels, oxen (go), buffaloes, donkeys, mules, carts and female elephants. The huts were made of uśīra grass. They had grass tents, blankets, clothes and other items for the trip. The equipment was tied tightly (adhiyujya) on the camels, etc.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**The Lord’s army shone brightly in the day with royal umbrellas, cāmara fans and huge flagpoles with waving banners, fine weapons, jewelry, helmets and armor, surpassing the sun. Thus Lord Kṛṣṇa’s army, noisy with shouts and clatter, appeared like an ocean stirring with agitated waves and timiṅgila fish.**

**Комментарий:**

During the day the army shone with the rays of the sun. The army made noise like an ocean stirring with agitated waves and timiṅgila fish.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Nārada was honored by Kṛṣṇa, who bowed to him. All of Nārada’s senses were satisfied by his meeting with Kṛṣṇa. Thus, having heard the decision of the Lord and having been worshipped by him, Nārada placed him firmly within his heart and departed through the sky.**

**Комментарий:**

Nārada departed (verb is missing) by the path of the sky (vihāyasā). Although the verb is missing, it is understood.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**With pleasing words, the Lord addressed the messenger sent by the kings: “My dear messenger, I wish all good fortune to you. I shall arrange for the killing of King Magadha. Do not fear.”**

**Комментарий:**

The phrase mā bhaiṣṭa, “Do not fear,” is in the plural because Kṛṣṇa is addressing the kings.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Thus addressed, the messenger departed and accurately relayed the Lord’s message to the kings. They then waited expectantly for their meeting with Kṛṣṇa, eager for freedom in order to see him.**

**Комментарий:**

The kings waited for Kṛṣṇa (pratyaikṣan).

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**As he traveled through the provinces of Ānarta, Sauvīra, Marudeśa and Vinaśana, Kṛṣṇa crossed rivers and passed mountains, cities, villages, cow pastures and quarries.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa passed through the provinces of ānarta, Sauvīra, Marū and Kurukṣetra (vinaśanaṁ), crossing (atīyāya) mountains and rivers.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**After crossing the rivers Dṛṣadvatī and Sarasvatī, he passed through Pañcāla and Matsya and finally came to Indraprastha.**

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**King Yudhiṣṭhira was delighted to hear that the Lord, whom human beings rarely see, had now arrived. Accompanied by his priests and dear associates, the King came out to meet Kṛṣṇa.**

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**As songs and musical instruments resounded along with the loud vibration of Vedic hymns, the king, honored by Kṛṣṇa, went forth to meet Hṛṣīkeśa, just as the senses go forth to meet the consciousness of life.**

**Комментарий:**

As the secondary prāṇas meet the chief prāṇa, Yudhiṣṭhira went out to meet Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**The heart of King Yudhiṣṭhira melted with affection when he saw his dear friend, Kṛṣṇa, after such a long separation, and he embraced the Lord again and again.**

**Комментарий:**

Sasvaje means he embraced.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**The eternal form of Kṛṣṇa is the everlasting residence of the goddess of fortune. As soon as King Yudhiṣṭhira embraced him, the king became free of suffering separation and immediately felt the highest bliss. There were tears in his eyes, and his body shook due to ecstasy. He completely forgot that he was living in this material world.**

**Комментарий:**

He embraced the limbs of Mukunda, which are the uninterrupted (amala) shelter of all beauty (ramā). He forgot all worldly pastimes (loka-vibhramaḥ) since he was submerged in the bliss of extraordinary prema.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Then Bhīma, his eyes brimming with tears, laughed with joy as he embraced his maternal cousin, Kṛṣṇa. Arjuna and the twins— Nakula and Sahadeva—also joyfully embraced their dear friend, the infallible Lord, and they cried profusely.**

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**After he offered respects at the feet of Yudhiṣṭhira and Bhīma and after Arjuna had embraced him once more and Nakula and Sahadeva had offered him their obeisances, Kṛṣṇa bowed down to the brāhmaṇas and elders present, thus properly honoring the respectable members of the Kuru, Sṛñjaya and Kaikaya clans.**

**Комментарий:**

Details of the embracing are given.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Sūtas, Māgadhas, Gandharvas, Vandīs, orators and brāhmaṇas all glorified the lotus-eyed Lord—some reciting prayers, some dancing and singing—as mṛdaṅgas, conchs, kettledrums, vīṇās, paṇavas and gomukhas resounded.**

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Thus surrounded by his well-wishing relatives and praised on all sides, Kṛṣṇa, the crest jewel of the justly renowned, entered the decorated city.**

### Text 31-32

**Перевод:**

**The roads of Indraprastha were sprinkled with water perfumed by the liquid from elephants’ foreheads, and colorful flags, golden gateways and full waterpots enhanced the city’s splendor. Men and young girls were beautifully arrayed in fine, new garments, adorned with flower garlands and ornaments, and anointed with aromatic sandalwood paste. Every home displayed glowing lamps and respectful offerings, and from the holes of the latticed windows drifted incense, further beautifying the city. Banners waved, and the roofs were decorated with golden domes on broad silver bases. Thus Kṛṣṇa saw the royal city of the king of the Kurus.**

**Комментарий:**

The city is described in two verses. The city was splendid (virājamānam) with flags, etc. Each house was decorated by lamps and flowers, etc. They were attractive (ruciam) with incense streaming from the lattice windows. In it were palaces of the Kuru kings.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**When the young women of the city heard that Kṛṣṇa, the reservoir of pleasure for human eyes, had arrived, they hurriedly went onto the royal road to see him. They abandoned their household duties and even left their husbands in bed, and in their eagerness the knots of their hair and garments became loose.**

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**The royal road being quite crowded with elephants, horses, chariots and foot soldiers, the women climbed to the top of their houses, where they caught sight of Kṛṣṇa and his queens. The city ladies scattered flowers upon the Lord, embraced him in their minds and expressed their heartfelt welcome with broadly smiling glances.**

**Комментарий:**

They welcomed him nicely, enquiring of his well-being, etc., through their smiles.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Observing Mukunda’s wives passing on the road like stars accompanying the moon, the women exclaimed, “What have these ladies done so that the best of men bestows upon their eyes the joy of his generous smiles and playful sidelong glances?”**

**Комментарий:**

The women are like stars accompanying the moon (uḍu-pa-sahāḥ). What piety has been performed by them?

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**In various places citizens of the city came forward holding auspicious offerings for Kṛṣṇa, and sinless leaders of occupational guilds came forward to worship the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

The heads of the various communities (sreṇī-mukhyā), who earn their livings by particular arts, worshipped Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**With wide-open eyes, the members of the royal household came forward quickly with affection to greet Mukunda, and thus the Lord entered the royal palace.**

**Комментарий:**

Welcomed as he arrived (abhyupetaḥ) he entered.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**When Kuntī saw her nephew Kṛṣṇa, the master of the three worlds, her heart became filled with love. Rising from her couch with her daughter-in-law, she embraced the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

With Draupadī, Kuntī rose and embraced him to her chest. But Draupadī embraced him just by seeing.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**King Yudhiṣṭhira respectfully brought Govinda, the Supreme God of gods, to his personal quarters. The king was so overcome with joy that he could not remember all the rituals of worship.**

**Комментарий:**

Overcome with joy, Yudhiṣṭhira forgot the proper methods (kṛtyam) of worshiping Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa bowed down to his aunt and the wives of his elders, O King, and then Draupadī and the Lord’s sister bowed down to him.**

**Комментарий:**

Subhadrā (bhaginyā) then welcomed Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 41-42

**Перевод:**

**Encouraged by her mother-in-law, Draupadī worshipped all of Kṛṣṇa’s wives, including Rukmiṇī; Satyabhāmā; Bhadrā; Jāmbavatī; Kālindī; Mitravindā, the descendant of Śibi; the chaste Nāgnajitī; and the other queens of the Lord who were present. Draupadī honored them all with such gifts as clothing, flower garlands and jewelry.**

**Комментарий:**

Encouraged by her mother-in-law (śvaśrvā) Kuntī, Draupadī worshipped all of Kṛṣṇa’s queens.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**King Yudhiṣṭhira arranged for Kṛṣṇa’s rest and saw to it that all who came along with him—namely his queens, soldiers, ministers and secretaries—were comfortably situated. He arranged that they would experience a new feature of reception every day while staying as guests of the Pāṇḍavas.**

**Комментарий:**

He made arrangements such that each day was a new experience (navam navam).

### Text 44-45

**Перевод:**

**During his stay, he and Arjuna satisfied the fire-god by offering him the Khāṇḍava forest, and they saved Maya Dānava, who then built King Yudhiṣṭhira a celestial assembly hall. Desiring to do other pleasing actions for the king, the Lord resided at Indraprastha for several months. The Lord also took the opportunity to go riding in his chariot in the company of Arjuna, surrounded by a retinue of soldiers.**

**Комментарий:**

What did Kṛṣṇa do there? He was with Arjuna. Kṛṣṇa assisted him being under the control of his prema. He satisfied the fire by giving Khāṇḍava forest to it. They freed Maya from the fire, who then made the attractive hall for the king. Though these events were related in the fifty-eighth chapter, they are repeated since they are attractive. This is the sequence of events. Kṛṣṇa stayed in Indraprastha for the four months of the rainy season. During this time Kṛṣṇa burned the Khāṇḍava forest, won the Gāṇḍīva bow for Arjuna and obtained Kālindī while hunting. Then Kṛṣṇa returned to Dvārakā, married Kālindī, Bhadrā and other queens, killed Naraka and performed other deeds. Then Kṛṣṇa was invited to the Rājasūya sacrifice.

## Chapter 72 - The Slaying of the Demon Jarāsandha

### Text 1-2

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: One day, as King Yudhiṣṭhira sat in the royal assembly surrounded by eminent sages, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas and vaiśyas, and also by his brothers, spiritual masters, family elders, blood relations, in-laws and friends, he addressed Kṛṣṇa as everyone listened.**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventy-second chapter, giving permission for the sacrifice, and advised by Uddhava, Kṛṣṇa has Jarāsandha killed by Bhīma. Two verses go together. After sitting, with his hands joined in respect (āsthitaḥ), Yudhiṣṭhira spoke to Kṛṣṇa while others listened (śṛṇvatām).

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Yudhiṣṭhira said: O Govinda, I will worship your auspicious, opulent expansions by the Rājasūya sacrifice, the king of Vedic ceremonies. Please make our endeavor a success, my Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

I will worship even the devatās as your vibhūtis. This indicates the exclusive devotion of Yudhisthira to Kṛṣṇa. These devatās will come to purify themselves and they will purify others.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Purified persons who constantly serve, meditate upon and glorify your shoes, which destroy everything inauspicious, are sure to obtain freedom from material existence, O lotus-naveled Lord! Even if the devotees desire something in this world, they obtain it, whereas others—those who do not take shelter of you—are never satisfied, O Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

“O best of kings! What is this determination that has arisen in you, my exclusive devotee—a determination which is filled with violence, the essence of Rājasūya!” Fearing such a response from the Lord the king speaks three verses. O Lord with lotus navel! Those persons who constantly serve, meditate upon and glorify your shoes, which destroy all faults such as ignorance (abhadranāśane), being pure (śucayaḥ), attain liberation (bhavāpavargaṁ). If they desire material enjoyment, they attain that. You grant those desires for liberation and material enjoyment, which are favorable for bhakti. Those who are averse to your feet do not attain these. Their attainment of happiness is only a semblance.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O Lord of lords, let the people of this world see the power of devotional service rendered to your lotus feet. Please show them, O almighty one, the position of those Kurus and Sṛñjayas who worship you, and the position of those who do not.**

**Комментарий:**

You should arrange what I desire. O Supreme Lord (deva-deva)! Let the people existing in the world see the power of service to your lotus feet. Among relatives, friends and kings, some consider you the Supreme Lord. Some do not accept this, and rather hate you, thinking you are a human being. Show the real and unreal perspectives (niṣṭhām) of both these types among the Kurus and Sṛñjayas. The meaning is this. O Lord! We, being unalloyed devotees, are not enthusiastic for the Rājasūya sacrifice. But on that pretext, inviting the controllers of the universe and brahma-ṛṣis, and in their assembly, when it is shown that the person whose worship should be done first by their choice is you, the lotus-eyed Lord, then our desire to pull out the arrow in our hearts will be fulfilled.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Within your mind there can be no such differentiation as “This one is mine, and that is another’s,” because you are the Supreme Absolute Truth, the Soul of all beings, always equipoised and enjoying happiness within yourself. Just like the heavenly desire tree, you bless all who properly worship you, granting their desired fruits in proportion to the service they render you. There is nothing wrong in this.**

**Комментарий:**

“But O King! Do I also have attraction and hatred like others, that I elevate some and diminish some?” You do not have a mentality of prejudice, distinguishing on the basis of “my side” and “other’s side” (sva-para), since you are full of great qualities (brahmaṇaḥ). All the jīvas are yours. You are the master of all of them (sarvātmanaḥ). Thus you see equally. Since you are equal in vision toward all jīvas, you have nothing to do with those who are happy and those who are suffering. You experience extraordinary bliss (sva-sukhānubhūteḥ) in yourself. “But then my qualities of compassion and generosity cannot be expressed?” You show mercy to those who serve you, like a desire tree. After cutting the bondage of karma of your servants and then giving them your own self, you show them mercy. Those qualities do not disappear. According to the degree of service one achieves proportionate results. There is nothing besides this (viparyayaḥ).

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: Your decision is perfect, O King, and thus your noble fame will spread to all the worlds, O tormentor of your enemies.**

**Комментарий:**

O King! Certainly, you have my permission to perform the Rājasūya sacrifice, which you have resolved to do. O tormentor of enemies! Addressing him thus, Kṛṣṇa gives him the power to conquer all kings. If you cannot conquer the enemies even by such influence, then what is the use? By this sacrifice your fame will spread to all worlds. These words follow worldly convention.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Indeed, my lord, for the great sages, the forefathers and the devatās, for our well-wishing friends and, indeed, for all living beings, the performance of this king of Vedic sacrifices is desirable.**

**Комментарий:**

He clarifies his permission further.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**First conquer all kings, bring the earth under your control and collect all the required paraphernalia; then execute this great sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

Collect (saṁbhṛtya) the ingredients and perform (āharasva) the sacrifice.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**These brothers of yours, O King, have taken birth as partial expansions of the devatās ruling various planets. And you have me under control, you have conquered even me, who am unconquerable for those who cannot control their senses.**

**Комментарий:**

“How will I conquer the kings?” You brothers have appeared as expansions of the rulers of various planets. I am conquered by you. I exist as being subordinate to you. This is stated even in Mahābhārata: Carry out the desired sacrifice while I am present. Engage me in your service. I will follow your words. I cannot be conquered by those who are averse to me, who have not performed bhakti with their mind (akṛta-ātmabhiḥ).

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**No one in this world, even a devatā—what to speak of an earthly king—can defeat my devotee with his strength, beauty, fame or riches.**

**Комментарий:**

There is no fear that you will be defeated by others. I say this with pride. Even if some devotee of mine is lacking in power, etc., he cannot be conquered by anyone; what then to speak of you, having power and being most dear to me? If devatās cannot conquer you, how can insignificant worldly kings?

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Upon hearing these words sung by the Supreme Lord, King Yudhiṣṭhira became joyful, and his face blossomed like a lotus. Thus he sent forth his brothers, who were empowered with his potency, to conquer all directions.**

**Комментарий:**

The sandhi of tejasā (potency) and upabṛṁhitān (fortified) is poetic license. Otherwise, the word can be taken as teja in which case there would be normal sandhi according to rule.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**He sent Sahadeva to the south with the Sṛñjayas, Nakula to the west with the Matsyas, Arjuna to the north with the Kekayas, and Bhīma to the east with the Madrakas.**

**Комментарий:**

Nakula, Arjuna and Bhīma were assisted by Matsyas, Kekayas, and Madrakas respectively.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**After defeating many kings swiftly, these heroic brothers brought back abundant wealth for Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja, who was going to perform the sacrifice, O King.**

**Комментарий:**

They brought the wealth to Yudhiṣṭhira, who would be performing the sacrifice (yakṣyate).

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**When King Yudhiṣṭhira heard that Jarāsandha remained undefeated, he set to pondering, and then Kṛṣṇa, the source of all avatāras, told him the means Uddhava had described for defeating Jarāsandha.**

**Комментарий:**

When he became absorbed in thought (dhyāyataḥ), the Lord, the first being (ādyaḥ), spoke to him.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Thus Bhīmasena, Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa disguised themselves as brāhmaṇas and went to Girivraja, my dear King, where the son of Bṛhadratha was to be found.**

**Комментарий:**

They wore the markings of brāhmaṇas. Yataḥ means “where.”

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Disguised as brāhmaṇas, the royal warriors approached Jarāsandha at home during the appointed hour for receiving guests. They submitted their entreaty to that dutiful householder, who was especially respectful to the brahminical class.**

**Комментарий:**

They begged from Jarāsandha at the time meant for ritual hospitality for the householders (gṛha-medhinām). He was devoted to brāhmaṇas (brahmaṇyam).

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**\[Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna and Bhīma said:\] O King, know us to be needy guests who have come to you from afar. We wish all good unto you. Please grant us whatever we desire.**

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**What can the tolerant not bear? What will the wicked not do? What will the generous not give in charity? And how will those of equal vision see another person as an outsider?**

**Комментарий:**

“You should request by naming it. Otherwise, what if you request my son, most dear, or umbrella and cāmara (signs of royalty)? How can I give that? Someone will chastise you in anger.” Examples are given in the reply. What is intolerable such as separation from a dear son, for those with tolerance? Nothing is. What will not be given by those who are generous? What will not be done by persons who are nondevotees and prone to wicked acts? Since they beat even the righteous.“How can I give my body if it is requested by others? ” Who are “others” for those who help all, who are equal in their vision? Since Dadhīci gave his own body to others. Thus what is the use of mentioning what we want by name?

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**He indeed is to be censured and pitied who, though able to do so, fails to achieve with his temporary body the lasting fame glorified by great saints.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, a wise donor such as Mudgala gives even his life to those who ask. He who does not acquire fame is to be criticized (vācyaḥ) and lamented (śocyaḥ). What will happen to him in the future? This should be thought.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Hariścandra, Rantideva, Uñchavṛtti Mudgala, Śibi, Bali, the legendary hunter and pigeon, and many others have attained the permanent by means of the impermanent.**

**Комментарий:**

“But who were such persons in the past?” He shows them. To pay off his debts to Viśvāmitra, Hariścandra sold everything he had, including his wife and son. Yet even after attaining the status of a caṇḍāla, he did not become disappointed. He went to heaven, together with all the inhabitants of Ayodhyā. After going without even water for forty-eight days along with his family, Rantideva somehow obtained some food and water. But he gave it to his guests. In this way Rantideva attained Brahma-loka. Mudgala (uñchavṛttiḥ) followed the practice of gathering grains left behind in the fields (uñcha-vṛttiḥ) after the harvest. With his family he suffered for six months. By hospitality toward uninvited guests, he went to Brahma-loka. King Śibi attained heaven by giving his own flesh to a hawk in order to protect a pigeon who had taken shelter of him. Bali Mahārāja realized the Lord by giving all his property to Vāmanadeva when the Lord disguised himself as a dwarf brāhmaṇa. A pigeon and his mate gave their own flesh to a hunter as a show of hospitality, and thus they were taken to heaven in a celestial airplane. Seeing their goodness, the hunter became very detached. and went off to perform severe austerities. After he burned his body to death, he was promoted to heaven. Thus many personalities have attained an enduring place (dhruvaṁ gatāḥ) on higher planets by using their temporary material bodies.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: From the sound of their voices, their physical stature and the marks of bowstrings on their forearms, Jarāsandha could tell that his guests were fallen kṣatriyas. He began to think he had seen them somewhere before.**

**Комментарий:**

Jyā-hataiḥ means “by the calluses on their shoulders made by bowstrings.” He understood they were fallen kṣatriyas since they were begging. He thought he had seen them previously, at the svayaṁvara of Draupadī.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**\[Jarāsandha thought:\] These are surely members of the royal order dressed as brāhmaṇas, but still I must grant their request for charity, even if they beg me for my own body.**

**Комментарий:**

Being merciful, he confirms his faith in charity.

### Text 24-25

**Перевод:**

**Indeed, the spotless glories of Bali Mahārāja are heard throughout the world. Viṣṇu, wishing to recover Indra’s opulence from Bali, appeared before him in the guise of a brāhmaṇa and made him fall from his powerful position. Though aware of the ruse and forbidden by his guru, Bali, king of the demons, still gave Viṣṇu the whole earth in charity.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. The fame of Bali, who fell from power because of Viṣṇu, who disguised himself as a brāhmaṇa, is heard and spread everywhere. Na is sometimes seen instead of nu. In that case the meaning is “Is not the fame of Bali heard and spread everywhere?” Though prevented by Śukrācārya, Bali, knowing that this brāhmaṇa was Viṣṇu, gave the earth.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**What is the use of an unqualified kṣatriya who goes on living but fails to gain everlasting glory by working with his perishable body for the benefit of brāhmaṇas?**

**Комментарий:**

Of what use is the body of a fallen kṣatriya, who is living, if he does not desire (na ihatā) great fame by using his perishable (patamānena) body for the benefit of the brāhmaṇas? It is of no use at all. Patamānena means which tends to decay. It is formed by the affix cānaś.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Thus making up his mind, the generous Jarāsandha addressed Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna and Bhīma: “O learned brāhmaṇas, choose whatever you wish. I will give it to you, even if it is my own head.”**

**Комментарий:**

Jarāsandha made his decision.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O exalted King, give us battle in the form of a duel, if you think it fitting. We are princes and have come to beg a fight. We have no other request to make of you.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa speaks the truth and indicates the purpose. “But here the lie ‘we are brāhmaṇas’ is not possible, since lying is included in the eighteen faults and since the Lord’s svarūpa is not touched by those faults.” True. Faults such as speaking lies, etc., are only a semblance and the cause of pastimes which give happiness to the devotees. Thus they are related to the Lord’s svarūpa, since there is no question of the faults of the material world existing in the Lord’s svarūpa. This is described in detail in Siddhānta-ratna (Chapter Two).

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Over there is Bhīma, son of Pṛthā, and this is his brother Arjuna. Know me to be their maternal cousin, Kṛṣṇa, your enemy.**

**Комментарий:**

If you are kṣatriyas, tell your names.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Thus challenged, Magadharāja laughed out loud and contemptuously said, “All right, you weaklings, I’ll give you a fight!**

**Комментарий:**

Having been informed, Jarāsandha laughed loudly since he was internally satisfied by their humility which was understood by their disguise as brāhmaṇas. O weaklings (mandāḥ)! If you were frightened of fighting, why not just accept my body? I understand you are weak because you came disguised as beggars. If you are still obstinate then fight. But Sarasvatī devī (giving another meaning) breaks of the word as amandāḥ: O intelligent ones.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**“But I will not fight with you, Kṛṣṇa, for you are a coward. Your strength abandoned you in the midst of battle, and you fled your own capital of Mathurā to take shelter in the sea.**

**Комментарий:**

He refuses to fight with Kṛṣṇa. Because of fear, you gave up your attractive city and took shelter of the salt ocean. But Sarasvatī devī says, “I will not fight with you, who are fearless and very strong (tvayā abhīruṇā), as my heart is now distressed (viklava-tejasā). By your own will you left Mathurā and went to live in your house by the sea, to manifest your pastimes there.”

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**“As for this one, Arjuna, he is neither as old as I, nor he is very strong. Since he is no match for me, he should not be the contender. Bhīma, however, is as strong as I am.”**

**Комментарий:**

Arjuna is not very strong and even by age is not equal (vayasātulyo). He is not my equal in body. I will not fight with him. But Bhīma is equal to me in strength.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Having said this, Jarāsandha offered Bhīmasena a huge club, took up another himself and went outside the city.**

**Комментарий:**

Jarāsandha gave (prādāya) a large club to Bhīma.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**The two heroes thus began battling each other on the level fighting grounds outside the city. Maddened with the fury of combat, they struck each other with their lightning-bolt-like clubs.**

**Комментарий:**

In the fighting arena (samekhale) they struck each other with clubs.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**As they skillfully circled left and right, like actors dancing on a stage, the fight presented a magnificent spectacle.**

**Комментарий:**

They moved from left to right making various moves in club fighting (maṇḍalāni) like actors dancing on a stage. The analogy indicates fearlessness and skill in club fighting.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**When Jarāsandha’s and Bhīmasena’s clubs loudly collided, O King, the sound was like the impact of the big tusks of two fighting elephants, or the crash of thunderbolts.**

**Комментарий:**

Caṭa-caṭā is the onomatopoetic sound clubs make when striking against each other. It was like the cracking of lightning bolts or the clashing sound of the tusks of fighting elephants.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**They swung their clubs at each other with such speed and force that as the clubs struck their shoulders, hips, feet, hands, thighs and collarbones, the weapons were crushed and broken like branches of arka trees with which two enraged elephants furiously attack each other.**

**Комментарий:**

When the clubs contacted the opponent’s shoulder, waist, etc., they became crushed to powder. They fought like two elephants fighting with inflamed anger (dīpta-manyvoḥ) using branches which got crushed.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Their clubs thus ruined, those great heroes among men angrily pummeled each other with their iron-hard fists. As they struck each other, the sound resembled the crash of elephants colliding or harsh thunderclaps.**

**Комментарий:**

When the clubs were destroyed, in anger they beat and crushed each other’s limbs (apiṣṭām) with fists, whose touch was like that of iron.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**As they thus fought, this contest between opponents of equal training, strength and stamina reached no conclusion. And so they kept on fighting, O King, without becoming tired.**

**Комментарий:**

The two (tayoḥ), Jarāsandha and Bhīma fought.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**O King! The two fought for twenty-seven days and at night acted as friends. O King! Once Bhīma spoke to his cousin,“O Kṛṣṇa! I cannot defeat Jarāsandha in battle.” Kṛṣṇa knew the secret of his enemy Jarāsandha’s birth and death, and also how he had been given life by the demoness Jarā. Considering all this, Kṛṣṇa imparted his special power to Bhīma.**

**Комментарий:**

The verse is spoken with the idea that “Killing Jarāsandha was an act of Kṛṣṇa. The fame that arose from that was given by Kṛṣṇa to Bhīma” Kṛṣṇa knew that Jarāsandha was born in two pieces, and that he could be killed by separating the pieces. The witch named Jarā had given Jarāsandha life by joining the two pieces. Knowing that he had been joined together, Kṛṣṇa thought how to inform Bhīma. He empowered Bhīma with his own power to split open Jarāsandha.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Having determined how to kill the enemy, that Lord of infallible vision made a sign to Bhīma by tearing in half a small branch of a tree.**

**Комментарий:**

Visible to Bhīma, Kṛṣṇa took a branch in his hand and showed by sign, “Just as I tear apart the branch, you tear apart Jarāsandha.” Iva here is used in the sense of limitation (of the sense of the words, i.e. he did just that much to indicate and nothing more).

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Understanding this sign, mighty Bhīma, the best of fighters, seized his opponent by the feet and threw him to the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding Kṛṣṇa’s hint (tat), Bhīma seized his opponent.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Bhīma pressed down on one leg with his foot while grabbing Jarāsandha’s other leg in his hands, and just as a great elephant might break the branch of a tree, Bhīma tore Jarāsandha apart from the anus upward.**

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**The king’s subjects then saw him lying in two separate pieces, each with a single leg, thigh, testicle, hip, shoulder, arm, eye, eyebrow and ear, and with half a back and chest.**

**Комментарий:**

The citizens saw the two parts (śakale) each with one leg, one arm, one ear, etc.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**With the death of the lord of Magadha, a great cry of lamentation arose, while Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa congratulated Bhīma by embracing him.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna honored Bhīma with praise (pūjayāmāsatuḥ). This action is befitting only you, the lion among kṣatriyas.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**The immeasurable Lord, the sustainer and benefactor of all living beings, coronated Jarāsandha’s son, Sahadeva, as the new ruler of the Magadhas. The Lord then freed all the kings Jarāsandha had imprisoned.**

**Комментарий:**

Sahadeva was Jarāsandha’s son (different from the Pāṇḍava).

## Chapter 73 - Lord Kṛṣṇa Blesses the Liberated Kings

### Text 1-6

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Jarāsandha had defeated 20,800 kings in combat and thrown them into prison. As these kings emerged from the Giridroṇī fortress, they appeared dirty and shabbily dressed. They were emaciated by hunger, their faces were dried up, and they were greatly weakened by their long imprisonment. The kings then beheld the Lord before them. His complexion was dark blue like the color of a cloud, and he wore a yellow silk garment. He was distinguished by the Śrīvatsa mark on his chest, his four mighty arms, the pinkish hue of his eyes, which resembled the whorl of a lotus, his lovely, cheerful face, his gleaming makara earrings and the lotus, club, conch and disc in his hands. A helmet, a jeweled necklace, a golden belt, and golden bracelets and armlets decorated his form, and on his neck he wore both the brilliant, precious Kaustubha gem and a garland of forest flowers. The kings seemed to drink his beauty with their eyes, lick him with their tongues, relish his fragrance with their nostrils and embrace him with their arms. Their past sins now eradicated, the kings all bowed down to Kṛṣṇa, placing their heads at his feet.**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventy-third chapter, Kṛṣṇa is seen and praised by the freed kings, bestows bhakti upon them and satisfying them, goes to Yudhiṣṭhira. He wore (nivītam) a forest garland around his neck. With great desire for his form, etc., they all offered respects to his feet. They seemed to embrace him with their arms (rambhantaḥ).

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**The ecstasy of beholding Kṛṣṇa having dispelled the weariness of their imprisonment, the kings stood with joined palms and offered words of praise to that supreme master of the senses.**

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**The kings said: Obeisances to You, O Lord of the ruling! O destroyer of your surrendered devotees’ distress! Since we have surrendered to you, O inexhaustible Kṛṣṇa, please save us from this terrible material life, which has made us so despondent.**

**Комментарий:**

By addressing him as ‘deva-deva’ they indicate his supremacy over all, by ‘prapanna’ his affection toward the surrendered and by ‘avyaya’ his nature of being unchanging.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**O master, Madhusūdana, we do not blame this king of Magadha, since it is actually by your mercy that kings fall from their royal position, O almighty Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why should I free you, who are attached to enjoyment and have great hatred for Jarāsandha?” We do not hate him. We do not find fault in him. Anu sūyamaḥ instead of anv asūyamaḥ and ena instead of enam are poetic license. “Why?” We lost our kingdoms because of him and by that loss we got your mercy.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Infatuated with his opulence and ruling power, a king loses all self-restraint and cannot obtain his true welfare. Thus bewildered by your illusory energy, he imagines his temporary assets to be permanent.**

**Комментарий:**

In three verses the kings prove how losing a kingdom is the cause of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. Unrestrained (unnaddhaḥ) by pride in his wealth and power, a king thinks his temporary wealth to be permanent (acalāḥ).

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Just as deer consider a mirage to be a pond of water, so those who are irrational look upon the sense objects to be useful.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking that wealth produces happiness is an illusion. Unintelligent persons consider wealth, the transformation of sense objects such as sound, touch, etc. (vaikārikīṁ), created by māyā, as eternal and unchanging (vastu). Just as fools see a mirage as water, although it is actually light, similarly foolish kings see the distress arising from the objects of enjoyment as happiness. Vaikārikī is formed by adding the suffix ṭhak, in the meaning of itself. Though wealth is different from mirage by being useful, the example of the mirage is used to explain the useless aspect of enjoying material objects (rather than to explain that matter is unreal).

### Text 12-13

**Перевод:**

**Previously, blinded by the intoxication of riches, we wanted to conquer this earth, and thus we fought one another to achieve victory, mercilessly harassing our own subjects. We arrogantly disregarded you, O Lord, who stood before us as death. But now, O Kṛṣṇa, that powerful form of yours called time, moving mysteriously and irresistibly, has deprived us of our wealth. Now that you have mercifully destroyed our pride, we beg simply to remember your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

We ourselves exemplify this. They explain in two verses. Wanting to conquer the earth (asyā), we competed with each other, not seeing you standing before us as death. Previously we were intoxicated with pride. O Kṛṣṇa! We, those same persons, have today lost our power by the influence of time, your śakti (tanvā). By your mercy we desire to remember your feet. A prayer is expressed by the imperative (smarāma). We have understood that losing our kingdoms is the cause of your mercy.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Never again will we hanker for a mirage-like kingdom—a kingdom that must be slavishly served by this mortal body, which is simply a source of disease and suffering and which is declining at every moment. Nor, O almighty Lord, will we hanker to enjoy the heavenly fruits of pious work in the next life, since the promise of such rewards is simply an empty enticement for the ears.**

**Комментарий:**

Having developed knowledge by the mercy of the Lord, the kings become detached from kingdom, etc. They speak. Because of this (atha), we no longer desire a kingdom, since it is devoid of happiness. This kingdom is served by a temporary (śaśvata patatā) body, a field of sickness (rujāṁ bhuvā). It has not a drop of happiness.“They say the kingdom is a lotus full of the fragrance of material bliss. Why do you renounce it?” It is imagined like that by persons in illusion, not by those who know the truth. “Situated in your kingdom, you performed jyotiṣṭoma sacrifices and desire Svarga, its result.” We do not desire the results on attaining afterlife, since it’s pleasing only to the ears. Even there, there is no happiness since competition, etc., do not cease there too.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Please tell us how we may constantly remember your lotus feet, though we continue in the cycle of birth and death in this world.**

**Комментарий:**

“But I will now establish you in your kingdoms. Otherwise there is no fame for me.” Then teach the method by which we will not forget your lotus feet, though we are situated in our kingdoms, though we are absorbed in royal duties (saṁsaratām). They indicate pure bhakti.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Again and again we offer our obeisances unto Kṛṣṇa, attractor of all beings, the son of Vasudeva. That supreme form of prema, vanquishes the suffering of all who surrender to him, and appears as a cowherd boy.**

**Комментарий:**

The kings, chanting his names, offered full prostrations. It is necessary to chant the Lord’s names while offering obeisances.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus the kings, now freed from bondage, glorified the Supreme Lord. Then, my dear Parīkṣit, that merciful bestower of shelter spoke to them with sweet words.**

**Комментарий:**

Ślakṣṇayā means sweet.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: From now on, my dear kings, you will have firm devotion to me, the Supreme Self and the Lord of all that be. I assure you this will come to pass, just as you desire.**

**Комментарий:**

O Kings! May bhakti to me manifest as you desired. Bāḍham indicates his consent.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Fortunately you have come to the proper conclusion, my dear kings, and what you have spoken is true. See how human beings’ lack of self-restraint, which arises from their intoxication with opulence and power, simply leads to madness.**

**Комментарий:**

He praises the determination of the kings. O Kings! What you have said is true (ṛta-bhāṣiṇaḥ). The truth is shown. What has been determined by you—that bhakti alone is to be done—is by your good fortune (diṣṭyā) because lack of control (unnāham) arising from intoxication, arising from power, arising from wealth (śriyā), produces madness for kings. The singular in the word paśya (see) instead of paśyata (plural)is a poetic license.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Haihaya, Nahuṣa, Veṇa, Rāvaṇa, Naraka and many other rulers of devatās, men and demons fell from their elevated positions because of infatuation with material opulence.**

**Комментарий:**

This lack of control is the cause of falling. Kārtavīrya (haihayaḥ) was killed by Paraśurāma, the son of Jamadagni, because he stole the desire cow of Jamadagni. Nahuṣa, while being the king of the devatās, had the sages carry him on a palanquin to associate with Indra’s wife. He fell from his position and became a snake by the sages’ curse. Vena, thinking himself the Lord, insulted the brāhmaṇas and was killed by them who uttered huṁkāra (in contempt). Rāvaṇa, desiring Sītā, was killed along with his followers by Rāma. Naraka was killed by me because he stole Aditi’s earrings. Others also, devas, demons, and kings, fell from their positions because of intoxication with wealth.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Understanding that this material body and everything connected with it have a beginning and an end, worshipping me by Vedic sacrifices, and with clear intelligence you will protect your subjects in accordance with the principles of religion.**

**Комментарий:**

My devotees should perform Vedic karmas for teaching the people. Rakṣatha stands for rakṣata.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**As you live your lives, begetting generations of progeny and encountering happiness and distress, birth and death, always keep your minds fixed on me.**

**Комментарий:**

You should spend your time producing sons (prajā-tantūn), tolerating happiness and distress and encountering prosperity and poverty (bhava-abhava).

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Be detached from the body and everything connected to it. Experiencing my pleasant form, steadfastly keep your worship of me, while concentrating your minds fully on me, you will ultimately attain me, the Supreme Brahman.**

**Комментарий:**

Be absorbed in the svarūpa of the jīva (ātmārāmāḥ). After giving up the body you will come to me, full of great qualities (brahma).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus instructed the kings, Kṛṣṇa, the supreme master of all the worlds, engaged male and female servants in bathing and grooming them.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa engaged men and women in rubbing oil on the king’s bodies, bathing them and other services.

### Text 25-26

**Перевод:**

**O descendant of Bharata, the Lord then had King Sahadeva honor them with offerings of clothing, jewelry, garlands and sandalwood paste, all suitable for royalty. After they had been properly bathed and adorned, Kṛṣṇa saw to it that they dined on excellent food. He also presented them with various items befitting the pleasure of kings, such as betel nut.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. Having them bathed, he had Sahadeva (Jarāsandha’s son) honor them with cloth and other items befitting kings. Having fed the kings, he engaged Sahadeva again in serving them.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Honored by Mukunda and freed from tribulation, the kings shone splendidly, their earrings gleaming, just as the moon and other celestial bodies shine brilliantly in the sky at the end of the rainy season.**

**Комментарий:**

The kings appeared resplendent like the moon and other planets (grahāḥ) after the rainy season.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Then the Lord arranged for the kings to be seated on chariots drawn by fine horses and adorned with jewels and gold, and pleasing them with gracious words, he sent them off to their own kingdoms.**

**Комментарий:**

Prīṇayya means pleasing them.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Thus liberated from all difficulty by Kṛṣṇa, the greatest of personalities, the kings departed, and as they went they thought only of him, the Lord of the universe, and of his wonderful deeds.**

**Комментарий:**

They were released by Kṛṣṇa, having a most generous mind (sumahātmanā).

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**The kings told their ministers and other associates what the Lord had done, and then they diligently carried out the orders he had imparted to them.**

**Комментарий:**

The kings told (jagaduḥ) their ministers (prakṛtibhyaḥ).

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Having arranged for Bhīmasena to kill Jarāsandha, Keśava accepted worship from King Sahadeva and then departed with the two sons of Pṛthā.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was worshipped by Sahadeva, the king of Magadha.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**When they arrived at Indraprastha, the victorious heroes blew their conchs, bringing joy to their well-wishing friends and sorrow to their enemies.**

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**The residents of Indraprastha were very pleased to hear that sound, for they understood that now the king of Magadha had been put to rest. King Yudhiṣṭhira felt that his desires were now fulfilled.**

**Комментарий:**

Śāntam means he died.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Bhīma, Arjuna and Janārdana offered their respects to the king and informed him fully about what they had done.**

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Upon hearing their account of the great favor Keśava had mercifully shown him, King Dharmarāja shed tears of ecstasy. He felt such love that he could not say anything.**

**Комментарий:**

The king could not say anything because he was stunned with the bliss of prema. Refers to the pariniṣṭhitas

## Chapter 74 - The Deliverance of Śiśupāla at the Rājasūya Sacrifice

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus heard of the killing of Jarāsandha, and also of almighty Kṛṣṇa’s manifestation of power, King Yudhiṣṭhira addressed the Lord as follows with great pleasure.**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventy-fourth chapter, the killing of Śiśupāla, related to the agra-pūjā of Kṛṣṇa by brāhmaṇas during the arrangements for the sacrifice, is described. Hearing about the killing of Jarāsandha and Kṛṣṇa’s powers the king spoke to him. The word ca indicates that he saw that the Lord acted according to his order.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Yudhiṣṭhira said: All the exalted spiritual masters of the three worlds, together with the inhabitants and rulers of the various planets, accept your command, which is rarely obtained, which comes from your mouth directly or through the Vedas.**

**Комментарий:**

The gurus of the three worlds such as the Kumāras along with Brahmā and other rulers, carry on their heads your order, which is rarely obtained (durlabham). They respect it greatly thinking that it is attained by good fortune.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**That you, the lotus-eyed Supreme Lord, accept the orders of wretched fools who presume themselves rulers is a great pretense on your part, O all-pervading one.**

**Комментарий:**

You, that Supreme lord, out of affection follow the orders of miserable persons like us who still think themselves kings of earth. That is a great mockery since it puts you in a minor position.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**But of course the power of the Absolute Truth, the Supreme Soul, the primeval one without a second, is neither increased nor diminished by his activities, any more than the sun’s power is by its movements.**

**Комментарий:**

“How can I be the Supreme Lord for I perform excellent and low activities like the jīva?” Your power does not increase by excellent actions such as killing Jarasandha and does not decrease by low actions such as following our orders, just as the sun’s effulgence does not increase by shining on the house of Brahmā on Mount Meru or decrease by shining on the house of an outcaste on earth. The Lord is one (ekasya), since there is no other lord. You are without a second (advitīyasya) since there is nothing beyond you, who possess śaktis of jīva, prakṛti and kāla (time). You are Brahman since you have unlimited, great qualities. You enter the jīvas, prakṛti and kāla, and stimulate them to action (paramātmanaḥ). Since you are of this nature, your powers do not increase or decrease by those actions. The eternal greatness of the knower of Brahman does not increase or decrease by karma. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad [4.4.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bau/4.4.23)) We know that you manifest these activities by your mercy out of affection for the devotees and since you are the protector of the universe.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**O unconquerable Mādhava, even your devotees make no distinctions of “I” and “mine,” “you” and “yours,” for this is the perverted mentality of animals.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why cannot I think that since I am thus the complete Supreme Lord, it is improper for me to be engaging in those activities?” O unconquered lord! Your devotees do not think in terms of “I”, “mine” and “you”, “yours.”“I am greatly learned. Thus whose orders can I follow? You are not learned. Everyone is your employer.” This is all irregular intelligence. If your devotees do not have this crooked mentality, what to speak of you?

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having said this, King Yudhiṣṭhira waited until the proper time for the sacrifice was at hand. Then with Lord Kṛṣṇa’s permission he selected suitable priests, all expert authorities on the Vedas, to execute the sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

At the proper time for the sacrifice (yajñiye), namely spring, Yudhiṣṭhira appointed suitable (yuktān) priests such as hotṛ, etc., (ṛtvijaḥ) to do it.

### Text 7-9

**Перевод:**

**He selected Kṛṣṇa-dvaipāyana, Bharadvāja, Sumantu, Gotama and Asita, along with Vasiṣṭha, Cyavana, Kaṇva, Maitreya, Kavaṣa and Trita. He also selected Viśvāmitra, Vāmadeva, Sumati, Jaimini, Kratu, Paila and Parāśara, as well as Garga, Vaiśampāyana, Atharvā, Kaśyapa, Dhaumya, Rāma of the Bhārgavas, Āsuri, Vītihotra, Madhucchandā, Vīrasena and Akṛtavraṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The selection is described in three verses. Beginning with Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana and ending with Akṛtavraṇa, he chose (vavre from previous verse) them as ṛtviks, witnesses, etc.

### Text 10-11

**Перевод:**

**O King, others who were invited included Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra with his sons, the wise Vidura, and many other brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas and śūdras, all eager to witness the sacrifice. Indeed, all the kings came there with their entourages.**

**Комментарий:**

Others such as Droṇa were invited. All those who were desirous of seeing the sacrifice came (iyuḥ) there.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa priests then plowed the sacrificial ground with golden ploughshares and initiated King Yudhiṣṭhira for the sacrifice in accordance with the traditions set down by standard authorities.**

**Комментарий:**

The priests ploughed the sacrificial ground (deva-yajanaṁ) with a golden plough and initiated Yudhisthira by a dīkṣā-saṁskāra.

### Text 13-15

**Перевод:**

**The utensils used in the sacrifice were made of gold, just as in the ancient Rājasūya performed by Varuṇa. Indra, Brahmā, Śiva and many other planetary rulers; the Siddhas and Gandharvas with their entourage; the Vidyādharas; great serpents; sages; Yakṣas; Rākṣasas; celestial birds; Kinnaras; Cāraṇas; and earthly kings—all were invited, and they came from every direction to the sacrifice of King Yudhiṣṭhira. They were not in the least astonished to see the splendor of the sacrifice, since it was quite appropriate for a devotee of Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The vessels were made of gold, just as previously at the Rājasūya of Varuṇa. All these persons came to the Rājasūya of Pāṇḍu’s son. They were not surprised and thought he had made fine preparations since he was a devotee of Kṛṣṇa. What is impossible for the devotee of Kṛṣṇa? They came with Brahmā and Śiva who were the main persons among them. They came with the Lord’s associates (sa-gaṇāḥ). Sagaṇāḥ refers to Garuḍa, Viṣvaksena and other Vaikuṇṭha associates. Sages like the Kumāras came. The birds were Garuḍa’s sons. They came with affection (sam), in joy (sma). Vai means certainly.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**The priests, as powerful as gods, performed the Rājasūya sacrifice for King Yudhiṣṭhira in accordance with the Vedic injunctions, just as the devatās had previously performed it for Varuṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

The priests such as Vyāsa had more effulgence than the devatās. They performed it just as the ancient sages among devatās (amarāḥ) performed it for Varuṇa (pracetasaṁ).

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**On the day of extracting the soma juice, King Yudhiṣṭhira properly and very attentively worshipped the priests and the most exalted personalities of the assembly.**

**Комментарий:**

The king who conquered all directions (avanī-pālaḥ), Yudhiṣṭhira, with faith (susamāhitaḥ) worshipped the best in the assembly (sadasas-patīn) on the day of extracting soma (sūtye ’hani).

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**The members of the assembly then pondered over who among them should be worshipped first, but since there were many personalities qualified for this honor, they were unable to decide. Finally Sahadeva spoke up.**

**Комментарий:**

Those in the assembly who did not know Kṛṣṇa’s glory, considering who was qualified for the first worship among the people present in the gathering, could not decide. Why? They could not decide because of the many persons present (anaikāntyāt). Brahmā and others, Dvaipāyana and others thought, “If Sahadeva, in charge of agra-pūjā, does not say, then we will say.” Thus, they remained silent.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**\[Sahadeva said:\] Certainly it is Acyuta, the Supreme Lord and chief of the Yādavas, who deserves the highest position. In truth, he himself comprises all the devatās worshipped in sacrifice, along with such aspects of the worship as the sacred place, the time and the paraphernalia.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa deserves the highest position, since he is eternally full of six qualities (bhagavān). He is the master of great devotees like Nārada (sātvatāṁ patiḥ). Since they are worshipped by the whole world, it is established that he, their master is the highest.“But the devatās are the best since they are worshipped in sacrifices.” Having unlimited śakti (acyutaḥ), he is the form of all devatās since all the devatās are a form of his śakti.

### Text 20-21

**Перевод:**

**This entire universe is founded upon him, as are the great sacrificial performances, with their sacred fires, oblations and mantras. Sāṅkhya and Yoga both aim toward him. He is the one without a second. O assembly members, that unborn Lord, relying solely on himself, creates, maintains and destroys this cosmos by his personal energies, and thus the existence of this universe depends on him alone.**

**Комментарий:**

This is further explained. This whole universe is actuated by and pervaded by him (yad-ātmakam). Therefore, to a greater degree, sacrifices are actuated and pervaded by him. The aṅgas of sacrifice such as fire are also actuated by and pervaded by him. Kṛṣṇa alone is the object (yat paraḥ) of jñāna (sāṅkhya) and aṣṭāṅga yoga since he is the Supreme Lord. He then confirms this further. He is one only, since he is the only Supreme Lord. Eva indicates that it is not impossible. He is one with everything (aitad-ātmyam). Śruti says aitad-ātmyam idaṁsarvam: everything has the Lord as its ātmā. (Chandogya Upaniṣad) The affix ṣyañ is applied after etad-ātmā to form aitad-ātmyam. Since he creates, maintains and destroys this universe by his svarūpa possessing śaktis of jīva, prakṛti and kāla (time), he is independent (ātmāśrayaḥ), and unchanging (ajaḥ).

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**He creates the many activities of this world, and thus by his grace the whole world endeavors for the ideals of dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa.**

**Комментарий:**

He deserves the most worship. All people (ayam sarvaḥ), who have associated with devotees, perform various āśramakarmas such as reciting Vedas, etc., for him alone (yad-avekṣayā). Because of him, they engage in dharma, etc. which purifies the heart and which then produces perception of him. Tam etam ātmānaṁ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena dānena tapasānāśakena: they desire to know him by the words of the Vedas, by sacrifice, charity, austerity and fasting. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad) Thus what doubt is there about him being worshipped first?

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Therefore we should give the highest honor to Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord. If we do so, we will be honoring all living beings and also our own selves.**

**Комментарий:**

He concludes in this verse. If Kṛṣṇa is worshipped, everyone’s worship occurs since everything depends on him, just as by watering the root of a tree its branches become watered. No one should have objection to this.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Anyone who wishes that the honor he gives to be reciprocated infinitely, should honor Kṛṣṇa, the perfectly peaceful and perfectly complete soul of all beings, the Supreme Lord, who views nothing as separate from himself.**

**Комментарий:**

“What happens by that?” Honor should be given to Kṛṣṇa, who is the ātmā of all moving and nonmoving beings since he nourishes them and pervades them. Yet he is attached to the devotee (ananyadarśine), and devoid of agitation (śāntāya) since he is complete in himself (pūrṇāya). The rest is clear.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Having said this, Sahadeva, who understood Kṛṣṇa’s powers, fell silent. And having heard his words, all the saintly persons present congratulated him, exclaiming “Excellent! Excellent!”**

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**The king was delighted to hear this pronouncement of the brāhmaṇas, from which he understood the mood of the entire assembly. Overwhelmed with love, he fully worshipped Kṛṣṇa, the master of the senses.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding the brāhmaṇas’ intention and agreement, pleased due to his desire being fulfilled, though overcome with prema he brought Kṛṣṇa who was engaged in washing others’ feet and worshipped him. Samarhayat instead of samāharayat is poetic license.

### Text 27-28

**Перевод:**

**After bathing Kṛṣṇa’s feet, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira joyfully sprinkled the water upon his own head, and then upon the heads of his wife, brothers, other family members and ministers. That water purifies the whole world. As he honored the Lord with presentations of yellow silken garments and precious jeweled ornaments, the king’s tear-filled eyes prevented him from looking directly at the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

The worship is described in two verses.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**When they saw Kṛṣṇa thus honored, nearly all who were present joined their palms reverentially, exclaiming “Obeisances to you! All victory to you!” and then bowed down to him. Flowers rained down from above.**

**Комментарий:**

Some said, “I offer respects” and some said “Victory!” And some said “I offer respects. Victory!” Thus, the sacrifice was accomplished with all its limbs.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**The intolerant son of Damaghoṣa became infuriated upon hearing the glorification of Kṛṣṇa’s qualities. He stood up from his seat and, angrily waving his arms, fearlessly spoke to the entire assembly the following harsh words against the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing Sahadeva’s words and finally the shouts of namaḥ and jaya, Śiśupāla, raising his right arm, spoke harsh words in anger, without fear after the worship. His intention was this. If I criticize Kṛṣṇa at the beginning, after worshipping some other suitable person, the sacrifice with its limbs will take place and Kṛṣṇa’s desire will be fulfilled. But if I criticize him after the worship, when all of us relatives, kings get up and leave the hall amidst cries of dismay that this sacrifice is spoilt (on account of the statement below), then Kṛṣṇa’s desire will be thwarted and my desire will be fulfilled. In the place where those who are not to be worshipped are worshipped, there is offense to those who are actually worshippable. There will be famine, death and fear. (Pañcatantra)

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**\[Śiśupāla said:\] The statement of the Vedas that time is the unavoidable controller of all has indeed been proven true, since the intelligence of wise elders has now become diverted by the words of a mere boy.**

**Комментарий:**

To have his words accepted in the assembly he first spoke while conciliating the assembly through words embedded with criticism. Time is not possible to counteract (duratyayaḥ). The Vedas speak the truth. Because of time (yat), the intelligence of elders has been diverted by a child’s words.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**O leaders of the assembly, you know best who is a fit candidate for being honored. Therefore you should not heed the words of a child when he claims that Kṛṣṇa deserves to be worshipped.**

**Комментарий:**

“What is that intelligence?” O leaders of the assembly! It is the intelligence which approves Kṛṣṇa for worship. The reason is you know best who is a fit candidate (not the boy Sahadeva). The meaning of his words according to Sarasvatī devī is “The Vedas are true. Do not give regard to my words who am foolish (bālasya) since you are knowers of who is qualified for worship, since Kṛṣṇa, Parabrahman, is accepted for worship.”

### Text 33-34

**Перевод:**

**How can you pass over the most exalted members of this assembly— topmost sages dedicated to the Absolute Truth endowed with powers of austerity, divine insight and strict adherence to severe vows, sanctified by knowledge and worshipped even by the rulers of the universe? How does this cowherd boy, the disgrace of his family, deserve your worship, any more than a crow deserves to eat the sacred puroḍāśa rice cake?**

**Комментарий:**

When there is no one qualified for worship, somehow worship him, but when there are many of you qualified for the worship in the assembly why worship him? In two verses he explains his position. He has spoiled the name of his family by killing his uncle (kula-pāṁsanaḥ). Sarasvatī devī however gives another meaning. He is the protector of the cows, earth and Vedas (gopālaḥ). He kills those like me who speak rubbish (ku-lapa-aṁsanaḥ). He is appropriately (yathā) devoid of material happiness and suffering (akākaḥ) since he is the personification of eternal bliss. How does he, the Supreme Lord, just deserve offerings of rice cakes like Indra receives in worship? Rather he deserves full surrender.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**How does one who follows no principles of varṇāśrama or of family ethics, who has been excluded from all dharmas, who behaves whimsically, and who has no good qualities—how does such a person deserve to be worshipped?**

**Комментарий:**

For the three verses beginning with this, the meaning as revealed by Sarasvatī devī is explained. Since he is Parabrahman he is free from varṇa, etc. Avarnaṁ agotram: the Lord has no varṇa or gotra. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)He is beyond all dharma, not touched by them. Since he is like that he acts independently (svaira-vartī). Since he is the Supreme Lord, he is devoid of qualities, not touched by material guṇas. Since he is like that, how does he deserve just this much worship? He deserves much more worship.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Yayāti cursed the dynasty of these Yādavas, and ever since then they have been ostracized by honest men and addicted to liquor. How, then, does Kṛṣṇa deserve to be worshipped?**

**Комментарий:**

Though their family was cursed by Yayāti, they have been delivered (bahiṣ-kṛtam) from the curse by the great sages (sadbhir). Thus Kārtavīrya and others ruled. The family is absorbed in protecting the earth (pāna-ratam). Therefore why is worshipping the Yadus useless? Rather it has great value.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**These Yādavas have abandoned the holy lands inhabited by saintly sages and have instead taken shelter of a fortress in the sea, a place where no brahminical principles are observed. There, just like thieves, they harass their subjects.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking shelter of lands served by sages and brāhmaṇas, they punish the impious citizens, making them reject the difficult to understand principles of the pāṣaṇdas devoid of the power of the Vedas. Abrahma-varcasamsa-mudram means those with the markings of the Buddhists and Jains, which are devoid of the power arising from the study of Vedas, i.e., the pāṣaṇḍas. Durgam means difficult to understand because of lack of dharma, since there is understanding because of being dharmic. Dasyavaḥ can be in the accusative. The Yādavas, strict followers of dharma, punish the thieves who pose as citizens.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Bereft of all good fortune, Śiśupāla spoke these and other insults. But the Supreme Lord said nothing, just as a lion ignores a jackal’s cry.**

**Комментарий:**

He was like a lion hearing the howling of the jackal. But taking the secondary meaning for his words: As Śiśupāla, whose auspiciousness was not lost (anaṣṭa-maṅgalaḥ) since his liberation was close at hand, spoke these very auspicious words, compared to which nothing is more auspicious (abhadrāṇi), Kṛṣṇa said nothing just as Nṛsiṁhadeva (siṁhaḥ) hears the prayers spoken by Śiva (śivā-rutam)(but remains silent).

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Upon hearing such intolerable blasphemy of the Lord, several members of the assembly covered their ears and walked out, angrily cursing the King of Cedi.**

**Комментарий:**

They walked out cursing him, “Die immediately.”

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Anyone who fails to immediately leave the place where he hears criticism of the Supreme Lord or his faithful devotee will certainly fall down to hell, bereft of his pious credit.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse gives scriptural evidence supporting their leaving the hall. Adhaḥ means hell.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Then the sons of Pāṇḍu became furious, and together with the warriors of the Matsya, Kaikaya and Sṛñjaya clans, they rose up from their seats with weapons poised, ready to kill Śiśupāla.**

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Undaunted, Śiśupāla then took up his sword and shield in the midst of all the assembled kings, O Bhārata, and hurled insults at those who sided with Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Asambhrāntaḥ means fearless.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**At that point the Supreme Lord stood up and checked his devotees. He then angrily sent forth his razor-sharp disc and severed the head of his enemy as he was attacking.**

**Комментарий:**

The meaning is this. My associate (Śiśupāla) is very strong. In a fight with the Pāṇḍavas who are extremely strong, the sacrificial arena will be sprinkled with blood. Therefore, they should not kill him. Considering this, Kṛṣṇa cut off his head with his cakra from a distance. And blood did not fall on the earth.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**When Śiśupāla was thus killed, a great roar arose from the crowd. Taking advantage of that disturbance, the few kings who were supporters of Śiśupāla quickly left the assembly out of fear for their lives.**

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**An effulgent light rose from Śiśupāla’s body and, as everyone watched, entered Kṛṣṇa just like a meteor falling from the sky to the earth.**

**Комментарий:**

The body of his associate (jyotiḥ) situated subtly by aṇima-siddhi in Śiśupāla’s body, approached Kṛṣṇa (vāsudevaṁ), like a meteor falling from the sky to earth. Flying into the sky it entered Vasudeva’s son. The associate attained his master, Vikuṇṭhā’s son (who stays on the Vaikuṇṭha within the material world).

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**Obsessed with hatred of Kṛṣṇa throughout three lifetimes, Śiśupāla attained the Lord’s nature for one’s consciousness determines one’s future birth.**

**Комментарий:**

Meditating on the Lord with hatred for three lifetimes, he became absorbed (tan-mayatām) in him. This means that he became the Lord’s associate, with similarity to the Lord, like the insect meditating on the wasp since it is said that they went to the Lord’s side in the following verse: vairānubandha-tīvreṇa dhyānenācyuta-sātmatām nītau punar hareḥ pārśvaṁ jagmatur viṣṇu-pārṣadau These two associates of Lord Viṣṇu—Jaya and Vijaya— maintained a feeling of enmity for a very long time. Because of always thinking of Kṛṣṇa in this way, they regained the shelter of the Lord. (SB [7.1.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/1.47))

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**Emperor Yudhiṣṭhira gave generous gifts to the sacrificial priests and the members of the assembly, properly honoring them all in the manner prescribed by the Vedas. He then took the avabhṛtha bath.**

**Комментарий:**

The king took the avabhṛtha bath at the conclusion of the sacrifice. He was the sole ruler (eka-rāṭ)since he had now attained his kingdom.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**Thus Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of all masters of mystic yoga, saw to the successful execution of this great sacrifice on behalf of King Yudhiṣṭhira. Afterwards, the Lord stayed with his intimate friends for a few months at their earnest request.**

**Комментарий:**

Though Kṛṣṇa was the controller of the lords of yoga such as Śiva, he followed his devotee Yudhiṣṭhira controlled by his prema.

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**Then the Lord, the son of Devakī, took the reluctant permission of the king and returned to his capital with his wives and ministers.**

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**I have already described to you in detail the history of the two residents of Vaikuṇṭha who had to undergo repeated births in the material world because of being cursed by brāhmaṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

Vaikuṇṭha-vāsinoḥ refers to Jaya and Vijaya.

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**Purified in the avabhṛtha ritual, which marked the successful completion of the Rājasūya sacrifice, King Yudhiṣṭhira shone among the assembled brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas like the king of the devatās himself.**

**Комментарий:**

Sura-rāḍ means Indra.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**The devatās, humans and residents of intermediate heavens, all properly honored by the king, happily set off for their respective domains while singing the praises of Kṛṣṇa and the great sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

The devatās like Brahmā, the humans, such as the kings, and the khecaras such as the Siddhas, after being honored, returned to their abodes.

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**\[All were satisfied\] except sinful Duryodhana, the personification of the age of quarrel and the disease of the Kuru dynasty. He could not bear to see the flourishing opulence of the son of Pāṇḍu.**

**Комментарий:**

All the devotees were joyful. The wicked however are distressed by their own sins. To understand this, the pain of the chief wicked is described. He did not praise Kṛṣṇa or the sacrifice. Neither did he go home joyfully. He remained burning with lamentation.

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**One who recites these activities of Kṛṣṇa, including the killing of Śiśupāla, coronation of Yudhiṣṭhira, the deliverance of the kings and the performance of the Rājasūya sacrifice, is freed from all obstacles to bhakti.**

**Комментарий:**

Vitānam means sacrifice.

## Chapter 75 - Duryodhana Humiliated

### Text 1-2

**Перевод:**

**Mahārāja Parīkṣit said: O brāhmaṇa, according to what I have heard from you, all the assembled kings, sages and devatās were delighted to see the wonderful festivities of King Yudhiṣṭhira’s sacrifice, with the sole exception of Duryodhana. Please tell me why this was so, my lord.**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventy-fifth chapter, the joy of the avabhṛtha bath among the friends, the activities of the sacrifice and the breaking of Duryodhana’s pride are described. I have heard from your mouth (śrutam).

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bādarāyaṇi said: At the Rājasūya sacrifice of your saintly grandfather, his family members, bound by their love for him, engaged themselves in humble services on his behalf.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva already mentioned one reason why Duryodhana, who could not tolerate the opulence of the Pāṇḍavas, was envious (yo na sehe srīyaṁ sphītāṁ - SB [10.74.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/74.53)). Now he describes the remaining portion of the sacrifice, which arose in his mind, as the cause for his intolerance according to the logic of the lion looking back . They acted out of prema, not out of orders from the king.

### Text 4-7

**Перевод:**

**Bhīma supervised the kitchen, Duryodhana looked after the treasury, while Sahadeva respectfully greeted the arriving guests. Nakula procured needed items, Arjuna attended the respectable elders, and Kṛṣṇa washed everyone’s feet, while Draupadī served food, and generous Karṇa gave out the gifts. Many others, such as Yuyudhāna; Vikarṇa, Krtavarmā, Vidura, Bhūriśravā and other sons of Bāhlīka; and Santardana, similarly volunteered for various duties during the elaborate sacrifice. They did so because of their eagerness to please Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, O best of kings.**

**Комментарий:**

Who was engaged where? First two verses go together. Sahadeva was engaged in respecting guests (pūjāyāṁ). Nakula supplied various articles (dravya-sādhane). Arjuna applied sandalwood to the elders (guru-śuśrūṣaṇe). Kṛṣṇa, out of prema for Yudhiṣṭhira, oversaw the washing of feet because those who had pride could not do so.“My devotee’s sacrifice should not be stopped by this action.” Vikarṇa was the brother of Duryodhana. Hārdikya refers to Kṛtavarmā. Ādayaḥ after Vidura refers to Bhīṣma, Droṇa and others. Bhīsma and Droṇa were engaged in ascertaining what to do and not to do according to the description in Sabhā-parva, Mahābhārata. The son of Bāhlīka was Somadatta. Somadatta’s son was Bhūri. The word ādyaḥ means Bhūriśravā, another son of Somadatta. Yet Bhūri is called Bāhlīka’s son here since sons and grandsons are not considered different. Santardana refers to a prince of Kekaya, a son of Śrutakīrti, sister of Kuntī.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**After the priests, the prominent delegates, the greatly learned saints and the king’s most intimate well-wishers had all been properly honored with pleasing words, auspicious offerings and various gifts as remuneration, and after the king of Cedi had entered the lotus feet of the Lord of the Sātvatas, the avabhṛtha bath was performed in the divine river Gaṅgā.**

**Комментарий:**

When the priests, delegates, and learned sages were worshipped properly with affectionate words, by gifts of ornaments and donations, they all bathed Yudhiṣṭhira, on the occasion of the avabhṛtha bath. The word dyu-nadyām (in the “divine river” i.e. Gaṅgā) is used with the desire that the karma be related to the Gaṅgā just as it was related to the Yamunā (which actually flows near the city) and with regards to the honor of the family capital city (Hastināpura, which is on the bank of Gaṅgā).

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**During the avabhṛtha celebration, the music of many kinds of instruments resounded, including mṛdaṅgas, conchshells, panavas, dhundhuris, kettledrums and gomukha horns.**

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Female dancers danced with great joy, and choruses sang, while the loud vibrations of vīṇas, flutes and hand cymbals reached all the way to the heavenly regions.**

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**All the kings, wearing gold necklaces, then set off. They had flags and banners of various colors and were accompanied by infantrymen and well-adorned soldiers riding lordly elephants, chariots and horses.**

**Комментарий:**

Going to the bath is described till verse 16. They went with elephants, chariots, and horses which had colorful flags and banners and were accompanied by soldiers.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**The massed armies of the Yadus, Sṛñjayas, Kāmbojas, Kurus, Kekayas and Kośalas made the earth tremble as they followed Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja, the performer of the sacrifice, in procession.**

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**The assembly officials, the priests and other excellent brāhmaṇas resoundingly vibrated Vedic mantras, while the devatās, divine sages, Pitās and Gandharvas sang praises and rained down flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

The assembly officials and others went with the chanting of Vedas.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Men and women, all adorned with sandalwood paste, flower garlands, jewelry and fine clothing, sported by smearing and sprinkling one another with various liquids.**

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**The men smeared the courtesans with plentiful oil, yogurt, perfumed water, turmeric and kuṅkuma powder, and the courtesans playfully smeared the men with the same substances.**

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Surrounded by guards, King Yudhiṣṭhira’s queens came out on their chariots to see the fun, just as the devatās’ wives appeared in the sky in celestial airplanes. As maternal cousins and intimate friends sprinkled the queens with liquids, the ladies’ faces bloomed with shy smiles, enhancing the queens’ splendid beauty.**

**Комментарий:**

The wives (nṛ-devyaḥ) of King Yudhiṣṭhira such as Draupadī, Yaudheyī, etc., went out of the city on chariots to take part in the fun, just as the wives of the devatās enjoy riding in their celestial airplanes. They were sprinkled with water by friends and cousins. Their faces blossoming with shy smiles, they shone.
