The word mātuleya (maternal uncle’s son) refers the husband’s cousins such as Kṛṣṇa, etc., just as “nephew” would refer to nephews on the husband’s side. They, Kṛṣṇa and others were the queens’ devara (husband’s brothers) and also by connection with them others such as Bhīma, etc. The friends (sakhi) were those who were almost like brothers of Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma, etc., They could joke with them. This is mentioned in the next verse. It would be improper for the queens to joke with maternal cousins on their side.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**As the queens squirted water from syringes at their husbands’ brothers and other male friends, their own garments became drenched, revealing their arms, breasts, thighs and waists. In their excitement, the flowers fell from their loosened braids. By these charming pastimes they agitated those with contaminated consciousness.**

**Комментарий:**

They sprinkled water on their husband’s brothers and friends using leather bags and colorful cloth (dṛtībhiḥ) filled with water. Their hair became loose from absorption in splashing water. By this play they agitated Duryodhana and others (mala-dhiyām) and not the devotees.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**The emperor, mounted upon his chariot drawn by excellent horses wearing golden collars, appeared splendid in the company of his wives, just like the brilliant Rajasūya sacrifice surrounded by its various rituals.**

**Комментарий:**

After the water play, the king shone with Draupadī and others, who came to their husband, just as the king of sacrifices, Rājasūya, personified shone with its aṅgas.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**The priests led the king through the execution of the final rituals of patnī-saṁyāja and āvabhṛthya. Then they had him and Queen Draupadī sip water for purification and bathe in the Gaṅgā.**

**Комментарий:**

The priests had the king perform patnī-saṁyāja, a special sacrifice, and other actions related to the avabhṛtha bath (āvabhṛthyaiḥ).

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**The kettledrums of the gods resounded, along with those of human beings. Devatās, sages, Pitṛs and humans all showered flowers.**

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**All the citizens belonging to the various orders of varṇa and āśrama then bathed in that place, where even the most grievous sinner can immediately be freed from all sinful reactions.**

**Комментарий:**

After Yudhisthira bathed, others, even outcastes (narāḥ), bathed because one becomes freed from sin, by bathing in the Gaṅgā, the pilgrimage of avabhṛtha, supervised by Vyāsa and others.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Next the king put on new silken garments and adorned himself with fine jewelry. He then honored the priests, assembly officials, learned brāhmaṇas and other guests by presenting them with ornaments and clothing.**

**Комментарий:**

Ahate means new.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**In various ways King Yudhiṣṭhira, who had totally dedicated his life to Kṛṣṇa, continuously honored his relatives, his immediate family, the other kings, his friends and well-wishers, and all others present as well.**

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**All the men there shone like devatās. They were adorned with jeweled earrings, flower garlands, turbans, waistcoats, silk dhotīs and valuable pearl necklaces. The lovely faces of the women were beautified by their matched earrings and locks of hair, and they all wore golden belts.**

### Text 25-26

**Перевод:**

**Then the highly cultured priests, the great Vedic authorities who had served as sacrificial witnesses, the specially invited kings, the brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, devatās, sages, forefathers and other living beings, and the chief planetary rulers and their followers—all of them, having been worshipped by King Yudhiṣṭhira, took his permission and departed, O King, each for his own abode.**

**Комментарий:**

Mahā-śālāḥ means “of a great family.”

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**As they all glorified the wonderful Rājasūya sacrifice performed by that great saintly king and servant of the Lord, they were not satiated, just as an ordinary man is never satiated when drinking nectar.**

**Комментарий:**

Praising the great eminence of the Rājasūya of the king, skillful with knowledge (ṛṣeḥ), exclusively devoted to Kṛṣṇa (hari-dāsasya), they were not satisfied. Rather they continually praised him with affection, just as a person afflicted by disease, subjected to laws of death (martyaḥ), drinking nectar delicious to taste, which removes sufferings such as disease and death, is never satisfied.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**At that time Yudhiṣṭhira stopped a number of his friends, immediate family members and other relatives from departing, among them Kṛṣṇa. Out of love Yudhiṣṭhira could not let them go, for he felt the pain of imminent separation.**

**Комментарий:**

After the priests and others left for their own homes, out of affection, he prevented his friends from leaving though they wanted to go home.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**My dear Parīkṣit, the Supreme Lord remained there for some time to please the king, after first sending Sāmba and the other Yadu heroes back to Dvārakā.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he is Bhagavān, he was controlled by his prema.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Thus King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, was at last relieved of his burning ambition, having by the grace of Kṛṣṇa successfully crossed the vast and formidable ocean of his desires.**

**Комментарий:**

Having crossed the ocean of his desire (which he expressed previously in verses SB [10.72.3-5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/72.3)) due to Kṛṣṇa, Yudhiṣṭhira was free of worry (gata-jvaraḥ).

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**One day Duryodhana, while observing the riches of King Yudhiṣṭhira’s palace, felt greatly disturbed by the magnificence of both the Rājasūya sacrifice and its performer, the king, whose life and soul was Acyuta.**

**Комментарий:**

Now Śukadeva describes how Duryodhana’s pride was broken. Yudhiṣṭhira’s mind was absorbed in Kṛṣṇa alone (acyutātmanaḥ). The meaning is this. Out of great pride Duryodhana usually stayed in his own camp. Though during the sacrificial festival he now and then went to the palace, he did not pay much attention because of the crowds and occupation with his duties. Now, with his envy aroused on constantly hearing about it, he went there and saw the wealth of the kingdom. And having seen it, he experienced pain.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**In that palace all the collected wealth of the kings of men, demons and gods were brilliantly manifest, having been brought there by the cosmic inventor, Maya Dānava. With those riches Draupadī served her husbands, and Duryodhana, the prince of the Kurus, lamented because he was attracted to that wealth.**

**Комментарий:**

In the palace various treasures of kings shone in various ways, made by Tvaṣṭā. With that wealth, Draupadī served her husbands. Duryodhana developed a heart (visakta-hṛdayaḥ) greedy for that wealth (yasyām). He felt pain because of envy. “I am king of the Kauravas.”

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa’s thousands of queens were also staying in the palace. Their feet moved slowly, weighed down by their hips, and the bells on their feet tinkled charmingly. Their waists were very slender, the kuṅkuma from their breasts reddened their pearl necklaces, and their swaying earrings and flowing locks of hair enhanced the exquisite beauty of their faces.**

**Комментарий:**

What more to speak of that place where the wives of Kṛṣṇa, directly Lakṣmī, played? Their jingling feet moved slowly because of their heavy hips. They had attractive waists between their heavy hips. They had beautiful faces which shone (verb missing).

### Text 34-35

**Перевод:**

**It so happened that Emperor Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, was sitting just like Indra on a golden throne in the assembly hall built by Maya Dānava. Present with him were his attendants and family members, and also Kṛṣṇa, his special eye. Displaying the wealth of Kṛṣṇa himself, King Yudhiṣṭhira was being praised by the court poets.**

**Комментарий:**

Yudhisthira was sitting in that hall made by Maya, which was most extraordinary. This is described in Mahābhārata, Sabhā-parva. That hall had pillars of gold, ten thousand hands wide. Its exalted, divine form shone like fire, like the sun and like the moon. Eight thousand Rākṣasas called Kiṅkaras, directed by Maya, protected and maintained the hall. Surrounded by Kṛṣṇa who was like his eye, advising what was beneficial or harmful (sva-cakṣuṣā), he shone (verb should be supplied). Pārameṣṭhya was explained previously (in SB [10.70.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/70.41)).

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Proud Duryodhana, holding a sword in his hand and wearing a crown and necklace went into the palace in the company of his brothers. O King, in anger he then made insulting remarks.**

**Комментарий:**

He entered and abused the door keepers with sharp words, out of pride. He came with his brothers, holding a sword in his hand to show his bravery.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Bewildered by the illusions created through Maya Dānava’s magic, Duryodhana mistook the solid floor for water and lifted his lower garment. And elsewhere he fell into the water, mistaking it for the solid floor.**

**Комментарий:**

Duryodhana mistook the solid ground for water, so he lifted the end of his lower cloth. By mistaking water for solid ground, he fell in the water. Thus his crown fell off and his clothing was in disarray. By Maya’s expert arrangement which made things appear opposite to their true nature for those with inimical attitude, and by the destruction of his pride he was bewildered, made a fool.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**My dear Parīkṣit, Bhīma laughed to see this, and so did the women, kings and others. King Yudhiṣṭhira tried to stop them, but Kṛṣṇa showed his approval.**

**Комментарий:**

Even the women laughed. Though prevented by the king, who indicated by his eyes, “Do not laugh,” they were permitted by Kṛṣṇa. Moving his brow, he indicated, “Laugh.”

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Humiliated and burning with anger, Duryodhana turned his face down, left without uttering a word and went back to Hastināpura. The saintly persons present loudly cried out, “Alas, alas !” and King Yudhiṣṭhira was somewhat saddened. But the Supreme Lord, whose mere glance had bewildered Duryodhana, remained silent, for his intention was to remove the burden of the earth.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa desired to remove the burden of the earth.“The seed of quarrel being sown by Bhīma and others’ laughing, growing into a thorny tree of quarrel, dividing the Kurus, will destroy them.” Thinking in this way he was silent. By his glance Duryodhana was bewildered. The illusions of Maya were only the instrument for that.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**I have now replied to your question, O King, concerning why Duryodhana was dissatisfied on the occasion of the great Rājasūya sacrifice.**

## Chapter 76 - The Battle Between Śālva and the Vṛṣṇis

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Now please hear, O King, another wondrous deed performed by Kṛṣṇa, who has a humanlike body to enjoy pastimes. Hear how he killed the master of Saubha.**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventy-sixth chapter, when Śālva fights with the Yadus, Pradyumna retreats from the battle on being hit by the club of Dyumā. Hear the astonishing actions of Kṛṣṇa, having a form which appears like human, prominent with pastimes. According to Viṣṇu Purāṇa, he is paraṁ brahma narākṛti: Parambrahman in human form.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Śālva was a friend of Śiśupāla’s. When he attended the wedding of Rukmiṇī, the Yadu warriors defeated him in battle, along with Jarāsandha and the other kings.**

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Śālva swore in the presence of all the kings: “I will rid the earth of Yādavas. Just see my prowess!”**

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Having thus made his vow, the foolish king proceeded to worship Śiva as his deity by eating a handful of dust each day, and nothing more.**

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**The great Lord Umāpati is known as “he who is quickly pleased,” yet only at the end of a year did he gratify Śālva, who had approached him for shelter, by offering him a choice of benedictions.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiva controlled Śālva by giving a boon.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Śālva chose a vehicle that could be destroyed by neither devatās, demons, humans, Gandharvas, Uragas nor Rākṣasas, that could travel anywhere he wished to go, and that would terrify the Vṛṣṇis.**

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Śiva said, “So be it.” On his order, Maya Dānava, who conquers his enemies’ cities, constructed a flying iron city named Saubha and presented it to Śālva.**

**Комментарий:**

Maya Dānava gave Śālva a chariot having the appearance of a city made out of iron (ayas-mayam) called Saubha.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**This unassailable vehicle was filled with darkness and could go anywhere. Upon obtaining it, Śālva went to Dvārakā, remembering the Vṛṣṇis’ enmity toward him.**

**Комментарий:**

It was covered with darkness (tamo-dhāma) and thus it could not be seen by the eye (durāsadam).

### Text 9-11

**Перевод:**

**Śālva besieged the city with a large army, O best of the Bharatas, decimating the outlying parks and gardens, the mansions along with their observatories, towering gateways and surrounding walls, and also the public recreational areas. From his excellent airship he threw down a torrent of weapons, including stones, tree trunks, thunderbolts, snakes and hailstones. A fierce whirlwind arose and blanketed all directions with dust.**

**Комментарий:**

Babhañja (literally destroyed) means “he attempted to destroy the city” since it is impossible to destroy them. Tolikā means walls. Vihārān are playgrounds. He threw weapons from Saubha. A whirlwind arose from the rapidly whirling Saubha.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Thus terribly tormented by the airship Saubha, Kṛṣṇa’s city had no peace, O King, just like the earth when it was attacked by the three aerial cities of the demons.**

**Комментарий:**

The city was about to be tormented (ardyamānā).

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Seeing his subjects so harassed, the glorious and heroic Pradyumna told them, “Do not fear,” and mounted his chariot.**

### Text 14-15

**Перевод:**

**The chief commanders of the chariot warriors—Sātyaki, Cārudeṣṇa, Sāmba, Akrūra and his younger brothers, along with Hārdikya, Bhānuvinda, Gada, Śuka and Sāraṇa—went out of the city with many other eminent bowmen, all girded in armor and protected by contingents of soldiers riding on chariots, elephants and horses, and also by companies of infantry.**

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**A tumultuous, hair-raising battle then commenced between Śālva’s forces and the Yadus. It equaled the great battles between the demons and devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

Śālvānām refers to persons coming from Śālva’s province.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**With his divine weapons Pradyumna instantly destroyed all of Śālva’s magic illusions, in the same way that the warm rays of the sun dissipate the darkness of night.**

**Комментарий:**

Uṣṇa-guḥ means the sun.

### Text 18-19

**Перевод:**

**Pradyumna’s arrows all had gold shafts, iron heads and perfectly smooth joints. With twenty-five of them he struck down Śālva’s commander-in-chief \[Dyumān\], and with one hundred he struck Śālva himself. Then he pierced Śālva’s officers with one arrow each, his chariot drivers with ten arrows each, and his horses and other carriers with three arrows each.**

**Комментарий:**

Pradyumna pierced Dyumān, the commander-in-chief (dhvajinīpālam) of the army, with twenty- five arrows having depressed joints (sannata-parvabhiḥ). Netṝn means chariot drivers.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**When they saw the glorious Pradyumna perform that amazing and mighty feat, all the soldiers on both sides praised him.**

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**At one moment the magic airship built by Maya Dānava appeared in many identical forms, and the next moment it was again only one. Sometimes it was visible, and sometimes not. Thus Śālva’s opponents could never be sure where it was.**

**Комментарий:**

Tat refers to Saubha.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**From one moment to the next, the Saubha airship appeared on the earth, in the sky, on a mountain peak or in the water. Like a whirling, flaming baton, it never remained in any one place.**

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Wherever Śālva would appear with his Saubha ship and his army, there the Yadu commanders would shoot their arrows.**

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Śālva became bewildered upon seeing his army and aerial city harassed by his enemy’s arrows, which struck like fire and the sun and were as intolerable as snake venom.**

**Комментарий:**

Śālva’s army and city were severely afflicted by the arrows released by the Yadu’s (pareritaiḥ) which were intolerable like snake venom (āśī-viṣa-durāsadaiḥ).

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Because the heroes of the Vṛṣṇi clan were eager for victory in both the worlds, they did not abandon their assigned posts on the battlefield, even though the downpour of weapons hurled by Śālva’s commanders tormented them.**

**Комментарий:**

They desired to control the upper and lower worlds (loka-dvayajigīṣavaḥ) by spreading their fame in order to benefit the universe.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Śālva’s minister Dyumān, previously wounded by Pradyumna, now ran up to him and, roaring loudly, struck him with his club of black steel.**

**Комментарий:**

Previously afflicted by Pradyumna’s weapons, Dyumān attacked with his club made of black steel (maurvyā).

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Pradyumna’s driver, the son of Dāruka, though his valiant master’s chest had not been shattered by the club, knowing well his duty, removed Pradyumna from the battlefield.**

**Комментарий:**

He removed (apohvāha) him from the field, taking him elsewhere, though his chest was not shattered (aśīrṇa-vakṣaḥ-sthalam)thinking, “rest for a moment and then subdue the enemy (arindamam)”. The chariot driver possessed the dharma of prema for Pradyumna (dharma-vit). He worried about the blow from the club, because of prema, which worries about the safety of the object of love. He had this nature because he was the son of Dāruka (who was Kṛṣṇa’s charioteer).

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Quickly regaining consciousness, Kṛṣṇa’s son Pradyumna said to his charioteer, “O driver, this is abominable—for me to have been removed from the battlefield!**

**Комментарий:**

Pradyumna had obtained a hint (labdha-saṁjñaḥ), he understood of his fainting from the charioteer due to being taken away from the battle. Saṁjñā means suggesting a meaning according to Amarakośa. He recovered in a moment. O charioteer! You removed me, who was unwounded, from the battlefield out of prema. This is not glorious since it appears like my cowardice to people. But I pretended to faint to increase the enthusiasm of the enemy. One should not believe the superficial meaning of these two verses, since such events like getting wounded and fainting are not actually possible for the Lord.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**“Except for me, no one born in the Yadu dynasty has ever been known to abandon the battlefield since I have attained a stain because of a driver with a coward’s heart.**

**Комментарий:**

Except for me who has attained a stain (prāpta-kilbiṣāt) because of a driver whose heart is without valor (klība-cittena), there is no one in the Yadus who is known to have abandoned the battlefield.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**“What will I say to my fathers, Balarāma and Keśava, when I return to them after having simply fled the battle? What can I tell them that will befit my honor?**

**Комментарий:**

How will I speak of my suitable action (kṣamam), when asked?

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**“Certainly my sisters-in-law will laugh at me and say, ‘O hero, tell us how in the world you turned into such a coward in battle with your enemies.’”**

**Комментарий:**

The wives of my elder cousins will speak. Tell us how you became impotent in the battle with the enemies (anyaiḥ). The word kathaṁ is repeated twice to show their astonishment.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**The driver replied: O long-lived one, I have done this knowing fully well my prescribed duty. O my Lord, the chariot driver must protect the master of the chariot when he is in danger, and the master must also protect his driver.**

**Комментарий:**

The affix mat (in āyuṣman–having long life) is used to indicate an eternal connection. O person spread over all time (ayuṣman)! O person spread over all places (vibho)! I did not have a trace of worry about your safety yet I have done this, knowing in detail about dharma. He explains the dharma: the charioteer will protect the fighter in danger and the fighter will protect the charioteer.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**With this rule in mind, I removed you from the battlefield, since you had been struck by your enemy’s club, were injured and became unconscious.**

**Комментарий:**

I took you elsewhere (apovāhitaḥ). Apovāhitaḥ instead of apavāhitaḥ is poetic license. I removed you, who were tormented (upasṛṣṭaḥ), from the battlefield because you fell unconscious (mūrchitaḥ) from the blows of the enemy’s club. It arose in my mind because of affection for you. I will take the chariot back into to the battlefield. Conquer the enemy. Please forgive me.

## Chapter 77 - Lord Kṛṣṇa Slays the Demon Śālva

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After refreshing himself with water, putting on his armor and picking up his bow, Pradyumna told his driver, “Take me back to where the hero Dyumān is standing.”**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventy-seventh chapter, Kṛṣṇa kills Śālva when he displays his bewildering powers and crushes the Saubha. After performing ācamana to remove the fault of leaving the battlefield, Pradyumna (saḥ) put on his armor (daṁśitaḥ).

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**In Pradyumna’s absence, Dyumān had been insulting his army, but now Pradyumna counterattacked Dyumān and, smiling, pierced him with eight arrows.**

**Комментарий:**

Pradyumna approached Dyumān who was shouting out of disrespect.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**With four of these arrows he struck Dyumān’s four horses, with one arrow, his driver, with two more arrows, his bow and chariot flag, and with the last arrow, Dyumān’s head.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse describes how he dispensed the eight arrows.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Gada, Sātyaki, Sāmba and others began killing Śālva’s army, and thus all the soldiers inside the airship began falling into the ocean, their necks severed.**

**Комментарий:**

The soldiers riding in the Saubha aircraft (saubheyāḥ) fell in the ocean with their heads cut off.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**As the Yadus and Śālva’s followers thus went on attacking one another, the tumultuous, fearsome battle continued for twentyseven days and nights.**

**Комментарий:**

The fight lasted twenty-seven days and nights (tri-nava-rātraṁ). Tri-nava-rātram is a dvigu compound of tri and nava-rātraṁ, which is again a dvigu compound of nava and rātri.

### Text 6-7

**Перевод:**

**Invited by Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, Kṛṣṇa had gone to Indraprastha. Now that the Rājasūya sacrifice had been completed and Śiśupāla killed, he took leave of the Kuru elders and the great sages, and also of Pṛthā and her sons. He returned to Dvārakā, while seeing inauspicious omens on the way.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said to himself: Because I have come here with my respected elder brother, kings partial to Śiśupāla may well be attacking my capital city.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse expresses Kṛṣṇa’s thoughts on the road. I have come here with my honorable (miśra) elder (ārya) Balarāma. Or I have come with those who have come with (miśra) Balarāma.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the omen he arrived at Dvārakā and saw his people defending the city and also saw Śālva and his Saubha airship. Keśava then addressed Dāruka as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking thus, Kṛṣṇa arrived at Dvārakā. Kṛṣṇa saw Śālva’s decimation of his forces. Entering Dvārakā by a secret passage, assigning Balarāma to protect the city, seeing Saubha and Śālva, he spoke to Dāruka.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] O driver, quickly take my chariot near Śālva. This lord of Saubha is a powerful magician; don’t let him bewilder you.**

**Комментарий:**

You should not be afraid (sambhramaḥ) since he is a magician (māyāvī), but not a warrior by nature.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Thus ordered, Dāruka took command of the Lord’s chariot and drove forth. As the chariot entered the battlefield, everyone there, both friend and foe, caught sight of the emblem of Garuḍa.**

**Комментарий:**

Everyone saw the chariot with the Garuḍa emblem (aruṇānujam) on its flag enter the battle.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**When Śālva, the master of a decimated army, saw Kṛṣṇa approaching, he hurled his spear at the Lord’s charioteer. The spear roared in a frightening way as it flew across the battlefield.**

**Комментарий:**

Though all of Śālva’s generals had been almost destroyed (hataprāya-baleśvaraḥ), he still threw his spear at Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Śālva’s hurtling spear lit up the whole sky like a mighty meteor, but Kṛṣṇa tore the approaching weapon into hundreds of pieces with his arrows.**

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa then pierced Śālva with sixteen arrows and struck the Saubha airship with a deluge of arrows as it darted about the sky. Firing his arrows, the Lord appeared like the sun flooding the heavens with its rays.**

**Комментарий:**

With its dark blue color and rapid movements, the Saubha aircraft appeared like the sky (khaṁ). Kṛṣṇa’s arrows are compared to the sun’s rays in terms of their being countless and creating unbearably scorching heat. Kṛṣṇa himself is compared to the sun, in terms of his being all-potent and victorious over opponents.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Śālva then managed to strike Kṛṣṇa’s left arm, which held his bow Śārṅga, and, amazingly, Śārṅga fell from his hand.**

**Комментарий:**

Verse 15 and 16 are repetition according to worldly perception but not the opinion of Śukadeva Gosvāmī since his opinion is stated ahead. It is similar to worldly perception where Karṇa appears to be superior to Arjuna or weapons wound Kṛṣṇa. This has just been repeated by Vyāsadeva. Śālva struck Kṛṣṇa’s left arm. Doḥ is neuter since Raghu-kāvya says savyaṁ dor acchinat tasya: he injured his left arm. The falling of the Śārṅga bow (tat) was amazing.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Those who witnessed this all cried out in dismay. Then the master of Saubha roared loudly and addressed Janārdana, destroyer of the wicked.**

### Text 17-18

**Перевод:**

**\[Śālva said:\] You fool! Because in our presence you kidnapped the bride of our friend Śiśupāla, your own cousin, and because you later murdered him in the sacred assembly while he was inattentive, today with my sharp arrows I will send you to the land of no return! Though you think yourself invincible, I will kill you now if you dare stand before me.**

**Комментарий:**

Because you stole the bride of our friend and your brother, the son of your father’s sister, Śiśupāla, and in the assembly, not the battlefield, you killed him while he was inattentive, I will kill you today (apunar-āvṛttim). He cries out “O friend” in great grief. Sarasvatī devī gives the meaning: O one due to whom there is no ignorance (amūḍha)! O giver of knowledge! You took Lakṣmī, who is actually your rightful wife, while we and our friend Śiśupāla, your paternal cousin, were watching, and were completely ignored by you. You killed our friend who was acting wildly and using bad words like a drunkard. By your arrows, today I will attain you due to whom one does not experience saṁsāra since you give liberation, who are not defeated by anyone, and who are worshipped. The root is naya (to go).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O dullard, you boast in vain, since you fail to see death standing near you. Real heroes do not talk much but rather show their prowess in action.**

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Having said this, the furious Lord swung his club with frightening power and speed and hit Śālva on the collarbone, making him tremble and vomit blood.**

**Комментарий:**

Śālva (saḥ) trembled and vomited blood.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**But as soon as Kṛṣṇa took up his club, Śālva disappeared from sight, and a moment later a man approached the Lord. Bowing his head down to him, he announced, “Devakī has sent me,” and, sobbing, spoke the following words.**

**Комментарий:**

When Kṛṣṇa again took the club in his hand (sannivṛttāyām) Śālva disappeared. The opinion of others is expressed from here till verse twenty-nine. The man who appeared was an illusion created by Śālva.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**\[The man said:\] O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, mighty-armed one, who are so affectionate to your parents! Śālva has seized your father and taken him away, as a butcher leads an animal to slaughter.**

**Комментарий:**

Your father being insulted or being injured has been taken away (apanītaḥ) by Śālva, like an animal taken away by a butcher. The meaning revealed by Sarasvatī devī is this. Someone who is not your father (apitā), but similar, made by illusion, has been taken away.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**When he heard this disturbing news, Kṛṣṇa, who was playing the role of a mortal man, showed sorrow and compassion, and out of love for his parents he spoke the following words like an ordinary conditioned soul.**

**Комментарий:**

Ghṛṇī means having compassion for his father.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] Balarāma is ever vigilant, and no devatā or demon can defeat him. So how could this insignificant Śālva defeat him and abduct my father? Indeed, fate is all-powerful!**

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**When Govinda was speaking these words, the master of Saubha again appeared, apparently leading Vasudeva before the Lord. Śālva then spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Śālva brought some form looking like Vasudeva before the Lord.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**\[Śālva said:\] Here is your dear father, who begot you and for whose sake you are living in this world. I shall now kill him before your very eyes. Save him if you can, weakling!**

**Комментарий:**

Here is the person who produced you (not the person who fed you) (janitā), your father (tātaḥ). For him you live. As a good son, you should give up your life for him. O ignorant person, ignorant of my power (bāliśa)! But Sarasvatī devī suggests another meaning. This person did not produce you (ajānitā), thus he is not your father (atātaḥ) but an illusion, on account of whom you show your strength (arthamjīvasi) to me. Jīvasi can mean you show strength as well as you live, since roots have multiple meanings. While you see, I will kill this form. Watch the show. The etymology of bālīśa is: O omniscient lord who destroys (śyati) the foolish leaders of the assembly (bālin)! The word cet is used for emphasis as in the sentence yadi vedāḥ pramāṇaṁ syuḥ. Deliver me from saṁsāra since you are completely independent (īśaś cet).

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**After he had mocked the Lord in this way, the magician Śālva appeared to cut off Vasudeva’s head with his sword. Taking the head with him, he entered the Saubha vehicle, which was hovering in the sky.**

**Комментарий:**

He cut off the head of the form appearing to be Vasudeva.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**By nature Kṛṣṇa is full in knowledge, and he possesses unlimited powers of perception. Yet for a moment, out of great affection for his loved ones, he remained absorbed in the mood of an ordinary human being. He soon recalled, however, that this was all a demoniac illusion engineered by Maya Dānava and employed by Śālva.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa remained overcome (upaplutaḥ) with the sentiments of an ordinary human (prakṛtau) out of great affection for his father because the head was severed. He was greatly mistaken (su abodhaḥ). After that, the Lord (mahānubhāvaḥ), understood that it was a demonic illusion created by Śālva, taught by Maya.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Now alert to the actual situation, the Lord with indestructible knowledge saw before him on the battlefield neither the messenger nor his father’s body. It was as if he had awakened from a dream. Seeing his enemy flying above him in his Saubha plane, the Lord then prepared to kill him.**

**Комментарий:**

After a moment, he observed externally the situation. An example is given. A person even in dream realizes “This is a dream.” After an instant he does not see the objects related to the dream.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Such is the account given by some sages, O wise King, but those who speak in this illogical way are contradicting themselves, having forgotten their own previous statements.**

**Комментарий:**

Having presented the opinion of others (verses 21-29), Śukadeva Gosvāmī now refutes it. Some, though sages, lacking understanding (anvitāḥ), disregarding the context of previous and later statements, do not possibly or certainly remember that they contradict themselves because of their own words (sva-vacaḥ). Nūnaṁ is used in the sense of conjecture or certainty. Śrī Kṛṣṇa did not go to participate in the Rājasūya sacrifice in the company of Balarāma, since it was previously stated: saṅkarṣaṇam anujñāpya, “Kṛṣṇa went to Indraprastha after taking leave of Balarāma.” (SB [10.71.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/71.13)) Thus how can the statements of Kṛṣṇa related by them, ārya-miśrābhisaṅgataḥ,“Because I have come here with my respected elder brother” (verse 8)be reconciled? Even if Rāma had gone for the Rājasūya sacrifice how can it be reconciled with their statements such as kathaṁ rāmam asambhrāntaṁ jitvājeyaṁ surāsuraiḥ: “How could a weakling like Śālva defeat Balarāma, who is unconquerable by demigods or demons, and take away my father?” (SB [10.77.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/77.24)) Thus those who are not learned speak thus. But that is not so.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**How can lamentation, bewilderment, material affection or fear, all born out of ignorance, be ascribed to the infinite Supreme Lord, whose knowledge of ātmā, perception and power are all similarly infinite? COMMENTARY Impossibility of this in Lord is described. Where is lamentation, bewilderment, etc., described by them and where is the infinite internal consciousness, etc., of the Lord? Kva (where) is repeated twice indicating impossibility. Similarly one can never say that connection with darkness is present in the sun. The meaning is this. How did Kṛṣṇa manifest lamentation, illusion, and affection in regard to Vasudeva? If it was impossible for Kṛṣṇa to be afraid of Śālva, then how is it said that Kṛṣṇa’s Śārṇga bow fall from his hands (verse 15), and that seeing the ill omens he feared about Dvārakā (verse 8). By calling all these emotions as ajña-saṁbhavāḥ (born of ignorance) it is understood that there are other emotions which are born of knowledge. On seeing the suffering of the materialists, Prahlāda revealed his sorrow to Nṛsiṁhadeva. At the beginning of the story of Brahmā’s bewilderment, Śukadeva was bewildered by prema. Bharata became merciful and affectionate to King Rahugaṇa, who knew nothing of the Lord. The Kumāras described their fear (of the offence) caused by their curse of the door keepers of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha. The Lord himself in the Dāmodara pastime established these contrary displays (such as being controlled by his mother though he is the controller) by showing that his nature is to be merciful to the devotees.**

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**By virtue of self-realization fortified by service rendered to his feet, devotees of the Lord dispel the bodily concept of life, which has bewildered the soul since time immemorial. Thus they attain eternal glory in his personal association. How, then, can that Supreme Truth, the destination of all genuine saints, be subject to illusion?**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord cannot be bewildered by Śālva’s tricks. This is stated by kaimutya logic. Even the devotees cannot be bewildered. By knowledge nourished by service to the Lord’s feet, the devotees keep at a distance the bodily concept which opposes the ātmā without beginning. They attain liberation with realization of their svarūpa (ātmīyam) and Vaikuṇṭha (aiśvaram). How then can Kṛṣṇa fall into illusion by the tricks of Śālva? Thus one should not believe the descriptions.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**While Śālva continued to hurl torrents of weapons at him with great force, Kṛṣṇa, whose prowess never fails, shot his arrows at Śālva, wounding him and shattering his armor, bow and crest jewel. Then with his club the Lord smashed his enemy’s Saubha airship.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa crushed (ruroja) Śālva’s aircraft with his club.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Shattered into thousands of pieces by Kṛṣṇa’s club, the Saubha airship plummeted into the water. Śālva abandoned it, stationed himself on the ground, took up his club and rushed toward Acyuta.**

**Комментарий:**

Tat refers to the vehicle. Toye means “in the ocean.”

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**As Śālva rushed at him, the Lord shot a dart and cut off his arm that held the club. Having finally decided to kill Śālva, Kṛṣṇa then raised his Sudarśana disc weapon, which resembled the sun at the time of universal annihilation. The brilliantly shining Lord appeared like the easternmost mountain bearing the rising sun.**

**Комментарий:**

The astonishing cakra is described. In the fight, the cakra was very effulgent and the Lord appeared most beautiful.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Employing his disc, the Lord removed that great magician’s head with its earrings and crown, just as Purandara had used his thunderbolt to cut off Vṛtra’s head. Seeing this, people shouted in amazement.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord cut off the head of the demon endowed with great illusions (puru-māyinaḥ) pulling the head in front of his troops. The Lord did this with the head’s crown and earrings intact, to show his sporting nature.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**With the sinful Śālva now dead and his Saubha airship destroyed, the heavens resounded with kettledrums played by groups of devatās. Then Dantavakra, wanting to avenge the death of his friends, furiously attacked the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Sālva fell down, completely dead (nipatite) since he obtained liberation, with no return. Dantavakra came there to avenge the death of his friends such as Śiśupāla, Śālva, etc., by subduing their enemy as if performing their death rites (apacitam). He was foolish in doing this.

## Chapter 78 - The Killing of Dantavakra, Vidūratha and Romaharṣaṇa

### Text 1-2

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Acting out of friendship for Śiśupāla, Śālva and Pauṇḍraka, who had all passed on to the next world, the wicked Dantavakra appeared on the battlefield in a great rage, O King. All alone, on foot and wielding a club in his hand, the mighty warrior shook the earth with his footsteps.**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventy-eighth chapter, Kṛṣṇa kills Dantavakra and Vidūratha and Balarāma kills Romaharṣaṇa-sūta while on pilgrimage. Two verses describe how Dantavakra took revenge for the death of his friends as stated previously (in SB [10.77.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/77.37)). Though they were not present, Dantavakra came to do his duty as their friend (pārokṣya-sauhṛdam). Possessing great strength (mahā-sattvaḥ) he shook the earth (imām) with his footsteps.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Dantavakra approach, Kṛṣṇa quickly picked up his club, jumped down from his chariot and stopped his advancing opponent just as the shore holds back the ocean.**

**Комментарий:**

Since his opponent was on foot, Kṛṣṇa dismounted (avaplutya) from his chariot. Kṛṣṇa stopped Dantavakra just as the shore checks (vela) the ocean waves.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Raising his club, the reckless Dantavakra said to Lord Mukunda, “What luck! What luck—to have you come before me today!**

**Комментарий:**

Dantavakra was born in Karūṣa province (kārūṣaḥ). Sarasvatī devī speaks as follows. Being freed of false pride (durmada), Dantavakra spoke to Mukunda: Now at the end of third lifetime you will give liberation (mukundam).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**“You are our maternal cousin, Kṛṣṇa, but you committed violence against my friends, and now you want to kill me also. Therefore, fool, I will kill you with my thunderbolt club.**

**Комментарий:**

Dantavakra’s mother was Śrutadevī, sister of Vasudeva. Thus Kṛṣṇa was his cousin from his mother’s side (mātuleyaḥ). O Kṛṣṇa!though you are my cousin, you killed my friends and you want to kill me. Sarasvatī devī gives another meaning. Though you are our Lord, you have now appeared as my cousin. Nevertheless, it is proper that you desire to kill me, who am envious of my own cousin (mitra-dhruk-mām). O supreme one (amanda)! Due to your club, Kaumodakī which shines like diamonds (vajra-kalpayā), which is my killer, I will attain you.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**“Then, O unintelligent one, I who am affectionate to my friends will have repaid my debt to them by killing you, my enemy disguised as a relative, who are like a disease within the body.”**

**Комментарий:**

Thus I will repay my debts to my friends. I will kill you who appear to be a friend but are actually a great enemy (bandhu-rūpam). You are like a disease causing great suffering to one’s body. But Sarasvatī devī gives the following meaning. O omniscient one (ajña)! Out of affection for my friends, I will free myself of my debt by liberating them by having a relationship with me, your devotee, after understanding that you, seen as an enemy because of the curse of the Kumāras, are actually a friend who gives benefit, the antaryāmī who resides in the body and destroys mental pain (vi ādhim).

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Thus trying to harass Kṛṣṇa with harsh words, as one might prick an elephant with sharp goads, Dantavakra struck the Lord on the head with his club and roared like a lion.**

**Комментарий:**

The “harsh words” is in reference to the apparent (external) meaning of his words. The words did not cause any inner pain to the Lord. The blow to his head was to stimulate his vīra-rasa.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Although hit by Dantavakra’s club, Kṛṣṇa, the deliverer of the Yadus, did not budge from his place on the battlefield. Rather, with his massive Kaumodakī club the Lord struck Dantavakra in the middle of his chest.**

**Комментарий:**

Hit by his club in the fighting (ājau), the chief of the Yadus did not fall.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**His heart shattered by the club’s blow, Dantavakra vomited blood and fell lifeless to the ground, his hair disheveled and his arms and legs sprawling.**

**Комментарий:**

The phrase keśa-bāhv-aṅghrīn in plural is poetic license.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**A most subtle and wondrous spark of light then \[rose from the demon’s body and\] entered Lord Kṛṣṇa while everyone looked on, O King, just as when Śiśupāla was killed.**

**Комментарий:**

From his body (tataḥ) a light, the body of Vijaya, the Lord’s associate, very subtle, since it could not be seen by the eyes, entered Kṛṣṇa. The light was not small by measurement since when Śiśupāla died it was said ulkeva bhuvi khāc cyutā: he was like a meteor falling from the sky to the earth. (SB [10.74.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/74.45)) It was astonishing (adbhutam) due to being extraordinary. But all people saw it directly by the Lord’s will, to broadcast his glory. Like Śiśupāla he entered the Lord. Since both were associates of the Lord, it is suggested that they both entered the Lord in a similar manner .

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**But then Dantavakra’s brother Vidūratha, immersed in sorrow over his brother’s death, came forward breathing heavily, sword and shield in hand. He wanted to kill the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Vidūratha, brother of Dantavakra, was different from the Yādava Vidūratha .

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**O best of kings, as Vidūratha fell upon him, Kṛṣṇa used his razoredged Sudarśana disc to remove his head, complete with its helmet and earrings.**

**Комментарий:**

When he rushed forward (āpatataḥ), Kṛṣṇa cut off his head.

### Text 13-15

**Перевод:**

**Having thus destroyed Śālva and his Saubha airship, along with Dantavakra and his younger brother, all of whom were invincible before any other opponent, the Lord was praised by devatās, human beings and great sages, by Siddhas, Gandharvas, Vidyādharas and Mahoragas, and also by Apsarās, Pitṛs, Yakṣas, Kinnaras and Cāraṇas. As they sang his glories and showered him with flowers, the Supreme Lord entered his festively decorated capital city in the company of the most eminent Vṛṣṇis.**

**Комментарий:**

After killing the demons, though they had intolerable prowess for others, Kṛṣṇa was worshipped by others. He was surrounded by the most eminent of the Vṛṣṇis, such as Pradyumna, etc., and Balarāma and others who now approached him after they had been killed. He entered the city which was naturally decorated, or was especially decorated after the killing of the most wicked. The details concerning the killing of Dantavakra are given in the Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa beginning with the verse: Then, hearing that Śiśupāla had been killed, Dantavakra went to Mathurā to fight against Kṛṣṇa. The essence of that section is this. After Śālva was killed by Kṛṣṇa, to fight with him, Dantavakra came close to Mathurā to attack his territories (i.e. Dvārakā). Hearing about this from Nāradā (in verses such as SB [10.71.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/71.9)), to carry out the request of Uddhava, eager to see the people of Vraja, he came by chariot to the gate of Mathurā at the speed of the mind and there killed him with his club. Bathing in the Yamunā he went to Vraja. By that he made following statements true: As he departed, that best of the Yadus saw how the gopīs, were lamenting, and thus he consoled them by sending a messenger with this loving promise: “I will return.” (SB [10.39.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/39.35)) Now you should all return to Vraja, dear father. We shall come to see you, our dear relatives who suffer in separation from us, as soon as we have given some happiness to your well-wishing friends. (SB [10.45.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/45.23)) \[Uddhava said:\] Infallible Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the devotees, will soon return to Vraja to satisfy his parents. (SB [10.46.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/46.34)) He lived upto his name Satyavāk. In Vraja he met with the extremely joyful residents, greeted them, and had pastimes with them for two months. Then he entered with them into a special manifestation of Vraja, called Vaikuṇṭha, described as gopānāṁ svaṁ lokaṁ (SB [10.28.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/28.14)) in the story of Varuṇa’s taking Nanda. He sent the aṁśas of Nanda and others such as Droṇa to Vaikuṇṭha. In one form he mounted his chariot and returned to Dvārakā. The residents of heaven perceived that Kṛṣṇa is going to Vaikuṇṭha with his relatives. And those who dwelled near Vraja perceived that killing Dantavakra, taking his parents, etc., he has gone toward Dvārakā. Some of them were surprised that suddenly all the people of Vraja had disappeared somewhere. The order of events is as follows. First the eclipse at Kurukṣetra, then the Rājasūya sacrifice, then the gambling match, and the exile of the Pāṇḍavas, then the killing of Śālva, Dantavakra, and his return to Vraja and the concealing of Vraja pastimes. When the Pāṇḍavas returned from the forest, Balarāma was on pilgrimage. The journey to the eclipse at Kurukṣetra took place not too long after Kṛṣṇa had killed Kaṁsa. Bhīṣma and others were present there.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Thus Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, the master all mystic power and Lord of the universe, is ever victorious. Only those of beastly vision think he sometimes suffers defeat.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he has such powers, the materialists are not astonished at his actions. “Kṛṣṇa easily conquers even the strongest. Yet he is defeated by Jarāsandha.” Persons with animal vision like Duryodhana think like this. He is never defeated since he is the master of yoga, Bhagavān, the lord of the universe.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma then heard that the Kurus were preparing for war with the Pāṇḍavas. Being neutral, he departed on the pretext of going to bathe in holy places.**

**Комментарий:**

After killing the wicked ending with Vidūratha, Kṛṣṇa gave up killing them. But Balarāma killed Romaharṣaṇa Sūta and Balvala. Śukadeva describes that topic. “Yudhiṣṭhira is dear to me and Duryodhana is my disciple. Thus whose side should I choose?” Thinking thus, on the pretext of pilgrimage, he left Dvārakā, being neutral to both parties (madhya-sthaḥ).

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**After bathing at Prabhāsa and honoring the devatās, sages, forefathers and prominent human beings, he went in the company of brāhmaṇas to the portion of the Sarasvatī that flows westward into the sea.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma went to Sarasvatī and bathed in the part that flows backwards.

### Text 19-20

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma visited Pṛthūdaka, Bindu-saras, Tritakūpa, Sudarśana, Viśāla, Brahma-tīrtha, Cakra-tīrtha and the eastward-flowing Sarasvatī. He also went to all the holy places along the Yamunā and the Ganges, O Bhārata, and then he came to the Naimiṣa forest, where great sages were performing an elaborate sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

Regarding the well Tritakūpa it is famous that Trita was the brother of Eka and Dvita. Cheating himself, he went ahead of his two brothers who were herding cows, and, in fear of a wolf, he fell in that well and there he worshipped the devatās with the Soma beverage and came out of that well. Thus the well was named after him. Tritakūpa is on the bank of the Sarasvatī River. He went to Cakra-tīrtha (cakram). Balarāma visited all the holy places along (anu) the Gaṅgā and Yamunā and then went to Naimiṣa.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Recognizing the Lord upon his arrival, the sages, who had been engaged in their sacrificial rituals for a long time, greeted him properly by standing up, bowing down and worshiping him.**

**Комментарий:**

They understood that he had come. In respect they first stood up, then they offered respects on the ground and welcomed him. Then they worshipped him.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**After being thus worshipped along with his entourage, the Lord accepted a seat of honor. Then he noticed that Romaharṣaṇa, Vyāsadeva’s disciple, had remained seated.**

**Комментарий:**

As a disciple of Vyāsa, Romaharṣaṇa should have had good qualities such as good conduct. But he remained seated. Therefore he was a great offender.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma became extremely angry at Romaharṣaṇa and the brāhmaṇas upon seeing how this member of the sūta caste had failed to stand up, bow down or join his palms, and remained seated.**

**Комментарий:**

First Romaharṣaṇa did not rise. Then he did not offer respects or fold his hands. Then he was seated above the brāhmaṇas. Moreover he saw that he was sūta class by the special marks. With each of these items, Balarāma became more and more astonished. Romaharṣānā was sitting high above the brāhmaṇas, since he was reciting Purāṇas.

### Text 24-25

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Balarāma said:\] Why does this fool born from an improperly mixed marriage sits above all these brāhmaṇas and even above me, the protector of religion? He deserves to die. Being a disciple of the divine sage Vyāsa, he has thoroughly learned many scriptures from him, including the lawbooks of religious duties and the epic histories and Purāṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

Why is this fool seated higher than these brāhmaṇas dedicated to sacrifice (imān) and even me the protector of dharma? It is not because of any other reason but only because he is foolish (durmatiḥ). It should not be said that he remained seated out of ignorance, for he is the disciple of Vyāsa and learned.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**All this study has not produced good qualities in him. Rather, his study of the scriptures is like an actor’s studying his part. Because he has not controlled his mind or senses, his scholarly authority is useless.**

**Комментарий:**

The scriptures studied by him will not bear results such as peacefulness of mind.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**The very purpose of my descent into this world is to kill such hypocrites who pretend to be religious. Indeed, they are the most sinful rascals.**

**Комментарий:**

Dharma-dvajinaḥ refers to those who show that they follow dharma though they are devoid of dharma.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Although Balarāma had stopped killing the impious while on pilgrimage, Romaharṣaṇa’s death was inevitable. Thus, having spoken, the Lord killed him by picking up a blade of kuśa grass and touching him with its tip.**

**Комментарий:**

Speaking all this to himself, though he had renounced killing while on pilgrimage, Balarāma killed him with the tip of a kuśa grass since his death was destined like that. He killed with a piece of kuśa that he held in his hand while he acted as a brahmacārī while going on pilgrimage.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**All the sages cried out, “Alas, alas!” in great distress. They told Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa, “O master, you have committed an irreligious act!**

**Комментарий:**

The real meaning of their words is “You have done the highest dharma (adharmaḥ).”

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**“O favorite of the Yadus, we gave him the seat of the spiritual master and promised him long life and freedom from physical pain for as long as this sacrifice continues.**

**Комментарий:**

“How can the killing of a son born of an improperly mixed marriage, which is devoid of dharma, be a fault?” He was given the seat to recite the Purāṇas with the benediction of long life without physical suffering.

### Text 31-32

**Перевод:**

**“You have unknowingly killed a brāhmaṇa. Of course, even the injunctions of revealed scripture cannot dictate to you, the Lord of all mystic power. But if by your own freewill you nonetheless carry out the prescribed purification for this slaying of a brāhmaṇa, O purifier of the whole world, people in general will greatly benefit by your example.”**

**Комментарий:**

Although you are omniscient, you have acted just like an ignorant man. You should not incur sin by this since you are the lord of yoga. You are not under the control of scriptures (āmnāyaḥ) which say that the brāhmaṇa should not be killed. Yet if you, not being ordered by others, atone for the killing of a brāhmaṇa on your own, then that will teach people. There is no alternative. O purifier of the worlds!

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: I will certainly perform the atonement for this killing, since I wish to show compassion to the people in general. Please, therefore, prescribe for me whatever ritual is to be done chiefly.**

**Комментарий:**

You should prescribe the chief (prathame) atonement (nirveśam).

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**O sages, just say the word, and by my mystic power I shall restore everything you promised him—long life, strength and sensory power.**

**Комментарий:**

To please the brāhmaṇas he speaks. O brāhmaṇas (bata)! Say what you desire (āśāsitam) for your reciter of Purāṇas, Romaharṣāna— strength, power of senses, and anything else. I will supply them all by my yoga-māyā.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**The sages said: Please see to it, O Rāma, that your power and that of your kuśa weapon, as well as our promise and Romaharṣaṇa’s death, all remain intact.**

**Комментарий:**

O Rāma! May it happen in such a way that the truth of your weapon, your power and death of Romaharṣaṇa and our words remain intact.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: The Vedas instruct us that one’s own self takes birth again as one’s son. Thus let Romaharṣaṇa’s son become the speaker of the Purāṇas, and let him be endowed with long life, strong senses and stamina.**

**Комментарий:**

To fulfill that Balarāma speaks. The Vedas say: You have taken birth from my various limbs and have arisen from my very heart. You are my own self in the form of my son. May you live through a hundred autumns. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad [6.4.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bau/6.4.8)) Therefore let Romaharṣaṇa’s son, Ugraśrava, be the reciter of the Purāṇas for you, and let him be blessed with long life, power of senses and strength. Thus, since Romaharṣaṇa is not directly alive, the weapon and his death will remain true. Since long life, etc., are assured in the form of his son, your promise will remain true.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Please tell me your desire, O best of sages, and I shall certainly fulfill it. And, O wise souls, please carefully determine my proper atonement, since I do not know what it might be.**

**Комментарий:**

First, I should give some gift to you wise brāhmaṇas who will instruct me on atonement. Please tell what you desire. I will fulfill that. After that, you should think carefully and establish the proper atonement for an ignorant person, and think of my atonement too. O intelligent sages!

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**The sages said: A fearsome demon named Balvala, the son of Ilvala, comes here every new-moon day and contaminates our sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

First they express their desire in two verses. On every dark moon Balvala comes.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**O descendant of Daśārha, please kill that sinful demon, who pours down pus, blood, feces, urine, wine and meat upon us. This is the best service you can do for us.**

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, for twelve months, you should circumambulate the land of Bhārata in a mood of serious meditation, executing austerities and bathing at various holy pilgrimage sites. In this way you will become purified.**

**Комментарий:**

They then explain the atonement. You should travel around (parītya) Bhārata undergoing penance (caritvā). Only one year is stated since it is performed with fully concentrated mind and senses (su-samāhitaḥ). By this you will attain pure fame. The actual meaning taking the implicit causative meaning is: you will purify the universe even more, by your spotless fame.

## Chapter 79 - Lord Balarāma Goes on Pilgrimage

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Then, on the new-moon day, O King, a fierce and frightening wind arose, scattering dust all about and spreading the smell of pus everywhere.**

**Комментарий:**

In the seventy-ninth chapter, Balarāma kills Balvala, goes to many tīrthas, sees the fight between Bhīma and Duryodhana and returns to Dvārakā. Upāvṛtte means “arrived.”

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Next, onto the sacrificial arena came a downpour of abominable things sent by Balvala, after which the demon himself appeared, with trident in hand.**

**Комментарий:**

Saḥ refers to Balvala.

### Text 3-4

**Перевод:**

**The immense demon resembled a mass of black carbon. His topknot and beard were like molten copper, and his face had horrible fangs and furrowed eyebrows. Upon seeing him, Balarāma thought of his club, which tears to pieces his enemies’ armies, and his plow weapon, which punishes the demons. Thus summoned, his two weapons appeared before him at once.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together. He was very dark, like a mass of broken coals. His hair was like melted copper. His face had terrible teeth and a frown.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**With the tip of his plow Balarāma caught hold of the demon Balvala as he flew through the sky, and with his club the Lord angrily struck that harasser of brāhmaṇas on the head.**

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Balvala cried out in agony and fell to the ground, his forehead cracked open and gushing blood. He resembled a red mountain struck by a lightning bolt.**

**Комментарий:**

His body flowing with blood was like a mountain flowing with red minerals.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**The exalted sages honored Balarāma with sincere prayers and awarded him infallible blessings. Then they performed his ritual bath, just as the devatās had formally bathed Indra when he killed Vṛtra.**

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**They gave Balarāma a most attractive Vaijayantī garland of unfading lotuses and they also gave him a set of divine garments and jewelry.**

**Комментарий:**

They gave Balarāma a Vaijayantī garland of unfading lotuses which was the abode of beauty.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Then, given leave by the sages, the Lord went with a contingent of brāhmaṇas to the Kauśikī River, where he bathed. From there he went to the lake from which flows the river Sarayū.**

**Комментарий:**

In response to the question “what is that lake” he answers: it is the lake from which Sarayū originates.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**The Lord followed the course of the Sarayū until he came to Prayāga, where he bathed and then performed rituals to propitiate the devatās and other living beings. Next he went to the āśrama of Pulaha Ṛṣi.**

**Комментарий:**

By following the course (anu-srotena) of the Sarayū, Balarāma eventually arrived in Prayāga. Pulaha’s hermitage is Hari-kṣetra.

### Text 11-15

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma bathed in the Gomatī, Gaṇḍakī and Vipāśā rivers, and also immersed himself in the Śoṇa. He went to Gayā, where he worshipped his forefathers, and to the mouth of the Ganges, where he performed purifying ablutions. At Mount Mahendra he saw Paraśurāma and offered him prayers, and then he bathed in the seven branches of the Godāvarī River, and also in the rivers Veṇā, Pampā and Bhīmarathī. Then Balarāma met Skanda and visited Śrī-śaila, the abode of Lord Giriśa. In the southern provinces known as Draviḍa-deśa the Supreme Lord saw the sacred Veṅkaṭa Hill, as well as the cities of Kāmakoṣṇī and Kāñcī, the exalted Kāverī River and the most holy Śrī-raṅga, where Kṛṣṇa has manifested himself. From there he went to Ṛṣabha Mountain, where Kṛṣṇa also lives, and to the southern Mathurā. Then he came to Setubandha, where the most grievous sins are destroyed.**

**Комментарий:**

He went to all the places listed. He also bathed (āplutaḥ) at Śoṇa. Though his father and grandfather were living, Balarāma performed pitṛ-yāga at Gāyā by Vasudeva’s order in consideration of those sons of Vasudeva who were born before him. He bathed (upaspṛśya) at Gaṅgā-sāgara. He did not go to Puri, which falls on the way, since he would also be embarrassed to worship himself directly as Kṛṣṇa, Balabhadra, and Subhadrā. He then saw Parāśurāma. He saw Saptagodāvaram (is a samhāra-avyayī-bhāva compound). Godāvarīm is poetic license. He went to Śrī-raṅgam where the Lord resides (sannihitaḥ) as ŚrīRaṅganātha.

### Text 16-17

**Перевод:**

**There at Setubandha \[Rāmeśvaram\] Balarāma gave brāhmaṇas ten thousand cows in charity. He then visited the Kṛtamālā and Tāmraparṇī rivers and the great Malaya Mountains. In the Malaya range, Balarāma found Agastya Ṛṣi sitting in meditation. After bowing down to the sage, the Lord offered him prayers and then received blessings from him. Taking leave from Agastya, he proceeded to the shore of the southern ocean, where he saw Goddess Durgā in her form of Kanyā-kumārī.**

**Комментарий:**

At Sāgara-setu he gave cows to the brāhmaṇas who lived there. He bowed to Agastya and praised him (abhivādya).

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Next he went to Phālguna-tīrtha and bathed in the sacred Pañcāpsarā Lake, where Viṣṇu had directly manifested himself. At this place he gave away another ten thousand cows.**

**Комментарий:**

Phālgunam is Ananta-puram. He went to Pañcāpsarasa-tirtha. Bathing there, Balarāma gave (asparśat) ten thousand cows in charity.

### Text 19-21

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord then traveled through the kingdoms of Kerala and Trigarta, visiting Śiva’s sacred city of Gokarṇa, where Śiva directly manifests himself. After also visiting Goddess Pārvatī, who dwells on an island, Balarāma went to the holy district of Śūrpāraka and bathed in the Tāpī, Payoṣṇī and Nirvindhyā rivers. He next entered the Daṇḍaka forest and went to the river Revā, along which the city of Māhiṣmatī is found. Then he bathed at Manu-tīrtha and finally returned to Prabhāsa.**

**Комментарий:**

Going through Kerala, after also visiting Goddess Pārvatī, who dwells on an island (dvīpāyanīm), Balarāma went to the holy district of Śūrpāraka.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**The Lord heard from some brāhmaṇas how all the kings involved in the battle between the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas had been killed. From this he concluded that the earth was now relieved of her burden.**

**Комментарий:**

At Prabhāsa he heard that all the kings had been destroyed from brāhmaṇas who had come on pilgrimage there.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Wanting to stop the club fight then raging between Bhīma and Duryodhana on the battlefield, Balarāma went to Kurukṣetra.**

**Комментарий:**

He went to Kurukṣetra (vinaśanam) without going to Dvārakā.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**When Yudhiṣṭhira, Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna and the twin brothers Nakula and Sahadeva saw Balarāma, they offered him respectful obeisances but said nothing, thinking “What has he come here to tell us?”**

**Комментарий:**

They remained silent, wondering, “What will he say?”

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma saw Duryodhana and Bhīma with clubs in their hands, each angrily striving for victory over the other as they circled about skillfully. The Lord addressed them as follows.**

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Balarāma said:\] King Duryodhana! And Bhīma! Listen! You two warriors are equal in fighting prowess. I know that one of you has greater physical power, while the other is better trained in technique.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhīma is greater in physical strength and Duryodhana is greater in knowledge of club fighting.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Since you are so evenly matched in fighting prowess, I do not see how either of you can win or lose this duel. Therefore please stop this useless battle.**

**Комментарий:**

I do not see how either of you can win or lose (anyaḥ) this duel.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] They did not accept Balarāma’s request, O King, although it was for a good purpose, for their enmity was deep and long standing. Each of them constantly remembered the insults and injuries he had suffered from the other.**

**Комментарий:**

They did not listen to Balarāma’s meaningful (artha-vat) words.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Concluding that the battle was the arrangement of fate, Balarāma went back to Dvārakā. There he was greeted by Ugrasena and his other relatives, who were all delighted to see him.**

**Комментарий:**

The war had been arranged by Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord (diṣṭam).

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Later Balarāma returned to Naimiṣāraṇya, where the sages joyfully engaged him, the embodiment of all sacrifice, in performing various kinds of Vedic sacrifice. Balarāma was now retired from warfare.**

**Комментарий:**

They engaged Balarāma, who though the personification of sacrifices (kratv-aṅgam), had now given up fighting (nivṛttākhilavigraham), in performing sacrifices. This shows that he was qualified for sacrifice.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The all-powerful Balarāma bestowed upon the sages pure spiritual knowledge, by which they could see the whole universe within him and also see him pervading everything.**

**Комментарий:**

By that knowledge they could understand that the universe and they themselves were within the Lord (ātmani), and that the Lord was pervading the universe.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**After executing with his wife the avabhṛtha ablutions, the beautifully dressed and ornamented Balarāma, encircled by his immediate family and other relatives and friends, looked as splendid as the moon surrounded by its constellations.**

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Countless other such pastimes were performed by Balarāma, since he had great prowess, continuity, inconceivable powers, and a spiritual form of a human endowed with great mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

There are many such pastimes of Balarāma, by whose māyā humans are created (māyā-martyasya) or who had a human form of pure consciousness.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**All the activities of the unlimited Balarāma are amazing. Anyone who regularly remembers them at dawn and dusk will become very dear to the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

One who regularly remembers the amazing pastimes of Balarāma at dawn and dusk will become very dear to Kṛṣṇa (viṣṇoḥ), the younger brother of Balarāma.

## Chapter 80 - The Brāhmaṇa Śrīdāmā Visits Lord Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: My lord, O master, I wish to hear about other valorous deeds performed by Kṛṣṇa, Mukunda, of noble character, whose valor is unlimited.**

**Комментарий:**

In the eightieth chapter, Kṛṣṇa, having worshipped Śrīdāmā who comes to his house, asked in joy about their stay in the guru’s āśrama. O Lord! O master! I wish to hear about Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**O brāhmaṇa, how could anyone who experiences the sweetness of the topics and is disgusted with endeavoring for sense gratification give up the transcendental topics of the Lord with excellent glories after hearing them repeatedly?**

**Комментарий:**

“You have heard topics for many days? Why do you ask again?” After repeatedly hearing about the Lord, who could give up those topics? No one could.“But we see few people even give up the topics.” The person who realizes the special sweetness and glories of the topic (viśeṣa-jñaḥ) does not give up those topics. Thus when realizing that speciality giving them up is out of question but even to destroy suffering which is experienced at all times one does not give up the topics. That person is disgusted with searching for material enjoyment. He destroys that interest just by hearing those topics.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Actual speech is that which describes the qualities of the Lord, real hands are those that work for him, a true mind is that which always remembers him dwelling within everything moving and nonmoving, and actual ears are those that listen to sanctifying topics about him.**

**Комментарий:**

The ears are useless without hearing those topics. In order to show this, Parīkṣit gives examples of other senses along with the ears. Real hands are those which engage in work for the Lord. Real mind is that which remembers the Lord who is situated in moving and nonmoving beings. Real ear is that which listens to the Lord’s topics which purify (puṇya).

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**An actual head is one that bows down to the Lord and his devotee. Real eyes are those that see only the Lord, and actual limbs are those which regularly honor the water that has bathed the Lord’s feet or those of his devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Real head is that which bows completely (ā-namet), to the deity forms of the Lord and to his devotee (ubhaya-liṅgam). Real eye is that which only (eva) sees the forms of the Lord and devotees. Then the limbs should always (nityam) honor the water that has washed the feet of the forms of the Lord and the devotees. The water should be placed on limbs above the navel since placing the holy water lower than that is forbidden.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Suta Gosvāmī said: Thus questioned by Parīkṣit, the omniscient son of Vyāsa replied, his heart fully absorbed in meditation on Vasudeva’s son.**

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Kṛṣṇa had a certain brāhmaṇa friend \[named Śrīdāmā \] who was most learned in Vedic knowledge and detached from all sense enjoyment. Furthermore, his mind was peaceful and his senses subdued.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses go together.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Living as a householder, he maintained himself with whatever came of its own accord. The wife of that poorly dressed brāhmaṇa suffered along with him and was emaciated from hunger.**

**Комментарий:**

Śrīdāmā’s wife exhibited the same qualities (tathā-vidhā) as him. But one of her qualities of tolerating hunger (kṣut-kṣāmā), was superior to his since whatever she received as food, she served to him.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**The chaste wife of the poverty-stricken brāhmaṇa once approached him, her face dried up because of her distress. Trembling with fear, she spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

She was distressed (sīdamānā) because she could not obtain any food for her husband. Out of fear of her husband she was also trembling (vepamānā), because she knew that he did not want to beg the Lord for anything other than devotion.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**\[Śrīdāmā’s wife said:\] O brāhmaṇa, isn’t it true that the Lord of all wealth is the personal friend of your exalted self? That greatest of Yādavas, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, is compassionate to brāhmaṇas and very affectionate to the surrendered.**

**Комментарий:**

“How could the husband of the goddess of fortune befriend a poor person like myself?” He is compassionate to brāhmaṇas. “But I do not have the qualities of such a brāhmaṇa.’’ Kṛṣṇa gives shelter (saraṇyaś) to anyone who surrenders to him. “Who is he?” Kṛṣṇa is Bhagavān, and the greatest of the Sātvatas. He has appeared on earth in that form.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**O fortunate one, please approach him, the real shelter of all saints. He will certainly give abundant wealth to such a suffering householder as you.**

**Комментарий:**

Approach Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of the devotees (sādhūnām) and miserable persons (ca). He will give to a suffering householder. You are suitable candidate for charity.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa is now the ruler of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas and is staying at Dvārakā. Since he gives even his own self to anyone who simply remembers his lotus feet, what doubt is there that he, the spiritual master of the universe, will bestow upon his sincere worshiper prosperity and material enjoyment, which are not even very desirable?**

**Комментарий:**

He is in Dvārakā. I have heard from the brāhmaṇas. Mentioning the names of Bhoja, etc., indicates that even Kṛṣṇa’s followers will give. Here the wife’s nature was to act for the happiness of the husband. The purpose of the husband was to see Kṛṣṇa and seek food because of his wife’s words. They are both without desire. I am ashamed to beg wealth from my friend. He gives himself to the person who is just engaged in remembering his lotus feet (samarataḥ), what to speak of someone who performs nine types of bhakti. He becomes controlled by that person, what to speak of giving material goods and what is desired? The reason these goods are insignificant is that they are not really desirable since they are ultimately distasteful. Approaching him, remain silent. He will give the great treasure and the lotus feet that you cherish.

### Text 12-13

**Перевод:**

**When his wife thus repeatedly implored him in various ways, the brāhmaṇa thought to himself, “To see Lord Kṛṣṇa is indeed the greatest achievement in life.” Thus he decided to go, but first he told her, “My good wife, if there is anything in the house I can bring as a gift, please give it to me.”**

**Комментарий:**

Bhārya or wife means “one whom the husband must support.” He had to follow her words in order to maintain her. His mind was not too pleased with her pleas but on consideration he became pleased. He asked for some gift to give to him. It is not proper to go to a friend with empty hands.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Śrīdāmā’s wife begged four handfuls of flat rice from neighboring brāhmaṇas, tied up the rice in a torn piece of cloth and gave it to her husband as a present for Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

She begged chipped rice (pṛthuka-taṇḍulān) from brāhmaṇas.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Taking the flat rice, the saintly brāhmaṇa set off for Dvārakā, all the while wondering “How will I be able to have Kṛṣṇa’s audience?”**

**Комментарий:**

Perhaps I will be blocked by the guards at the door.

### Text 16-17

**Перевод:**

**The learned brāhmaṇa, joined by some local brāhmaṇas, passed three guard stations and went through three gateways, and then he walked by the homes of Kṛṣṇa’s faithful devotees, the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, which ordinarily no one could do. He then entered one of the opulent palaces belonging to Kṛṣṇa’s sixteen thousand queens, and when he did so he felt as if he were attaining the bliss of liberation.**

**Комментарий:**

The description of a gulma, part of an army, is as follows: A gulma has forty-five foot soldiers, nine elephants, nine chariots and twenty-seven horses. However, in this case gulma figuratively refers to places outside the city for housing troops who guarded the gates. He passed the gate, long houses and courtyards within the city (kakṣāḥ), accompanied by brāhmaṇas of Dvārakā. He entered one palace among the palaces of Kṛṣṇa’s sixteen thousand queens, among the houses of the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis which could not be entered (agamya). This was Rukmiṇī’s house according to Padma Purāṇa. “How could he enter the houses which were all well-fortified?” They possessed dharma of the Lord who was firmly fixed at all times in his own glories such as being kind to the brāhmaṇas (acyuta).

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**At that time Acyuta was seated on his consort’s bed. Spotting the brāhmaṇa at some distance, the Lord immediately stood up, went forward to meet him and with great pleasure embraced him.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa got up and went forward (abhyetya) into the courtyard and embraced (paryagrahīt) Śrīdāmā in great bliss.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**The lotus-eyed Supreme Lord felt intense ecstasy upon touching the body of his dear friend, the wise brāhmaṇa, and thus he shed tears of love.**

**Комментарий:**

Śrīdāmā was his friend, since they played together under the same teacher. He was dearest (priyasya), the object of special prema. He was a brāhmaṇa and a sage, who knew the svarūpa of the Lord. Kṛṣṇa was blissful (nirvṛtaḥ) and most affectionate (prītaḥ) to him. The Lord had most beautiful lotus eyes.

### Text 20-22

**Перевод:**

**O King! Kṛṣṇa seated his friend Śrīdāmā upon the bed. Then the Lord, who purifies the whole world, personally offered him various tokens of respect and washed his feet, after which he sprinkled the water on his own head. He anointed him with divinely fragrant sandalwood, aguru and kuṅkuma pastes and happily worshipped him with aromatic incense and arrays of lamps. After finally offering him betel nut and the gift of a cow, he welcomed him with pleasing words.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa sprinkled the water that he used to wash Śrīdāmā’s feet (pādaavanejanīḥ) on his head. Fragrance of jasmine, etc., was mixed with the sandalwood, etc., to make catuḥsama. He drew patterns on his limbs (vyalimpat), making him beautiful. He inquired about his well-being (abravīt).

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**By fanning him with her cāmara, the divine goddess of fortune personally served that poor brāhmaṇa, whose clothing was torn and dirty and who was so thin that veins were visible all over his body.**

**Комментарий:**
