Rukmiṇī, the queen, with qualities like those of her husband, served the brāhmaṇa directly with her own hands. The word kucelam (worn out clothing), suggests that they did not give him new clothes. His body was discolored (malinam) because of lack of beauty. Veins were visible all over his body (dhamani-santatam).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**The people in the royal palace were astonished to see Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of spotless glory, so lovingly honor this shabbily dressed brāhmaṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the person with unkempt cloth being worshipped by Kṛṣṇa, the people of the palace, who most probably did not know his identity, were astonished.

### Text 25-26

**Перевод:**

**\[The residents of the palace said:\] What pious acts has this unkempt, impoverished brāhmaṇa performed? People regard him as lowly and contemptible, yet the spiritual master of the three worlds, the abode of Lakṣmī, is serving him reverently. Leaving the goddess of fortune sitting on her bed, the Lord has embraced this brāhmaṇa as if he were an older brother.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses describe the astonishment of the people. He was wearing inferior dress (adhamena). Thus he had done no puṇyas. Saṁbhṛtaḥ means “was worshipped.”

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Taking each other’s hands, O King, Kṛṣṇa and Śrīdāmā talked pleasantly about how they once lived together in the school of their guru.**

**Комментарий:**

Gṛhya stands of gṛhītvā.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear brāhmaṇa, you know well the ways of dharma. After you offered the gift of remuneration to our guru and returned home from his school, did you marry a compatible wife or not?**

**Комментарий:**

Did you marry a compatible wife or not after graduating from the gurukula? Kṛṣṇa asked with doubt as a pastime since Śrīdāmā was dressed as a householder but he did not appear to be enjoying any material pleasure. O knower of dharma! In order to avoid the fault of having no āśrama after graduating, you must have accepted a wife. anāśramī na tiṣṭheta dīnam ekam api dvijaḥ The dvija should not remain without an āśrama for even one day. (Mahābhārata) You know dharma. Kṛṣṇa repeatedly addresses him as brahman (O brāhmaṇa). His repeated addressing him as brahman is for Śrīdāmā, who was ashamed, to turn towards Kṛṣṇa. By this he shows his attachment to see him.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Even though you are mostly involved in household affairs, your mind is not affected by material desires. Nor, O learned one, do you take much pleasure in the pursuit of material wealth. This I am well aware of.**

**Комментарий:**

Since Śrīdāmā did not deny it, Kṛṣṇa inferred his marriage. You are situated in married life but are not attached. You do not desire material enjoyment. I know this. You are not much fond of wealth such as clothing, etc. O learned one (vidvan)! This is proper for you. The words prāyaḥ and ati indicate that since he needed material objects because of the request of his wife, they will be obtained in plenty.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Having renounced all material propensities, which spring from the Lord’s illusory energy, some people execute worldly duties with their minds undisturbed by mundane desires. They act as I do, to instruct the general populace.**

**Комментарий:**

I know that you did not take sannyāsa after brahmacārī life, even though you are very renounced. Some, devoid of desire in their hearts, perform their karmas such as sacrifices. But some perform their karmas in order to (tyajantas) renounce impressions composed of subtle impressions (prakṛtīḥ) made by the Lord.“The second option is possible but not the first.” This should be done in such a way as to teach the people.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**My dear brāhmaṇa, do you remember how we lived together in our spiritual master’s school? When a twice-born student has learned from his guru all that is to be learned, he can obtain supreme tattva, which lies beyond all ignorance.**

**Комментарий:**

To make silent Śrīdāmā speak, Kṛṣṇa made him remember incidents in the gurukula in twelve verses. Learning from the guru (yataḥ) the supreme tattva (vijñeyam) one surpasses saṁsāra (tamasaḥ).

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**My dear friend, he who gives a person his physical birth is his first spiritual master, and he who initiates him as a twice-born brāhmaṇa and engages him in karmas is indeed more directly his spiritual master. But the person who bestows spiritual knowledge upon the members of all the spiritual orders of society is one’s ultimate spiritual master. He is as good as my own self.**

**Комментарий:**

There are three gurus: the father, the one who gives knowledge of karmas, and the teacher of tattva. Among them the last is the most worshippable. Yatra (because of whom) should be added three times. In this world (iha), because of whom there is birth (sambhavaḥ) that father is the first guru (ādyaḥ), because of whom there is arousal of sat-karmas for a person who is dvija (brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiṣya), the teacher of knowledge of karmas (upanetā) is the second guru. Because of whom there is knowledge of tattva for the person in the āśramas, that teacher of Vedānta (jñāna-daḥ) is the third guru. He is to be worshipped the way I am worshipped (and not in a lesser way).

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Certainly, O brāhmaṇa, of all the followers of the varṇāśrama system, those who take advantage of the words I speak in my form as the guru and thus easily cross over the ocean of material existence best understand their own true welfare.**

**Комментарий:**

Those are most intelligent who take shelter of a guru who gives knowledge, who is equal to me. For certain (nanu), in this world, among those in the varṇāśrama system, those persons are learned in their own highest good, who cross the ocean of saṁsāra without effort by my mantra (vācā), by the guru who teaches about me (mayā) who is my form.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**I, the Soul of all beings, am not as satisfied by ritual worship, brahminical initiation, penances or self-discipline as I am by faithful service rendered to one’s guru.**

**Комментарий:**

Service to the guru who knows tattva is the highest dharma. I, the Supreme Lord, spread everywhere (sarva-bhūtātmā) am not satisfied by varṇa-dharma of homa (ijyā), by householder dharma of begetting offspring (prajātibhyām), by vānaprastha dharma of austerity (tapaḥ), or by sannyāsa-dharma (upaśamena – cessation) as much as I am satisfied with service to a guru having knowledge of tattva.

### Text 35-36

**Перевод:**

**O brāhmaṇa, do you remember what happened to us while we were living with our spiritual master? Once our guru’s wife sent us to fetch firewood, and after we entered the vast forest, O twiceborn one, an unseasonal storm arose, with fierce wind and rain and harsh thunder.**

**Комментарий:**

Do you not remember our lives living with guru? Plural (naḥ) is used because Balarāma was also there. Apartau means it was no longer monsoon season, but winter, but it rained. Clouds thundered (stanayitnavaḥ).

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Then, as the sun set, the forest was covered by darkness in every direction, and with all the flooding we could not distinguish high land from low.**

**Комментарий:**

Low land (nimnam) and high land (kulam) could not be distinguished because it was flooded with water.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Constantly besieged by the powerful wind and rain, we lost our way amidst the flooding waters. We simply held each other’s hands and, in great distress, wandered aimlessly about the forest carrying wood.**

**Комментарий:**

We wandered all around. Babhrima used instead of babhramima is Vedic usage (the root being bhram). Or it means we carried the wood around, the root being bhṛ (to carry). Then babhrima instead of babhṛma is also Vedic usage.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Our guru, Sāndīpani, understanding our predicament, set out after sunrise to search for us, his disciples, and found us in distress.**

**Комментарий:**

Intuiting our distress (etat), the great Sāndīpani searched for us.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**\[Sāndīpani said:\] O my children, you have suffered so much for my sake! The body is most dear to every living creature, but you are so dedicated to me that you completely disregarded your own comfort.**

**Комментарий:**

The guru spoke. Ātmā here means body.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**This indeed is the duty of all true disciples: to repay the debt to their spiritual master by offering him, with pure hearts, their wealth and even their very lives.**

**Комментарий:**

You have truly done service to guru. One should repay the debt to the guru by offering the body (ātmā) from which come all assets (sarvārthā).

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**You boys are first-class brāhmaṇas, and I am satisfied with you. May all your desires be fulfilled, and may the Vedic mantras you have learned never lose their meaning for you, in this world or the next.**

**Комментарий:**

I am satisfied with you three. The result of his satisfaction is described. May the Vedic mantras that you have learnt from me, not be worn out, nor lose their results, and not be forgotten by you (ayātayāmāni). Yāta-yāma means worn out according to Nānārtha-varga of Amara-koṣa. It is said that cooked food after one prahara becomes yāta-yāma or devoid of its essence. Secondarily, other items also may lose their essence and become yāta-yāma by secondary meaning.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**We had many similar experiences while living in our spiritual master’s home. Simply by the grace of the spiritual master a person can attain the highest happiness and realization of the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Do you remember many such incidents (vṛttāni) that happened to us while living in gurukula? By the mercy of guru, one then attains great happiness (praśāntaye).

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa said: What could I possibly have failed to achieve, O Lord of lords, O universal teacher, since I was able to personally live with you, whose every desire is fulfilled, at the home of our spiritual master?**

**Комментарий:**

Finally, being asked many times, the brāhmaṇa spoke. What was not achieved (anirvṛttam) by us? Rather everything was achieved. We lived in the house of the guru with you, whose desires are all fulfilled (satya-kāmena). The meaning is this. You who are omniscient and full in your desires studied under a guru and carried firewood for him. That was to teach the world to accept the Vedas from guru and serve guru. It was our good fortune to be with you at that time.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**O almighty Lord, your body comprises the Absolute Truth in the form of the Vedas and is thus the source of all auspicious goals of life. That you took up residence at the school of a spiritual master is simply one of your pastimes in which you play the role of a human being.**

**Комментарий:**

You perform pastimes to create auspiciousness for the world. Staying in the gurukula was just a festival of pastimes (viḍambanam) for you, the Supreme Lord, the personification of Vedas, whose body is Brahman made of Vedic hymns (chando-mayaṁ brahma), the sprouting place of auspiciousness.

## Chapter 81 - The Lord Blesses Śrīdāmā Brāhmaṇa

### Text 1-2

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, perfectly knows the hearts of all living beings, and he is especially devoted to the brāhmaṇas. While the Supreme Lord, the goal of all saintly persons, conversed in this way with the best of the twice-born, he laughed and spoke the following words to that dear friend Śrīdāmā, all the while smiling and looking upon him with affection.**

**Комментарий:**

In the eighty-first chapter, after eating the chipped rice of his friend, Kṛṣṇa, though giving him great wealth, thinks himself indebted. Kṛṣṇa, the ocean of qualities such as friendliness to devotees and favorability to brāhmaṇas, talked happily with his friend. Knowing the minds of all beings, he certainly knew Śrīdāmā’s mind. He knew that his friend was ashamed to offer him the chipped rice though he had brought it. He smiled to make him blissful. He laughed, joking, “Why are you hiding the dear gift given to me by your wife?” He looked with affection at the knotted cloth containing the rice and informed him by that glance, “Tomorrow you will not be poor” since he was the shelter of the devotees (satām gatiḥ).

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: O brāhmaṇa, what gift have you brought me from home? I regard as great even the smallest gift offered by my devotees in pure love, but even great offerings presented by nondevotees do not please me.**

**Комментарий:**

You have come to me after a long time with a gift. I know by inference that you have a gift with you. “But I am ashamed to show it because it is meager.” I regard as great even the smallest gift offered by my devotees in pure love.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**If one offers me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept that gift of devotion.**

**Комментарий:**

“I took this from my house to present to you, given by my wife. But now I think that it is crude, unsuitable for you to eat, so I am not giving it.” Overwhelmed by the bhakti, I enjoy everything, even a leaf, offered with devotion by the person who has no material desire, whose mind is purified by bhakti (prayatātmanaḥ). The word bhakti is repeated, indicating that bhakti alone pleases me, not good birth, knowledge, etc.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Even after being addressed in this way, O King, the brāhmaṇa felt too embarrassed to offer his palmfuls of flat rice to the husband of the goddess of fortune. He simply kept his head bowed in shame.**

**Комментарий:**

He was embarrassed because Kṛṣṇa was the husband of Lakṣmī. He still did not give willingly his four handfuls of rice to Kṛṣṇa but in embarrassment had a downcast face.

### Text 6-7

**Перевод:**

**Being the direct witness in the hearts of all living beings, Kṛṣṇa fully understood why Śrīdāmā had come to see him. Thus he thought, “In the past my friend has never worshipped me out of a desire for material opulence, but now he comes to me to satisfy his chaste and devoted wife. I will give him riches that even the immortal devatās cannot obtain.”**

**Комментарий:**

What did the Lord resolve to do? Knowing all hearts, knowing the reason for his coming, Kṛṣṇa considered.“Previously, he did not worship me with a desire for wealth but with a desire for my friendship.” “Then how is that has he come now for the sake of wealth?” He has attained me due to his desire to satisfy his wife, but he has come just to see me. Since, it is said ayaṁ hi paramo lābhaḥ: the Lord is the highest attainment,(verse 12) he does not desire wealth but does this to please his wife. This is secondary. I will give wealth rare even for Indra and others.“But why did he not go to someone else who gives?” He is a friend. In giving me up, his friend, and going elsewhere, the friendship is broken.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Thinking like this, the Lord snatched from the brāhmaṇa’s garment the grains of flat rice tied up in an old piece of cloth and exclaimed, “What is this?**

**Комментарий:**

With his own hands (svayam) he pulled out from his side the rice bound for a long time in the worn-out cloth.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**“My friend, have you brought this for me? It gives me extreme pleasure. Indeed, these few grains of flat rice will satisfy not only me but also the entire universe.”**

**Комментарий:**

Certainly, this gift you brought is most pleasing to me, because it is brought by a friend (sakhe). Thus it is not crude. It is not a small amount since it satisfies me and thus it satisfies the whole universe even more, just as water on the root satisfies the whole tree.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**After saying this, the Supreme Lord ate one palmful and was about to eat a second when the devoted goddess Rukmiṇī took hold of his hand.**

**Комментарий:**

Saying this, Kṛṣṇa ate once a handful. Quickly (tāvat) Rukmiṇī grasped her husband’s hand prohibiting him from eating it. The meaning is this. You should not eat everything sweet which comes from your friend’s house. Even we members of the house desire some of it. According to some the word tat-parā (dedicated to Lord) indicates that she prevented him thinking, “being satisfied eating everything, he will even give me to him.”

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**\[Queen Rukmiṇī said:\] This is more than enough, O Soul of the universe, to secure him an abundance of all kinds of wealth in this world and the next. Prosperity is a cause (product) of your satisfaction.**

**Комментарий:**

She forbids him with another thought. Eating one handful is enough. You should not eat more. O ātmā of the universe! If you are satisfied, the universe is also satisfied. “Since I desire to give him great wealth, I should eat a second handful.” In this world or the next, pleasing you is the only cause of attaining all wealth for men. Toṣa for toṣaḥ is poetic license. That wealth has already been attained. Thus we should divide and eat the remainder. Stop eating, dear husband.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa spent that night in Acyuta’s palace after eating and drinking to his full satisfaction. He felt as if he had gone to the spiritual world.**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇa felt as if he was truly (yathā) situated in Vaikuṇṭha (svar-gataṁ) because Dvārakā was Vaikuṇṭha, by being the Lord’s eternal abode.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**The next day, Śrīdāmā set off for home while being honored by Kṛṣṇa, the self-satisfied maintainer of the universe. The brāhmaṇa felt greatly delighted, my dear King, as he walked along the road.**

**Комментарий:**

The next day, being honored by Kṛṣṇa, the creator of the universe (viśva-bhāvena), full of his own bliss (sva-sukhena), the brāhmaṇa walking in bliss went to his house. Just by his will, the Lord creates millions of universes and remains unchanged. What endeavor was there for him in creating a palace for Śrīdāmā?

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Although he had apparently received no wealth from Kṛṣṇa, Śrīdāmā was too shy to beg for it on his own. He simply returned home, feeling perfectly satisfied to have had the Supreme Lord’s audience.**

**Комментарий:**

Though not obtaining wealth from his friend Kṛṣṇa, he went home. And he had not asked. The reason is that he was ashamed. “Though I have no desire, I went to him for wealth.” But he was happy on seeing the Lord.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa is known to be devoted to the brāhmaṇas, and now I have personally seen this devotion. He who carries the goddess of fortune on his chest has embraced the poorest beggar.**

**Комментарий:**

His bliss is described in four verses. I have seen his devotion to brāhmaṇas for (yad) he embraced me to his chest, the residence place of Lakṣmī-devī, who shines there as a golden line.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Who am I? A sinful, poor friend of a brāhmaṇa. And who is Kṛṣṇa? The Supreme Lord, full in six opulences. Nonetheless, he has embraced me with his two arms.**

**Комментарий:**

Though (iti) I am a fallenl brāhmaṇa, I have been embraced by his arms.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**He treated me just like one of his brothers, making me sit on the couch of his beloved consort. And because I was fatigued, his queen personally fanned me with a yak-tail cāmara.**

**Комментарий:**

He treated me like his brothers, like Balarāma and others.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Although he is the Lord of all devatās and the object of worship for all brāhmaṇas, he worshipped me as if I were a devatā myself, massaging my feet and rendering other humble services.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover, I was welcomed (pujitaḥ) by his serving me, in the form of massaging my feet though he is worshipped by the devatās and brāhmaṇas. I was worshipped as if I were his family deity (devavat).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Devotional service to his lotus feet is the root cause of all the perfections a person can find in heaven, in liberation, in the subterranean regions and on earth.**

**Комментарий:**

He imagines in two verses, the cause of the Lord not giving wealth is though he was worshipped. The cause of attaining Svarga is his feet.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Thinking “If this poor wretch suddenly becomes rich, he will forget me in his intoxicating happiness,” the compassionate Lord did not grant me even a little wealth.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the cause of wealth is his feet, he did not give me wealth out of his mercy, thinking,“By wealth he should not become a brahmāṇa devoid of remembrance of me.” This is his mercy on me. Or not giving me wealth is int itself great wealth, since there is no interruption to the wealth of remembrance of his feet.

### Text 21-23

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] Thinking thus to himself, Śrīdāmā finally came to the place where his home stood. But that place was now crowded on all sides with towering, celestial palaces rivaling the combined brilliance of the sun, fire and the moon. There were splendorous courtyards and gardens, each filled with flocks of cooing birds and beautified by ponds in which white, blue, pink and fragrant lotuses grew. Finely attired men and doeeyed women stood in attendance. Śrīdāmā wondered, “What is all this? Whose property is it? How has this all come about?”**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking of his secret internally, not revealing it externally, he came close to his house. His house is described. He saw his place surrounded with heavenly houses like airplanes, shining like the sun and fire. The place had lakes with blossoming lotuses and male and female servants well ornamented. Hariṇākṣibhiḥ is a poetic license for hariṇākṣībhiḥ. The following should be understood. That night, his wife slept in the house. In the morning she awoke and saw that the place and her body were spiritual. She understood that this was caused by Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. Waiting for her husband, she engaged the servants in work. First, he saw the great effulgence and thought,“What is this?” Then seeing the houses which resembled airplanes, he thought, “Whose house is this?” Then he determined that it was his house and thought,“How did this happen?”

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**As he continued to ponder in this way, the beautiful men and maidservants, as effulgent as devatās, came forward to greet their greatly fortunate master with loud song and instrumental music.**

**Комментарий:**

He accepted the servants in his mind thinking, “My friend Kṛṣṇa has given them to me.” Later they accepted him as their master. He was most fortunate. He too attained a spiritual form by the Lord’s mercy.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**When she heard that her husband had arrived, the brāhmaṇa’s wife quickly came out of the house in a jubilant flurry. She resembled the goddess of fortune herself emerging from her divine abode.**

**Комментарий:**

His wife, now beautiful came out of the house as if Lakṣmī were coming out of Vaikuṇṭha.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**When the chaste lady saw her husband, her eyes filled with tears of love and eagerness. As she held her eyes closed, she solemnly bowed down to him, and in her heart she embraced him.**

**Комментарий:**

Her eyes were filled with tears of love and longing. She closed them out of shyness.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Śrīdāmā was amazed to see his wife. Shining forth in the midst of maidservants adorned with jeweled lockets, she looked as effulgent as a devatā in her celestial airplane.**

**Комментарий:**

The husband was astonished. “This is the power of the Lord’s will.”

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**With pleasure he took his wife with him and entered his house, where there were hundreds of gem-studded pillars, just as in the palace of Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

It was like Indra’s palace. Kṛṣṇa brought the treasure of Indra to earth for his devotee beggar Śridāmā. (Sahasra-nāma-stotra, Uttara khaṇḍa, Padma Purāṇa)

### Text 29-32

**Перевод:**

**In Śrīdāmā’s home were beds as soft and white as the foam of milk, with bedsteads made of ivory and ornamented with gold. There were also couches with golden legs, as well as royal cāmara fans, golden thrones, soft cushions and gleaming canopies hung with strings of pearls. Upon the walls of sparkling crystal glass, inlaid with precious emeralds, shone jeweled lamps, and the women in the palace were all adorned with precious gems. As he viewed luxury of all varieties, the brāhmaṇa calmly reasoned to himself about his unexpected prosperity.**

**Комментарий:**

Four verses describe the house. Bedsteads were made of ivory (dāntā). There were seats made of gold. Ahaitukīm means suddenly manifested.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**\[Śrīdāmā thought:\] I have always been poor. Certainly the only possible way that such an unfortunate person as myself could become suddenly rich is that Kṛṣṇa, the supremely wealthy chief of the Yadu dynasty, has glanced upon me.**

**Комментарий:**

He determines the cause of his prosperity. Bata expresses joy. The cause of prosperity for me (etan-mama), devoid of fortune of prosperity (durbhagasya) since I was always poor is none other than the glance of Kṛṣṇa, who has infinite wealth (mahā-vibhūteḥ).

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**After all, my friend Kṛṣṇa, the most exalted of the Dāśārhas and the enjoyer of unlimited wealth, noticed that I secretly intended to beg from him. Thus even though he said nothing about it when I stood before him, he actually bestowed upon me the most abundant riches. In this way he acted just like a merciful rain cloud.**

**Комментарий:**

“But if he gives great wealth just by his glance then why did he not say,‘I will give you wealth.’” My friend, Kṛṣṇa, though not saying anything, has secretly given plenty to me, who secretly asked (asamakṣam yāciṣṇave). He has given more than requested. “How does he know that you asked him imperceptibly?” He knows because he is omniscient (svayam īkṣamāṇaḥ). He gave more because he is embarrassed to give just a little (bhuri-bhojaḥ). An example is given. He is like a rain cloud (parjanya-vat) welcomed by the farmer. At night without thundering, it rains more than the farmer requested. He is the chief of the Dāśārhakas, devotees who are also givers. If they are givers what to speak of him! The idea in giving him indirectly and without speaking of it is this.“My devotee begging items which are rare in his house, gave to me. How can I maintain my words that I, who am giving items easily available in my house, do reciprocate according to their surrender to me (BG [4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11))? Thus, he gave in shame.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**The Lord considers even his greatest benedictions to be insignificant, while he magnifies even a small service rendered to him by his well-wishing devotee. Thus with pleasure the Supreme Soul accepted a single palmful of the flat rice I brought him.**

**Комментарий:**

He cites his own case. The Lord considers even great things given by him to be small. What the devotee gives, though it is small (phalgu), he considers to be great (bhūri-kārī). He accepted the handful of rice that I brought and was overjoyed, taking it as infinite wealth. He is most worshippable, having the nature of being the friend of his devotee and being soft with compassion.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Life after life may I attain friendship and service to him and may he be my companion and intimate associate. May I attain association with his devotees, since he is the reservoir of all qualities and powers.**

**Комментарий:**

Though urged by my wife who wanted wealth, I went to him, desiring simply to see him. Yet he gave wealth to make my wife happy, but I desire only bhakti to him. Life after life may I attain affection (sauhṛda), intimacy (maitrī) situated with friendliness and service to the Lord endowed with an ocean of qualities like affection for his devotee (tasya). May there be association with his devotees (tat-puruṣa-prasaṅgaḥ)for me, who am endowed with association of the Lord who is the abode of qualities like beauty, youth and mercy, who possesses great powers (mahānubhāvena).

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**To a devotee who lacks spiritual insight, the Supreme Lord will not grant the wonderful opulences of this world—kingly power and material assets. Indeed, in his infinite wisdom the unborn Lord well knows how the intoxication of pride can cause the downfall of the wealthy.**

**Комментарий:**

“But how is it that you desire bhakti even after attaining happiness and wealth, the result of bhakti?” The unborn Lord does not increase wealth (sampadaḥ), power (rājyam) and opluences such as family (vibhūtīḥ) in order to give happiness to the devotee but makes bhakti firm since the devotee does not have deep understanding (adīrgha-bodhāya). The Lord is skillful at benefitting the devotees. He sees the fault of wealth. Prahlāda and others with deep understanding, have no problem with wealth. Because I have no deep understanding, I will have problem with them. Thus may I have bhakti and not wealth.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Thus firmly fixing his determination by means of his spiritual intelligence, Śrīdāmā remained absolutely devoted to Kṛṣṇa. Free from attachment to enjoyment, he enjoyed, together with his wife, while giving up the sense objects.**

**Комментарий:**

Gradually practicing renunciation, he enjoyed objects. Why? Because of his wife (jāyayā), to give pleasure to his wife, otherwise there would be harm to dharma. He was not too attached to those objects (na ati-lampataḥ).

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, worshipped by all the devatās, the giver of results of all sacrifices, and the supreme ruler, accepts brāhmaṇas as his masters. For him there exists no deity higher than them.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa’s affection for devotees and affection for brāhmaṇas became famous in this world. Though the Lord is the master of everyone, the brāhmaṇas are his masters. Though the Lord is the lord of the devatās, the brāhmaṇas are his deity. Though the Lord is the master of sacrifices, the brāhmaṇas are his worshippables in sacrifice.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Thus seeing how the unconquerable Supreme Lord is nonetheless conquered by his own servants, the Lord’s dear brāhmaṇa friend felt the remaining knots of material attachment within his heart being cut by the force of his constant meditation on the Lord. In a short time he attained Lord Kṛṣṇa’s supreme abode, the destination of great saints.**

**Комментарий:**

Having spoken of the devotees’ comfort in present life, the next life is explained. Seeing and following (dṛṣṭvā) Kṛṣṇa, though unconquered by all, being controlled by his devotees, cutting the knots of attachment by meditation (previously performed), he attained Dvārakā (dhāma).

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**The Lord always shows brāhmaṇas special favor. Anyone who hears this account of the Supreme Lord’s kindness to brāhmaṇas will come to develop love for the Lord and thus become freed from the bondage of karma.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing the story of the handful of rice and in that description the Lord’s affection for brāhmaṇas, one will develop prema.

## Chapter 82 - Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma Meet the Inhabitants of Vṛndāvana

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Once, while Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa were living in Dvārakā, there occurred a great eclipse of the sun, just as if the end of Lord Brahmā’s day had come.**

**Комментарий:**

In the eighty-second chapter, Kṛṣṇa, absorbed in the ocean of the bhāva of Gokula, meets with his friends at Kurukṣetra during the solar eclipse. A new topic out of sequence is introduced (atha). The events of this chapter occur after Balarāma’s visit to Vraja and before Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira’s Rājasūya sacrifice and Bhīṣma and others came to this gathering. This is explained after the killing of Dantavakra.(SB [10.78.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/78.15) commentary)Ekadā means on one occasion. The eclipse was like the end of Brahmā’s day when everything is destroyed.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Knowing of this eclipse in advance, O King, many people went to the holy place known as Samanta-pañcaka in order to earn pious credit.**

**Комментарий:**

Knowing through astrologers of the solar eclipse in advance, people went to Kurukṣetra, hearing that they would gain great puṇya. Paraśurāma had made five lakes together there (samantapañcakam). The people wanted pious credits from bathing and giving charity.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**After ridding the earth of kings, Paraśurāma, the foremost of warriors, created huge lakes from the kings’ blood at Samantakapañcaka.**

**Комментарий:**

The place informs of the valor of Paraśurāma. He created huge lakes (mahāhradān)due to which the place was named.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Although he is never tainted by karmic reactions, Paraśurāma performed sacrifices there to instruct people in general; thus he acted like an ordinary person trying to free himself of sins.**

**Комментарий:**

The place frees one of sin since it freed Paraśurāma of sin. “But where does he have sin!” He did this only to teach the world, just as those who are expert in karmas (anyaḥ) perform atonements.

### Text 5-6

**Перевод:**

**From all parts of Bhārata-varṣa a great number of people now came to that Samanta-pañcaka on pilgrimage. O descendant of Bharata, among those arriving at the holy place were many Vṛṣṇis, such as Gada, Pradyumna and Sāmba, hoping to be relieved of their sins; Akrūra, Vasudeva, Āhuka and other kings also went there. Aniruddha remained in Dvārakā with Sucandra, Śuka and Sāraṇa to guard the city, together with Kṛtavarmā, the commander of their armed forces.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhāratīḥ in the accusative, should be understood as nominative. The Vṛṣṇis desired to be free of sin but this is only worldly perception since they actually had no sin. Aniruddha remained in Dvārakā to protect it because as the Lord of Śvetadvīpa (i.e. as Kṣirodakaśāyī Viṣṇu) he is the maintainer (while Brahmā and Śiva are the creator and destroyer respectively).

### Text 7-8

**Перевод:**

**The mighty Yādavas passed with great majesty along the road. They were attended by their soldiers, who rode on chariots rivaling the airplanes of heaven, on horses moving with a rhythmic gait, and on bellowing elephants as huge as clouds. Also with them were many infantrymen as effulgent as celestial Vidyādharas. The Yādavas were so divinely dressed—being adorned with gold necklaces and flower garlands and wearing fine armor—that as they proceeded along the road with their wives they seemed to be luminaries of the sky.**

**Комментарий:**

Their chariots were like devatās’ airplanes (deva-dhiṣṇyābhaiḥ). The horses travelled like waves. The Yādavas had great majesty (mahātejāḥ). The word teja ends in the syllable a (i.e. it is not tejas).

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**At Samanta-pañcaka, the saintly Yādavas bathed and then observed a fast with careful attention. Afterward they presented brāhmaṇas with cows bedecked with garments, flower garlands and gold necklaces.**

**Комментарий:**

At those lakes (tatra), they fasted because of the eclipse of the sun, not because of being in the tīrtha. Smṛti says muṇḍanaṁ copavāsaś ca varjayitvā kurukṣetram: at Kurukṣetra one does not shave or fast.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**In accordance with scriptural injunctions, the descendants of Vṛṣṇi then bathed once more in Paraśurāma’s lakes and fed firstclass brāhmaṇas with sumptuous food. All the while they prayed, “May we be granted devotion to Kṛṣṇa.”**

**Комментарий:**

After the eclipse was over, they bathed again (punar āplutya) to be free of the effects of the eclipse.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Then, with the permission of Kṛṣṇa, their sole object of worship, the Vṛṣṇis ate breakfast and sat down at their leisure beneath trees that gave cooling shade.**

**Комментарий:**

After describing activities on the day of the eclipse, now Śukadeva describes activities on the next day. The Vṛṣṇis had obtained his permission to end the vrata. They sat down comfortably in the cooling shade under the trees.

### Text 12-13

**Перевод:**

**The Yādavas saw that many of the kings who had arrived were old friends and relatives—the Matsyas, Uśīnaras, Kauśalyas, Vidarbhas, Kurus, Sṛñjayas, Kāmbojas, Kaikayas, Madras, Kuntīs and the kings of Ānarta and Kerala. They also saw many hundreds of other kings, both allies and adversaries. In addition, my dear King Parīkṣit, they saw their dear friends Nanda Mahārāja and the cowherd men and women, who had been suffering in anxiety for so long.**

**Комментарий:**

They also saw Nanda and others, who had come there. The idea is this. Kṛṣṇa had said, “We will come to see our relatives.” (SB [10.45.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/45.23)) By this, their going to Mathurā was impeded. Thus being extremely eager to see him, they came there on the pretext of pilgrimage.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**As the great joy of seeing one another made the lotuses of their hearts and faces bloom with fresh beauty, the men embraced one another enthusiastically. With tears pouring from their eyes, the hair on their bodies standing on end and their voices choked up, they all felt intense bliss.**

**Комментарий:**

Now the happiness of men and women meeting their mutual acquaintances is described generally in two verses. Their faces and hearts were beautiful like blossoming lotuses due to the gush (raṁhasā) of happiness on seeing each other.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**The women glanced at one another with pure smiles of loving friendship. And when they embraced, their breasts, smeared with saffron paste, pressed against one another as their eyes filled with tears of affection.**

**Комментарий:**

The women had clear eye-corners due to smiling out of great friendship. Seeing each other, pressing (nihatya) their breasts against each other’s they embraced with their arms.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**They all then offered obeisances to their elders and received respect in turn from their younger relatives. After inquiring from one another about the comfort of their trip and their well-being, they proceeded to talk about Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Details are given in this verse. They offered respects to those who were older (vṛddhān) and received respects from those who were younger (yaviṣṭhaiḥ).

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Queen Kuntī met with her brothers and sisters and their children, and also with her parents, her brothers’ wives and Mukunda. While talking with them she forgot her sorrow.**

**Комментарий:**

Kuntī and Vasudeva is described in detail in five verses. Brothers were Vasudeva and others. Sisters were Śrutadevī and others. Their children were Balarāma, Gada and others. Parents were Śura and his wife Bhojyā. Brothers’ wives were Devakī and others. She gave up the sorrow of not seeing them for so long. Or it can mean she shed tears (śucaḥ jahau).

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Queen Kuntī said: My dear, respectable brother, I feel that my desires have been frustrated, because although all of you are most saintly, you forgot me during my calamities.**

**Комментарий:**

I have not done any pious activities since you did not remember me during my calamities though you are most respectable. It is my misfortune, what offense did you commit?

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Friends and family members—even children, brothers and parents—forget a dear one whom fate no longer favors.**

**Комментарий:**

They do not remember even a relative whose fate is unfavorable (adakṣiṇam).

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Vasudeva said: Dear sister, please do not be angry with us— ordinary men, playthings of fate. Whether a person acts on his own or is forced by others, he is always under the Supreme Lord’s control.**

**Комментарий:**

O mother (amba)! O most affectionate! O younger sister. We are playthings of the Lord (daiva). People act independently or are made to act, depending on others. Both the situations are under the control of the Lord.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Harassed by Kaṁsa, we all fled in various directions, but by the grace of the Lord we have now finally been able to return to our homes, my dear sister.**

**Комментарий:**

We Yadus have now (etarhi) been able to return home by the Lord (daivena), not by our powers. Here vayam (we) is used by including the Yādavas (since Vasudeva was himself in prison and had not fled anywhere). O sister! You have heard this because you are my sister. Or consoling her he makes her happy. Etarhi (now) is used since this pilgrimage was simultaneous with Yudhiṣṭhira’s attaining half the kingdom after the marriage with Draupadī, after Kaṁsa’s killing.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Vasudeva, Ugrasena and the other Yadus honored the various kings, who became supremely blissful and content upon seeing Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

Though mutually worshipping each other was suitable, it is mentioned that the Yadus worshipped the kings since the Yadus, by being superior to them, welcomed them all.

### Text 23-26

**Перевод:**

**All the royalty present, including Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and her sons, the Pāṇḍavas and their wives, Kuntī, Sañjaya, Vidura, Kṛpācārya, Kuntībhoja, Virāṭa, Bhīṣmaka, the great Nagnajit, Purujit, Drupada, Śalya, Dhṛṣṭaketu, Kāśirāja, Damaghoṣa, Viśālākṣa, Maithila, Madra, Kekaya, Yudhāmanyu, Suśarmā, Bāhlika with his associates and their sons, and the many other kings subservient to Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira—all of them, O best of kings, along with their wives, were simply amazed to see the form of Kṛṣṇa, the abode of all opulence and beauty, standing before them.**

**Комментарий:**

The names of the kings are listed. Nagnajit is called great (mahān) because he gave his daughter to Kṛṣṇa out of his profuse bhakti. Viśālākṣa is someone. Maithilaḥ is Bahulāśva. Jarāsandha and Śiśupāla are not mentioned because they did not come out of hatred for Kṛṣṇa. They were dedicated (anuvratāḥ) to Yudhiṣṭhira, since at that time Yudhiṣṭhira had obtained half the kingdom. Seeing the form (vapuḥ) of Kṛṣṇa, the abode of all beauty (śrī-niketam)along with his wives, they were amazed.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**After Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa had liberally honored them, with great joy and enthusiasm these kings began to praise the members of the Vṛṣṇi clan, Kṛṣṇa’s personal associates.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma personally honored each of them.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**\[The kings said:\] O King of the Bhojas, you alone among men have achieved a truly exalted birth, for you continually behold Kṛṣṇa, who is rarely visible even to great yogīs.**

**Комментарий:**

The kings address Ugrasena since he was recognized as the leader, being the king of the Yadus.

### Text 29-30

**Перевод:**

**His fame, as broadcast by the Vedas, the water that has washed his feet, and the words he speaks in the form of the revealed scriptures—these thoroughly purify this universe. Although the earth’s good fortune was ravaged by time, the touch of his lotus feet has revitalized her, and thus she is raining down on us the fulfillment of all our desires. The same Lord who pervades everything, who makes one forget the goals of heaven and liberation has now entered into marital and blood relationships with you, who otherwise travel on the hellish path of family life. Indeed, in these relationships you see and touch him directly, walk beside him, converse with him, and together with him lie down to rest, sit at ease and take your meals.**

**Комментарий:**

You not only see him always, but have great fortune. This is expressed in two verses. In yad (in verse 29) and tad (in verse 30) the genitive and instrumental case-endings are deleted respectively by Vedic usage (they are not in compound). His fame (viśrutiḥ), his foot water (Gaṅgā) and his words, the scriptures in form of the Vedas —these three purify the universe (idam) eminently. In purifying, the former one is more powerful (than the latter one). Though the earth’s glory was ravaged by Kali, which had entered at that time, by the touch of his feet, she has developed power of giving all things and showers us with all things. He has established blood relationships (sapiṇḍa) and marriage relationships (sayauna) with you by which you can see him, touch him, follow him (anupatha), converse with him (prajalpa), sleep, sit and eat with him (aśana). Moreover, Viṣṇu personally manifests or shines (āsa) in your house without your endeavoring. He destroys desire for Svarga and liberation by the bliss of serving him for his eternal associates who have rejected saṁsāra (nirayavartmanaḥ). Apavarga means impersonal liberation predominated by one’s own happiness and power.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When Nanda Mahārāja learned that the Yadus, led by Kṛṣṇa, had arrived, he immediately went to see them. The cowherds accompanied him, their various possessions loaded on their wagons.**

**Комментарий:**

After describing the happiness of the conversations between Kunti and Vasudeva and others briefly, there is now a detailed description of the happiness of Lord’s conversations with Nanda and others, for which purpose he had come on the pilgrimage. This continues till the end of the chapter. Understanding that the Yadus had arrived in Kurukṣetra, Nanda, mounting an attractive chariot, came to the gathering. He was surrounded by Upananda and other cowherds and their wives riding on attractive carts and chariots, with goods loaded on carts. They had brought materials for Kṛṣṇa to enjoy and for living close to him.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Nanda, the Vṛṣṇis were delighted and stood up like dead bodies coming back to life. Having felt much distress at not seeing him for so long, they held him in a tight embrace.**

**Комментарий:**

They were like the limbs that become active attaining the prāṇa, which had reached fainting state, and which again circulates. They stood up simultaneously showing that Nanda possessed great affection for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva embraced Nanda Mahārāja with great joy. Beside himself with ecstatic love, Vasudeva remembered the troubles Kaṁsa had caused him, forcing him to leave his sons in Gokula for their safety.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva’s reaction is described in detail. He remembered on seeing Nanda, how Nanda had helped him greatly to be free of many tribulations. He also met with Upananda and others.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**O hero of the Kurus, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma embraced their parents and bowed down to them, but their throats were so choked up with tears of love that the two Lords could say nothing.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva and Devakī led Yaśodā from her tent into their tent. Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa came there along with Nanda. Śukadeva describes the happy meeting there. Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma honored and greeted Nanda and Yaśodā but could not speak properly, because of prema. Their throats were choked with tears. Since they were first embraced by their parents, there was no opportunity to greet them. Then released from their embrace they greeted their parents. Thus it is mentioned that way (first embracing and then greeting) O Kurūdvaha! Such is the conduct of those coming in a great family of which you are a similar member.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Raising their two sons onto their laps and holding them in their arms, Nanda and fortunate mother Yaśodā forgot their sorrow.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva had Nanda and Yaśodā enter his colorful tent, decorated gorgeously among all the huge tents, in order to relax comfortably. Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma also came there so that they could be caressed by them. That event is described. They gave up the sorrow of separation. The ca indicates Nanda as well. First Yaśodā embraced because of greater parental affection, and then Nanda.“How could the two parents place Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma on their laps without fear since the two showed such evident powers?” They always regarded Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma with affection as their sons (sutau) since thinking of them as their sons eclipsed thinking of their powers and since Yaśodā had parental affection for them.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Then Rohiṇī and Devakī both embraced the queen of Vraja, remembering the faithful friendship she had shown them. Their throats choking with tears, they addressed her as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

When Nanda had gone outside the tent to meet Ugrasena and the other elder Yadus on Vasudeva’s invitation, Rohiṇī and Devakī met with Yaśodā. The two, seated, embraced Yāśodā who had Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa on her lap. Śukadeva calls Yāśodā the queen of Vraja due to his greater respect for her than even Rohiṇī and Devakī.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**\[Rohiṇī said:\] What woman could forget the unceasing friendship you and Nanda have shown us, dear queen of Vraja? There is no way to repay you in this world, even with the wealth of Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

When in this way, Yaśodā was absorbed in the sweet ocean of paternal affection, Rohiṇī, situated in front of her, spoke. Who (referring to herself) would not always remember the beneficial conduct (maitrīm) of you two, that cannot be repaid (anivṛttām)? Since we cannot do beneficial acts for you in return (pratikriyā). O queen of Vraja! She addresses her with respect and indicating affection. Or that friendship was continuous (anivṛttām). You always served us by sending servants to take news about our well-being and always sending presents to us since we were without wealth. And you came here personally on the pretext of pilgrimage. The expression aindram aiśvaryam avāpyāpi (you cannot be repaid even with the wealth of Indra) is just worldly usage, since the opulence of Dvārakā far exceeded that of Indra.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**\[Devakī said:\] Before these two boys had ever seen their real parents, you acted as their parents and gave them all affectionate care, training, nourishment and protection. They were never afraid, good lady, because you protected them just as eyelids protect the eyes. Saintly persons like you never discriminate between outsiders and their own kin. O good lady! You are respected by all.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa’s prema for Yaśodā, with uncertainty, thinking, “Is she the mother of these two or are we?” she spoke somewhat loudly. The two boys were not familiar (adṛṣṭa)with their parents, what to speak of being caressed by them. Balarāma was born in your house and never saw his father. But as soon as Kṛṣṇa was born in Mathurā he was placed in your house. But receiving affectionate care, etc., they lived in the house of you two, who are directly their parents by performing parental duties such as the jāta-karma. You satisfied them by giving them things they wanted (saṁprīṇana). You made them grow by that (abhyudaya), nourished them and relaxed with them (lālana). Even in the other reading—pālanāni, the meaning is the same. They were without fear completely (akutracit bhayau) being maintained because of being entrusted to you. You were like eyelids in protecting them. This was suitable for you. Devotees do not discriminate between self and others. You are the best of devotees. O most respectable (bhavati)! Since Yaśodā had sunk in the ocean of vātsalya for her son, like an arrow-maker concentrating, she did not hear those words and thus did not reply. Otherwise desiring to speak words of a mother, giving up all respect, at that very moment with the help of the cowherd warriors she would have taken her son and returned to Vraja. And Devakī’s words to her are not useless since both their sons were one and Devakī’s son was also present. Kṛṣṇa’s lack of attention to his mother Devakī is suitable. The Lord who is bound by love, is mainly delighted with one who has intense vātsalya and he is only secondarily interested in others. Thus testing her in an assembly of mothers like testing gold amidst inferior stones, the real mother would be clear. Though Devakī knew the nature of the Lord, still since her conception of Kṛṣṇa being her own child manifest then, she was doubtful (whether Kṛṣṇa was born from her). Seeing the overwhelming bhāva of Yāśodā and Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, she went to another tent to respect Kuntī and others, thinking it was not time for further discussion.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: While gazing at their beloved Kṛṣṇa, the young gopīs used to condemn the creator of their eyelids, \[which would momentarily block their vision of him\]. Now, seeing Kṛṣṇa again after such a long separation, with their eyes they took him into their hearts, and there they embraced him to their full satisfaction. In this way they became totally absorbed in ecstatic meditation on him, although those who constantly practice mystic yoga find such absorption difficult to achieve.**

**Комментарий:**

Śrī-ṛṣir uvāca (the sage spoke) means due to omniscience about the bhāva of Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs,Śukadeva knows them in truth and thus one should believe his words. When he rose out of the ocean of prema, receiving permission from his mother, Kṛṣṇa went outside the tent and knowing the gopīs were in a nearby tent, pained to meet them, since he was a bee attracted to their lotus like prema, he entered their tents directed by his friends Uddhava and Balarāma. The gopīs, extremely thin from separation from their beloved, with only their beauty remaining, having obtained Kṛṣṇa, their desired object, after a long time, brought him into their hearts by their eyes (hṛdī-kṛtam). Or they always held him in their hearts but now with their eyes they embraced him and became fully absorbed in him (tad-bhāvaṁ) as when they imitated him (in SB [10.30.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/30.19)). Thus, only then did they become satisfied. Hṛdī instead of hṛdi is Vedic usage. That bhāva is described. It was rare for the best of yogīs or for Rukmiṇī (nitya-yujām durāpam). The gopīs are described. They cursed the creator for making eyelids on the eyes meant to see Kṛṣṇa. “O you who has created eyelids which interrupt the vision, may you not have auspiciousness!”

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord approached the gopīs in a secluded place as they stood in their ecstatic trance. After embracing each of them and inquiring about their well-being, he laughed and spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Approaching them at night in a solitary place, knowing their bhāva, Kṛṣṇa, with his śakti of pervading everywhere, embraced them all tightly, simultaneously, though they were all bewildered by full absorption in him as described in the previous verse. By the tight embrace they recovered. He skillfully asked them, “Has the pain of separation been destroyed by my embrace at this time and by my message spoken by Uddhava”? After some moments, when they were pleased, he spoke the following (idaṁ) to the gopīs while laughing.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] My dear girl friends, do you still remember me? It was for my relatives’ sake that I stayed away so long, intent on destroying my enemies.**

**Комментарий:**

O friends! With a desire to act on behalf of Vasudeva and others, relatives of my father (Nanda), to kill Kaṁsa, I went away for a long time since I had a mind to destroy enemies. Since I had no opportunity to come to Vraja, do you remember me?

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Do you perhaps think I’m ungrateful and thus hold me in contempt? After all, it is the Supreme Lord who brings living beings together and then separates them.**

**Комментарий:**

“O Lord! Why would we remember you, since we are devoid of love for you and are attached to the happiness in our houses? However, you know about love and have given up the happiness of the house. Do you feel pain on remembering us?” Fearing such a crooked response, he speaks in order to explain the reason for his being dependent on the supreme Lord in not remembering them, in order to drink the nectar of their exclusive devotion to him, when they showed him smiling glances and gestures. O friends! If you do not remember me by good qualities what to speak of remembering me by faults? This is explained in two verses. Svit indicates a question. Do you repudiate me, thinking that I am ungrateful? But it is the result of our actions.“If that is so, why did you not communicate with us? Being dependent on the Lord, it was impossible for me to communicate.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Just as the wind brings together masses of clouds, blades of grass, wisps of cotton and particles of dust, only to scatter them all again, so the creator deals with his created beings in the same way.**

**Комментарий:**

An example is given. As the wind scatters (ākṣipate) clouds, etc., the Lord (bhūta-kṛt) also deals similarly with all beings.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Rendering bhakti to me qualifies any living being for eternal life. But your prema for me, which has existed to bring the highest fortune, has caused you to attain me directly.**

**Комментарий:**

“O crown of cleverness! Not considering our words, saying that you are subservient to the Lord, you pierce our ears with a hot needle. Who, other than you, is the Lord?” Knowing this reply of theirs, he speaks with the intention that though that is so, still, I am subservient to your prema. Bhakti to me, such as even one limb among hearing, etc., qualifies all beings for liberation. But your affection for me which has existed is auspicious since it causes increase in my bliss. Attracting me, it will bring me to you (madāpanaḥ). Very quickly you will attain my association completely.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Dear ladies, I am the beginning and end of all created beings and exist both within and without them, just as the elements ether, water, earth, air and fire are the beginning and end of all material objects and exist both within and without them.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord, crown jewel of cleverness, as in sending Uddhava with a message, spoke words with two meanings to the gopīs, who were most intelligent. I exist as the beginning and end of all beings such as devatās and humans, and in the middle also, and outside them, just as the five material elements beginning with ether spread in all material bodies. Thus, speaking of separation from me, who is spread everywhere is meaningless. O women! Among all beings situated at all times, I exist previous to enjoyment with you (ādiḥ) and exist at the end of that enjoyment, and in its middle as well. Thus I always have a relationship with you. Sometimes I go outside because of obligation to other duties. You should not feel pain by a little separation.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**In this way the basic elements of creation pervade the bodies, while the spirit souls pervade their bodies. You should see both of these—the material body and the self—as manifest within me, the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

He confirms this. The elements like ether exist pervading all bodies. The jīva (ātmā), the controller of the bodies, spread (tataḥ) by dharma-bhūta consciousness. See both the body and the jīva (ubhyam) manifested in me, the Supreme Brahman (pare), existing externally. I am spread everywhere. Since I exist pervading your bodies and ātmās, there is no separation. I appear externally during meeting, and appear from you during separation. Thus you should inquire about your perceptions.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus been instructed by Kṛṣṇa in spiritual matters, the gopīs were freed of all tinges of false ego because of their incessant meditation upon him. And with their deepening absorption in him, they came to understand him fully.**

**Комментарий:**

The results of the teachings are described. Having been awakened (śikṣitāḥ) by Kṛṣṇa with teachings concerning himself (adhy-ātmā), their doubts (jīva-kośa) destroyed by remembering his svarūpa that they experienced before, they understood him (adhyagan). Here jīva-kośa does not mean the subtle body since as his eternal associates they did not have subtle bodies. They are his eternal associates due to the Lord’s statement, ballavyo me mad-ātmikāḥ: the gopīs are of my nature. (SB [10.46.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/46.6)) These kind of instructions are given because of the opinion of knowers of rasa: dvyarthaiḥ padaiḥ piśunayec ca rahasya vastu: one should reveal confidential matters with words having dual meaning. (Sāhitya-darpaṇa)

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**The gopīs spoke thus: Dear Lord, whose navel is just like a lotus flower, your lotus feet are the only shelter for those who have fallen into the deep well of material existence. Your feet are worshipped and meditated upon by great mystic yogīs and highly learned philosophers. We wish that these lotus feet may also be awakened within our hearts, although we are only ordinary persons engaged in household affairs.**

**Комментарий:**

The gopīs, thinking of his intention, “As long as I do not return to Vraja,I will take them to a place with lotuses and give them joy,” praising him, pray. O Kṛṣṇa with lotus navel! May your lotus feet always manifest even in the minds of us who serve the houses in Gokula. By your mercy may they manifest in our laps. Those feet are the object of meditation in the minds for your devotees (yogeśvaraiḥ) with profound intelligence. They deliver those who have fallen in the well of saṁsāra. Will not those feet which destroy suffering for those who meditate on them, take away our suffering when they appear in our minds? Just by meditation on your lotus feet, we will pass our time. But we will never attain the form which performs pastimes with us. Kṛṣṇa was embarrased by that. They remained joyful since he said, “Very soon you will know that I have come to Vraja.”

## Chapter 83 - Draupadī Meets the Queens of Kṛṣṇa

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus Kṛṣṇa, the gopīs’ instructor and eternal goal, showed them his mercy. He then met with Yudhiṣṭhira and all his other relatives and inquired from them about their welfare.**

**Комментарий:**

In the eighty-third chapter, Kṛṣṇa is praised by groups of friends and his wives describe their marriages to Draupadī. He showed mercy in such a way that the gopīs became pleased. He was their instructor (guru) and object to be attained (gatiḥ). Atha means after giving the gopīs mercy. Till then he did not even experience a flash of remembrance of Yudhiṣṭhira and others. He then asked Yudhiṣṭhira about his welfare, freedom from injury (avyayam).

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Feeling greatly honored, King Yudhiṣṭhira and the others, freed of all suffering by seeing the feet of the Lord of the universe, gladly answered his inquiries.**

**Комментарий:**

They were honored with various gifts (su-sat-kṛtaḥ). Seeing the Lord’s mercy, they became joyful in mind and all suffering was destroyed.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa’s relatives said:\] O master, how can misfortune arise for those who have even once freely drunk the nectar coming from your lotus feet? This intoxicating liquor pours into the drinking cups of their ears, having flowed from the minds of great devotees through their mouths. It destroys the embodied souls’ forgetfulness of the creator of their bodily existence.**

**Комментарий:**

O Lord! Where is the inauspiciousness for those having bodies as long as they drink though their ears the nectar of your lotus feet, its sweetness, its descriptions? How is it attained if it is so rare? It flows from the minds of great devotees through their mouths. It destroys ignorance (asmṛti) produced by the body at sometime when they experience the bliss of prema.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**The radiance of your personal form dispels the threefold effects of material consciousness, and by your grace we become immersed in total happiness. Your knowledge is indivisible and unrestricted. By your yoga-māyā potency you have assumed this human form for protecting the Vedas, which had been threatened by time. We bow down to you, the final destination of perfect saints.**

**Комментарий:**

Therefore, we worship you. The word hi indicates astonishment. We offer respects (natāḥ) to you by whom the three states of consciousness created by aversion to the Lord in the jīva (ātmā) are destroyed by showing your form (dhāma), due to whom one drowns (samplavam) in bliss. By seeing you the three states are destroyed, one drowns in an ocean of bliss. How could there be a speck of inauspiciousness near you? You are all-pervading (akhaṇḍam). You are complete, eternal consciousness (akuṇṭha-bodham), the function of our minds. You perform activities (kṛti) such as protecting the devotees and destroying the demons, through yoga-māyā, for maintaining laws destroyed by time. You are the goal of the paramahaṁsas such as the Kumāras. We must definitely serve you.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**The great sage Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: As Yudhiṣṭhira and the others were thus praising Lord Kṛṣṇa, the crest jewel of all sublimely glorified personalities, the women of the Andhaka and Kaurava clans met with one another and began discussing topics about Govinda that are sung throughout the three worlds. Please listen as I relate these to you.**

**Комментарий:**

I will describe to you the topics sung in the three worlds that the women began discussing.

### Text 6-7

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Draupadī said: O Vaidarbhī, Bhadrā and Jāmbavatī, Satyā, Satyabhāmā and Kālindī, Mitravindā, Rohiṇī, Lakṣmaṇā and other wives of Kṛṣṇa, please tell me how the Supreme Lord Acyuta, imitating the ways of this world by his mystic power, came to marry each of you.**

**Комментарий:**

Kauśale refers to Queen Nāgnajitī. Tell me without deception how Kṛṣṇa married you, imitating actions of this world. You are his eternal consorts.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Rukmiṇī said: When all the kings held their bows at the ready Text 9\] Draupadī Meets the Queens of Kṛṣṇa 309 to assure that I would be presented to Śiśupāla, he who puts the dust of his feet on the heads of invincible warriors took me from their midst, as a lion forcibly takes his prey from the midst of goats and sheep. May I always be allowed to worship those feet of Kṛṣṇa, the abode of beauty.**

**Комментарий:**

When the kings such as Jarāsandha raised their bows to make me marry Śiśupāla, the Lord, who puts his foot dust on the heads of warriors who were invincible by others, took me from that crowd. May that Lord put his feet on those kings. He did this just as a lion takes its share from a herd of sheep and goat. This indicates his lack of fear. May his feet which are the residence of beauty be worshipped by me.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Satyabhāmā said: My father, his heart tormented by his brother’s death, accused Kṛṣṇa of killing him. To remove the stain on his reputation, the Lord defeated the king of the bears and took back the Syamantaka jewel, which he then returned to my father. Fearing the consequences of his offense, my father offered me to the Lord, even though I had already been promised to others.**

**Комментарий:**

To remove the stain created by my father Satyajit, whose heart was pained by the death of his brother Prasena, the Lord defeated Jāmbavān, took the Syamanaka jewel and gave it to my father. Fearful of his offense, my father offered me to the Lord (prabhave), though I was promised to be given to others. This shows the great power of the Lord.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Jāmbavatī said: Unaware that Kṛṣṇa was none other than his own master and worshippable Deity, the husband of Goddess Sītā, my father fought with him for twenty-seven days. When my father finally came to his senses and recognized the Lord, he took hold of his feet and presented him with both me and the Syamantaka jewel as tokens of his reverence. I am simply the Lord’s maidservant.**

**Комментарий:**

My father (deha-kṛt) Jāmbavān did not at all know (prājñāya) that Kṛṣṇa was the Lord, his master, the husband of Sītā, and fought with him for twenty-seven days. Previously it was said they fought for twenty-eight days (SB 10.56.24). Here it says twenty-seven days. In this case the last day is not counted. In the word tri-navahāny, the a is short to comply with the rules of meter. Recognizing that this was the husband of Sītā, the Lord, understanding his svarūpa, holding his feet, he offered me along with the jewel as gifts.“You appeared in Treta-yuga and had strong determination for the Lord for a long time. Now, you have married him. You are the best.” In embarrassment she says, “I am his servant.”

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Kālindī said: The Lord knew I was performing severe austerities and penances with the hope of one day touching his lotus feet. So he came to me in the company of his friend and took my hand in marriage. Now I am engaged as a sweeper in his palace.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa came with his friend Arjuna (sakhyā).

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Mitravindā said: At my svayaṁ-vara ceremony he came forward, defeated all the kings present—including my brothers, who dared insult him—and took me away just as a lion removes his prey from amidst a pack of dogs. Thus Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of the goddess of fortune, brought me to his capital city. May I be allowed to serve him by washing his feet, life after life.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa, the residence of Lakṣmī (śriyaukaḥ) defeating the kings and my offensive (apakurutaḥ)brothers, carried me, who was amidst the kings, off to his city, as a lion takes his food among pack of dogs. May I wash his feet birth after birth (anubhavam).

### Text 13-14

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Satyā said: My father arranged for seven extremely powerful and vigorous bulls with deadly sharp horns to test the prowess of the kings who desired my hand in marriage. Although these bulls destroyed the false pride of many heroes, Kṛṣṇa subdued them effortlessly, tying them up in the same way that children playfully tie up a goat’s kids. He thus purchased me with his valor. Then he took me away with my maidservants and a full army of four divisions, defeating all the kings who opposed him along the road. May I be granted the privilege of serving that Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Seven strong bulls that had power, vitality and very sharp horns were arranged by my father for testing the prowess of the kings so that he could give me to the strongest suitor. It was previously said that such bulls were arranged so that among kings only the Lord would attain her. Taming those bulls which destroyed the pride of warriors,Kṛṣṇa bound them up like children tying up small goats. The plural is used (śiśavaḥ, children) since he manifested himself in seven forms to tie up seven bulls as previously explained. Kṛṣṇa took me given by the price of his courage (vīrya-sulkāṁ), to his city along with my maidservants and a full army consisting of four divisions: chariots, horses, elephants and infantry (catuḥaṅgiṇīm).

### Text 15-16

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bhadrā said: My dear Draupadī, of his own free will my father invited his nephew Kṛṣṇa, to whom I had already dedicated my heart, and offered me to him as his bride. My father presented me to the Lord with an akṣauhiṇi military guard and a retinue of my female companions. My ultimate perfection is this: to always be allowed to touch Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet as I wander from life to life, desiring to worship him.**

**Комментарий:**

O Draupadī (kṛṣṇe)! My father offered me to Kṛṣṇa, the son of my maternal uncle. She mentioned the name of her husband directly (though this is normally not done) because of remembering that his name should be chanted. Wherever the Lord appears in this world, may I touch his feet there as I travel about due to my desire to worship him (karmabhiḥ)and by which there will be auspiciousness of great happiness (śreyaḥ). To take the direct meaning of karmabhiḥ (as karmas) would be an error since she did not have any karma, since karmas are burned to ashes when knowledge of the tattva of the Lord arises and since one is ineligible to touch his feet while wandering about by karmas.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Lakṣmaṇā said: O Queen, I repeatedly heard Nārada Muni glorify the appearances and activities of Acyuta, and thus my heart also became attached to that Lord, Mukunda. Even Lakṣmī chose him as her husband after careful consideration, rejecting the great devatās who rule various planets.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing how the other queens spoke their stories of their good fortune very briefly, though the weddings were spectacular and seeing that Draupadī seemed to know the excellent arrangements of her own wedding, and not tolerating both situations, Lakṣmaṇā then spoke of her wedding as it happened. My heart became (āsa) attached to Mukunda. Therefore I, who carry a lotus in my hand, chose Mukunda after rejecting various planetary rulers.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**My father, Bṛhatsena, was by nature compassionate to his daughter, and knowing my decision, O saintly lady, he arranged to fulfill my desire.**

**Комментарий:**

Matam means her decision to attain Mukunda.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Just as a fish was used as a target in your svayaṁ-vara ceremony, O Queen, to assure that you would obtain Arjuna as your husband, so a fish was also used in my ceremony. In my case, however, it was concealed on all sides, and only its reflection could be seen in a pot of water below.**

**Комментарий:**

She describes the method. O Queen! As (yathā) your father arranged for a fish desiring Arjuna, so my father too arranged in a similar way. As the fish was by pierced Arjuna’s arrow (pārtheṣuṇā instead of pārthepṣayā), so the fish was pierced by Kṛṣṇa’s arrow. “Then why couldn’t Arjuna pierce the fish in Lakṣmaṇā’s case?” The speciality is described. In your case, the fish was covered from periphery but not from the inside so that it could be seen by glancing upwards from the base of the pillar. Thus, Arjuna, expert at aiming could pierce the fish. But in this case, the target could not be directly seen but only a reflection in the water at the base of the pillar was seen. To shoot the target it was necessary to look down and aim up at the same time. Therefore only Kṛṣṇa could strike the target.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Hearing of this, thousands of kings expert in shooting arrows and in wielding other weapons converged from all directions on my father’s city, accompanied by their military teachers.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing about this amazing and enticing challenge, many kings came.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**My father properly honored each king according to his strength and seniority. Then those whose minds were fixed on me took up the bow and arrow and one by one tried to pierce the target in the midst of the assembly.**

**Комментарий:**

The special bow was placed there by my father. They made great efforts to pierce the fish in the assembly (parṣadi), being attracted to me in their minds (mad-dhiyaḥ).

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Some of them picked up the bow but could not string it, and so they threw it aside in frustration. Some managed to pull the bowstring toward the tip of the bow, only to have the bow spring back and knock them to the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

Some picked it up but could not string it. Some strong warriors managed to pull the string from one tip of the bow to the other tip but were struck by the bow since they were unable to string it. The bow recoiled and hit them.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**A few heroes—namely Jarāsandha, Śiśupāla, Bhīma, Duryodhana, Karṇa and the King of Ambaṣṭha—succeeded in stringing the bow, but none of them could find the target.**

**Комментарий:**

Ambaṣṭha refers to the king of that region. Jarāsandha and others, having power, could not find the target (avidan).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Then Arjuna looked at the reflection of the fish in the water and determined its position. When he carefully shot his arrow at it, however, he did not pierce the target but merely grazed it.**

**Комментарий:**

With great concentration (vi), Arjuna repeatedly saw (īkṣya) the fish reflected in the water and understanding its location with effort released an arrow. The arrow only touched the fish in one part and not in the center. One could understand that the arrow touched the fish because there was a mark left by the arrow. But it did not pierce the fish. Arjuna did this on purpose in order to spread the glories of the Lord, his friend.

### Text 25-26

**Перевод:**

**After all the arrogant kings had given up, their pride broken, the Supreme Lord picked up the bow, easily strung it and then fixed his arrow upon it. As the sun stood in the constellation Abhijit, he looked at the fish in the water only once and then pierced it with the arrow, knocking it to the ground.**

**Комментарий:**

He pierced the fish at noon (abhijiti sthite). With the sun high in the sky above the fish it was much harder to aim.

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Kettledrums resounded in the sky, and on the earth people shouted “Jaya! Jaya!” Overjoyed, devatās showered flowers.**

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Just then I walked onto the ceremonial ground, the ankle bells on my feet gently tinkling. I was wearing new garments of the finest silk, tied with a belt, and I carried a brilliant necklace fashioned of gold and jewels. There was a shy smile on my face and a wreath of flowers in my hair.**

**Комментарий:**

Remembering her joy on that occasion, Queen Lakṣmaṇā describes her choosing Kṛṣṇa at that time in two verses. I entered the arena with my two feet jingling with ankle bells, holding in my two hands with respect a jeweled garland shining with gold, wearing fine silk cloth tied with a belt. The cloth was new, as expected at a wedding. I was smiling shyly and had a garland in my hair.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**I lifted my face, which was encircled by my abundant locks and effulgent from the glow of my earrings reflected from my cheeks. Smiling coolly, I glanced about. Then, looking around at all the kings, I slowly placed the necklace on the shoulder of Murāri, who had captured my heart.**

**Комментарий:**

Then my beauty became unique. My cheeks shone with jeweled earrings and abundant locks of hair near the ears. Lifting my face, I glanced with cooling smiles that removed pain (śiśira).

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Just then there were loud sounds of conchs and mṛdaṅga, paṭaha, bherī and ānaka drums, as well as other instruments. Men and women began to dance, and singers began to sing.**

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The leading kings there could not tolerate my having chosen the Supreme Lord, O Draupadī. Burning with lust, they became quarrelsome.**

**Комментарий:**

O Draupadī (yājñaseni)! Afflicted with lust generated by seeing my counter-form made of māyā standing in front of me, becoming competitive, they could not tolerate the choice.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**The Lord then placed me on his chariot, drawn by four most excellent horses. Holding his bow Śārṅga, ready for combat, he stood on the chariot, and manifested his four arms.**

**Комментарий:**

Ready (sannaddhaḥ) to fight (ājau), he stood on the chariot and manifested his four arms. He embraced me of timid nature with two arms and took up his bow and arrow with the other two arms.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Dāruka drove the Lord’s gold-trimmed chariot as the kings looked on, O Queen, like small animals helplessly watching a lion.**
