**Комментарий:**

Like a lion watched by other animals, Kṛṣṇa left (verb missing). Possessive case (miṣatāṁ bhū-bhujāṁ) is used to show disrespect for the kings.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Somekings pursued the Lord to stop him. Left behind, some kings, with raised bows, gathered on the road. They were like village dogs with a lion.**

**Комментарий:**

The kings, with raised bows, pursued Kṛṣṇa from behind (anvasajjanta) to stop him, like dogs with upraised tails chasing a lion.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**These warriors were deluged by arrows shot from the Lord’s bow, Śārṅga. Some of the kings fell on the battlefield with severed arms, legs and necks; the rest gave up the fight and fled.**

**Комментарий:**

Some fell in the battle (pradhane) and others gave up (santyajya) the battle and fled.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**The Lord of the Yadus then entered his capital city, Kuśasthalī \[Dvārakā\], which is glorified in heaven and on earth. The city was elaborately decorated with flagpoles carrying banners that blocked the sun, and also with splendid archways. As Kṛṣṇa entered, he appeared like the sun-god entering his abode.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa entered Dvārakā, his abode, which was decorated with wonderful arches and cloth banners that blocked rays of the sun, like the sun entering its abode (ketanam).

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**My father honored his friends, family and in-laws with priceless clothing and jewelry and with royal beds, thrones and other furnishings.**

**Комментарий:**

My father honored the Lord’s friends and relations.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**With devotion he presented the perfectly complete Lord with a number of maidservants bedecked with precious ornaments. Accompanying these maidservants were guards walking on foot and others riding elephants, chariots and horses. He also gave the Lord extremely valuable weapons.**

**Комментарий:**

He gave weapons along with maidservants, etc., to the Lord even though the Lord is already complete. The Lord accepted everything because the king had bhakti. He accepts even leaves, flowers, fruits and water, which are offered with bhakti.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Thus, by renouncing all material association and practicing austere penances, we queens have all become personal maidservants of the self-satisfied Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described herself profusely due to absorption in the bhāva described previously, she now in embarrassment satisfies all the elder queens by speaking humbly. Because of being complete in himself, he is qualified to perform pastimes only with himself. Still, we eight queens have become his household servants by giving up material association, by svadharma (tapasā). We were accepted by him just out of his mercy. In fact, he, being complete, enjoys with his queens who are his expansions, forms of Lakṣmī, since it is said: He enjoyed with his Lakṣmīs. (SB [10.59.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/59.43))

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**The other queens said: After killing Bhaumāsura and his followers, the Lord found us in the demon’s prison and could understand that we were the daughters of the kings whom Bhauma had defeated during his conquest of the earth. The Lord set us free, and because we had been constantly meditating upon his lotus feet, the source of liberation from material entanglement, he agreed to marry us, though his every desire is already fulfilled.**

**Комментарий:**

The sixteen thousand one hundred queens speak. Knowing us to be the imprisoned daughters of the kings who were defeated by Bhauma when he conquered the earth, Kṛṣṇa freed us. Though he is full in his desires he married us, who constantly meditate on his lotus feet, which give liberation even from saṁsāra. What to speak of remembrance causing freedom from the prison. We desire the foot dust of that person (verse 42).

### Text 41-42

**Перевод:**

**O saintly lady, we do not desire enjoyment from dominion over the earth, the sovereignty of the king of heaven, mystic power, the position of Brahmā, immortality or even attainment of the kingdom of God. We simply desire to carry on our heads the glorious dust of Kṛṣṇa’s feet, enriched by the fragrance of kuṅkuma from his consort’s bosom.**

**Комментарий:**

“If that is so then he will give all desired objects to you who are devotees of his lotus feet.” O chaste woman! We do not desire kingdoms on earth (sāmrājyam) or kingdom in Svarga (svārājyam) or enjoyment of all objects accomplished by them both (bhaujyam) , yoga siddhis such as aṇimā, etc., (vairājyam), the post of Brahmā (pārameṣṭhyam) or liberation endowed with happiness and power (ānantyam) or even a place in the spiritual world (hareḥ padam). The sequence is in terms of successive superiority. “Then what do you desire?” We desire to carry on our heads the foot dust of he who held a club to kill Bhauma, which is endowed with all beauty (śrīmat) or which gives all beauty. Gadayā nirvibhedādrīn: with his club the Lord broke through the rock fortifications.(SB [10.59.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/59.4)) The foot dust is smeared with the kuṅkuma from Rādhā’s breast. The word śriyaḥ does not refer to Lakṣmī of Vaikuṇṭha since she herself desires that dust but does not attain it. To attain the dust of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet the goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. (SB [10.16.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/16.36)) When Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa was dancing with the gopīs in the rāsa-līlā, the gopīs were embraced by the arms of the Lord. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or other consorts in the spiritual world. (SB [10.47.60](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.60)) This also does not refer to Rukmiṇī, since they eternally have the dust of the Lord’s feet endowed with the kuṅkuma of her breasts (since the queens already possess it, they cannot be asking for it). Thus śriyaḥ here refers to Rādhā alone. On Kṛṣṇa’s two sides are Candrāvalī and Rādhikā. Lakṣmī, Durgā and others are Rādhā’s expansions. (Puruṣa-bodhinī śruti) Rādhā is all Lakṣmīs. (Gautamīya-tantra) In relation to the rāsa dance it is said: anayārādhito nūnam: he was worshipped by one gopī. (SB [10.30.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/30.28)) This is explained in the commentary to mean Rādhā.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**We desire the same contact with the Supreme Lord’s feet that the young women of Vraja, the cowherd boys and even the aborigine Pulinda women desire—the touch of the dust he leaves on the plants and grass as he tends his cows.**

**Комментарий:**

They clarify that desire. Vraja-sriyaḥ refers to Rādhā’s sakhīs such as Laliltā, and suhṛts like Śyāmalā. Pulindyas are young śabara girls who attained mahābhāva by Rādhā’s mercy. They desire the dust from the grass and plants since it is said, pūrṇāḥ pulindyaḥ: the Pulinda women became satisfied. (SB [10.21.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/21.17)) Uddhava praised the bhāva of the gopīs in astonishment: How amazing it is that these simple women who wander about the forest, seemingly spoiled by improper behavior, have achieved the highest levels of mahābhāva for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul! (SB [10.47.59](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.59)) The cowherds are priya-narma-sakhās such as Subala and Ujjvala. They desire that which touched the feet of Svayam Bhagavān (mahātmanaḥ). The truth is this. Kṛṣṇa spoke to Uddhava, who is bound by love, about the glories of the gopīs’ love in the assembly of his wives. He especially spoke about the love of Rādhā. From that time, the wives know about this love and desired to see it. Because of the influence of that glory in the meeting, their desire to see that love was stimulated. Knowing that the recipients of Kṛṣṇa’s great prema were present near by, directed by Kṛṣṇa, with gifts in their hands they quickly went to see the gopīs, their own aṁśinis. Astonished by their beauty, they offered prayers to them. The gopīs, rising up, respected them with embraces, kind words, priceless cloth, ornaments, perfumes and garlands.

## Chapter 84 - The Sages’ Teachings at Kuruksetra

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Pṛthā, Gāndhārī, Draupadī, Subhadrā, the wives of other kings and the Lord’s cowherd girlfriends were all amazed to hear of the queens’ deep love for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord and Soul of all beings, and their eyes filled with tears.**

**Комментарий:**

In the eighty-fourth chapter the sages and Kṛṣṇa praise each other, Vasudeva asks a question and performs sacrifice, and Nanda departs. Kuntī and others, hearing of the deep attachment of the wives for Kṛṣṇa, were surprised.“These queens, the Lord’s better halves only honor his service!” The word atha, used with Draupadī (yajñasenī) and Subhadrā (mādhavī), indicates that the two were at this time situated together. In sva-gopyaḥ, the word sva (own) indicates that they are most dear to Kṛṣṇa. They are mentioned separately from all others since they were not present in the gathering. Thus Kuntī and others heard of this through grapevine (and not directly) since it would be improper from the queens to talk of such fun pastimes independently in front of them. Draupadī asked and Subhadrā heard it directly because of friendship with her and the Lord’s queens.

### Text 2-5

**Перевод:**

**As the women thus talked among themselves and the men among themselves, a number of great sages arrived there, all of them eager to see Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. They included Dvaipāyana, Nārada, Cyavana, Devala and Asita, Viśvāmitra, Śatānanda, Bharadvāja and Gautama, Lord Paraśurāma and his disciples, Vasiṣṭha, Gālava, Bhṛgu, Pulastya and Kaśyapa, Atri, Mārkaṇḍeya and Bṛhaspati, Dvita, Trita, Ekata and the four Kumāras, and Aṅgirā, Agastya, Yājñavalkya and Vāmadeva.**

**Комментарий:**

While the men were talking to the men and the women were conversing with the women, the munis came to see Kṛṣṇa. The list of sages is given.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**As soon as they saw the sages approaching, the kings and other gentlemen who had been seated immediately stood up, including the Pāṇḍava brothers and Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. They all then bowed down to the sages, who are honored throughout the universe.**

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and the other kings and leaders properly worshipped the sages by offering them words of greeting, sitting places, water for washing their feet, drinking water, flower garlands, incense and sandalwood paste.**

**Комментарий:**

As all others worshipped the sages, Kṛṣṇa with Balarāma worshipped the sages.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**After the sages were comfortably seated, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose body protects dharma, addressed them in the midst of that great assembly. Everyone listened silently with rapt attention.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa was the preacher of dharma (dharma-gup) as indicated in the next verses. Sadasaḥ in the genitive means the locative “in the assembly.”

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: Now our lives are indeed successful, for we have obtained life’s ultimate goal: the audience of great yoga masters, which even devatās only rarely obtain.**

**Комментарий:**

We are seeing the masters of yoga, which is rare even for the devatās, what to speak of humans.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**How is it that people who are not very austere and who recognize God only in his deity form in the temple can now see you, touch you, inquire from you, bow down to you, worship your feet and serve you in other ways?**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks with astonishment.“How is it that we humans see the sages when it is rare for devatās?” For humans with little austerity, generated by bathing at tīrthas, etc., who see only the deity as worshippable and not you, how is touching you, etc., possible? It is impossible.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Mere bodies of water are not the real sacred places of pilgrimage, nor are mere images of earth and stone the true worshippable deities. These purify one only after a long time, but saintly sages purify one immediately upon being seen.**

**Комментарий:**

He explains further in three verses. Are not places filled with water tīrtha? They are tīrthas but purify after a long time.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Neither the devatās controlling fire, the sun, the moon and the stars nor those in charge of earth, water, ether, air, speech and mind, who see in terms of duality, remove the sins of their worshipers. But wise sages who see the Lord destroy one’s sins when served for even a few moments.**

**Комментарий:**

Deity of fire and others are worshipped but do not remove the root of sin, vāsanas of people. Who are they? They bestow results according to the degree of service rendered (bheda-kṛtaḥ). Those who know tattva, like you (vipaścitaḥ), devoid of seeing difference in the degree of service, destroy the sins by a moment of service. There is a great difference. Speech and mind are to be worshipped according to: yo vācaṁ brahmety upāste mano brahmety upāste He who worship the voice as Brahman is free to speak as he wishes within the realms reached by speech, and he who worships the mind as Brahman is free to act in the realms reached by the mind. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**One who identifies his self as the inert body composed of mucus, bile and air, who assumes his wife and family are permanently his own, who thinks an earthen image or the land of his birth is worshippable, or who sees a water body as a place of pilgrimage, but who never identifies himself with, feels kinship with, worships or even visits those who are wise in spiritual truth— such a person is no better than a cow or an ass.**

**Комментарий:**

One who avoids saintly persons and instead identifies his self with body and other objects is to be criticized. He who thinks that the corpselike body (kuṇape), composed of mucus, bile and air (tri-dhātuke) is himself (ātmā), who thinks that his wife and children, who have a similar understanding, are his own (sva-dhīḥ), who thinks that images made of earth (bhauma) such as of Śiva, etc., are devatās (ijya dhīḥ), and who sees river and other water bodies as holy place (tīrtha-buddhiḥ), thinking, “I am purified having taken a bath by this water”, but who never thinks of men who are knowers of tattva (abhijñeṣu) to be like worhippable (ijya) or holy (tīrtha) is an ass (go-kharaḥ) among those which carries loads of grass. Some say that gokhara is a useless animal, in the forest on the bank of the Sindhu River. Others say gokhara is a non-Vaiṣṇava: Persons ignorant of dharma, mantras, spiritual knowledge concerning the Lord, even though they are kings, are called gokhara. Those who do not think that knowers of tattva are worshippable yet think that the deity of the Lord Hari is worshippable are not to be called gokhara. He is a kaniṣṭha according to the Eleventh Canto: A person who is very faithfully engaged in the worship of the deity in the temple but does not know how to behave toward devotees or people in general is called a kaniṣṭhaadhikārī. (SB [11.2.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.47)) Similarly, those who do not think that the knowers of tattva are holy but who accept waters such as Gaṅgā, etc., as a tīrtha are not to be called gokhara since there are many statements similar to the one from Eleventh Canto.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Hearing such unfathomable words from the unlimitedly wise Kṛṣṇa, the learned brāhmaṇas remained silent, their minds became filled with doubt.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing the words of Kṛṣṇa starting in verse 9, words which were incoherent (duranvayam), since he spoke like a person dedicated to karma, the brāhmaṇas (sages) became filled with doubt in their hearts (bhramad-dhiyaḥ).

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**For some time the sages pondered the Supreme Lord’s behavior, which resembled that of a subordinate living being. They concluded that he was acting this way to instruct the people in general. Thus they smiled and spoke to him, the origin of all good qualities in the universe.**

**Комментарий:**

Considering for a long time his acting with extreme devotion to the sages (īśitavyatām), they smiled slightly, concluded that he did this to teach people since he is guru of the universe.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**The great sages said: Your power of illusion has totally bewildered us, the most exalted knowers of the truth and leaders among the universal creators. Ah, how amazing is the behavior of the Supreme Lord! He covers himself with his humanlike activities and pretends to be subject to superior control.**

**Комментарий:**

They express the incomprehensible nature of his words. We sages, the best among knowers of tattva, and the lords of creators of universe such as Brahmā, though omniscient, are bewildered by your māyā because (yad) you Supreme Lord act like a jīva (īśitavyāyati) while being difficult to notice (gūḍhaḥ) due to your human actions (īhayā). Your activities are most beautiful since they contain your prowess enclosed within them, like a mirror hidden by paintings on the glass. They are most astonishing.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**The humanlike pastimes of the Almighty are simply a pretense! Effortlessly, he alone sends forth from himself this variegated creation, maintains it and then swallows it up again, all without becoming entangled, just as the element earth takes on many names and forms in its various transformations.**

**Комментарий:**

Even your activities showing power are astonishing. You are one, without another doer (ekaḥ). By yourself (ātmanā), without the assistance of another cause, you create and destroy this universe with multifarious names and forms, yet you are not bound up, not contaminated by its faults. You are devoid of actions of hands (anīhaḥ) since you create by your will alone. An analogy for the Lord’s being one and yet taking various names and forms is given. Earth though one, becomes many in the form of pots, etc., (bhaumaiḥ). Therefore, actions of you, the Lord, mock our intelligence (viḍambanam).

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Nonetheless, at suitable times you assume goodness to protect your devotees and punish the wicked and as a pastime, instituting varṇāśrama, you nourish the eternal path of the Vedas. You are beyond all human intelligence.**

**Комментарий:**

Though you have inconceivable saṅkalpa-śakti, at the time of creation, to destroy the demons so as to protect your devotees, you support sattva in the manifest universe. Being the institutor (ātmā) of varṇāśrama as your pastime, you nourish the eternal path of the Vedas. This is also difficult to understand since all this can be accomplished just by your will. How to consider this? You are the person beyond all intelligence (paraḥ).

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**The Vedas are your form of mercy, and through them one can perceive—by means of action, understanding and self-control— the Lord beyond the universe and prakṛti.**

**Комментарий:**

“But do I protect my devotees by nourishing the path of the Vedas?” The scriptures called Vedas (brahma) are the form of your heart (hṛdayam), made of pure mercy (śuklam). In the Vedas, the supreme tattva, Brahman (sad), beyond the effect (vyaktam) and cause (avyaktam), is known along with tapas, etc. Tapas means performance of dharma. Svādhyāya means learning the meaning of the Vedas. Saṁyama means drawing the mind away from other subjects. By supporting the Vedas, you protect your devotees.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O Supreme Brahman, you honor the members of the brahminical community, for they are the perfect agents by which one can realize you through the evidence of the Vedas. For that very reason you are the foremost worshiper of the brāhmaṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

“If I am like that, why do I worship you sages?” Because the Vedas are your heart, you fully worship (sabhājayasi) the community of brāhmaṇas who carry the Vedas. They are the best place for understanding (sad-dhāma) you, who are proved by the Vedas (śāstra-yoneḥ). For that very reason, since you worship the community of brāhmaṇas (tad), you are the foremost worshipper of the brāhmaṇas. Thus you always engage yourself in dharma for teaching the people. You honor the brāhmaṇas to teach the people. In the manner that they started the discussion with this concept, they finish with the same statement.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Today our birth and knowledge of spiritual and material topics have all become perfect because we have been able to associate with you, the goal of all saintly persons. You are the ultimate, supreme blessing.**

**Комментарий:**

What is the use of our thinking of the inconceivable! Now we will reveal the bliss in our hearts. Being met by you, the goal of the devotees, our human birth has become successful. Study of the Vedas (vidyāyāḥ), scriptural knowledge which arises from that study (tapas), and realization of Lord (dṛk) have become successful since you are the supreme limit (paraḥ) of human goals (śreyasām), since you are Svayam Bhagavān. The deletion of genitive case-ending of janma is poetic licence.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Let us offer obeisances unto that Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, the infinitely intelligent Supersoul, who has disguised his greatness through his yogamāyā.**

**Комментарий:**

You may praise or offer respects to us to teach the common man, but we must bow down to you, our worshippable Lord.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Neither these kings nor even the Vṛṣṇis, who enjoy your intimate association, know you as the soul of all existence, the force of time and the supreme controller. For them you are covered by the curtain of māyā.**

**Комментарий:**

The Vṛṣṇis and others are most fortunate. Those kings who have incessantly gathered here such as Nagnajit, whom you enjoyed intimately with when sitting and resting and the Vṛṣṇis such as Satyaki, do not know you as being covered by the screen of māyā. They experience you as the Lord full of knowledge and bliss (ātmānam), the Lord within all beings who impels everyone (kālam) by your svāṁśa, the Paramātmā, spread to the eyes and other senses quickly by qualities such as beauty and omniscience (īśvara). Īśvara is formed by applying suffix varaṭ to the root aś when the meaning is “he does quickly” (Uṇādi-sūtra 5.57). Here it should not be taken to mean that they perceived the Lord suddenly since that would be against the following statements: Then, with the permission of Lord Kṛṣṇa, their sole object of worship, the Vṛṣṇis ate breakfast and sat down at their leisure beneath trees that gave cooling shade. (SB [10.82.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/82.11)) The Vṛṣṇis were so absorbed in Kṛṣṇa consciousness that they forgot their own bodies while sleeping, sitting, walking, conversing, playing, bathing and so on. (SB [10.90.46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/90.46)) However, Uddhava says: This universe with all its planets is most unfortunate. And even more unfortunate are the members of the Yadu dynasty because they could not identify Kṛṣṇa as the Lord, any more than the fish could identify the moon. (SB [3.2.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.8)) But this refers to Yadus who were previously devatās, not the eternal associates since the later statement refers to their quality of knowing the Lord and that they were exclusively devoted to the Lord: The Yadus were all experienced devotees, learned and expert in psychic study. Over and above this, they were always with the Lord in all kinds of relaxations, and still they were only able to know him as the one Supreme who dwells everywhere. (SB [3.2.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.9))

### Text 24-25

**Перевод:**

**A person even while sleeping between the two states, knows you with your qualities and not devoid of qualities since he realizes that truth of your qualities. You are manifested as by the senses and seen with forms with names. Similarly, the senses of one whose consciousness is bewildered by illusion perceive only the names and forms of material objects. Thus, such a person loses his memory and cannot know you.**

**Комментарий:**

They support their statement. A person, among the Vṛṣṇis and kings, even while sleeping knows you (ātmānam) as endowed with qualities and not devoid of qualities since he experiences that your qualities are real and eternal (guṇa-tattva-dṛk). You are manifested as Śyamasundara with senses like eyes, with a form (mātrā) and with names like Kṛṣṇa (nāma-mātreindriyābhātam). The deep-sleep of the person is samādhi in you and is not a function of tamas. All the yogī’s mental functions of waking, dreaming and deep sleep take shelter of the Lord. (Garuḍa Purāṇa) Other meanings of this verse should not be accepted. The person devoid of bhakti is low. An opposite example is given. Just as one person among the Vṛṣṇis and the kings, though sleeping, knows you. Others like Duryodhana, even while awake, do not know you since they are devoid of knowledge of their ātmā and Paramātmā (vibhrama-cittaḥ) because of destruction of memory by māyā due to engaging the senses in sense objects like sound which are names alone (viṣayeṣu nāma-mātreṣu). The sense objects are names alone since they are flickering like lightning. Pleasure is known as contact with touch, taste, sight, smell, and hearing, which lasts for the time it takes an arrow to fall on the ground. (Mahābhārata)

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Today we have directly seen your feet, the source of the holy Ganges, which washes away volumes of sins. Perfected yogīs can at best meditate upon your feet within their hearts. But only those who render you wholehearted bhakti and in this way vanquish the soul’s covering—the material mind—attain you as their final destination. Therefore kindly show mercy to us, your devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Wanting to leave, the sages request mercy. We have seen the feet of you who have the qualities mentioned, the shelter of the Gaṅgā which destroys (marṣa) piles of sin and which are the meditated upon in the heart by yogīs for attaining suitable results but are not seen by them. An example is given of themselves. Please give us devotees mercy. “Since siddhis are attained by yoga, what more can bhakti give?” Those who have destroyed the subtle body (jīva-kośa) characterized by desires (āśaya) by intense bhakti attain your shelter. Without bhakti one cannot attain you by yoga alone. One can understand me as I am, as the Lord, only by bhakti. And when one is in full consciousness of me by such devotion, he attains me. (BG [18.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.55))

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus spoken, O wise king, the sages then taking permission from Kṛṣṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Yudhiṣṭhira and prepared to depart for their abodes.**

**Комментарий:**

Dāśārham means Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that they were about to leave, the renowned Vasudeva approached the sages. After bowing down to them and touching their feet, he spoke to them with carefully chosen words.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the sages preparing to go, Vasudeva approached them, offered respects, grasped their feet, and spoke. The sandhi in babhāṣedam is poetic license. Since he was the father of the Lord, he was famous (mahā-yaśāḥ). He was very polite (suyantritaḥ). Right now I will ask what should be asked to sages who can cut all doubts, who have gathered together by extreme good fortune.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Vasudeva said: Obeisances to you, the residence of all the devatās. Please hear me, O sages. Kindly tell us how the reactions of one’s work can be counteracted by further work.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to you, in whom all devatās reside. Yāvatīr vai devatās tāḥ sarvā veda-vidi brāhmaṇe vasanti: All the devatās reside in a brāhmaṇa who knows the Vedas.(Taittirīya-āraṇyaka) Please teach how karma can be destroyed by properly performing karmas.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Nārada Muni said: O brāhmaṇas, it is not so amazing that in his eagerness to know, Vasudeva has asked us about his ultimate benefit, for he considers Kṛṣṇa a mere boy.**

**Комментарий:**

When the sages remained silent on being asked, Nārada spoke since he was the chief of them. The meaning is this. Vasudeva is definitely not ignorant like others since he is an avatāra of viśuddha-sattva, since he showed his learning in the maternity ward and since he is also worshipped in the āvaraṇa around the pīṭha of the king of mantras. He is eternally liberated. Not asking Kṛṣṇa, who is present here and knows everything, he asks you in order to teach people just as Kṛṣṇa praised you through verses such asvayam janma-bhṛtaḥ (verse 9). O brāhmaṇas! Though Vasudeva knows everything, he thinks of Kṛṣṇa as a son like Gada and others and thus putting him aside asks us about the best method for the highest goal. That is not astonishing. He gives a side glance (api). Citsukha’s version has ati instead of api. He does this to teach people.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**In this world familiarity breeds contempt. For example, one who lives on the banks of the Ganges might travel to some other body of water to be purified.**

**Комментарий:**

He gives an example to show why he asks the sages, thinking Kṛṣṇa a small boy. An object always in proximity, though most excellent for men, becomes the cause of lack of respect for the object, not thinking it excellent anymore. Those who assume pastimes as a human have such a mood. Just as giving up the Gaṅgā, the people living on the Gaṅgā’s bank go to another tīrtha to purify themselves.

### Text 32-33

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord’s awareness is never disturbed by time, by the creation and destruction of the universe, by changes in its own qualities, or by anything else, whether self-caused or external. But although the consciousness of the Lord, who is the supreme one without a second, is never affected by material distress, by the reactions of material work or by the constant flow of nature’s modes, ordinary persons nonetheless think that the Lord is covered by his own creations of prāṇa and other material elements, just as one may think that the sun is covered by clouds, snow or an eclipse.**

**Комментарий:**

“The reason for not recognizing the true nature of Kṛṣṇa, everyouthful, when he is continuously in proximity is made up by Vasudeva for teaching people, thinking,‘When I who have knowledge of this, ask question regarding karma and perform karma, even those who are ignorant of them will accept them.’” Nārada speaks suggesting this. The Lord’s omniscience (anubhūtiḥ) concerning his svarūpa, qualities and powers is never destroyed (riṣyati) but people other than Vasudeva, like Duryodhana (anyaḥ) think that Kṛṣṇa, shining as ever-youthful, is covered by material prāṇas, etc., the vibhūtis of the Lord, just like themselves. Vasudeva however, knowing Kṛṣṇa as the highest and ever-youthful, acts like them to teach people. He clarifies how the Lord’s knowledge is never destroyed. His knowledge is not destroyed by time like how cucumber is, though time is the great cause of destruction and creation of the universe (asya). It is not destroyed on its own (svataḥ) like how lightning is. It is not from another object (anyasmāt) like a pot destroyed by little rock, or by qualities (guṇataḥ)like a body whose pervious form is destroyed by the appearance of another form. An opposite example is given to support what is stated. The Lord’s knowledge is not destroyed by sufferings (kleśa) such as rāga, etc., and karmas, which cause those sufferings and their results (paripakā) – happiness and distress, or the successive flow of guṇas like sattva, etc., (guṇa-pravāha) because he is the Lord, with no equal (advitīyam). An analogy is given. The sun is not touched by clouds, snow, or eclipses.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**\[Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:\] The sages then spoke again, O King, addressing Vasudeva while all the kings, along with Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, listened.**

**Комментарий:**

After this, understanding the intentions of Vasudeva and Nārada, the sages spoke. O crest jewel of success! O most worthy of worship! The genitive case (sarveṣāṁśṛṇvatāṁ rājñāṁ) is used to express the locative case since they instructed the kings and testified the meaning of their words.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**\[The sages said:\] It has been definitely concluded that karma is counteracted by karmas when one executes Vedic sacrifices as a means of worshiping Kṛṣṇa, giver of results for all sacrifices, with sincere faith.**

**Комментарий:**

In this verse the sages reply to Vasudeva’s question about eliminating karma by karmas (verse 29). Sacrifices will not destroy karma unless one understands that it is worship of Viṣṇu. Another specific reason that he is present in the sacrifice is that he is the Lord of all yajñas, the giver of the results, since he is the lord of all devatās. The author of Vedānta-sūtras says: The Lord alone gives the results because that is reasonable. (Brahma-sūtra) If that is what you desire, then worship your son by other methods.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Learned authorities who see through the eye of scripture have demonstrated that this is the easiest method of fixing the mind on the Lord and that it is a method which brings joy to the heart.**

**Комментарий:**

This method (yogaḥ) characterized by karmas shown by learned, who have the eyes of scripture, easily performed like an amalaka in the hand, can be performed even without conquering the senses. It causes the mind’s concentration on the Lord to a great extent (upaśamaḥ) since one performs it aiming at the Lord. Śamo manniṣṭhatā buddher: śama means fixing the intelligence on the Lord. (SB [11.19.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/19.36)) Brahma-vidyā is contained within it like the fibers in a lotus stem. It brings joy to the heart and is dharma. It produces liberation in the form of bhakti since it destroys bondage by offering to Viṣṇu. By purification all faults are removed, just as poisonous mercury nourishes health (when administered according to Āyurveda).

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**This is the most auspicious path for a religious householder of the twice-born orders—to selflessly worship the Lord with wealth honestly obtained.**

**Комментарий:**

“It is said that liberation is achieved only by renouncing karmas. Nakarmaṇāna prajayā dhanena tyāgenaike ’mṛtatvaṁānaśuḥ: not by karmas, sons or wealth, only by renunciation, can one attain immortality.(Taittarīya-āraṇyaka) Why recommend karmas?” It is recommended since renunciation of karmas is not possible. This karma-yoga is the auspicious path for the householders of three upper varṇas. Svaty-ayanaḥ means a tool for creating auspiciousness according to karaṇādhikaraṇayoś (Pāṇini 3.3.117) The Lord is worshipped by white or pure money (śuklena) since it honestly earned.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**An intelligent person should learn to renounce his desire for wealth by performing sacrifices and acts of charity. He should learn to renounce his desire for wife and children by experiencing family life. And he should learn to renounce his desire for promotion to a higher planet in his next life, O saintly Vasudeva, by studying the effects of time. Self-controlled sages who have thus renounced their attachment to household life go to the forest to perform austerities.**

**Комментарий:**

Without niṣkāma nature, destruction of karma will not take place. And niṣkāma nature arises in this way. One should reject the desire for wealth by yajña and charity which are results of wealth. One should think, “What is the use of this wealth other than doing this?” One should give up desire for enjoying the wife and attaining sons by enjoying objects suitable to house. By experiencing them, one gives up enthusiasm for them. One should give up desire for higher planets by hearing that even devatās die (deva-kālena). This practice is then substantiated. The wise gave up household life (grāme) and performed austerities in the forest.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**A member of the twice-born classes is born with three kinds of debts—those owed to the devatās, to the sages and to his forefathers. If he leaves his body without first liquidating these debts by performing sacrifice, studying the scriptures and begetting children, he will fall down into a hellish condition.**

**Комментарий:**

For one not doing these karmas there is no auspiciousness. A brāhmaṇa who is born, takes birth with three debts. By studying the Vedas he pays his debt to the sages. By sacrifice he is freed from debts to the devatās. By producing children, he is freed from his debts to the Pitṛs. (Taittirīyasaṁhitā) By brāhmaṇas, the three upper varṇas are indicated in the śruti. By not repaying (anistīrya) the debts to them he falls. Liquidating the three debts the mind should concentrate on liberation. Not liquidating the debts, and striving for liberation, one goes downwards. (Manu Smṛti) Here taking shelter of the Lord is not explained, but in taking shelter of the Lord there is no fault since it will be said: O King! One who has given up all varṇāśrama duties and has taken full shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, who offers shelter to all, is not a debtor to or servant of the devatās, great sages, ordinary living beings, relatives or Pitṛs. (SB [11.5.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.41))

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**But you, O magnanimous soul, are already free from two of your debts—those to the sages and the forefathers. Now absolve yourself of your debt to the devatās by executing Vedic sacrifices, and in this way free yourself completely of debt and renounce all material shelter.**

**Комментарий:**

The word tu indicates Vasudeva in particular. You are certainly (vai) free from debts to Pitṛs and sages. Become completely free of the three debts and become houseless (aśaraṇaḥ). Leave the house. We have answered according to the question. But in their hearts, they said, “Viṣṇu (a) is your shelter. By hearing about him, take shelter of him alone.”

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**O Vasudeva, without doubt you must have previously worshipped the Lord, the master of all worlds. Both you and your wife must have perfectly worshipped him with supreme devotion, since he has accepted the role of your son.**

**Комментарий:**

Having answered the question to give example to the people, the mood of Vasudeva and Nārada is clarified. O Vasudeva shining with the treasure (vasu) of bhakti, respected by all the eternally liberated devotees! Though you and your wife are not qualified for karmas, but you engage in them to teach the people, just as Kṛṣṇa does.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After hearing these statements of the sages, generous Vasudeva bowed his head to the ground and, praising them, requested them to become his priests.**

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Thus requested by him, O King, the sages engaged the pious Vasudeva in performing fire sacrifices at that holy place of Kurukṣetra according to strict religious principles and with most excellent ritual arrangements.**

### Text 44-45

**Перевод:**

**When Mahārāja Vasudeva was about to be initiated for the sacrifice, O King, the Vṛṣṇis came to the initiation pavilion after bathing and putting on fine clothes and garlands of lotuses. The other kings also came, elaborately ornamented, as well as all Vasudeva’s joyful queens, who wore jeweled lockets around their necks and were also clad in fine garments. The royal wives were anointed with sandalwood paste and carried auspicious items for the worship.**

**Комментарий:**

Holding articles in their hands, anointed with catuḥsama (āliptāḥ), they came to the arena.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**Mṛdaṅgas, paṭahas, conchs, bherīs, ānakas and other instruments resounded, male and female dancers danced, and sūtas and māgadhas recited glorifications. Sweet-voiced Gandharvīs sang, accompanied by their husbands.**

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**After Vasudeva’s eyes had been decorated with black cosmetic and his body smeared with fresh butter, the priests initiated him according to scriptural rules by sprinkling him and his eighteen wives with sacred water. He resembled the regal moon encircled by stars.**

**Комментарий:**

His eyes were anointed with mascara and his body smeared with newly-churned butter. He was like the full moon, with no blemish (soma-rājam).

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**Vasudeva received initiation along with his wives, who wore silk sārīs and were adorned with bangles, necklaces, ankle bells and earrings. With his body wrapped in a deerskin, Vasudeva shone splendidly.**

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**My dear Mahārāja Parīkṣit, Vasudeva’s priests and the officiating members of the assembly, dressed in silk dhotīs and jeweled ornaments, looked so effulgent that they seemed to be standing in the sacrificial arena of Indra, the killer of Vṛtra.**

**Комментарий:**

They were dressed in cloth with gems hanging at the edges. The simile is used to create astonishment for a moment.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**At that time Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, the Lords of all living entities, shone forth with great majesty in the company of their respective sons, wives and other family members, who were their expansions.**

**Комментарий:**

Jīveśau means the two are the Lords of all jīvas.

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**Performing various kinds of Vedic sacrifice according to the proper regulations, Vasudeva worshipped the Lord of all sacrificial paraphernalia, mantras and rituals. He executed both primary and secondary sacrifices, offering oblations to the sacred fire and carrying out other aspects of sacrificial worship.**

**Комментарий:**

He worshipped the Lord according to rules pertaining to sacrifice (anu-yajñam). The rules are related to agnihotra, etc. Vasudeva worshipped Viṣṇu, the Lord of all sacrificial paraphernalia such as cakes (dravya), mantras (jñāna) and rituals (kriyā) by primary sacrifices (prākṛtaiḥ) such as jyotiṣṭoma and darśa-pūrṇamāsa, which are prescribed in detail in revealed scriptures and by secondary sacrifices (vaikṛtaiḥ) such as the saurya and satra, whose details are obtained from the primary sacrifices by extension (atideśa)through injunctions (codanā), characteristic signs (liṅga), etc.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**Then, at the appropriate time and according to scripture, Vasudeva remunerated the priests by decorating them with precious ornaments, though they were already richly adorned, and offering them valuable gifts of gems, cows, land and marriageable girls.**

**Комментарий:**

After the sacrifice (atha), he decorated the priests with ornaments and gave them donations consisting of great gems, and gold, land, cows and girls.

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**After supervising the patnī-saṁyāja and avabhṛthya rituals, the great brāhmaṇa sages bathed in Paraśurāma’s lake with the sponsor of the sacrifice, Vasudeva, who led them.**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇas performed the patnī-saṁyāja ritual and rituals related to the avabhṛthya. Then they performed the avabhṛthya bath (sasnuḥ).

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**His sacred bath complete, Vasudeva joined with his wives in giving the jewelry and clothes they had been wearing to the professional reciters. Vasudeva then put on new garments, after which he honored all classes of people by feeding everyone, even the dogs.**

**Комментарий:**

After he bathed, Vasudeva’s queens gave cloth and ornaments to the reciters. They worshipped the various castes and others down to the dog (ā-śvabhyaḥ), by offering food. Pūjayat instead of apūjayat is poetic license.

### Text 55-56

**Перевод:**

**With opulent gifts he honored his relatives, including all their wives and children; the royalty of the Vidarbha, Kosala, Kuru, Kāśī, Kekaya and Sṛñjaya kingdoms; the officiating members of the assembly; and also the priests, witnessing demigods, humans, spirits, forefathers and Cāraṇas. Then, taking permission from Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of the goddess of fortune, the various guests departed as they all chanted the glories of Vasudeva’s sacrifice.**

**Комментарий:**

He worshipped (apūjayat previous verse)them beginning with the Yadus (bandhūn), ending with Cāraṇas, with gifts as tokens of his affection. Then they all departed.

### Text 57-58

**Перевод:**

**The Yadus were all embraced by their friends, close family members and other relatives, including Dhṛtarāṣṭra and his younger brother, Vidura; Pṛthā and her sons; Bhīṣma; Droṇa; the twins Nakula and Sahadeva; Nārada; and Vedavyāsa. Their hearts melting with affection, these and the other guests left for their kingdoms, their progress slowed by the pain of separation.**

**Комментарий:**

Details are given of some who departed. Anuja refers to Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s younger brother Vidura. Characterized by pain of separation friends departed. Others too were indifferent.

### Text 59

**Перевод:**

**Nanda Mahārāja showed his affection for his relatives, the Yadus, by remaining with them a little longer, together with his cowherds. During his stay, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma, Ugrasena and the others honored him with especially profuse worship.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva speaks suggesting that the Lord arranged for the departure of all others so that he could stay for a long time in Kurukṣetra with the people of Vraja without any feeling of restriction. The word tu distinguishes Nanda from all the others at Kurukṣetra. Nanda was worshipped much more elaborately (bṛhatyā), even than the sons of Kuntī. Nanda stayed because he had great affection for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, more than even friends like Vasudeva.

### Text 60

**Перевод:**

**Having so easily crossed over the vast ocean of his ambition, Vasudeva felt fully satisfied. In the company of his many wellwishers, he took Nanda by the hand and addressed him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

After the death of Kaṁṣa, Vasudeva had the desire that he along with Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma should meet the people of Vraja in some great tīrtha and have a huge festival with all relatives, children, sages and kings. He was now pleased to have crossed over very easily that great ocean—something hard to arrange. On another day, surrounded by friends, with all his brothers and sons, he went to Nanda’s residence. Sitting on a seat, facing Nanda and taking his hand in affection, he spoke to him. He had come to pacify Nanda who would suffer at the time of separating from Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 61

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Vasudeva said: My dear brother, God himself has tied the knot called affection, which tightly binds human beings together. It seems to me that even great heroes and mystics find it very difficult to free themselves from it.**

**Комментарий:**

Learned Vasudeva, who is going to explain that his bond of affection with Nanda is difficult to give up due to being spiritual, speaks of material bond of affection in order to show how much greater spiritual affection is than material affection. O brother! I think the knot called affection of humans for brothers or sons is difficult to give up by them since it is created by the Lord. It is difficult to cut for warriors by their strength and difficult to give up for yogīs by discrimination. It is difficult to cut since even kings and yogīs such as Vaisiṣṭha became overwhelmed with grief at the death of their sons. Thus though it is temporary knot, if it is difficult to give up then what to speak of our affection, which is eternal? I am eternally bound to you with affection.

### Text 62

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord must have created the bonds of affection, for such exalted saints as you have never stopped showing matchless friendship toward us ingrates, although it has never been properly reciprocated.**

**Комментарий:**

Since I cannot repay the beneficial acts you did for me out of affection as a friend or brother, I am a debtor to you always. He speaks while drowning in an ocean of humility. To us bound in Kaṁsa’s prison, the friendship shown by you, the best of the devotees, in the form of protecting our wife and sons, is incomparable (apratikalpā) since it is ordained that the substitute for one’s children and wives is oneself. It has been fruitless (aphalā) since it was devoid of desire for reciprocation. It can never be repaid. We are ungrateful, not recognizing the favor you have done. In this way he establishes that he is a debtor.

### Text 63

**Перевод:**

**Previously, dear brother, we did nothing to benefit you because we were unable to, yet even now that you are present before us, our eyes are so blinded by the intoxication of material good fortune that we continue to ignore you.**

**Комментарий:**

In this verse Vasudeva explains his failure to show gratitude. Previously, subordinate to Kaṁsa because we were unable (akalpāt), we could not repay your beneficial acts. Now, after the killing of Kaṁsa, though we are independent, we are blinded by wealth.

### Text 64

**Перевод:**

**O most respectful one, may a person who wants the highest benefit in life never gain kingly wealth, for it leaves him blind to the needs of his own family and friends.**

**Комментарий:**

He criticizes wealth that causes blindness. Mā abhūt instead of mābhūtis poetic license. O Nanda who respects others (māna-da)! Since you give respect to others though you have royal wealth, that wealth is suitable for you. He speaks in this way to put himself in a low position in front of Nanda, though the Yadus are not actually blinded by wealth since it will be said: How could the brāhmaṇas curse the Vṛṣṇis, who were always respectful to the brāhmaṇas, charitable, and inclined to serve senior and exalted personalities and whose minds were always fully absorbed in thought of Lord Kṛṣṇa? (SB [11.1.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/1.8))

### Text 65

**Перевод:**

**ŚrīŚukadeva Gosvāmī said: His heart softened by feelings of intimate sympathy, Vasudeva wept. His eyes brimmed with tears as he remembered the friendship Nanda had shown him.**

**Комментарий:**

Vasudeva’s heart became softened with friendship naturally. He again remembered all of the friendly acts of Nanda and wept. This shows the deep affection between the brothers.

### Text 66

**Перевод:**

**And on his part, Nanda was also full of affection for his friend Vasudeva. Thus during the following days Nanda would repeatedly announce, “I will be leaving later today” and “I will be leaving tomorrow.” But out of love for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma he remained there for three more months, honored by all the Yadus.**

**Комментарий:**

“Tu” indicates Nanda’s different intention. Vasudeva’s intention was different from Nanda’s. This suggests that Nanda’s heart was deep like an ocean. He was respected by Vasudeva and others. Because of his prema for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma and their prema for him (premṇā), he forgot to leave. Moreover, he was a benefactor (priya-kṛt) of his friend Vasudeva. Though he had heard that Vasudeva says that even Kṛṣṇa is his son, he did not show anxiousness to take Kṛṣṇa to Gokula (Govinda). In this way he became dear to his friend. The following should be known. Though Nanda heard such statements of his brother Vasudeva, had said nothing since he had no doubt that Kṛṣṇa was his son due to recognizing that Kṛṣṇa was sometimes born from Vasudeva due to Garga’s statement prāg ayaṁ vasudevasya: previously, Kṛṣṇa was the son of Vasudeva. (SB [10.8.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.14)) And since out of faith he had vātsalya for Kṛṣṇa, endowed with great qualities. He was not anxious to bring Kṛṣṇa to Gokula since Kṛṣṇa discussed with him in private: “O mother! O father! I went to Mathurā on your insistence to benefit Vasudeva and other relatives. Kaṁsa and others were killed by me. But there are other enemies. Without destroying them, they will not be free of worry. Giving up the relatives and going with you to Gokula at this time will not be glorious. Please consider this O respected father! Moreover, going to Dvārakā from here, going to the Rājasūya sacrifice invited by Yudhiṣṭhira, then killing Śiśupāla there, returning to Dvārakā and killing Śālva, killing Dantavakra at the southern gate of Mathurā, then going to Gokula, performing pastimes with you, I will stay with you always. Vasudeva and others will be addressed in another way. Until I come, closing your eyes, see me within your hearts. Know that I will certainly come. Nothing other than this will happen.” He made this vow at the feet of his father.

### Text 67-68

**Перевод:**

**Then, after Vasudeva, Ugrasena, Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava, Balarāma and others had fulfilled his desires and presented him with precious ornaments, fine linen and varieties of priceless household furnishings, Nanda Mahārāja accepted all these gifts and took his leave. Seen off by all the Yadus, he departed with his family members and the residents of Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

After three months (tataḥ) Nanda, having conviction that he attained Govinda’s feet, went to the province of Mathurā with the people of Vraja, his friends. His desired bliss in the form of Kṛṣṇa coming to Gokula, staying there and performing pastimes were fulfilled, first in general by Vasudeva and Ugrasena and then in particular by Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava and Balarāma. In this regard, Vasudeva and Ugrasena satisifed him by saying, “As long as the two are distracted in checking the enemies they cannot come to Gokula. That would happen in the future by Kṛṣṇa’s will so that the Lord, affectionate to relatives, can live in Vraja and in Dvārakā.” Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma satisfied him. After killing Kaṁsa, he said to his father, “I will come to see my relatives.” (SB [10.45.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/45.23)) He had an opportunity to do this. “On some pretext we will come and will stay there.” Uddhava satisfied him by saying, “I confirm this.” In his mind he resolved the issue due to understanding their supreme power.“The two endowed with acintya-śakti are capable of sporting in both places.” Similarly he was satisfied by the Yadus. The gopīs thought, “Dearest Kṛṣṇa will associate with me without restriction, after killing Dantavakra.” \[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] My dear girl friends, do you still remember me? It was for my relatives’ sake that I stayed away so long, intent on destroying my enemies. (SB [10.82.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/82.41)) Satisfied with priceless ornaments, etc., accepting with affection household goods given by Vasudeva and Ugrasena and Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and others, Nanda went to Vraja, seen off by Vasudeva and others. A superficial meaning of the words (that Nanda desired the gifts given to him) is not possible. These devotees of Vṛndāvana, have dedicated their homes, wealth, friends, dear relations, bodies, children and very lives and hearts only to you. (SB [10.14.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.35)) The cowherds, had dedicated everything to lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa. (SB [10.65.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/65.4)) The people of Vraja had desire only for Kṛṣṇa. And Nanda is described as having all prosperity.

### Text 69

**Перевод:**

**Unable to withdraw their minds from Govinda’s lotus feet, Nanda and the cowherd men and women returned to Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

They were unable to withdraw their minds from Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet where they had placed (kṣiptam) them. They went quickly to Vraja, in the province of Mathurā.

### Text 70

**Перевод:**

**Their relatives having thus departed, and seeing that the rainy season was approaching, the Vṛṣṇis, whose only Lord was Kṛṣṇa, went back to Dvārakā.**

**Комментарий:**

When their friends Nanda and others (bandhuṣu) had gone back, the Vṛṣṇis went to Dvārakā.

### Text 71

**Перевод:**

**They told the people of the city about the festive sacrifices performed by Vasudeva, lord of the Yadus, and about everything else that had happened during their pilgrimage, especially how they had met with all their loved ones.**

**Комментарий:**

They told the people of the city about the festive sacrifices performed by Vasudeva.

## Chapter 85 - Lord Kṛṣṇa Instructs Vasudeva and Retrieves Devakī’s Sons

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bādarāyaṇi said: One day the two sons of Vasudeva— Saṅkarṣaṇa and Acyuta—came to pay him respects, bowing down at his feet. Vasudeva greeted them with great affection and spoke to them.**

**Комментарий:**

In the eighty-fifth chapter, Vasudeva praises Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma as Brahman, the six children of Devakī are brought back and Bali praises Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. Vasudeva had bhakti predominated by awareness of the Lord as Brahman, with awareness of him as son being secondary. Both of you, husband and wife, constantly think of me as your son and as Brahman and have shown affection. Thus you will achieve the highest perfection. (SB [10.3.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.45)) In order to show that his bhakti was less than the bhakti of Nanda, which was different, he speaks this verse. This happened sometime during the morning sandhya-vandana.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Having heard the great sages’ words concerning the power of his two sons, and having seen their valorous deeds, Vasudeva became convinced of their divinity. Thus, addressing them by name, he spoke to them as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing the sages’ words at Kurukṣetra, which indicated his sons’ powers (dhāma-sūcakam), Vasudeva, having strengthened his conviction by seeing their valorous acts again, addressed them by name and spoke. He was famous for having such knowledge previously since he said: I know you directly as the Supreme Person beyond material existence, as the impersonal Brahman, as Paramātmā and Bhagavān. (SB [10.3.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.13))

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**\[Vasudeva said:\] O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, best of yogīs, O eternal Saṅkarṣaṇa! I know that you two are personally superior to Māyā and Mahāviṣṇu.**

**Комментарий:**

Since his feelings for them as his sons is eclipsed by his conception of them as Brahman he speaks. O possessor of acintya-śakti (mahā- yogin)! I know the direct causes of the universe (asya sakṣāt) Kāraṇodaśayī and Māyā. I know you two who are superior to even them. Kṛṣṇa is Svayam Bhagavān. Balarāma is his second vyūha, Mahā-saṅkārṣaṇa. Kāṛaṇodaśayī is his svāṁśa and Māyā is his servant. This I know.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**You are the Supreme Lords, who manifest as the Lord of both nature and the creator of nature \[Mahā-Viṣṇu\]. Everything that comes into existence, however and whenever it does so, is created within you, by you, from you, for you and in relation to you.**

**Комментарий:**

You, the Parabrahman, endowed with prakṛti, jīva and kāla (time) śakti, are the ātmā of the whole universe. Whatever object like a pot (yat) exists in any place (yatra), by any cause (yena), from any source (yataḥ), in relation to anything (yasya), to be given to anything (yasmai), by any means (yathā), at any time (yadā), is you. It is not different from you who possess four śaktis . Some say that the universe is you since you pervade it. Singular is used since both of them are one. Prakṛti and other items are famous as your śakti.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**O transcendental Lord, from yourself you created this entire variegated universe, and then you entered within it in your personal form as the Supersoul. In this way, O unborn Supreme Soul, as the life force and consciousness of everyone, you maintain the creation.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover you are even the sustainer and nourisher of the universe. Entering the universe as antaryāmī (ātmanā), you maintain and nourish it in yourself and make it active as sūtrātmā (prāṇaḥ)and make it conscious as the conscious ātmā (jīvaḥ). By giving action and knowledge, you maintain and nourish the universe.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Whatever potencies the life air and other elements of universal creation exhibit are actually all personal energies of the Supreme Lord, for those energies are subordinate to him, because of similarity of the energy and its devatā. Thus everything active in the material world is set into motion by the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

“Since it is understood that various śaktis like prāṇa are the cause of the universe, how is it that the Supreme Lord is the cause?” Expecting this question, he answers saying that prāṇa and other śaktis are also under the control of the Lord. The śaktis of sūtra (prāṇaḥ), etc., which create the universe belong to the Supreme Lord, since they are dependent on him. Just as the power to pierce is not in the arrow but in the person who shoots the arrow. “Prāṇa, etc., depend upon their presiding devatās not on the Lord.” They are the same (sādṛśyāt). Both prāṇa and the devatās are equal being material. They are both dependent on the Lord who is conscious. Thus they are śaktis of the Lord. “But if prāṇa, etc., are devoid of śakti how can they perform actions?” Only the action belongs to active things but the śakti does not. For instance, arrows have speed because of the śakti of the human who shoots the arrow. Grass moves by the śakti of air.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**The glow of the moon, the power of fire, the radiance of the sun, the existence of twinkling of the stars, the permanence of mountains and the aroma and sustaining power of the earth—all these are actually you.**

**Комментарий:**

The śakti of all objects belong to you. The glow of the moon, the power of fire, the radiance of the sun, the existence of twinkling (sattā) of the stars, are actually (arthataḥ) your śaktis. The sun does not shine in the spiritual sky. Nor the moon or the stars. Lightning does not flash, what to speak of fire. Everything shines following the Lord who shines. By his light everything shines. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) The splendor of the sun, which dissipates the darkness of this whole world, comes from me. And the splendor of the moon and the splendor of fire are also from me. (BG [15.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.12)) The steadiness of mountains and the fragrance and functions of earth to support living beings (vṛttiḥ) are your śakti (bhavān).

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, you are water, and also its taste and its capacities to quench thirst and sustain life. You exhibit your potencies through the manifestations of the air as bodily warmth, vitality, mental power, physical strength, endeavor and movement.**

**Комментарий:**

The natural quality of object and objects are you alone. This is expressed in four verses. O Lord! The quality of water to give satisfaction (tarpaṇam) and cause life (prāṇanam) is you. Water (tāś) and its taste (tad-rasaḥ) are you alone. Ojas, saha, etc., of air is all your śakti since that is the way the verse begins.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Because you are the shelter of everything, you are the directions and their accommodating capacity, the all-pervading ether and the elemental sound residing within it. You are the primeval, unmanifested form of sound; the first syllable, oṁ; and audible speech, by which sound, as words, acquires particular references.**

**Комментарий:**

You are the space of the directions, regions of ether which are unlimited, by which living beings exist and move. You are the directions. You are general ether and its shelter. You are the śabdatan-mātrā (sphoṭa) or vāk, parā sound. You are paśyantī and madhyamā (nādaḥ). You are the syllables and oṁ-kāra. You are from whom come the names (pṛthak-kṛtiḥ) of objects (ākṛtīnām). This is vaikharī. This is described: vaktre vaikary atha rurudiṣor asya jantoḥ suṣumnābaddhas tasmād bhavati pavana-prerito varṇa-saṅghaḥ What arises from mūlādhara first is called parā. Later it becomes paśyantī at the heart and madhyamā in combination with buddhi. At the mouth it becomes vaikharī for the living entity that desires to speak, being checked by the suṣumnā. Then it becomes combinations of varṇas pushed by air. (Prapañca-sāra-tantra 2.43)

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**You are the power of the senses to reveal their objects, the senses’ presiding devatās, and the place where these devatās reside or sensory activity. You are the capacity of the intelligence for decision-making, and the living being’s ability to remember things, ordinary objects and the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

You are the śakti (indriyam) for manifesting sense objects for the senses (indriyānām). The word indriyam emphasizes verbal action. You are the presiding deities of the senses such as Sūrya. You are the śakti of the seat of the senses (anugrahaḥ). You are the śakti of ascertaining (avabodhaḥ) of intelligence. You are the śakti of investigation related to the jīva concerning ordinary topics (anusmṛtiḥ) and spiritual topics (satī).

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**You are false ego in the mode of ignorance, which is the source of the physical elements; false ego in the mode of passion, which is the source of the bodily senses; false ego in the mode of goodness, which is the source of the devatās; and the unmanifest, total material energy, when the living entities merge into prakṛti.**

**Комментарий:**

You are the cause of the elements such as ether (bhūtānām): bhūtādi or ahaṅkāra in tamas. You are the cause of the ten senses: taijasa or ahaṅkāra in rajas. You are the cause of the devatās (vikalpānām): vaikāra or ahaṅkāra in sattva. Vikalpā means the devatās according to the etymology that they are conceived variously. You are the cause of jīva’s saṁsāra: the three guṇas and pradhāna.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**You are the one indestructible entity among all the destructible things of this world, like the underlying substance that is seen to remain unchanged while the things made from it undergo transformations.**

**Комментарий:**

Since moon’s glow (verse 7) and other objects are not different from the possessor of all the śaktis and all high and low beings are pervaded by him, he is nondifferent from them. But in his svarūpa he is different. To make this clear, their opposite nature is described. Among all destructible objects you are the indestructible Brahman. Just as among the temporary effects such as a clay pot, the five elements which are indestructible, are discerned.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**The modes of material nature—namely goodness, passion and ignorance—together with all their functions, become directly manifest within you, the Supreme Absolute Truth, by the arrangement of your yogamāyā.**

**Комментарий:**

In order to establish that the Lord is permanent, temporary objects are described as being dependent upon him. The three guṇas and their transformations like mahat-tattva (tad-vṛttayaḥ) are made (kalpitāḥ) by your acintya śakti in you, the shelter, directly Parabrahman. Here kalpitā means “created” (and not “capable”) since the śruti says: The creator made the sun and moon as he did previously. (Ṛg Veda 10.190.3)

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**At the time of pralaya when all these effects are dissolved they no longer exist and you do not exist in them. During creation, you remain as the producer of material existence.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord is not touched by the guṇas and their transformations. Because you have acintya-śakti, supreme powers (tasmāt), when these transformations —sattva, etc., (amī bhāvāḥ) are created in you at the time of creation, they do not touch you (santi). You, their creator by your will alone, are not in those transformations. You are not touched by them. The supreme Lord, by his mind, controls earth, antarikṣa and heaven and remains in control. (Mahābhārata) At other times, at the time of destruction, even by your will you do not bring about those activities, but exist in your eternal abode. Thus you are indestructible.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**They are truly ignorant who, while imprisoned within the ceaseless flow of this world’s material qualities, fail to know you, the Supreme Soul of all that be, as their ultimate, sublime destination. Because of their ignorance, the entanglement of material work forces such souls to wander in the cycle of birth and death.**

**Комментарий:**

Due to ignorance of you who have such nature, the jīvas continue in saṁsāra. The jīvas fallen in the flow of guṇas are ignorant of the fine goal of the ātmā of all beings, i.e. they are ignorant of you. Due to kāmyakarmas and niṣiddha karmas functioning through ignorance, they wander in saṁsāra.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**By good fortune a soul may obtain a healthy human life—an opportunity rarely achieved. But if he is nonetheless deluded about what is best for him, O Lord, your illusory māyā will cause him to waste his entire life.**

**Комментарий:**

This knowledge is attained in human birth by association with devotees. He who does not attain it laments. Sukalpām means birth suitable for achieving the highest goal.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**You keep this whole world bound up by the ropes of affection, and thus when people consider their material bodies, they think, “This is me,” and when they consider their progeny and other relations, they think, “These are mine.”**

**Комментарий:**

You bind up those who are devoid of devotee association, who are averse to you. You bind up the whole world with ropes of affection for the body and its connections such as sons (anvayādiṣu) with thoughts of I and mine. You also liberate the jīvas from the ropes of saṁsāra by ropes of affection for the Lord. kaivalyadaḥ paraṁ brahma viṣṇur eva sanātanaḥ Eternal Viṣṇu, the Supreme Brahman, is the giver of liberation. (Skanda Purāṇa)

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**You are not our sons but the very Lords of both material nature and its creator \[Mahā-Viṣṇu\]. As you yourself have told us, you have descended to rid the earth of the rulers who are a heavy burden upon her.**

**Комментарий:**

He speaks because of the disappearance of affection for Kṛṣṇa as a son by the momentary appearance of his great power. The plural is used instead of the dual: you are not our (naḥ) sons. This is according to the rule asmado dvayośca. (Pāṇini 1.2.59) You said this at the time of your birth. Present tense is used even to indicate past which is close to present.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Therefore, O friend of the distressed, I now approach your lotus feet for shelter—the same lotus feet that dispel all fear of worldly existence for those who have surrendered to them. Enough! Enough with hankering for sense enjoyment, which makes me identify with this mortal body and think of you, the Supreme, as my child.**

**Комментарий:**

Though he is eternally honored as a father, because of the surge of knowledge of the Lord’s powers, the affection as a father reduces. Thus thinking himself a servant of the Lord, he surrenders to him, praying to him for benefit of the world. Because you cause bondage of the world, I surrender to your lotus feet for destroying that bondage.“Since I cause bondage, how can I involve in liberation?” You destroy fear of saṁsāra for those who have surrendered. You have such power. “The world has not surrendered but you pray for that.” O friend of those suffering! One should not worry about this since you are naturally merciful. Make the world surrender and cut their bondage. “I will destroy that bondage since you pray like Prahlāda. But you are my father. Experience the wealth of a kingdom such as elephants, horses, etc. Why be humble?” Enough with greed for enjoyment! Since from that enjoyment I will become absorbed in the bodies of elephants, etc., as things to be enjoyed. May I not think of you, the Paramātmā (pare), as my son, considering, “this (wealth of kingdom) is given by my son,” and may I not have desire for enjoying that since I am your servant. Make me think of you as my master. Create auspiciousness for the world.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Indeed, while still in the maternity room you told us that you, the unborn Lord, had already been born several times as our son in previous ages. After manifesting each of these bodies to protect your own nature, you then made them unmanifest, unaffected like the sky. O supremely glorified, all-pervading Lord, who can understand your material māyā?**

**Комментарий:**

“If you criticize considering me as your son, then how do you consider me your son?” In the maternity room you spoke to us. “What did I say?” I was born to three couples (anu-yugam), to Sutapā and Pṛśni, to Kaśyapa and Aditi and to Vasudeva and Devakī. Yugam can mean couple according to Amara-kośa. From you three couples, I, without material body and senses, having unfailing knowledge and power, appeared to protect your bhakti (nija-dharma-guptyai). You said this. Though obtaining you as my son is difficult yet I think like this (that you are my son) on the authority of your statement. “Just because I entered your body, you say that I am your son. But I cannot be your son by just that. Otherwise since it is heard that I spread in bodies of all jīvas. I must be everyone’s son. Tat sṛṣṭvā tad evānuprāviṣat: having created the world he entered it. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)” You enter the various bodies of the jīvas and regulate them, but like the sky you remain unattached. When the bodies are destroyed you give them up. O glorified Lord (urugāya)! Who will give regard to māyā, composed of a small portion of the power of you, the Lord (bhūmnaḥ)? The statements of the learned that your entrance into us (your parents) is praised by Brahmā and others, and that you are respected is the proof. But due to my lack of qualification, it becomes impossible to comprehend.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having heard his father’s words, the Supreme Lord, leader of the Sātvatas, replied in a gentle voice as he bowed his head in humility and smiled.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord born to the Yadus (sātvata-rṣabhaḥ), heard Vasudeva’s words indicating the Lord’s supreme powers and served by ascetic sages, whom Kṛṣṇa accepted as a father, beyond the scope of Brahmā’s desires, and smiled. After I killed Kaṁsa, I increased their prema as parents but they have not given up seeing me with great power, which is very crude. Attracting his father, he bowed in humility and spoke words which gave rise to his appropriate bhāva.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear father, I consider your statements appropriate, since you have explained the greatness of the Lord in reference to us, your sons.**

**Комментарий:**

He praises his father’s words. O father! I greatly (upa) respect your words, full of correct meaning. You have described all truth concerning the vibhūtis of the Lord, making us, your sons, the object of that description. It is true that we are the Supreme Lords and thus appropriate objects of those descriptions. But we are also your sons. Not considering that, you should treat us, though the Supreme Lords, as your sons.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Not only I, but also you, along with my respected brother and these residents of Dvārakā, should all be considered in this same philosophical light, O best of the Yadus. Indeed, we should include all that exists, both moving and nonmoving.**

**Комментарий:**

Moreover O best of the Yadus! Just as you consider me and Balarāma to be eternal, all you Yādavas, residents of Dvārakā, all my associates, even the dealer in shells and betel nut maker, the animals and birds, creepers and shrubs, should be considered eternal.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**The supreme spirit, Paramātmā, is indeed one. He is self-luminous and eternal, transcendental and devoid of material qualities. But Paramātmā manifests as many among the various bodies by the guṇas arising from the Lord’s māyā-śakti.**

**Комментарий:**

One should not at all doubt that the residents of Dvārakā, jīvas who are my associates, are equal to me since even jīvas situated in saṁsāra are equal to me. This is expressed in two verses. The jīva (ātmā) is fixed (ekaḥ), has a svarūpa of consciousness (svayaṁ jyotiḥ), himself revealing to himself. He is eternal, without destruction. He is different from his two bodies (anyaḥ). He is endowed with definitive (niścita) eight qualities (nirguṇaḥ). He goes into various bodies of devatā and human by karmas related to sattva and other guṇas (ātmā-sṛṣṭaiḥ) and is perceived as devatā, etc. Though going to various births by karma, the jīva is actually full of consciousness, is endowed with eight qualities such as apahatapāpma. Thus, he is equal to me.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**The elements of ether, air, fire, water and earth become visible, invisible, minute or extensive as they manifest in various objects. Similarly, the Paramātmā, though one, appears to become many.**

**Комментарий:**

Variety in jīva takes place by variety in upādhis. Just as elements like ether, etc., entering the bodies (tat-krṭeṣu), produce variety, not exceeding the stock of karmas, the jīva also develops variety by identifying with various bodies such as devatā or human. In liberation (āvis) and in destruction (tiro), as a fly, etc., (alpa) or as a devatā, etc.,(bhūri) the jīva though one in svarūpa, but by karma in ignorance takes many forms. Actually, the jīva is equal to me being endowed with eight qualities and having the nature of consciousness and bliss. Thus, he is my friend. Dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāya: there are two birds together as friends. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad)

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, hearing these instructions spoken to him by the Supreme Lord, Vasudeva became freed from all ideas of grandeur spoken by the sages. With prema for Kṛṣṇa, he remained silent.**

**Комментарий:**

After hearing instructions of the Lord,Vasudeva’s conception that Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were the Supreme Lord and that he was their servant and that he was not eligible to be their father, was destroyed. Thinking of himself as their father, he became satisfied.

### Text 27-28

**Перевод:**

**At that time, O best of the Kurus, the universally worshipped Devakī took the opportunity to address her two sons, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. Previously she had heard with astonishment that they had brought their spiritual master’s son back from death. Now, thinking of her own sons who had been murdered by Kaṁsa, she felt great sorrow, and thus with tear-filled eyes she beseeched Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.**

**Комментарий:**

Having eliminated his father’s rough knowledge of the Lord’s power which was contrary to seeing the Lord as his son, he eliminated even his mother’s perception of considering others as her sons. To introduce this, he starts a new topic with the word atha. Devakī is the devatā of everyone (sarva-devatā) because she was the mother of the Lord and has a spiritual form since she is glorified in Viṣṇu Purāṇa, tvaṁ parā prakṛtiḥ sūkṣmā: you are the superior prakrṭi. This pastime occurs for producing joy in the Lord’s pastimes. It arose by the Lord’s will since it will later be said mohitā māyayā viṣṇoḥ: she was bewildered by the Lord’s yoga-māyā. (SB [10.85.54](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/85.54))

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Devakī said: O Rāma, Rāma, immeasurable Supreme Soul! O Kṛṣṇa, Lord of all masters of yoga! I know that you are the ultimate rulers of all universal creators, the primeval Lords.**

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Taking birth from me, you have now descended to this world in order to kill those kings whose good qualities have been destroyed by the present age, and who thus defy the authority of revealed scriptures and burden the earth.**

**Комментарий:**
