You have appeared in me to destroy the kings whose good qualities were destroyed by time. O original Lord (ādya)!

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**O source of the universe! The creation, maintenance and destruction of the universe are all carried out by a fraction of an expansion of an expansion of your expansion. Today I have come to take shelter of you, the Supreme Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

Having praised both of them individually, she surrenders taking them both as one person so that they both agree. The creation and destruction of the universe takes place by portion of the guṇas such as rajas which are a portion of prakṛti, which is a portion of Kāraṇodaśayī, who is your portion. Now I surrender to you, making a request.

### Text 32-33

**Перевод:**

**It is said that when your spiritual master ordered you to retrieve his long-dead son, you brought him back from the forefathers’ abode as a token of remuneration for your guru’s mercy. Please fulfill my desire in the same way, O supreme masters of all yoga masters. Please bring back my sons who were killed by the king of Bhoja, so that I may see them once again.**

**Комментарий:**

You brought back the guru’s son from Yama’s abode (pitṛ-sthānāt) as guru-dakṣiṇā to please the guru (gurave).

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**The sage Śukadeva said: Thus entreated by their mother, O Bhārata, Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa employed their mystic yogamāyā potency and entered the region of Sutala.**

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**When the king of the Daityas, Bali Mahārāja, noticed the arrival of the two Lords, his heart overflowed with joy, since he knew them to be the Supreme Soul and worshippable deity of the entire universe, and especially of himself. He immediately stood up and then bowed down to offer respects, along with his entire entourage.**

**Комментарий:**

He saw the Lord the ātmā of the universe (viśvātma-daivam). Singular (daivam) is used since Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma are seen as one. Sānvayaḥ means with his family.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Bali took pleasure in offering them elevated seats. After they sat down, he washed the feet of the two Supreme Lords. Then he took that water, which purifies the whole world even up to Brahmā, and poured it upon himself and his followers.**

**Комментарий:**

With his associates (sa-vṛndaḥ) he put on his head the water which purifies (punat) the world including Brahmā.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**He worshipped them with all the riches at his disposal—priceless clothing, ornaments, fragrant sandalwood paste, betel nut, lamps, sumptuous food and so on. Thus he offered them all his family’s wealth, and also his own self.**

**Комментарий:**

Previously he had offered everything toVāmana, representing a sea and now he offered everything to Svayam Bhagavān, Kṛṣṇa representing an ocean. Due to this difference his offering again is not a fault. Vāmana, who had stood at the door, had entered into Kṛṣṇa. Thus Bali did not see him separately at that time.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Taking hold of the Lords’ lotus feet again and again, Bali, the conqueror of Indra’s army, spoke from his heart, which was melting out of his intense love. O King, as tears of ecstasy filled his eyes and the hair on his limbs stood on end, he began to speak with faltering words.**

**Комментарий:**

Indrasena means Bali, who was victorious over Indra. The etymology is ‘he whose army (senā)is (victorious) on Indra.’ His heart was soft due to prema (prema-vibhinnayā).

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**King Bali said: Obeisances to the great Ananta, to Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, the creator of the universe, the goal of jñāna and yoga, who is thus Brahman and Paramātmā.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to Saṅkarṣaṇa, who is the aṁśī of even Śeṣa (bṛhate’nantāya). I offer respects to Kṛṣṇa, Svayam Bhagavān, the doer of everything (vedhase), who distributes knowledge of cause and effect (sāṅkhya) and aṣṭāṅga-yoga the cause of realizing the truth about self and others. I offer respects to Brahman, the Lord possessing great qualities, since the śruti says: bṛhanto hy asminguṇā: the Lord is he who has great qualities. (quoted by Madhva) I offer respects to the supreme ātmā, lord of Lakṣmī, full of bliss and consciousness.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**Seeing you Lords is a rare achievement for most living beings. But even persons like us, situated in the modes of passion and ignorance, can easily see you when you reveal yourself by your own sweet will.**

**Комментарий:**

Hi means certainly. Ca means api. Thus, the verse means “Certainly seeing you two, though difficult to achieve for demons, is also not difficult to achieve since you both mercifully let us see you.” yasya prasādaṁ kurute sa vai taṁ draṣṭum arhati The person to whom the lord gives mercy can see the Lord. (Mahābhārata)

### Text 41-43

**Перевод:**

**Many who had been constantly absorbed in enmity toward you ultimately became attracted to you, who are the supervisor of goodness and the source of scriptures. These reformed enemies include Daityas, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Cāraṇas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Piśācas, Bhūtas, Pramathas and Nāyakas, and also ourselves and many others like us. Some of us have become attracted to you because of exceptional hatred, while others have become attracted because of mixed bhakti. But the devatās are not attracted to you in this way.**

**Комментарий:**

The devatās are qualified to see you since they are fixed in sattva but not the demons, including me who are fixed in rajas and tamas. This is expressed in three verses. The demons and others have continual enmity to you, who have a form of consciousness and bliss as defined in bhakti scriptures (śāstra-śarīriṇi). Sātvata-śāstra-vigraham: the Lord has a body as described in devotional scriptures. (SB [6.16.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/16.33)) The Gandharvas, Siddhas, Vidyādharas and Cāraṇas, are some followers of the demons since those who follow the devatās do not have enmity toward the Lord. Your abode, Vaikuṇṭha is pure sattva (viśuddha-sattva-dhāmni). The reason for their enmity is given. Some, endowed with intense hatred and others endowed with bhakti mixed with material desires (kāmataḥ), such as Gandharvas and others. But they do not have affection for you who has such a body. The devatās are not like this since they are joyful with sattva. They are attracted to you and are qualified to see you.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**What to speak of ourselves, O Lord of all perfect yogīs, even the greatest mystics do not know your spiritual powers.**

**Комментарий:**

Yet who can know the cause of us seeing you? Persons like the Kumāras do not generally know your acintya-śakti (yoga-māyām) in its svarūpa (idam) and in this way (ittham) what to speak of us knowing. Bali spoke in this way only out of humility since he is the best of devotees.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Please be merciful to me so I may get out of the blind well of family life—my false home—and find the true shelter of your lotus feet, which selfless sages always seek. Then, taking the nature of your servant, having attained your lotus feet, I will leave my followers and wander in the company of devotees, who are the friends of everyone.**

**Комментарий:**

The cause of letting unqualified people see you is the acintyaśakti, characterized by mercy, engaged in glancing at the devotees, which is present in you. Because of this (tataḥ), be pleased with us, though we are unqualified and fulfill our desire. What is that desire? Rejecting the dark well of family life which is different from the shelter–your lotus feet, which are sought by those who have no material desires (nirapekṣa), and obtaining a living through naturally fallen fruits, etc., at your lotus feet which are the roots of the benefactors of the whole universe (viśva-śaraṇa) who are the tree and having given up enmity with the devatās (śāntaḥ), renouncing dependents (ekaḥ), I will wander with devotees, who are friends to the whole world.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**O Lord of all subordinate creatures, please tell us what to do and thus free us of all sin. Even one who faithfully executes the rules of the Vedas is free of sin.**

**Комментарий:**

Please tell me why you have shown yourself to me today in this way. O master of all us jīvas (īśitavyeśa)! “You are qualified to accomplish my goal.” Make us sinless: destroy the obstacles which are opposed to that qualification. Since a person who follows your orders in the form of the Vedas, what to speak of directly following your orders with faith, becomes free of following the rules (codanāyāḥ). He does not become a servant of rules.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: During the age of the first Manu, the sage Marīci had six sons by his wife Ūrṇā. They were all exalted devatās, but once they laughed at Brahmā when they saw him preparing to have sex with his own daughter.**

**Комментарий:**

Agreeing to his request, the Lord states his reason for coming in five verses. In Svāyambhuva manvantara, Marīci’s six sons were born to his wife. Those six devatās laughed at Brahmā when he tried to approach his daughter Sarasvatī for union.

### Text 48-49

**Перевод:**

**Because of that improper act, they immediately entered a demoniac form of life, and thus they took birth as sons of Hiraṇyakaśipu. The goddess Yogamāyā then took them away from Hiraṇyakaśipu, and they were born again from Devakī’s womb. After this, O King, Kaṁsa murdered them. Devakī still laments for them, thinking of them as her sons. These same sons of Marīci are now living here with you.**

**Комментарий:**

By the sin of laughing at him, they immediately took birth from Hiraṇyakaśipu in the wife of Kālameni (his son). O King Bali! They were placed in Devakī’s womb by Yogamāyā to be killed by Kaṁsa. Pointing his forefinger, he indicates “These (ime) are those sons.” They had been placed in his vision by Bali, best of devotees so that the Lord would see them.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**We wish to take them from this place to dispel their mother’s sorrow. Then, released from their curse and free from all suffering, they will return to their home in heaven.**

**Комментарий:**

Freed from the curse after my taking them, they will go to Devaloka (Svarga and higher) since they still have desires for enjoyment.

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**By my grace these six—Smara, Udgītha, Pariṣvaṅga, Pataṅga, Kṣudrabhṛt and Ghṛṇī—will return to my eternal abode.**

**Комментарий:**

He gives the names they had when they were the sons of Marīci. Smara and Udgītha should be separated as names. They will later (punaḥ) attain the destination of the Yādavas (sad-gatim), the concealed Dvārakā.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**After saying this, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, having been duly worshipped by Bali Mahārāja, took the six sons and returned to Dvārakā, where they presented them to their mother.**

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**When she saw her lost children, Devakī felt such affection for them that milk flowed from her breasts. She embraced them and took them onto her lap, smelling their heads again and again.**

**Комментарий:**

By the will of the Lord, to please his mother, the sons took on their infant forms.

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**Lovingly she let her sons drink from her breast, which became wet with milk touched by Kṛṣṇa. She was entranced by the Lord’s yoga-māyā, by which the Lord’s associates are made to appear in the world.**

**Комментарий:**

Her breasts were abundantly flowing with milk which had been touched by Kṛṣṇa and other sons. She was bewildered by yogamāyā, by which those associates involved in the pastimes are made to appear in this world.

### Text 55-56

**Перевод:**

**After drinking her nectarean milk, the remnants of what Kṛṣṇa himself had previously drunk, the six sons, touched by the hand of Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of all beings, attained their original identities. They bowed down to Govinda, Devakī, their father and Balarāma, and then, as everyone looked on, they left for the abode of the devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

The sons drank the milk which was the remnants of what Kṛṣṇa had drunk, by the will of the mother and the Lord since he had drunk it. Though the sons were fully grown up, some were seen sucking their mother’s breast during marriage ceremonies. They became aware that they were devatās (pratilabdhātma-darśanāḥ).

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**Seeing her sons return from death and then depart again, saintly Devakī was struck with wonder, O King. She concluded that this was all simply an illusion created by Kṛṣṇa.**

**Комментарий:**

She considered that their coming and then going was produced by Kṛṣṇa’s māyā. She considered their coming from and going away to have been effected by Kṛṣṇa in order to achieve purposes like cheating Kaṁsa. She thus gave up her semblance of affection for them and continued to have firm affection for Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 58

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa, the source of all things, the Lord of unlimited valor, performed countless pastimes just as amazing as this one, O descendant of Bhārata.**

**Комментарий:**

He reveals unlimited pastimes since Nārada witnessed in that way.

### Text 59

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: This pastime enacted by Murāri, whose fame is blissful, totally destroys the sins of the universe and serves as the eternal ornament for his devotees’ ears. Anyone who constantly hears or narrates this pastime, as recounted by the venerable son of Vyāsa, will be able to fix his mind in meditation on the Supreme Lord and attain auspicious Dvārakā. It is the excellent ear ornament of the devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva summarizes. This pastime of Kṛṣṇa whose fame is sweet, described by the son of Vyāsa, my guru because it has such fame, destroys completely the disease of contamination of saṁsāra. The person whose mindconcentrates on the Lord by this story attains the Lord’s place devoid of fear (tat-kṣema-dhāma). But for the devotees who have crossed saṁsāra, it is the excellent ear ornament (sat-karṇa-pūram) and always relishable.

## Chapter 86 - Arjuna Kidnaps Subhadrā and Kṛṣṇa Blesses His Devotees

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: O brāhmaṇa, we would like to learn how Arjuna married Balarāma’s and Kṛṣṇa’s sister, who was my grandmother.**

**Комментарий:**

In the eighty-sixth chapter Arjuna in disguise steals Subhadrā, and Kṛṣṇa goes to Mithila to see his devotees—the brāhmaṇa and the king. Marriages from Balarāma to Aniruddha were described by Śukadeva but not Subhadra’s. Thus Parīkṣit asks about this. Vijayaḥ is Arjuna. Subhadrā is my grandmother. Thus I must hear about her marriage.

### Text 2-3

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: While traveling far and wide visiting various holy places of pilgrimage, Arjuna came to Prabhāsa. There he heard that Balarāma intended to give his maternal cousin Subhadrā to Duryodhana in marriage, and that no one else approved of this plan. Arjuna wanted to marry her himself, so he disguised himself as a renunciant, complete with triple staff, and went to Dvārakā.**

**Комментарий:**

He heard that Balarāma will give Subhadrā, his maternal cousin, to Duryodhana. But others, such as Vasudeva and Kṛṣṇa, did not want to give to him. He disguised himself as a sannyāsī, with a tridaṇḍa to fool Balarāma by this worshippable dress.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**He stayed there during the monsoon months to fulfill his purpose. Balarāma and the other residents of the city, not recognizing him, offered him all honor and hospitality.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma did not recognize him since by Kṛṣṇa’s will his omniscience was covered.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**One day Balarāma brought him to his home as his invited dinner guest, and Arjuna ate the food Balarāma respectfully offered him.**

**Комментарий:**

One day at the end of cāturmāsya, Balarāṁa invited him and brought him home. He ate the food offered by Balarāma.

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**There he saw the wonderful maiden Subhadrā, who was enchanting to heroes. His eyes opened wide with delight, and his mind became agitated and absorbed in thoughts of her.**

**Комментарий:**

Arjuna (saḥ) saw Subhadrā (kanyām).

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**Arjuna was very attractive to women, and as soon as Subhadrā saw him, she wanted to have him as her husband. Smiling bashfully with sidelong glances, she fixed her heart and eyes upon him.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing him she understood that he was not a sannyāsī but Arjuna who wore the dress of a sannyāsī in order to obtain her. Smiling, she desired him as her husband.

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**Meditating only on her and waiting for the opportunity to take her away, Arjuna had no peace. His heart trembled with passionate desire.**

**Комментарий:**

He waited for an opportunity to kidnap her (antaram). He obtained no happiness (śam) with his heart agitated by strong amorous desire.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**Once, on the occasion of a great temple festival in honor of the Supreme Lord, Subhadrā rode out of the fortress like palace on a chariot, and at that time the mighty chariot warrior Arjuna took the opportunity to kidnap her. Subhadrā’s parents and Kṛṣṇa had sanctioned this.**

**Комментарий:**

This was a festival where Lord Viṣṇu, who has risen at the end of cāturmāsya, is carried on a chariot. The reason for stealing her was the permission of Kṛṣṇa and her parents who were persuaded by Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa placed her on his own chariot so she could give him the chariot and other equipments (for fighting). “But stealing her from amidst the Yadu members would be difficult!” He was the best of warriors (mahā-rathaḥ) since he was the dear friend of Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Standing on his chariot, Arjuna took up his bow and drove off the valiant fighters and palace guards who tried to block his way. As her relatives shouted in anger, he took Subhadrā away just as a lion takes his share.**

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**When he heard of Subhadrā’s kidnapping, Balarāma became as disturbed as the ocean during the full moon, but Kṛṣṇa respectfully took hold of his feet and, together with other family members, pacified him by explaining the matter.**

**Комментарий:**

Balarāma became pleased by sweet words (anvaśāmyata).

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Balarāma then happily sent the bride and groom very valuable wedding gifts as well as elephants, chariots, horses and male and female servants.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding the permission of her parents, turning back due to affection for her, arranging Subhadrā’s marriage with Arjuna, Balarāma sent gifts pleasing to the bride and groom. He sent most valuable colorful cots and other things.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: There was a devotee of Kṛṣṇa’s known as Śrutadeva, who was a first-class brāhmaṇa. Perfectly satisfied by rendering unalloyed devotional service to Kṛṣṇa, he was peaceful, learned and free from sense gratification.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva narrates a special pastime of Kṛṣṇa which attracts the heart by being filled with direct mercy to devotees and by involving himself, though it is not unasked. Since new topic is introduced, it is not a fault to repeat the words “Śukadeva said.” There was a devotee who took Kṛṣṇa as his master.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**Living as a religious householder in the city of Mithilā, within the kingdom of Videha, he managed to fulfill his obligations while maintaining himself with whatever sustenance easily came his way.**

**Комментарий:**

As a householder he lived in Mithilā city of Videha province. He served Kṛṣṇa (nija-kriyaḥ) with whatever enjoyables came without endeavor.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**By the will of the Lord he obtained each day just what he needed for his maintenance, and no more. Satisfied with this much, he properly executed his religious duties.**

**Комментарий:**

That was also agreeable to Kṛṣṇa. He obtained what he needed because of Kṛṣṇa (daivāt). Yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham: I maintain what the devotee has and supply what he lacks. (BG [9.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.22)) He obtained as much as was necessary for maintaining himself and his family. Uta means that there was never a lack. Satisfied with that much, he performed his duties which were conforming to bhakti (yathocitāḥ). He did not accept extra. The person with wisdom concerning material objects accepts as much as is necessary for surviving. By accepting more or less than that, the person will fail to attain the highest goal. (BRS [1.2.108](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.2.108))

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Similarly free from false ego was the ruler of that kingdom, my dear Parīkṣit, a descendant of the Mithila dynasty named Bahulāśva. Both these devotees were very dear to Acyuta.**

**Комментарий:**

The protector of that province (maithilaḥ), the king, was equal to the brāhmaṇa by his devotion to Kṛṣṇa. He did not have the pride of thinking himself a king (niraham-mānaḥ). Thus without distinction, they were both dear to the Lord.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Pleased with both of them, the Supreme Lord mounted his chariot, which Dāruka had brought, and traveled to Videha with a group of sages.**

**Комментарий:**

The phrase tayoḥ prasanno, “satisfied with both of them” implies that both King Bahulāśva and the brāhmaṇa Śrutadeva could not come to Dvārakā to see Kṛṣṇa because they were duty bound to serve the Lord’s deities. Therefore, Kṛṣṇa bound by their love, pleased with the two, was anxious to let them see him. Understanding that the sages would become fatigued, Kṛṣṇa forcibly placed them on his chariot and then sped off to Mithilā, though they were unwilling to do so.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Among these sages were Nārada, Vāmadeva, Atri, Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana Vyāsa, Paraśurāma, Asita, Aruṇi, myself, Bṛhaspati, Kaṇva, Maitreya and Cyavana.**

**Комментарий:**

The sages are listed by name. Kṛṣṇa means Vyāsa. Rāma means Paraśurāma. Aham refers to Śukadeva.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**In every city and town the Lord passed along the way, O King, the people came forward to worship him with offerings of arghya water in their hands, as if to worship the sun which had risen and was surrounded by planets.**

**Комментарий:**

He was like the sun rising with the planets. This is simile implying an impossibility (abhūtopamā), since one does not see the planets when the sun is rising.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**The men and women of Ānarta, Dhanva, Kuru-jāṅgala, Kaṅka, Matsya, Pañcāla, Kunti, Madhu, Kekaya, Kośala, Arṇa and many other kingdoms drank with their eyes the nectarean beauty of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus face, which was graced with generous smiles and affectionate glances.**

**Комментарий:**

The provinces, listed in order when travelling from Dvārakā to Videha, were close to the path. Others were far from the path. Men and women far from the path came running in those places. They saw his lotus face with extreme attraction.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Simply by glancing at those who came to see him, Kṛṣṇa, the spiritual master of the three worlds, delivered them from the blindness of materialism. As he thus endowed them with fearlessness and spiritual vision, he heard devatās and men singing his glories, which purify the entire universe and destroy all misfortune. Eventually, he reached Videha.**

**Комментарий:**

“Since Kṛṣṇa is a form of Brahman how could they see him, while he was turned away, with their material eyes? How could they follow the chariot which went as fast as the wind?” Tebhyaḥ (to them) indicates both men and women by the sūtra: pumān striyā (Pāṇini 1.2.67). He gave the realization of the highest spiritual object (artha-dṛśam) and bhakti-yoga by which his sweetness is perceived (kṣemam) to them who had eyes in which ignorance was destroyed by his glance of mercy. Bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś cāsmi yadṛṣaḥ: one knows me by bhakti as I am. (BG [18.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.55)) Hearing his glories which purify the ends of the directions sung by the devatās in the sky, and by humans who were meeting, he went to Videha slowly, since he was delayed by sweet talks with them.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Hearing that Acyuta had arrived, O King, the residents of the cities and villages of Videha joyfully came forth to receive him with offerings in their hands.**

**Комментарий:**

They approached him from front (abhīyuḥ).

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**As soon as the people saw Uttamaḥśloka, their faces and hearts blossomed with affection. Joining their palms above their heads, they bowed down to the Lord and to the sages accompanying him, whom they had previously only heard about.**

**Комментарий:**

They placed their hands above their heads so that they could see his beautiful face. They bowed to the sages in the same way (tathā).

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Both the king of Mithilā and Śrutadeva fell at the Lord’s feet, each thinking that the spiritual master of the universe had come there just to show him mercy.**

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**At exactly the same time, King of Maithila and Śrutadeva each went forward with joined palms and invited the Lord of the Daśārhas to be his guest, along with the brāhmaṇa sages.**

**Комментарий:**

They both at the same time invited the Lord along with the sages to their houses.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**Wanting to please them both, the Lord accepted both their invitations. Thus he simultaneously went to both homes, and neither could see him entering the other’s house.**

**Комментарий:**

Understanding that both Śrutadeva and Bahulāśva wanted him to visit their homes first, Kṛṣṇa, by two manifestations, entered both houses without anyone seeing two forms, since in this way they would be pleased.

### Text 27-29

**Перевод:**

**When Lord Kṛṣṇa and the sages, who are out of reach of impious persons had come to his house, they were seated on seats brought out for them. After they were all comfortably seated, the wise king, a descendant of Janaka, his heart overflowing with joy and his eyes clouded by tears, bowed down to them and washed their feet with intense devotion. Taking the wash water, which could purify the entire world, he sprinkled it on his head and the heads of his family members. Then he worshipped all those great lords by offering them fragrant sandalwood paste, flower garlands, fine clothing and ornaments, incense, lamps, arghya and cows and bulls.**

**Комментарий:**

The reception of the king is described in nine verses. His eyes were moist with tears and his heart was joyful (uddharṣa). The word īśvarān, “great lords” refers not only to Kṛṣṇa but also to the exalted sages in his company who were equal to the Lord. Go-vṛṣa means bulls.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**When they had eaten to their full satisfaction, for their further pleasure the King began to speak slowly and in a gentle voice as he held Kṛṣṇa’s feet in his lap and happily massaged them.**

**Комментарий:**

After they were satisfied with food, pleasing them with words like, “I am most fortunate. I am most successful by your presence,” he spoke as follows.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Bahulāśva said: O almighty Lord, you are the soul of all created beings, their self-illumined witness, and now you are giving your audience to us, who constantly meditate on your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

You pervade all living beings (ātmā) and are the direct witness of all their actions. You have eternally perfect knowledge (svadṛk). Because of this (atha), you have become visible to us who remember your lotus feet in our houses, but who could not come to you because of worshipping your deity. You show affection for those surrendered to you.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**You have said, “Neither Ananta, Goddess Śrī nor unborn Brahmā is dearer to me than my unalloyed devotee.” To prove your own words true, you have now revealed yourself to our eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord’s name is satya-vak satya-saṅkalpaḥ: he who speaks the truth and he whose will comes true. (Nārada-pañcarātra) Because of being so, you have acted in this way. “Ananta as a brother, Lakṣmī as a wife, and Brahmā as a son are not dear but as my pure devotee are dear.” You have revealed yourself to make this statement true. Otherwise your coming this far away from Dvārakā to our country would not have occurred since there is no other purpose.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**What person who knows this truth would ever abandon your lotus feet, when you are ready to give your very self to peaceful sages who call nothing their own?**

**Комментарий:**

Evaṁ-vit means one who has such knowledge.

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Appearing in the Yadu dynasty, you have spread your glories, which can remove all the sins of the three worlds, just to deliver those entrapped in the cycle of birth and death.**

**Комментарий:**

Tac-chāntyai means for destroying saṁsāra.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Obeisances to you, Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, whose intelligence is ever unrestricted, who remain as Nārāyaṇa in Badrikāśrama. You reveal the Vedas, are full of bliss and perform kṣatriya dharma to benefit others.**

**Комментарий:**

The king praises Kṛṣṇa to make him stay in his home for a few days. The Lord has unrestricted knowledge (akuṇṭha-medhase): he knows my bhāva. In your expansion you are Nārāyaṇa in Badarīkāśrama, the sage who knows the Vedas. You should reside in my house and make this country auspicious, just as you stay in Badarīkāśrama, making Bhārata-varṣa auspicious. He speaks with humility thinking, “Since here the luxuries of Dvārakā are not present, it will be austere for the Lord.”

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Please stay a few days in our house, along with these brāhmaṇas, O all-pervading one, and with the dust of your feet sanctify this dynasty of Nimi.**

**Комментарий:**

He explains his intentions. Sametaḥ means “with”.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Thus invited by the king, the Supreme Lord, sustainer of the world, consented to stay for some time to bestow good fortune on the men and women of Mithilā.**

**Комментарий:**

Requested with insistence (upa-āmanitritaḥ), he stayed.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**Śrutadeva received Acyuta into his home with as much enthusiasm as that shown by King Bahulāśva. After bowing down to the Lord and the sages, Śrutadeva began to dance with great joy, waving his shawl.**

**Комментарий:**

Śrutadeva’s reception is described. By saying “like the king (janako yathā),” he extends the details of the king stated in verses beginning with pravṛddha-bhaktyā (verse 28) to the brāhmaṇa. Due to absorption in prema, Śrutadeva held his cloth and waved it above his head.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**After bringing mats of grass and darbha straw and seating his guests upon them, he greeted them with words of welcome. Then he and his wife washed their feet with great pleasure.**

**Комментарий:**

He offered seats. Bṛṣi means a grass seat. They were made of kuśa. He had Kṛṣṇa and others sit on new mats brought from within his house and neighbors’ house, and washed their feet personally. Avanije for avaninije is Vedic usage.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**With the wash water, the virtuous Śrutadeva copiously sprinkled himself, his house and his family. Overjoyed, he felt that all his desires had now been fulfilled.**

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**He worshipped them with offerings of auspicious items easily available to him, such as fruits, uśīra root, pure, nectarean water, fragrant clay, tulasī leaves, kuśa grass and lotus flowers. Then he offered them food that increases the mode of goodness.**

**Комментарий:**

He satisfied (ārādhayāmāsa) the Lord with worship (saparyayā) by offering auspicious gifts, etc. He offered auspicious gifts (phala), then articles of worship like arghya (arhaṇa), then uśīra root as incense, then he offered water as sweet as nectar, made by cooked and dried āmalakī fruit sprinkled one by one into every pot in order to sweeten the water. After they were relieved of fatigue, for the noon bath he offered them fragrant earth made by placing ketakī and other flowers with it for a long time in sealed new vessels. Then he offered tulasī, etc., for use during worship. He offered what was easily available. He offered pure rice (andhasā) which increases sattva. He also offered ācamana and other items.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**He wondered: How is it that I, fallen into the blind well of family life, have been able to meet Lord Kṛṣṇa? And how have I also been allowed to meet these great brāhmaṇas, who always carry the Lord within their hearts? The dust of their feet is the shelter of all holy places.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the Lord had come to his house with his exclusive devotees, Śrutadeva did not become proud, but due to realization that the Lord’s mercy is the cause, only humility arose in him. He deliberated, “For what reason have I met Kṛṣṇa and these brāhmaṇas such as Nārada within whose minds the form of Kṛṣṇa (asya ātmā) always appears?” Ā expresses remembrance and nu expresses astonishing. The cause is their mercy alone and not my good fortune. He concluded thus.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**When his guests were seated comfortably, having each received a proper welcome, Śrutadeva approached them and sat down nearby with his wife, children and other dependents. Then, while massaging Kṛṣṇa’s feet, he addressed Kṛṣṇa and the sages.**

**Комментарий:**

Śrutadeva was situated nearby with his wife, relatives and children who were his advisors. Massaging Kṛṣṇa’s feet gently, he spoke.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**Śrutadeva said: I have attained the audience of the Supreme Person not only today, but when you created this universe with your energies and then entered it with sandhinī śakti.**

**Комментарий:**

“O sage among the brāhmaṇas, Śrutadeva, due to puṇya I have met you today?” When Kṛṣṇa said this, Śrutadeva replied with extreme humility expressing his beginningless aversion to the Lord. O Supreme Lord, not only today did you get to see us but even from the beginning when by your sandhinī śakti you entered this universe, created by sattva, etc., (śaktibhiḥ).

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Just like a sleeping person who creates a separate world in his imagination and then enters his own dream and appears within it.**

**Комментарий:**

Creating the universe is just your pastime. You exert no effort in this work. Suggesting this he speaks. Just as a sleeping person, with his mind combined with the desire of the Lord (ātmā-māyayā) creates a different dream world full of chariots and horses and appears within it; in the same way, you, creating the universe by your will, exert no effort at all. Dreams are created by the Lord for it is said: sandhye sṛṣṭir āha hi The Lord creates objects in dreams because that is stated in the text. (Vedānta-sūtra) Thus you see us at all times but we, being averse, did not ever see you. But today you have let us see you by your causeless mercy.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**You reveal yourself within the hearts of those persons of pure consciousness who constantly hear about you, chant about you, worship you, glorify you and converse with one another about you.**

**Комментарий:**

“It is not rare for devotees to see me.” Even for those who discuss with devotees about you (samvadatām), etc., you manifest only in the hearts. But for me you are visible to my eyes. This is a great display of your mercy.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**But although you reside within the heart, you are very far away from those whose minds are disturbed by their entanglement in material work. No one can grasp you by his material powers, for you reveal yourself only in the hearts of those who have learned to appreciate your qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

“I manifest in all hearts as the witness according to śruti.” That is true. You reside in all hearts. Yet you cannot be perceived (agrāhyaḥ) because of the ahaṅkāra, etc., of people whose hearts are agitated by karmas. You are concealed by their ahaṅkāra, etc. You are seen as being situated close (anti) to those whose minds have obtained (upeta) your shelter (guṇa). He is far and he is also near. (BG [13.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/13.16))

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**Let me offer my obeisances unto you. You are realized as the Supreme Soul by those who know the Absolute Truth, whereas in your form of time you impose death upon the forgetful souls. You appear both in your causeless spiritual form and in the created form of this universe, thus simultaneously uncovering the eyes of your devotees and obstructing the vision of the non devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Śrutadeva offers his respect, explaining this. I offer respects to you always. You are understood as Parabrahman (paratmātmane) for those who know their own and the supreme ātmā. You are not known as the object of knowledge (anātmane). You remove saṁsāra by your form (svātma-vibhakta-mṛtyave) for those who are devoid of such ātma-jñāna, i.e. for wicked persons like Pūtanā, etc. This indicates the Lord’s extremely merciful nature as in aho bakīyam: giving liberation to Pūtanā. (SB [3.2.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.23)) “Some consider my form to be made of māyā. How can it give liberation?” You have a form (liṅgam) which is temporary, the virāṭ-rūpa, and a form which is eternal, full of consciousness. The word liṅga means form as in mukunda-liṅgālaya-darśane dṛśau his eyes in seeing the form of the Lord. (SB [9.4.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/4.19)) Since they do not know of the second form which is eternal, they think like that. “Why are people ignorant of that form?” By your māyā, you are uncovered for those who know you and covered for those who are averse to you. tvatto jñānaṁ hi jīvānāṁ pramoṣas te ‘tra śaktitaḥ From you alone the knowledge of the living beings arises, and by your potency that knowledge is stolen away. (SB [11.22.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/22.28))

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, you are that Supreme Soul, instruct us since we are your servants. How shall we serve you? My Lord, simply seeing you puts an end to all the troubles of human life.**

**Комментарий:**

You who are the Lord as described, should instruct us. “How will my instruction be effective while you continue in saṁsāra?” Seeing you who have a form full of consciousness and bliss (bhavān), puts an end to all troubles.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After hearing Śrutadeva speak these words, the Supreme Lord, who relieves his surrendered devotees’ distress, took Śrutadeva’s hand in his own and, smiling, spoke to him as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing that Śrutadeva’s respect to him is as if more than respect toward his devotee brāhmaṇas, the Lord who considers devotion to his devotees to be more complete than devotion to himself, speaks in order to fulfill what he prayed for. Taking Śrutadeva’s hand in his, smiling, he spoke. With a portion of friendliness, he held his hand like Śrīdāmā’s. “You know my nature. You should be taught something by me, who know your nature.”

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear brāhmaṇa, you should know that these great sages have come here just to bless you. They travel throughout the worlds with me, purifying them with the dust of their feet.**

**Комментарий:**

By addressing him “O brāhmaṇa” Kṛṣṇa indicates, “Due to being a brāhmaṇa, do you not show much respect to his own varṇa?” Know that these sages came, bringing me (samprāptān), to show mercy to you. They have no other goal. Know them along with me, situated in the heart and sometimes situated externally. Thus they are the chief due to the rule saha-yukte ’pradhāne: with saha, the subordinate takes instrumental case (Pāṇini 2.3.19) Thus I am dependent on them.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**One can gradually become purified by seeing, touching and worshiping temple deities, places of pilgrimage and holy rivers. But one can attain the same result immediately simply by receiving the glance of exalted sages.**

**Комментарий:**

Devatās (deities) and others are not like them. The deity forms of the devatās, holy places (kṣetrāṇi) or holy waters (tīrthāni) purify gradually, and that too over a long time. But it is said that these sages travel for purifying. Even the devatās, etc., can purify only by the glance of the great devotees. In this way they are superior to the deities, kṣetras and tīrthas. eṣāṁ vicaratāṁ padbhyāṁ tīrthānāṁ pāvanecchayā Your personal associates, devotees, wander all over the world with a desire to purify even the holy places of pilgrimage. (SB [4.30.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.37))

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**By his very birth, a brāhmaṇa is the best of all living beings in this world, and he becomes even more exalted when he is endowed with austerity, learning and self-satisfaction, what to speak of devotion to me.**

**Комментарий:**

He establishes their qualities using kaimutya. By birth (janmanā), by following svadharma (tapasā), and knowledge of scriptures (vidyayā) the brāhmaṇa is the best of all living entities. What to speak of being engaged in worship of me (mat-kalayā).

### Text 54

**Перевод:**

**Even my own four-armed form is no dearer to me than a brāhmaṇa. Within himself a learned brāhmaṇa comprises all the Vedas, just as within myself I comprise all the devatās.**

**Комментарий:**

Worshipping the brāhmaṇa is very dear to me. Why? He is composed of all Vedas: he is the abode of all its knowledge. Since the object of proof (i.e. prameya) is dependent on the proof (i.e. pramāṇa) The Vedas are the proof that I am all the devatās. The brāhmaṇas are composed of those Vedas. Thus they are more dear to me than my form as Vedas.

### Text 55

**Перевод:**

**Ignorant of this truth, foolish people neglect and enviously offend a learned brāhmaṇa, who, being nondifferent from me, is their spiritual master and very self. They consider worshippable only such obvious manifestations of divinity as my deity form.**

**Комментарий:**

Not knowing this, thinking that the deity form alone should be worshipped, those who are envious offend the brāhmaṇa. They cannot tolerate his qualities due to thinking that he is similar to them. Thus, they are ignorant. The brāhmaṇa is described. He is worshippable by birth, etc., and even in that he is the teacher of tattva (gurum), and is nondifferent from me (mām) due to meditation on me. Just as kings quarrelling today become united tomorrow, etymologically ātmā is related to atati: to go continuously. Thus, ātmānam means “he who continuously pervades all the dharmas described in the Vedas as something to be taught and performed.”

### Text 56

**Перевод:**

**Because he has realized me, a brāhmaṇa is firmly fixed in the knowledge that I am the basis of everything moving and nonmoving in the universe, and also the primary elements of its creation.**

**Комментарий:**

He shows that such a brāhmaṇa who was called “me” (māṁ in previous verse) due to attaining meditation on the Lord, is the greatest devotee. He considers in his mind that the cause of the universe, such as mahat-tattva (bhāvāḥ) are my bodies (rūpāṇi). A person devoted only to the Lord should bow down to ether, fire, air, water, earth, the sun and other luminaries, all living beings, the directions, trees and other plants, the rivers and oceans, seeing them as the body of Kṛṣṇa. (SB [11.2.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.41)) Why does he do this? Since he sees me situated as antaryāmī in all those things (mad-īkṣayā). In this way, it is intended that brāhmaṇas who are averse to the Lord should be respected only from a distance. Even if one is a brāhmaṇa and is qualified with all the brahminical qualifications, he is considered degraded if he is averse to worshiping Lord. (SB [7.9.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/9.10))

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**Therefore you should worship these brāhmaṇa sages, O brāhmaṇa, with the same faith you have in me. If you do so, you will worship me directly, which you cannot do otherwise, even with offerings of vast riches.**

**Комментарий:**

Among brāhmaṇas, worship these brāhmaṇas such as Nārada, who know the truth of my svarūpa and are dearest to me. O Śrutadeva (brahman)! If you do this with extreme affection (mac-chraddhayā), I am worshipped directly. If you worship me without faith in my devotees (anyathā), then I am not really worshipped even if by great wealth.

### Text 58

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śuka said: So instructed by his Lord, with single-minded devotion Śrutadeva worshipped Kṛṣṇa and the topmost brāhmaṇas accompanying him, and King Bahulāśva did the same. Thus both Śrutadeva and the king attained the ultimate destination.**

**Комментарий:**

Worshipping the Lord with concentrated mind, the brāhmaṇa and the king attained the supreme abode (sad-gatim).

### Text 59

**Перевод:**

**O King, thus the Lord, who is devoted to his own devotees, stayed for some time with his two great devotees Śrutadeva and Bahulāśva, teaching them the behavior of perfect saints. Then the Lord returned to Dvārakā.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva concludes. The Lord taught his two devotees, the brāhmaṇa and the king (sva-bhaktayoḥ) the path of the Vedas (sanmārgam), bhakti-yoga chiefly constituted of bhakti to the devotee. He stayed (uṣitvā) there a long time to please them since he had great respect for the devotees (bhakta-bhaktimān) and prema since he had himself come there to show this. The suffix mān in bhaktimān indicates praise and Lord’s eternal possession of bhakti for his devotees.

## Chapter 87 - Prayers by the Personified Vedas

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Parīkṣit said: O brāhmaṇa, how can the Vedas directly describe the Supreme Absolute Truth, who cannot be described in words? The Vedas are limited to describing the qualities of material nature, but the Supreme is devoid of these qualities, being transcendental to all gross and subtle causes.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to the son of Nanda, to the Lord most affectionate to the devotees, to the child of Yaśodā, to Govinda, the devotee of the devotees. In eighty-seventh chapter, Kṛṣṇa, Svayaṁ Bhagavān is glorified by the Vedas, which Nārada ascertained from the lord of Badarī’s recitation. May the feet of the great devotees who explained the prayers of the Vedas be mine, as I also explain the verses. At the end of the previous chapter, it was said that the Lord taught the path of Vedas and left (SB [10.86.59](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/86.59)). It was explained there that the self-evident Vedas (sat) instruct the path of bhakti to Bhagavān, Parabrahman. When the Vedas can describe Brahman (either directly or indirectly, etc.) , they can teach bhakti to Brahman. But they cannot describe Brahman. Thus he asks. O Śukadeva! How can the śrutis directly describe Brahman? It is not possible to describe the indescribable in terms of similarity to conscious or unconscious objects. Śrutis say that Brahman is different from either of them. Na tasya pratimā asti: Brahman has no resemblance (to anything). (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) It is devoid of the three guṇas. Sākṣī cetāḥ kevalo nirguṇaś ca: Brahman is the witness, consciousness, pure and without guṇas. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) This is because it is superior to gross effects and subtle causes (sat-asataḥ pare). The śrutis describe directly expressible object through jāti, guṇa and kriyā—which are modifiers of dravya (guṇavṛttayaḥ). The meaning is this. The function of the śrutis in relation to Brahman is denied. In vyākaraṇa, words have three different roles in regards to a substance (dravya). This description is like the concept of an object used to model real world in computer programming. An object (dravya) has state (guṇa) and behavior (kriyā) and is an instance of a class (jāti). The contention here is that since Brahman does not have any of these properties, then how are the śrutis able to describe it? From Brahman words return. It is not attained by the mind. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) And the function of the śrutis in relation to Brahman is also seen. Brahman is the goal which all Vedas talk of. (Kaṭhopaniṣad) Brahman can be and cannot be approached by the mind: Brahman cannot be conceived by the mind. (Kena Upaniṣad) Brahman should be realized by the mind. (Bṛhad-ārāṇyaka Upaniṣad) Thus, how can the conflicting statements of the śrutis be harmonized. This is the question.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvamī said: The Supreme Lord manifested the material intelligence, senses, mind and vital air of the living entities so that they could indulge their desires for sense gratification, take repeated births to engage in fruitive activities, become elevated in future lives and ultimately attain liberation.**

**Комментарий:**

By saying nirguṇaś ca (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad), the śrutis deny only the material guṇas in Brahman since Viṣṇu Purāṇa says: sattvādayo na santīśe yatra ca prākṛtā guṇāḥ: sattva and other material guṇas do not exist in Brahman. But Brahman is the creator of the universe, omniscient, blissful, giver of liberation, etc. These attributes which are related to svarūpa, exist in Brahman. He is the cause, the agent, the Lord, the source of Brahmā. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) This Lord arranges all real objects in this world. (Īśopaniṣad) He created the whole universe. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) The Lord is omniscient. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) The person who knows blissful Brahman, from which words and mind turn back, does not fear anything. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) Meditating on this syllable one attains whatever one desires. (Kaṭha Upaniṣad) Thus, due to the qualities such as being the creator of the world, etc., the śrutis describe Brahman. The Lord created the intelligence, senses, etc., of living beings for the enjoyment of objects which are the results of karma (mātrārtham), for performances of karma which is the cause of birth (bhavārtham), for knowledge of self and the Lord (ātmane), and for liberation (akalpanāya). Without intelligence, etc., there can be no enjoyment of results of karma, no karmas to give results, no jñāna-bhakti-yoga involving control of mind, etc., and no mokṣa, their result. He created them for those purposes. Yato vāco nivartante: words cannot describe him. (Taittiīrya Upaniṣad) This simply means that Brahman cannot be completely described by words since it is said, kārtsnyena nājo’py abhidhātum īśaḥ: even Brahmā cannot describe the Lord completely (SB [12.4.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/4.39)) and since here the word pra has been used . Saying that by bhāga-lakṣaṇā (partial meaning given to words) Brahman may be understood to be cin-mātra (consciousness alone) is impetuous since Brahman is devoid of properties which delimit its nature of being an object of lakṣaṇā vṛtti and since lakṣaṇā is unsuitable because it is accepted that words cannot describe Brahman completely. It should not be said that “even without pravṛtti-nimittas (i.e. abhidhā) and lakṣaṇā the spiritual aspect (i.e. consciousness) of Brahman is understood due to the inconceivable nature of the śakti of words just like the sentence ‘daśamas tvam asi (you are the tenth)’” since this is not accepted by the author of Mahābhāṣya and is speculative. It should not be said that “in the śruti statement, satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ brahma: Brahman is real, conscious and infinite (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) —by atad-vyāvṛtti lakṣaṇā (double negation), from the words satya, etc., the understanding of Brahman having the svarūpa of satya, etc., is just like the statement—‘go-bhinna-bhinno gauḥ’” since by the existence of knowledge of something different from what is not that, the possessor of qualities is proved.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Those who came before even our ancient predecessors meditated upon this same confidential knowledge of the Absolute Truth. Indeed, anyone who faithfully concentrates on this knowledge will become free from material attachments and attain the final goal of life.**

**Комментарий:**

He glorifies. These two verses (1-2), an Upaniṣad concerning Brahman (brahmī), was placed in minds of Nārada and others (pūrveṣāṁ) by Sanaka and others (pūrvajaiḥ). Even in their minds these two: the question and the answer were produced. Or the verses starting with jaya jaya serve as an Upaniṣad. The person who has nothing except the processes of bhakti and jñāna (akiñcanaḥ), who concentrates on these verses with faith, attains liberation.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**In this connection I will relate to you a narration concerning Kṛṣṇa. It is about a conversation that once occurred between Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi and Nārada Muni.**

**Комментарий:**

A history is related to make the stated meaning strong. It is a history (gāthām) in the form of a dialogue with Nārāyaṇa as the speaker (nārāyaṇānvitam).

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Once, while traveling among the various planets of the universe, the Lord’s beloved devotee Nārada went to visit the primeval sage Nārāyaṇa at his hermitage.**

**Комментарий:**

Nārāyaṇa has an eternal form, and was son of Dharma (ṛṣim).

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**From the very beginning of Brahmā’s day Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi has been undergoing austere penances in this land of Bhārata while perfectly performing contemplation on the Lord, knowledge of the Lord and bhakti-yoga for the benefit of liberation and material happiness.**

**Комментарий:**

He has been performing austerity for liberation (kṣemāya) and for material happiness (svastaye), starting from the first part of Brahmā’s day (ākalpāt).

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**There Nārada approached Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi, who was sitting amidst sages of the village of Kalāpa. After bowing down to the Lord, O hero of the Kurus, Nārada asked him the very same question you have asked me.**

**Комментарий:**

He asked this very question: “O brāhmaṇa, how can the śrutis describe the indescribable Brahman?”

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**As the sages listened, Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi related to Nārada an ancient discussion about the Vedas that took place among the residents of Janaloka.**

**Комментарий:**

The Lord told to Nārada that discussion of Brahman that took place among Sanaka and others living on Janaloka.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: O son of self-born Brahmā, once long ago on Janaloka, wise sages who resided there performed a great sacrifice concerning the Vedas. These sages, mental sons of Brahmā, were all perfect celibates.**

**Комментарий:**

O Nārada, son of Brahmā! Brahma-satram is where people of equal qualification discuss Brahman as speaker and as listener. Just as where similar sponsors perform karmas as ṛtviks, etc., is called karma-satra.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**At that time you happened to be visiting the Lord on Śvetadvīpa. A lively discussion fully endowed with the Vedas arose among the sages on Janaloka as to the nature of the Supreme Absolute Truth. The same question arose then that you are asking me now.**

**Комментарий:**

“Then why did I not know of it?” You were on Śvetadvīpa. Ha means clear.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Although these sages were all equally qualified in terms of concentration on the Vedas, and although they all saw friends, enemies and neutral parties equally, they chose one of their number to be the speaker, and the rest became eager listeners.**

**Комментарий:**

Who was the questioner and who was the speaker? One was chosen as the speaker (pravacanam). The word pravacanam is formed by the suffix lyu used in the sense of the doer. This was for the purpose of giving special bliss to all qualified speakers.

### Text 12-13

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Sanandana replied: After Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa withdrew from manifesting pastimes with the gopīs at the end of day, he slept. After this, the śrutis reawakened him using words indicating his qualities, just as the poets serving a king approach him at dawn and awaken him by reciting his heroic deeds.**

**Комментарий:**

Sanaka and others asked what was mentioned in the first verse, and Sanandana spoke as was mentioned in the second verse about intelligence and senses being created. To show that the śrutis are proof in that regard he introduces this verse. Withdrawing the actions he produced during the day, which were understood by our intelligence, at night in his palace, Kṛṣṇa was sleeping with his śaktis, his consorts. At the end of night, the śrutis woke him up with words describing his qualities (liṅgaiḥ). Though he was omniscient, they made him attentive to the meaning of their prayers. This happened in Gokula and in Dvārakā. Such an explanation is not improper since Nārada offers respects to Kṛṣṇa, with Kṛṣṇa as the subject of the prayers of the Vedas (in verse 46). This is supported by statements such as this: These women fully absorbed their minds in meditation on Kṛṣṇa’s powerful arms, which are like the bodies of great serpents. We want to become just like the gopīs and render service to his lotus feet. (SB [10.87.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/87.23)) “Why is Kṛṣṇa the cause of creation as mentioned here?” Since that is mentioned several times in the prayers and since creation, etc., actions of his svāṁśas are included in him, the aṁśī to a greater degree (and thus he is a superior creator) and since the subject of the śrutis is Kṛṣṇa and since Kṛṣṇa, the lord of Vraja, is spoken of in relation to the prayers of śrutis through the Tenth Canto verse: The glories of the Supreme Lord are studied through the three Vedas, the Upaniṣads, the literature of Sāṅkhyayoga, and other Vaiṣṇava literature, yet mother Yaśodā considered that Supreme Person her ordinary child. (SB [10.8.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/8.45)) Thus, Śukadeva himself resolves the issue. The other verse (13) is clear.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**The śrutis said: Victory, victory to you, O unconquerable one! By your very nature you are perfectly full in all opulences; therefore please defeat the eternal power of illusion, who assumes control over the modes of nature to create difficulties for conditioned souls. O you who awaken all the material and spiritual energies of the jīvas, sometimes the Vedas serve you as you sport with your material and spiritual potencies.**

**Комментарий:**

First, the śrutis dedicated to the qualities of the Lord such as power, compassion, etc., glorify him. The meter is nardaṭaka. It is described as follows: Nardaṭaka is composed of the following metrical gaṇas: na ja bha ja ja la ga (sss sls lss sls sls sl) . O Lord! Manifest your excellence (jaya jaya). Jaya is repeated to express joy or respect. “How?” Destroy (jahi) the ignorance (ajām) of the jīvas having moving or nonmoving bodies (agajagad-okasām). “Why should māyā full of guṇas be destroyed?” Its guṇas are grasped by the fault of aversion to you (doṣa-gṛbhītaguṇām). In the word “gṛbhīta,” bh is substituted for h (gṛhita), due to the rule, hṛ-grahor bhaś chandasi hasya: the h of hṛ and grah may change to bh in Vedic usages (Mahābhāṣya 8.2.32). Her guṇas are the cause of anarthas. They are unfavorable for turning towards you. O unconquered Lord (ajita)! You alone cannot be conquered by māyā. All others are bound by guṇas. “Why is māyā not able to conquer me?” By your svarūpa (ātmanā) of consciousness and bliss, you are endowed with complete six powers (samasta-bhagaḥ) of aiśvarya, vīrya, yaśas, śrī, jñāna and vairāgya. Devoid of those qualities, she cannot approach you. “Even with disappearance of māyā, one cannot attain me without bhakti.” O Lord, who awakens all śakti (akhila-śakti-avabodhaka)! Just as you awaken the śakti for performing karmas and enjoying its results, in the same way you awaken the śaktis of jñāna and bhakti to make the jīvas realize you. “But bhakti is not given by me.” karhicit sma na bhakti-yogam: I never give bhakti. (SB [5.6.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/6.18)) At the time of creation, the Vedas serve (anucaret) you as you sport (carataḥ) with māyā (ājayā) and the jīvas (ātmanā). By his will the Lord enters pradhāna which is subject to change and also enters the jīva who is not subject to change, and agitates both of them at the time of creation. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) While you play with them, the Vedas serve you becoming the proof. Carataḥ in the genitive stands for the accusative. These śrutis (which speak this verse) are: Brahman is consciousness and bliss. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) The Lord is omniscient. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) Brahman is understood by the mind. He is the controller of prāṇa. He is effulgent, and his every desire is fulfilled. He is all pervading, performs attractive pastimes, and is endowed with all enjoyment, all fragrance and all tastes. He encompasses everything. He is silent. He is without worries. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) He is the controller of all. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad) He is the shelter of all. He is the friend of all. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) From him the jīvas’ consciousness has expanded at the time of creation. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) The Lord willed, “Let me be many, may I produce offspring.” (Chāndogya Upaniṣad)

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Some define you as matter since it remains after destruction of the universe. It is like the transformation of clay into a pot. Some śrutis testify that the universe appears and disappears while Brahman remains unchanged. Some of the śrutis take you to be the mind, words and actions, but, by indicating you in terms of material objects like pots, such a statement appears to be ignorance to us.**

**Комментарий:**

“You śrutis do not describe me alone. Rather you praise even Indra and others through verses such as indro yāto ’vasitasya rājā: Indra is the king of the moving and immobile beings. (Ṛg Veda)” Fearing this objection, some śrutis praise the Lord as the cause of the universe consisting of Indra, etc., and as having eternal svarūpa. Yātaḥ means “of moving beings”. It is formed from the root yā prāpaṇe, by applying śatṛ suffix. Avasitasya means “of non-moving beings”. It is formed from the root ṣiñ bandhane preceded by ava and with the suffix kta. The wise perceive this universe with Indra, etc., perceived by the ear and other senses (upalabdham) as Brahman. “Why?” Because of transformation of the universe there is creation and destruction (udayāstamayau) while you, possessing the three śaktis as Parabrahman, remain (avaśeṣatayā). The word vā indicates an analogy. It is like the creation and destruction of pot and other transformations from clay and into clay while only clay remains. In the same way the universe consisting of Indra and others is not different from you who are endowed with the śaktis of prakṛti and jīva. This is how the author of Vedāntasūtras states: From the Brahman arises the world which is non-different from it. This is proved by statements starting with vācārambhaṇa. (Brahma-sūtra) “Then do I transform?” Though the form of the universe changes, you, the form possessing śaktis remain (avikṛtāt). Thus Gajendra says: You are the cause of all causes, but you have no cause. Therefore, you are the wonderful cause of everything. I offer my respectful obeisances unto you. (SB [8.3.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-8/3.15)) Thus you are the cause of the universe, and are eternal. Those who see reality (ṛṣayaḥ), place their mind, words and actions in you, the shelter of śaktis, eternal, full of consciousness and bliss. They make you the subject of their meditation and praises. Thus though we describe Indra and others, we make you the ultimate subject of praise. They mention another purpose. How can the feet of men who live on earth, though sometimes placed on trees, etc., become untrue (to their meaning)? Their feet cannot deviate from earth. Just as words denoting cowness indicate a real cow, so words denoting śakti indicate the possessor of śakti. These śrutis and their meanings are: Everything is Brahman. The peaceful person should worship Brahman as the creator, destroyer and maintainer (ja-la-an). (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) Why is everything Brahman? Since from it everything is born (ja) and into it everything merges (la) and by it everything is maintained (an). Clay takes on a name as it undergoes transformation expressible by words. But the word clay is real. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) The name “vikāra” (transformation) is begun to be used due to the actions (of bringing water using a pot) preceded by the words, “Bring water by a pot.” But the name “mṛttikā” (clay) is authoritative since it remains unchanged. Instrumental (vācā) is used for the result with the intention to speak of it as the cause. The Lord is the chief eternal and the chief conscious entity. The single Lord fulfills the desires of the many jīvas. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad)

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**O master of the three worlds! Therefore, the wise get rid of all misery by diving deep into the nectarean ocean of your topics, which wash away all the contamination of the universe. Then what to speak of those who, by having spiritual strength rid their minds of bad habits and freed themselves from time, are able to worship your true nature, O supreme one, finding within it uninterrupted bliss?**

**Комментарий:**

Those śrutis dedicated to pastimes and dedicated to worship praise Kṛṣṇa. O master of the worlds situated above, below and in the middle! Because of this (iti), the wise (śūrayaḥ), submerging themselves in the sweet ocean of your topics which eliminate all impurity up to ignorance, give up ādhyātmikā and other pain or hardships. This shows sādhakas. The siddhas, purified of the qualities of time such as old age and the qualities of the heart such as rāga (attachment), etc., by your potency (svadhāma), worship your feet in such a way that they have perpetual happiness. What to speak of them give up pain? They definitely do. O eternal husband of Lakṣmī (para-ma)! These śrutis are: I speak of the valor of Viṣṇu who created the earth and heaven, who established the worlds above and below. (Ṛg Veda) Kṛṣṇa is supreme, all-pervading, and most worthy of praise. Though he is one, he is also many. The wise who worship him in the pīṭha obtain constant happiness not available to others. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Only if they become your faithful followers are those who breathe actually alive, otherwise their breathing is like that of a bellows. It is by your mercy alone that the elements, beginning with the mahat-tattva and false ego, created the egg of this universe. Among the manifestations known as anna-maya and so forth, you are the ultimate one, entering within the material coverings along with the living entity and assuming the same forms as those he takes. Distinct from the gross and subtle material manifestations, you are the reality underlying them all.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis praise while saying that jīvas have a useless birth without worshipping the Lord as mentioned. O Lord! Though obtaining a birth suitable for worshiping you (te anuvidhāḥ), if jīvas gratify their prāṇas and senses (asu-bhṛtaḥ), becoming lusty for sense objects, then their birth is useless. Or because they are lifeless like corpses due to lacking bhakti, they uselessly breathe like bellows, which are lifeless. If they become favorable to you, then they are described as living, maintaining prāṇas. The śrutis further describe the glories of the Lord mentioned by the word te (first line). Mahat-tattva, ahaṅkāra, etc., obtaining power by your glance, have become capable of creating the universe (aṇḍam). You are thus worthy of worship. “But what is my svarūpa, who am to be worshipped?” Expecting this they speak. Among all the puruṣas starting with anna-maya you are the final puruṣa. Five puruṣas are described in Taittirīya Upaniṣad in the verse beginning sa vā eṣa puruṣo’nna-rasa-mayaḥ: anna-maya, prāṇa-maya, mano-maya, vijñāna-maya and ānanda-maya. Among them the final puruṣa is ānanda-maya. He is the form of puruṣa (puruṣa-vidhaḥ in Taittirīya Upaniṣad) existing with the other four puruṣas (anvayaḥ) since it is said: Different from the vijñāna-maya puruṣa is another ātmā within the vijñāna-maya puruṣa, the ānanda-maya puruṣa. The vijñāna-maya puruṣa is pervaded by the ānanda-maya puruṣa. He has the form of a human, like the previous puruṣa. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) “But I would be affected by the faults arising from the contact of anna-maya-puruṣa and other forms on entering into them.” You are different from the conscious beings (sat) and matter (asataḥ). Though you enter them, you are devoid of the fault arising from associating with them. You are eternal. You remain the unchanging substantial entity (avaśeṣam) when mahat-tattva, etc., are destroyed. After millions of years, at the time of cosmic annihilation, when everything, manifested and unmanifested, is annihilated by the force of time, the five gross elements enter into the subtle conception, and the manifested categories enter into the unmanifested substance. At that time, you alone remain, and you are known as Śeṣa. (SB [10.3.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/3.25)) Moreover since it is later said (in Taittirīya Upaniṣad), raso vai saḥ: the Lord is rasa, you, who are filled with mādhurya-rasa, are truly attained by us in the form of gopīs. This is substantiated in Bṛhadvāmana Purāṇa and by the verse: These women fully absorbed their minds in meditation on Lord Kṛṣṇa’s powerful arms, which are like the bodies of great serpents. We want to become just like the gopīs and render service to your lotus feet. (SB [10.87.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/87.23)) These śrutis are: The planets attained by the demons (asuryā), full of misery, are certainly covered with deep darkness. Those who defame the true nature of Viṣṇu enter those planets after death. (Īśopaniṣad) Asuryāḥ refers to the planets attained by the demoniac, who are averse to the Lord. The wise, who worship Kṛṣṇa in his pīṭha—Kṛṣṇa who is the principal being among many, who is the chief eternal among eternals and the chief knower among knowers, who satisfies their prema—attain eternal bliss not available to others. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) The former verse shows the fault of lack of bhakti and the latter verse shows the good quality of having bhakti.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**Among the followers of the methods set forth by great sages, those with less refined vision worship the antaryāmī in the region of the abdomen. The Āruṇis then worship him in the heart, which allows one to come close to the Lord. From there, O unlimited Lord, these worshipers raise their consciousness upward from there to Satya-loka and then to Vaikuṇṭha. They reach that place from which they will never again fall to this world into the mouth of death.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis which teach bhakti mixed with yoga in the manner of gradually progressing by steps, taking the opportunity of the five puruṣas just mentioned, like pointing at a branch to locate Arundhatī star, praise the Lord. Crude yogīs in the sampradāya of sages worship the antaryāmī of Vaiśvānara fire situated in the stomach region, the Lord who gives kriyā-śakti by stimulating anna-rasa, etc. I am the fire of digestion in the bodies of all living entities, and I join with the prāṇas, outgoing and incoming, to digest the four kinds of foodstuff. (BG [15.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.14)) Kūrpa-dṛśaḥ means “having eyes clouded by dust.” They have gross vision. This is because the abdomen is grosser than the heart. Others say that kūrpa means subtle or acute vision since aiming at the subtle form (of the Lord) situated in the heart, they first worship the Lord in stomach in order to enter that subtle form (called daharākāśa). But the sages known as āruṇis, of the Āruṇa dynasty, worship the antaryāmī of the jīva, situated in the heart, a subtle form called daharākāśa, the Lord who bestows jñāna-śakti by inspiring intelligence, etc. The heart is the path of the nāḍīs which spread out (parisara-paddhatim). It is the place where the nāḍīs branch out. The result is described. O Ananta! From the heart, the place of perceiving you, the suṣumnā nāḍī, filled with light, rises to the head. Beginning from the mulādhāra, from the middle of the heart, it proceeds to the brahma-randhra. Attaining that place, one does not fall to the mouth of death again. Liberated, they attain you. These śrutis are: udaraṁ brahmeti śārkarākṣā upāsate hṛdayaṁ brahmeti āruṇayo brahmā haiva tā ita ūrdhvaṁ tv evodasarpat tac-chiro ’śrayata Those whose vision is clouded identify Brahman with the abdomen, while the āruṇis worship Brahman in the heart. Those who identify them both (stomach and heart) as Brahman travel upward from the heart to take shelter of the Lord who is manifested at the top of the head. (Aitareya Āraṇyaka) mahān prabhur vai puruṣaḥ sattvasyaiṣa pravartakaḥ The Supreme Lord becomes the puruṣa to initiate the expansion of this cosmos. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) aṅguṣṭha-mātraḥ puruṣas madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati The Lord resides within the body with a form the size of the thumb. (Kaṭha Upaniṣad) utkramaṇe bhavanti There are a hundred and one nāḍīs of the heart and chief one goes to the top of the head. Going through this nāḍī one attains immortality. The others are for going out of the body. (into another body). (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) The stomach is called Brahman because it is inhabited by Brahman as Vaiśvānara. The heart is called Brahman because it is the place to realize Brahman. Brahmā haiva means those who meditate on both the stomach and heart (tā) as Brahman (brahmā). In both tā and brahmā the dual ending au is substituted by ḍā (Pāṇini 7.1.39). That Brahman goes upwards and takes shelter of the head.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Apparently entering among the variegated species of living beings you have created, you reveal your śakti in them in various degrees, just as fire manifests differently according to the shape of what it burns. Therefore those of spotless intelligence, who are altogether free from material attachments, realize your attractive svarūpa to be the permanent among all these impermanent life forms.**

**Комментарий:**

“Since the Lord becomes indistinguishable from the jīva by entering the stomach, etc., how can he be worshippable?” Some śrutis praise the Lord as being worshippable because he is distinguished by his acintya-śakti. O Lord! You enter into the various bodies of devatās, etc., produced by you, as the antaryāmī of the jīvas, as their inspirer, and reveal (cakassi) your śakti to them in various degrees. This is stated. After you enter them who are created by you, and activate such śakti in them. i.e. you later produce transformations in the effect (their bodies). tat sṛṣṭvā tad evānuprāviśat tad anupraviśya sac ca tyac cābhavat Having created the universe, he then entered it. Entering that he became sat and tyat. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) Within all these distorted forms, which have become different, like fire manifesting in proportion to the amount of wood, persons of pure intelligence understand your svarūpa (dhāma) which has entered everything, personification of pure consciousness and happiness (ekarasam) with no material distinctions (samam), and undistorted (avitatham). They are detached (abhivipaṇyavaḥ). Paṇa means to transact. These śrutis are: The one Lord, free of karma, resides unknown within all beings. He is all-pervading, residing as the ātmā of all beings. He inspires actions and is the shelter of all beings. He is the witness, the creator of the universe. He is devoid of material guṇas and is free of material action. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad)

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**The individual living entity, while inhabiting the material bodies he has created for himself by his karma, actually remains uncovered by either gross or subtle matter. This is so because, as the Vedas describe, he is part and parcel of you, the possessor of all potencies. Having determined this to be the status of the living entity, learned sages become imbued with faith and worship your lotus feet, to which all the Vedas testify and which are beyond birth.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis, speaking of the relationship of the worshiper with the Lord and from that about the Lord’s worship, praise him. Some say (the śrutis of previous verse) that the jīva (puruṣaṁ), in bodies created by (sva-kṛta-pūreṣu) you because of their karmas, was created by the kṣetrajña-śakti, your aṁśa. Thus the jīva exists without a beginning. In order to justify this, they elaborate. You are the possessor of three śaktis (akhila-śakti-dhṛtaḥ). The Lord is described like that in Viṣṇu Purāṇa: The Lord has a superior energy, another superior energy called kṣetrajña (jīva) and a third energy, which is different called avidyā-karma. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) This jīva is not your fragment like some piece of stone cut off from a rock by a chisel since this would contradict your own statement about the jīva being eternal: The jīva is my part and eternal. (BG [15.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.7)) You then would undergo transformation and the jīva would have a beginning. This is contemptible. The jīva is your representative as your aṁśa, like a white disc which is a portion (by reflection) of the moon-disc. It is not covered (saṁvāraṇam) internally or externally. It is by svarūpa a particle pervaded with dharma-bhūta consciousness internally and externally. prajñayā śarīraṁ samāruhya sukha-duhkhe āpnoti The jīva, having taken possession of the body by consciousness, experiences happiness and pain. (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad) Considering this condition of the jīva, the wise serve your two lotus feet, which are explained in the Vedas (sown in the field of the Vedas) and which destroy saṁsāra (abhavam). Service to the master is proper for the servant. The sages have faith (viśvasitāḥ), in your statement mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te: I deliver from māyā those who surrender to me. (BG [7.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.14)) These śrutis are: One is a portion of Brahman and enjoys the fruit and the other is the witness. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) One who worships my deity form nondifferent from me while living in the district of Mathurā or, indeed, anywhere in Jambūdvīpa, becomes most dear to me in this world. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) The meaning of the prayer of the śrutis is that Brahmā and others are all your servants and you are the master.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**My Lord, some fortunate souls have gotten relief from the fatigue of material life by diving into the vast nectar ocean of your pastimes, which you enact when you manifest your personal forms to propagate your form, qualities and pastimes. These rare souls, indifferent even to liberation, renounce the happiness of home and family because of their association with devotees who are like flocks of swans enjoying the lotus of your feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis praise bhakti as the highest goal. Some, having got relief (pari) from fatigue (śramanāḥ) by immersion in the waves of the sweet ocean of pastimes of you, who have a manifest form (ātta-tanoḥ) in order to reveal your qualities, powers and sweetness in truth, and which is difficult to understand, do not desire (parilaṣanti) liberation predominated by happiness and power (apavarga), what to speak of the position of Indra. Those greedy for bhakti are rare (kecit). While mentioning the cause of attaining the Lord, they specify those people. O Lord! They give up their houses due to the association of your exclusive devotees (haṁsa) who taste the sweetness of your lotus feet.
