These śrutis are: All the devatās, those desiring liberation and brahma-vādis offer him respects. (Nṛsiṁha-tāpanī Upaniṣad) Brahma-vādīs are liberated. They have the tendency to become fixed with the Lord (brahman). The root is vada sthairye. Those who are liberated worship the Lord; bhakti gives the highest bliss to even liberated persons. (Sauparṇa śruti, Quoted by Madhvācārya)

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**This human body, related to the ātmā, is actually temporary. It acts as one’s self, friend and beloved. But unfortunately, although you always show mercy to the conditioned souls and affectionately help them in every way, and although you are their true self, people in general fail to have attraction for you. Instead they commit spiritual suicide by serving temporary objects related to their bodies. Alas, because they persistently hope for success in their devotion to the unreal, they continue to wander about this greatly fearful world, assuming various degraded bodies.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis, saying that without bhakti taking a body is useless for the jīva, while offering praise intend bhakti. This body (kulāyam), which merges into earth, and which possesses ears, etc., is suitable for hearing, etc., about you (anupatham). It appears as one’s self, friend and beloved because of its relationship with you. Yet they do not take pleasure in you, the ātmā, full of consciousness and bliss, favorable to them because of your merciful nature (unmukhe), their benefactor out of friendship (hite) and affectionate to them (priye). Bata indicates lamentation. They do not worship you as servants. Rather they cover their svarūpas (ātma-hanaḥ) by false service in the form of playing with their children along with their wife and study of unauthorized scriptures. Having desires produced by false service, they accept low bodies such as jackals, etc., and wander in the cycle of saṁsāra. If a person is attached to useless argumentation to understand the Lord, he gains no result. He is born as jackal wandering in the forest. (Mahābhārata) These śrutis are: All people see the Lord’s place of pastimes. But no one sees him. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad) This means they cannot see the Lord without surrender to guru. You do not know him who produced these creatures, who dwells within you and have become opposed to him. Surrounded by ignorance, uttering mantras to maintain themselves, the priests carry out their actions. (Ṛg Veda) O those fixed in tarka (jalpyāḥ)! you do not know (vidātha) the Lord who has produced (jajāna) all these beings and who resides within you. You have become averse to him (anyat). Covered by ignorance (nīhāreṇa) you perform only karmas (uktha-śāsaḥ) and become bewildered.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**Simply by constantly thinking of him, the enemies of the Lord attained the same Supreme Truth whom sages fixed in yoga worship by controlling their breath, mind and senses. Similarly, we śrutis, who generally see you as all-pervading, will achieve the same nectar from your lotus feet that your consorts are able to relish because of their loving attraction to your mighty, serpentine arms, for you look upon us and your consorts in the same way.**

**Комментарий:**

The inconceivable power of your remembrance is such that it delivers even unfavorable person just as it delivers the favorable. Some śrutis praise by saying this. By remembrance due to intense hatred, enemies such as Kaṁsa have attained the same entity that the sages practicing strong yoga with controlled (nibhṛta) prāṇas, mind and senses worshipped in their hearts. The gopīs and we śrutis also, with our minds attached to your snake-like arms, will attain the nectar of your lotus feet. That the śrutis attained the Lord by bhakti filled with amorous desire can be seen in Bṛhad-vāmana Purāṇa. How are we similar to the gopīs? The gopīs and we are similar (samāḥ) in being objects of your mercy. You (te) see equally those who remember you (samadṛśaḥ). That remembrance makes you equal even toward those who are unequal in qualities. The word api repeated indicates that there is no difference in the object of attainment of the gopīs and śrutis. Though the sages and enemies and the śrutis and gopīs all attained the Lord, there is difference in quality. Like the ocean with no waves and the ocean with waves, the qualities were different because of differing bhāvas and since it is said, ye yathā māṁ prapadyante: as they surrender to me I respond. (BG [4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.11)) Still the svarūpa of Kṛṣṇa, the possessor of qualities, is not different however in both cases since it is said, ekam evādvitīyam: he is one without a second. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) These śrutis are: O Maitreyi! The Lord should be seen, heard about, thought about, and meditated upon with fixed concentration. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Everyone in this world has recently been born and will soon die. So how can anyone here know this topic, since Mahāviṣṇu existed prior to everything else and gave rise to sense devatās and rulers of planets like Brahmā? When he lies down and withdraws everything within himself, nothing else remains—no gross or subtle matter or bodies composed of these, no force of time or scriptures.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis praise the Lord saying that one can only understand the Lord through scripture since it is otherwise difficult to understand about his svarūpa, qualities and vibhūtis. O Lord! What person knows you, who existed previous to the creation of the world since everyone has recently been born and will die (avara-janma-layaḥ)? “How is that?” From you arose Brahmā before all others and after him (yam anu) those who renounced such as the Kumāras and those involved in activities such as Indra (ubhaye) arose (the change in the plurality of the verb is understood). When after destroying everything, you lie down with eyes closed towards the activities of the universe, then at that time, previous to the next creation, gross elements like ether and subtle elements like mahat-tattva (sad-asat) and the body made by the two (ubhayam), the disturbance of time which is the cause, and the senses which give knowledge of scriptures, do not exist since they have all been made to enter you. The Lord, after manifesting the scriptures, and desiring to make names and forms for the jīvas, then pursued prakṛti, who desired to create the universe, but who moves only by his power, and who by his will alone bewilders the jīvas. (SB [1.10.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/10.22)) Due to this statement, at the time of creation since scriptures were manifested first, from them, being taught by a guru, your svarūpa, etc., are understood. Thus you are known only through them. These śrutis are: Who in this world actually knows, who can explain, how has it arisen, whence this creation has come? The devatās, after all, are younger than the creation. Who then knows whence this world has come into being? (Ṛg Veda) Who knows him directly (addhā), from whom this world (visṛṭiḥ) arose? No one knows and there is no one to inform also. How has it come? “But the devatās can say.” The devatās were recent by being created by him. Atha is used in the sense of absence of interval.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Supposed authorities who declare that matter is the origin of existence, that the permanent qualities of the soul can be destroyed, that the self is completely aloof from the body or that attaining results of work is the only reality—all such authorities base their teachings on mistaken ideas that hide the truth. Some say the Lord is a jīva covered by the three guṇas. All these philosophies are created out of ignorance since you are above matter.**

**Комментарий:**

The svarūpa of the jīva and you, the Lord, can be known from scriptures, revealed at the beginning of creation, studied under a knower of truth but not by one’s imagination. Some śrutis praise in this way. The logicians say that the world arose from combination of two, three or more atoms (asataḥ), among one, two or more atoms. The Buddhist proponents of kṣama-bhaṅga-vāda say that matter is destroyed without remainder (sataḥ mṛtim) like extinguishing a lamp. The Lokāyatikas see difference in ātmā in terms of being brāhmaṇa, etc., or thin, etc. The followers of karma say that Svarga, etc., the result of karmas (vipaṇam), is true (ṛtam). All of them, who teach their students, are proceeding by false logic (ārupitaiḥ). All this would have been true if the jīva (pumān) were composed of three guṇas. But that is not so since jīva in reality is beyond the three guṇas. This mistaken idea that the jīvas is made of three guṇas arises from ignorance (abodha-kṛtā). Those who have studied the scriptures from a knower of truth say that the real world arises from the Lord. It disappears in him like a bird disappearing in a forest. They reject such differentiation in the ātmā and do not say that results of karma are eternal. “If there is ignorance in the jīva, who is equal to me, then ignorance affects me also.” It is not present in you since you are beyond ignorance (paratra). Tamasaḥ parastāt: the Lord is beyond ignorance. (Puruṣa-sūkta) You have a form of consciousness and bliss (avabodha-rase). Darkness covers a particle of light, which is gold in color, but not the sun, a mass of light. These śrutis are: Caught in the grip of ignorance, self-proclaimed experts consider themselves learned authorities. They wander about this world befooled, like the blind leading the blind. (Kaṭha Upaniṣad [1.2.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/katha-bs/1.2.5)) They are prone to bad logic (dandramyamānāḥ). The details in this regard may be understood from Tarkapāda (2nd chapter, 2nd pāda) of Govinda-bhāṣya.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**The mind composed of the three guṇas, carrying out action within you, appears to be the giver of true knowledge. But those who know you see you as the root of everything. Just as things made of gold are not to be rejected, since their substance is actual gold, so this world is to be accepted as real, being a manifestation from the Lord, who created it and then entered within it.**

**Комментарий:**

It has been said that those who think they are learned, but simply imagine things, are mistaken. But those who have received scriptures from an authorized guru, knowing that you who are endowed with three śaktis, are the form of the universe, become happy. Some śrutis praise in this way. Knowers of ātmā, who are knowledgeable, think that the unlimited universe made of subtle (asat) and gross (sat) up to human birth which has differences like brāhmanā, etc., is your body (ātmatayā). It is said: Ether, fire, air, water, earth, the sun and other luminaries, all living beings, the directions, trees and other plants, the rivers and oceans—whatever a devotee experiences he should consider to be an expansion of Kṛṣṇa. Thus seeing everything that exists within creation as the body of the Supreme Lord, Hari, the devotee should offer his sincere respects to the entire expansion of the Lord’s body. (SB [11.2.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.41)) “Why are they like this?” The mind made of three guṇas (tri-vṛt) always accepts as real what is related to you. Iva is used in the sense of restriction. The universe is not rejectable since it is the effect of your śakti. An example is given. A person desiring gold does not reject a bangle which is a transformation of gold since it is a form of gold. “Gold enters into a bangle. But I am not like that since I am dissociated from matter.” The universe made by you, is entered into by you. Tat sṛṣṭvā tad evānuprāviśat: creating the universe, the Lord entered it. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) In order that you do not transform, you do not contact the universe though it is under your control because of your acintya-śakti. Thus it is ascertained (avasitam) as your body (ātmatayā) by them and thus they become happy. One who does not desire anything within this world, who has controlled his senses, who has fixed his intelligence on me, who regards heaven and hell equally, and whose mind is completely satisfied in me finds only happiness wherever he goes. (SB [11.14.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/14.13)) These śrutis are: The Lord produced himself. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) tat sṛṣṭvā tad evānuprāviśat Creating the universe, the Lord entered it. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**The devotees who worship you as the shelter of all beings disregard death and place their feet on his head. But with the words of the Vedas you bind the nondevotees like animals, though they are vastly learned scholars. It is your affectionate devotees who can purify themselves and others, not those who are inimical to you.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis praise the devotees’ excellence and non-devotees’ inferiority. Those who worship you (tava) as the abode of all jīvas (sattvaniketatayā), they alone (uta) kicking the head of death (nirṛteḥ) step over it. Genitive tava means accusative. The ye intervening between pari and caranti is not a fault according to chandasi vyavahitāś ca. (Pāṇini 1.4.82) You tie up (parivayase) like animals those persons expert at scriptures but averse to you by the words of the Vedas. Time acts on them. Another quality of the devotees is mentioned. Those who have made friendship with you purify other people. The nondevotees cannot even purify themselves what to speak of the other people. These śrutis are: The Lord is the abode of all beings. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) When he sees the Lord who is served and understands the Lord’s glory, he gives up lamentation. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) Juṣṭam means served by oneself. Knowing him one becomes liberated. There is no other path except knowing him. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) Anāya instead of ayanāya is Vedic usage.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Though you have no material senses, you are the self-effulgent sustainer of everyone’s sensory powers. The devatās and material nature herself offer you tribute, while also enjoying the tribute offered to them by their worshipers, just as subordinate rulers of various districts in a kingdom offer tribute to their lord, the ultimate proprietor of the land, while also enjoying the tribute paid to them by their own subjects. In this way the universal creators faithfully execute their assigned services out of fear of you.**

**Комментарий:**

He whose senses are connected to his svarūpa and who is the ruler of everyone is you alone. In this way some śrutis praise the Lord. O Lord! You are without senses related to ahaṅkāra (akaraṇaḥ). You possess parā-śakti which is composed of senses such as eyes, ears, etc., (kāraka) which are all-pervading since they are connected to your svarūpa. The author of the Vedānta-sūtras too says so: If one objects that the Lord cannot be the creator because he has no senses, the answer has already been stated. (Brahma-sūtra) You are independent (sva-rāṭ). Your knowledge and activities are under your control. The devatās (animiṣāḥ) offer gifts to you, their master, out of respect. They along with Māyā (ajayā) enjoy (samadanti) enjoyable objects given by you (which are offered by people in sacrifices). She also offers a gift in the form of creating the universe. An example is given. The kings of various provinces of Bhārata offer gifts to the emperor of all land and those kings enjoy their portions given by the citizens. The devatās are described. Brahmā and other creators of the universe engaged in duties by you, perform those duties out of fear of you (cakitāḥ). This is different from the example given. These śrutis are: He has nothing to produce, nor any instruments with which to produce. No one can be found who is equal to or greater than him. From the Vedas we hear how that Supreme Lord possesses multifarious energies— the potencies of knowledge, strength and action—each of which acts autonomously. (Śvetāsvatara Upaniṣad) Svābhāvikī means related to himself intimately. bhīṣāsmād agniś cendraś ca mṛtyur dhāvati pañcamaḥ The wind blows out of fear of him. The sun rises out of fear of him. The fire, moon and time, the fifth among them, run out of fear of him. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) Bhīṣā means out of fear. Mṛtyuḥ means time.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**O eternally liberated Lord, though you sport with your devotees, after glancing at them with spiritual power, your material energy causes the various moving and nonmoving species of life to appear by activating their material desires. You, the Supreme Lord, see no one in the world as an intimate friend and no one as a stranger, just as the ethereal sky has no connection with perceptible qualities. In this sense you resemble a void.**

**Комментарий:**

You, the independent Supreme Lord, arrange for birth of jīvas in this world. Some śrutis praise the Lord in this way. O pure Lord (vimukta)! If you sport with Māyā (ajayā), at that time the jīvas manifest with various bodies—moving or nonmoving. But you are beyond Māyā (parasya), untouched by her. The various species are described. They are joined with subtle bodies or with their karmas which arise by your glance (udīkṣayā). “Let it happen just by my glance. What is the use of arising by karmas?” For you who are faultless, the enjoyer of Lakṣmī (paramasya), there is no favored one (aparaḥ) and no unfavored person. Without karmas a diverse world does not arise from you. An example is given. Just like ether, being uncontaminated has no partiality. You are not similar to ether, rather ether is similar to you. It is comparable to emptiness (śūnya-tulām). These śrutis are: Just as small sparks emanate from a big fire, similarly all living entities, all planets, all the devatās, and all material elements such as the earth emanate from the Supreme Lord, possessor of three śaktis. (Brhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad)

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**O shelter of everything! If the jīvas were unlimited and eternal, and all powerful, the scriptures would not say that they are under your control. But the jīvas are not so, and thus are under your control. The product which has the qualities of the cause cannot be separated from the cause. The cause is thus the controller of the effect. Those who think you are like other objects are in ignorance since they reject the conclusion of scripture.**

**Комментарий:**

“The logicians and Sāṅkhya philosophers say that the jīvas are unlimited, eternal and omnipresent. They do not originate from me.” Some śrutis, rejecting this opinion, praise the Lord as the regulator of the jīvas. O eternal form (dhruva)! If the unlimited, eternal (dhruvā) jīvas (tanu-bhṛtaḥ) were all-pervading (sarva-gatāḥ), then there would not be any regulation that they should be under your control (śāsyatā). Antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānām: the Lord entered and controlled all beings. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) Thus the regulation that they are to be disciplined by you, is accepted. The śrutis which speak of the soul leaving the body at death would be contradicted since the all-pervading have connection with all bodies (and such an all-pervading soul cannot ‘leave’ a body and ‘enter’ another body). It is impossible to give determined results of the karmas performed by them due to equality (of all the jīvas). The distinction created by instrument and will is not there since the allpervading are present everywhere. But if they are small (itarathā), then the regulation that they are controlled by you is accepted. This does not contradict śruti statements which speak of the soul leaving the body at death and solves the problem of determining the giving of results of karma. Since it is heard that the jīvas arise from you, they can be controlled by you. Fire gives rise (ajani) to sparks. The fire releases sparks, its effect and by its śakti it acts as a controller (niyantṛ) by pervading the sparks. Without that śakti that function is impossible. In the same way, you have pervaded the jīvas, which arise from you, by your śakti. Thus they are very small. Your svarūpa as the antaryāmī is equal (samam) to all jīvas. “Please show this like an āmalaka in the hand. What is the use of words?” It is not known by people who think they have knowledge (anujānatām). Moreover the knowledge which is the cause of pride is faulty. Thus, it cannot be shown. These śrutis are: When the upper point of a hair is divided into one hundred parts and again each of such parts is further divided into one hundred parts, each such part is the measurement of the dimension of the spirit soul. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) He is the controller of all and master of all. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad) The person who thinks he cannot know Brahman completely can know Brahman. He who thinks he knows Brahman completely does not know Brahman. For those who think they know Brahman, Brahman cannot be realized. For those who understand that they cannot know Brahman completely, Brahman can be realized. (Kena Upaniṣad) This is the opinion of the author of Vedānta-sūtras: The jīva is atomic because scriptures describe how the jīva exits and enters bodies. (Brahma-sūtra [2.3.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vs/2.3.18))

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Neither material nature nor the soul who tries to enjoy her are ever born, yet living bodies come into being when these two combine, pervaded by you, just as bubbles form from the combination of water and air. And just as rivers merge into the ocean or the nectar from many different flowers blends into honey, so all these conditioned beings eventually merge back into you, the Supreme, along with their various names and qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

“What is the opinion of the śrutis which say that the jīvas arise from me? If they say that a portion of my svarūpa appears in the form of the jīva, then it is a fault to the eternal nature of the jīva since the eternal nature would be destroyed. If they say that prakṛti, my śakti, appears in the form of the jīva, then this makes the jīva material and liberation would be destruction of that very svarūpa.” The jīva, but not its svarūpa, arises by a combination with transformation of prakṛti in the form of bodies of devatās, humans, etc., due to your glance on prakṛti, invoked by the pursuit to give the jīva enjoyment. Some śrutis, expressing this feeling, praise the Lord as being merciful. There is no birth of prakṛti or the jīva (puruṣa) since scriptures do not speak of their birth (ajayoḥ). But by their combination the jīvas manifest possessing body, senses and prāṇas—the transformations of prakṛti. The jīva is born, attains a body, and is connected with sins. Leaving the body and dying he gives up those sins. (Bṛhadārāṇyaka Upaniṣad) O chief of the Bhāratas, know that whatever you see in existence, both the moving and the nonmoving, is only a combination of the field of activities and the knower of the field. (BG [13.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/13.27)) An example is given. Bubbles do not arise from either water or air alone but by their combination. In this way it is explained that the jīva is unborn, possesses birth, and has its karma activated because of the combination with the body, a transformation of prakṛti. Their birth arises from you, the source of their śakti. Thus, the jīvas, having those upādhis, with various names and qualities, merge into you, the possessor of the śaktis, during each creation. Merging of the jīvas is of two types: on liberation and after the universe is destroyed. An example is given of the first: rivers merging in the ocean. An example of the second is flavors merging in honey. The first is understood from the context. These śrutis are: One jīva serves unborn prakṛti which is red (rajas), white (sattva) and black (tamas), and which creates many forms similar to it. Another entity (the Lord), gives up prakṛti, which has been enjoyed. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) One is the jīva and the other is the Lord. Just as rivers flowing into the ocean, giving up names and forms (colors), disappear, so the man in knowledge, liberated from names and forms attains the attractive Supreme Lord. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) In liberation only the upādhis are merged into prakṛti, the śakti of the Lord. The liberated jīva attains the attractive Lord. It is not that this example says “the jīva becomes nondifferent from the Lord who is aimed at,” since there is no oneness, though the rivers are not perceived individually, like a handful of sesame thrown in a pile of sesame. Thus Yamunā remains different from the seven seas. Actually it is an example showing that the liberated jīva sees the Lord in liberation. It is like bees seeming to merge in flowers. Handsome one! Bees produce honey. Gathering juices from trees from different directions, they make it one as honey. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) Bees produce (nistiṣṭhanti) honey. Gathering juices from various trees ripened in various ways (atyayānām) they produce one essence. The essences do not distinguish and think “I am the essence of that tree. I am the essence of that tree.” Handsome one! Similarly, all the living beings merging in the Lord are not aware “We have merged in the Lord.” (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) In every creation, the gross upādhis alone merge but not the subtle upādhis too. To illustrate the example of the bee is given. Just as the drops of honey of flowers, being situated in the final honey, do not distinguish themselves, similarly the jīvas though merged in Brahman with prakṛti do not know you, though you are different from them, since their knowledge is restricted.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**The wise souls who understand how your māyā deludes all human beings perform bhakti which produces joy at every moment to you who stop birth and death. How can fear of material life affect your faithful servants? On the other hand, your furrowing eyebrows—the triple-rimmed wheel of time—repeatedly terrify those who refuse to take shelter of you.**

**Комментарий:**

Those with devotion for you, the cause of the universe, have no fear of time. Some śrutis praise the Lord in this way. Among those men who think they are learned, described in the last two verses, those who have developed wisdom from guru, understanding various false philosophies produced by your māyā, perform (vidadhati) bhakti (bhāvam) according to rules to you, who destroy saṁsāra (abhave). That bhakti produces joy at every moment (anuprabhavam). “How does this make one fearless of death?” How can fear of death affect those wise persons since the wheel of time with three spokes of hot, cold and rain, in the form of your frown, constantly creates fear only for those who do not surrender to you. These śrutis are: To they who always diligently worship Lord’s transcendental form without any trace of material motivation, the Lord, in his form as a cowherd boy (gopa-rūpaḥ), shows his lotus feet. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) Tadaiva indicates that such a person quickly becomes fearless.

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**The mind is like an impetuous horse that even persons who have regulated their senses and breath cannot control. People in this world who try to tame the uncontrolled mind but who abandon the feet of their spiritual master encounter hundreds of obstacles in their cultivation of various distressful practices. O unborn Lord, they are like merchants on a boat in the ocean who have failed to employ a helmsman.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis praise the Lord, stating that without devotion to the ācāryas one cannot attain Kṛṣṇa. O unconquerable one! Not taking shelter of the feet of guru who is your devotee, people attempt to control the mind which is uncontrolled (adānta), like a wild horse, by conquering the senses and prāṇas through strength of yoga practice and become frustrated in trying to control. They become overwhelmed by many types of suffering (vyasana) and remain in saṁsāra (iha). They are like merchants in the ocean, who have not accepted a helmsman. One conquers this ocean by the mercy of guru. These śrutis are: A person who has an ācārya knows that the Lord is here. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) To understand thoroughly about God, one must humbly approach, with firewood in his hands, a spiritual master who is learned in the Vedas and firmly devoted to the Supreme Lord. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) One who has unflinching devotion to the Supreme Lord and as much devotion to the spiritual master as he has for the Supreme Lord, to that great soul all the purports of the scriptures that have been spoken become revealed. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad)

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**To those persons who take shelter of you, full of knowledge and bliss, the embodiment of all spiritual pleasure, what further use have such devotees for their servants, children or bodies, their wives, money or houses, their land, good health or conveyances? And for those who fail to appreciate the truth about you and go on pursuing the pleasures of sex, what could there be in this entire world—a place inherently doomed to destruction and devoid of significance—that could give them real happiness?**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis praise the Lord, stating that he is attained by niṣkāmabhakti, not by sakāma-bhakti. When you are necessarily obtained as the highest goal for the person among men (nṛṇām) who takes shelter of you, of what use are good servants, good sons, healthy body (ātmā), chaste wife, many jewels, attractive houses, fertile land, healthy prāṇas and chariots decorated with bells and gems, which are desired? They are of no use at all. You are personification of all-pervading consciousness and bliss (ātmani) and produce all happiness (sarva-rase). For persons who do not know the glorious object (sad ajānatām), who act for sexual pleasure in uniting with women (mithunataḥ), what object such as good servants, etc., can make them happy in this world (iha)? Nothing. Certainly (nu), this world is self-destructing (sva-vihite), being devoured by time, and its greatness is negated by itself (sva-nirasta-bhage), since it transforms at every moment. In the other reading—sva-vihitaḥ and sva-nirasta-bhagaḥ—they are the two modifiers of good servants, etc. These śrutis are: Bhakti is the process of worshiping the Supreme Lord. It consists of fixing one’s mind upon him by renouncing material desires for enjoyment in this world and the next. Indeed, this negates karma. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) Bhakti consisting of hearing, chanting, etc., which are famous in Purāṇas is called worship of Kṛṣṇa (asya). It arises by renouncing desire for results other than Kṛṣṇa (nairāśyena). It is a form of bhāva through which the mind is offered. This bhakti is naiṣkarmyam. The word naiṣkarmya is formed by the suffix ṣyañ which is used in the meaning of its own sense. It destroys the bondage of karma or it is not covered by smarta-karmas (naiṣkarmyam).

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Sages free from false pride live on this earth by frequenting the sacred pilgrimage sites. Because such devotees keep your lotus feet within their hearts, the water that washes their feet destroys all sins. Having turned their minds toward you, the ever-blissful soul of all existence, they no longer dedicate themselves to serving family life at home, which simply robs a man of his good qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis praise the Lord, saying that the Lord is attained quickly by those possessing niṣkāma-bhakti and who are detached. Those who see bhakti-tattva (ṛṣayaḥ) who live in pure tīrthas on earth like Puṣkara or in your abodes such as Mathurā (sadanāni), quickly attain you. Their pride in learning, etc., has gone away (vimadāḥ). They meditate on your lotus feet in their hearts. Their foot water purifies the universe, destroying all sin (agha-bhit). They do not serve the houses, typified by servants, sons, healthy body and wife. What to speak of them, even those who, due to association of devotees, once concentrate their minds on you, the personification of all-pervading consciousness (ātmani), eternal happiness (nitya-sukhe) even they do not again take shelter of (upāsate) the houses which are places which steal away the essence of humans—knowledge, renunciation, etc. These śrutis are: One who worships my deity form nondifferent from me while living in the district of Mathurā or, indeed, anywhere in Jambūdvīpa, becomes most dear to me in this world. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) Meditating on me in Mathurā with attention, one quickly becomes free of obstacles to attaining me. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad)

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**The universe arises from the real Lord. If one claims the world is also the Lord, that claim cannot be true since it is illogical. Sometimes objects in the world are very different from the Lord. Some say the world is illusory but it is not. The Lord also is not illusory or the cause of illusion. The illusory world is imaginary. But real objects are desired for transacting in the world. The theory of illusions is insubstantial like a series of blind men. The words of the Vedas with their meanings also bewilder persons whose senses are dulled by the sacrificial mantras.**

**Комментарий:**

“But how is it that houses steal away the essence of human life? In verses such as yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante: everything comes from the Lord (Taittirīya Upaniṣad), since houses arise from you who are composed of consciousness alone, they could be of the same nature like gold transforming into gold bangles. Thus the world is not some superimposition (falsity) on Brahman. The root jan (jāyante) is not used in the sense of superimposition. But the world is also not identical with you for that would contradict the instructions regarding renouncing the world. One should thus use another type of logic. The world is not identical with you and not a superimposition on Brahman. But it is temporary.” Saying this, some śrutis praise the Lord for being the cause of the universe which is different from him. Repeating the opposition’s view while stating their opinion, they deny complete oneness. This universe (idam) arose from you (sataḥ), who is consciousness alone, who is described as the cause (sataḥ) by the word sat (real) in sad eva saumya idam agra āsīt: O gentle one! This universe was real (as cause) previously. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) But if one claims that the universe is absolutely identical with the Lord (sat), that is not true. O Lord (nu)! That proposition is refuted by logic (tarka-hatam). By mention of ablative case (sataḥ), there is difference because one can see two states in the form of the cause and effect in the example of gold bangle arising from a gold nugget. The universe arises from you just as an elephant arises from a desire tree. Thus the universe is also different from you. This is then described. Sometimes the similarity between desire tree and elephant fails and only difference is perceived. Since the universe does not have all the same qualities as the Lord, it is established that the universe is not identical with the Lord. “Why is the world not a superimposition on Brahman like seeing shell as silver since otherwise it would contradict statements like sad eva saumya idam ?” Sometimes due to illusion, silver is superimposed on shell (i.e. shell is wrongly thought to be silver) but not always and neither does silver arise from shell. Actually everything arises from the Lord according to yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante. “But even the scriptures should speak of the origin of the universe as a superimposition.” You cannot be definitely connected with either the object of superimposition or the agent of superimposition (ubhaya-yuk) since there is no agent of superimposition, and superimposition on something which cannot be perceived is impossible (since the object of superimposition is false). Or kva ca mrṣā na tathobhaya-yug means: it is not false, both are real. Though silver perceived on shell is false, the existence of cause and effect is not false just like the existence of pot and cloth. The author of Vedānta sūtras states that independent existence—which is described in the two śruti statements, viśvaṁ satyaṁ: the universe is real (Ṛg Veda) and tat satyam: the Lord is real (Ṛg Veda)—exists in both: The effect is non-different from the cause because the effect exists in the cause even before manifesting. (Brahma-sūtra) “But due to simplicity let there be only one existence of the Lord. By that even the universe would be perceived as real.” For the sake of the omniscient Lord’s actions like maintaining the universe (vyavahṛtaye), the different states in the form of cause and effect, of the one possessor of śaktis is approved (iṣitaḥ). Otherwise the universe being created by the omniscient would be contradicted. A bangle made of the illusory silver of the shell cannot be maintained or worn. Or the different states are desirable for actions like carrying water (vyavahṛtaye). By the state of the pot made of clay one can carry water. Similarly, Lord’s another state (the universe) is fruitful. “But due to the śruti statement, akṣayyaṁ ha vai cāturmāsya-yājinaḥ sukṛtaṁ bhavati: the puṇya of the performer of cāturmāsya sacrifice is indestructible (Āpastamba Śrauta Sūtra, Kṛṣṇa Yajur Veda), and since it is inferred that the universe does not lack this nature of indestructibility (i.e. the universe is indestructible) according to the logic yaḥ kalpaḥ sa kalpa-pūrvaḥ: this kalpa is the previous kalpa (day of Brahmā) (quoted in Mimāṁsā-nyāya-prakāśa) how is it that houses steal away the essence of human life?” These words of the Vedas (bhāratī) bewilder karmīs with secondary interpretation of words (uru-vṛttibhiḥ). The words bewilder by erroneous conclusions. These people have great faith in karmas due to special mantras recited in sacrifices. “How is there error in the conclusion regarding the Vedas received from gurus in paramparā?” Just as blind people lead by blind people fall into a hole, persons taught by persons having erroneous conclusions become bewildered. Otherwise, śruti statements about destruction of the universe would be contradicted. These śrutis are: As a spider produces a web from his body and then withdraws it, as plants grow from the earth, and as body hairs arise from a man, so this universe arises from the imperishable. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) The word akṣara (imperishable) indicates that the Lord is different from matter.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**If the universe were not created after destruction, it could not be said that it came from you. After destruction and during maintenance, it exists in you, who remain pure. It appears false to others, by imagining it to be made of illusory objects. Those who speak these mental concoctions and those claim that the world is completely non-different from you are fools.**

**Комментарий:**

“The similarity of Brahman and the universe, like gold and a particle of gold has been stated in verse 26. But their difference like a desire tree being different from an elephant (which is produced from the desire tree) has been stated in verse 37. That cannot be. Before the creation of the universe, the universe did not exist. Asad vā idaṁ agra āsīt: The universe was previously asat (unreal). (Taittirīya Upaniṣad)” In reply to this objection, some śrutis praise the Lord while confirming what was already said (that the universe was real previously). Asat here means subtle (i.e. unmanifest, it does not mean ‘unreal’). This universe did not exist previous to creation and will no longer exist after its annihilation. But only between these two it is an object of knowledge (mitam). It shines falsely within you, who remain as pure consciousness (ekarase). The universe is inferred to exist (as illusion) in Brahman by the method of “snake in rope and silver on shell.” The truth (ṛtam) is that this universe is a useless mental exercise (vitathta-manovilāsam) — fools conclude in this way. The wise however conclude that the universe is the effect of your śakti and, like you, is real in all three aspects of time. The one Lord with his own purpose, by his śakti produces many forms of great variety. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) This universe was real previously. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) This world was created as a reality by Paramātmā. He is omniscient, controlling the minds of all, the best and independent. Such a Lord has created real objects eternally. (Īśopaniṣad) Yāthātathyataḥ means real. Tathya means real according to Halāyudha kośa. Therefore the statement: “the universe created by the Lord is real. Those who say it is unreal are fools,” is well said. Since even minds are included in the universe, the perception that the universe is imaginary is also illusory. The śrutis which say this have been shown.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**The jīva contacts matter by the influence of māyā, takes on similar form due to upādhis, and enjoys material objects. He thus experiences saṁsāra. You, however, avoid the material energy in the same way that a snake abandons its old skin. Glorious in your possession of eight qualities, you display unlimited greatness.**

**Комментарий:**

Some śrutis praise the Lord saying that the jīva is dependent whereas the Lord is independent, thought they are both situated within prakṛti. From when, by ignorance in the form of beginningless aversion (ajayā) the jīva, agitated by desire for material enjoyment, embraced (anuśayīta) māyā (ajām), which bestows things favorable for that enjoyment, then onwards, endowed (juṣan) with body and senses (guṇān), it takes on similar form (of matter) and qualities (sarūpatāṁ). Because of that, after this (anu), his eight auspicious qualities covered (apeta-bhagaḥ), he accepts saṁsāra (mṛtyum). He again and again takes birth and death. But you are devoid (jahāsi) of māyā, since you are devoid of relationship of dependence on her, like a snake and its skin. This shows that the Lord is extremely indifferent to her. The Lord of the millions of kāmadhenus (desire fulfilling cows) has no need of māyā. You are eternally endowed with your eight qualities (ātta-bhagaḥ). This is supported by the next sentence. You are worshipped (mahīyase) with your eight eternal qualities in your self-manifesting form which is impossible to be covered by māyā, and in which the eight eternal qualities are without distinction. It is not that your qualities are just eight alone since they are unlimited (aparimeya) since it is said in Viṣṇu Purāṇa: The Lord is endowed with unlimited auspicious qualities. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) These śrutis are: Two companion birds sit together in the shelter of the same pippala tree. One of them is relishing the taste of the tree’s berries while the other refrains from eating and instead watches over his friend. (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad) Dvā stands for dvau (two) according to the rule supāṁ suluk (Pāṇini 7.1.39). The dual ending au is replaced by ḍā. Suparṇā means two birds. The two are similar because they accept and give up various residing places (i.e. bodies). But one bird is situated as the enjoyer while the other as the cause of the other bird to enjoy. They are united, devoid of mutual hostility (sayujā). The tree is the body and the fruit is the result of karma.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**Members of the renounced order who fail to uproot the last traces of material desire in their hearts remain impure, and thus you do not allow them to understand you. Although you are present within their hearts, because they have other interests, for them you are like a jewel worn around the neck, but which is totally forgotten. O Lord, those who practice yoga only for sense gratification are deprived of enjoyment and the bliss of your association since they continue to suffer and to not become attracted to your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why is the constant companion (of Paramātmā i.e. the jīva) never liberated?” You are not attained even by yoga devoid of niṣkāmabhakti of hearing, etc., about you. In this way some śrutis praise the Lord. O Lord! Even sannyāsīs (yatayaḥ), if they do not uproot the desires for enjoyment (kāma-jaṭāḥ) in the heart, then you are hard to attain for them, who are contaminated with pride in their fourth āśrama and yoga (asatām), though you are in their hearts, and thus their companion. “How so?” You are like a jewel worn around the neck, but which is totally forgotten, just like a jewel, though situated on the neck is forgotten at the time of absorption in material desires, etc. Because they forget you, they do not attain liberation. Not only that, but anarthas appear. Without bhakti, the sannyāsa, etc., becomes a livelihood for the yogīs dedicated to satisfying their prāṇas on the pretext of practicing sannyāsa and yoga. Such people suffer in this life and the next (ubhayatra). The suffering of this life is described. They suffer in this life due to troubles in the form of admiration from others, earning money, enjoyable objects and clothing, which have not ceased (anapagatāntakāt). The suffering of next life is described. They suffer because they do not become favorable to your lotus feet (nādhirūdha-padāt) since they neglect you. These śrutis are: Even a renunciant, if he maintains any worldly desires and thinks he should be worshipped, he will be forced by his karmic reactions to take birth again and again in various circumstances. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) Manyamānaḥ means he is a proud sannyāsī who thinks, “I am worshippable for I am greatly intelligent.”

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**When a person realizes you, he no longer cares about his good and bad fortune arising from past pious and sinful acts, since it is you alone who control this good and bad fortune. Such a realized devotee also disregards what ordinary living beings say about him. Every day he fills his ears with your glories, which are recited in each age by the unbroken succession of Manu’s descendants, and thus you become his ultimate goal. You are the shelter of even liberation.**

**Комментарий:**

For the devotees who know you as their Lord, who are fixed in your bhakti, their sin which causes downfall perishes and he still attains you. Some śrutis praise the Lord in this way. Your devotee, who knows your svarūpa and qualities, does not know the connection with good and bad qualities of the pious and sinful prārabdha-karmas (bhavad-uttha-śubhāśubhayoḥ), which are still maintained by you like burnt cloth by your desire to preach the sampradāya of bhakti, though they are mostly burned up by the fire of knowing you. He does not consider opinions offered by others related to his good qualities such as compassion and good conduct, or his bad qualities such as anger and attachment to material enjoyment. At that time, he does not know the words of praise or criticism (giraḥ) of living beings (deha-bhṛtām) either. “Why does he not know?” O lord, ocean of host of qualities such as omniscience and mercy (saguṇa)! The reason is that you fill up his ears daily by the flow of the chanting of qualities of you who appear in every yuga, which is carried by saintly people. You are the giver of prema (apavargagatiḥ) according to Fifth Canto. These śrutis are: I am the object of all worship. Even if the residents of that place fail to properly cultivate the religious principles that one should observe in the holy land, they still become devoted to me just by virtue of living there. Even if Kali \[the present age of quarrel\] has them in his grip, they still get credit for living in this place. My devotee who lives in Mathurā is just as dear to me as you \[Brahmā\] and your sons—Rudra and his followers—and Goddess Śrī and my own self. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) The Lord purifies them of sins which have occurred by fate and accepts them as devotees.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Because you are unlimited, neither the lords of heaven nor even you yourself can ever reach the end of your glories. The countless universes, each enveloped in its shell, are compelled by the wheel of time to wander within you, like particles of dust blowing about in the sky. The śrutis, following their method of eliminating everything separate from the Supreme, become successful by revealing you as their final conclusion.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way hearing the Lord’s svarūpa, qualites and powers and the futility of various sādhānas according to the opinion of those who are averse to and inclined to the Lord, some śrutis describing the indivisibility of his svarūpa, qualities and powers, summarize their prayer. Eva indicates collection. Even all devatās such as Brahmā put together cannot reach your limit. What to speak of others, even you, who are omniscient, omnipotent, who are without beginning or end, do not reach your limit. “Then how is it that I am omniscient and omnipotent?” Because you have no end (anantatayā). Not knowing a rabbit’s horn (which does not exist) does not destroy your omniscience and not obtaining a rabbit’s horn does not destroy your omnipotence. The unlimited nature is shown. The universes are within you. Oh (nanu)! The collection of universes with their seven coverings, each ten times thicker than the previous covering, wander about within you simultaneously along with the wheel of time (vayasā) not one after the other, like dust particles in the sky. But your form is of medium size. Such is your greatness. Because of this (yat) the śrutis bear fruit in you: they possess meaning by direct connotation (mukhya-vṛtti) due to abundance of pravṛtti-nimittas. “How do the śrutis express my unlimited nature?” They show that you have qualities such as truthfulness, that you have a real svarūpa by rejecting what is opposite. Brahman is real, conscious and unlimited. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) Brahman is consciousness and bliss. (Taittirīya Upaniṣad) They completely reject similarity of the Lord with conscious or unconscious objects: It is different from what is known and it is different from what is not known. (Kena Upaniṣad) It is not big or small, not short or long. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad) They reject that he can be measured: The lord is great, infinite, boundless, condensed consciousness. (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka Upaniṣad) In this way they conclude in you (nidhanaṁ) by direct connotation (mukhya-vṛtti). These śrutis have been shown. In this way the group of eighteen śrutis glorified Kṛṣṇa.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord, Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi, said: Having heard these instructions about the Supreme Lord, the sons of Brahmā now understood their final goal. They felt perfectly satisfied and honored Sanandana with their worship.**

**Комментарий:**

Having heard the teachings about the Supreme Lord, the explanation of verse two, they understood their goal, the Supreme Lord (ātmanaḥ gatim).

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**Thus the ancient saints who travel in the upper heavens distilled this nectarean and confidential essence of all the Vedas and Purāṇas.**

**Комментарий:**

The sages distilled the essence of unlimited scriptures: the prayers of the śrutis (rasaḥ).

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**And as you wander the earth at will, dear son of Brahmā, you should faithfully meditate on these instructions concerning the Lord, which burn up the material desires of all men.**

**Комментарий:**

O son of Brahmā (brahma-dāyāda)! Carry (dhārayan) these instructions in your heart.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi ordered him in this way, the sage Nārada, with strong vows and peaceful heart, who hearing once remembered everything, who was fixed in the Lord, accepted the command with firm faith in the teachings. Now successful in all his purposes, O King, he replied to the Lord as follows.**

**Комментарий:**

Receiving the teachings from Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi, Nārada felt satisfied (pūrṇaḥ). He kept the teachings that he heard in his mind (śrutidharaḥ). He was a naiṣṭhika brahmacārī (vīra-vrataḥ).

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**Nārada said: I offer my obeisances to him of spotless fame, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who contains within himself attractive avatāras so that all living beings can extinguish suffering.**

**Комментарий:**

Nārada, having heard the śrutis’ prayers, by taking support of the verse beginning striya urugendra (verse 23), determining that all the śrutis conclude in Kṛṣṇa, the Svayam Bhagavān, he offers respects to him. Since he does not use tubhyam (to you) but tasmai, he considers respect to his teacher Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi to be included in respect to Kṛṣṇa. I offer respects to Kṛṣṇa who is glorified in the śrutis and smṛtis: Therefore, Kṛṣṇa is the supreme being. One should meditate on him, experience his sweetness, worship him and serve him. (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad) Kṛṣṇa is the complete form of Bhagavān. (SB [1.3.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/3.28)) He is the cause of the jīva’s knowledge of oneself and the Supreme Lord (akuṇṭha-medhase). He manifests (dhatte) his attractive (uśatīḥ) svāṁśas (kalāḥ) such as you for liberating (abhavāya) all beings. Present tense indicates an eternal condition. Those who are inquisitive should see Siddhānta-ratnam for particular deliberations in this regard.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**After saying this, Nārada bowed down to Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi, the foremost of sages, and also to his saintly disciples. He then immediately returned directly to the hermitage of my father, Dvaipāyana Vyāsa.**

**Комментарий:**

In this way, or after offering respects to Kṛṣṇa (iti), he bowed to Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi. From Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi’s hermitage he went directly to my father’s (Vyāsa’s) hermitage. Śukadeva appeared from the semen of Vyāsa after it somehow fell on aranī when Vyāsa was churning the sticks for making a fire. This is mentioned in Mahābhārata.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**Vyāsadeva, the incarnation of the Lord, respectfully greeted Nārada Muni and offered him a seat, which he accepted. Nārada then described to Vyāsa what he had heard from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi.**

**Комментарий:**

Bhagavatā means “by my father.”

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**Thus I have replied to the question you asked me, O King, concerning how the mind can have access to the Lord, who is indescribable by material words and devoid of material qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

The words anirdeśya and nirguṇa were previously explained (verse 1). The mind should be fixed in śruti.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**He is the Lord who eternally watches over this universe, before, during and after its manifestation. He is the master of both the unmanifest material energy and the spirit soul. After sending forth the creation he enters within it, accompanying each living entity. There he creates the material bodies and then remains as their regulator. By surrendering to him the jīva covered with upādhis can escape the embrace of illusion, just as a dreaming person forgets his own body. One who wants liberation from fear should constantly meditate upon this Lord, who destroys māyā by his pure svarūpa and gives freedom from fear.**

**Комментарий:**

Accepting the meaning of the prayers of the śrutis, Śukadeva makes Parīkṣit remember the Lord. Creating intelligence and senses for the jīvas, which have minute impressions for the sādhanas of karma, etc., which are merged in me and which at the end of the merging have awakened desires for enjoyment, I will again and again inspire them. Mercifully he glances (utprekṣakaḥ) at the universe to accomplish this. He is eternal, for he exists at the beginning, middle and end of the universe. He is the controller of the world made of māyā and jīva. Having created the universe, he enters it and makes bodies (puraḥ) through Brahmā (ṛṣiṇā). He puts those bodies under governance (śāsti). The jīva, who is left with his remaining karmas after he has experienced them (anuśayī), coming to the world, taking shelter of the Lord by devotee association (sampadya), gives up māyā (ajām). By surrender to the Lord, the saṁsāra stops. “But the body of the surrendered person can still be seen. How then has māyā been defeated?” Just as when sleeping one does not see the body (kulāyam), the surrendered devotee too does not notice his body. The body which follows the devotee like a burnt rope, does not affect him. One should meditate on attractive Kṛṣṇa (harim) who destroys birth, the cause of bondage, by just absorption in him (kaivalyanirasta-yonim) even for demons. Those who saw Kṛṣṇa on the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra attained their original forms after death. (SB [1.9.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/9.39)) Dhyāyed indicates prescription. One should meditate in such a way that there is no fear (abhayam). One should meditate giving up fear of time and hostile people. He who drank Yaśodā’s milk and became Arjuna’s chariot driver is full with his qualities. That has been sung here and is supreme.

## Chapter 88 - Lord Śiva Saved from Vṛkāsura

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**King Parīkṣit said: Those among devatās, demons and humans who worship Śiva, a strict renunciant, usually enjoy wealth and sense gratification, while the worshipers of the Supreme Lord, the husband of the goddess of fortune, do not.**

**Комментарий:**

In the eighty-eighth chapter, it is glorified that the devotee of Viṣṇu becomes liberated and the devotees of devatās attain powers. Though he knew that the wealth of Dhruva, Ambarīṣa and other devotees, which was given by the Lord is unlimited, the king asks this question to destroy the doubts of those who see with materialistic vision. Śiva is perceived as inauspicious (aśivam) since he stays in a crematorium, wears ashes and skulls. Those who worship Śiva among the devatās, etc., attain enjoyment (bhojāḥ). Those who worship the husband of Lakṣmī do not enjoy. Why?

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**We wish to properly understand this matter, which greatly 496 Vaiṣṇavānandinī \[Ch.88 puzzles us. Indeed, the results attained by the worshipers of these two lords of opposite characters are contrary to what one would expect.**

**Комментарий:**

Those who worship Śiva, a beggar, attain wealth. Those who worship Viṣṇu, the husband of goddess of fortune, become beggars. This is not logical. The possessive (viruddha-śīlayoḥ prabhvoḥ) indicates the accusative case.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Śukadeva said: Śiva is always united with his personal energy, the material nature. Manifesting himself in three features in response to the entreaties of nature’s three modes, he thus embodies the threefold principle of material ego in goodness, passion and ignorance.**

**Комментарий:**

I give those persons firm faith in those devatās whose forms they desire to worship faithfully. (BG [7.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.21)) According to this statement of Gītā, the devotees of Śiva and others are given results for their worship by Viṣṇu, situated within those devatās. But those results are temporary and do not end in liberation. But such results, given by Viṣṇu to his pure devotees, are different. His fame of giving wealth, like not giving two or three when one can give millions, is due to his giving the great result, liberation. With this intention Śukadeva begins to speak. Śiva is endowed with the śakti of prakṛti consisting of three guṇas as upādhi. When the guṇas are agitated, he accepts the three guṇas as upādhis (tri-liṅgaḥ). He becomes covered by those guṇas (saṁvṛtaḥ) which request him to accept them. But he is not bound up forcibly like jīvas since he represents Viṣṇu. “Then why is tamas his upādhi?” There are three types of ahaṅkāra (aham) starting with vaikārika. Thus he, their supervisor, is also threefold. Tamas is most prominent in him and the other two are secondary.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**The sixteen elements have evolved as transformations of that false ego. When a devotee of Śiva worships his manifestation in any one of these elements, the devotee obtains all sorts of corresponding enjoyable opulences.**

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Lord Hari, however, has no connection with the material modes. He is the Supreme Lord, the all-seeing eternal witness, who is transcendental to material nature. One who worships him becomes similarly free from the material modes.**

### Text 6

**Перевод:**

**Your grandfather, King Yudhiṣṭhira, after completing his Aśvamedha sacrifices, asked Acyuta this very same question while hearing the Lord’s explanation of dharma.**

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**This question pleased Kṛṣṇa, the king’s Lord and master, who had descended into the family of Yadu for the purpose of bestowing the highest good on all men. The Lord replied as follows as the king eagerly listened.**

### Text 8

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: If I especially favor someone, I gradually deprive him of his wealth. Then the relatives and friends of such a poverty-stricken man abandon him. In this way he suffers one distress after another.**

**Комментарий:**

I will take away the wealth gradually of the person whom I want to bring to me quickly (anugṛhṇāmi), who is without material desires and has wealth. The genitive (yasya) indicates accusative. Future is used to express intolerance (hariṣye) according to anavakḷptyamarṣayor akiṁvṛtte ’pi. (Pāṇini 3.3.145) I take away his wealth, not tolerating it. If I take it away suddenly, he will be greatly disturbed. By taking it away gradually he becomes indifferent and takes pleasure in the association of devotees. Thus his relatives reject him, a poor person. He suffers grief after grief. This is public perception of him.

### Text 9

**Перевод:**

**When he becomes detached from attempts to make money and instead befriends my devotees, I bestow my special mercy (such as giving wealth) upon him.**

**Комментарий:**

Though driven by the desire to seek wealth at the insistence of relatives, futile in his attempts by my mercy when he becomes detached (nirviṇṇaḥ), then I quickly show mercy in the form of bringing him close to me for the person who has made friends with devotees (mat-paraiḥ). The future expresses the present since it is close to the present.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**I give mercy which is indescribable, the greatest, hard to understand, eternal, arising from my spiritual śakti. (Understanding this, he is freed from the cycle of material life.)**

**Комментарий:**

The mercy is described. It is Brahman. It is a form of pure consciousness (cin-mātram). It is glorious (sat) and unlimited (anantakam). The mercy, like Brahman, is identical with the Lord since it is eternal, etc. The second line (beginning with vijñāya) is a later insertion (and not accepted in the sampradāya).

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Because I am difficult to worship, people generally avoid me and instead worship other deities, who are quickly satisfied. When people receive kingly wealth from these deities, they ignore rules, intoxicated with pride and become neglectful. They dare to offend even the devatās who have bestowed benedictions upon them.**

**Комментарий:**

Because they do not attain wealth, people who have material desires reject me and worship Śiva and others (anyān). I am difficult to worship since they do not know how to worship me and think that I give results without considering properly. Actually, I am easy to worship since worship can be done by offering easily available leaves and flowers. “But one hears of and sees some wealthy devotees.” I give indestructible great opulence to devotees like Dhruva who want a kingdom and Ambarīṣa who want service. And after they have enjoyed that, I gave closeness to me. By that people’s indifference to my worship is removed. This would not be possible by taking away the wealth of devotees. “Is the suffering of niṣkāma devotees caused by karma or by the Lord? It cannot be karma since it is almost burned up by the fire of tattva-jñāna. It cannot be the Lord since this would mean the Lord is merciless.” The cause of the suffering is the Lord. When a person realizes you, he no longer cares about his good and bad fortune arising from past pious and sinful acts, since it is you alone who control this good and bad fortune. (SB [10.87.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/87.40)) “What is the result of the Lord giving suffering?” It is for the benefit of the devotee. The father, though affectionate, opening the wound of his son, puts medicinal salt on it. Taking away enjoyments, he makes his son take up troublesome studies. He acts for the son’s benefit. The Lord acts similarly. One should not say that seeing the devotee suffering, the Lord lacks good qualities. The devotee does not actually suffer. He no longer cares about his good and bad fortune arising from past pious and sinful acts, since it is you alone who control this good and bad fortune. (SB [10.87.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/87.40)) One sees this in the story of Prahlāda. “Then what is the purpose of such actions of the Lord?” Only the Lord knows. Bhīṣma says: O King, no one can know the plan of the Lord. (SB [1.9.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/9.16)) The knowers of truth conclude that the purpose is increase of prema for Lord and by that his joy and eternal closeness to him. Becoming proud without restriction due to devatās who are easily satisfied, giving without considering who is qualified or unqualified, becoming careless, they forget the devatās who gave benedictions and even if somehow remembered offend them.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and others are able to curse or bless one. Śiva and Brahmā are very quick to curse or bestow benedictions, my dear King, but the infallible Supreme Lord is not.**

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**In this connection, an ancient historical account is related concerning how the Lord of Kailāsa Mountain was put into danger by offering a choice of benedictions to the demon Vṛka.**

**Комментарий:**

The danger is explained next.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**The demon named Vṛka, a son of Śakuni, once met Nārada on the road. The wicked fellow asked him which of the three chief gods could be pleased most quickly.**

**Комментарий:**

Vṛka was the son of Śakuni.

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**Nārada told him: Worship Śiva and you will soon achieve success. He quickly becomes pleased by seeing his worshipper’s slightest good qualities—and quickly angered by seeing his slightest fault.**

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**He became pleased with ten-headed Rāvaṇa, and also with Bāṇa, when they each chanted his glories, like bards in a royal court. Śiva then bestowed unprecedented power upon each of them, but in both cases he was consequently beset with great difficulty.**

**Комментарий:**

You should not say, “If that is so (that he becomes angry quickly), I fear him.” He cannot do anything to you who are powerful due to the boon. Examples are given. Śiva encountered serious difficulty from Rāvaṇa’s uprooting his residence on Kailāsa-parvata, and because of the service of having to guard Bāṇāsura’s capital.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Thus advised, the demon proceeded to worship Śiva at Kedāranātha by taking pieces of flesh from his own body and offering them as oblations into the sacred fire, which is Śiva’s mouth.**

**Комментарий:**

He worshipped (upādhāvat) Śiva with his own body. “How?” By his flesh he worshipped Śiva who has fire as his mouth. He sacrificed his flesh for Śiva into the fire, since it is the mouth of all devatās, at Śiva’s abode called Kedāra.

### Text 18-19

**Перевод:**

**Vṛkāsura became frustrated after failing to obtain a vision of the lord. Finally, on the seventh day, after dipping his hair into the holy waters at Kedāranātha and leaving it wet, he took up a hatchet and prepared to cut off his head. But at that very moment the supremely merciful Śiva rose up out of the sacrificial fire, looking like the god of fire himself, and grabbed both arms of the demon to stop him from killing himself, just as an ordinary person would do. By Śiva’s touch, Vṛkāsura once again became whole.**

**Комментарий:**

Not seeing or attaining the presence of Śiva (upalabdhim), he began to cut off his head with a sword (sudhitinā). Śiva rose from the fire like the fire god and stopped him, just as we would stop a person who wants to kill himself because of suffering. By Śiva’s touch, Vṛka’s body became whole again.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Śiva said to him: My friend, please stop, stop! Ask from me whatever you want, and I will bestow that boon upon you. Alas, you have subjected your body to great torment for no reason, since I am pleased with a simple offering of water from those who approach me for shelter.**

**Комментарий:**

There is no purpose in cutting off your head (alam). Repetition of alam is due to perplexity.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**The benediction sinful Vṛka chose from Śiva would terrify all living beings. Vṛka said, “May death come to whomever I touch upon the head with my hand.”**

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**Upon hearing this, Rudra seemed somewhat disturbed. Nonetheless, O descendant of Bharata, he vibrated oṁ to signify his assent, granting Vṛka the benediction with a smile, as if it were nectar.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiva seemed to become aggrieved (but did not actually become aggrieved), since the disturbance in his mind decreased on thinking that the Lord would find some remedy.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**To test Śiva’s benediction, the demon then tried to put his hand on Śiva’s head. Thus Śiva was frightened because of what he himself had done.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiva became afraid of the benediction he had given (sva-kṛtāt). It is said that the demon was greedy for Devī’s beauty and made attempts to obtain her.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**As the demon pursued him, Śiva fled swiftly, shaking with terror. He ran as far as the limits of the earth, the sky and the corners of the universe from the north.**

**Комментарий:**

Pursued by Vṛka, Śiva fled while trembling. He ran intently (udagāt) to the limits of the sky, earth and all directions from the north (udak, which is his abode).

### Text 25-26

**Перевод:**

**The great devatās could only remain silent, not knowing how to counteract the benediction. Then Śiva reached the luminous realm of Vaikuṇṭha, beyond all darkness, where the Supreme Nārāyaṇa is manifest. That realm is the destination of renunciates who have attained peace and given up all violence against other creatures. Going there, one never returns.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā and others did not know the remedy. Śiva went to Vaikuṇṭha called Śvetadvīpa which is in the milk ocean. It is beyond prakṛti (tamasaḥ) since it is an avatāra of Mahā-vaikuṇṭha like the Lord.

### Text 27-28

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord, who relieves his devotees’ distress, had seen Text 29\] Lord Śiva Saved from Vṛkāsura 507 from afar that Śiva was in danger. Thus by his mystic yogamāyā potency he assumed the form of a brahmacārī student, with the appropriate belt, deerskin, rod and prayer beads, and came before Vṛkāsura. The Lord’s effulgence glowed brilliantly like fire. Holding kuśa grass in his hand, he humbly greeted the demon.**

**Комментарий:**

He came in front of Vṛka as a brahmacārī. His power is described. He was like a glowing fire. Blessing the demon, he made the demon bow to him.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: My dear son of Śakuni, you appear tired. Why have you come such a great distance? Please rest for a minute. After all, it is one’s body that fulfills all one’s desires.**

**Комментарий:**

The body (ātmā) fulfills one’s desires (sarva-kāma-dhuk). Therefore, do not be pained by the fatigue of running.

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**O mighty one, please tell us what you intend to do, if we are qualified to hear it. Usually one accomplishes his purposes by taking help from others.**

**Комментарий:**

One strives for (samīhate) one’s goals by taking assistance of others (dhṛtaiḥ). Knowing what you have decided, I can help.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thus questioned by the Lord in language that poured down upon him like sweet nectar, Vṛka felt relieved of his fatigue. He described to the Lord everything he had done.**

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord said: If this is the case, we cannot believe what Śiva says. Śiva is the same lord of the Pretas and Piśācas whom Dakṣa cursed to become like a carnivorous hobgoblin.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiva was cursed to act like a piśāca (paiśācyam).

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**O best of the demons, if you have any faith in him because he is the guru of the universe, then without delay put your hand on your head and see what happens.**

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**If the words of Śiva prove untrue in any way, O best of the demons, then kill the liar so he may never lie again.**

**Комментарий:**

Kill him in such a way that a trust-worthy person will not again speak lies again (vaktānṛtam).

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**Thus bewildered by the Lord’s enchanting, artful words, foolish Vṛka, without realizing what he was doing, placed his hand on his head.**

**Комментарий:**

His mind was cheated by the words which were bewildering (citraiḥ) and superficially attractive (supeśalaiḥ) and he became forgetful (vismṛtaḥ).

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**Instantly his head shattered as if struck by a lightning bolt, and the demon fell down dead. From the sky were heard cries of “Victory!” “Obeisances!” and “Well done!”**

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**The celestial sages, Pitṛs and Gandharvas rained down flowers to celebrate the killing of sinful Vṛkāsura. Now Śiva was out of danger.**

**Комментарий:**

Śiva was freed from danger by Viṣṇu.

### Text 38-39

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord then addressed Śiva, who was now out of danger: “Just see, O Mahādeva, my lord, how this wicked man has been killed by his own sinful reactions. Indeed, what living being can hope for good fortune if he offends exalted saints, what to speak of offending the lord and guru of the universe?”**

**Комментарий:**

What the Lord said to Śiva is described. O Śiva, worshipped by the universe (deva), since you are the greatest of all devatās (mahādeva)! He was killed by his own sins, not by me. O Śiva, though you are capable of killing him (īśa), you did not kill him because you thought of him as your servant. What person who offends great devotees will be safe? No one will. What to speak of Vṛka, who offended you, guru of the universe. The Lord however due to being an ocean of good behavior, did not scold him saying, “You not foreseeing the consequences, did not consider danger to yourself for you gave even such a wicked benediction.”

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**The Lord is the directly manifest Absolute Truth, the Supreme Soul and unlimited ocean of inconceivable energies. Anyone who recites or hears this pastime of his saving Śiva will be freed from all enemies and the repetition of birth and death.**

**Комментарий:**

It is not astonishing that Viṣṇu delivered Śiva from danger since he is the Supreme Lord. The Lord is untouched by māyā, and is an ocean (udanvataḥ) of śakti of nonmaterial substance (avyākrṭa). Viṣṇu and his devotee, free of material guṇas experience happiness, whereas the master and servant, endowed with the guṇas experience great suffering.

## Chapter 89 - Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna Retrieve a Brāhmaṇa's Sons

### Text 1

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Once, O King, as a group of sages were performing a Vedic sacrifice on the banks of the Sarasvatī River, a controversy arose among them as to which of the three chief deities is supreme.**

**Комментарий:**

In the eighty-ninth chapter, the superiority of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva is tested and the greatness of Kṛṣṇa is shown by bringing back the brāhmaṇa’s sons. Śukadeva narrates another story to show that Viṣṇu should be worshipped since he is greater than others.

### Text 2

**Перевод:**

**Eager to resolve this question, O King, the sages sent Brahmā’s son Bhṛgu to find the answer. First he went to his father’s court.**

**Комментарий:**

To resolve the question of which lord is the greatest (tasya), they sent Bhṛgu. He was suitable to go because of his greatness which is described as maha-rṣiṇāṁ bhṛgur aham: Among sages I am Bhṛgu. (BG 10.25) He too went to his father to reveal that greatness.

### Text 3

**Перевод:**

**To test how well Lord Brahmā was situated in greatness, Bhṛgu failed to bow down to him or glorify him with prayers. The lord became angry at him, inflamed into fury by his own passion.**

**Комментарий:**

To test Brahmā’s greatness (sattva), he did not bow down or glorify him.

### Text 4

**Перевод:**

**Though anger toward his son was now rising within his heart, Brahmā was able to subdue it, in the same way that fire is extinguished by its own product, water.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmā controlled (aśīśamat) the anger towards his son in his mind (ātmani) which arose to kill him by himself, without his begging forgiveness, since he was capable of reflection (prabhuḥ), since he was born from Viṣṇu (ātma-bhūḥ). He thought as follows. “As my representative, he is a son since has arisen from me.” An example is given. Just as someone extinguishes fire by water, Brahmā existinguished his anger.

### Text 5

**Перевод:**

**Bhṛgu then went to Mount Kailāsa. There Śiva stood up and happily came forward to embrace his brother.**

**Комментарий:**

Having seen rajo-guṇa in Brahmā due to his mental offense in the form of direspect to him, Bhṛgu understanding that Brahmā failed the test, in order to test Śiva even more than Brahmā, committed a more serious offense by verbally insulting him. This is explained in two verses. Śiva is called Maheśvara because he is the controller of everyone’s ahaṅkāra.

### Text 6-7

**Перевод:**

**But Bhṛgu refused his embrace, telling him, “You are a deviant heretic.” At this Śiva became angry, and his eyes burned ferociously. He raised his trident and was about to kill Bhṛgu when Goddess Devī fell at his feet and spoke some words to pacify him. Bhṛgu then left that place and went to Vaikuṇṭha, where Janārdana resides.**

**Комментарий:**

He told Śiva that he followed an unauthorized path since he smears ashes from the graveyard on his body. Thus he did not want to embrace Śiva. Śiva became angry and took up his trident. Thus tamo-guṇa was seen in him. Understanding that Śiva failed the test, Bhṛgu, in order to test Viṣṇu even more, committed even bodily offense to Viṣṇu. He then went to Vaikuṇṭha above Satya-loka in the material world, manifested by the son of Vikuṇṭha (Vaikuṇṭha). It is Mahāvaikuṇṭha, the Lord’s expansion.

### Text 8-9

**Перевод:**

**There he went up to the Supreme Lord, who was lying with his head on the lap of his consort, and kicked him on the chest. The Lord then rose, along with Lakṣmī, as a sign of respect. Coming down from his bedstead, that shelter of all qualities bowed his head to the floor before the sage and told him, “Welcome, brāhmaṇa. Please sit in this chair and rest awhile. Kindly forgive us, dear master, for not noticing your arrival.”**

**Комментарий:**

In Vaikuṇṭha, in a solitary place, Viṣṇu was lying with his head on Lakṣmī’s lap on a jeweled cot. He kicked Viṣṇu on the chest with his foot, not with his fist. This was a great offense. Viṣṇu was not attentive to his arrival since he desired to show the greatness of his devotee though the devotee had acted liked that due to his desire to touch his devotee’s feet. Bhṛgu had come to test sattva-guṇa. However, he saw viśuddhasattva, a portion of the superior śakti, in Viṣṇu. After being kicked, seeing Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu stood up suddenly with Lakṣmī. Standing up from the cot, coming down, he offered respects to the sage and spoke. Since you are merciful please forgive the offence that has happened due to not respecting you by coming in front of you, etc., for I was not attentive that you had come. Please sit down.
