He had no anger toward the sage, though the sage had committed offense when he came at that time. Rather he begged forgiveness showing the quality of viśuddhasattva, which is fixed in Parabrahman.

### Text 10-11

**Перевод:**

**“Please purify me, my realm and the realms of the universal rulers devoted to me by giving us the water that has washed your feet. This holy water is what makes all places of pilgrimage sacred. Today, my lord, I have become the exclusive shelter of the goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī; she will consent to reside on my chest because your foot has rid it of sins.”**

**Комментарий:**

If you have forgiven this offense then please shake your feet and kindly give us the water from your feet. This water makes tīrthas such as Gaṅgā into tīrthas. “I am sinful for committing offense to you the Supreme Lord and to your great devotee Lakṣmī. What is the use of my foot water?” Seeing Bhṛgu’s pain, he pacified him. “You have done a great help to us both.” I have become (āsam) today the supreme shelter of Lakṣmī. O sage endowed with all powers (bhagavan)! You alone are capable of making me so. Thus Lakṣmī (bhutiḥ) will always stay on my chest. Your foot has destroyed my sins in the form of neglecting you. You are the cause of her staying on my chest. Without kicking me, the sins would not be destroyed and she would not stay there.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Bhṛgu felt satisfied and delighted to hear the solemn words spoken by Vaikuṇṭha. Overwhelmed with devotional ecstasy, he remained silent, his eyes brimming with tears.**

**Комментарий:**

On hearing the grave words of the son of Vikuṇṭha, Bhṛgu was at ease in his mind and was pleased. He was silent unable to utter praise since his voice was choked up.

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**O King, Bhṛgu then returned to the assembly of the wise Vedic authorities and described his entire experience to them.**

**Комментарий:**

He described how he tested them.

### Text 14-15

**Перевод:**

**Amazed upon hearing Bhṛgu’s account, the sages were freed from all doubts and became convinced that Kṛṣṇa is the greatest Lord. From him come peace; fearlessness; bhakti; along with detachment and realization; the eightfold powers of mystic yoga; and his glorification, which cleanses the mind of all impurities.**

**Комментарий:**

The sages became convinced that Viṣṇu, who spreads throughout the universe by his glory, was the greatest among three—Brahmā, Śiva and Viṣṇu (bhūyāṁsam). Because of him, others, like Bhṛgu, became peaceful, without disturbance, even if they have committed offenses. Like Bhṛgu others became free of fear. What then to speak of his own peace and fearlessness. From him comes dharma in the form of bhakti characterized by hearing, etc., always. From him comes direct experience of the Lord (sākṣāj jñānam) and by that experience the accompanying detachment too. This detachment is endowed with prema and experience of the Lord and is not dry. The three (bhakti, experience and detachment) appear simultaneously as stated in the Eleventh Canto: Devotion, direct experience of the Supreme Lord, and detachment from other things—these three occur, simultaneously for one who has taken shelter of the Supreme Lord. (SB [11.2.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.42)) Instead of tad-anvitam sometimes catur-vidham is seen. These four types of detachment are called yatamāna, vyatireka, ekendriya and vaśīkāra. vaśīkāra. Yatamāna means the detachment in which the desire for honor (mānaḥ) is subdued (yata). In yatamāna, indulgence in sense objects is present. Vyatireka means indulging in sense objects even without salt, etc (which give taste). Ekendriya means the detachment in which the senses are inclined towards the object of meditation (but the mind is not). Vaśīkāra means complete disinterest in sense objects of this and the next life. The later in the sequence are superior. From him eight types of power come, which are not sought: The devotees certainly do not desire attainment of the happiness of the material universe piled up by māyā, the powers of yoga-siddhis following bhakti, the auspicious rewards of residing in Vaikuṇṭha, or the bliss of Brahman. But the devotees attain the planet of me, the Supreme Lord. (SB [3.25.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.37)) From the Lord come fame, which destroys envy (mala) in the mind of the hearer.

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**He is known as the supreme destination for those who contemplate, who give up violence, who become satisfied, who see everything else with disinterest, who possess nothing except the Lord, and who give up all cheating dharmas.**

**Комментарий:**

Viṣṇu should be worshipped since even when he bestows powers there are no cause of distress. He is the supreme goal of devotees. The devotees are described. They practice meditating on Viṣṇu (munīnām). In order to be free of distraction in that meditation, they give up violence to other beings, a great fault (nyasta-daṇḍānām). Thus due to being absorbed in the Lord, they are satisfied with whatever comes on its own (śāntānām). Thus since they desire the Lord alone, they see gold and stone equally (sama-cetasām). They have no desire for what is experienced by others apart from the worship of the Lord (akiñcanānām).

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Brāhmaṇas who are worshipped like deities, who have good intelligence, who are devoid of attraction and repulsion and thus peaceful, worship that Lord who is the merciful basis of material sattva.**

**Комментарий:**

Though the Lord is beyond guṇas, he is merciful to those in sattva-guṇa. Sattva-guṇa which is his domain of control (mūrtiḥ), is suitable for his mercy. Brāhmaṇas are his worshippable deities since they are fixed in sattva, and even among them those who have fine intelligence, who are niṣkāma and devoid of agitation (śāntāḥ) worship that Lord who is devoid of fear.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**The Lord expands into three kinds of manifest beings—the Rākṣasas, the demons and the demigods—all of whom are created by the Lord’s material energy and conditioned by her modes. But among these three modes, it is the mode of goodness which is the means of attaining life’s final success.**

**Комментарий:**

It was mentioned in the previous verse that sattva-guṇa is the Lord’s dear abode. Thus in response to the question “What abodes are not dear to the Lord?” Śukadeva speaks, distinguishing the three abodes. Three forms are created by māyā’s guṇas. Among them Rākṣasas are in tamas, asuras are in rajas and devatās are in sattva. Viṣṇu is the controller of all of them. “Viṣṇu is nirguṇa, why is he merciful to even those in sattva?” Sattva is the door to understanding scriptures which teach of Viṣṇu (tīrtha). Sattvāt sañjāyate jñānam: knowledge arises from sattva-guṇa. (BG [14.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/14.17))

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The learned brāhmaṇas living along the river Sarasvatī came to this conclusion in order to dispel the doubts of all people. Thereafter they rendered devotional service to the Supreme Lord’s lotus feet and realized him.**

**Комментарий:**

Repeating their words, Śukadeva himself now speaks. The brāhmaṇas, had acted to cut doubts. In this way while the supremacy of Viṣṇu (puruṣasya) is established, Śiva should not be disrespected, since the Lord says: The person who worships me daily with exclusive devotion but criticizes Śiva goes to hell for certain. (Kūrma Purāṇa) Rather Śiva should be respected as the best devotee, since it is said, vaiṣṇavānām yathā sambhuh: Śiva is the best devotee. (SB [12.13.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/13.16)) One should not think that Śiva is equal to Viṣṇu due to supremacy of Śiva seen in Megha-vāhana Parva (Chapter 14 of Anuśāsana Parva, Mahābhārata), since the equality is not the conclusion there and since Padma Purāṇa says: The person who sees Viṣṇu as equal to Brahmā, Śiva and other devatās is certainly a pāṣāṇḍī. (Padma Purāṇa) Thus for the sake of encouraging worship of Śiva is such description given in detail elsewhere even in Megha-vāhana Parva.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: Thus did this fragrant nectar flow from the lotus mouth of Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of the sage Vyāsadeva. This wonderful glorification of the Supreme Person destroys all fear of material existence. A traveler who constantly drinks this nectar through his ear-holes will forget the fatigue brought on by wandering along the paths of worldly life.**

**Комментарий:**

Sūta praises the teachings of his guru, which cut all doubts. If one drinks constantly through the ears this story of Viṣṇu (parasya puṁśaḥ), which conveys the truth, the traveller on the path of saṁsāra (pānthaḥ) will give up fatigue. He will become liberated. The story is nectar with the fragrance of a lotus of Vyāsa’s son and destroys the malady of material life (bhava-bhit). Due to the fragrance of lotus it attracts the bee, a person with knowledge of tattva.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Once, in Dvārakā, a brāhmaṇa’s wife gave birth to a son, but the newborn infant died as soon as he touched the ground, O Bhārata.**

**Комментарий:**

Having stated the supremacy of Viṣṇu among the three deities, in order to establish the supremacy of Kṛṣṇa among the various forms of Viṣṇu though they are nondifferent from each other, Śukadeva tells another story due to remembering it.

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa took the corpse and placed it at the door of King Ugrasena’s court. Then, lamenting because of great grief, feeling misery, he spoke the following.**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇa placed the corpse at the gate of King Ugrasena (rājadvāri).

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**\[The brāhmaṇa said:\] This duplicitous, greedy enemy of brāhmaṇas, this unqualified ruler addicted to sense pleasure, has caused my son’s death by some discrepancies in the execution of his duties.**

**Комментарий:**

My son died, not because of my fault but because of the fallen kṣatriya Ugrasena’s fault of hating brāhmaṇas.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Citizens serving such a king who takes pleasure in violence because of bad character caused by uncontrolled senses are doomed to suffer poverty and constant misery.**

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**The wise brāhmaṇa suffered the same tragedy with his second and third child. Each time, he left the body of his dead son at the King’s door and sang the same song of lamentation.**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇa made the same allegation (gāthām): that the king hated brāhmaṇas, etc.

### Text 26-27

**Перевод:**

**When the ninth child died, Arjuna, who was near Keśava, happened to hear through others the brāhmaṇa’s complaint. Thus Arjuna addressed the brāhmaṇa: “What is the matter, my dear brāhmaṇa? Isn’t there some lowly member of the royal order here who can at least stand before your house with a bow in his hand? These kṣatriyas are behaving as if they were brāhmaṇas idly engaged in fire sacrifices.**

**Комментарий:**

Arjuna had come to Dvārakā from his own city. O brāhmaṇa! Is there not even a fallen kṣatriya holding a bow at your house? Kim svit indicates a question. What to speak of one who is devoted to the brāhmaṇas. “But the Yādavas are there.” They are brāhmaṇas. They are performing sacrifices. Thus he shows contempt for them.

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**“The rulers of a kingdom in which brāhmaṇas lament over lost wealth, wives and children are merely imposters playing the role of kings just to earn their livelihood.**

**Комментарий:**

He criticizes the Yadus. The kṣatriyas make a living wearing the dress of kṣatriyas in whose living presence brāhmaṇas bereft of wealth, etc., lament, since those kṣatriyas are merely role playing, gratifying their prāṇas.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**“My lord, I will protect the progeny of you and your wife, who are in such distress. And if I fail to keep this promise, I will enter fire to atone for my sin.”**

**Комментарий:**

Vāṁ (both of your) indicates that out of great lamentation the Texts 30–31\] Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna Retrieve a Brāhmaṇa's Sons 527 wife had also come. If my promise is not fulfilled rather broken (anistīrṇā) then I will enter fire. By that I will be rid of my sin of breaking the promise.

### Text 30-31

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa said: Neither Saṅkarṣaṇa; Vāsudeva; Pradyumna, the best of bowmen; nor the unequaled warrior Aniruddha could save my sons. Then why do you naively attempt a feat that the almighty Lords of the universe could not perform? We cannot take you seriously.**

**Комментарий:**

We do not believe this (na śraddadhmahe).

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Arjuna said: I am neither Saṅkarṣaṇa, O brāhmaṇa, nor Kṛṣṇa, nor even Kṛṣṇa’s son. Rather, I am Arjuna, wielder of the Gāṇḍīva bow.**

### Text 33

**Перевод:**

**Do not minimize my ability, which was good enough to satisfy Śiva, O brāhmaṇa. I will bring back your sons, dear master, even if I have to defeat death himself in battle.**

**Комментарий:**

Pradhane means “in battle.”

### Text 34

**Перевод:**

**Thus convinced by Arjuna, O tormentor of enemies, the brāhmaṇa went home, satisfied by having heard Arjuna’s declaration of his prowess.**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇa developed faith by Arjuna’s boldness. Hearing (niśāmayan) Arjuna’s declaration the brāhmaṇa went home.

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**When the wife of the elevated brāhmaṇa was again about to give birth, he went to Arjuna in great anxiety and begged him, “Please, please protect my child from death!”**

**Комментарий:**

According to some, Arjuna remained in Dvārakā for one year until it was time for the child to be born. Others say that he came from his city on understanding the birth would take place. The wife said, “Bring Arjuna.” The brāhmaṇa going close to Arjuna at night, begged him.

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**After touching pure water, offering obeisances to Śiva and recollecting the mantras for his celestial weapons, Arjuna strung his bow Gāṇḍīva.**

**Комментарий:**

Arjuna, also went to the brāhmaṇa’s house, and offered respects to Śiva since he disregarded Kṛṣṇa for the fault of ignoring a brāhmaṇa and since he had great respect for Śiva as his guru, who gave him the pāśupāta and other weapons.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Arjuna fenced in the house where the birth was taking place by shooting arrows attached to various missiles. Thus the son of Pṛthā constructed a protective cage of arrows, covering the house upwards, downwards and sideways.**

**Комментарий:**

He used weapons of various types such as brahmāstra, etc.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa’s wife then gave birth, but after the newborn infant had been crying for a short time, he suddenly vanished into the sky in his selfsame body.**

**Комментарий:**

The child disappeared into the sky with his body. Even the body could not be protected by weapons given by Śiva, without the will of the Lord.

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**The brāhmaṇa then derided Arjuna in front of Kṛṣṇa: “Just see how foolish I was to put my faith in the bragging of a eunuch!**

**Комментарий:**

The brāhmaṇa criticized Arjuna in front of Kṛṣṇa (kṛṣṇa-sannidhau), since Arjuna would not have grieved when criticized in private.

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**“When neither Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Balarāma nor Keśava can save a person, who else can possibly protect him?**

**Комментарий:**

How can anyone else protect a person whom (yasya for yam) Pradyumna and others cannot protect?

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**“To hell with that liar Arjuna! To hell with that braggart’s bow! He is so foolish that he has deluded himself into thinking he can bring back a person whom destiny has taken away.”**

**Комментарий:**

Arjuna foolishly wanted to protect (āninīṣati) a person who was killed by the will of the Lord. Not only was he foolish but had bad intelligence since he claimed he was better than Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa (verse 32).

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**While the wise brāhmaṇa continued to heap insults upon him, Arjuna employed a mystic incantation to go at once to Saṁyamanī, the city of heaven where Yamarāja resides.**

**Комментарий:**

Arjuna obtained his powers (vidyām) from Śiva.

### Text 43-44

**Перевод:**

**Not seeing the brāhmaṇa’s child there, Arjuna went to the cities of Agni, Nirṛti, Soma, Vāyu and Varuṇa. With weapons at the ready he searched through all the domains of the universe, from the bottom of the subterranean region to the roof of heaven. Finally, not having found the brāhmaṇa’s son anywhere, Arjuna decided to enter the sacred fire, having failed to keep his promise. But just as he was about to do so, Kṛṣṇa stopped him and spoke the following words.**

**Комментарий:**

He did not see the child since the child’s form which could be understood by the power of his vidyā, was not visible. He went to the city of the moon (saumyām). Because Arjuna trusted Lord Śiva implicitly as his guru, he did not bother to search the northeast (Śiva’s s abode), since Śiva would not take the child. He went to other places such as Brahmā’s abode. Arjuna was prevented (pratyuktaḥ) from entering fire by Kṛṣṇa who stopped him (pratiṣedhatā). Arjuna’s lowliness as devotee of Śiva, which entails disrespecting Viṣṇu, is shown but not of Arjuna as a devotee of Viṣṇu. No one in this world, even a devatā—what to speak of an earthly king—can defeat my devotee with his strength, beauty, fame or riches. (SB [10.72.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/72.11)) But there is no fault of his since he respected Śiva as the best of devotees.

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:\] I will show you the brāhmaṇa’s sons, so please don’t despise yourself like this. These same men who now criticize us will soon establish our spotless fame.**

**Комментарий:**

Do not disrespect yourself (mā avajña). I will show you the brāhmaṇa’s sons. “Do not stop me. Otherwise, people will criticize me as a kṣatriya.” The same ones who are criticizing will establish our fame by this action.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**Having thus advised Arjuna, the Supreme Lord had Arjuna join him on his divine chariot, and together they set off toward the west.**

**Комментарий:**

The words bhagavān and īśvaraḥ suggest that the Lord, though capable of bringing back the child just by his will, went there as a pastime. Kṛṣṇa’s horses had descended from Vaikuṇṭha in order to fulfill their desire to see the earth. His steeds now acted confused to astonish Arjuna and other spectators and listeners of the pastime. This was in line with Kṛṣṇa playing the role of a human. Thus Lord Kṛṣṇa’s offered respects with folded hands to Mahā-Nārāyaṇa, etc.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**The Lord’s chariot passed over the seven islands of the middle universe, each with its ocean and its seven principal mountains. Then it crossed the Lokāloka boundary and entered the vast region of total darkness.**

**Комментарий:**

The seven islands had seven mountain ranges each. They entered a covering of darkness (tamaḥ).

### Text 48-49

**Перевод:**

**In that darkness the chariot’s horses—Śaibya, Sugrīva, Meghapuṣpa and Balāhaka—lost their way. Seeing them in this condition, O best of the Bhāratas, Kṛṣṇa, the supreme master of all masters of yoga, sent his Sudarśana disc before the chariot. That disc shone like thousands of suns.**

**Комментарий:**

In the darkness (tatra), the horses lost their way. He sent his cakra and not his own effulgence to light the way because he was imitating human actions.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**The Lord’s Sudarśana disc penetrated the darkness with its blazing effulgence. Racing forward with the speed of the mind, it cut through the fearsome, dense oblivion expanded from primeval matter, just as an arrow shot from Rāma’s bow cuts through his enemy’s army.**

**Комментарий:**

The cakra pierced the darkness which was dense (gahanam) and extensive (mahat), a transformation of prakṛti (kṛtam).

### Text 51

**Перевод:**

**Following the Sudarśana disc, the chariot went beyond the darkness and reached the endless spiritual light of the allpervasive brahma-jyoti. As Arjuna beheld this glaring effulgence, his eyes hurt, and so he shut them.**

**Комментарий:**

Then by the path following the cakra, going behind it, beyond the darkness, Arjuna saw a disk of great effulgence (param jyotiḥ). His eyes blinded by that he covered them with his hands. He was not able to gaze at it. It was spiritual (param) and spread everywhere (samaśuvānam). Kṛṣṇa explains in Hari-vaṁśa: The divine expanse of Brahman effulgence you have seen is none other than myself, O best of the Bhāratas. It is my own eternal effulgence. It comprises my eternal, spiritual energy, both manifest and unmanifest. The foremost yoga experts of this world enter within it and become liberated. Kṛṣṇa says that he is that light, since the effulgence and the cause of the effulgence are non-different.

### Text 52

**Перевод:**

**From that region they entered a body of water resplendent with huge waves being churned by a mighty wind. Within that ocean Arjuna saw an amazing palace more radiant than anything he had ever seen before. Its beauty was enhanced by thousands of ornamental pillars bedecked with brilliant gems.**

**Комментарий:**

Beyond that, Arjuna entered the Virajā River (salilam). Padma Purāṇa says pradhāna-paramavyomnor antare virajā-nadī: between the material and spiritual worlds lies the Virajā River. It was ornamented with huge waves because of strong wind. Within the river was an effulgent palace called Paravyomā. He saw this (verb in verse 55).

### Text 53

**Перевод:**

**In that palace was the huge, awe-inspiring serpent Ananta Śeṣa. He shone brilliantly with the radiance emanating from the gems on his thousands of hoods and reflecting from twice as many fearsome eyes. He resembled white Mount Kailāsa, and his necks and tongues were dark blue.**

**Комментарий:**

Four verses go together. In that palace first he saw Śeṣa (anantam) who had an unlimited body (bhoga) because of his hoods. He was unprecedented. He shone with the jewels on the hoods of his thousand heads. He was ferocious with twice as many, two thousand eyes. He had the effulgence of a crystal mountain. He had blue (śiti) throats and tongues. Śiti means blue according to Amara-kośa. This suggests Ananta’s attractiveness.

### Text 54-56

**Перевод:**

**Arjuna then saw the omnipresent and omnipotent Supreme Lord, Mahā-Nārāyaṇa, sitting at ease on the serpent bed. His bluish complexion was the color of a dense raincloud. He wore a beautiful yellow garment. His face looked charming. His broad eyes were most attractive, and he had eight long, handsome arms. His profuse locks of hair were bathed on all sides in the brilliance reflected from the clusters of precious jewels decorating his crown and earrings. He wore the Kaustubha gem, the mark of Śrīvatsa and a garland of forest flowers. Serving that Lord of groups of liberated Brahmās were his personal attendants, headed by Sunanda and Nanda; His cakra and other weapons in their personified forms; his consort potencies Puṣṭi, Śrī, Kīrti and Ajā; and all his various mystic powers.**

**Комментарий:**

Arjuna saw the great Lord seated comfortably on the coils of Ananta. He had unlimited powers (mahānubhavam). He was more excellent than even Vāsudeva who is more excellent than the three puruṣāvataras. He was the best, Mahā-Nārāyaṇa. He had thousands of locks of hair which radiated splendor. Though he has four arms at that time he showed eight arms to show to Arjuna that he had something additional to Kṛṣṇa who manifested four arms. He was served by his queen Lakṣmī, and her friends Puṣṭī, etc., and by Ajā along with Kīrti, all full of powers like aṇimā, etc. He was the lord of Brahmās who were liberated at the end of their term.

### Text 57

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa offered homage to himself in this boundless form, and Arjuna, astonished at the sight of Mahā-Nārāyaṇa, bowed down as well. Then, as the two of them stood before him with joined palms, the almighty Mahā-Nārāyaṇa, supreme master of all rulers of the universe, smiled and spoke to them in a voice full of solemn authority.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa’s actions are described. Though Kṛṣṇa is Svayam Bhagavān, he offered respects to the great Lord (ātmānam), his vilāsa form just as he did during the festival of Govardhana. Tasmai namo vrajajanaiḥ saha cakra ātmanātmane: the Lord bowed down to this form of Govardhana Hill, thus in effect offering obeisances to himself. (SB 10.24.36) He offered respects along with Arjuna for otherwise Arjuna should not bow down since he had friendship with Viṣṇu (knowing that he is non-different from Kṛṣṇa). It is not that by bowing down, Kṛṣṇa is less than Mahā-Nārāyaṇa for the same difficulty would arise since he offered respects to even Nārada. Thus this is just his pastime. Arjuna was full of respect (sādhvasaḥ) on seeing MahāNārāyaṇa’s powers and Kṛṣṇa’s bowing down. Mahā-Nārāyaṇa spoke with bold words, understanding Kṛṣṇa’s intention. The words created respect in Arjuna. Mahā-Nārāyaṇa smiled. As I am your vilāsa expansion, I will act according to your will and show by my words, my superiority to you and at the same time hint that I am your vilāsa form, and that you are superior. Arjuna will later understand this.

### Text 58

**Перевод:**

**\[Lord Mahā-Nārāyaṇa said:\] O lord who have appeared with your expansions! I brought the brāhmaṇa’s sons here because I wanted to see the two of you. As soon as you finish killing the demons who burden the earth, quickly make them come to me.**

**Комментарий:**

He addresses the two as me kalāvarīrnau (O my two kalās who have appeared in the world!) “With a desire to see you two, my kalās, I stole the brāhmaṇa’s sons. Take them and killing the demons who are a burden to the earth, quickly come to me.” This statement is to bewilder Arjuna. But this meaning is not the real intention because the words me and kalāvatīrṇau are separated. And the meaning of itam as “come” is not obtained without the prefix āṅ. āṅ. It is impossible that MahāNārāyaṇa had to make efforts to steal the sons ten times to see them if he is their aṁśī and Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna are his aṁśas. The real meaning is this. O two personalities who have descended with all your śaktis (kalā) to protect dharma! The sons were taken to my abode by me, as I desired to see your beauty. Take them. “You have seen us. Now what should be done?” Again, killing the remaining demons which are a burden to the earth, quickly send them to me since my abode which is beyond the eight coverings of the universe is the place of liberation. Thus show your mercy. Anti is a non-conjugated particle with a dative meaning (in order to come to me). Tvarayetam is a causative form in potential mood. In Hari-vaṁśa Kṛṣṇa explains to Arjuna, who asks about MahāNārāyaṇa’s desire to see Kṛṣṇa’s form: “He stole the children in order to see me.” Kṛṣṇa went for the sake of the brāhmaṇa. Otherwise he would not go there. Mahā-Nārāyaṇa did not get to see Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā, though he had gone there many times. This indicates Kṛṣṇa’s greater power. It is not surprising that he wanted to see Kṛṣṇa, since as Svayaṁ Bhagavān, Kṛṣṇa attracts even Mahā-Nārāyaṇa, his vilāsa form. Thus even Lakṣmī, Mahā-Nārāyaṇa’s consort desires to see that form as in yad vāñchayā śrīḥ lalanācarat tapaḥ: with that desire Lakṣmī performed austerities. (SB [10.16.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/16.36)) That form exists only there (in Vṛndāvana) and nowhere else. What austerities must the gopīs have performed! With their eyes they always drink the nectar of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s form, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed. That loveliness is the only abode of beauty, fame and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and extremely rare. (SB [10.44.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/44.14)) Kṛṣṇa’s form causes astonishment even to himself: The Lord appeared in the mortal world by his internal potency, yoga-māyā. He came in his eternal form, which is just suitable for his pastimes. These pastimes were wonderful for everyone, even for those proud of their own opulence, including the Lord himself in his form as the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha. Thus his \[Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s\] transcendental body is the ornament of all ornaments. (SB [3.2.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.12)) Without having them come here, I cannot see them. Thus for that purpose Mahā-Nārāyaṇa acted in that way. Kṛṣṇa is the svayaṁ rūpa since it is said: Kṛṣṇa is the original form of Bhagavān. (SB [1.3.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/3.28)) aṣṭamas tu tayor āsīt svayam eva hariḥ kila The eighth son was the Supreme Lord himself—Kṛṣṇa. (SB [9.24.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/24.55)) Mahā-Nārāyaṇa is Kṛṣṇa’s vilāsa form: I worship the Supreme Lord Govinda by whom respective powers are given to the abodes of Durgā, Śiva and Viṣṇu, which are situated below his own planet of Goloka. (Brahma-saṁhitā [5.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/43)) Bhīṣma too suggests this in the prayers he offers: Parabrahman has no beginning or end. (Kṛṣṇa-stotra, Śānti Parva, Mahābhārata) It should not be doubted that “Why did he not want to see Arjuna’s form?” Arjuna’s form is similar to Kṛṣṇa’s since he is his friend. Kṛṣṇa says to Arjuna in Viṣṇu-dharma: He who knows you knows me. He who follows you follows me. O son of Pāṇḍu! I know you as nondifferent from myself. (Viṣṇu-dharma) Thus what is said is more proper.

### Text 59

**Перевод:**

**Although all your desires are completely fulfilled, O best of exalted personalities, you have appeared as Nara and Nārāyaṇa for the stability of those who practice dharma which is for the welfare of the world.**

**Комментарий:**

“Though you are full in your desires, you should perform (ācaratām) dharma in such a way that the world continues to engage in dharma for protecting Bharata-varṣa (sthityai).” This meaning too is not the intention for it contradicts the previous statement if it meant “Quickly come to me.” Thus, the actual meaning is this. You two, the best of all (ṛṣabhau), have appeared as Nara and Nārāyaṇa, practicing dharma, to protect the religious beliefs of pariniṣṭhita-jñānīs who perform dharma in such a way that the world continues to engage in dharma. This shows their merciful nature.

### Text 60-61

**Перевод:**

**Thus instructed by the Supreme Lord of the topmost planet, Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna assented by chanting oṁ, and then they bowed down to almighty Lord Mahā-Nārāyaṇa. Taking the brāhmaṇa’s sons with them, they returned with great delight to Dvārakā by the same path along which they had come. There they presented the brāhmaṇa with his sons, who were in the same infant bodies in which they had been lost.**

**Комментарий:**

Parame-ṣṭhinā means by Mahā-Nārāyaṇa situated in the spiritual sky. They returned to their abode called Dvārakā by the same path, going through the effulgence, etc. The sons were with the same appearance as when their father, etc., had last seen them. Some say the brāhmaṇa was Sunanda, who was sent as a messenger by Rukmiṇī.

### Text 62

**Перевод:**

**Having seen the domain of Viṣṇu, Arjuna was totally amazed. He concluded that whatever extraordinary power a person exhibits can only be a manifestation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

The meaning of the incident is explained. Seeing the power of Viṣṇu, who shone on the seat of Ananta, in his abode, who was served by associates and śaktis, who was offered respects even by Kṛṣṇa and gave orders to him, and seeing Kṛṣṇa’s complete powers which even such Viṣṇu desired to see and spoke of, and due to Kṛṣṇa’s statements such as mad-darśanārthaṁ te bālā hṛtās tena mahātmanā: That great soul stole the sons in order to see me (quoted from Hari-vaṁśa in verse 58), concluding that with great effort Viṣṇu saw Kṛṣṇa, he was greatly astonished. “During recreation, etc., with words indicating opposite meaning such as ‘You, my friend, performing human pastimes are true to your word, simple and sincere,’ Kṛṣṇa would become humble; How is it that he was desired to be seen by such a greatly powerful Mahā-Nārāyaṇa?” He was most astonished. He considered that whatever powers a man including MahāNārāyaṇa displays arise by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa. It is all included in Kṛṣṇa’s powers. Mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat: there is nothing superior to me. (BG [7.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.7)) My friend Kṛṣṇa is Svayaṁ Bhagavān and MahāNārāyaṇa is his vilāsa. Concluding this he became satisfied. In this way it is determined that Kṛṣṇa is the chief shelter.

### Text 63

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa exhibited many other, similar heroic pastimes in this world. He apparently enjoyed the pleasures of ordinary human life, and he performed greatly potent fire sacrifices.**

**Комментарий:**

Though Kṛṣṇa displayed many other heroic activities equal to those previously described, as a pastime he enjoyed even worldly objects, forms of rasa. Sarva-rasaḥ: the Lord is all rasas. (Chāndogya Upaniṣad) He worshipped the devatās by excellent sacrifices.

### Text 64

**Перевод:**

**The Lord having demonstrated his supremacy, at suitable times he showered down all desirable things upon the brāhmaṇas and his other subjects, just as Indra pours down his rain.**

**Комментарий:**

He showered desired objects just as Indra pours rain since he is Bhagavān and that too eternally endowed (āsthitaḥ) with completeness (śraiṣṭhyam).

### Text 65

**Перевод:**

**Now that he had killed many wicked kings and engaged devotees such as Arjuna in killing others, the Lord could easily assure the execution of dharma through the agency of such pious rulers as Yudhiṣṭhira.**

**Комментарий:**

He established dharma up to bhakti.

## Chapter 90 - Summary of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s Glories

### Text 1-2

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvamī said: The husband of Rukmiṇī resided happily in his capital city, Dvārakā, which was endowed with all opulences and populated by the most eminent Vṛṣṇis and his gorgeously dressed wives. When these beautiful women in the bloom of youth would play on the city’s rooftops with balls and other toys, they shone like flashing lightning.**

**Комментарий:**

In the ninetieth chapter, Śukadeva describes the prema-vaicitrya of the wives playing in the water, enumerates the Yadu dynasty and shows the eternal nature of the pastimes. Madhureṇa samāpayet: One should end with sweetness. According to this dictum, Śukadeva who will be describing Kṛṣṇa’s water sports, describes the beauty of the city which acts as an uddīpana in five verses. Śriyaḥ refers to Rukmiṇī.

### Text 3-6

**Перевод:**

**The main streets of the city were always crowded with intoxicated elephants exuding mada, and also with cavalry, richly adorned infantrymen, and soldiers riding chariots brilliantly decorated with gold. Gracing the city were many gardens and parks with rows of flowering trees, where bees and birds would gather, filling all directions with their songs. Lord Kṛṣṇa was the sole beloved of His sixteen thousand wives. Expanding himself into that many forms, he enjoyed with each of his queens in her own richly furnished residence. On the grounds of these palaces were clear ponds fragrant with the pollen of blooming utpala, kahlāra, kumuda and ambhoja lotuses and filled with flocks of cooing birds.**

**Комментарий:**

After describing the internal beauty, the external beauty is described. The chariots were crafted with gold (kanakojjvalaiḥ). Nāditāyāṁ is formed by the suffix kta in the sense of locative. “In what way did he enjoy?” He simultaneously pleased all the queens. This is not impossible for he took many forms (tāvad victira-rūpaḥ). Pastimes in the tanks of water in the palaces are described. He played in pure water scented with pollen of lotuses, etc. The verb is in verse 7.

### Text 7

**Перевод:**

**The Lord would enter those ponds, and also various rivers, and enjoy sporting in the water while his wives embraced him, leaving the red kuṅkuma from their breasts smeared on his body.**

**Комментарий:**

His play in rivers is described. He was embraced by his wives in the rivers (hradinīṣu). Here it is understood that they were surrounded by high screening walls since that is suitable.

### Text 8-9

**Перевод:**

**As Gandharvas joyfully sang his praises to the accompaniment of mṛdaṅga, paṇava and ānaka drums, and as professional reciters known as Sūtas, Māgadhas and Vandīs played vīṇās and recited poems praising him, Kṛṣṇa would play with his wives in the water. Laughing, the queens would squirt water on him with syringes, and he would squirt them back. Thus Kṛṣṇa would sport with his queens in the same way that the lord of the Yakṣas sports with the Yakṣī nymphs.**

**Комментарий:**

The Gandharvas and others were outside a cloth screen. The Gandharvas and others played drums with the singing. The sūtas (bards) and others played vīṇās along with recitation of Purāṇas. The queens used golden syringes (recakaiḥ). He played like Kuvera with Yakṣīs. This is to show Kṛṣṇa’s boldness.

### Text 10

**Перевод:**

**Under the drenched clothing of the queens, their thighs and breasts would become visible. The flowers tied in their large braids would scatter as they sprayed water on their consort, and on the plea of trying to take away his syringe, they would embrace him. By his touch their amorous feelings would increase, causing their faces to beam with smiles. Thus Kṛṣṇa’s queens shone with resplendent beauty.**

**Комментарий:**

The flowers fell from their long braids. Making a pretense of taking his syringe, they embraced him.

### Text 11

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa’s flower garland would become smeared with kuṅkuma from their breasts, and his abundant locks of hair would become disheveled as a result of his absorption in the game. As the Lord repeatedly sprayed his young consorts and they sprayed him in turn, he enjoyed himself like the king of elephants enjoying in the company of his bevy of she-elephants.**

**Комментарий:**

His garland became smeared (viṣajjita) with kuṅkuma from their breasts.

### Text 12

**Перевод:**

**Afterward, Kṛṣṇa and his wives would give the ornaments and clothing they had worn during their water sports to the male and female performers, who earned their livelihood from singing and from playing instrumental music.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa and his wives gave ornaments and cloth to the dancers and other performers. The possessive case (naṭānāṁ) stands for the dative (gave to the dancers).

### Text 13

**Перевод:**

**In this way Kṛṣṇa would sport with his queens, totally captivating their hearts with his gestures, talks, glances and smiles, and also with his jokes, grabbing them and embraces.**

**Комментарий:**

Their minds were controlled (hṛtāḥ) by his jokes, by his touching of their breasts (kṣveli) and embraces.

### Text 14

**Перевод:**

**The queens would become stunned in ecstatic trance, their minds absorbed in Kṛṣṇa alone. Then, thinking of their lotus-eyed Lord was absent, they would talk as if insane. Please hear these words from me as I relate them.**

**Комментарий:**

They as if insane (unmatta-vat), talked in a way that one would be devoid of discrimination (jaḍam). This is called prema-vaicitrya, a type of anurāga. It is a characteristic of the sixth stage of prema. In this condition, one feels the distress of separation even in the direct presence of the beloved. Their words are as follows:

### Text 15

**Перевод:**

**The queens said: O kurarī bird, you are lamenting. Now it is night, and somewhere in this world our husband is asleep in a hidden place. But you are wide awake, O friend, unable to fall asleep. Is it that, like us, you have had your heart pierced to the core by the lotus-eyed Lord’s munificent, playful smiling glances?**

**Комментарий:**

Controlled by unmāda, they speak to the kurarī (female osprey) and others while seeing their own bhāva everywhere. O friend, the osprey! You alone in this world are sleepless. You lament and do not sleep. You do not want to sleep. That is improper. Why is this? Our husband (īśvaraḥ), remaining hidden somewhere in the night which prevents anyone from finding him, sleeps. It is impossible to find him. Kaccit indicates a question. You should be asked. Like our hearts, has your heart been deeply pierced by the arrow-like, smiling, generous glances of lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa?

### Text 16

**Перевод:**

**Poor cakravākī, even after closing your eyes, you continue to cry pitifully through the night for your unseen mate. Or is it that, like us, you have become the servant of Acyuta and hanker to wear in your braided hair the garland he has blessed with the touch of his feet?**

**Комментарий:**

They speak to the cakravākī. Your husband cannot be seen at night. Because of that you cry. Without seeing your husband, you cry in pain. But this is not the only cause of your crying. You have also become Acyuta’s servant.

### Text 17

**Перевод:**

**Dear ocean, you are always roaring, not sleeping at night. You constantly stay awake at night. Or is it that, as with us, Mukunda has taken your good qualities and you are hopeless like us?**

**Комментарий:**

They speak to the ocean on seeing it. O ocean (udanvan)! Giving up your gravity, you constantly roar (niṣṭanase). Please tell the reason. By saying, we will understand. Have your qualities like gravity been stolen by Mukunda, as he has stolen our qualities? You are like us and have reached a condition that cannot be overcome. This is a great disaster.

### Text 18

**Перевод:**

**My dear moon, having contracted a severe case of tuberculosis, you have become so emaciated that you fail to dispel the darkness with your rays. Or is it that you appear dumbstruck because, like us, you cannot remember the encouraging promises Mukunda once made to you?**

**Комментарий:**

“Though the animals and ocean are wailing with more and more intensity because of Kṛṣṇa’s absence, why is the moon, full of good qualities, silent?” We should ask the moon. O moon! You have a serious case of tuberculosis. Thus, you are weak. Even in full moon you cannot destroy the darkness by your rays (dīdhitibhiḥ) like how the sun does. Perhaps this is not the reason. There is another reason. Considering in this way, they ask. Have you forgotten the secret promises of Mukunda to you and, thinking intently, have become speechless? You are seen like that by us. Is it that like the kurarī, due to the chastisement, you don’t reply to even this question. Like us, you have forgotten his promises because of pain of separation when he left you, and thinking of that, you are speechless.

### Text 19

**Перевод:**

**O Malayan breeze, what have we done to displease you, so that you stir up lust in our hearts, which have already been shattered by Govinda’s sidelong glances?**

**Комментарий:**

They speak to the Malaya wind which blows gently at the end of night. Nu indicates conjecture. O Malaya breeze! What did we do to displease (apriyam) you? For you spread the fire of passion in our hearts which have been pierced by the glance of Govinda. This is not proper for you. You do this though we are not your enemies.

### Text 20

**Перевод:**

**O revered cloud, you are indeed very dear to the chief of the Yādavas, who bears the mark of Śrīvatsa. Like us, you are bound to him by love and are meditating upon him. Your heart is distraught with great eagerness, as our hearts are, and as you remember him again and again you shed a torrent of tears. Topics of Kṛṣṇa brings such misery!**

**Комментарий:**

They speak to a cloud which at that time is sprinkling drops of water. O revered cloud! You are dear to the king of the Yadus. You are his friend for you are bound in prema. You meditate on his Śrīvatsa mark. Your heart is withered in dejection (śavala). Like us, you thus release streams of tears as water drops. Why have you made friends with him? Since even topics of him cause suffering.

### Text 21

**Перевод:**

**O sweet-throated cuckoo, in a voice that could revive the dead, indicating our lover is near, you are vibrating the sounds taught by your lover. Please tell me what I can do today to please you.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the cuckoo warble, they speak to it. O sweet-sounding cuckoo (priya-rāva kokila)! You give advice (padāni) by your words (girā). Pada means what is ascertained. Those words give life to a person dying. O sweet-throated (valgita-kaṇṭha)! How may I please you (karavāṇi)? Please say. In separation, since the words of the cuckoo give sorrow, by expressing contrary emotions, I will crush your beak!

### Text 22

**Перевод:**

**O magnanimous mountain, you neither move nor speak. You must be pondering some matter of great importance. Or do you, like us, desire to hold on your breasts the treasure of the feet of Vasudeva’s son?**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Raivataka mountain they speak. O mountain! You are contemplating some important matter since you do not move. Perhaps this is what you desire. As we desire to hold his feet on our breasts, you desire to hold his feet on your peaks. If you agree this is so, you too will reach our state.

### Text 23

**Перевод:**

**O rivers, wives of the ocean, your faces have lost their beauty of lotuses, and your hearts in the form of pools have now dried up. Alas, you have shriveled to nothing because of not seeing your husband, the ocean. Are you, then, like us, who are withering away because of not receiving the affectionate glance of our dear husband, the Lord of Madhu, who has cheated our hearts?**

**Комментарий:**

In summer, seeing the rivers with meager water, they speak. Now in the summer, these wives of the ocean have become thin and weak, not attaining the glance of their beloved husband, the ocean, in the form of full showers of water from clouds. Their lakes or hearts have dried up. Their lotus faces also have dried up. Thus they have become like us. Our hearts have been cheated (muṣṭahṛdayāḥ), not attaining his glance. Or, O wives of the ocean! Now you have dried up lakes since you do not attain the glance of your dear master the Lord of the Yādavas, who sleeps somewhere, who gives happiness to even you.

### Text 24

**Перевод:**

**Welcome, swan. Please sit here and drink some milk. Give us some news of the descendant of Śūra, dear one. We know you are his messenger. Is that invincible Lord doing well, and does that unreliable friend of ours still remember the words he spoke to us long ago? Why should we go and worship him? O servant of a petty master, go tell him who fulfills our desires to come here without the goddess of fortune. She is the only woman exclusively devoted to him.**

**Комментарий:**

Imagining a swan sitting there as a messenger, they speak. O swan! Welcome. Sit down. Drink some milk. Considering it a guest, they pray. Tell us. We know you are his messenger. First, they ask about his well-being. Is the Lord who is not controlled even by prema happy? They show impatience. “O queens! Without you how can he be happy?” Does he remember his answers to us which showed his steady prema? “He remembers you, who are most devoted to him.” He has unsteady prema (cala-sauhṛdaḥ). “He desires you.” They speak with anger. Why should we worship him? He has no love which is the cause of worship. “He who fulfills desires, who is afflicted by separation, should be worshipped.” O low swan! You have come from a low master. Call the person who fulfills desires here. We will not go there. He should come without Lakṣmī. Greedy for him, she resides on his chest as a golden line. She enjoys with him unseen by us. Do not bring that enemy. “How can she be excluded, since she is dedicated to him?” Among all women is she the only one who is dedicated and not us (striyām)? If we take the alternate reading kṣaudrālāpam akāma-dam, the word kṣaudra means “honey.” Why should we worship the person who simply speaks sweetly but does not fulfill our desires for love? She alone worships him though not respected by him since among women, she is fully dedicated. She is interested in happiness from amorous dealings, but we are interested in good treatment.

### Text 25

**Перевод:**

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: By thus speaking and acting with such ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, the master of all masters of mystic yoga, his loving wives attained the ultimate goal of life.**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva now explains the greatness of the queens. The wives of Mādhava attained the state (gatim) of Viṣṇu, who spreads everywhere (vaiṣṇavīm). They were situated in the same way as he was since they are forms of Lakṣmī.

### Text 26

**Перевод:**

**The Lord, whom countless songs glorify in countless ways, forcibly attracts the minds of all women who simply hear about him. What to speak, then, of those women who see him directly?**

**Комментарий:**

“How did the queens who were right next to him attain this state?” That person, Kṛṣṇa, full of knowledge and bliss, having beauty that derides a million Cupids, who is praised by Nārada and others profusely with many songs, which being heard, attracts the minds of young girls by force. He makes them fully devoted to him. He attracts them who see him at that time. What to speak of his wives who are more than them, associated with him constantly?

### Text 27

**Перевод:**

**And how could one possibly describe the greatness of the worship performed by other women, who serve the Supreme Lord, thinking of him as their husband, by mentally massaging his feet.**

**Комментарий:**

“Please tell the sādhana for how they attained his mercy?” They are nitya-siddhas. Thus, austerities are not described for them. Reme ramābhiḥ: he enjoyed with his consorts. (SB [10.59.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/59.43))

### Text 28

**Перевод:**

**Thus observing the principles of duty enunciated in the Vedas, Kṛṣṇa, the goal of the devotees, repeatedly demonstrated to others the household goals of dharma, artha and kāma.**

**Комментарий:**

Padam means place.

### Text 29

**Перевод:**

**While fulfilling the highest standards of householder life, Lord Kṛṣṇa maintained more than 16,100 wives.**

**Комментарий:**

The dharma of the householder is most excellent (param) since it is the shelter of all other āśramas. It is also said: te’py atraiva pratiṣṭhante gārhasthayaṁ tena vai varam Those who are sannyāsīs, vanaprasthas, and brahmacārīs are all dependent upon the gṛhasthāśrama. Thus, it is the best. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) This is what the author of Vedānta-sūtras says: Because the household āśrama contains rules of all āśramas, it alone is mentioned in the passage concerning realization of Brahman. (Brahma-sūtra)

### Text 30

**Перевод:**

**Among these jewel-like women were eight principal queens, headed by Rukmiṇī. I have already described them one after another, O King, along with their sons.**

**Комментарий:**

Among the sixteen thousand hundred and eight queens (tāsām), the eight were principal queens. The sons number 161,080.

### Text 31

**Перевод:**

**The Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose endeavor never fails, begot ten sons in each of his many wives.**

**Комментарий:**

This is reminded.

### Text 32

**Перевод:**

**Among these sons, all possessing unlimited valor, eighteen were mahā-rathas of great renown. Now hear their names from me.**

### Text 33-34

**Перевод:**

**They were Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Dīptimān, Bhānu, Sāmba, Madhu, Bṛhadbhānu, Citrabhānu, Vṛka, Aruṇa, Puṣkara, Vedabāhu, Śrutadeva, Sunandana, Citrabāhu, Virūpa, Kavi and Nyagrodha.**

**Комментарий:**

The Aniruddha mentioned here is Kṛṣṇa’s son (and not Pradyumna’s son Aniruddha).

### Text 35

**Перевод:**

**O best of kings, of these sons begotten by Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Madhu, the most prominent was Rukmiṇī’s son Pradyumna. He was just like his father.**

### Text 36

**Перевод:**

**The great warrior Pradyumna married Rukmī’s daughter \[Rukmavatī\], who gave birth to Aniruddha who was as strong as ten thousand elephants.**

**Комментарий:**

Aniruddha was as strong as ten thousand elephants. This is from worldly perception. He actually has unlimited power since he is the Supreme Lord.

### Text 37

**Перевод:**

**Rukmī’s daughter’s son \[Aniruddha\] married Rukmī’s son’s daughter \[Rocana\]. From her was born Vajra, who would remain among the few survivors of the Yadus’ battle with clubs.**

**Комментарий:**

Aniruddha married his maternal cousin, Rukmī’s granddaughter.

### Text 38

**Перевод:**

**From Vajra came Pratibāhu, whose son was Subāhu. Subāhu’s son was Śāntasena, from whom Śatasena was born.**

### Text 39

**Перевод:**

**No one born in this family was poor in wealth or progeny, shortlived, weak or neglectful of brahminical culture.**

### Text 40

**Перевод:**

**The Yadu dynasty produced innumerable great men of famous deeds. Even in tens of thousands of years, O King, one could never count them all.**

**Комментарий:**

One cannot enumerate even those who performed famous deeds, what to speak of enumerating all the others. It is well known that the Yādava kings in Mathurā numbered five hundred and sixty million. Most respected was Ugrasena.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**I have heard from authoritative sources that the Yadu family employed 38,800,000 teachers just to educate their thousands of children.**

**Комментарий:**

The reason they cannot be counted is given. The teachers numbered 38,800,000. For every thousand students there was one teacher. This is well known.

### Text 42

**Перевод:**

**Who can count all the great Yādavas, when among them King Ugrasena alone is accompanied by an entourage of thirty trillion attendants?**

**Комментарий:**

Counting them all is impossible but the count of the eternal servants of the king is this much. Āyutānām ayuta-lakṣeṇa “with a lakh of ayutas of ayutas” means three times 10,000 (ayuta) times 10,000 (ayuta) times 100,000 (lakṣa) or 10,000,000,000,000, which is one śaṅkha. Since the plural ayutānām means three, the number is 3 x 10,000,000,000,000 or 30,000,000,000,000 i.e. three śaṅkhas. Among them (yatra) King Ugrasena stays with 30,000,000,000,000 servants. The present tense (āste) is used due to a manifestation of the eternal pastimes to Śukadeva.

### Text 43

**Перевод:**

**The savage descendants of Diti who had been killed in past ages in battles between the devatās and demons took birth among human beings and arrogantly harassed the general populace.**

**Комментарий:**

The demons who were most ferocious, in later births becoming proud, harassed the population.

### Text 44

**Перевод:**

**To subdue these demons, the Lord told the devatās to descend into the dynasty of Yadu. They comprised 101 clans, O King.**

**Комментарий:**

They were in 101 clans, not individuals, since the individuals are impossible to count. At the conclusion of pastimes, they gave up those bodies and returned to Svarga. Regarding them alone (and not the eternal associates) was it previously said: This universe with all its planets is most unfortunate. And even more unfortunate are the members of the Yadu dynasty because they could not identify Lord Hari as the lord, any more than the fish could identify the moon. (SB [3.2.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.8))

### Text 45

**Перевод:**

**Lord Kṛṣṇa alone is the testimony of their power. Among them, all those who were his intimate associates especially flourished.**

**Комментарий:**

Kṛṣṇa alone could estimate the power and number of all his eternal associates. All the Yādavas who were eternal associates of the Lord increased unlimitedly in powers and numbers. The Lord alone was the testimony (pramāṇam) of their power and numbers, not Brahmā or Śiva.

### Text 46

**Перевод:**

**The Vṛṣṇis were so absorbed in Kṛṣṇa that they forgot their own bodies while sleeping, sitting, walking, conversing, playing, bathing and so on.**

**Комментарий:**

Their exclusive dedication to Kṛṣṇa is described.

### Text 47

**Перевод:**

**When the Lord descended among the Yadus, his glories eclipsed the Ganges as a holy place. Both those who hated Kṛṣṇa and those who loved him attained the Lord. He is endowed with the highest beauty and qualities, untouched by others. To see him everyone else struggles. His name destroys all inauspiciousness when heard or chanted. He alone has set forth the principles of the bhakti to the succession of sages. What wonder is it that he, whose personal weapon is the wheel of time, relieved the burden of the earth?**

**Комментарий:**

Summarizing the tenth canto, the ocean of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, Śukadeva explains his five excellences which indicate him as Svayaṁ Bhagavān. O King Parikṣit! The tīrtha in the form of Kṛṣṇa’s fame which took birth among the Yadus—Nanda and Vasudeva and their followers—lessened the status of Gaṅgā, the heavenly river which is his foot water. Previously Gaṅgā was greatest among all tīrthas, but from now the fame of Kṛṣṇa is greater than Gaṅgā. His enemies like Pūtana and friends like the gopīs attained the svarūpa of concentrated consciousness and bliss. Killing Pūtana and others, who were inimical, and he made them blissful by giving them the position of nurse, etc. This shows his supremely compassionate nature. Distinction even in the appearance of equality of svarūpa is inevitable. This should not be forgotten. Others like Brahmā make efforts to attain his mercy (yad-arthe). To attain him Lakṣmī gave up her husband Nārāyaṇa and performed austerities: yad vāñchayā śrī (SB 10.16.36) His name destroys completely all inauspiciousness. The name is the best of all avatāras. It destroys all faults upto ignorance. nāmnāṁ mukhyataraṁ nāma kṛṣṇākhyaṁ me parantapa Kṛṣṇa is the chief of all names, O conqueror of enemies. (Skanda Purāṇa) The result of chanting Viṣṇu-sahasra-nāma three times is attained by chanting Kṛṣṇa’s name once. (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) This is heard and recited. Like a mantra to remove poison, it does not depend on understanding the meaning. By Kṛṣṇa alone, pure bhakti (dharma) was established firmly (ago) in this world (atra) since he accepted those who possessed pure bhakti as saintly even if they had engaged in sinful activities according to api cet sudurācaraḥ (BG [9.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.30)) and because of his promise that they will not deviate from him. Or he established dharma without regard for good family (agotra-dharma). Māṁ hi pārtha vyapāśrityaḥ: those who surrender to me attain the goal. (BG [9.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.32)) Or he established prema along with a family relationship with him for Nanda, etc. (gotra-dharma). Or he performed a festival for Govardhana (gotra) the best of his servants disregarding even Indra. These five items are remarkable in Kṛṣṇa since they are not available elsewhere. Relieving the earth of its burden is not remarkable since that could be accomplished by his devotees. The special reason is this: he has a weapon: time, which is a cakra since it revolves like a cakra. He destroys the demons by his śakti of time as described previously.

### Text 48

**Перевод:**

**Kṛṣṇa is the ultimate resort of all living entities, and is also known as the son of Devakī and Yaśodā. He is the guide of the Yadu dynasty, and with his mighty arms he kills everything inauspicious, as well as every man who is impious. By his presence he destroys all things inauspicious for all living entities, moving and inert. His blissful smiling face always increases the lusty desires of the gopīs of Vṛndāvana. May he be all glorious and happy!**

**Комментарий:**

Śukadeva who is about to speak of the Lord’s disappearance, gives his conclusion to make Parīkṣit’s intelligence steady. Kṛṣṇa, whose glorious pastimes have been recited, not perceivable to others, remains excellent in his abode. He shines eternally with all excellence (jayati). He is the shelter of his associates (jananivasaḥ). He is concluded (vādaḥ) to have manifested by imitating birth pastimes from the wife of Nanda and Vasudeva (devakī). Discussion among those who know the truth is called vāda. He served (pariṣat) the Yadus situated in Vraja as cowherds and in Dvārakā as kṣatriyas. He destroyed adharma, non-vedic teachings by propagating the truth about himself through his devotees and teachers who are like his arms. He destroyed the suffering of saṁsāra for moving and nonmoving beings by propagating teachings and the grief arising from separation of the people of Vraja and Dvārakā by showing himself. By his smiling face, he increased the mādhurya-rasa (kāma-devam) of the dear women of Vraja and Dvārakā, who possessed extreme affection. The present tense in asyan, vardhayan and jayati indicates the eternal nature of the pastimes. Details should be seen in Siddhānta-ratnam. The following should be understood. Kṛṣṇa took birth from Yaśodā and Devakī. Cowherds and Yādavas are his associates. The daughters of cowherds and the daughters of kings are his wives. They were all Lakṣmīs, the essence of the hlādinī śakti combined with the essence of samvit śakti. Some of the gopīs’ names are mentioned in the Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa in the conversation between Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣthira: gopī-nāmāni rājendra pradhānyena nibodha me Hear from me the names of the principal gopīs, O King! The ten gopīs are Gopālī (head of a group friendly with Candrāvalī), Pālikā (friendly with Candrāvalī), Dhanyā (an unmarried gopī), Viśākhā (Rādhā’s sakhī within her own group), and as well Dhaniṣṭhā (Lalitā’s sakhī), Rādhā, Lalitā (Anurādhā), Candrāvalī (Somābhā, Rādhā’s chief competitor), Tārakā (Rādhā’s sakhī, somewhat distant) and Daśamī. Anurādha is Lalitā. Somabhā is Candrāvalī. In the Prahlāda-saṁhitā of the Skanda Purāṇa, starting with the words lalitovāca, a (different) list of the eight chief gopīs is given. These are Lalitā (Rādhā’s chief sakhī), Śyāmalā (in a group friendly to Rādhā, in a suhṛt-pakṣa), Dhanyā, Viśākhā, Rādhā, Śaibyā (one of Candrāvalī’s chief sakhīs), Padmā (chief sakhī of Candrāvalī), and Bhadrā. Only these eight are mentioned but their expansions should be understood. They are all forms of Lakṣmī since it is said: Having attained as their intimate lover Lord Acyuta, the exclusive consort of the goddess of fortune, the gopīs enjoyed great pleasure. They sang his glories as he held their necks with his arms. (SB [10.33.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/33.14)) The gopīs serve Govinda with devotion. (Brahma-saṁhitā [5.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/29)) Among them Rādhā is most excellent. She is Kṛṣṇa’s queen. Rādhā, accompanying the form of Kṛṣṇa, is the queen of Vṛndāvana. (Kṛṣṇa Upaniṣad) The eight daughters of kings, Rukmiṇī and others become doubled to sixteen and for variety in service to Kṛṣṇa, each became a thousand. They are mentioned in Skanda Purāṇa by Śiva as forms of vidyā: Long ago when powerful Kṛṣṇa went to Prabhāsa with all the five hundred and sixty million Yādavas, sixteen thousand queens also gathered there, along with one hundred and six thousand sons. The sixteen vidyās were there. O Pārvatī! I will list their names. Be attentive. They are Lambinī, Candrikā, Kāntā, Krūrā, Śāntām, Mahodayā, Bhīṣaṇī, Nandinī, Śokā, Vimalā, Kṣayā, Śubhadā, Śobhanā, Puṇyā and Haṁsa-sītā. Haṁsa is Kṛṣṇa or Paramātmā. These sixteen śaktis of his are glorified, O Pārvatī! Kṛṣṇa is like the moon and the śaktis are like his sixteen phases. The sixteenth portion is Mālinī. She makes the circle complete (full moon). The moon moves through them starting with the first lunar day. Each of the sixteen portions which have the form of queens divides into thousands. O Pārvatī! I have explained to you the secret which gives rise to knowledge. He who knows this is known as a Vaiṣṇava by the wise. Here the word gopyaḥ means the queens. Gopa means king according to Nānārtha-varga. Lambinī is the avatāra-śakti. Krūra is the śakti which manifests the Lord’s hard nature for the demons though he is soft. She is indicated in mallānām aśaniḥ: Kṛṣṇa was like a thunderbolt for the wrestlers (SB [10.43.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/43.17)) Bhīṣaṇī is the śakti which manifests Lord’s fearsome nature to the wicked though he is compassionate. She is indicated in mṛtyur bhoja-pateḥ: for Kaṁsa, Kṛṣna was death. (SB [10.43.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/43.17)) Śokā is the śakti which manifests Lord’s nature of causing lamentation (śokā) to demonic persons, though he is the highest bliss. She is indicated in asatām kṣiti-bhujām śāstā: he was a punisher for the impious kings. (They would lament when Kaṁsa was killed). (SB [10.43.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/43.17)) The śaktis act just like the brilliance of the sun which displays darkness to owls. They are forms of vidyā but manifest as such for demons. Mālinī, the sixteenth śakti is Rukmiṇī, the best of them. They are all forms of Lakṣmī: There, fully saturated with a special prema, he enjoyed with Lakṣmīs, and like an ordinary husband he carried out his household duties. (SB [10.59.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/59.43)) Thus they are related to his svarūpa. That is expressed by candrarūpī mataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ: Kṛṣṇa is like the moon (in the verses quoted above). Just as Lord of Dvārakā is the full manifestation (pūrṇa as compared to pūrṇatara and pūrṇatama forms) of Svayaṁ Bhagavān, the lord of Gokula, so the queens are full manifestations of the gopīs. In his kaiśora age, his consorts who were the gopīs, were the princesses in his youth. (Padma Purāṇa)

### Text 49

**Перевод:**

**To protect the principles of devotional service to himself, Kṛṣṇa, the best of the Yadus, accepts the pastime forms that have been glorified here in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. One who desires to faithfully serve his lotus feet should hear of the activities he performs suitable to his human form, that appear like human acts, which destroy karma.**

**Комментарий:**

He advises hearing about Kṛṣṇa, who has such nature. One should hear the activities of the best of the Yadus, whose body is composed of pastimes manifested (ātta) out of a desire to protect bhakti (nijadharma). Those activities suitable to his form composed of pastimes surpass (viḍambanāni) others’ actions which appear similar or make the actions of the avatāras inferior. The Lord’s actions expand his transcendental glories. (SB [2.7.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.26)) These activities destroy the bondage of karma, though they are forms of activity (karma-kaṣaṇāni). Thus they are astonishing. One who desires to follow (anuvṛttim) his feet should hear these activities.

### Text 50

**Перевод:**

**By regularly hearing, chanting and meditating on the beautiful topics of Mukunda with ever-increasing sincerity, a mortal being will attain the divine kingdom of the Lord, where the inviolable power of death holds no sway. For this purpose, many persons, including great kings, abandoned their mundane homes and took to the forest.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of following his feet is described. Any human being, serving the Lord’slotusfeet, attains Kṛṣṇa’s abode by contemplating through hearing and chanting the topics of Mukunda which give all the wealth (śrīmat). The contemplation is nourished by the longing (edhitayā) ‘When or how will one attain this?’. In that abode the onslaught (java) of time (kṛtānta) which is difficult even for Brahmā to escape (dustara) is absent. It is not affected at all by time. Desiring this goal, even kings left cities, crowded with citizens and went to the forest. Renouncing kingdom, they meditated on the Lord in solitude. Following the Lord’s feet, they attain the Lord’s abode which is free of fear and happily live there at all times. May the tenth canto, the shelter of the swans (paramahaṁsa devotees), full of Kṛṣṇa’s rasa, the undecaying lake, remain ever excellent, from which thousands of such streams flow out. Kṛṣṇa becomes controlled immediately by the devotee by his efforts in bhakti. Will the excellent Lord not glance at me because of my efforts at explaining the tenth canto? May the merciful devotees, knowers of Kṛṣṇa’s rasa, glance upon this commentary on the tenth canto written by Vidyābhūṣaṇa. About Śrī Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa Śrī Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa (Śrī Govinda Dasa) appeared in the 1600's near Remuna, Orissa. In his youth, he mastered Sanskrit grammar, poetry, and logic. After carefully studying the commentries of Sankara and Madhva he took initiation in the Tattva-vadi disciplic succession of Śrīpad Madhvacarya. Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa became a dig vijaya pandit (conqueror of all opponents) and began visiting the holy places. Wherever he went he defeated the local sages, scholars, and sannyasis. In Vrindavana, he studied Śrīmad Bhagavatam under Śrīla Vishvanatha Cakravarti Thakura and worshipped Radha-Syamasundara. In 1706 A.D. Vishvanatha Cakravarti Thakura sent him to Gulta (near Jaipur,Rajasthan) to uphold the credibility of Mahaprabhu's movement. The local Ramanandis (a branch of Śrī Vaishnavas) were claiming that the Bengali Vaishnavas had no right to worship Govindaji they had no commentary on the Vedanta-sutra. Lord Govindaji Himself directly revealed the Govinda-bhasya (a Vaishnava commentary on Vedanta) to Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa. Using it, Baladeva solidly established Gaudiya Vaishnavism as an independent philosophy. He also reinstated the Bengali Vaishnavas in Govindaji's service in Jaipura. Govinda-bhasya is the only bhakti commentary on Vedanta-sutra. Śrī Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa was a niskincana-parama bhagavata, fullyrenounced topmost Devotee of Lord Krishna. His more than twenty-four books and commentaries have helped thousands of Vaishnavas understand the sublime philosophy of Krishna consciousness and the intimate writings of the six Goswamis. Since he was devoid of false prestige, he never wrote about his birth, parents, lineage, personal life. According to Śrī Bhaktivinoda Thakura in Navadvipa-dhama mahatyam, in Chaitanya lila Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa is Śrī Gopinatha Acarya, the brother-in-law of Śrī Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya. In Vraja he serves as Śrī Radha's eternal maidservant Ratnavali Devi.
